reviews.comment: Reasonable and super nice!

The lectures were not very intriguing and I felt like it was very difficult to learn from her. She lacks excitement when teaching and wasn't always able to answer students questions. The TA was also impossible to work with. This class is my least favorite in all of my college courses ive taken.

This professor almost made me fall asleep during every lecture. We would be on the same slide for almost the entire class. She did not explain the material well and I think she tried too hard to appeal to the students. The TA is another story too!

Professor Prorok was a very good professor, however I will say that it may have just been a tough TA, but the grading rubric was quite difficult. Lecture notes are posted if you miss a class but does take attendance with iClickers. Material was interesting which helped but there were a lot of readings.

Professor Prorok is a good professor. Her lectures are very engaging and she really enjoys teaching .The class is pretty difficult. There are a lot of readings and quizzes are pretty hard to get a 10 on unless you are lucky. The papers are not terrible but make you apply the concepts. The midterm and Final take up to 50 percent of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Prorok is a phenomenal professor. However one thing to note, she doesn't have lecture slides and will write some things on the board but you have to listen carefully and take notes. As long as you do that, you'll do well in the class. It is also very evident that she cares about her students and try to help them succeed as best she can.

Frequent quizzes reinforced the material and encouraged consistent studying. Exams were challenging, but steady effort paid off. The professor was accommodating with scheduling. My only concern was the ACI code marking and retention penalties, which sometimes felt arbitrary and inconsistent. Overall, I learned a lot.

This is the worst professor I've ever had. There's a quiz every two weeks, and some of the material wasn't even covered in class. There are only four assignments, but each one is basically over 15 pages long. During office hours, instead of asking him questions, he tells you to go back and review the material yourself.

Professor Bassem Andrawes teaches really well. His classes are engaging and interesting. He also encourages participation of students during his class. Also, gives only 4-5 Homeworks in a Semester. However, the questions that he asks in exams have a lot of wordplay and are tricky in general. He teaches well but comes of as unfriendly at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He does a good job in explaining material with clarity and practicality. He also gives good examples in class. However, as a person, he is very unfriendly and arrogant.

One of the worst professsors you can ever have. He basically reads his previous notes, no real explanation really.   Very unmerciful. He graded us 0 for quizzes that were handed in a few seconds after he said time is over.  Very racist and unfriendly. Arrogant.

Prof. A. is one of the best professors in the CEE department. Very fair, places emphasis on homework and quizzes, and is a very clear teacher. He does not assign excessive homework and does a good job matching his exams to what he teaches. He's a no non-sense guy, and I recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I have ever had. He bases all of his grades on his personal opinion of you as a student/person.
Prof Alam is the best lecturer I got. He was a life saviour in explaining complicated mathematical details.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Generous grader (sometimes), but has very difficult personality and is an extremely poor lecturer. You can get an easy A but you will learn almost nothing. Its a weed-out class but not on the basis of difficulty, just on your patience to deal with the profs antics.

HW problems are verbatim from lecture slides, so students have no opportunities to think critically until the exams, which are the vast majority of the grade. The content is taught poorly, and many students have had to retake with a different professor because so much knowledge was lacking. Prof is an unbearable lecturer and skips critical content.

The class is not too difficult, but he curved our class down. His assignments  may have you do unrelated computer projects that are graded incredibly harshly. His schedule is inconsistent with the syllabus, and he does not reply to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course was both one of the least informative and yet easiest courses I have ever taken, not because the tests were reasonable but because the curves were incredibly high. Material we seldom ever worked with became the majority of the final, and everyone suffered because of it. He was also very insistent on getting positive feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While the course itself is laughably easy, in addition to the other reviews, he very blatantly used AI to create the last section of material, and has not bothered to remove the dead giveaways, often giving wrong explanations to students as a result. Although he has an impressive educational background, I'm skeptical of what he actually knows.

This professor flies by the seat of his pants, he changes the syllabus as he pleases, there is no consistency in expectations, he changes, adds, and drops major assignments all of the time and changed the weightings of exams midsemester. He is also vindictive, he asks for feedback and if you give any sense of negative feedback, he will get angry.

I had a 95% all throughout the semester doing well on both exams, he then proceeded to have us fill out a feedback form before the final, where he put content from classes not yet covered, so we all said he was great. He clearly wrote his own RMP when he was at Mizzou. If you like nuclear you need to tough it out for his classes. Good luck.
Very disorganized. Doesn't care about her students. Wouldn't recommend her as an advisor.
Average and condescending. I'm not sure if she has the self-awareness to know that.

Prof. Kou is a pretty good lecturer imo. While she doesn't go beyond the syllabus, her lectures are straightforward and well structured. If you go to her office hours or ask questions after class, she answers them really well. The course itself is extensive, but that isn't something she can do anything about.

"ok" is the first word I can think of to describe. I went to Paul Kwiat's lectures a couple of times and he was more enthusiastic about the material and had more understandable explanations. Professor Kou does her job though. She takes time to try and explain the slides and does cool demos, but I would not say she's likely the best option.
She was alright.  Definitely have to teach yourself outside of class but that's pretty normal.  Just did clicker questions or demos in class and didn't learn much in the lecture. Kind of boring.
Actually, I don't think she is so bad. At least, her design of the course helps me easily pass the course as long as you can figure out the homework problems by yourself.
Prof. Kou not teach us anything, all we did in lecture was iclickers. Lectures are required though. Be prepared to learn everything outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I hate her and all the phys 212 course staff. Stupid style of examination allows for no partial credit and all or none. No wonder everyone takes this class over summer
Mid lecturer. The final was BS, and that could be an understatement

There was no real teaching that went on in her class. Students are expected to learn the material on their own and the lecture is just a place where misunderstandings can be corrected. She misspeaks so often during lecture that it makes her explanations hard to follow. I relied entirely on the textbook to get through this class.

Lectures are so stupid. They are the exact same thing as the prefectures however attendance is graded so you have to attend them anyway. I found myself either sitting through the entire lecture on my phone or would skip through the whole prelecture then take notes in class, it's redundant to have both. She's a fine lecturer but nothing outstanding.
Sometimes it felt like there was a disconnect between prelectures and lecture. Most learning comes from prelectures and discussions. The actual lecture period doesn't feel very productive

Lectures are just re-reading slides from checkpoints and prelectures. Answers to students questions are regurgitated from the formulas given on these slides and little input is given on how to conceptually grasp the material, which is particularly important in this class. Angela is nice and loves physics, but the lectures are mind-numbingly boring.
If you do the prelectures and checkpoints, the lectures become much easier to understand. Professor Kou was good at answering questions and the demos were interesting.

Does not have any idea of how to explain concepts effectively, nor any idea of how to listen and try to understand students' questions, nor any idea of how to pace the lectures so that we can spend time on important things that are harder to grasp. Monotone. Do not choose her lecture section, it's on a totally different level than Stelzer's.

No. Avoid this Professor. He mumbles when he talks, no relation between what he says (if you can understand) & what is on the poorly organized slides, badly organized course and assignments that do not teach you the basics. How this Prof still retains his job is a mystery & a misery - he could have easily redone the lectures over the years
Class is pretty easy to get by with not a lot of work and it being mostly online but the lecture videos are not good, won't learn a thing
Nothing really changed since 2021. Slides are really bad, reading out equations, few explanations. Everything is still holding true from prior comments. Quiz and MP are barely related to the lecture.

His lecture videos and slides are extremely inefficient, you learn nothing of value and its explained horribly. The workload is light but coding assignments have nothing to do with the content and are explained poorly and the quizzes are intentionally tricky. This class needs a rework, poor quality all around

Being a fully online class, it is hard to engage with the professor. So, I appreciate his efforts to stay in touch with students with his "live" office hours, despite not taking much advantage of it myself. The material is neatly organized on Coursera, and everything is graded immediately. No exams, so grade is based on assignments only.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not sure who hired this Professor for a teaching position, I got nothing useful out of his 'lectures'. If you can find a different professor, go with the other professor.

The lectures are trash for this class. They are boring and 1-Dimensional. The MPs are fine, I guess, but they go into way more detail than he'll ever explain. Kind of a waste of time, but an easy A for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors in UIUC. Please avoid CS 441 if you can. He just reads off slides which usually make little to no sense. The programming assignments are somewhat okay but the lectures are horrendous.

I am sorry, but if a university like UIUC keeps hiring professors like this, its reputation will soon go down to that of a community college. This professor mumbles when he talks, does not  explain things clearly at all, heavily disorganized and wastes time. You do not learn anything from the classes

How does a university as reputed as UIUC get a Professor like this? :(  The lecture slides were not organized, lectures do not have correspondence with the slides being shown, I can hardly follow what is being said because of the accent. Little effort has been put in preparing the lectures. Hoped to learn the basics of ML, but did not learn much.

This class was online and I'm not sure if it was because of the professor or because I'm tired of online classes, this class wasn't ideal for me. I had high hopes. Instead of basic ML, I got good at NumPy manipulation. The professor has online videos in the name of lectures in which he mostly reads off the slides. Take this class in person.
Does not explain properly

If you are taking 441 online, you basically will only be interacting with TAs anyways. I think the prof's name is slapped onto the course for some authenticity. Pretty easy A and the class can be done in half a semester. The only time you hear the prof talking is him reading the slides out for his lecture videos. Basically a self taught class.

SOOOOO BAD at lecturing... Just reading through slides and the slides are the worst I've ever seen... Really really hard to understand what he's trying to teach even for the materials I've learned before. I feel bad for those who haven't learned ML before and wish to get a general idea of this field.
Just reads out the slides
I enjoyed a math class for the first time ever because of Prof. Hoffmeister. That should tell you all you need to know. She is the very best!

Prof Hoff was very caring for her students inside and outside of class. As long as you do the homework and keep up on the content this class is extremely manageable. Her exams are very easy and usually examples very similar to those in the workbook or done in lecture.

Professor Hoffmeister is the best! She clearly cares so much about her students, and she makes sure to explain concepts in a different way if you are confused. Calc 2 is a hard class no matter who teaches it, but prof hoff made the class much more bearable :)
Good lectures, the exams are straightforward as long as you study. She is also one of the sweetest professors ever

Professor Hoffmeister has her students' best interests at heart. She is kind and very engaging in lecture. Calculus II is challenging, but Professor Hoffmeister's succinct and clear explanations boosted my confidence in my mathematical reasoning.

Professor Hoffmeister was an amazing lecturer and overall made Calculus II much easier. I attended all of her lectures and I rarely left any of them wondering what we just learnt. If you have the option to take her I would genuinely do it she is the GOAT.

I went into this class with starry eyes. Ended the course with bags under my eyes. She made me realize how much I prefer 8 hour shifts more than this. She walks into 8 am lectures with so much energy, all energized by student tears. I had to tell my parents 'I love you' (I never said that before) since things got so bad... don't take this course.
Very knowledgeable and kind professor that cares about her student's success.
Best Professor for 231. Very nice and makes lectures understandable. Attendance is not mandatory, but is necessary to do well. Best professor I have had thus far.
I have attended lectures with both 231 profs, and I definitely prefer Dr. Hoffmeister's class. She is great at explaining and really tries to help us understand the topics.

Signed up for this class fully prepared to suffer, but Dr. Hoffmeister made it way better than I expected. She explains tough concepts clearly, adds humor to keep you awake, and cares if you understand. It is still a challenging class, but you will learn a lot if you put in the effort.
very fun and nice teacher, i need her to teach calc 3 im begging
She is the best math professor and such a nice person. We need her to also teach 241. PLEASE. I miss her lectures. I actually understood when she would explain things.
Loved giving extra credit. Very inspirational. One of the best professors to start off my college career with. 100% would recommend.
Easily the best class for teaching math. I want to be like Prof. Hoffmeister when I grow up.
Favorite class and professor of my first semester. I actually wanted to attend lecture because she is that good. You do need to study to do well in the class. Dr. Hoffmeister, your students love you.

Great professor and a great person. Detailed lectures that explain all of the steps to solve problems along with the derivation for them. Cares a lot about the students and had lots of opportunities for extra credit along with raised the cutoff for an A to be 90% and an A- to be 88%.

Probably my favorite class ever was with professor Hoffmeister. Nothing extremely difficult but it was super hands-on and interactive and she was very easy and fun to work with in terms of material creation. Learned a lot about mathematics teaching from her! Definitely someone you'd love to work under!!!!
sas goooooood
Dr. Hoffmeister is the best! Her lectures are so good. She really cares about students and is funny, too.
Shes very nice, but the class has caused some trauma for me. I went from I want to get an A to I just want to pass in 2 weeks. Go to office hours.

good professor but beware of the very picky graders. that honestly made this class 5x more tedious for me. if you have credit for calc from hs DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS HERE even if your advisor recommends it, you'll probably find it to be more of a burden than a help. take the proficiency exam instead and just review the stuff you may have forgotten

amazing instructor, one of the best in the math dept honestly in terms of instruction quality. however, i really hated how the class itself was structured (pretty high percent of grade for discussion) and my ta was horrible. the graders can be very stingy so be careful with the "little mistakes" if you're prone to careless math errors.
Had her for a brief stint, but she was fantastic. She was very kind and taught the material very well.

I loved Dr. Hoffmeister. She was so approachable and caring. She thoroughly explained each concept and cared if her students struggled or not. She was my absolute favorite professor. The class is hard, but having Dr. H makes it a whole lot more manageable.

If you want to get an A or do well on the tests, you will want to go to office hours. A 5 credit hour class is definitely demanding. I was in office hours every week going over my lecture notes just to begin to understand them. Fantastic TA's there to help. Never had to watch any youtube vids or anything, but office hours are a must.
She explained the concepts well, and had comprehensive review sessions.
I hate math, but Dr. Hoffmeister is the best!  I still have yet to meet anyone who doesn't like her.

Professor Hoffmeister is a great lecturer and a really kind person. Her lectures are easy to follow and her notes are easy to read and she gives very helpful tips. Calc isn't an easy class, but her lectures are very helpful. My advice is to try not to skip lectures.

Very engaging and involved professor. Made sure to answer every question and slow down so ppl could understand. I  didn't miss a single lecture because she was kind and friendly. Graded by few things (disc. attendance, homework, exams) so make sure to try your best. The class is fair but make sure to study everyday, especially for the final.

She was so nice, highly recommend! Calc can be difficult but she tried her best to make the information clear and exams were pretty straight forward. Definitely take Calc 1 with Hoffmeister if possible.

If you're taking Calc, take it with Dr Hoffmeister. She's so good students from other sections sneak into her lectures. Everyone knows she's the best. I will not miss calculus, in fact I will do the very opposite of missing it, but I will miss seeing Professor Hoffmeister every week!
Best 220 teacher, dont take Kim
Professor is really nice
I loved her class. The homework can be challenging but if you cannot figure it out you can always go to office hours to get help. The tests and final were straightforward.
I was never that good at understanding math until I took professor Hoffmeister. She explains topics very well and is super funny. I loved her!

Dr.Hoffmeister is a goat. She is so caring, understanding, and effective with her way of teaching. She makes students feel seen and she goes out her way to do the best she can to help students. She encourages her students to do the best they can, and she provides other resources. Homework is similar to tests so make sure to not procrastinate.
She has pretty decent lectures, and has great TAs that make sure you really understand the concepts

I was honestly scared to take Calculus at first but Professor Hoffmeister made it so easy to follow along and understand the concepts that it made learning enjoyable. She always asks if there are any questions and makes sure you understand the material. Her lectures are also very entertaining. Definitely the best calc professor there is!

Dr. Hoffmeister is truly an exceptional Calc professor who cares about her students and their future success in higher math classes. Her explanations are clear and thorough and she makes sure to explain how and why some topics work, which I really appreciate. Her lectures feel personal and engaging which makes the learning process so much easier!

One of the best Professors I've had so far. I really want her for Math 220 as well. Definitely wants her students to succeed and makes sure to check in with students. Even with the large class size, she is very approachable for help.

Truly the best math professor I've ever had. Her lectures are very understandable and she explains heavy, in-depth material simply and clearly. She also takes time to answer each student's questions after the lecture and provides a good explanation. If you have the chance, definitely choose this professor's class. Highly recommended

If I had the chance, I would like all new students to choose this professor. First of all,  This professor's pronunciation is very standard and clear. Secondly, Professor Hoffmeister's teaching atmosphere is very humorous and makes us feel very relaxed in class. The professor's professionalism is also very high in my personal opinion.

-She explains the materials in depth and in a clear way.
- Trys to answer questions in class as much as possible.
- Not too strict when teaching.
- Funny
Best lecturer I've had.
Dr. Hoffmeister was awesome the whole semester; it was apparent that she cared a lot about all of her students. Her lectures are very clear and helpful.

She's an amazing professor! Absolutely love her classes, 90% is an A (not 93). She had extra credit opportunities toward the final which was super helpful. The class workload was not bad, pls attend discussions as they have 13% weight. Totally possible to get an A with just a little effort. Final is only 20% of the grade, midterms (15% x3 = 45%)

doctor hoffmeister is my favorite professor. i have adhd and i found it so easy to pay attention in her lecture since she seemed so passionate in what she was teaching. i did not put in as much effort into the class as i should have due to personal circumstances but i found it fairly easy to catch up

Professor Hoffmeister is absolutely amazing! She really cares on if you understand the material and always answer questions. If you go to lecture/discussion and do the homework, you will be fine. She gives plenty of review material and is truly the best professor I have ever had! The exams are very fair and over material we studied so no surprises.

The class is as advertised. Most of the time I hear she never takes attendance and she never has in my class so I haven't been since September, but I would actually recommend going if you have her. She takes questions in class and answers them well and the lecture pace is great for all different levels of skill in math. TAs are great.

Is very easy to understand her lectures with her not simply throwing proofs and equations at you but doing math beforehand that sneakily puts the concept in your head to the point it feels obvious. Very easy to access outside of class with fast response times and is always helpful. I would take her class again if possible and I would recommend it.
Best prof of my freshman year by far. Super caring and fun. Made precalc enjoyable somehow.
That is the BEST professor I have ever seen!!!!!!!!!!

This was my favorite class this semester. This is a class geared towards teachers, so I liked that Dr. Hoffmeister spoke to us like peers and sometimes even asked us what we would do as educators if we were teaching the class too. She is very understanding and knows that we sometimes need a class some weeks that are slower paced.

I took 3 different courses with April; CA and graded two of her courses. April cares for her students far past the grades in her class. She offered me endless opportunities to grow. As a CA she taught me so many valuable lessons I use in my classroom today. She continues to guide me through my teaching career today. I am forever grateful for her!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Mrs. Hoffmeister was an extremely kind lady and attended to her students almost immediately if contacted. In my experience math teachers are my least liked teachers; however, I truly appreciated her teaching style, friendliness, jokes, and flexibility with ensuring students are understanding material prior to moving on to the next lesson.

She makes sure to explain Math in a way you can understand it and if you have a question she will go through and explain the problem until you do understand it. Very easy to reach through campus wire and gets back to you in a timely manor. Also very flexible with her course if things do come up or if she sees a trend happening in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Hoffmeister is the absolute best! Not only is she willing to take time outside of her workday to help us when needed, but she also makes her lectures both enjoyable and extremely informative. In all of the classes I have taken with her, she has made it extremely clear how much she cares about her students and how she believes we can succeed!

Personally, I enjoyed every lecture I attended. Hoffmeister works at a fast pace but if you attend most of the lectures and use your course packet, you will be fine. She offered office hours every day which was an extremely helpful resource. Overall, she was my favorite professor this semester!

Dr Hoffmeister is such a caring professor. She truly wants us to succeed and makes doing so enjoyable and feasible! She is clear, interactive, made references to Mean Girls when we talked about limits, and occasionally told funny stories in between problems. Great Professor and I hope to have her again.
I learned a lot about preparing lessons and from how my classmates explained material. Dr. Hoffmeister's feedback on our lessons and teaching was very helpful!
A very good professor. She explained the content well in her lecture videos and did bend over a backwards a few times for me when I didn't submit the homework right at 3pm on Sunday.

Dr. Hoffmeister is one of the best professors I think UIUC has. She is extremely compassionate and caring about all of her students. It is very apparent that she wants each and every one of her students to succeed. I would love to have her as my professor again!

Dr. Hoffmeister was honestly the best professor I could have asked for. She was super nice whenever I would go to her office hours and was always willing to help me when I needed help. She answered all of my questions clearly and never made me feel bad about the questions I had. She's also really funny and has the best stories to tell!

Prof. Hoffmeister was always very enthusiastic during her in person lectures and always put the student's understanding of material at the forefront of the course. She always made sure everyone was clear of what we were discussing and never hesitated to go over a topic that seemed confusing. Overall, a great prof. who truly cares about her students

Great professor. Her ability to adapt due to tough time (covid-19) made the class way less stressful and worth it. She genuinely cares for all her students and made most if not all of us feel worthy and respected. Honestly one of the best professors you will ever have.
Great

Professor Hoffmeister was one of the best Math professors that I have had! Class-time was structured in a group-based way where we completed different problem sets in our groups. Prof was awesome at helping concepts make sense in a variety of ways. It is clear that Professor Hoffmeister cares about her students and is passionate about Math.

There is a heavy emphasis on group work for practice problems, but Dr. Hoffmeister is always available for help. She answers emails quickly and is available outside of class if you're struggling. It's easy to see that she has a passion for math education, and that's what makes her a great professor!

Easily one of the best professors at UIUC. She genuinely cares for her students' success and assists in any way if you have questions. As a future educator, Dr. Hoffmeister is an inspiration to follow. Would definitely take another course with her again!

April Hoffmeister is an amazing professor. You can tell she genuinely cares about her students and wants every single one to understand the material. Lectures aren't mandatory but they're important and helpful. She explains the material in a very simple way, so even if you aren't great at math but put in the work, you will succeed in this course.

Dr. Hoffmeister is a very good professor. She cares about the students and wants you to do as well in the class as possible. She's very interactive and wants students to ask questions if confused. The class relies on both lecture notes and student participation, which is the best style of teaching. In this class, participation helps most students.

April was genuinely a really good prof. She cares a lot about her students and makes tests easier to prepare for with how clearly she outlines things. A lot of notes, but overall made math much easier for me and I suck at it.

My favorite math class i've ever taken, and I don't normally enjoy math. She is easy to follow, and she wants you to ask questions. She goes relatively slow and gives you a chance to learn. Sit up front, though because she is not very loud.
She was very nice and caring! Explained lecture nicely and clearly. There was a lot of practice problems though.

Professor Hoffmeister has been the BEST professor Ive had so far. Shes funny and cares about her students. Lots of notes in lecture but theyre all helpful! She makes sure you understand things and encourages questions. I wish she could teach all of the math classes.

Lectures are a lot of notes, but she is really nice. She answers questions and will stay behind to help students. Notes might not help with the HW, but there are office hours like 6 times a week for 2 hours at a time with different TAs. 3 tests and a final.

Probably one of the best professors I have ever had , and she not only cares about your academic achievement, and her lectures are anything but boring. Her class does have a lot of course load, but she does a great job at helping you if you need it. Love her! Would definetely have her again!!

April is a great teacher. Sometimes she would give too many confusing definitions, but lots examples. At times lecture didn't exactly line up with worksheets. She always took questions and made sure we understood things. Great personality and easy to talk to. Always made sure TAs were avaliable for help. Takes forever to answer emails, like 4 days
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Hoffmeister was a good professor. She explains the material quickly but thoroughly and WANTS you to ask questions if you are confused. If you don't pass the tests, it's literally your own fault because she gives you a list of what material you should study and a lot of the test material is taken from homework.
I loved having Dr. Hoffmeister as a professor and always enjoyed going to lecture.  She has high expectations of her students, but also really cares about your success in the course.

Math 103 was very hard. Don't think it is easy because of the course description. But Prof. Hoffmeister is great. She is nice and cares about you doing well. She gives lots of outside help in office hours. GO TO OFFICE HOURS IF YOU ARE HAVING A HARD TIME!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Hoffmeister is an amazing instructor.  I am not sure where these people come up with the idea that her exams are impossible.  You are attending a well-respected four year University, AND you are preparing to become educators yourselves.  Quit whining, grow up, and start acting like responsible adults and not spoiled little brats.

Professor Hoffmeister is definitely tough, but she is indeed fair. She talks about her children a lot and incorporates what they are learning into our lessons. The class itself s incredibly tough. There are four exams and, so far, 2 of the 3 taken have been impossible. There is so much material, and it is never truly clear what to study.
Professor Hoffmeister was great and very clear of her expectations.  Really inspirational and helpful! Talked a lot about her kids which was a nice touch. Definitely would take courses with her again

Lectures are based, bit of overexcited scientist vibe—lots of side quests, stories and attempts at jokes. He gets pretty deep into topics, and keeps the class engaged but if you're a totally new to programming, it can be tough I guess. None of the 220 sections take attendance so you can just hop into another section.

Thought it was over after the midterm but ended up doing ok. Class was pretty average. Lectures were boring, could be skipped. His boardwork was much better than the slide reading. Lab was the best part by far. Worth taking the course just for the lab!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: ECE 486 is great, enjoyable topics and the lecture handbook is great for learning the material (written by previous professors), So id highly recommend taking it. This prof is just pretty bad at teaching it. I would recommend taking it with someone else but if you have to take it with him, You will still have plenty of resources (Not his lectures)

Reviews are so peak. Some tests were rough ngl (see below), but scored hella lenient. Had him for 220, low key a vibe. Lectures are big on intuition and examples but can feel rushed. Except lab, course is mostly math, gotta do homework & keep up.

I'm not even sure why this guy is teaching the course, Besides the fact that he's basically just a text-to-speech for the lecture slides, he writes quizzes and exams that can't even be finished on time.

Ivan Abraham appears unprepared to effectively teach this course. Lectures are largely limited to reading slides, and the instructor often struggles to answer student questions. He's very disorganized with his teaching. It's disappointing because I love this course but I have to settle for this mediocre instructor.
He can leave you feeling super confused... not 'coz you aint smart enough to grasp..  He simply can't impart knowledge effectively. Spins fancy words, rambles, hardly gets to the point. Zzzzz

Nice lecturer. Slides/talks are often deadpan, sometimes witty. Does live coding in class. Knowledgeable, sometimes geeks out on advanced material zzzz. Exams are straightforward but weird: tests in a programming class are paper-based.
no idea how to run a class. his slide annotations are incomprehensible, and all his lectures inevitably end in a tailspin

I'd give him above average because at least he has slides. The first guy didn't even bother! However, he NEVER finishes a whole slide deck and the lecture predictably goes into a tail spin in the last 20 minutes with him rushing it.


complete mess | disorganized | rambling | chaotic | disjointed | unfocused | zero logic | Even the professor seemed lost in his own explanations

Abraham does a nice job lecturing on course material, though his accent is heavy. Slide are detailed, delivery is well paced with pauses and questions to check our understanding, often with a dry style of humor. Like other reviews mention, course could be structured better/different as it is too test heavy but that isn't in his control AFAIK.
well well well well
He communicates very well in lectures and has a humorous presentation style. Even through 80 minutes of lecture time he continues to keeps students engaged and learning

ECE 220 was structured very poorly. A significant portion of the exams are conceptual, but the lectures do not cover conceptual concepts enough. The homework is no help either, since it's only programming. During lectures, he would quickly type code on the screen with very little explanation, but expect you to immediately understand everything.

Terrible lecturer. He goes way to fast without explaining a topic well or doing examples with it. The majority of this class is just learning the material in discussions or outside of class. He spends more time going over proofs that you will ever use instead of showing us how the material is helpful at all.

ECE 220 Was not a well structured class , tests were made very difficult and tested on portion that was not taught in the course. Tests accounted to 65 percent of the course grade. Material was poorly structured.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was managed quite unprofessionally. The professor did not provide any support to students and would neglect student concerns. He looked down upon students who who didn't understand course content. In classes, instead of explaining things sequentially, he would simply type the code and expect everyone to follow what he is saying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty good lecturer
Unfair grader. Extra credit doesn't mean anything to her, so don't bother doing it.
Pretty easy class, mostly group presentations

This professor has an attitude toward her students and her class makes no sense. She treats some students differently and acts like a high school teacher. No one knows how she takes attendance, and you have to Google everything to learn. She makes students present every class, doesn't teach, and even turned off my camera once for no reason.

Dr. Brosseder is a great professor! I had her for HIST 105 and she was a super engaging lecturer. She grades very reasonably and cares a lot about her students. Honestly as long as you participate and put in a decent amount of effort you should do great!

On the first day of classes when people stated why they were taking her class she got really annoyed when saying it was to fullfill a gen ed. She does not have many assignments just like 4 in class journals that consist of lectures, readings and videos but she is a tough grader. You will lose points if you do not give really specific answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Confusing grader- stay after class to discuss assignments.
Teach yourself- review slides with index cards
Was against making outlines for exams??? 
Would forget about assignments posted on the syllabus?
Never told you what to study for exactly 
Easy to talk to
Overall choose another course if not into reading or self teaching yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Drop the class as soon as you could, she oversteps her power as a professor and tries to give lectures on how people lack creativity when she literally just reads of a powerpoint and asks us what we think. Like aren't you as a teacher supposed to teach us! Also her quizzes arent related to the content she teaches, she ruined the subject for me.

Overall I would not recommend this class, its structure is very weird and the professor doesn't really engage well with her students. The professor has a weird way of grading which I say is not very ethical, the course is pretty heavy and the professor can be unfair at points which caused me to stress out a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she accused most of the class of plagiarism without proof 0/10 would not recommend, all of them were latinos interesting womp womp :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the class was ok, i enjoyed the material more than anything. but her grading scale is weird as the only grades you can get are A(100), B (80), C(70), D(60), and F(50), there is no in between. i luckily got a good grade in the class, but she also speeds through lectures are rarely posts them to canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took history 205 with prof. Brosseder and loved it. It took a week or two to figure out the structure of the class, but after that I really enjoyed the class. We covered really interesting topics, and the workload wasn't bad at all. Prof. Brosseder is so fun to have as teacher, and I would take another one of her classes in a heartbeat.

P. Brosseder is a good history professor. She cares about the student. Her lectures could at times be little boring, but she mixes things up once in a while with group activities. She cares about you participating in class. Grading is a bit tough since a perfect score is an A+ while one single point off puts you at an A range.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't really helpful. They were hard to follow and he isn't the greatest teacher. I would rely more on studying the content off youtube because he wasn't helpful. The midterms are CBTF and you have to rush through them. The final exam is basically the same questions that are on the practice tests on canvas so make sure to go over them.

He provides material that should be sufficient for exams, however his lectures and lecture videos are both difficult and don't pertain particularly well to the content. He is not very responsive to emails and his tests averages were usually in the D- to F range, however his “curve” is a take home retake, but does not have one for the final.

Unit exams are not hard (imo), but the final is brutal and nothing like them. feels like it was written by someone else and is 30% of your grade. My lowest unit exam was a 91, but I scored about half that on the final (though I was very sick but generally good at test taking). aside from that attendance is optional and extra credit was offered.

DO NOT HATE ON MY GOAT. His exams were verbatim to discussion assignments and practice exams. He gives you so many practice problems, and he answers questions after class. You don't have to buy anything extra for his class (other than PrairieLearn). His final exam replaces your lowest midterm exam grade, AND he also drops your lowest quiz grade.

Do everything if your power to get Ray for Chem104. Tests are all CBTF and heavy on questions where I struggled with completing everything on time. His lectures are boring, only point getting EC iclicker- I still got higher than the average on all exams when skipping lectures and tutoring myself on concepts. Almost no curve is given for retakes.

His lectures are disorganized as many people previously mentioned. Exams were in an average of 60s, and very difficult to follow. The majority of this class grades are just exams. The only curve is take home retake which doesn't really raise anything much. I doubt he will curve anything else. Consider taking this class with a different instructor.

His teaching is disorganized, and he wouldn't go through all the definitions as deeply before jumping into much harder questions. He doesn't nail his lecture to any textbook or framework for you to refer back to, or at least try to learn yourself. His grading is also strange.

Had him for 203 and 104. Lectures and content were pretty disorganized and difficult to follow. All exams were cumulative CBTF midterms with no partial credit, and a majority of the final grade was from exams.

His exams were very difficult, and all of his averages were failing. He does not provide a curve either which makes it even more difficult. The homework and pre lecture assignments help on the exams. If you can get a different professor do so.

first two tests there were no partial credit 1/4MCQ and avg was less than a 60 with a little to no curve.  the only thing that got me through that class were prayers and substances on the weekends when I wasn't at the CBTF trying not to $%!.  couldn't answer ? directly in lecture and would often get his own ? wrong during class, VERY disorganized.

Do not take him. His exams are not similar to homework like everyone says. He seems like a nice guy but never answers emails when you need help. He does not care and does not care if you do bad. Please avoid if you want a grade higher than a B.

Tests were some what hard and no partial credit was given for the first two tests. He switched it mid way so that we'd get partial credit for exam 3 and the final. He is not that good at explaining concepts, and makes me confused on content that I already knew.
I would pray before an exam that CBTF would burn down with me in it

Everything he taught was disconnected, I never knew what was going on and I never missed a lecture or discussion. His office hours aren't worth it, you'll get one question in and he will barely help you and move on to the next person and never come back to you. On the other hand, he loves discussing things with his students and is very supportive.

Andino is a pretty good professor. He is able to lecture well and is accessible outside of class frequently during office hours. His tests are challenging due to being in the CBTF and offering no partial credit, but they aren't impossible to do. No major complaints, nothing done exceptionally well. Just overall a pretty good professor.

His teaching ability is exactly average, not remarkably amazing or awful. If you pay attention to the prelectures/lectures, you should understand the brunt of the material. There is no partial credit on the exams which can be tough considering the very large or very small numbers you are calculating.

Professor Andino is a good lecturer and cares about his students. He assigns fair and manageable homework. However his exam grading is unfair. CBTF with no partial credit, his exam averages are 50s-60s. He said there'd likely be a curve for the final if everyone did bad (average was same as the midterms), but he didn't curve. Grade went from A to B

Andino was a very good chemistry professor and spoke in a way that made understanding the topics very clear. The tests can be kind of difficult, but they are very similar in style to the practice problems/homework that he gives on PraireLearn and the practice reviews that take place in discussion.

Dr. Andino is the professor you want to take CHEM 104 with. His lectures are entertaining and thought provoking, while still addressing the core principles and concepts of the material at hand. He also provides you with all the resources you need to succeed. Additionally, his tests are very fair. There are no trick questions.

Dr. Andino is very approachable and caring. Exams are very much like the homework, practice homeworks, and practice exams. Go to office hours! Don't wait until the last week to get the bonus, I beg (it gets very crowded). The final exam is 30%, which brought my grade from an A to a B+, so prioritize it if you could.

Andino is really a nice guy but unfortunately the material he teaches can be difficult to grasp. This semester all his exams were exactly like the homework problems and its very easy to memorize how to do these problems then apply that to the exams.

I actually really liked him. Andino is a rlly good professor. His test averages are low, but the tests are not weighted that much in the gradebook so people usually get a letter grade ish or more in the class than their test average. Take notes on the prelecture videos so during class you can add small things he talks about. SO much extra credit.

Basically all the scores come from the lab report, and this score is determined by your TA. Therefore, if you get a good TA, you will think this course is okay. The content of his lectures is average. Many key points are different from what the TA wants to see. If you encounter any difficulties, ask your TA for help, not Andino.
Doesn't teach content well. Tests are not too difficult. Be prepared to self-learn most content

Great professor - cares about his students. Make use of your TA's office hours because they're the ones that grade your reports. Lab reports take anywhere between 5 and 12 hours and there's one due every week
Great professor, difficult exams. His lectures were very entertaining! I would definitely take him again. Be prepared to spend half your time studying though.

Andino's class was very easy if you understand chemistry and are willing to sit down and grind a lab report on mediocre dining hall food and willpower. Hopefully you get a good TA because its pretty much luck of the draw and will be the main impact of your grade.

I really don't understand why andino has such a low rating. Exams were exactly like the HW and lectures were always entertaining, so I don't think exam averages really reflected his way of teaching.Extra credit also helps if you don't do too well on an exam. Definitely recommend andino for 104.

There is homework and prelecture video due every lecture that you HAVE TO WATCH to understand what is going on during lecture. All the tests are in the CBTF and he makes the tests representative of the homeworks and practice tests. You really have to pay attention, but he offers 5% extra credit overall and lets you earn back points on tests.

he is a solid lecturer and helpful + accessible at office hours. but exam avgs were insanely low. he provides ways to make up pts but cbtf exams where u don't get partial credit for ur work makes the exams unfair. he would also include questions on the midterms that the syllabus said wouldn't be covered in that midterm (orgo in electrochem exam)
Andino is not a bad professor but the class did feel unnecessarily tough. I get it's a weed-out but more/better resources could have been provided to help students succeed in this class.

Andino is a competent instructor who can convey the information well if you have a solid foundation in chem. I struggled more with this class than any other course I've taken in my college career thus far, and while I was able to get out with a passing score, I recognize now how heavily it affected my mental health. I would avoid if possible.

Since he changed the structure of the class, our whole class did terribly compared to previous semesters. Averages were around 50% or below, and the retakes only added on a few more points. The grading of the class was very confusing and caused a lot of uncertainty. The PrarieLearn grading system was unreliable and frustrating.

He isn't as bad as people are saying. The lectures are not that great but the exams are exactly like the homework so I always felt prepared. Plus, the retake he gives is super helpful to make up extra points since there is no time limit and you take it at home.

PLEASE DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Averages for all the exams have been Fs. He refuses to implement curves because points should be earned which is fair BUT when your averages are BELOW 30%, there is a problem. Up until the final, the TAs told us that less than 1/3 of the class was even PASSING. I will probably have to retake the class bc of him.

GOOD LUCK TO FUTURE STUDENTS! This class had me contemplating withdrawing from school and checking myself into a mental institution. Be prepared to immerse yourself into the wonderful world of self-hatred and low self esteem. Unless you have nothing else to do but spend your entire day at the CLC then don't expect anything better than a C.

Please for the love of God choose a different professor, if the average on a exam is a 34% you know something is wrong. Sure, you can say the students our lazy but a day before the final exam my man straight up removed a the whole course so you couldn't even study he fixes it (without providing an explanation) and then it happens again!

Andino recently changed the exam structure so that there were no second attempts (no partial credit). The content is easy to understand, but because you have to input the answer yourself, if you get one step wrong or input a wrong number, you just lose 8 or 6 points. No curve either, just a retake that doesn't do much except add a few points.

If you're on your phone he calls you out in the middle of class & asks for your name & writes it down so he can keep track. If you get called out more than once, you have to leave lecture. If someone is choosing to be on their phone instead, that's on them. Don't interrupt the entire class for something so small. This isn't kindergarten.

Appeared to be on a perpetual power trip. Hostile learning environment. In 2019, he singled out 1 student on their phone in a 300 person lecture to reprimand his intelligence, accuse him of distracting everyone, and yell at him to get out. Nobody noticed the student until Andino went out of his way to take several minutes putting him in place.

Chem 104 is a very math heavy course which can be difficult, but there are so many resources at your disposal which helps when navigating topics. As long as you pay attention in discussion and do all of the homework you will do pretty well in the class. Lectures are pretty engaging and if you miss one they are uploaded online after.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are not the most useful, but you can understand the material pretty easily on your own. Easy exams where the questions are just like homework. Have exam retakes. Quizzes are collaborative Just do the homework and you will be fine.

Andino was very helpful this semester. i met with him privately every week for personal office hours and i found that he explained topics so much better during these hours. we had great conversations that went beyond chemistry and i learned that he not only is passionate about his job but is also a great person. he truly wants everyone to pass.

This professor explains things quite clearly in his lecture, but most (i would say 70%) of the work is done by TA. Also, the slides and other relevant resources he offers are not quite good. Well, i think he is an average professor

My experience with Dr. Andino was good, granted I took him Spring 2021 so, my lectures were online and I chose to do Merit for the class, which gave me extra practice out of class. I would recommend doing all of the homework because the the exams are very similar and be very careful because they are only 15 questions long.

Dr Andino cares students a lot with lots of office hours. He presents lectures clearly with practice problems to help review and do homework. Homework and Pre-lectures are due on the last day, giving more time to finish. Exams and quizzes are tricky, but Prairie-learn tells you answers and grades immediately after finishing it. Always Practice!

Rambles on during lectures and never finishes the material planned for the day so we end up rushing through it the next lecture, then repeat. Noticed several typos on exams and he forgot to provide critical information on questions. Left 2 of the same correct answer choice on the final, so it was a 50/50 guess as to which was the real one.

People believe his lectures are good. They are only good for those who have a strong understanding of chem if you dont GOOD LUCK. No real explaining of the fundamentals of each topic and seems to think his students already have an idea of the topic. Test are like prairie learn. If you need more teaching to do better TAKE RAY!!!
Lectures are very easy to follow but there is a lot of work. Honestly the fairest of UIUC chem prof. And I've taken classes with 3 of them
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Andino gets a bad rep man. His lectures are directly correlated to the homework and the homework is directly correlated with exams which I think is more than what most profs even do. You can get up to 10% more on exams with the ratakes which are unproctored. Make sure to practice a lotttttt. You can tell he loves his job & chemistry, very inspiring

Heard hes awful for 104 and avoiding him next semester. As for 203 he would just expect you to know when lab lecture is and never tell you when or give a schedule. Shallow depth of material but good speaker. If you have him for 203 or lab youre fine.

Absolutely horrid professor. Gives the easiest homework and then throws extremely difficult quizzes and exams at you. Class test averages regularly score at or below 50%. Answers he gives in lectures are poor and lack depth. Never have I had such an awful experience. Avoid at all costs.

Honestly speaking, hes not a bad lecturer, but in terms of exam grading he was horrendous. The semester I had him the exam average was poor - below 56% I believe. When asked if there would be a curve, he stated that some people got 100% and said that since some students got those grades everybody can. No curve and can be rather petty.
Literally the worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life. With school being online you would think he would try to help but no this man is literally an awful professor who should not have a job
This guy gets pissy for every little thing. I've never seen such a frail personality that greatly affects classroom instruction the way I saw here.

Overall he was very good at teaching us the information we needed and was very accessible both through email and by having lot of office hours. He does however, make you work for all the points you get but if you do the homework, the extra credit assignment (an additional 2.5%), go to lecture, and ask questions, you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good teacher and explains things well in lecture and unlike most chem professors his exams are very straightforward and very similar to the homework. Exams are only 15 questions however so if you get a few wrong your grade drops tremendously and hes not lenient with curving or anything so be careful

I heard that Andino was a tough professor, but I had a great time in chem 104. I have an extremely high grade and feel like exams and homework weren't bad at all. He responded to emails quickly and answered questions well. Overall, he was very kind and wanted his classes to succeed!

I read many of bad reviews about Professor Andino before taking the class and got pretty discouraged. However, after nearly finishing the semester, I am confused as to why so many people dislike him. Put in the effort and you'll get the result you want. I've learned a lot from his class. Great lecturer and very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unlike most chemistry professors testing you on your knowledge of an overall concept, he tests on very minuscule examples that were shown in lecture for a brief moment. So even if you understand a concept you might not do well if you don't memorize every little detail of homework and lecture slides.

I was not a fan of the online exams. There were 15 questions with 50 min given. I did not do well on the second exam because I was rushed for time which affected my grade by a lot. The material was't bad, but it was frustrating when topics that were brushed over in class were the ones that were on the exam. Would not take this class again.

Lecture is clicker but its only two percent of total grade. Lecture is a good resource but you so a lot of developing on your own. Homework is good practice, it creates a bigger understanding. Midterms are repetitive, and are very easy to fail so its important to double check your work (cbtf). Do all homework or you'll kill your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man used a SCOOTER BOARD in class!
Very knowledgable and explains concepts very thoroughly. Sometimes falls behind in lecture and you have to teach yourself. Some curve balls on exams. Overall good professor though

Need to go to class to get iClicker points (not extra credit). Barely gives any review materials to prepare for midterms/final. Good luck if you screw up on one midterm because most of your grade depends on it. Lectures are useless and homework has nothing to do with what is on the exam. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: When in lecture he doesn't know how to teach Sometimes I leave more confused then when I walked in. Also will kick you out of lecture if he sees you on your phone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Andino is a great guy! He truly cares about making his students understand the material. If you care about the topic and show that you want to put effort into his class, then he will put effort into making sure you do well. Don't go on your phone/laptop in class bc he will roast you for it and it's disrespectful. I have learned so much from him
made chemistry enjoyable. amazing professor and person. make use of office hours he really wants to help you. retake quizzes helped boost exam grades and exams are pretty straightforward. take andino

Andino was an okay teacher. All the lecture material was put online and material that was covered in lecture was in the book. For me, the book explained things a lot better than the demos. Clicker questions were worth points and were not extra credit, so I went to lecture just to get clicker points.

Dr. Adino is very passionate about teaching the students and gives great examples in class to help us understand the concepts. He might be a little disorganized and uptight, but he is always there to help the students. He also makes ice cream for the highest scoring section and student, so that is a plus :)

Honestly, Andino wasn't that great of a teacher. He constantly rushed lectures towards the end, extremely disorganized, and not great at explaining. He knows his material, so if you go to office hours, he is useful one on one. Otherwise, you learn the material by pure repetition or by actually using the book (which I didn't)

If you need to take Chem and only are in it for the GPA, take Andino. His tests I found were much easier than what i've heard from other students with different professors. Also, you can retake exams online and gain back 30% of what you missed. Not a bad lecturer either, you still need to work for your grade though.

Andino really cares about teaching, but is more of a "it happens because it happens" kind of guy. See him after class if you really want to understand the meaning of something. Overall, lectures are not super useful and tests are pretty straightforward.

I didn't go to any lectures because slides are online and he doesn't teach much.  I taught myself everything without the textbook; I only used the assignments and Google.   Tests are hard but padded by all the hw. The timed quizzes are representative of the questions you can expect on the midterms. In all, turned out better than I thought it would.

Lectures are pretty much useless. He goes extremely slowly at the start and rushes through all the slides during the end. Moreover, the slides are pretty much the textbook. His tests are pretty hard as just 2 mistakes can get you down to a B.

Really bad at explaining concepts, so you practically have to teach yourself everything. Tests, quizzes, and homework don't often reflect what you concentrated on in lecture so sometimes you'll have many questions on a test covering a topic you went over very briefly in lecture. TAs not great either.
Just soso
HE IS THE ALL TIME WORST. I HAVE LEARNED NOTHING. NOTHING IN HIS LECTURES IS IN THE HOMEWORK HE ASSIGNS OR THE WORKSHEETS IN DISCUSSION. DROP OUT.

Andino is passionate about the subject and really wants you to learn. That being said, he is very available and helpful during office hours. Lectures are generally pretty interesting, but not always very easily understood. Tests are usually harder than homework, but they're still manageable. Overall, would definitely recommend!

Before taking this class, I heard so many bad things about Andino, but they are all wrong! He is by far my favorite professor I have ever had.  He is always available for office hours and wants all of his students to succeed. The exams are challenging but definitely manageable by attending his review sessions and going to office hours! TAKE HIM!
Professor Andino is a great guy. He's really nice and you can tell that he cares about his students. Go to office hours!
lectures are very confusing and not worth going, his exams and quizzes are 100X harder than homework and what is discussed in class

Andino is a great guy but his lectures are very boring and almost seemingly pointless to go to. Tests are very hard. He gives practice exams, but they are from another teacher and are nothing like his exams.
Absolutely terrible lecturer. Be prepared to read chemwiki his sldeshows make no sense. lectures are pointless

Andino was super nice and wanted to help when students asked questions, but he was not a good lecturer. He was so confusing during lectures and I could understand maybe 60% of lectures. We always had homework on stuff we didn't learn yet and exams were tough.

He's a great person, and loves to help, but lectures are boring. The first exam is pretty easy, the second one is really hard, and the third was alright. I like the structure of Andino's class better than Ray's, but I like how Ray does more practice problems in class. If you can, take Ray, because Kell for organic chem is the worst teacher ever.

Andino's lectures are not very informative as he tends to go through his lecture slides which he posts online afterwards.  He will send emails reminding you of due dates for online quizzes and such which is helpful if you miss a lecture.  Office hours are very frequent and very helpful for specific questions.  Take Andino

Professor Andino was a very intuitive professor who knew what he was talking about all the time. On the other hand, we noticed that he had a hard time communicating his vast knowledge unless we went to office hours. Overall, very nice lecturer.

One of the worst professors I've ever had at UIUC. Nice guy, really approachable, and knows the material, but he is a terrible teacher. Practice exams are nothing like the real exam. Lectures are terribly organized, spends 30 minutes reviewing and then rushing through important material. The exams do not coincide well with lecture either. BEWARE!!!

He gives you all this material to prepare for exams, and then the tests are a complete blindside. Don't expect a curve on these ridiculous exams either. He believes it's better to "curve the class at the end". Hope you're okay with the class average on the exams being a failing grade. Everyone says the textbook is essential, yet its not required.

Andino was very frustrating for me as a student. He's a nice guy, really is. But his lectures don't seem to cover his exams. I'll nearly ace the mock exams and practice lecture problems, and get a very poor exam score. The grading system is generous, but the class was a huge morale dump for me at times.
No room for mistakes and very harsh (e.g. failed a whole lab for 800 students because of one messy balance), but passionate about the subject. On the bright side, the TAs are great.

Really awful teacher as of fall 2015. Practice exams Andino gives are literally from Dr. Rays class, and they are nothing like Andinos exams. Lectures are spent discussing previous days assignined "prelecure" problems. Ray gives instructional videos to help with these, Andino does not. The book is your only friend in his class.

Really disorganized and his teaching methods assumes you know certain things that he never went over. Lectures were never clear and I didn't learn anything from this class. The one positive is that his grading pretty forgiving in that I had plenty of chances to raise my grade.

He is a very disorganized teacher. He also changes the grading of the class as he goes on (he's a new teacher, this was his second semester teaching) such as making clicker points based on participation not accuracy. However, despite two of the exams and the final having 66% averages, he did not curve the class. Would not recommend.

Nothing learn from the class, but you need to go for participation points. Funny thing is, he gave full participation points for all students at end of the semester, ignoring the students who attended every class. Exam is not Chemistry exam but similar to the Math exam. Just take Marvile's class. She teaches better, exam is much more balanced.
It's a bit unfortunate that I enrolled in his class. Miserably bad teacher, prepare to learn most of the material on your own. Also, there's little correlation between lectures and quiz material

I actually enjoy Andino. Now that he's gotten into the groove of things, I definitely think hes a worthy professor. He does a good job of letting us know what is going to be on the exam and gives us more than enough practice material. Office hours are worthwhile too. He really tries to make sure you understand the material.
His lectures were kind of pointless and he wasn't always clear about what he was trying to say

Andino started out really awful, but it's only his first year teaching, so I understand. He quickly adapted his lectures to fit our needs. Although he does skip around sometimes, if you pay attentions and ask questions, you'll do fine.  He's very kind and open to questions during lecture.

I'm not sure why everyone is complaining about Andino. I've gone to every lecture and paid attention to what he has said and I've been doing fine. If I was confused about something I could go to his office hours and he'd explain everything nicely. It's not his job to baby you through the material. This is college.
Mock exams really help!
Really, really bad teacher.  EXTREMELY unorganized.  There is no structure to his class.  Andino is constantly jumping all over the place.

His can't explain relevant information. During lecture he will go over one problem which will take the majority of the time. He often repeats the same simple concepts over and over. The homework and tests are nothing like what is gone over in lecture. He uses a previous prof's pre-lecture videos to teach most of the material. Do your best to avoid.

I thought my high school AP chem teacher was bad, but Prof. Andino is on another level. He is always unorganized in lecture, often repeating the same basic concepts over and over, when there are a lot more difficult topics to cover. Test and quiz questions come out of nowhere, and he's a master of expectingyou to study one thing and apply another.
Had him for a lab, it was very unorganized and he was never clear about what we were supposed to be doing.

Does a good job at explaining topics.  Sometimes ran out of time to finish lectures. Practice on your own and in discussion is necessary.  Lot's of people complained about this course, but they likely weren't using all resources that were available.  With a few more years of experience, I expect him to be a very good (also funny) professor.

He is pretty good. He's really into chemistry and likes teaching it. The material is not that easy but he tries to help you understand the best he can. He's not the greatest at answering questions, but overall a pretty decent teacher. I like how he does demos too.
He is not really good at teaching (tho he is very kind). Lectures were mostly boring
He is a really nice and kind person, but unfortunately, I personally did not find him to be the strongest lecturer. I just ended up self studying without going to the lectures :((

Professor Bhowmik clearly cares about his students, but like many others have said, he is simply not a good lecturer. He stutters, stumbles over his words, and struggles to explain the content clearly. It makes it even more difficult to learn in what is already a weed out class. Exams are also extremely hard compared to the given study materials.
Professor Bhowmik is the goat I don't care what anyone says. He's enthusiastic about what he teaches and in my opinion he teaches it well.

Prof is okay at teaching. However the exams are much harder than the content we go over. (And much harder than the given practice exams) 

If you want to do well study a lot. Read the Lumetta notes, course text book (don't buy it, just google the name), and course slides. Office hours and the official review sessions were also very helpful.
Horrible lecturer, not so helpful in answering questions

Great experience with this professor. 

GOAT of ECE 120
If i could i would give him a 0

Professor Bhowmik seems like a genuine and caring guy, unfortunately, he is an absolutely horrid lecturer. I only learned this class from MP's and office hours his lectures were that incoherent. His tests are also quite difficult, especially the second midterm, additionally the review materials he provides are not helpful in the slightest.
He is a good and caring professor.

Super nice and caring guy, really approachable and easy to talk to. That is about it though. He is simply terrible at delivering lectures. His lectures are incompetent, and he cannot explain any slightly difficult concept with any coherence. Avoid him at all costs, it will make ECE 120 much more enjoyable

Professor Bhowmik is a great guy, but his lectures aren't that great.  The concepts are not hard by any measure, but his explanations are confusing. His accent isn't that bad. I did most of my learning from Labs, HW, and Lumetta notes anyways so it wasn't a big deal. He definitely tries his best, but he could be better.

A caring professor who goes out of his way to help you. He cares a lot about his students and tries hard, but the fact is that he is just bad at giving lectures. He is awesome in everything except lectures and he has difficulty conveying ideas well. I learned mostly from Labs and HWs and fortunately the class itself is extremely well structured.
I like Professor Bhowmik. He supplied all the materials you need to complete the class. He tries his best.

Overall, the best way to describe Prof. Bhowmik is that he is a great person, not the best lecturer. His lectures cover what is necessary, supplementary materials are given, but it could better. However, outside of the classroom, he will go out of his way to help you understand material and tries his best to make himself available.
( I recommend!)
Not the best professor. His accent is a bit hard to understand and he cannot explain the concept well. Had to watch other professor's videos or youtube videos.
Prof. Bhowmik in my experience is a weak lecturer; however, I recommend him because he is understanding and very accessible outside class.
Bhowmik was an amazing prof and taught his lectures very clearly and concisely. highly recommend him for 120 and 220, this class.
prof was great at teaching during lectures and was very understanding of circumstances that came up. highly recommend him for 120 and 220.

Bhowmik is underrated. Idk if I'd give him a 5 if his rating wasn't so low, but he's a nice guy and an improving lecturer despite his really thick accent. I had to use the lumetta notes along with the lectures, but it was overall a solid experience.

Ujjal Bhowmik is a caring guy, truly motivated to see all students succeed. Many believe his lectures are terrible, but in my opinion they're really not that bad, and they always cover all of the material we need to know. Keep an eye out for his review sessions as you'll likely get general information about questions on upcoming midterms.

I'm conflicted. He is a super sweet person and he lays out the course very well. There are more than enough resources. But the lectures are less than ideal. I often find myself watching the online lectures instead since they're much more comprehensible. I feel more like I'm in an asynchronous class which I don't love. As a person though he's great.
unintelligible handwriting, terrible lectures, students reduce by less than half from first day, put your everything into changing away to take it with the other professors instead
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Bhowmik is not at all who you would expect teaching a top engineering school. His lectures are  inefficient and his teaching style is flawed. After the first few lectures, the amount of empty seats in his lecture visibly increased, and rightfully so, as spending 20 minutes studying would yield better results than an entire lecture of his.
Avoid at all cost, very poor at explaining concepts, and is inaccessible outside of class. The class isn't hard, learning from him is. Under no circumstances ever need extra help, you won't get it.
Very difficult to follow concepts. Does not explain the best.

Ujjal Bhowmik is a genuinely nice, kind guy with a great sense of humor. Please read the negative reviews with a grain of salt, they are from freshman ECE underclassmen that got smashed by their first relatively difficult ECE class. At times he can be a bit hard to understand but  he improved significantly as a lecturer. He has a great attitude
A bad lecturerer who rarely explained concepts clearly. The workload is huge and the tests are super hard. Would recommend taking other professors' classes even if you register his sections.
Homeworks were way too difficult, nothing like the lectures. Graders would cut points for very weird reasons.
An Awful Teacher. He doesn't curve exams and the exams are super hard especially for midterm 3 and final.
I learnt many thing from the class. He is a good professor.
Just Take Levchenko if you have not learn to program before, If you do know how to program, watch Lumetta's lecture on your own

One of the best professors I've had. He is extremely caring and makes sure no one has questions unanswered. He covers everything in lectures and will answer any question you have during class, after class, or during office hours. ECE classes aren't supposed to be easy. You need to go to more than just lectures to get a proper understanding.

This professor has such an unintelligible accent. About midway through the semester I only went to about a third of the lectures because I couldnt learn anything from him.
