He means well but doesnt know enough English and thats beyond the accent, its word knowledge. I learned more from TAs, the internet, and other students BY FAR.

Honestly don't know why people say he's bad. I think its just his accent, but his teaching is actually pretty good. Idk most of my friends agree with this. He's a nice guy and teaches things pretty well.
Just take Levchenko, you can drop in on any lecture.

If you really pay attention to his classes, you will notice that he does a good job of teaching you the contents. He is also a really nice person who is very flexible, don't know why people say he's bad.
He is terrible at explaining concepts and I always left lectures knowing just as little as I knew coming in. I would recommend switching professors.
Not a good lecturer. It's very hard to understand him, doesn't explain concepts well at all. I had to switch to a different lecturer. I advise you to do the same.

Very bad professor overall. Altough he tries to be professional and caring, he has the worst accent in the ECE department (cannot understand 90% what he's pronouncing) and not understanding the materials at times.

This is the only RMP ive written, he really should not be teaching 220. Took it over summer with him and he had to stop explaining the operation of the stack half way through lecture because he didn't know what he was talking about any more and a student had to get him back on track. Do what you have to in order to not be in his lecture.

Professor just cannot explain the concept clearly. His students have to do lots of self-study in order to catch up with the class progress. Honestly, I will suggest him to practice English oral skills. Also, I cannot understand why he would write the C codes in horrible handwriting on Tablet instead of typing them in the IDE.

I thought he really just didn't explain the concepts of 220 really well. Found his ability to answer questions rather cyclical and didn't help much. Ended up going to the other instructor when I could and him for the rest which was basically learning half a class. Shame

You need to put in a lot of work to succeed but it's well worth it. A difficult grader, sometimes off-putting, condescending, and seemingly unfair, but if you didn't understand his method by the end, you didn't really get the class. Release ego and you can learn a lot from him. Reviews are just mad about grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I did not feel comfortable seeking help after several interactions. The whole experience was very taxing on my mental health. I also felt that he treated a few others in a different way, although I cannot know his intentions. The lectures often focused on his personal interests.

Do not take this class with this professor. Should have been a super easy class. You can put in just as much/more effort than those with much higher grades. Inconsistent with grading and feedback. Not worth a hit to your GPA. Wish I never took.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: objectively very unlikeable and also immensely self centered . He is although undoubtedly a very smart guy and a very good lecturer that truly captivates each lecture. The course itself is not structured good at all, with random assignments and deadlines being assigned. Also never used canvas and was inaccessible through email.

reviews.comment: incredibly inaccessible outside of class as he doesn't believe in online communication. lectures are fine and class content is interesting but he is one of the most condescending people i have ever met, especially if your views do not align with his
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Is incredibly inaccessible outside of class as he doesn't believe in online communication. Lectures are fine and class content is interesting but he is one of the most condescending people I have ever met.

reviews.comment: He's genuinely a good person and a good professor, I just really didn't like the class. I rarely did the reading and still did good in the class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Biondi is one of the BEST lecturers. He speaks clearly, concisely, is disgustingly intelligent, and pushes you to be a better thinker. Even if you don't read the textbook, if you attend all his lectures, you'll be peachy. Take notes! Grading criteria? Lowkey vague, but the assignments are straightforward. Go to his OH, too, he's chill.

Grading in this course is intentionally ambiguous, with no fixed criteria provided despite significant weight placed on written assignments. Expectations are unclear, lecture content is not recorded, and feedback are abstract not actionable. Grading is not anonymous and follow-up questions often go unanswered.
No mandatory attendance but you will miss out on tips for exams. Getting an A definitely requires work, but I suppose that's expected.

I have taken both PHIL 107 and PHIL 421 with Dr. Biondi as someone not studying philosophy and have thoroughly enjoyed my experience in his classes. He is one of the most knowledgeable professors on this campus. That being said, his classes are not for everyone. While attendance is not mandatory, you will fall behind quickly if you are present.

Best professor at UIUC. Life-changing material. A philosopher's philosopher. Be prepared to read, write, and think deeply. I'd come out of every Ethical Theories lecture utterly invigorated.

I've taken several courses with Dr. Biondi, I have friends who've also taken multiple--take his classes, push yourself, you will grow so much as a thinker.

Worst professor at UIUC. Completely subjective grading, no transparency. Heavily penalizes introverted students through unquantified participation grades. Can give zeros claiming AI without proof. Harsh, intimidating demeanor. Forces purchase of his textbook. Grades based on personal preference, not merit. My only C in undergrad, totally random.

I really enjoyed his class. Even though attendance isn't strictly mandatory, if you miss class, you will struggle. I highly recommend going to office hours for both the professor and the TA and asking for feedback. If you're the type of person who doesn't like to be pushed hard, I wouldn't recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really biased, did not cover much about Plato, Socrates, and Aristotle in an ancient philosophy class. Very fixated on stoicism. Would recommend taking it with another professor.

For being a required class, tougher professor than you would hope for. Amazing and insightful lectures, but tough grading. Understanding really hinges on attending lectures, not just reading. Go to office hours, it's worth it. This isn't an inspiring review; you might not want to be pushed this hard, but you  need it. I definitely did.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a polarizing guy. I'll be frank: I don't like him. At the same time, he has affected me more significantly than any other professor ever has and likely ever will. I am a different person now—the trajectory of my life has shifted. Take that as you will.

The material he chooses is really interesting as he intentionally goes for stuff many philosophy students would never hear of. When he's not lecturing he's a bit of an oddball, but not in a bad way. You'll have the best time if you sit in the front and give your thoughts to the questions he asks.

Lots of readings and graded by a few exams (multiple essay prompts) and longer essays. The lectures were very enjoyable as the professor analyzed readings in a thorough and engaging manner. Grading and essay prompts were a little vague. I really enjoyed attending 421 lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Well organized lectures, but not a fan of the course structure or content. Doesn't really cover any of the typical ethical theories. Grades based off two essays and two exams. Grades hard and only gives out letter grades (no number or % based grades) so it's often confusing to figure out what your grade will be at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of the discussions we do are pretty unnecessary and he tends to make people feel like their ideas are dumb unless they align with his. He'll tell you how to get a good grade in his class and then when you do it he has a dozen more things to hold your grade down as if you're supposed to know.

an entire semester devoted to BS effective altruism-approved discussions on "AI" instead of real philosophy on AI. you mean to tell me 'what if we can create ai capable of being called conscious' is a more contemporary issue than using algorithms to uphold institutional oppression?
dude was really weird about stoicism, only spent like 2 weeks on plato, miss like 2 classes and you missed all his coverage of aristotle

Dr. Biondi was more interested in reading nonsensical metaphysics than he was in anything else. We spent forever studying the most forgettable pseudo religious explanations for the world instead of some of the truly fascinating and lasting philosophy that came from the early modern period.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS THERE IS A NEW TA. My issue with this class was with the TA. He would grade the papers and critique trivial things (like one paragraph being formatted incorrectly) and it would be an entire letter grade. Also he would ask for more detail but limit how much you can write. He would also take points and not explain why.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor structured this class in a manner that led me to believe he had never taught a class prior. His notes are scattered, he doesn't know how to illicit student responses, and he was entirely unprepared for how to structure our midterm. No rubrics are given. Graded on only 5 things. Classmates were left confused when leaving lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor to learn from. AE100 is a super easy class, but Woodard makes it feel like it's worth going to.
Never dreaded going to this class

He is very passionate about aerospace and knows a lot about the subject. The rocket and glider projects were both fun and taught me a lot about aerospace engineering. He has great lectures that keep you engaged and excited to learn, and he gives good feedback on assignments and projects. However, there were quite a lot of writing assignments.

AE100 with professor Woodard was incredibly enjoyable. He is incredibly passionate about aerospace and it shows. Assignments are graded fairly and the workload is entirely reasonable. Couldn't ask for much more from an AE100 Professor.
the most chill guy and pretty hilarious at times as well. Had a lot of fun with the projects and hearing about his research
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Woodard is a nice and funny guy. His classes are engaging and enjoyable to attend. Glider and rocket projects are also very rewarding. Would take again.

Woodard is a solid professor with a sense of humor. He tossed airplanes in class and his lectures are very loud and clear. The class is easy, but watch out for his Python assignments. He just tosses you work to do without teaching it so if you can't code, watch out. Some lectures get boring and his assistants are picky when grading assignments.

Dr. Woodard is a really personable and caring professor, and makes the intro aerospace class super engaging. The class itself is quite straightforward and is actually enjoyable, as it is mostly project-based. As long as you do the weekly assignments and are engaged during class, it will be a breeze.

Professor Woodard was an amazing teacher to have my first semester of college. I truly enjoyed getting to know him, and he truly cares about all of his students. Even with COVID restrictions, Prof Woodard made a great effort to continue to teach in-person and have us still work on all the fun AE100 projects in a safe manner.

Woodard is an awesome guy with great NX12 knowledge and honestly really funny. Homework was a little difficult sometimes and to pass the exams you basically got to practice outside of class. His office hours are helpful and you can get help from so many people in the aero lab as well. Don't be afraid to ask for help
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His AE100 class is pretty straight forward and doesn't require too much effort to get an A. He is a pretty charismatic professor and clearly likes his job, but can be somewhat more demanding with certain assignments, as in his grading and expectations aren't as laid back. It is still very organized, and not that bad.

I've had this professor for multiple classes and he is truly one of my favorite professors on campus. He comes to lectures with a lot of energy so you don't need to worry about them being boring. He is also very accommodating with meeting students outside of class to explain things. Overall if you have this professor you're in good hands

Lectures are mandatory, but for the most part they are completely useless. He "teaches" about CAD or Matlab, however you have to teach most of the information to yourself. His TA writes and grades the assignments, so most of the time what is taught and the homework don't match up. Also if you mess up be prepared for a snarky arrogant response.

The lectures were not useful. His assignments were straight forward. His TA will help you if you show up to office hours. He had an english TA grade our essays. NO! We are engineers in training not english majors. That sucked. She butchered my grade and the grades of others. I'm sure my class of aero students hate her. I do.

A great enthusiastic professor. He was always in the lab after hours looking to help and was very understanding if you couldn't get the cad to work. It's more homework than a 2 credit class normally but if you do the work you'll get the A.
Very good at teaching. His instructions are clear, his assignments are reasonable and he's willing to improve based on student feedback. He's also very friendly and approachable.
Come to class, do the fairly easy CAD assignments. Quizzes are simple. Hardest part is the project he gives you, no final test just have to make CAD plane.

Incredible attitude, witty presentation, and attentive instruction. Loved the class so much! Highly recommend. He's a busy guy, so your best bet at meeting with him outside of class is impromptu or Calendly.
You might get bad grades but in the end everyone gets an A. If you enjoy thoughtful discussion and political theory take this class. Honestly the most enjoyable class I've taken at UIUC.

A gem of a professor, probably the best I've had at UIUC. His style is an acquired taste, but he clearly puts tons of care and attention into his classes. I have learned so much from his class. If you want to take a course that is easy or low maintenance he is not your guy. But if you can handle a lot of reading this class is fs worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly not too bad, do the readings and come to class and you will be fine. The grading criteria is not that clear and can be stressful, but a lot of it is predetermined (eg. no one is getting above an 88 on this assignment) kind of thing. Miller has great lectures and I think everyone should take this class, don't sweat the weird grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Miller really cares about his students, and he really cares about making an impact through teaching. You can tell that he's really passionate about what he's talking about when he lectures. The class is weirdly graded but other than that I'd say it's worth it. Participation is what matters most I'd say though. He'll like you more if you're listenin
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, course lectures were helpful towards not only the course but philosophy and my political understanding. No final exam either, and only a couple of major assignments that weren't too heavily graded if you put a bit of effort. Also, there were short online quizzes on the night of every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While being a fairly good lecturer, thats about it. hes not accesible at all outside of class, and the ta's the semseter i took the class were quite simply awful, as they where not only rude and boring, they also seemingly took personal gratification when grading toughly, as no matter how you reached out them, they give no grade justification.

This professor does not respond to emails. There aren't final exams. There are 3 major assignments but he's always saying how we aren't going to do well and that their really hard. There are 2 online quizzes a week that are like 2-3 questions and you only have 6 minutes to finish. annoying.
Brings a rubber chicken to class and talks about his cat a lot during lecture.

Professor Miller is extremely passionate about what he is teaching, but lectures do tend to feel like a yap fest, a lot of the information is honestly not needed. The work is not tough but can be lengthy especially because there is no feedback given for the briefs. Group work heavy do not take this class if you like to not talk with your group!

Mr. Miller is an excellent teacher. His academic achievements are impressive, his coursework is intriguing, especially his discussions about political philosophy, and his coursework is relatively easy to follow if you put in the effort. I highly recommend taking his course. With that being said, mandatory attendance is not giving.

I have to say I actually enjoyed his course. His lectures were somewhat engaging and he's quite attractive in a sapiosexual way. His content was interesting, especially his discussions about philosophers. I will always remember his black cat. With that being said, the permanent attendance aspect of his course is unreasonable.

Do NOT agree to cancelling lecture. Because it is a total points class, he will then change the weightings of the participation category in the end!!! Grading on case briefs can be harsh, but if you read wikipedia (you're totally set). Boring lecturer, only stayed awake during lectures because of iClicker attendance questions sprinkled throughout.

This course and professor are incredibly boring. I took it because it is an easy A, especially with a high percentage of the grade being participation. If you did high school debate, then you already know everything. He tries to stretch barely any content into an entire semester. This is 3 weeks of content max. Beware of getting cold called!
Professor Miller does well to accommodate student needs and his lectures will make you rethink your political beliefs. It takes effort to do well in this class but it is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Miller is a great professor! Justice in the Law is a manageable class albeit with heavy readings each week. No exams, just case briefs and other assignments like weekly journals reflecting on political values. You will become better at reading and analyzing case briefs as well as political philosophy. He really cares about his students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable during lectures, just go to class to get the points. The case briefs are not difficult and provides feedback during office hours if needed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing amazing professor, one of the best instructors I have ever had! He is so knowledgable and really cares that his students learn. You will get a lot of out of this class if you participate and make a meaningful effort - it's worth it! He is also very willing to meet with students outside of office hours since they tend to fill up quickly

Professor Miller knows what he's talking about. Lectures are extremely thought provoking and if you don't understand a concept, he is more than happy to walk you through it. The class can be very intimidating at first, but the amount of knowledge and perspective you gain outweighs any doubts you had in the beginning. No exams or final!

Ben provides a great introduction into political theory/philosophy, where you read the works of political theorists and their beliefs about freedom and equality, challenging your own in the process. The readings can be difficult but lecture and discussion makes things clear. Ben is very knowledgable and works to make himself available after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: professor Miller is great giving lectures and wants his students to have clear understanding of the topics. course work is not an overload.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I absolutely love this professor. He is such a genius if you have an opportunity to take a class with this man consider yourself lucky to even hear the thoughts in his mind. All his lectures are mandatory but they are all incredibly interesting and he's incredibly lenient with excuses. I love Ben Miller
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I want Ben Miller to be my father. He is inexplicably knowledgeable. After taking this course, my brain grew by 6 sizes.

This class and professor are both incredible. The time commitment is worth how much you grow as student, person, and citizen; you just have to commit to putting the work in, and you'll get so much out of it. Prof. Miller is a genius and he does his best to help you succeed, not only in this class but in all of your future endeavors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ben's the best PS professor I've had. Listens to student feedback and made the final brief optional and reorganized the schedule to debrief a brief. Explains the material in a digestible way (take 270 first for more in-depth lectures). This class differs from 270 by being more group based. Very blunt but wants you to succeed

Professor Miller is an amazing professor! One of the best in the department by far and I have enjoyed both this class and 270. I think this class is easier than 270 but both are great! Most of the 370 class was based on court cases with some reading on philosophy, which wasn't too important to read, but the cases were great and I learned a lot!

Best and most intelligent professor I've ever had at UIUC. I get why people might be intimidated by him/ a little scared of him, but he just wants his students to genuinely succeed and learn from his class. Asks you to clarify what you are saying often, but just because he wants to give a genuine, meaningful, and clear answer.

Absolute genius of a professor. Challenges your thought very hard, but explains the tough content like he's talking to a pre-k student, making it much easier to follow the Logic of his thought. Truly a brilliant mind
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was unsure if I would like this class bc the syllabus looked daunting but this has been the best class ever. I love that you are required to go and participate bc being forced to show up helps. The content is very interesting & makes you think a lot about what you thought you knew. Professor Miller was a great lecturer and Kevin was an amazing TA

My first political theory class I have ever taken. Miller makes theory clear to understand as long as you put in the effort. Quizzes are based off of the readings and can be a bit confusing, so it is important to read carefully. Heavy emphasis on discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing class and professor, and very easy to get an A as long as you put time into your assignments. No exams or papers, just weekly take-home quizzes, weekly reflection journals, and four bigger assignments. Prof Miller is awesome and is not only very knowledgeable but very caring as well! I would highly recommend both him and this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: An amazing professor, one of the best teachers I have ever had. Understands what he is teaching and teaches it well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class material can be kind of dense but Dr. Miller is actually soo smart and he seems like a really cool dude. I respect tf out of him.

I love this man. Easily the best class I've taken at this school and the best professor I've ever had. Taking one of his other classes next semester just cause he's so good at teaching. So understanding, cares about learning, makes the content interesting, and overall makes his classroom a great environment to learn in.

Prof. Miller relies heavily on theoretical/philosophical material, which is literally in the title of the class. It is tough to follow if you dont put in the work but if you do, it is fascinating, and lectures are great. The cold-calling to answer qs is scary but you get used to it. He is brilliant, precise, & you will learn a lot if you want to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He was rude to some students that answered publicly, but every time I talked he didnt critic what i said much. his grading seems ridiculous. EVERYONE in section seems to have serious disagreement with it. I havent finished yet, and am expecting a huge curve. He, and one other professor, are the only teachers here that I actively avoid during regis
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very tough grader on subject matter that often is subjective. Both he and the TA came off as very rude, and they left you feeling dumb after each class. Not my first philosophy class, but by far the most challenging. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great prof overall. Very engaging and articulate. Can sometimes come across as rude, but it's all in the interest of making things very clear. Assignments are graded pretty particularly (especially the first) but he rewards participation and attendance significantly and you get extra credit for meeting with him in office hours. Very reasonable guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ben is by far the best professor I have ever had. If you get the chance to this class, I would 100% recommend (especially if you're interested in political theory and legal reasoning). I have learned more in this class than I have in any other Political Science class. Ben is extremely intelligent and logical, and he really cares about his students.

Ben is blunt and may come off as rude but he's not he just thinks logically. 4 small assignments, reflection post each week, takes attendance with iClickers and 3-4 questions on his quizzes on his material on the days you meet. I wasn't doing well in the class but I ended with a A-

By far my most favorite professor I have encountered. There are no exams nor quizzes and only a few assignments. He takes the time to teach/help you with the assignments at the beginning of the course and is genuinely invested in wanting you to learn, rather grades. With that said, he also directly states what you need to do to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I took this class because I assumed he was a good professor. He ended up being very condescending and often rude/blunt. The quizzes were impossible and the reading load was unfathomable. No extra credit nor exams, but attendance is mandatory and even showing up late ONCE tanks your grade. Expect to work hard but continue to feel stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: 2 hard quizzes weekly. They are timed; questions/answers are often subjective or have answers that seems like they could all be correct. Likewise, they often have grammatical/spelling errors. A lot of heavy reading that is very dense and therefore hard to understand. We don't get specific feedback on assignments. Do not take if you want an A.

The online quizzes, which count for 29% of the final grade, are hard. Some of the questions are subjective, and a lot of them are confusing. The lectures for this class are awesome and really make you think. He is happy to answer all questions, in or outside of class and is really accessible. Some of the readings are 80+ pages so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best class that I have taken so far. It's very interactive and his lectures are more like casual discussions. As long as you do the work, it's not that hard to pass. Ben understands that we have other assignments and doesn't load us with much busy work. He also almost always lets us out of class early.

Ben is legit my favorite professor here. Super nice and very understanding. You have to go to class, do readings, and go to discussion, but there is a big extra credit project. He is always up to discussing anything outside of class and doesn't care about your grades, just wants you to learn. Anyone interested in poli sci needs to take his classes.

Ben is literally the best professor I've ever had. He makes classes simple by administering no exams, only a small amount of homework. Readings are very important but he also makes sure to make class extremely fun and helps you learn so much! Amazing personality, the only reason I get out of bed for class honestly

The class is really amazing! We discuss a lot of stuff like happiness and justice, which is not just limited to the ancient philosophy.  The class helps us to do critical thinking. Professor Miller is interesting and willing to help everyone.
Clear lectures, fair exams.
He is all right. His class thought me so much on different fronts. I recomend to people who seek to be challenged and learn :) else there are plenty of easier classes that are also good options!

Mid lecturer, and that's his only good quality.

Loves ruining students' lives.

Bailey is a very articulate speaker, though he can move pretty fast at times (Zbigniew did most of the lectures anyways). He's very approachable if you want to talk about your grade or other things. It's 391, so I think the curriculum is fairly standardized regardless of who's teaching it. It will be very stressful, but just do your best
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very well organized class, learned a lot. MP started off hard, but got easier through the semester. Exams were hard: highest score was barely 90% (including grad students). You could lose point if you said something wrong. Don't worry too much though, the class is curved in the end.

This course is a covers a bunch of security topics/concepts and Bailey does a great job. I learned a lot of useful and applicable stuff in this class, thoroughly enjoyed it and would absolutely recommend to anyone.
a little bit too online and involved

The class itself sucks (1.5 hr lectures twice a week that are genuinely AGONY to sit through, especially since most content could be covered in 20 minutes). Still, the material is straightforward: study the learning goals for exams and do the extra credit. I can't hate on Clegg, though; he's super kind and genuinely wants students to succeed.

Amazing lecturer that uses iClicker questions in lecture, which are taken for participation and not accuracy. There is a notebook that he requires you to purchase that he created from the bookstore but it is actually very helpful. A lot of extra credit opportunities as well. Only bad thing are his TAs who dont seem interested in teaching.
He really wants everyone to do well in his class. He offers extra credit throughout the semester. His office hours are extremely helpful! Attend lectures because they are helpful as well.

I only did well in the class because of the extra credit. I never got above a C+ on exams. He tests in a way that he wants you to understand the material, not memorize it. He cares a lot about your education, so go to office hours. This class took up a lot of my time, but just get all the easy points and do ALL the extra credit.

I took IB 150, and while the first few lectures can seem intimidating, Dr. Clegg is a great professor and cares about his students. If you put in the work, do the extra credit, and show up to all of the lectures, you will get an A. If you skip, you will fall behind. Above all else, though, STUDY for the exams and don't skimp on office hours.

Pay attention to wording during lectures for exam questions, the practice exams are long but some contain exam questions, what he says about learning this process to solving questions is true, the discussion activities are relevant, utilize office hours with the TAs, and skip the textbook, it's not necessary!

I really disliked this class. Basically edged us with clicker pts at the end of lecture (ppl would leave) bc he went overtime almost every class. Discussion wasn't helpful. Never used textbook, and the homework was tedious, though the practice tests were somewhat helpful. People glazing but I hated it. I failed every exam, BUT ended with a C sooo.

I loved this class. Ben and his TA's (shout out Adrien Seabloom) are great. If you don't understand something they make sure to explain in different ways. The lecture is almost 2 hours and can sometimes be redundant or too fast if you're running low on sleep lol. However, by far one of the best courses I've taken!

LOVED this class. Was it challenging, a little bit yeah but it is college level biology. He is such an amazing professor and while lectures felt rushed if you went to the 4-6 hour review sessions before the exams and went to office hours Ben and his TAs would clear everything up for you. Loved this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Clegg is great at explaining concepts. His lectures and pre lectures are a little redundant at first, but the structure of his class this way helps. Very kind person— only thing is that he usually goes a few minutes over, so try to avoid having a class right after lecture.

This class isn't THAT hard. Its a four credit hour course and requires the ability to apply the knowledge you learned in class instead of memorizing. This does make the exams hard but as long as you do the practice exam and the online review session, you can succeed. He can just come off a bit condescending and his teaching style was not for me.

Dr. Clegg is an amazing, fun, and passionate professor. He would stay on reviews for 4-6 hours at a time, and really cared about his students success and wellbeing. Doing his prelectures, and actually taking time to understand it/ take notes, made lecture very easy. You have to dedicate time, but if you use his resources you'll do very well.

He talks a lot and honestly it interferes with learning the material since he is constantly talking away.. he will try to make a point yet go in a thousand different directions and never truly reach a conclusion. Also, the way he words his questions are confusing and hard to understand, he tries to be so extra with all the extra wording.

Do not be a first-generation freshman. He preaches how important health is but if you get COVID and reach out to him, you're on your own. I would avoid speaking to him outside of class as he seems to have a penchant for eighteen year olds.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You have everything you need to succeed, it's up to you to put in the work. Nice guy, boring lectures and he would always talk way after the class ends. Overall, just study as the lectures come since the exams are long with a ton of content and you can lose track of the earlier topics of the unit.

Overall, he was good. The content wasn't necessarily “easy,” but it was mostly intuitive. His lectures explain concepts in great depth, lots of EC opportunities, and homework is similar to exams. He can kind of ramble a lot, and personally the class didn't resonate with me. Was still fine though!
Very good lecturer and very doable class. Everything on tests is covered and there is a lot of practice available.
amazing prof
takes attendance way too seriously and always takes class 5 minutes after it ends

Nicest man on the planet. Pre-lecture videos are sometimes long, but contain a lot of important information. Definitely take notes during lecture. Exams were very similar to practice problems given before the exams, and he will gladly provide you with help if you need it!

The class isn't easy, but definitely achievable. Ben is super nice and inspiring. He's a great professor and gives great advice. He's super honest about what you need to do to get an A and he's the kind of professor who believes everyone in class can get an A. Honestly, other professors should be more like him.

I truly loved having Clegg as a professor. He cares about how people perform in his class, and he wants everyone to succeed. His lectures are engaging and his humor helps with the extensive length. He is enthusiastic to teach, and I would definitely take another class with him if I could.

Easily one of the best, if not the best, professors on campus! Tons of extra credit (which is the curve) and makes concepts easy (I know that's contrary to my grade, but got burned out.) This class is a lot of work yes, but if you don't fall behind you will succeed! Make sure to always do your pre-lectures as well! The TAs are also very good!

Ben is the BEST teacher I've ever had, which is saying something considering he's teaching a class of about 600 students. The course is extremely well thought-out and doing the work ON YOUR OWN (although it can take forever sometimes) helps you tremendously. I'd take this class again and again if I could.

Very nice professor and very helpful during his office hours. Lectures and pre-lecture assignments can be hard to follow or understand. Application based so studying isn't as easy because memorization is only a small portion. If you stay on task and don't fall behind this class won't be too difficult. Lots of time given for tests.

Professor Clegg has a lot of energy and really cares about his students. He makes sure you understand every lecture and encourages you to participate. He also gives lots of extra credit opportunities and his pre lecture videos are always really helpful too.

From a guy in a busy frat and multiple extracurriculars, I have been looking for a class that makes me feel smart and gives me time to focus on other activities. Ben's the man, bro, he teaches stuff both in class and outside of class whenever I am confused. Good job, Ben!

I strongly encourage this guy. Dr. Clegg is a great person that wants to see you succeed and seems to enjoy what he is doing. He is very charismatic and passionate as well as supportive and kind. Although there is no curve, he offers plenty of extra credit which can easily bump your grade a whole letter.

This class was pretty easy and enjoyable. There are 2 pre-lecture assignments (45 minutes each), 1 pre-discussion question assignment (15 minutes), and 1 long homework assignment at the end of the week (1 hour). You should not waste your money on the textbook, it was really expensive and I never opened it once and still did well in the class.

Professor Clegg's lectures are engaging, and the class workload is manageable. Utilize the provided resources, like the pre-lectures and extra credit, to succeed. unstuck AI was also super helpful for preparing for exams.
This class is really annoying and has a lot of unnecessary work.

Dr. Clegg is a great teacher and very engaging! Do not waste money on the Pearson textbook (I never used it)! Pre-lectures and homework took a lot of time for me outside of class in order to fully understand and take notes on the material. Study well ahead of time, focus on learning goals/pre-lectures/homework to prepare for exams.

I found the course load a bit heavy at times (two pre-lectures, one HW assignment, and pre-discussion questions per week) mostly because I found the pre-lectures a little unengaging. That being said, I really liked everything else about the course. Dr. Clegg and my TA really cared about their students and the extra credit is also super helpful.

Both Dr. Clegg and my TA for the course were caring and wanted students to succeed. Lectures were engaging and fun. Dr. Clegg offered lots of extra credit opportunities and had plenty of resources to help understand the content. Clear expectations. A book is recommended for the course, but I stopped using it after a few weeks so save your money.

Professor Clegg is an incredible human- he genuinely cares about all his students, and you can tell that he's passionate about his material. He's also just a cutie pie. I definitely could've gotten an A if I had studied better, so don't be intimidated! Biggest tip is make sure you're reviewing material every week (or as often as possible!

He is a great professor and the lectures are not really engaging but make sure to do the pre lectures or else everything is confusing. IB 199 really helped me more that the lectures also make sure to take advantages of the resources and to do the extra credit from the beginning.
Great professor, lectures are engaging and useful to the test material. Plenty of resources are provided to understand the content.
definitely take him if you can- ive never had a teacher so compassionate about not only what they're teaching but also the students in the class and their success

Professor Clegg cares. Since his first lecture, I knew right away that he loves biology. IF you do all your homework, attend class/discussions, AND DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, you will be fine. I think his teaching style may not always work with everyone, but he does try really hard to make students excited about the various topics. Clegg is great!

Clegg is an amazing professor!He is incredibly good at teaching the material and he is also very passionate about what he is teaching.The way he structures the lectures and pre-lectures is very helpful when it comes to setting your own pace for learning but also to help the material really stick and not just be memorized.Cherish Clegg he is amazing

His passion for the material made me want to study integrative biology as a major. He really cares for each of us--and a what a teacher! His lectures were amazing.
     I would recommend this course to others.
If you don't pay attention to those pre-lectures, you're going to struggle throughout the class.

Ben Clegg is one of the best professors I've had during my educational career. He doesn't teach you to memorize biological concepts, he teaches you to KNOW them. I would 1000% take this course (or any other course he teaches) again.

Dr. Clegg single handly make this university worth it. He has the highist quality of pre-lectures, lectures, and has the best teams of TAs. If you have time to take this class for any major who is interested in life itself, then there is no better place to start than Ben's IB 150.

Dr. Clegg is a fantastic professor and I would take again. Lots of extra credit opportunities every week, and unlike other biology classes, whats in lecture is whats on the tests. Dr. Clegg will stay after class to answer all your questions, and even takes a week out of the semester where all classes and regular assignments are cancelled.

Ben Clegg is amazing at teaching and a sweetheart!!! He cares about our mental health just as much as he does about our grades, which is so important in a professor. Even if you get a B or a C on an exam, you can still get an A in the class because of his extra credit opportunities and because his class is built around a "growth mindset".
I loved professor Clegg. He is super excited about what he is teaching and really wants you to succeed. Awesome class.

Professor Clegg was by far my favorite professor this semester! His lectures were well organized, and it is very clear that he is passionate about teaching and cares a lot for his students. The content can be challenging if you do not put in effort, but overall the assignments and exams were not bad! Final is also optional :)
too judgy

Ben was hands down my favorite professor last semester. I loved how his class was organized and how all the work you had to do was useful and helped solidify your knowledge by the end of each week. He also gives a ton of extra credit chances (like 5% of your grade). There is a book to buy but no one I knew ever read it and we all got A's.

Clegg has been my favorite STEM professor so far. He's good at teaching and he's actually super helpful. His pre-lectures genuinely prepared me for lectures, so just make sure to take notes on the pre-lectures. He made the class interesting as well. Office hours were also a life-saver. Lastly, DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT IT SAVED MY GRADE!!!

amazing professor. genuinely cares, his TAs are all competent (to my knowledge), gives an abundance of extra credit. my advice to excel in this course is to actually do all the pre-lectures (and if you're going to cheat on pre-lectures/hw try it first and then check yourself before submitting), attend all lectures, and DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT.

Dr. Clegg is a fantastic professor. Easy to get along with, is always willing to talk about course content, and is very thorough in his lectures. BE SURE TO WATCH THE PRE-LECTURES! That is where most of the learning is. The lectures are also helpful, since he goes into detail about the content. Take the merit section, if you can (IB 199).
Very passionate and very friendly. Much love for Ben! Really cares about his students and does everything to keep people on track and prepared.

Best class I've ever taken. Dr. Clegg obviously cares about his students and his subject which makes it easy and fun to learn. If you do the pre-lectures and pay attention in class, you'll do well. It's more about understanding and application than memorization. Plenty of extra credit throughout the semester along with an optional final exam.

Don't buy the textbook, you don't need it. Pay attention during the pre-lectures, that's where you learn. Take the actual lecture seriously, because that's where he clearly explains the pre-lecture. Do the extra credit like your life depends on it. The class is really easy if you work. Makes MCB 150 look like a PhD level course. Work hard offrip!

Graded lecture questions, but if u watched the lecture, they weren't too difficult. Super informative and I learned a lot. I loved discussion too. He is extremely kind and just a fun guy all around.  His final wasn't that bad either. You have to study and review. Not an "easy A" class but it's very manageable and fair.
Dr. Clegg is amazing! I highly recommend him as a professor. You can tell that he loves biology and wants his students to succeed.

Easily one of the best teachers I've ever had. Ben structures his class in a way that he WANTS you to succeed -- he has TAs give office hours every day, gives an optional final that can replace your test scores if you do better on it, has multiple opportunities for extra credit, etc.

He is also very enthusiastic about what he teaches

Ben Clegg is genuinely great at his job and you can tell that he has a passion for biology. Hes gets a bit dragged down as time goes on but he still has boatloads of enthusiasm. Hes an absolute stand out guy and I respect the hell out of him. Great professor 10/10 would recommend.

Amazing professor! Responds super well to student needs, office hours are helpful, lectures are super clear and interactive! Super approachable professor who explains every topic very well and is clearly passionate about what he does! Highly suggest taking this class!

Dr. Clegg is my favorite teacher from my freshman year. He is approachable and really wants his students to not only succeed but be excited about biology. His lectures are great and he has great TAs as well. He has weekly extra credit and each week you get the same assignments so you know what to expect. He is truly amazing at his job!
Ben had a very fair grading policy, and I enjoyed taking his class a lot! As long as you put in the effort, you can succeed in this class. I would definitely recommend him to anyone.

The content of the class itself can be challenging, but Dr. Clegg made it seem super manageable and was always available to answer questions and discuss course content. From staying at exam review sessions for 5+ hours on Sunday nights to inspiring pep talks, Dr. Clegg is extremely invested in student success.
Phenomenal! Dr. Clegg really wants his students to succeed!

He is so passionate about biology and does a really good job at explaining different concepts in a manner that will help you learn rather than help you memorize. The classwork and homework is clear and concise and easy to access. He is very humble and accessible outside of class.

Dr. Clegg is an amazing integrative biology professor. His class was not particularly hard, and he is always willing to go over topics you don't understand. He also has review sessions the weekend before an exam and will stay until everyone's questions are answered.

Professor Clegg is an amazing instructor. He clearly cares about his students mental health and encourages his students to not strain themselves over his course. In addition, he always had study sessions in which I highly suggest you take advantage. He has these sessions for students to ask questions about anything about the unit being taught.

I swear this man cares more about his students than he does himself. All he wants is for his students to love biology as much as he does and to feel like they can have a future in the field if they want it. Really thats all I could ever ask for in a professor. A true needle in a haystack.

Amazing professor. Not only was he kind and respectful, but he cares so much about us students and provided us with all the resources needed to succeed. Brad from MCB 150 needs to take notes from Dr. Clegg!!

All of the reviews basically say everything needed to say - Clegg, even on an online format is great. The material and application can be challenging so I highly recommend a tutor and taking advantage of other resources including the extra credit he offers. There's a grade resurrection policy and he absolutely wants everyone to succeed.

Clegg cares about his students so much and always wants them to succeed! Extra Credit can save your grade by a bunch, and its super easy. He always has a positive attitude and makes you feel so welcomed. Amazing professor!
Dr. Clegg is an amazing professor who really cares about the success of his students. The passion he has for biology is evident and contagious. Im so grateful to have had him as a professor!

My first class at UIUC. I LOVED Clegg he was so encouraging and if you put in any effort at all he would do the same for you. He had an extreme amount of resources available for students to get extra help. I love clegg

Do the course objectives thoroughly. The class was very fair and you have 3 exams, and 1 optional exam; if it's higher than the average of your 3 exams, he'll replace it. Lots of extra credit. He's very enthusiastic and will spend hours upon hours for reviews and office hours. I didn't really study and I got a B+, study and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Clegg is actually hands down, one of the best professors I've had. Provides a lot of extra credit opportunities, makes it a point that he actually wants us to learn instead of making us memorize information, and shows a lot of care for his students. If you put in the work and effort for this class, you will be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I believe I would take this class again just for the professor. I really enjoyed the content in this course. At times, the questions on tests would be a little confusing, however, I feel like it was really similar to biology offered in high school. There are many extra credit opportunities, so if you complete all of those, it'll help your grade.

Clegg is great. Very motivational for preparing for tests and has great exercises and lectures and de-stressing. A genius when it comes to Biology. One thing: he overexplains a lot and is sometimes hard to follow in lectures.

Professor Cleggs exams were very difficult, but there is a ton of extra credit available. He really cares about his students and is always sending inspirational things to keep us positive. He hosts review sessions that last for 6+ hours.

There is a bunch of extra credit opportunity every week through the whole semester. You can put low effort and still do really well in this class because Clegg teaches so well that you don't need to learn anything by yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ben is currently my favorite professor ever. This class was definitely a learning curve as a freshman, but once you get the hang of it this class can be quite easy. You need to know how to study for his tests, or else you might be stuck with a bad grade. Although, his class is very forgiving and offers a lot of extra credit.

You can tell how much Clegg cares about his students. The class would be better in person, but it is what it is. His review sessions last for hours, he answers questions until he physically can't stay awake. The only reason the class is not super easy is because it is online, but he still puts a lot of effort into his lectures. Nicest person.

Clegg was AMAZING for IB150. Absolutely take! I didn't study for his tests at all and only went to his legendary review sessions the night before and got an A on all 3. I also did all 55 points worth of extra credit which is a ton considering the course is out of 1000 points. The man is legendary and is easily the nicest, most caring professor ever

He focuses on your ability to apply your understanding of a concept so be prepared to come across examples you haven't discussed in class. Homework is harder than exams. He hosts long study sessions before the exams that are very helpful, he'll thoroughly talk about every concept. He gives out A LOT of extra credit so make sure to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This man is the most caring and helpful professor/teacher I've ever had. He's constantly encouraging and giving out advice. The exam info section saved my life. If you have the opportunity, do yourself a favor and take his class.

Dr. Clegg is one of the best profs at UIUC. He puts so much time and effort to ensure that his students thoroughly comprehend concepts. He genuinely wants students to do well. He holds review sessions and office hours. He goes above and beyond! Tip: he is not a regurgitate prof, you NEED to understand concepts. Overall, I had a great experience!

Professor Clegg is the best professor Ive had. He genuinely cares about the students, and is extremely friendly. He replies fast to emails, even with hundreds of students. He makes class very interesting and is a great lecturer. He takes the time to hand grade over 600 tests as well, so you see he really cares. I would absolutely recommend Clegg!
Honestly one of the best teachers I have ever had. Goes out of his way in order for his students to not only succeed, but actually understand and learn the topics.

Hands down the most caring, helpful, and kind professors at UIUC. I am so sad he only teaches this one class. The exams are very conceptual, this isn't a memorization based course. Cherish Clegg, you will never have another professor as amazing as him again!

Every student deserves to have a professor like Dr. Clegg. I wish all professors were as dedicated and cared as much about their students as he does. His exam review sessions that go until 2 am are legendary. You have to put in the work to learn the material, but you truly do learn. I'd take another class with him in a heartbeat.

Professor Clegg was one of the best teachers I have ever had. He wants you to do well and gives your opportunities to do so. He truly wants you to succeed and gives you great tips on how to do so! Loved this class so much IB is my major now!

I wish this professor could teach all of my classes. His lectures and content are well put together, he plans ahead, and he goes out of his way for students. Although the class was a bit conceptually difficult, he was always able to explain things in multiple ways. Definitely attend his review sessions! He does the absolute most to benefit students
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: prof clegg is super nice and really cares about his students. in review sessions on zoom he was funny as hell and stayed on until 3am just to make sure everyone had their questions answered. the lectures can be long but never too bad. they're pretty interesting. the online HW is really helpful. i didnt use the textbook once don't bother with it

My favorite professor I have taken so far. His lecture videos tell you exactly what you need to know, and he makes learning the material easy. As for accessibility, he holds review sessions before each exam that last until all the questions are answers. I've stayed on a zoom session with this man from 6 pm to 2 am! Truly dedicated.

Professor Clegg cares about his students by holding lots of office hours(OH) along with TAs. He even holds every OH before every exam until very late in the morning. Such a responsible and enthusiastic Professor as well as caring TAs! Offering lots of extra credits. Despite mandatory meeting in discussions, the material is fun and interacted.

Clegg really cares for his students and wants them to do well. He's one of the best professors I've ever had and even though the information was difficult for me, I wish I could take the class again. He offers a lot of extra credit and hosts long review sessions before the exam. Highly recommend him :)

Dr. Clegg is the most caring professor at UIUC. Before every test, he holds a review session to answer every single person's questions. The last review session lasted from 6pm to 2am. He obviously is passionate about teaching and about making sure every student has the chance to succeed. Truly one of a kind.

Do EVERY SINGLE EXTRA CREDIT. This year, if you did all of the extra credit, you could raise your grade by 6.1%. Clegg WANTS you to succeed; I have never met a professor who goes above and beyond like him, and who does things like review sessions before tests until 3am. Also, tests contain a few qs from homework/practice tests.

He is an amazing teacher. He cares about you and your place in his class. The best example of this: he hosts large exam review sections with up to 200 students on the weekend before a test. He will sit there and answer EVERY question until EVERYONE is satisfied and prepared. You will not find a better teacher.

This class is supposed to be a joke but its not. The online lectures sometimes do not explain all the slides provided. Clegg is a great guy and cares for you. He gives a total of 55 points of extra credit total!! Make sure to read the textbook, do the homework BY YOURSELF, and do lots of practice problems. I didn't really need office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Clegg made the class enjoyable and really taught how to understand the material, not just memorization of facts. He was funny and engaging in lectures. He explained concepts well. Office hours and exam prep were very helpful too.

Ben genuinely cares about each of his students' development. He tests on overarching concepts (unlike MCB150 with is mostly memorizing details), and during lecture, he walks you through the thought process he wants you to have. Lectures are a must. He gives out a ton of extra credit points (nearly 4% of the entire course grade). Do them all.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had Clegg for IB 150 Merit, and I have to say he is one of the best lecturers/teachers/professors I've had. He cares for his students greatly and wants everyone to get an A, but, more importantly, he wants you to be successful later in life. You definitely need to work to do well, but he provides you with everything you need to do so.

Ben is an extremely caring professor. He's here to support you and make sure you are doing everything to the best of your abilities. There is weekly homework which is often difficult, but between him and his TAs, they have office hours mon-fri which are very helpful. He gives a lot of extra credit and cares a lot about his students.

Please make sure you know the learning goals! Very very important in order to pass the test. The TA's are phenomenal during office hours (please use them if you need help! highly recommended) There's online homework due every week and after each test, go to lecture bc he'll give out extra credit in a quiz format. Ben is super passionate
I had him for IB 150 this year. The class itself wasn't too hard, but he offered lots of extra credit if your grade was low. He genuinely cared for his students and wanted them to succeed.

Ben is an amazing professor and lecturer. He is very passionate about his students and what he is teaching. He tests are very application-based, but he never throws in any curveballs. He only expects you to understand what you were taught in class, or else he will give you background information on the question.

The only thing I don't like about Clegg is that sometimes the lectures don't completely follow the given handouts in the course binder, and sometimes the homework is unnecessarily difficult. Otherwise, he is a great professor who explains concepts thoroughly and makes sure we actually understand the material. The tests are very straightforward.
He really wants his students to succeed.

This class was the hardest thing I've ever done and Dr. Clegg will make you work hard but in the end it's totally worth it. He has the grading scale set up in a way that you have room to make mistakes and learn - I came out with almost an A+ in the class, even after failing the first exam. Definitely my favorite class so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Great guy who genuinely cares about and believes in his students. Lectures were always interesting to me and the binder keeps you involved. But decent amount of homework and tests can be kind of difficult. Best advice is redo the practice weekly homework a couple times and take the practice exam before the real exam. Its definitely doable!
I LOVED going to class. He is so enthusiastic and loves to teach. He makes you love the class and content. 10/10 guy

This class really is amazing! Ben knows how to teach and is really passionate about bio. When I am in lecture I genuinely stay focused and try to understand the material, not just memorize it. He is one of the very few teachers who cares about their students and more importantly believes that they can succeed. He is a fantastic professor!!!!!!

Dr. Clegg is a very nice man, but an incredibly ineffective professor. His lectures are often incoherent, ambiguous and convoluted. He very frequently takes simple concepts and makes them very difficult to understand. The TAs in this class know almost nothing about the topic, and are incredibly difficult to work with.

Dr. Clegg is an outstanding professor and a great person. His class is well run, and he prepares you well for his exams through his learning targets/ objectives. You can tell he is a genuine person, that cares about his students, and has a passion for education. He has really accessible office hours as well.

Genuinely good professor and person overall. I only struggle in his class because my high school did a poor job of teaching me the material we were supposed to know prior to this class. However, he does provide you with plenty of resources if this is the case.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable professor. Show up to lecture and do all assignments and you'll be fine. Seemed a little department driven, as if he were simply going off a script. He's very clear about what will be on exams, no curveballs

Dr. Clegg is one of the best professors I have had. He is very passionate about teaching and biology, which made me excited to come to lectures. The way he structures his class allows you to actually understand the material, instead of just memorizing facts. Overall, Dr. Clegg genuinely cares about his students both academically and personally.

Professor Clegg is one of those professors who really cares for your success. His lectures are mandatory but they help a lot. He talks fast sometimes but it's just because he is super passionate about biology. His course demands that you put work outside of class if you want to receive a good grade. He's also hard to catch during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's great one on one but he kind of sucks if you only go to lectures. If you meet him for office hours or take it JS like I did, you'll love him. He's very caring and wants to see you succeed, he's not just there for his own research.

Dr. Clegg is an amazing professor who is really passionate about the course that he teaches. The course was very well structured. Although the course mainly covers basic biology topics taught in high school, lectures are still really interesting and the questions he asks in lectures makes you think about these topics from a different perspective.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Clegg will be a professor I will remember forever because he genuinely cares about his students. IB 150 is a decently tough class but he makes it more bearable. He gives a lot of extra credit and gets excited when students do well on tests. Highly recommend taking any classes with Clegg

Professor Clegg is a really great teacher, and it's obvious that he cares about all his students. He's super enthusiastic about biology, and can give good explanations to any questions you may have. The class isn't easy, but there is a lot of extra credit given, and you get a lot of points just for showing up to class. Overall, a solid professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Clegg is amazing, he takes time for every student that needs it. He is one of the rare few that actually cares about every single student's success. If you get a chance to take the James Scholar section, do it, because the Professor teaches your discussion section. I can't emphasize enough how good of a teacher he is.

Great teacher and really shows that he cares about his students. Willing to meet with you outside of office hours if you need extra help. Gives tons of extra credit to help boost grades. Exams are hard but he makes it clear what he expects to be known. Be ready to put in work, though!

Did not really learn anything new in this class. If you have an AP Bio background, you are basically set to breeze through the course. I did not particularly like the way lectures and discussions were set up, but they were not the death of me, either. Just be sure to do the practice exams and go over the learning objectives/goals before each exam.

IB150 is in fact the easiest one comparing to all the other MCB courses I have taken. If you have taken AP biology or other bio courses in high school this course should not be a problem. Plus, even if you already know most of the knowledge you could still gain something new as he uses interesting examples. His learning strategies are great!

Ben Clegg is not a good professor at all. His lectures are very boring and make no sense. This unit, I did not attend a single lecture and still did well on the exam. The one time I went to lecture, I did not get anything out of it and left like it was a waste of my time. He does a terrible job at explaining concepts.

IB 150 is supposed to be the easiest bio ever, but it did not feel that way. I put in so much work, did all the EC/HW/readings, and studied like crazy to end up with an A-. He was good, but his TA's aren't the best. The set-up of the course is also irritating. He himself is a good and knowledgable guy nonetheless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Clegg is the most caring professor I have even had. He gives so many opportunities for success in his class. To get a good grade show up to lectures to receive clicker points, do all of the homework because it is a huge chunk of the grade, and go to TA office hours.

Prof. Clegg is an excellent lecturer who tries to make learning the material as interesting as possible, but his lecture activities can sometimes be hard to follow. The exams are pretty difficult, but there is a lot of padding and extra credit and a nice resurrection policy. I got Cs on my first 2 exams and managed to get an A in the course.

I'm really glad to have had him this semester, he's a pretty good professor. Despite the huge lecture size, he does a good job of making it seem smaller. Additionally, the exams for this class are application-based and can be somewhat difficult; however, there's lots of extra credit and resources to get help. Overall, I'd definitely recommend him.

Super thankful to have had Ben as a professor. Hes super passionate and makes class very interesting. Anyone who likes bio will love this class. Defintely deserves more than one pepper on the hot scale.

ben clegg is an amazing professor, very talented. kinda obsessed w him tbh. the class was difficult in my opinion as nothing is about reciting material when it comes to the test, you need a very strong basis in order to apply the information on exams. hopefully im praying for a c. requires access code to mastering bio
He cares a lot about his students. However his lectures are kind of confusing. I never used the text book for this class but I heard he requires Mastering Biology now.

Clegg talks really fast, and definitely deserves the spot to teach. Prepare to learn more about life than you thought you could, because this was the hardest class I had ever taken. If you work hard, and truly understand what you are learning, and do the extra credit, you should get an A. Prepare well for his exams and learn outside of class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ben is a really cool guy. Lectures can get a little boring, but he tries 100% to keep the giant class interested and connected to the class. He highly recommends the textbook, but personally I never touched it and still got an A- in the class. You can feel how passionate he is in the way he teaches and how he treats every student with respect.
Large lecture consisting of near 600 students (Clegg teaches as to not leave ANY behind; very slow)
Clegg is nice guy who is very passionate about biology and explains things very clearly.

Genuinely cool guy and fun lecturer.  Plenty of lecture activities to demonstrate concepts and is actually fun to talk to outside of lecture.  Very fair with exam questions, just do the homework and pay attention

Best teacher I had this semester! He is very approachable, is generous with extra credit, holds review sessions for every exam (including final), and is passionate about the subject. There's a decent amount of busy work but it's well worth the easy points to buffer your grade. Just overall a solid professor.
he knows the content really well. office hours are great for extra help.

Amazing professor.  Can get a B average on all the midterms+final and still easily get an A with the hw and participation points.  ALSO DO THE EXTRA CREDIT.  He really cares about all of his students doing well and understanding the material.  Would Recommend for sure.

Clegg is a great professor who makes bio fun and easy.  He also really cares about his students. One time, I accidentally overslept an exam and panicked so I immediately went to his office hour, but Clegg was understanding and let me take the take the exam at that moment.

Really passionate about what he was teaching, made lecture really interesting. Not super difficult material, but he's one of those teachers who wants you to apply concepts on the test rather than just recite material, so you need a really strong foundation to do well. Pretty easy intro course though, not hugely challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A really great teacher. Made difficult concepts easy to understand for all levels of ability. He also holds 6 hour study sessions the weekend before the test, and stays until every last question is answered -- he's really committed to making sure students understand the material, not just get the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He is a great lecturer and he really cares that every student understand the material. Before every test, he did a study session that lasted until the last student left. He gives feedback extremely quickly (in less than a week). This is great, especially considering that he has over 600 students! I'd definitely take another course offered by him.

There's a decent amount of online homework , which can be tedious but is pretty easy and boosts your grade. There's extra credit every week to make up for when you forget an assignment or skip lecture. Clegg does review sessions before every test and if you go you're pretty much guaranteed to do well on the test.

Clegg is a funny man, very energetic and obviously passionate about biology. His test are nothing like his slides, notes, etc. They are mostly critical thinking problems which makes them extremely difficult and confusing. Some would say this is a blow off class, I beg to differ.

The class can be a little difficult but the professor goes above and beyond to make sure each student receives the help that he/she needs to pass. Obvious that he is very passionate and knowledgable about the subject. Takes student feedback into consideration. Phenomenal professor.
great. helps with whatever you need. will always be available. even if the class is hard, you'll be okay as long as you put some effort in.
It is easy class. There's a lot of chances for extra credit. I got 75 for my first exam and 80 for my final, but still managed to get an A.
Easier than AP bio, and the final has a generous curve. My raw score was a solid B, and with the curve it went up to a solid A

I loved Ben! He truly knows the subject he's teaching and is super eager to make sure we understand everything. Toughness is average, and it's not hard to get a good grade if you put in the effort. His office hours are great, and you can tell he's wants us to learn, which is great. He cares more about our learning than just points.
Great teacher. Loads of extra credit,  easy online homework. Tests are fair if you study.

Ben is great!!!! Very generous with extra credit.  Tests are reasonable, but be sure to study.  Online homework is pretty easy, lots of answers can be found on Quizlet and other webpages.  Highly recommend him.  Wish I could have another class just like this one.

Dr. Clegg was such a great professor. He makes the class pretty easy. Do the extra credit, it adds up to around 75 points. I blew off the last test and final and still got an A. Don't forget to do the learning catalytics and homework though. They definitely boost your grade. Overall great, and interesting class.

Sooo nice! Tests aren't particularly hard if you review the prelectures and lecture powerpoints. Extra credit galore. And very enthusiastic about what he teaches! I'm sad that I'll likely never have him again, and I actually wish I had gone to office hours to get to know him better. Only bad part is grading can be harsh on experimental design stuff

He is a good professor. Enthusiastic and clearly enjoys the subject he teaches. If you need any help, office hours are very useful and he hold review sessions before all of the tests. Tests are fairly easy, and he usually drops a question or two. Due to the nearly 80 extra credit1000 total points, it is pretty easy to get a good grade as well.
Very great professor! My fellows all admire him a lot. Clarity and efficiency!

Clegg literally jumps at the chance to help his students. He is a good teacher because of his great passion for biology and he really cares about his students whether he knows their names or not. He is a really good guy. On the negative side, he can occasionally ramble and his lectures can be a tad confusing.

Although Dr. Clegg's lectures can seem confusing at times, he is a great teacher who is willing to invest all of his time into his students. He is very passionate about Biology and wants to ensure that everyone understands the material taught. If you do the Learning Goals before each Hour Exam, you'll do well on his tests. Lots of extra credit too.
Good!
class is super easy just the test are kind of hard so study and go over notes.

He was very into teaching and would really spend time with the students during office hours explaining a certain concept. If you really show up during lecture and finish off all the work, there's no reason not to get good grades.

Great class to take freshman year. It provides a different perspective on biology and Ben is a great professor! However, if you really want to pass, I suggest going to office hours and studying outside of lecture as some of the material has a lot of content to cover.
So down to earth. Wants you to love the subject instead of worrying about points. Offers tons of extra credit and will sacrifice all his time to help you
Great Professor! Take the class! Would recommend saving it for senior year so you can kick back and relax for the semester!
