reviews.comment: Great teacher; he wants his students to not just memorize the material but actually learn it. Dont underestimate this class or his exams, you need to put in effort for the grade. 1st exam shows what he expects but dont let the score discourage you. Record all lectures, take notes from the textbook and review screencasts. Hard but not impossible.

Mehrtens does a good job at explaining things, however, he also does a good job at complicating things. He gives very in-depth answers because he wants you to really understand the concepts. Tests are very difficult and tricky. You have to really know your information then be able to apply it in a series of trick questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brad is a great guy and professor. Great lectures, at least when they're traditional. Make sure you study and don't underestimate the first exam. I tried studying using "concept mapping" or connecting idea that we learned and it worked great! would highly recommend for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His tests are the hardest tests you'll ever see (I'm talking 60% averages), but they're doable if you work hard. You have to come to lectures and watch screencasts. However, Brad does answer every questions and gives you a lot of resources. You just have to make sure to really be on your A game for this class.

Brad is honestly one of the best professors I've ever had. Yes, MCB 150 is a hard class, and will require a lot of work, but if you study, attend a few office hours, and take discussion seriously, there is no reason why you shouldn't be able to get at least a B. I got an A-, but i put in a significant amount of work, but still really enjoyed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Brad's passion for mcb is contagious and he's an amazing lecturer! I would definitely consider this a weed out class (an 84%A-) so take it seriously. Do all the assignments and DO NOT skip lectures, it will pay off in the end. The exam questions are EXTREMELY specific so you must know the info thoroughly to do well. Study hard and you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Though the class is quite challenging, you know that it extensively prepares the students for the MCAT and the career world after that. Additionally, the class has a balance; it is demanding, but with a solid work ethic and a study schedule, an A is attainable.

He is a very enthusiastic and thorough professor. It is a tough but doable class, but if you do all the readings and watch all the lecture videos you should do well. The class is graded very fairly. I would take one of his classes again.
He is definitely a great lecturer. Unfortunately, I don't find myself really into biology. It's still interesting to learn and memorize all the stuff tho.
Brad definitely know the information. Very approachable guy, he is also an adviser in the biology department as well. Definitely do not forget to do the homework. Oh, and he curves the class A LOT!

Brad knows what he's talking about. He sounds like an audio textbook during lectures, which make it hard to stay interested. He wants his students succeed, but the exams are ridiculous. The class is curved heavily, but the exams are still unreasonable. Be ready to spend a couple of hours every day reading

Brad is one of the greatest profs I have had. He used to be a theater major which keeps lectures engaging. Record lectures because he tests on some of the details not in the slides. The class is difficult but getting an A is possible. You learn a lot about MCB. He really makes you think. (Side note: go to him for advising to!)
Listen to lecture recordings, look at homework problems.  Tests are difficult, but know the right materials to study off.
Brad is there for his students and really tries to test the concepts and understanding. Definitely is a weed out class for those who don't want to spend the time on Biology.
Brad made me look forward to lectures. He had tough exams but as long as you studied enough they were manageable. He's a G

Brad is an amazing professor and lecturer. He has so much passion for MCB and knows the material inside and out. The only hard thing about this class is that the tests are extremely tough and tricky. If you do not go to lecture or actively listen, you most likely won't get an A.  Finishing MCB150 was bittersweet, simply because you're leaving Brad.

However, all of the homework and lecture participation points really help you bounce back from the terrible exams, I promise! You will feel like you know nothing and are going to fail, but you will make it. As long as you record & listen to everything Brad says more than once, you will see he tests you word for word on what he has already said.

This guy literally has the entire textbook memorized word for word! The lectures are extremely well structured and he breaks down difficult concepts. His exams are ridiculously hard for a 100 level class! Do NOT underestimate the difficulty of this course! Great professor, very approachable, but this class requires time.
Gr8

Prof Mehrtens is a godsend.  No way I could of gotten through this course with a lesser teacher.  His jokes are super lame, but he genuinely cares about his students doing well, and is BEYOND patient when helping students struggling to understand the material.  I wish he taught more courses!!

Class is hard. Definitely record lectures and don't cram. Study a little bit every day, and I don't mean doing just the daily mastering biology. Office hours is helpful when you have questions, try to go whenever possible. But when you have a question and are confused and ask him about it, he is sure to explain it clearly to you.

Mehrten's class was very interesting, although it seemed like he made his tests way harder than it needed to be for a 100 level class. Tests are very, very hard to get an A on, and this class will consume a lot of your study time.

He may claim he doesn't try to trick you on tests but he often uses rather confusing wording or complicated question styles. The material is not very difficult but there can be a lot at times. Many questions are repeated off of old exams. His lectures sound overly scripted but they aren't too boring. I heard his office hours are rather helpful.
Great class, great teacher
Great class

Brad is an amazing lecturer, and very helpful with office hours. Make sure you go to class and don't fall behind. The class is definitely difficult, and you'll have to work your butt off even for a B. Study a lot for the tests.

Brad is a popular professor, despite teaching one of the toughest classes the freshmen take. He is a fantastic lecturer, always prepared and as clear as can be. He is pretty funny, but his exams are nothing to laugh at. Don't skimp when prepping in his class.

Mehrtens is a hall-of-fame lecturer. He never says "um" or "like." Everything is clear and deliberate, like he has his lectures memorized in his head. That being said, the class was not easy for me, and I highly suggest not skipping. Tests are difficult, even if you study diligently, but his grading scale gives you a legit chance to do well.
Great lecturer, extremely difficult exams. Be sure to utilize office hours on a weekly or at least bi-weekly basis if you want an A. Ask questions as often as possible.

Brad is a great lecturer who explains the material well. Must show up to lectures or you will be lost. Don't focus on the textbook. record the lectures and listen to the lectures again before the exam and you should be okay.

Mehrtens made "the study of life" very lively with his natural zeal for teaching. He will make you work for it, but it is totally worth it if you wish to go down the pre-med track. Office Hours is where you can really get to know the material from Mehrtens himself! Bottom line, he will really teach you biology like no other professor. 3 Thumbs Up!
Majoring in IB so not all that interested, but Brad made the class a lot of fun. Brutal tests, but great grading scale! Didn't love the material but Brad made it the best it could possibly be.

Brad is a great professor who really cares about students. There is a LOT of content that is covered in this course. If you want to do well, you MUST show up to lecture and do the assigned readings. Brad presents information in a very clear manner during his lectures and he is always available to help. That being said, this class is not an easy A.

Brad is a truly exceptional professor. I can't imagine having a better experience in MCB 150. Brad truly cares about his students and makes himself available regularly for the student's convenience. It isn't hard to tell that Brad has a knack for teaching. He makes what seems like an impossible course enjoyable. Would definitely recommend his class

The BEST teacher ever had. Took a bio course a year ago and HATED it. Everything was like a confusing web of terms and I hated it all. at first I dreaded taking mcb 150.  2 weeks later, I loved bio, loved going to class. Brad made everything make so much sense. He provided us with all info needed for exams. no joke here, got 100 on the third exam

Mehrtens explains everything very well and can help with any questions but he makes the exams ridiculously difficult. I wouldn't take the class if you don't have to but if you're really passionate about the subject then it might be worth it. The system for class participation really sucks. Logging in before class starts can sometimes be a challenge

Brad is the bomb. You do have to work hard in this class to get the grade you want, but Brad helps your every step of the way. He provides you with all of the materials you need and is very clear about the content. I learned an incredible amount of material and feel very prepared for any other MCB class I have to take in the future.

I took Online over summer failed (SUPER HARD). Then in the fall in class got a B+. HAVE TO attend lecture to pass exams. About 2 questions per exam come from the book. Most questions are what he SAYS in lecture. You have to work for this grade. Studying the night before WILL NOT WORK. Only take if it is a requirement to graduate.

I Love this guys teaching! BEST TEACHER YET! You really have to understand concepts and biological methods for exams but he really prepares you for them. Relisten to lectures (recordings) and screencasts. Ive never had such a good professor. He reexplains concepts in different aspects and repeats them several times. really prepares you for mcb 250

Amazing teacher. knows how to explain concepts well. exams are 99% lecture, 1% txtbk. for exams: recrd lectrs, study slides, watch screencasts, skim txtbk. got As on exams. funny, makes class interesting. never even tempted to fall asleep in class. hahah see what he does if  your phone goes off. but seriously best teacher yet. an A is def possible

The class is though because there is so much detail but Brad makes sure you have the necessary materials to do well in this class. You learn so much from this class, its by far my favorite class at UIUC so far. If you put time into it, you can definitely get an A. Brad is great at explaining things and he wants everyone to do well in his class.

I HATED this class and this professor. His lectures were awful and he only emphasized the unimportant material on the test. He is also very condescending to students when they approach him to ask questions. If it can be avoided, do not take this class.

I don't know what people are saying about lectures they are useless he just says the same damn thing four times with no detail what so ever. Then the test are about minute details he said you don't have to know or are on the next subject in class. oh and the book ins't detailed either.

One of the hardest classes I've taken in two years here - the amount of content you go through is ridiculous for a semester long course. That said, Brad is very good at explaining concepts and helping you out if you need it, but can seem condescending at times during lecture. Take the exams very seriously from the start and you'll be fine

Class is tough, but if you go to class and RECORD lectures you should do fine. Its pretty easy to get an A- (you can get 70% on exams and get 100% on hw and you will get the A-), to get an A (you can get 80% on exams and get 100% on hw). Overall he is my best professor freshman year.

Brad Mehrtens is a great professor, don't get me wrong, but his lectures are VERY ANNOYING. His voice can be very condescending when he means to be thorough, like he's speaking to fifth graders. He also seems extremely rehearsed, partly since he's taught the course for about 20 semesters.... Other than that, his content is all clear and concise.
Bradley Mehrtens is the man.  He legitimately is interested in molecular and cellular biology and he tells the best jokes. If I could grow up to be one person it would be Brad.

He is enthusiastic while lecturing and youll understand everything he says during the lecture. Its necessary you read the book too tho. Some of the test questions are NEAR IMPOSSIBLE. You literally need to know every single detail (that you would normally think is minuscule) about every option on a multiple choice question in order to get it right

For the love of all that is holy DON'T MISS LECTURE! His exams are waaaaaay too hard, but the class is understandable in general. Read and re-read the books and listen to the lectures and you should get a decent grade. BTW, the 2nd exam is a nightmare.
He is a great, clear professor. Record and re-listen to the lectures and you'll be well on your way to a great grade.

Brad is an AMAZING teacher. He is so helpful, crystal clear when explaining things, and is very enthusiastic. I looked forward to going to class. Remember to record his lectures because he is a fast speaker. Just listen to the lectures a couple weeks before the test-- you're going to have close to all the knowledge you'll need. You'll love him!
Brad is a great professor. His lectures are clear and easy to follow, and he is very friendly as well. MCB 150 is a difficult class, but you can do well if you put enough work into it.

He's a great lecturer, but in office hours he's not very... human. Doesn't turn down the "I'm a proffessor and therefore superior" -vibe at all, which is weird. I would have really enjoyed his class more if his office hours were more personal and less business because he seems like a cool guy. Class is hard, not impossible: it teaches you to learn.

Brad's an alright professor, although I think his theatricalness can sometimes be a little distracting. If you want to get an A in this class you need to put in the work (going to class, re-listening to lectures). Grading scale is lenient but no curve.

This course has made me and countless others decide that we do not want to pursure the MCB major. Brad speaks too quickly and expects too much out of a 100 level class. I hate this class and going to lecture is almost a chore now. If you don't have to take it, don't.

Brad is a great professor. He explains everything perfectly exactly as he wants to. You can succeed in class by going to lecture, but PAY ATTENTION. Exams aren't bad if you relisten to lectures. Time consuming but if you do it, it's pretty easy to get the grade you want. It's a very good class and you will learn a lot.

Brad is a great professor! His tests are difficult though. Sometimes, I feel that your exam grade really depends on luck (ex. do you remember that small indiscreet comment he made that one time that this q is referring to...?)  The way to study for this class is to listen to lectures over and over again. If you're lucky, you'll get an A.

Brad is the best teacher i have ever had! He makes biology interesting to learn and he is a very smart man. If anyone thinks this class is hard it is because they are not trying hard enough. if you study and go to class, you can get a B or higher easily.
I really enjoyed this class. It's amazing how much you learn (if you are putting in the effort). Brad is great at giving lectures, but in office hours he is very condescending.
This class takes a lot of work and studying. Its very difficult, but definitely doable. Brad makes lectures interesting kind of a theater guy. Bring a recorder to lectures and study the power points.
Great teacher. Lion Kinged his baby in Follenger. Love.

For the purposes of MCB 150 Mehrtens is not a bad professor, but if you have to take any MCB above 150 I recommend you pass on him if possible. Test are from lecture and contradictory to the book, where the homework is from. My TA was great, probably why I got a C. There was even one time when my TA said he told us Mehrtens gave us incorrect info
the class is tough because the exams are hard, but overall I didnt think it was bad especially because an 88% is an A.
Awesome professor. Convinced me to become a bology major. Lovin' life (no pun intended)

SOme people say hes the best professor at uofi I personally think he is extremely fake, and wrongfully theatrical which detracts from the learning.The tests are 90%lecture  (as you are paying to be taught, not so you can teach yourself through reading)which can be a problem for those that skip, PARTY HARD but PUT IN EFFORT for school DON'T SCREW UP

Best prof ever!!!!!! He makes bio so interesting to me! He well organizes all the course material and makes hard stuff really easy. I strongly suggest everyone should try to go to his lecture sometimes. It is such an enjoyment.  After taking his MCB 150, I set my mind to switch my major to biochemistry from chemistry.

Brad is a fantastic teacher.  He makes complicated material easy to understand and is clearly very interested in what he's teaching.  It's a hard class, but Brad is aware of this and prepares students well for the exams.  Even though the exams are hard, there really aren't any surprises as long as you record the lectures and read the textbook.
Brad is very enthusiastic about teaching. Tests are really difficult but if you go to lecture and pay attention a B is not that hard to get
UUGHHHH!!! This is one hell of a difficult class.. I bought the voice recorder, attend all lectures, I read and go to all of the discussions and still do poorly on exams..  Need a miracle for a C

Brad has been my favorite professor so far at UIUC. His lectures are very engaging and he keeps the material fresh and interesting. Advice...RECORD the lectures and listen to them, exams are very hard and require acute attention to detail. Go to office hours and read the important sections of the book. He is the bomb!!

Extremely gifted instructor. Brad is very animated, engaging and articulate, presenting difficult material in a clear and coherent manner. This class is particularly challenging for freshmen, but upperclassmen who have taken hard classes will find that it compares favorably to many upper-level courses.

Brad is by far my favorite prof ever. He loves teaching and is ALWAYS ready to help students. He's very clear on what he expects, but exams are a little tough so be prepared. Discussion sections are pointless to the class, but go or else you'll lose a decent number of points. If you pay attention in lecture and go to OHs you'll do just fine.

I LOVE BRAD! He is very enthusiastic and is always willing to help. He's the best. The class is very hard but it is so interesting and my favorite class. I wish this class wasn't insanely hard because Brad is just such a great guy. Go to office hours!
Incredibly passionate, funny, and interesting. Has very high expectations but you'll learn more in his class than in any other intro Bio class you can take.

Really tough class, but AWESOME professor. He expects a lot out of you, but you'll learn way more. Yeah, his tests are pretty hard, but if you just read, go to lecture, do your quizzes, go to discussion, etc, you can still pull an A or B. U of I couldn't have picked a better professor to teach the class, though.

It amazes me how much material he can fit in the course of a lecture. There's SO MUCH TO KNOW. Everything is fair game on exams (even the seemingly most unimportant concept). He is very clear though in his teaching and what he expects from you. Overall, he is an excellent teacher charged with delivering an overwhelming amount of material in no time
Hardest class, hardest professor, worst semester of your life. Seriously, just say no.

I hated this guy. I went to office hours confused and he told me to go borrow the lecture recordings from someone. He refused to explain what I didn't understand, and instead blamed me for not understanding it in the first place. The book helps with pre-lecture questions online, but most of the exam material is from lectures. Class is crazy hard.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Loves to joke around and is EXTREMELY clear and helpful. His exams are DETAILED but FAIR. He loves biology and is very interested in making sure all his students do well. He will answer every question in detail but in a way that you'll understand it. The class is a lot of work but you'll learn a lot.

Great professor and lecturer. I absolutely hated biology prior to this class, and after, I almost reconsidered becoming a MCB major. He is very helpful during his office hours, and enjoys and takes interest in helping students that come asking questions.
Great lecturer. Be prepared to put in the work, and you'll get a decent grade. Make sure you attend lectures and try your best on the online quizzes!
AWESOME!

The BEST professor I ever had. He's a really good lecturer, maybe is because he's also a theater actor. He's helpful and clear. Don't miss any lecture, because he says important stuff that are not on the notes but will be on the exam.
Great Professor. Just be prepared to put in the work, and you'll do fine. Make sure you attend lectures and don't miss an online quiz!

He is a great lecturer, but you better know how to pay attention because he talks fast. 50 minutes will fly if you can follow (or will drag if you can't). The book is helpful if you didn't understand something in lecture, but the lectures are really where you do most of the learning especially for exams. I would take a class with him again any day.

Here's what to do to get an A: record lectures and just pay attention on the professor during lecture, take notes a day or two after the lecture listening to the recording, and start memorising the notes about 10 days in advance of the tests. Skim the book readings the week before and of the test. Exams aren't that bad if you study enough.

MCB with Mehrtens its not easy. The exams are pretty much what he says and what he says does not pop up on exams. Reading the book will help you understand things more but dont expect to find any questions related to the book on exams. He is a good professor though but having to teach a class of like 600 students its not gonna work out very well.

Talks faster than I though imaginable and when asked what is important in the class he claimed "Anything that comes out of my mouth" It is impossible to keep up with him. His tests are not on the same level as his lectures or the reading material. The discussion section is useless, completely unrelated to anything you learn in lecture.

Brad was a great professor.  You can tell he really cares about his students and would help each and every one of them if he had the time.  His exams and homework problems can be a little wordy so look out.  He is very clear during lecture and I really enjoyed the class.

Prof Mehrtens is a great teacher. Very approachable and willing to help. Tests are challenging and your grade depends on how much work you put into it. The class is very interesting and I def learned a lot.
He is a great teacher and extremely helpful. Very challenging tests. The grade you get depends on the amount of work you put into it.  But go to lecture and always review them!
good afternoon to you all. welcome to mcb150.
quality of teaching: 10/10. personality: 10/10. amount of pure eye-blinding awesomeness: 10/10. Seriously, why is he so awesome?

Class was difficult as hell, but Prof Mehrtens is one hell of a great teacher. I did terrible on my first test, then boosted up and aced the final 3 (inc the final). As a bio major, he is one of my fav teachers and I still keep in contact with him

He is a great teacher and is definitely knowledgeable in the topic. His tests go into very great detail but it motivates you to study and attend the lectures. Overall, I learned a lot in this class. The class is curved so even though it takes a lot of work it's not too hard to receive a reasonable grade.
what can i say...he deserves a nobel prize for excellent teaching...thought this doesn't mean his class is easy
Merhtens is an extremely interesting guy and he makes the class fun. If you pay attention and study hard you can get an A in his class.

He is very clear in explaining things. Having an AP Bio background immensely helps but even if you didn't take a good bio class in high school, you will do fine if you go to all of the lectures and pay attention.
One of the best teachers I had in college. More helpful and clear by far than any I've seen. He really loves teaching, and you can tell. Ask him anything, don't be shy, but always follow his rules!

He is a great professor! This is UIUC so the material is hard. His tests are hard and very specific, but he warns you of that way ahead of time. Be prepared to study, and go to OH's all the time. He is super helpful and can explain in more detail there. He loves his job and that comes through in his teaching. Overall a GREAT teacher!

Best biology teacher ever. Crystal clear lectures and challenging materials. This is UIUC, and you're taking a general biology course that is more advanced than those offered by most other schools out there.

You will be doing homework every single day, and it is almost always extremely difficult to find/figure the answer. His exams are the most difficult of any course I have ever taken at the university level, with each question and answer being overly verbose and over-complicated. He is very knowledgeable but that doesn't help you as a student.

He was a great professor. He was helpful and communicated all of his ideas really well. However, his tests were really hard so be prepared to study a lot. I would recommend studying as you learn the material. If you go to lectures, ask for help, and study hard, you will do well in the class.

He is a good teacher and very organized, too. You have to study the material regularly; if you study last minute before a test, you will fail. At times he rushes to get the material in, but that's cause there's so much info. packed into 50 minutes. Only take this class if you're willing to pay attention and actually study.

Please disregard all negative opinions of this professor. HE IS AMAZING. I enjoyed going to class each and everyday. He made learning Biology that much more fun, and was very engaged in and out of class. Make sure to go to OH's from the very beginning of the semester, you want this man to know you personally. Hard exams,so study 2 WEEKS ahead.
Fun, enthusiastic about teaching and very live. He does talk extremely fast so its always a good thing to bring your recorder to class. Overall the best professor I've ever had.

Brad Mehrtens is a pompous professor that enjoys hearing his own voice. He talks quickly and packs a lot of information into 50 minutes. He expects his students to almost read his mind to do well. His exams are only designed to be deliberately misleading and unnecessarily difficult. Exams are not representative of knowledge gained in lecture.

Mehrtens is an amazing professor. I had covered everything in my biology classes in high school so it was really a review for me. He did such a good job explaining everything, and was very clear about what he expected out of students. Go to class and study your notes. There is no reason to do poorly in this class.

A terrible class through and through. One of those unfortunate professors who love listening to their voice, he lectures without caring much to make any sense. I know it is a large class and the university is going through tough times, but I do wish we had an alternative to him for MCB 150. That would perhaps compel him to get his act together.

Absolutely wonderful professor.  He knows what he is talking about and he LOVES it as well, which makes lectures that much more interesting.  I honestly have never had a professor that I have learned more from and respected as much as I do Brad Mehrtens.

I like Prof Mehrtens, but he talks very fast, and expects you to know more than what the average person actually does. If you are really smart/really like biology, you'll do okay, but if you aren't a biology whiz or haven't had biology in awhile, the course is very difficult, I hated it, I dropped it after I got F's on the first two tests...oops

He is an excellent lecturer. He has to cover all of the material so he obviously moves at a very quick pace. If you want to get an A in his class this is what you do. 1. Record all of the lectures. Go over these lectures the week before the exam so its fresh in your mind. 2. Go to OH the week before exams. 3. Skim over all of the special feature se
Make sure to attend office hours if you are unclear about something, its extremely  helpful and he will answer any questions. Also make sure to do the textbook readings.

Professor Mehrtens expects a lot out of his students, and his tough exams definitely reflect that. Many of the questions are vague, and some are intentionally misleading. I found lectures to be monotonous, with lots of material packed into the full 50 minutes. Overall though, you'll get out what you put into the class. As are definitely attainable.

He's a very good lecturer and gets his points across.  (He does have a theatre background.) He clearly loves what he does.  He does write tricky exams, however.  I found attendance to be necessary, since a lot of things on the test are words that come out of his mouth, and not written on the slides.

One of my favorite lecturers during college. (Besides Physics 101) Definitely a high-quality professor.  Knows his stuff.  Organized and easy to follow. A voice recorder is a must for many different classes, so I would just get 1 right away.  Definitely a great intro class to the MCB major!

Mehrtens is really a jerk. He makes the class a thousand times harder than it needs to be; test questions are worded badly and he asks about very minute details. He is very arrogant (yes, he knows his material well, but he will always make sure you know about how intelligent he is...) Overall, I guess this class can be summed up as a premed weedout

"Happy Monday Everyone!" Bradley G Mehrtens is my favorite professor.  The class is challenging but just like any other MCB class, if you put forth the time and effort it is relatively painless.  He is very animated and keeps class interesting. This is probably the only class that I can honestly say I consistently attended all semester.
Good

The concensus amongst my group of friends was that his class is really bad and not just because he makes papers that are so hard. Early on he said' this is not a class in which you will be molly cuddled' and he took it to the extreme. He is difficult to deal with and the  most high headed/rude teacher I have come so far. What a waste of time.

Mehrtens comes off as cocky sometimes, but he knows his stuff. His class is difficult. I would recommend coming to every lecture and possibly purchasing a recorder because he talks so fast. His tests are tricky and difficult. This is a class you will find yourself dedicating most of your time to, so some advice- don't take it if you don't need it.

Maybe because he is NOT a PhD, there is still unease about his teaching despite him being at the helm for 7 years. All semester long, a course coordinator & a dept. head sat in front, watching his every moove. Bradley was nervous around them and avoided the side where they sat.. Overall, not the best teacher out there. Not even close.

This was a difficult, challenging class. Mehrtens, however, is a great professor. He has sort of a celebrity air about him; I felt that I was being taught by a consummate expert. His vocal inflections convey enthusiasm and remind me of Wayne Newton. Exams are quite hard because you must do more than memorize content--you must APPLY that knowledge.

A great professor.  His class is difficult, but he explains concepts really well and makes himself very available for students.  He really knows his stuff.  His exams are pretty hard because they really test your understanding.  You CAN'T cram for his exams.  Memorization will not work

The class IS difficult, but if you put in the word and actually learn the material it's not terrible. He is a great lecturer! You have to record the lectures or find a recording to catch everything. Re-listen to the lectures for the tests.

Very animated and enthusiastic. If someone knows about the subject, its him. However, sometime a little scary to approach, but very willing to help most of the time. DEFINATLY go to his office hours and get to know him!

He is AMAZING! One of the best lecturers I've ever met. Clearly knows what he's talking about. It's not a very easy class, but you really get to learn stuff after the lecture. He does talk fast, I recommend you to buy one of those voice recorders, they are really handy to get you through this class. AWESOME CLASS.
Very good teacher, one of the best lecturers I've ever had and a great resource to students that need help or just want to talk.

He was great.  The class isn't easy, but he knows what he's talking about and speaks very well.  He talks fast, though, so be prepared to write frantically.  In my opinion, lectures are essential as anything he says in class (a lot of which is not written on the powerpoints) could be on the tests.
He is a very knowledgeable person, and a great public speaker. However, his questions are rarely clear. Also, he expects you to know something just because "it was mentioned in class".

AMAZING TEACHER! He's very clear and you know EXACTLY what he expects you to know on the exams. Although he does not curve, his grading scale is ridiculously generous where a B is an A. AMAZING!  He is definately one of my favorite lecturers ever.  True he can seem like a bit of a jerk sometimes but that is only cuz he wants you to think about the material. Mehrtens is a pro at teaching. Sure the class may be hard, but if you are willing to put in the effort, I guarantee it will pay off.

Brad is a very articulate and really knows his stuff.  The class isn't too bad if you keep up with it.  Make sure not to slack on pre/post lectures; I recommend doing them right after class. Class is tough, but if you go over lectures after every class and review new information regularly and study about a week in advance for exams, you should get an A...Good luck.

One of the worst professor ever, in fact, he shouldn't even be a professor because he is unwilling to help and he has an attitude.  He is xtremely rude and he doesn't respect or care about his student! Hated his class!!!
One of my favorite professors!  Mehrtens is clear and explains the criteria well.  Very helpful at office hours.  A recorder is a must because he is a fast talker.

Excellent teacher!!  Extremely clear and concise.  Tests can be tricky but as long as you know all of the lecture material it will be fine :)
He's a tricky little man, with tricky tests. But he gives all the answers to his questions in lectures. Sounds easy but he talks extra fast. Recommended to get a recorder.
great teacher
He's a good professor. Talks fast, a little ridiculous with the exam questions for even the most studious... But overall, not bad.
The required text book has only a little to study from. The supplemental books were more helpful for exams.
Review your lectures 100 percent because your 100 percents on your tests are based on the lectures. buy a recorder and focus on lectures, then I will guarantee at least A

this was my hardest class freshman year, but dr. mehrtens was very helpful. he gets straight to the point, and tries to be extremely clear and meticulous in his lectures and notes. his tests are hard, you have to really study. go to his office hours for help.

Great professor, tough class. Make sure you go to lecture. Recording lectures and listening to them again is very helpful. Helpful during office hours, answers any question, very patient. Very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the subject. He provides quite a few helpful study resources on the website. Really tough class, but if you pay attention in lecture and put in the study effort, you'll do fine.
very challenging class. prof is extremely intelligent and he could answer any question you could ever have. dont fall asleep in lecture. read the textbook, it helps.

he's a pretty good teacher. class was easy too, just have to take intense notes and really understand them. i usually started studying about 3 days before the test and aced all of them. so work hard, and you will be just fine.

He's extremely clear and precise, but his tests are ridiculously difficult. Though class is not mandatory, you pretty much have to be there in order to get a good grade because he adds a lot of information that aren't in the notes but are on the test.

This is a challenging course, but Mehrtens tries to make everything clear. He has a very orgainzed way of presenting his lectures. He always tries to help out. He is also a really good advisor. It really helps to tape record his lecture so that you dont miss anything he says because pretty much anything he says is fair game for the tests.

Brad has the voice of a goddess. It's soothing, and worth going even just once to hear how well he speaks. Honestly, unlike most teachers at U of I, you will not have a problem understanding any word that comes out of his mouth. He's very nice, and willing to help anyone who asks. Enthusiastic Professor!  Really wants to come and teach in lecture.  Tests are really hard, but go to office hours and talk to Prof. Merhtens.  He is really nice and willing to help out!
good teacher. easy class. easy A/ A-

150 is a challenging course, but Mehrtens is an excellent instructor who does extremely well presenting the material clearly, keeping the class up to date on what is expected of us, and he is always friendly and generally enthusiastic about the class.
HARDEST CLASS at UIUC. DONT take it if u dont have to!!! it screwed up my gpa so much i got a D in the class and it made me hate biology forever!!!
lecures go over alot of stuff to remember, seems simple but the tests are very tricky. Need to figure out how he thinks then the tests get easier. Do the practice exams.
DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU DON'T HAVE TO!! HARDEST CLASS OF MY LIFE. TESTS ARE SOOO CONFUSING AND NOTHING LIKE THE PRACTICE EXAMS!!! I THINK I'M GUNNA FAIL!!

awesome

Easy "A" Class

He is an amazing teacher...I would say my favorite. He never hesitates to help! Great Guy! :)

very hard /tricky tests. study and go to lecture!

Haha.. He's really funny and is a great speaker who lectures clearly and knows what he's talking about. Make sure to take notes, and re-read the powerpoint slides before a test, and you should be fine.

One of the best biology teachers I have had. He lectures really well, and he is extremely helpful and organized. Tests are hard but they represent class material.

PLEASE TAKE Donovan. He is the best tbh just make sure you go to lecture for in class assingments

Professor Sanchez truly cares about his students. He is consistently available to talk to outside of class. Additionally, he makes a genuine effort to get to know his students. reviews.comment: Professor Sanchez is amazing! He is knowledgeable, deeply caring, and has a contagious outlook on life. Professor Sanchez provides students with relevant advice and helps you build an explicit plan, enabling you to feel confident and enthusiastic about your financial future. Take this class your senior year, you will not regret it!

This class was very straight forward. All quizzes and the exam were open note/open internet. There were two midterm projects and a cumulative multiple-choice final. Attendance was based off a weekly pop quiz that you would not know which day he would have it. Great speaker, and clearly loves his job. I wish he had more classes I could take!

Prof. Sanchez is an amazing teacher! He puts a lot of work into his course and is the most caring person that I've met at UIUC. He genuinely cares about his students.

It was a hard class, but he always gave great feedback and made it clear how to succeed in his class. If you can, take a class from Donovan Sanchez; you'll be better for it!

Honestly one of the best classes I've taken. Teaches real finance + how to actually analyze the news and what it means for markets.  not just textbook stuff — lots of real-time analysis of actual world events and what they mean for markets.

Professor Lariviere is deeply knowledgeable in the field of HFT and it's easy to see that from his lectures. He's also very easy to contact whether that's for general questions, final project guidance or anything else. The class is mostly graded on a final project that is completed in a group.

The project based structure of the class really puts the onus on you to build something interesting, and the grade for this class is almost entirely based on your project performance. The professor is always available to help out and connect you to the right person whether it be another group or someone in the industry, which I found very helpful.

IE 421 was a great learning experience. Professor Lariviere really fosters a culture of interactive learning and thinking at a very deep level. He is also extremely accessible and is always willing to clarify any doubts and questions. Most importantly, what is taught is directly applicable to real-world scenarios.

The structure is looser than most others (1 lecture a week, 1 semester-long project, 1 test. That's essentially your entire grade) and there are plenty of resources at your disposal (access to SOTA hardware, compute, a professor extensive industry experience), so you the value you gain is dependent on how engaged you are with the course.

Although the course is lecture heavy, the professor makes an active effort to engage with students in lecture, especially during the "In The News" segment which is where the professor goes over world events that affect the financial markets. He is easy to get in contact with outside of class and HW is fairly easy to complete.

I liked the concepts in this class and the lectures were  cool. But the David is unorganized and he only gave us one month to finish a final project that was supposed to last a semester. I don't think you should take this class if you value

Terrible Class. Dont' take. The professor was truly unorganized and all he did was spam us on discord with message after message giving us "tips to find a job". I'm surprised by all the positive comments, don't trust them. He also didn't give any justification for the final project grade, was lazy with it. how he got this job is beyond me.

The “In the News” section keeps you current with global events. Lectures build essential financial literacy. The professor focuses on applied skills over book content. Homework is easy if you follow class material, and exams are manageable with proper attention in lectures.

Poorly taught. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. 
Prof gpts everything. Final was a gpted 150 (!!) mcq test. the TAs (also USELESS) thought it was ridiculous. 
The lectures are 3 hours long and unprepared. He spends half the time talking about himself and random things that will "get you hired". 
I learned nothing. wish I had read an HFT book instead.

- very engaging lectures with great insight into how HFT firms work 
- learnt a lot about financial markets and how they behave with different ongoing events 
- relevant and impactful group projects to work on

The BEST professor I've ever had! Whether you're already familiar with financial markets or completely new to finance, you'll learn a great deal. Each class begins with a discussion of recent economic events and teaches you how to think like a financial engineer. I have no doubt that I've grown tremendously through this course.

His lectures cover both finance-related news and financial engineering related materials. He's extremely knowledgeable and explains very clearly. Truly useful information and isn't even hard if you pay attention! Class is project-based. He cares a lot about his students and their project, and is willing to help anytime, so it's not too challenging.

Absolutely loved the course, learned incredibly relevant things (how orders are processed by different exchanges, levels of market data different exchanges offer, and the true challenges HFT firms are competing around (not so much the 'smartest algorithms' as I'd previously thought). Professor is incredibly involved with students.

Absolutely amazing professor. This is not your average class with a set syllabus but the markets define what you learn on a daily basis.
This class helps in learning a new skill - reading the markets.
Extremely helpful with career advice. Very easy to reach out to, outside of class.
I would take his class again without a doubt. Crazy experience.

Prof Lariviere is awesome! His experience straddles industry and academia so he is able to bridge that gap. His "in the news" section is v unique and keeps students aware of industry developments and teaches them how to analyze news pieces. Class is project-based and Prof Lariviere mentors each group so it is an amazing learning experience!

I had Professor Lariviere for FIN556, his teaching style is different to other professors, but I learned way more than I would have expected and he was really approachable at any point. He was clear with what he wanted and how he wanted it, loved the class gave me so much knowledge into a new industry.

Prof is one of the best in his ability to explain in a digestible manner. When he is present, he is truly helpful. However, he lacked prioritization for the class. He only allotted 1-2 weeks for what was supposed to be a semester long high frequency trading project, which was why most people chose the class. Class is also graded very arbitrarily.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Lariviere is very knowledgeable about the low latency trading industry and he is always available to teach students about the nuances of this industry. I can say this with confidence having take his courses in Fall 23, Spring 24 and Fall 24. The class structure is also relatively flexible. I would definitely take another course with him.

The Professor is very Knowledgeable about low latency trading industry and wants to impart that knowledge to students. I can say that with confidence as i have taken 3 course under him each for Fall 23, Spring 24 and Fall 24. The class structure is also relatively flexible for ease of students. I would definitely take another course with him again.

Class is comparable to an internship. You get to work with the latest tech on some really fascinating projects that employers are extremely interested in. Lectures are very insightful. My only issue with the course was the lack of organization, but it's understandable considering how much work the professor has outside of lecture hours.
Only one lecture a week but lectures are 3h each and fairly unprepared. Poor lecture quality, would not recommend.

I took this class a year ago, and so much of the stuff that we learned still comes up in my every day work and classes. Professor Lariviere gives you a lot of information so that you understand how each part of High Frequency Trading works, and then based on your interest, you are able to dive deep into one specific area with the group project.
I took IE 421 (HFT) with high expectations; turned out to be an absolute disappointment. It is moderately easy to score in the course, but I personally did not get what I wanted out of it.

I took IE 421 at UIUC two years ago and had a GREAT experience. The course requires focus but isn't overwhelming if you're passionate about quant finance. The professor provides insights beyond textbooks and is very friendly and helpful.

Learned lots of important skills such as Bloomberg Terminal, core HFT industry-standard technologies, ML for Finance, and he taught us what we need to know in order to get jobs. He was super accessible outside of class and responded to all of our questions with super in depth answers. Some ppl in our class actually got finance jobs due to the class
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

Professors lectures involved using the Bloomberg terminal a lot and had an In-the news section which was thoroughly enjoyable and applicable to the real world unlike most other courses which are very theoretical and exam heavy, after which you forget all the material that was taught. Very useful if you have little to no knowledge in finance.

reviews.comment: Great course in risks! All topics can be applied to real life. Instructor is always well prepared and professional.

first off this is for CLCV 220 but it wasn't an option above idk why. the prof is really nice, caring, and can hold convos on anything even out of class. lectures were rlly chill and ppl get really engaged, but u don't need to pay attention or anything bcuz the graded assignments r basically completely separate from lectures. it's just attendance.

This class is poorly designed, which she's trying to fix. One lecture/week is not enough for so much content. Assignment directions are vague and often just wrong. reviews.comment: Special relativity is a very technical discipline. Unfortunately, Professor Koptieva maybe made it through 2-3 coherent English sentences per lecture. She has no command of the classroom and is not fit to teach relativity. Prepare to not understand anything; all learning is outside of lecture.  I'm very disappointed in the PHYS 225 course at UIUC.

Prof. Koptieva isn't a bad professor but I hated the class. The lectures were really the only good thing about it. Homeworks were really long and not related to what was on the tests. The midterm wasn't bad but the final threw me off because they mislead us a little on what we needed to study. Grading isn't ridiculous but get points where you can.

Avoid her at all costs. Lectures are useless - the only thing I've gained out of them all semester is a bunch of formulas with no explanation of their use. And her exams test things that aren't covered in any of the material we're given or the supplemental reading. If you're planning on majoring in physics and she's teaching 225, don't.

The course was designed to help you succeed. The material was well explained, and a point was made in the lectures to help you understand the concept for homework, discussion, and the exams. The professor tried to build a personal relationship with the students despite the big class size. Tough but fair grading because of the challenging material.

She's nice and she is knowledgeable about what she teaches, but she moved here from Ukraine recently and speaks accented/occasionally broken English. Does not understand students' questions sometimes due to language barrier, and the class structure is questionable. At least tests are only 50%, but she expects a mathematical maturity past what students have. Tests are purely on relativity, but that is only about half of the course content, so unsure why we learn about groups, index notation etc.
Hard course and barely no curve or extra credit
The class is so hard to follow and the exams are pretty tough
Lost in his own world. He doesn't care that no one follows what he's talking about.

Throws in new terminology, notations, concepts in one sentence without explaining what they mean. At best this is a refresher if you already know tensors and manifolds. If you don't, his lectures will be annoying.

I completed the Math 416 course through UIUC's NetMath program where the lecture videos were from Professor Kerman's Fall 2016 Math 416 section. Sometimes seems nervous in class.  Has trouble understanding students' questions, and therefore answering them.  Test questions more difficult than information covered in class.  But, if you do all homework and pay attention, you can do well in the class.

I slacked more than I should have, but even so, I had no idea what would appear on the first test (and bombed it).  The rest of the tests were reasonable.  Class was really boring though; I had trouble staying awake often (my eye lids were literally significantly heavier once he started talking).

I don't see why other reviews complain a lot. He is willing to understand student's situation and his grades are fair. Exams are not by the book but if you do what you are supposed to, you will do fine.

I had him as well for Calc 231 but I dont see the problem. I liked him a lot. He was the right level excited. He was very competent, hence the PhD in Mathematics, he was nice to answer any questions, neat and organized and fair. He wasn't amazing neither was he awful. Tests were fair. Just do the suggested problems and you'll be good.

Calc 231 was definitely a challenging course.  Had an A in Calc 221 and I super-aced my first exam in Calc 231, but things kinda went downhill from there. The homework was always much easier than the exams (except for the first one). Kerman isn't the best lecturer; he just copies his notes on the board and repeats it. My T.A did a better job.

Ely was the worst professor I have ever had in my life. His incompetence and lack of grasp on general social skills made him impossible to follow and his lectures overall useless. He's a lot easier than other Calc 2 teachers I've heard of, I strongly recommend him. His tests are definitely ace-able, as long as you know the information.

Prof. Excell treated the class with immense rudeness and didn't seem to care whatsoever about any question a student may have, especially regarding an assignment worth a substantial portion of the grade. Students were left out to dry, with just sub-par modeling videos to watch as a "guide" for the financial model. Would not take again.

Excell deterred me from not only the academies but finance as a whole. Class is unstructured and has hours worth of videos and model building. He was always in a bad mood, rude, and sometimes yelled at the auditorium for things we didn't do. Made a class that was focused on building skills and helping with academy recruitment into something more complicated than a class for a major. Prof. Excell is one of the best professors and teachers I've ever had. He brings decades of industry experience and a genuine passion for teaching and helping Illinois students. This professor is terrible at lecturing. His slides are full of words and he just reads from them without actually spending time to make students understand the material. You will always get lost in his lectures. Please avoid him!

Terrible professor, doesn't teach at all and doesn't care about the students. Entire class is just him reading straight from the slides without explaining anything. This prof is horrible. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE avoid him

looked at prof solomon's slides from previous semesters instead of evan's useless lectures. loved the extra credit, hated that labs and mps were due so close together (sunday vs monday), exams were okay

pretty easy due to a lot of extra credit but a fair bit of work

A great professor for CS 225, did his best in Fall 2020 to keep things going smoothly at all times. A lot of people complained about office hours and other things that were hard for him to control, if you look past that he seemed like a really great guy and professor!

I have to admit that this class sucked. The lectures didn't make sense and that there was so much work. Office hours is a hit and miss at times. Horrible- unnecessary discrepancies between local tests and online ones in POTDs. Quizzes are like all or nothing. Disorganized. Nightmare professor overall.

Had Evans for CS173 and got an A but was really hoping not to have him again, hes unhelpful and kind of a jerk. Had him for CS225... Again, got an A because I taught myself everything, didnt go to a single lecture because I knew from 173 how terrible a professor he is.

Pretty dreadful lecturer honestly, fortunately, the notes posted online are decent enough to help you through the labs and MPs if you're willing to put in the work to understand it. As with many CS classes, stackoverflow may be your best friend for this class

CS225 is the ultimate easy A. And the contents have been taught really well.

Absolutely horrible. Had him for 126 but now stuck with him in 225. Don't bother attending his lectures, because he has zero teaching ability. I would like a refund on my tuition...
Average lectures, although sometimes on interesting topics. Knows his stuff, doesn't teach it very well.

He misspelled the words "peppermint" and "lettuce" live in front of us and that's when I knew that I was in for a treat that semester. The class itself isn't difficult though.

His lectures are fairly detailed and he's good at explaining confusing topics. The work load is extremely heavy in this course, with weekly projects ranging from 5 to 15 hours a week. The rubric for projects are not often explained well.

Even though I haven't taken too many CS classes in UIUC, I believe that he is the single worst professor I'll meet. His lectures are boring, full of professional vocabs, no intention to explain things the easy way. His rubric is vague, but the TA can just take off points whenever they want. Homework load is HUGE. Expect at least 10 hours a week.
Memorize Angrave's wiki and get an "A"

reviews.comment: I think Evans is a pretty new professor, and was teaching a course that changes a lot. Still, I think he did a great job teaching the course: his lectures were mostly clear and useful; he was funny, but not to the point that it detracted from his lecturing; and he made a HARD course interesting and doable. I HIGHLY suggest ATTENDING his lectures.

The WORST lectures I've seen from a professor at UIUC. Slides are blocks of text with changing fonts, and stock pastes of the entire mechanisms even when explaining specifics. We were just told to memorize everything and his review sessions were worthless. I learned from reading the slides myself then his ramblings. Learning from him is a mistake

These were the WORST lectures I have ever seen from any professor at UIUC. They are all blocks of text, with font size changing every slide and pasted entire mechanisms on each slide even when explaining specifics. Exams we are just told to memorize everything, and his final review session was worthless. Trying to learn from him is a mistake

I think his reputation is bad because he teaches the more difficult part of MCB 450, compared to the prof that teaches the 1st part of the course. His explanations are actually not bad, and he seems like a chill guy. The stuff he teaches is just tough.

Haven't even finished the course yet, but his portion of the course has been the worst class I've ever had. Lectures are packed with material, and he expects you to know all of it for exams. Exam questions are multiple choice, but all answer choices are extremely similar, which makes it hard to do well unless you know everything perfectly.
extremely terrible, unable to deliver knowledge clearly, unable to make normal powerpoint that have proper text size.

Dr. Fratti seemed like a kind professor and spoke slowly during lecture, which made taking notes easier. However, the content was 100x harder than with Cheng due to the intense mechanisms. I wish the details of lectures were reduced, but I did enjoy the fun video links and FYI that were included in the slides.

Pretty solid professor imo. Explains everything very well. Exams were fair. You'll need to devote a LOT of time towards watching the prerecorded ( & reused) lectures. Wish there were more practice questions/exams, esp since there's no discussion section in the course.
Rudy's lectures are uninteresting, need someone with energy for this class (biochem).
Not much different from the other comments written before. Additionally, all answer choices on exams are almost identical to one another which makes it unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You better hope you did well with Chen. Fratti is unclear, doesn't really help you during office hours, and his tests are crazy difficult. Get ready to memorize each and every slide, because he'll pull questions from literally ANYTHING.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took biochem online. So far, it is an example to how lazy a teacher can be. All lecture videos are recorded last semester so there is zero interaction and assignments are recycled from last semester as well. They do nothing to reach out and have students interact. The only way to pass is by sitting alone doing flash cards over and over
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Here bc I got my cheeks clapped on an exam. Dont take him and if you have no choice do well on the other half of the sem where the profs switch off bc this one will ruin you. Tests are a free for all and the book wont help either bc he pulls questions out of his ass so basically good luck to all of yall and keep a therapist on standby.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hes the worst professor I have ever had at my time in the university. Never explains things thoroughly, and when tests come, he always puts questions that were talked about disproportionately to how much they appear on the test. Avoid taking biochem with him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very confusing professor. Uploads exam review only to have found that nearly half of the review was not tested on the exam. Avoid taking Biochem with this professor at all costs. Averages were good at about 70% and then got my cheeks clapped by the final exam where it was a 50% average.
Seems like he's a really nice person. As for being a good professor? Based on this course, not so much....

Reads off the slides word for word and is surprised when the next slide comes up. No practice exams or any helpful tips for exams. He makes a review powerpoint with all the slides copied from lectures. Don't know what to expect for exams at all. Do not take mcb 354 with him if you want to have a fair professor.

Doesnt seem prepared before lecture, really just reads off of the slides without adding any additional content. Is confusing when you ask questions about exam content, and spends too much time focusing on certain mechanisms and then doesnt put them on the exam. If possible, take this course with a different professor teaching the 2nd half.

I think the material itself did not interest me, a lot of tedious math. The professor was not bad and cared about the students. Was curved. Multiple textbooks were often confusing; however, the lectures were useful. Only 6 practice sets were nice, although they were long. If I had an interest in CMP this class likely would have been more enjoyable.

Really good guy and good teacher. Lectures for the most part were clear. I feel most of the problems I had with the course were because of the Physics department, and not him, including allowing me to attend a family event and makeup and exam when the department would not let me.
best professor ive ever had

Professor Mahmood is one of the best professors I've had thus far. He teaches well but still manages to liven things up in lecture. The SmartPhysics platform is great and taught me so much more than I learned in high school. Labs and discussions get to be a bit much but the workload is more than reasonable for the four credits the class offers.
Way better than the other female professor. Actually cares about what he teaches and is great at coming up with analogies to explain concepts.
He teaches rly rly well.

Mahmood makes the most of the terrible structure of the PHYS 21x classes. His lectures are always interesting and most importantly, he never skips steps, speeds through explanations, or assumes you know things you don't, which is not true of most professors that teach 21x classes. He goes through everything slowly and thoroughly

Really nice guy. Physics 212 is a challenging class in general, especially for STEM majors who are not as interested in really theoretical electricity and magnetism topics. However, Fahad is a great guy and his lectures are pretty good. Highly recommend taking this class with him.

This class is difficult, and the homeworks are tough, but Professor Mahmood makes the material entertaining. He makes himself available for many extra office hours to help with homeworks and exams too. Professor Mahmood brings an experimentalist's perspective to the subject as well, which I appreciated. Overall, a great experience.

Go to office hours! Professor Mahmood has a great sense of humor and cares a lot about the success of his students. The material is challenging but highly rewarding. The course relates the material to active research with cleverly written checkpoints and homework questions. Overall 10/10 would take again, essential to my development in cond. mat.

Prof. Mahmood's lectures were very clear and engaging and he answered questions very well. His way of explaining and reasoning through E&M concepts was always very intuitive and this trait definitely sticks onto you to help you approach homework and exam problems if you pay attention in lecture. 12/10 teacher!
I really did not enjoy PHYS 212 material all that much, but this professor made it worth it! He was pretty great in lecture, went over things well and is extremely smart. Overall, amazing professor!

Although I took E&M in high school, his lectures were very clear and helped me to understand the material much better than I did in high school. Not to mention, if PHYS 212 is still online, he actively reads the chat to check for and answer questions before moving on. I was so surprised when he said it was his first time teaching this semester!
Good

Super funny and chill professor who just wants to help you get through the class. He brings up interesting points in each lecture and tries to make things as easy as possible. The classes required readings but they weren't too bad.

Dr. Fogelman is a genuinely caring professor that does a great job teaching global studies. He's kind, flexible, and makes the content engaging. It's clear that he cares immensely about what he does. More professors should be like him.

Class was always fun and he let students give lots of input during lectures. Grading on essays was kind of tough but thought provoking. Great during office hours and was always around to help or just talk.
The class is super interesting. He's authentic and will give things to you straight. He's funny and also kind of a dork, but he loves his job and is passionate about the things he talks about.

Any class by Charles is a good time. He is funny, flexible, and enjoys connecting with students. He doesn't teach anything in either of my majors but I still try to take his classes. If you are looking for a class to take off the pressure of studying during a global pandemic this is your easy A. Makes zoom classes enjoyable and no breakout rooms!

If you want to learn a whole lot of something while feeling like you've learnt a whole lot of nothing you've come to the right class. Fogelman's lectures are unparalleled at UIUC. From the dramatic readings of the White Man's Burden to the riveting hand flailing Fogelman will keep you at the edge of your seat every class. Takes long bathroom breaks
Charles is a great professor, but most importantly, he's worth 60 camels and 5 cows! Those stats could be better but that's alright because the quizzes are ageist

Charles is a really amazing professor that genuinely loves what he does and is extremely knowledgeable in his area. He does assign a good bit of reading but a quick skim will get the job done. He is super understanding and always willing to find time to talk
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Really nice guy who genuinely cares and wants to see you succeed. Super engaging and always tries to make class fun. Also love him as an advisor!!

Charles was by far the best prof I had this semester. The class is a lot of work- quiz and discussion post every week, three 750 word papers- but it's also a double gen ed. He makes even the most boring content interesting just because he's an engaging teacher and just a funny guy. Really open to feedback as well. Definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Charles is definitely one of the real gems of this university. Whether it be the feedback he gives or the compassion and genuine interest that he shows during his lectures, Charles definitely is a professor that everyone should have. Take his class seriously and you will definitely get something out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This is the best educator I have ever had in my entire life. He is down to Earth, funny, and really cares about the content and how it comes across to the students. He will work with you if you have any problems and the coursework is always reasonable. This is my third class with Charles and if you are thinking of taking a class with him, DO IT!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Charles is great! He's a nice guy and he talks a lot about going to Lesotho. He has an really high vocabulary for someone as chill as he is. Shows us pictures of his kids, who are adorable. Clearly loves what he does and cares about his students. Can't recommend him enough!
Great professor! Very energetic and helps you with all assignments. Even if you submit late he will only take a few points off. Online quizzes can be annoying but overall great class and professor
Very harsh grader compared to other professors. A lot of hidden requirements for speeches he wants to get a full score on certain categories. Too harsh for a communications beginner class.

He was the best professor I have ever had. He makes learning fun again. I had him last year, and I wish I could have him again! I see people from the class he taught all the time, and we never fail to bring up how badly we miss taking his class.

This class was not hard at all. As long as you follow the rubric for each speech you're guaranteed an A. I am definitely not the best at public speaking but was still able to do really well. Truthfully, if you believe that he is a tough grader you are not following the criteria that he hands to you... also he is very nice!
Not a cool guy.

This professor TRIES to be funny, but harsh regarding grading. He's very very strict with format and is not tolerant. Took this non-native class, and he was strict with international students. Class is organized, but I feel like he's not the best at teaching, and we rarely did speaking activities compared to other classes. But gives a lot of info.

He tries to be funny and personable but his instruction and teaching technique is very poor. He doesn't really take correction or criticism well. Isn't considerate about mistakes or poor communication on his part and has a more "it is what it is" attitude when it causes a student to lose points rather than being lenient due to it being his fault.
Funny Teacher, interesting class, but his grade is as low as ****.
This dude is quite funny, but the score given is low like shit.

I just took him this past spring and I will see this. He's one of the worst teachers I've ever had because he's very very sneaky with how he grades his stuff and puts it into AI to create everything and plus he doesn't really look at the whole picture and I would never recommend him to ever teach a class.

Gary is one of the best accounting professors I've had. The course was well structured, and I felt that the more time and effort I put into learning the concepts, the more I gained from it, all while feeling fair and reasonable. Gary himself is very friendly, accessible, and open-minded, and he is always willing to take the time to help students.

This professor is good, but as you progress through the class, somethings seem off. The lectures are great, and Gary is wise. I'm someone who actually works hard, and had to do most of the projects by myself or with one other person because most people didn't want to pick up their slack. It's just a weird experience, and it annoys me to get a C+.

Professor Gary honestly is one of the best I have ever had. Throughout the course there are moments where you are like what is going on but the more effort you put in then it all comes together, plus he is actually ALWAYS available or he does his best. Only way I can see people hating is if they just don't care to learn. Professor is the best!!

I had the pleasure of being taught by an exceptional professor. His open-mindedness and emphasis on effective communication as a teaching style made the learning experience truly remarkable. The course concepts he presented were not only captivating but also provided ample opportunities for deep reflection and intellectual engagement.

One of the best teachers I've ever had. Also very funny. Makes a huge effort to make himself available outside of class. He's not just reading off slides and repeating what you can find elsewhere. It's definitely challenging - you have to work to put all the pieces together, but if you do, especially on the group projects, you will learn a ton.

Best professor I've had. The course was really interesting and prof Hecht is a very thorough teacher. Clear on expectations and gave really in depth exam prep. Only one exam, worth 32% of grade. Grading was fair and more heavily weighted on the work you do throughout the course as opposed to the final exam. But be prepared for group projects.

Gary was an awesome Prof! He is very clear on the material and is more than willing to help you outside of class as much as he can. His HW and exams were pretty straight forward. The exams can be hard since he only administers finals, but they are all on covered material. He is very understanding and is willing to work with students if needed.

Professor Hecht is very good. He gives good feedbacks on group assignments. His quiz and assignment are fair, not too difficult but closely related to the material. He respects students and is very assesible. Have a good sense of humor.

Prof.Fleck is very helpful. And her textbook make knowledge easy to understand. Also, she is really experienced and can explain knowledge in an easy way. I highly recommend her.

Examlets genuinely could be a piece of cake or the worst test you'll take at this university. It's based on your luck.
Class is 90 percent test, Professor doenst know how to teach, test depend on luck

reviews.comment: Examlets are worth a huge part of the grade, but they are pretty easy to study for with the given practice problems and past examlets. Lectures are a little helpful in solidifying material, but most of the learning comes from the textbook readings outside of class. She explains concepts in practical ways for students to understand.

Class isn't the best structured, but also not the worst. It focuses on BREADTH more than DEPTH. Quizzes are hard and test tiny details. MP's require self-learning Python.

Best advice: If you plan to take several AI-related courses (e.g. 446/447), then taking 440 first provides a good background and is useful; otherwise choose a different course.

reviews.comment: She might have been a great teacher in her prime but she lwk doesnt remember anything anymore. She constantly forgets her content even though she wrote the textbook. The 90% weightage of tests is really great!!!

Notes/videos/free textbook are great. Grade is fair but 90% tests with a few questions so easy to drop big on one mistake. Horrible lectures...seems to have forgotten her material? Spends 10 mins fighting the projector then the rest trying to remember how to solve the problem. Lots of mistakes/long pauses, says she's "demo-ing the process."
it is good
Prof Fleck is a great professor and her lecture content is amazing. It was too much of a load with an MP every week and a quiz every two weeks. Learnt lots from her lectures though.

reviews.comment: I am giving her a 5 star because she adjusted the A cutoff to 92.5%, so that I got an A. My lecturer of this course isn't even her. The course structure of this course is ridiculous, so it is not completely her fault. As a CS+ student, it is mandatory to take this course, so forget about avoiding it.

Ignore all the positive things that people say about her. After a long time of anything, you get worse at the one thing you were good at. That's exactly what happened. Apparently she used to be great, but nope. She is not the best. Close to worst.

reviews.comment: One of the best professor's I've had since entering college. The website is a labor of love, it's comprehensive, thorough, and so thoughtfully constructed, including ample study resources, clear guidelines on how to succeed in the course, words of encouragement and a wealth of information on supporting resources.
Genuinely one of the nicest and smartest professors I have ever had. Her textbook is amazing and she is extremely helpful in office hours for questions.

Get ready to read! :D

For real though, she assigns readings and recorded videos for homework for one week and only uses the lectures as an opportunity to go through examples. Do not expect to learn anything from the lectures.
