reviews.comment: His lectures were sometimes confusing if you don't read the chapters ahead of time, but he always offered to set up appointments for office hours if anyone needed help. Of course, you have to put in the work to get a good grade. His tests are reasonable as long as you study and read the questions carefully during the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've ever had. Do everything you can to make sure you do not have him if you want a good grade in chem. Tests are almost impossible and are nothing like the practice exams.

Hes very condescending when students do badly on his difficult tests, even though he admits to making them hard on purpose. Also, aftee a student said he used too many stories/metaphors in his explanations and it was confusing, he started to use even more stories.

He has a genuine desire for his students to succeed. However, the class is very difficult. The quizzes and practice exam questions do not adequately prepare you for the tests. Be prepared to do a lot of additional practice problems and reteaching yourself the concepts.

His tests are very difficult and dont match the content we learn in lecture/discussion at all. Despite students doing very poorly on his tests, he simply tells us that were not thinking hard enough, and looks down on students who do poorly. It seems that the positive reviews are from previous years, when his class was much easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Reads off slides which he copies straight from the textbook. But then he puts in useless anecdotes and train-of-thought concepts that make no sense and makes the class nonsensical. His exams are twice as hard as any homework, quiz or online assignment. Bad teaching, worse prep. Also no retakes - not close to as good or lenient as other professors.

His lectures were extremely convoluted and at sometimes seemingly philosophical. He does not explain the material on which he tests on because he expects you to understand the "story" behind the content and assumes that most of his questions can be solved using basic logic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't have anything to say
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a genuinely nice person who really cares about his students. HOWEVER, his lectures are the worst. He doesnt explain things well and I always leave lectures more confused than ever. He gives out curves, but I really had to study a lot on my own to get the grade I did. At one point I stopped taking notes because it was impossible.

Dr.G is not a great teacher. His lectures were basically useless and they never helped me in discussion. I often felt like it was my first time seeing test question on the test. His quizzes are near impossible the first time around but he does do retakes. The only reason I'm going to pass the class is bc of all the EC. If you can take Hummel do it.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very caring and wants everyone to do well but his lectures make absolutely no sense. I can't follow his train of thought and most of the time left lectures more confused than when I went in. He has a lot of office hours so use those but beware of his tests that are never even close to the review guides especially the final.

Dr. G is an easy A. If you put in the work, it will directly reflect in the grade you receive! Tons of extra credit, nearly impossible to fail. Also, significantly easier than all the other chem 102 teachers!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. G is an extremely caring fellow  he bent over backwards for his students. I do not regret taking him over Hummel. If you can  take him! Loads of wiggle room to ensure you get a good grade. This does not mean he is easy, though. Watch out for his midterms after the first one! They get tricky...

Dr. G is one of the most caring teachers I have ever had. He always puts his students first and is super nice during office hours. I will say through that his tests are quite difficult and sometimes the material on the exams is not thouroughly covered during class. Overall a solid prof. but get ready to work for the grade
Strongly recommend. Very caring about his students. Has many extra credits. Great review session before final.

Honestly one of the greatest people you can talk to. Cares about all his students even though the course itself is very difficult with a very low average GPA. Lots of people complain about the pace of the course due to it involving a lot of various topics, but honestly very manageable as long as you work hard.
Great lecturer, sometimes goes off on tangents though, tries to be fair in terms of grading, good amount of extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: terrible. impossible to understand his trains of thought in lecture, and then half the exam has nothing to do with anything that was covered in lecture or from worksheets- and you're supposed to just know it, OR occasionally mark E on the scantron if it was something he expected you to not know!

Thought i got a 12% on the 2nd exam, and he was extremely helpful.. found out 5 days later i got a 60% instead. He is very lenient extremely professional and he loves helping students. Hes very considerate of your progress in his class. Exams arent impossible, and he is very straight up about exam difficulty. Recommend him highly

Pretty cool guy but the material you end up being tested on is near impossible to fully study whether out of the book or past exams (which there are very few). He rarely curves and just taking notes from his lectures will not prepare you for the exams.

Terrible. Teaches a weed out class, but believes no one should be left behind, then has to increase the pace of the course to twice that of other classes in order to catch up. Puts material you havent learned yet on tests and expects you to answer E) Not enough information. Goes off on random tangents about how he is doing this for your benefit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I despise chemistry with all my heart but somehow Dr. G makes this class seem interesting and not too bad.
He will make sure everyone fully understand's whatever topic you guys are covering and then he moves on. Class gets a little behind at first.
Prof Goldstein really wants each of her students to succeed. The class was very informative and also fun honestly. lectures are kinda pointless and most learning is done during labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Goldstein is a truly fantastic professor who genuinely cares about their students, their well-being, and overall success within the course. SE101 is extremely time-intensive and largely based on the final group project. She is very approachable outside of class and during her Office Hours. Her LA team's Office Hours made SE101 passable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of work but she is a great professor and wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Goldstein is the best ISE professor by far. This class was designed so well and I actually enjoyed and learned so much from it. Prof. Goldstein was accessible and understanding. I wish I could take this class again.

SE101 was a lot of work and took a lot of effort, but Goldstein seemed to care more about how much effort you put in than final product. She is very understanding and great to talk to, as well as she gives great advice and direction. Her lectures are great and she provided more than enough resources to do well in the class.
She was great, very nice and explained the concepts with enthusiasm and well.

She is a good professor and her class is graded on a lot (modelling exam, 4 sketching quizzes, 2 theory tests, weekly assignments, and 35% on the group project). You learn a ton in this class but the sketching quizzes and assignments are brutal and tiny mistakes will be there difference between 40/40 and a 15/40. The group project is a lot of work.

Prof Goldstein is honestly an amazing professor. Lectures can be a bit hard to follow so I recommend looking in the textbook/doing practice outside of class to get a better understanding. The group project is really important so make sure to communicate with your group members and don't procrastinate. Also make sure to study for the midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: professor is nice but the class is ridiculous good luck getting a decent grade if your group isn't good

Goldstein is an excellent professor. She's very kind and understanding, and I would recommend getting to know both the professor and your TA. Be advised that this doesn't mean you can slack off because the class is completely dependent on the semester-long group project, which will take up a lot of your time.

Professor Goldstein is a great person, but her lectures are useless. The TAs do the majority of the teaching - they do a great job. The class itself is very work heavy if you don't have a good group that prioritizes equal workload. The sketching and modeling homework is straightforward. The modeling exam and project determines your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Graded on a ton of things, great opportunity to learn a lot. Group project can become really time consuming at the end, be ready to be in the lab a lot. Clear grading criteria and very rubric-oriented class. Overall a caring prof and class where you can learn a lot, albeit while doing a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She made what otherwise should've been a painful class pretty manageable. SE101 is just bad. You have individual midterms AND a large group project to complete. 2 labs a week. 3 credit hour class btw. Goldstein and her TAs/LAs are what make the class manageable. Just hope and pray your group is competent
I didn't take a real class of hers but a very nice professor and super easy going.
professor is good, se101 it self is a horribly designed class......

SE101 is a useful class that will teach you a lot, but it comes with a lot of work. It's easy to feel overwhelmed by this class because of how time-consuming the assignments can be. That being said, Professor Goldstein is great to talk to for advice on any issues you are facing. She's understanding and makes sure grading is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Spent a lot of time in Lab completing the modling project. She was not very helpful and all of her lectures never helped for the project only for exams. Puts a lot of pressure on TA's and most of them do not know a lot as well. Sketching quizzes and modling exams taught by TA's. She seemed to care too much about students rather than teaching.

Goldstein's class is fun, but your group can make or break both your experience and your grade. Her lectures were understandable, but not usually worth going to.Tests were based on the textbook that she wrote. Lots of assignments. I learned more by myself than from her lectures, but she is super helpful to students.

Professor Goldstein is one of the best professors I've had this year. She is very understanding and cares about her students. The class itself was relatively easy, although there is a semester long group project and your group members make or break your experience in this class. The grading policy in this class is also very fair.

Cares a lot about students so introduce yourself and ask questions. A lot of lectures seem kind of pointless while others are good practice. Guidelines and expectations were sometimes unclear or introduced pretty late. Be prepared for a LOT of late nights in the lab, especially the week before the Design Project is due.
Goldstein cares about her students a lot, and is clear and straightforward in her lectures. Would recommend.

Cared very much about all her students. Seemed to remember everyone's names even those of people who never interacted with her (in a class of 300). Definitely lots of work but not unmanageable at all. Overall loved the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: TAs are horrible. Do not teach us anything and are very harsh graders. Design project is very hard and takes a very long time, be ready to pull all-nighters right before it is due. The lecture sessions were pointless and could have used that time to work on design project. Overall, the class could be organized in a much better way.

Professor Goldstein is awesome. Super nice, really cares what her students have to say. Class is not super hard, but will take up a lot of your time. Expect a 4 to 5 credit hour workload- especially near the end when you are working on the team final.

Professor Goldstein is genuinely caring and nice, and it's really made the course better. The Sketching assignments for the Fall 2020 semester were quite tough, but the quizzes were okay. The modelling assignments were tough for me, but there is ample support hours and the LAs are really helpful. The project takes long, but a good team helps.

Overall a good professor. At the beginning, she couldn't really explain the concepts clearly, but after the first exam she got better at explaining them. Sketching and modeling assignments are a little bit hard. Modeling exams were okay, but written exams are harder than expected. A tough final project. She cares about you and every student.

Prof. Goldstein really cares about her students. The group project is rough, especially when you are assigned groupmates that don't do their work, but the professor is really good about adjusting the project grade accordingly if you let her know. Sketching quizzes/exams are rougher than they should be for a 100 level class.

Her class had A LOT of homework that was sometimes quite difficult, and the lectures and labs don't really relate, but she was very, very caring and considerate when I was in the hospital for 2 weeks and could not get much work done, and gave me chances to get caught up. Overall good class but the final project is rough if you have a bad group

Prof. Goldstein was in her first semester as a professor when I had her, so I expect she will improve, but she was kind of rough as a lecturer. The class is structured fairly well, though the final project can be pretty overkill if you're in a lot of classes. She definitely cares though, she just seems to not really cover material that well.

Professor Goldstein was extremely passionate and a great teacher. Many people do not succeed in the class if they don't put in the work, but she makes it so that if you want an A, you can get an A. Tests weren't easy, but weren't unfair either. Final project is rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Avoid this Professor if you can - the homework, quizzes, exams are very tough and he is also harsh in grading. Though you will learn a lot through the lectures.

Professor Gupta is awesome-clearly knowledge about the topic (I mean, he MADE the SWIM protocol), super accessible outside of the class, and is also very personable and funny. His lecture slides are awesome, I was a 3CH student so only did HW's, but HW's left me feeling like I understood the lectures well. Final was brutal, but awesome teacher.

Content is amazing but the quality of delivery is not. The class is not engaging - only one way conversation and topics are explained in a very difficult way - there are many videos available online which teach the same content in a very easy manner.
Useful class. The professor doesnt lecture well. If you are in 4credit, the MP scheduling is weird. Overall MP workload is accpetable, but the load spikes time to time.

The material and structure of this class was very different from any CS/ECE class here. Full of interesting concepts, Indy is very funny and knowledgeable & teaches clearly. Only downside tests are VERY memorization heavy, just SO many concepts gone over in class. Everyone bombed the final but got curved very generously.

Best lecturer I've ever had at UIUC. Amazing lectures, very articulate, great slides, and truly cares about his students learning experience. Very organized.

Class was tough and definitely requires a lot of studying. But it wasn't unreasonable. Never even had to use the textbook since his lectures were so good.
Best prof in UIUC, curved my grade from C- to A-. Woot Woot!!

Indy's extreme caution against academic dishonesty hampers learning. Questions aimed at clarifying lecture content or exploring key concepts get vague responses from Indy and his TAs. Responses often include unhelpful, snarky remarks instead of constructive guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There's a lack of depth in presentations and tries to do a lot of things without teaching any specific thing well.

Indy is a VERY knowledgeable professor. His classes are hard, but if you put in effort you will learn a lot. The lectures are history focused, but the MPs give you practice in solving real-world distributed systems problems. MP docs are intentionally vague to give you design experience. HW assignments have some fun lore.
Indy is an amazing instructor, he paces his lectures really well, and keeps the material engaging. I highly recommend taking CS 425 if you're interested in working in Systems or Software or Cloud~

Awful, teaches many useless things, and for those useful things, he never dives into the deep. There are many great online resources to learn distributed systems, which are all better than this one. The MPs of this course are impractical, and there is no auto grader to check your code. Barely learnt anything from this course.

Professor Gupta is awesome. Sometimes the lectures can get a bit confusing because the material is so dense, but I feel most of the material is pretty applicable and real-world. He's really helpful and approachable during office hours. Homeworks are long af but there are only 4 throughout the semester, so just start early and you'll be chilling.
Quite clear lectures/ hws/mps

I have this chance to be student of this professor at coursera online courses. I should say that every second of this guys lectures are full of new things to learn. I really love this professor and waana to be in his circle of students.

Every student reviews 4 papers every week, but it's almost impossible to get a meaningful feedback for it. Hard to learn something solely from paper reviews. Take ECE 526 instead  to "learn" something.  I highly recommend you to collaborate with his grad students or to do a project that he understands and likes if you're taking this course.
Awesome professor and class with really entertaining homework and MPs.
Great teacher, really knows his stuff. Tests are a bit difficult and lab code is not well documented.
took an online class with him, he was clear, direct, and easy to follow.

Professor's knowledge is remarkable. Very organized course. Engaging assignments, exams and MPs. Helpful TAs. Lectures are awesome. Just listening to his lectures is enough for preparing for the exam. There were 1 or 2 minor incidences where even though students wrote what was taught in class, they were not given full credit but otherwise no issues

A knowledgeable prof. Lectures were fast & felt like speeches (not engaging. if u r lost in the lect, good luck!) I love the topic but I was unable to connect together the different & many concepts, presented in the lects (think a math student trying to memorize formulas wo understanding the concepts behind them). C is used. I'll learn on my own.

He decided to cut down the MP's from 4 to 2 in the middle of the semester, still keeping 20% of your grade dedicated to the MP's. This is problematic for students who prioritized class work based on how much it effects their grade.   MP's are done in C, the documentation for them are (as usual) not well done.
Good teacher

Indy is a great teacher, and completely defied my expectations coming into the class. He likes to incorporate humor into his slides, and - though he has an accent - is entirely understandable. The MPs got to be a bit tough, but if you're interested in the subject matter then you shouldn't have a problem.
He is the professor who knows what he is teaching about. MPs are interesting and challenging. HWs and Exams are quite easy and straight forward. One can learn quite a lot from his class.
No Comments
I did not enjoy the class. Too much homework and the progess is so fast-paced that I struggle to keep up.

I think CS 233 was a really enjoyable class for a variety of reasons. I think 233 is able to pull off the hybrid learning (online lectures, in person 'labs') a lot better than other courses which do the same which I think it's really a bit testament to Prof Herman and the rest of the course staff. This was a really fun class to take!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I think CS 233 was really enjoyable class for a variety of reasons. I think 233 is able to pull off the hybrid learning (online lectures, in person 'labs') a lot better than other courses which do the same which I think it's really a bit testament to Prof Herman and the rest of the course staff. This was a really fun class to take!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class just brought me too much stress. I don't know how he's doing in in-person sections, but I don't feel like he's paying attention to online section students. Videos are old and textbook are long. Also too much repetitive problem in homework which brings a lot of pressure.

Herman is one of the few professors that is able to implement the "flipped classroom" teaching style effectively. He is kind and genuinely cares about his students, ranging from granting test extensions for illness to devoting the entire in-person class time to making sure each student understands the relevant concepts.

Unfair academic integrity policy is used for his courses. He would allege someone for cheating by simply claiming "you used concepts/techniques that we did not teach during class." For example, I myself learned verilog in high school and know techniques beyond the CS233, and he filed a FAIR allegation which was later proven false by the Committee.

He's been filing a number of false academic integrity allegations. Many students were honest and actively learning from external resources. However, he issues FAIR allegations on labs claiming the use of AI merely based on "using functions / syntax not taught in this class." If you don't know how to detect AI properly, then don't be irresponsible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get into a good routine. Try to find people who are reliable. It is hard to collaborate on the assignments sometimes as groups of 3, but you can get a rotation going. It is one of my favorite classes I have taken at UIUC, with super well-organized and interesting material. Some pipeline exercises weren't super clear. Requires a lot of practice.

The class follows a flipped format, so there is not much interaction with the professor outside of office hours / other non-official meetings. However, he is clearly passionate about teaching and has put a lot of time and effort into developing the class materials to be as good as possible. A good class, interesting by virtue of its organization.
The course is incredibly well-organized, and if you follow the materials provided, the tests are very fair and straightforward to prepare for.

The best course I've ever taken. It has a lot of work but it prepares you so well that you don't have to do anything extra for the quizzes/final exam. He gave a lot of extra credit and flexibility to make the class less stressful.

Herman is part of what makes CS@UIUC a top program. He structures the class so that you will learn through struggle. Though the content in the class may seem daunting, after each assignment you will appreciate how much you've learned. Grading is very generous, and it is clear in the way he manages his class that he wants every student to succeed.

Good class and content. However, professor is very academic integrity / FAIR trigger happy. Be prepared to potentially get FAIRED over the absolute stupidest / and pointless things. I believe too FAIR trigger happy for his own good. Just beware.

Prof. Geoffery Herman is a great professor! The course is hard but rewarding. While everything is on Prairielearn, there are very clear instructions and video explanations for harder questions. I attended the in-person section at 9 am, but I am motivated to go to CIF. The TAs and CAs are very helpful and caring.

One of the best CS courses I have took. Herman is just so nice and did really great job on how the course is structured. Even the content and quizs are pretty hard, but as long as you finished all the assignments, you are prepared. And they do provide you practice exam with multiple variants, so dont worry about that. And every quiz have a retake.

my favorite class thus far in the CS curriculum. 233 is extremely well designed compared to other CS classes, although it is a ton of work, be prepared for that (6 assignments/labs a week). even coming in with little knowledge about hardware you'll learn a ton, and the course staff do everything they can to decrease stress as much as possible
Herman was always nice, understanding, and flexible. 233 was my favorite class during my Computer Science undergrad.

Prof Herman is the BEST professor you can ever get. He cares about his student and knows the stuff his teaching.

The class is so well structured and offers very comprehensive lectures and video tutorials for most of the questions plus he walks you through some of those difficult question types before the actual quiz.
Made a boring class fun. Best made course ever, an expert in education.

The course has many moving parts, but Prof Herman keeps everything clear and on track. He has structured the course exceptionally well, building simple concept upon simple concept until you look back and realise how far you've come. There are few professors as caring and accessible as he is, and I would gladly take any course he decides to run.

He cares a lot for students! Every exam has 2nd chance. There are plenty of extra credits, and final weighs only 10%. The course is interesting (cuz I am a great fan of computer architecture, but anyway, you will learn A LOT), and the concepts are generally not too difficult. You should spend more time learning stash, cache, and conscious coding.
Very good professor, really knows his stuff
Amazing professor, he really knows the content in and out and actually cares about the students. Definitely made a boring class fun!

Prof. Herman is a great person and instructor. The course material isn't easy, but he gives you lots of opportunities for extra credit and often grants extensions when the whole class is struggling. You can tell he cares about his students. Plus he knows his material in and out. Overall very well structured and organized class.

The course content could be better taught. Prelecture small clips are super good but under explained sometimes so the GAs and labs can become stressful. Class induces unnecessary stress that can be avoided if the content is taught better. But the class is very very well run otherwise. Other classes at this school should learn from professor Herman

The class is organized and run very well, other professors could learn a thing or two from Professor Herman. The content itself is difficult and the labs + GAs are stressful, but that is true for all all large coding projects. If you can complete every assignment by yourself you will do fine in the course, and there is a lot of EC if you can't.
His presence didn't make a class where I hated every second of the content worse. This is just one of those classes that I had to drag through.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Class structure was very organized and facilitated learning very well, truly one of the best. The lectures were usually solid, and the group work provided great practice for the quizzes. Overall, as long as you do all the work recommended by the prof (which isn't that much) you are guaranteed an A.
The class sucks but I think it's unavoidable given the subject matter. Prof is interesting and smart, and there's a lot of ec and stuff to help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really fun professor and a good lecturer. There's a LOT of work in this class but it's clear what you need to study for and TAs and professors are really helpful. The material is really fun and engaging.

If you have never taken a hardware class don't think of skipping the videos he uploads. He goes over things very well but sometimes he just skips over topics to save time which is why I rated a 4/5. This class is a grind so be ready for that

Love his bite-sized condensed lecture videos. He went the extra mile by creating 1-2 hr long quiz review videos and other briefings which were super helpful, and even makes other videos on demand. Tons of practice to understand the material and I learned a great deal. Impeccable course structure, organized, and he was communicative over Campuswire.

Even though I struggled a bit in his class, Professor Herman was a very good professor at UIUC. He gave a lot of practice problems to help understand the concepts and even offers videos to watch to help understand the concepts. In fact, he adjusts accordingly according to feedback and always there for his students to succeed.

This class is the best taught CS class I've taken at this school. Very difficult topics were broken down into digestible 5 min videos followed by questions to reinforce learning. Wish every class was taught like this, can't handle 50 min lectures with unrelated homework anymore. Professor Herman really spoiled us.

Professor Herman is one of the most incredible CS professors I've met so far. He does a great job of teaching content (which by no means is easy content to teach) and does a lot to alleviate student stress. He gives many opportunities for students to get extra points and continuously listens to feedback and adjusts his class accordingly.

Nice and helpful. Active on Piazza. Seemed fair and flexible. Lectures and homeworks prepared you for exams. Assignments were managable. However, for many exams, I felt like I was more drilling specific types of problems than learning concepts.
a good lecturer and overall the class is run very well. he gives you the option to opt out of lecture but i wouldnt, you get ec for participating and it will make it so much easier to learn i promise
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Computer Architecture is not easy. Prof Herman makes it explicit and undertandable. There are pre-flight videos and some conceptional questions before lectures so make use of these , lectures are clear and efficient, hw are well designed definitely do it. If you done the above, exams will be OK. Labs are time consuming, start early.

Professor Herman was the best professor I had the semester I took that class. The class has a steep curve in terms of the material, but he explains everything really well, has review sessions and great exam tips. Also, he kept taking feedback about all sorts of things throughout the semester, and immediately acted on them.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a solid lecturer and is someone you would be glad to talk with. The exams are reasonable, but exam 6 is much harder than all the rest. Start the labs early and attend the lectures and discussions for free points. The labs vary in difficulty. The class teaches useful material.

Professor Herman is a good instructor even though occasionally he did not explain the material very clear. Self-teaching matters A LOT in this class, and be careful that this class gets harder before you realize it.
He defines me. Never mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He definitely cares about the students, but sometimes the lectures can be boring
He really cares about students. Responds to emails quickly. Very clear lectures. Great Prof.
Professor Herman is Great. The lectures are clear, and the online mini clips are great. Easy to understand, and the best teaching quality ever.
Awesome teacher, too good to be true. Enthusiastic, happy and knows his material well. Will gladly take another class with the dude
GG always re. Herman best professor NA.

He is super enthusiastic, and will go over everything very clearly. If you have questions however, it is best to go to office hours because if you ask during class he just sort of repeats what he just said. At office hours he is fantastic. Just a super nice guy overall! Hard course though...

Students cant understand full circuit design unless their homeworks deal with more fundamental simple design concepts. Grades are important  so challenging problems on graded homeworks with less time to figure them out debilitate confidence if there is no corresponding support provided in teaching. Can improve course structure greatly.
Great prof. Too bad he is not here all the time.

Professor Herman's version of ECE290 is exciting and educational, giving us the chance to get into team based learning at the sophomore level. He's a very enthusiastic lecturer as well, definitely would recommend taking 290 with him if you can.

He was a good guy, fun, and seemed to want the best for students. He listened and changed some things based on midterm feedback surveys. The quizzes get pretty hard tho I would be prepared to fail the initial quiz, ask TAs how to solve them after, and do well on the retake. He also did make the final option for spring 2026.

Had him for 212, he's awesome but the class is not. Mastering the homework is a baseline to barely earn a B in this course. I purchased an additional textbook for harder practice problems so I actually felt prepared for the quizzes and final. 212 doesn't need to be hard, they just give you nothing to study. Atleast Golecki is good teaching.
Honestly the goat!! Will tell my kids the legacy he had on to the class of spring 2026.if ykyk.
Amazing professor, lectures are informative. Class can be difficult at times but Golecki does as much as possible to ensure that all of his students succeed.
THE GREATEST OF ALL TIME, INSPIRATIONAL FIGURE WHO ACTUALLY CARES FOR HIS STUDENTS. I LOVE YOU!!!!

Genuinely caring professor who values feedback and tries to make the class interesting with real-world examples. His lectures are well-structured and and pretty easy to follow. Homework is pretty difficult, but helps you prepare for biweekly quizzes.

The first three quizzes are very easy. The difficulty of the last three quizzes skyrockets. The lectures and homework do not cover material at a similar level of difficulty as the quizzes. The quizzes also did not give you enough time to think through and try the problems. I don't even know how should I study.

**FOR TAM251**

Dr. Golecki is a great lecturer, and made the at times complex concepts of TAM251 very easy to grasp. Lecture was a good balance between example/content. The class was also well structured in general, and you could tell that Dr. Golecki knew his stuff. Great and interesting class, great and interesting lecturer.

Super good class, I hope he teaches it again. Long homework assignments (and hard) but you learn a lot from them. Some problems with class formatting but I think he will fix it in the future. Clearly cares about how much his students enjoy his class and wants us to learn rather than just do well on exams. Lecture is sometimes tough, but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Goated ngl

The grading is brutal. Homework requires huge effort (5+ hours minimum each), but the graders are salty as f. Gives straight 0's without any partial credit. Honestly, the grading is the only factor that made the course disgusting. 

The lectures are very enjoyable, the professor is goated.

Did not follow my letter of accommodations and had to talk with disability services who said while he was in the wrong they don't have the power to make him do anything. Not sure what the point of accommodations are then.
Had him for TAM251. His lectures are clear and well-organized. He explains complex topics in a way that actually makes sense, and the examples make the material much easier to understand.

Genuinely my most enjoyable class so far. You get to see the real world applications of every single topic learned and all with an enthusiastic professor that had lectures I looked forward to going to. Projects and homework can be a bit tough, but the aim is to help not hurt and in the end you learn a wealth of information that applies everywhere.

Prof. Golecki cares about his students, tries to make lectures interesting with examples, and is very active in campuswire. The main issue lies in the course structure of ME270; the lecture feels pointless without exams backing it, and the homework is very tedious and doesn't feel applicable. The projects are more interesting but also tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for TAM 251. best Tam professor I've had. He gave really interesting lectures with real life examples and experiments. The content was hard and you will have to learn outside of class. He will let you have friday's off some times too! Go to lecture and discussion... they do count a lot for your grades

Cares about his students, brought his industry experience to the classroom through case studies. Would also bring physical examples of parts manufactured using the methods discussed in class so students can see how this class may apply to their careers. Very energetic lecturer and seems passionate about teaching.

I really like the guy, but going to lecture is sort of pointless. To succeed in this class you really have to figure out the homeworks. He is very energetic and cool, but the class structure is what it is and I don't think it changes based on the professor. He's good, but the class isn't. Just learn the homeworks, everything else is a waste of time

Honestly Golecki is the best professor I've had up to this point. The examples he uses in lecture are so helpful and make the course content interesting. He also shows examples of real-world applications every week related to the current lecture topics. Overall, very nice, cool guy and his passion is contagious, got me excited about physics again.

Most of the stuff he teaches in lectures does not coincide with the hw and quizzes. He only goes over the simplest examples. When he does "teach" he works out super long derivations which are not useful at all. The average grade on the final was a 68% and he chose not to curve it. So I guess professor golecki wants his students to do poorly.

Tbh this class is just poorly constructed but it doesn't help that the grading criteria is not well laid out and you can't really get an answer from Prof Golecki. The class also has a LOT of writing and very little designing, which was not great. At least he publishes the power points with all the notes so all the quizzes are pretty easy.
He is a really cool person. The course content he is teaching is not super interesting but he is probably the best professor to take the class with.

TAM 212 grading is very fair, the quizzes are similar to the homework. The reference pages are super helpful, and the professor makes content interesting with real world applications. Not too difficult.

He's cool but the class is VERY difficult. Most of the lectures are pointless because roughly only 25% of the material taught in lecture applies to the hw and the quizes, yet attendance is mandatory. Discussions are the BIGGEST waste of time. You'll have to navigate the reference pages to figure this class out on your own. Good luck it is VERY HARD
Golecki is awesome. TAM 2-- grading is super fair. The class is not very easy, but he tried his best to make it enjoyable with real world applications.
Does not give proper guidance outside of class, gives assignments with lack of instructions, and grading is not consistently done.

His class feels disorganized to put it simply. The syllabus description is for a different class. There are errors in project assignments. Class is canceled with inadequate notice. He is approachable, but the way the class is set up you almost need to go to office hours for help because the lectures are hard to follow and there are no videos.

Get ready for a tough semester. Most of the assignments are opened ended by design this is good because it lets you figure out problems your own way but it also makes the process very confusing and the grading unclear. I would HIGHLY recommend going to office hours to make sure that your project meets the graders criteria.
Condescending and never owned his faults.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class starts hard with having papers every week. It gets better once you start your feasibility project, but you have no guidance, and the TAs grade harshly and inconsistently. Even if you go to office hours, one TA will tell you something and another something else. Henschen was pretty nice when it came to helping, though.
He cares about students and explains very well. The lab parts are super cool and you get to see concrete exploding!

CEE weeder, all my groupmates switched out of the major. Rubrics are vague. Grading is very harsh and inconsistent. Expect to have points taken off for minor mistakes. Provided examples for papers are useless. Seek upperclassman help if possible. Henschen is approachable but you will need to seek him out yourself. Class is terrible, prof is fine.

CEE 190 is a nightmare of a class, but ultimately pretty useful. Henschen was a really harsh grader, but he was also helpful when I talked to him outside of class. I wouldn't take 190 again, but if he taught a different class, I wouldn't discount it just because he's the professor.

Gives a large body of work and without guidance the group project can become both a hassle and a grade killer. However, he is very approachable and when talking to him you can get the sense that he cares about students' success, but there is also a disparity between the examples and "expectations" that are stated and the actual grade on assignments

Inconsistent grading rubric so don't ask other professors for feedback and advice because this professor is the only one in charge of grading. Would regrade assignment that's graded by TA and take off 20%+ grade for some groups. Harsh and unreasonable feedback and points off. Gave students a "C" past example for assignment reference.

Best interest is not in students. 

He had examples of student projects for an assignment which students used, of course, to understand what they should put in there work. Then he removed the example after the assignment was already graded saying "this example is D- material" and didn't give students another chance to redo their assignment.

lectures are somewhat disorganized, focusing heavily on structural applications. The group project, overly time-consuming for a 4-credit course, requires over 6 hours weekly for corrections, not counting homework and review time. Additionally, the project lacks clarity, leading to errors that even he struggles to resolve.
Teaches real-world application of structural design well. Exams are a bit of a time crunch for some but provides partial credit.

Extremely lazy teaching and organization. The project assignments did not even have correct course labels, but instead had labels and information from his previous university. He makes the class very arbitrary and it requires a lot of time in office hours to clarify what he means for both exams and the project.
He is very condescending to students in office hours. He reads off lecture slides that were made by professors who previously taught the class without elaboration.

The online portions were pretty easy, but the discussion part moves fast! Ask questions; do the practice in class (and save it!) bc it will help with HW and future assignments. Also, never assume the HW will be a quick 15min, all of the R code will take you a while, AND so many assignments are due at 2pm! Plus, beware the Final group project lol

I don't write reviews, but oh my god RUN from this man! Second day of class he assigned a pop quiz and told people to get out of his class if they didn't read the case study. You could never expect what was going to come next, and every class was a new horror waiting to happen. PLEASE for your own sake, DO NOT TAKE A CLASS TAUGHT BY THIS MAN!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was hybrid, so the TA taught the lab and the prof uploaded online lectures. His online lectures half of the time were two AI bots talking to each other, which was a god awful way to learn. The content is very difficult, and he does not adequately explain the content or the instructions on assignments. You also never knew what to expect.

Fantastic teacher, you will get what you put into his classes. He is very knowledgable and cares about what he does. Many students simply do not wish to engage with the material and get upset when he expects us to know what he is talking about. I completely disagree with the other reviews for him. He is also very lenient with grading.

probably the worst class i've ever taken. i should've looked at his 1.4 review before i took the course. overall confusing, slow and hard to understand, and became a problem around the final when he wouldn't accept my late work after my best friend died and the university sent him an emergency letter but he didn't check his email

The worst professor I have had in my time at UIUC and im a senior. Nothing he said made sense, his lectures were confusing and in person lectures had no structure. I had to email him multiple times THE WEEK OF FINALS to get any grades to know where I stood. If you have the chance to take this class with literally any other professor, take it.

He is poor at explaining things and the way he approaches lectures can frighten many students. He relies on his TA to grade for ~45 students and grades were not until a week after the end of the semester. Things are explained poorly as well.
Incredibly hard to work with. Yelled at us on the first day of in-person class. Grades were never put in. Not great at giving directions.
No idea how a professor could be this awful. Pretty impressive ngl.
Pretty bad at teaching, and he doesn't explain to students if they're not sure about something.
He is insane
Harsh is great. Seems like he cares. Lectures were hard to get in to but he was a great professor.

Harsh lives up to his name - he's harsh. Never gave feedback on any of the assignments, and gave very unclear instructions. Harsh expected us to know things he never even taught us, and he insulted our intelligence on many occasions. A fellow student even went to the Dean to report Harsh for being such a bad professor. Never again.

This was a relatively easy class that was extremely group project heavy, in a good way. The tests were very easy to get through and the lessons were interesting enough that they still stuck with me. 

I would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interrupts students, not clear project outlines, quizzes are testing memorization much more than knowledge of concepts.

He is a though grader. He was unprepared for class, very inefficient and a waste of time. But there is a lot of homework after class. He wastes class time and leaves all the tasks to you to teach yourself.
Please do not take his course. He is totally unprepared before class and even cannot answer some questions asked by students during the class.
No Exams, but the amount of groupwork and papers that are due will make an ordinary person go crazy. Horrible grading !!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor always says Go out into the world and be successful but it should start from his own course. Professor himself is funny, enjoyable but his support staffs are horrible. The instructions for assignments are all convoluted.
This guy thinks marketing is god's gift to earth. He's going to waste your time with silly assignments that do little to further the content of the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall the professor cares more about attendance than teaching. The class is easy and the material is basic, but the TAs are instructed to grade very harshly on silly things like format. Every week is a scavenger hunt to find assignments and requirements. Every week is a lecture on how important attending live sessions is. Overall annoying
Hayden is the man. He's super engaging and entertaining to listen to and he's really funny. I really enjoyed the class mainly because he was teaching it. His video lectures are nice as well

This is not a course where you can get away with not participating. Professor Noel makes an effort to get everyone to speak. There is a lot of content every week, and of all my classes (Master's student) his course took the most time. I enjoyed the content and I felt like I learned a lot because we were expected to put time in. He's very optimistic

Prof. Tibebu is passionate about AI, technology governance, and policy. This course definitely teaches you all the technical details of AI governance, including hands-on experience. The discussions are great
He genuinely cares for his students and is highly approachable. He is willing to meet outside of scheduled office hours to support my group with my final project.

This class involves coding, and the professor does a great job of supporting us. That's one of the things I appreciate most. He encourages us to use technology while also making sure we clearly show our own understanding and ideas.
Pro Tibebu's discussion scenarios and debate sessions are engaging and interesting. He is a kind person too.
He is good professor, I like the course structure and I enjoy the coding lab sessions.

The class is both technical and theoretical with a bit of coding. The prof is clear, so it's easy to keep up. The project isn't a brain-breaker, but definitely don't leave it until the last minute because it's time-consuming
The professor is pretty fair if you actually show up and join in on the lectures and discussions. Most of the topics are game-based and honestly pretty fun.
I took MLC IS597 taught by Professor Tibebu, and it was one of the best practical courses I've taken. I especially like how the course focused not only on ML, but also on responsible RAI.
I took IS467 last semester, and I'm posting because I recently landed a job thanks to the final project from this course.

Most valuable aspects was how accessible the professor was. I met with him four times during office hours, and each time he was helpful, and genuinely invested in helping students succeed. He's very approachable and makes it easy to ask questions or seek clarification. I'd recommend taking advantage of his office hours, you'll see for yourself.

Professor Tibebu is incredibly passionate about AI and AI accountability. You can clearly see his enthusiasm in every lecture, and he genuinely wants his students to become just as passionate. He always try we actually understand the material. Would take every class he offers.

Lecture presentations definitely needs a bit more work. Expectations for certain parts of the assignments are clear but a good portion of other assignments were not clear. Needs balance. Needs to work with the TA more since our TA is sometimes unclear about Mr. Tibebu's instructions. Overall, his class structure is very poor but can be fixed
He's approachable during office hours, fair with grading, and clear about expectations from the start. Not an easy A, but if you put in the effort and stay engaged, you'll learn a lot and do well.

Professor does not follow what his syllabus says, based on his syllabus and what he said verbally in class, my Kahoot winning group was promised we will earn the 1.5 points from the Kahoot, but we only received 1 point. Our group emailed the professor, and he is unwilling to give us the extra 0.5 points since he needs to keep grading consistent.

Weekly assignments are extremely writing heavy, attendance required, and your entire grade basically relies on group work. Disorganized class and there was no actual interaction between students. No student-led discussions about ethics either.

Don't take his class!!!! RUNNNNNN!!!!!
He's over concern about the class 'discipline'. 
He said:"Shame on you! for those who didn't submit the work".

He grade our work even before the due.

Weekly 5-page paper with a group, somewhat condescending in class. Clearly very smart and accomplished, research is interesting, which I appreciate, but the WHOLE class is his research. Random debates during discussion, but overall haven't learned much.

This class is extremely unorganized and boring. Weekly group papers, almost half of them are just writing about a paper he wrote. VERY strict on attendance and not inviting for extra help. I would suggest taking this class with a different professor.

The professor has deep knowledge of AI policy and ethics-related stuff. I enjoyed his class; he tries to engage students by asking many questions. The class includes a lot of group work activities, so if you don't like group work, this is not the professor for you. He is also very approachable if you need help.

An incredibly unorganized course. Lectures do not relate to weekly assignments. Discussion sections have repetitive 4-minute presentations every week from each group where notes of any kind & slides are banned. 

Every single assignment in this course is a group paper, so good luck getting your group on the same page & having everyone contribute.

I learned extensively about AI policy, regulation, national/international law. Some lectures were technical, including coding for responsible RAG and fairness metrics. Assignments drew from his research papers. He's helpful and accessible outside class, currently involving me in his research. He is strict on attendance.

Professor Tibebu is incredibly kind, patient, and dedicated to his students' learning. He explains complex topics clearly, makes classes engaging, and is very supportive outside of class. He even offers students research opportunities. Definitely take his class if you can!

In this class right now, and I can advise you to NOT take this professor. He's a good guy, but his lectures are boring, the class is terribly structured, and I dont feel like I'm learning anything. All of the assignments are just paraphrasing a paper that he wrote.
Unorganized and extremely boring. Just not a good professor, but the class isn't really hard.
Had her for TAM 211 and ME 170. Very helpful lectures with many examples and many opportunities for help through CAs and TAs

Structure of TAM 210 is pretty poor. That's more on the class than on the prof. You use python to do the math on both the hw and the quizzes, but she does not teach you how to do the problems with python during lecture and you have to learn that as well as a lot of the material yourself. Still, she is your best bet for TAM 210/211.
She is a great teacher. However, the class is quite boring which made lectures somewhat hard to get through. However, she does have a lot of passion for what she is teaching and it shows.
I love her she's amazing and wants you to succeed

She's organized during lectures, explains it well, presents the topics clearly, and does examples along with the material. As long as you pay attention during lecture it's pretty easy to get an A in the class. The quizzes are just like the homework, but the retry's get harder the later in the class you get so try to get a good score the first time.

The lectures were okay but definitely not enough to be ready for the test. You are expected to use hw problems for exam prep which I often found not enough. Second exam was diabolical, do textbook problems.The course structure is amazing tho. She is not accessible outside of class like at all so only TA help. Biggest advice: come to office hours!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Halloran cares about each one of her students; I had accommodations which I needed to be fulfilled and she was always on top of things by periodically checking with me to make sure she is doing what she needs to. I knew fusion 360 before the class, but I could tell that fusion is taught pretty well in the labs, so don't worry too much about it.

Halloran is the best for TAM 210/211. She is very clear and knowledgeable and has plenty of exam/quiz level examples during each lecture. Show up to lecture to get the i-clicker points. I went to office hours for help on any HW problem I couldn't do, and that prepared me for the quizzes and final. TAM can be tough, but Halloran is great for it.

Halloran is a very good prof. ME170 lecture content can be boring but she explains it well. She gave good feedback on the presentation for the final project and clearly answered engineering career and Fusion360-related questions. The lectures matter a lot less than your group for the group project did. As long as you work on the project, it's easy.

She's great. The lectures are a bit boring at times, but it's mostly due to the material and not because of Prof. Halloran. She's quite active during office hours and is easily accessible by outlook, which is helpful. However, this class in general is made to be quite easy. The only annoying thing is that you may have to settle for a 8am lecture.

ME 170 is a great class, but the fact that it is only taught at 8 AM does make it a bit annoying. Lectures can get boring sometimes, but you do learn a lot during the labs and the team project. Overall, its a pretty easy and chill class and you get a lot of hands on experience with Fusion 360.

Great lecturer. Good at explaining hard TAM concepts, does plenty of practice questions, and answers questions clearly. Also wrote reference pages and frequently uses them in class. TAM sucks but Halloran at least teaches it well.

Professor Halloran was an amazing instructor. Her lectures were clear and easy to follow, and her recorded videos honestly carried me through the class. Grading was fair and on the lenient side, which made the course way less stressful. Overall, a great prof—definitely recommend taking her class!

Great professor with clear notes and lectures. Loves to answer questions during lecture. The course is designed very neatly and doing the homework is plenty enough for the exams. (If you're stuck on homework, office hours are extremely useful as well!) Overall, I learned a lot from this class and I would highly recommend learning from her.

This class is taught well but man it could so be two lectures a week. Half of each lecture would be review and sometimes the lectures lowkey felt like purgatory. Its good that Dr. Halloran is a nice, respectable, and personable lecturer who teaches the content in a way that is easy to understand though.

Prof. Halloran is great. She has great lecture slides and as long as you pay attention and do the homeworks you're set for the class. Just don't space out or else you might miss something. The TA's are really helpful during office hours, although the discussion sections are kind of useless imo
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great prof, cannot recommend enough. Her teaching style is very intuitive, albeit the subject matter itself is pretty easy as well. On top of that, she actually cares about the class and is enthusiastic every lecture so the mandatory attendance isn't a chore. One of my most enjoyable classes.
Really nice professor but a kind of boring lecture, not too hard of a class tho

This class suffers from the poor structure, and the fact that it is at 8am. Otherwise, the class is easy and gives you a good foundation in Fusion 360. The Cadlabs were really frustrating, and the graders graded pretty strictly. Dr. Halloran is a good lecturer/teacher, but the lectures at 8am are extremely hard to pay attention to.

Professor Halloran is the goat. Her lectures were super clear and organized, she emphasized being a visual learner which is very helpful for TAM and answered questions very clearly. HW was easy, quizzes and final were slightly harder but doable and it was easy to get an A, especially with retakes.

I found the lectures quite boring at times. The fact that they are at 8 a.m. does make them a pain. The labs are good, and it's pretty easy to do well there. Some lectures are pretty useless or just a very small part of what is being tested in this class. CAD is not taught in lectures at all and it's only taught in labs.

Dr. Halloran is great. This class is a pretty easy one as long as you follow the rules in the pdf assignments, and the rubric outlines exactly what the graders are looking for. She and all of the TA's want you to succeed so I highly recommend going to office hours. Imo lectures were a bit boring but maybe it's because they're only offered at 8 AM.
Prof. Witek has good TAs that explain very good, but Prof. Witek is not good at explaining

She is a very meticulous and clear lecturer, though her handwriting is sometimes hard to read. It's a naturally hard subject and you have to read the lecture notes and Taylor on your own to get the full picture. Homework load is not too big, and exams are very fairly designed and timed. Office hours are a blessing. If you have her you'll be fine.
Hard lectures
Great professor, great lecturer, very nice and caring towards her students, and always happy to talk.
Material was difficult, but her lectures were well paced and very clear. I really felt like I learned a lot in this class.

By far the worst physics class I have taken, tried rewatching lectures for notes and studying but the recording is facing away from the board. Also sometimes hard to understand and very blackboard heavy; derivations would be online though. Needs some time to figure out the class structure

I took General Relativity with her ( a 500 level course, she is an expert in this). I highly recommend her. The lecture notes were helpful, lectures were clear. A lot of homework but she is available during office hours. She's passionate and caring . Ignore the 101 reviews, professors do not choose the rules in these basic courses

This course was taught almost entirely by lecture but she was clear and easy to understand. The exams are easy if you do and understand the homework, and two of them offered bonus points. I would have liked more rigor with some of the derivations, it was easy to get a bit confused at times.

If you have the option to take a high level PHYS class w/ Prof Witek, I highly recommend her. The lecture notes were extremely helpful, lectures were clear, and tests sometimes had extra credit problems. The class is homework heavy but she is available with office hours. She's a passionate and caring professor, disregard the low level PHYS reviews.

She is a very good professor and constantly stays mindful of those who have questions or need clarification in her class. This class specifically is very difficult in terms of content. It is hard to say if it was difficult because of her teaching or content itself. Her office hours were very helpful. She gave a lot of opportunity for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Didn't give good lectures for such a difficult class

terrible professor  terrible class. if you're into failing this is the class for you. not an easy class to drop either because it's 5 credits. it will ruin your GPA. every week kids from my lab and discussion groups drop out. the class is an absolute mess. exams are graded unfairly as well. if you miss 1 question, the grade can drop to a B.

It is her first year here but to be honest, no one cares. Gen Ed or not, we want to be able to succeed in the classroom and did not do a very good job of that. Her TA's were better than her. Lecture size decreased from 200+ to almost 10 by the end of the year. She also lies about the Exam Scores, probably cause she doesn't want to expose herself.
Awful professor, genuinely did not watch one lecture because they confused everyone even more. 7 people would show up to her 200+ person lecture. Self-taught myself all material.

This was Prof. Witek first year at the university, which I'd like to give her lenience for, but college is hard enough, especially physics, and is why I can't rank her higher. I believe she's made the class harder than it should be. Lectures were pretty useless and being self taught is the only way to go for this course. Tests also try to trick you
The WORST. Doesn't even know her own material.

The lectures are useless, the exams are almost weekly with additional weekly quizzes, students aren't given a break from discussion on exam weeks, some discussion "review" sections are completely worthless because they take place after the exam, and the grading scale is shifted to make getting a good grade even more difficult. 0/5 horrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This woman is incompetent and a horrible teacher. Do not take Phys 101 with her unless you want to fail. The lectures do not help at all and you learn more in the prelectures than you do in actual lectures. The tests are online in the CBTF and are quite unfairly weighted. If you have to take it with her good luck.

Most of us could not understand his speech so barely anyone went to lectures. You need to be able to self-teach everything. The tests were CBTF but were the easiest out of any of the other profs. If you value actually understanding calc 3, don't get this prof. If you want to not really understand and just memorize for the tests then Ivanov is fine.

sergei is my goat. all midterms in cbtf and so much easier compared to other professors, final is tough but he had a good curve on it. all homework is online, don't bother going to class with his heavy accent just self learn.
broski is my goat heck yes

ivanov my goat..he does not deserve all these negative reviews. sure his accent might make it hard to understand, but his lecture notes are exceptional and make up for it. lecture also isn't mandatory, so why are we hating on his accent?? exams are in cbtf so he makes them easy, and he always gets grades in on time. 5/5 my king

This professor has a very thick accent, and speaks unclearly, which makes lectures hard to understand. However, his notes are detailed, and discussion sections were useful. When I took his class, he seemed to be the "easiest" professor of all of the calc 3 professors, bc his CBTF tests were easier and gave lots of extra credit.

He made extra credit possible for every homework assignment and held all midterms in CBTF. The practice problems for each midterm more than prepared me for each test. Overall, the class was very straightforward and easy to pass as long as you do your work and stay focused.
worst professor Ive ever had.

His accent is totally fine; notes are very good; only 15% of the class comes to lecture.
This may change, but Fall 2025 he had exams in CBTF which no other prof had. If nothing else, I would recommend him just for this. CBTF is convenient and the exams had high averages.
If you excelled in calc 2, take the honors section; this will be too easy.
He does have a thick accent but the lectures and slides are pretty easy to comprehend. He did offer extra credit when midterms came around and is a nice guy overall.
can't understand him

Worst professor I have ever had, should not even be a professor, MR. IVANOV, would make the DRES exam harder than other normal exams, and have the thickest accent that makes u think he is teaching in full Russian, torturing both TA and STUDENTS.

Although Professor Ivanov does have a thick accent and is hard to understand, his notes are very clear and full of good information. His exams on the other hand aren't the most difficult so if you study well you'll do better than your friends with other professors. Another good thing is the extra credit there is lots of it! Overall not the worst.

As it has been said by many others already, Professor Ivanov has a very thick accent that can make him difficult to understand at times, especially when his microphone cuts out and no one decides to mention it to him. However, his notes were very clear and helpful for completing homework and studying for exams and he gave a lot of extra credit.

Professor Ivanov was an incredible professor. He was a little difficult to understand in lectures, but his notes were immaculate, and his reviews reflected the exams. He makes Calc 3 intuitive and gives a lot of EC. 10/10

He copies all his notes from a different professor; none of it is his. He is very passive-aggressive and honestly doesn't like being wrong. I find it unforgiving that he makes the DRES exams way harder than the regular ones just because they have more time to take the test, but that beats the whole purpose of getting the accommodations.

First time teaching MATH 241 I believe or in a long time, HAS A THICK ACCENT which makes it hard to understand, however the lecture notes he posts are super informative. However what I do it is watch professor Leonard then then review the lecture notes. GO to office hours, it helps, also you maybe get extra points for it.

Math 241 broke me. 
I got an A+ in Math 231, but I cried a lot because of this class.  The way it's taught doesn't help at all, and honestly, it left me traumatized. I'd say it's the worst class I've taken at UIUC.
Basically just reads off lecture notes, not necessary to attend class. Can be a little passive aggressive with asking questions. Tests are very similar to reviews.
Good class

Had him during covid. Lecture was online, just read off lecture slides, which was exactly the same as the video lectures he posted on the course webpage. I stopped going to his lectures, so did most of the class. Study on your own for this class. Also, he is unforgiving of deadlines, no matter what the circumstance.

Worst professor I've ever had. His thick accent makes his lectures very difficult to follow. He just reads from the lecture notes and hardly even looks up at the students or does example problems. Exams are pretty straightforward but going to lectures alone won't help. I honestly stopped showing up to them midway through the semester. Avoid!

Math416 is supposed to be a proof based class while he made it more like Math415 which only has some short easy proof. He gives extra credits if you present reviews questions on the blackboard and all exams will be based on the review problems he gives us. So if you want to get easy A then go for him, if you want learn strong proofs then avoid him.

I can't understand his English! And he is not willingly to help you with the homework questions. Basically learn it by yourself. ] He even told his students this is a hard class and if you can't do so just drop it.

I really liked professor Ivanov.  His sense of humor was...weird, but he taught the material decent enough.  The homework was fair and the tests were easy.  Before each test, he would give out ~25 problems and guarantee that the test would be made out of 6 of those only changed slightly. Overall, I learned a lot.  Review sessions are useless though

Did not learn much by going to lecture. Pretty much taught myself through the book. Overall, was not horrible. The homeworks were difficult and so were the tests; however, the final has some problems straight from prior tests and homeworks.
Got easier after alternating groups.

His homework can be pretty tough due to the many proofs, but those are seldom graded. He has quizzes every week, but they can be cancelled at times. Gives bonus points during review sessions, and had a Thanksgiving quiz. Exams are pretty simple. They are pretty similar to the questions he emphasizes during the review and the quizzes

I loved having Adel! I took him for an 8am ACCY 410 class, and he is easily the most engaging ACCY professor I had during undergrad. the material in the class is very difficult, but you can tell that he is very invested in making sure that you not only learn the material but understand how to apply it.

The content of the course is not that difficult. But professor Ibrahim's constant yelling and confusing analogies make simple concepts difficult to understand. You will need to dedicate a lot of time studying outside of class to succeed in this course. I remember feeling lost during his lectures.

Good lectures, but if you miss any class you are absolutely lost. Homework is hard but doable.Tests are much harder than homework and he takes pleasure in his own disappointment when his students have not practiced the niche topic he went over a month ago that has not come up again. He does not do notes well and there are no review guides or slides
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: BEST PROFESSOR EVER. I have never seen a professor care as much as Adel does. His office hours are the best ever. He makes the classes sooo interesting- I have never once spaced out in them. He cold calls to keep his students attention- and it works. His cold calling is not bad as you dont have to answer but just be more attentive. He is the best.

He is kind and funny. He made an effort to make us understand the concepts and learn a lot of things. 
He cared us with thinking about our busy schedules.

I will definitely take his class in Spring again.

Thank you Adel!!!!!! You are the best!

He is kind and funny.

I guess the reasons why his rate is low is because most of students who take 501 do not have accounting background. Therefore, sometimes his lecture is confused. However, if we get used to the accounting principles, we would be able to enjoy his class a lot.

I am taking his ACCY501 now.

When I first started taking his class, I was lost because of lack of my accounting knowledge.

However, when I ask him some questions, he teaches me well and responds me quickly.
Also, he sometimes gives us extra credit opportunities, and funny examples.

We have group pop quiz once a week. Overall, he is funny & kind!

The class was confusing and made no sense. Cold calls on students often. He tries hard to make examples to visualize concepts but ends up overcomplicating them in the end. You will struggle to memorize concepts just to pass the exam instead of actually understanding the concepts. Very helpful for homework help during office hours, though.

Ibrahim is an amazing professor! His lectures are very intense and really draining, but I swear he is there to teach you. The material is not easy, but he tries to make it as painless as possible. There's about one hw and in class exercise per week. Everything is open note. Not that bad, I swear!

His teaching style is better suited to textbook writing than explaining to students in that he delivers his knowledge in an extremely straightforward method that does little to help unearth additional understanding or provide greater context. Listening to this dry style over an extended period, it becomes difficult to latch onto the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing lecture with tough tests.
Professor Adel Ibrahim is amazing.

He knows the material very well and really knows how to give lectures. Becaise of majority of accy lectures are boring, Adel will call students' names occasionally to keep their attention. 
He gives harder exams comparing with other sections to make sure that his students aware of materials the chapter. 
Adel will give curves base on percentile.

Worst professor ever. I'm an accounting undergraduate and this is the hardest accounting course I've taken. Homework/quizzes/peer review/group projects/lectures, the work load is excessive. Quizzes are way more difficult than they should be and he doesn't give enough time to complete. Would NEVER take a course from him again. Terrible experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Sink or swim. You must have a solid foundation in accounting and keep up with his lecture materials as he expects everyone to know it by the lecture date. Doesn't do a good job explaining concepts. He gets visibly frustrated and loud during lectures, then tries to justify his actions by saying he's passionate about accounting. Hard quizzes and test

Quizzes and exams were too long for the time allowed. Not unusual for class averages on quizzes to be 60%. It's not that material is difficult, it's that you don't have the time to complete the quizzes. I frequently ran out of time with one problem unfinished (20% of the quiz).Initially refused to provide specific feedback to groups on projects.

Lectures are okay but he prides himself on grading hard with a curve. The problem is that the quizzes are way too long for the time allotted so he basically tests speed rather than knowledge. So disappointing.

All material including slides and problems just taken from the intermediate accounting. Adel takes pride in setting very hard exams with the expectation of scaling. Again all test questions are taken from the book. This is the first ACCY course I have got less than an A. Often gets visibly angry/frustrated when the class doesnt get it.

Professor As could be a good teacher. He really knows the lesson. I think the problem with him is that he is not a good lecturer. He does not explain very well and the tone of his voice (really high like screaming) make it really hard to catch up what he is saying. So I will say he knows the lesson but dont explain it really well.
na

Adel is probably the best instructor I've ever had. 517 is one of the toughest ACCY courses, but it's worth putting in the time.
