I usually have a hard time paying attention in ACCY lectures, but Adel always kept my attention and definitely makes lecture worthwhile. He explains difficult concepts in ways that just make everything click.

Arguably the hardest college class taken alongside Fin 300. You'll learn a decent amount but there's a fine line between what he teaches and what he tests on.  Overall, it can make for a pretty miserable experience and I'd recommend avoiding this teacher whenever possible.
The way he teaches makes you doubt if what he said is real. Would better be a good actor rather than a teacher.

The professor is amazing and always willing to help students. The course seems to be difficult at the beginning, but spend time and efforts on it, and try to understand the logic. If you understand the logic and the way of thinking, the homework and exams won't be that hard. You'll really learn something useful from this class. Worth it!!

ACCY 517 & Adel are the hardest class I have ever taken, including FIN 300.  I have learned so much from ACCY 517 and it is the most beneficial class I have ever taken in my collegiate career.  He pours his passion into the subject, he slows the class down when students don't understand, he holds tons of office hours to help.
He's a really good professor, I don't usually say that I enjoyed a class, but I enjoyed Adel's teaching style and his lectures.

The class is tough, not because of the professor but the actual material. The class requires a lot of time and effort. If you don't want to put in the time and effort this isn't the class for you. What you walk away from the class is knowing how to analyze the FS of a company. A skill I will carry on with me for the rest of my life.
This professor doesn't seem to control his anger. He yelled at his students and I was always uncomfortable in his class
Worst professor ever!! Cant explain anything but ends up putting very difficult exams.. Never take any of his classes.. Screams in class all the time! Talks nonsense half of the time

He is the worst professor I've ever had. He can't explain things clearly, but always has high expectations towards students. I guess what he wants is just making the students fail at his tricky exam. He always spends half of the class time talking about nonsense. That's why he can't catch up the class schedule or finish the class on time.
terrible course. he truly loves tricks but can never explain things clearly. always make simple things extremely hard to understand. also, he YELLED all the time. HURT TO EARS!
unique style. really helpful, force students to think.
Worst teacher ever. Do not take any of his classes. Unorganized teacher, mean, can't teach any topic in accounting.
One of the best professors in accounting department.
Amazing !!
His style of teaching is better than most instructor. He prepares wonderful questions for exams and force students to think about what they know.
Talked down to the class, was disorganized, workload was inappropriate and unclear.
If youre not a CS major and have a choice between taking this class and CS 101, PLEASE take 101. I was told 124 was easier. There is no way that is true
Explain things really well

why are we vibe coding in an intro level coding class? Got the feeling he would rather be giving ted talks about all the wonderful amazing benefits of AI rather than teaching. Though it's hard to rate him, as I only saw him in discussion maybe twice and never heard him speak a single word.

You will see the professor once at the start and never again. All the "lectures" are pre-recorded videos online, and the only help comes from fellow students who are "tutors". He specifically does not want you to email him and is very condescending in his response. Rely heavily on AI usage and requires you to pay for ClaudeAI premium yourself.

The class was chill enough until the final MP, which I think should be renamed to the "Geoffrey Challenge" because of how hard it was. Weekly quizzes, online work 5 days a week that can take 5 minutes to an hour depending on the assignment, overall not bad besides the final project which I think is like universally hated here.
Good teacher but the videos provided to self teach in this class are way to long and kinda boring, everything else about this course is good and fairly easy

Extremely inorganized course. Adding extra tasks before deadline. Never show up in classes. Getting confused about a question in an actual quiz? Congratulations! He doesn't have office hours and his TA cannot pull out the quiz for you.
The instructions for the tasks are unclear. He added a new task for the final project only a week before the due date, and couldn't give a clear instruction on how the gradebook works.
Clear lectures, fair exams.
Never show up in anywhere
"effort logging", with claude code. Hard to take this university seriously anymore.

Dislike him and his teaching style. Makes little to no acceptions for anything. Would NEVER take again. Attendance is now mandatory. He forces you to only use Claude code 4 the MP. You have to be ON TOP of your work every week - grades start plummeting quickly especially for the homeworks and quizzes which is a hefty amount of your grade.

It is surprising to incoming freshmen that it is online and self-paced. I, for one, liked it. The website is well organized, quizzes had practice which were almost identical. MPs weren't super hard; online office hours get overcrowded. Heard the class has changed massively recently, though. Proficiency testing out of this class is not a bad idea
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Daily lessons were pretty good, MP was not designed super well
I have seen the comment "His teaching style is decent" like wdym. HE DOES NOT TEACH BROTHER.
RUN. JUST RUN.

I get the impression that he does not really enjoy teaching. The course is essentially built around a website for students to teach themselves. While cs124 might seem straightforward at first, the lack of actual teaching makes it much more demanding than expected. You have to take on the full responsibility of learning the material on your own...
Is he hacking rmp to make his ratings higher? because he deserves 0
One of the worst classes I have taken in UIUC. For the prospective students, if you are reading this, please just take the proficiency test.

I am shocked by how this course is structured. It is entirely online and self-study. UIUC's CS is ranked among the top 5, and it is surprising to have a class where the prof seems largely disengaged and may not even be aware of what students are actually learning. I am definitely not the only one who feels this way, school needs to check this out.
I have never met the professor since the first discussion class. He does not have his own office hours either since he does not care about his students.

His teaching style is decent, and CS124 is an easy class if you are keeping pace. Most of the quizzes are easy, especially if you took a practice quiz, and you can make up missed quiz questions later for full credit. The tutoring system is also very well thought out and works great.

MPs are just vibe coding... 
you can't learn anything
How does he have a higher rating than Nowak, lol? Honestly, both of them are pretty rough CS instructors at UIUC. If I could, I would rate him a 0

The professor is almost never present in person. The course is essentially fully online, so you end up teaching most of the material to yourself. When you email the professor, you typically do not receive a response (or he responds but in an extremely rude way). He does not know how to respect students. Never take this course.
MP basically was intro to vibe coding. But eventually you gotta teach yourself!
Professor Challen is a really good teacher and cares a lot about what he is teaching. As long as you do the work and dont fall behind, then you will succeed in this class.

A fully-online* introductory programming class offered in two languages, probably easy for people with prior coding experience and challenging otherwise. The class is well-designed for an online class, but sometimes not engaging with too many videos. Changes coming next semester include (probably) required in-person discussion sections.

The CS 124 website is pretty helpful to learn all of the basics. The quizzes were alright, allowing for 1 retake the week after. However, the Machine Project at the end of the semester was harder than it needed to be. We didn't even apply what we learnt in the first half of the semester. It was just telling Claude code to pass the tests.

The class was easy since I was not new to programming. However, the project was a bit difficult. Make sure to do well in the first few quizzes since the last few can be hard. There is a quiz every week and no final exam. The quizzes offer a re-take of the previous week's quiz. I do think that he and the tutors can be kind of rude sometimes.
i mean its alright, a fine intro course, kotlin is chill and you get to vibecode

This course is overall very easy, especially after taking AP CSA in high school, but it's definitely still beginner-friendly. The course did not properly prepare for the MP at the end of the course, which was definitely the most frustrating part. Also, he and almost all tutors were often very aggressive when students would ask very valid questions.

Quizzes are 70% of course grade, but you can make corrections on them the following week after you take them the first time. MP is stupid and really complicated, but Challen is very nice and his videos are very informative and teach you well. It is very important to stay on track of daily lessons to keep up in the class.
Good lessons on CS124. I took APCSA in high school but didn't understand anything but I understood everything that was taught in this course

I took java in high school and the course was pretty easy, I capitalized on the quizzes and was able to not do much on the MP, MP was very confusing and the CA's sometimes lead you on a stray path rather than properly helping. Don't wait till last second on the MP, start early so you can get proper help.
Never saw him once. the whole thing was online

(Had prior Java experience) The everyday lectures and weekly quizzes were fine. Grading was fair. The MP was atrocious. Thrust into android programming without explaining most of what we were doing was recipe for disaster. Stack up extra credit from early deadlines so you can avoid doing the last parts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes and daily homework. Not hard as long as you put in some time and effort. I had some pre knowledge and slacked a bit but still was on the border of a B+/A-. The MP is hard but doable, just go to the in person tutoring at the CIF (online tutoring isn't very helpful).

It's a pretty manageable course as long as you put the time and work in. I did learn a lot and the lessons were usually pretty clear with multiple explanations for topics. There's a lot of time commitment with daily homework though. The MP was also a pretty big jump in difficulty from the work done throughout the semester.

Geoff, in my opinion, is a decent professor. He makes most things clear and gives you plenty of resources to succeed. This course is A LOT of work though. You'll be doing daily assignments and homework. It can be difficult but it is possible. My best advice for taking this course is to pay attention, ask for help, and google things occasionally.

i really enjoyed this course. the difficulty of the course depends on your experience coming in. i had no experience in cs at all but i found i could learn everything i needed through the course generally. BUT, some things aren't explained really clearly in the lessons and you may benefit from outside resources and def the tutoring site...

I think that this is a pretty good course, with good and helpful videos, but it is definitely intense. You can take it as an intro class but it will probably require a fair amount of work if you haven't coded before. I think that the machine project is somewhat poorly managed, but it is very doable especially with the extra credit offered.

Challen is not a bad person, he does offer alot of quirks for extra credit. However this class is ALOT of work especially if this is your first coding class, NOT beginner friendly and moves at a fast pace. There are weekly quizzes which are alot of work. If you have never coded do not take class along with 3 tech class u will be miserable.

Fully-online daily lectures, lessons, and homework. Weekly quizzes that aren't super difficult. Class is easy for the most part, the semester project can be difficult if you're new to coding.  Online tutors are always busy so go to the in person tutoring. Utilize course forum, as you will prob never speak to challen in person.

I get a high grade but I will not say I ace in Java after this class. Only finished 40 percent of the lectures because I was dissociating of his metaphor all the time, not very intuitive and it's definitely better turn to Youtube. Be aware of BIG lines when you want to get some in-person tutoring for mp, which for many of you have to do.

It is an online lecture based class. If you are new to coding, please for the love of god go to the in person discussion to get help if you need. Online tutors do not help at all. Other than that, no matter previous experience, you will be fine if you put the work in. If you dont put work in, you will suffer even if you are good at coding.

This is a very good course that teaches you how to write and implement codes. Although there is a quiz once a week, you'll be fine if you review the lessons carefully and do some practice problems. Professor Challen is a good instructor, and he often answers questions I posted on the forum. The grading policies are also very lenient. Easy A.

Great instructor, made learning Java fun and informative. Most of his homework is easy but some will stump you. Excellent material to prepare for exams. The final MP for the class is the most difficult aspect of it which you may find to get stuck on. Depending on class TA's you may be helped or provided little direction but the project is doable.

Geoffrey Challen (previously gwa) is a character. My favorite pastime is logging onto the forum to see 80 new questions with only 10 one-word answers by Geoffrey which are at best useless and at worst rage maxxing. Do you know how infuriating it is to wake up in cold sweat after reading the words "what debugging steps have you taken?" everyday.

As someone who's taken AP CS A before, I have no idea how anyone in CS 124 w/ no prior Java experience could succeed. The class is structured in a weird way, and the final MP deals with topics that we have never learned before. Geoff gets angry whenever someone asks for help, ignoring half the questions about grading in an attempt to be mysterious.
very hands off and fast paced

Challen knowns a lot about what he is teaching however CS 124 is not a course for a student who has no experience in coding. The course goes at an insane pace, weekly quizzes that are very hard to study for, the TA's aren't helpful, and at the end of the semester you are thrown into a final project that is really confusing with little guidance.
Lectures were clear, and while the prof doesn't provide much 1-on-1 help, the weekly quizzes and challenging MPs kept me on track. I found Unstuck ai super helpful for quiz prep - saved me some time.

Funny how previous classes had starter code and the Homework was worth more as a percent of grade, therefore you're getting punished for taking the class later, funny aint it? Love the way the practice quizzes aren't representative of the exam, so sad!

He clearly knows his stuff and can teach it pretty well, but it's just confusing when you get to the project. Generally, I usually felt pretty well about the course until the project, but still, it wasn't that hard bc of AI.
absolute stressful and awful experience

He was chill but gave no guidance whatsoever. We had to do a lot of things, and since everything was horrendously taught, you were on your own. The MPs were hell because they threw you into Android Studio with zero preparation, which wasn't very pleasant. Thankfully, we could use ChatGPT(it was allowed for the MP) because it made no sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably won't have face to face interactions with Geoffrey, but his lectures were clear for the most part.

CS 124 itself was structured decent. Expect weekly quizzes (2 hours of studying), + 1 hour of daily homework/lessons. There is a useful help site as well.

The prof. takes feedback and cares and is decent w/ his videos, but sometimes his material is irrelevant to quizzes. For Machine Projects or hard HWs, use AI because lessons aren't good enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The course was online, but the only interaction from the professor was his reused recorded lesson videos from who knows how many semesters ago. The course was not objectively difficult, but it was often hard to pay attention and get through all the content in the daily lessons. Not all the topics were covered in detail and were often pretty long.

This class is structured to be as hands off as possible for Geoffrey. After creating the initial content its essentially reused work semester to semester. And this is honestly a good thing. Geoffrey is not helpful and doesn't want to be. He clearly wants to put off as much as he can on the 200 different Assistants and collect his paycheck.
He's cool

I had almost zero experience in programming, and this was the perfect intro to cs for me. prof challen always go above and beyond when explaining concepts. My favorite memories from this class are when he takes 10 minutes explaining a concept, then write the whole logic in one line.
He's a great professor also a nice person. The syllabus is kind. The challenging tasks are the MPs, also the weekly quizzes. Overall, you work hard, you will get an A

This course is pretty difficult for those who never coded before, I think I spent around an hour minimum everyday on the lessons to keep up with the coursework. It is straightforward if you do the work, but what was frustrating was that when I was sick, the profressor didn't offer many accomodations and recommended that I drop the course instead.

As someone who did not have any previous coding experience, this course was difficult for a supposedly "introductory course." There are daily lessons that took around 40-80 minutes and quizzes every week which are straightforward if you keep up with the work everyday, but they don't offer many accommodations to missing work when you are sick.

Even if you didn't take APCSA, which I didn't, the class is still very easy and it's not hard to keep up. Expect 40-80 min of work a day. Love the help site and the help staff! Some of the walkthroughs should be abridged, but most were fine. Quizzes are very straightforward, and you get drops. I would definitely not call it a nightmare.

The class is completely online and asynchronous. Daily homework assignments, weekly quizzes, and no final exam. Towards the end of the semester, there are 2 MPs. These were tough because support is hard to find and they're new. The website was very well organized though, and many drops were offered for homework and quizzes. Def recommend!

Class is decently easy as long as you keep up with daily lessons, the TAs on the help site were great. Easy to see how to earn points but finally grading scale happens at end of year but most will get an A so don't worry. Lecture recordings felt longer than they needed to be, and the MP could use some better explaining but the TAs are great help.

The course itself is fairly easy. Tests are pretty straightforward but daily lessons were too long and repetitive. The professor offered no support through the forum or help site. He also lacks compassion. I had a medical condition at the start of the semester and inquired about a 1 day extension on homework and he suggested that I drop the class.

CS124 is a class set up for you to succeed. If you put in the work, you can easily get an A (no A+s). However, in terms of support from Challen, don't expect any. He will almost always direct you to the tutoring site; however, the TAs and CAs on there are extremely helpful especially when the MP is on, queue is on the longer wait time though.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had Java experience before, though it could be difficult for those without. All interactions are with course staff at not Challen, MPs were hard (don't delay those), and voice recordings got old fast, but the course is designed for everyone to get a good grade (with a good amount of drops). So you can learn a lot and get a good grade (avg. 95%).

Extremely slow and repetitive. You have to be incredibly patient to listen to someone saying the same thing for over 15 minutes. Problem is (and this was a challenge for me), during those 15 minutes, he does say some important things in the middle. So after losing attention due to repetition I needed to rewatch the whole thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is a good introductory class, but if you haven't taken APCSA, it can go by really fast and it can be hard to keep up. If you have taken it, then it becomes a lot of review and not that worth it. The lectures can be annoying at times and long, but they are easy enough. The HW was never too hard to manage and the help was good too.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: My first CS course, a living hell and a nightmare. Would not recommend it for people who are unfamiliar with programming and have a decent workload. Time-consuming, daily homework. Many people found this course easy, but there are also many who are struggling through it. Poor explanations, doesn't know how to teach.

Nothing to say about the professor; from my point of view, those lectures are clear and straightforward. CS124 itself is easy, so I never went to the office hours. The most challenging part is the quizzes since there is nothing for you to prepare with them. Generally, if you put effort into it, you will get a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
This is a coding class that encourages you to not test your code. All the assignments are hosted through the website but he doesn't let you copy / paste so it's hard to test it in an environment that actually allow unit tests.

I honestly thought he was joking half the time because the stuff he was telling us was so wrong.

CS 125 in a nutshell:

1. Challen builds own website.
2. Part of website doesn't work.
3. Someone reports that part of website doesn't work.
4. Challen gets mad about it and doesn't want to accept responsibility.

Easily the most egotistical teacher I've had in my time at Illinois.
the videos are annoying. make sure to watch them at no less than 1.5x speed to save some time

He's okay. Lecture is understandable, not too much homework, office hour avaliable for everyone. Just the attitude is not great, he always seem to have a bad day, and when you meet him in OH he will not explain further about anything he said in the lecture, even some of those are confusing.
There were very few times when I felt lost in this course, even as a beginner to Java. Just make sure to do all of the homeworks. Grading policy is very fair.

If you put in work this class is an easy A. That being said there is a lot of homework and weekly quizzes, although I thought the class was totally fair and think anyone can succeed. Do not get behind on homework and the MP, try to do all of the homework a bit early and take advantage of the help site. I chose Kotlin, and enjoyed the class greatly.

Get ready for a world of pain. 
A new Lesson every day from Monday to Friday, each due the day after it is scheduled.
Each lesson is 45 minutes of reading and watching the lecture, and the homework itself takes half an hour upto 2 hours.
Do not fall behind on your homework or quizzes.
Work in groups, and make sure to get those MPs in early

despite having decent lectures, he provides zero actual help. The course staff are not well versed enough in CS to provide adequate help to all the people in the course, and Challen is pretty much MIA when you need him. Also, the MPs are nothing like what we learn about in class but he expects you to know how to do them yourself.

Challen has created the CS124 website to have a HEALTHY buffer of course assistants and TAs to provide help to the students with their computer science problems. This is good; however, if you have an issue with something that the help site cannot solve, good luck because if you contact him directly he will just push you back to the help website.
Provides little to not help on instruction. Students that do not already have a background in computers should stay far away.

I mean the mps were too hard for me. Every week we have quizzes and we had to study online, so inefficient and so much work of research needed on our end. For those that doesn't have a lot of time and no prior experience should rethink wether to take this course.

The course as a whole is pretty good. Challen's videos and walkthroughs are the best and he is quite personable. On the forum he does come off as condescending and definitely has built a hierarchy so that he can have as little interaction with students as possible. Overall, CS124 has a beautiful website and a great overall structure.
You do not know what you're signed up for until week 4.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

He said it himself that the class was not going to get easier. The concepts were not even difficult, I felt confident in the material, but the exam covered nothing that was going on in class. Do not take his class.
Gives bad lectures with useless lecture slides that don't relate to course material. Gives extra credit to curve a bit as well as simple(ish) exams.
Test materials are mostly not from lecture slides.

Only reads off powerpoints, which consist of screenshot from textbook. Lectures are useless, midterms doesn't correlate to difficulty of homeworks, lectures. Would never take his class again unless necessary. Should stop teaching.

This professor's course is tough. Last year's exams were Excel-based, but SOA said it was too easy, so now there are 3 paper midterms with 5 questions each. You need 85% for UEC credit, but one mistake ruins it. His lectures are unclear, reviews are useless, and exams don't match. Passing the FM exam outside school is easier.

I've had Icaza a few times and I enjoy his classes. For 210 I thought he just read off the slides too much, but I did get an A. For 406 and 411 I think he did a great job of explaining the concepts and giving us study materials (past tests, annotated slides, etc.). Homework was fair and he's very clear about his expectations. Good dude.

Lecture is lengthy it is and all he does is go off powerpoint slides. Class itself wasn't too hard as long as you do the homework and review you should be fine. He suggest to do the reading, but it isn't that helpful. You can still pass with an A without doing the reading. He is very easy to access outside of class and helps break concepts down.

Personally, I did not enjoy having Icaza as an instructor. He would only read off of powerpoint slides (mind you this is linear algebra...) and overall it was waste of time. I will say the review days for exams and final exam were helpful and made studying for and taking them easy.

Overall I thought the class was well structured and not too hard. Professor Icaza is a kind professor who will help you with material. My only complaint is that the lectures rarely go much deeper than whats on the slides. It would be so much better if he focused more on practice problems and participation than just reading what's on the slides
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Excellent professor, hard class, & I asked a lot of questions, but each time he responds, the answer is always detailed & direct. As long as you take the time to study for his exams, you should be fine. I highly recommend attending lectures. He goes over examples and concepts with clarity, and the lecture is always open for questions. Definite 5/5.
very bad pedro cimentada 4D
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: If youre fine working 90% of the class in groups this is your class, but honestly its too much information, and most of the work has to be done in groups which is not for me, because not all people participate, for me this class was so confusing, and unclear most of the time.
Ane is literally one of the best TA's I have ever had! Her passion for teaching has no bounds, and she is so incredibly approachable and sweet.

The class is a bit difficult, but Ane does an amazing job of explaining everything. She definitely makes the material & class fun/interesting. She will help you if you don't get the material. You have 3 exams & a final project, which isn't too bad. Lots of class participation so make sure you go to class. She posts the slides online too.

Ane is amazing and I'm bummed I won't be able to take another class with her. I definitely learned more about the Spanish language in one semester in her class than I have in all previous years of taking Spanish.

Ane is by far my favorite professor I have had at U of I. She is attentive, cares about her students, and does a great job of explaining things you are confused about. Although the content of Span 303 was not my favorite, she made it super enjoyable.

This was Ane's first semester teaching SPAN 208 and I think she did a great job of it, considering she's used to teaching more lecture heavy classes. She's extremely hilarious and it definitely seemed like everyone in the class enjoyed being there! It's a speaking class, so just make sure you participate and you should be golden!
A lot of homework, hard to understand.

Class is fairly simple all the way through. It is sometimes hard to tell what parts of the lectures are important or not, but the homeworks are a good representation of the exams. Professor is funny and not too strict, but attendance is randomly taken and for a grade. At least he gives 2 drops.

Prof Nikolaev is the perfect professor for this course. The homework can take a few hours but is mostly straight-forward. If you understand the content, the exam problems are easy--no tricks or surprises. There is a dramatic increase in intricacy at the end of the class, but it is completely manageable if you practice and review the online notes.

Amazing class. Everything you learn is a cool interesting twist on something youve learned in the past. Igor is a super nice professor, highly recommend going to his office hours just to work on the homework. Tests are easy compared to the homeworks which aren't bad either. Highly recommend this class
Funny if you listen carefully. flies through lectures, you will have to go back after class.  Office hours are your friend

I did not like this class and I could not understand what the professor was saying. The class does not prepare you for the exams and is just hard. He was a kind teacher, but just the way he taught the material was very difficult to understand.
Perfect professor.

Really kind and caring professor! His lectures and notes are pretty dense, you cover a lot in just one lecture, but he does explain things thoroughly and provide relevant examples for the hw/exams. Exams were pretty fair and reasonable so long as you do the hw and look at lecture examples. Overall, a nice professor!

Gives very dense lectures that are somewhat hard to follow in class because of how much he throws at you, but gives enough examples that once you return to your notes, it'll all make sense. He tests you hard on how well you conceptually understand what he teaches and won't just hand you points (same for 444), so don't take him lightly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Very good lecturer who cares about his students. Teaches in a fairly rigorous way, so I think you should have some proof-based math experience before taking his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is so caring and a wonderful lecturer. I am taking Math 446 this semester with him again and I feel so lucky. Best Math Professor ever.

Prof Igor is a really nice guy. Although he gives lots of homework, he sets the mid terms really easy. His classes are more proof based which makes them slightly boring. He is very easy to talk to and willingly helps to clear your doubts. On the flip side, the course is rigorous, questions are asked on proving math theorems etc
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is so caring and almost perfect when giving lectures. Best math course I have ever taken!

Definitely a hard course, but he makes it as simple as possible. His lecture is perfect and he posts well-written lecture notes online, so do not worry if you miss a class. If you have anything unclear about the course, go and ask him during office hours or through e-mail. He will answer everything clearly and thoroughly.

Professor Nikolaev likes to teach in depth of the materials. People usually don't get the point the first time. He makes the materials hard but reading notes helped a ton. Professor Nikolaev is super helpful outside of the classes. He basically wants you in all his office hours and he will do the homework for you. He curves so MUCH in tests/quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the hardest math classes but if you work hard, it pays off. Study from day 1 or else it's impossible to keep up. Work with a bright classmate on homeworks. Tips for scoring high: prepare for midterms really well, they are quite doable once you figure out the system. The final exam is a killer so dont leave it to the last to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This course is tough and you'd better be well-prepared. Make full use of the lecture notes because the textbook is useless for most of the time.

This professor was amazing and felt like learning from my grandpa. Didn't know what he was saying half the time, but I learned math notation really well from him. Exams were weirdly hard and I always felt like I was on a different page than he was. All in all though, it wasn't bad because he'd solve the honors homework for you if you got stuck.

Not the most interesting material but he does a pretty solid job explaining concepts - some days better than others but overall not bad at explaining most of the proofs.  Extremely proof-heavy (expected) and errors in his online notes but not a difficult class.  Tests are easy-6 questions you choose 4 and he tells you 3 a week early (Thm proofs)
Took honors section of MATH 231, loved it, hard and super proof heavy but learned a ton. Always happy to help if you show up to office hours, really hard class, but super rewarding.

Great notes, made them available online after lecture. Strict on attendance. Homework out of the book was a bit difficult, but this was good practice for exams. Exams though, were quite difficult, grading techniques were pretty harsh. If you go to lecture, pay attention, do your homework, and study you'll do fine. If you dont, well...

Worst teacher ive had. Ever. Spends too much time proving theorems, neglects to teach how to apply them. Seems to assume you already know material. Office hours directly after class(middle of day)and on days after homework turn in and before you know enough to try the next. Always behind, takes attendance, so hard to go to other lectures to learn.

Lectures were dry--he would go through proofs of theorems with a few examples here and there for the entire time. His exams were great, though. Each was 6 problems, of which we had to do 4. Of these, 3 were hw problems and 3 were proofs taken from a list given to us to study from. Overall decent teacher for a challenging course.
Good notes, fair tests

Presentation of material isn't very clear, neglects to explain fundamentally important things.  He runs through everything on the board too fast.  It seems like he assumes that everyone already knows the material and expects everyone to instantly know whats going on with minimal explanation.  I wish I signed up for a different section.

Extremely useful, helpful I`ve ever had in this school. Teaches clearly with examples, puts every lecture notes on website. And interesting. Tests are not hard at all. Tells exactly what is gonna be on test. Little Russian accent, but understandable. Overall, great professor.

With all honesty, he is probably the easiest Math 241 teacher.  I don't know why all these people are giving him such poor grades.  Sure his Russian accent is a little thick, but I think he is a great teacher.  He goes a lot slower than the other Calc 3 teachers (often behind by 1 chapter), but that's only because he does so many examples in class

Wonderful professor: teaches very clearly. Generous grading scale and willing to give extra credit. Puts all lectures and homework solutions on internet. Extremely helpful during office hours: encourages questions and does not mind staying late. (Slight accent, but easy to understand.)

Good Professor, but definitely one of the harder 221 Sections(You will learn a lot). Test can be scary but he gives huge curves and with his grading scale a 56 is still passing. Comes from Russia so he has a bit of an accent but he is easy to understand. Makes really corny jokes.

Tests were difficult. The curve was not substantial. Homework and quiz grades only accounted for 25% of the total, and the rest was tests. I think that another teacher would probably be easier, but he is fair enough if you have to take a class with him.

His exams compared to other professors exams are levels harder. The homework assigned in class does not prepare you for the exams either. The lectures are not too bad. I didn't find his accent to be to thick. Hard to take notes in class because he has them pre-written and just flies through them. I do not suggest for Math 221.
Teaching was okay. Did a lot of proofs which was not required. Exams were not hard, but a little tricky. Understanding of topic is important as he'll test your fundamentals.

I took calc in high school and excelled really well. I thot I would take this class as reinforcment b4 calc 2.  Big mistake.  I am now no longer going to continue with math after this class. He is a nice guy but not a good teacher.  Does not explain things well, but he does drop a lot of low grades and curves all the tests...

It is not so much him that I do not like.  It is just that the TA does not speak english well enough to teach our class.  He has an extremely thick Russian accent that I can not understand very well either

His accent isn't too bad, it just takes a couple of lectures to get used to; you also have to get used to some different terminology he uses (ie "modulus" for "absolute value") other than that, he's great. He goes through multiple examples for each concept so it should be really clear as to what he wants on tests.

His accent isn't too bad, it just takes a couple of lectures to get used to; you also have to get used to some different terminology he uses (ie "modulus" for "absolute value") other than that, he's great. He goes through multiple examples for each concept so it should be really clear as to what he wants on tests.
He does have an accent but he explains everything very clearly. He actually works through problems and explains how he goes about them. Best math prof I've had at UIUC.

I don't understand all these people who complain about Professor Nikolaev.  The class was very easy as long as you do the homework.  His lectures were very helpful understanding the material.  As it is calculus 3, its not easy to get a good grade with out putting in much effort, but definately one of the best professors you can have for math 241.

Horrible textbook first of all.  Tests seem easy however grading is very harsh.  Questions seem unrelated to concepts taught in class.  Hard to follow lectures due to complex notation that is not explained.  Friends in Denka's class say she is a better professor.  Avoid Igor in 241 if possible.
His accent is really not bad AT ALL. His tests are VERY fair if you do the homework.  He does a pretty good job explaining things. I'd recommend taking a course with him if you have the option.
This man is horrible, thick accent, doesn't explain things well, and impossible to understand his lectures... the only thing good about him was that the tests weren't that hard and one got curved.

Explains lots of examples in lecture, and posts everything online.  Tests are very reasonable but might catch you off guard if you aren't prepared.  The grading is also very beneficial.  Best math teacher I had at U of I, is also easy to understand so don't be discouraged by the name.

One of the best math teachers I have ever had, I learned so much, and on top of that his class and tests weren't overly hard.  You have to apply yourself a little in his class, but if you do you won't have too hard a time.
Just don't take him. Every other option is better. His lectures are a complete waste of time. I didn't go to anyone's lectures and did great overall.

Extremely off topic, did not cover content at all and frequently behind schedule. It was clear he did not care about students learning. Struggled with technology and went on rambles about unrelated topics.  Very nice and kind but extremely unaware of the rigor of the course. I went to Bhowmik

Professor Iyer is a nice guy and a very knowledgeable about ECE. His lectures devolve into tangents(mostly about the Blackwell chip), he is hard to understand and frequently mumbles, and he frequently skips slides. His slides are hard to follow and use Google ai. Would not reccomend

Professor Iyer's lectures often wandered into incoherence and unrelated tangents: although the class itself was extremely interesting, the way it was managed and structured was atrocious. It must be re-worked entirely to maintain the engagement of students and reduce the amount of stress it causes, especially for a freshman class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class itself was not that difficult, but unfortunately Professor Iyer's lectures were not the best, evidenced by the ever dropping attendance in lecture to the point that only 1-2 rows of seats are filled in class. Prof. Iyer murmurs so you can barely hear half the time, and often forgets to put the slides up. Those sequoia trees were nice.

DONT TAKE IYERS LECTURE BRO IS LIKE THE ULTIMATE YAPPER ABT ANYTHING BUT THE COURSE CONTENT he does not teach properly and is always behind on lecture slides until he suddenly decides to do smth funny, skip a bunch of slide sets, and all of a sudden be like wow we're ahead for once! the only thing that makes this course hard is iyers poor teaching

Absolutely do NOT take your 120 lecture with Iyer. He really does not care about covering course content and oftentimes struggles to utilize technology to the fullest. Additionally, he loves going on tangents and does not get through the course content even with his overwhelming use of AI. I deeply regret registering for this lecture!  :(

If at all possible, do NOT take Professor Iyer for ECE120. If for some reason you have to take his lecture section, attend another professor's lecture if at all possible. Professor Iyer often got sidetracked talking about material irrelevant to your success in the course, and he will consistently fail to get through all of the content for the day.

He gives pop quizzes but never put in the extra credit grade for them like the other lecturers. He doesn't know how a mic works or the projector. You will have a difficulty absorbing the material covered in his slides which is very important for discussions and homeworks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you get him as a prof just know you are going to learn nothing from the leature and you will have to go to office hours and talk to ta's and other student in order to learn course content I suggest you sit in on another prof's leature to actually learn something if possible
YOU MEAN YOU CANT SEE BEHIND THE TREES?

iyer will make a joke once and repeat it every lecture after that until it's more beaten than a dead horse. you know what he won't repeat? the course content. he yaps the whole time but still skips over EVERYTHING IMPORTANT. what i would give to go back in time and hit myself on the head with a 200 pound weight to prevent myself from taking ts

This guy is super nice and super approachable, but an absolute joke when it comes to teaching. He spends the class reviewing slides full of useless information instead of what we actually need to know, speeding through important stuff like he's allergic to it. ECE is already hard enough, but this guy just makes it extra confusing.

Whoever gave Iyer good reviews is actually an opp. He goes on many tangents during lectures, does not seem interested in the subjects covered, and talks about topics that will never appear on any test, quiz or any other grading metric. Going to Iyer's lectures is less worthwhile than skipping. Choose sleep, don't choose Iyer.

Never on topic during lectures, always a gamble with whether or not there will be a quiz when he says there's going to be one, never fixes technical issues (mic not working, projector broken, slides not showing), wastes entire lectures on topics that will never appear on the exam, uses google AI screenshots as part of his slides, DO NOT TAKE

Professor Iyer is a clear and knowledgeable instructor for ECE 120. He explains tough topics well and connects them to real-world uses. The course is hard, especially if you're new to programming or logic, but it's very rewarding. His lectures are organized, and if you keep up, you'll build a strong foundation. Made with ChatGPT
You can tell teaching is the eternal burning fire in his heart called passion.
Great professor, loved how he took the time to teach. Thank you for letting me get an A.
Iyer is so good that it wasn't even worth going to lecture. I didn't attend a single one for half the semester, that is how good Iyer is. He's so good.
This professor is the best professor I have ever had, he is so engaging and awesome and I got an A+ because of him.

Touch grader. Get your points off for some tiny details Unrealistic exams and MPs, so if you do not understand the topics beforehand, the things he teaches does not prepare you at all for his class. Also mandatory lectures, which sucks.

From my understanding, the special 313 section is the lesser of two evils. That being said, this class still made me feel very stupid. IMO, the TA's and Iyer did a very poor job teaching the concepts of this course. I had no idea what was going on for the last few hw assignments. The MP's were kind of interesting, but also not very straightforward.
Great teacher, enthusiastic lecturer.

Boring class but I appreciate how engaged he is during lectures. He is extremely funny and I did learn some interesting material. participation pop quizzes force you to show up because you don't know which class he will give you one in, and the two hw assignments are dumb but a good grade booster. Tests are  easy and the labs are useless but free A
Professor is fine and class is easy but Dr. Wang was often unresponsive to emails and way too much of the grade is attendance.

Lecture was informative+prof was knowledgeable. Grading was not prompt. While theres a homework category worth 10%, we were only given two homework assignments towards the end of the semester. The in-class quiz category is worth 16%, which is more than what an exam is worth (13%), so if you miss a class your grade average is significantly affected
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took the 4 week summer offering of GEOL 117: The Oceans. Goes by fast, but engaging and inspiring! Looking into minoring in oceanography or earth sci. after this? Cool class and great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took the class over winter break. The only part I didn't like were the discussion sections, but only because the 4 week course meant that I had about 3/week. Other than that, interesting class! A bit difficult because I'm not a science major, but pretty straightforward. Grades were released late but it wasn't a big deal.

Honestly just don't take GEOL 117 online. The textbook is $90 and then you're forced to pay $25 to take the final on ProctorU. The class is way too much work for a gened and the final is so ridiculously hard that he had to curve the exam. Just save yourself the hassle and money. He's a super nice guy but this class is not worth it.

Professor/Dr. Pettijohn is one of the best professors I've had at UIUC! I was struggling a lot mentally last semester, and he extended a lot of help to help me succeed. It's difficult to find empathetic professors in STEM, and Professor P is the exact antithesis of that stereotype. Although there is a lot of content, the lectures are interactive.

Fantastic professor in every aspect. The only negative comment I would provide is that for this specific class, a $100ish purchase of Pearson is required. Other than that, he is the most caring as well as effective professor!!! 10/10! Very knowledge able on what he is teaching!
Amazing professor! So understanding and helpful. He replies so fast answering any questions. Super fun and easy class if you put the work in.
One of the best professors I've had my whole entire college career. Very engaging and very passionate about his work. He is very funny and makes you actually like the class.
Prof Pettijohn is a very caring instructor. GEOL117 is a class that you can get a solid grade in as long as you put in the effort.

Great professor. He is so enthusiastic about this course and you can tell he wants every student to succeed. He offers lots of extra credit as well. All of the homework and assignments are discussed in his lectures, wish all of my professors were like him!
class is lecture heavy, memorization heavy, and VERY time consuming, but if you are willing to put in the work, it is an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Pettijohn is great! GEOL 104 is super interesting, it was a fully asynchronous class and it wasn't too difficult. There were no exams, but a big final project. Content was super interesting. He also offers a good amount of extra credit. If you ever need help, he will definitely find you an answer in a timely manner. Definitely recommend!

There was a lot of information in this class and there is one cumulative final. However, it is open book. Although the lectures are pretty easy to follow, it requires a lot of paying attention and he tends to talk pretty fast in the recorded lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great Professor, lectures were interesting with real world connections.
Easy gen ed

This class covers a lot of interesting material about the oceans and climate change through discussion posts and lectures. It's not difficult to understand and he's very very flexible with due dates. If you need to take a science course I would 1000% recommend this over anything.
Interesting content with short lectures that get to the point. Easy homework and grading.

I took this course online for a gen ed credit. It was a 4 week class, which is very intense no matter what you take. The grading was clear, the content was interesting, and the instructor was quick to respond. There is a lot of reading and online module learning to complete, but it was pretty well structured. It was interesting overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Very flexible on deadline if you explain the reasons. Responsible and Approachable teacher and answers email really quick. He understands students' needs and anxiety. He offers great amount of extra credit, and the final is quite manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 8-week class full of information so be prepared to read! Dr. Pettijohn is such an engaging teacher and is very knowledgable. This is my second class with him and if given the chance I would take another. He answers your email faster than any professor I have ever had and is always willing to help. I highly recommend taking any class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--EXTRA CREDIT--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is a really nice guy and he responds to his emails. There is video lecture for the online class and assignments due Friday and Sunday night. If you actually try you will probably get an A. I didn't try at all so I got a B but that was the result of my own laziness. He gives a lot of extra credit.

If you have the option to take a class with Dr. Pettijohn you should take that opportunity! He is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. He genuinely cares and always makes time to help. The class is super cool and I learned a lot. Make sure you make time to do the modules and you should be fine!

There's a lot of work but Pettijohn is my favorite! Very understanding and some very fun lecture videos where his cat makes appearances. There is a lot to do sometimes, but you just do it and get on. He is super great at responding and always helps if needed! Love my class with him!
Very good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I took GEOL 117 during the winter and it was my first time taking a 4-week online course. The work was supposed be very intense, but Dr. Pettijohn was very helpful and accepted late work for points off. He was very understanding of our personal lives, and made the class enjoyable. He loved to get feedback on the assignments as well. Great class!

Professor Pettijohn is overall a great instructor, advisor and person. If you can take one of his classes, do it!! He's passionate about everything he teaches and he genuinely wants the best for all of his students. This class is a lot of work/very accelerated because it's an 8 week class but he made me really enjoy it!!!

Professor Pettijon is really energetic about teaching and cares about his students. Most of the work in the class is reading from the textbook and watching lectures based on the chapters, with some reading quizzes too. A good chunk of work, but a fun course about the oceans if you're interested.

Prof. Pettijohn is such a great professor. Sometimes online classes can get boring, but he is VERY engaging and passionate about what he teaches. He structures the class very well too. As long as you focus on the lectures and don't let assignments slip by, this is an easy class. Plus, you'll actually learn meaningful things!

The class is a well rounded course where the professor is patient and does not skip steps or large portions of dense material. This is a great class to take for a general education credit. It keeps your brain working.
Dr. Pettijohn is the sweetest thing. He really want you to do well and is flexible on extensions and is very accessible. Great class!
He is a pretty good instructor, but because I am currently taking this course in an eight week format, the information does seem a bit rushed, but it is supposed to be an accelerated course.

Very interesting class with relaxed workload and pacing. Dr. Pettijohn was very attentive and responsive to questions and really tried his best to make the experience as good as possible for everyone.
Great teacher! Very engaged with students and very passionate about what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall, Dr. Pettijohn made a fun and engaging learning environment for The Oceans. Everything was easy to find and complete with a clear due dates. The workload was not bad and we connected with other students despite the online nature of the course. I would take another course with him as the professor.

I'm an online degree student and I took Prof Pettijohn my first semester and he set the bar so high for all my future professors. He is passionate about what he teaches and his lectures are engaging. He incorporates informative and inspiring articles and videos into the learning materials. He grades fair, if you do the work you should pass.
Was able to make online classes accessible and engaging! His enthusiasm about the material is apparent and makes lectures enjoyable. Very easy to reach over email and has a cute cat to boot!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Mrs. Pettijohn is a great professor to work with. He is really nice and reachable at anytime. :)
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Pettijohn is very caring for his students and helps with any problem you have with the course. He gives good feedback and are well prepared before class. He gives related material with the course and includes many activities. The 8 weeks section is pretty short and intense for me but I would recommend to those who like ocean.
Really had lots of materials to memorize, but Prof. Pettijohn really did a great job in organizing them.
Best Professor ever. Love his online course. He really cares about students and responds really quick. Extra credits every week.

Makes a full effort to accommodate all students in any situation, even recorded himself voicing over the required videos because some of the students thought the voices were unpleasant. Cares a whole lot about everyone learning and passing but packs a lot of information in so you will still have to work for your grade. Ideal teacher overall.
Would absolutely take again

reviews.comment: Great class but since I took the 8 week course there is a lot of information and work to do for it. Overall, would recommend. They give out extra credit every week so that was really helpful.
He is a great professor. Recommend to take this course.

Prof Pettijohn is one of the best professors I have had at UIUC. He is thoughtful, easily accessible, and his enthusiasm and upbeat personality really helps you engage in the material and get excited about the class. I would most certainly take a class taught by him again and anyone who is interested in geology/ the oceans should take his class!

Awesome professor, especially for an online-class. You can tell he is super passionate about the issues he includes in the curriculum. The professor is extremely organized and clear about the grading criteria. There is an unbelievable amount of extra credit offered and if you are on top of your workload, it is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great Prof and great class. Prof lectures are focused and succinct, and somewhat interactive (you will actually pay attention). I have taken many courses with Prof Pettijohn and think he is one of UI's best for online learning.

Really great professor. You take his class because you're interested in the subject and then love it by the end because of the passion he puts into it. Do the work and it's an easy A. Definitely would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

Online courses can be very "alienating."  A student can feel alone with the material, but Pettijohn did everything to make sure that did not happen.  This is a difficult class, but worth it

great class! lots of work, but fun to learn the geology of the national parks after a few road trips to parks with my dad and sisters growing up
He's a great professor and I would recommend anyone to take his a least once. He works with you and helps you understand what he is teaching in the class.

This professor is one of the BEST! Highly recommend him! He's tough but fair. His online lectures are by far one of the best and most engaging online lectures out there! There is quite a bit of coursework but nothing too difficult.

Prof Pettijohn is awesome! Hands down best professor I've ever worked with. He's fair, super understanding, and so funny. A very informative experience for all! :D

Always sending e-mails with explanations, quick to respond, and very understanding!  Does everything he can to help his students succeed.

really helpful professional development assignments that made the class extra good
Great Class!

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the lecture given by Prof Pettijohn. He's always very quick to respond to emails and is very understanding of students when we come across problems in the course. Because the course is 3 credit hours, and only eight weeks, the work load is pretty intense but overall worth it!

One of the best online professors I have ever had.  Makes lectures interesting, informative, and comparatively short.  Second online course I have taken with him and I highly recommend both courses to anyone considering.  Uses newer technologies for course so it's not same old boring slides and audio.
excellent instructor & always available for questions!

Hard Class but Great Teacher, well worth it. You need to buy the book and it is online also.  Beware of deadlines because they matter. He will work with you if you start to fall behind, hes really encouraging in that way. I'm glad I took the class, it was a lot of work but he kept it interestin and I learned a lot of new things. So, it was worth it

Prof. Pettijohn is awesome!! He gives the best feedback and makes you feel like you're doing a great job. Emails (that he responds to super fast) are very personalized and detailed regarding assignments and your progress. Even tho the class is a lot of work at times, his weekly reminders make it very manageable and, dare I say, fun!

Be prepared to work on the class almost every day, as you can quickly fall behind. This online class was not like other online classes I've taken or heard about (in a good way) and was very engaging. I'm graduating and wish I could have taken another of Prof. Pettijohn's classes!

The ATMS 322 Online course was great! The professor was very clear and detailed in his lecture videos. He was very helpful and responded very quickly to emails. This professor gives the best and most detailed feedback ever! It was great knowing what I did that was good and what was wrong. The professor is also very friendly, funny and understanding
Excellent professor.  Made our online learning environment enjoyable.  Was very punctual and clear with all assignments and feedback.  Would (and plan to) definitely take again.
I think that Mr. Pettijohn is a great professor, even thought it is a online class. I would like to have him for an on campus class. Mr. Pettijohn overall is a great professor.

I've never received as good of feedback from any other professor. He sent out a weekly email detailing what was good and what wasn't quite as good. He really cared that everyone did well and was understanding the topics.  He was great at responding to emails; he replied to my emails at 10 or 11 pm on the weekend once.

Professor Pettijohn does an awesome job at online courses. If you are a student who dreads exams, this is the course for you. Not the traditional online course. Discussions and different techniques for learning.
His assignments are good and help in real world projects

The final project was only briefly mentioned in one class and not clearly explained until near the end, when some extra clarification was given. This made it confusing to prepare. The material itself was helpful, but the class was not very engaging.
The course is not well-structured and sometime make you feel sleepy

reviews.comment:
The professor really care about the growth of students. In the first class he said he wanted to teach something that can actually help us in future studies and work. We spent time discussing logic of the algorithms, rather than repeating things we could learn on our own.
He is a professor who truly loves his career, life, and everyone of student.
Mr. Weible is definitely the best instructor in iSchool! Though you might need to spend plenty of time on his homework, you will learn a lot from it! Recommendeddd!!

He's one of the gems at iSchool and has a very good industry experience. The assignments and lectures are very clear and he makes his explanations clearly. He also cares a lot about students and organizes activities like quiz apart from assignments to help the students revise. The course involves a project in the end. Highly recommended professor.

Weible is genuinely interested in helping you understand what he's talking about if you ask. There was never too much work to handle and he was a decently lenient grader. I think if you attempt to show him that you care about the material, you're good. I'd suggest getting a jump on the final project because it'll take longer than you think.

Professor Johnson is warm, caring, and clearly cares about not only the material of her course but her students as well. Our lectures were interesting and concise, as were the midterm and final criteria. I wish I could take her for every English course. She's just the sweetest person and an amazing professor! :)

Professor Johnson's lectures are quite engaging. She posts all of her lectures on Canvas so even if you decide not to go you can still be successful on weekly quizzes. reviews.comment: You'll regret your whole college life if you didn't take her class.

Just one word for her: amazing.
Definitely one of the best professors I've ever met in school; recommended her classes to every single person who asked me which class to take.

I took Grimm's Fairy Tales in Context with Prof. Johnson and class was very straightforward and engaging. She would use the fairy tales as a starting point to get into philosophy, history, and art in a very interesting way. Show up to lecture and discussion, take some notes, and you'll get close to a A+ in the class.

This was the second class I've taken with Professor Johnson, and in my opinion, everyone should take one of her classes. She is so much fun, and you can tell she loves her job. She is very caring and engaging, one of the best professors at this university, honestly.

I wish every professor was Laurie Johnson. She truly loves her students and the material she gets to teach. If you sign up for this class just because it sounds vaguely interesting, you will learn SO much about literature and history, but the work is never demanding and Laurie is the most approachable professor ever, always willing to help out.

Dr. Johnson's lectures are always super interesting and enjoyable. The class as a whole is very well put together, and is quite easy to do well in provided you show up to most of the lectures and do most of the readings. From my experience, she also has very helpful TAs for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Frau Johnson is one of the funniest professors I've had. She challenged the class with interesting topics and showed us a wonderful array of not only literature in German Literature but videos as well. Always incredibly bubbly and sweet! Just talking to her, in general, is always refreshing! If you can take her, you'll love it!

A very kind individual. She really cares about her students and is willing to work with the needs of her students. I was personally having mental health issues and she is the first person that noticed it and actually reached out to help me. For that I am grateful. Her class is very chill and not hard to cope with. She makes class time go by fast.

One of the nicest, funniest professors out there. I thought the material sometimes dragged on throughout the semester, and that made me dread going to class at times. But she really is incredibly understanding and helpful. Take this Advanced Comp with her if you can! I think she is a fair grader too, as long as you know how to present an argument
She makes interesting points sometimes, but she just rambles on in her lectures about any and every thought that comes into her head.
Professor Johnson is extraordinary. That is all.

Professor Johnson is so sweet, funny, helpful, knowledgeable, personable and caring. It's a delight to come to class and it's easy to see that she thinks so too. Students vie for spaces in her courses and it's certainly not just for the material. Definitely one of the best professors at UIUC. I really want to give her a hug!!!

Professor Johnson is the best professor I have ever had. She is incredibly intelligent and kind. She knew my name after only one class. If you have the chance to take a class with her, DEFINITELY take it. Plus, GER 250 is really fun and interesting.

Professor Johnson is, in one word, awesome. She is very knowledgeable about her subject and is always willing to give extra help. I was having a bad day once and she took the time to send me an e-mail with her best wishes- such a sweetheart!

Lectures would have been incredibly useful... if I'd managed to stay awake. I'd continually drift off, but wake up just as she was finishing a useful thought. She knows her stuff. Come to class and pay attention, and you'll be fine.  I had a great TA also, and that was pretty much motivation for this class.

Prof. Johnson just won a high-profile teaching award on campus, and it's clear why, she's the cut. The commenter below probably was only in class on the days psychology was covered. These lectures rocked out. Easy on the eyes too. She expects you to think, some folks don't love that

Prof. Johnson is really into her subject, and it makes her lectures very interesting. She's extremely knowledgeable about German, history, psychology, etc, so expect a lot of ground to be covered, Overall really fun and funny, and class not too hard. Only skip class if your TA is good enough to fill you in.

Prof. Johnson's lectures are awesome, and she talks about much more than psychology. European history, culture and literature beyond tales, and social issues are covered. People taking this just for the requirement don't want to think too hard. Prof. Johnson will challenge how you think.

GER 250 is a good class for an adv comp, but dont expect to enjoy the lectures. All she does is talk about psychology in the tales, so you better have a really good understanding already going into the course if you want to succeed. Hope you have a good TA who will help you through the course. Bad lectures but she occasionally gives pop quizzes
No Comments

I took Life Drawing with him. He consistently had a bad attitude towards students and constantly complained about how much work he had to do outside class. Project introductions were vague and confusing, and we did basically the same thing every class. He wasn't specific enough with homework assignments, and grading seemed to never be consistent.

The whole class is always confused when he gives out assignments in and out of class. He will get passive aggressive because students do not automatically understand him. Although he says he's openminded, he is very picky and will tell you that he hates a student's work because it does not fit his style. Strict on tardiness but is usually late.

Not resourceful at all, he literally tells the class that he's too busy with his art so he won't be answering any emails. Its not clear what he uses the class fee money for, he makes you buy $200 worth of oil paint but later on makes you pay for random supplies that are not stated in the syllabus. He is not clear at all with instructions.
Professor Kingery is one of the best professors I have ever had! She is such a sweet soul. Just make sure you complete all your weekly assignments and quizzes and you'll be fine!
She is very caring and easy to talk to. I always looked forward to her class. Very motivational

Linda is great. She really cares about her students well-being and learning experience. She listens to feedback and provides time outside of class for questions and discussions. I'd take her again in a heartbeat. She shows relevant videos in and outside of class. She talks about current situations and information. She doesn't require a textbook.
This professor is very understanding and the material isn't heavy. A very interesting class that's easy and does not have a lot of work outside class. She is literally amazing.
Best professor Ive ever had. There for you and cares about your class experience and learning.
Wonderful person and really cares for her students, wants to make learning fun!

One of the best professors I've had. She's motivating, inspiring, & relates lectures to real world issues. I'm in her SOCW 455 course again this semester bc of how great she was. She is there for her students to make sure that you get something from the class.
This professor really is awesome!! She has great lectures and involves everyone. She is clear with grading structure and teaches so much in a relatable manner.

Great professor. She cares about her students and wants them to learn without being harsh. She is genuine and fun to be around. Even though attendance wasn't required, I went to every class because it was exciting, informational, and fun. There are assignments, but she is very laid back.
Great professor. Learning was fun and exciting.

This professor is absolutely amazing! She was very helpful throughout the entire semester. Super understanding and cares about each and every one of her students. If I could take another class with her I definitely would! Favorite class I have taken on campus!!!
One of my favorite professors I've ever had! Super nice and helpful to all students. Also, very funny and entertaining. I love going to this class
Absolutely one of the best professors I've ever had. She genuinely  cares about her students and the learning process and it shows.

Very laid back professor. She lets the class decide what and how they want to do things. Very collaborative learning. She does not require attendance, however, i did not miss a single glass. Very interesting topics are covered and there was never a dull or silent moment. Okay with no set due dates? Then i definitely recommend her!

I had Prof. Searsmith years ago and still remember her. She was bright, prepared, insightful, and funny. More than anything, I learned a lot about literature and how to read it perceptively. It was evident she brought intelligence and life experience to bear upon her work and that she was passionate about both literature and teaching her students.

Condescending is a perfect word. She has no empathy and she feels that her word is right and everything she says is THE WAY it must be. To be fair, she's very knowledgeable, but she doesn't really care about the students at all. She behaves as if she is above everyone else and she is the law. She is also contradictory. And she thinks she's funny.
Condescending and rude, especially when asked a question. Changed the syllabus so many times that I had no clue what needed to be done. At least she's only a temporary professor...

She took over for Prof. Johnson and is destroying what was a cool course.  The most arrogant prof I've had and I've taken quite a few MCB courses.  Lectures are all over the place, who knows what you're supposed to get out of them.  Not only arrogant but also seems to take pleasure from harassing her students.
This was supposed to be a non-major class but she treated it like we had 2 years of university-level english. She is very arrogant and condescending.

Professor Khessina is hilarious. She truly masters insightful discussions and her facials expressions are insanely funny! I enjoyed her class and cases. She is a tough grader, but is very clear with her expectations. Follow her rules and you'll be fine, she does care about her students and I learned when we had a call with her about our team project.

reviews.comment: He is a very kind and caring professor. However, the class is hard. You need to do and understand every single hw problems and past exams to succeed.

Smith is a nice guy who clearly cares about his students. However, his class is very difficult. The vast majority of your grade are exams, and he writes the exams to really test a deeper understanding of course material. You'll learn a lot, but be prepared for a challenge.

If you have the chance to take a class with Kyle, take it. He actually cares about his students. My entire degree hinged upon this class and after doing poorly on the first test, he offered me the opportunity to do well on the final and "overlook" the 1st test. I did well and ended up with a B in the class. Much respect for this man.

320 is difficult, and Smith's exams are tough. However, curves are VERY generous and it's clear that he wants students to succeed. #1 tip to succeed in this class - actually do the homework, go to office hours if you are lost. He's very helpful and is not a professor that is trying to screw you over.

If you take the course with him, make sure to both: go to lecture and read the text book. Also, the Labs for the course can make or break your grade.
Amazing professor. Genieunely focused on learning not just throwing assignments at you. Great lectures and a friendly face in the department.

Really nice Professor. I love the way he engages with the students and keeps us all active through the class. He does tend to grade a bit harsh sometimes, but he also provides you incredibly useful feedback, extra credit opportunities, and help in classes and group projects. Overall, a really cool Professor.

Good and passionate at teaching. Makes frequent use of real life demos and in class problem solving sessions. Learning with him is an enjoyable endeavor, though sometimes it feels like he dumbs it down maybe a little too much. He tends to go heavier on applications rather than theory which may leave concepts a bit hanging and nebulous. Overall good
ME370 - Wandke is the goat. One of us!
please delete this review - it's for the wrong professor

Expects you to take notes even if that isn't your style. When asking for help she dismisses the question and blames you. Gives no support for students and has unrealistic expectations.
Professor Kalsotra's class is difficult but he really does help you succeed in it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class
