reviews.comment: Dr. Kalsotra gives very in depth lectures. All of the information found on the exam come from the lectures so it is very important to attend each class. The professor does a great job at connecting the material to high yield topics on the MCAT, so if you are pre-med, you will be prepared. Dr. Kalsotra's office hours are also very helpful.

MCB 354 was great due to this professor. He explains things really well and makes it easier to memorize the pathways. Exams are straightforward with no surprises. The content comes back into a full circle, making it much easier to understand.
I loved Dr. Kalsotra! I could really understand his way of teaching. Biochem in general is super hard to grasp but he made it more fun and easier to learn!

Kalsotra was a great lecturer and it is clear he wants his students to succeed. He was often available for office hours multiple times a week. These sessions were extremely helpful. He was always very eager to answer any questions we had. Highly recommend reviewing his lecture slides, everything you need to know will be on there.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kalsotra is an amazing professor, he cares for you to do well and his office hours are also really helpful. He made Biochem very digestable and he cracks good jokes here and there!
Dr. Nash is amazing, his lectures are so fun and he makes biochemistry so digestable, very clear with what he looks for!

He has a fast-paced, upbeat teaching style. He is clear about what will be tested and focuses on key concepts, like glycolysis enzymes and pathways that show up on exams. The material is heavy at times, but he does a good job outlining what to prioritize for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class and the content itself was very dense but because of his slides and how he taught the class with practice iclickers made the class not only a lot more interesting but also made it a lot easier for everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kalsotra was an amazing lecturer. I personally loved his Amino Acid Biosynthesis and metabolic integration units. He made biochemistry more interesting, so it became easy to study. It wasn't one of those classes that were hard yet boring; it was one of those classes that were hard but interesting to learn because of his teaching style.

354 was the first biochem course I ever took, and I am glad it was Dr. Kalsotra who taught it. He truly wants you to succeed, and his efforts are seen in his preparation for lectures. He made the concepts easy to understand and connected them to real-world examples. He is also very approachable, and I had no problems asking him questions anytime.

Dr. Kalsotra is one of my favorite professors! His half of the semester was great-- the second half of biochemistry content wise was much harder, with extremely dense content-- but he does a great job of breaking down each step in a digestable format. He's clearly very passionate about teaching, and his lectures made biochemistry very enjoyable!

He was a great professor. His lectures were always in-depth and gave a lot of detail that helped when taking the exams. He also helped outside of class a lot and made sure his students understood the material.

Dr. Kalsotra was an amazing professor. Biochem is a difficult course inherently, but Dr. Kalsotra genuinely cares about his students and about their success. He explains the difficult concepts clearly and is always willing to help during office hours. You can tell he is passionate about teaching and makes a tough class more enjoyable.

You can tell that Professor Kalsotra cares very deeply for his students and is passionate about the topics taught. I enjoyed how much he integrated medicine with course content. Only downside was how fast he talked and progressed through the slides, it was hard to follow oftentimes.

Dr. Kalsotra is such a passionate professor! He is one of the few that is truly into their subject matter and loves to to teach it. While the course is very difficult, arguably one of the most difficult classes a biology major will ever take, Dr. Kalsotra makes learning the content manageable and ties everything together in a comprehensible way!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kalsotra is an amazing biochemistry professor! He takes away all of the fear and anxiety that comes with the name of the course and instead builds a safe, curious community for all of his students to learn. His office hours were awesome (highly recommend going if you can) for recapping his lectures and asking any questions you may have.

Dr. Kalsotra is an amazing professor. His lecture slides do have a lot of content but he makes sure to go over every slide and makes it clear which slides will be tested and which will not. He's always willing to answer any questions during or outside of lecture. Overall, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Usually do fine in MCB courses (including this one, before second half). Lecture slides are dense, VERY disorganized. Forced to purchase textbook to complete waste of time “adaptive quizzes”. iClickers not based on lecture material but last week's reading. Frequently when 5-10 mins past class time. Told not to memorize pathways, but exams test this
Dr. Kalsotra's office hours were really useful, he made sure to go through everything with a lot of detail and also made connections to the real world.

Dr. Kalsotra is an amazing professor! His passion for the subject is evident in his teaching. He makes lectures enjoyable and connects the concepts to real life, which made biochemistry a lot more interesting. His slides are really comprehensive, and his office hours are also super helpful. The best MCB professor I've had!

Dr. Kalsotra made a challenging course engaging and rewarding. His passion for biochemistry shines, and he truly cares about student success beyond the classroom. Office hours were incredibly helpful, with every question answered with patience and depth. He pushed me to think critically and apply concepts, not just memorize them. One of the best!

The lectures are too hard to understand because everything is so dense and fast. I get lost first 3 minutes into lecture and I sit there for 47 minutes thinking qh I don't blame him because material itself is a lot to memorize.

Dr. Kalsotra's teaching style is very straightforward, easy to understand, and very easy to catch because he makes the slides the core of what he's saying and tests us on the information given to us, not what he's saying!

Dr. Kalsotra is a great professor! Biochemistry is tough, but Dr. Kalsotra made it manageable. He often connected topics to everyday life which made the class interesting. He is also very approachable and you can tell he is passionate about biochemistry. You will have everything you need to do well and he is always available for office hours!

Dr. Kalsotra is a very thorough lecturer who manages to cover a lot of material in only an hour of time. He also delivers this information in a comprehensive way that is easier to understand. If any questions do arise, he is very accessible through office hours and takes the time to explain very difficult concepts. Overall, great professor!

Very helpful and frequent office hours. Visibly passionate about his work and class material. Does stuff a lot of content into every lecture and some of them might be a bit fast/overwhelming. But the exams are reasonable and only come from the lecture slides. Overall not a easy class but great professor.

Dr. Kalsotra made an amazingly difficult and information-intensive class seem manageable and interesting. His notes and lectures were jam-packed with useful information that had all you needed to succeed on exams. Overall, Dr. Kalsotra's classes were very engaging and clear, which made MCB 354  one of the most rewarding courses I've ever taken.
There is a lot of content but the professor does a great job of explaining everything and ensuring that all of the students' questions are answered.

A difficult course, however, Dr. Kalsotra makes it very clear what to expect, and everything we need to know is stated in lectures. While there is heavy memorization, Dr. Kalsotra has always made the experience enjoyable by cracking jokes in class, giving real life examples, go to office hours he is nice to talk with and cares about the students!

I took MCB 354 in the fall of 2024 and loved the class. Not only did I feel like the material was interesting, but Dr. Kalsotra taught the material with enthusiasm. Dr. Kalsotra is very easy to reach out to, and he hosts office hours every week, which I found very useful. The lecture videos are also posted in case you miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lectures that cover material comprehensively

While MCB 354 is pretty content heavy and definitely a challenge, Dr. Kalsotra is an excellent professor. He presents the information clearly in lecture and is very transparent about exams. You can tell he wants his students to succeed and offers a lot of extra help should you need it.

While this class is challenging, Dr. Kalsotra makes the content very relevant to the world and healthcare. Everything that is tested is provided in the slides, so you don't have to read the textbook, and he is very approachable for office hours. Be prepared to spend time studying outside of class, but there are many opportunities to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kalsotra's lecture slides are very detailed and informative giving a good understanding of the material. He makes sure to explain all the pathways in detail. Office hours are very helpful where he is always willing to clarify material and synthesize it for better understanding. He cares about whether his students are doing well in the class.

Exams are hard, though if you study they are managable. Content was very enjoyable, as it was made applicable to every day processes, though movie clips, tangents, and examples. Dr. Kalsotra was an enjoyable lecturer. He paced content comfortably, though lectures were very content heavy. Optional attendance and slides have everything you need.

Dr. Kalsotra is one of the best professors I've had here at UIUC. His lecture slides are thorough and he does his best to connect lecture material to the real world. His office hours and review sessions were both extremely helpful, so definitely attend those! His exams are tough but very possible to do well on if you put in the time and effort.

Biochemistry is a tough course, but Professor Kalsotra does a great job teaching and making sure you understand the material. His office hours are great as well, and he is very easily approachable and willing to take his time to walk you through the material to make sure you truly understand it. I would highly recommend his course!

354 was hard and the content was super challenging but Dr. Kalsotra clearly enjoyed what he was teaching and made lectures interesting. He would add in real life connections to things we learned about that made it a lot easier to retain and had office hours frequently. The exams are hard but he does a good job of explaining.

This course was very challenging, but Professor Kalsotra was very good at explaining the concepts clearly, especially if you have some trouble understanding them the first time. He made every lecture interesting and captivating, and clearly outlined for us what we should expect on the exams. He was fair and provided us every opportunity to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Kalsotra loves what he is teaching and it shows. He genuinely wants his students to succeed and is very willing to help. MCB 354 is one of those classes where students must be willing to work hard, but Dr. Kalsotra teaches the material in a way that makes sense. He is such a kind and interesting professor. I highly recommend taking his class!

This course is challenging, due to the content and the amount of material covered. However, Dr. Kalsotra made the material very intriguing and his lectures were very engaging! You can tell he is very intelligent, and is passionate about the material. The real life examples and stories he tells during lecture were also very beneficial!

MCB 354 was the most challenging and interesting class in my curriculum thus far due to the amount of content. Dr. Kalsotra is very personable, intelligent, and makes early lectures interesting by telling stories and giving real life examples. He gives good advice and is more than happy to help during his office hours and after class.

Dr.Kalsotra helped anybody in the class with understanding the material and provided help to anybody. During his office hours, he provided real world examples to the material that we were learning for that week. Overall with his help, I would not have learned as much as I did about the material which is so predominant on the MCAT

I really enjoyed taking MCB 354 (biochemistry) with Dr. Kalsotra as the instructor. I will not lie, the course was very content-heavy and moved at a quick pace, however, Dr. Kalsotra knows so much about the subject of biochemistry that any confusing concepts we learned were made understandable once he broke it down. I would take this class again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was retaking Biochem so I was very nervous about the course but after Dr. Kalsotra started lecturing, the class became so much more manageable and easier to understand. He is approachable and explains his lectures very thoroughly. He wants you to succeed so ask questions! I even got an A on the final when it was my downfall the semester prior.

Professor Kalsotra made this class very easy to learn although it's very challenging. There was so much information you had to know, but he was very good at explaining the content. He made the class a lot more interesting & it was easy to follow during lectures. His lecture slides were always very detailed & always helped when reviewing for exams.

not sure if he does not know how to teach or does not care. the lectures were very dry and boring, it was impossible to stay awake during his lectures. I still did well but that was because I just studied the material on my own. the first half of the course taught by the other professor was way more interesting. i wish he taught the second half too

I took this course in Fall 2021. Lecture attendance wasn't mandatory and recordings were posted online. Dr. Kalsotra was always available during office hours and even offered to meet at alternate times. He taught the course thoroughly and provided real-world examples of critical BC processes. Ask questions and understand concepts, don't memorize!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kalsotra made a very detailed topic such as biology very fun and easy to learn. I never felt overwhelmed in the class! I really enjoyed that class and thought he was one of the easiest teachers in explaining the difficult topics.Professor Kalsotra is very approachable and easy to talk to as well. It is for these reasons why I did so well

Professor Kalsotra made a very detailed topic such as biology very fun and easy to learn. I never felt overwhelmed in the class! I really enjoyed that class and thought he was one of the easiest teachers in explaining the difficult topics. Professor Kalsotra is very approachable and easy to talk to as well. It is for these reasons why I did so well

MCB 354 is a very difficult course due to all the information that is given to students, but Dr. Kalsotra makes this information very digestible in lectures. Plus, he has so many office hours for students to take advantage of, where he goes very in depth on certain topics. Dr. Kalsotra explains biochemistry so that it is easier to understand.

Kalsotra is an engaging lecturer and is great at breaking down the material. The material is challenging, but his lectures are thorough and focus in on the topics most relevant to the exams. The lecture slides are easy to follow and the review lecture before each exam was super helpful. Definitely a doable class if you put in the work!

The content covered by Auinash would usually be very hard and overwhelming but he delivers it in digestible amounts and correlates it all to make sense and easy to learn. One of the best professors I've had, super chill, approachable, and has his students best interest at hear

Nice guy. Used interesting examples that helped make the dense material more interesting. Moved through a lot of material at a fast pace. Would help if he cut down on the number of subjects he tried to include on each exam. Tests cover a lot of material which is tough, but he asked questions that have a bit less depth than actual lecture material.

exams were in person but class was online, does not actually teach/just regurgitates what's on his lecture slides, does not connect big ideas/concepts together, tests are ridiculous and are over a ridiculous amount of content, heavy accent so sometimes difficult to know what he was saying
This class was online and was mediocre. Before this class I thought I liked BC but it was just rote memorization and test-heavy. I learned a lot more the first half of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is being taught by kalostra the first time,,, epic fail. He just reguritates what is said on the slides and clearly reads from a script with zero emotion. Won't answer emails on time and his practice exam is a complete 180 from his actual exam. Sad because I heard he was really decent for MCB 450
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nash is probably one of the best professors I have ever had. He really makes you work hard for your grade, but he knew the students were struggling in his class so he added an extra office hours. If you put in the work you will do well in his class. Even though biovhem can be a very dry topic he makes it interesting and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took her for LING 307 and she was helpful in the sense that if you were attending class, you would be fine. If you ever chose to skip a few days, be careful about asking for more help. She was very passive aggressive to me when I asked a simple clarifying question but when someone else asked a similar question, she answered it normally.

Personally, I think the LING 100 professor is very helpful — she will carefully answer your questions during office hours and outside of class。 However, since exams make up 60% of the grade and the midterm and final have very few questions, it means you need to get almost everything right to earn an A. But overall, LING 100 is a very easy course.

Professor Newkirk is clearly knowledgeable, but her explanations were often hard to grasp for students new to linguistics. The single midterm and final made up most of the grade. I know people including myself who studied hard for the final and found it more complicated than what we had done in class.

She is a good professor teaching LING100: Intro to Language Science. Her handouts are very useful. But maybe because of the restraint of time and intro-level nature of the course, some explanation of materials is not sufficient to Linguistics students. Overall, very good, recommended for students not majoring in LING to take for GenEds

He's fine. 246 was interesting but they didn't teach the necessary physics to understand the problems you are working on so after you pass a certain point you just do exactly what they tell you to without really understanding the underlying physics.

My favorite class of the physics 21X sequence. It was an ok class and similar in difficulty to the others, although it may be the easiest. Nice lecturer, probably limited by teaching the smartphysics material

This was a fine class. It was what you expect from all the 21x physics sequence, nothing more or less. This course was on the harder end of difficulty, and the material was interesting. He liked silence in class, which was nice. As many students talking is distracting, I appreciated him stopping that.

Might be the worst Physics professor at this school. His lectures are fine, but most of the content is learnt through the prelectures (as in 211 and 212). Has the worst attitude of a professor I've seen. If he hears someone barely talking to another, he stops class and calls them out. For a class of over 200, people are gonna talk to each other.

Many people say his lectures are irrelevant, but if you read the pre-lectures before hand they are actually insightful and help clarify the content, which seems to be how most physics classes work at this university. The labs and the demos are very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goes off on irrelevant tangents in lecture and doesn't convey the big topics that actually matter for homework and exams. Be prepared to teach yourself almost everything.
i hate this guy

Rude to people asking questions, and is just generally unhelpful. Lectures are mandatory but seem almost useless. I feel like he gets off track a lot and the lectures are hard to follow. Be prepared to learn almost everything outside of class

The demeanor that Prof. Wagner exhibits towards his students is completely unproductive as an educator. He will not help you through problems adequately and holds an ire for his students that don't come to class (optional attendance). His inability, or unwillingness, to provide genuine help creates a very negative atmosphere.

Consistently gives incoherent lectures and references other materials instead of explaining them. I took two classes with this professor and in the second he was paired up to teach the class. He actively made the class worse for the other professor.

He's just so boring. He yaps about the most useless stuff all class, while I had to learn majority of the material on my own. It sucked the lectures were mandatory, because I felt they were a waste of time. I loved 211 and 212, but he made me hate 213. Doesn't have the same fun vibe as Kwiat or Stelzer.
Made the class more difficult than necessary and often belittled people when they asked questions.
Not a great lecturer. Sometimes hard to follow, goes quickly over concepts and tends to ramble on. Not a great structure to his lectures IMO.

The class material is actually quite enjoyable but this professor and the way the class is taught destroy any appreciation you might have for the subject. The professor is alright in office hours but during lecture he would often go off into meaningless and somewhat random derivations of equations that we don't need to know for the class.

Petty.  Would call out students in the middle of large lectures for things like coughing or discussing which felt very unnecessary and awkward.  Taught like he already expected me to understand quantum physics.  Only two exams and a final which had very little practice material.  Felt like material wouldn't have been so confusing if taught better
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Passive aggressive, explains material well but terrible at answering questions. We got only one practice paper and the exams would always be quite different.

The class isn't as bad as people make it out to be. However, Professor Wagner is just a bit of a mid lecturer imo. He's a bit of a snowflake and has an ego that I don't like. He's a nice guy overall, though. The exams are about average difficulty and not bad if you are well versed with the formulas. Just make sure to do homework and practice tests.
THIS IS THE WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE HAD.

Terrible professor. He is very unresponsive when students ask questions and he expects them to know just as much as him. Super passive aggressive and petty when answering questions on piazza like he knows everything. I worked hard on all the homework, quizzes, and practice exams but when I got to the actual exam, half the content I never learned.

Stelzer is better lul. Wagner doesn't like answering questions although they may be relevant to the class and the material itself. 99% of the learning is in discussion and on hw, lectures are completely useless, along with the garbage prelecture notes.
no curve

He cares about the students but with some 200+ you have to put in work. Lectures are good but HW/discussions are where everything comes together(practice). Course isnt the most well defined in terms of derivations, so master the basics. Also, I felt as though many who struggle never went to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He doesn't teach very well, you have to learn most of the material using the discussion book/discussion sections. He doesn't like answering questions

Had him 213/4. In 213, he was actually fine for the most part, though his lectures arent always great at preparing you for the HW in my opinion. My biggest problem with him however is how he will outright refuse to answer certain questions because they are from older exams in the course, even though the question itsef is actually relevant.
Better than the other physics classes at UIUC. Really hard but Wagner made this class bearable, especially with all the jokes!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Wagner was a solid professor for quantum. His lectures were always fun and interesting, and he would walk around during the iclicker questions to see if everyone understood the material.

The difference between teaching ECE120 and ECE391 is night and day. He was good for ECE120, but for this class, it is a total mess. Makes mistakes in both lectures and presentation slides. As it is a required class in order to graduate, it would be better to take the class with DKW in the summer semester.

Is not good at explaining things during lecture. It feels as if you have to already know what he's talking about to comprehend what he's talking about. Only remember 2 or 3 times over the semester when he was actually clear at explaining some concept. Additionally, documentation for MPs is poor.

Professor and course staff are the most petty and careless people. This professor and his course staff robbed me of one of the most important courses ECE at UIUC has to offer, due to their disorganization and pettiness.
refuses to give solutions to the few practice exams literally for fun. negative study material just for the sake of maximizing pain and minimizing learning.

Worst class I have ever taken. The professor designs the MPs as vaguely as possible and doesn't give you enough documentation or feedback after. Then uses an autograder to grade you on stuff you were never taught and won't ever get from the given resources. Exams give you a whole new system and expect you to understand it and implement it.

The professor cared more about cracking jokes than actually teaching students. Would constantly insinuate that the entire class was cheating while giving incredibly disorganized lectures and MPs, which you are given ZERO meaningful feedback on by the way. The biggest issue with the course is the complete opaqueness of MP grading and specifications.
run away as fast as you can
Professor does not have a public github account. 0/10 do not recommend

Very boring lectures and ocassionally unprepared. Slides during lectures are sometimes incorrect and not up to date especially when using slides from previous semesters and trying to be different from previous semesters to prevent cheating. Sure, changing up how the material is taught is good, but the slides are not following how it is taught.
The instructions for MPS are very unclear. Many implementations in the MPs are not even mentioned in the material.
Class was very disorganized, partly due to the reorganization of the class. Humorous but not as great as explaining concepts.

Levchenko's handling of MPs is poorly managed, with numerous errors present in the materials. The scheduling is disorganized, and MPs are often released very late. Emails are never responded. The pace of lectures is slow, and lots of the content covered is irrelevant or unhelpful.

Had him for 120 and loved him, but not great for 391. Lectures are hard to follow, and the class is poorly structured despite being a core, notoriously difficult course. MPs were created as they were released, resources were minimal, and practice materials were nonexistent. Demos were behind/rescheduled. Best part was Deniz.

Dude tell jokes during every single lecture, but these jokes will be somewhere in the midterms and backstab you. Course has no midterm review material and he would not provide full slides. He would literly post a 30 page slide just before lecture and by the end of lecture he was showing slide page 74. He always make simple consepts miserable.

I can't understand why this process can handle such an important course. He is humorous but he make all the concepts messy. He changed the mp and have inclear instructions for it. The lecture is also too late to provide the skills required for the mps. Please not take his ECE391 if you want to get a good grade.

Prof. Levchenko is amazing, he deeply cares about his students success and his lectures are very engaging, they remade the class this semester so it is very disorganized, but he helped me debug me code during office hours and you can tell he really wants to see his students succeed. ECE391 is a very time consuming class, but very rewarding!

Humor prof BUT he explains everything like a mess. I can understand why people like him for easy courses like 120 but for 391 he is just terrible. He uses 0 diagrams so everything is jamed together. You will have no idea how a concept is related to another. He makes jokes on class but he tests you those jokes like wtf

One of my favorite professors in ECE. Had an online flipped section that I think was ran quite well. It was very helpful for exams to see the professor doing the problems in class, although occasionally the worksheets weren't great. He is a really funny guy and cares a lot about his students' success
Fun and interesting lectures, would definitely take again
Such a great explainer. Personally I didn't like the way his section was set up but his lectures were always enjoyable and made the class miles easier. He's a must take for 120

Levchenko's flipped lectures are usually interesting and he tries to make them as engaging as possible. He also does a good job of answering questions and stays after class to make sure students understand the material. Definitely would take him again.
You will definitely love him. He makes intense material very easy to understand and fun to learn.
He made "lectures" very engaging and was more than willing to stay after to answer questions, the flipped setting isn't my favorite, but it was definitely worth having him as a professor.

Fantastic Professor! His lectures are basically structured office hours. Cracks a lot of jokes which makes the class fun. Very helpful and accessible; his explanations make even the most difficult concepts make sense. He is attentive, and will take as much time as you need to make sure you understand. One of my favorite professors by far!
A masterpiece periodit.

Professor Levchenko made this class much better. Yes, the worksheets that we complete during lectures are useless and that makes the class way harder than it needs to be but Levchenko is great at answering questions, especially in office hours. Overall chill guy and I wish we did not have such a terrible lecture setup so he could teach us more.

I had him during covid semester (spring 2020) and he was very nice and helpful! In my opinion his lectures got a bit boring and the content became very difficult to understand towards the end of the semester (take this with a grain of salt though because again it was right when the pandemic began)
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He made class great and maintained a good balance between getting stuff done and cracking jokes. I enjoyed lectures and the homework and tests made sense because of him.

If you are in his flipped-classroom section, most of the learning you will be doing on your own with materials the department assigns. Therefore I seldom went to his sessions, which were essentially structured office hours. However, when I did go, his sessions were helpful and engaging. You can't go wrong with him.

He's engaging, and even though I took this class online, he made it fun and tried his best to help us through the pandemic. Lectures weren't compulsory, but I felt like joining would only help my grade.
ECE 120 was a breeze with this man.

Professor Levchenko is a LEGEND. I had my doubts coming into ECE but Levchenko turned my hesitation into a deep love for the field. His lectures are engaging and is VERY easy to talk to. He ditches the slides in favor of more example based learning. 120 is hard if you don't have experience, but if you get Levchenko it's entirely worth it. Love him!
His Lectures are super engaging and always a joy to attend. He takes his time explaining all the concepts and makes sure we have a firm grasp of everything. Overall a great dude!
This man is the most amazing man on earth! He is so nice and he's also an amazing teacher!!!! Would go to the ends of the earth for this man

The GOAT. Most interesting class I've been in, didn't matter that attendance was mandatory, would have shown up anyway. The guy has multiple published papers in his field so he knows his stuff and makes it interesting when teaching. Assignments were spamming a website, SEO and other similar things.
Lectures were hard to follow. Discussions were even harder to follow. However, still an easy class. The exams are annoying but online.

Lectures are pointless. Too many exams and you don't get proper review for them just practice questions that you haven't learned the material for. Even discussions don't really go over much. Tells you to memorize certain things or put them on your cheat sheet instead of pushing you to actually understand the concepts.

He's a very solid guy and lecturer but they aren't that useful. I think the course design is kind of meh. Extra credit is vague point totals are vague, there's an exam two days before the final, and some questions on the exams are just genuinely never touched on in the course. Tests are online though and myself and everyone I knew got an A.

TA discussions are required, but lectures are not. Sometimes EC available for attending lectures. Teaching style is not great, I learned nothing from lectures. Was caring and considerate during canvas hack and final exam issues.

Solid guy and class is really easy. Just was not a fan of having 4 midterms and one two days before the final. Faded almost every lecture and TA sessions were also pretty worthless. I pretty much self taught the material and did just fine.

Disrespectful conduct. No reason why it should take ten days to respond to a student's email about a loss in the family, just to give a sarcastic response when the student follows up. Not something I needed while grieving.

"Extra credit" never actually gets added, lectures are irrelevant, doesn't really teach. Only really was able to learn anything because the TAs actually cared about helping students understand concepts. The online exam proctoring was good once you get the hang of it. 4 midterms is excessive, especially when the 4th is the day before the final....

Lots of exams (a midterm the day before the final exam...), doesn't really teach- TAs did the heavy lifting in terms of explanations and actually helping students understand. Went on irrelevant tangents, teaching could have been more efficient. Online exam format and proctoring was good once you get the hang of it. "Extra credit" never gets put in

This class was pretty easy, most lectures did feel like ted talk more than a lecture and the content was not really on the exam. It is an easy class as long as you do the modules. And you can typically get extra credit for going to class. There are four exams and they use proctorU but it really does not work so sometimes they're not proctored.

Hated this class, he barely actually taught anything and lectures were different from tests. Only upside was that they allow cheat sheets and most of the exams were online, so it's pretty hard to fail. Didn't learn a thing
Lectures were interesting because he related Econ topics to things that were happening in the real world. Exams were online using proctorU which was nice.

Vazquez is a good guy that wants his students to do well. He made econ topics interesting and I liked going to lecture. He also basically tells you exactly what will be on the test so exams are very easy to prepare for. As long as you go to lectures sometimes and do the practice exams and hw, it's very easy to get an A. Highly recommend.
Not to hard to get an A, workbook he has was helpful to prepare. Kind off bland but he's solid.
Great teacher and very easy to follow

Professor Vazquez is a really funny and caring guy. His lectures are interesting, and I rarely skipped because they usually only lasted 30–40 minutes. I didn't find the TA sessions very helpful and felt like they dragged on. Vazquez genuinely wants you to get an A and makes it very clear what you need to do to earn one.

His lectures are for the most part pretty irrelevant to the tests- although, he does tell you some of what's specifically going to be on the test. He does randomized attendance 5 times for extra credit & you can drop your worst test grade. TA sessions go into unnecessary detail that you don't actually need to know. also you're allowed a cheat sheet
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Macro with Professor Vazquez. He's an extremely caring guy who genuinely just wants his students to do well! I really appreciate the extra credit opportunities we got in lecture, so I would go! I also really liked my TA! Overall, I would say Professor Vazquez is a great lecturer and a very generous grader!
very caring towards students and wants to make sure everyone has a chance if they try hard enough to get a good grade. at lectures he offers extra credit for your final grade

pretty chill proffesor. Ended lectures after 30 minutes. Gave extra credit. Lectures were pretty easy to understand but you need to do work outside of class to get through the class. Tests are online and pretty easy.

He wants you to do well in his class but doesn't offer much study opportunities. He only counts exams towards the grade but gives only three practice exams that don't tell you the correct answers. Makes it really hard to study.

I honestly didn't learn anything in this class, but somehow it was still so easy. Professor Vazquez is a nice guy, but he's hard to follow, and I didn't get much out of his lectures.This course won't add much to your workload at all.

He is not a very good lecturer and isn't good at teaching. ECON 103 is so easy that it doesn't matter but if you want to actually learn the material you need to teach it to yourself. His lectures are kinda redundant except for the occasional extra credit he gives out. Lecture isn't mandatory and you can get by just fine without going to lecture.
would study my hardest and still do bad on tests. lectures were NEVER helpful. doesn't help that uiuc packs hundreds of kids into each lecture. if you can avoid. had to teach myself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Vazquez is an okay professor, but you have to love Econ to enjoy the class. The class is not difficult itself, and the tests are fair and mostly online, but his lectures are long and hard to follow a lot of the time (DONT TAKE THE 9 am ONE WORST MISTAKE OF MY LIFE).

Little to no homework, if you pay attention in class and you do all the test prep you will pass all the test, because he uses the same questions on the test prep. Also 3 of the 4 test are at home and lowest grade gets dropped( besides the in person one)

It was a little tough for me at the beginning of each new lesson since I had never took an economics class. In the end, it wasn't difficult. As long as you show up to lectures, discussion, and make use of the practice exams, there's no way you won't get a passing grade. What you see on the practice exams is what you'll see on every exam.

He was a good lecturer, and explained topics pretty well. I wasn't very engaged in lecture but still left at least learning something. Very little online homework, and exams are pretty easy. As long as you go to lecture, you should be fine
What can I say. He's the GOAT.

Overall really great class. Don't worry too much about the class contents. The professor explained everything during the lecture and if not you will probably find it out in the discussion or online. For the tests, there are mock exams beforehand and test questions are literally in the pratices and the mock exam.
The lectures vary in length. The professor is a cool guy. There is very little homework, so exams are very important.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Vazquez makes the course engaging despite the large class size. The lectures are informative, and the textbook is helpful. Attendance is mandatory, but there are plenty of extra credit opportunities. Unstuckstudy AI proved invaluable for exam prep.

Overall, this class is very poorly taught and managed. The lectures are very short and of horrible quality. $100 for a textbook which is supposed to be your only material in this class, and the professor has little to no role. I am a non-degree student for the summer, and did not expect this from a top public university, especially Illinois.

Overall a great professor. Given the size of the class it's difficult to get to know him personally but you can really tell he cares about his students. Not a difficult class, just study for the exams. They're all multiple choice. Lecture attendance is randomly taken and discussion attendance is mandatory. Overall great class

Great professor. Only assignments were from the online book and were due the day of exams. 3 midterms (FRQ and MC) and final (MC only). Buy his textbook because almost everything he says in lecture is on exams. Do practice exams because answers on there are on exam. Wasn't the most interesting class, but it's definitely not anything to stress over.

Didn't learn much in lectures but he seemed like he cared. Offered a FRQ drop, and allows 3 practice exams per exam. Offers 5 EC opportunities randomly in lecture, and homework assigned is actually what teaches you the course content. The workbook has the exact FRQs that will be on the exams and is very useful. Boring lectures. Decent class.
King Jose

His class is very easy and he offers a lot of extra credit but I didn't learn much from him. His lectures weren't very well organized but at least the homework was easy. Tests are also open book so its very easy to get a good grade in his class. But if you're someone who actually wants to learn economics, you might be better off with someone else.
My favorite professor at UIUC! I have taken multiple classes with him. He always genuinely wants students to be happy and have a fun time in class!
While this course may be a little overpriced for it's materials, the professor is hilarious and gives a ton of leeway on numerous things!

50% of your grade is just by showing up and completing the online homework (not graded on accuracy). The other half of your grade is for exams. Lectures were interesting and insightful - professor was VERY GENEROUS with extra credit too! Discussion attendance is mandatory. Beware that exams do get harder as you progress throughout the semester.

3 midterms, open note, online. Class is basically asynchronous. You have to pay $100+ for the online textbook where you complete the homework (required but completion grade). Lectures were mostly irrelevant but attendance earns you extra credit points on random days, so it is advantageous to show up. Did not learn much.

The class wasn't organized and structured properly. Some information from lectures were irrelevant compared to the midterm questions. He offered a lot of extra credit and all exams were open notes. The TA sessions didn't help much either because most of them weren't good at teaching. The textbook is $100 and you need it to do hw (completion pts).

Lectures were pretty boring and sometimes what he taught was irrelevant for the exams. Often felt like he forgot to teach us certain things that we needed to know, but the class is still easy. If you want to learn as little as possible and still get an A, take him for econ.

There are 3 midterms, all open note. I never learned anything & the tests are kinda hard but because it was open note, I got great grades on the tests. You have to pay 100$ for the homework, but they are incredibly easy. Basically paying for an A.

He is a really good guy, but the material isn't really taught to you. You'll definitely pass because homework is a free 100%, but exam scores are low. Overall, easy class besides the material is mostly self-taught so be careful on exams. They are also open note.
Great guy. Dont get slacking because of the easy homework however, class average for exams have been low 70s-80s. Actually show up and do the work and you'll easily get an A.
This guy is the best and I love him
What a great guy.

Incredibly easy class, but I'm not sure if I learned a thing. The professor stated that lecturing was like his platform as an actor. It felt more like a performance than teaching with his lectures, so I stopped going the first week of class. He is a nice guy, and the work is really easy, but there is A LOT.

I was in his Honors section, and the expenses for us appear to be less than for the regular section since we never used Sapling. It was self paced and the coursework was very easy. His teaching in the videos is meh, and not the best if you are actually interested in Econ. But it was an easy A and I got honors credit for it too.
when the course is online it's simple but learning as at your own pace. Easy A, but I guess if you want a more rigorous process go a different route but he's a good professor

This is definitely a pay to get an A class. I paid $100 for the CPMs and the Sapling-which is where you did your homework. He didnt put anything on Moodle except how to get to the coursework accessed and paid for. While it was an easy class and a GPA booster, I really didnt appreciate having to pay so much money just to do the classwork.
This class is a joke he doesn't teach at all. It's an easy A but you wont learn anything. If you actually want to learn the material you have to teach yourself.

Literally left the school in the middle of the semester without explanation. I get people can have personal reasons, but students deserved an explanation. Literally learned NOTHING in this class. Absolutely useless. He doesn't even have lectures.

Fall 2020, COVID semester. Completely asynchronous so I finished the class a month early. Tests and quizzes are open note and unproctored. Course Modules were based on completion so those were a breeze too. The website for our tests/quizzes was $85, but the class is super easy. Nothing due until the end of the semester, except a test every month.

He does not care about the students. he hands out A's like crazy. If you are looking for an A take his class. It is a joke. However, I learned nothing and as a business student it really hurt when I moved to upper level econ and finance courses.

Honestly an amazing guy. His lectures weren't as content heavy and were mainly problem based which can be confusing if you don't do the readings beforehand but all of the work was insanely easy for this course and anyone can get an A+ if they put in the slightest amount of effort.
Great guy. Seems to care about students and wants them to succeed. Always available and helpful.

Vasquez is one of THE funniest professors I've had. Lectures are NOT mandatory because the course is divided into two components: Packback and Sapling. If you do end up going to lectures, you'll end up leaving with a smile on your face, but like I said, you don't need to go to them at all. Definitely take 102 with Vasquez if you need to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was a joke. You won't learn anything if you don't try to by yourself. His lectures don't teach anything, and he even tells students not to go to lecture. He made us buy two separate websites (over $100) just to complete mandatory assignments when the university uses free websites. Would not take him again even though it was easy.
Awesome professor! His lectures are so interesting and attendance is not mandatory.

The definition of an Easy A. He cares more about you actually learning the material rather than the grade. Majority of the class is online things with unlimited attempts. You can learn as much as you want. Either he is doing this class just for money and actually just wants to focus on his research/other projects, or he actually cares. (He cares)

This class was an easy A as long as you did the online homework and did the TopHat during lecture. I showed up for almost every lecture, but you can do most of the in-class work online from the comfort of your own home. Fun times.
Woke up at 1 everyday. Did tophat on my bed. Got an A+.

I had him for ECON 102 and even though I could've still gotten an A without going to lecture, I enjoyed going because he is a witty geunius! The class is really easy and for those complaining below, you can get as much out of the class as you want. There are the tools to learn a lot. Likewise, you do not need to pay attention to pass, just do work.
Very easy to get an A in the class. Lectures are optional but are very interesting.
Best Prof ever. Love Jose. Super easy class and hes so funny. His lectures are great. You dont need to pay attention but if you do, you can learn a lot.

I had the online discussion section and the only thing I hated about this was the amount of software you have to buy to participate in this class, but it's fine. All of the online modules are really easy and you can actually learn in the class if you want to, but it's just as easy to not pay attention and still make an A.
Super easy class. Make sure to take packaged section. Final was literally optional, just make sure to do all online homework. You can get participation points without even going to class.
Too quiet.
You literally don't learn anything because the class is so easy but he is a very fun professor so its good enough for an intro econ course especially if its not a requirement for your major
He skips many lectures...
A joke of a class, everything online. Got an A+ and know literally nothing about microeconomics. If you want to get anything out of the money you pay to take econ, do not do it with Vazquez.

Probably one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. For instance, I completely forgot to do one of the High Stakes Quizzes and did so-so on the others but still got an A. Despite being easy, I didn't think I actually learned the material as well as I should have. Vazquez makes the lectures enjoyable and topical, not mandatory but would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You can either choose to attend classes and get a straightforward A or skip all classes and take the final also for an A. Class is fun, though not very closely related to what appears on quizzes. Need to learn by yourself sometimes

Literally the easiest class youll take at UIUC. Its pretty much a guaranteed A. Quizzes are a pretty big portion of your grade, but he lets you take them an unlimited amount of times. If youre actually interested in economics I wouldnt recommend this class, but if you need an easy Gen Ed then this is the class for you.

Lots of thought provoking and interesting lectures. We didn't cover the material very frequently in class it was more discussion based and quizzes and high stakes quizzes would be completed on our own. Overall great teacher and great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is super easy, getting an A+ is no problem. However, if you didn't take Micro in high school or do independent studying outside of class, then you may fail to actually learn any concepts. He only reviews the most difficult examples in class, which may confuse those who don't have a strong understanding of the concepts.

It is an easy A class overall, and Dr Vazquez is really nice in grading. Honestly, I learnt all materials on my own during the spring break in order to finish take-home online quiz. It is amazing that I did not listen to him for one second ever but I got an A+ eventually haha

Prof. Vasquez is a rational and entertaining instructor. He is funny and passionate enough to make a topic I don't find interesting not too bad to learn about. The class is practically participation based, and with minimal effort it is easy to obtain a solid grade.

I took Econ in high school and this course completely confused me on everything I had learned before. The pre-lecture and lectures were not helpful at all, and the quizzes had challenging questions that weren't even covered in the course. Thank god it was an easy A where you had infinite tries on tests. Just show up, do your work and you can get A+
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: While Professor Vazquez's ECON 102 class is the easiest class you will ever sign up for, do not expect to learn too much. His class is 100% based on attendance and completion. Nothing is graded for accuracy and therefore you should earn an automatic A+. He also gives extra credit every class so you should get over a 100% in the class.
Best Professor in UIUC, just show up in class and there is NO midterm, NO final, only online test, which you can attempt unlimited times ! Easy A+

Not a great teacher, spends most of the lecture "debating" with himself to try and make a point but mostly just makes it difficult to know what we should be writing down. Exams were super challenging, except for the final which was 80% questions straight from midterms. He also requires you to use his website, which you have to pay for.

Lecture is useless. Rather than building up your knowledge, Vasquez likes to choose the most convoluted, specific examples, adding unwritten context, and spending the entire lecture explaining why the majority of the class is wrong. He has not deepened my understanding of econ. Take for an easy A, but not if you need harder econ classes

Took it FA 17' and the class was cake. You can take the exams as many time as you want, they are online due at the end of the course. everything else is graded for effort. You can do the classwork at home, since it is on packback. Easy A

He is not a good teacher, I actually know less about Econ now purely because I was confused. But I took this as an elective so I'm not too bothered. I do not deserve an A+ but I got it because you can retake exams an infinite amount of times. Bad professor, but you should take the class for a free A.

Vazques makes you pay for Flip It and Packback for the class. You do Pre-lectures, Bridges, Quizzes, and HSQs. I suggest going to class and doing the Classwork. Classwork is 20% of your grade and for a lot of people make a difference. Go to class, do homework, and participate in EC and you are guaranteed an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good class to take for honors credit - knows what he is doing.

Professor Vazquez is currently conducting research in teaching techniques and how to engage students. The class has many components (Piazza, Packback, FlipIt, and Moodle). However the course structure changes by year. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you show up everyday you wont need to take the final. Vazquez is interesting and makes you think

His lectures are very interesting and the work is very easy. There's no midterm and the final is optional, and you can reattempt all quizzes and tests, so as long as you do the work, it's an easy A. The only downside is that FlipIt is like $80 and it's worth a good portion of your grade.

So this is tough to admit. Jose makes you work a lot, but its actually really worth it.  I think this might be the first class where I'm really genuinely interested in whats going on. He has the capability of making you sit at the edge of your seat on what comes next. Class seems hard, attendance mandatory. Packback is really fascinating and "fun".

When i took Prof. Vasquez's econ class fall semester of 2016, it was a relatively fair and easy class. However, as some people have mentioned, he totally changed the rating of the class from easy to extremely difficult. Some of my friends took it last semester and were struggling because of how hard the exams were. Hope he makes it easy again!

Vazquez is a big fan of the "make you do the material on your own" approach. All lectures are preassigned, but behind a paywall on his own website. Given that you get grades 80 on your exams, you will pass without the need for homework. Although his first and final exams are kind of unfair in their question phrasing, he offers a lot of EC.

I am currently in this class because of what other students said. Its easy blah, bah, blah. However, once I got into the class, the professor decides to switch it up, now it happens to be one of my hardest courses. The highest I have gotten is a C- on the midterms. Honestly, I hope you get an easy semester because he is not consistent.

I took this class because it is required for my major and heard it was an easy A. The class has changed a LOT since last semester. Online and in class tests are impossible (the highest I've gotten on a test so far is a 68%) I study and we get to use notes and our laptop and everyones still getting D's and C's which is awful.

The class is pretty straight forward. Just about all of the work is online, and class isn't mandatory but he uses iclickers and you can get extra credit from it if you go. Midterm is online and final is open note, but would still probably study a little for it anyway.
This class is very easy to get an A in. However, you don't really need to learn anything to get a good grade.
awesome teacher really allows students to succeed
ECON102 is a class you should not miss in your college life and I extremely like the music Prof Vazquez plays everytime before class.
Amazing Person
He has awesome lectures. Most of the work in the class is done online. Going to class will not matter a ton in the end, but I honestly look forward to his lecture every time.
all online work

The easiest course I have ever take. You do not need to go to class, if you find read the materials he posted online is helpful. The midterms and final are all open book exam. You don't need to remember anything, just write them down on your notes and you will get almost full grade.

He's... okay. Honestly, I haven't learned anything. My friend has the other teacher, and she's actually learning things in ECON while I don't think I've learned much. You can use your notes for midterms and exams, sure, but I'd rather have been able to actually learn something. It just feels like he doesn't care.
Easy to pass, vivid lectures.

Basically show up and get the clicker points to get a B. The 3 exams are online so you can google all the answers. He has 12 quizzes on moodle. 2 are dropped. The final is in class and open note. I got a C+ which sucks, but I never went to class. So 'm very salty about how dumb I was. Don't be me. GO TO CLASS!

Super easy online quizzes. You take 3 midterms, all of which are also online. What makes this better is that out of the 3 midterms you take, only two are counted towards your grade. Final is open note, and is all repeat questions from past quizzes/tests. Super easy if you take the time to learn the basic concepts.
The easiest A I have ever gotten including high school courses.
Lots of free points if you show up to class. One midterm is dropped, and you can use your notes to help you on every test.

Easy A. You get unlimited tries on the weekly online quizzes. The midterms were all online. He let you take an answer bank into the final. I would recommend joining study room for the answer banks. Overall, very easy A.

Awesome teacher! He gives out so much extra credit. Midterms are online, as well as weekly quizzes, and prelectures. Final is open book/notes. If you have to take ECON, Vazquez is the only way to go. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you get extra credit by going and doing the I-Clickers.
This professor offers many chance for bonus points.
Easiest class ever. Show up to lecture for a whole bunch of extra credit.
too good to be true. 3 credit hour class, but study like you'd do for 1/2 credit hours. amazing lectures, amazing grades
It is an easy A.

If you're looking for an easy grade without learning a whole lot, take Vazquez.  I ended up with a solid A in his class, but can't tell you the basics of microeconomics.  His style of experimenting with teaching styles hinders the whole learning environment but he makes up for it with a LOT of extra credit and by giving relatively easy tests.
Class was really very easy and the lectures were interesting and clear. The prelectures were (mostly) great. If you show up you'll get an A.

Should be a pretty easy A. Online test are pretty easy and his lectures are ok. He gives out a ton of extra credit which is nice. The final is open note but he changed a lot of the questions this semester which is why grades are lower this semester.

Very easy and by far my favorite teacher. Weekly online homework assignments that you have multiple attempts on. 2 out of the three midterms were open booknote and they were exactly the same as the previous exams. The third midterm was online and you could easily find the answers. Lowest midterm dropped. Highly recommended if you like easy A's.
Vazquez makes lectures fun while still clearly going over the material from the prelectures .

Horrible instructor. Great entertainer. Lectures are treated as a game constantly meant to trick and not teach you.  No incentive to learn, given the easiness of the material. Too many people get grades not indicative of effort and knowledge of the subject. Class did little to add to what I learned in AP Macro.

Econ 102 is in a huge auditorium.  Uses iClicker questions as participation extra credit.  Very amusing in class, usually explains things well.  On occasion he has been misleading, but I only noticed because I had already learned what he meant from the online lectures before class.  I wish I could take another class with him.

Great professor! Made lectures comprehensible and enjoyable. Given material was so good and applicable that the textbook wasn't needed at all. Very understanding and helpful when you have issues too. Workload was fair.

Super easy teacher but feel that I only aced the class bc all the questions were basically the same with little variation. As far as real world application, I feel like I didn't learn much. You don't really need to go to class. Lectures were confusing to me, I relied mostly on the prelecture videos. Textbook is available, but I didn't buyread it.

OMG Jose is the best. He is the hottest teacher you will ever have in your life. His lecture is hilarious and he gives a lot of extra credits. Quiz and mid terms are all online, which is very easy. He is very nice guy... gosh I want to take ECON 102 again

This is the kind of professor that I look up to. As an electrical engineer, I took this as a Gen Ed, and I would take it again. I love this class, and I will remember it for the rest of my life. The class itself is very easy, discussion sections and lectures can be skipped, (although I would never skip the lectures). Easy A as well.
Vazquez is a fun and solid professor. Sometimes lecture can be a bit fast and I feel like he skims topics without enough depth, but he's popular with his students.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! You technically don't need to go to his class to pass because it is all on line but I  found myself going anyways because he is so entertaining. Test are very easy and online so you can taking it with friends or google.

He's a very easy teacher that gives out a lot of extra credit.  Also, the tests are online and the final is open-note and open-book.  His lectures are great, though, to be honest.  He is very entertaining, too.
Vazquez is awesome. Gives out a lot of credit and class is easy.

Lectures are interesting, must go to them bc use of iclicker points. Online quizes that you can retake multiple times to get full points. Tests arent too difficult. Would recommend if looking for a class without alot of work.

JOSE IS THE BEST. Seriously take this class with him it will be the best decision you ever make for your career at UIUC. He's amazing. All exams are online except for the final, but the final is open book, notes. You get to drop your lowest midterm grade as well. Weekly quizzes & prelectures but he drops a lot of them. And he's big on extra credit.

Joseee!!! He's the best professor ever, he canceled classes frequently but that didn't even matter since he made his classes fun. Barely use the book, drops a exam, drops quizzes and pre lectures. hes basically giving you a A. all the exams are online as well.
super funny, he brought his dogs to explain concepts of economics. He's a cool guy

best thing you can do for yourself as a student at u of i is taking econ with him. not only is his class ridiculously easy, but all the other econ teachers are very boring and their classes are hard. everything is online, lots of extra credit, no papers
Easiest class ever. gives out a lot of extra credit, quizzes and exams are open notes. Jose is funny and an interesting teacher.

Vazquez was one of the easiest profs ever. He makes lecture interesting and gets the students' attention. His accent was hard to understand at first but it got easier with time. The exams were really easy and were taken straight from the weekly quizzes. The only time I ever used the textbook was on the final. He also gives a lot of extra credit.

By far the best professor I have had so far. Very interesting and engaging, knows how to keep the attention of close to 600 students in a lecture hall. The exams were easy but still taught me a lot of skills. One of U of I's biggest assets for economics/finance/business.
Very funny and entertaining man, but very confusing. Has trouble explaining the material where it can be understood. You basically have to teach yourself, which makes the class seem pointless.

The class is quite easy. You will have weekly online quizzes, pre-lecture quiz to take (only 4 questions at most).  Attendance is not mandatory, but he always has iclicker questions.  He offers a lot of extra credit.  Vazquez is a very funny guy and makes the class interesting.  Explains course material clearly, and make the course enjoyable.

This guy is the bomb! From giving extra credit for ppl going on dates to bringing his dogs in to class, Jose Vazquez has definitely converted a subject that could otherwise be extremely tedious and boring into the most fun class of this semester for me :D
awesome

Very easy class. Lecture not required, but very interactive and lots of extra credit opportunities. 3 exams all open note, internet, book, etc. Weekly quizzes that can be taken until 100% is earned. Basically impossible not to get a good grade. Discussion section is somewhat helpful.
Easy course for almost every one. And Jose's is fun
He is one of the best in the university. Although my major is CS, I start loving Econ because of him.
he is cool
great techniques
His lectures are very entertaining and enjoyable. Best lecturer I've had so far by a long shot. He makes good use of IClickers to his audience of several hundred students engaged.

While Jose was an interesting and funny guy, his lectures were often confusing, despite the generally easy concepts. He kept his TAs uninformed, and overall the class was sloppily put together. Luckily, all three of the midterms are online, and there is no reason why someone shouldn't get a good grade in this class. If you want an easy A, take him.

He does not teach in his lectures. He just gives questions for i-clicker extra credits during lectures. His midterms were online, which are pretty much all found online. There are weekly quizzes. The final was word for word from the midterms. Just teach yourself by reading the book and practice the quizzes before exams.

Worst. teacher. ever. he explains nothing, and gives awful examples that i cant understand. iclicker questions in class are usually much simpler than quiz questions. you get to the quiz and wonder when you discussed any of it in class. basically ,you teach yourself if you dont want to fail. i also have trouble understanding his accent.

Literally, the most confusing teacher/professor I've ever had. He "knows" economics, but has no idea how to explain it to anyone. His clickers/quizzes/exams are so contradictory and usually have more than 1 right answer, but you're supposed to choose the "most correct" answer. I barely learned anything and regret having him "teach" me.

i would not advise taking econ with him. going to class is pointless since he explains nothing. his i clicker questions are easy but the quizzes are so much more difficult. i have gained nothing from taking econ with vazquez.
It's extremely easy and even don't have to pay attention. Just do all the practice questions posted on the website before the exam and you will get an A. And he is soooooooooo charming!

His lectures are interesting and his test questions are the practice questions that he posts online word-for-word. Even the final is comprised of practice questions and old midterm questions AND you even get extra credit for attending lecture! I'd highly recommend taking his class.

It's like the easiest class ever and he literally throws extra credit at you. Don't even have to go to class unless you like extra credit and then you don't even have to pay attention. He even drops your lowest test grade.
Good professor. Too cool for school. Isn't too clear but has amazing teaching techniques.

I really liked Vasquez until I took the final.  I was doing well in his class and enjoyed his lectures, he made them interesting and applicable.  However, a lot of people, including myself, failed the final after doing well on the tests all semester.  I felt that it was totally unexpected and unfair which is why I'm no longer a fan.

One of the best Econ profs at U of I. He uses good examples and makes the class more interesting. If u go through the practice questions the midterms are easy and u r allowed to bring a cheat sheet. But the final was ridiculously hard
He is nice and helpful, but his class is extremely hard!!! Half the class failed the first midterm and he doesn't curve at all! Don't take him if you want an A or B in the class!!!

The class was pretty easy, but pretty much everyone got a D or failed the final. He wouldn't respond to students on Compass who were complaining that there was a fundamental problem with it; no one did well on it. His questions all throughout the semester were ambiguous and just odd in general. And your fate in the class depended on those questions

This class was very stressful. They must have screwed up the scantron arrangement or something. I like economics a lot and I worked hard on studying, and I left the exams feeling confident, and then I'd get my grade and I'd have a 60% or something. On one exam I got 13/25 when they returned with my grade. I do not trust Vazquez or his TAs' exams.

I believe that the test for the final had a fundamental problem and professor refused to address this. By not responding to emails, this def put heavy burdens on the students. I also cannot emphasize on the deceptive word of "extra credit". Do not trust that word. I assure you; it will not help you out much. Do well on tests!!!!
Lectures were boring. Just attended them for Bonus points. Exams were easy. Easy class
Easy and interesting class, easy midterm, but hard final.
Def. an easy A class. Tons of extra credit. Best economics class I have ever taken.
Gives out a lot of extra credit. The final was ridiculously hard but ended up with an A. Definitely the best ECON professor here hands down.

Very easy teacher. He makes lectures interesting with plenty of relevant examples. Test are made from questions from the homework and the lectures, so they are all problems that you have done before. He lets you use cheat sheets on all the tests, so put example problems on the Cheat sheet! he also drops the lowest midterm and homework assignment.

Jose uses examples that make class more interesting and are more relevant to our age group. He gives you tons of practice questions before exams, and cheat sheets. The questions on the exams are always the practice questions, so just put the practice Qs on your cheat sheet! If you have to take Econ 102, i would DEFINITELY recommend Jose!!

Jose makes the class really easy with lots of extra credit. You get to use a cheat sheet for each of the 3 exams (and 3 cheat sheets for the final). Lowest midterm is dropped. But, the final is considerably more difficult than the other exams and practice questions. You really need to know the material for the final! (Fall 2011)
easy a class. great professor, offers a lot of extra credit and you get to use cheat sheets on the exams! and he drops the lowest exam grade. makes econ an interesting subject. jose is awesome!

By far the easiest 302 professor.  This class was way easier than 102 and 103.  He basically gives you the answers on the tests on compass and the homeworks are very simple.  You  drop your lowest test.  Also a lot of extra credit.  This really should not be a 300 level class.  Try to get him as the other 302 classes are notoriously difficult.
Good teacher. Gives a lot of extra credit opportunities
i love him soooo much. I have never saw such a charming professor. He explains everything well, and he is so hot. I really want to be his TA when i were a mater of econ.

Jose goes above and beyond to make sure his students succeed. He offers extra credit and makes sure that everything you need to be successful on exams can be found online. He is a quality professor. I highly recommend him.

Jose is one of the best Econ professors that I have had. He makes lecture fun. I have NEVER fallen asleep in class.He always stay after class and after office hours to help answer questions. It's almost impossible to not get an A with all of the extra credits, drop lowest test score, straight-forward exams.I highly recommend him!

Jose is the man. He keeps a subject that many find dull quite entertaining. The lectures are based off the text, but are much more conceptual than fact based. He provides a real world perspective on a very theoretical subject. HE IS AWESOME!
Awesome teacher.  The class is pretty much a joke but he teaches you the material in a way that is really easy to understand.  All of these negative posts are wrong.

He was an okay lecturer but never responded to emails and basically refused to have any contact with students outside of class. He also forgot to submit our grades at the end of the semester, giving everyone a NR for the course and repeatedly blamed issues on "the grader" instead of taking responsibility for his own mistakes.

After forcing the entire class to read the syllabus and take a quiz on it to make sure we understood, he completely disregarded the syllabus and ignored the grading policies it outlined.  He doesn't realize that pop quizzes don't make sense in an online setting.  Weekly homework was long, and some questions were verbatim repeats of others.  Avoid!
Doesn't know what he's talking about, makes easy calculations seem like 500 level math theory.  Tests are confusing as hell and lecture is pointless.  Take it at a community college.

Pretty easy course. A lot of online homework, 3 tests where cheat sheets are allowed, and a little extra credit offered throughout the semester. The extra credit wasn't really worth it based on the amount of work put into it, but it's good that it's there. I didn't go to lecture the majority of the semester and I still did well in the class.
Has to be the easiest professor for this class. four 6 question tests that you get a cheat sheet with anything you want on it. If you can take it with him absolutely do
Jose is not a bad professor...he's just a terrible test maker. It all seems relatively easy until you get his tests which were ambiguous as hell and you don't feel at all prepared for them.

He keeps the class interesting, the homework relates to the lecture material, but his tests were totally off. They were worded weirdly and were confusing. Even though I studied, I didn't do well on the tests, which messed up my grade.
Definitely a fun class and need to attend to get the 2 bonus points + bonus points on the exam. Wait for this guy to teach before taking gotheil.
BEST ECON 102 Professor at U of I. Gets straight to the point in class material. Keeps students engaged. Jose is a genius.
Awesome professor. lots of bonus questions. you should definitely wait until you can get a class with him. goes circles around gohteil.

This course is easy and I think Jose is trying pretty hard to keep the students' interest. So I give him props. He basically provided everything[cheat sheet,taped lectures,previous exams,extra credit] you need to get an A, sadly people failed to take full advantage. He dresses well..but it doesn't suite his age.

I don't see why everyone is saying the material he teach in class is unrelated to microeconomics. He cut straight to the point. His tests are easy too. Anyway previous exams are the best material, read over textbook, and go over the clicker questions and you'll ace the course.
Tests were ridiculously hard compared to lecture material.  Several of the questions had grammar errors as well which led to ambiguity.
His tests did not seem to have to do with what he was teaching and some of the questions were ambiguous due to the way they were worded.

Vazquez seems like a pretty good guy and he dresses like a model, but his test have almost nothing to do with lecture.
