And the information in the lectures don't really allow you to truly comprehend economic principles; you have to use your book for that.  Also, the test are way to hard for the material presented.

This class SHOULD be easy, but sadly it's a Gen Ed that's harder than it should be. The material is easy enough, but Vasquez' tests are ridiculously ambiguous, so you never know what he's really getting at. His lectures are pointless except for the occasional iClicker extra credit and he also seems to get crap TAs. Just read the book and good luck!

Jose is the man. His keen fashion sense and stylish jeans make coming to class a must. He claims that he isn't trying to "trick" you on the tests but his exam questions are always tougher than his example questions. Beware of hard tests.

Lectures are pretty pointless with examples pertaining to sex, drugs, or alcohol. Makes simple concepts confusing. However, if you have background knowledge in econ, this class should be a breeze for you. Get cheat sheets on tests and extra credit points from iClicker and labs.
tricky exam...

Jose is amazing! What a great guy! He is hilarious, cool, and HOT.  He is hard to understand at first because of his accent, but you will get used to it. He is much better than Gottheil.  If you have the choice between the two, take Jose all day :)

Really easy. Drops the lowest midterm. But lectures are just short of useless. They mostly contain pointless examples relating to parties/alcohol/sex. He thinks it helps keep college students attentive but it doesn't. Just reading the relevant chapters properly before the exam guarantees a good grade. Exams contain a lot of Aplia questions.

Ugh. This man is the most useless prof ever. I knew the material going in, but if anything he made it more confusing. He complicates the most basic material with irrelevant examples. probably better than gotheil though..

Easiest econ teacher ever. He doesn't teach much though. But If his exams were any easier, it'd be unfair. You get a cheat sheet and he drops 1 exam grade. Gives extra credit with iclickers/labs, so theres an incentive to attend class. I never went, but read a little from the book to do the online homework. If you have common sense you'll get an A.

Irresponsible and Incompetent Economics Professor who doesn?t teach very well (Agreed Fact). He uses the same PPP deck that he used 4 semesters ago, and he does not change the ERRORS in them. Once said, "Last semester nobody found this error" (thinks its funny) People like him because he lets the class use Cheat Sheets and drops your lowest exam.

I found this class to be more difficult than I expected. His lectures, while fairly engaging,  don't really do a good job of covering the material on the exams. The fact that one of the three major exam scores is dropped makes this class fairly easy, but don't go in expecting a cakewalk just because he isn't Gottheil.

i'm not a big fan. i took econ before, so i knew the concepts but when he would explain i would just end up confused. he likes to do examples and stuff BEFORE teaching the concept, which isnt helpful. he likes to walk around FA as he talks, which is distracting. but good news you get cheat sheets, tests all mc, drop lowest exam, and no book!

Everything you learn is common sense. Many concepts arent even covered in class and often the concepts are just alluded to and arent directly engaged. After the first few weeks I stopped going to class, wound up with an A+. In terms of covering the material, easily the worst prof Ive had. That being said, the class is really easy.

He is awful.  Tries to make things "cool" and "interesting", but you just end up missing the point.. I wouldn't recommend this for Econ majors because you're actually going to need to know the material later.  For all else, it's ok if you don't need to retain anything from this class.

You get a cheat sheet on exams and your lowest grade is dropped, but that didn't make the class easy for me.  Exams are pretty vague.  I wasn't really a fan and didn't learn much, but I'd still take Vasquez over Gottheil when it comes to micro econ.
He sucks. The guy cant even speak or write in proper english and the tests are nothing like the homework or classwork.  This was by far the most disappointing class I've taken at the university.

GREAT GUY!!  The class was really hard and confusing (bcus i don't understand econ). But if you went in for help he made things REALLY clear!  Our class had 3 take home exams and a TAKE HOME final!  No work except for like 2 really busy weeks at the end and a term paper. REALLY nice HOT guy! amazing dresser too.
I'm sure he knows his econ well, but is overall not a smart person. He certainly enjoys being himself. It's an easy class to take if it's required.

202's similar to his 102. There are 3 midterms, one of which is dropped. Online hw, clickers. and a final. In fall 06, he basically made every waste $ on a crappy clicker (not an i-clicker). We were pretty angry. Go to the discussion for further help. Jose's exams have a lot of variance. Some are really easy, some are pretty hard.

This guy is a great teacher.  He tells you exactly what you need to know for the exam.  GREAT TEACHER!  Sometimes, you will have to make an effort and study because some of the stuff may be fuzzy like a panda.  BESIDES THAT HE IS HILARIOUS!!!! HE DRESSES LIKE HE IS GOING CLUBBING!!  MY FRIENDS ALWAYS LAUGHED AT THAT!!  SILLY JOSE!

What can I say? Jose is just that dude. His class is enjoyable and he is very fair. He lets you drop your lowest test score and his tests are not that bad. Reccomend him for any econ class. Much easier than everyone else.

He is just awesome.  If you took any kind of stats in HS you'll do just fine.  He's so laid back and you get out of class early almost every lecture. Accent = TOTALLY HOT! If only his teaching skills were as good as his fashion sense...

Jose's a good professor, but he has the privilege of having some great TA's. Harry Tsang and Micah Pollak are great teaching assistants, and if you have either of them, you are very lucky. Jose has a great option of dropping your lowest midterm grade (out of three exams) which is good in case you have a bad night or anything like that. Good luck!

he was very unapproachable. when i got sick and spent part of the day in the hospital and missed an exam b/c i had a 102.3 temp, he refused to let me make it up although i had a doctor's note. i felt like i was being treated unfairly, almost as if i was being punished for getting sick. i was very upset over this.

Fundamentally one of the easiest teachers you will ever have - however he doesn't teach very well. Lets you use cheat sheets on exams and gives extra credit if you attend lecture. The problem is he asks VERY ambiguous questions on the exams. I would still pick him over any other teacher though.
Alright teacher, however we're 5 weeks behind. Lets you use cheat sheets on all exams, and drops the lowest exam grade - the material he teaches is extremely ambiguous though.
Great Professor. Keeps dry material interesting.
SexY :-)

Great professor, very helpful. The class is weighted very heavily, but its easy to get a B or A. If you show up to class and do the labs you automatically get extra credit, and class is usually pretty funny.

This guy is great. Don't need the book. His lectures have tons of mistakes but with all drug and beer examples this is the only class i went to during the semester. The dude is simply a baller. Oh and supposedly he's my father-in-law.

Pretty easy class.  Basic stats are learned, nothing really too tricky.  He moves slowly so it's easy to keep up.  First exam was extremely easy, 2nd pretty tough, 3rd alright.  Cumulative Final, HW is online, not too bad.

First off, I never used the book. I would advise you to just borrow one, if ever needed. I have Vazquez again for 202. His exam questions are quite vague. I feel like I sufficiently argue that multiple answers are right depending on how you read the question. My TA was terrible so I never went to discussion.If you have a good TA, they help with HW.

Don't know if he still teaches this section. I took all his lecture notes and helpful examples for granted and ended up with a B in the class -- if I hadn't, I would have had an A. He is really organized and will take the time to sit down with you. Recommended! 302 is hard in general, don't know about his teaching in that class.
I enjoyed his class, though it was pretty difficult. Lowest grade I've received at U of I.

Wow.. where do you even begin. Honestly, out of my past 3 years at U of I, "Jose" is by far the worst professor I ever had. He has so many mistakes and errors on his homeworks, exams and everything in between it's unreal that he is still employed at the University. His tests are ambiguous, his grading style is ridiculous, and he has wasted my life.
Much harder class than I thought it would be because his tests are ambigious. He is a good teacher but wierd grader.
Awesome professor!

I agree with the comment below mine, students should understand material before the test, not after he answers thier questions regarding the test.  He also has a very unclear grading system that make it impossible to accurately gauge your progress in the class.  He tries very hard to make econ intersting, but he still fails as an effective teacher.

The tests are extremely ambiguous and questions sometimes deal with the craziest topics I've ever heard discussed in economics! Sure, he explains things well, AFTER the test is done and people bombard with questions due to his lack of ability to create a clear and straightforward test! Many people seem to be orgasming over his dress, but who cares?

Highly recommended.  Econ 302 is supposed to be an extremely difficult class, and it is.  But if you take it with Vazquez, you'll feel a lot better.  Much better to take it with him than any other professor.  He's a fun guy and you'll really enjoy him.

Vasquez wants people to do well.  The first exam is overwhelming (50% mean) because it is unlike anything you've ever taken. Text not necessary. Attend lecture, he often takes attendance through turning in class labs.  2nd and 3rd exams he allows cheat sheets, very similar format to 1st exam. Study by doing homework and lab questions several times.

Great professor, was clever in the way he taught. Put many of the economic topics into perspective with great examples. His tests aren't the easiest, but I learned a lot in his class, I really recommend him.
This teacher was horrible, his accent got in the way of my learning and he was just too difficult to learn from.  My TA spoke like she just got off the boat from China.
Prof. Vazquez keeps lectures interesting, and I've learned a lot this semester.
He is interesting to listen to in class, though sometimes his accent can get in the way.

I hated him at the beginning of the class because it seemed like he was not explaining the things that were on the test. It is a very differnt way of thinking about economics. His first test will be a shock, but once you realize how he wants you to think. THe material is pretty easy. 3 tests, no quizzes, and easy online HW's

I already took 2 classes that he teaches and am taking the another one next semester. He is definitely easier then the other professors though at times I feel I'm not learning what I need to learn. Class is very organized. He makes millions of mistakes on his powerpoints.
Good and fair prof.

His beautiful accent made paying attention in my 8am with Professor Jose Vazquez no problem.  He was very helpful and a great dresser, not to mention the fact that he's somewhat young and with it!  I went to his office to discuss a paper and he was burning incense.

He is a funny guy. He explains things very well and his tests are relatively easy (no suprises- you know what will be on the test). Such a snazzy dresser- i'm sure if I paid as much attention to the lecture as I did his appearance I would have done better.
He's got that fire, what else can you say.  Plus, he's good with numbers.  You wanna know what your chances are with him.... he could probably calculate them for you.
Jose is amazing!  He is very clear, very concise, and there will never be surprises on the exams.  Don't take econ with any other professors if you have a chance to take it with Jose!
Great Professor. There are no supprises on the exams, especially if you go to review sessions and are in class before taking the exams.

I love Jose, and you will too. I think he actually might be associated with 202 next semester, but definitely give him a try. If his dressing doens't impress you enough, then maybe his teaching will! :)

As everyone else said, he did dress rather well! For someone who had to take the class for a gen. ed., but hates numbers/econ, this was a great class. He explains things really well and grades fairly. If you can get Harry Tsang as your TA, he's really helpful (and a little crazy).

Omg i love this guy Vasquez, one of the best professor in this univerity, he goes very easy on the exams, and the overall course is fairly student friendly so u won't be stressed out, highly recommended

This is the guy you want to take. Much easier than Schultz.  You want to get in good with your TA becuase he might help your grade out in the end if your TA thinks you were deserving. Take Wen for a TA if you can. She rocks!

Jose is such an amazing guy! He's very skilled at economics! He's also pretty hunky! He dresses so nicely... I wish every guy dressed like him. And he's really easy to approach and talk to. He'll explain anything, and he gets back to every email he receives.
I've never actually gone to office hours or anything for him, but from lecture he's pretty clear.  Plus he's a snazzy dresser and man that accent whew.  Sorry I might need a moment.

Vazquez was a nice guy, but his class is completely unorganized.  He used another teachers slides, and then posted different ones online.  He was all over the place and exams tested concepts that we never covered in class.  He made the class much more complicated than it should have been.
Great teacher. Explains everything clearly. A tremendous imporvement on Baer or Gothiel. Has a great accent too. Dresses so sharply!

Though the class itself is difficult, Professor Vazquez really tries to make it more understandable. He is always willing to help and involves students in class discussion. I would recommend him if you have to take this course.

He was an okay professor but he has horrible organization. He used another teacher's course packet, lecture slides, and mallards and tested on random concepts from all over the place. If he had his class in order, it would have been a breeze.
Easy class, tests easy, just as long as you understand it.  He used his own stuff but made us buy the notepacket.  Don't get the textbook you dont need it.

Great Economic Statistics teacher.  Examples are to the point, and he makes even hard statistic concepts easy to understand.  Test reflect exactly what is taught and there are no surprises.  Good lecturer too, highly recommend choosing him for any econ classes you can.

This guy can have a real problem with boundaries, honesty, ethics, owning up to his mistakes and errors, and he can be downright ruthless when you are at odds with him. Not above petty crime in the field. However, it is entirely possible and likely that many of the positive reviews above were honest and accurate. He can be that person, too.

Impossible to follow. Doesn't have a clue how to teach. Tests aren't based on anything useful. Just random things he said during class to check if you were there. If you're a visual learner or need any amount of structure in a lecture then dont take this course

Prof Stewart was a great professor for GEOL 208. He genuinely cared about his students and would answer any questions that you had. His exams are rather difficult as a lot of questions on the test were related to specific things he said during lectures. Do go to the lectures! The field trip was a very fun component of the course.

Fair professor. Understanding that you have a life outside of school. You basically get out of the class what you put in. Complete the readings, show up to lectures, and do the work. They will work with you to make sure you pass the class.
Long lectures and is very dry in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Stewart is a great lecturer and pretty funny and easygoing. His tests are fair, but focus heavily on lecture material. I suggest going to every class. If you write down everything he says in lecture and study from your notes, then his tests aren't so difficult. Textbook feels supplementary because all test questions come from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good professor. Clearly knows his stuff. Don't skip lecture, everything on the test is based on lecture. Gives pop quizzes. He makes lecture interesting and has a passion for the subject. However, he can be a bit disorganized. The midterm and final were hard and very specific. Don't expect practice tests or a review either. Would recommend.
Prof Stewart is a babe. An absolute gem. He's really witty/funny which makes the class fly by he and explains things very clearly. A+

See that flaming red pepper? Yeah, I'd say that's accurate. Stewart is a spicy man with layers of  intelligence and wit. I took this class thinking I was going to be watching  vids of seals and dolphins, but boy was I wrong. As long as you study, pay attention, and find men age 50+ attractive, you'll be fine.

Professor is a child. Seemed like he was high during class, would go on long rambling monologues that had little to do with the topic. Refused to add structure to course when I told him I had difficulty learning in his lecture. Failed his class, retook with another professor and got a B+.
Stewart is awesome. Not only does he make lectures more interesting, they are easy to understand. Essays are super easy because he doesn't even grade them himself.

Currently a freshman in my first semester and Dr. Stewart is definitely my favorite professor. I look forward to going to class and he makes his lectures very fun. It's a very good natural science gen-ed to take, though you have to work for an A. You will learn a lot of "cocktail information" from this guy. He's hilarious!

Hands down one of my favorite professors. He made class interesting, fun and I looked forward to his class. No one notices if youre not in class but i clicker points are taken. I learned much more than I expected and he his personality makes lectures enjoyable to attend. I definitely suggest taking any class with him!

I personally think that he's funnier than Altaner, but I would rather take the course with Altaner because he doesn't do i-Clicker participation. Go to classes because attendance is a huge component in your grade.
Easy. Cool dude.
Funny!

He is a good professor and is always making the class laugh.  The material gets boring at times but he tries to make it interesting.  Attendance for both lecture and discussion is mandatory because I clicker is 10% of grade and discussion assignments and homework due in discussion are a huge percent of your grade.

BEST CLASS I'VE EVER TAKEN! he makes jokes constantly during lecture. the homework is easy and you don't really need to read the book although this is not a blow off or easy A class! overall he makes this a great class and i always looked forward to his lectures...and i even learned some things in the process.

Its a large class so no one notices if you're gone. but the clicker questions presented during lecture do count into your grade. He goes off on tangents often which can be annoying but he's funny and you actually learn something from the class. You do need to read the book though, he doesn't always go over everything on the exams.

He was definitely interesting...always expect to stay exactly until the bell rings, he never lets class out early. He taught us what we needed to know. Made sarcastic comments a lot, so that made class bearable.
it is very important to attend class for clicker questions. He is really funny and i thought he was hot. HW was not difficult but it is really important to not blow the class off..

This class was NOT the blowoff I thought it would be...you really have to go to class for your iclicker points and so you understand the material...reading the book doesn't really help.  The tests are kinda hard...he's really funny though and his rants are great!  I guess he's kinda cute in an old guy sort of way...Do the extra credit in discussion

Going to class is pretty important to understanding the material and what will be on the tests.  He tells funny, interesting stories, and loves his work.  I'm not much of a science person, but I love this class.  The tests are medium-difficult.  You definitely have to study.  Not a blow off class, but not a TOO much work.  He's a great teacher.
After the first exam I realized that going to class was important, as well as very interesting. Great teacher. Not a blowoff class as I was hoping, but definitely recommended

Pay attention in lecture and study the notes you should be able to get an A.  The online quizzes and extra credit on the group portion of tests are easy points. Dr. Stewart is hilarious, tells crazy stories, and I really looked forward to going to class.

Great professor. One of my favorites at UofI. Really funny and loves talking about iceland, gin and tonic and how much his kids make him crazy. The Oceans isn't about marine biology its about the geology of the oceans but it still ends up being interesting. You do have to study some but its not that difficult unless you're useless in science

Prof. Stewart is hilarious and very good looking. He tries to fill the lecture with good 'cocktail party' information. However, this class is difficult. He's a cool guy, but if you are not interested in the oceans (how they're made and all that jazz, not swimming in them) or if you are terrible at science, I would not recommend this class.
stewart is a babe and class is very interesting. takes some work to do well..but its worth it

This class is def. NOT A BLOW OFF CLASS. It is also NOT about dolphins and pretty blue ocean water, like I thought it was. If you go to class and study for a good 15 hours before each test,you should get an A. Stewart is really hot though, and he is pretty funny! =)

So this class definitely isn't a blow off and takes a lot of studying to do well on the tests...but regradless the class is a lot of fun and full of interesting information and can be easy if you put in the work.  Prof stewart makes the class worthwhile.  He's a hotty and he is super funny so he keeps it interesting.  Likes to drink and let us know
He's really funny and a good teacher, I just don't like the class in general.

His classes are not blow off classes. He structures the tests so you have to go to class to be able to do well on them. If you go to class everyday and pay attention you should get a easy A, otherwise this class is somewhat difficult. He is a really funny and cool guy though. He loves to drink and smoke but he can also use a few spelling lessons.

Very funny, uses great examples in class. Tries to explain math, which may/may not be helpful. Tests are hard, but extra credit is available for each. Lab grading is very confusing, and the lab grade makes up a lot of your grade. Overall, the class is really interesting, as is Dr. Stewart, but labs and exams are quite a bit of work.

TAKE HIS CLASSES! he's hilarious, goes on funny rants during lectures. make sure you go to lecture for the iclicker points. Be sure to study hard for the exams though, it's definitely not a blowoff class, but one that you will enjoy.

I expected a somewhat easy physical science gen-ed when signing up for the course, but I ended up having to work hard for my A. Dr. Stewart's sense of humor  keeps the  lectures interesting, but make sure you keep detailed notes. The tests are DIFFICULT. Make sure you do the extra credit in discussion to keep your grade up.
Pretty easy class. Tests tend to be difficult, but enough point to make up for it. Likes to drink and makes sure you know it. Interesting topics.

Great prof.  Very funny, and knew what he was talking about.  Very fair on tests, helpful during reviews, and extremely clear at explaining topics.  Liable to go off topic from time to time, but it helps keep you awake.  I think you would have to try to bad grade, and it would still be difficult.  But seriously...coolest liberal ever.
Take this class! Easy A, very interesting

he's a nice teacher, likes the subject and i learned a lot. try to pay attention in to lecture and the tests are pretty good. he tries to help students understand, and most of the time you do understand.

Group exams, but make sure you still study yourself.  He is very passionate about this subject and it shows which makes being there more bearable .  Funny man.  I thought there was something cute about him for a 45-ish y/o guy.  Discussions did require some work.  Super approachable teacher.  Take this class for the Gen Ed.
He's totally hilarious. This class actually does require some effort, but I think it's pretty interesting. Lecture's totally bearable, discussion sections are kinda tedious.

michael stewart is a boss. He is hilarious and he makes going to lecture very easy. The online quizes are an automatic 100% for about 20% of your grade. The rest is based on the tests and the final. Go to lecture and study and you will be fine. The key is to not let the easiness of the first test deceive you into thinking they will all be that easy
very funny and definately out there. exams are based almost completely off lecture notes and slides and hardly ever text so attendance definately helps.
Hilarious and quirky. Makes things easy to understand and tells really funny stories about his college days.

This guy is amazing! I didn't know anything about this class before I took it, but boy am I glad I did. He is always telling jokes and stories. The class is actually kind of interesting too, which surprised me. Study the notes for an hour or two before the exams and you'll get an A easily.
funniest teacher at UIUC, class was challenging but fun and interesting with never a dull minute, TA Chris Henderson was awesome too!  Too bad he graduated. :(
I loved pro stewart hes a stud!!!
Cool guy, lectures are interesting, but by no means is this a blow off class. In general, if you go to class and study, you can do well. I did not, and got a C.

Stewart is a great professor. I went into the class not expecting much, but I ended up loving the class. Group exams. Tests are directly from lecture. Lots of pictures in lectures. Actually stayed awake in lecture.

Dr. Stewart is my favorite teacher here so far.  He was very goofy and told many off-the-topic stories, he's a little strange but its funny.  If u study the notes the tests are easy and u never have to open your book.  Good class and teacher!

Professor Stewart is one of my favorite instructors of all time. He is very funny and interesting, as well as informative.  I learned a lot from the class and it wasn’t difficult at all. Honestly, I never even opened up the book; all of the material that he tests you on is right out of the lectures. I highly recommend Dr. Stewart to anyone.
great...group tests are very nice and material is actually kind of interesting. lots of visuals. overall, need to study for the tests but if u know it ur fine.

An interesting class, but NOT rocks for jocks. This course IS DIFFICULT. I thought it would be a blowoff for a Gen-Ed, but his tests are quite hard. Interesting material and a funny guy, even at 9 AM, but I cannot repeat this enough: NOT rocks for jocks.
sooo incredibly clear. he explains things really well whihc means he actually teaches. and well for that matter.
It was a little harder than I thought, but I still did ok. Stewart can be pretty funny too.
Not as easy as I thought it would be. Clear in lecture.  Approachable. Funny. But he drops the lowest test grade???
he's a nice and funny guy, his powerpoints are really helpful, especially since he post it online, but the tests aren't as easy as I think they would be
Yeah ditto. NOT A BLOW OFF CLASS. totally hated it. but Dr. Stewart is funny and interesting. the class is pretty interesting too. But I got a C because I did terrible on the tests.
Good teacher and funny.  Can explain a bit too much at times, but all in all good!  Group exams, and he drops your lowest exam grade!

I took it as a blow off...its definitely not.  Who knew there would be so much to know about the oceans? Anyways hes a nice guy and his powerpoints are really clear and helpful.  he is Kinda sarcastic and goofy but thats one of the best parts of this class.
This class is harder than i thought, i took it as a blow off and ended up doing bad.
No Comments

No longer rocks for jocks, you have to study hard for those tests but lecture is interesting b/c he relates things to real life, section is tedious and boring, I dreading going every week, make sure you get a TA that speaks english
This class is supposed to be easy...apparently no one told him that!  His test blow!
No Comments
boring and slow lectures, not much information given on tests, projects, and homework. you are assumed to know everything from the start, and theres not many resources for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clemon is a nice guy, but his 270 lectures are very boring. I showed up just for I-clicker credit and worked on other stuff. The HW and exams are easy, but the factory projects are very time-consuming and tedious. I also thought the labs were pretty boring. Make sure you get a good group for this class or you will be painfully sorry!
Lectures are boring, monotone, have nothing to do with tests or lab. Lab TAs are all disorganized and disconnected. Bad class structure.
Lectures are boring and monotone, barely relate to tests and lab. Lab TAs do their own thing and are completely disconnected from the rest of the class. Very bad class structure overall.

Poor communication with TA team. Projects are long and difficult with vague grading criteria. Prof Clemon is not aware of what is going on in lab sessions. His lectures are confusing and not engaging. Lots of notes with no pauses or clarification. I don't recommend this professor at all. Fails to take accountability for his mistakes.
makes me want to transfer to gies
Bro has no clue what is going on in his own class. wants to make class harder for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is not helpful and assigns way too much work that is confusing and difficult for no reason
It is what it is.
Don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: No clear explanations, boring lectures
Homework graded like the graders had something against the class. Projects and labs were straightforward in expectations, although these may have been changed in future semesters. Vegemite.
The labs are amazing and educational.
ban ts guy from teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very dull lectures, projects have no clear guidelines. Very difficult to understand what you need to do to suceed in this class.
He has basically no resources for students. Does not discuss midterms or projects in lecture; he pretends like they do not exist. He makes you feel not smart when you ask a question.
Like he is so boring and the lectures are required and the notes are like 100000 pages long
evil man evil evil evil

Lots of homework which takes forever and is very difficult. Overall, it's just a harder class than it needs to be, and the professor is not very lenient. The class is not well structured. The tough homework grading leads me to retaking the class because I just didn't have the time to spend on it.

Lectures were aight, decently informative and engaging but they were slow sometimes. Homeworks sucked, a lot of stuff that was barely covered in class apart from a couple slides and a few of them were really tedious. Really time consuming

Awkward course structure. Homework has extremely harsh grading, and is only vaguely relevant to the lecture material. Group/individual projects were more manageable, but they take a massive amount of time with little to gain from. 
Additionally, the cutoff for an A is 94 which ended up dropping my final grade.

Pros

Cons
HW takes 4 hours minimum
HW graders will give straight up 0s for minimal mistakes
Regrade only gives back 1~2 points
Project 3 requires 40~60 pages minimum start early.

HWs and Projects are a complete waste of time. Absolutely disgusting.

Class needs reconstruction

Taking a 1-credit ice skating class would be more useful than this

Interesting lectures with engaging video demonstrations. However, homework seems to be unrelated to lecture slides. Some questions ask things that were never even covered in class. He expects us to use certain equations on homework that are not on canvas. Homework is graded harsh and all projects have confusing/vague instructions.

This class is just a little annoying sometimes, such as the homeworks which are graded insanely strictly (like 60% average) for content we spend little time in on class. Otherwise, the class is fine. Dr. Clemon is a solid lecturer and a funny, personable teacher. Lectures just go a little fast imo.

He did not respond helpfully when contacted by email or in Campuswire. The TAs are hit or miss. Homework is difficult and graded harshly. Most people I knew received about a 70% average on them. The project documents were worded confusingly. Overall, the class was demanding and required a lot of hours of work outside of the lectures and labs.

This guy has horrific handwriting but is generally okay. He's a new professor and teaches quite clearly, but the homework is god awful. It's common for a HW average to be in the 60s. They use the equations from lecture, but easy to lose lots of points. Projects and labs are graded by TAs, most of them are nice. Just remember proper formatting.
Clear lectures, fair exams.

Completely unclear grading. The whole class is based around his AI-slop centric ideas. Also I'm pretty sure 100+ students had to get their grade amended after final grades were due because he is incapable of grading correctly.

I wish this class was not required. It's poorly structured, and the grading is unclear. No point in going to the lectures either. The guy is impossible to contact outside of class. For 1 crh and no other requirements satisfied, it's not worth it.
Unclear grading criteria, low-quality instruction, and poor course management. I was a graduating senior and this was clearly the lowest-quality course I have ever taken.

He gave many students a final grade that is not A, but students have no way to check the grades that compose the final letter grade. The grades are literally non-transparent. We dont even know where we lose the points. I cant believe this kind of person can be and be called as professor or teacher. He is absolutely irresponsible.

The most poorly organized class I've ever taken. The deadlines kept shifting, the assignments kept changing. Not once in the entire semester was I ever fully clear about what to do. The lectures and assignments were AI slop. Using AI directly would've taught me more than him just prompting AI to run the class.

Genuinely such a joke class. EVERY assignment is an AI prompt response pasted into Canvas. The few lectures I attended were comprised of unhinged ramblings; for sure was just free styling the entire 50 minutes. Class is entirely one large group project with a "Team Mentor", which appears to be a pure dice roll whether they even contact you or not.

Bro had no original thoughts, the entire class was written by AI. He just pasted his prompts into a google doc for lectures and didn't even have the decency to put it in a slideshow. The grading was also super slow, but at least the class was easy.

This class is a joke. Every assignment, announcement, and post is generated completely by AI. I'm not even sure Michael proof-reads any of the assignments he posts, as there are countless mistakes. I do not know why this guy is getting paid 90k a year to be a ChatGPT wrapper.

Puts very little effort into the class and over utilizes AI to the extent that I'm not sure he actually knows what he's assigning (because he can't answer questions about them). Poorly organized class and lecture is blabber. He's not malicious but definitely impressively lazey, so he won't put effort to help you fix his mistakes.
Lectures prove you don't need to be an llm to produce ai slop

This is a really easy course (at least for me given our TA). The professor doesn't really matter for this course, it's just whoever your group mentor is. The prof is pretty funny in lecture even if you barely ever end up listening to the lecture.

This professor rly didn't do anything-good or bad. The course itself was always so unorganized. The deadlines kept shifting as well as expectations. They weren't that responsive on campuswire either. Honestly, it was just a semester long group project with some lecture quizzes that weren't that relevant. Didn't walk away with a whole lot.

The bulk of the course grade is from the group project's weekly updates, that is graded by a TA. This professor's lectures are fine: not super fun, but I appreciate the content. The quizzes can be done by just referring to the lecture slides. I think the professor is cool, and my group was lucky to have a chill and understanding TA for the project.

Lectures are really useless and taught completely by TA. Quizzes are super easy and can be answered from a quick glance at the slides. Knock out your project early so you don't have to worry about it during finals :)
He's a really nice professor but his class is not very useful.
There is no help in this class. The class is not structured properly and unnecessarily stressful. Learned absolutely nothing from this class.

Professor Woodley is great at communicating if you reach out to him, but the structure of CS 126 has been frustrating. The grading rubric is incredibly subjective and the only solution is to email your code moderator with every step. There is no time between projects and we aren't taught the material necessary to complete them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Lectures are merely a quick recap of the readings, he don't go into detail at all. The lectures themselves are not particularly useful.

Very hands off, delegating way too much responsibility to the course staff, who were generally unhelpful and did an awful job designing the assignments. His lectures are fine and the class isn't too difficult if you put in the required time, but the way that he runs the course vastly overcomplicates what should be an incredibly easy class.

Lectures were barely helpful during the first month of class. I stopped attending after they continued to be that way. Didn't bother to watch any of them later nor did I need to. I ended up having to use a ton of outside sources to work on my weekly projects. After 6 weeks, we switched from Java to C++. Pretty much expected to learn C++ overnight.

He never responds to emails and solely trusts senior staff and your grader to deal with your issues. He was often distracted during lectures and many times came with broken code. This made lecture even more confusing than it needed to be. Most people only came for iClicker points...

terrible prof, doesnt do anything in lectures, the TA's do all the work and theyre very bad at communication. dont teach you how to code at all, documentation for MP's are often wrong/not helpful. office hours havent helped at all. feel bad for any future students since unfortunately cs 126 is mandatory for cs majors.

The class would function better without the professor. The projects were created by the former instructor. Woodley's lectures are rambling nonsense and are mainly about himself - you have to learn everything on your own. If you are assigned a tough code mod, you will get the same grade as someone who put in much less work but had a lenient grader.

While people are talking about grading, it's his lectures that are his weakest. It's very unorganized and he would just talk for half an hour about random stories, which are rarely helpful. This semester, he realized that nobody cares about his lectures so he had to start doing iClicker to force students to come in.
Great lectures!
Best professor in UIUC!

Extremely unfair grading. What grade you get totally depends on if your section TA likes you or not. You might do much more than other students in your section but get a lower grade than them. It's a joke they say you can argue about that, because you know if you ever argue with the TA he/she will be more picky about you next time.
I loved the lectures. The assignments were also very practical and taught me a lot. Well-planned and organized course. I highly recommend this to any CS major that wants to enter industry.
He is an amazing lecturer. Sad that this is the only class that he teaches. I hope he teaches more classes.
My friend in another discussion section got the same grade as I did (did all requirements) for just showing up in the discussion. :))))))))))))
Fake extra credit, students beware.

Lectures are a joke, he reads off the outdated course website and tells anecdotes. Grading and Piazza are 100% handled by the TAs. Your only actual teacher in this class is StackOverflow, since even the documentation the class provides in insufficient. Professor is a complete non-factor in this class, be ready to learn a lot of code on your own.

There's no actual grade normalization. This means that you get whatever grade your moderator gives you, which means certain moderators will definitely give you a higher grade and you don't get to pick.
He didn't keep up with what was previously mentioned. Way too much subjectivity and no actual normalization.
Keeps lectures short and realizes if he doesn't have anything else to say. Casual attitude in class which was enjoyable.
Class is hard, but really approachable since professor is mainly looking for your attitude towards this class. Strongly recommanded

Prof. Nobili's lectures were very accessible and gave all the information I needed to do well in his class. There are a few books required for this class which cost quite a lot, but other than the books I had no issues with his class. Grading, especially on the midterm and final, is lenient.

reviews.comment: Professor Mauro Nobili's History of Africa provides a wealth of information through heavy lecturing supplemented by extensive readings. Grades are primarily determined by the midterm and final grade (70%) which can be scored high on by actively digesting course material. Sometimes lectures can get overwhelming, so individual review is recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Nobili is one of the most knowledgeable professors. He truly cares about his students and work. This class is very easy if you put in the work. Make sure to pay attention in lectures and take notes. He will give you hints on the exams and extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Definitely reading-heavy but doable, even as a gen-ed, if you do the readings before lecture and discussion. CHECK THE SYLLABUS! He's an amazing professor, and the class is definitely entertaining. You can tell he's very passionate and knowledgeable in everything he does, which is one thing that makes this class enjoyable. Would love to take 112
He is a great professor and has so much knowledge in his field! If you have the chance to take his class you should because getting a professor as knowledgeable as him is a rare experience.

History 200 was very tough, although It did teach me what I needed to know regarding essay writing. Still, this class kept me up very late at night all semester, i lived in the library, and it made me very stressed. Mauro knows what he is talking about, but bruh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. He's incredibly passionate about the subject but also very knowledgable and great at teaching. He's also a very kind person who remembers who you are and is very accommodating. His class is really interesting, you'll learn a lot. Some of the readings are lengthy but you can skim and get the main idea. Best professor I've had!

Great professor, and clearly very knowledgeable about what he teaches. Lots of writing but that's to be expected in any history course. Overall an amazing experience, prof is super nice and knows what he's talking about. I learned a lot of in-depth content that I don't think any other prof could teach. 100000/10.

Very easy and interesting class as long as you actually pay attention in lectures. You can get away with not reading the textbook. You should definitely read the documents and slides and watch the documentaries. Pay attention to class right before test are due for clearer instruction. If you don't do any of those be prepared to spend hours on test.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher, passionate about African history. Lots of readings but you can get away with skimming a lot of them. Super accommodating. Caring guy, very clear with what he wants on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Nobili is very passionate about what he does, and it's clear to see that through his lectures. The class is pretty easy, you mostly don't really have to do the readings to get a good grade. Very understanding, attendance would be mandatory but because of the pandemic he is compassionate.

Mauro was a really laid back and fun professor. He  made it really clear what he wanted from us and pretty much told us exactly what would be on the midterm and final. He doesn't give many assignments but he did expect quality on the few that we had.

Constantly forgot his train of thought, did not know how to answer student questions, was not helpful in office hours. In the exam he had mcq questions worth 10 points each which would auto drop you a letter grade on the exam if you got it wrong. Discussion sections were not productive at all. Very smart but cant lecture well.

Really bad lecturer. Lectures are fragmented and hard to keep up. Get ready to watch him stop for no reason halfway through class to buffer his head. If you have him switch IMMEDIATELY. Not joking. None of my classmates that I talked to about him had anything good to say other than the Chinese kids who liked his accent and the way he dressed.
If you get stuck with him, try to switch IMMEDIATELY. Not joking. Nobody I talked to who took his class had anything good to say other than the Chinese kids who liked his accent.

Bad lecturer, often forgets what he's talking about and in general is hard to understand. Tests are out of 100 points and have some MC and FR, but one MC question wrong could drop you down to a 90 already. Also is bad at answering questions, the times I did ask more often than not the response I got was "I don't know" or "I don't understand."

He taught very badly as he didn't know the materials well. He usually just stopped and found that something was wrong. Tests are really hard, and each question is like 10 marks with 100 total. You can literally just have 1 wrong or down A.

lectures make no sense whatsoever. everyone agrees because as every week went by, less and less people showed up to lectures. he consistently gets confused with what he's teaching and one time even said "uhhhh okay let's just move on to the next topic." basically had to teach the whole course to myself. practice exams very similar to real exams tho

Poorly structured course. You're graded by two tests and two presentations. The material is also very dense and his lectures were also very burnt as he just read off the slide. As someone else mentioned, I dont really have anything against the guy, way the course is structured is awful Theres a 1 midterm 1 final that are 50% of the grade and 20page essay for the other half. reviews.comment: Reading was too much but his lectures were clear and good.

Grossman is one of the best poli sci professors I've ever had, he makes his lectures equally entertaining and informative. Super nice and easy to talk to. Exactly everything that was on each exam was taught in the lectures, though I recommend studying with the weekly textbook readings as well. As for the essays, the difficulty of grading varies wildly, since your TA grades them.

As annoying as it was to only have 3 assignments (midterm, final, and paper) this class was really not that bad. Grossman's a great professor would recommend

I liked Grossman a lot but I honestly wouldn't recommend this class unless you have to take it or you're really into IR. It's only graded by the midterm, final, and a paper. No study guides. The class isn't bad, I just personally wish I didn't take it.

Grossman is a rockstar. His lectures were the highlight of my week, and I felt welcome to participate in class. He gave solid feedback on my work, and was always willing to meet. reviews.comment: He goes on tangents a lot. The lecture slides are basically blank, and its hard to listen because he talk about random stuff that sort of has to do with the topic. Very lecture-heavy course, and the assignments (4 essays) are basically representations of how much you understood lectures. Near impossible to get 100% on the essays. Very engaging lecturer, often sneaks lots of pop culture references and humor into his explanations of real-world events.  Makes political theory easy to understand with lots of anecdotes and detailed run-downs of all the political theories.

Professor Grossman is a fantastic teacher with super interesting and entertaining lectures. He's always there to help and give feedback on papers. I learned so much from taking all of his courses; his teaching style is top-notch. Highly recommend!

reviews.comment: awesome prof who is funny and knows what he's talking about!! workload is very reasonable!

Professor Grossman is one of my favorite professors at the university. He is very intelligent and his lectures are always entertaining. If you want to learn, he makes it fun and enjoyable. This is the 3rd class I have taken of his and each course was great.
So easy. The whole class was graded by discussion posts and two opinion papers. One of the easiest classes I have taken.

Not much to say. Cool professor. Lectures are interesting, especially for (but not limited to) PoliSci students. The entire course consists of three papers, a final paper, and lectures -- very straightforward. Would definitely recommend as an easy GPA boost.

Professor Grossman clearly loves what he teaches, you can tell by his lectures. He is super fun and makes lots of references, so people understand his content even more. Really great professor who is focused on making sure you learn as much as possible and is always accessible during office hours or after class to talk with students.

reviews.comment: Grossman is a great professor. The courses he teaches in he loves, he is really nice to students, and he has his own news site he publishes in. reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory and lecture slides are posted online, but the material is definitely revisited on the midterms. Grossman is very open to guiding the lecture to what students want to talk about. Syllabus isn't always followed but it doesn't really affect you. Funny guy. Knows his stuff.
Good experience. Knows a lot about National Security. Would definitely take again.

The daily lessons take forever, and there is so much convoluted text/videos to go over literally nothing. Also, I'm pretty sure many written explanations are AI generated. Easy course after he gave an additional drop. You can drop your last two quizzes to finish this course before two weeks of the final week.
Why are the lessons so long everyday? They aren't explained well either.

This is the worst class I've taken at UIUC. The lectures are poor at best, and Professor Nowak frequently reads off a script. The tests are very easy to fail due to no partial credit. This class truly hurts UIUC's CS reputation.

This class has a lot of busy work. The lessons do not adequately support learning. Even though I have an A it is because of a lot of extra effort that I have had to put in. The class gives you nearly no ways to succeed. I would recommend taking the profficiency exam or taking the course at Parkland and transferring it in.

Frustrating professor that makes quizzes lots of content in limited amount of time and huge MPs that are lots of work. Recitations aren't very helpful and his lessons are pretty unhelpful as well. Overall just a class that is way more work then it should be.
Worst professor ever!!! He doesn't know how to teach. His quizzes are extremely hard.

Easy course, professor who doesn't care about students but more about the TAMU tradition of HOWDY

CS 128 is structured terribly because of him. Why am I taking 2 CBTF tests that cover random assignments from 2 weeks ago??? really bad

The lecture system is abysmal and hard to follow many times. Course work is also way higher than typical classes and the assignments are often confusing or redundant. This class is basically impossible for beginner cs students.
One of the worst teachers I've had in 3 years. Needlessly difficult. Incredible load for no reason. If he ever gets a class outside of CS128 -- AVOID. Sorry if you're stuck with him.
This class has a far too intense workload for a 3 credit hours.

Avoid at all costs. Run. I mean it, run. If you can't, make sure you're already a C++ expert by the time the course starts. Otherwise, MPs will take up all day every day, TAs are both hard to access and a lot of them are as confused as you are, and the professor's only advice is to watch his videos, which are super long, and unhelpful. Good luck

The class is structured so atrociously shit. He chooses to make students lives a pain in the ass by not including make files and starter code. The lessons are at times poorly worded. There’s literally no sense of community in the class. MPs are unnecessarily long and vague. It's many aspects of this class that make it absolutely dreadful.

This class is an absolute waste of time, and I am not sure how he was able to get his job. There are too many lectures, the MP's are straight up ridiculous and interfere in my time to do many other things. For a CS major, I am worried for my career and my future due to this absolute nonsense of a class.

I would say avoid him at all cost but you likely won't have a choice. It's a required class and you basically have to teach yourself everything through the videos. Don't expect to get help since at least half the time the queue is frozen as ice and on top of that there are rules on when you can and can't go to office hours

Good luck with his 5 - 9 lessons (each lesson with 30 - 60 minutes videos and with multiple choice questions or coding homework), 1 quiz (varies from 20 to 40 lines of code, and maybe out of contents), 1 lab(at least 30 lines of code) and 1 MP(varies from 100 lines to 400 lines of code) every week!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Came mid semester to comment that the lectures are always longer than they need to be because he fails to get to the important teaching points effectively. The lecture questions are too often slightly irrelevant to what he's directly talking about or worded very strangely.The lectures are just straight up boring.

The class was just so boring in so many ways. There are so many ways he chooses certain aspects of the lab and MPs to be unnecessarily hard and hard to understand and it's such a waste of time. It's so frustrating and annoying I've never experienced this in a class before. For Intro II CS class, it sure did not ignite my passion for CS.
Terrible professor

Absurd amount of lecture time, especially compared to later CS courses. Not a good understanding of his students level - overexplains certain things and leaves you confused in others. Asisgmnets are hastily made and often rely on you having watched 50 minutes/day of specific material that you won't use again.

Very difficult to get from a TA/CA. Prof cannot give much useful feedback if you are stuck with MP, he would tell u to review his lesson again(which, btw, onlined version and I wonder if he would update them each semester). So you are basically on your own for this class and shall not anticipate too much help from course staff.

A really good lecturer. Really no problems with him as a teacher, but more as a course organizer: having warm-up exercises along with each lecture would prove really helpful since most coders learn better by trying and failing at applying new concepts rather than watching lectures.

Nowak is one of the most passionate professors I have met. He is always super quick to respond on the discussion forum, and his online lectures are as good as they get. Unfortunately, they are phasing out TRAs, which were probably the nicest kind of assignments since they involved fewer but smarter lines of code.

If you are comfortable with basic programming before this class, it isn't too hard. I found the lectures very useful, but they aren't necessary and you can just read the slides he posts. The class is a solid amount of work: an MP, TRA, and lab weekly (about 10hrs total/wk) + 200 minutes of lecture. If you put in the work, it's a fairly easy A.

I think all of the reviews here are slightly harsh considering FA21 is the pilot semester for CS128. That being said, Nowak's lectures aren't exactly fun or innovative. He isn't inspirational and seems to have a problem answering your questions on the forum. Nothing exceptional. The class is a lot of work but it definitely teaches you a lot.

His class, CS 128 is run abysmally. No support whatsoever. Office hours (for later MPs) are a 3-4 hour wait and often the queue is just closed. Forum answers are helpful at times, but is a slow and clumsy way to communicate, like email. The professor, from my experience, is old fashioned in his teaching approach and not willing to change.

Heavy MPs, incompetent professor. He changed the deadline early 4 hours of "checkpoint" of MPs without any form of notification just because his student asked him why the deadline of the checkpoint is different from normal assignments. His lectures are also boring, feeling lucky that I know most of the course materials and not watching his lectures

Lectures are fine but all prerecorded, and honestly professor is not understanding at all of student responsibilities and life. As someone who has already taken 225, the material/mps are a breeze but it still irks me how poorly run this course is and the professor seems a bit narrowminded in his approach towards teaching and interacting w students

He's not the worst lecturer on the planet but he has no idea how to run a class. Office hours are constantly backed up and he provides almost no help to students on the forum, telling them to just re watch the lessons even though the solutions aren't there. He also scheduled the most difficult MP of the semester during exam week.

Genuinely one of the best teachers @ Gies. You'd be very fortunate to have him as a teacher. Very accessible through email and office hours. 312 is definitely a hard class but he's very good at teaching it and helping you understand. Just make sure to ask questions if you have any and not fall behind

Professor Osswald is a great professor because he cares about his students and his teaching material. Each assignment he gives has clear instructions and references to all the necessary notes. There are times when the topic of the class might be boring, but his attitude and high energy make it interesting. One of the best Accountancy Professors.

Very nice guy who cares about his students. Kind of goes through the lectures quickly, but he would post the recordings online. Would give a lot of help for the projects and taught the class well. Could be more clear on conveying the material, but he was a fair grader and was interesting in class. Liked class participation, but didn't require it.

First, I took this class in person in the spring, NOT ONLINE. Prof O makes all of his theories and concepts applicable to our everyday lives. He is so knowledgeable as well. I think the grading policy is quite fair. This is much more of a "politics" based class rather than communication.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I had Professor O'Gorman for CMN 310, CMN 450, & one independent study. I thought he was very educated on what he teaches & was easy to talk to when you need help. His classes are paper heavy, but this is to be expected in a communication class. As long as you show up to class, take notes over lecture, and complete assignments you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: O'Gorman's class covers some very dense material, and there is a LOT of reading that can't be skimmed if you really want to succeed. That being said, he really knows his stuff and his lectures focus on getting the absolute most out of the material. While the course is intense, you'll get a lot out of it if you put in the time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
DON'T TAKE! Writing assignments take hours, due for every class PRINTED. Expect a ton of big deadlines one after the other without any room to breathe. He grades harsh & unclear.

Attendance required. 3 min tardiness is 1/3 of an absence and over 20 minutes is a full absence. After 2-3 absences he docks -2% of total grade for any more absences.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Three hundred and fifty characters are not enough for me to articulate how infuriatingly annoying this class was. Every week multiple papers are due on extremely dense material that requires a considerable amount of prerequisite knowledge. The professor seems to think that his class is more important than all others and far too much tedious work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this course asynchronously over winter break, and though it was a lot of content crammed into a short amount of time, I felt that the pacing was good and the expectations were reasonable. He lectures a bit slow but I just watched everything at 1.5x. Always gave me clear feedback on assignments and encouraged me when I did well.

Professor clearly knew what he was talking about and enjoyed what he taught, which was nice. Lectures were sometimes dry, and received little to no feedback on any papers or assignments throughout the semester. Very few opportunities for points, so one or two bad grades can really mess you up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I looked forward to watching Professor O'Gorman's lecture videos every single week. The content of this class was so interesting, and the way that Professor O'Gorman presented the lectures made this class so notable. He is very passionate and seems like a great guy. Really will miss this class & his lectures.

Class is very dry. Lots of tedious homework assignments in the form of mini papers. A homework assignment that takes multiple hours is due every class. Flipped lecture takes an incredibly large amount of time. Attendance is mandatory. The only redeeming quality is that we didn't have to buy a textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: grading criteria is not clear. no specific and instructive feedbacks.

Clear enjoyable class. Lectures are dynamic enough. He does a good job of blending both the important thoughts and the background history of the time period. There is a lot of reading and writing. You will have to work. Attendance is important. Discussions are important. I would take the class again.

Teaches a tough course but he is engaging and funny. Professor is specific and clear. Going to class is a must for this professor. Notes are important. Classsmates that skipped often and didn't read or take notes didn't do well on tests. Go to lecture. He is engaging and funny. Freedom to express your opinion. Standard, do your work you'll do well.
Dense reading. Strong background in rhetoric/philosophy necessary.

One of the best professors across Grainger in terms of teaching, which is especially rare for someone at the sophomore/junior level in ECE. She makes a great effort to resolve student questions, even during lecture time. Any class with her will be an easier time than without.

By far the easiest ECE course I have taken, Prof Mironenko did an amazing job explaining the topics in a clear and understandable way. This course should be an easy A if you put in any amount of work. She is the best professor I have had; I 100% recommend taking any of her sections.

An absolutely amazing professor.  She really cares about her students and wants to make sure everyone understands what's going on in lecture and goes above and beyond to help.   She always came to lecture prepared and did a lot to make them engaging and interesting for the students.  I definitely recommend taking her section

Professor Mironenko is by far the best EE Professor for any class. If you have the chance to take her course, DO IT. She genuinely cares for her students. Ignore any posts made about her accent. While she has an accent, it is not something to complain about; you can clearly understand what she is explaining. Take her class, you won't regret it!

I cannot recommend taking her lectures enough (had her for 333 and 330). Very nice professor who always comes prepared and is willing to go beyond to help her students. Easy to understand and follow her lectures and she really tries to make sure everyone is following along and at the same point.
Professor's lecture are very clear, and makes sure that all students understood the materials for every single lecture.
Extraordinary instructor, explained concepts clearly, and inspired interest in the topics we were learning. I never wanted to miss a lecture because it was so well taught.

ECE 210 is a hard class no matter what, but it will make you a better engineer. Professor Mironenko is probably the only reason that I got such a good grade, she loves the subject material and loves teaching it to students who are willing to learn. My favorite teacher at UIUC. She puts smiley faces on your test questions when they are correct :)
Really good
Amazing professor, actually made zoom lectures enjoyable. Encourages participation and always makes sure students are not confused about the lecture content. 100% would take again.

ECE210 is a hard class regardless of professor you choose. Professor Mironenko does a good job explaining concepts and walking through problems. Make sure to keep up by going to all 4 lectures a week and/or diligently reading the textbook in addition to doing and fully understanding the HW to do well in this class.
Great lecturer! Always started and ended lecture with a recap and came very prepared. Always had good answers to questions

This course is impressively well organized. Lecture notes are very good, lectures are worth going to, and homework and exams while time-consuming are reasonable. Put in the time and you do well. 

She's also quite cute, which helps me pay attention during lecture haha

Fantastic professor! Extremely caring, and great at explaining concepts. Course is fairly easy, lectures are 80% examples. She can almost always sense when students are lost, and does a lot to encourage participation, which helps everyone learn more. Prof. Mironenko made this course a blast!

Professor Odom might be the goat. He takes great care to ensure everybody in the class feels included and is very respectful. He allows many extensions and is understanding when things come up and you turn in your assignments late. He grades very lightly and gives great feedback, but be prepared for lots of essays and stay on top of your work.

Had him Fall 2021. Probably one of the best professors I've had so far. Very understanding of the fact that we're all coming from different backgrounds and we all have different writing styles. I felt like I'd absolutely dread this class but it turns out it was one of the best I've had so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The classes seemed long for no reason. Most of the classes consisted of talking about essay strategies but they didnt need to be an hour and 15 minutes. Fair grader, you got a bad grade bcs your essay was bad and you got a good grade bcs your essay was good. Lenient on attendance and easy to talk to about an essay problem. I recommend
He's a really nice guy, too many printouts you have to bring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His class is a battery of complex writing exercises. The main focus is on examining tough issues like technology, economics, philosophy and the education system. The views presented in the reading assignments are diverse, and Instructor Odom makes every argument accessible. The end-game is being able to read and write ambivalently and with nuance.

Mr. Odom was a solid professor. He is enthusiastic about the material and is a grader that will help you grow in writing if you listen to his criticism. Some might say he's a tough grader but that's really if you're trying to get by doing the minimum. Great talking to one-on-one
Great teacher and loved the class, but he grades way too harshly. Made me decide not to major in English.

Mr. Odom's feedback is very reliable and you should always take it as constructive criticism. His class was not something I like at all, I hate english but I was always motivated to go. he has definitely helped my writing developed.

He's a very good teacher. He can be a bit tricky grader but you will learn a lot from his feedback. I would definitely recommend him as a teacher and make sure you are ready for 12 pages of research paper!

Mike is great if you're really into the subject. He brings great life into poems and story lines and is really good with clarifying. Exams were decently easy but you did have to know authors/titles/plot to pass. Discussion board was a pretty easy grade.

He's a nice professor but the class is a little hard because we have papers to write almost every week. His feedback are useful and go to his office hours if you want to get more help. We had 2 chances at the end of the semester to do paper revisions, definately take this chance it will boost your grade up at the last minute.

READ THE BOOK IS YOU WANT BROWNIE POINTS... OTHERWISE DONT BOTHER. DEFINITELY GET THE COURSE PACKET. THE ESSAYS IN THERE HELP WITH YOUR PAPERS. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. HE IS EXTREMELY HELPFUL IN TELLING YOU WHAT TO WRITE. PARTICIPATE, ITS IN YOUR GRADE. YOU CAN REVISE 2 PAPERS. VERY FAIR GRADER. 5 ABSENCES ALLOWED.

He gives the best feedback and you learn to be a better writer at the end of the semester. Don't be discouraged if you don't do as well as you like on your first real paper and keep in mind that you can revise 2 of them.

If you are gonna take this class, take the fewest credit hours possible, since you will have to take a paper almost every time you go for lecture. If you are an engineering I can assure you that you will get frustrated by the end of the semester. The papers are very long, especially the research paper and paper 3 and the grading is very hard.
Class was quite easy overall as long as you follow his guidelines and read the material.  He managed to interest me in literature which is hard to do.
Amazing teacher; great feedback; super easy; take his class for english 200!!!! =]

Class was boring most of the time but it was mandatory to go. You never knew how you were being graded, just how much it was worth for your overall grade. Recommend taking it, he's easy going and tries to be fair to everyone.
He's a great prof. Had some of the best discussion of any class in his.

sound guy. class easy but can get more out of it by looking past his simple class teachings. has to be easy as so many none eng mahor take it. ask him questions. see him after class then you get more out of it. top draw southern drawl.

Great class!  Interesting topics, helpful prof.  If you're extensive and go over the required page #s, he usually gives a better grade.  A lot of reading, though.  We get a writing assignment every week or every other week (easy).  2 papers.
Easy class, but half the time I felt like my peers and I knew more than he did. I guess that's why it was easy. Really boring, too. (ENGL 200 in 04/05 is now ENGL 201 fyi)

This class was kinda boring just because it was too long. He lets everyone participate which makes it a little easier to understand. He will help you with any trouble you have with your papers. The paper topics were a little difficult but he grades relatively easy. Overall: good.

Mike was extremely helpful and always available for an appointment. However, his grading takes years to get back and seems to be slightly lower than what you predict. But aside from that he's a nice man.
great guy, totally southern
No Comments

This class sucks.  Mike grades really hard, much harder than the other rhet 105 teachers.  He gives way more written assignments than the other rhet 105 teachers.  Class is extremely boring and you don't really learn too much, but you have to take it to graduate so...
No Comments
She fight of students' rights when we encountered a CANVAS attack and couldn't take the final as we originally planned.
best professor ever

Prof. Clifton is very kind but not a good lecturer. Unless you sit front and center it's hard to read the chalkboard at the edges. Her examples in lecture are far more complicated that what you need to know for homework and exams. There are no discussions so the only grade padding is the quizzes. Just read the textbook and do all of its exercises.

I did not have Prof. Clifton officially, but she was super accommodating. I got sick and she allowed me to take the test a week later. Very understanding and kind professor. Lectures didn't make a whole lot of sense to me, but handwriting was better than most of the other DiffEQ Profs. Highly respect and recommend
Very nice professor, but poor lecture style. Lacks authority often making lectures mundane and boring to attend.

Prof. Clifton is a very kind person but a confusing lecturer. She loves the chalkboard and it's often hard to see what she is writing. Her explanations of simple topics overcomplicate them so much that it leaves many students confused. Many students didn't attend lectures or attended other professors to better understand topics.

Professor Clifton is really really a kind person, and she helps us a lot for this proof class during the OH! i couldn't pass the class without going to her office hour.....highly recommend to take her class!

Brilliant professor. Tips: 1 During class, he skips most of the steps in formulation derivation to cover all the material -IT'S A LOT-, if you do it by yourself, you'll likely get an A, as formula sheets aren't allowed. 2 Challenging homework, so attend the TA's office hours in person. 3 Don't skip his lectures: every topic is connected.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overwhelmingly Positive again
Overwhelmingly Positive

Oscar is a great guy and very funny. Very difficult class. Exams are impossible but partial credit is given so it's not bad if you know what you're supposed to be doing. Homework is only doable with the help of the TA. Unfortunately, the class is not applicable at all to real-world engineering, other than some research.

He teaches the conceptually tough classes with patience and passion. I think he can be a part-time comedian with how many jokes he drops, making the content bearable. He's easy to talk to and can relate to students. He makes the work tough but grades with grace. And he is very intelligent. One of my favorites for sure.

Professor Lopez-Pamies was one of the most arrogant professors I've ever met. He uses a textbook that is just a pdf of his lecture notes, with no clear explanation of concepts. The homework does not reflect the content taught in class and without attending office hours there is no chance of following along. The exams are impossible as well.

I took CEE 598: Computational Fracture Mech with Prof. Lopez in Spring 2025. It was an amazing experience; his lectures were perfectly structured and crystal clear, with every topic presented precisely and in depth. His passion for the subject was obvious, and while the course is not easy, you'll truly enjoy it if you're curious about the topic.

Professor Oscar is a brilliant man. If you're sincere in class and study every day and actively ask questions, you will get good grades. He has a very friendly aura about him and genuinely cares about his students academics. And very knowledgeable. Makes class interesting and very interactive.
He is one of the best teachers I have ever had. Explains things very well.
Toughest course ever.

Yes, the course is tough but if you put in the work you can really understand it. The math required is higher than what is usually expected for engineers, so if you are taking the course to directly apply mechanics, this might not be the right class. I enjoyed the course because it teaches us the basics of the of structural mechanics very well.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Horrible professor, do not take his class if you don't have to. Mechanics and FEM are taught in different departments as well, take those instead of this professor.

Prof. L. is unable to emphasize key points, explain problems from A to Z, and most importantly, re-iterate key concepts. He lectures far too fast and his writing is sloppy and hard to differentiate between variables. He curves heavily, but I wish he taught better so there would not be a need. Brilliant man, strange class, poor pedagogue.

He presents material in such a way that he expects the class to all be geniuses. The homework problems expect you to already be experts in the material, rather than building on concepts to ensure understanding. The exams are nearly impossible. If there was ever a "weed-out" class, this is it. I feel I learned nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS
