reviews.comment: A very clear professor, a very though course, expect really difficult homeworks and exams. In the end you understand mechanics. Not friendly at class.
Awesome prof. Comes very well prepared. Strongly recommend taking AE 353 with Prof. Ornik

Awesome professor. Awesome TA. Awesome projects. Very practical and at the same time strikes a very good balance between theory and implementation. The favorite part about the course were the projects.

I took the course in FA23 and it has to be one of the best, most organized, well taught courses. Enjoyed every bit of it from the professor's teaching to TA's project explanations to professor's feedbacks. There was plenty of opportunities to learn and better ourselves.

Really great lectures, is well prepared and explains things clearly with the use of example problems. The projects in this class are very fun, and he gives plenty of opportunity to earn extra credit on both projects and tests.

Prof Ornik explains concepts well and if you are looking to learn about optimization, without lot of math rigor, I recommend taking AE504. He is pretty focused on whether students are learning the material & he makes lot of effort to ensure you are not wasting time by attending his lectures.
It's was alright
In all my years as an undergraduate, I never felt I understood concepts to such details! He's dope.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Man knows his stuff

Passionate and very knowledgable about Latin American art history to the point where I became more interested in the topic outside of class even. Very sweet and understanding, willing to provide extensions. The yellow outlines in the slideshows should be taken note of!!! Tests are writing based + little memorization. Pay attention to the class = A

This professor doesn't grade anything until like after the finals which is very dumb since you dont know what grade you are aiming for to get the grade you want. Participation is 5% of your grade and it is very hard to get the points. Lectures are extremely boring and papers/exams are dependent on if your TA is in a good mood...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Vazquez was really great. For ARTH 260 he provided TONS of online notes that made it easy to study for exams and writing assignments, would recommend that class BTW. He explains things well and has a passion for his work. He sometimes goes a little fast on the lecture slides BUT they are posted afterwards. Don't believe the low rating!!!

Professor is a really kind person. Though he grades harshly, you learn a great deal in this class. Tests are hard and have essay questions, you have papers too but they are fun to write. I think he cares about his students.

Lectures are packed with information and Professor Vazquez doesn't leave enough time to write down important information on slides, but slides are posted to canvas later on. Discussion class was boring, but if you have a good TA, you should overall be fine. Essays and exams are not that bad, the instructions and grading criteria are clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Long readings, you can't get a good sense of what's going on throughout the class. 10 weeks into the semester and hasn't graded a single assignment so far. Readings and lectures are disengaging with his monotone voice. He seems lost and tries to make everything sophisticated more than it actually is.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring and dreadful. He still uses iclickers so you have to pay for a subscription. There is a lot of reading that gets talked over during section. There are a few lectures that are interesting but most are boring and also confusing what he even is talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very nice guy but terribly disorganized. Without good TAs the class would be difficult. He lectures like he is speaking from a textbook but that is just his vibe. He gets a bad rep but he is very passionate and nice but boring!! He is overall not a bad teacher.

Very boring in lecture, it was hard to stay awake. He rarely responded to my emails, and grades were never posted in a timely manner. It's the end of the semester and my first assignment still isn't graded. Also didn't post the grades for the first exam before the second exam opened.

Lectures were dry and as others have mentioned, he tried to use iClickers, but could never figure out how to make them work. Exams use material taken directly from powerpoint slides, but graded really nit-picky. Same with essays: no rubric/vague rubric given and takes points off just because he can. This class was a huge waste of time.

I'm an art major so I like him he is a woke king but he is also a boring king if you don't like art. Honestly, you can skip class because he doesn't know how to use the iclickers. Just be super chill with the TAs and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: doesnt know how to get iclickers to work half the time, lectures drag on from the slides themselves, hard to pay attention to monotone voice. nice professor though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Reads directly from his slides in a slow rambling voice. Graffiti and Murals was way more Murals than graffiti, and many of his slides repeated information. He wanted iclickers but they never worked and we eventually stopped having physical classes, and he was already uploading his PowerPoints. Tests are almost word for word from his slides.

Don't take a class with him if you want to have a clue about the subject. He's long winded and rambling, and in the class I was in we never got our papers back promptly (a class of 5 had over a month with no papers back despite continually asking) and never received any sort of prompts. It was impossible to tell how to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I've taken a few classes with Dr. Vasquez.  He has always been helpful and funny.  I would highly recommend his collection class or his public art class. He's a sweetie and a cutie.

He speaks soooo slowly, drags out and complicates his sentences, which causes a lot of confusion. Other than that he's actually a really nice guy, very willing to help students. You will never pronounce "origin" the same after this class ("or-IDGE-in"). His assignments are useful and we learn a lot with them.
Lots of information on his slides so it's hard to write everything down but he posted all the powerpoints online. A lot of memorization, but a fun art history class.

Vazquez really isn't too bad. The class certainly isn't a blow off, it requires a lot of studying and memorization, and essay portions of exams are difficult to score well on.  Lectures can get boring and vazquez seems kinda out there. But super nice guy and def knows his stuff!! Great class to take all things aside
Has a needlessly bad rap. Very nice guy and very intelligent. Has his own style of lecturing, but interesting once you've gotten used to it. Tests come largely from study guides.

This class is useless. You get graded on attendance, tests, and papers. I have watched The Office on my laptop through every class, and I still have enough knowledge to get myself through the class on my own. It's not easy, but if you study hard for the exams, you never need to step foot in the classroom. Oscar is useless, dry, and boring.
Unless you're extremely interested in the material already, this professor won't do it for you. You have to really focus in on what he's saying to get anything out of class. =(

Agree completely with the other 2 '06 comments: very disorganized, lacked coherence in most lectures because of his tangents, did not go chronological which throws most of the course off, and made a pleasant topic monotonous and extremely cumbersome. Very frustrating!

Smart guy but loses his 112 class when he goes off on wacko tangets. Super-disorganized, had to leave class to go get a presentation on CD that he left at home. Often late, hates the concept of "chronological order". Material is interesting enough to save your grade. TAs are a godsend in deciphering his antics.
can not operate powepoint

I took more than one class with this professor. He was extremely helpful. He asked us to write thesis proposals for research projects of our choice, something that is actually practical.  The other ratings are written by fine art majors who think school is hard.
No Comments

this is worst class ever. who the hell can follow what the professor is saying? He is impossible to understand in terms of his word choice. This course could be interesting, but the profesor makes it BORING

I thought I would give my realest perspective with no prior knowledge of finance. Do the work, it's actually quite easy. I don't see why other reviews don't mention that every exam/quiz is just problem set questions. Try your hardest to understand lectures, and grind each problem set, and congrats you got an A.

This is the hardest class I have ever taken. His slides offer little guidance and are very confusing. Lectures are difficult to follow and engage with. The average GPA in his FIN 300 class is a 2.77 (really low for any class). If you can, avoid taking. The tests are extremely difficult as well (averages below 70% with no curve offered).

Never wrote an rmp for anyone but he is my exception. The class as is, is difficult. But relies on weekly quiz for 15% of your grade (retakes not allowed, 4 drops) and large portion of total is very difficult exams with impossible to read markings. Very boring lecturer/difficult class. DO NOT TAKE HIM. Need 111% on final for an A- at 82%!
Test heavy + boring lecturer. Take any other teacher if you can but stay away. Even if it delays your graduation to not take
would not rec
His class was hard, but I think I'm better for it. Really made students learn the material.
He gives you more than enough materials to prepare for exams and quizzes. He explained concepts very well and set clear expectations. I learned a lot from him and am glad I took him for FIN 300.

Communication was a major issue, despite multiple attempts to ask questions, responses were either delayed or unhelpful. The most frustrating part was the sudden grade change at the last minute without any explanation or opportunity for discussion. It's better to take other professor's class.

Super smart man.  As long as you read the book, pay attention in lecture, and practice what you learn-  you will succeed.  He gives you all the resources you need.  Before each quiz and test he gives you practice problems that will help you so much, you just have to practice.  Take good notes from his examples in lectures- I wouldn't skip class.

I absolutely loved both classes I took with Dr. Peters. He gives students all the resources to succeed but has high expectations for students with difficult but reasonable exams and quizzes. I learned way more from his classes than other finance classes I took due to his standards and lecture ability.

I took FIN 300 over summer online, I found the class to be a bit rushed for weekly material but thats my fault for taking an 8 week class. Other than that the professor provided all relevant formulas in his notes and his problem sets were great as they would be the same on projects and exams. Class is hard, overall great curve to make up for it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is very smart and always willing to help the students, he gives a very clear rules of the course and gives us specific guidelines. There are a lot of homework but if you take it seriously, it will really helps you to understand the materials well and it is a good preparation for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Some many homework! Even though this is summer session, there is 8 assignments in the first 2 weeks, each takes 30 minutes to over 2 hrs!
Lecturer only read PPT, calculate the numbers by himself; No elaborations on concepts or tricky questions, boring class
Makes no attempt to teach but presents material as if students have a phd in finance. Unrealistic expectations for online modules, generally abrasive and difficult to talk to.

I really enjoyed Peter's teaching style. He gave us many resources to help us do well on quizzes and exams and made guided notes and problem sets for each section. This is a class where you need to show up, pay attention, take notes, and practice the questions outside of class for at least a couple of hours each week to do well on quizzes.

I did not like his teaching style. There are no PowerPoints, no slide decks, no online presence so if you suck at taking notes good luck. there was way to much group work and overall I was unclear what was asked in the class. It often felt disorganized. He is a really interesting and nice guy but I hated his teaching style.

I've taken this professor twice now and would take another class with him if given the chance. The other poor ratings seem to be coming from students who have a difficult time taking notes and going to class. No online material so notes are essential. You could get an A without opening the book. Overall: relevant, knowledgable, and applicable.

Funky grading method and curve, but go to class and study a reasonable amount and you'll do fine. He takes a bit of warming up to, but in the end Professor Peters provided really useful & practical knowledge about business and Finance. His class is simple (but not easy) and straightforward. Class discussions were enjoyable. Overall good professor!

As I look back on college, Peters was definitely one of my favorite instructors. If you participate in class and study the material you'll be fine with the curve. Think a little outside of the box. The material is super interesting and pretty useful in the financial world. Don't take him if you want to sit in the corner and avoid learning.
Easy grading scale, Cool guy. Interesting in class. Not sure what these other kids are talking about. Probably not business majors and don't know basics.

Of the handful of Finance classes I've had to take towards my Actuarial Science major, this one is by far my favorite because of Professor Peters.  He is a fantastic professor who pushes his students towards critical thinking beyond the textbook.  The class wasn't "easy", but the knowledge I'll for sure use later on is well worth a B in the class.
Avoid him if you can.

Do not be deceived...this man is not a good teacher..he tries to act like he knows what he is talking about and is above everything but really is just rambling a bunch of nonsense about banks. I don't even bother with class anymore b/c full-credit is impossible to obtain with his exams and the grading approach he uses or however the hell he grades.
Seriously? He seems to think that he is extraordinarily smart, and you should easily know what he is talking about. My recommendation: don't take him.
No Comments

Considers himself smarter than the textbook, tests are essay/short answer(with partial credit- arguing for more points will do you NO good).  Finance majors might do alright in his classes, but everyone else should steer clear.

Super enthusiastic and interesting lecturer. Lectures were helpful and interactive. he frequently had worksheets for people to practice concepts printed out in lecture. Get a good team and keep on top of it and youll be fine

He's very scatterbrained in this course and it was not run very well at all. He clearly knows what he is talking about but does not get it across well. Bad handwriting makes notes impossible to follow. He is accessible in office hours, which was the only thing that helped. Grading was not clear at all, but at least a huge curve helped us all out.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his class when we did the fruit slicer project. It was good, but sometimes the labs were not run well. He was very passionate about the lecture content and delivered it very well. Sometimes the quizzes were not supported by lecture content well, but the class is overall very doable. Just make sure you stay on top of the project.

Pablo is intimidating but he is a good and funny guy at heart (pinky promise you this, my lab partner and I cracked jokes with him during every lab). BUT THE GRADING IS JUST THE WORST THING IN THE WORLD. You will come out grateful for learning a lot, but getting a good grade is just extremely difficult.
Can seem harsh but is fair. Pay attention in the lecture, take advantage of office hours for feedback on lab reports/deliverables, and study the lecture slides. You will get out what you put in.

65% of your grade is determined in the last 2 weeks and he does not give partial credit for most assignments. extremely harsh grading, makes fun of students in private and is generally unpleasant. very little availability outside of class. mumbles/speaks quietly when he talks so you can't hear him when lecturing. would never take this guy again
The class is not as hard as others say. You need to refresh basic biology concepts and follow the guidelines posted on the website.

Make sure you understand the syllabus, work hard and you will be fine. Getting a B is easy, getting an A is difficult because you will be tested in different ways and you will have to do well in every assignment. It is a good course and a good teacher but don't expect an easy A like in pretty much every other course in bioengineering.

He is a tough grader but fair. You will get the grade that you deserve and useful feedback. Attendance is mandatory and he is very strict. If you have questions he will reply to emails instantly. I learned a lot in this class but I had to work much harder than any others.
Guidelines are vague for lab reports, averages incredibly low. 65% of your grade is the last two weeks of class, extremely stressful.
Not sure how I went from getting 130% A+ grade in 205 to a D+ in 202. I enjoyed the course but it is a lot of work and grading is inconsistent with other courses.

Very harsh grader and generally just very unsupportive of his students. Most of your grade is determined by last week of assignments. Expectations are very unclear with really any of the assignments (good luck finding a rubric or instructions).

Instructions for big projects(each are worth about 20% of your grade) are incredibly vague, yet his grading is incredibly harsh. Stressful experience during final weeks of course as grades were completely up in the air. He did not create a friendly environment for learning.

Sometimes difficult to understand during lectures/lab. 60% of class grades are earned in the last two weeks of school, and that format is not likely to change in the future. Rubrics for bigger projects are vague and grading is strict. The material is useful, but the harsh grading will probably sour your experience of the class as a whole.

This class is difficult but rewarding and requires a some knowledge of thermodynamics. The professor was very accessible outside of class and was more than willing to help with any questions or concerns. He seemed to want the students to truly understand the topics as much as he does. The grading was more than fair and reflected the amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Exam 1/2/3: 30/30/40%. No mandatory HW or attendance. 
His class is very challenging and goes very deep - not recommended if you want an easy A without heavy work. But his lectures are excellent, clear, and he's always open to questions. Highly recommended for motivated grad students. I learned a lot that directly supports my research.

The student professor is very conscientious and responsible and tries to teach a lot of things. The professor is very responsible and is always willing to answer questions. After each exam, he/she will send emails to provide personalized feedback to each student. Students need to study it hardly and not try to get a grade without putting effort.

Professor Brewster is one of the best professors I've had at UIUC. ME 404 is tough but deeply rewarding. He explains complex ideas step by step, answers questions with patience, and truly wants students to learn. I gained a real understanding of thermodynamics that still helps me in grad school today. I truly respect him.
Avoid this professor. He is incredibly difficult to get a hold of outside of class, and provides little useful feedback on exams/projects. Lectures are very difficult to follow.

The worst professor in the mechanical engineering department without a doubt. 

We had an A before the *completely discretionary* faculty advisor adjustment grade, where he subtracted 15% off of our grades one day before grades were released. 

Do not take a project with him!!!

The worst professor in the mechanical engineering department. If you take senior design with him, get ready for unreasonable expectations (such as a full design/prototype on 48-hour notice) as well as a hugely negative grade adjustment at the end of the semester. 

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!

If you have the option to take his class, don't. He makes you feel stupid for not understanding and expects everyone to understand things immediately. This class covers 1.5 textbooks and you need intensive knowledge from chemistry and quantum mechanics to understand it. The worst professor I've had on this campus.

The class is interesting, especially if you already are intrigued by the topic. Brewster is very smart, and I think he thinks his students to be just as smart, so his tests were very difficult and very unlike the homeworks, which were very straightforward. Overall, I did well in the class, but probably because everyone else did so poorly.
Great professor, homework is reasonably straight forward but an assignment is due every single class. Tests are very focused on derivations and can be brutal. Overall would recommend.

The course lectures were not very helpful in understanding the material, and the slides often felt disconnected from assignments. The instructor was difficult to reach outside of class, and feedback on assignments was limited. In some cases, guest speakers led class sessions instead of the instructor.
Uses AI and communication is difficult between students and them
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is a waste of your time. The professor doesn't read her own readings, ChatGPT's every slide, and cannot seem to send a competent e-mail with less than 90% AI on GPTZero. I've had to contact my advisor to mess up my four year plan to drop this course and I've never been happier. I do hope the professor changes and becomes a better person.

DO NOT take this class. Everything in this class is AI-generated, and what little isn't is written with the intelligence and skill of a middleschooler. There is nothing of substance that I have learned from this class, and it physically pains me to copy down the AI slop slides that she reads from verbatim. Easiest A of my life, do not take.

No lecture material is provided, expect to be attending every single lecture. Midterms typically averaged in the 40s. He does not give out easy A's and demands a lot, but his lectures are very educational. The only way you can fail his class is if you put in absolutely 0 effort, but if you care about your GPA you should find another section.
He is a fantastic teacher and gives awe-inspiring lectures. He only gives the notes if you ask for them in class. He loves questions and is an incredible mentor.

Don't ask any questions regarding math concepts you would've learned in calc 2/3 or diff eq, otherwise you will be yelled at. Questions about concepts or anything else related to the class have to be as specific as you can make it. He doesn't decide what % corresponds with what letter grade, so the midterm averages were mid 40s. Have fun...

Avoid taking any important classes with this guy. He is unreasonably mean and irritable, and will personally memorize and form an opinion about every student in the class. Exam distributions range from 0-100 and are awfully skewed. Even with perfect lecture attendance, good luck scoring above a 60. There is no clear cutoffs either, he just picks.

No lecture notes u gotta take you're notes
Exams are extremely and unreasonably difficult
The guy is unreasonable, if u try and ask a question get ready for a grilling session
No notes sheet allowed for tests which is crazy for fluid mechanics
If the class average is a 40, somethings gotta be wrong with this style of teaching

He's a genius but not a nice guy. Gets to know everyone who regularly attends lecture by name, so make sure you show up. At the end of the class he ranks everyone by of total points in the class, and then he draws the line arbitrarily between who gets what letter grade based on if he thinks you deserve it. Don't take this class if you don't have to

This guy has no joy in his life. Lectures are terrible and boring, he's mean and arrogant, and expects you to know as much as he does. Old school lectures (chalk and blackboard) probably because he has no idea how to use a computer. This guy is not with the times at all. Grading is insanely hard but luckily there is a curve. Stay away

Pearlstein is not your typical professor at UIUC. But that's for the best, as he demands understanding of the material while also supplying thorough lectures. Homeworks are tough and that was the biggest annoyance of the class, but they aren't weighted for much and office hours are helpful. Take him if you really want to learn the material
Amazing Professor
I hate this dude. Heard a lot of strange allegations about him too. School should look into it more. Arne is not a saint

Does not use or post lecture notes and regularly makes fun of students who ask questions in class. Never makes it clear what content will be on exams and does not elaborate on grading. Does not care if his students learn the material, as his goal for exam scores is a normal distribution around 50%. I would not wish his class on my worst enemies.

Obviously very smart, but is an extremely intimidating person. Yells at students for asking pretty valid questions. Lectures are just derivations of equations that have very little practical use and homework is very different to lectures.

This man is literally the bane of my existence. It's like the anti-Christ has descended unto humanity and his name was Arne Pearlstein. He's very knowledgeable in his field, and does a lot of his lecture form memory. Conversely, he does not upload any lecture notes, nor does he work from a note sheet that people can follow.

High expectations from students. Killer exams, but his lectures are original and unique. He knows the material and can talk at length and in detail without great preparation. Lectures supplement reading rather than repeat it. Strict, somewhat intimidating, and does not take BS. Demanding professor, but best classes I've taken have been with him.

Great teacher and knows his subject(s). Committed to helping students understand the material. For ex., he created homework questions (pretty difficult) and the exams were a direct reflection of the homework. Also organized help sections for the homeworks.. But, yeah, he can be intimidating. And he expects you to know what was taught in the lecture
Notorious for being the toughest professor in the university. Talk in his class and get kicked out regardless of whether it deals with the class.
Writes an essay on the board during each lecture. NO correlation to the book material. Expects a class full of students such as Mr. Meyers. Test bends you over. Class is Class Impossible.

Different than most professors. Makes the course more about understand why things are the way they are, rather than just having you learn it to test it. Learned more in his class than any other. Go to office hours, if he sees you've made an honest effort on the hw and you ask intelligent questions, he will walk you through them.
Don't miss class and ask plenty of questions. Office hours are a must, extremely helpful if he believes you are trying. Very tough but certainly doable.

He makes exams very difficult, but definitely do-able. Be a good student, go to class, and most importantly, show him you care about the material and he is a very helpful. People say avoid him, but I learned more about problem solving and engineering than I would in any other class. He only expects out of you what you can accomplish. Don't be lazy

This professor is infamous among ME majors at UIUC for being the worst professor you'll ever take.  Bad at teaching (spent 2 lectures canceling units on one problem), bad at helping (yells at students and even other professors), bad at writing exams(average on the first exam was 28%).  Avoid at all cost!

Comments said he is too harsh while I should say the comments are way too harsh. Pearlstein is a very patient guy who would explain something you don't understand many times. Exams are hard but not impossible. I was worried when I saw the comments before taking this class but it turned out that the class is the best one I've taken so far.

Great professor, lectures are clear, homework questions are useful and helpful for exams. Exams are not that hard as long as you go to the lectures and do the homework. He also held question sessions weekly which are really helpful. He welcomes questions through email and answers them quite decently. Uses blackboard a lot. Like his way of teaching.

Everyone will tell you to not take a class with this professor, however he ties everything he teaches into the real world industry. He has more office hours per week than all my professors combined and yes, he WILL make fun of you for mistakes, but suck it up, you are there to ask questions. Exams are difficult, but definitely possible.

He's a grumpy old man that clearly does not know how to teach. The lectures are extremely boring. He wastes tons of time doing arithmetic rather than helping people understand the big picture. Frankly, he is quite an unpleasant person. Make a point to not take this class with him, as he turns it into a much bigger ordeal than it should be.

He prepares for this class the least of any professor I have ever had. He wastes so much time in class going over extended examples (which he does on the fly) that are not relevant at all to the material. He also gets angry very easily and is an overall unpleasant individual. NO PEOPLE SKILLS.

Class is extremely difficult and professor is definitely that stereotypical genius professor.  That being said office hours can be very helpful and he does offer lots of office hours/question sessions.  Definitely expect to work very hard in this class.

Where do I start? Worst class I have ever taken.  Going to class does not help, doing the homework does not help, going to office hours does not help... nothing helps. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM. He gave 4 people a 2 out of 100 on a midterm and said there wasn't going to be a curve because someone got 100.
DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!

If you like to learn by having someone talk in front of you for 50 mins and write down every single word that comes out of his mouth then this may be the professor for you. We rarely did example problems. Exam are hard but he says there is a huge curve. He really makes the test so someone as smart as him will ace it
He talks straight into the board and the tests are extremely difficult.  As he puts it if you know the information (and by that he means to his level of knowledge) then you will pass.

Avoid taking any class taught by this man. He's your typical genius, arrogant professor that expects everyone else to be inherently brilliant. He seriously talks straight into the chalkboard for 50 minutes, and writes down every single word he says. Honestly, he is my worst professor throughout college thus far.
I was getting a B+ until he gave me a 0 on the third test because I was in the hospital with a 105 degree temperature!  He did not let me make it up and he gave me an F in the class.  He is a POS.

People would tell you to avoid taking him, but I think he was a good teacher. The avg on the tests are very low, but if you at least work through most of the problem, you'd curve pretty high. Though he'd take 3 weeks to  grade your exam, his trying to make sure he's fair in grading. His notes are good, help very much for exams. Gives extra off.hrs.
Grades harshly, does not help, going to class is worthless

The average on our two exams that he graded were 37 and 58. did not explain how his weighting system works. Funny at times, but sometimes unbelievably harsh. Laughs at some questions (mockingly which does not give a vote of confidence). At one office hour, went on tangent about units.Grading on homework is sick: +1 if it's correct -5 if incorrect.
dont expect to go to office hours for help, unless you want to be yelled at and called stupid!  this guy is a freak!
comes off as a hardass but in the end is a good guy.  its funny when he laughs at stupid questions too
No Comments
Brilliant professor and expects a lot from his students.
he once yelled at this kid for coughing too much.
No Comments

Worst professor. Absent for 1/4 of the term with only 2 HWs total. For 3-credit students, the final is a massive 45%, yet grades were never shown and no curve was applied. Extremely disorganized; you have no idea where you stand before the end.
Worst Professor, worst grader. no exact rubrics. doesn't curve at all.

does not have a clear grading rubric, not good lecture notes clarity, TA's are very bad graders, homework is easy but does not help for exam. Professor does not have a clear grading rubric either. Three exams 30% each, homework 10%. TA's are not helpful at all.
I learn a lot, for sure, and I never regret.
I would say he is extremely friendly, and you better pray that he is your professor in this department.

Most useless class I have ever taken. 20 minutes of class dedicated to nothing that we should be learning in class. The curriculum was based on no actually important skills or knowledge for planning. Biggest waste of time being taught by a man who likes to hear himself talk.
One of the best professors I've ever had
Makes class enjoyable, enthusiastic, and funny, but delivers a good lecture.
He is an awesome teacher and a very engaging speaker! Long lectures though so drink coffee I sometimes get drowsy

Professor Qiu's lecture is very thorough and detail oriented, always followed by concrete examples. The homework and exams are in consistent format, with sufficient guidance provided for studying. Overall, very nice professor.
Amazing and very organized lectures if you come to every class and do your work. If you don't do your part of the job, you may find the classes difficult to follow and the exams very hard.
probably the worst professor ever.

You will not pass this course if you don't attend lectures. She won't post any notes to compass. This is the most stupid course that I have EVER attended in U of I. You just need to memorize everything. You won't use what you learned from this course in real life. Basically, this course sucks. The grader is the toughest grader I have EVER seen.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The worst professor in ECON major, I would rather choose Petry than her even Petry is in prison RN. Required 3 hr final exam and she only gives two hrs and saying "another one hour is for TA collect exam papers" too many calculations needed in an 80 min midterms.
She gives amazing lectures, very organized and crystal clear. Her teaching is very thorough. Probably the best econ class you can get in UIUC.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: best prof and best class ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendence is important. Extremely easy class if you take notes. The exams and homework are the same as exercises in class.
Great professor and great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Only 4 Homework assignments that count basically as quizzes. 3 Midterms and Cumulative final. Alot of formulas to memorize and little room for error since one mistake can determine a whole letter grade. Attending class is more vital than the slides since she only gives and solves practice problems in class.
5 homeworks and 3 exams for the whole sememster, you will find them pretty easy as long as you go to every class
Best of them all
Obviously just another crummy grad TA working on an English degree at UIUC. He's very into himself (figures for someone in fine arts), and the class was nothing more than boring/typical.

Quentin was so intelligent, kind and helpful! The work was pretty hard but I went to class and did well. I think the other student just got a bad grade, probably because s/he never went to class and never did any work.
poor class, learn nothing from class. the grading is not clear, i dont even no my final score

Great course if you want to build a stronger conceptual and practical understanding of statistical modeling. The material can be challenging because you need to apply ideas rather than memorize procedures, but it is rewarding if you stay engaged.
Very hard grader, lecture notes are very confusing and hard to understand, exams are overly complicated, she doesn't even release final grades, would not recommend

This class is unnecessarily hard, lecture slides are confusing and not helpful at all, exams and HWs are hard to complete since they don't line up well with the slides. Very harsh grader as well, would not recommend
Notes and lectures are extremely insufficient, little to no practice problems, exam problems are much more difficult then HW and in-class examples, brutal
Dr. Yu is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students. Her lectures are clear, engaging, and easy to follow. I learned a lot in Stat 426 and really appreciated her dedication!

Dr. Yu is the best professor I've had at UIUC. Her teaching style is clear and incredibly effective. I learned so much from her—not just about statistics, but also how to think critically and apply concepts meaningfully. She truly cares about her students' success, and it shows in everything she does. I'm grateful to have taken Stat 426 with her!
Worst stats class I have ever taken.

The worst course i've taken in the stat core sequence. Most of it is due to the prof. My biggest issue was trying to work with her with disability accommodations as she would constantly make it difficult to have my needs met. Otherwise I thought the content was okay, pretty typical stat modeling stuff.

One of the worst professors I've ever come across. She cares more about failing her students and giving out penalties than actually evaluating students based on their understanding of her material. I submitted an assignment five minutes late and she tried taking off 10% of my overall grade and retroactively failing my old homework assignments.

The lecture is way longer than it should be because he takes up most of class talking about himself and telling stories to make himself look smart. I wish we couldve just gotten through the notes without random side tracks and preaching about how fufilling it is to adhear to traditional & steryrotypical gender roles. I never wanted to come to class
Prof. Quick was an excellent professor. Very understanding of any outside of class situations.

Professor Quick has been my favorite professor in my 3 years here on campus. He always brings the energy to lectures, always has a fun or interesting story to tell, and actually cares about your success and interests.

Prof. Quick is amazing, and his lectures are very high quality. There's a lot of information, but he breaks it down into very understandable chunks. TA's are also amazing. His lectures are very engaging, and he's very funny. As long as you show up and complete the course packet (notes) and study, you'll do great! There's also extra credit!
I am more used to stern and serious profs but I can see why people like him. I personally don't because I like someone who is more information dense. He is very enthusiastic.
All I can say is that Prof. Quick made this class absolutely fascinating. I took this class last semester and I still think about many things quick taught all the time.

Loved his class, reason I decided to take a minor in CMN. Honestly, I just learned sm from his lectures and enjoyed going. Super engaging and always has a fun story or experience to share. fav thing about this class is just how welcoming it always felt. the class itself is pretty easy, youll ace the exams as long as your taking notes and review!
he makes the course interesting and knows how to make students pay attention. he is hard to reach via email but overall super easy and informative course.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For 465, this class was like 102 with the notes fill in book and test structure. There is a major group project that is research based but is not very difficult! The grading rubric is a little vague for some of the project parts but you can always ask. He has a lot of energy and is always passionate about the material he teaches. Def recommend!

He is a good and positive teacher for sure. I enjoyed his stories. Class is pretty much mandatory because you do the notes inside the book packet, but I like it that way. Overall, I liked his style and the tests were not bad.

He really brought the energy and passion for the subject, which I appreciated. For my class, we were discouraged from tech usage + all used paper notes which actually helped me focus a ton. The expectations for the class were clear from the start. It was very attendance focused though, and if you missed lecture/discussion, you would lose points.

Professor Quick is such a great lecturer! The only thing is that you can't really miss lecture or you'll lose points in the class. The grade isn't based on many projects- in class assignments and exams. I really recommend this class, Quick seems like he's really interested in what he is teaching.

This was such a fun class to take and Quick made it such an engaging and easy class. The lectures were very note-heavy but they were easy to follow as note packets were provided. There are only three exams throughout the semester and you don't have to take the final if you are satisfied with your grade. Overall Quick is such a fun and easy teacher!

Prof.Quick was an excellent professor. His lectures were super engaging, even when discussing already well-known topics. Additionally, there was a workbook that included pictures of all the slides with space next to each for notes. This made lectures extremely easy to follow along and to study for exams.

Professor Quick is a great lecturer! Although the class can be very lecture-heavy, professor Quick makes the lectures very interesting and engaging. The midterms are fairly easy if you look over your notes. The TAs in the class are also amazing in preparing you for the midterms, so attending the discussion sessions will be extremely useful.

Prof Quick is amazing! His lectures are interesting and engaging. There is however a LOT of material that he covers which may be a little difficult when studying for his exams, but the material itself isn't necessarily difficult. So as long as you study and pay attention in the discussion section you should be good!

Professor Quick teaches excellently, but it seems there are too many things to learn for such a basic class. Maybe he should decrease the quantity. The overall classes are not difficult, but it's just too many.
He is a great guy

Prof Quick was an outstanding teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about each and every topic. So much energy. His lectures kept me awake and looking forward to the next class. Buy the course packet, study the notes, show up for class, and you will be fine. I recommend this class. Prof Quick is amazing!

The class is not too bad, if you study and pay attention you will be fine. Professor Quick tells too many stories that are too personal and it is a bit unprofessional at time. Plus, he teaches with his opinion too often.

Lectures aren't mandatory but you need the notes so I recommend going. Super fun class that covers a lot of interesting material you wouldn't normally see in other courses. It's 4 credit hours which is nice because it's definitely the work of only 3. Exams can be tough but pay attention in lecture/lightly study and you will be fine

Professor Quick is genuinely the best instructor that I have had in college. He is hilarious and his lectures are so engaging. He was also extremely fair with grading and always made sure that we knew he was available and willing to talk with us about anything. I would definitely recommend his class!

Prof Quick is an amazing professor. He is funny, knowledgeable, and I love how he ties social marketing principles to the real world. After this class, I learned a substantial amount about the field and I now know I want to apply more social marketing principles to my future research projects. Take this class! You won't be disappointed.
I took the online version one. Show up to discussion cause it is not recorded and some questions will come from discussion sessions. But Prof Quick is amazing and super easy to understand.
PROF QUICK IS AWESOME!! he brought his dog to class !!

Prof Quick does a great job of making communications interesting. I would love to take another class with him in the future and I would recommend CMN 102 to anyone who is trying to decide what to do or wants an easy gen-ed. I took it for my cmn minor and I was worried it would be boring, but it's a really useful class and Quick is a great teacher.

Professor Quick is a very kind, personable guy. He is lively and his lectures are engaging. In COMM102, you get course packets so it is very easy to take notes. If you miss class you may miss some important examples that he gives that aren't found in the course packet, and they may show up on the tests. So I suggest you don't skip.
Very passionate about his lectures and had more energy than most people could dream of. He clearly cared a lot about his lectures and research and seemed like a great professor.

Prof. Quick is such an inspiring professor and made me actually want to come to class. His lectures are fun and engaging and I learn so much in them. I really recommend trying to get him as a teacher for a CMN course cause he's the best. Sad to be done with his class.

Former grad student - B L QUICK world renowned... Look up psychological reactance.. organ donation campaigns. This persuasion seminar... 1. MA and PhD take together. If you're MA you will be overwhelmed, stressed, and feel dumb at times. But Brian is very nice. grading consists of a midterm paper, final paper, how well you lead discussion 1x etc

Prof Quick was my favorite teacher this semester! He's pretty laid back and there's literally only 1 homework assignment a week. He does a good job of making lecture's interesting. An overall awesome and genuine guy!

Prof Quick is awesome. He makes his classes easy- for sure an easy A. There's no textbook- just a workbook with all the notes that was $25. There are three exams and one final- lowest score is dropped. For most, people keep their first three scores and don't take the final. He's so passionate and easy to listen to- take his class!!

Brian is the most inspirational professor I have had while at Illinois. He is a masterful researcher and his lectures are fun and very engaging. He makes no qualms about meeting outside his classroom for help, career opportunities or even just to talk. Teaching the first class that CMN majors must take, he puts to rest any doubts that you may have.

Brian is very passionate about his research and is a very nice person. Great lecturer. Discussion sections are easy and almost always get out early. Exams are basically all of your grade and you only have to take 3 of the 4, or you can take all 4 and drop your lowest grade. A lot of theories and application to remember, but other than that decent.
Great class and awesome teacher. Everything you need is in one fill in workbook.

Prof Quick's lectures were fairly easy to be engaged in because he is funny and relates his personal life to what we're learning to make it easier to understand. I definitely had to study and attend lecture to do well but even studying minimally usually got me an A or B on the exams.
He's really funny, shows good examples in class, and makes class interesting. I wish I could take another class with him, but he only teaches one other one in Health Campaigns. Overall, fun class!

Prof Quick is great.  He makes his lectures pretty interesting, and he can be funny sometimes.  Barely any homework but you do have to take decent notes at lecture (its guided notes) then study for like 4 or 5 hours for each exam.  Four exams total (including the final) and you can drop the lowest one.  A few extra credit opportunities as well.
Really great professor. Loved his lectures!

Professor Quick is great. He knows what he's talking about and he's good at what he does. I feel bad for using my phone in class, but he's never called me out. He makes the learning environment in lecture like lecture/discussion because it's so interactive. I learned a lot.
Professor Quick is the best professor that I have ever had. His lectures were interesting and he always tries to make the class fun.

He is very passionate about his teaching and he is very good at it. Very interesting lectures. The information is not very difficult as long as you pay attention and take good notes. Definitely recommend this class!
Awesome
He's the best professor in this university!I promise you won't regret taking his class!Lectures are amazing and inspirational!I wish I can take it every semester!

Prof Quick is awesome! He's so enthusiastic and cares about the students. Great TAs as well. Discussions are mandatory to recieve participation. Only 4 exams and you get to drop 1. At least 5 opportunities for extra credit each semester.

Prof. Quick is a cool cat and a great teacher. He explains concepts well and is easy on the eyes. Most importantly, he is one of those teachers that CARE about their students. He isn't on a power trip. I HIGHLY recommend taking a course with him! Tip: You need to take notes in class though!
notes from lecture are necessary, but no participation grade. you can skip all sections and write a term paper, or go to all but one and complete an easy weekly worksheet. very easy class

Listen up: this is the best professor in the CMN department and debatably the entire university. It is literally unreal how great of a Professor he is. I am now a senior and I have never had an experience quite like his class. He dumbs down the material so much! If you are a CMN major, do not even THINK about having someone else teach this to you!
Brian is a really nice guy and i really find this class useful and practical.

Not only was he engaging, hilarious, and nice to look at, but he was a great teacher. Always made the content clear and relatable with a lot of examples. Discussions also really helped clarify concepts. Tests were easy as long as you reviewed your notes. No book.
Pretty fun class, required for my major. Interesting, and interactive lectures.
Funny and interesting, tests can be tough though. If you spend 4-5 hours in total studying for each exam you should be good though.
Interesting lectures, very accessible professor.

I wouldn't recommend taking this class unless you have to. There was a lot of material. Tests were tough, but the assignments were easy.  Tests were worth 75% and assignments were worth 25% of our grade. They only give you notes to study from because there's no book. Professor Quick is a nice guy, but I still would fall asleep in class.

Nice and charming. Gives you great examples and the lectures are mostly interesting and fun. A lot of people show up even if there is no attendance taken. Course materials are fully covered, while the best thing is it's not hard to get a good grade!
Best Prof of my freshman year. Great Prof and made me feel better about big lecture halls
Everything you could want in a professor, and then some. You can tell he really loves what he does.

He is a great professor! I was kind of nervous about taking this class because I am normally not good with understanding and memorizing theories but he is very good at explaining them and he made class a lot of fun. He is very outgoing and is a pretty funny guy. You will definitely enjoy taking this class with him.

Class is easy as long as you do the hw assignments (based on completeness and effort) and fill in the blanks in the notes section of your book and attend discussion sections to get extra info that's on the exam. Also, the 10 points extra credit is a big help since the class is only out of 400 points

Brian is one of the best professors I have had so far at this school. He really cares about his students. There are 3 non-cumulative exams and 1 final and you can drop 1 of them.  There are also weekly assignments that are very easy and short due in discussion every week. I highly recommend this class! It persuaded me to major in communications!
Great professor! He kept the class engaged and he is very passionate about what he teaches. Yet, sometimes you might think you understand the material but think again because the exam is very tricky.

The best professor i had in the CMN department. The class has two group project, one classroom presentation, grades a lot base on eye contact and final paper on a health campaign. Two exams total,the exam were more towards concept applying in a scenario, not memorization of the definition. He grades fairly as long as he see you try and the ideas.

Brian is a nice guy but I hate the way he lectures. He shares way too much personal info about his life and calls the class "gang" which is kind of belittling. The exams seemed disorganized and disproportionately harder to the way the material was taught.
Prof Quick is super nice. He's passionate about what he teaches and makes each lecture engaging. He loves his students and wants them all to do well.

Quick loves what he does and teaches the material effectively. CMN theory is pretty dry but he tries to make it more interesting. Don't be afraid to get to know him and use the resources he offers you to your advantage. Go to class as much as you can and you should be alright.

The class itself is very interesting and informational, you actually get to learn a lot of practice stuff. It is consist of 3 exams and a final project. Overall the exams are easy, it is divided into 80% lecture notes and 20% reading material. There are three types of exams format u get to pick which kind you want to take, such as multiple choice.

There are 3 exams and a cumulative final, but you get the drop the lowest exam grade of the 4 exams. This allows some people to not take the final, but if you do take it, it is the same exam questions as the previous 3 exams but they don't allow you to see what questions you got wrong on the first 3 exams so I feel like I made the same mistakes.

Professor Quick is a fun professor, he tries to make the class very interesting possible. The class itself was not hard, as long as you takes notes and do the course pack readings. There are 3 exams and one final. However, only 3 exams counts, so final was optional. However, what i don't like about this class, is that final was cumulative.

he makes lectures interesting and gives great examples. the exams are kind of tough, but you get to drop one and there is a TON of extra credit. overall, good class, great guy. oh, and we got out of class early almost every day.

Great Prof. he will love to teach stuff and explain things very well. Also like making fun and make the class more interesting. I did learn l lot form him. In addition, care about his students, give reasonable extra credit

Prof Quick is awesome. He makes lectures fun and interesting. Make sure that you print off or have the powerpoint slides because sometimes he will lecture off of those and not the work book. I would also suggest going to office hours. He's a cool guy to talk to one-on-one with and very helpful.
Prof Quick was super cool. The class was interesting and he kept it fun. He was very helpful in answering questions at his office hours.

He's a cool guy who is obviously interested in the subject and does a good job explaining the information. Make sure to pay attention to the power points because that's what the exams are based off of.

Prof Quick is a super nice guy and his class is pretty easy.  There is no attendance in lecture.  Attendance is taken in discussion by turning in 9 very easy homework assignments.  The tests were harder than I thought judging off lectures.
This class is easy and fun. Prof. Quick makes lectures interesting and he's pretty lenient about the tests.
Very enthusiastic!  He tends to go a little too in depth to some examples, but he's very straightforward and approachable.

Prof Quick is a a lot of fun and obviously cares about his subject. He jokes around and really encourages class participation even in a huge lecture. Class is not very hard and both Prof Quick and the TAs are very helpful when there are questions.

The best lecturer I have ever had. He explains everything so well and tries his best to make everything seem intuitive. All the lectures are recorded and all the materials you need are just there on the website. The exams are not too tough as long as you pay attention and make a good cheat sheet.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Best professor at UIUC!!! Found the class to be amazing.
The professor promised to help with equations (even write them on the board) so we don't have to memorize every single thing. He didn't even show up to midterm and the TAs had no clue.

The way Romit explains complex algorithms with steady pacing, great analogies, and constant involvement of students is very enjoyable. Gives nice signal processing primer to CS students - his FFT lecture is the best lecture I've ever heard. Some MP descriptions/gradings are weird but they took the advice and started changing them for next semester.

The best professor I have met in my 4 years at UIUC. Very passionate about teaching, explaining things very clearly. Give the lecture in a humorous way and you will never get asleep on his class. MP and HW are challenging but you also learn a lot from them.

Romit is a humorous professor who can explain the concept with interesting words, wonderful visualization, and many interactions. He draws some colorful notes for some lectures to illustrate the knowledge. The MP and homework are well-designed. As a beginner to the computer network, I should say I learn quite a lot from this course.
One of the best lecturer, explains tough math concept with intuitions. Very excited about course materials and his research.

One of the best professors I've taken a class with. Every lecture was clear, concise, and logical. I didn't understand linear algebra before I took this class. The midterm was challenging, yet fun! I think that can be said for the entire class. The material is non-trivial, the math is non-trivial yet his presentation of the material made it fun!

His lectures are the best I've ever seen, by a far margin. Every detail is presented in a logical way that shows *why* rather than just *what*. And, his drawing skills are amazing, which helps explain concepts in an interactive way. However, exams often include ambiguous wording. Combine this with their harsh grading and this ends up being unfair.

Great lectures and interesting projects. You definitely will learn something through them. But I have to mention the professor and his TAs are really harsh in exam grading. Better audit this course instead of taking it for credit.

Easily my favorite ECE/CS professor I've had at UIUC. Explains everything clearly and responds to every student question in detail. He paces lectures to make sure the class understands the material, and is extremely knowledgeable of the material he is teaching. I liked him so much as a professor that I'm taking ECE/CS 498 RR, Smartphone Mobile Sens

Grading was completely off the wall and I definitely was marked incorrect multiple ties for correct answers, there is no way to prepare properly for the exams, but I think the curve was amazing however, I can't say I learned much from the class
Uncaring teacher, grading criteria unclear
Worst teacher ever. Dr. Sennet talks in circles, but always misses the point. Her inconsistent teaching paired with her lack of enthusiasm makes for the worst class at the U of I.

By far my best teacher so far. I've only spent a year with her so far and am looking forward to the next 3. Although she seems very business oriented, she seems to genuinely care. Totally knows all here stuff and is a supreme performer.

Prof Sennet is the best teacher I've ever had, hands down. She knows exactly what she's talking about and even if I didn't practice as much as I should she still makes the most of all the lesson time. Can't say enough good things about her, truly an exceptional teacher and musician.
The professor taught really nice, but the content was not easy and you need to spend plenty of time to interpret it. Exams are super difficult

Very good professor. I was lucky to take class with him. He knows the subject thoroughly and the most important part is that he knows how to pass the knowledge to the students. He is a great teacher and I look forward to taking more of classes taught by him.
He is the best professor I've ever had.
Great professor. Excellent presentation of material. Pay attention and ace the course.

RS cares very much about the success of his students, but he also teaches a very tough course and has very little patience if you don't understand the material. Workload is staggering, but large. Weekly quizzes in this class are rather difficult for just being weekly quizzes. His patience is fleeting, but he does care and tries to do what he can.

R.S. is a stud, bottom line.  The most badass Indian man I've met, if you goto class, and pay attention, you'll be set for an A, at worst a B.  All of his tests are half in class/half take home.  If you aren't retarted you'll get an A on the take home every time.  Definately look for classes taught by this Indian God...
R.S. is an awesome guy/teacher. Very clear lectures and notes - makes the learning process for controls much easier. Be prepared to hear the phrase "nitty-gritty" about 10 times per lecture though...
I really like the way professor Rao focuses on figuring out the strengths and weaknesses of different scenarios and headlines. I can now debate with me parents and use evidence to make my arguments
Rao's CAs are the best. They taught me how to study and take notes, and I got As in my psych classes because I knew how to think about the stats. You have to work hard but its low-key worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Rao has created a class which was not designed with the students' best interest in mind. This was a very difficult class. Only take it if you have to.

OMG his last lecture made me cry. He's the most caring professor on campus. He sends you an email if you do well on his exam. He always answers your questions after class. He makes stats actually interesting. His stories are so meaningful and from his heart. The class is hard, but it's worth it. Professor Rao is worth it.
Read the book. Take notes. Go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I don't like him. Lectures are like 600+ people and the CA problem reviews don't help at all during the lecture because they don't explain very well and he also doesn't explain things clearly so i just don't go and do tutoring instead. If you don't have to take stats don't. Do it at CC instead. waste of time and dropping my GPA for this bogus class

I thought Prof. Rao was a pretty clear teacher in terms of what he wanted us to learn, but sometimes the classroom environment would get hostile or aggressive because of the way he would address the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend this class to anyone; very passive-aggressive. You read the assigned chapter, go over the same chapter in class, and maybe, IF you're lucky, do a practice problem. Offers review sections, aka go over vocab. Lacks further explanation, practice problems, but no key. Extra credit surveys help, hard to study and even harder tests.

Who's not here!!!! Professor Rao is the best. I learned so much from him. All the stats in my psych classes is just low key everything Prof Rao taught. Ngl I'm getting As in psych because of stats while everyone else is confused.
You can tell he loves his students and cares about them so much! I loved hearing him speak about stats, you can really tell he loves what he does too. He tells excellent stories!
Read the book. Go to class. Take notes. Study the way he suggests. Get an A+. You definitely have to think but he low key tells you exactly what to study and how. Just do what he says.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I like professor Rao. He actually makes stats interesting. Read the book and go to class and take good notes, the exam is all the things he says in class.

Didnt like him. He was constantly complaining about students talking in a 500-person lecture. I don't know what you expected. Kept trying to hold us over class time, and then tried to make people feel bad for leaving when class was over, and he kept talking.

The material feels like it shouldn't be difficult and makes perfect sense until you go to lecture. He acts like if you do everything, then you're guaranteed to do well and understand, but unfortunately that's not true. Most of what he talks about in lecture is actually irrelevant to the coursework, and just makes the class more confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Teaches well, homework and textbook is super helpful. The exams aren't overly hard and the review sessions for the exams are really helpful too.
PROFESSOR RAO IS THE GOAT

I can't believe I got an A- in this class tbh. It feels like a lot of the answers to his questions are ambiguous. For the mandatory lecture, you need an iClicker which he uses to ask you questions. Unfortunately, if you get it wrong, you lose points. There are a lot of extra credit surveys you can fill out though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Had to teach myself everything, always yapping about apples to apples yet I still don't know what that means. save yourself

Hard class but professor does care a lot. Nice curves and cheatsheets as well as practice before exams. Follow the workbook/textbook and you'll be fine. Would be best to make friends and study in groups to understand the concepts better.

Professor Rao seems to get a lot of hate, but I don't think it's warranted. I got a D on my first exam and was frustrated, but then I started reading the book, paying attention in class, and I got an A on the next two exams. Prof Rao is a great guy who's personable and wants to see his students succeed. You'll get out what you put into the class.

I have mixed feeling on this class. I got an A on all exams but I almost entirely taught myself the material. I didn't find the lectures and his teaching style very helpful and I despise the way he does iClicker. Also the TAs are just as confused as the students. However, Prof Rao really cares about his students and wants to make you think.

Rao is the GOAT. I emailed him because I thought I was going to get a C, I did good on exams but missed a lot of homeworks and never went to class so had like a 0 participation score. He said because my exams grades were better than my homework he was going to adjust my grade to match my exam scores!! I went from a C to an A-. GOAT.

Read before class and his lectures make sense, otherwise it's hard to understand what he is explaining. You have to work to get an A but it's worth it. Everything he teaches shows up in all my other classes. Most valuable gen ed I have ever taken.

While I did get an A+, I think that his teaching needs ALOT work. I self taught myself the whole class because his explanations were confusing. This class took so much more time then it should have. The class would have been so much better if he improved his teaching skills. He was really kind, but just not a good professor at all.

professor rao is a great guy and very passionate about statistics and this course. he wants his students to get an A, but you do have to try somewhat in order to get it. he gives out a lot of extra credit that adds up at the end of the semester. you could lwk get a high c on every exam and then do all the extra credit and get an A.

Honestly anyone complaining about this class just didn't put the least amount of effort into this class. He makes it pretty easy to study for the exams as everything is available on canvas. Even if you don't do well on the exams, you can still manage a good grade, for example, my friends got Cs on the tests and still managed to pull out low As.
Don't take this class, it's useless info, and he made up the whole book himself. He also can't explain anything at all.

He does not know how to teach a class well, and this class will take up more time for you than it should. He is a nice person overall, but just a very bad lecturer. He made up this whole class himself, and then when you go to office hours, they don't seem to help. He makes it more confusing than it needs to be because he knows this is just a gen ed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: the homework doesn't prepare you for what the tests look because the questions are written a lot differently. has resources for you to get help if you need it. He sometimes fails to explain topics that most of the class doesn't understand. must study outside of class to get a good grade!

Why is everyone hating on Rao? If you feel like he didn't help you it's low key your fault. Its definitely a lot though. My roommate and I both took it. She never showed up or read the book so obvi she was always confused and thought Rao is the worst. I actually went to class and took notes and got an A. It's really not bad if you actually try.
Show up to class because he does Iclickers, He does not know how to teach and you basically have to teach yourself the material so take the course online if you can. Always do the surveys.

This was literally the worst class I took this semester. If I'm gonna be honest, he makes everything up the whole class he made up himself. He wrote the book in 5 minutes, and you can tell by the number of mistakes he made throughout the book. He refused to help me understand the material, and sent me to the tas who got even more wrong then I did.

I was gonna write a horrible review, but then he lowkey gave us a crazy deal: he would raise the weight of our second or third midterm grade, and my 91% bumped to a 99% in the class despite getting a D on the last exam. Rao is not so bad. He is a miracle worker, and he's the GOAT. After a semester of suffering, this made it worth it.
Don't take

Stats can be intimidating, especially if you're a beginner. However, professor Rao is a great lecturer. He really explains concepts very well and he also makes stats very interesting and applicable. 
While there is a lot of reading involved, its clear he wants you to succeed and enjoy his class.

I went into this class thinking it would be a traditional, math based course. This was WRONG. There is minimal math- he typically pulls numbers from the air. However, Rao wants his students to think like him and question everything. This is a very conceptual class and if you don't do well with that, good luck and godspeed.

Prof Rao is really a caring professor. Sometimes he gets fed up with people being lazy or talking over him, but he does try and seems like a nice guy. Class content is hard, and he does not always explain well, but there are chances for extra credit. Come to office hours too!

Prof Rao is a great person overall and I will definitly use what I learned for classes/labs. While at points the class gets confusing like  "maybe " as a answer, I get that things arent always definite. Even in a giant lecture hall he will try and connect with students as a person and even sends congratulating emails if you did well on a test

Professor Rao is extremely understanding and reasonable with personal matters. He will make you feel important even in a class of 900. The class is not very difficult and the homeworks/labs are very easy, and PAL surveys allow for a lot of extra credit. He teaches very clearly and provides many resources.

I really like professor Rao, but some of the ideas here at the end are really confusing. He challenges your thinking, which I really like though, even if it is confusing. This is definitely the course that I learned the most from. Exams are doable, just make sure you study hard and go to office hours every week. don't fall behind!

You are going to sit in this class and wonder if any of this is even real. Here's the answer: literally everything feels made up. This is the only math course that I have ever taken where "maybe" was an answer on the exam. Rao wrote the textbook, so you have to think like him to do well on the exams. At heart, he is a good person and means well.

Rao definitely wants you to succeed, but omg, is he confusing. The exams are nothing like what you do in lecture and assignments. They are 10x harder. He has me feeling like I am in a philosophy class, with making us think "ish-ness" and having "maybe" as an answer. All I gained from this class was to be uncertain about everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Rao is a great guy, but his class made no sense most of the time. Lots of the answers to questions will be "maybe" or "it depends" which is annoying. Midterms get harder and harder so be prepared to study. Watch the lectures online and go to office hours for help. If you fall behind on the material, you've gotta hope for a miracle.

He talks quickly during the lectures, and I had a hard time understanding. However, if you do the surveys and study hard for the exams, you will be ok. Most of the content sounds made up and fake. My advice is to hold on and lock in. The only thing that really stuck with me was that compression socks may or may not make me run faster.

Easy A , very good intro course for stats. Lectures are very easy to understand, but most of the information was  intuitive. Few assignments, quizzes were easy, and he gave late credit for a lot of work. Midterm and final were a lot harder and will catch you off guard if you aren't properly prepared. Very sympathetic, understanding, and kind.
PROFESSOR RAO IS THE GOAT!

If you want to talk with a professor like two human beings, If you want a professor who sees you as a person and not just a student, If you want a professor who cares about you and your well being, You want Professor Rao.
Prof. Rao is the best. If you need to take stat 100, take it with him!!

Rao was genuinely one of my favorite professors I had my freshman year--he really cared that his students learned the content. I was sometimes confused so I would go to office hours and that was always very helpful. You can tell he really cares about his work, I have lots of respect for him as a person and educator.

SUPER caring, seems like a great guy outside of class. As a teacher, he was very difficult for me to learn from personally, and I went to almost every lecture. His teaching method was far too slow in the beginning and far too quick at the end imo.
Not an easy class, but it's very clear exactly what you need to do to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took his class over the summer and online. If you have the time and need the credit, I recommend it. You definitely will find yourself studying for the exams, but again, if you have the time, it's not too hard.

I'm not a math person and this course was not at all easy, but I liked Prof Rao's book. Some of it was confusing but it also didn't really have a lot of confusing math. Go to every office hours, I started after quiz 2 and wish I went all summer. The TAs are really helpful. Prof Rao also is really understanding and easy to email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I thought this class was impossible to pass since I failed my first exam, but what had helped was going to office hours with getting that help. Ask questions. I made sure to study the whole week coming up to the exam date. He is a caring professor and if you need to talk to him. Also make sure to do all the extra credit, and there will be curves.
Hard but useful especially if you are in a lab
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He makes the test much more complicated then it needs to be for a 100 level class. I had to study a good amount for a topic that seems like common sense. I took the online version of the class. Its easy to complete one week worth of homework the day before its due if you are on a time crunch. If your going to take this class you need patience.
Homework included a quiz and practice problems after every lecture and weekly problems and a data set quiz.

Gives LOTS of extra credit and highly recommends reading the chapter before coming to class. In-class lectures are a bit boring, and he rushes through topics at times. He can be nice, he has his moments where he is stern (phones away, no talking, don't do assignments last minute, etc.) The first exam 2 proctorU while the others were CBTF.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: My roommate and I took stats together. She was online, I was in person. She didn't like Prof Rao, but she never talked to him. You have to go to class or office hours and actually talk to him. He is so caring and supportive and will make time to help you. He just has a million students so if you don't talk to him it feels like he doesn't care.
this professor was really amazing! he made stat 100 actually enjoyable and gave a lot of extra credit. prepares you very well for the exam and cares about his students.
