If you read the book and come to lecture you will be fine. The difficulty will sneak up on you so you better stay on top of your readings. Lazy students will have an issue with this class, others won't. Simple as that.

Rao is a super chill guy who you can tell is passionate about statistics and making sure his students succeed. I'm not a huge fan of statistics since I'm better with numbers but as long as you read the chapters and do the example problems this class should be a breeze.

I took the online version. Getting an A is definitely possible if you study hard and are good at math. overall the class is useless and as he says, you have to think like him. I didn't really learn anything that wasn't either already common sense or that could be used outside of this class. but a good thing is that that there's a lot of ex credit

Didn't really enjoy the class or find it useful. The second and third exams were quite difficult and I found it super frustrating how we couldn't view our exams or see our originals scores before the curves. It's not difficult to receive an A, you just have to study for it.

Didn't really learn anything and didn't really find anything useful. The second and third exams are quite difficult, but there was a large curve. It's not difficult to recieve an A in the class if you work for it.
He's alright. That is really the best i can describe him as

Professor Rao is the kindest. I did really bad on the second test, so I worked really hard went to every class went to every office hour and got an A on the third exam. And then I get an email from this man congratulating me on my hard work and saying he's proud of me. I low key cried. He's the only professor I've had who makes me feel seen.
Hard class, but I feel like I've learned more from professor Rao than any of my other classes

I hate Rao. It's an online class. But exams are in person? And then he tells me because I didn't follow his instructions he's going to take 10% off my exam if I take it late? And don't even try emailing him, he'll send you a grumpy message about the syllabus saying to email the class email account and not him.
he is alright

Professor Rao is a great professor. I'm taking the online Stats 100 class at the moment. I struggle with stats due to my weakness in conceptual understanding and trick questions, so I might end up with a C or lower. Still, I respect him he genuinely tries to help students. There's also lots of extra credit, so make sure to do them.
I love professor roa. The class is hard, but he does a lot to help students. And it feels really useful. Do all the extra credit. Go to all the office hours. And take good notes.
Soo much better than econ 202. There's a lot of reading and the exams are tough, but there's not so much equations and math which I like. Go to office hours every week and try to work with Rao.
some things are confusing, but there's so much extra credit, and you get unlimited attempts. love the ca's. theyre really nice and helpful
Take stat with Rao! I'm pre-law and didn't think about it would actually help me but turns out asking who's not here and what was compared is helping me on practice LSAT questions!
Amazing lectures he is very passionate
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you took AP Stats in highschool, this is nothing like it. This class amazing. Professor Rao truly cares about his students and he really takes the time to make sure everyone is learning and not falling behind. He gives you multiple opprotunites to acheive an A in this class and prepares you very well for the tests. Very easy to get an A!

Rao's class isn't a typical math class, which I loved!! He focuses on big picture ideas. I spent about 4-5 hrs every every week outside of class after midterm 1, reading the book and watching lecture recordings to take good notes. It's worth it though, I learned more from Rao than any of my other classes.

If you aren't a fan of not questions being vastly different on the practice problems than on the exams I'm not sure I would recommend him. He is very caring about his students and take advantage of office hours. However you can't look at your wrong answers on past tests or on any of the practice problems so how do you know what to study??

Professor Rao is the best. You have to work hard, but he makes it interesting and relevant. Every exam has a curve. And he sends you an email at the end of the semester if you get an A to congratulate you! So sweet ❣️

i took this class thinking it would be my easy A. wrong. rao's stats class was a lot of reading and understanding concepts instead of math, which i thought it would be. he is a very caring professor and you can tell that he genuinely wants you to do good, but his class was pretty hard. he does give a lot of extra credit towards the end so do those
I had a terrible semester. Professor Rao was very helpful and supportive. I am very grateful for Professor Rao.
Professor Rao's dedication to students is amazing. He made stats interesting instead of intimidating. He and the TAs also communicated great given how many students there are.

The tests cover material, but the questions are worded in an extremely confusing and overly complicated way. It often feels like the tests are more about deciphering what the question is asking rather than focusing on the content. Additionally, we don't go over problems, and I can't see previous tests. How am I supposed to learn from my mistakes?
Genuinely cares about students so much, literally wants everyone to get an A

I'm only writing because I'm surprised what other people are writing. If you take college seriously, and you want to learn a lot, and are willing to work hard, take Professor Rao. I'm so thankful I had him. The course pushes you, but Professor Rao and the CAs are incredibly supportive. 

If all you want to do is goof off, then don't take the class.
Lectures are so boring and unengaging so be prepared but his grading curve saved me for real. He gets really sassy if you try to leave lecture early so beware. Also study extra hard for midterm 3.

Professor Rao sent me an email congratulating me on getting an A on the midterm. I've never had a professor do that before. He's such a good professor and he's really kind and caring. Take as many classes with him as you can.

Exams are hard but it's useful. I have friend in the other section and they're just doing a bunch of math. We don't do calculations, it's a lot of reading. But I like that. I don't like math. Rao makes stats actually useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Would stop his lectures to wait for 600 people to be silent before teaching. Made participation checks for problems worked on individually in class for points, but then wouldn't always go over the correct answers afterward so I couldn't find out what I did wrong.
Stat 100 is my hardest course. I am learning a lot that shows up in my other psych classes, so it is useful. But I didn't think I'd have to work so hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's good. Not a lot of equations and math.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Rao is the best

Easy class if you actually go to class every day and pay attention. I skipped class a lot and got a C on the first exam. Then I started going to class everyday and got an A on the next exam. Rao is really helpful if you ask questions. But he does expect you to do your work. If you're goofing off in class he'll call you out.

You can tell he genuinely cares about his students and what they are going through..I had a few issues and communicated with him directly about it and he was nothing but understanding and kind, clearly just wanting his students to succeed inside and outside of the classroom. His lectures are engaging and not boring either; highly recommend him!!

easy online class. unlimited attempts on homeworks. kind of tough exams but huge curve. pretty straight forward to get an A. and it's actually useful -- a lot of what professor roa talked about are showing up again in my  other clases
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: im in stat100 right now. his lectures are the best compared to my other intro classes. i like being able to ask the ta questions in class. we just got midterm grades. there was a huge curve. my friends that come to class we all did really well.

Easiest class ever. Professor actually wants you to succeed. So many grade replacement opportunities, I believe he curved every test, everything you need is in the workbook. Lectures are a bit boring but he records them all and doesn't take attendance. Pretty much stopped going in-person after 2 weeks. Just watch the videos to study.
HUGE curve. It moved me B+ to A. Study hard for final. My final replaced my.midterm score. Makes big difference in final grade
Do what he says you should do and you'll get an A
Just finished the summer online course. I thought the midterms were a little tricky, but the curve professor gave was AMAZING. Easy A, and low key kind of interesting.

I made a HUGE mistake and didn't realize our midterm was due in Saturday (I thought it was due Sunday). Professor Rao allowed me to take it on Sunday anyway without penalty. Instead of a C, thanks to professor rao's kindness, I'll be getting an A. I really appreciate how understanding professor Rao was. Plus he's a great instructor
Professor Rao is a great professor. You can tell he really cares about his students.

Professor Rao is the kindest and most generous professor I've ever had. I missed several assignments because of some health flare ups, and he accepted all of them without a penalty, and even assigned one of the TAs to work with me to make sure I did well on the exam. No other professor does that. I'm so thankful I had professor Rao

Rao's lectures are actually low key kinda interesting. Plus he drops your first midterm if you do better on the final. If you put in the effort, Rao's class is an easy A, plus you actually learn interesting things. Some other stats classes are easier, but you just memorize and don't actually learn anything there. Take stats with Rao!

I took Stat100 online. We just watch lecture recordings and go to office hours. Rao's lectures are pretty entertaining, for an online course at least. I waited until week 4 to go to office hours which was a mistake -- go to office hours every week! The CAs were really helpful. My grade improved a lot after I started going to office hours.

I did not like his lecture style so I chose to watch most of them through the recordings he posted. Overall very flexible which is nice if you get sick. But i did end up teaching myself most things. Although I didn't find the lectures engaging, I know that Rao/his CAs are very open to helping students, and the office hours were helpful.

I am NOT a math person, and thank God I chose Rao. He taught us about effect sizes and making causal inferences and using statistical models, all things that show up in my psych classes. This is probably the most useful 100 level class. 

Just make sure you actually show up and ask questions. My roommate never came to class and got a C. I got an A.
Lectures were really hard to follow. The content in the book is often different from the lectures. Quiz questions don't help you prepare for exams. Too hard and overcomplicated for 100-level class.

When he said "attendance is optional" that was code for "if you don't wanna do/discuss the practice problems in class, just leave." If you participate and ask questions to Rao/the CAs, you should be good. Coming from AP Stat, I really think this course gave me a better appreciation for statistics and how it's actually used, not just using a TI-84

I understood where Rao was going with the class, but his teaching style was difficult to follow. After week 1 of class, he emphasized that attendance was not mandatory, making it difficult to be present and attentive. He posted video recordings for every lecture which was nice when it came time to study for exams. Grade is all quizzes and exams.

Professor Rao was a good guy but I just never really aligned with his teaching style. Cares about what he is teaching and his students, I just always found his lectures quite confusing and found teaching myself was what I was doing most of the time.

Cares about students, offers multiple opportunities for extra credit. However, I found his lectures difficult to follow at times. Some topics are overcomplicated and the wording in the book is confusing to me. Also, lectures do not follow the book 100%, and he skips over some review questions. More challenging than I expected for 100-level course.

Great professor and really cares for his students. Math isn't really my forte my he made it somewhat easier to understand. There is a fair share of homework and quizzes throughout the semester. Two exams, the midterm and final. Both are done before midterm and finals week though. Lots of extra credit opportunities.
Very good lecturer for STAT 100. He understands that its a beginner level stats course, and makes everything easy to understand.

A guided notebook is the required textbook for the class, although it was poorly utilized by Professor Rao. He skimmed over the examples, making it hard to understand the concepts. The content of the lectures would be easy to understand if the lecture was given in a way that explained the concepts with context and utilized the guided notes.

Professor Rao is one of the kindest and most effective instructors I have had. He can make classes with 600+ people feel personal and his effort/ability to care for his students is evident. Rao is very inspirational and overall a great teacher. This is definitely the best class to take for the QR1 requirement.

I

Dr Rao is a very attentive professor who truly cares about the content of his class with a passion. His class is structured in a way to ensure all his students can succeed with reasonable effort while understanding the content. His lectures are very well presented and recordings are offered actively, giving students a lot of flexibility

Prof Rao is loved by many, but for me, I found his lectures hard to follow. He often just skims over what is in the book. However, it is fairly easy to get an A in the class. Only rating to suggest to take the course with one of the other Professors. We had a lecture done by Karle Flanagan one day, and it was much better and easier to understand.

His assignment structure made it very easy to hold a high grade in the class and his lectures were always enthusiastically presented. A good lecturer and a professor that only wants to see his students succeed in understanding the content. We need more professors like Dr. Rao.

Really nice guy, easy grader, this class is pretty much impossible to not get an A in. All homework assignments have two tries (including quizzes) and the content is pretty easy especially in the first half of the class. His tests have little to no actual calculations in them, Cheat sheets on all tests. No final!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Rao overall is a great educator in the field of statistics, and provides students the ability to both learn the very basics of statistics and apply it in a useful "common day" manner. Depending on the lecture it is easy to check out halfway - end, but overall they are still useful and available online. Great professor and addition to U of I.

Makes it very easy to get an A. HW is due about every other week and is very simple. If you get a 70 or above on both midterms, you get an A in the class and don't have to take the final. Class is very basic level knowledge level of stats.

professor rao is amazing. his lectures are great, but you dont have to come to class to do well. you get two tries on everything. plus he's really caring. i have covid and he just said to rest and dont worry about the course, feel better soon. all my other professors told me to keep up while at home. i wish they were all like professor rao

While some material was genuinely interesting, a lot of it just felt unrelated and was just boring. Exams will test you on random facts so make sure to have detailed notes. There's also imo far too much homework given for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 10/10 class, well organized, engaging content, and overall not too bad besides heavy readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This prof's lectures are very engaging and thought-provoking. He speaks very clearly and presents current real-world problems in CS to the classroom and in assignments. I have learned a lot about ethics in CS, and my perspectives have broadened from his teachings. His discussion sections are also fun, as they are done in game or role-play styles!
Passionate about material and passionate about teaching students the material. Cares more about understanding the content than test grades.
Really good professor who is extremely passionate about the material. Didn't think I would care about ethics but ended up learning a lot.
One of the best professors that I had. Learned A LOT from his class, really sparked my interest in technology. Grading isn't that hard at all if you pay attention and actually want to learn.
He's an interesting and inspiring lecturer who leaves a tad to be desired and overall I completely recommend him for any cs courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: If you are not CS major get ready to die. At the beginning class(101)seems easy, but when you get your first homework where you should write whole code by yourself , that's madness. However, midterms are not so bad , but the final is tough because there are free-response  questions.
Good teacher, but the homeworks are a little tough, especially if you are not a CS major. Would suggest utilizing TA office hours, and befriending people!

Very condescending. Answers Piazza posts in a very disrespectful way. Gets really mad when people don't attend lecture so he makes the tests really hard which doesn't benefit anyone. Kind of acts like a child when it comes to people not paying attention to exactly what he expects. Needs to grow up a little bit.
He wanted his students to succeed. He's a great professor that really wants everyone to succeed.

He's a very intelligent, young guy who is very clear, cares about his students, and honestly seems like the most personable professor I've ever had while on campus. I've had him three times, and I recommend him to any student taking any computer science oriented courses. He knows his stuff.
One of the best Professors I've ever had. Very nice and helpful. Lectures are engaging and clear.

I think at times the lectures are unevenly organized (lots of time spent on some sections at the expense of others) but mostly, the lectures are quite good. The homework is difficult and so are the tests. You need to know the material really well so be ready for that and make use of labs and practice exams. Good luck.

Good professor. Only issue is that keeps trying to explain "intuition" in a way that doesn't ever click. Other than that pretty standard and all. Not really her fault since no one speaks up about teaching style afaik

In the spirit of gratitude, I've decided to write about Professor Mehta here. In short, in addition to being a great lecturer, she cares a lot about students' learning AND their well being. 

Go to her office hours, because she WILL help you - she truly wants you to succeed, and don't take it for granted - such professors are few far in between.
Amazing course, and amazing teacher.
Amazing course. Prof. Mehta's lectures are clear, interactive, and with lots of examples. The HWs are tough but fun to work on. The course is demanding overall due to it's difficult content.

She is caring and nice to students, but her lectures are disorganized and her notes are hard to read. Homeworks are really hard, much more than the lecture examples. Office hours are online and uneffective. Spend more time reading the textbook bu yourself and prepare well for exams.
Fine i guess

Easy grader, very kind and funny, but the lectures were on blackboard and felt scattered and old-fashioned. Long difficult HWs made up for it though. Good professor but lectures could use some modernization.
Great professor who really cares about whether students have understood the material. Gives plenty of homework and practice problems to ensure content mastery
Worst lectures I've ever attended

I barely learned anything from the lecture. The only reason I attended is that it is mandatory. Professor cannot clearly explain the material, not to mention helping you understand those equations. To get an A, practice homework over and over again. Don't ask why the equations work, because even the professor won't explain it well.

I've had him for 340 and 360 and I love Salapaka! He's hilarious in class when you pay attention to his jokes, REALLY cares about his students understanding the content. Always open to questions. I wish all professors were like him. He really knows his stuff, and while his homework is sometimes tricky, he will walk you through it.
Awesome guy, really passionate about his subject. Very easy to approach and very helpful. Homeworks are hard and long but exams are fair. Knows his stuff.
Good guy. Lectures were pretty helpful and he's always helpful in answering questions. The exams were pretty fair as well
Good professor. Very helpful and likes answering any question a student might have.  Does not move too quickly during lecture to ensure full understanding.

Salapaka is an alright professor but what I really didnt like about him was that he was not careful at all about writing lecture notes. There were always mistakes which made the class even harder to understand. He bases his exams on the hw and class examples so going to office hours really helps clear things up. He also keeps candy in his pockets

If you know basic calculus stuff like the chain rule, this class will be a breeze and you will learn a ton. Vasu does a pretty good job explaining things and does a ton of examples, but got rushed for time at the end of the semester.
lectures are very helpful, talks a little fast sometimes.  I'd take him for another class if i could
Nice guy, but not always good at explaining complicated material.

Good professor. I learned a lot about 3D-making techniques from her class as a graphic design major. The design projects had clear demonstrations and opportunities to engage with peers. She is accessible outside the classroom.

Spends the first 20 minutes of class talking our ears off over nothing, way too many rules for a DESIGN class. incredibly boring and doesn't seem like she knows what she's talking about, definitely never helps us understand. ugh
Professor Mania is kind and smart. She responds quickly to any queries, and the projects that we did for her ARTD101 class were interesting! Sometimes she overexplains, but that is fine.

Mania is not very knowledgeable in what she teaches, for "Human-Centered Design", she teaches very briefly about what the subject is, but the rest of them, including projects and progress checks and more, are all exactly the same as a basic 102 or 202 course. In summary, her classes are too easy and most things students have already learned.

He changed it so there is no test drop anymore. You're assigned a random group to do one worksheet together in each class. Tests are heavily dependent on the like 3 free response questions. Towards the end there's a group project which isn't that difficult just time consuming. Lectures aren't great as he seems unprepared at times and scared.

Disliked his lectures because he is very quiet and unsure of himself. He often has issues with his code in class and can't answer questions well. He was impatient with a specific student in our class that frequently had questions and he didn't maintain a professional demeanor.

Four midterms, no final or cumulative exam. Fair grader. There are three group projects, and it's easy to get >=97 on each. Some midterm questions are tricky but not too hard. I took AP Stat, so the concepts felt easy to me, but the worksheets and examples may not be enough for students without prior stats experience.

No point in the lectures, apart from getting the answers to the worksheets. The 10 CBTF quizzes were very easy and based directly on the homework and worksheets. The class needs a major redesign as the prarielearn workspace coding is very slow and crashes constantly.

One of the most unprepared lecturers that I have had at UIUC. If you are taking him get ready for him to stutter through his unprepared notes and then introduce you to material that you do not need whatsoever. His class is not laid out well at all and his students are constantly correcting his errors. Overall, very disappointing class.  Good luck

Lectures are just him coding. Nice guy, but class is super unhelpful. You watch him code, then try to code in groups for worksheets. Lectures did not effectively teach the concepts that come up on homework. I think stats requires a good conceptual understanding of the material, but if you don't have that already, 202 might get hard.

Consistently unprepared & confused during lectures. Unable to answer questions or explain material; especially coding. Often contradicted the syllabus & gave misleading advice on major assignments. Teamwork issues dragged down individual grades & ignored repeated complaints. Unfairly removed extra credit for students who completed all their work.

This professor is very nice, but get ready to learn everything by yourself. He often make mistakes in lecture and he continues typing in R when the rest of the class are clueless. Tests structure is awful, questions weighted heavily and for most questions you only get 3 tries if not 2, imo doesn't reflect how much you've learned.

He lectured by mumbling while typing into an R-markdown. He never taught the key concepts of any units, and many students had large fundamental gaps, which made in-class work and tests hard. His syllabus said that the lowest of the 4 midterms could be dropped, and without announcing it to the class, he changed it to only the lowest of the first 3.
He is supportive all the time during the semester.
He clearly did not know the material, and office hours are basically non existent. A nice guy but lectures are extremely useless and the guidelines for the project make no sense.
Work in groups to solve worksheets for attendance. Plenty of ways to get help. Exams are fair.
Prof didn't know the material very well. Learned everything through the answer keys of the worksheets and the review sessions. Final project isnt too bad.

This professor lacks empathy. CS374 is mandatory to almost all people reading this unfortunately. This prof lacks an understanding of fairness, in both personal outreach and class. He wouldn't boost an 89.99 if you were in the hospice.
I would rather spend some time discussing quantum physics with my friend's Samoyed than listening to this guy's lectures.
I actually had him for ECE220 over the summer and he was a great professor. Super great at explaining and was able to explain notes in a very comprehensive way.

Besides him being nice, the guy has nothing going for him. He just repeats what Lumetta says in lectures but worse. He gets confused while teaching concepts and says sry then spends 10 more minutes on one thing. As soon as the concepts got difficult, the professor became worse at teaching than your average Undergrad who took the class and got a B.

Worst professor ever—he rips Kani's materials, tweaks them, and claims them as his own. His lectures are so unclear everyone learns from Kani's videos. He grades harshly: no curve on a tough final, splits 3 midterms into 4 brutal exams, and delays the final-drop decision. Pure incompetence.
CIA should use his lecture recordings as interrogation tools

Half the time I'm unsure if he knows what he's teaching. I wish that Lumetta dude was still teaching here, I honestly don't know why I even attend the lectures anymore. I only got through the first few weeks because I learned lots of basic content over break, and still he made things I've learned already seem confusing.
he is a nice guy but his teaching is crazy boring
perfect cure for insomnia

Some ppl don't like him but I think he is really nice. There were some things that could have been improved but he was incredibly understanding and receptive to feedback. 374 is a hard class whether you want to admit it or not but his exams were not bad and he tried his best. More humble than a majority of other profs here, cares ab students lots

Consistently put DIY on example problems, was inconsistent with THE SYLLABUS, and overall not great. There was always something unexpected with these exams. The curving he implemented made little or no sense.
DIY.
Professor skips slides during lecture very often, and concept w
DIY
He made jokes. I liked the way he taught.

Professor subbed in for Prof. Nickvash Kani during the Fall 2023 semester. He is okay. It's his first time teaching lectures ever. So I hope it gets better over time. Is awful at time management for lectures, reads off lecture slides and doesn't necessarily understand the lecture presentations made under Prof. Kani. Watch video lectures instead.
Great person but made mistakes on midterms. He gave the points back. Class is not hard at all.
Great speaker

He is honestly one of the best lecturers out there. He really makes everything intuitive and easy to grasp - given you attend the lectures. The exams were in the CBTF which means no partial credit, which is a bit odd for a stats course. The homework felt a little too tedious for the course, and the discussion section is not useful at all.

Class was incredibly mismanaged this semester, each CBTF exam having grading issues/typos worse than the last. Despite this, there was a heavy air of condescension in emails and in-person communication concerning these issues. Almost half of the final exam was on topics that were not covered on any midterm. Decent lecturer and homework was fine
Take class with Yu
sucks dont take him

Good lecturer and engaging. Homeworks are a little tedious but not too time-intensive. The online tests (for STAT 400) were frustrating since they offered little/no partial credit, which is strange for a statistics class since it disproportionately penalizes small calculation mistakes on problems requiring many steps.

Very caring guy, material is rather easy but as mentioned by a lot before me, the exams and Ed Discussion are handled terribly. No responses and tedious exam grading. It did fortunately get regraded but still no communication to students. Be aware of this, its okay if you have prior Statistics experience, but otherwise steer clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never felt more disrespected taking a class. Shows up 5 or more minutes late to lecture every single time. Questions on discussion forum are only ever answered by the same poor TA that can be bothered to log on (shoutout Adam Tonks fr). Material is incredibly easy but class is graded very strictly, particularly exams, and homeworks are so tedious.

Class is hanging by a thread. Super mismanaged class. Earlier, it used to be pen & paper, but now CBTF, which is where it has all gone downhill. Would recommend taking Professor Albert Yu's class instead, as it is still Pen and Paper!

I heard good things about this professor and class coming into stat 400 this semester but it turned out to be one of my worst experiences here so far. It feels like students aren't taken seriously because no one answers our questions on ED, midterms in cbtf have been hell, class in general has been very disorganized too.

I truly believe my degree is worth less for associating me with this professor.

CBTF exam questions consistently had incorrect answers and were met with absolutely zero response from the professor, despite literally 100+ Ed discussion posts asking about the blatant errors. Clearly doesn't care about his students whatsoever. Run fast and run far.

They ask u to post question on Ed, but important one never get answered on time, and the homework grading expectations are extremely unclear, u barely can get 100 in hw. If you can, take STAT 400 with any other professor.
worst organization skills in a professor I seen in a while

Right now, we're dealing with an AWS outage, so we can't access anything on Canvas. Tell me why he provides us with a drive with the stuff from canvas, but the homework due tomorrow or the exam material isn't posted. Like you cannot be this disorganized. On top of that, they don't respond to student messages about this issue. Genuinely, so stupid.

Currently taking the class, and the professor and his TAs take forever to respond to questions on Ed Discussion. Like there's questions from a month or like weeks ago that STILL haven't been responded to. So if you have a question or if there's any issues going on, good luck.
Easy exam content, but will take off points for the most tedious reasons. Easy to get an A though.

he is a nice man. however, his organization skills are horrendous. he frequently makes changes to the course's grading, homework submission rules, and he didn't even give information about when the cbtf exams are until at most a week before. have to go to lecture since he doesn't announce these changes on canvas or the forum.
Take what is said in the syllabus with a grain of salt.
I was his student in 2023. He is nice and knowledgable.

The professor isn't bad but I just self taught everything for STAT400 by using online resources. The homeworks and exam practices were significantly harder than the actual exam content. His lectures are readily available to watch online and from the minimal lectures I did attend in person hes pretty easy to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Unger's STAT 400 section is pretty easy. The homework takes a while but isn't too bad. The midterms are always easier than the practice problems he posts so I wind up very prepared. Lectures aren't very interesting but that's because he paces things pretty slow to ensure a complete understanding of the concepts behind the formulas.
Awful grading policy!!

Overly strict marking mechanism. both TA and professor tried every possible way to get my marks deducted. Multiple requests for regrade were pointless. Completely changed the point that assignments are meant to help students understand and learn better. I am very anxious and overly stressed.

This class is just AP Statistics with calc 2 in the beginning but harder since Unger explains how the distributions are derived from, as well as basic probability questions with notations.

Ppl criticize Unger for being too easy, but if you haven't done stat, his class is helpful. Be aware of MLE, it is hard, but will not show up until final.

Great lecturer with a sense of humor. Enjoyable lectures (can study without attending), although lectures do become very important after the second midterm. Has 50% of your grade assigned on HW, which are not so bad (4-6 hours per week). The midterms were fair with a harder final. Overall the class is fine if you stay on top of your HWs.

One of my favorite professors so far, his lectures are great. He is accessible at office hours and him and his TAs were great at helping me understand things. He is great at using tech with recorded lectures and online gradescope grading. Exams are easy and HWs are of medium difficulty. Concepts are a great foundation of basic statistics.
Lectures are very engaging. One of my favorite teachers I've had so far. The participation points are easy to forget about though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. If you take STAT400, he is definitely better than Albert Yu.

(Actually had STAT 400) 
He's pretty good, not exceptional but did a good job explaining the concepts and breaking down the formulas. His homework can be tough, but it's bearable. I don't enjoy how he does participation, it's open after class until noon the next day, making it easy to forget.
I actually took him for stats 400. He was very good

I have to say that Professor Unger is easily one of, if not the best math lecturers I've had. He is very articulate in class and is happy to answer any questions, and is super knowledgeable. He's easy to follow along with during lectures. I felt that the homework required some self learning, but ultimately I enjoyed this class and would take again.

Very frustrating and time consuming class with overloaded homework and quizzes. Over half the semester is done and he has not released the grades for any of the homeworks. Awful experience. If you can take this class from a different professor please do as it might be less frustrating and more organized.

Professor Unger very clearly teaches you the material. The homework was very engaging and directly applicable to what was being taught in lectures. Due to this course and his teaching have certainly further developed my skills in R and have been properly introduced to SQL.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For those who are not ready to teach themselves, do not take this course. For those who are not familiar with R, you will rarely learn anything. I do not like self-learning courses, but it is easy to get a high GPA. Thank you, Professor, so much

The professor's teaching method is more than effective. I am always amazed as to how much I have learned after taking a class with this professor. Thanks to his courses, I am able to say I am an advanced user of R and SAS.

Changed the final date by five days ahead. Announced on Monday in class that final will be on Wednesday the same week without sending an email or posting an announcement on compass. Regularly late 10 minutes for class. Often canceled classes until the last minute. Never post grades on time. Still do not know midterm grade in final week.
Unger was a great professor. If he is available, take his section for sure

I'm not sure if this was Unger's fault but the class this class was a joke; Unger basically just read off powerpoints basic SAS syntax;  most of the class finished without knowing a proc import statement. It really should be a 100 or 200 level class; take 448 instead. I would be 90% of the class got As. Its insane grad students are in this class
Very nice professor!

He is so engaging during lectures, no extra effort is needed to prepare for exams if you follow lectures carefully. Lectures are almost similar to SAS certification contents and illustrates nut& bolts of SAS programming. Except heavy home works this course is good, easy to score A.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Like him a lot, very nice, crystal-clear English, excellent analogies, describes and explains everything for any level right there in lecture. So far, just excellent.

David is a kind, emotionally stable instructor. If you see him in his office hours, he will treat you decently and go the extra mile to help you understand the material. His exams are pretty hard though while the classes/homeworks may not always prepare you for an A if that's what you want.
really nice teacher, no extra credit, no curves, very fair, good lecturer
Extremely easy class. The lectures are super slow, but I found it easier to use the recordings and put them on 2x speed. I really cant comment on how he is as a lecturer too much.

If this class wasn't CBTF based, it would be much more enjoyable; however, professor Ravaioli gives fair questions on the exams outside of a few tricks. The Prairielearn homework is OK, sometimes going overboard on what is actually necessary for the exams. This course required the least amount of time for me this semester.
Best class I've taken this semester. He is a very nice guy, and the content is very straightforward. it was easy to get an A. my GOAT

GOAT Professor in ECE. Living Icon. Cares about what he is teaching and is very accessible for questions outside of class, both on class content and beyond. Very good teacher. Wish he taught more classes I could take.
Great professor, lectures are not mandatory and mostly consist of solving example circuits. Lectures are recorded and posted online. Funny guy.

ECE 205 content is so simple, it is not worth going to lecture to hear this man give 15 minute examples and long tangents. He's funny, but that's really about it. Consider watching the videos at 2x speed or just reading the annotated slides. Better yet, just try the prairielearn answers until you somehow get it right. It got me an A+.
very enthusiastic about teaching, but teaching methods aren't efficient. a lot of extra credit offered.
Nice professor! 4% extra credits, and exams are not overly hard. Do the work, and get the reward.
Teaches us cirquits better than ECE majors

He is a nice man and clearly cares. The class is not overly hard (I am bad at circuits and did fine) but can feel like a lot at times. The lectures can feel very boring but I personally found them useful. The extra credit was amazing.

Professor Ravioli clearly wants his students to succeed and is enthusiastic about what he teaches. He gives great lectures that are recorded, but I'd recommend going to class. Quizzes are pretty similar to the homework assignments. He also offers some extra credit that's definitely worth doing. Overall a very good professor that you need to take.

Prof Ravaioli loves what he does, and it shows. He's always so enthusiastic when he's talking about circuits. All of his lectures are recorded and put online, but I recommend going in person anyways. Be warned: he puts some extra content in his slides that you won't be tested on but he is still very good at presenting the content.

He is very passionate about teaching. He knows almost everything that students brought up during class. He can talk about something for a long time, and make sure he made everything clear. If you want to do research, he is definitely a good professor to seek.
Excellent professor, and pretty funny. Don't skip class, though. You'll regret it.
Good Professor, uses slides rather than the board - 'so no need to take notes' :) Very useful class, but dont skip, and u will be fine

I took a dual credit environmental science class in high school, so this course was really easy for me since it was basically the same stuff--actually probably less in depth than my first class, but if I didn't have that environmental science knowledge it would have absolutely sucked. There would be so much you'd have to read and watch.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: do not take NRES 100. the class takes around 12 hours a week and nothing is ever graded on time. the semester is about to be over and 50% of my grade is still unknown. you also will get docked points for things that don't even make sense. overall, would not recommend anyone take this class unless it is mandatory.

My major is not related to environmental science, and I took this course to fulfill a gen ed within 8 weeks. For my purposes, this class demanded more than I expected. Considering the course was completely online, Ugarte was not very involved, though she replies to emails. The class had more lengthy assignments than I expected.

Her class format is typically a week's worth of fast video lectures (lecture slides are uploaded) with a class discussion board, a writing assignment to do, and a simple quiz. I'd have gotten a better grade had I not forgotten to do two of the quizzes, but overall this class's work is very flexible to fit into wherever you have time.

Govt and NFP Actg was a great class and helped with FAR prep for the CPA exam! Dr. Ulla was wonderful and caring and made class very enjoyable. There is a lot of material, but as long as you stay on top of it, the workload is manageable. She ensured that we all succeeded and provided many resources to help us grasp the topics. Highly recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is THE best professor I have ever had. She is super caring and genuinely makes so much effort to remember everything about you. She personally cares about the success of each student in her class. She is super accessible every time and will do anything in her power to help and support her students.

Notes were available online and you just fill out all the info during lecture. Lectures were packed with information. Tests were hard and a lot of people ran out of time. Despite course material difficulty, Prof. Ulla is incredibly nice and cares about her students. One of my favorite professors at Illinois but you need to put in the work.

Prof Uribe was nice but she is the worst at responding to emails. Do not think you will get a response from her the entire semester because chances are, you will not. Not responding to important student emails in my opinion, is extremely unprofessional.

She is a somewhat okay professor but her lectures are extremely long and hard to follow. 12pt font and smaller on all of her slides and they are very confusing. When you want further elaboration through office hours, she gives you the feeling like you are not worth her time and she is strictly business only. One of my least favorite poli sci profs

She was a good professor. When asked questions, even off topic, she would try to engage them and give good responses. I personally thought her grading methods and assignments were clear. This was my first introduction to law material and she made it really easy. She's very useful if you have questions, especially if you're asking the right ones!

McGuire is great. Ive taken her 3 semesters in a row because I learn a lot in her class and it is very manageable. She is writing me my letter of reccommendation for law school and I feel like she prepared me well. Sometimes lectures felt long, but if you read the cases ahead of time and are interested in them, I found lectures to be interesting.

Take this website with a grain of salt. People generally only write a review if they really love or hate a professor, and it's usually the latter because of how school is. 

McGuire was one of my favorite professors at the University of Illinois. It's as simple as that.

Be prepared for long and boring lectures. She reads off a slide and notes, and finds a way to make interesting topics boring. Also, you can go the entire semester without her responding to a single email (I did). Not to mention extremely unclear grading procedures, that vary significantly from grader to grader. Worst professor I have had at UIUC.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: unclear grading criteria for case briefs/seemingly had no parameters for her graders other than telling them to command+f specific terms. if you didn't word things in the case brief precisely how she wanted, likely due to a lazy grading regiment that didn't require her or her graders to actually read your work, your homework grade would suffer.

This professor is just so boring. She has mandatory attendance but everything she says during lecture is just read off slides. Going to this class feels so unnecessary and boring. This class is all about memorization and incredibly stupid assignments. I really do not reccommend taking this class unless you have to for your major.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor McGuire is very knowledgeable about the Constitution and her lectures gives a lot of good information . She is pretty understanding and will acknowledge when she makes a mistake or when grading is off for an assignment. The case breifs are not bad, although some take while. But the midterm/final paper is very long and can be intimidating.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Uribe is very sweet, but she is not a good lecturer. Very boring, and presentations are vague. Her exams are hard and worded weirdly (she did let us redo some responses for points back). Studying for the exams, good luck finding the definition unless you went to every single class and paid 100% attention. Can't even find them in the book

I had this professor for two semesters in a row and i absolutely love her class. She was so helpful during covid and modified some things to make it easier on the students. Lectures can feel a bit long and tiring but the content is very interesting. She is hard to reach on emails but a little effort in this class goes a long way

As a student participating in her online class, I have reached out to her many times for assistance and she has responded to nearly none of my emails. It's quite disappointing when you sign up for an online class (COVID-19) and you need to get in touch with your professor and they don't give you any response. Not able to ask questions as a student.

I have had class with her for two semesters in a row and a few things became clear to me. She is very hard to reach, the grading is super inconsistent, and the text book is useless. Her lectures are very dry and not very interesting, but they have a lot of good information. Research HEAVY final paper.

An absolutely awful professor who does not know how to lecture. Four relatively easy case briefs, a mediocre midterm and final, and a research heavy final paper. The grading is probably the worst part of this course, it is not uniform at all. One paper will get a 90% and the same exact paper will get an 80%. Lastly, the book is a waste.

Lectures tend to be not very engaging and generally have low attendance. Briefs for the class are easy, the midterm is reasonable, and the final paper is an immense amount of work. Criteria for briefs, and especially the final paper are unclear and do not establish concrete expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: For this class we wrote four short briefs (one page, pretty easy), and one long brief (10 pages, requires lots of work). There was a midterm and a final which were not too bad if you study. Overall not a bad course.

Professor Uribe-McGuire has amazing lectures, she really brings the issues to life whereas simply reading a book explanation of the issues can fail.  She gives the class a better understanding of The Constitution and the Supreme Court Cases that shape our current law.  Excellent professor.

I took her Separation of Powers class. I thought this class would be hard at first (especially when we went into game theory) but it wasn't as bad as I expected. Her slides are clear and concise-no extra bs. They have everything you need to know for exams. There's one group project  that was difficult, but she's a lenient grader.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof has excellent lectures. They're simple and not too flashy, but they really help for learning the materials. Super fair grader as well.

Goes way too fast during lecture. Can't understand what she is talking about. Not a good professor for someone who knows little to nothing about physics. She explains everything as if you should already know what you are doing.

She is one of the best professors I have ever had. Her experience in the field shows in her lectures and her explanations. I have taken her courses since my undergrad and glad to continue to have her in grad school. Marci is an inspiration to what I can become and who I want to be.
Very helpful, clear, and cares about her students inside and outside of class. One of my favorite instructors throughout college.
She's extremely helpful and wants everyone to do well. Be prepared to write tons of notes everyday.

Dr. Ray is an amazing professor! Be prepared to struggle on some content, but if you go to him for help he takes the time to explain concepts until you understand (he has multiple review sessions, is quick to respond to emails, and is usually available immediately following lecture). **Every other week there is a 10-12 question quiz in the CBTF*

Dr. Ray is such a nice professor. He was funny, his lectures were engaging, and his iClicker policy was very fair. What they say about his exams is true: they are hard. The first few were easy, but the last ones were brutal. That being said, Ray is very accessible outside of class and truly cares about his students. Take his class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Funny guy and teaches well. However he refuses to write out the chemical equations and instead draws them as organic molecules, which would be fine if he did not have the worst handwriting in the world. The tests are hard and nothing like the practice he gives. He also has a "kitchen sink" problem which he brags about being extremely difficult.

GOAT professor who cares a ton about his students and does his best to make sure they succeed. After the Canvas incident that just occurred, he sent an email letting finals be optional. His midterms were not bad if you studied hard, and each had an option for a retake. Attendance is not required after "x" iclicker points. Among the greats of UIUC.
Dr. Ray is the only reason CHEM 104 was tolerable. Great lecturer and really cares about students!

I loved this class with Ray. You could clearly tell he cares so much about each student's success. Ray was very approachable and personable with his students and he understands what its like to be a student in his class. Very little homework in general and the tests were very easy. I would defiantly recommend Ray if you plan on taking Orgo.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had throughout my entire education. He explains difficult concepts in a way that actually makes sense. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students' success and puts a lot of effort into making lectures engaging. I learned a lot from this course and would highly recommend taking 104 with Ray.

Genuinely one of the best professors I've had throughout my entire education. He explains difficult concepts in a way that actually makes sense. You can tell he genuinely cares about their students' success and puts a lot of effort into making lectures engaging. I learned a lot from this course and would highly recommend having Ray.

Genuinely the best professor I've had so far. Professor Ray cares deeply about the students and this class. Tests arent too bad if you study hard, and retakes make up for it a ton. After getting traumatized in gen chem 1, gen chem 2 felt challenging, but no longer chaotic. I feel absolutely prepared for orgo.

I took the online version of this class and Ray's online lectures were alright. A little vague sometimes so I had to use other sources to understand the material. Quizzes were graded brutally via CBTF. However, his curves at the end of the semester were amazing, which is the main reason why I give him a high rating.

Sweetest Professor I've ever had, you can tell he really cares about people succeeding. Unfortunately, Chem 104 is just an extremely difficult class if you're not pre-med or stem-heavy in the major department. I've studied for weeks, got failing grades.

Very good teacher, actually cares about his students. Really nice when getting to know him outside of class. Homework and prelecture assignments are pretty easy, but quizzes have hard questions, so studying really matters. Overall, really recommend and would take again! Offers retakes on quizzes too :)

He makes learning CHEM 104 simple and straight forward. He's also genuinely a very nice guy, especially if you see him in office hours. I would recommend getting to know him. His homework is very light but the quizzes are pretty tuff. They can take multiple steps but if you understand the material you should be able to get an A.

His quizzes were difficult and you really had to interested in the material to keep up. Our quiz averages were consistently around 60 and is what he expects. He does give the class a bit of a curve tho. Not a bad teacher, he was really nice, just a difficult class.

Excellent professor, this course has biweekly quizzes that can be retaken the following week for an average of the scores taken. Don't skip office hours, be sure to do the practice quizzes, and memorizing specific problems won't get you very far here, you need to understand content. The discussion worksheets reflect the final more than the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ray is great. Super nice and helpful. I'd say that the online 104 class is more difficult than taking it in person, as it's easy to get behind on the lecture videos. The 6 quizzes at the CBTF are difficult, but he curves the class nicely. Final exam was a lot easier than the quizzes.

Good guy. Definitely seemed to care about his students and was funny. Tests were kinda hard and always would put questions that majority of class would get wrong. But, they were doable. Just wish the class wasn't so heavily weighted on tests.

I loved Professor Ray, he always approaches students with kindness rather than judgment. He doesn't make students feel stupid for asking a silly question. Grading criteria are clear, discussion wrksheets are completion points. Workload can be pretty heavy as you have a pre and post-lecture every class period. Quizzes have review questions everytime
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, really cares about his students and being a good educator. I like that he provides supplementary videos to the lectures. On some quizzes the questions can be a bit hard to understand but that might just be on me.

Great lecture and teacher, the tests were unreasonably hard in my opinion, lowkey fried me every other week when I knew the material but make some stupid mistake to get zero points in the CBTF. Still cool professor and enjoyable class, class is mandatory and requires physical iclicker.
Dr. Ray is such an amazing person and teacher, his class is just HARD, I can't even rate him poorly because it has nothing to do with him, the course he teaches is just inherently hard.
I will admit professor Ray is really friendly and gives off major dad energy but I think sometimes he does that to throw us off on how hard his quizzes are because they never reflect his kindness
Ray Ray slays the house down. At times, bit of a diva—but a chem to it. He knows his stuff. I'd say he's funny similar to Trisha Paytas and Anna Stawowski !!
holy goated

CHEM 104 is tough, but Ray is a great lecturer. He provides a lot of useful resources, and is generally excellent at clarifying concepts (although this varies on the content). Pay attention, use practice materials, genuinely try, and you should be fine. What made CHEM 104 difficult for me was the amount of tests, not Professor Ray.

Honestly this class is not that bad. I really like the quizes every two weeks as it forces you to stay on top of the material. The most helpful thing for this class to to find past tests and practice tests and study from those. He pre-lecture videos are also really helpful so don't really need to go to lecture. Also good teacher.

Ray is the best professor I have had at UIUC. He is such a kind guy that really cares about his students and their success. The course itself is pretty hard, but he is such a great lecturer and makes the content actually understandable and doable. 6 quizzes instead of 3 exams, which is great for this type of course. I strongly recommend his class!

Dr. Ray has been one of the best professors I've had. He is not only excellent at explaining complex material clearly, but also brings humor into his lectures, making them enjoyable. It's clear that he genuinely cares about his students' success. While the quizzes are challenging, if you put in the effort, you will do well.

Dr. Ray is the coolest dude you'll meet in the chem department. If you need help, find him before or after lecture and he'll be more than happy to explain. His lectures make sense and are closely related to the coursework, so show up! His tests are difficult, but study well and consult people who took the course before and you should do fine.

Ray is amazing. He is one of the kindest professors you'll have and genuinely enjoys his job. The class is hard but he does a great job teaching the material and posts videos so you can look back on lessons. If you are struggling go talk to him!!!!! He gives great study tips and is super helpful in office hours.

Oh my god dr ray is everything you could ever want or need in a friend, human, or teacher. I wish he taught every single class i needed. He is funny, personable, caring, humble, and very reasonable. Discussions were actually helpful and there were 6 quizzes with lots of practice and retakes available instead big, anxiety inducing tests. LOVE him

I just love this professor, the goat for teaching concepts especially the ones i won't forget for a long time, the lectures are really fun especially for an intro class ! the quizzes are doable until you practise a lot
Not gonna lie, this class is hard. I struggled because there are just so many quizzes that we get no break. It makes the semester go very fast.
The class is difficult, but Dr. Ray is a very good lecturer and such a caring person. His explanations are clear, and he is very accessible outside of class.

Literally had to write a review at 4 pm on a Tuesday simply because I love Dr. Ray. He makes life so much better because chem is hard but he makes it digestible. Super caring, super fun. Great lectures. Respectable man. Love him. God bless Dr. Ray. Thank you Dr Ray!!!!!
He is overall such a great person! He is a great professor and you will learn a lot from taking his class.

Dr Ray was an amazing professor. He knows how to teach the material and make concepts easier. Be aware that the quizzes are hard, and more often than not you'll find yourself running out of time to complete it to its entirety. The final is fair, but you do have to dedicate quite a few hours to studying. The curve at the end really saves you.
Professor Ray is very clear when going over lecture material.

Great person, cares about students. The course content is tough, but not his fault. The only issue is that he's not a very organized person, so that makes navigating the Canvas difficult. Have study buddies for this class and read about the topics online. The homework is helpful but overwhelming.

Ray makes a 300-person lecture feel cozy. He's caring, funny, and explains concepts clearly. The tests are tough, but quizzes are doable if you study hard. unstuck study was a lifesaver for extra practice.

Dr. Ray is extremely helpful and invested in students' success. If you pay attention in lecture, practice, and attend his review sessions, you can do well. The material is pretty difficult, and the grade breakdown weights quizzes heavily, but Ray's explanations are clear and he provides plenty of resources. Time-consuming class.

PROS: final is hard but its impact is forgiving, RETAKES, good teacher and has study sessions every week, provides extra practice sheets that prepare you well for tests, passable class if you study and take advantage of retakes
CONS: lecture notes can be hard to follow, grading is very test heavy, your TA matters
I struggled a lot in this class, but Dr. Ray was very gracious and helpful every week. goat

Dr Ray was caring and funny. He explained concepts well and gave plenty of resources to practice. He clearly knows what works for students and has good availability. I enjoyed the many demos that were performed during lecture as well. Tests are worth 82% of the class with little extra credit, but the quizzes were not hard if you studied well.

Dr Ray was caring and funny. He explained concepts well and gave plenty of resources to practice. He clearly knows what works for students and has good availability. I enjoyed the many demos that were performed during lecture as well. Tests are worth 82% of the class with little extra credit, but the quizzes were not hard if you studied well.
Manages to make a 300 person lecture feel like a high school classroom. Chill and funny guy!

I really enjoyed this class. I felt like lectures were easy to follow and the fact that they are available online is a huge weight off of your shoulders because if you miss lecture or don't understand you can go back and rewatch it. Dr. Ray is really nice and cares deeply for his students. One of the best professors I have ever had.

Overall, I really appreciated all the help that Ray gave me. I started off the class really confused, and close to having to drop the course. But, go to his office hours, and really put in the time meeting with him one-on-one, he really helps in giving advice on how and what to study if you need. There was a lot of work, but it was all helpful.

Class was hard as hell, every quiz made me lose a part of my soul, but Ray restored my hope for the next 2 weeks before I had to take another. Lectures were well organized and overall helpful and Ray is good at explaining and offering additional explanations outside of class. Overall, a win in my book.

A fantastic professor who is kind, caring, and is amazing at lecturing. Offers a ton of resources to help students with chemistry. His quizzes are a bit difficult, but the retakes/worksheets are helpful.

Dr. Ray does a pretty good job at teaching the content, as well as making good analogies to help us visualize what something is. There was homework due before every lecture. His quizzes were pretty hard, but manageable. Most of the course was based off of the quizzes and the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As a professor, Dr. Ray is very good at teaching the content! He engages with students well and is available to help outside of lectures. Although he is a good teacher, the quizzes are harder than the practice, the final is worth 30%, and there is a lot of homework. I learned a lot from him, but I definitely struggled in this class.
The class he teaches is quite difficult if chemistry is not your strong suit, but he is very accessible during office hours and over emails and wants all of his students to succeed.
Great teacher who really cares about his students. Explains difficult concepts in an easy to understand manner. Would definitely recommend for CHEM 104.

After taking Dr. G's class in CHEM 102, I found it hard to continue my existence on the planet Earth. But Dr. Ray single-handedly restored my will to exist. His lectures are very organized and understandable after watching the pre-lecture. His quizzes are a bit hard but with the LON CAPA practice problems, you will be well prepared.

After 102 I was terrified, but Ray is seriously one of the best professors I have ever had. Lectures are recorded if you miss one you can watch them on your own time. He gives you a lot of resources to prepare for quizzes. Do the practice quiz problems and the discussion worksheet over and over and you'll be fine. Also go to office hours!!

assessments aren't easy but if you understand lectures & homework well enough to explain it to someone else rather than just memorizing the steps then you should be good for the quizzes. He has very thorough & efficient pre-lectures and posts all of his lectures online. He's also available to answer any questions and gives almost identical retakes.

Clear, helpful explanations are given during lecture, and can also be found in concise online videos. The expectation for what you need to know is clear and straight forward. While he likes to include what he calls "kitchen sink" questions, the quizzes are reasonable and resemble the practice content.

Dr. Ray is a great professor who truly cares about his students. The quizzes are quite hard however and are not very representative of the practice material that he hands out. The nice thing is that he offers a retake and allows you to see your old exam so you can review what you got wrong and ensure you ace the retake, he then averages both scores

This class is very quiz-heavy and rigorous. Topics were challenging and sometimes, the quiz questions did not reflect the material being taught in class. Dr. Ray cares for his students and is available outside of class, but sometimes lessons were crammed and not all materials were covered during the course of a lecture.

His tests/quizzes were extremely hard. I am a good test taker, but the CBTF sucks. His practice problems were always way easier than the quiz. Lectures are a mess and its hard to take notes. He does have good prelectures that you have to take notes on. Lots of HW but it is a chem class so that's expected. Andino is the better choice IMO

This class was stressful especially with the quizzes being every other week, and the I hate the grading that the CBTF does because one small mistake drops the grade so much. Ray seems pretty nice and has good relationships with the students, but it was hard to understand concepts from lectures, and the quizzes were so much harder than the practice.

Don't get me wrong, Ray is a great guy, but his class is hardddd. Chem104 was a requirement for me so I had to take it and the biweekly quizzes killed me. His lectures are informative but I still struggled with the content. Beware this class is really difficult with Ray. If you reach out, though, he will be glad to help.

Christian Ray is a well-respected figure in the community. He is a strong lecturer, with a ton of experience under his belt. Yes - his exams are fairly difficult, but many of us persevered, and can actually say we learned a ton once all was said and done. He was recently recognized for his excellence in teaching with a huge award. Go for him.

Solid professor, but if this is your last chem class/ the topics don't actually matter for you, go with the other section for an easier time. I think everyone who said that you can just do practice problems had access to past PL quizzes lol. Get a good TA or ask friends for their TA's resources since they know the problems to focus on :P

One of the best chem teachers here. Chemistry is a hard subject, but he's a really good teacher and explains things in detail. If you have questions, he will answer with really good explanations. He provides practice quizzes and his office hours are very helpful. If you put in the work, you will be rewarded.

This class is hard for someone who doesn't love chemistry. I am an animal science major, so I just need to get chem out of the way.  Prof. Ray has weekly review sessions and reasonable windows for office hours. even though I ended up with a C, I actually learned a ton.
You can tell Dr. Ray cares about teaching. Though the class is difficult, he is always available and wants to see students succeed. I wish he taught more classes!

Dr. Ray was an amazing professor. He is so good at explaining things and he genuinely cares about everyone. If you are struggling in his class you can always find help. If you put in the effort in the class you can pass!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Most grading  quiz-based, but you will never run out of practice problems and quiz prblms are 99% of time from these practice problems. Retakes avail (takes avg so may hurt) Lectures were fine; type to be personable. Check out TA Jessica Xhumari's youtube for review. If you have a chance, take her section! (super helpful & review sessions galore)

Ray is a pretty easygoing professor who is also happy to talk with students outside of class. His lectures were decent; although I have seen better lectures before, he generally did a good job of helping me understand the material. He also gives retakes for the two midterms and partial credit on multiple choice questions.

A lot of people like to give Dr. Ray more credit than he deserves because he is a really nice guy. However, as a teacher, he is not good at teaching the material. He spends way too much time talking to his students about his personal life and not enough on actual explanations of the material. He is also hardly available outside of class to help out

Not sure how Ray gets such high ratings especially after this semester. Expect everything you learn in lecture and in the practice quizzes to be NOTHING like the actual quizzes. Almost everything we learn in class has no reflection on his quizzes. Also 82% of your grade in this class is made up of quizzes and the final exam. Ruined my gpa

The lectures are very basic compared to the rigor of what is on the exams. The exam and quiz questions have many curveballs and the grading is very harsh. I think the average on the quizzes is usually in the 40s and on the exams is usually in the 60s.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures on thermodynamics were difficult to understand and didn't do a good job of teaching the more abstract and conceptual stuff that a lot of students struggle with. Quizzes only have 3 questions and sometimes the questions are almost impossible to get right on the first try. Class is basically just meant to wreck premeds GPA.

Prof Ray isn't a bad professor, just not fantastic. Definitely cares about his students, but lectures are very basic-level and just showing up in lecture is definitely not enough to do well. Test questions are difficult but doable w/practice. I would recommend taking notes on the optional Openstax readings + doing all the practice problems offered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ray is a nice person. However, he has some policies that I found unfair. The class is 82% exam; he doesn't curve/give extra credit, but gives retakes which is helpful. Also, he's a good lecture (not bad/not great). The class is hard, threw curveballs. He is better than the avg chem professor at UIUC. I recommend lots of practice!

Dr. Ray is the best 104 Professor. He uses analogies to teach, personal anecdotes etc.. which makes understanding chemistry much more manageable. His office hours are also very helpful. Jessica Xhumari is the best TA who does 6 hour review sessions before the final, and she is probably as good of an instructor. Ray + Jess are your key to success
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Dr. G last semester for CHEM 1o2 so Dr. Ray was an amazing 180 turn. You can tell that he enjoys teaching because his lectures are very engaging, and he is great at explaining complicated concepts. The biweekly quizzes can be challenging, but he gives plenty of practice problems and materials. I recommend taking the merit section CHEM 199.

Dr. Ray is amazing. Easily the best professor Ive had at this school. He makes CHEM 104 feel like such a relief after taking 102. As long as you truly understand the content from his lectures (pre/post) and do the practice quizzes, this class should be an easy A. The retakes are also very helpful so make sure you always get them done.

he's great at explaining things and is easy going. he understands that we have lives outside of schoolwork. his quizzes can be tricky, so definitely study his provided practice questions. there isn't a textbook, he teaches you what he wants you to know. overall great guy and professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Amazing lectures--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: amazing

Dr. Ray was a decent instructor but I was very disappointed in him towards the end of the course. He promised an overall class curve, fell through and refused to round grades that were .5 or higher from the next letter grade. Thats just unnecessary considering were in a global pandemic and he did nothing to account for this when grading.

DO NOT listen to the person below me, there were no specific instructions for the extra credit and talked about a curve the whole semester just for him to disregard it. Great teacher for the most part especially when semester progresses. He just did not follow through with his promises and around 30% of the class have to retake this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ray is genuinely my favorite professor! He made chemistry so easy to learn because he would give you pre-lecture, post-lecture, and even host Zoom lectures. If you want to succeed, take advantage of them! Yes, he did offer extra credit but our class didn't follow the instructions, so it's fair that he didn't give any. I completely understand him!

This is a challenging class and requires hours of studying. I strongly recommend taking a merit discussion section while taking this class because having a great TA will make a huge difference. Dr. Ray offers retakes for each quiz, and also holds review sessions every Friday to help with digesting difficult material.

Although I can see why many of my peers were upset about our final grade situation, I genuinely really liked and respected Dr. Ray. I think he is a great professor and made chemistry as a subject much easier for me to understand. I did much better in this chem class than I have in any other, so I am grateful to him for getting me through it.

I think I would've been better off I take his class in person, I don't feel that online was his thing. I myself went through a lot of personal issues with family members passing away and I just feel that sometimes he was dismissive towards the concerns/issues of students. Great guy, but I just don't really know how I feel about him online.

THE BEST professor Ive had at UIUC. He really shows a passion for chemistry and wants his students to succeed. He isnt out to fail you, if you work hard and show it you get the grade you deserve. Wish there was a Dr. Ray in all of my classes

Ray was great/fair the majority of the semester. That being said, I lost a bit of respect at the end. I ruined my mental health studying hours each week, getting above average on every quiz. While a B+ is a fine grade, he had promised us a class curve if any of our quizzes were deemed unfair (we had a 55% average on one). He did not follow through
Great professor!

Dr. Ray has been one of the best chemistry professors Ive had. I know some of my peers are upset that there wasnt a curve overall in the class but he did curve some of our individual quiz scores. He was always available to help us, got to know a lot of us on a personal level during the pandemic and empathized with us. Overall, a wonderful prof.
