Instead of exams there is a quiz every other week. The quizzes are difficult and are worth many points so you will still end up studying a lot of material and spending a lot of time every 2 weeks. Would not recommend taking this class with other difficult classes because I had to sacrifice a lot of time for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had so much respect for Dr. Ray before the final. He is a great person. However, this class specifically has ruined my mental health. He promised a curve to the class but did not follow through. This class makes me rethink my choice of attending the University of Illinois.

For the majority of the semester, Ray was a great teacher, very understanding and fair. Unfortunately, he ruined that in the end. After promising a *class* curve all semester, he only selectively gave one out. Although C's and above are in a better position, it is not fair to be that successful w a C-A during a pandemic & not get the same reward.

Was not accommodating at all during a pandemic, he has curved the class in past semesters but would not do so even this semester even though he knows majority of us were struggling and would not round up even if we were so so close to the grade we needed.

Knowing that we are in a pandemic, he still refused to give us the extra credit points that many of us needed to raise our grade. Aside from that, many of us had internet problems yet he was not very accommodating and said it was out of his control. Many of my classmates agree that this class ruined their GPA and could possibly ruin medical school.

This professor is not accommodating especially not during a global pandemic. He wants students to fail so he can keep a bell distribution of grades. Dont take this class. Not sure how others gave him 5 stars ...

Dr. Ray is a great professor who does an excellent job explaining concepts in an easy to understand manner. He is very patient with people who ask questions and takes the class at a very reasonable pace. His test questions are very fair and as long as you keep up with learning materials, you should do just fine,

Best professor I have had thus far. He has a lot of quizzes, but he is very clear about what he expects you to know and will give you plenty of materials to prep with. He is a genuinely great person and cares about his students a lot. If you have him you're set!

Ray is awesome! He really cares about his students and going to office hours is EXTREMELY helpful. The practice quiz questions are basically the real quizzes which is great. Definitely use the practice materials given on lon capa. There are 6 quizzes which makes it easier to stay on top of materials. Lectures are really engaging and fun:)

Dr. Ray is one of the best professors I've had so far. His lectures are engaging and fun and he's really good at explaining difficult topics. He genuinely cares about his students and makes sure to gauge understanding on difficult topics. Overall, amazing.

Professor Ray is a perfect example of what all professors should aspire to be. He actually cares about his students, and is so incredibly talented at taking a lot of difficult material and condensing it into easily understandable chunks. He is fair, he is cool, by far the best professor I've ever had. Do anything you can to get a seat in his class!

Dr. Ray is such a great chem teacher. He made me not hate chemistry for once in my life and actually made me curious about it instead of dreading it. He GENUINELY cares about his students and works with you. One of the best professors I've had at UIUC.
Ray is an angel sent from above. He was born to be a chem professor. He made me not absolutely hate chemistry. Do whatever you have to do to get into his section.
Very kind and understanding. Biweekly exams are exhausting and the practice problems arent reflective of the actual exam
His lectures were enjoyable because he didn't just speak nonstop about chemistry for 50 minutes like a textbook. He included life stories and demonstrations that made concepts much clearer.

Ray was great at taking difficult or abstract ideas and making them manageable, and not seem so daunting. I would strongly advise going over the prelecture content he provides online, it only takes a few minutes, and it really helped me.

Ray is probably the best general chemistry professor on campus. His lectures are crystal clear, and the quizzes are very similar to the practice quizzes he gives. He will give a generous curve to the class if needed, but as long as you pay attention to the lectures and review all the practice quizzes, you will do great in his class.

LITERALLY THE MOST AMAZING PROFESSOR EVER!!!!!! I was able to pay attention in every single lecture - he has such a great teaching style. Made me love chemistry!!!!! Also such a nice guy in general. He makes it so easy to follow what is going on in class.

He genuinly cares for all his students and makes an effort to make sure everyone understands the material. His lectures were extremely enjoyable and not boring. Lastly, His teaching style is amazing. I love this man for sure!
one of the best professors I've ever had

The lectures were always very interesting, and he very clearly taught the material needed for the exams. He gives you everything you need to be successful in the class, and he sometimes brings his kids to lecture.

He is a great lecturer. His tests are more straight forward then CHEM102. Don't need to go to class even though there are clickers because he posts video which are easier to understand on LonCapa. Ray also is good at explaining and answers all your questions thoroughly. Great teacher

Dr. Ray is the best chemistry professor I have ever had. He genuinely cares about his students which was evident on the first day when he made an announcement about caring about student mental health. He is vey busy but usually is available outside of class and puts in a lot of effort to help you succeed.

Dr. Ray is the most amazing professor that I have ever had. His lectures are easy to understand because he takes scary topics and breaks them down. Take good notes and do all the practice exams. Make sure you ask if you do not understand something! Dont let questions build up. Hes always available before and after class. Great prof and class!

Ray was a gem -- if you have the opportunity to take him, I HIGHLY recommend you do so. This is not to say that his exams were easy (they were rather tricky), but he was FAIR throughout the entire semester. As long as you participate in lecture, take good notes, DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS, and just spare some time throughout the week, you will be gold.

Dr. Ray is one of the BEST professors one could ever have! Do not defer the opportunity to have him as a professor. His exam questions are slightly convoluted and tie multiple things together, but as long as you understand the concepts, it's not all that bad- he does not try to trick you on exams! He will go out of his way to help you succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly the best professor I've has at this University so far. I found him extremely funny and was very knowledgeable about the subject. Exams need a pretty big time commitment to do well, homework is relatively easy. Put in the time and this class is very doable.

Makes you work extremely hard to keep your grade up in the class, seems to be easy to pass, but with what grade you want is to be determined how hard you work and understand the material. Tests sometimes don't exactly reflect the material taught in my opinion. Overall, would not say this is an easy A, but an easy pass is definitely a possibility.

Dr. Ray is the best professor I have ever had. His lectures are easy to understand and he does not speak too fast. His office hours are wonderful and he will remember you by name. The project isn't bad as long as you get a group of people that actually do work.

Dr. Ray is a good professor but his exams are pretty difficult. Don't think you can pull your grade up with them for the most part. Do all the little homework assignments and get them all right and you will have some padding for the exams. He has a group project for some lectures that sucks so make sure to start early on it.
You need to go to lecture, and he can be intimidating at office hours, but he's a nice guy.

Professor Ray is an amazing teacher. His gives a lot of resources to help prepare for tests and his tests are similar to those materials. He doesn't curve, but he does give every student a chance to "earn a curve" by doing an online retake with multiple tries. These helped my grade a significant amount!

Dr. Ray is extremely knowledgeable, and always seems to love to come to class. He makes lectures interesting, and is always there to help you if you need ANYTHING. I wish I could take every chemistry class with him as my teacher - he is awesome!
I thought he was amazing!  Really great at coming to lecture early and had good office hours at the CLC.
Gives you everything you need to do well on exams but they can be a bit tough. easily one of the best professors i've had so far on campus

As much as Ray was a very nice professor, he was extremely difficult. He was a good lecturer & I performed well on homework and quizzes, but majority of the class grade is from exams. He states at the beginning of the semester that he challenges you on the exam with questions you haven't seen before. Easy to perform poorly on them & kill your grade
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is my favorite professor to date. Given that I am just a freshman, take that with a grain of salt, but I have previously taken Chem 104 in high school and retook it for a grade boost, and the way he teaches the concepts is very similar to my high school teacher. He really walks through exactly how to do problems and makes lecture fun.

The only redeeming quality of this class was the online lecture videos. He talks constantly about his own life, and never replies to emails. He is late in posting on Ion Capa and his grading system is very test heavy. He is a nice guy but really shouldn't be a teacher. Puts little time into the class.

He's a good lecturer but that's about it. Takes weeks to reply to emails. Is always late up loading exam material therefore, giving students very little time to study. The answer keys were littered with mistakes. You will end up knowing more about his personal life rather than chemistry. Would not recommend.

I thought Ray was an exceptional teacher because he actually made the expectations of the class clear, so you knew exactly what to study. He gives you all the resources you need to succeed. If you're willing to put in the work then you should do great!

So long as you're willing to put in the work and keep up with lectures, you should do fairly well in this course. Ray explains the material thoroughly and provides additional resources, such as his pre- and post-lecture videos. Definitely the best choice when it comes to Chem104. Never have I enjoyed chemistry this much prior to taking the class.
Good professor overall. Project was fun, and we learned a lot from it. Lectures were clear and he is very approachable. Will try and work his hardest to ensure your success

I had high expectations for Ray, but was kind of disappointed. He had lots of office hours, but they weren't as helpful as I'd hoped. He's an ok teacher, but there were many areas where we were left to fill in the gaps/find the unwritten rules. For as hard as the tests were, he needed to have been more thorough in his teaching and homework problems

Dr. Ray is such an amazing teacher. I didn't like chemistry very much going into the class, but my opinion has entirely changed. He explains very well and there are a ton of ways he presents the material. You have to put in work to do well, but the material is so well presented that it's not hard to keep up. I couldn't recommend anyone more.

Took 104C which has a group project which was interesting but rushed. Ray wasa great teacher and did his best to get everyone to understand material. Glad I took this section. Never used the textbook but it was free!

Up until I took this class, I hated chemistry. I used to do terrible in even the easiest high school chemistry class but this course has completely changed that. The professor is super friendly and turn chemistry into something you can enjoy. He holds office hours by himself and clearly understands what each student is having difficulty with.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Extremely personable, brilliant, and knows what he's doing when it comes to teaching. Lectures are enjoyable. The material is hard, but he explains it clearly and thoroughly. Also extremely helpful at office hours. For CHEM 104, take advantage of the optional problems that are available online.

He is one of the best professor I had during my time at UIUC. Yes, his class is hard, but it's chemistry at U of I so that is expected. He lectures clearly, and is also clear about what is expected of you. If you go in to office hours, he is the most helpful and genuine professor you could have. I would recommend him as a professor any time!

Amiable character, but absolutely disastrous as an instructor. He overstates this fantastical concept of "critical thinking", which turn out to be quixotic when exams are expected to be completed in blitz speed this giving little room for "thinking time". Quite ironic indeed as he expects one thing, and does not provide the resources to meet them.

Professor Ray was a great lecturer. He reinforced the material presented in the pre-lectures and his tests and homework was right in line with what he was teaching. He's been the best professor I've had at the U of I. I would definitely make you schedule work around having him as a teacher.

I took him after having a semester with Overcash who was pretty awful. Ray's a great teacher and really cares about his students doing well. He also offers retakes and all the tests. Keep up with the material and you should do fine. He also posts pre and post lecture videos online which are very helpful. Best teacher for 104

I took this class when he taught chem 204, but the material is pretty much the same as 104. He is the best option for 104. Tests are hard, and he claims he doesn't curve, but he does. He offers retakes as well. Just keep up with all of his material. An A shouldn't be hard to obtain at all.
Enjoyable to go to class.
He's one of those professors where you learn more about him than the actual course.
Ray is the best teacher that you can get for Chem 104. Work your schedule around his availability. He makes things clear and exam resemble what is gone over in class.

He is the best, he teaches in the most simplest terms, however his tests really test the concepts that are learned in class. SO YOU BETTER KNOW YOUR STUFF. Watch the online videos because they really help, do all your homework assignments. Also he makes class really FUN!

After a terrible semester in CHEM 102 with Jamieson, I didn't think I could look at chemistry ever again. But Ray actually made me have an interest in chemistry. He is literally the best chem professor I've ever had!I wish he could teach all of my chem classes. If you have a choice, PICK RAY!
Took his chemistry class my freshman year. He is a great professor

He was a good teacher and the class was pretty easy with him. He was new to the class and his tests are pretty simple. You just want to make sure you go to his review sessions because they help especially before the exam
Best Professor I have ever had.
He is a fantastic professor! Just amazing! He really cares about the students learning. His   tests are difficult but really put in perspective what the material is about. Take him!

Dr. Ray is probably the best professor I have had at U of I. He really loves teaching and cares about students. He is always willing to help. Also, the class isn't that hard. The online quizzes were the hardest part, but he lets you work in groups. Overall, he's a great professor.

Favorite class I've taken in college.  Dr. Ray is a great professor and is super helpful during office hours.  Go to office hours the day or two before exams and ask how to do the practice test Q's and you're golden for exams.

He's not that bad. He's really nice, cares about making his students learn, and is really helpful. You don't need to go to class, because he posts lecture videos online that get straight to the point and are exactly the same(rather than sitting in a 50min class)He even curved our class at the end!

One of the best professors I've had. You can tell he has enthusiasm for the subject. Real nice guy and his exams are fair. If you make sure to understand the homework you should be getting an A, the material isn't that hard. The only thing I found annoying was that sometimes the review sheet for the exam wouldn't be posted until two days prior...

He offers multiple ways for you to learn the course. Online lectures were very efficient and well done. Of course, like many chem courses at UIUC, material is not homogeneous, so expect much harder exams than homework and quizzes. And for Fall 2012, half the class is --not-- failing, more like 10-ish% after curve.

Dr. Ray probably the best teacher I've had at U of I.  If you ever struggle with a concept, go to his office hours. The class is not hard if you put the time into study and do the suggested practice problems. He writes hard tests  but offers online retakes that can get you point back for the original test. This man was meant to teach chemistry.

Chemistry is something I really struggle with, and the only reason I'm doing so well is because Dr. Ray is a fantastic teacher. It is a difficult class, but he's absolutely wonderful. He tries to put everything at students' fingertips so that they can do as well as possible. He really cares about his students.

He's really nice but a terrible teacher. He doesn't explain things very well and expects you to learn most of the material on your own. His online lecture videos are sort of helpful but he doesn't go into much detail.

Professor Ray was one of the best professors I've had so far at the University. He's passionate about teaching and is extremely helpful when it comes to helping students understand the material. He makes pre/post lecture videos which really help. Practice problems; that's the key!

I hate Chemistry. Dr. Ray is incredibly nice. Never met a teacher who cares so much about his students. He wants you to understand more than anything. Everyone warned that he was hard but honestly I thought his exams were very fair if you actually study and do practice problems. Extremely helpful during office hours. I wish he taught Orgo.

If you go to his office hours he really makes an effort to get to know you and find a way to help you out that works for you.  He tailors his explanations to your learning style.  With all this, he is a difficult professor and his midterms are challenging, but doable.  Much better than Hummel.
His office hours should really be used. He is extremely helpful when people just ask. He also has lecture videos that are greta for studying and catching up if you miss class.

Really wonderful. Loves to tell stories but also teaches in a nice manner. Numerous examples and an abundance of practice material. Exams are exactly what he warns you they will be. Overall, awesome class. Dr. Ray loves his job and it is apparent through his teaching.

Dr. Ray is awesome. He definitely loves his jobs and is interested in what he teaches. He is always willing to help and does not want his students to fail. His exams are a bit rough but he gives great practice problems and practice exams. Just go to class and take notes.

Nicest guy I've met yet. Feels bad when we are confused or don't understand. Loves to teach. He'll help you with any problem you might have. Exams are fine if you study decently. Uses a peculiar system to get points back once you've taken them. His video lectures online are gold. Answers questions during lecture. He is such a good person.

Great Professor! He helps you if you have ANY questions, and his pre/post lecture videos are AWESOME! This class is totally doable if you put the effort in! Watch the videos, attend lectures, and do the practice exams, and you will do just fine! :) Dr. Ray is by far the best professor I've had thus far!

fantastic teacher. Very good at explaining hard concepts and answering student questions. Easy to approach and relates well with students. You really want to have Dr. Ray if you plan on taking Orgo, his class lays a wonderful fondation for CHEM 232.
he is literally the best. i love going to lecture because he's funny and clear and very willing to help. tests are hard, but you get a chance to make up some points for each test

Couldn't have asked for a better professor. He asks a lot of you in his exams, but what he gives you is outstanding. He has pre-lecture videos (5 min. long) so you're prepared for lecture, post-lecture videos in case something isn't clear, and any question you ask him will get answered. Don't take anyone but Ray for CHEM 104.

The guy was great for the first month.  Then he had a baby and everything went downhill.  I was in the online section and he was supposed to post videos lectures every week.  Ended up being three weeks behind schedule.  I had to learn the entire three weeks and the current week of material for an exam within 4 days.  I'm an A student, he burned me.

Good lecturer! Very clear, and explains most things well. I worked pretty hard but did not dedicate as much time as I could have to the class - don't make that mistake! On a regular basis you should watch the pre-lecture videos, go to lecture, then review the lecture. For exams, review notes and take the practice tests.
Great professor! Always open to answering your questions. Exams can be a little bit challenging but if you go to your discussion or his Friday tutoring sessions you should be just fine.

Really great teacher. He goes out of his way to make sure you understand, but the catch is, YOU have to ask him. Never had a question go unanswered. Online lectures are exactly what is covered in class so it is very good review material. If you study and actually ask him to explain stuff to you, he will. Great class, hope to have him in future.

Dr. Ray really wants his students to learn and tries to help as much as possible.  He also personalizes the class which is cool.  The material is hard (especially orgo) but go to class and study a lot.

Watch pre-lecture videos before lectures, read the book for what is unclear, go to class knowing what is discussed that day, participate during it, DO NOT BE AFRAID of asking questions, watch the post-lecture videos, go to his Friday tutoring, go to office hours if you must, and you'll be golden. Made me love chemistry and pursue biochem.

He talks a lot, but he's adorable, easy going, funny in a dorky way, DILF. :D He writes difficult exams, but he is an AWESOME teacher, and he puts the lectures online, which are really convenient and concise.
The best professor I've ever had. He actually cares. Office hours help a ton.

good lecturer. very clear, and explains everything well. Got an A+ in the class, didn't work exorbitantly hard. Watch the prelecture video, go to lecture, then review lecture. Then just review notes for the exams, and take the practice tests. Tests are not that hard provided you are not an idiot. most of the test problems are exactly like homework
great professor. his lecture video and notes help a lot. glad to help his students. exam is kinda difficult however if u have done the previous exam u should be fine

A bit pretentious and annoying. Course material and test material didn't always match up. Felt unprepared for tests, had to show up for class but ironically didn't learn too much from them that would actually benefit me on the test.

Great teacher. ALWAYS open to answer questions. His lecture videos are very helpful, and he holds review sessions every week. It's a tough class, exams are difficult.  If you put in the work and take advantage of all the practice problems, review sessions, and lecture videos you should be fine.

If you don't like chemistry, this class is tough. Class attendance and discussions are helpful, but not always good enough. I studied for every test and could only achieve a C or D. Quizzes were somewhat difficult. Do the practice problems from the book. Doing  minimum work will not get you a B. Tests resembled the practice ones and were fair.

Hes a cool professor to talk to, but hes really not a good teacher.  I found his exams to be unreasonably hard despite studying.  Hes a fairly nice guy, but I would definately recommend Yerkes or Shapely...He expects you to go out and learn alot of stuff on your own.  I felt like I put in alot of time into the class but was not happy with my grade.

Ray is definitely a cool guy who is excited about teaching and relates well with his students.  Nevertheless, his exams were very difficult.  And since they are multiple choice, it is really easy to lose points fast.  I would for sure recommend Ray to anyone taking chem 104, but be prepared to study hard.
Great teacher. I could tell he really cared about the individual success of his students and would go out of his way to help.

I truly felt that he taught better and in a more efficient manner in his lecture videos than his physical lectures, so I rarely went to those. When finishing exams, make sure to check those over because every question is .7% of your grade. Because of the unreleased criteria he uses for the grading scale, nobody really knows his grade until the end.

Dr. Ray is tough, and if you miss a lecture its easy to fall behind & hard to catch up.  Sometimes its hard to understand, but he's always open to questions, if u keep them specific.  His curve is generous, so as long as you try you should be able to pass.  Be prepared to put in a lot of work and be sure to have a friend you can work with..it helps
Really helpful, funny, and reasonable. Go to lectures and things will come much more easily. Be prepared to learn plenty about his family!
Great teacher. He explains subject matter quite well. Exams are tough tho. Be prepared to work hard on org chem.

This professor is the best I've had at UIUC. I hate and am terrible at chemistry but he made it completely enjoyable. He cares about the students and does everything in his power to get his students to understand and learn the material. He will challenge you on exams but he does well in preparing you.

GREAT TEACHER. He made chem so much fun. People in other reviews bag on him, but honeslty they probably didn't do the practice problems or watch the NUMEROUS lecture videos that he posted, and they probably didn't go to his review sessions that he holds every friday. GREAT TEACHER. Ignore the negative posts. Take him if you can!!!!!

If you can get in his lecture, TAKE IT. He is a great professor. I hate chemistry, but LOVED this class. He has tons of lecture videos and prelecture videos, practice problems, suggested problems, and ton's of help available. Go to lecture, get your clicker points, WATCH the videos he posts, and do the suggested/practice problems and you've got an
I love love love him. I hate chemistry but you can tell how much he cares about his students and puts in so much effort to help you succeed!

Excellent professor in all aspects. The best lecturer I've had. Not an easy class, but any problems you have you can post on the compass site, and he will probably respond on the same day... very helpful. Also manages to make chemistry fun. Highly recommended.

Great professor! Actually makes me enjoy going to lecture. Gives you all the tools you need to do well and thoroughly understand the material, including tons of practice problems. My best professor at this university so far.

All in all great teacher. His power points are organized and his pre lecture videos are very helpful. Also has a lot of suggested problems to help prepare. Exams aren't bad at all, wayyy easier than yerkes' exams. I actually enjoyed going to class. And he's a hot live version of Doug Funny...
Best Professor I have had so far here!!! This lecture videos he posts on compass are so helpful.. if you miss lecture you have no problem catching up! I love his class!

He's one of the best professors I've ever had. Very good at teaching and really cares about how his students are doing. Puts a lot of effort into this class! Exams really test you, but LONCAPA, quizzes, and the curve should boost your grade.

Dr. Ray is a good professor if you go to his office hours, prepare your questions in advance, and ask him directly outside of his lectures.  The problem is that his office hours are often extremely filled because he is quite popular, so it's very hard to get his help when there are so many people surrounding him.  He is nice, but overrated.

Great lecturer. Responds well from student feedback and genuinely cares if you don't understand concepts or need help. The only drawback is that he really tests you with his exams. But if you put forth the effort, I'm sure you should do fine in his class.
An ok class. Exams can be tough though. And Ray is not very helpful.

Dr. Ray was one of the best professors ive ever had! i never have written a review on a professor before but Ray is worth commenting on. Excellent teaching, not exactly easy material but Ray is very fair and if you go to class (which i would HIGHLY reccomend for chemistry) and put in the time/effort you will be fine.
Taught material well. His tests were hard, but the curve made up for my poor scores on the tests and I received an A.

My favorite professor yet! I loved dr. ray! Although the material is not very easy, he does everything possible to help you learn and gives plenty of opportunities to have things explained outside of lecture. Go to lecture and discussion and its a pretty easy class. Dr. Ray is AWESOME!

Dr. Ray is 'friendly' and interesting and, it seems at first at least, genuine. But if you read his 'teaching philosophy' on the Chem dept website it is all spelled out. To me he did not appear spontaneous; it was as if he was too mechanical. After a while the 'novelty', if any, wears of and you almost start wishing for a more genuine professor.

Take Chem 104 with Dr.Ray!He is a great professor,and very down-to-earth.Favorite prof so far!He does challenge you,but pay attention,do suggested problems,and take advantage of his online office hours and the TAs to master it.The class is curved since the tests are challenging.He is really good at explaining complicated things.He made me like chem
Dr. Ray is my favorite professor thus far in college. He's cool, smart, and his exams are very straighforward as long as you understand the material. Overall he's a cool professor.

He is well liked by students because he does not have an attitude problem and appears enthusiastic about what he is doing. He is not,however,very good at it. He often relies upon prepared notes, sometimes seem a bit confused -and it is not too difficult to loose focus during class. Some demos are all style and no substnce. Overall, he is ok.

Ray is a fun-loving guy. He is a great guy but I'm not sure if he's a great professor. He seems to prejudice one over the other and his tests are extremly hard compared to the tests of the other Chem 104 professor.
Dr. Ray is a great teacher. He made going to class worth the effort. He also provided a great pre-organic chemistry base before heading onto organic chemistry.

Rey makes his class interesting and fun to attend which is very refreshing after CHEM102 which made me hate chem. His lectures include lots of demos and he clearly explains everything which is unique to this campus. Definitely recommend!
Amazing!  Be sure to do suggested problems, lectures were helpful
One of the few entertaining lectures ever! I actually loved going to his class! A good advise for this class is to do the suggested problems and read his notes and you are good! Now I love chem!
Terrific instructor with energy, enthusiasm, and the rare ability to connect with an auditorium sized class.

Dr. Ray is a really good guy, he is very helpful and very approachable, Class is tough but if you do practice problems, go to office hours, do the readings, you should be good. This class is all about how much effort you are willing to put into it. If you are gonna take this class, I would say take it with Dr. Ray.
Dr. Ray is an amazing teacher! Loved this class.
I absolutely looove him!  He was so great and chemistry ROCKS!!  The class is awesome and he's hott!!!!!  He's also good at teaching :)

Super awesome chemistry teacher.  Seriously, if you have to take this class make sure to get Ray!  Not only does he make chem really interesting, he's just overall a great teacher.  Do all the suggested problems (trust me you'll be thankful on the exams) and do practice exams and go to class!  Chem 104 is nothing but a good time with Ray!!!!

Dr. Ray is an awesome professor.  He absolutely loves teaching, and he always talks about how it is his dream job.  I'm really glad I had him instead of Dr. Yerkes.  She bores me to death, and doesn't really teach.  Dr. Ray keeps you interested.  You should see his lectures.  They are packed full!

Dr. Ray is an amazing teacher.  He's incredibly helpful, and as long as you do the suggested problems, go to every lecture, and understand the material the class will be a lot easier.  Before exams review suggested problems and do all of the old exams!  Dr. Ray is extremely helpful, so use the Chem 104 website frequently.  Awesome class!
Fun teacher; last day of class is "blow stuff up day." Tests have the usual tricky questions. In comparison to Yerkes: Yerkes teaches better but Ray is more entertaining.
All around great guy. He loves what he is doing, is always willing to help you, and always has some sort of demo during class. If you apply yourself, it should be an easy A.
good lecturer. somewhat interesting, good demos, seems like he cares about students

He's GREAT! Lectures were actually understandable and he had GREAT demos! Obviously it's a hard class- but with a lot of work you can get a great grade. Ray made things really clear and he's a really nice guy.
Good guy, definitely makes lectures worth going to. A lot of cool demos, explains things well, but he doesnt just lay everything out in front of you.  Exams are fair and curved well.

The corey matthews look-a-like really makes class interesting, so that you wish there was more time. You don't receive a grade for homework, but you HAVE to do it to do well on exams! Take quizzes seriously, too.

Great professor.  Makes a real effort to constantly improve his teaching.  If you read the book before lecture and do the problems he recommends you doing, you will succeed.  I never thought I liked chemistry, but now I have a definite interest in it.
Great professor!  Had easily understandable and very enjoyable classes!  Also, gave fair exams. Definitely recommended!
Dr. Ray is amazing.  Definitely one of my favorite professors.  He makes boring chemistry interesting.

Very enthusiastic professor!  Extremely hard tests, but the curves aren't too bad.  I would definitely go to office hours to catch up on stuff you don't understand.  Prof. Ray will only get better as he gets more experienced!  I would definitely take his class!  Go Cubs!

Dr. Ray is fantastic. I am terrible at chemistry and was excited to go to lectures... he makes the material interesting. Office hours were very helpful--he was great at rephrasing things I didn't understand and was really interested in my success. It's a tough class, you have to put in the effort, but Dr. Ray is a great professor.
Very interesting professor, always brings in current events that deal with what we are learning. Great speaker. Hard exams.

Dr. Ray is great.  He does fun demos and his teaching methods are awesome.  His focus for research is improving chemistry teaching, so he definitely knows his stuff. And he's great at chemistry too, but thats really just a bonus.

He was a super nice guy, however his lectures were so broad that when it came time to do the homework, I was lost. His tests are super hard and I feel like he almost sets us up to fail. Overall, nice guy but not so good at teaching.
Hard tests, but very fair grader and generous with curves. Lots of demos, good analogies in class

Nice teacher but not all that clear. Instead of having power points he writes his notes by hand on the board which really reduced the amount of information you can learn in class. But go to lecture because his test questions are derived directly from lecture. The 1st test is hard just to scare you and the rest are easier- final was very easy!

Dr. Ray was amazing. Sometimes in lecture things could get a little confusing but he tried really hard to give real life examples. Go to his office hours! It really helped me understand better plus he is really fun to talk to about other stuff not related to chem. I think he will get better the more he teaches.  Best chem teacher I have had
very helpful and enthusiastic. lets you know exactly what will be on the test. beware of all the whiners in chem 104.
Entertaining-makes you want to come to class; helpful in office hours; takes personal interest in students' progress.

Nice guy but if you take the class learn concepts more in depth then what is presented in class. Tests require that you know ALL of chem and he teaches only about 20% of it in lecture. You are better off staying home and reading the book.
he was a good teacher, pretty helpful. didnt mind if you came into his office at anytime.
Even though I'm doing really bad in his class, his lectures were interesting... I enjoyed taking his class, and I may be taking it next semester too! :(

Not ready for lecturing at all.  I learned more in my discussion than in lecture.  Horrible explainer and doesn't give any examples for anything he explains.  He hardly prepares you enough for the tests which were hard.  I wasn't great at chemistry in the first place and he did not help at all.  If only I had known this before...
No Comments
Great (young) guy, but would barely cut it as a TA.  Definately not ready to lecture.  Explanations are confused--he clearly does not have much experience with Chem 104.
If you need to take PSYC 100 I would 100% recommend Belgin. I know the class is annoying to have to take but she's a great lecturer and makes the class a lot more bearable.

I have to give Belgin credit where credit is due. PSYC100 is run by L. Travis, but the TAs are who the students deal with. Belgin was my TA and despite the course being setup in a weird, almost non-sensical way, Belgin did a great job navigating through and was great at reminding students of due dates and upcoming exams. She also made lecture good.

Belgin is really understanding of extenuating circumstances and will go out to bat for you with the course coordinator if you need help. Lectures are long and this class felt like a verbatim repeat of AP Psych in high school, but you need a 5 to get credit. I had a 4 so this class was pretty boring and I personally didn't learn any new information.
Shes very kind and gives amazing lectures.

Great person, very knowledgeable, willing to help out. Lectures are not great--she uses complex vocab very quickly after defining it and doesn't really define what it means. Read the book for extra help. DEFINITELY do the homework. I personally found searching up YouTube videos helped fill in the conceptual gaps.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Very smart professor that cares deeply about what she is doing. Most of these reviews are from the calculus series, but she is great at teaching upper division math. The exams are very challenging, but it requires you to have a deep understanding of the material. She also replies to emails on Saturdays, showing her commitment.

She had no clue what she was doing most of the time and I learned nothing from her lectures. She would do problems and students would often have to correct her work during the class. Might be a better teacher in higher level math courses.

She explained the bulk of the material well, but sometimes struggled to explain in detail. In class exercises everyday (graded). Students would complete the problem in small groups, then she would explain/review at the end of class. I wish she saved more time for the explanation part, cause most days I was lost while doing the exercises alone.

Not the worst professor but a but all over the place since shes more used to teaching upper level math. Had the same slides as heller so can go to his lectures. Some days you'd walk into lecture and need to review again but some days you'd be enlightened. Overall not the worst but heller is the best of you have the option to take him
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures could be a tad confusing but she posted slideshows and recorded lectures which helped a lot. Two exams were laughably easy but the rest were ridiculously difficult. That's no fault of Dr. Stojanoksa, just an issue with Calc 3 here.

Lectures were pretty bad, we were behind a lot the beginning of the semester. Gave a grade cutoff adjustment outline before the final that would've moved each grade cutoff by about 8% but she only adjusted the grade cutoffs by about 1%, just overall did not know what she was doing.

Calc 3 is not a good course at UIUC, not entirely her fault. She knows the subject well can be unclear at times. Homework is way harder than lecture. There are 4 midterms and a final worth 28% of the grade, and they are either really easy or really hard. Overall she's not bad, but not great and other professors may be better or worse.

Excessive homework and exams, mandatory attendance at dull discussions, and a professor who disregards students' workload and the impact of her flawed course design. She teaches poorly—illegible writing, unclear explanations, and no acceptance of feedback. Her sole skill seems to be deploying sophistry to defend her ridiculous course planning.

Professor Stojanoska is a decent lecturer. Although her lectures could be clearer and more concise, she is able to get the content of the class across and helps students understand it. While there could be improvement in her lectures, she is one of the better professors for MATH 241.

Her lectures are horrible, she normally doesn't know what she is talking about and gets things wrong on the lectures all of the time. The tests are hit or miss, they can sway between extremely difficult with tedious questions and stuff not shown on any practice tests to easier than a calc 1. Find other lectures if you get cursed with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She couldn't answer most questions people had and explained certain topics poorly.

1-2 hours of homework every 2 days. tests are difficult. during lectures it is hard to follow along. I feel like the concepts are never explained very well. If you are not a math major or extremely smart in mathematics you are going to get very lost.

On the rare occasion you get a step-by-step workout of problems you'll never see on the exam, it is straightforward and clear. But none of those procedures help you on the exam because the way they want you to answer the exam requires a solution you were never taught.

She gives a lot of homework compared to other professors but only grades 1/4. She also expects you to know how to answer her questions both from homework and exams even tough. Even if you are an undergraduate, she expects you to be her (doctorate) level. She is willing to help you during office hours, but she expects nonsense from you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is a great lecturer, but once the material starts getting difficult it is hard to follow along. The homework grader is extremely harsh and rarely gives higher than a C-. The only thing fair about the class is that the exams aren't too difficult if you study hard for them

She's not the greatest at explaining the material during class, takes too long to go through little material. Office hours are very broad and she doesn't help as much. Exams are hard, but she curves the exams A LOT.

Super nice professor, and she really tries to explain the concepts. Unfortunately, this caused us to be behind for most of the semester. There are additional materials on canvas and media space, which I found to be helpful. She also does office hours outside of class, which are very useful.
I took 210 with her and she is genuinely the best prof I have ever had. She is an incredible lecturer and explains concepts really well. Will take any class with her.
A really good professor who cares for students and is very kind during office hours and lectures. Definitely would take her teaching course again. I took ECE 210 with her for Fall 2025.
Tough class, but Professor Shao made it very enjoyable. Always encouraged answering questions in class, and answered those questions very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good teacher
Very organized and great at answering questions. Would recommend

Victoria Shao was a good lecturer but not excellent. She was very helpful in office hours and explained questions well in class. Sometimes see would go through a topic too fast but it is because it is a fast course and I think she did her best with the time constraints.

Prof. Shao is an excellent professor. She provides invaluable feedback and pushes students to go above and beyond for senior design and other courses as well. Many Professors have a reputation as being tough or unkind in the department and prof. shao is extremely nice and supportive. She's also brilliant and gives advice that saved me weeks of time

Zooms through lectures like she's on crack and does not wait for you to understand something she said before she moves on. Be ready to watch lectures twice or three times, at least once to take notes and another to actually listen to what was said. Slightly scatterbrained when solving examples, doesn't have a clear flow on examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is very funny--I will give her that, and the lectures were never hard to get through. But her grading is ridiculous. She says, "to get a A all you have to do is answer the questions in the prompt" but then even after you do she finds something wrong with it. Don't get me started on the ridiculousness that is her participation system.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. V is very fun. Her lectures are engaging and often humorous. She's also flexible to accommodate student needs. Some say she's a tough grader- I disagree. She won't just "give away" A's but you'll get the grade you earn from your effort. The class itself is a lot of reading but the texts are both super easy and interesting. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's an overall really funny person and knowledgeable about what she teaches. I had her for Asian American Lit, and she really explained a lot of the topics well. Grading is based on participation in class, and the assignments are only writing. She is tough on grading, but fair. If you pay attention in class, it's not hard to get an A.

Dr.Villanueva did a decent job of outlining the criteria for her class but was exceptionally rude very often. She clearly knows her stuff and will give good criticism if you ask, but in class can be unpleasant with the somewhat condescending and exasperated tone she takes in many situations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very strict grader. No matter how hard I tried The highest grade I could get was a B+ on every assignment. Her feedback and instructions are also pretty vague so it is a pretty tough class. She was also rude at times when she saw people do poorly on some of the papers. It was not a bad class but you have to do the impossible if you want an A.

This professor made me despise writing and the English language. Unnecessarily harsh when it comes to grading. Especially for low stakes assignments and attendance in the midst of a pandemic. Does not let you refute the comments she makes on your essays and says that they are final. This defeats the entire purpose of actually learning.

Dr. V is awesome! She was super accessible outside of class and offered office hours for each essay and gave great feedback about your topic. She also gave students the opportunity to write about subjects of their choice any chance she could. I enjoyed that class and believe she helped me strengthen my writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Even though we had to write 4 papers, there was tons of time to do them. Dr. V gives good feedback and as long as you apply it, youll improve in your writing. Dr. V is also very clear in her grading criteria and if you follow it, you should have no problem getting As on your papers. Attendance policy for the English department is strict though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures were often confusing and not engaging. I pretty much had to teach myself everything even when I did go to lecture. Had an A the whole semester and then my grade went down after our last midterm had a failing average that dropped most students significantly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of homework extra credit opportunities. Very boring lecturer but you get used to it. 5 CBTF midterms (at least my semester) that were doable. Not as bad as people say. The online notes are very helpful. Make sure to get as many homework extra credits as you can, they help in the long run. The homework was doable too

Up until the last exam, I loved this professor. He had amazing notes, exams were not easy but not difficult, and there was no final exam. However, on the last exam, the average was a 56%. Despite the majority of the class failing the test, there was no curve, just grade cutoff adjustments. Because of this test, my grade dropped 2 letters.

I took Calc 3 with Dr. Zharnitsky when the course had 5 midterms and no final. Pros: Each lecture had clear and well-structured reading, lecture notes, and homework. The professor was helpful and caring during office hours. Cons: Some midterms had technical issues/problems barely covered in class. Luckily, the grades were adjusted in such cases.

I didn't pay attention/go to any lectures because the posted notes are good enough. Lecture isn't necessary because attendance isn't taken and he posts notes. Exams are in CBTF with 4-5 attempts on each question only losing 1pt (out of 10 possible per question) for each attempt. Exam averages were 90% or higher except the 5/last one. NO FINAL EXAM!
A very friendly professor.

I don't understand the hate of this professor, he's very generous with his grading, the exams are very well put together, he gives you many attempts for the CBTF exams, 5 attempts on each question to get it right. His notes incredible, the greatest notes I might have ever seen. I would highly recommend this professor.
Taught too many concepts without many complex examples. Examples and solutions were very unclear, and the handwriting was hard to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very well structured course overall. The lectures are fairly helpful and the notes provided are very useful to solidify understanding of course concepts. Grading and tests are very reasonable as well overall.

Very unclear explanations during the lectures. Did not provide any notes or study materials. I missed 2 weeks of class due to being sick and asked him for the notes, He just told me to get it from someone else.
The explanations in the class were very unclear. The exams were very hard, and the average grade was very low, around 60 points.

I'm not gonna pretend I did well in this class, but nonetheless Professor Zharnitsky was a very nice and seasoned professor. His lectures could be hard to decipher at times, but in conjunction with reading the textbook AND PAUL'S ONLINE MATH NOTES, it makes enough sense. The exams are much easier than the homework, so just be ready to study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not awful as a teacher, but the study materials are terrible. This is a huge flaw since the two midterms were 25% each and the final was 40%.
I have never had a panic attack in my life before tonight. Our final exam is tomorrow morning and I've studied so hard for it, but I still feel lost. I'm terrified

Final exam tomorrow. 40% of grade. I am in hell because I spent a week straight studying problems directly out of the book that he told us to practice and took a practice exam and I would've gotten like a 25%. This is my 6th semester. I've gotten one B- and the rest Bs and higher in all college. A 59% on the exam might get me a C. Miracle needed.

Taken a few lectures so far. He just keeps making mistakes on the recorded lecture. Sometimes it's even worse, as he make a mistake on another mistake, and the whole lecture just goes into a nonsense.
Tough course with a tough professor. Rough accent and doesn't really help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Speaks quietly and draws amazing 3D shapes that he does not explain very well. He does not ask the class enough questions throughout lecture and when he does every one is confused. Reads directly off the lecture notes available online and sometimes makes mistakes despite having the notes.
Awful at explaining concepts and giving reasoning for his methods while solving problems.
Very difficult class and not a great teaching style. TAs were helpful. Curved by a ridiculous amount at the end of the semester because test averages were so low.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The trouble at first is accent, later it's not a problem cuz u'll get used to it.
Great professor for 441. Extremely strong grasp of material. Very helpful. Very direct presentation of material.
It is somewhat difficult to understand what he is explaining on the board but the exams are easy since the exam problems are very similar to the homework problems.

Each day I had this class, it was probably the best part of my day. Professor Zharnitsky enjoys answering conceptual questions, and takes time to make sure students are understanding. He's really approachable and helpful during his office hours. Although homework/exams were somewhat tricky, he grades fairly. Hoping to take another class from him.

This class was really enjoyable--It was probably the best part of each day I had it. Professor Zharnitsky is really considerate and likes answering conceptual questions. He's also really helpful and approachable during his office hours. Homework/exams were normally somewhat challenging, but he graded very generously.
Very each class to get an A. Professor would often times get lost on a problem and waste ten minutes trying ti figure it out.
He's a smart professor who means well. I had trouble understanding him with his accent though and his test were not easy. Mediocre class overall in terms of passibility

Horrible horrible teacher. Couldn't understand a thing. I sometimes doze off while listening to him talk. He may be very fervent/dedicated in teaching but he really doesn't know how to present the material. He'll stop in the middle of sentences and lets you finish the thought process, which is unhelpful in addition to his accent.
can't understand anything. i had trouble with him and lectures, but i didnt go to many of them. Math is my best subject and i got a C+, but scale was weighed. i only recieved a 62%

English is not his native laungue and it is very hard to understand what he is saying.  He was extremely boring and unhelpful.  Most people do not even go to his lecture and just go to discussion. The grading was fair.  All quizes were based off homework and exams very not extremely hard.  He does curve when needed.

English was not his first language. Hard to understand in lecture. However, tests are extremely easy. If you have trouble understanding material in lecture make sure to get a good TA for discussion. Some TAs are awesome, others are terrible.

He's a very smart man. He rewrites the book examples most of the time. He also posts his notes online so you can always look at them later. However sometimes he gives out important info. during lecture such as what's gonna be on the quiz the next day etc. so you might want to go. His exams are either really easy or really hard.

This guy fails at speaking english and at teaching.  He's boring, and is profoundly uninterested in teaching.  However, I'm terrible at math, yet I think his tests and quizzes are ridiculously easy.  This guy is your ticket to getting credit for Calc 2 without doing any work at all!

GREAT TEACHER!! exams are very easy, i remember taking his class last year and he realized after he gave us the 1st exam that it was too easy. Apparently i was in a class filled with dumb ppl so our averages were still lower than the usual grading scale. I got an A in this class, and i recommend him as a teacher

As a professor, he is useless. But the class is EASY! Taylor Series, which is supposed to be incredibly difficult, I got a 97% on the exam with moderate studying. And he uses MathZone for hw, which is really nice.
No Comments
Not a very easy class as it is but did not help with Zharnitsky teaching.  Does not answer email
He is the best professor ever. This class was also one of my lowest grades, but I learnt a lot and would still recommend taking it because of him.
Every lecture by the professor is very serious, and the guidance on learning is meticulous. They also show a great understanding of the difficulties students may face.
Arguably the best professor I've had since I've been here at uiuc. Genuinely takes his time with students and make sure everyone understands them.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tough class but he lectures well and is overall just a good dude.

The lectures are quite clear and he always uploads the recorded lecture on the same day. 
It takes ages to grade the labs and exams.

The best professor I've ever had here at UIUC. I accidentally joined his office hours Zoom outside of office hours and then he emailed me right away trying to help me. He understands what it is like to be a student and tailors the course to fit the students. I learned a lot and had fun without feeling so pressured.

Truly the best professor I have had thus far in my college career. He takes his time to privately meet with students to explain concepts further if you are having any difficulty. As long as you reach out and put your effort he will do his best to help you.

I've had amazing teachers before and Dr. Vogiatzis comes in at #2. I'm currently in the class and he really cares about the success of each student. He not only grades for correctness, but he also grades on your understanding of the material. He will also take on the job of both professor and tutor in order to make sure you understand everything.

Prof. Vogiatzis was by far the best professor I had at UIUC. He really cared about us and was super accessible, and really changed the format of the class for the better. The office hours he has 3 times a week are so worth it. I expected this class to be one of the worst, but I dont think any class tops this.

Thus far, I have not had an instructor that is more dedicated to my learning and success than Professor Vogiatzis. For IE 300, Chrys held office hours three times a week, and whenever there was a quiz/exam coming up, he extended those, along with online office hours. Further, he emphasized how the course material applied to real world situations.

I'm in his class now. Great professor, Dr. V clearly cares about us learning the material. There are a lot of notions to keep track of, but he repeats them again and again in lectures. He is very nice so go find him during office hours. I highly recommend him for IE 300!
This guy is the boy.

Lectures are very theoretical, and homework is your way to apply the theory. The material and homework can be challenging at times, but office hours are available and should be taken advantage of. If you're serious about the subject and are willing to work hard, you will do well and learn quite a bit.

Vakakis has unfair reviews. Teaching 340 for 20+ years, he knows the material. Take if you're actually serious about ME and want to learn. Handwritten notes(posted), hw can be long, tedious. Easy labs every 2 weeks worth 10%. Cheatsheets for exams. Nothing unexpected for 3rd year course. Go to lecture/office hrs, study, do the hw. You can get an A.
good luck to whoever has him in the future...

I can't believe my tuition money is used to pay this guy.
He's taught for decades but doesn't know how to use a microphone
He makes tons of math errors during lecture, which makes me question if he's actually qualified
He admits he purposely leaves out important topics in the notes to make people come to him in person.

Also just not a nice person.
Old fashioned professor
Homeworks can be challenging for TAM416. Need time to digest the lecture content. Be ready to work very hard for this class but you'll learn a lot about nonlinear phenomena.

You want to take Prof. Vakakis' class if you want to go deeper into dynamics and vibrations, because he is an expert in this field. He actually teaches some more material than the usual scope of this class and be ready to be challenged. Be very proficient in calculus and linear algebra for TAM412, cuz you'll use them a lot.

Worst. Professor. Ever. His rigid way of teaching and inability to be an open-minded person makes him a very difficult professor to deal with. He doesn't use online resources and sticks to pen and paper for notes. Never. Ever. Take a class with him. He's extremely critical and harsh when he speaks.

Dr. Vakakis is a thorough and considerate professor. The homework assignments while difficult are not too far from reach using the notes from class. In all, Dr. Vakakis does his best to create a course that challenges his students but also helps them in a number of ways. I highly recommend this course for anyone interested in dynamics.
would not recommend

He relies on in-person teaching to provide all the material we need for exams and homework. Homework will be impossible without a study group, and everything is graded incredibly harshly. The labs will be a learning curve, but exams and homework are the hardest part of this course. Be prepared to be humbled and take a different professor if you can

worst. professor. ever. His labs are useless and teaches what feels like made up concepts. doesn't teach matlab, has extremely hard homework assignments, lectures start to not make any sense, wastes time by telling people to shut up, absolutely horrible. Take any other professor because this class is tough as it is, his teaching makes it worse

One of the toughest classes I've ever taken. However, you do learn a lot. Professor doesn't have lecture slides/notes. You have to show up to class and hang on to his every word because what he says is what you got (aka. you're writing your own textbook). Homework took ~12-15 hrs/wk working with ~1/5 the class each weekend. Tests are comparable.
Teach everything in a really fundamental way, give me a really deep understanding of what is happening, not just blindly applying equations.

Pros: drops all you need to know in lecture, rewards hard work, is nice
Cons: Very old fashioned, and starts the semester off really hard before you get the groove of it
Honestly, a decent dude as long as you work hard. Be sure to attend lectures for the hints he drops, and form study groups for homeworks ASAP. Good luck!

Vakakis is easily the worst professor I have had at UIUC. He just reads off of a projected note sheet for lectures, he grades homework extremely strictly, he expects undergrads to perform the same as grad students, and he refuses to curve. Around 15% of students get below a D or below and he says his this is "very good."

Does not use book and everything he teaches comes from his notes, so attendance is a must. Very knowledgeable and a great teacher. Homework is impossible to do alone and group work is a must in order to pass class. Grades very nicely. Very helpful if you ask for it. Really challenges his students. Makes sure you learn a lot.
His lecture is super boring and you have to write everything he wrote on the board because there is no lecture notes or any other things u can use to study. HWs are super duper hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Homeworks are hard but graded nicely. As long as you go to class and participate you will do fine but make sure you're not caught not paying attention because he will call you out and ask you questions specifically. "Have you been reading your notes?"
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The best professor!

Amazing professor; don't let the sheer amount of work cloud your judgement. He prefers writing on the board old-school style. If you take good notes, you shouldn't need a textbook. But if you skip a single lecture, you will fall behind. He was very helpful in office hours (which you WILL need). Be ready to work hard and with other classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: smart,clear and the best.
Awesome Professor. He'll work you hard but you learn an amazing amount.

Overall, a very nice guy. He definitely shows his interest in teaching the subject. The material can be hard at times, but he does his best to teach everything thoroughly. He is also very helpful in answering questions. Don't get the textbook though, the class is based entirely on notes taken in class (an incentive to attend).
Went out of her way to support my work schedule and helped me stay on track.

I learned quite a bit about environmental health and communicable disease, but what this class really showed me how is just how much global politics and finance mattered in people's health. It made me sad sometimes, but Valeria reminded us that human behavior is not set in stone, and had us think critically about solutions.

Valeria is a great lecturer who clearly cares about her students. She alternates between theory and data but makes it easy for students, the examples are very relatable. Most readings are on Canvas, but you will need to choose a reading book for the group project. I don't like online classes, but I know some people need them.

Professor Bonatti creates a very welcoming environment, and is supportive of mental health. A couple of times I fell behind, she and the TA worked with me to help me stay on track. The lectures have a lot of data, which will be really helpful for the future.

This professor poses complex, thought-provoking questions but often expects immediate, polished responses without giving students enough time to reflect, especially in an online format. Feedback can feel dismissive or uninterested, creating an uncomfortable environment that discourages participation. Also, she never graded our final paper.

She was a great professor, honestly. Very willing to help and encouraging. However, she was not always up to date on her grades. I had to write a 15 page paper for the final; she never ended up grading it, so it was pointless. Definitely was upset about this, especially when she did not tell us, and we were not given any credit for it.
Discussion & attendance are important to the class, be ready to engage. Overall, a solid professor, her teaching just isn't my style :)

Dr. Bonatti does a good job at managing online lectures and class discussions. She is also very nice and ready to answer question, and offers either a break or to finish early.
Some weeks had pretty heavy readings, but you don't really need to read in depth before class.

The class is very informative, and the professor is very nice and understanding. 
Grading is fair but a bit slow with the homework at times.

I took Resistance Movements in its first year on campus, so the expectations of it may improve in the future. That being said, I really dreaded going to this class. The lectures were full of concepts that were hard to pay attention to and understand. Multiple lengthy readings per week. Prof is very caring, but intense concepts for 100 lvl class.

Bonatti is one of the most understanding and kind professors, in my experience. Shes extremely well spoken and conveys the material in a way that makes it easy to understand and really interesting. Shes a very fair grader and gives helpful feedback, and shes always willing to listen if you need to talk.

There was quite a bit of reading, and it helped if you did it, but she basically went over the reading in class. Also, she posted all of the reading on Moodle for us, so you don't have to buy a book necessarily. Tests were take-home essay questions (2 exams, no final), and were easy if you put in some good work for them.
Good class, would take this professor again

You won't pass without the textbook. She is a repeat offender of posting assignments without telling the students. Quiz, data collecting and 45-50 page chapter reviews every single week. Doesn't answer emails, ambiguous instructions for papers, & doesn't tell you why points were taken off assignments. Do not take this professor. Run from Bonatti.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very poor professor. Has no empathy for the students who are struggling in class. I asked for additional help as I am not a finance student.
One of the best faculty members in the iMBA program. Teaches in the entire Core 2 concentration. Do the work and you will be fine!
He's ill educated, can't articulate,feel his education is fake, he should not be teaching, bane for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable. Doesn't like to be tested on his grading. The rubric says one thing, but the reasons given for credit are another. Not sure if it is a miscommunication or personality issue, but it is rubbing people the wrong way. No issue with his lectures or information presented. I would take his class again if grading was fixed.
Overreaches his powers - he's just a mere professor but presumes he's the overlord of everything. Not that smart or knowledgeable either. Very disrespectful in his tone and mannerisms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is just mean and uncaring.

Professor is literally a pain, claimed all of my assignments could not have possibly been that right, created a claim and decided to give me an F tainting my reputation and my GPA, truly an awful professor

Terrible professor, would avoid at all costs. Was on the edge of two letter grades and needed 1 point to be given the higher letter grade, and denied all of my claims. No empathy or sympathy when it comes to grading, he grades by a non-existent rubric that we have no access to on exams.

He seems to lack empathy and insight as to why people are asking many of the questions that are asked. The typical UIUC business professor is very good at explaining/connecting between simplified models used in class and the messier situations we face in the real world, and they are polite and clear. Not so much for Vlad. He seems annoyed.
Very patient and knowledgeable. Go to Vlad's office hours, even if you don't have a question to ask - absolutely awesome.

awful. 

completely out to lunch with his logic. 

having an educational background in finance/banking/economics is great, but work experience in the industry provides credibility and expertise that cannot be gained by reading a textbook or attending a lecture hall.

took in 2021. Microeconomics is a big topics for 8 weeks. Prof. Vlad is knowledgeable, assignments link with content. People who hate math will complain.  Personal opinion it is a master level course, not a class for pre-k math. Understandable seeing Prof. Vlad lost patience with those trying to ask math solutions. He does try to answer patiently.

This instructor is a joke. He thinks this is some course where learning can be by rote. Business courses are more about developing a sense/acumen to be successful not just completing textbook examples and stupid math problems that dont have any connection with the course material.
The professors lacks the ability of conveying simple economics principles. He makes also a big deal when asking to review the assignment that was incorrectly graded.
I took his class which wasn't difficult. However, his explanation were bad and not convincing, I would prefer to attending his office hours as he is not helpful
I did not feel that he was helpful during office hours. I felt that he was providing wrong answers so that we do not  score well but this is against the principle of office hours.
Extremely unprofessional professor who does not seem to really enjoy teaching things.

Do not take his class. He will do every effort to make sure that students grades are reduced. Student learning is exceptionally low in his class. Very rude on Discussion board, not very helpful. Try to make things confusing. Exams are hard, expect PhD level knowledge or may be more from students even if you are not PhD student.

Prof. Vlad is extremely helpful and will go the extra mile to make sure students understand. He will help you when you don't understand, walking you through the reasoning. I have been to pretty much every office hour he holds and I could not be able to get through the course without his office hours. Extra helpful, in my opinion.

Co-teaches the class with DeBrock. Mostly responsible for office hours, Q&A, and administration of grading. If you ever have questions, join office hours - really helpful and explains concepts really well.
Extremely mean when answering student questions.
He has lot of patience and would recommend again

Great course if you want to learn how statistical methods are used in real data analysis. The class emphasizes both modeling ideas and practical implementation, so it is useful but requires consistent effort.

I learned a lot in this class. The instructor strikes a good balance between teaching R programming and connecting it to real statistical problems. Topics like bootstrap, simulation, and resampling were explained in a way that made them click, and questions during and after class were always welcomed.

Prof. Wang is one of the best professors I have had. He is patient, enthusiastic, and genuinely cares about his students' learning. Stat 428 has been one of the most rewarding courses I have taken thanks to his teaching.

Lectures are both boring and hard to follow. A lot of people are saying he was a good lecturer, which is confusing to me. They were so bad, in fact, that there were plenty where I was the only one to show up. Had Phd student TA tell me that this class was probably the hardest he's seen.
STAT 428 was a challenging yet rewarding course. Despite the heavy homework load, I learned a great deal and gained valuable skills in statistical computing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: STAT525 has been one of the most impactful courses in shaping my research interests.The instructor's ability to present complex optimization concepts in an engaging and accessible way made the course both challenging and rewarding. I gained a deeper understanding of advanced optimization methods and learned how to apply them to real-world problems.

I had the pleasure of taking STAT 428 with Professor Wang, and it was an exceptional experience. This course is known for its complexity, but Professor Wang made it incredibly engaging and accessible.

The instructor is very talented and very passionate about the subject. The lecture materials are well-prepared and provide solid knowledge about modern optimization. The assignments are challenging but can help students absorb the materials.

I enjoyed taking stat428 with Prof. Wang. The lecture slides contained many examples. The professor showed the proofs after introducing the concepts so we could understand why the tests work. He was always clear and thorough with going through the contents.

He's very nice as a person but I don't think he is a good professor for this class. He talks very fast and his handwriting is sloppy. The homework questions are very difficult and nothing at all like the material discussed in lectures or slides. If possible, I'd recommend taking this class with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Wang is very knowledgeable! He is helpful during office hours. The course materials are very useful as well. Plus, this course doesn't have a final exam.

The content of the course is not that hard. The grading is usually very lenient. Prof. Wang is the best (of this semester, at least). He is willing to stop to make sure that students can really learn something. Also the course is pretty practical, and inspires me to learn more in this field.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love Prof Wang and his STAT 428! The workload is heavy but I learned a lot of practical tools. Very useful for the other projects I am working on! The professor is very nice and willing to hold extra office hours to help us.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: hard to understand in class, bad teaching style, lot of content on final project was not covered in class/textbook. would highly suggest not taking STAT428 with him if possible. worst stat professor I've had at UIUC.

This is a great course if you want to learn optimization and have some background in statistics. Professor Wang is very knowledgeable. He cared about our feedback and added many examples in class after the midterm feedback survey.
Did not listen to our entire class when we begged for help over and over. The homework took forever and the final project was ridiculous. He rarely responded to emails as well.
Hard to understand his accent. He only covered shallow points of the material and never gave any concrete example.
The course is great, and easy to follow if you get good statistics background. The professor is nice and super smart.
