This is one of the most useful stat courses Ive taken at UIUC. Although I need to spend a lot of time, definitely worths it. The lectures are well-structured. The professor has some accent, but I can understand it.

Definitely not an easy A class. The workload is heavy, but the course materials are helpful for my research. Listen to all the lectures and go through the requested reading, then you can survive this class. Also, the final grades are curved a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Just got an A from this class. A really tough class, but totally worths all the hard work. The materials are useful, and the professor is helpful during office hours and holds extra office hours upon your request.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: From the Piazza response time and "you should have learnt this in STAT410/ Read the textbook", he doesn't seem to care if students can understand the concepts. Lecture videos are unclear, and the quizzes contain very ambiguous questions. The final project is worth 50% of the grade, which is unbelievable and put lots of stress on us.

The difficulties of the assignments are unstable. The questions on the quizzes are random and semantically vague. There are often typos on assignments and quizzes. Does not show much concern for students in piazza. Not very fluent in teaching

Useless lectures, confusing quizzes, unclear homework, has no respect for students, has zero compassion for the unique situation of taking an online class during a deadly pandemic. I am 100% sure he said during one of the lectures that "since the p-value is very large, we reject the null hypothesis," which is just incorrect. I learned nothing :')
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Poor communicator and harsh grader. Points are taken off for random nitpicking penalties. Teaching quality is mediocre at best; most learning is done through textbook reading during online quizzes/HW. Part of the poor communication could be blamed on the all online format, but I still wouldn't choose this professor for an in-person class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor at UIUC, name called and belittled students on the piazza. Incredibly hard and obscure grader. The class final had a penalty that he didn't announce.

He has no idea how to teach properly. The whole class is a disorganized mess and consisted of listening to his "lectures" reading off his slides copied off the textbook, doing quizzes filled with questions made ambiguous by grammatical errors, and completing homework with the majority of the instructions added on the fly.

"The textbook example of a bad teacher. We did not spend thousands of dollars for this teacher to tell us to read the textbook to learn. His lectures are unclear and have no respect for his students. " written by the other commenter fully express voice. Can not agree more.
He didn't care about the class. It was like he was going through the motions of being a professor.

The textbook example of a bad teacher. We did not spend thousands of dollars for this teacher to tell us to read the textbook to learn. His lectures are unclear and has no respect for his students. This semester his class was forced to be online and it didn't seem like he had prepared or is lenient about the fact that there is a global pandemic

The worst professor I've ever seen in my college life. No midterms in this class so homework , quizzes, and final project will be your grades. The lecture is simple but will not prepare you for the homework and final project at all. Terrible accent and do not have any consideration for students. Avoid him at all costs.

Clara Chen is a great caring professor who knows her stuff. She is very interactive in class and is helpful outside as well. She brings personal examples from her life, incorporates pop culture, and is enjoyable to listen to. I think she did a fantastic job teaching us non accounting folks accounting.

BAD teacher. Super harsh grader. Didn't know what she's talk about. Wish I could've choose another section. Hope there's going to be an individual curve for our section otherwise it's just not fair to get much lower average on cases than other sections.

Lectures are pretty good, but the pace is fast. She convey concepts clearly and the power points are posted so you can review things you don't understand. The book also is helpful in this class. Only two tests so try to do well on the first one. Overall, I'd say she is one of the best professors in the College of Business.

I like her even though she can be a bit bland. Her lectures are fast paced and can be confusing (her accent doesn't help) but if you ask her to explain something after class, she's very nice about it and extremely helpful. Class is straightforward and if you study the material, you should be fine. I expect I'll get a B+ or A- in this class.

She is a very nice professor. You go over activities in class. Some of the material is quite difficult to grasp. The final was pretty difficult a lot of open ended questions where you have to make a decision.

Even though I am in her 8am class, time passes by quickly because of the way she teaches--lectures for 15-20 minutes, does an activity related to what she just lectured, and then repeat until class is over. On days in which we turn in our memos, we get out of class after discussing the memo, which usually takes about half an hour. Great professor.
Really really good professor. Her accy class is my favorite accy class so far.

she is very friendly.  thats all that is good about her class. she reads in mono-tone voice for AN HOUR every class, almost word-for-word, directly off the slides.  then you have to teach yourself an activity for the next 40 minutes.  i didnt learn a single thing.  the overall consensus within the class was that accy302 was their most miserable cla
She's incredibly nice, and a really good teacher.  One of the best professors I've ever had.
awesome teacher! sweet, soft spoken, knows what she's talking about. Tough, but approachable, fair, and very willing to help.
Fantastic! She was a great teacher, very approachable, and very fair in her grading. She was one of the best professors I've had here so far!

So helpful and very friendly! She is extremely fair and wants her students to do well.  The cases are hard to do well on but she will adjust unfair grades given by the assistant. Would highly recommend her!

she explains concepts clearly. Material is sort of confusing at times but she breaks it down pretty well. must go to class but her class doesn't drag. tests are kinda tricky buts its because the material is really conceptual. goin to class and a little hard work will get u a decent grade

Chen is extremely nice and the class is formatted clearly.  There is no presentation, as opposed to other sections of 302.  Her exams can be tricky, but as long as you study and do plenty of practice problems, you'll do fine.
ha, looks like it is a scam, too good to be true.
As far as I know, she only starts teach here since Fall 2006. I wonder how did the previous person take her class last semester.

I didn't think there was a such thing as an easy A in ACCY 302, but Chen is definitely the easiest way to it.  She is very helpful and I was amazed at how little I actually did to earn the A.  DEFINITELY take this section if she teaches it next semester.

His topics are rarely boring. But, where he falls short is that he uses incredibly specific examples from his lectures and required readings on tests. He is doing this to prevent the use of AI, but it ends up hurting students who attend lecture and do the readings the most, as his quizzes and tests become VERY hard to get a good grade.
His exams are based on random examples he uses in class, and some of the questions make no sense at all. Avoid at all costs.

Professor Wirtz's class is definetly tough, but I think many of these reviews are harsh. The lectures do have rambling and sometimes jump around, but if you can take good notes and spen time studying it's very possible to earn an A!

Honestly, the worst professor I have had at U of I. He is inappropriate with his examples in class, calls students out in disrespectful ways, and laughs when you ask questions. Stickler about technology. Everyone in this class looks at each other when he goes on his unfiltered tangents. I think he has tenure, so the university won't get rid of him.

reviews.comment: Awful professor. He is a nice guy, but does not do much to help students succeed. Rushes through slides, does not share the slides, and rambles on about subjects, sometimes without finishing his thought. It is very hard to get a good understanding of the content and material, given the way he conducts the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wirtz is, by far, the worst professor I have ever had. Not only are his exams quizzes of random examples that he used in class, but nearly 65% of the grade was due within the last two weeks of class. I paid attention, took notes, and attended every lecture, yet barely earned an A. Stay away from Wirtz if you care about your GPA or well-being.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went to every lecture. I paid attention to everything he was saying. I asked questions. And I did not learn a single thing this whole semester. He rambles about anything and jumps around on the slides making it impossible to retain a single piece of information displayed on them. He is on tenure so he clearly does not gaf. Good luck.

Slides are impossible to follow and in addition to a final exam he assigned two final strategy applications; the first involves watching 8 hours of videos to get a certificate and the second is over 10 pages of short analysis instructions alone. Said it was in place of a final and then had a final anyways. Quizzes are specific and not enough time.

I am actually so confused on how he has 5- and 4-star ratings. Wirtz cares about his students but is a horrible professor. I am not sure what changed, maybe it was him getting tenure or his medical issues, but his lectures, slides, and tests make absolutely no sense. When he teaches, he jumps all over the place and I have no idea what's happening.

I so badly wanted to finish the public relations minor. However, after a few weeks of this course, I realized that is not possible without an entire semester of anxiety both in and outside of class. The quizzes are incredibly specific and impossible with confusing slides that are difficult to follow, especially with his speed.

he is a sweet and understanding person and is accommodating, but I have no clue in the slightest what has been going on in this class. lectures are really fast paced and his lecture slides make no sense. i don't hate him, i hate this course format. the "case study" quizzes are also short on time for the amount of questions that are given.

Wirtz cares about these students and has tried to accommodate them when necessary. However, his lectures are incredibly confusing and fast, especially when he tries to explain concepts that others are all over the place. I'm often confused in that class.

Quizzes are extremely difficult and once you choose an answer, you unable to go back and review your work before submitting. Wirtz has had temper tantrums and has angerly cursed at our class of mostly women rather than calmy expressing what he needs to say.

John has a lot of passion for PR and he is not the type of professor who tolerates students who cut corners. He wants you to learn. Very strict no phone policy in class. While the quizzes and exams were online and open-note, they were challenging. Be sure to take good notes (and especially note examples he uses in class). I would take him again.

He's actually so nice. Lectures are kind of confusing. Open note quizzes and tests but they are still a bit difficult. He is a good guy and wants you to learn. Although one of my more difficult courses, I would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His class isn't for those who aren't willing to try. If you actively go to lectures and keep up with the material, it isn't difficult to get a higher grade. The material is actually useful and interesting, plus very relevant to those interested in a future in PR.

There was a previous rating from someone who took his summer class that stated Prof. Wirtz had technology issues. It's safe to say that he ironed out these issues in the fall. He kind of delegated email response to his TA so that it is possible to get a hold of someone if you have any questions. The class is straightforward and easy if you keep up.

I love Professor Wirtz. He's a funny guy and fair grader. His lectures are very useful to someone who wants to go into PR. You will actually learn things that apply to real life. There are quizzes after every lecture but they are easy if you do the readings. I learned so much from this class, it was my favorite this semester.

Professor Wirtz is a really kind and fun professor. He looks out for his students and is willing to make adjustments for us. I just finished taking his summer course for ADV 310 and unfortunately, he doesn't work with technology well. I have had issues with accessing videos and quizzes. Worst part about Wirtz is he NEVER responds to your emails!

Wirtz's class definitely isn't for people who aren't going to try their best to get a good grade in the class. He's tough but only because he really wants you to do well and he is more than willing to help you if you reach out to him or go to his office hours. If you're interested in the PR field then you should definitely take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you go to class and pay attention it's easy (and enjoyable). Wirtz is a nice guy who wants you to learn and succeed in his class. If you don't go to class then don't get expect to get great grades. The material is easy to follow and understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Wirtz is nice but should stick to research, not teaching. Monotonous voice makes students fall asleep. Pointlessly drones on for an hour on things that should take 5 minutes. I have had 400 level courses that are much easier. Hardest class I've ever taken. Quizzes are impossible as questions are vague. He expects too much out of a 300 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Surprised at the 2.3/5 rating for Wirtz. You do actually have to do work (bummer ik). But if you actually enjoy PR/Media Careers in general, Wirtz will be one of the few people at UIUC that will guide you down the right path. And make it enjoyable. By no means am I a good student, but I still got an A and looked forward to this class every week.

Honestly, a lot of the reviews here make it sound worse than it is. Wirtz is a good guy who will help you if you need it. You HAVE to go to class, there's not any graded attendance but his tests are completely dependent on lecture materials and examples from class. If you go to class, take good notes, and read the assigned reading you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is an intro to PR class but Wirtz makes it as difficult as possible. He says that he doesn't want his students to do poorly, but the format of his tests begs to differ. He's THAT professor that has exams that have the options "A, B, C, A and B, B and C, All of the above, None of the above." They are also extremely difficult to study for.

He's really not as bad as these reviews say. If you go to class and to his office hours, he's helpful and will tell you what you need to do to succeed. But you HAVE to go to lecture. He posts outlines of slides online but the majority of exam material is things he says in lecture. He also gives 3 analysis assignments that make you apply concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class. His tests are not super easy. He provides an exam outline and highlights important terms on the slides. The short answers are pretty obvious. GO to class he puts examples on the slides and they will appear on the exams. Don't miss attendance points, and do the extra credit and you'll do fine. He's a good professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: horrible, horrible, horrible. I would never take Wirtz again. His lectures are impossible to pay attention to and the exams are close to impossible. Avoid his class.

I didn't think he was as bad as everyone made him out to be. His class is interesting since he ties in current events to help explain things. It's easy to expect what he wants because he highlights important notes in his slides. Only downside are his test formats like everyone said. Also does a few in-class participation assignments so show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: John Wirtz is really a character, let me tell you. His boring lectures pretty much put me to sleep and it is a struggle to go. Unusual personality but a dry sense of humor. He invented the term "media snacking" and asked us all to tweet about it to get his word trending. Tests are so hard it hurts and every question has almost every letter in it

Content is relevant if you are into public relations/journalism, but often does not make content compelling. Also, kind of rude. Often will call out people for looking on cellphones even though everyone has a computer; kind of hypocritical. Teaching style is lecture heavy with decent amount of reading.

Wirtz has gotten a few bad reviews but honestly he's not that bad of a guy. His lectures are interesting and he makes it clear what he wants you to know. The only thing I don't like are his exams. He has options A,B,C- Only A & B- etc. and it makes you second guess yourself. In order to pass the exams you HAVE to study at least 3 days in advance.

Wirtz is one of the most paranoid professors I have ever come across. He will call out students during class for taking pictures of the slides and gets smart when students ask him to slow down. His cynical and condescending attitude is really off putting. How he has ever had any job involving interactions with other humans is beyond me.

Hated him. Very difficult exams. His questions were always a, b, c, a&b, all of the above type. Asks stupid questions on exams like what did wirtz say about... Random participation 8 times throughout the semester, doesn't post notes online, lots of work in the last 3 weeks of class. Very overwhelming

A bit full of himself and a weird teaching style, but he's fair. All of the information on the tests is covered in lecture (important stuff highlighted). He has so much knowledge to offer if you can get past him being a little preachy. I am certain that I've benefited from taking this class because of the content, and the rest is fine if you try.

What a self-righteous junky egotistical piece of mashed potatoes. Never wrote a book but routinely asks "what did wirtz say about...". Tests are WAY too specific, asks a, b, c, a and b, a b c and d. Most BS professor I've ever had in all of professorship. Doesn't matter how prepared you are, it matters how much he likes your particular class.
Worst math professor i have ever had. Hard to communicate with, bad lecturer, hardly any information posted online. Do not take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Decent professor.

His class was difficult at first until you understand his style. He does not like to answer questions in class. Very helpful in office hours. You will have to take notes in his class because many of his examples actually come out in the exams. His homework was difficult in my opinion but the exams were very straightforward.

Overall the course was very manageable and workload is light to moderate. Exam problems are very similar to homework and depending on how the class does, he also curves the exams. All homework is directly from the textbook. I recommend supplementing the textbook with google. Lecture is not required, but you need to turn in homework every week.

(SP16) Prof. Li is a strong lecturer. The 2 midterms and final were challenging but fair. There's a lot of homework, including graded sets due on exam days. No email use nor use of a grade-tracking system like Compass or Math Score Reports. Text (Ross, Analysis, 2ed) is comprehensive, making attendance optional.

His class is easy overall; as long as you do the homework and understand it, you'll get an A. The tests are very similar to the problems he does in class. However, if you need help, go to a tutor or ask a friend, because he is absolutely no help in office hours. He is very well prepared during lectures, but is unable to answer students' questions.
The lecture is clear and the exam is closely related to the problem he did in class. And he is a kind teacher really.
His homework is very helpful.

At first I was skeptical of Professor Li, but after the first weeks I warmed up to him. He is purely a lecturer so if you ask him how he got an answer, he will just look at you and say "Verify" His rests are just like homework problems and are curved very heavily. If you do the homework and learn the methods rather than the formulas, an A is easy.

After taking many different math courses at the university, I have to say he is the best prof I have ever had.  His examples in the notes are extremely helpful and prepare you well for the exams which are very fair (difficult, but fair). However, he isn't that helpful during office hours. If you go to class and do the work, you're guaranteed an A.

Professor Li is the best math professor I have had at UIUC.  If you can get past his accent, you will find a professor who slowly goes over all the details in an example and focuses on a few examples only. His exams are fair, and his homework prepares you for them.  I wish more professors at this institution were like him.

Awesome teacher! I was really nervous to take Math 347 because of all the bad things i had heard about it.  The material is difficult, but he teaches it really well.  He prepares you for his exams very well, but you have to go to class and take good notes.  If you have to take math 347, i definitely recommend taking it with xiaochun li!

He is a fantastic professor.  His notes are extremely clear! Homework is hard, but exams are fair IF YOU STUDY and go to class!  You have to go to class to get the notes, but other than that it's not bad.  I've heard horror stories about other Math 347 classes, but I promise this one is not bad at all!

Tough subject, but I can see that Prof Spencer genuinely wants her student to understand the knowledge she provided. She keep repeating the concept, asking everyone whether the current concept is clear or not to make sure no one get left behind. This course expect you to spend time study on yourself to catch up, but I really respect Prof Spencer.

*This is for FINN 500, not FINN 411

Without a doubt the worst professor I've personally ever taken. 

Has no idea how to teach a class, she just speeds through the lecture slides and assumes everyone is up to speed. The lessons are all over the place and chaotic, the class has no idea what to focus on. 

Completely unrealistic expectations.

When students start discussing with their peers whether it's about the class topic, problem-solving questions, questions about the calculator, etc. she would be like "May I join the conversation?" "I want 0 talking" "No talking." During quizzes, she walks around and makes me distracted and only have 5 minutes to do the quizzes. No open notes.

I had FIN 411 with her, she is a very sweet and kind person. However, she does a poor job explaining the main concepts. It was not until most of the class failed the first exam that she realized she needed to adjust her teaching methods. Lock-in for this class: I did poorly on the first exam and earned a C+ at the end. Avoid her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor does a poor job explaining core course concepts, is not helpful during office hours, and has quizzes every other class. Exams are hard and course materials are inferior to other professors offering the class. Thus, grades are lower/2nd lowest on average than every other professor offering the class. Strongly recommend avoiding.

She is definitely one of my favorite professors on campus. Her lectures are organized, efficient, and easy to understand. Taking fin 300 with her truly made me interested in the topic and gave me a direction for my career. 100% would recommend taking Fin 300 with her if you are interested in the various financial markets.

She was very helpful and would explain things when people didn't understand. The exams were hard but fair. It wasn't her fault the class sucked because she had to conform to Professor Waspi's ridiculous rules. Overall, she was an amazing professor
She was great.

I loved this professor! They inspired me to get into Neuroscience classes and now it's a part of my field. The class isn't easy, you definitely need to pay attention and study, but the prof gives plenty of opportunities for credit and is very forgiving with grading so long as you try your best. Truly a great class to get started and so fascinating!

Professor Xinzhu is extremely accommodating. My group forgot to submit our project proposal on time and talked to her about it the day after. She gave us full points for the proposal. Rubric and lecture schedules are very clear, tests are a majority of the grade (but the lecture before is a review session), optional textbook, would recommend.

Professor Yu is very clear with what's on exams. Pay attention during lecture and review her slides, you'll get an A in the course. She reviews 80% of material that is covered on the exam the lecture before. The course has 2 midterms,1 group project,1 final, and short weekly discussions. The class is point based and is decently curved at the end.

Foundations of Neuroscience was fun with Prof. Xinzhu, she is very passionate and shows her research examples in her lectures. Lectures are very content heavy and you need to write fast or go to office hours. There is only a few grades, but the review sessions for the exams are very helpful. Her answers to questions are clear, and encouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took 210 with him over summer. The only class where I never had to use outside material. Going to his lecture, though a bit fast paced, will give you everything you need to succeed in every aspect of this class. One of the best professors I've had.

Really solid lecturer. It's obvious he cares about teaching and is very passionate/energetic even during a 1.5 hour lecture. Sometimes the example problems he uses in class to explain new topics can be unnecessarily more challenging than what the course expects of us, but in general he made the class very entertaining.

Chen is an incredible lecturer. One of his lectures is worth more than 3 of another prof's. Has a detailed way of making concepts make sense. However, he holds you to a very high standard; if you make a simple algebra error he will not be forgiving. Even so, he is an amazing prof. I found myself often giving tutoring to students not in his lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor since he explains concepts very clear. He teaches stuffs very organized so even the difficult points are sometimes not hard to understand, so his lectures are significant and don't miss them. Labs and homeworks are also extremely helpful of enhancing the understanding of the lecture materials.
Great professor. Homework can be time consuming sometimes, but if you know how to do the homework you will do fine on the exams.
Took 210 with him over the summer. Gives very clear explanations, and incredibly fair exams. One of the best professors I've had here.

The best lecturer among all the instructors this semester. Exams are mostly from the lectures. He is fair to every student and asks us to rely on our efforts but not curves. This semester professor Xu offers everyone a chance to override the lowest midterm with final. I missed a midterm but rely on that still get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Took the course in summer. Good lecturer. Handled online delivery during the pandemic quite well. Don't miss class.
He's a nice and interesting guy, always well prepared for class. Some people said his loud but actually his voice is okay.
Lectures are simply horrible.

Although this course is easy to get A, you almost learned nothing from it. Professor's lecturing was so boring and sometimes his answers to students' questions were wrong. He seemed not interesting in and responsible for teaching this course. Overall, this course is useless. I would not recommend it at all!

Not good at lecturing-often spends multiple lectures rambling on about the same topics. Project he has us use for the course is buggy and poorly documented. Slow at getting grades out and final exam format was weird (and included stuff we barely even touched on during lecture). Group project is a nightmare. Class overall wasn't too hard, though.

The BEST BEST BEST professor you can ever had for MATH347. Cares about his students, responds fast on campuswire, great lectures and notes to study for your midterms and final. Definitely recommend.
Plus: he grades exams really quick
No

He is a very good professor. The professor has obtained PHD in many schools. I think his confidence in algebra is average, but he is really very tolerant in the exam. He will give two types of questions, A and B. You can choose an A is the argumentation and B is the calculation.  It is very happy to communicate with him.
He really cares about his students, replies fast, medium hard exams.

MATH416 is inherently difficult but Xuesen made passing with a good grade achievable. Grade= homework 30%, midterms 40%, and final 30%. 3 midterms, lowest is dropped. He also made A&B versions for problems on exams. A/proof based, B/more computational. You pick which one. He replies to emails fast, is up late at night, answers questions well.
Not flexible with anything at all
She seems like a nice person but her class, Ace 449, is terrible. Nobody ever knows what is going on in this class and the material is super unorganized and makes it hard to study.

The tests are easy if you know how basic stuff about retirement and pay moderate attention in class. There is an in class assignment each class and you don't get the points if you don't turn it in so attendance is mandatory. No homework otherwise other than a short 10 question quiz the night before class, but you get 2 chances.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If a course with her isn't required don't take it. Otherwise, good luck
Memorize the lecture slides and you'll get an A.   Ask a question beyond what is presented on the slides and you will get directed back to the information that is presented on the slides.

Lots of material but Professor Shao tries to stay on track and be consistent as much as possible. Not 100% of it is understandable at this level but he never makes you feel like you're not smart enough. Grading was pretty lenient, not too tough at all.

Overall, I would definitely recommend taking this course

I took his STAT425 and that is the best statistics class I ever have, he not only teaches students solve statistics problems but also convey the principle ideas. He considerate carefully when preparing the lectures and put himself in the shoes of students. He teaches how the science idea work, not just simply applying R packages.
As of Oct 19, 24 out of 90 students dropped this course... If you are in undergrad, avoid taking this class
Unable to follow the Lectures.

Expert in time series, awful lecturer. The lecture is all over the place. He often uses concepts without defining it, and confuses everyone. The lecture goes super fast. He assumes people are as smart as he is, which at least I am not. Yeah he's an expert, but has no idea how to teach. (ranting completed. going back to study

He over-complicates simple problems; material came from many places so it was difficult to teach yourself; homework was difficult theoretical problems (i.e. complex number parameter estimates), not very applicable; over half the undergrads dropped the course, he should have just made it a grad level course at that point;
Organized with easy midterm. However, the final is on a different level.
Really like this professor! well prepared notes for the class and clear statement.But you have to attend class because his material is different from the books.Though the exams are not easy.

It seems like every lecture is from a different chapter and that some lectures are from "imaginary" chapters because the material isn't found in the textbook we purchased for class. This would be somewhat manageable if you could follow what the guy was saying; I mean how many times can you ask "what is is that or what is this professor?"
Terrible professor!

Professor Shao knows what he's talking about and knows how to answer your questions. He structures the class so you learn a lot of it by yourself. The exams are T/F and usually one or two problems like the homework. He tests you on mostly everything during the final, but you're allowed three cheat sheets. I'd say most people get A's or B's though.

Class is very confusing for much of it because there are no numbers and he wants you to figure it out on your own.  Homework is much harder than the exams.  Exams are mostly homework problems changed slightly and true/false questions.  Final is harder than the midterms, though.  No one got lower than a B though.

Honestly, she wasn't my actual instructor but every time I emailed her about a question that I had, she always responded quickly and she was very nice about it. Many professors give vague answers and don't clarify properly but because she did, it literally made my school work a 1000 times easier after getting the information that I needed.

Dr. Yarrington and my TA, Grace Leyton, have made this class unnecessarily hard and distressing, given that it is still a class requirement for many students. This is the type of TA that will give you zero credit for tiny mistakes, or take off major credit and only give you a line of feedback. They expect you to get everything automatically.

She is very nitpicky about literally everything. She says she does not expect you to learn everything right away yet expects you to pick up on concepts and very specific things right away after seeing them for the first time. There are assignments every class and multiple exams. She counts going to the bathroom as missing part of class.

Because it was hybrid I didn't have her as my instuctor for the majority of the time, that being said, my ta was an absolute godsend. He was amazing and did the best he could with what he had, but in my and my classmates eyes, the curriculum is horrendous. I wish I had enough space to talk about it.

They changed the Span 122 so it is hybrid, I didn't see much of the actual professor, my Ta was amazing though. There is kind of a lot of homework through out the week and it gets VERY repetitive quickly. I wish there was more focus on really learning the vocab in the book and in class. Everyday in discussions you have to work with someone else.

She is a fine professor, if a bit stiff. She was not very helpful in class but when asked specific questions outside of class she actually gives great feedback. The class is far too difficult to be a 100 level class. There is way too much material to get through every week which means there's less attention to detail on each assignment.

Really harsh grader and the group assignment at the end of the class was way too hard for a 100 course. Doesn't explain grammar in class so students aren't where they need to be. She also wasn't that good at Spanish and is the director of the program which was confusing.
lots of redundant homework and weekly timed quizzes.

Overall, she is not bad. She is friendly in class and helps out when she can. I will say there is a lot of homework, but each assignment takes less than 5 minutes. She also does not lecture in class. You have to watch videos embedded in the assignments to learn anything.

Class was the same every day + she doesn't always speak in Spanish/seem enthusiastic, which is sometimes annoying. Overall she was helpful in 1 on 1 meetings, but this is a class you definitely can't miss due to attendance points + you have to really try on the few big assignments, because they're worth a lot of the grade.
She is really enthusiastic about what she teaches and a generally nice person, whose teaching style is very easily understood.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Yarrington is not a bad professor, but don't expect her to explain everything that you're working on. You must work outside of class. That's the only way I passed this class. I have nothing to compare her to, but I enjoyed the classes and she is undoubtedly enthusiastic about teaching. I would recommend but be prepared for some work.

Professor Yarrington is an excellent teacher. The only criticism I have is she does not do a lot of teaching. You watch videos outside of class and in class all you really do is speaking exercises. She is very helpful and will help you if you do not understand what is going on. Overall, I would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Kara Yarrington is not a teacher. First off, she does not know how to speak Spanish at all. She will speak in English 75% of the time and for the remainder 25% she will say basic phrases that you would learn in your first year of Spanish. Her idea of a lesson is getting in groups and answering questions on a powerpoint, or watching a buzzfeed video
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Was teaching one of my classes for a week as a substitute and it was absolutely ridiculous. Was glad when our teacher came back. Extremely impatient and if you dont know the answer will make a very big scene out of it. Only had her for a week but made the class extremely uncomfortable. Try to find anyone but her for Span122

Class wasn't too bad. 2 papers & no final. Read the rubric carefully on compass because points will be taken off for minor things like stylistic choices/title. Textbook was useless, but you need it for the online homework (do it in a group, 2 tries per person, the more people the more tries you get).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course was average. Studying lecture notes and sample exams will be sufficient. He curved midterms.
Avoid at all costs. Take the course at Parkland or something, you'll actually end up learning more because of how poorly this course it taught. Terrible lectures, terrible labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor who is very knowledgeable on the topics which he teaches. Always available for help and want's to see you succeed. The class is tough but it really sets a foundation for understanding more complex environmental concepts that are applicable in the world. Grading was tough, but fair. Extra credit offered often which is great.

I've taken classes at 3 different colleges over 3 years including UIUC, and this is by far the worst class I have taken, worse than gen chem, calc or anything. And it's a shame, because the professor is a nice guy and funny. The lectures are useless and attendance is mandatory, lab quizzes are awful. You can learn everything just from the book.
Do the extra credit work. It helped my exam grade.

Really made an effort to get to know students. Helped lead lab and was very friendly and lab was very fun. Hard class but he makes it entertaining. Lectures aren't technically mandatory but he will notice if you miss any lectures. Honestly made the class much more interesting than expected.
Extra credit helped me but I needed to attend lectures to get assignment questions

This professor is a luddite. No recording his lectures, no phones, no laptops, no tablets, not even graphing calculators. Frequently went off lecture to rant about the dangers of technology. Made inappropriate comments to some of the students - no wonder he didn't want any recordings of his lectures.
He was very accomodating and easy to talk to.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Arai was a decent teacher. He always provided study guides, which were a huge help on exams. It was definitely hard to get through the material because it could be boring and he's not the most lively person. Also, the only thing you get graded on is labs and exams, so that makes the whole class more difficult.

He is a great professor and even better person. He truly wants the best for you and helps you to highest level. You have to put in the work though. Not an easy A. Gives you study guides but although attendance isn't mandatory I would treat it like if it was. The LECTURES are how I passed, but to get a great grade, READ!
Great professor who truly cares for his students. The class is really informative and I learned a lot.
Do well on your problemset. Exams are not easy but he curved every exam.
Exams are multiple choice questions and calculations. Fortunately he curved all exams. Labs and quizzes were easy.
Do the study guides! They're very helpful.
It wasn't as bad as I thought. I found this class to be a little challenging, but the exams were always curved.

The class was good... an interesting information about soils. 3 tests and you can drop one so I didn't take the third one. He gave a study guide before each exam. There was a big curve for exams. Labs and quizzes were super easy.
Lab and pop/grp quizzes were easy. Exams were curved, but they were challenging. It is easy to get a B in this class.

Class was difficult, attendence is not mandatory but the pop quizzes make up about 20% of your grade. Tests are all 50 question multiple choice and are difficult. He does curve the class but it is still difficult to get a good grade. Do not take unless required, and do not miss class.

His lectures are boring and don't teach the material very well, but the class overall is well organized. He offers extra credit for doing homework early and full credit for attending the discussion. There are 5 CBTF midterms; each midterm is worth a chunk of your grade. As long as you can teach yourself the material, it's easy to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't listen to other rating
He is a very good prof, and you can get a lot from his lectures. You will get an A as long as you follows his step, listen carefully to his lectures and do the HW by yourself.

Easy A, but not worth it. Exams are super simple, and essays basically guarantee an A, but the teaching quality is really poor. Lectures are unorganized, and explanations are unclear. If you just want an easy grade, take it—but don't expect to actually learn much.
Very good professor, the content is easy, exam is easy. You will receive a good grade as long as you work hard.
Very easygoing and caring professor, would recommend.

Yucong is a professor that always cuts you off when you ask a question. Expect to learn more outside of class from YouTube videos opposed to learning from the professor himself. His assignments and grading is fair, which is good, but his actual lectures are so hard to follow, as he just looks off his phone during lecture to copy his examples down.
Really good professor, exams are easy and explain complex analysis very well
His class is very easy, exams can be covered by the exercise. Office hour is detailed analysed is you bring you problems to him.
Exams would be easy if you finish exercises assigned for review. Office hour is helpful and he is easygoing.
Dude is nice and easygoing, the amount of homework is far less than I anticipated. And by going through the practices he assigns or recommends, the exams are going to be extremely easy.
He is a very good prof. Complex Ana is diffcult, but I got a good score in his class and learnt a lot. No attandance, exercrise before exams.
Great, exam is easy, practice is enough.
Not a good teacher, gets lowest grade in class, learns nothing. Speaking is bad, OH is not helpful. He ruined my dream to be a successful mathematician!!!

AlthoughTheFinalisFairlyEasyAndTheGradingCutoff is lower(45/50forA+,42/50for A), the midterm is difficult all questions are writing proof and definitions; before the exams: no practice questions or completely irrelevant questions. Apart from that, grading of the homework is harsh, a small mistake may trigger the whole points off.Avoid JIANG YUCONG!
Exam questions have no relationship to the stuff he taught in lectures. He can't even explain questions clearly during OH.
Not a good professor, Exams are hard, no curve. Go back to UofToronto.  No practice exam, lectures are not helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not recommended

Took this as an easy class for credit hours. The material is not difficult, but the assignments are tedious. The class follows a typical online format (weekly discussion post and 2 replies + assignment), but the weekly assignments come out to 3 pages single spaced minimum. Never had trouble w/ online classes before but this one was genuinely awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: 117 is not hard but is busy. Assignments are due 3 times a week & turned in on time. Grading is done by TAs and Dr Carey. Dr Carey and the TAS  are very flexible. if you have problems during the semester makes sure you email Dr Carey, she will help. I had some health problems and couldn't gett my work in on time and she was helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's an easy class but has lots of assignments. The graders won't respond but Prof. Carey will if you email her. Busy class but easy.
Dr Carey really helped me out, this is an easy class but I missed some due dates because I've had a hard time lately. Dr. Carey was supportive and even emailed to see how I was.
Good gen ed. class, Dr Carey responds quickly and will help you out with deadlines and the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Asynchronous class, the class has a lot of papers with a lot of graders. If you contact Professor Carey she will work with you on the content. The readings are not hard, there is just a lot of work to turn in weekly. Good class.

Class is a requirement. Professor Carey is available and wants you to think about the material, grading by TAs is tough. There is a lot of short papers but they are not hard. If you put the work in the class changes how you think about diversity issues. I recommend it.
super easy A gened. As long as you follow the rubric on assignments you will get a full score. Lots of reading but you don't really need to read them to do the assignments. Dr. Carey super nice
Super dumb grading standards, unclear and unnecessary requirements for papers that leave students feeling stressed. You're better off taking another gen ed unless you're willing to deal with bull

Professor does not teach anything and is just rude. Class is just reading articles/books and writing reflections on them. One midterm paper and one final paper and one discussion post/2 replies and weekly assignment a week. Ridiculous grading standard. Takes of points for no reason and does not give any justification. NO REGRADES. Lot of work for A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Interesting class. Readings and videos are easy to follow, assignments take time but not too hard.
Do not recommend this course. Ridiculous standard of grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: TON of work but Yvonne is awesome. She LOVES this stuff, she gets you excited about it and shows you how to use all of the ideas in your own room.
This class is a ton of work, it's way to much reading but well worth it. She's a great professor, loves to teach and talk about learning. It's good fun in the class too.
Amazing lectures and timely feedback. Goat
Amazing lectures and timely feedback. Goat!
Amazing lecturer, explains clearly and patiently, very kind in office hours, creates fair grading rubrics

This is truly a math-dense but very very interesting course. If you are interested in why ml classifies a camel on the grass as a horse, why we can retrieve all sensitive information from a netflix database with sensitive info hided, etc., definitely consider taking this course! Professor Zhao explains all concepts very clearly and inspirationally.

446 is a theoretical course and requires a solid foundation in linear algebra and probability. Prof Zhao is good at explaining intuition and mathematical concepts behind the ML model. You can definitely learn a lot through this class.

Prof. Zhao explains complex math derivations extremely clearly, with both rigorous proof done on paper and nice intuitions. His exams and homeworks are pretty tough requiring thorough understanding of math. Very knowledgeable professor, definitely recommend.

His logic flow is really clear and he explains every concept thoroughly. His pronunciation is clear and he teaches with passion. The math formulas become really simple with his explanation and he always raises a lot of inspirational questions which I think is the best takeaway from his course. Hope to take CS442 as early as possible with him!

You can never know why he is so tough. His course is hard to understand and has no use about your project. I have to say it is a waste of time. And even if you follow his rubric, you still do not know why he gives you a low grade. Well, perfect.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredible instructor. I honestly felt out of my depth for the majority of his course, but Han has an incredible ability to break down and explain dense concepts. Topics are very well-motivated and interesting. Homeworks are entirely proof-based and very tough but rewarding. Highly recommend his course for those with some ML background.

Zohreh Sullivan is my favorite teacher/person I've met during my time at college. She's caring, hilarious and one of the most intelligent and inquisitive people I know. (She also retired many many years ago)

I took Professor Sullivan's ENGL 274 class.  I entered her class with very little interest in the subject matter, but I found that her passion for the material made the class very interesting.  At times I felt that she was overly critical of ideas with which she did not agree, but overall I believe that the class was taught very well.

Professor Sullivan is an extremely charismatic speaker and is one of those rare teachers who not only helped me "read the world," but also greatly increased my analytical reading skills with her engaging material on globalization and the relevance it still has today. Definitely an interested class to take.

If there's one word to describe professor Sullivan, it would be passionate. Part of what makes this course so interesting is the excellent assortment of literature she has compiled, along with her deep knowledge in the subject. I went into the class not even knowing what "diaspora" meant, and left feeling incredibly educated.

I took professor Sullivan's poetry class in the early 1970's.  I knew little about poetry before taking her class. She made inscrutable poetry meaningful and interesting. I still love her interpretation of Yeats' "Sailing to Byzantium" and TS Eliot's "Lovesong of J. Alfred Prufrock". I am glad to discover that she is still teaching.Thanks Zohreh!

She is very nice and means well. The class is extremely boring and dull. Quizzes are easy but unexpected so be sure to always do the readings. As long as you do the work in this class you will be fine!

A great professor who is always willing to help students. She always put off the deadlines=) She makes ENGL112 more interesting and enjoyable. If you do all the readings and writings, you will get an A. (PS. In fact there is not much work to do. She even cancels assignments to help students.)

Great teacher.  Very interesting.  The assignments are pretty easy if you listen in class, so attendance is really important.  Overall, a great class.  Take her classes if they're offered.  She's semi-retired though, so I don't know how long they'll be offered.

Although I received a good grade in the only class I took with her, she told me that I would be better off applying for a masters degree elsewhere since my work would not be "up to par" with what get me into that particular university.  I assumed she would be the first to encourage any of her students to apply anywhere.

She has a very interesting background and her accent is adorable! Overall, I think the class did not allow for in-depth discussion of the texts, since it was mainly a lecture, but the political and historical knowledge of world events that came from this class is invaluable.
Great Teacher!

She is a great teacher! She loves what she's doing and is very passionate...which makes it more interesting for the students. Although I hated reading Kim, the rest of the books were very interesting and not alot of hmk was required besides readings. It's a freshman only class, and a great lit to start off with.

She seems to care about her students, so she'll change due dates and give extra assignments (for points) if you bring it up.  Also, I love British accents... the only bad thing is that all she did was summarize the books in class.  Minimal analysis and not much room for interpretation/creativity : (

Professor Sullican was extremely nice, very funny, and did everything in her power to try to make class interesting. (she succeeded). She was always more than willing to help and was very accomodating. Also, the work was very little...read and push some effort into the homework and you will get an A.

Professor Sullivan is a sweet, witty, and extremely intelligent woman who loves to work her students.  Lots and lots of reading that you MUST keep up with to get a good grade in the course, as all of her quizzes and tests are based on readings and movies we watch in class.

Took several classes with Prof. Sullivan, several years ago. She is one of the best teachers I have ever had, brilliant, knowledgeable, into the material, witty. Definitely not for those who are unwilling to work.   And she used to be very attractive in a kind of a British upper class way, but as I said, this was some years ago.

She's so intelligent that she doesn't really know how to speak to students. She's so confusing, but if you do the readings you'll be fine. If you don't like lit., definately don't take this class with her.
Great! funny too
She's a very smart professor. Tries very hard to accomodate students. Be prepared to use compass and if you plan on sleeping you may as well stay home and sleep there because she'll embarass you.
Professor Sullivan is a great teacher.  Her passion in both her subject matter and students engage the students.
Very smart, but it is difficult to understand her.  And she has a hard time keeping my interest in what she is saying.
Brilliant lady, but do not sleep in her class. she's nice and flexible but embarrasses people when they fall asleep. some of the books are really boring.
very smart lady, but really unorganized and really bad to take notes with.  if you dont like compass, dont take this class.
very intelligent person; sometimes disorganized
Professor Zhang was always super excited and energetic when lecturing. She explained topics clearly and provided several examples for all concepts.

Professor Zhang has a very structured teaching style which makes her lectures very organized and easy to follow. She is super kind and go out of her way to help the students. She is very responsive and gets back to the students quickly about all the questions. From what I learned, I would definitely recommend the professor and this class.

Susu is an amazing professor. The lecture is easy to follow and uses many examples to solidify the conceptual topics in the class. The workload is very manageable and the professor is very willing to help and clarify the contents. Best instructor I have ever had!

Super nice professor, very understanding and flexible. Lectures can be long and sometimes boring, but not difficult. As long as you read over the slides and practice doing the example questions + practice exams, you should be good.

This guy is so intentionally and unintentionally funny and it's the best thing ever. Very kind and helpful

professor is super nice

g o a t, super nice and flexible

Amazing.

one of the best professors. Please take his class!

absolutely loved this class. i took this class online sadly but albert is the best and i'd recommend this class 10/10.

He is generous on grading that he would scale the scores up if the overall grade was not ideal. But you may not learn much during the lecture.

I'm so glad I'm taking this class for the first semester as an undergraduate because it gives me so much confidence that I can learn things all by myself. I'm not going to hesitate to choose 1 point professor anymore.   He is actually very cute, smiling all the time. The material is more difficult than the other section. Useful?- I don't know.
Reads off of slides and doesn't explain the material well (expects for you to have an above average understanding of the material presented)
Can't listen a word if you go to the lecture. He seems so into his own world and do not care about what his students are doing. Exams are so much harder than the other section.

One of the worst professors at UIUC. He comes to a 50 minutes class 10-15 minutes late. Mostly tries to read slides, but even that not correctly, he mumbles, makes mistakes, does not correct himself. It's a mystery to me how he conducts research.

The material is already pretty hard to understand, and the professor simply reads off the slides (from 10 years ago) in lectures. MPs are poorly designed and often contain mistakes. Although the final grade cutoff was pretty generous, it's not an enjoyable class and you don't really learn much.

Hard, not very interesting subject material made worse than it had to be. Not sure if uninterested or just totally lacks lecturing skill. Reading the book section the lecture slides had been taken from was much more helpful than lecture. Despite 10% extra credit attendance quizzes almost no one showed up.

He put zero effort in this class: the "lecture" consisted of him reading ppt slides that had code copy-pasted from the book; the MPs were unclear and they changed the requirements multiple times before the deadline (even the day it was due, for the last one); the exams contained bogus material; two out of the three TAs were useless

Agha is not a great lecturer. A lot his lecture slides were just lines and lines of code which he skimmed by very quickly while mumbling. The MPs were *terrible*, although I believe that one of the TAs (Minas) was in charge of those. TONS of revisions and extensions due to bugs, and an incredible amount of confusion and anger on piazza.

MP's were scarcely debugged before release, prompting multiple confusing changes. MP's are generally brutal and have little connection to the lectures, which lack student interaction and are taught quite badly. Office hours aren't too helpful and tests are too long for the average student to finish. Overall, more trouble than this class was worth.

Certainly he is an incredible instructor. MATH417 covers basic abstract algebra, which is supposed to be abstract. But he always gives you many concrete examples to help you understand. Always accessible through email/office hours (he has many office hours) so make good use of them! Take a course with him if you can!
One of the finer professors at UIUC, glad I was able to learn from him.
Goated lecturer and tests were super fair, I'd take his Calc 3 class over anyone else any day of the week. One of the best profs of all time at UIUC.

Professor Ahlgren is an incredible teacher. To have the best benefit from lectures, read the sections from the textbook ahead. The discussion worksheet is very useful for exams + the examples done in class. Go to the review lecture before a test. He is a very fair professor. Tough course that needs consistent study but very rewarding!

Flat out awesome. Great lecturer. Goes over basic ideas, then works his way up. Very easy to follow. Often provides nice proofs and examples. Also provides a great notes template. Always answers questions on Campuswire in a timely manner. Tests are very fair; expects you to know what he taught you, nothing more. Best MATH241 professor by a mile!

Professor Ahlgren is a great teacher; he's very friendly and understanding. As long as you attend the lectures and discussions, you should be fine. The exams are manageable as long as you study for them, and make sure to ask questions in discussion because the concepts can be very confusing.

Amazing professor, probably best math professor you will get. The lectures go in depth to proofs, so don't worry if you sometimes get lost. He is great at answering questions and makes sure no question goes unnoticed. SHOW UP TO LECTURE BEFORE A TEST. Amazing grader on tests and very fair tests.

Professor Ahlgren was extremely knowledgeable, engaging, and funny during lectures. Exams (the majority of the grade) were very fair, based on applying the course's concepts--do study theorems well--you learn in reasonable problems, instead of making you lose points with ridiculously hard algebra.
Overall a fantastic professor to take Calc 3 with.

One of the best professors you could take a math course with. He made a 200+ student lecture hall feel like a small high school classroom and you could tell he genuinely wanted every student to understand the coursework. Tests were fair, but still required a decent amount of studying as Math 241 is an inherently difficult course no matter what.

Literally the best professor you can wish for. Robust lecture notes, reasonable workload, extremely responsive on CampusWire, and exams are of fair difficulty. Hilarious dude but often makes calculation mistakes (just like us) so keep an eye on him and pay attention in lecture!
Best professor so far, I love you Professor Ahlgren

Best lecturer in my freshman year. I love this middle-aged humerous guy. Perfect pace of instruction, always finishes all the content in time. He is the only pfs that contributes directly to my grade, and also the reason why Calc3 is my only A+ of the semester.
His lectures are very clear and worth attending. The tests are very fair. If you do all the practice problems, youre set for his exams. One of the best Math Professor.

Strong lecturer and very clear that he's passionate about the content. Relatively fair 1-hour exams. Very friendly to students. Wish that he went through entire solutions during lecture and that he gave templates of what will be on the exams. Personally, I hated Calc 3, but I'm glad he was my prof (compared to the other guy).
The best math professor I've ever had. He explained things really clearly and made tests very fair.

I don't vibe with Scott, but seeing how many students enjoy his lectures, I can't change his rating. He will make a mistake when writing out a problem and then wordlessly change things without explaining, and he likes to say "I have X minutes left and I'll use them" when class ended 3 minutes ago, but most of his students love his enthusiasm.
You know he is goated when attendance is not mandatory and yet more than 80% of students still show up to his lectures

Literally unreal. Haven't taken an exam yet but he is organized and provides his lecture notes. Most math teachers just lecture nonsense and you can't understand them. He cares, he responds to campuswire posts, he tries to make lecture engaging, and he is very reasonable. AMAZING, TAKE IF U CAN.
Ahlgren is probably the best professor in the math department. I would definitely take him if you have the chance.

He explained concepts very well and made sure that students understood the concepts. Homework was sometimes challenging but he would always help during office hours or by email. He was accessible outside of class and made all students feel welcome.
Great lectures and a great guy.

Awesome professor! Really good at explaining concepts, and spends a lot of time with students. Quirky but in a fun way. Exams are quite easy, homework are somewhat challenging, but very helpful in office hours. Joined the class late but he made me feel welcome and fit in right away.

He is an amazing professor! He makes the best jokes in class, very laidback, and his class was so fun! His exams are extremely fair, he pushed back the due dates for the homework, and he is very accessible outside of class. He is a really nice guy and really cares for his students and likes his students. He also wore silly shirts which was fun.

If you get the chance to take him, do it! His classroom always felt accepting and encouraging, so I was never afraid to ask questions, even if he'd gone over them before. You can tell he really cares about the students and wants everyone to succeed.

Prof. Ahlgren was so, so nice and patient. One time, I submitted the wrong homework assignment, and he let me turn it in 3 days later for full credit! He's very compassionate and kind. Amazing professor.
Gem of a teacher. Lectures are extremely helpful and develop both theory and problem-solving techniques. He's always ready to help his students and goes the extra mile. Would highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Ahlgren really cares about teaching. His lectures contain his own understanding to the topic. Exams are not hard. He gives a lot of office hours, around three or four hours per week, and he is quite friendly during office hours.

Ahlgren is an awesome professor. He actually made calc 2 a great way to start the day. Lectures were some derivations and tons of examples, which is exactly what you need for the class. Not to mention, he's got a great sense of humor and is pretty down-to-earth, though he is really quirky, even bordering on awkward. Good guy, great teacher.
Do the extra practice problems in the book  A's on the midterms

Great professor even though the course can be tough for a lot of people. It's really important to study in this class, this is a subject that can trip people up, and a lot of difficult problems can show up on exams and get you. Funny guy too

He's a really really great professor! In the beginning, it was hard to keep up with what he was doing but as time went  on, I eventually got used to the fast pace of the course. Make sure you do the homework and use the office hours. And make sure you STUDY! Can't emphasize how many points I got off for silly mistakes on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's really funny and loves what he does.

He is a good lecturer. He is a really fair grader and explains every topic fairly clearly. I would recommend him if you are planning to take calc 2. He is also hilarious. Would recommend him for sure.

Professor Ahlgren is amazing!  He is really funny and makes math lecture an extremely pleasant place to be.  He is definitely the best choice for a Calc 2 professor.  I strongly recommend him.  He gives lots of good examples and explains everything very clearly!
He is the best math professor I have ever met. I love his lectures and he makes me really like math.
Lectures are hilarious! He really tries to get you interested in class with his many jokes (some self-depreciating). Really helpful prof, test not so hard. Got calc 2? Save urself by takin this prof.
Best Cacl II professor in this university!! Just take his class.
Great professor, had him for calc 2 made it enjoyable with jokes and made himself available  for students all the time.

His lectures are funny and self-deprecating. He goes out of his way to add extra office hours. He discourages rote memorization in favor of being able to work out the formulas you need.  Great prof, very likable.

This class is only easy if you actually do the work--there are online problems twice a week at most and they take about 2 hours, less if you know what you're doing/doing it with other people. Lectures are actually fun; he's funny so he keeps you engaged
He is clear when he teaches the material and makes it fun with his sense of humor.
Very clear and very nice guy. He goes through examples well! Tests are manageable, and sometimes curves.
Great guy. Tells bad jokes all the time. The lectures are well-organized. Attendance is not required and not much homework. He is kind and reasonable.
He is a very engaging professor, and his lectures are very easy to understand.

His lecture is truly superior to other professors in the department. It truly is worthwhile to go and is rarely booring. He is easier than Murphy 220 in my opinion. He does not reach out as much as Murphy did, but he provides an excellent tutoring center hosted by the TA's. Do the webassign review for exams, very similar.
Ahlgren is very funny and teaches the concepts in a way that is easy to understand. If you do the homework and attend lectures the course won't be hard.
He's humorous and explains things quite well.

overall, this is a doable class. alhgren teaches in way everyone can understand. the online hw is very easy and actually helpful. tests are easy considering the difficulty level of the material you are learning. only problem is the quizzes- one per week on material you just learned. if you prepare for those a small amount, you'll do fine

Though the class was interesting and he taught very well, his lack of concern for a students and his poor choice of TA affect the class. He showed no interest correcting a TA's unprofessional behavior in class.
Great professor!! The classes are very interesting. The professor is very funny and helpful. So is my TA. The class is not that hard if you read the book and go to lecture.
I love my life after taking his class. He's the best teacher ever. He makes math fun!!

Material is taught in an organized and understandable manner, with lots of bright chalk. Exams fairly test the material covered in lecture/discussion. Homework & discussions are helpful and doable. Questions are answered in a clear way. Lectures are fun and entertaining. Take his class and you will love yourself. And join the facebook fan club!

tests were difficult but there was never anything that we didn't go over in class. hw was tough, about 2 written and 2 online per week, the writtens usually took me about 3 hrs, they had some very hard problems. if you pay attention he makes little comments in lectures that are hilarious. he goes too fast but was always very helpful in office hours
Nice and entertaining teacher.  Online homework are easy points and written homework isn't too bad either.  Exams cover material from class and homework and are very fair.
Nice and helpful teacher. Go to his office hours. But classes can be tough. Toughes class in cal II.
Teaches the class very well and always answers students' questions during lecture. Has a pretty good sense of humor as well. Wish he tough all the math classes.
Best math teacher I've ever had! Explains everything well and in an entertaining manner. Made math easier and more fun than ever before!

Ahlgren is great.  But calc 2 is difficult regardless of who you get.  But if you are able to, definitely get ahlgren over anyone else.  He is a funny guy, doesn't have a foreign accent, and is good at making things clear.
Best math teacher I've ever had.
take his class, and you will feel Math is wonderful. I will request everyone to take his class!!!!
He's the best math teacher ive ever had....and he's a babe
He is awesome!!!Take his class!!!

This man is a genius, interesting, funny, all around awesome.  I loved going to lectures.  Don't get me wrong though, it was a hard class and required a lot of studying (it was the engineering section of calc II though).  He is even mentioned in the wikipedia page about number theory.  TAKE THIS MAN'S CLASS!!!
He's a great professor. I was doing terrible in the class and the only reason I didn't drop it was because of him. Turned out to be a really good class.
nice professor!
Oh if only you knew...
AMAZING professor! The best I've ever had. He has a great sense of humor, keeps the class entertained and is passionate about calculus... Which makes it a little more fun to study.

Excellent professor.  Makes the lectures somewhat funny with lots of nerdy jokes.  Explains things very well but it is a fairly difficult yet very reasonable class.  There ended up being a pretty big curve at the end.  It's good to go to the lectures even though there aren't any quizzes or anything.  Overall a good class and good professor.
Very good lecturer.  He is funny.  He is smart.  He is very clear.  But his classes are quite challenging.  NOT an easy A at all.  I highly recommend you guys take his lecture.
Good teacher and good guy.  This was my first semester of college and I could tell he really wanted to help me and the rest of his students.  Class is tough, but he always makes himself available.
Very enthusiastic and willing to explain unclear problems.  Very knowledgeable and actually wants to teach.

By far one of the best professors I had at U of I. I went into this class with 0 background on calc. I walked out with a B. That B was because of his great teaching, humorful attitude, and clarity in explanations. If you put the time in, he puts the time in. Take it as a discovery course is he still teaches. You get your tuition worth with Prof A.

Wants his students to succeed. The class I took was about 20 kids and met for 7 hours a week, but it was time well spent. The practice exams are EXACTLY like the real ones, and with a decent amount of effort you can get an A. Best teacher I've had at U of I. Very helpful and I loved the math jokes. Take this class!
Very clear and motivating.  A lot of work but that's the same with any calc class. i recommend him, especially for the First Year Discovery class for freshman.
Good teacher, but lacks confidence that kinda effects his teaching a bit.  Exams are more difficult than most teachers'.
Awesome teacher, sadly has a little too much math humor but it's funny to hear what he has to say, very helpful and stresses important points!
Awesome teacher, explains concepts well. Exams and quizzes reflected homework assignments. Quite possibly the best math professor I've had to date.
HE'S AWESOMEEE

He cares about the students and wants everyone to get an A. The class isn't curved, so he finds ways to give extra credit. He missed a few lectures so the first two test averages were awful. So he offered a makeup exam that could replace the lower of the two scores and put extra credit on that & the third exam. Very nice & approachable. No final.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Elbanna's class. He cares about his students and kept asking for feedback on his course. The exams are take home and the book is free online. The only hard thing for me was the MatLab projects as this was my first time using the software. TAs are really helpful.
One of the best prof. ever had. Very helpful, explains very wells.

This professor is very patient and friendly. His lecture is very focused on concepts and behavior rather than just solve problems. Also, it's one of the rare "do your job and you'll get an A" course! The only down side I can say about him is his lecture notes are not very detailed, but that is not a problem if you write down what he says.

Grading was very lax, but the course could have been run much, much better. He was often late to lecture and it seemed like he didn't have a lesson plan and was just winging it. Spent little time discussing homework, the project, exam prep, etc, in lecture and instead made you go to office hours to talk about it which wasn't always convenient.

She has since restructured the class since the past reviews. One reading every week, discussion about it on both class days. A group final project at the end of the semester. She is pretty chill and likes discussion in the classroom. Lots of extra credit opportunities. Would recommend for a gen-ed class.
