Very easy to understand, if you put in the time, you should expect to do well. Very lenient grading, as she cares more so about you understanding concepts rather than if you can type everything in the correct order on your calculator.  Her policies in general are also more than fair. If you ever go up to her she will be able to explain things well.

She has very specific requirements for her homework that are just formatting, so it's just unnecessary busy work - due every lecture.  The course itself isn't too hard because there are 4 exams for 10% each, and she repeats a lot of the iClicker questions.  Lab reports are a burden, but they graded more easily as the semester went on.

while this is a 101 class it is NOT easy!! The topics were rushed and work and variables were not explained. You were expected to have background knowledge in physics even though it is an introductory course. Professor was not very helpful either, and the tests were heavily weighted compared to the rest of the work.

Although its "101", it's NOT easy. Topics were crammed &not explained well.  Discussion was useless & my TA confused me more. Stay on top of the material! I wouldn't have minded less demonstrations& more time to discuss problem solving. He's a bright professor & I think this made it harder for him to teach at 101 level to non-majors.

He was the lecturer for my physics course. The course was bad  because they crammed as many topics as they could into 1 semester. Especially towards the end I learned nothing from lecture because he spent the whole time doing demonstrations that We didn't actually go over concepts. He tried to go over what students struggled with but failed mostly.

Very interesting class. You meet twice a week, once when she lectures, and another time with your group. The whole semester has one grade, a group project with about 10 people. You read a few small books, watch movies, and create one long document. She also cancels lectures about 5x a Semester. Super easy class, basically no way to not get an A.
she's funny

She's really sweet. Wasn't a terrible class, but lectures got quite boring. The class was self-run for the most part. She gives you things to read/watch and then answer questions for research. You get one graded assignment: the semester-long project. You only meet in person once weekly, and the other class day you meet with your project group.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had so much fun in this class! Attending his office hours was also so insightful, and I got to learn a lot more about BIOE during them. The class is very basic in terms of content, and the workload mirrors that. Overall, a great experience, and you word with other people almost every class.
Very understanding, passionate, and positive professor! Also, super relatable and easy to get along with. Great, low effort but very educational class, worth taking.
Absolute GOAT, enough said
Thank you for being such a nice professor and making our class entertaining
100000/10 bro easiest class and ansari made it super interesting. dw ur in good hands
Amazing inspiration for future bioengineers

No words can describe the GOAT. Legendary professor. He made this super difficult class really easy. He explained the course content really well, and was always open to having us in his office to answer whatever questions we had. Very fair grading, fun assignments and projects. Take this class with him if you can.
Cares a lot about student well-being and success and is very accessible through office hours. Dr. Ansari's slides and lectures are engaging and fun.
Truly an unreal teacher who cares about students more than I have ever experienced. Take his classes if you can.
Greatest Of All Time
He is an amazing guy, and really makes you feel cared about in ENG 100

The GOAT. One of the best professors in the Bioe departments. Amazing lectures, very fun and interactive.

Professor Ali is a great guy. The material was a little tough, but he made it really interesting and fun. He is easily accessible outside class.

Ask him about his One piece card collection
da best
She was tough but AMAZING! I was struggling after the first exam, she put time into helping me and was sooo helpful and honest! I would love to have her all the time!
She is so knowledgeable and kind. She prepared everyone well for the weekly quizzes and all exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: great professor, clearly knows her stuff. early quizzes are heavy and important to grade but just keep up with the reading and show up and you'll be fine.

I don't think I've loved a professor more. She's incredibly funny and helpful. She knows a lot about anything you would ever need help with. The class is difficult but she makes it manageable and worth it!

This is honestly a tough class, you need to keep up constantly keep up with. If I had any other instructor for this course, I would not have done as well. She explains concepts very well, especially in office hours. The weekly 8:30 AM Monday quizzes are a pain, but they force you to keep up with the material so you don't fall behind!

Dr. Pucilwowski is great! You can tell she is super knowledgable on the subject. She is also very approachable. SHS 300 was tough, but Dr. P makes it very clear what you need to memorize for the quizzes and exams.
I love Dr. Pucilowski! If you put effort into your work/ studying, it will be very rewarding. She's helpful and always wants to see you succeed.

Professor P. is a great professor! She is so intelligent and her knowledge in speech in hearing sciences makes you love the major even more. She runs a more challenging course, but it really shapes you into a better student. I 100% would take more of her classes.

Professor Ansell was clear that the student's needs & learning were prioritized. She was very accommodating. Exam's were fair as long as you studied her slides and knew how to apply them. Her lecture videos are posted online and she offered lots of extra credit opportunities. This class was a little harder than 101, so expect to put in more effort.
Explains things very well and clearly wants students to do well.

Her lectures (w/ I-Clicker) only covered the foundational idea of the material, but her slides are helpful to review on your own. Her homework assignments were typically much harder than the exams; I would focus on studying the conceptual material she talks about during class and the exams she posts on PrairieLearn. Definitely go to office hours.

Professor Ansell was always so sweet and enthusiastic about course content. Definitely attend lecture and discussion, as both will help you piece together the material and figure out what will be on the exam. Exams were usually pretty easy. Plenty of extra credit as well. Having never taken a physics course before, I did fine without excess effort.

I respect professor Ansell's ethics a lot: her exams are hard, but absolutely fair. You can do well on all of them if you do the homework (without cheating), go to office hours, and actively participate in discussion. A lot of work, but designed to be manageable. She's very transparent about the exams. One of my favorite classes I've taken!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: She works really hard on her lectures and her tests are really fair if you put in the work ; this class is really enjoyable and i wish she taught more courses !

The structure of this class changed and I found that helpful. There were 6 exams + a final which was daunting but was helpful to stay on track with the current material. The exams were reflective of the practice exams and weren't too difficult if you practiced the problems and went over the slides for understanding/memorizing concepts.

Prof. Ansell created a great learning environment. Highly recommend for anyone who was scared out of taking physics in high school. Structure of exams was every two weeks (daunting, but super manageable), and there were always slides covering the exact types of diagrams you would see on each exam! Do the extra credit and go to office hours!
Class is hard in general, but she is always willing to help.
really nice and office hours were very helpful. homework was hard sometimes though.

I feel that the lectures are not an accurate reflection of the level of difficulty that is tested on the homeworks/exams. Although she seems nice, she does not go over very important, fundamental concepts during lecture. Be prepared to spend at least 10-15 hours a week teaching yourself the material. Openstax textbook is EXTREMELY HELPFUL!

While she is nice and cares about the success of the students, not once did a lecture cover all of the material. I ended up teaching myself everything as the lectures only covered very surface level topics what would not translate very well to the exams. Be prepared to learn the material outside of class

Katie spends a lot of time talking about simple topics rather than focusing on the exam concepts and going over them in class. Quizzes, homework, and practice exams are unlike the exams as I relied heavily on past exams and external resources rather than lectures, quizzes, and homework. I highly recommend going to office hours and retake quizzes.

Professor Ansell is very kind and encouraging. However, we had not ever been able to cover a full lecture within the allotted time. So, many times, concepts were rushed through. I definitely had to spend a lot of time studying outside of class and teaching myself the material. Definitely go to office hours as much as possible to receive bonus pts.!
messy :( mostly taught myself the material.

We would cover so much material in class, it was going at the speed of light. She never held review sessions before exams and instead would just keep teaching material that we would then never use. The class was honestly super unorganized, could not tell you one thing I actually learned.

Extremely redundant to any intro psych class, basically psych 101, but easier. Lectures and discussions had mandatory attendance, but classes were extremely boring due to the repetitive material. Easy A, but I didn't gain anything useful from this class.

lecture was very redundant and the class is basically intro psych and some common sense classroom principles. TA sessions are lackluster but attendance is mandatory for both. weekly homework based off of textbook and sometimes can be frustratingly time consuming, there are no tests and the projects are really easy.
she's great easy A

The class was very boring if you have taken a basic psych class before. While not difficult, the teacher treats her students like high school students, with required attendance even though her lectures are repetitive if you have even skimmed the textbook. The weekly homework is time consuming but easy. Overall, the class isn't fun but isn't hard.
She was super nice, but you will be working mostly with your TAs this class. Be aware of group projects, because they are a big part of the class.

Easiest class ever just AP Psych again. However, everything in the class is a group project with an ambiguous rubric to allow for "creativity" making it so your grade is somewhat random. 

Biggest issues with the class was lectures take attendance as no one would go otherwise. Lectures and 2 hour discussion sections do not relate at all.

Pretty fun class but lectures are kind of boring because it's just restating everything from the assigned readings instead of building on it. Lecture attendance is mandatory which is dumb but whatever. Be aware there's lots of group projects including the final!!

Her course was probably my favorite one I took this semester. Overall not a bad course as it was fairly easy but be aware that the final project is a group project where you will have to create a lesson plan.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: No exams/quizzes. Weekly ~200 word responses to 3 questions based on the recorded lecture, and a few projects including one group. If you follow the rubrics to a T, turn in everything on time, and attend class, you WILL have a grade of 100%. Prof is amazing,super nice. You dont need psyc 100 knowledge,try signing up even if you dont have the prereq

Very knowledgeable and knows how to explain difficult concepts in a more digestible way. Exams are not easy. Go over the homework assignments and start preparing early to ensure you succeed. The class is super interesting and very applicable to current events.
She is really awesome and made personal finance interesting. When I took this course it was team taught with another professor and they worked very well together.

Prof Elmore is passionate and well educated on the class content. The class is by no means easy, but Ailie articulates the content clearly and is very amicable to offering extra clarification and assistance outside of lecture. You definitely have to pay attention in class though because the class can get confusing if you fall behind.
447 not 444 made comments that humiliated my intellectual capacities. Very boring classes, quizzes 2 times a week(every class).

his lectures are very monotone and boring. He does not give student's time to think or wrangle with the problem, rather just states the proof and expects us to memorize it for quizzes and exams. 

Can be rude/condescending at times when you ask questions after class.

Nice professor. To be honest the class is a little boring. but you can either choose to go to his office hours or work on your own to figure things out. exams are mostly easy as long as you spend a moderate amount of time on this class.

Class is easy but terrible teacher - basically writes textbook on board for lecture (no interactive or engaging elements for relatively small class). In addition, does not take partial credit for exams/quizzes. Nice guy but such a boring teacher.
The class is easy to get a better grade. The professor is very nice.

reviews.comment: You should definitely choose Aimo if you want to skip you four final. He never assigns any homework but do 15 quizzes in class. Top 10 quizzes will be counted. If you feel good about your midterm, you can drop the final. His cut off for A is at most 80%, and for B is at most 60%. This semester, 20 out of 26 in my class get an A.
A very good teacher. Explains very clearly. Examinations are fair. Happy to get his lecture.

At first he seems hard, but later I found that he was quite fair.  He is very good about explaining every concept without acting as though you know nothing or know everything.  He does grade most things on an all-or-none basis, but this works out well to help learn the subject.

His lectures go so in depth with proofs but his tests are pretty basic. Homework is pretty easy. Drops 1 out of 3 tests and then you can take your grade as is without final exam. Nice curve. Won't budge when arguing for points on tests. Definitely qwirky math type.

professor has a heavy accent, but definitely knows his material. loves explaining and using proofs. for 225 he gave out practice exams that were similar to the real test, drop 1 out of 3 exams. homeworks were easy points if u had the answer guide. shouldnt be hard at all. just do a little studying on the practice test before the test.
75 was still an A with no plusses or minuses, also no final in the class if you were happy with your grade or you could take it to try and improve.  Very good at explaining but a lot of memorization.
He has no sympathy in grading...it's all or nothing folks. In order to make it out alive, you have to work your ass off. He is funny in a "clueless math professor" sort of way. Fun accent.
must work very hard in the class. and use specific mathematical language. for the exam u have only pencil/pen, erraser and brain. no cheatsheet , no calculator.

The lectures where very helpful for learning material and as long as you go consistently you should be fine in the class. You only really need the textbook to get the questions for assignments. Essays can be intimidating at first but if you go to office hours the feedback is very helpful.

Lecture was not the most engaging but still delivered good material. The papers were difficult, but it's a writing class, and she gave very good feedback in office hours. I didn't use the textbook a ton other than to get hw problems. 301 in general is just kind of hard because of the nature of the subject, but overall I think she does a good job.

This was literally the worst class I've ever taken. She barely knows the material, and instead reads off of printed out hand outs. I left office hours confused, and she could barely answer questions. She grades homework too harshly considering she clearly doesn't know the material either.
Professor talic is amazing her class was a great introduction to syntax and shes very understanding. She really wants you to learn, and I feel like she valued that more than other professor do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was mandatory for my major, but it was so difficult to follow along. I don't think it was all on her teaching style, but just that syntax theory seems unnecessarily complicated. She's really helpful in office hours. Only used the textbook for assignments (which were in it), and teaching myself the content. Hard to stay focused in class.

reviews.comment: This class is super easy, and the quizzes are super light and only worth 2% of your grade. Professor Barbeau's lecture videos are super engaging and interesting. Sometimes the B101 zoom lecture seems useless, so you will get most of your learning from the section leaders and Professor Barbeaus' lecture videos.

Such a sweet and personable professor, also very engaging. Her short video lectures are to the point and what we learn is pretty interesting, and if you are able to take another BUS class with her then don't hesitate. More work than BUS201 but the class is so easy it's unreal.

Such an amazing class and professor!!!! Took this first semester but Barbeau made this such an easy class that if you just pay even the slightest bit of attention you will succeed. Attendance policy is a bit strict but it's because most of the in class activities are group activities. Can't wait to take BADM 340 with her again!!!
Very enthusiastic and kind. Good at explaining and makes lectures a little less boring. Strict attendance.

She is one of the best professors at Gies. Had her for BUS 101 and knew I had to take her business ethics class. She made the class fun and interesting and very easy to get an A with lots of extra credit opportunities. This is a great advanced comp class too with not too much writing. Highly recommend!
Very nice and upbeat! Fun to have.

I LOVE AIMEE BARBEAU. She was a great professor and always cared about her students. She made the class easy to understand and would always highlight external opportunities. She was very clear and always was easy to reach via teams. Professor Barbeau if you see this know that you are amazing!!!

One of the most understanding professors I've ever met. She was always available for questions about grading. The only downside is that the weekly readings take a lot of time and become busywork really easily. Other than that, the class is a good introduction to business and covers a wide range of different areas.

Gave very enthusiastic lectures for a boring class. Strict online and in-person attendence. Capstone project is a lot of stress and effort for a high-school quality 5 minute presentation. Assignments are mostly busywork. Most interesting part of the class is the encouragement of using AI, as long as you cite how you used it.
Capstone helped expand what I thought of as learning in school. Great class.

BUS 101 is a really easy class, but I still think it was a great experience. Prof Barbeau is really kind, and I remember she would stay after class and take her time answering questions from different students. The section leaders to my knowledge are all pretty solid, and I really enjoyed this class overall. Go to bed early Thursday though!

Barbeau was a good instructor for a boring class. The online classes were very strict on attendance and the work was easy but tedious. The grading was not strict and there were lots of opportunities for extra credit.
Super chill, but the weekly zoom meetings are mandatory and she is very strict about the attendance policy.

Best professor I had during my freshman year. Lectures were fun and often had guest speakers. Discussions were unnecessarily long but still enjoyable. Homework was very easy and there were only 2 easy exams. The final was a capstone project in groups but she walks you through every step so it was nothing to worry about. Highly recommend!
Super easy class, lots of extra credit. Only annoying thing was I had to miss class for a school sport and lost points for it but it didn't matter since the class was so easy. Teachers pretty good

Professor Barbeau was not only a great teacher, but really cared about the content she was teaching.  The course is super easy, and you are basically guaranteed to get an A.  Go to class and you will honestly get a lot out of it, great introduction to business and Gies.

Not only a free A, but a great teacher too. Homework is essentially just busy work you can bs. The few tests are open note, and the class is put together well and is easy to understand. You don't even have to pay attention to lectures to get an A--my type of class.

Having Professor Barbeau for BUS101 was a very good experience. Her lesson videos which we viewed in class were all very well-made and interesting, and the course structure was well laid-out and I did not at all feel rushed by the timeline.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Barbeau is truly passionate about helping Gies freshman transition into college life and really help them learn the essence of corporate responsibility and ethical decision making in the workplace. It's a very easy class and you really get a lot out of it, especially with the Capstone project and the many activities during discussion.
She's fun and she really knows what she's teaching. One of the best professors I had and will not forget. Just wish I had her class again...

If you show up and give minimal effort to complete all the assignments, you will get an A. The only annoying part of this class was the weekly discussion questions. You will most likely not interact with Mrs. Barbeau at all, but her lecture videos are very clear and concise.

Shares lots of business resources. Caring! Weekly discussion posts which require some reading. Exams were straightforward but sometimes very specific. The major project was hectic at times but very manageable and is great for introducing you to the business world. Lots of extra credit as well - take advantage!

Professor Barbeau was one of the best professors I have ever had. She offers so much extra credit it is virtually impossible to do poorly in this class. There are 1-2 assignments each week and they are easily accomplishable. Professor Barbeau has taught an enjoyable class that I highly recommend to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She was a great teacher and was really great with replying to my emails even thought there are so many students.

Easy class. Aimee's lectures were online but discussion was in person. Just show up and do attendance. Packback is easy and weekly assignments take an hour max. Super chill! The semester project is a little more time consuming but just meet after lecture and you'll be fine. Don't procrastinate on this easy class! Midterm and final - not bad!

This class was the most useful class I have ever taken. We were given points just for coming to class. If we did not make it to class, we were given opportunities to make up for it online. We got to interact with multiple alumni and many amazing employees of reputed companies. Even if you don't do anything in this class, you will still get an A.

Professor Barbeau is one of the best professors I have had at Illinois. She approaches every component of the course with the greatest care and works nonstop to ensure an optimal experience among students. She transformed the entire class, in the midst of the pandemic too! She serves as an inspiration to students and over 50 section leaders as well

This class was mainly on zoom, but you were allowed to go in person. I never did because it was at 9am- yeah no. Our TA(a junior) would literally just play videos of her talking about different aspects of business. If you show up and talk a little bit you'll get an A. The biggest assignment is your CapStone Project, so actually try for that.

First year she taught the remodeled intro class. For having over 800 students, she did a really good job staying available for students. Went to in person classes and always saw her in the BIF atrium in the morning and would say hi. Her recorded lectures were all easy to follow and organized. The course is great and easy but a lot of busy work

She has no knowledge of the material and everything is too open. Very impatient and takes decisions too quick. Groups assigned based on her own weird viewpoint and does not respect students views and opinions. Grading is unfair. Bioinspired Design is a totally useless course, a teaching team of 5 has no clue what to each in class.
Does not respond to emails and often gives out unclear or conflicting instructions. Worst class I have ever taken.

Terrible professor. Does not seem to be aware of the requirements and considerations regarding her own final project. Course logistics are disorganized and instructions are vague. Unresponsive outside of lecture, despite making the final project significantly more difficult than previous semesters.

Excellent professor who really knows what she's talking about. The class was hard, but she made it worthwhile. Lots of extra credit opportunities and clear expectations. I took this class during SP2020, and when the college went online, this was the only class I took that semester that handled the change well. Highly highly recommend her!

Really good at simplifying concepts and works out problems with students during lecture. Very enthusiastic about the subject and tries to create a warm atmosphere over zoom. Provides great feedback for the projects and is super helpful during OH. Receptive to feedback. Course logistics was a little all over the place, though. Offers extra credit.

This class is time consuming no matter what. Professor Wissa is a nice person and cares about her students, but she can be a little too quick to judge sometimes. Her exam policy is very flexible. She overall makes the course more manageable, but can be disorganized. If you put in the effort she will notice. Grading is iffy - depends on the TA. 8/10

Professor is bad at answering student's questions and seems barely prepared for class. He explains things in an unclean manner at times. He lacks any sympathy for the students when it comes to technical difficulties or miscommunications.

reviews.comment: Very amazing lectures, with extremely helpful examples. I personally prefer his annotated keynotes. ECE 210 is a tough class but if you understand all the examples very well and do a lot of practice exams, you will get a good grade.

reviews.comment: Approachable, caring, inspirational. Explained stuffs in ECE 210 very well and always willing to answer students' questions. Before everything moves online, Professor Han encourages students to participate actively in class, facilitating a congenial and supporting learnning environment.

I took ECON 101 with Prof Veras at Oberlin College. He's not too difficult of an instructor or grader, and you will likely do well as long as you complete the problem sets and review PowerPoints. His lectures are not always clear but the assignments are easy and he is always willing to help in office hours. A real sweetheart and very friendly guy.

This prof was the most confusing prof I have taken so far. He does not know how to teach or lecture. Yes, he is very knowledgeable, but when it comes to communicating that knowledge to his students, he fails tremendously. I had him as a visiting prof at Oberlin. Confusing just sums it all up. Nice guy though.

reviews.comment: I really like Henrique. Super nice guy that grades easy and is still young enough to sympathize with the plight of students. The project we did was cool especially the part where we wrote a policy proposal. Exams were easy and he preps you well for them. This was a development econ class. Sad to see him leave UIUC

The homework was not mandatory, she gave very clear lectures, tons of extra credit, tests were open book/open note. The content was challenging but it was not a stressful course. She was very friendly and approachable and even wrote me a letter of recommendation.

reviews.comment: Follows Griffiths and assigns hard homework problems, but the tests are fair and straight forward and are open book, notes, homework, discussion, etc.  She's quite nice and willing to help you out when you need it.
follows the textbook by griffiths

As with most physics lectures at UIUC, her's isn't worth going to. Loves pronouncing key terms awkwardly (e.g. CoooLOMS Law). Extremely boring, and the 90-minute duration is brutal. Go to all the discussions, run through 2 or 3 past hour exams, and read through all the lecture slides before the final, and you'll be fine.
No Comments
Lectures were very hard to understand, and painful to sit through--she gave off the impression that she disliked teaching and did not want to be there.  No excitement about physics at all.
d0gs41t prof held solely by tenure
Don't expect any help from this professor. rather talk to ChatGPT instead or the video lectures that are taught by a competent professor. or better yet don't have him at all.
Scribbles all over slides like Toddler. Grading is very bad. If you don't want to destroy your GPA take this class with a diff professor.

reviews.comment: Honestly a nice person, but the lectures are hard to follow. The handwritings are not very legible as well, which only confuses me rather than helps me learn.

Juan Alvarez truly dislikes his students and has no empathy for them. His grading scheme is unclear, the course setup is designed to make students struggle, and his research on "Student Response to Academic Failure" is completely mandatory and factors into your grade. Shows no concern for students, responding to all student requests and questions in a flippant, joking manner—whether by email or on Piazza.
Avoid Juan Alvarez as your instructor at all costs. He enjoys seeing his students fail instead of succeeding.

Instruction was largely ineffective, as the professor appeared disengaged from student success and lacked clarity when conveying complex ECE 210 concepts. The combination of a dismissive teaching style and unhelpful lab TAs made the course unnecessarily difficult and off-putting, leading to many students who wanted to transfer to ECE to drop out.
y u want everyone to fail brah be like my king Corey Snyder

You will learn better if you just learn by yourself. Download the textbook and combine that with the theory pdf would do it. I was very injured and sent to Carle but on the inside I was very relieved because I don't need to go listen to whatever the duck he has been saying in lecture for the entirety of 50 minutes.

Piazza responses were really passive-aggressive for no reason. Lectures were ok, would recommend trying out other lecture sections tho. Lots of exam review material. Homeworks were useful, but the required "survey component" of every hw for some research study got kinda obnoxious towards the end of the course. Grading system was imo nonsensical.

can someone tell me why

this diddyblud dont know what he doin his campuswire responses some straight ragebait please dont take his lecture section he prolly play logbait in clash and his hairline farther back than a beatdown push

the only thing good and interesting in this class is the lab with helpful TAs. I cant imagine how horrible his lectures would be bc i can feel how bad he is through how he structured the class. absolutely useless when emailing him or on campuswire. make me hate signal processing. worst professor i have ever taken a class with
He replaced professor Snyder for 2 lectures. Now I am completely lost in this course lol. Sorry for those who are in his sectiom.

Absolutely dreadful as a person. Has such a high ego that he is being passively rude to everyone. Definitely ruins interest in hardware and signal for me although the class contents are pretty cool. No idea how he is still teaching despite all the hate from students.

This is an example of a professor who hates his job. Never answer questions on Campuswire properly. Are not helpful at all in the office hours and is always passive aggressive. Have no mercy at all in emergency situations.

I emailed him requesting a 1 day extension on a homework assignment because my childhood dog was about to die. I wanted to drive back home to visit my family and be there when they put her down. He regurgitated course policy to me like he's not the one that designed it. Also feels like he grades harsh just for his research project...

I don't think this man has answered a single question. Every time someone asks him a question on the class forum, he answers with another question, even if it would've been quicker to just give the answer. Hes unreasonable at times, just recently a quiz worth 10% of our grade resulted in a 52% average. only 13/70 got a passing score. Avoid this man

Can hardly call himself a professor. Multiple students with the same work on an exam got graded differently because somehow their work showed 'varying levels of understanding' even though they had the same exact work. He literally could care less about how much you learn and instead feeds on the students collective misery from his unfair grading.
Terrible professor. Deliberately makes classes more difficult than necessary and grades very harshly.

Worst ECE professor I've encountered yet, avoid at all costs. If you take 210, you're at his mercy. Only responds to online questions with his own useless sarcastic questions. Interesting that a professor whose research interest is "Response to Failure and Success in Engineering" hands out the most failing test grades just to curve in the end.

Worst professor for ECE210. Avoid at all costs. ECE210 is a difficult course, but all the other professors are great and make content very clear. Professor Alvarez expects you to teach yourself and makes you feel like your questions are stupid. Very passive aggressive especially when you ask questions on CampusWire or email.

reviews.comment: one of the worst classes I have taken here. Intelligible handwriting, insensible lecture, harsh grading, exactly passive aggressive like the other comments said, answers during lectures and campuswire are really useless
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: horrible handwriting, awful teaching, terrible attitude replying to student questions online(I've never seen him answer a question directly other than saying like 'did you read xxx?/did you pay attention to xxx?') I had the impression that all of the concepts were just "injected" into our minds without any explanation of "why we are learning it."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is extremely passive-aggressive and will always think that he is correct over any other student's opinion
My previous rating got taken down for some reason so I'm writing this again - It's simply so unfortunate that I have to see this guy again for ECE 313..
Honestly, there are a lot of other professors that teaches this class a lot better. I was quite disappointed with his way of teaching and leading the course.

The WORST professor I've ever had. He does NOT know how to teach! He makes things more difficult than they have to be and is very uncooperative. He is very unreasonable, especially when it comes to his suppositions on what constitutes academic integrity and will inculpate you for the most trivial reason. I had a vexatious experience with him!
The class is tough, and Alvarez does not make it easier. Sometimes it is very hard to follow along in lecture, whether it be the handwriting or somewhat uninteresting content.

I'm surprised Alvarez has a low rating on this website. 210 is a very difficult course but Alvarez did a great job at explaining the material. The course is very fast paced but Alvarez proves every single concept and provides ample clarification for practice problems. He is also great during office hours.
Stupid professor

His lectures are hard to understand and his handwriting is cluttered and very hard to take notes off of. You are better off attending lectures from another professor. A nice person though, good to ask questions to but unfortunately it feels like he can't teach very well. Class is organized decently but is graded on an esoteric bell curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Assumes the worst of students if you are suspected of cheating even when you have not done anything wrong. Not understanding at all, does not accept any excuses, and quick to jump to conclusions. Worst professor I have ever communicated with
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class this semester. This professor does not physically participate in this class at all. He leaves it to his graduate students, TA's, and other faculty to conduct. During the covid crisis, he was very inaccessible and did not provide adequate responses to my inquiries about the class.

Refuses to make reasonable accommodations to students experiencing technical issues during our first fully-online semester. He has handed out zeros like candy to students who had minor issues with their exams such as: bringing a tablet that the instructor said was okay to do during lecture, zoom camera turning off on its own, etc. Not cool
I took 313 with him and he's a really good teacher for that. I understood the material very well with him teacher. The tests are extremely hard though, so taking practice tests help.
Very good professor. Explains stuffs really well and answers students' questions well. Once he used a cucumber to explain the concept of marginal joint pdf, very interesting.

I had him for 210 and 313, any course with him the worst experience throughout my college year. I understand the courses are difficult but he makes it even more difficult. The most strict grading professor, taking away points for the smallest mistakes.
Great professor overall, he teaches very hard classes with tough to digest material that he can make somewhat easily understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very helpful professor. Had him for two classes and each time, he has been super helpful in office hours and has been fairly clear in lecture
no curve

Overall a pretty solid professor and I would definitely sign up for his lecture again. Very helpful and will take time to explain difficult concepts. Also seems like he actually cares about students succeeding in class.

Very good at explaining materials. Give out many extra examples. ECE313 is not an easy course. The new summer online version has many administrative problems and I do recommend taking on-campus version.

I didn't have Alvarez as my specific lecturer, but he was the course director for ECE 210. Any experience I had with him was negative. Extremely unhelpful over email dealing with administrative stuff and extremely unhelpful when asking question on Piazza. In my opinion, he was an exceptionally bad course director. This class was run very poorly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Alvarez is a good lecturer. He obviously cares about the students and goes great lengths to answer students' questions.

Really good professor and lecturer, organizes his work very well on the board and lectures are well-paced. Even more helpful at office hours: cleared up a whole lecture's worth of confusion in 5 minutes.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer. Had him for 210 and 313. Answers your questions about homework and concepts after the class. Took 313 with him over the summer. The class notes for 313 is clutch. Both of these classes are hard though. Definitely have to put in time and hard work to get the grade you want for these classes.

Course was definitely made overly complicated by the Professor, especially in the way she teaches (handouts + worksheets only). TAs were decent for the most part, but you could tell there was a lack of communication between each other and the professor when it came to teaching concepts + grading. Honestly, not enough time given for exams either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor and TAs make this course more complicated than it needs to be. She uses over complicated language making it difficult. I dont know why she does this when she can make the course so much easier for students. The TA you have is very important as the professor does not reply to emails. She is not very approachable and neither are the TAs.

Hot take but I LOVED Professor Kerr and PHIL 103. This class is great for the pre-law track. Prof Kerr challenges you and tries her best to explain material that can be difficult to grasp at times. She's engaging, professional, and is always open to criticism. Although many will take this as a gen ed, she expects you to take this class like its not

I studied hard for this class, went to office hours, did everything. The final was material that nobody in the class was ever taught. I was genuinely upset, as were my peers. The review guides are often graded without reasoning and my TA (Reimer) honestly didn't seem to know too much. Also look out for the random pop quizzes.
I really enjoyed this class. I will say make sure you come to class because there will be pop quizzes, but she's very nice and willing to go over things multiple times so you understand the material.

This class is okay for QRII requirement. The professor doesn't grade exams fyi, leaving your grade dependent on TAs. Pop quizzes are randomly given in class so it's important to not miss and PAY ATTENTION. The exams are kind of challenging so make sure to study ahead of time. Not horrible to understand concepts but you need to put the work in.

I didn't really like the course as it is very memorization heavy (compared to the Calc 1-3 sequence), but Manfroi made the lectures as interesting as possible. His lectures prioritize examples over heavy theory/definitions. Sometimes lectures can be fast paced, but they are manageable. Also, don't be afraid to talk to him, he's a pretty cool guy!
One of the best professors in the entire school!

Prof. Manfroi was one of the most caring and accommodating professors I've had at the school. He was very willing to help out when needed, super easy to access outside of lecture, and very approachable. I highly recommend taking his class :)
This class gives you 285 reasons to love Manfroi.
Professor is really nice and funny but lectures a little pointless. Very easy to get lost during lecture because he goes fast, but just practice the review/homework, it'll be more beneficial.
Best lecturer in maths, only time in college I'd readily attend an attendance non-mandatory lecture.

Super funny, very chill and understanding. Practice exams prepare you super well for actual exams. Quizzes and homeworks are useful. Make sure to practice actually solving the problems along with the lecture notes instead of just looking at them.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a very engaging lecturer and a pretty funny guy. Class isn't required but go otherwise you will get lost and fall behind. Exams were always fair and pretty simple compared to the in-class examples he'd give. The grading scale is also very nice since a 90 is the cutoff for an A. Definitely an easier class that any calculus class.
The exams are pretty nice and his lectures are somewhat engaging.

Exams are relatively straightforward, and the class weighting makes getting an A very manageable. Lectures can be worth going to, but they get confusing if you get lost in the first few minutes. However, Professor Manfroi is really nice and does his best to help if you ask.

Exams are on the easier side, and the grading is forgiving too; +90 is considered an A.

Lectures aren't mandatory, and not very helpful, in my experience. He solves multiple questions instead of explaining concepts, if you learn well in these conditions you should go. His handwriting is quite hard to read.

Cool guy in general though. GOAT

I think for this semester the tests gotten harder, because before people said it was really easy. I still have an A but haven't gotten a single A on any of the midterms. He is a great professor and is really nice, but some of the harder material does show up on the test and can be confusing sometimes, especially the multiple choice questions.

This class is relatively easy, I wish I could tell you more about this professor but I stopped going to lecture after the first test and only really looked at his notes to study. His tests are super easy and concepts are interesting. Light at the end of the tunnel after all the calc classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goes quite fast in lectures, handwriting is often illegible (he jokes about it all the time). Exams and HW is easy, grading is easy but lectures can be long-winded and go over unnecessary stuff that is confusing.
He was an easy professor for sure, but did a poor time using lecture to get the information across. Stopped going to class after the second exam. He just does not know how to explain stuff.
His lectures are fast an sometimes it doesn't make sense but once you do the homework its very straight forward, come early to class and ask to play songpop!
He's pretty good at explaining stuff, and he's laidback and funny. Lectures are a bit quick though so it can be hard to keep up sometimes.

Don't get me wrong, this professor is very nice. He ends lectures early and the course is pretty easy. However, I didn't learn much from this class. It seems like he is lecturing b/c it's his job rather than b/c he loves it. If you just want a good grade for this class, he's great. If you want to actually learn something from this class, beware.

Don't get me wrong, I love Professor Manfroi, but not god as everyone tells. He's chill, lectures are clear and usually end early. My only thing is he has shorter and fewer office hours, and he's kind of fast through lectures but the exams are fair and he is great at explaining the content. Also be versed on music since we play song pop party

Manfroi made a class I expected to be difficult understandable in an engaging way. Be prepared to not be able to read his handwriting, but it's okay because he teaches at a very manageable pace. He can fit all the lecture info into his class without rushing anything, and class typically ends 5-10 minutes early. Highly recommend for DiffEQ.

He is not godlike as some suggest, but considerably better than other math professors here. Lectures can be helpful but I live by the textbook and practice tests, which I found to be more useful. Definitely pick him if you have a choice and plan on going to lecture
He's literally the best math professor I've had at this school.

Aldo is very good at balck board lecture teaching and will provide a lot of similar questions for a concept to make sure you understand the concept. He usually will end his lecture 10 mins early but the content is a lot.

absolute goat. love the grading scale (90.01 is an A). lectures could get a bit boring since he'd sometimes show the longwinded proofs, but he also is pretty hilarious and knows how to lighten the mood. he usually lets out early, but late afternoon classes finish even faster since he speeds through content, so take him early in the day
Great professor

If you have a disability he won't accomodate you unless you give him the accomodation letter early as hell so if it's causing you a bad grade and you don't figure that out until late you're screwed. Additionally, the website he uses for his tests are awful and cause you to loose a lot of points for no reason and his quizzes are very unforgiving

Professor Manfroi is AMAZING. This man can explain all the concepts with ease and make them more understandable than the textbook. He is also really funny and does small talk lecture (AMERICA'S CUP!!!). This makes the whole class a very entertaining and easy experience, but it still feels like we learn a lot. Best professor I've had at UIUC!
Best math professor I have ever had.
Greatest math teacher I have ever had. Homework is infrequent and extremely easy, almost impossible to fail this class. Also has amazing hair.
great professor, definitely recommend.

Prof Manfroi is extremely kind and caring and he makes his class so chill- he literally asks bonus questions about movies on his exams. Lectures weren't required but I went to every class willingly and took notes (only class I ever took notes in) because he was so engaging and passionate.

He was good, but bro literally didn't care about the math. It seemed like he just came in to teach, and not because he actually really cared. Also, the grading is pretty easy - the class could easily has a C or D average if he wants, so that is goated of him. But overall he just comes in to teach, not to actually be passionate about math.

I love Aldo. The course itself is not very hard. His lectures are informational. Although not mandatory, I still highly recommend u to attend. Not too much homework and homework is strongly related to exams. Only 90 points, u can get an A. Cheers!

Absolutely the best professor I have in Math department, much better experience than Linear Algebra with someone else. Practice tests and homework are really helpful for exam, and the lectures are great and clear with little efforts to fully understand the materials, and Prof. Manfroi is very chill and caring to his students.

"How's it going?" he asks us multiple times per lecture.
Very chill and laid back professor, always cracking jokes.
Everyone else seems to find this class very easy and get A's.

Manfroi wants you to do well and structures the class toward that. His lectures were clear, helpful, and understandable (until the last few weeks), and the homework reflected lecture and test material. Generous practice tests, grading, and test drop policy. Everything is also available online, but in-person lectures were more helpful.
Best professor ever!!! His practice tests were similar to exams. Super fair and kind!!
Best math professor ever. Never drop a single lecture of his.

Prof. Manfroi is great, he clearly cares about his students and structures the course in a way where almost anyone can succeed. I will say lectures were sometimes difficult to follow especially while taking notes at the same time, but with the help of examples, things usually became clearer.
Manfroi is really chill and makes the class feel fun instead of stressful. Also, the tests are easy As as long as you do the homework and pay attention in lectures.

Professor Manfroi kept a light atmosphere during his lectures but still kept them highly educational. He was always joyful and explained everything clearly. The class is much easier than Calculus at UIUC and is not a lot of work. The exams matched pretty well what was on the practice exams.

He's funny and carefree. In all his midterms he includes a movie question from a movie that students vote to watch. His lectures are very concise, clear, and to the point and he seems to not even put much effort into lecturing. Nearly all his lectures end early. He's just a talented lecturer and he tries to interact and connect with the students.
Use the note he give, that is really helpful.

So overrated. Lectures are very...ok? They're not bad but definitely not that great.  He seemed uninterested whenever I went to office hours for extra help, and was not that considerate about extensions. Class is soooo badly structured which made it hard to stay on top of work. Exams were super easy. But I've had way better math profs.

Funny quirky man. Explains things well (though with questionable handwriting). Textbook isn't mandatory but he gives you a PDF for the one he wrote for free. Just show up to lecture and take notes, you'll be fine.
Aldo is a great professor who is also very funny. Love him!
Take his class
one of the best professor, the exams were really similar to the practice ones
He's such a great professor and super funny. The class itself is not terrible and has plenty of practice exams provided, and the homework helps.

Professor Manfroi's lectures are very clear on what material needs to be known, and is very funny and friendly while answering questions. All exams on this class are on prairielearn and are very similar to the practice exams. If one puts in even some effort into this class while attending lectures, they should expect to do well.

Funniest prof at UIUC. You can tell that he loves to teach Diff Eq and he always comes to lecture very prepared. He will typically let you out of lecture 5 minutes early too. He will also try and make sure that he is entertaining, which is very good for a class that many majors have to take.

Second time having Manfroi, loved him both times. Very caring and smart professor. He'll periodically stop throughout his lectures just to make sure everybody's doing okay. Amazing person, best math professor

I can't give any other input that hasn't been given already. You can already see how goated this man is by the other reviews. Differential Equations with Manfroi was the most enjoyable math class I've had in college. I'm not great at math but I will likely end with an A (hopefully). Even if I don't, doesn't matter. He made the class great. 10/10.

My favorite professor this semester.  He was hilarious and was great at making the more difficult content digestible.  The tests aren't too difficult, they test for knowledge rather than try to trick you.  It's still a good idea to find extra practice problems on your own though.

The best professor in Math 241.  Highly recommended. The class is a lot of fun and the exams are not difficult if you understand all concepts and do the practice exams. I got 100 in the final and learned a lot from his class.
Profesor Manfroi saved my life from Math241.

I love having Manfroi so much that I also took Math 285 with him this semester. He is concise and I enjoy his lecture style. He really wants students to reach out and ask questions. He creates an inclusive environment for female students, which doesn't always happen in engineering classes.

Very good professor. He went a little fast during lectures but if you do the homework most of what he says will make sense. However, there are quite a few homework assignments and worksheets throughout the semester. Overall, he was pretty funny and seems to care that his students understand what he is teaching.

Absolutely amazing professor. Very engaging with his students and ready to answer any questions they may have. He was able to teach what should have been pretty hard material in an easily accessible and easy-to-learn way.
He was great. Made calc 3 so easy to understand and his tests are very fair.

I had Manfroi for Math241 and very much enjoyed it. His lectures are clear and his humor definitely livened up the atmosphere. Tests were straightforward so if you payed attention in lecture you were fine. 

At the time of this post his rating is a 5.3 out of 5.0 for some reason, but that is definitely a lowball compared to what he deserves.
Greatest math prof ever, it had been a while since I had taken any math before I took 241 so it was a little rough but he made it bearable.
The best professor I had!

dawg how this guy have a 5.1

good prof tho, would recommend

Manfroi grades as anything above a 90.00 is a flat A. His lectures are clear in terms of content, but if you don't sit close it is sometimes difficult to hear him. His tests are very reasonable and similar to past exams and practice exams. His sense of humor helps the class move along. Definitely take him if able, far easier than other 241 profs.
Funniest professor I had this semester. Very fair exams with straight-forward questions. Love this man so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Manfroi was a really good lecturer. Everything in the course could've been learned well via textbook, but his lectures were good enough that many including myself kept attending. I wish my grade was higher. I just suck at math. A's were 100% obtainable. Enjoyed enough to take Math 285 last semester.
Manfroi is the man! Enough said.

Extremely good professor. Everything he asks on exams is extremely reasonable and there are never any surprises. Very clear what you need to know. Lectures were decently engaging and all topics were explained well. He's a really funny guy and definitely cares about his students. My one complaint is that midterms were sometimes overly short

Loved having Manfroi for calc 3. He's really funny and cares that his students understand his lectures. His tests are extremely reasonable. The practice tests he gives are very similar to his exams and if you fully understand them you should be set for the exam. I'm already signed up for math 285 with him next semester.
Really funny guy. Helped me like math again after taking CALC 2. Really the tests were straight forward and for the most part didn't ask ridiculous questions.

the practice exams were so similar to the actual midterms, and manfroi was easy to approach and explained the material in a great way! way better than calc 2 if you had a bad experience with that, because so did i

Great professor. He provides a ton of resources to be successful. The practice exams he gives help u understand the types of questions he asks, and the actual exams are even a little easier. One exam gets dropped which is also nice

While Calculus III is not an easy class in general, Professor Manfroi did a great job teaching the complicated concepts in a digestible way. He was always willing to answer questions during class and office hours and while the class was a heavy workload (lots of homework, five exams, etc.) he always brought humor to his lectures.
I love manfroi's exams as they are quite easy to prepare for.
Amazing, 100/10!! Highly recommend, made calc3 the easiest and funnest class I've ever taken. Please take him if you have a chance and go to lectures!

Prof. Manfroi is a good professor and does a good job during lectures introducing the concepts, however, sometimes it can be a little dry and oftentimes not super engaging. The tests have MCQs each worth 5 points each so basically if you miss 2 MCQ problems but get everything else correct, you are down to somewhere in the B range on the test

Calc 3 is hard... In my opinion much harder than Calc 2. You have to memorize a TON of stuff. There is SO much material. Many times you will stare at a problem and not know even how to start it. Take this class over the summer at a community college if you can. I would avoid this class if possible. If you can't, find another professor. Good luck

He does not teach many things, and he only cares about the most basic part. If you want to learn something and  get a deep understanding of calculus, do not go to his course. Plus, there are only 8 problems in the exam so you may loss a lot of points if you just make a tiny mistake.

This man must have changed. For calc 3 he is terrible. His accent is hard to understand, and he is very quiet in lectures, very difficult to hear. He only lectures the easy examples. His midterms are very unfair. Our first one was very long for only 50 minutes. Our second one was shortened, so 1 wrong is a B. Unfair. AVOID this guy like the plauge.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Manfroi is AMAZING. If he's an option for a class PICK HIM. Manfroi was able to make an online asynchronous class fun and engaging. No other professor I had in the Frankenstein of a school year that was 2020-2021 even came close to being able to engage people with their lecture videos as well as Manfroi did.

Even though I had him asynchronously he made the experience still fun. The way he constructed the class made sure you would get an A if you did the given work. He was very approachable and accommodating during office hours. I wish I had him either online or in person because even reading some of his answers on Campuswire was just fun.
Amazing professor for DiffEQ, his lectures are in-depth he really knows how to explain the content.

Not even done with his class yet and I am writing a review. Best professor I've had thus far. Teaches the material so well AND he kept his lecture videos minimally short! Not alot of homework, but enough so that you understand what you're doing. Thought this class would be hard. It's not. Exams are very simple. If you're taking 285/86 TAKE MANFROI!
He was always funny and did a great job to stay connected with students during these tough times. Overall enjoyed the class and I am really not a fan of straight math! Awesome professor!

Online lectures were concise and full of example problems to prepare us for the exams. More importantly, this man Rickrolled us while learning about the Fourier series, so he definitely has my approval.

This professor made learning differential equations a breeze! In fact, I barely remember referencing the textbook at all, that's how clear his lecture videos are! I'll definitely try to take more of his classes in the future.
I ABSOLUTELY LOVE PROFESSOR MANFROI!! This dude is hilarious. He also doesn't assign more homework than you need to understand the problems. Will definitely be taking his classes in the future.
Amazing professor. Lectures are concise, specific and really well thought out. Exams and homework are really based on the lectures so that's a huge plus!
Great professor all around, highly recommend.
this guy is just amazing
Attend lecture and do the readings before-hand. Amazing guy
This guy is amazing. 90% of the time he finishes early and lets you leave, but you almost don't want to because this guy is so fun to listen to.
Honestly the best math professor I've had at UIUC. He's super chill and balances the material with humor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I honestly can't think of anything about this class I didn't like. He balances a chill environment with actually teaching the material well. Plenty of opportunities to ask questions are given and he genuinely cares that people understand. His office hours are flexible and he lets students set up appointments if they can't make the set hours.
The best professor I've had at UIUC.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: He is the great professor on this land. He is hilarious and loves all of his students and makes the class really enjoyable and easy. His practice exams are the only thing you need to get an A in the class
Definitely need to show up for class, but he let us out early 90% of the time. He is hilarious and I would take him again for sure.

I had the worst time with this professor for 115.  He was never organized, terrible at explaining and he made up his own math problems! sometimes the solutions wouldn't make sense and it didn't help me learn the material at all.  I spent the entire semester teaching myself from the book.  AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS
Loves students and enjoys answering questions and listening to us
Manfroi is great. He's funny, understanding, and explains things very clearly. His grading scale is also very lenient. Definitely take diffeq with him if you have the opportunity.

Aldo is a wonderful person. He makes office hours if you cannot make his. He is entertaining, friendly, and caring. however, his lectures are too fast and he writes lightly. It is very hard to follow along. His practice exams are honestly the only thing I used to study for exams.

Professor Manfroi is one of the best professors I've come across at UIUC.  He not only is a great teacher, but he also has an amazing sense of humor.  He is very organized when teaching and his explanations are quite clear.  I honestly don't think there is a better choice for a MATH285 professor than Manfroi.  He is extremely helpful.  Take him!!!

This is my first  semester on this campus. It is so great to have a considerate professor like him. He is easy-going, which means you can talk about things beyond math with him. His lecture is helpful and clear. He will teach some useful little tricks which are very important in Math. He is considerate, but you have to learn your own things.

This can be a challenging class but if you attend his lectures regularly, take notes during his exam review sessions and do the practice exams, you will do great in his class. He sticks to the textbook most of the time. First midterm was a breeze but then they do get progressively harder. The final was comprehensive but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Its not as easy as people say it is. First exam is just like the practice (Easy A). For the next 3, pay close attention and remember the tricks. I would do the practice exams as well as reviewing the homeworks as I'd say I usually did worse than I thought I would just doing the practice exams. Small mistakes will cost you a lot of points!!

Most engaging teacher I have taken at U of I. He loves his students, he loves to teach, and he makes sure everyone is on the same page. He gives many opportunities to get a good grade in his course. If you are taking math 285, take Manfroi without a doubt.
Great, engaging professor. One of the best math teachers at UIUC.
He is, by far, the man for MATH 285.

By far the number one professor you want for Math 285. Tests are super simple if you go to lecture (no tricks, very straightforward.) Also, he is a cool guy who tries to make dull material not to boring, and you can definitely tell he knows the material inside and out. TAKE 285 WITH HIM!

285 is not difficult conceptually but the way the tests are setup it's easy to lose a substantial amount of points over simple mistakes. If I could do it again I probably would have taken it with a different teacher - I'm better at beating a curve than I am at not making algebra mistakes. Nice guy though.

Easiest Math I have ever taken in U of I. 3 midterms 1 final, the worst one will be 5%. Tests are same as the homework, as long as you do the homework, which is worth 20%, you will be ready for the test. I will take his class again if he offers any other classes.

Best math professor I've had at U of I.  Very clear explanations and examples with some humor thrown in.  The material isn't the easiest, but do the recommended hw and practice exams and you should do well.  Worst exam is only 5% of your grade, so if you do well on the 3 midterms you won't have to take the final.
He is super good. He explains super well and is pretty funny. Make sure to take good notes during class because he goes through all the types of problems you need to know very carefully.
He's got a kinda weird accent but it's not that bad. The class really isn't that easy but if you do well enough on the midterms the final is only worth 5% so it's basically a joke.
Manfroi is funny and makes dif eq, not the most exciting thing in the world, an interesting enough class. This class is very easy
He's the best.

Awesome Diff Eq professor! Definitely worth switching into his class. Funny and good at explaining stuff and really cares that you learn. Attendance not mandatory but definitely a bonus since class in entertaining!

Very clear when teaching and great at answering questions. Also good at balancing fun with classwork. Is especially helpful when you go to office hours. Use the book a lot for reading (assigned every night-not required, but highly recommended!), and homework problems. Material is difficult, but if you do homework and pay attention you'll be fine.

he explains things really well with lots of examples, gives you a practice exam that is the exact same as the exam, doesn't do plus/minus, and makes your lowest exam grade worth only 5%. best diff eq teacher!

Simply put, this is the professor you want for Diff Eq. There are some must avoids, and some not to bad profs. But Manfroi is the best at simply explaining the material and making you understand it. I took it during the summer so slightly accelerated. His grading system is extremely fair too. Also, no +/- which honestly I prefer.
clear explanations and not-so-hard exams. however, diff eq with Manfroi could be like a double edged sword because there is no plus and minus in the final grade (except A+).
Great professor. Great at explaining things and he's hilarious. Has a funny accent too. Attendance isn't mandatory but I'd recommend it for the sake of not having to read the book.

Great professor. chill, funny, and patient. very well organized and presents clear lectures. usually lets class out about 5-10 min early. really good and fair grading structure. thought exams were easy (understand the concepts). highly recommend Manfroi, one of the best prof/class i've ever had. he makes math fun and easy
He is very patient with questions and offers a lot of help! Bet teacher I've had! And he's so cute!!

Manfroi is a fantastic teacher. He manages to cover the material very clearly and in good time (we got out 5-10 mins early most days). He's willing to stop to make sure everyone follows and will answer questions. Homework is graded fairly, and exams reflect the lectures very well. Class was entertaining and helpful. Go with Manfroi if you can.
Test aren't as easy as reviews make it seem. They are fair.  Grading policy makes exams less stressful which is very nice.  Take good notes, do the HW, and enjoy having a fun/nice/good professor.

definitely take him for diff EQ. his tests are easy. although i think the grading scale is screwed up b/c i end up getting an A in the class even w/o taking the final. highly recommend him for this class!
GREATEST MATH TEACHER EVER!! EXAMS ARE STRAIGHT FORWARD. EASY A

Great teacher! If you have the choice of taking 410 or 415, take 410 with Manfroi! He makes sure everything is very clear. The tests are very straight forward (basically the same as practice problems). Not much homework & it's easy. If you go to class, all you have to do is a few practice problems before the tests and you'll ace them
Great teacher - fair, understanding, intelligent.  Not too much homework, test that actually reflect the notes, and great notes.  I would highly recommend this teacher.
excellent teacher. Explained concepts very well.

Good professor. Very nice and easy to approach. ALways willing to answer questions and constantly asks if things are clear or not. Homework load is very easy. Tests are straightforward. I'd stick with him.
GREAT! Best mather teacher I've ever had at U of I. Take his classes if you can. He's straightforward, easygoing, and incredibly nice!

Very clear, very straightforward lectures. He doesn't spend a heavy amount of time on abstract material and instead uses examples (with numbers!) to demonstrate which helps very much so. His exams are also straightforward. Incredibly nice guy as well and being in his class was very enjoyable. I'd take any course by him in a heartbeat.
Aldo Manfroi is the MAN! His exams are so straightforward, not any of that trying to mix you up or fool you. Its what you learned in class and nothing else, usually easier than the homeworks
Only math teacher I've had who has actually done examples with NUMBERS on the board. He's awesome. Take his class if you get the chance.
excellent teacher for 285! explanations were clear, always ready to answer questions!
manfroi's exams are what he teaches a rarity in math he explains very well and is open to questions during lecture
Lectures were always fairly interesting for a math class. He speaks softly but he's a good teacher and is really welcoming to questions. Tests are really straightforward

He is a terrible professor. He is lazy so he doesn't give out solutions to exams so we can fix our mistakes and his handwriting is terrible. I don't know how he got a job here. If the class you chose have him as the professor, you should get out of there asap and take it on a different semester if other professors aren't available.

Manfroi is a terrible, terrible teacher.  The concepts of this class really shouldn't be that hard, but his terrible explanations and mumbling speech along with inconprehensible handwriting impede any chance of actual learning.  Just memorize the equations, even for the geniuses it's their only hope.

Very difficult teacher for Lin. Algebra. Exams are different from material covered in class. He's got a slight accent. It's easy to understand. However, he is hard to follow and understand. I'd avoid him, I've heard there are better 415 instructors out there.

Not a very good lecturer. He was not very loud so you have to sit towards the front of the class. Proofs he did in class were not always clear and concise. His tests were easy, which made for an easy A, but that was the only thing I really liked about his class.

This guy is the best math teacher I've had so far at this school. He's explains class material very clearly and concisely. He's patient and helpful. Homeworks reflect exactly what you need to know for exams, and the exams he gives are always simple and straightforward.
This is probably the nicest and most enthusiastic math professor one could have. Grading is more than fair and he keeps you attentive. Genuine, nice guy.

He is the best math professor I have had here at the university. He counts homework for 30% of your grade (very very few profs do this here) and tests are graded fairly. He is also easy to understand,

Poor instructor. Homework problems never relfected the type of problems on the test, which made it very hard to study for. Belittled you a lot. These are very reoccuring characteristics I have found in most math classes at this university and Im a math major. If not, tell the dept. that they need better instructors.

Amazing professor. Young guy and very enthusiastic. He will do anything and everything to make this class easier to understand. The class may get boring but the professor does his best! Highly, highly recommended.

This guy is great.  He explained everything very well with a good mix of examples and theoretical stuff.  He made everything make sense and his tests were really easy, and since he was such a good teacher the class average was really good.  Take his class.

very organized and professional, but down-to-earth. explains things pretty well but sometimes doesn't give examples of everything you need to know. homework graded harshly but tests graded pretty fairly. doesn't give dumb quizzes every week. kind of boring, but relatively easy, considering it's a 400-level math class.
Out of all the 385 classes, I only heard of people from my class who actually liked it.  He's very good at explaining and overall a good teacher.  It's a hard class, but I'd recommend him.

Dr Amos is one of the best profs I had, however sometimes she has a hard time accepting that she is wrong, like things HAVE to be done her way. But, she does help people a lot, very nice with re-grades and her office hours are very helpful.
The best and most organized teacher at UIUC.
She was a really sweet professor and I felt like she taught very well. She was very understanding and open to discussion about grades. She was super helpful during office hours too
Amos is a decent teacher and an amazing person. I don't feel that I learned very much in her class, though.
Dr. Amos is a great teacher, and for this class, you really get out what you put in. Office hours are also helpful, and she is very open to criticism or problems about the class.
Pretty easy class. Didn't learn anything.

Alex is the GOAT. He's very funny and while he might seem a bit rude, he's really extremely kind and caring towards his students. The material is difficult and lectures move fast but office hours are extremely helpful and the graders on the test are extremely generous. You'll have to work but you should enjoy this course.
Hilarious professor but hard course overall
Lectures are fast-paced but okay to follow, go to his office hours if you need help, and you'll end up good in this class.

Lectures are fast-paced and some of the materials were hard, but if you pay attention it will be okay to follow. Go to his office hours if you have questions on the homework; they're equally useful as lectures. Be sure to attend classes in person! Listening to the lectures is much more useful than studying based on online (recorded) material.

overall pretty not nice to students, him and his staff. makes jokes that are would go as funny with the right tone, but he seems to mean what he says, in a not so nice way. Too much storytelling in lecture and doesn't cover much. Does have a good sense of curriculum structure though.
Targeting students during the course

This professor is highly critical, and his classroom interactions can be very difficult. While he clearly knows the material, he is often discouraging when students ask questions. He teaches at an incredibly fast pace, making it very hard to keep up or take notes effectively, even for those who maintain consistent and regular lecture attendance.

Great course, so much to learn. For me the lectures were paced a bit too fast, but he provides many resources such as older lecture recordings and practice problems for all the topics. Exams will never ask anything which is not already in his material. Great prof!

The class is difficult, and lectures are necessary to understand the material. Alex can seem mean, but he's (almost) always joking, and actually cares a lot about his students (especially if he notices people going to lecture and office hours). Office hours are EXTREMELY helpful! Go even if you don't have questions, just to do the homework.

Lectures are clear and the material is explained well, but the classroom atmosphere can feel tense and discouraging for questions. The final exam relied heavily on advanced calculator functions, which added unnecessary pressure for some students.
