Axelson is amazing and makes orgo easy-ish. Don't lose points on homework and do all the extra credit if you want this class to be somewhat of an "easy" A.

All her lectures are asynchronous, and there's a lot of lecture videos. Even if you watch the lectures, it's still not enough to do well on the exams. I got an A in CHEM 104 and did all the lectures and practice problems, so I followed the same method with this class, still did not work. She used to have the exam open note, but not this sem.
I really love Jordan, though the class is extremely hard and you have to really make sure you pay attention. Go to as many office hours as possible, and make sure to keep up with the lectures.

Wonderful Professor. If you do all the materials shes given to you and take time to understand them, you will get an A, no questions asked. She cared about your success and gives you the tools to be successful. You just gotta use em!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Axelson is one of the best instructors I've ever had. Though the class itself was very difficult, she was always available to help, and she did as much as she could for me when I was sick with COVID. She even gave me private office hours on the day of the exam! Dr. Axelson was always available for help, and she gave us so many resources.

Orgo is a tough class but she did a great job teaching it which often led to longer videos, however, concepts were explained very clearly with plenty of examples. She is pretty strict with grading and doesn't make a lot of exceptions for individual students but does offer a lot of drops (including a midterm) which generally makes up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: As another review mentioned: hard class but if you have any emergency your screwed. Covid was an emergency and she really made the bare minimum accommodations. Says a lot about her as a person. Exams were brutal do all the practice exams and ws and still not ace it. :)

Last semester I was going through a lot with COVID, and I emailed asking for help. She gave no leeway. She gave 2 times the amount of online work than it would be if it was in person. She thinks she already made enough accommodations, but she was my least sympathetic teacher and didn't care about her students.

Axelson really cares about how well students do in her class. She's likely only professor I will ever see write out a unit summary to help guide studying for the test. She makes plenty of past exams available and they all follow the same format. You have to really know your stuff but taking good notes on lectures and practicing is your best bet.
Not an empathetic professor. Incapable of understanding and listening to her students. Was unable to adjust to teaching to the pandemic, and was not lenient at all. Do not recommend.

Axelson has the most detailed lectures possible. They might be lengthy but most of it is her re-emphasizing the concepts. She explains the concept well and clear. The rest is all based on the work of the students.

I really wanted to like Jordan Axelson's class this term. She seems like a nice person and knows her stuff but that's about all the positives I can say. There was 2x as much lecture material as there would have been in-person and she penalized the whole class when a few people cheated by making exams closed-note.

Wants students to fail. The lectures are way longer than what is allowed. She doesn't care about the students. Orgo Chem 232 is obviously a hard class, but she makes it harder than it needs to be. Good luck if you have her, you'll need it.

Dr. Axelson really makes Organic Chemistry easier to tackle. She provides all of the information that is needed to do well, but it is up to the students to practice outside of class. Organic Chemistry is very difficult, but it is up to the student to practice daily.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Keep up with her calendar. Pace is fast, but if you keep up you won't get bogged down fast, and preparing for tests gets easier. Also she has a lot of exams. This fall she had 5 total, including final. You get to drop one and replace it with the highest score. Overall a great and understanding professor. She usually extends deadlines too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Its orgo. Youll have to work for the grade. Axelson just makes it better :)

Axelson thought now that classes were online, students somehow magically had more than 24 hours in their days. So in order to compensate for a seemingly longer day, Axelson decided her allotted 50 minutes of lecture time wasn't enough. Instead, it would be a good idea to make lectures that are 70 and 80 minutes in length. Horrible all around.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It was absolutely incredible to see a professor so blatantly unempathetic, and ignorant towards the most basic of issues that arise with switching to online class. She is a perfect example of a professor who lacks perspective on what it is to be a student during the covid pandemic. Wholeheartedly she is a disgrace to what it means to be a professor

Her lectures are actually really useful if you pay attention to her. Review lecture notes before taking the exam and actually do all the practice worksheets. It is a hard class but if you put the work in you can definitely get good grades in her class.

Axelson is decent. Her lectures are rushed, however if you record them and go over them later, they turn out to be pretty useful. The exams are extremely difficult, although somewhat similar to the practice exams she gives. IMO, the class got easier after going online since tests were open note. But overall, considering Orgo is hard, she's good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. She expects everyone to be smart like her because she was able to pass orgo. Doesnt give credit like she says for regrades so dont bother. Didnt curve this semester but has curved every other semester. Was not sensitive to the fact that we went online. Class just got harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Axelson is a fine person. However, once the COVID pandemic happened, I had to move back into a bad home situtation and after reaching out received little support. The class also seemed to get harder after we moved to remote learning. I ultimately had to drop it and a lot of my peers did too. This class is doable if you dont have an emergency.

Axelson is simply an okay professor. She gets the job done but does not stand out to me. She goes through material far too fast and seems like she just wants to get it over with. However, she does a good job of explaining it. I would not call her a bad professor or orgo I a bad class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you put in the effort and attend office hours, the class isn't that bad. Make sure you keep up with the coursework and try to go to the exam review sessions. There are extra credit opportunities and you can drop an exam, but there isn't really a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took orgo the second time around with Axelson and I went from getting a D- to an A-. She's amazing, and one of the most approachable professors I've ever had. She's an excellent lecturer, and makes difficult concepts understandable. She provides great notes and really useful resources like the practice worksheets. Take orgo with her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Axelson is a pretty good lecturer. The class is test heavy, but they give you plenty of resources to study with like practice questions and old exams. There are also plenty of office hours available between Axelson, Grad TAs and Undergrad TAs which I recommend going to at least before exams. Also there's a pretty thicc curve at the end.

yeah, unless you're good at chem or really enjoy it, or unless you're a pre-med, then just take this class in the summer at a community college or online at a different school. you're basically screwed if you miss lectures and even then she goes through a lot of material really fast. Oregon state offers Orgo online with great reviews fyi.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite teachers at uiuc. This is a very hard class, I'm talking spending 8-12 hours a week outside of class on it. all of the grading is very fair, and you exactly what is expected of you on exams. if you use Chegg for the online homework youll get 100% then you only have to worry about the exams. there is a big curve at the end.

Axelson is an amazing professor. I initially thought the course was difficult but really came to enjoy the material. Most people who thought the class was hard did not put in the work needed to do well in the course. Its really dependent on the amount of work you put into the course.

Lectures are awful. She absolutely steamrolls through some of the most difficult material students at this point have ever seen, and will often flat out refuse to clarify things. Avoid taking this lecture anytime in the morning unless you wake up at 6am every day for a caffeine IV.
if I had to do it all over again, I would have skipped lectures and taught myself how to do the worksheets

Dr. Alexson is amazing. Her lectures are engaging and helpful. There are tons of office hours, practice worksheets, and practice exams. She really cares about her students and tries all she can to help everyone succeed. My best advice is to put in the work by going to office hours and staying up to date with the worksheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures are fine but not really as engaging as they could be. Some of the ways in which she tries to get you to prepare for tests aren't really that effective. The practice problems don't really reflect test material as well as they could. Very average.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Everyone knows Orgo to be hard. Averages on the midterms were around D- to F for my class, so if you fail: don't panic. I failed 3 out of the 4 midterms and still ended up with a B. Pretty sure she curved the class at least 7%, so it will be okay. Study hard, do Axelson's practice worksheets, and good luck. Summarized in one word? Intense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Axelson is the best professor I've ever had. She made this class very enjoyable, the lectures are heavy so make sure to stay on top of the material. She also gives you one test drop out of 4 which is convenient since I was sick and didn't go to the last exam. I enjoyed this class so much I plan to take orgo 2 in the fall.

Dr Axelson is an amazing professor! For Orgo 1 she makes it very clear what will appear on her exams, what to study, and gives optional practice worksheets, which I recommend doing to get an A. Provides all the study material needed to get an A. Recommend going to the DAILY office hours staffed by herself and TAs. Generous curve in the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's organic chemistry, it's going to be a monster, but she really does give you everything you need to succeed in her class. Super accessible. SUPER TEST HEAVY. If you are rusty in chem, go talk to her and she will recommend where to start from. DO NOT Fall Behind. BEWARE Exams are 45 min! AND don't be afraid to ask questions, she is nice, so ask
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr Axelson is such an excellent professor! Going to her office hours helped a lot. Ill be happy to take another chem class with her!

An awesome teacher and a great class. Dr. Axelson provides all the resources you need to understand the material being taught, but you have to put in the effort and time if you want to succeed. Don't let the stigma of organic chemistry being a hard class affect you. Just apply yourself.

It's organic chemistry. It's going to be hard. The lectures can be a lot to digest, so be ready to review your lecture notes every day. She's very approachable during office hours and wants you to succeed. Keep up with the content, and you should be fine

She made lecture interactive and interesting however, she always seemed to rush to get all of the material for lecture done on time. Tests were fair and as long as you studied the videos, it was very much doable especially since her lectures just reinforced what the videos taught. In her office hours, she seemed to care about her students learning.

Well in a word she's way too smart and expects other people to be very smart too.  You need to print out all the slides and fill them out with details in lecture. Attendance isn't mandatory but you're basically screwed if you don't show up to class.:) Very hard class and she said the average is gonna be curved to a C+ or B-. Be ready to put in 5/5
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken. Period.

The best professor I've had in my college career. He's extremely caring, outgoing, intelligent, kind, and very charismatic. He always takes the time to give thoughtful feedback on every assignment and comes to class with a smile, ready to teach. He also always makes time to be accessible outside of class.
For CMN213. Professor Barley is always positive and energetic, and he really cares about every student. HIGHLY recommended!

Great professor. Material was a lot to read but it was not the worst thing ever. Readings as light as 5 pages and as heavy as 30 pages. Doesn't seem bad because the concept are taught and applied well. Very tough grader on group project. Focus hard on that and don't forget about it.

Definitely my favorite class of the semester. His lectures are super fun and always shows up to class with high energy. The topics taught are super prevalent to real life and the way he presents it is very easy to understand. He always makes you feel included and you start to feel like your class is a small family. Highly recommend Prof. WB!

Overall was a great professor, he made it clear when he told you something is important and actually cares about our understanding. He's enthusiastic and knowledgeable of his field. Exams and Group projects are what matters but be ready to read a lot for a short quiz- they're easy but can screw you over if you don't do them.

I would have LOVED this class if this teacher didn't teach it. Take any other CMN class, but you will hate end up regretting this one. So many unnecessary group activities that didn't teach us anything. Pointless lecture topics, I read more interesting innovation articles online during class lol. Quizzes were easy bc all online but stay away!
I loved this class and professor!!! He is very passionate about the class content and wants you to succeed. He has great energy and is very straightforward on grading. Highly recommend
very unapproachable. avoid at all costs.

Often contradicts syllabus and "final project instructions" PDF. The way the final project assignment is presented makes it seem like you can go in basically any direction you want, but certain small subtle things he says here and there throughout the semester contradict that. If you take his class, be sure to make friends to stay on top of things.

After the first quiz I switched professors, it was so bad. For lectures you work through a problem, without being taught how to do it first, and then he might explain the right way to do it after the fact, I basically learned nothing. I almost switched majors because of this, his way of teaching the class made me feel like I wasn't cut out for ECE

This class is not ordinary. Here is the components: exams, finals projects, labs, computer labs, homework that takes a lot google to solve. (sounds like a 6 credit class) However, the grading is based on how many components you can do well, not how you can do everything well. It is a class if you want have industry experience, I got 70% but B+.

He'll fly through 50+ dense slides in lecture, which is impossible to learn from or take notes. He gives long homework assignments that have nothing to do with the lecture, as well as lab reports and confusing simulations which are poorly taught. If you like semiconductors, take 444 and avoid Bayram. You'll learn nothing and do a ton of busy work.
Always prepared for lectures and the material was explained well by him. A lot of frustration my peers had was from the Lab portion of this class, but he was not involved with that.

Horrible, horrible instructor. He behaves nicely, yes, but nothing else. He sends out 200+ pages of slides every class and doesn't care about students' learning. He promises to give us formula sheets for exams but important equations are missing. He updates instructions after your submissions and criticizes you not to follow them.

He floods you with powerpoint handouts, and flies through them without a proper explanation of what is going on. Lectures are too broad and too shallow. The course content needs to be revamped. Illegible handwriting. Homework is poorly worded and is often plagiarized from other textbooks. Computer labs are confusing.

Can's the man. Although he sometimes go off on tangents, he gets the job done. Always does an abundance of example problems. Stays on the lecture schedule so the homework lines up with what we're learning. He has a dry sense of humor (but it's ECE, what do you expect?) that's very endearing. Zero regrets taking him.

HK207 is a great course to take to fill a quant 1; it's not hard at all for anyone with even the most basic math background. Watch all the lectures on 2x speed, and do all the discussion posts at once, and then respond later. Makes workload much easier. Midterm was open, so was the final, both extremely simple. Great Class for a tough credit.
Best professor I've had!

Easy A online class, but the workload was a lot for 2 credit hours. Homework consisted of chapter reading, 1 discussion post on a 30 min-2 hour documentary, 2 peer responses, and a quiz/short project. Course lasted 8 weeks and 8 modules with 2 exams (no final cumulative). Lots of opportunities for extra credit. Overall, it was a solid class.

Was an easy class for 2.0 credits. Online so submit the work on your own time by Sunday, and it is eight weeks, and the course itself is not too demanding. But be prepared it is a lot of movie-watching paired with discussion posts. There is one project, a midterm and a final, and quizzes so a lot of test material. Overall a great course!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really like her, this class would have been much better if it were in person because online was kind of difficult- there was a movie to watch almost every week with a 400 word discussion post plus two 250 word discussion replies due on Wednesday (400) and Friday (replies)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are a lot of weekly assignments in this class. A discussion post, two reply posts (400 words and 250 words), a quiz and all the readings. You also sometimes have to watch lengthy documentaries to be prepared for the discussion (usually interesting and on Netflix). Overall would give this class a 3/5. It's not bad, but not my favorite.
Not engaging at all, content was basic and not 400-level, overall pretty boring

Professor Besser is knowledgeable in her areas of research. There isn't much homework in this class and content is pretty straightforward. Attendance is not mandatory, and she is one of the chillest professors I've had. There is a group project, as long as you have a good team you're set. She posts the lectures on Canvas if you ask. Overall great.

She is an amazing professor but I feel like the content we study in this class is pretty logical and instead of holding lectures 3 times a week, I would recommend 2 lecture days with recorded videos only that students can refer to anytime. Her assignments are straightforward but they definitely helped me become a better research writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The lectures are not required, and rightfully so. They're not too informative, but as long as you put in work on the assignments, you'll get an A.

IS 407 is NOT a intro to data science. Be prepared to read, read, read from the text books and from the internet just to stumble through the assignments, especially if you do not have any prior Python experience. Get ready to ask a million questions and lean on your group project members for support. The most difficult class I've taken at UIUC.

No drops for attendance or homework. Attendance system is a random number generator. The textbook is full of typos so you have to constantly check the errata. No practice exams and the exams are very different from homework. Lectures are repeats of the textbook. Concepts are taught very slowly and out of order.

MY 4.0 GPA WAS RUINED BY A DISHONEST PROFESSOR! I asked during office hours about an attendance issue, and he said that attendance will not count for credit. He didn't put in 0's for attendance until the end of semester (otherwise at least I could've stopped missing classes after realizing something was wrong), costing 10% of my grade.

Dude gave no partial credit on exams, which is especially impactful due to tensor calculation errors that may propagate through problems. Attendance policy is completely unnecessary. We are adults here.
RIDICULOUS TEXTBOOK&HWs, ALSO EXAMs ARE VERY DIFFERENT FROM THE HWs

Took him for 398QIC (site doesn't have 398 as an option) in SP22.  Lectures were well paced and he did his best to simplify difficult concepts, and course structure was very well designed.  Was always willing to help during office hours and had a good sense of humor.  Wish more professors were like him.

Took him for 398 (rate my prof doesn't give the option).  Pre-lectures introduce you to the following lecture so you know what to ask about in class.  Explanations were generally well articulated, very friendly and willing to reexplain topics for you.  Homework difficulty is where it should be, exams were fair.  Top notch
Very inspiring teach. The highest rating professor in my heart by now.
Not getting an A solely due to not attending lectures, I wish Professor Doug could delete lecture and iclicker point and focus more on how well students understand the materials.

His lectures provided no information outside of the textbook but you were still graded on attendance and were expected to have already read. He had the homework due at 9:00 and the lecture started at 9:30, so you had to come a half hour early for no reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures were not incredibly clear. Oftentimes it felt as though the material in the textbook was just being repeated, however topics that were unclear were not made much better by the lectures.

He and Makins traded off lectures, so I got to experience both of them. I personally learned better from Beck, but Naomi's lectures were definitely more fun. They both know their stuff and care about the students. It's hard to go wrong in the physics department.

He has a very straightforward teaching style. His lectures are simply PowerPoint presentations. His teaching is formula-based and not very conceptual. The prelectures are basically the same as his lectures
If you can learn from video 'prelectures' and a professor that doesn't teach you anything, this is the class for you.

Beck is a good teacher and a nice guy.  The entire class is taught off of smartphysics, which makes lectures occasionally pointless.  He has a lot of demos and enjoys teaching.  Maybe not the best teacher ever, but certainly not a bad pick.  The tests are easy to lose points on, though.  Make sure to check your + / - signs (they love those signs)

He's alright.. But what I do wanna say something about the class. This is a HORRIBLY designed course. It's way too ridiculous for a gened and, believe or not, most teaching is done through smartphysics. Let's just be honest, how many people can actually sit down and learn stuff from youtube videos?

E&M is a difficult topic but the system they use to teach it is great. I don't think it matters whether you get Beck or Gladding because its the system that matters. I didn't pay close attention in lecture but Beck didn't seem to explain things very well sometimes, and you could learn it all in the HW anyways.
Pretty good lecturer. Class is hard in general but he helped.
He is an okay prof.. the class is generally hard though.. and he does not really help make difficult concepts easy. the course would have been a lot better if it was curved though..
He is a smart professor and I found his lectures very helpful.  Do not take this course lightly, it will be difficult, but Beck's lectures help.
Definitely knew his stuff but made this very abstract topic extremely boring and difficult.  Very friendly, very approachable, but is not great at explaining concepts.

One of the best teachers I've had. I was really nervous about public speaking going into the class, but he made the environment so fun and comfortable that it honestly didn't feel scary anymore. If you take this course, definitely take it with him!!!

Professor Gailey is an amazing guy who genuinely cares about both what he teaches as well as the students he teaches. He's extremely helpful and communicates quickly and clearly. He's the kind of professor who actually makes you want to come to class. I can't speak highly enough of him. He's one of the best professors at UIUC!

He was so understanding when I was going through my own personal problems and was not able to attend class. He would communicate with me if I was good to go for a speech or if I needed more time because he knew what i was going through. SO CARING!!

Professor Gailey is super hilarious, he has the voice of an opera singer lol. The class was super easy, pretty much a guaranteed A as long as you don't be too outrages. Not a lot of homework, exams are super easy as well. Definitely take this class with Professor Gailey!
Gailey's a great guy! Always ready to help when needed and answers email questions clearly. Gives great and helpful feedback.

Galley is an amazing professor, he keeps his lines of communication open and is pretty easy to reach with assignments. His grading is very clear, and if you struggle with work he's always there to help. As long as you do your assignments and reach out when you're struggling the class is a really easy A. He's very funny and he answers questions well
BJ's awesome. He cares more about us learning than he cares about grades. Interesting, engaging lectures helped a lot.

Best professor I've had in college. Amazing guy, made class fun to go to while still teaching us good public speaking skills. Truly cared about his students, and was very understanding. Assignments were fair and not too difficult, wish I could have him for all my classes.

BJ is by far the best professor I've had. I have spent hours underneath different teachers across the world and he is the real deal! He is engaging, caring, and so funny that it feels more than just a class, but an awesome experience. I have taken two of his classes and wish he would just teach all of the CMN courses because he is that good!

BJ is awesome! He is one of those professors that you have in college that you'll never forget. He is both hilarious and helpful. He's very understanding whether you've made a mistake, turned in late work, and the like. Also, his classroom activities are fun and informative. Great guy, great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: BJ is definitely a lot of fun and a great teacher. If you have the option to take CMN 101 with him I'd definitely jump on it
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: Honestly, at first, I was really scared of this class because the tests were difficult and there were quite a few. But, as time went on, it ended up being good because he offers so much extra credit, which brings your grade up. His lectures are also pretty interesting as he splits the time up well. I would recommend this class as an advanced psych.

Attendance isn't mandatory, showing up gets you extra credit and it's so worth it in the end. The tests are very hard but the homework is pretty easy. If you can do okay on the exams and do all the extra credit it's okay. exams are the con of this class but grateful for all the extra credit. class is split into activity then lecture

You can tell he really took previous feedback into account because he restructured the whole course, and it's now great! It was well-balanced in terms of assignments and grades. The first half of lectures, you do an experience which helps you learn the content in the second half. He's really clear and if you go to class, it's easy to do well.

Attendance is not mandatory but it counts as extra credit. It's the kind of course where the amount of effort you put into it will be reflected through your grade. Heavy on reading. Lots of extra credit offered. Exam questions are difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are boring, they aren't very interactive other than a few group questions but the majority of the class is just the professor talking. There's such a lack of structure to this class, it's very difficult to excel with only the given material. I would never take a course from this professor again.

Extremely tough grader. Exams are worth 50% of the class, and he includes information on exams that he explicitly stated would not be on them. Guidance is extremely unclear for the essays in the class- prompts are less than a paragraph, no rubric is provided, and no explanation is given for points taken off. Tons of useless busywork each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I know other people didn't like him that much, which is understandable because he isn't always an engaging lecturer. However, there are certain lectures that he is really passionate about, and you can tell when it is one of those days. He also really likes demos, which can be helpful.

Always ends lecture early due to a fast pace, one time ending a lecture in 20 minutes and disregarding questions. Lectures also have frequent mistakes, such as a wrong equation or bad math. Exams are also just like the practice exams, and likely not written by him.

It is easy to succeed in this class if you read the textbook and do all the practice problems. The tests were fair and based on the practice test given. I thought he was one of the best physics lecturers I have had. Read the textbook repeatedly, do every problem, and you will do well. A 50% or 60% test weight is very forgiving.

Obviously does not care about his students' learning. Blasts through lectures at an impossible pace, adding little to no insight. Self-study required if you actually want to learn. Ends class absurdly early instead of taking time to go in depth into material. Avoid unless absolutely necessary!

I had heard awful things about him but 435 was really chill. Exams were similar to practice papers, homeworks were from Griffiths. He was really nice about excused absences even for homeworks. His lectures were mid but the lecture slides were fun to study from. He was pretty fair about curving exams too.
This is a self-teaching class. Exams are 50% of the grade, and he designs the exams quite inefficiently.

CHEEEEEEKS when it came to lectures and covering material. Exams pretty mid and passable but need to teach yourself most of the material. Extremely mid professor. Mid beard, mid notes, mid life. Peace

He's great at explaining things in lecture, goes slowly but is very precise and clear with ideas presented in class. I'm guessing the textbook would help with the first half of the class, however. Grading is homework heavy, which is a plus!

Hooberman is overall a very chill and understanding guy. Very patient with questions. His style of explanations I found sometimes a overly lengthy and hard to pick up the main points as a result. I highly recommend the textbook for this class. It's much more concise with explanations and helps greatly with homework.
Extra credits were rewarded for i-clicker attendance and extra homework. grading criteria was overall friendly.

Definitely do the prelectures and maybe take notes on them because they're really helpful to keep up in lecture, as the material is gone over very quickly. Personally I learned more from the prelectures than i did from the actual lectures because I could stop and take notes.
He is good at explaining the material and knows his stuff well. The class has the same structure as all 200 level physics courses, and they have put a lot of thought into the class's structure.

Professor Hooberman is such a cool guy that if you're picking Phys 212 you should take his class. Full of experiments in his classes, he's always the one who can explain hard concepts by pieces so that everyone can understand it! I really like him!

There were a lot of writing assignments with unclear guidelines as to what she wanted. Long exams. Grades very slowly. Never got to know my final exam or final project scores. Insanely messy lectures that were hard to follow. Very long exams as well. Assumes you are an expert in the field, even though it's a 100-level gen ed course.

Professor is definitely passionate about archaeology which shows in her lectures. Lectures are interesting if not slightly disorganized. Prof gives review questions that are similar to tests and allows note sheets. End-of-semester project is time consuming. Grading is often very slow but good feedback is provided.

- lectures were dense, unorganized. goes on long tangents sometimes. big issue when the exams are based on lectures + significance. 
- slides were not always complete with details, hard to use for review. pointless review ?'s too.
- REALLY slow grader. took a month to grade short assignments and exams. didn't give reason why.

would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ppl take this bc it's a 2 in 1 gen ed and the prof doesn't realize that ppl don't care about the development of ancient cities. lecture schedule wasn't followed and lectures were posted randomly. lecture videos were 2 hours+. tests were on small details from the 2 hour lecture and you can't change an answer once you move on to the next question

Prof. Bevis is a nice person, but goes on many tangents which caused the mandatory lectures to be very confusing and the class to miss two weeks of planned material. She is also a really slow grader. The first midterm took over a month to get graded, and we did not have the second grade going into finals, with a 7 page final project due as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bevis is a teacher whose lectures can be all over the place, but are still thoroughly enjoyable and contain good content. This class had group seminar discussions, and the readings could pile up if you didn't get to them in a timely manner, but she's lenient if you communicate any issues in a polite and timely manner. Enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The lectures were all over the place and were not structured in the most efficient way. When the test is solely based on lectures, this is a huge problem. She would also lie about how long lectures would be in the announcements she posted. Do not take this class with this professor.

please don't take this if she is your teacher. i can't really get into it due to word count but there are multiple 1.5-3 hour lectures posted speratically so you can't even plan out your week, and any random comment she says can potentially be on the test. so, if you don't write every word of the 2 hour lecture you are not getting full credit.

Very interesting lectures on cool topics, but she grades very hard. We're not historians! We're simply students taking a GenEd. Quizlet is your friend for this class: dates, definitions, and image recognition are very important: they are on the exams. A couple projects and extra credit chances, they aren't terrible, though she grades very slowly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very strange professor, but nice. Lectures are all over the place, and in an extremely lecture heavy class that became a bit of a problem. If you're not already obsessed with archaeology, just take a different gen-ed. You won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bevis was a great teacher. She does a good job keeping the material engaging for her students. She is a slow grader, and there is a lot of work for a gen-ed credit. That being said, extra credit is plentiful, questions over email have a quick response, and the class is graded fairly. I enjoyed taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Bevis is entertaining during lecture, but very unclear with her grading. She grades papers very late (e.x. submitted 3 of 12 grades by Reading Day) and is not entirely clear with how assignments should be formatted, such as using AJA format on an essay. In a class so open to interpretation, just use what the textbook tells you to believe.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Bevis is a wonderful professor and is clearly passionate about her work. However, for a gen ed class, the workload and studying can become very time consuming especially if paired with heavy courses (I'm taking Orgo & Anatomy). Be prepared to take notes and pay attention in class because the lecture slides are not enough to just look back at.

I had her for CLCV 160, very entertaining lecturer and I have learned a lot from her class. She is a tad unorganized, at least this semester. She seems to be very busy and has not graded much since the first test. This is a test heavy and memorization heavy course, so if you do not want to memorize dates and names this might not be for you.

Dr. Bevis made history exciting with jokes, engaging lectures, and relevant material. We reviewed in class, and she was understanding of conflicts. We did use the textbook for exams and before-class readings (short, manageable). Very fair grader. One of my favorite classes of all time. I CANNOT RECOMMEND DR. BEVIS HIGHLY ENOUGH!
Do yourself a favor and take an easier gen ed.

She is the best out of the 120 professors this semester - explains concepts thoroughly and pauses for questions throughout the lecture. Overall, Bhat is a great professor and it's clear that she cares about her students unlike the other professors.
great professor, learned a lot in her classes and helped with the exams and homeworks in the class
Have a hard time understanding her
She is a reachable and responsible professor
Wasn't clear at explaining harder concepts, and often times spent too long on things that weren't hard. Overall very easy to fall asleep.
Great lecturer. She articulates the class materials very well and she cares about the learning experience of students. Very good lecturer in general.

Suma was OK at teaching the relatively simple concepts, but for the more difficult ones, I would come out of lecture not understanding anything. For a lot of it, I had to go back and watch lecture videos from the other professors, and a lot of the time there was no time to do that so I just had to figure it out from friends or from YouTube.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Ok at best, her lectures are hit and miss on whether or not they make sense. If it's a really technical topic, watch Jaramillo's lecture videos, because he's way better at explaining things. The test in this class are pretty tough too, especially since the TA's grade them so ruthlessly. If you can I would get someone else for ECE 120 lecture.
He's cool...
he knows everything... and expects me too
ha ha poor sophomores been asking me how his class is :-)
Extremely smart
makes you go to class and calls you out if you even yawn. But he is brilliant and funny. Really knows his stuff.
Too much work. Grading is hard. Final grades are great.

The exams were tough and the homework was crazy. But the final grade was better than I expected. Really helpful guy but I was very scared to go up to him. Starts asking questions back if you ask him any.
This class is tough! Too much work but Bhargava is helpful if you speak to him. Kind of a cool guy in a weird way. Speak to him and find out that he really cares that the students learn.

Lots of work and hard grading is the story of this class.  Basically is the course work of 3 seperate classes all put together into 1.  Bhargava sees undergrads the same as grad students and has the same expectations.  Kinda ridiculous but probably going to be a useful class in the long run
was not a great experience.

He talked a lot in his class and it was solely based on the readings. He often questions people who do not have their hand raised, so get ready to read. His TA was extremely nice and made it impossible for people to fail this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: he has favorites and if you are not one of them, because you were not born a certain way he likes, good luck. avoid avoid avoid...
Horrible experience, awful semester. There are classes I cannot take anymore as they are taught by him. Mentally I felt drained in his classes. discriminates and not willing to listen. very stubborn

the worst professor i have ever met. he discriminates many students in the class. i also hope it is reported at some point. also, not a good teacher. lectures are boring and so hard to follow, zero structure.
Awful is an understatement. He discriminates against minorities, especially Black and Brown students. He treats many other BIPOC students awfully. I hope someday someone reports him.
very disrespectful and never prepared. he just wants to talk and talk and talk ; this class does not teach anything
he is dicriminatory. he definitely favors a certain group students in his class and ignores the rest. very disrespectful.

there are only two things he does in the class: discrimate students whom he does not like (mostly minorties that I dont wanna mention) and try to make unbearable jokes. oh, one more thing, he is so disrespectful.
RRR. Rude, repetitive, relies on student presentations to take up most of the class time.
he was never prepared. the only thing he does is to call out his students and discourage them. It was an awful semester.
he discriminates a lot. His class is very hard to follow. He always makes jokes that are awfully not funny. Never again. It is usually an easy A for obeyers. I was not one of them, so yeah.
Dr. Bhatt has been one of my favorite professors in the MATESL program. Get ready for awesome lectures and very engaging discussions. His classes are never boring!
Don't take his class.

I get that people can be late, but the class location was inconveniently located. Also, picking on students who are late is disrespectful. It's college, there will be at least few people late. I was just 5 minuets late and he picked on me once.  Lastly, why give big project towards end of the semester, why not during middle.
Really.... the worst class in graduate courses. Class is very, very difficult to follow.

He will call on you. I never did the readings because he will eventually tell you everything you need to know. Be forewarned, if you haven't read, he will be less than pleased. It was an interesting class and an easy A.
He's a nice guy except for when you are late.  He calls out a lot of people in front of the class.  Other then that, its a very simple class.  Easy A.

Very good teacher. Humorous, interesting, and instructive. By attending his class i really feel like i did my work and got my rewards, and a well-deserved one. But he doesn't like people being late though

Awful. Tells lots of Rambling, repetitive, unrelated stories. He's friendly but I learned nothing. Grade was based on participation which was difficult because I couldn't develop ideas on concepts I did not understand.
I LOVED this class! If linguistics is not your thing, maybe it's the best fit, but Dr. Bhatt is totally reasonable and has a great sense of humor. Great freshman class - super easy A.

First day in this class, I felt really interested. Professor Bhatt leads very good discussions; but tends to select a few students. This class was very easy. I got over 100% on everything.  Definitely a class I would recommend.

This class is really informal, really fun. Not difficult concepts, but you learn a lot. Bhatt really wants to know the students. Good teacher. Funny, keeps your attention. Lots of class involvement. Lectures not really necessary. Highly recommend. DON'T take LAS 101 freshman accompaniment .. that sucks. Stupid and pointless.

Cool guy. Easy A. Most of the material is common sense. Laura (the TA) is very helpful and runs the class when Dr. Bhatt doesn't come (which is a lot). Friday classes always have a quiz or short reflection paper. DON'T take the LAS class that goes along with it! I do recommend going to class to get the worksheets to help study for the midterm/final

He's a pretty cool guy that is easy to talk to and he wants to learn your name.  The class is very informal.  The material is interesting but gets repetitive. Laura (the TA) is very nice and helpful.  It is very easy to BS on the essays and quizzes because the questions are asking your opinion.  Good guy, good class.
Never take a sociolinguistics graduate seminar with this guy. YAWN! he insults students in class.

This class is SOOOO EASY!!! i havent done the readings in weeks and i have gotten 100% on every quiz and reflection paper (1 page)  If Laura is your TA you are set.  She is soo nice and basically gives you the questions on the quizes the night before.  The LAS 101 part of this class is sooo stupid and pointless though.  This class is an easy A/A+

I was a "5" in interest before the class started, now I'm at a "1". This is a pointlessly laborious class with the even worse addition of the mandatory LAS 101 class. Both suck in my opinion and are wastes of time. Avoid this if it's your general elective; take it if you are very much so interested in globalization...

this professor takes the award in the linguistics department! he is HORRIBLE! can't speak English, is not well-read and very anti-intellectual. interested in sociolinguistics? look in for anthro, education and communication programs.
No Comments
No Comments

The worst class I took  EVER! He was hardly prepared and I felt that I knew more about the field than he does. So I am not going to continue with this school for grad studies because I want to do a PH.D. in Linguistics. He is very unclear and needs to improve a LOT.
Total and complete Waste of time! the guy is an idiot. I had hard time keeping awake in his class.
No Comments
Pretty easy going. Great discussions, very informal setting.
really really cool and funny guy. shows at least a MILLION videos over the semster. papers are easy, class is great.
The class overall is great but she gossips.
Dr. Bishop genuinely cares about her students and wants them to improve their public speaking skills, so she gives a lot of feedback and is always willing to help out before or after class.
She really wants you to succeed. Offered interview help for students and was less focused on grading compared to improving students ability.
Super chill. It was a fun class to take. Felt like a family not a class by the end.
i love this woman. best prof ever. everyone should take a class with her if you get the chance
Dr. Bishop handled unwieldly and otherwise dull material with life and vigor, and made everything much more interesting.

Mardia is a great teacher for CMN101. She can be weird and quirky at times, but it's why students love her. You are required to buy the workbook for this class and you will definitely use it. My tips: Do every assignment (grade boosters!), get to class early on days you might sign up for speech times, sit in the front of the room, and PARTICIPATE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bishops Rhetoric of War class was amazing, thought-provoking. Best. Professor. Ever.
Dr. Bishop's class was a time--even though it's the basic com class, she still did a good job of making the material relevant and not mundane.

Prof. Bishop was by far the best professor that I've had in college so far. Her lectures and discussions in class are interesting and relevant. I always felt valued in the class. However, make sure you get to class on time.

Awesome all around teacher. Really willing to help students and take time out of class to go over tough material or issues with grades. Speeches are medium difficulty, and definitely need work put in out of class. Go to lecture and do your work, and you've pretty much got an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Brilliant teacher. This was the best class I've ever had in college. She cares and makes you think.
A great teacher. I was having trouble in the class and she helped me to get ahead. I would highly recommend her to any of my friends, and would want to take another of her classes.

I had her for CMN496. The class was pretty pointless. With only 9 people in class we basically listened to her conversations with the TA. This class is nothing like it sounds, but if you need an easy elective I would do it. 5 short questions on plays and 2 exams.

If you are bad at speech, she will give you a good grade. However, if you are good, she will grade your speeches harder and you will receive a lower letter grade. Class is pointless but you can only miss two classes before participation points are deducted.

Not the worst but her monotone voice and attitude towards students made me rate her a bit lower. At times I couldn't tell if she was purposely being a little rude or if her energy is just a little bit cold. The visual analysis would be annoying because it would be in groups and her grading was specific. Only good thing were online Friday classes.
great professor, provided positive feedback

prof. bigsby is a great professor who seems to enjoy what she does/teaches! Her class is interesting and easy as long as you show up to lecture and pay attention. There are weekly quizzes but you can drop a couple and then exams and one final group project that is fun! Her class is really enjoyable and fun to learn about!

Professor Bigsby is so awesome. Study before the tests, come to the lecture, and you'll get a high A for sure! I really love this class and she clearly cares and knows the material very well. Also-- participate! It's not necessarily mandatory but it definitely shows her you know what you're doing. Nothing but good things to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Bigsby was absolutely amazing! I had her twice for both semesters in one school year and I enjoyed her both times. She is a very fair grader and sets the standard and tone of the classroom at the beginning of the year. Take CMN 345 and CMN 421!
she's really caring about her students and if you put in the work, you're grade will reflect!

Dr. Bigsby is an amazing professor. She really knows her stuff and keeps her lectures interesting. This course is nothing like CMN 321(which was awful). It's very interesting content and she breaks up the lectures with class activities. Fair grader and the book is easy to read. Daily writing summaries, 3 exams, 1 paper, and 1 final research paper.

I absolutely loved this class. It was so interesting and she is an extremely FAIR grader. There is reading you have to do beforeclass and you write a short summary that is collected. Really recoommend this class.

She gives quizzes on each reading you do for class. You are not aloud to use the notes you may have taken so you essientially have to study each reading before each quiz. Also the lectures are not helpful and pretty much had to teach myself everything because she gave little to no clarification. No notes or structure given.
Very clear. Lectures are short with a group work. Tests are not bad, and she is helpful.

There are a lot of assignments in this class, and most of them are group work. However, the assignments aren't too hard and Prof Bigman was always available to help. She provided study guides that helped me get good exam scores. There were also in-class quizzes that usually I didn't do well on and there's a presentation at the end of the semester.

Exam was killer, class median was 65 with average of 69 with no intention to curve or do test corrections. Project has been a wild ordeal, little guidance and unorganized check points. I cannot get an A anymore due to the exam so im pretty much coasting the rest of the year for any B. Id stay away and take a much easier class.

Prof Bigman is a very kind person and very knowledgeable, but her lectures are so boring and some the material taught makes no sense. Exams are tough but assignments are easy. She can be a tough grader. I've gotten a lot of 9.2/10. Lots of material to know for midterms. I've had her for 2 different courses and I dread going to both. She is kind tho

Her lectures don't relate to the midterms or the readings, very vague about assignments. Paragraphs of information on the slides in class and she moves way too fast for you to write anything down. Currently week 8, only had a single 5 point quiz, and a midterm last week, midterm was a curveball of information that seemed unrelated to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be upfront about her needing to lecture slower (doesn't post her slides but has PARAGRAPHS of info on them), the final paper has some nonsensical source requirements + she isn't clear on what you are doing exactly content wise, and expect this class to take up a lot of time from the reading (that has related assignments due before each class).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She likes to go on tangents A LOT, but knows what she is talking about. Sometimes she didn't stick to the syllabus because we would get behind and so I wasn't always prepared to discuss some of the readings. Survived this class by being upfront about her needing to be organized. Always addressed and listened to suggestions. A lot of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The amount of homework to pass this class is absurd. The material is very interesting but the professor is obsessed about homework for every single class. Moreover, you have 3 exams (about 45 multiple questions + 5 essay questions) and a final essay. If you're taking other courses be aware that this course will take a lot of your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Bigman knows what she is talking about and her enthusiasm rubs off on the students. A good class.

She is the absolute worst teacher I have ever had at UIUC! I heard great things about this class with the other teacher who used to teach it, so I was excited to take this class. DO NOT TAKE IT if Ms. Bigman is your professor!!!

Poor explaining during his lectures and instead quickly goes through example problems without explanation of where anything comes from. He was only at  ~50% of the lectures throughout the semester with zero accountability. Yet when a student is gone for research/conference, he is not accommodating as he denies requests for the lecture recordings.

Great pedagogue; able to explain complex, difficult, concepts and problems that will make your head spin. Excellent teacher and a leader in his field. However, the workload is obscene. Also, he missed about 8 lectures, including his own final and three lectures prior to the midterm. Takes lots or trips to China; nobody holds him accountable...
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class! Learnt a lot and the homework was well designed.
Required grad course. Too much HW but good Prof
It is a very dedicated professor but it is not clear. The subject its really demanding but not conceptually clear. I found it not good in the end. To much work and not much learned.

I took Dynamics with Prof. Spencer. He is a good professor but very hard to get a hold of. Lectures are very clear. He uses a digital input instead of writing on the board which comes with its set of pros and cons.  TA was helpful in office hours.

He is not a good lecturer.  He diverted attention from the main principles of the class by getting us to focus on MATLAB, which was unnecessary for the subject material.    The book he asked us to purchase was terrible. There are books of better quality on the market that he could have recommended.  He showed very little interest in our learning.

He is very smart, and is very good at explaining things. He sometimes comes across as mean or crass, but i think in general he is a nice guy. The class is run very well. I didn't do well on some of the tests, but he curved the class substantially.

Good professor, very smart. However, if you go ask him a question and you are not an Asian female, he will be very condescending. Do not go to his office hours, you will be ignored. The class overall is run well. Tests aren't impossible and the homework is from the book and relatively easy, but this class TAKES A LOT OF TIME
Professor Vermillion is so fun, caring and a great lecturer!

Great teacher, but would recommend that you take a general film course before this, because he expects you to have a basic knowledge of film techniques and skills before entering the class. Always open to questions. Would recommend.

Billy is awesome. Period. He explains things so clearly. His method of teaching is conducive to learning- watch a movie, discuss readings about the movie and other topics, watch clips that tie both readings and movie together. These clips provide inspiration for papers. I've said too much. Billy is awesome, if you have a chance, take his class.

This guy really likes what he's doing, and that makes class so much more fun. He's seen every movie and explains things really well. Three 5-6 page papers and a midterm in class, no final (we had a final paper instead). Just come to class, do the papers, and enjoy. This guy is fun. I'd take him again.
puts a significant emphasis on attendance. Too much course material for a 100 level course. DO NOT TAKE AS A GEN ED.

If you don't like to read, don't take a class with Dr. Birkenholtz because there is a LOT of it, though generally if you go to the lectures and pay attention you can make it through without doing most of the readings. She's a decent lecturer, but covers way more than what is on the PPT slides. Papers were not too difficult, but the texts are needed
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Although this class required a lot of reading and a fair amount of writing, I would sign up for another class with her in a heartbeat! She really works to make the material accessible and engaging to students, and she seems to honestly care what students think.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Too much material packed into a simple 100 Level Course. It seems as if she cares more about you regurgitating what the Westerners say rather than actually encouraging free-thinking and critical analysis. WAY TOO MUCH WRITING and lengthy readings for a 100 level course. I got this overwhelming impression that she was trying to PROVE herself.

Knows what shes talking about but spends so much time talking there wasnt a single day she didnt go a few minutes past when class was supposed to end.  Theres a ton of reading and no time to catch up. If you end up taking the class (which I honestly dont recommend) watch out for the final paper because she gives you zero time time to work in class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is a good professor, but the course itself is much more advanced for a 100-level class. Weekly quizzes are not too bad if you go to lecture, but she only has one midterm and four essays before the final, and the midterm was pretty hard. Make sure to read the assigned texts and try to stay on top of what she says in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Annoyingly busy for a 100 level class...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Prof. Birkenholtz is a very engaging, enthusiastic professor. If you are interesting in Hinduism, definitely take a class with her. But don't take her 350 class unless you have a ton of time to read - we read an avg of  60pgs/class. She is super understanding if you need any extensions or are having trouble with the class. Be sure to communicate!!

Really fun class if you're interested in Hinduism! Professor B is amazing, she really knows her stuff. Pretty small class, so expect to participate. LOADS of reading. 2 midterm and 1 final. Bi-weekly response papers to readings (750-1000 words) which count for a significant portion of the grade. Also weekly reading quizzes. Mandatory attendance!

This Introduction to Hinduism class seemed far from an introductory course. She expected us to all have a pretty solid foundation of knowledge in the religion. Many of the students in my class did have a solid foundation and she seemed to enjoy them more. Would not take again. Hard A and tests incredibly lengthy and detailed. GL

Boring lectures. Reads off slides. Make sure you understand the material by closely reading the books. Do not depend on the lectures and TA sections. Weekly quizzes, and they are not the easiest. Tests are difficult, long, and require a lot of analysis; no practice exams. On a scale of 1-10, the amount of effort you have to put in for an A is 8.

Amazing professor, very knowledgeable about her field. Very helpful with me when I couldn't make deadlines and the topic was very interesting! If you are interested in women in Hinduism this is the professor for you!

This class was supposed to be an easy A before she replaced the previous teacher. She tries too hard to be cultural, and poorly reads off powerpoints. Exams were a lot of writing. Study hard, and an A is doable.

Dan is a great guy but beware that his classes are heavy on work. the grading isn't hard and its relatively easy to get an A if you put in the work for it, but that usually means lots of hours outside of class/labs per week. He expects you to come into the lab to work on all of your homework so you can't just do it at home on your schedule.

Block is admired for developing the class so I was excited. But, he mocked mistakes, loudly. Lectures were unorganized and labs were four full hours a week. It was hard to focus with him hovering and nitpicking. I want a class where trying something new and failing, is okay. He also leans on our shoulders when he's frustrated.

At first he was a nice guy since he seemed interested in us. Throughout the semester he has yelled/belittled students, and talked to us like we were kids. He will call you out/yell at you if you don't go to lecture, even though he is a horrible lecturer and can't teach. For a final project worth 30% of our grade, we have less than 2 weeks...

He is only nice to you when you are not asking for help. You constantly need his help because he can't teach. When you ask him for help, he is very rude. I always try to ask for the TA because the TA is nice and doesn't judge you. His lectures suck too, escpecially since they are mandatory in his mind. Just a rough class.

His lectures are useless. He goes all over the place. Honestly the only good thing about his lectures is he reminds you of the due dates. The TA is nicer and could teach this class better. He is a bad teacher. His examples are so terrible. This class is only easy to understand when you are a CS major. I regret taking this course. Also so mean...

No exams, all labs and projects. If you are not good at coding, then don't take this class. He is mean to the students that don't understand is lectures. He will be like, "I said this in lecture!" "you are not listening" "You can't do that." "lets go back to kindergarden and relearn how to listen and understand what I am trying to have you do" MEAN

I haven't learned anything in his class. His lectures suck, and they are mandatory. If you miss a lecture, he will basically cry about it to you until you come to class, because "you are missing important details" I go to the lectures and I am always lost in the labs and projects. Then he is mean to you when you don't understand his lectures...

His lectures are all over the place. I never understand what he is talking about, and he wants everybody at his lectures. Honestly, if you skipped all his lectures you would still be in the same place with everybody before the lab. When you ask for help, he can be very weird and mean to you. The TA is so much nicer than him. Worse teacher ever!

If you take any controls labs at the U of I, you will no doubt work with Dr. Block. One of the best professors and classes I have taken in undergrad. Dr. Block is very reasonable and works harder on his courses than any other professor/lecturer I've ever taken a class with. He wants you to learn and enjoy learning and I appreciate that.

Dan is really hands-on guy. ME461 taught by him is a good course if you want to gain more experience on the hardware side and see how exactly things like micro-controllers work. The lectures are decent but it is mostly from the labs, that you learn the most. His grading is pretty reasonable and course load is not that much
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Excellent professor, the best course I had in college.

Dan is hands down the best professor I had at UIUC.  I've learned more useful information from him than every other class, and his classes are the reason I got my job so easily.  Truly cares about his students, and will do anything to help.  His classes are very easy to get an A in if you do the work, which isn't always easy.  Highly recommend him
Very good at teaching control and aspects of mechatronics theory. Super patient with students. One of the most helpful professors I've had.

Great and patient professor! Love him so much. Before attending the class, he warns you not to take it if bad at programming. After enrolling, he tries whatever way to help. Learn a lot about mechatronics and DSP!

I didn't know he was fired, thought he just quit due to backlash from students. Most beneficial MCB department moment, I love them so much! They are so cool and I never knew that I could meet people that are so nice!
We need him back in MCB, was my favorite professor and they got rid of him after a few weeks, terrible decision.

Dr. Blank was a great professor, very understanding and kind! He wouldn't try to trick us on assignments or exams, and would prioritize our learning and our comprehension. He was also fair in general, and would give back points often. The MCB department made a terrible mistake when removing Blank from his position and I think they should be ashamed

I was sad to find out that they fired him. He was a nice guy who wasn't given the resources he needed by the MCB department. Totally believe he would've done well with teaching what we needed to know if they gave him some more direction instead of just throwing him into it.
He was a great professor but wasn't given a chance by the department
Boring lectures, good grading at the end. Take advantage of revision policy
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class is a lot of work, especially depending on your group members. Generally, it's a free A although grading can be tough on certain assignments. Blake can be disrespectful/rude to students especially during presentations. However, you will learn a lot in 470

I have mixed opinions about this class. Very time consuming, especially at the beginning and during admin terms w all the meetings. Johnson is a somewhat strict professor overall. At the same time I feel like this class has taught me a lot of useful engineering skills. And the grading is complicated but they're pretty lenient on larger assignments.

Blake Johnson is why ME 310 and 320 are so inconsistent in their labs. The TAs are not well-briefed on their labs or how to grade the labs, leading to very unclear in-class activities and even more inconsistent grading. In reviewing other section's work, I found that I received significantly lower grades for better work. He needs to step it up!
He grades things very harshly and the rubric is very unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Assistant Professor Blake Johnson is the last professor you would want to take. Good luck if your major is Engineering Mechanics because he is going to be in your way. Treat students extremely biased based on his favor. Students' grades are given based on vague evidence, with a nonsense grading rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is not a good person to run the labs. No clarity, and his grading policies are ridiculous. My TA was apparently instructed to take off points for every little thing (like italics, headers, etc), while another TA in the same section apparently did not. I loved the lectures, but this lab is atrocious.

Tough grade because I love Professor Johnson as a person, but this is the most unorganized and poorly run lab I've taken in 4 years at UIUC. The TAs (mine and a friend's in a different section) don't know what is going on or just aren't good teachers. Difficult to understand. Reports are weird and lengthy every week. Lab is loud and TA is on phone.
Worst guy at UIUC MechSE

He made the lab confusing and isn't responsive to emails. Lab reports are sometimes in weird formats such as TikTok videos and the grading is unclear. The lab videos he provided were edited to be sepia-colored, which made it hard to tell what was going on. He also made us go to lab (during COVID) even though we only did worksheets, not actual labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Johnson is respectable overall and gives relevant feedback on student projects. However he consistently makes low effort in communication which pushes projects back considerably. Difficult to contact via email unless you talk to him directly, which is only once a week. This is his main fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Johnson wasn't bad on his own. However, the course grading was unfair, and ultimately the quizzes single-handedly destroyed my otherwise perfect grade. Despite doing well on the final, homework, and showing up to every classes, the quizzes tore my grade apart. Unsure if these are his fault or not, but as the professor, it needs to be partly on him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Johnson is awesome. He is funny, approachable, and explains things clearly. TAM 210/211 is pretty difficult just due to the unfair set up of quizzes, however this is a fault of the department and Proj. Johnson. Definitely take a class with him if you have the option.
You will learn the ways of Blake Johnson. He is a legend. The class can be difficult, but Blake is always there to cheer everyone up, sort of, kind of.  Great professor, even better guy.

Class was pretty hard in terms of homeworks and exams. Very thorough lecturer but lots and lots of derivations. His notes are straight from the textbook. Pretty cool guy. Fluids is his field so he is very knowledgeable for this class

He was very clear throughout the semesters with his lecturing. Sometimes I think he  got too carried away with example problems that he did, but really all-in-all he was a great professor and I would choose his class every time.
Professor Johnson is all around amazing. He is a crystal clear lecturer with extremely fair homework and exams. Any course he teaches, regardless of what it may be, I would take in a heartbeat.

He is a great professor; TAM 212 is supposed to be one of the harder courses you take, but he made it seem very reasonable-even a little interesting!  Testsreports are very fair.  Would take any other class he teaches
Very clear during lectures and tests are very reasonable

Blake is a very energetic professor. Kind of tends to ramble and go off track a little bit, so sometimes it seems like it's not worth going to lecture. He is very receptive however and fair with exams and reports.
Didn't really like the class material, but he seemed like a pretty cool guy. Little nerdy in the sense that he loves what he does, but that really helps make lecture more interesting

One of the GOATS here at UIUC. Class structure is great; pre recorded lectures with in person discussion and online discussion board (Packback). He did an amazing job of covering many intro microbiology topics while still giving us interesting details, including things pre-meds, pre-dents, pre-pharm students will find particularly interesting

He is very generous and super approachable. Very fair by spreading the exam questions evenly for every lecture. After every lecture, he goes back to the slides and adds extra necessary info which was super helpful. His exam questions were sometimes vague, but overall exams were fair and reflected the material covered in class only (not readings).

He's an okay teacher. His lecture slides are LOADED with stuff, yet you only get tested on a fraction of it, so its hard to know what youre supposed to study. Had him for the second half of MCB 300 (first half was taught by Cari vanderpool) and his teaching/testing style literally ruined my perfect grade of an A+.

Prof Blanke is very very knowledgeable and knows the material very well. He does a good job bridging topics and making important connections and answers questions well. I'm not too fond of the huge amount of points figure presentations are worth, especially if you happen to end up with a lame figure. Study hard and attend class, and you'll do fine!
An amazing mentor and guide throughout the 2 courses. She is like a friend who is accessible and I can reach out to her for any of my personal struggles. Will 100% recommend her.
Very understanding and easy to access and teach

Dr. Bliss clearly cares about her students. She does so much out of class to make sure her students feel supported which meant a lot to me as a freshman with all online classes. She knows a lot and is amazing at sharing her knowledge. Her assignments are well thought out and manageable. I felt like I learned a lot.

The class was pretty easy. Because of COVID everything was online/zoom: lecture once a week and studio once a week. She offered a lot of extra credit opportunities. We had do to a weekly discussion post, quiz and weekly reading, not hard. There was a lot of drafting involved was time consuming, but not too difficult.
He was difficult and gave me lots of unecessary stress
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Easy A. Teacher personality very poor.
Horrible Teaching Assistant. One of the worst classes I've taken at U of I.
Joel is really laid back. Attendance is mandatory because there are pop quizzes and in-class writings. It was pretty easy.

He's a great teacher, and has a pretty good sense of humor. You don't have to show up to class, but he does do pop quizzes. If you don't do the small readings and study the pp you won't do well. His tests are completely based on his pp, word for word. Easy A.
Great!

I wasn't too impressed by the class. Lectures were bare bones slides she threw together right before coming to class, and the four response papers we had to write I basically wrote in 10 minutes and my only feedback was a letter grade and a one-word descriptor - "great", "good", "excellent", etc. I didn't learn much but I got to see cool films
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Blake was an absolute joy to have as a professor. The class was on the second half of French and Comparative Cinema, and the list of films was incredibly curated. I enjoyed almost every film screened in class, and the PPT presentation she gave following the film gave new insight. The assignments were manageable and interesting. Great Prof!

I loved this class. Professor Blake's discussions were provocative and I had an amazing experience with her. She is vague about grading and projects, but I found her enjoyable. Her style of teaching isn't for everyone, but if you have any interest in the subject matter, her classes are great.

Nancy Blake is the worst professor at the University of Illinois. She studied under eminent theorist Jacques Lacan and obviously learned nothing. She quoted wikipedia and Sparknotes gratuitously and spoke in a slow, inoculating tone. She is awful and hope that you never have to take a class with her. Grading is completely based on your TA.

I think the others explain her perfectly! Her class wasn't too bad except she was very vague about the exam content. She flat out said to just study EVERYTHING for the exams with no study guide or anything, although paying attention to recurring themes in lecture hint at the exam contents. I didn't like that she was so vague in that way.

This woman is boring as hell...  The lectures have so much discussion of the history and so little discussion about important aspects of the works we read.
