She mentions something in lecture one time and it appears on the final.  Her outfits are ridiculous and her French attempts are annoying.  Lastly, her she seems to read something like wikipedia

Nancy is kind of crazy.  She has interesting clothes though...it's kind of an incentive to come to class to see her new outfits.  She tends to stray off the subject of the readings and talk a lot about unrelated artwork...so make sure you read!
not very smart?

Pop quizzes during lecture make attendance a must. Lectures interesting and helpful. Don't be fooled that plot summary during lectures will carry you through exams and essays--you have to read in order to get points.
brilliant
Be prepared to learn by yourself.

Knows labor econ well, but grading and expectations felt unclear all semester. Feedback on assignments was limited, so it was hard to know how to improve. During the Canvas outage before finals, he refused to email study materials/slides despite sending class-wide emails, which made an already stressful situation worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Doesn't really give material to help prepare for the exam and not a lot of guidelines of what to be prepared for. For the veery little material we do have to study is homework assignments that are not graded so it is unknown if you are even studying the right answers. Does not use a standard grading scheme.
One of the best professors I have ever had, he explains things very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: If you do all the work, you're guaranteed at least a C. Readings and lectures were interesting and he pretty much goes over the whole exam during the review. If you show up, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has no regard for mental health.
The most interesting econ class I have taken. The readings were actually interesting and you can tell that he's super passionate about what he teaches. I wish I could take another class with himm

The class requires 12 reading summaries and 6 problems sets - large burden for international students. However, when giving out grades, he considers the performances of the whole class and across the whole semester of each students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Slightly disorganized (e.g. posting assignments late, late to office hours), but a lenient in grading which makes up for it. High quality, if slightly disorganized, lectures. Explains things very thoroughly and actively engages with students. His class format required one-on-one discussions with him, which were very helpful for my understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: THE ABSOLUTE BEST
Absolutely phenomenal professor...The best.

Very smart and enthusiastic guy who does present material which is not necessarily enticing ( at least in the first half of the course ) in a way in which we can fully grasp it and truly be excited to learn it. The weekly readings are a bore most of the time but he lectures over it well. His TA Erik is awesome as well! Overall would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The best experience I've had with a philosophy professor during my undergraduate career. His conversations with students are helpful and informative, and although long and tedious, the class is very rewarding. Easy grader and straightforward exams if you've done the readings. You can tell he loves engaging with the texts and students; very smart.

Cancerous. Upwards of seven hours of work per week, much of which is redundant. You'll be writing the same thing twice or three times a week. The essay prompts leave little to no opportunity to present your own ideas, and don't get me started on the revision exams. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He taught pretty well and his lecture videos were very helpful in understanding the readings. It was honestly just a lot of work, from video lecture notes, to live lecture assignments, weekly annotations, video assignments, and exams. The main thing I didn't like was having to annotate a long article every week, but class was thought provoking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is awful. He says he gives you a optional zoom. THAT SHIT IS NOT OPTIONAL. You have to go. Also the way everything is structured sucks. This is a gen ed but he treats it like its the entrance to the military.

Good lectures and the exams were easy enough as long as you read the texts/ watched the lectures. Heads up for a bunch of Canvas notifications but they are mainly small daily assignments. Tons of extra credit and regrade opportunities so nothing to complain about here
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: this was a really fun class! i especially like the peer reviews, but some students clearly submitted chat-generated answers (peep those mad down below) which made my efforts to comment on their work feel useless, but overall fun and I learned a lot :)

Entertaining and easy if you're willing to put in the effort. It's an ACP class, so expect essays for an exam, but note that the essay is easy as long as you know your material. For example, what are the views of the philosophers in question and have an example or two prepared. ProctorU is terrible, but it can't be helped bc of ChatGPT cheaters.

Worst class ever taken. Horrible course structure. Disorganized. This guy hold his “lecture” on time that's different than class you see on self service. Nothing on syllabus is kept. 8am proctoru essay exams that are completely bs. Do no take this class.

This class is very doable. 2 readings (annotations) every week which takes about 2 hours. The 8AM essays exams were annoying but the TAs grade pretty fair and the regrade was generous. I averaged an 80 on the first ones and 88 after regrade. There's 7 pts extra credit too. The class is disorganized though so you need to stay on top of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There are some problems with the online format (ProctorU bs) but compared to other online classes I've taken, this has been much smoother. This is a ACP course, so we have to write pretty frequently, but the essay exams are short (
I would not recommend this class. The professor and course were unorganized. Assignments and homework were made up along the way. Assignments did not have a set schedule for due dates

Fun lectures and teaching style, very interesting material. Really nice guy, very easy to talk to and intelligent. Does not answer emails all the time, janky final exam. You'll need to put effort into your papers, but it's worth it because it does develop your philosophical writing skill.

He told a lot of fun stories but the homework was actually insane. Depending on your TA the class can be miserable. Definitely would not suggest taking this class if you don't like writing 1,000-word essays as your final during a class period.

Way to much homework given for a philosophy class that is 3 credit hours. Almost an hour of homework for every other day and it is really irrelevant homework that is due unless your interested in Philosphy. If you want an A you really have to try. Also 2 hours to write an 1,000 word essay for final exam which is insane.

Don't take! Way to much homework is given for no reason and he made 2 homework assignments due the same day as an exam. Exams are the WORST! 3 1,000 word essays are the exams and you have to do it on ProctorU which I understand but it is impossible to write an 1,000 word essay in the little canvas box without being able to do anything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: As long as you do the assignments and give them their due diligence, it's hard not to do well in this course. Doing all the assignments gives lots of extra credit and essay rewrites make getting a good grade pretty stress-free. I thought the readings were mostly fair for an intro PHIL course. It does get a bit tricky when it gets to Mill and Kant.

Professor Bo is one of the best professors I have ever had. He puts thought and care into his lectures and incorporates student feedback in a meaningful way. Even though the class is quite difficult, Bo always makes himself extremely accessible and genuinely wants every single student to succeed. His enthusiasm continually inspires me to improve.
Best professor I've had yet. Explains difficult accounting concepts very well. Always willing to answer any questions or help you if you're confused. Gives a lot of study material for exams.

I personally struggled with this class, but Bo Ren is an amazing professor who truly cares for his students and making sure that they understand the material. It was his first semester teaching but he quickly adapted and has been one of the best professors and people I have EVER met. Overall, a great professor who makes his lectures fun and useful.

Literally my favorite professor I've ever had. The content of the course was difficult and heavy at times, but Bo explains things so well and makes every class entertaining. He was available to email or message at anytime of the day and always helped with homework, quizzes, and cases. Such a fun and caring guy.
The GOAT. ACCY 303 is a pretty hard class, but Bo helps make your life a bit easier. Lively lecturer and super accessible if you need help. He really wants you to succeed more than anything.

Prof. Boppart clearly knows what she's talking about. Some people might think of her as hard to approach or scary, but once you talk to her you realize this is not the case. This is probably the hardest 100 level KIN class, but it's very interesting. There isn't much work outside of class, but you have to have to understand the lectures well

Prof. Boppart was (in my opinion) a good lecturer. She could be monotone at times, but make sure you take notes in class. Few assignments are graded, aside from a weekly quiz. If you pay attention, these quizzes are not hard, and she also drops your two lowest quiz grades. She also offers study sessions outside of class time for the unit exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, very knowledgeable. Only downside is little to no extra credit, and quizzes can make or break your grade (missing a question drops your grade to a 75%). Great at explaining difficult concepts but tends to be quite monotone in lectures. Offers review sessions and appointments to discuss grades if/when struggling.
Super boring professor. Did not make the class interesting, and talked in a low  voice. However if you wanna be successful in this class make sure to pay attention and take down notes.

Aside from tests, lab reports and weekly quizzes(which are only 5 questions so if you miss one question you literally get a 75%)there aren't many assignments to get points. Dr.Boppart is very monotone so its hard to stay focused and interested. She also posts lectures online so you basically only have to go when there's a quiz.

Professor Boppart is very passionate about what she teaches and makes lectures engaging. It does require a bit of work to maintain a good grade, so it is important to attend lecture if you want to do well on the weekly quizzes.

I did not like that she was not understanding in some cases like work interfering with school. It sucks because given we are in a pandemic some of us need to work too. She did not even give me at least 1 retake pass :/

Prof. Boppart cared about her students and would always ask if they wanted any part of the lecture to be explained again before moving on. Questions on exams do require thinking as well as memorization. Her exam reviews were really helpful

KIN150 is a class that makes you work for a grade, but Professor Boppart is always wiling to help outside of class. Make sure to go to review sessions because she provides hints for the exams. Also, attendance is not mandatory, but there are pop quizzes on previous lecture material, so it is beneficial to go to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: if you dont want to memorize 300 slides per exam don't take the class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes usually on every Monday and the lecture material can somewhat be overwhelming. Labs are pretty straightforward and easy, but the tests are decently hard so make sure to study notes. She also gives you a study guide for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Engaging class. Labs are easy and fun. Pop quizzes, but they aren't designed to trick you. First unit/exam is the hardest, but everything gets easier from there. No final if you have an A going in. Lectures are clear and interesting, and the textbook was actually very helpful. I'm not a KIN major but I didn't struggle to do well.
The topics discussed in class are interesting but she makes them boring. She is not very good at going into detail and explaining topics that are more difficult to understand.

Marni Boppart is a passionate professor. Her class was interesting and was relevant to my Kinesiology major. Be prepared for pop quizzes, which are usually are on Mondays. I suggest either printing out her lecture notes or using ppt slides on your computer. If you have an A (90%) before the final exam, you don't have to take the final.

This class is one of the best courses in the KIN department. It gives you a basic understanding of exercise physiology, and Dr. Boppart is an excellent lecturer. Put in the hard work and you will succeed in this class. The labs are fun too! If you don't enjoy this class, then you're not a true Kinesiology student.

Tough but fair. The lectures are interesting but can get confusing. Exams, if you study are fairly easy. There is a lot of lab homework, if confused ask your TA for help! No Final if you get an A! Quizzes are tough so be sure to study your notes before class!

She is a very good teacher.  Go to class because she explains a lot.  Her power points and study guides do a good job of preparing you for the test so the book isn't completely necessary.  She definitely makes the class interesting.

You have like 12 quizzes throughout the semester, they are easy. Exams aren't that bad. It just helps if you have some idea of human anatomy makes learning so much easier. she explains everything really well and tries to make it interesting. the study guides and review sessions are really helpful!

Random quizzes worth 10 points about 15 over the semester.  Lab homework isn't pretty easy, lab only meets every other week. Do good on labs and set for at least a B. Tests aren't all that bad, get easier as semester goes on. Overall good teacher and depending on your TA can be really good.  Gives study guide for all tests as well as review session

If you take this class you should like lots of quizzes and exams because there are alot. What is bad is the third exam was taken 1 week before the final which is cumulative. Also at least a 10 point quiz every week and you dont know what day. Tons of lab homework. 1000 points to be earned in this class while my others were only 500. Hard class.
He is a really good lecturer and sets up a clear criteria for grading-an extremely fair class where the grade you get is equivalent to the effort you put into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bolton was fine for the half of the class that was in person, but once we switched to online learning during the pandemic, he basically just stopped teaching all together. He sent us his notes on the powerpoint slides and basically told us to teach ourselves.
Very good professor!

The most boring lecturer ever. Seriously. Exam questions come from the slides, the class material is interesting and easy to self-teach. You just need to make a Quizlet of concepts and straight up memorize all of it. Easy A class overall.
He's a pretty nice guy. Engages the class well. He only teaches a small portion of endocrinology, three class periods, and he did a decent job teaching.

Dr. Bolton's lecture style is pretty dry and he goes over certain concepts  multiple times, but the material is really interesting and lectures were always clearly organizedeasy to understand.  Exams are fair and he's not out to trick you.  He's a good guy and is approachable after class or in office hours.

Best professor I had in UIUC. Took his ECE340 and now taking ECE405 with him. His lectures are so easy to understand and explains everything well. Very willing to answer questions and explains everything well.

One of the best professors I have had in UIUC. His analogies are very helpful for explaining hard concepts. He is always enthusiastic and prepared of lectures and is very accessible in office hours and after class. Strongly encourages taking his interactive lectures and participate in his questions.
Very good professor, made a very tough course (some may argue the toughest in EE curriculum) feel like a breeze. Engaging lecture, good presentations, would recommend

Absolutely fantastic professor. His lectures are engaging and he presents such descriptive analogies for the complex topics covered in ECE 340. He truly cares that students come to conclusions themselves instead of just giving the explanation. Would highly recommend his teaching style for those who like to learn through the lecture.

Class is overall very light, however, I would not recommend skipping the reading. Clara is very nice and accessible outside of the class, and the material is genuinely interesting. As a CS student who has a tendency to just do CS work during lectures to min-max productivity, I found myself getting engaged in her lectures, which speaks volumes IMO!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CLCV224- Engaging, kind, passionate, and explained the content very clearly. Exams mostly follow lecture content and are very easy. Readings weren't too long or boring. Attendance was mandatory because iClicker, and readings were followed by simple discussion-section quizzes. TA's were very helpful. Attend class, take notes, and read to succeed.

I took history of Ancient Greece. This class was more of an english class than history because we analyzed texts more than learned history. Three different must have textbooks. 4 2 page essays. 1 5 page paper. Grade based on papers and final. Clara is funny, knowledgable, understanding. Wants people to learn and be interested. Very kind.

Really really good at explaining things and breaking them down to understand easier- actually usually overexplains things which I think is even more helpful. Really encourages questions and makes lectures useful/interesting.

Overall solid class, the material is really interesting and the extra credit coding assignments, labs, and mps are all really cool and helpful. Lectures could be improved, less focus on the proofs and more code examples would be solid but overall they are good. Quizzes are worst part, not bad but wish coding question on each wasn't 50% of the grade

I really enjoy Brad's lectures, they're quite engaging and he teaches the material well. The course itself isn't too hard, I think with work you can get through it quite well, especially with 7% extra credit.

Good professor, speaks clearly and explains topics well, attendance is not mandatory and he offers tons of extra credit. He is also pretty good about responding and accommodating to unforeseen situations. W professor, really enjoyed this class.

Professor Brad was good. He is good at explaining things but frequently runs out of time in lecture. His inclusion of his research is interesting. That being said, the amount of extra credit drastically decreased when I took it, compared to previous semesters, which means we had to do better on exams. Exam coding questions are basically 0 or 100.
just don't. its going to be the worst CS course you are ever going to take in your life.

MPs and Lab instructions are not clear and confusing. Lectures are terrible, only going over vague ideas then expecting us to automatically know how to implement the code with zero guidance given. Doesn't allow you to see what you got wrong on exams. Lecture slides are super unhelpful

Brad Solomon is one of those professors that shows genuine passion and interest in the subject he teaches. CS225 is doable as long as you put in the work to understand the material early on. If you go to office hours, ask questions during lecture (the discord makes it a lot easier) and read the material, you'll be fine on exams and mps.

The instructions for the MPs are trash and lead to students completely wasting there time trying to understand what the functions actually want. Exams are worth way to much of a grade, shouldn't be worth more than MPs. Not enough concrete code examples in lectures. Also office hours have been super unhelpful as the TAs can never give a clear answer

This class is supposed to be difficult -- data structures and algorithms involve a lot of theory, which can be hard to understand at times. However, Prof. Solomonn does a great job reviewing any confusing material, and helping students prepare for the exams with practice exams.
Really great professor who cares about his students. I took his class CS 277 and although it was hard, he tried his best and I appreciate that.

CS277: He is clear when it comes to deadlines and everything is accessible online but the course is very exam heavy and the exams are nothing like what is taught in lecture. The same thing goes for the lab, you are expected to either just know how to do the code or learn it yourself. He would go over the overall concept in lecture but the codes.

Solomon is a great professor.  His lectures are super helpful, and available online too (I mostly watched them online).  He is clear in his teaching and grading, and gives a lot of extra credit, which makes this class have a focus on more learning than tough grading.  You'll learn a lot in this class.

The lectures were boring, but they were all posted online with annotated slides, which were very helpful. The MP documentation for some MPs was straight trash, but it was very doable during office hours. The labs were beneficial for learning and understanding concepts. The class was structured well. The Extra Credit in this class is a lot.

overall a very well organized class. lectures are helpful and all of them are posted online. plenty of other extra credit opportunities that can raise your grade up to an entire letter grade. The exams are similar to practice exams and reviewing the labs before exams was helpful

Professor Solomon explained topics with ease and gave and numerous examples. He also takes a lot of student questions, though this kinda dwindled later into the semester. Unfortunately the lectures are just not enough preparation for the MPs, labs, and exams. There is a LOT of extra credit though, which is nice. Overall, great professor.
Why would the lecture matter if content being tested on for coding is vastly different from what is learned?

exams pretty much make or break your grade, granted most people to well on most of the MPs. everyone says there's a lot of extra credit which is true, but if you don't do well on exams (which rely entirely on timed coding) then you can't expect to do well.

Professor Solomon is an amazing guy, his lectures are fantastic and he always spend time on discord answering questions,For such a large class like cs225 Professor and course staffs is still gives enough individual helps. However the test can be difficult and the MP could be time consuming, but there's alot of extra credits and you'll learn alot.

Genuinely a good lecturer who makes concepts understandable and leads a well-supported course. There's a very useful Discord, interesting and challenging MPs, and I feel he really does care about the success of his students. There is a lot of work though: bi-weekly MPs, CBTF exams, and weekly lab sections that feel like mini MPs.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: CS225 is not a hard course. MPs are a little time consuming, but there is 10 percentage points of extra credit. Quizzes are very similar to practice tests. Brad Solomon is clearly a professor passionate about CS, but most of the lectures are not too relevant, and seem a little bit rambly. You can get most content with lec slides saving time.

The best I can say is he's a good lecturer. I found the structure of his class to be entirely too demanding and too reliant on code in a class that at least by its description seems that it should have some graded component related to theory. Exams are unfair and limited staff means many students are left behind. He favors high performing students.

He is 'ok' in terms of like speaking clearly. However, for a cs class thats just not enough. He speaks without any variation in tone, making it difficult to grasp the important points of concepts. Moreover, unlike Evans, he just keeps 'stating facts' when teaching and saying 'whats the xx for xx? well thats xx'. Not feeling inspirational at all.

The class is very test heavy, and Professor Solomon has been making the class harder compared to previous semesters, for instance, the course now has a mandatory final exam and the final project is completely a project of your choice (which he is then much more likely to reject because of staff availability).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Like many of the 100-200-Level CS courses, CS 225's struggles come from having so many students taking the course each semester. However, Professor Solomon in a great person if you attend his office hour.

There's not any point going to lecture, you'd be much better off studying the material from YouTube videos. The exams have different levels of difficulty depending on which prompt the system gives you and if you ever ask him for help or a reassessment of an assignment score, good luck getting him to reply to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, great course. I also took him for the honors section. He gives nice lectures and is very communicative.
Took CS 225 and CS 225 Honors, loved his lectures, great professor.

CS225 Honor is a great course by Mr. Solomon (sad he won't teach honor next semester but do take his CS225! It will be fantastic). He explains the string algorithms in a really organized, understandable, and fun way. The homework require a little bit of thinking but you will do well if you absorb the stuffs in lecture.
He's a great professor and I really enjoy his classes, would definitely recommend.
Such a nice guy teaching a great course! Would take again if i could.
The assignments were interesting. The lecture content was dense and hard to grasp at times but I appreciate that he made time to adjust the class based on student feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were not useful. He barely taught the class in lecture and the slides are nearly all blank so you cannot find filled-in notes anywhere. Exam outlines were posted late which made it difficult to not have to cram in studying.
Super chill
He will post slides for each lecture that you can take notes on pretty well, and the class is pretty easy to grasp as long as you have an understanding of basic statistics.

Be prepared to teach yourself the material. The slides are not very helpful. In some of the examples that were presented, he got his own math wrong but assumed it was the students making the mistakes. He is also the kind of professor who embodies the "I'll wait" teacher. No one wants to speak in his class, so we spend half the time waiting.

Don't read the textbook, do what you need to to get an A on the homework. In group projects make sure everyone's part meets the criteria bc that's the majority of your grade. Notebooklm is your bestfriend for memorizing the lecture knowledge for the test, that paired with the study guides. Writing and rewatching vids is waste of time. Memorize only

Absolutely terrible teacher. Slides are terribly formatted and difficult to read, let alone understand. Tests are poorly created and ask questions on topics that were never covered in class or even mentioned. Group projects are just busy work, don't help with comprehension, and poorly graded on a rubric that doesn't make sense

I did not enjoy this class and the lectures were a bore to attend. Wilson says that lectures are optional, but a good chunk of the total grade is from the iclicker questions. The exams can be quite detail oriented and unforgiving. I do not recomment this class at all.

literally terrible. expects you to know things even though it's an introductory class. you need to memorize the slides and once you get to the test it's almost nothing like the slides in lecture. very vague explanations and doesn't break concepts down
Brenda is amazing and always willing to help students. Lecture slides are important so be sure to pay attention in class.

this class is supposed to be introductory but there is little to no explanation of basic terms, expect to not understand a single thing that's going on. group projects err boing but helpful or grade but there is no curve whatsoever
Horrible lectures, terrible class overall, couldn't stay awake

For a 1 credit class, this was ridiculously heavy in coursework and ALL of it was useless. We were given assignments that were found in high school biology curriculums. Everything she wasted my time with was information that I could've gotten from a 5 minute article. Not to mention that she was a ridiculously picky and harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Overall the class was decent. Lectures were dry, but weren't awful. There are many terms that Wilson throws out that she just expects us to know, despite this being an introductory course. The group projects are doable with some effort. Test preparation requires rote memorization of the slides, so expect to spend a lot of time studying.

Exams are purely memorization of the lecture slides. She releases the exam study guides morning of the exams. Schedules review sessions with no agenda, and when we ask questions of what we should focus on and study she responds very vaguely. Exams are too hard for a 100 level course and she takes zero responsibly when the MEDIAN score is a 59%.

SP24 Throws terms like you should know them already, but most dont. Her exams are extremely difficult, memorizing the slides is the only way to do well on the exams, but says she doesnt support memorization? Our exam 2 had average of 59, she did not address this but blamed on us. She is not helpful, directs you straight to the textbook or slides.

The professor tries her best to improve this class, but the truth is there is a lot of material to covered in class and the exam are either too hard or too easy. If you did well in exams and do all the work, you'll be fine. Again, remember to STUDY FOR THE EXAMS!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was a bit difficult, but her policies are forgiving and the group projects help boost your grade. Tests can be quite challenging, but study/memorize the Powerpoint slides! They are key to doing good on the exams. Her lectures could be more clear/better structured. Don't worry too much about the textbook readings, the slides help plenty.

Fa22. I personally did not care for her lectures or exam. They were very convoluted. The iclickers were decent enough and add up. Really not much to say except that I didn't care for her. She does the 1st half of the class.

WAY too much work for a one credit hour class. I genuinely had to do more work for this class than my advanced level MCB classes. There were 3-4 assignments due every week and if you fumble one deadline you're screwed since you need a 95% for an A in the class.

She had a 60% class average on our midterm and she blamed it on us completely not taking any responsibility whatsoever. Asking her for help doesn't get you anywhere either, she will just point to the website and be really annoyed that you're asking her something she had said months ago. She not very encouraging or approachable for help.
Professor has high expectations for the students despite it being an introductory course. Exams are not curved and you're expected to know the material very well by the time you take your exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This course is one of the worst 1 credit hour classes I have ever taken. First - why are there so many quizzes and lecture activities? This should not be listed as a 1 credit hour course - 3 would be well-fitted. Group projects every other week over the course of the entire semester. just audit the class - rather than taking it for credit.

Professor Wilson helps students a lot. During online mode, she helps every student question as her best ability, despite not the most clearly. However, she cares about her students. She even sometimes holds extra office hours with students along with Professor Kieffer. Definitely pay attention to group projects as well. Lowest scores would be drop.

Class was fine until we went online. Then, tests got super hard even though I was getting average scores before. Since this class will be online again in the fall, skip it until the spring and take another class you need instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For a one credit hour course, you have to do a lot. However, it was not too bad. The lecture topics were pretty interesting. The group projects are what you make of it and were not too tedious. Just beware of the quizzes! There are not a lot of points you can miss.

She is brilliant (has degrees from Columbia, John Hopkins, and Harvard) but that does not mean she is interesting. Even Shankland could not stay awake in lecture. Her exams were more straight forward than in MCB 150. All exam material comes from her lectures. Pay attention to all the details. This class weeds out the weak. Free iClicker points.

Dr. Wilson is  one of the best professors in the School of MCB. She genuinely cares about her students, and is an extremely fair grader. If you put in the effort she expects of you, you will do well. However, her classes are difficult. You have to work for your grade. But I enjoyed her classes enough to take every single one she taught at the time!

Overall this class sucked. Tests were so hard it isn't even funny. And seeing as tests are almost the only grade for the class... Its a shame, because I may have enjoyed the class if it was not so difficult. The only thing that is good about the class is the curve. As for Wilson, all she does is reads off slides.

This class was harder than I had heard from others. The tests are super tricky with short answer questions at the end worth 1/3 of test grade. Everything is off the powerpoints, but there is SO much information. The quizzes are really tricky too, but if she gives practice probs def look at those.

Love, love, love this class!  It is very difficult at first, but it enhances your problem solving techniques.  I have learned more in this class than all my MCB courses combined.  She is amazing, and knows her material.  She actually makes you think and not just memorize and forget everything after the test.

This class is one of the hardest MCB classes I have ever taken and I put in a lot of time. It was totally worth it though. If you go to office hours, go to class, and do a lot of practice exams you will do great. I went from getting a 47% to a 95% on my exams and got an A in the class bc of Dr. Wilson's awesomeness!
I really enjoyed this class. People who say that it is too hard are just plain lazy. If you pay attention and/or go to office hours, you'll do great.
Brenda Wilson is so hot.  She's a great professor too.

Be PREPARED TO STUDY!!! This class is one of the most difficult classes I have ever taken, but you will learn a lot.  Study the practice exams and go to office hours to get the answers to these.  Her test are essentially generated from these old tests.
This class was hard, but I learned more in it than in all of my other classes combined that semester.  She knows her material, and has real life examples to back it up.
A knowledgeable teacher and does care about the education of undergrads- but not very considerate. Also has some very odd (outdated) notions about women in science.
Great professor.
good prof, but EC is not, its part of the curve!

He was not only a great teacher but very kind and patient. Truly cared about his students and wanted them to succeed in the course AND enjoy themselves. The students are lucky to have him. He was understanding and provided a lot of resources to succeed.
One of the best math instructors in this school. Patient  and nice. I hope he could be the instructor of Graph theory in the future.
Super excellent professor
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
- Generous
- Cares about students
- Plenty time for exam and quiz (first time in a proof course xd)
- Detailed grading explanations
- (Comparatively) low pressure
- Materials are not easy though
Currently in his class. He's the best math professor I've at UIUC. He cares about teaching the material and helps you succeed.

The most easy-going instructor I've ever met. The grading is generous. What I particularly appreciated was the instructor meticulously reviewed each line of our work and provided detailed comments. I only received a B- due to my own struggles with coming up rigorous proofs :( 

Overall, I highly recommend this course with Peter!

Dr. Bradshaw clearly cares about students' understanding of the material. He lectures in an engaging way and is accessible outside of class. In addition, he gives detailed feedback on midterms and grades grades them quickly. Homework was reasonable, and tests required understanding of the material rather than just regurgitating the homework/review
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bradshaw cares very much about his students' understanding of the material. The tests are based on understanding and problem solving and not just memorizing the practice/homework questions. He was accessible after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bradshaw gave great constructive feedback and guidance on all the midterms. The homework was reasonable and his lectures were good. The grading policy was fairly generous even though the syllabus didn't mention any curves. He is accessible outside of class time as well. 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I feel like the material and concepts are pretty straight forward to grasp, but even so Buckley is very thorough and welcoming to clarification. I never went to discussion sections, so I don't know what those looked like, but if you are struggling it seems to be quite helpful.

This is an incredibly easy course and I think that Prof. Buckley does his best to make the subject not be mind numbingly boring. To be honest, you can fully snooze through this class and do well but I am happy that when I went to my lectures, I was at least somewhat awake due to Prof. Buckley's engaging style of presentation.
I have taken Dr. Buckley for three classes, 102, 302, and 415, and he is absolutely amazing.  His courses are run incredibly well, with clearly communicated material and expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best prof at UIUC. I take courses just because he teaches them.
He explained things very well and as long as you take notes in lectures, it's pretty easy to pass the class

Manages to make econ less boring for sure. Could pass the class without ever attending lectures but the examples he gives makes it worth going,
plus he gives great lectures and isnt afraid to point out how relevant it is to modern topics.  Great guy definitely take him!!

Truthfully didn't really go to class or try my hardest. That being said I think the criteria is really clear and prepping for tests is just on how you study. Get his workbook, it has a lot of practice tests in them that aren't on Canvas. Homeworks every week can be boring but worth it. Also don't need to spend too much time.

Professor Buckley is a great lecturer, he makes the concepts interesting and understandable with real world examples. I attended every lecture and barely had to study. He also has a great sense of humor.

Very passionate and kind. Has a whole lot of prep in canvas and not too hard to follow. Post lecture slides on canvas too so don't have to show up in person. Just make sure you study and you'll be fine. Tests weren't that hard or tricky.

Econ 102 w/ Buckley is a light course, structured incredibly well. Each week you have a lesson assignment and a lesson quiz which both total around 15 to 20 multiple choice questions and optional worksheets. Extra credit is provided. Professor is nice and sound quality depends on room sound system it has nothing to do with how he sounds.

Just like 102, 302 with Buckley is a great course. The content is just an extension of 102 with calculus. Buckley is once again a great lecturer. Content may get dry at times, so make sure to stay on top of things by attending discussion (but are optional). Homework is unlimited attempts which is nice. Overall with minimal work one can get an A.

Buckley's econ 102 class is super light, insane amount of opportunities to get your grade up and extra credit. Seems like a super solid dude as well, easy-to-follow lectures and the guy knows what he's doing. Highly recommend the class

Overall, the class was pretty light. I only needed to study the day of the exams and that was plenty. Attendance isn't mandatory and he posts all the slides, which explain the concepts nicely and there's even extra credit for just taking midterms and doing other practice assignments, which I thought were helpful studying for the exam anyways.

Overall Professor Buckley is a great professor and makes Econ and concepts very clear and understandable. You sadly dont interact with him, since it is a giant lecture, but the work load is easy and fair.

He is a funny lecturer. You don't really interact with him since it's an auditorium lecture. Attendance is not required (and not really necessary if you can learn from the slides/tutorials). Homework is simple and weekly, taking about 10 minutes or so (including the quiz, lesson assignment, and tutorials). Many chances on assignments. Easy tests.
You don't need to go to anything, but go to the discussion if you're not understanding anything, because they give a full summary of the lectures with practice that looks just like the exams
His lectures are very good, using real world examples. He grades based only on online quizzes, assignments, and exams. His Microecon class is incredibly easy, and he teaches it very well.

Class has various resources to use such as book, tutorials, tutor handouts and lecture slides. Their was various extra credit and grade boosters opportunities. People who rated him a low score, I guarantee did not use their resources to their advantage. Please study throughout your week as this was helpful for me. Overall his class is very easy.

Very easy class. Barely gives homework and what he gives is very simple. Only knock on him is that he needs to speak up during lectures and sometimes gives too much examples to where it can distract you from the main points. Overall, he's pretty solid.
He explains things great. Makes the material easy to understand. There are weekly quizzes and assignments but it is tolerable and the workload is definitely manageable. He also has great TA's.

Don't need to show up to lecture to succeed. Very very good online materials and practice to learn the content on your own. Seems like a chill guy too. Tests should be light assuming you did practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The students bashing this class are simply bad students. This course was so easy. Homework had quizzes which were 2 attempts, and lesson assignments unlimited attempts (all MCQ). 3 tests and a final, and technically you could just take the final and it would be worth 75% of the grade. Good lecturer with useful examples. He does speak softly though.

I thought he was very clear with what we needed to know. I took AP Micro and Macro in high school and did not receive credit for the AP exams, finding them quite challenging. However, Buckley is incredibly easy to understand. Exams are not required to be taken, but will make the final worth more if neglected. Very easy A for me.
Super easy class. It takes skill to not get an A. Could barely hear him during lecture and read off slides so never ended up going. Notes posted online

Even though I currently do not have a good grade in his class, I am still so interested in what he has to teach. I feel as though if I were in this situation with other professors, I would hate the class and the professor him or herself. However, he is so engaging in lectures that I feel myself learning a lot from him and loving the course.

The professor was extremely rude and did not care that I was experiencing a health difficulty. He told me he didn't understand why I don't understand his class even he speaks looking away from the audience and slams you with information in a tiny lecture. Even Econ MAJORS failed his class.

Worst class I have ever taken. Speaks so quietly during lectures it is difficult to understand him unless you're literally in the front row. TA sessions were not one bit helpful at all and were a COMPLETE waste of time, test's had material that was not even remotely covered in class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS take this with Diilani i've heard much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: King Buckley.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring and long, basically reads word for word off slides. The test prep assignments are not helpful during the test. He makes the test questions more confusing than need be.

This class was harder than expected. The homework was very difficult because it gave you no feedback and you have to start over until you get your desired grade. The exams were okay as long as you studied. The book with practice exams can help. Lectures are very boring and he basically reads off the slides.
Easy A as long as you attend the lectures and complete the weekly quizzes and extra credit assignments.

Class was based on homework, 4 total exams, and optional extra credit. While attendance isn't mandatory, the lectures are worth going to, since Dr. Buckley is great at explaining. Homework was incredibly tedious and annoying to complete, but not too difficult overall. Doing the work guarantees a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Can't go wrong with Buckley :D. If you go to class and are attentive in the lectures, you'll succeed. Most of things he taught is very valuable and he uses a lot of real world example to help you understand the concepts. 

You get what you put into the class!

This class will take 20-25 hours per week. There are few resources for this course, and the tests are tough!! The recorded videos are made well. However, they give very few instructions on how problems are carried out. Overall, this course is miserable. Take an alternative if you can.

I had Buckley for 102 and 302 for the econ minor. He is great. Very clear criteria, posts all notes/slides on Canvas. HW was annoying: unlimited attempts but have to start over with like 10+ different problems. Did not give HW answers. Never went to lecture and easy to learn on your own.

Very easy class, professor knew what he was talking about. Despite being good at what he does, his lectures were pretty boring, but the content was very easy to understand and pretty intuitive. He had great grading policies and an A was pretty much guaranteed if you somewhat paid attention. Great guy overall.

I've had Dr. Buckley for ECON 102 & 302, and he is one of my favorite professors.  He has very clear grading criteria, and offers many resources to make it easy to learn the material.  Unlike my other professors, he leads his own office hours to help answer questions.  He is definitely a professor you should try and take if you can.

He is a great lecturer. I felt bad for him because only a few people were showing up to class by the end. Pretty much all of what you need for the exams is posted to canvas. I didn't always show up but when I did I always felt glad that I went.

I went into the class knowing nothing about economics and came out of it somewhat knowing basic economics. What I learned about economics was thanks to TA handouts and the assignments on Moodle, not the lectures (since I fell asleep in about 75% of them due to how boring some were and how quiet Prof. Buckley's voice was). Chill grading system.

For ECON102: The course was well structured and followed the schedule and syllabus. The lectures were detailed although sometimes boring. All the required materials are accessible online (PPT & notes), there is a textbook (~$30) but not mandatory. Only complain would be that there was always a delay with grading, for all 3 midterms and the final.
Buckley explains the topics very well and provides more than enough resources for one to succeed in the course.

Buckley is friendly and passionate about his field, but his teaching style left much to be desired for an advanced course. Lectures overall are largely unengaging. Material is not too difficult, essentially his Econ102 but with calc. However, the difficulty of the exams are not accurately reflected the coursework and hw is mind-numbingly tedious.

Surprised that many found his lectures to be hard to follow, as I thought he was a very good lecturer. He always answered questions in depth as well. Homework can be tedious, just make sure to start it early. TONS of extra credit. Some of the tests had weird questions tbh, like there'll be a random question about something that wasn't even covered

Buckley does some things right, but he also misses some things. He posts guided notes, has an optional attendance policy, and gives easy extra credit. HW is tedious but you have unlimited attempts. Discussions are terrible - TA had no idea how to teach. No additional materials to study for exams - stare at your notes! Tests get harder as you go.

You can't learn from the lecture and be prepare for so many extra time spending outside the classes. This professor use a very lowering voice to speak in the auditorium, so you are easily distracted by other things. But one good thing is that the grading system is chill.

I had a really bad semester when I took this class, but still ended up with a B- with nearly no effort. Attendance for lecture wasn't required when I took it, and he uploads every resource you'll need in Canvas so you can learn everything on your own. Everything is organized extremely well and he even offered tutorials you can do for extra credit.

Lectures were some what boring to listen to and I would often not pay attention. There are weekly assignments and quizzes that taught me the material. The exams were not that bad, but you do need to study for them. Pretty easy extra credit is offered. Buckley's class is very organized, and he gives out follow along notes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoy taking his classes! Would love to taking more of his classes!

Buckley is a great professor, has a great personality, and wants you to succeed. The way the course is organized is excellent and easy to understand. Guided notes during lectures and quick and easy assignments. Exams weren't too hard either. Overall, I wish every class was built this way.
Great professor, answers questions thoroughly after class, and also teaches well. Would recommend

easy to understand the material. going to lecture isnt required but always helps. I got by studying for the exams on my own and it was fairly easy to do so. not much homework and he is an easy grader.

You do not need to go to lectures. They are pointless and repetitive, I would just do the notes on my own time. During lecture it is hard to hear him, his tone moves up and down and I couldn't seem to understand much. The practice test in his textbook are nothing like the tests, and the tests are nothing like what is learned in class.

Buckley is a fun lecturer, but all of the slides can be found on Moodle so a lot of students don't go. The exams were fair and you can buy a review packet with a practice exam for each midterm and final. The only other work are weekly quizzes (lowest 4 dropped) and assignments with unlimited attempts. Up to 2% easy extra credit is also available.
His lectures tend to be boring when he goes off topic. Whenever class is almost over, he will start speaking fast which leads to no time to write down your notes.
This professor will teach the basics of Microeconomics and does a very good job at it!

Prof Buckley's lectures are just him reading off powerpoints that he posts on Moodle. Everybody shows up to the first two lectures, but later they realize that the lectures were useless and it was just easier to look at his powerpoints online. The rather easy weekly quizzes are nice because they force you to study so that you are not behind.

The material is thought provoking. He streams using zoom in case you're out sick. The math & models aren't any more complicated than intermediate courses. I didn't make below 94% on any assignment or test. Doesn't require a book; he provides you the slides. He responds to e-mails and is willing to talk outside of class. Few assignments.

The class structures are pretty messy and unorganized.

Somethings on the syllabus were not true or contradicting itself...

Econ 302 used this alternative website called "learn" or "Moodle" instead of canvas and the UI was horrible. 

Just did not feel the effort / enthusiasm from the professor as much.
soooo many quizzes and exams, this class is supposed to be very easy-i took an equivalent at parkland- but the way he teaches and the structure of the course make it hard to pass and keep up.
Lectures are pretty easy to understand but I was drowning in hw and articles to read on top of everything
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Excellent lecturer for Economics. Anyone with very little knowledge about microeconomic concepts can learn very well from Buckley. Class is also structured very well with homework and tutorial assignments giving ample amount of practice opportunities for students. Exams can have tough questions at times but they are very reasonable.

Pretty easy class. Mr. Buckley is a good lecturer and the subject is actually very interesting. You can do the homework as many times as you need for a perfect score before the due date and if you get the optional workbook it has some very useful practice exams. Exams are also very straightforward without any curveballs/trick questions.

Overall, Buckley himself is a good professor. He teaches well and I did learn a lot in his class. However, the amount of effort I put into the class did not reflect in my grade. The tests and quizzes were super easy to mess up on, and one little mistake can tank your grade. I really expected myself to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 100% recommend taking! Unlimited takes for hw with ample extra credit - take advantage! Buckley's lecture/slides made it very easy to understand the content. Exams very closely mirror hw. If you miss class, everything you need is in the slides and once you take the 5 min quiz for discussion you're good to go.

Econ 102 was very easy. The presentations and many assignments(a lot of easy extra credit) were available on moodle and helped me ace all my tests. Everyone rarely went to the lectures and in the discussions left the class within 10 mins of starting after giving the weekly 5 min test. Its the easiest class. Highly recommend to take this class!

This class is incredibly test heavy, 70% of your total grade is based on exams. There are weekly quizzes, 4 of which were dropped for my class. There is a decent amount of extra credit. The exams are optional in the sense that if you feel like you arent solid on the material you can skip it and the weight will be transferred over to the other exams

Professor Buckley excels at presenting his information in lectures, keeping us engaged and being very straight forward with exam content. If you do the weekly assignments the questions are near exact to exam content. Extra credit is abundant and he will make accommodations if you ask him early enough. lecture slides are posted online with answers.
Econ 102 is a very easy class in general. Prof. Buckley is an easy grader and his slides are easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Buckley is by far one of the best professors I have met on campus. His lectures are very easy to understand & he certainly has a passion for the topic. I took Microeconomics in Fall of 2021, & I would recommend him to anyone needing to take Micro. Attend the lectures/do the extra credit he offers, it adds up & can totally save your grade!

DO NOT take this class if it is not required. If taking, be prepared to take weekly. quizzes. Also, lectures are him going over his slides, so feel free to miss. Exams are hard because they are all application problems . My advice is to study the definitions so you can easily apply them to problems. There is a lot of extra credit tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a good professor. I took micro in hs and didnt do well, but I am passing this class with flying colors. My favorite professor. 10/10

Homework is graded for accuracy. TIme-consuming class, lectures are posted in video format but are filled with irrelevant material. Exam material is relatively easy but is made unnecessarily more difficult due to course structure. All exams are proctored making the class unnecessarily expensive.

I took Econ 302 with Buckley last year and will be taking Environmental Economics this semester. One of the classes I'm looking forward to the most. Actually I look forward to all my Econ classes next semester :P

The class is test heavy, every test (there are 3 plus a final) is about 20% of your overall grade. If you don't do good on the exams, don't expect to pass. You get graded on a few things: exams, math, *concepts, and *vocab. In the lecture we don't learn, we all just follow the examples on the slides. Lots of sleepers, he's truly boring. Never again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Some of the pros of this course include the practice exams and extra credit opportunities. That being said, while the professor is very passionate about what he teaches, the lecture format of the class is extremely boring and very ineffective at teaching. In addition, the lack of frequent homework assignments makes studying difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Buckley is a great guy. His lectures can be dry but he does bring in interesting real-world examples. The class is very test-heavy but they aren't very difficult. Make sure to do all the extra credit and practice the math problems before the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend taking his Econ 302 course, unless you have no other choice. Take a different professor's Econ 302 course if you can! Professor Buckley does somewhat of an okay job going over the math used in the course, but does not go over any of the conceptual stuff. Overall, he does not teach this course well, at all. He's not a good prof.
Great guy, very passionate, go to lecture and get the workbook and you will do great as well as learn a lot about econ.

He is clearly smart and knows what he is talking about, but his teaching style is just not very good for a large lecture. His powerpoints are endless and not very helpful. But the hardest part is that there is little homework and it does not correlate to the tests at all. The practice tests are somewhat helpful, but more practice is needed to prep.

Lectures are very boring with a lot of extraneous info. There are a lot of materials to study and learn from. Definitely go to discussion and buy the work book and you'll do fine. Lectures as aren't totally necessary but at least study the slides
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: exam is so hard
If you buy the workbook, you'll basically be set for the course. You can study the practice tests in the workbook for the midterms and final. Overall, decent professor.

ECON302,482,490 - One of my favorite econ professors at UIUC. The classes he teaches all follow a very similar format. The workbook(302) is very helpful as it has sample tests/exercises that resemble the exams in class. There was extra credit in all his classes. Lectures may sometimes be dry, but he is very passionate and is just an awesome guy.
He should more time explaining the math portion.
Hes okay. He is good at teaching what is going to be on the test but his political views on business regulations are extreme.
One of the best professors I have had. He gives so much material to get you ready for all the exams and the final exam as well.
Excellent teacher!!!

Do the extra credit each time you do a homework assignment so you don't have to cram it all in later. Went to class probably three times. Wasn't a good idea because I had to study for like 30 hours to have any idea what was going on on the practice final exams in the book. And the final was way harder than the other exams. Still got an A tho

I thought this class would be an easy A, it wasn't. Buckley is good teacher, but the lectures are dry and hard to focus on. I 1000% recommend getting the notes packet and not slacking. Do as much of the extra credit as you can and study! Discussion was optional, but I advise that you go.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is incredibly enthusiastic and energetic. He is a great lecturer, even though the material itself is really boring. Try to go as often as you can because he will often include really interesting historical segments regarding the subject at hand. I did not go to office hour, but he seems like a very kind and approachable guy.

He actually cares about students - there's just so many in this class that it's hard to really connect with him in any meaningful way. He makes economics fun. If you pay attention in class, do the extra credit, and use the study booklet you should have a fairly easy A.
He's a good professor who definitely is very passionate about the subject, but the class was way too basic and easy, especially since you get so many practice exams that are very close to the exams.

ECON 302 is just not a hard course. I found his lecture quite tedious because he digs on to something really easy, but doesn't cover that much important stuff (like he has 50 slides of doing derivatives but just skims through important concepts).
He thoroughly explains simple concepts but does not prepare you for the super difficult exams. He offers LOTS of extra credit and the online homework is super easy.

Professor Buckley is a fantastic lecturer. If you go to class and the discussion sections a majority of the time and do the workbook problems, you'll get an A. He's also accessible outside of class if you need any help. He genuinely cares about his students.

Bryan isn't the most exciting lecturer, but he is good at explaining the material. Class is optional and he posts all of the lectures online. If you take his class, I recommend doing the extra credit mastery points on the homework site.

Buckley is a decent teacher but wastes so much time in lecture talking about the simplest concepts.  However, the tests are difficult and full of tricky questions. He does not curve tests. He lets you skip tests, but that is a poor strategy, and I have no clue why he offers it. He goes off on tangents about his opinions. Be ready to teach yourself
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Buckley is a great guy. In his class there are 4 exams (1 final). If you want you can skip all 3 exams except the final, it just puts all the weight on the final. If you are someone who skips lectures but is willing to study before the exam, do the practice exams they are just like the final. 100% on the homework is so easy, and its 30% of ur grade

Easy A+ class. The lectures are long and boring but you do not need to attend them. Work on his past exams in the workbook and you will do well in the class. It is easy to get 100% on the homework and he also gives a lot of extra credit.

SUPER EASY! Just do the some problems on the workbook and review the lecture notes before test you will be find. He really gave so many extra credits like 5%. I got an 95 on this course but end up with a 100% because of the extra credit.

He is a good teacher and has incorporated some good teaching techniques in order to make the material interesting and clear cut.  His ECON 302 Final was tricky but his mids are medium hard, few small tricks to keep you on your toes.  He is a good teacher who has embraced tech (lectures slides odf) and personality to make learning smoother.

VERY boring lecture (especially when they are longer than 50min) but overall his exams are fair. Homework will take about 10 minutes to complete so make sure you are actually learning the material as you go along and not cram everything before the test.

Does the best he can with lectures given the dry material. Homework is a piece of cake and worth a decent amount of the overall grade. Be sure to pay attention in lecture and do the practice problems, as the test a based very closely off of these.

He is one of the best econ professors here. The lectures are actually really helpful and he is great at explaining things. Tests are not tricky if you go to the lectures and discussions. Buckley is the man

Great lecturer, is extremely clear in presenting the material and goes through many different examples on the power points he posts online with step by step instructions on how to solve it. Always goes into great detail on questions and is passionate about the material. Only downside is there's little interaction with students

Professor Buckley is great. I find econ boring  but he's great at explaining things and making lectures interesting. He always finds a way to tie in real life situations with the example problems and show how certain economic decisions affect us. You can tell he really cares about his students and teaching. Exams aren't hard if you go to lecture.

Bombed the first exam. studied the practice exams in the practice book, got 98s on the next two. My final exam grade is unknown, but I got an A in the course. Do the homework, pay attention in class and do not fall behind.
Swaggy B is dope. Tests are decently hard, final was impossible. Homework is the easiest 30% you'll ever get. Take Vazquez for the easy A, take Buckley (or DIianni apparently) if you want to learn.
He posts all the needed material. You can skip lectures and discussions. However, do the weekly practices and read the lecture to get yourself ready for the test.
Multiple attempts for homework. You can definitely get 100% on homework. Tests are not hard at all, as long as you read the lectures and do the weekly practices. He posts all the needed material.

Not a bad teacher, but he's a too aligned with rules. I accidentally missed the final for my section, asked if I could take the final with the other section, denied me. Thought that was a little harsh especially when I explained to him I was a senior and needed the course to graduate. If you take him, be sure to keep up to date with class.

He really tries to make class fun but I just find intermediate microecon super boring. The 1.5 hour lectures are too long and I literally stopped going to class after the first midterm. Tests aren't too bad but you need to study really hard if you don't go to class. Some say he's easier than Dillani, some find Dillani a better teacher.
He cares about his students and actually TEACHES. Recommend him if you actually care about learning.

Plain and Simple, Dr. Buckley. He is a man who is VERY interested in economics. He tells you what is on the midterms, because his lectures are structured around them. TA Wkshts are helpful for FRQ on midterms and online HW is for Multiple Ch. Coming to the midterms, they were fairly simple. Overall, Dr. Buckley does his job and does it well.

Copied straight from exam: "If it takes me 3 minutes to understand your unique way of organizing the math for a single question, that could take me 72 exams * 3 minutes = 216 minutes = 3.6 hrs to grade a single question. I won't do that." I can understand it would take a while, my concern is: how is that our problem? Have TAs help you grade, idk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests are based on things he never mentions, lectures about, not in the readings he expects you to read, and not anywhere. The amount of sass is almost disrespectful at times and expects us to know everything before even taking the class. Furthermore, he leaves you in the absolute dark for exams and doesn't really explain what is being tested ever.

I'm taking the summer course (450). He talks a lot, but not much of it is actually useful information. He has a lot of filler information when he talks, and it makes it very draining to listen to him as he keeps talking about the same slide for incredibly too long. You end up having to completely depend on the textbook for this class.

The moodle is so disorganized and it's hard to find anything onthewebsite. You can't evenfindtheanswers to the studyguide on moodle. The exams are awful and mostofthe class got below 50% onit. The labreport average was so bad that he gave us another chance to do it and yet mostofus still didn't doitright because the feeback he gave wasnot helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: DONTTAKE This man does not teach at all expects you to know how to do everything. The tests aren't even part of what you do in class and the study guide never matches the exam. You can't even find the answers to the study guide in the course. The lab reports are so long and the feedback he gives are awful and don't even tell you what you did wrong.

This review is for MCB 450.

This class definitely makes you work to get an A, I had to read the textbook almost every day. Lectures are not too bad, he just goes on tangents a lot. For his tests you need to memorize the learning objectives. He's really helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of fun and Dustin is one of the more relatable instructors you'll ever take from. The only warning I have is that this class is very research oriented and there is lots of discussion and writing involved and the protocols are often multi-faceted and complex. Be prepared to be really confused (and to learn a lot)!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Having taken classes from all current 236 professors, I believe he is the best of the three. Lack of communication and overall disorganization creates a very demoralizing environment, however, he is a tremendous lecturer when present, and exams, while brutal, test conceptual intuition instead of mechanism memorization.

Our second exam average was a 34% and instead of owning up to this at all, he skipped our 9am class and had to be called by the TAs 15 minutes into class. He then started assigning us longer homework assignments to encourage us to "do better" and had a TA teach for him half the time. He also wouldn't tell us what our actual grade was all semester.
Should have a 1 rating
Burke will pay for his sins
Nothing worse than Marty
Didn't know professors could skip class without any heads up. Marty did:(
Couldn't of asked for a worse professor
33% average
You really rocked that Marty! At this point you should have let Casper the Ghost teach!
What a bum. Skip class again buddy.

His exams and problem sets suggested that he expected us to know significantly more going into the class than we really did (arrow-pushing, frontier MO theory, etc.). Great lecturer and conversationalist when he didn't skip his lectures and office hours. Be sure to work through practice problems more often than reading/watching videos
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One day, Burke will pay for what he's done.

Professor Burke's is really good when he lectures, but the problem is, he doesn't attend a lot of them and has one of the TAs lecture. Also, a lot of the content that comes up in the exams isn't directly taught.  Our exam 2 average was a 34%, and after that exam, he assigned us extra-long problem sets to "encourage" us to do better on the next exam

Class felt unorganized and didn't follow the syllabus, making it hard to prepare for lectures. Exams focused on random details instead of what was taught. TAs did most of the real teaching, and the professor missed classes often. Hard class already, but the teaching style made it much worse.

Dr. Burke comes off as a genius. The class seemed like his personal research playground. I loved his lectures, but his exams were IMPOSSIBLE. He didn't change the layout after 40-50% averages. The TWO TAs seemed overwhelmed & did majority of the work for him. He did not hold office hours or engage outside of class/on Canvas. Hardest class ever.

He is very passionate about the field, but as a professor he is the absolute worst. I've never met such an egotistical professor until him. The work was very difficult for orgo 1 and the TAs agreed. He was not reachable outside of class so don't bother emailing. He even stated in class that he wants the class to be as hard as humanly possible.

While Dr Burke is incredibly passionate about chemistry, he is not outstanding at teaching it. He does not hold office hours, and even the TAs admitted that a lot of what he taught seemed unnecessarily difficult for the level of the course.

He is absolutly one of the best professor I met at UofI. He present the knowledge very consistent and organize them systematically. I ask questions after each class and he'll answer in patient. He introduce his idea of lego chemistry into the class. The tests are not simple organic synthesis yet analyse research so it's challenging.

Do not take this proffessor he has the wosrt reputation for teaching. He barely taught the basics and gave all his work to his TA's. Doesn't have office hours and its like he wants you to fail. I've never heard anyone have a good experience with him. He's literally sadistic the avg for exams are literally F's and he would smile and make it harder.

Clear and concise in lecture. If you pay attention and copy down everything he writes, you only need to use your notes, problem sets, and practice exams to do well on the tests. I barely touched the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Burke is hard, he barely shows up to class but when he does he is so clear, so effective at teaching, welcomes questions and people coming up to the board and is approachable but teaches a very hard class. His tests are the hardest I've ever taken, but you learn SO much chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: So difficult!

Professor Burke's 436 was one of the best classes I've ever taken. Be prepared to work hard and be challenged and pushed more than you have ever been before, but if you can get through it you will feel so incredibly rewarded and like you've gained so much. Also, he curves the class A LOT. The test averages are low but he just cares about improvemen
Maybe you haven't seen better, but that doesn't make him the best prof in chem department. I would just say Zimmerman is way better than this guy.

Best professor of Chemistry department. Although exams are hard, but the final grades are given with curves. The lectures are really inspiring and interesting. He knows how to teach. My favorite professor so far.

Probably the most knowledgeable professors I have had at UofI. The course is very difficult however Prof. Burke is excellent at explaining concepts and  can answer almost any question asked by students. He also will lecture about his research at times which can be very fascinating. Would recommend, just be prepared for a tough class.
One of those guys who teach courses just because he has to. Shows to probably 3/5 of his lectures and the TAs teach the rest. Doesn't really put much effort to undergrads.

It used to be a tough choice for a ChemE between MCB 450 and Chem 436. Now it is trivial; in 450 you'll learn to memorize basic biochem, in 436 you get taught by one of the best professors at U of I. It is an incredibly difficult course (you will fail most of the tests), but you will dominate orgo (and the curve boosts your grade, lots of B/C's).
his problem sets are weird reactions he picked from random literature just to torture your brain. Exams have unbelivable low averages. Yes, and it's 8am MWF~enjoy!

Excellent at explaining concepts, and expectations for his class are very clear.  The material is very difficult, but I have a stronger understanding of organic chemistry than I do any other topic thanks to Prof. Burke.
Great guy, very clear and helpful. Subject coursework can be very challenging, but I honestly feel like I've learned a lot and have a good understanding of organic chemistry.
