reviews.comment: The WORST professor! 1. She is the laziest teacher. she doesn't have office hour and wouldn't return your Email. she makes classes shorter and cancel many classes! she doesn't explain much on lecture. 2. She makes the trickiest exams with the her calculator's rule and tons of steps, especially on final 3. No help, no teach, just video watch
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Terrible Exams. I learned a lot in class but the exams are unnecessarily hard. It will leave you feeling dumb. She does not know how to make an exam that is representative of what she taught in class.

I'm not kidding this is the worst professor at University of Illinois and I've seen them all. She makes you use calculators from the stone age to try and trip you up every step of the way. What would take 5 minutes takes an hour with these brutal calculators. The lecture videos seem simple and then when the practice test come around you're screwed.

One of the worst professors I had. This class is more so how to use a very basic calculator rather than actually learning economics. You'll find yourself finding the class pretty easy, but hard exams due to her strict rules.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Unnecessarily difficult. Take stat 100 instead if possible

All material learned in this class is very outdated and inefficient. She doesn't let her students use anything more than a five dollar calculator let alone excel. Don't bother going to class you'll be better off using that time to study the online lectures and HW. This class needs a curriculum change. Good Luck typing in those tedious numbers.

Finally a professor that I learn so well from! If you don't like learning on your own then you may have a tough time, but I love how lectures are studied on your own online. Makes it so much easier for me. Clear schedule, understandable topic progression, fair homework load and tests. Do your work and you will get an A! Best class at UIUC so far!

She has a ridiculous rule about calculators that handicaps students from using technology that is readily available to them in their everyday lives for absolutely no reason. She may argue it is to help students understand what they are doing, but that is a ridiculous argument because the calculator is only as smart as the person using it....
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Makes you jump through hoops and has super specific specifications for a calculator. Also doesn't lecture in class, makes you learn the material on your own, as well as homework. Lecture pretty much functions as a discussion and some people like it, but I didn't sign up for an online class.

Despite the negative reviews, I found her to be a very clear lecturer and her exams to be fair and straightforward. The calculator rule is unpopular with students but is necessary because of the statistical functions on advanced calculators. Overall, it's a fairly difficult class that makes you work for an A, but if you go to lectures, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Personality meh, but her teaching style is very clear and straightforward with plenty of example problems. The homework is easy too because you have 3 attempts. It tells you how to fix your mistakes & takes your highest attempts. Although it's time consuming, it's easy to get 100%. Memorization heavy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Puts trick questions on exams. Homework is far different than the exams. Grades harshly. Students are not allowed to have any electronic device in class for any reason other than the most basic calculator possible; this causes the vast amount of calculations required in the class to take an unnecessary amount of time.

She teaches and explains pretty well in class so I would strongly recommend going. Her tests are mostly basic questions we cover in class with a few that we never even talk about. Her biggest problem is the calculator rule. We can only use super basic calculators which are super easy to make mistakes on and can really screw you up.
Awful professor!! Avoid her!
The material in this class is pretty easy. All the problems on the tests are basically the same as what she does in-class. Not much more to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The class starts off easy but then gets extremely difficult for no reason. The professor moves way too quickly in class and is really bad at explaining. I would not recommend taking this class if you don't have to. She curves but barely enough. Also clicker points counts as a quiz grade so class is basically mandatory.
You just have to show up and pay attention in class. Colleen does a pretty good job of explaining everything in class. Midterms are super easy but the final was very hard.

Exams consist of ridiculously long calculations. Punch the wrong key on the calculator? Get the next five questions wrong! Lots of material was also tested of which we spent little on in class. Posted no resources/lectures slides online and prohibited pictures of her slides. She's clearly a professor who doesn't care about her students.
This course is not that hard, and the professor is good. However, those TAs are really terrible. The practice exams before the final have lots of mistakes. Study by yourself is the best option.

Her teaching is alright, she kind of rushes through everything. Her exams are a different level though. The material itself is moderate but it's as if she uses every sinew of her body to trick us. Also, she doesn't posts her powerpoints online and doesn't allow any use of electronics in her class. Welcome to the 21st century
You need to go to class to pass and get participation credit. Shes always there for you if you ask for help. I think she teaches pretty well.
Colleen is not a friendly outgoing teacher, but she gets the material across and teachers her students. If you pay attention in class, you'll learn the material.

WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER MET. It's like she is trying to trick her students in every possible way on purpose. First time homework due on 5AM? !No announcements and reminders at all about pop quizzes?! Tests have much more difficult content (even brand new stuff) than homeworks?! Take her Econ202class and you will understand "desperate". CNMB.

She explains well. Gives more than enough of iclicker and homework points. Tests are indeed tricky but you can get a decent grade as long as you don't make any careless or conceptual mistakes. Know your content well and you should be fine. Her ppt is enough for both exam preparation and learning.

Here's a few things to take away:  1) This class is really hard, so study and know everything  2) She makes her tests tricky, with "None of the Above" options, which is why the averages on tests are low 3) It is possible to get an A. I did, and I got a D on my first midterm  She curved the class by about 6-7% at the end of the semester.

No matter how much you study the material, she will always try and trick you on the exams. There were times when my T.A. didn't know the answer to some of the exam questions. I thought that was very unreasonable. Overall, if you study enough, it should not be too hard to pull off a B.

I would avoid at all costs. The material isn't extremely tough, but she plays so many tricks on her exams that it's almost impossible to get an A, not unless you spend your entire life reading the chapters and continually practicing problems. This will be my first B I've ever gotten.

The material isn't impossible and stats can be interesting. Colleen made the exams consist of only challenging problems and did not focus on us understanding the material. Also, she throws in a lot of last minute curveballs (i.e. she changed our test from mult choice to free response on the day of the exam).   Overall good lectures, tough exams.
She teaches and explains everything well. However, it is very hard to get an A.
Never have a teacher meaner than her
Many mistakes in homework and exams
8 AM Quizzes

Although the material is not too bad to learn, the exams (which make up 85% of your grade) are filled with tricks that are sure to fool anybody. No matter how well I knew the material, I still managed to fall for her tricks on each exam!

This class has been the hardest class I've ever taken. It sucks because you are required to take it as a business major and she's the only professor. They intentionally make the midtermsexams very difficult so do not underestimate them!
SOOOOOOOOOOOOO BAD! I wish I had taken Stats100 instead of this class

you get iclicker points for going to class but she isn't a very good teacher. you are really going to be on your own in this class so find a helpful group to study with. luckily the material isn't difficult at all

Colleen Schultz is easily the worst professor at the University of Illinois. It's a disgrace she's allowed to continue to teach. She doesn't explain anything, but magically expects you to know everything she never even mentioned to you on the test. Homework doesn't even help. Avoid her at all possible costs.

There are only four tests in the whole semester and she doesn't give you much opportunity to buffer your test scores. Lectures are not clear and she doesn't teach you everything that's on the test. She throws a lot of curve balls on the tests and she requires you to do your work out at the sixth decimal place which leaves large margin for error.

Where do I even start? iClickers everyday sucked ass especially at 8AM. She is very lazy and makes no effort to help her students directly. She doesn't have office hours - NOOO that lowly task is for TA's according to her (I probably learned more from them than her). Even in emails she says go to office hours instead of  actually helping

Schultz is a good teacher. Make sure you go to class and do the aplia assignments. The tests are easy, but the final is more difficult. The curve at the end is very high. I got an 87 and that ended up being an A.

TAKE STAT 100 INSTEAD!!!!!! do not take econ 202 with her, shes a good enough teacher but her class is 90% tests and the tests are hard. Stat 100 covers the same credit and its 10x easier. Schultz is actually a good teacher  but she makes her class impossible to get a good grade in, save yourself the time and effort and dont take it.

Colleen does a poor job on accurately testing students for the subject matter learned in class. She generally carries herself with a poor attitude in class, and seems to be irritated when students ask questions. She does not appear to be passionate about teaching.

Worst professor I had so far at UIUC. Tricky exam questions and unhelpful TA sections. The final is not fair, and the questions are not hard, but very confusing. Whatever, you can not avoid her since only she teaches econ202 for years. Bear with it!

Colleen is the worst professor I've had at U of I. She tries to trick you with her exams and makes statistics much more difficult than it has to be.  I learned more by myself than from her. It's a shame that this course is required for business majors.

Quite horrible professor. You need to be in class as much of the material is out of order or not presented in the book in the same manner that is presented in class. She also uses the iClicker system for points every class period. She will try to play tricks on exams, and doesn't allow audio recording. Doesn't post answers to PP slides if you miss.
Although she can be crabby and boring she is amazing at explaining things clearly.  Go to class, pay attention, and you'll get a good grade.  Her grading policy is very student friendly and fair.

The class itself was average as far as difficulty. The best way to learn the material is by going to lecture. The tests can be a bit tricky. I don't know if this is typical or if I just got lucky but at the end of the semester she pretty much threw points out for free to the whole class. Overall she's alright.

I hate this professor.. She was awful and her tests were the trickiest test I've ever seen. Horribly boring lectures. She is extremely sarcastic when you go to her for help. Avoid her at all costs. She is terrible

While the material itself is really easy, Schultz makes the exams as tricky as possible. Class is pretty boring, but can be helpful. The final was optional which was nice. Overall, it is very easy to get a B, but don't expect an A without a lot of studying, despite the easiness of the material.

Exams may be tricky, but they aren't terrible as long as you attend lectures and do all the homework. You should make sure you understand all the homework problems and the trickiest problems because they will always appear on exams. Easy A or B. Anything less is because you didn't understand all the concepts taught or in the homework.
Some questions in the exams are tricky. But generally the class is easy. The professor is kind of lazy.

Agree with below. This is an easy A class if you pay attention to in-class problems and do your hw. The in-class problems and practice tests resemble the actual tests, so just learn them well and you'll do great. On one of our midterms, 30% got perfect scores. Yes, seriously.
just not a fun person at all. no technology allowed in class, no laptops no phones out, can't use camera phone to take picture of a PP slide.

Seems like a bitter person. Also, she kept saying the hw is due wednesday but not the time. Turns out its due wednesday morning at 5 am hahahaha. I had not paid for the program yet as i registered for the course late. TA says she repeated the time many times which she did NOT.No lowest score drop policy so she is basically out to make life hell.
Her class is challenging, no doubt about it. Go to class everyday, pay attention and take good notes. Her exams can be hard, but if you study beforehand, you won't have a problem.

Relatively straightforward and helpful. I had a few questions and she was good about responding in a timely manner. My TA was also very helpful. She has clear and reasonable expectations, should not be too difficult if you are willing to put in the effort.
This professor is extremely tricky!!! I've been to the TA office hours and even the TAs can't solve her questions sometimes.
The class is a complete joke, but she is literally the WORST professor I've had on campus. She will definitely try to trick you on exams so be super careful when reading each question.

She has a very weird calculator policy, you can only use the 1$ basic calculator. She uses numbers with 6 decimals in her problems to her delight) and you have to do all the calculations with that calculator so if you hit a wrong button by mistake, you have to start all over. I hated every second of her class: useless, boring and uninteresting.

She at times seems uninterested, there are many tricks put on the test so make sure to review things from past exams because that always has a large enough impact on the following tests, the tests are not curved but the class is, if you put in the work to understand the material, you should do well.

Literally one of the easiest classes at this school. If you do not do well on the tests then that is your fault. You get a cheat sheet for every test and this class is all about knowing how to use the formulas given to you on the cheat sheet. Although she might not be the best professor, this class is easy.

Tests are not reflective of what you know in the class.  TA's are completely useless and can ruin your grade by giving you misinformation. By far one of my least favorite classes and I love economics.  Be sure to do well on the first test because it is the only one that is relatively straightforward.  The rest will not relate to what you learned.

For material that is not difficult and rather straightforward, she always finds a way to throw curveballs on exams that you are not prepared for at all. All multiple choice tests with answers within .0001 from each other. Exams are not indicative of whether you know the material. By far my least favorite class on campus so far.

Schultz's course isn't a walk in the park, but it isn't extremely difficult either. Great preparation for 203 with Petry. It's a statistics course so exams and problems are going to be inevitably tricky. If you take 203 and dislike it, then business or economics isn't for you. Good preparation to think quantitatively and critically.

Schultz is a completely awful professor. Do not take this class unless you really have to. I emailed her to ask about a test I took and it took four emails and two emails to the Econ department head before she replied. Additionally, it was incredibly snippy and condescending. Decent teacher; awful person.

My experience in her class has easily been the worst of any class I have taken at U of I. Her lectures leave you ill prepared for the exams and the TAs are completely incompetent. When I emailed her asking to meet with her, I ended up sending her four separate messages over 4 weeks before giving up and tracking her down after lecture. Unbelievable.

Great teacher. Go to class. Discussion was helpful sometimes. In discussion we either went over new material or it was a clarity/review type session. Do the hmwrk bc it helps a LOT.  If you do the hmwrk n understand it, u should do well on the tests
This class isn't all that bad.  The material is very straight forward.  Just make sure to always double check your work on the tests.  The homeworks help you prepare for the exams.

My TA was inept, but Prof Schultz did her job well.  Overall this class was relatively straightforward.  You get formula sheets, so every test is essentially open book and you have ample time for the 20 mc questions.
Terrible.  The material is straight forward and easy to learn on your own, she is useless.  Her exams are ridiculous, and not like the homework or examples you work in class.

Schultz just stands up on stage and reads off the power point slides.  You basically have to teach yourself everything and the exams can be pretty tricky.  It is a shame that there isn't another option for this course.  My only B in college.

Colleen has an attitude and is not a very nice person.  Her teaching style is lazy and careless. The course is set up so if you make tiny mistakes you will get significant points off. econ 202 caused me a lot of stress but i somehow got an A.  not looking forward to econ 203...although she doesnt teach it. thank god

Her teaching style is easy to follow, as all of her notes are given from her powerpoint lectures. Her tests are only 20 questions and some times tricky, making it difficult to get an A. Overall she is not a pleasant person, but if you attend lectures and do the homework it's not terrible.

A community college level professor teaching for a Big Ten University.This rushed course teaches on the same level as it confuses.The prof knows very little how to teach when away from her pre-made slides (wonder who made them for her)? Add that the TA's sometimes teach opposite what is taught in lecture. The whole course is economic diarrhea.

The class is straight forward so if you take the time outside of class to look over the material and get help from the TAs then you will be fine. She does her job of teaching the material and explaining it, along with answering any questions students might have.
Colleen is pretty good at teaching, very clear and concise with her explanations. Concise enough to get out of class early 90% time. She is kind of lazy though...

She is a very good lecturer and explains the material well if anyone has questions. The homework can sometimes be stressful because it requires precise answers due to mallards format. As for her exams, they are 20 question MC so it is difficult to get an A, however if you study and attend class this should breeze by as an easy B at least

Class material is simple if you attend lectures. But because of this the test material can be out to trick you at times. Colleen doesn't respond to emails, and doesn't care about students individually. She is also unavalible for office hours so if you don't understand something go to the TAs. You can still get an easy A or B despite her uselessness

i dont get how people say shes hard and useless. the class is VERY STRAIGHT FORWARD. all you do in class is do problems, which are the same as the exam. she also answered questions clearly. Lecture is not mandatory but useful and she usually let us out after 20 mins. if u didnt like this class your going to hate 203 and 302
One thing I noticed about her is that she has no office hours. The TAs are usually not competent enough to answer your questions.

Lectures and content of the class are very straightforward. Exams are bull. Seem easy but your grade depends on 19-20MC questions where there's much room for error esp using the one line calculators to calculate really long numbers, check and triple check your answers

Her lectures are good. Homework is pretty easy. Discussion is pointless to go to except to turn in homework. The class may start out seeming VERY easy, but the test are NOT. She can be very tricky on them & it's confusing. All the tests excluding the 2nd are somewhat hard. The 2nd midterm is VERY easy, but if you study hard, you'll be good.

Possibly one of the worst professors the University offers. Has a email policy set up to her advantage, if you don't send her an email the right way she doesn't have to answer back. This ultimately allows her infallibility if she forgets to respond to your email, she can claim you didn't write it the correct way. Terrible exams, No Compass grades.

She is very good at explaining the topic she teaches. Its a really easy class, but the tests are unfair. They are pretty easy and relate to the homework/material but are only 20 questions multiple choice. Its too hard to get an A on a short MC stats exam. There is too much room for error and she of course puts the tricks on the exams.

You get a sense that she is a good orator.Class is not too bad but exams can be challenging and you will never know how you you fare in the final. A radom grade that may or may not correspond with your earlier test scores is assigned in the end.Though if you have taken Gotheil, you will know that he does the same as well. Take STAT 100 if you can.

Honestly, I enjoyed her class probably one of the best profs I've had at this university, she knows her stuff. Yeah we're let out early 75% of the time but that's bc there's no reason to keep us longer. Exams are legit-based on hw & everything in notebook used in lecture. Go to class, or u won't understand the material! willing to help u if asked.

I had low expectations but have been pleasantly surprised how very effective a teacher she is.Extremely competent and forthright about the tests.Unlike Gotheil,she also did not force students to waste 150 bucks on self-written books. In fact none was required; we learned everything in class.  The class was not the easiest but not rigorous either.

Professor Schultz keeps things short and to the point. She tells you exactly what you need to know for the test, nothing more nothing less. We often get out early because she likes to keep the classes on the same pace and ours moves much faster for whatever reason. I would recommend her because she shows you exactly what you need to know.

She has abundant teachjing experience in Econ 202, which makes students understand things easy. In fact, materials you will cover are VERY easy. Attendance is strongly recommended. You need a TA for homework assignment. Exams are also easy, IF you study. People complaining her are either who love procrastination or just stupid.
No Comments

She should be teaching Let-Everyone-Go-Early 101 instead, since that's apparently what she specializes in. Seriously - I can't think of a day when we didn't get out at least 15 minutes early. Oh, and if you struggle in this class - all I have to say is: good luck in ECON203, which is a total LOL-fest.
easy to understand, class is not difficult, follow along and go to class and it will be easy

Honestly, despite the general consensus here, this class is EASY. What is more likely: that Schultz is a mean-spirited, incompetent demon trying to "trick" everyone, or that a vocal minority of students were over-confident in their skills prior to tests, and then realized that they either were not smart enough or did not study enough to get an A...

Actually, I did real well in the class and still feel like it was a dysfunctionally organized class from top to bottom. It was so bad that I remember she gave questions on tests she never went through in lecture or discussion or through announcements. SHE IS OUT TO TRICK YOU. Repetition is the key and practicing the online quizzes doesn't help.

If you complete the course packet in class and do the homework, then you should get an A (I got an A). DO NOT BLOW OFF STUDYING FOR THE FIRST 2 EXAMS. Put in 45 minutes to study for them cause they will keep your grade high since the 3rd exam is very difficult and the final is fairly difficult.

class is very easy, people that wrote underneath myself are just very incompetent and dont know what they are talking about, class is structured, hw is made difficult so you understand the material, repetition is key, more times you do something, better you get at it, take this class and do the hw dont listen to people who gave her bad ratings
They really need to restructure this class.  It is like a cattle call.  Hope you have a good TA because Schultz won't teach you anything.  She is an an absolutely horrible teacher.

Grades in this class are mostly determineed by the exams; Half of your grades on the exams are determined by what you know in statistics, and the other half is determined by your ability to outsmart Colleen's test architecture, which heavily punishes anyone who second-guesses themselves. Take ECON 202 elsewhere because UIUC's offering is very poor.

Not an organized class. The online quizzes are difficult b/c they are not multiple choice, you don't know what the real answers are, and questions are different each time.The tests are more difficult than they should be and she will put stuff on the test that she never went through in class. She doesn't even teach, anybody could instruct that class

I've gotten through Calc I & II but this class was ridiculous.  The exams are extremely hard & its not like a normal math class where u got a book to do practice problems; its just ur binder from class.  You get SOME online homework before quizes, but you have no way to know what you did wrong and correct it. Horribly organized class.

Schultz left mid semester to have her baby without telling us (and we didn't even know she was pregnant).  That was nice of her.  The class wasn't that bad.  I didn't find homework difficult, but the exams were really hard and didn't reflect the material always.  There was minimal out of class work.

You definately need to attend lecture and discussion to keep up. As long as you put in effort and keep up with the homework you shouldn't have any trouble. Homework is VERY ANNOYING but in the end helps with drilling some of the concepts into your head. Overall I enjoyed this class, and recommend it.

The homework is annoying and time consuming but overall this is the easiest class I have taken on campus/in the college of business. Does not require much time committment and the tests are very straight forward. She gives you a sheet with all the equations to use on exams.
If you go to class and do the (often frustrating) homework carefully this class really isn't that bad. The tests are tricky, but the course is curved very generously.
Easy material. She's clear about laying down what's expected of students on tests and what not. The online homework is ANNOYING! The class is on a curve.

This is a STAT course, with little relevance to Economics in general.  A few impossible questions on every exam.  I felt like we were expected to know things after little or no demonstration.  Schultz is really not a pleasant person to look at or listen to.  I put forth a decent amount of effort.  B for the class, but a 59 on the final...
That wasn't easy. That's for sure. If you take this class, GO TO lectures!!! Work hard and you'll do better than me.If you don't need this class don't take it as Gen ed or somth. It's tough.
Very thorough in class and explains things very well. Tests are little tough and you really need to understand the concepts to do well on them. I am anticipating an A in the class but I like Econ.
Nice lady, horrible exam.

I don't know what you all are talking about.. this is the easiest class I've taken at UofI. The only thing that would make this class remotely difficult is memorization of the formulas, but she gives you a formula sheet for each test with everything you need. Tests are very straightforward.
Very easy class... lecture helps, but come test time it is all about execution.
Fantastic teacher!  Highly recommended

worst teacher ever. she wants you to do poorly and her test reflect this. She was the first teacher I've ever had that actually curved grades so that they would hurt you. The most worthless woman in the world.

Seems nice in class but once test time comes, your opinion of her will change. TAs are either not proficient in English or not helpful and therefore useless in either case. There is no reference-based textbook for this class, so if you find yourself in a state of confusion, don't expect to be able to simply look it up later.
Terrible teacher. Overall she was not very helpful with regard to learning the material and tests are very hard.

202 focuses mostly on memorization of formulas and random definitions. I expected to be able to actually understand stats, but she introduces things without any comment on meaning. Tests are putative and don't cover the material fairly. No textbook exists that teaches it "her" way so you have to rely on the awful notes and braindead TAs.
this is a super easy class. its all formulas and study her notes and u will get an A. take her
Not recommended for your own good ...
She told me there was gonna be around 30 questions on the final...there ended up being 67 questions.  She never went over any of the crap on the test either...:(
Very hard, makes tests a lot harder than the material needs to be compared to what she taught in lectures.  TA's don't help much either.  Overall poor class.

i'd taken statistics before, and expected to breeze through this class. unfortunately this woman made things very difficult. she purposely tricks you on her tests and doesn't give you a clear idea of what's going to be on them. the icing on the cake is her beautiful singsong voice, which makes lecture soooo wonderful.
The material is easy, her tests are not.  The trickiest tests I've ever taken, the class set-up is awful.

the tests in this class are tricky as hell. you can make up for your grade with the homework somewhat. there was a big curve in the class too. the one problem is that colleen schultz is extremely hot and may distract both male and femalte students with her  excquisite beauty

In all my time being a student, I have not experienced a more arrogant, useless, and evil instructor as I did when I was in Colleen Schultz/Houlihan's class. It is a shame people like her are given a salary to teach. I want a refund.
I am the walrus...coo coo cachoooooooo!  This class isnt that hard, but the tests are complete bull**** compared to the homework

Unfortunately this class is required..if its not..dont take it! The exams are much harder than the lecture material so theres not much you can do. TAs are sometimes hard to understand so basically you are on your own.

SCHULTZIEEE.O I thought the class was REALLY easy, but the tests are TRICKY. She's arrogant, like knowing basic statistics makes her the "God of the Class." TheTAwas good,and she's won awards,butIfelt like it was a trip back to the bad highschool teacher that felt like she knew it all,but shedidn't.

Very hard teacher, TAs are just plain bad. Tests are designed to kill your grade. There's always a trick on a test that was never presented in class or in any other way, so you're totally on your own.

Class looked easy at the beginning. Then the first test came, and it was crap. You have to study and know what you are doing for this class. There is a good curve, but if you don't know the material backwards and forwards, you're screwed.

Prof. Schulz isn't at all friendly. Plus, she can't  explain things in simple English. You have to really know your stuff before the exams. Simply taking the practice quizzes won't cut it. You need to know how to handle all the problems, while also watching out for tricks and twists on the exams.

Prof. Schultz is a tough professor. She speaks very un-clearly in class and definitely doesnt explain things too well. You pretty much teach yourself the material, so going to class is pretty important, esp. for pop quizzes! Tests are difficult so study your butt off!
whats with this woman? i get an A on the first test and all of a sudden i feel like a chicken with my head cutoff, i know the material but tests are crap, and she's a total **** outside of class.
Worst prof. in the entire world.  Not very friendly, tests don't test what you know.  They are designed to fail you.  Have fun w/ this class.

I don't really like Econ, but she makes it fun and entertaining. //'tying rope around neck'// The exams are very easy.  //'climbing up on chair'// I love her and could be more pleased with the way she teaches. //'tying rope to fan'// Props to her.  //'kicked the chair out'//   Aaaghhh.
Seems to take pleasure in seeing students fail.  Test questions are designed to be missed.
Could care less about you and whether you learn or not. Unfortunately there's little choice in who to take this class with. TA's seem incompetent.

Exam points are strangely distributed; some questions seem trivial.  TA's are questionable - shouldn't the TA's teach the students, not vice versa?  Mallard quizzes can sometimes seem impossible - doesn't really follow the "recommended text"
I hate her.  I knew that material, yet bombed her bloody tests.  Schuuuuuuuuuuuuuuultz.

Go to lecture, definitely.  Questions are answered a little curtly.  Exams weren't too bad.  Lecture notes help, but if don't review them before a test, then good luck--sometimes feel you are on your own She does slow down if things are unclear.

I love her, great class notes.  TAs aren't the best, but what can you do.  Oh, and don't talk during her class--she HATES it!  She will stare you down until you shut up.  Just go to lecture every day and PAY ATTENTION and do the online quizzes.

I think this prof. is okay: not bad, yet not exceptional. What I liked was that most of the assignments had extra credit points for doing them early, which I took advantage of. The prof. did hold "study sessions" during the cancelled lecture periods, which I appreciated. His lectures are fine too, as mostly they are recaps from the pre-lectures.

Zilles was apparently once well respected and highly competent. Not sure what happened behind the scenes, but 233 under him was a rolling disaster of labs and course plans being dropped as he badly rewrote them on the fly, and such utter silence from the top that course staff couldn't figure out what the trajectory of the class was. Worth avoiding.

This was my first time taking a CS class, it wasn't too bad but I feel like learning new things isn't too challenging for me. Everyone is different, but although Zilles wasn't an amazing teacher, the material isn't too bad as long as you study and practice through homework and quizzes. I had to teach myself a lot of it though.
made my cry at least once a week
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors ever. Lecture points are based on accuracy, labs count for points but are useless, and exams are horrible. Grading weights make it almost impossible to succeed in the class since the majority of grading are on exams. Try to take this course outside of U of I to avoid the abomination that is this class.

All these other ratings could not be capping more. If you do the readings, you'll be fine. Craig was light-hearted and fun, literally no complaints. The homework's go MUCH MORE IN DEPTH than the tests, so even if your really only understanding half of it, your fine. Gives out practice test week before test. Questions mirror those seen on test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Awful!!!

Lectures are confusing, fast paced, and do not cover material on exams. Lectures are all iclicker questions for points. Labs are not helpful. Exam format and grading system is horrible. The text book does not relate to the homework. The whole format of class is terrrible. I absolutely HATE this class.

Pretty fun at times, but the class is basically only your homework outside of class: working on a digital textbook and other coding activities each week. The digital textbook is long and tedious, and challenging sometimes. Lectures are boring and do not cover the hard topics. Not too bad of a class overall. Exams and quizzes can be flown through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Solid class

Horrible professor and horribly taught class. Both the labs and lectures were completely unhelpful and the TAs were rude and made you feel stupid for asking questions. You were basically expected to learn an entirely new "language" by reading a textbook. The class is also completely useless for gies majors since it barely focuses on excel.

I have never suffered so much anxiety and stress because of a class in my life. The class is so large that it is nearly impossible to ever speak directly to him. The way the class is run works for some but definitely not for all. I put 12-15 hours of work into this class a week, about the hours of a part time job.This class needs some serious work.
This professor does not help. His TA's do all of the work. Even then they often cancel their office hours. Lectures are mostly poll questions. This class is NOT beginner friendly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked the class structure of CS 105 with the distribution of labs and lectures along with how the assignments were laid out similarly every week with the textbook participation and challenge problems. It is also very easy to reach out for help in this class. Only caveat I have was how the lectures were simply just poll questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Craig is chill, people complained that CS105 was hard... well programming is hard. His course along with David has taught me basic phyton skills that can give me the confidence to take higher-level CS courses.

Craig is the worst professor I've ever had. You have to teach yourself. The only way to learn is Zybooks. There are a variety of ways to get "help" in this class, but they're useless. Responses take hours to receive and help is always incredibly vague.

Prof Zilles is probably the smartest professor I have found at UIUC. His course requires you to do a lot of additional work and studying outside of class, however, he provides all the materials to you to practice. Study 15+ instances of the exams and go through 20-25 of the practice final and you'll be fine. For homework either get chegg or tutor
It is a fun class and the lessons are fun, but the professor doesn't do anything. It's the TAs doing all the work and I don't really understand why the professor's really there.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Even though this class was for non-computer majors and I had no prior coding knowledge, I felt like this class was easy. As long as you do the material, attend lectures, and do the practice quizzes he gives out you'll be fine.

The lecture is a bit annoying since there are poll questions that need to be answered. Decent amount of work outside of class compared to others since there's an interactive textbook and prarielearn assignments. My advice is to do the practice exams A BUNCH. The questions are normally the same types for the practice exam and the real one.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zilles is a really nice person. He's good at explaining difficult concepts and lecture are quite fun considering it's CS. I'm glad that I took this class despite its heavy workload. You don't normally get extra credit or curves in the class, but the practice tests are really helpful and exams are fair.

There is an incredible amount of homework and almost every weekend there was a quiz or exam. My best advice is to actively read the textbook and do a bunch of practice tests (I did 5 for each quiz/exam but I also had no prior knowledge of CS). Knowledgeable prof but the textbook is essential in learning the material. With effort, you'll be ok!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Exams are 60% of your grade. He gives out 1 or 2 opportunities for extra credit , like 0.25%. There is a lot of homework. A lot. But they're all on a fixed schedule so they're easy to keep up with. DO NOT FALL BEHIND. Go to office hours, do the homework and you'll easily get a B. The book is mandatory and so is attendance to labs and lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: CS105 is the worst class I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was incredibly hard. You had to read a whole interactive textbook chapter (and code during it), turn in hundreds of assignments, and attend the hour long lecture for points. I was only in this class for a week or two before I realized this is NOT for beginners. Please do not take this class first semester. Take it second semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I came into the class knowing nothing about CS. This class is about how much you apply yourself. It's hard as F but if you go to the lectures and study for the exams, you should be walking out with an A or a high B.

I can write an essay about how bad this class is. I'll keep it brief though, WAY too much HW, deadlines are horrible, too many consecutive quizzes, you learn more through zybooks than you do the profs, lectures don't teach you anything. This class is a stress generator, avoid it if you can. Worst class I've taken in regard to student mental health.

Run. Got stuck on a problem so I asked where to look in the textbook to help teach myself and this was what I got: "Zybook doesn't necessarily teach you to solve all types of questions that you will encounter in this course, just as college will not teach you to solve all types off questions you will encounter in your future career" ??

I strongly agree that people who rate this class/professor poorly are the people who take this course expecting to be easy without any effort. A lot of students came to the lab without reading the textbook and expect it to be easy. He gives you a lot of resources, and you just have to do a lot of practice quizzes and tests to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've ever taken and lectures did not help or make any difference. I had to retake a test because my computer broke and they never got back to me the whole semester so I got an F. Refused to curve any of our tests but curved the tests for people the following semester. very inconsistent. overall learned nothing

People who rate this class/professor poorly are the people who take a CS course expecting to spend 2 hours a week and minimal effort into it and walk away with an A. The class requires a good amount of work, as all CS courses do. Concepts were explained very clearly. Be ready to devote lots of time, but if you put in the work it's not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: CS105 is a *class* and you are in it to LEARN programming! Negative reviews on this page are uneducated and ignoring the fact that this class is still a **Computer Science class**. Come into the class with an open mind and work ethic, and it will actually be pretty easy. Homework is manageable with unlimited attempts, there is quite a bit though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I actually like this professor a lot. I have no idea why people give him bad comments. He cares about the student and gives us a week off so that we can be more focused on our work.

Unbelievable for a 100 level class that some people are just taking as an elective. As everyone has mentioned, the work load is beyond heavy and crazy. You will spend HOURS on this class every single day. The fact this is allowed is unreal. On test days, you have lectures after that as well - just to put that into perspective. Avoid at all costs.

I took CS105 at UIUC and Zilles was a fair professor. The class is not an easy A, but he gives you all the resources to succeed. He gives practice exams available which are always very close to the real exam. Do not memorize the questions. You need to know the material to succeed in this class.
This class is way too hard to be doing online, he doesn't care about our grades at all...

The majority of individuals came into class with no experience in CS. The grading for this class was based on a bunch of midterms (10%) and quiz (2%), with a midterm every three weeks, a quiz every three weeks, with one week without an assessment. No curve, but the opportunity to offset the tough assessments with pretty easy homework.

You'll have to put in lots of work. I spent the most time of all classes on this class. It's really not that hard of a class if you give it enough time and not get frustrated for not understanding something. There's basically always office hours and tutoring appointments available to make for help. Lecture at 9 sucks. I loved the challenge though!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If I had taken this class in person, or if I was allowed to take it in person, I would do much better. You can tell he knows what he's doing but he's not good at putting it through a screen. I was confuesed for 90% of the semester. His lectures are just clicker questions and it doesn't really feel like you learn from them.

He and his TAs weren't very considerate of students grade or their concern in the middle of the pandemic. While students asked him questions about grades in lecture when he gave us the chance he ignored them and answered what he wanted. He is very sarcastic and has a way with words.

He takes no leniency for personal issues and does not take into consideration a wholistic grading perspective. He is more worries about logistics than students actually learning. Overall brutal professor who throws lots of work at you. I barely managed to get an B-.

you would think in a class for non-tech majors the material would be a smidge easier. nope! literally the hardest & least favorite class i've taken at uiuc. TAs are rude and unprofessional, and lecture slides & homework were posted up to 5 days late....5 days! so so many exams and tests. if this class isn't specifically required, stay away!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Zilles was great. The class was enormous (600 people), so I didn't ever interact with him directly. However, he is a terrific lecturer, and the course was laid out in a very clear and understandable way. I would highly recommend Zilles and this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Apparently CS 105 was revamped this semester. There were four exams and the final, so a bit test heavy, but the quantities of homework and practice quizzes and exams were very helpful.

There's a lot of reading outside of class, but you get a lot of practice with the code. Practice exams are almost identical to actual exams, so it makes studying pretty easy. He said he wouldn't curve our exams but ended up curving exams 2 and 3 in the end, so that was a bonus. Overall the class is doable if you put in some effort.

He became the new professor for CS 105 after the old professor left because of a family member's illness. He completely changes the class, makes it way more difficult and time-consuming, and gets rid of the large curve that the last professor gave out. There was no reason for him to change the class so much and I will never like him for doing that.
Took his CS225 last semester and had a lot of fun. The MPs are hard and lots of homework, but this is what CS225 like from the past. Super humorous and make this class funny.
Was looking forward to taking this class, however this professor did not explain concepts in depth well enough. Expect to do a lot of outside learning

Personally, I disliked the material, but he gives humorous and informative lectures. He explains the subject and answers questions quite well. Lots of info and materials posted on the course website. This particular class starts out stupidly easy, but ramps up significantly through the semester, ESPECIALLY in the last few weeks. Don't slack!

When I took CS 126 with Prof. Zilles in its second semester, it was clear that the course hadn't yet fully matured. Rubrics came out late and could be confusing. Despite these setbacks, I really enjoyed 126. Zilles connected well with students, was entertaining, and very knowledgeable. Lectures were somewhat slow, but informative nonetheless.
Zilles is notorious for being mean to his students. CS126 is poorly organized.
Professor Zilles is a great lecturer and takes time to ask the class if they have any questions or needs clarification.  I also had him for lab section and he is easy to talk to outside class.

Prof. Zilles was awesome for lectures. He made a great environment for participation even in a large lecture . Very smart and always knew what he was talking about and was able to effectively answer all questions.

Craig is a great professor.  His lectures are well paced and he will stop and ask students if they have any questions (and actually scan the room) rather than just racing ahead through the lecture.  I also had him for my discussion and he is helpful at explaining discussion problems.

He is a fantastic professor who is very good at explaining concepts, and always willing to answer your questions. But be sure to pay attention, because the class goes FAST, and the last 7 or 8 weeks covers a lot of challenging material! But all lectures are posted online, so it's not hard to learn the concepts you miss if you put in the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: best professor EVER!!!!!!!!

Craig is a wonderful teacher and amazing lecturer.  He teaches well while also throwing in humor to keep you interested in the material.  The class did seem to suffer from a lack of communication at times.  However, I screwed up on an exam by incorrectly submitting part of it, and Craig allowed me to do a makeup assignment as to not ruin my grade.

IMHO, the first 3/4's of this class is totally manageable. But around when midterm 6 hits, this class just went downhill. Not only that, we didn't really have much time to do SPIMBOT. Also, the last midterm was ridiculously hard (it's 20% of your grade) and studying from just course materials was not sufficient.
I'm very glad I took this course. I learned new things every day. This is the fairest course I've ever taken in terms of grading. That said, the lowest grade I've ever received was this class.

Class is fairly easy except for the fact that you learn nothing in lecture and learn 95% of the material in 5 minutes of discussion and doing labs. Then, he ruins your grade on a last test worth 10% more than the final. Which he follows up by not telling you any information about what's on/the format of the final and you inevitably fail that.
I LOVE CRAIG

Awesome teacher. The best CS professor at UIUC by far. Very detailed in his instructions and teachings. I had him as a TA this past semester as well as the professor in lectures. He is just as good as a TA as he is as a professor. Funny guy too which keeps things entertaining.
Awesome!!
Best professor on campus. If you can register for his discussion section, go for it! He's very helpful and explains things very well. Second-chance exams, extra credit from quizzes...
He's very nice and gives a helpful lecture. I'd say he's pretty good at explaining the material.

Sometimes assumes everyone has prior experience with Java, so his explanations are unclear for those of us who have not. The incredibly generous extra credit points makes up for the difficulty of the class, though. I would say his forte is in CS 398 and not 125, though.
He's honestly one of the best professors that the CS department at Illinois has. He's crystal clear, exceptionally helpful, and hilarious. Definitely look forward to having him for 398 next semester.
He a good professor, but not the best. I enjoy his classes, and it's always crowded.
A very nice professor!!

Amazing professor - attend lectures and discussions! Well structured, extremely interesting. Lab assignments were helpful to see what we learned practically. Very clear in class, lots of office hours (prof + TA). Subject matter very useful in the real world and extremely interesting. Recommend it without hesitation - even if you're not a CS major!
Zilles is awesome. Extremely clear, very interesting, everything you could want. This course is CS398 right now and was a little unorganized (understandable since the class is new).

Extremely nice and likable guy. The material is interesting, he presents it well, and he's very entertaining without being over the top. Very knowledgeable about what he does, and has a quite generous grading system (all exams have a 'second chance' where you can retake questions).
Cool and fun professor!

He's amazing. Knows how to talk, extremely knowledgeable, uniquely funny and enthusiastic. Very helpful (held a review session for a midterm at 7pm) and gets concepts across very well. The material itself was super interesting and makes you think differently. Highly recommend this class (if you're not a CS major; it's mandoatory for CS majors)

One of the best Professors I have ever seen in my life. Crystal clear teaching. Knows everything in his field. Makes class interesting with his teachings and jokes. Makes this class easy even though it's pretty hard
Amazing guy.  Very smart, knowledgeable.  Really cares about class and students.  Unique sense of humor.

Despite the fact that Craig teaches my least favorite topic in CS (architecture), I still found him to be very enjoyable and his lectures informative. He's always well-prepared and really understands the subject well. He also teaches one of the discussions section (unheard of). One of the best professors at U of I, period.

By far the most amazing professor I've encountered at this university. Extremely knowledgeable, knows how to effectively convey that knowledge, and is super patient with questions after class. He really cares about his students and it shows.
Awesome, easygoing, funny professor.

The class is very interesting but hard. This probably is the first cs class that you can learn real stuff from and Craig knows a LOT. He can literally explain every single question you can possibly come up with. He's extremely helpful and cool, probably the best cs professor in the department lol
By far one of the best professors I have ever had the pleasure of learning from.  If you ever have the chance to take a course with him, do it ... you will not regret it!
100% Heart, 100% of the time

Best professor at uiuc hands down. He really wants you to learn and will do everything in his power to do so. Very easy to talk to. He writes new exams and homeworks every semester. If only he taught more classes...

This guy reminds of Bill Gates, in a good way. Out of all CS Dept. teachers, he is by far the most interesting. He has won Engineering College teaching awards many times and will continue to do so with his dynamic and helpful style.
Definitely the best CS professor I've had so far at this university. He made me want to come to class every time, and that's saying a lot!
Great professor -- explanations are excellent. Wish't he taught more classes though.
Best CS professor at UIUC by far!
Comments given on 5/2/07 say it all :D

Craig Zilles is one of the best profs. I've ever had! He's animated during lectures, has a great sense of humour, knows what he is talking about and is able to explain it very very clearly. Full marks

Mr. Dickerson is extremely sweet, understanding, and flexible to his student's needs. He encompasses a safe environment from day 1. His criticism and advice on writing projects is helpful and makes sense. His attendance-optional writing workshops are really helpful.
Good professor, graded fairly. Gave good feedback. Definitely take him for RHET105
He's just a great teacher and person overall. Would recommend.

I took RHET105 this semester and all I have to say is this was such a good class. Mr.Dickerson is such a nice professor and is there to make your life easy as possible. His classes are normal and lets us out early at times. There are 4 papers but he gives you plenty of time. Over all amazing teacher and would 100% take this class again

I absolutely loved having Curtis as my professor. He gave really good feedback and plenty of time to write your essays. He also was super courteous of students and understanding. I recommend him to all my friends for RHET105!!

Kind and understanding professor, but the course was extremely unorganized. Roughly three weeks of content were cut due to slow lecture pacing and organizational issues. Several homework assignments were extra credit in order to save time. As a result, I cannot confidently say that I learned much from the lectures. No practice exams were provided.
Not a good professor and does not really care about teaching students.

He is friendly and will help guide you if you get stuck on a problem. I relied more on the textbook and problems than the video lectures. His grading policy is lenient, so I felt that he was understanding towards students. 

He really left an impact on me with his encouragement and kindness. I admire him a lot and think he is an excellent teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not the best lecturer & moved through slides too fast. The slides though were very detailed and clear, which made them good for HW and studying for exams. It was a pretty reasonable course, and extra credit was offered to raise your grade, as well as an optional final to replace your lowest test score.
Fairly nice, but poor lecturer. Bad at explaining things. Goes too fast. Lecture material and homework is difficult. Thankfully, tests were rather easy. Somewhat reasonable. Odd sense of humor.

His STAT410 is way much easier than I've expected. He has a good latex skill and makes super helpful slides. (Though I have to take 1pt off because of his lectures) Easy exams & homework (literally the same spirit.) If you are a good self-learner, definitely take his class.

Most of the people on here complaining about this Professor are: 1.) Mad because you have to attend to get FREE attendance points (so sad right?) 2.) Mad because you have to actually study (an average amount) to do well (so sad again right?) 3.) Mad because they don't get a 'cheat' sheet for formulas. He does give poor answers to some questions.

The median on the first exam was an A, second exam was a B. No reason for level 5 difficulty. Gives helpful hints before exams, says 'Would this be a good question?' during class *hint hint*. He rescheduled classes, but made the attendance bonus. One session was used as an exam review when the projector was broken, which was helpful not hurtful.

He decided to reschedule classes to evening despite normally meeting in the day. When addressed with the concern that people have conflicts, he made no effort to make the lecture content available anywhere else. He also gives attendance credit which students are missing just because they have a conflict they couldn't get out of in a week. Horrrible
worse prof ever

He seems very careless and nonchalant, to the point where the projector screen wasn't working the day before the exam and he decided we didn't have to cover that material and he would just answer questions instead. He also struggles to explain ANYthing, even the simplest of concepts, and went way out of logical order when teaching the class.

Has a very "I don't care" attitude while lecturing. Weekly quizzes which seems a bit excessive. Material was difficult and he didn't take the time for everyone to grasp the difficult concepts. TA's were also useless and clueless

Worst professor Ive met. He makes the tests so hard and yet is unable to explain the concepts properly. Its hard to pay attention in class as his voice is kinda soft and theres a lot of ummm in his sentences. There were some mistakes in his notes too. Youre better off just studying the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Worst Professor Ever. There's never certainty in any of his lectures; expect a lot of "umm... maybe... it looks like..." so you naturally doubt anything that he says. Also, his answers to the students' questions are always vague so you may have been better off googling the answers. In fact, you'll be better off having google as your instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He makes STAT 420 the hardest and most useless statistic class I have ever taken. I am curious why he still cannot explain the content clearly even if he teaches the same class every year.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's bad at explaining things and the midterms were hard.
Awful. 0/10. Would not recommend. Sounds boring when lecturing. Doesn't know how to explain difficult material to students. Terrible.

He was a  nice guy but his teaching method was to have his typed notes on the projector and say "First you do this, then this, then this" while underlining things.  He was not good at explaining even the most basic concepts.  After lectures I could not tell you what I had learned. I would suggest trying to take another professor if at all possible.
Terrible teaching skill. He says textbook is not required, however, you will suffer if you don't read the textbook because his lecture is tedious and hard to understand.
he is just not a good teacher, terrible classroom atmosphere makes you fall asleep all the time. AVOID his course unless absolutely necessary
The class is super hard and confusing, but Professor Culpepper curves all exams and the final at the end. You can still manage at least a solid "C" even with bad exams scores.
Classes are boring.  He is a good professor, though, trying to teach us everything he knows.  This term, I opted out of the final and this is really great! Maybe not next time.

I've never felt compelled to rate a professor before, but he is just not a good teacher. What he covers in class is fine, but it is not especially relevant to the homework. The homework is quite challenging and the material we have not covered. He does not do examples in class. The tests aren't awful, but there is no curve (avg  65%).

Look as far as a human being, he seems like genuinely a nice guy, but in terms of teaching, he is awful. He explains super basics in class to where its almost pointless to go and then gives super tricky homework and test questions and does not say anything helpful in office hours or respond to emails at all. Basically he sees this class as a game.

I heard this class was supposed to be impossible, but to be honest I didn't find it that bad.  He did a good job explaining the concepts and really if you did the HW problems on Compass for practice the exams were super reasonable.  Was patient and didn't move on until all questions were answered.  A professor that actually liked teaching - finally

Cant explain things very well. Could not answer my question during office hour. Nice guy though, and gives relatively easy grade. But never make me to understand, and I feel I am suffering for the semesters.

This man could teach statistics to a class full of preschoolers and they would all catch on. He's the best. Super pleasant, genuinely nice, patient, and can explain difficult material in a way that makes it seem like you're simply learning the alphabet.  Awesome class.

He made the class enjoyable and gave clear lectures. He always explained things in a way that made the content seem fairly simple.  Exams were fair and not that difficult if you did the HW he assigned every week. Love the extra credit policy also. One of the best classes I've taken at U of I and one of the best professors. Definitely take the class

Not a very good teacher, but he could be much worse. Homework can take a long time and there are usually one or two questions on test that are really hard. He offers a descent amount of extra credit to make up for lost points though.

Steve was by far one of the most reasonable and fair professors I've ever had.  Found the lectures to be useful and he explained example problems really well.  Could work on answering students' questions better, but overall a great professor. Fairly easy tests and very nice/patient/helpful during office hours. Lots of I-clicker Extra Credit ?s also

Steve is a really friendly and helpful guy.  His teaching is pretty solid and it's not too hard to get a good grade.  Attendance in this class was among the lowest i've ever seen on campus.  I would recommend going to lecture and discussion.  HW is not easy, but between Steve and the TAs you will be walked through it.
It never allowed curve your grade. Moreover, after final exam, he ignored all e-mail. (No reply). During class, he tempts a student to keep his class by extra credit, but it is not significant.

This class is super easy to get a good grade in...extra points on each of the midterms and a replacement policy with the final.  He is moderately helpful in class.  I think he gets slightly more flak than he deserves, in my opinion.  Also, if you go to lecture and read the slides he posts online, I don't think that the textbook in really necessary.
Worst instructor I have ever had so far. He makes do the homework before he teaches the material.

He is really nice but does not explain things very well. When I ask him a question in class he just looks and me sympathetically and says, "Um, well, if you look at the board you can see how we got there." So I'm teaching myself from the book for the most part :( At least he's cute!

I am pretty disappointed of this course because I feel like he does not know how to teach. Most of us were just confused even after his lecture. Though he is a nice person. He did not do a good job teaching at all...

He is very very nice. However, he probably couldn't teach basic algebra. He gets lost in what he is doing. He uses a photo-copy-of-the-book powerpoint to teach...and the book is useless. Which, in turn, so are his lectures. The homework takes hours a week to do, and really is not that useful. Avoid at all costs.

This is the worst class I've ever seen at the university level.  The professor is very nice, but he doesn't teach. He will not work problems in class.  He explains nothing. Instead, he has the students work problems, telling them to "discuss the problems with your neighbor". Class is social hour. I had to learn from the book on my own. :-(

Good lecturer, but his class was the most challenging math I have ever taken. Managed an A- but it took 10+ hours per week on the HW and lots of TA office hour time. If you like to be really challenged,  take this class. He's also extremely attractive!

A really nice guy who will help students if necessary.  The 1st test was easy, after that, they were ridiculously hard but generously curved.  In essence, the lectures did not adequately prepare us for the exams.  On the bright side, because of curving, its easy to get at least B overall.

He is probably one of the worst professor in UIUC. Does not know how to use the blackboard to teach math. His slides are just copies from the textbook which are equally bad as the professor himself. I passed this course on my own. The TA's do a better job than him.

Prof. Perry is truly enthusiastic about the course and care for students, and he gives detailed, wonderful feedback for our essays! (My final paper received one of the longest feedback I've ever had and I learnt a lot from it ^-^

Class is discussion-based. only assignments were 3 four page long papers and some short quizzes that made sure we read it and asked for our thoughts on the readings. Based on the check +/- system, like many English professors, so it wasn't stressful and focused on our enjoyment and interest of the material rather than memorization and such.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weird guy, goes off topic a lot. Not sure how much I learned in the class. He's very unclear about what he expects, but the syllabus is reasonable and he grades easy. He used check/check minus grading which was confusing. 3 or fewer check minuses equalled an A. Doesn't use Canvas.

I really enjoyed taking Early British Lit. from him - he is knowledgeable and passionate about the subject + expectations for the class are clear from the start. If you do your reading and come to lecture, you should be fine.

Did NOT enjoy this class. He wasn't clear on what was expected of us to get high grades (3 out of 3) and even when asked to clarify, didn't explain well. Felt like he had too high of expectations for students and made me disinterested in the rest of the class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: From reading past comments & talking to people, it seems he's much better in a small class setting than a large lecture hall. He's my favorite prof, personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He always replies e-mails as soon as possible.

My ability to read, comprehend, and analyze texts became much strong because of this class. The midterm was too long, but the final was manageable. In lecture, you had to rely more on what he was saying rather than the powerpoint - I never looked at the powerpoints; I just concentrated on what he was saying. Quizzes in discussion were hard.

reviews.comment: ANGER MANAGEMENT ISSUES. He got so angry once and yelled/slammed his fist on the table of a kid who sat in front due to his wheelchair. Relies so much on his notes and is just overall kind of an uncomfortable person. BAD.

If you have the chance to take another professor for this class, do it. Perry's lectures are super boring, I've fallen asleep during almost every class. He's all over the place when talking and his PowerPoints aren't very useful.

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Perry wasn't great. His lectures are very dry and boring and the content he picks to read is often too dense to understand in the time he gives you to read the material. His weekly quizzes are full of passage identification questions for very specific pieces of the text and are often confusing and very tedious. Bad experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was a non-Shax revenge tragedies class, and he was fantastic. Lectures were fun and helped fuel discussion. He made it so much fun to close read and discuss this stuff that people usually had a lot to say. Also quite approachable and sensitive to how students are responding to texts and assignments. Definitely recommend.

Overall, I've had great experiences with the English staff at UIUC, but the head of the department really let me down. His exams were impossible because of the term section, which no amount of studying could help. His lectures were horrible, very confusing and did not help you understand the texts at all. Very rude and took himself too seriously.

Second time around with Prof Perry, rated him for 209 earlier as a freshman. This class was smaller, a little more intensive as it is a 400 level. Captivating speaker, knows everything- not just Shakespeare but Renaissance Drama in general. If you need someone to write a letter of recc for grad school, having the head of the department isn't so bad

Professor Perry is so much fun! He is a great lecturer, and he really knows what he's talking about--he makes lectures interesting. While lecture attendance isn't mandatory, it does help a lot with understanding the material. Perry makes quirky jokes, but helps get the point across.

The Best Lecturer i've ever heard. Wants to get to know all of his students. Very clear, very funny, very casual in his lectures. Great powerpoints and incredibly honest and humble. Class has tough materials but you dont even need to read if you consistently attend lecture and pay attention. Great person with a passion for English Literature.

Professor Perry kept things quite interesting in lectures, and also gave a very good analysis of all the texts we read. He spoke clearly and was easy to understand, and also very helpful if you ask him for help. I learned a lot in this class and also had some fun.

The lectures for Educ 201 were pretty straightforward and outlined the content for the week. Attendance was taken with questions during lecture, but they weren't very content heavy. Very accommodating with volunteering assignment issues and lecture slide were posted online.
Curtis Mason is super friendly and kind, willing to help whenever needed. I've taken two classes with him and I've enjoyed both.

Dr. Mason is the best! His lectures are casual and interesting, and he is very kind and accommodating. As an education major, I loved this class. There was lots of reading required, though if you're passionate about education, you'll enjoy it. I had an excellent experience at the Kid's Club for my volunteering. No exams, just papers.

Dr. Mason was a knowledgeable professor, but the course was often boring and tedious. The 20-hour volunteering requirement, alongside classwork and a job, added to the challenge. There was a lot of group work and presentations, which is typical for an education course. Overall, it was an easy class with no exams, just papers and projects.

Wouldn't recommend the class as a gen ed or if you're looking for an easy A as their is a community service portion to this class (20 hours) but overall wasn't too bad of a course. There are weekly 500 word reflection s based on the reading(s) of the week and the readings tend to be long and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Mason is a nice guy - though his course was not. The lectures were useless, the discussion sections got boring (two hours long), and a good amount of reading. As long as you turn in your homework on time you will be good.

reviews.comment: Super nice, decent amount of reading but not impossible by any means. Topics were interesting, lots of guest lectures too.

Dr. Mason's lectures are in-person at 9 AM, but he kindly records them all and posts them to Canvas so you don't actually have to wake up then. He's smart and thorough with the content. Discussion sections with TAs can get long and boring, but they're nothing that some caffeine can't handle. Homework is easy. You can get away without the readings.
na
Good course structure. Understandable material.

Teacher appears nice on the surface but does not grade fairly and does not explain assignments well. When giving feedback focuses on very minute details and uses tough language. Does not respond to emails. I would not take a class from her again.
Would not recommend. Does not explain assignments well and grades very harshly.

Meanest person I ever met. Looks very polite and nice but spits hurting words every now and then. Extremely rude and condescending. She is quite frankly the meanest teacher I've ever had, she tries to play nice but eventually, her true character comes out. Go to class, says Fridays are optional but if you do not show up she judges you. Phony, tells you one thing and does another. Kinda all over the place but she's relatively nice during the lectures and she's funny, too. Very fake though.

Professor Buckley is one of the smartest people I have ever met. She is personable and approachable. Don't let the comments on here scare you off of give you a bad impression of her. Easy if you do required work. Learned a lot and got an internship

I would not recommend, very condescending rather than helpful
Unfair exams, unprofessional teacher-student communication, lack of consistency

Dr. Buckley is one of the worst professors I've had at UIUC. I took this class because it's a 100 level sociology course, and it sounded interesting, so I thought "how hard could it be"? At first, you might think she is really nice but she is actually very condescending.  She has pretty high expectations for an undergrad level course in my opinion but it is doable. Good teacher all around, but class can be tough.
Rewrites to higher grade a plus

Rude and unprofessional. Cold call people in-class to answer her questions; if you can't, she publicly shame you.
Not bad overall.

Her class can be a little hard to follow sometime since she never repeat anything. Also can be disrespectful from time to time. But you could say it's a good practice for dealing with real-world managers.
She is a tough grader and has a boring class. She is just a slide-reader

Cynthia was a horrible experience for me. In class she expects you to teach yourself and is very rude if you don't understand something right away. This class was really easy to be honest. Everything was online and the exams and quizzes are all open book. You dont need to use the textbook and its not required to purchase. There is also extra credit too. Overall, getting an A in this class shouldnt be too hard. I got a B-, because I missed two discussions.

I took PSYC 216, child psych, online and it was literally so easy. All asynchronous, so you could do the lectures on your own time. All exams, quizzes, homework were open note.
