The worst. topic is so cool but poorly structured class and tests are way out of control.
Topic is extremely interesting but the professors are just awful for this class. If it's not mandatory, DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. The tests are extremely confusing. Good luck. You were warned.

reviews.comment: Horrible class. Such an interesting topic but taught so poorly, and there's like 5 different teachers so it's super off-putting. Class is beyond boring and the slides aren't even engaging, literally white background, black times new roman font, no clear bulletted levels, just words regurgitated on a page.

Attendance is not mandatory, but there is extra credit if you go. This class is split up and taught by 5 different professors, so no time to get used to anyone's teaching style.  Getting an A is impossible unless you read the book and memorize the slides. 10/10 would not recommend. Also if you get an A or A- it is a 4.0 a B+ or B- is 3.0... etc.

You have to attend her class to understand what's on her slides. She leaves quite a lot of questions in her slides without answers, so attend her class. Her class is the most boring among the others'. Rmb to refer to yr textbook!! Well she's a nice person. Talk to her and she'll help.

While she was nice to students, she could be a little difficult to follow.  The grade for her team-taught class (psych 216) was based solely off of 3 exams.  Would not recommend if you are a bad tester.
Very knowledgable teacher, test was easy.
She was a very knowledgeable teacher who loved what she did. She was clear in her lectures and more than helpful in the review sessions.

She was BORING AS HELL! She was the most awful teacher of the 9 we got as part of the team taught Psyc 216. I went to 1 of her lectures and skipped the next 3. Still got a perfect on the test, proving that her lectures were useless. If I ever see her as a the teacher for a psych course I DO NOT take it.
Rude and disrespectful to students.

She led the team teaching approach to 216... it was very hard to follow and much harder than I thought. All your grade goes into 3 tests, and with differing teaching styles it is difficult to succeed.

Chill prof, chill class. RHET 105 is a writing course so there are several major essays assigned throughout the course of the semester. As long as you don't wait until last minute, the workload is fairly reasonable. Mr. Topaum is very understanding about extensions and late submissions, and he also gives EC towards the end of the semester.
Awesome teacher, very easy grader
I had Topaum for RHET 105. Very knowledgeable about the content of the class, and gives good feedback on essays.

Cyanne is such a sweet guy, you can tell he really cares about his students. Extremely laid back and chill, pretty funny too. I wanna preface I took him for english 109, NOT 105 (105 was the only option). There is a bit of heavy reading but its pretty much all you do in the class, outside of a few essays. Easy grader. Live laugh Cyanne

Topaum was a very relaxed and respectable professor. He understood his students' other heavy coursework and was very lenient with his late work policy. He is easy to communicate with and come to for questions or concerns. He never treated my class rudely or with a bad attitude. Lovable nerdy guy.
She is such a sweet woman and wants her students to succeed; will always give an extension if asked.
Her notes are garbage. She thinks you should take notes as she speaks. She prefers using pictures instead of bullet pointed notes. If she made proper notes this class would be much better.

She's very funny and knows how to keep your attention in class. If you have a question about a paper grade (there are 5 papers)  go into her office hours to ask her about it. All of my papers were graded by our TA so when I asked for her input she actually raised my grade from what he put. Very helpful! :)

I really loved her as a professor.  She kept lecture interesting and really engaged with the students.  The tests were difficult but you just need to come prepared.  I bombed my midterm but aced my final because I learned what she expected.  I thought over all this was a great class and she was an awesome teacher who used relevant information.

Wachter is an amateur. Tries to make exams tricky. There's always an essay portion to answer, so beware if she doesn't deem your answer to be precise enough (although most questions are broad). Overall, just like an HDFS class. She doesn't teach like other 300-level professors. Needs work.

Teaches exactly like a high school teacher. Very annoying, irrelevant information was shared in class. If you don't need the class, DON'T TAKE IT! Isn't taught at the 300-level. She attempts to make the tests difficult by using tricky wording and essay questions (which are usually opinion, but she'll take points off anyway). Overall, not impressed.
Great class. Was really fun and laid back. Her quizzes can be tricky so showing up to class helps. Put effort into projects and you'll get an A
No Comments

Her tests are worded strangely.  The concepts are very easy but tests are not all that easy.  Solid professor, a lot of passion for the topic.  Maybe too much (anybody that has had her would agree).  C'mon, its leisure!

an easy class. iclicker points every lecture, easy online discussions, and with quality study time A is most def possible on exams. she seems nice and that she would help w w/e needed. very down to earth lady. teaches wat u need to know, tho sometimes words q'ns weirdly
Fun and engaging. Use clicker questions. Really nice and talks in a perky voice. Easy class. Easy exams.
She is comparable to a bad, low level, highschool teacher.  Her test questions are terribly worded and are obvious proof that she has no knowledge except what she remembers from reading the book.
Dr. Wachter is really nice and her class is interesting enough that attending the classes (recommended, since there are response papers in-class as well as clicker points) is not tedious. Good class!
Super easy class. Before the exam just read the definitions and chapter summaries in the book and should get an A. You need to come to class because she has pop quizzes and clicker points.
very borring class but pretty easy, must go for pop quizzes
Amazing teacher always willing to help!
really nice professor. the lectures are long and boring, but the material is easy.

She's a very gifted teacher with an amazing ear, but cancels university lessons for private students all the time.
Wonderful Teacher! She is really a gem of the midwest. You will work hard, but sooo rewarding!

One of the most amazing voice teachers in the country! Her students sing professionally all over the world, and have won major competitions. Her incredible musicianship and insistence on unmanipulated vocal production make her an invaluable resource for singers, young and old!

One of the greatest voice teachers in the country! Her professional experience as an opera star abroad and in the US is incredible (and helpful!), and her technique, singing with complete reliance on the breath, produces some of the finest young artists in the US today. One of my most important musical instructors of all time!
Made the material easy to understand
Professor Turner is awesome - the material definitely is not the easiest but she is so helpful and willing to go the extra mile to help anyone who asks. One of the best I've had so far :)
Awesome teacher that makes the unbearably boring topics discussed in class somewhat exciting. She has a lot of common sense and I really enjoyed her approach to teaching. Worth taking.
Great teacher who keeps you interested during class.  Her tests aren't difficult if you put in the time to study.
Very cool teacher who really wants her students to do well. Tests are pretty hard, but the rest of the work load isn't too bad. She's da bomb

She is very nice and friendly. The midterm is VERY hard (with D. being "None of the above...and then you have to fill in the blank in order to get credit!) She likes to say "Um" a lot. BUT, I would recommend taking Accy 302 with her.
Her class is more difficult than you'd think.  Her midterms are hard and she knows/loves it.  Very nice person though who likes her students.
Best accy teacher hands down. If you are taking Accy 302, take it with her. She makes the material as interesting as it can be. She really likes her students and makes her class fun.
A fairly difficult class, but Prof. Turner is very helpful and you always know what she is expecting from you.
she is the only great professor i've had ever! very clear, to the point, you learn a lot in her class.

Ms. Turner is the best accounting teacher here.  She is really a great teacher and the class is actually  interesting.  The only bad thing about her is that she makes you realize just how awful your other accounting teachers are.  And we are rated #1 in accounting?  Haha, yea right.  Our program is total garbage.

She is a "long run" teacher, as she puts it.  Goes beyond typical accounting mechanics to try to make you really understand the material.  You will work in the class and there is a curve.  Very fun teacher too.

very straightforward class, she was really laid back and we rarely went the whole class length. tests are hard but if you study for them and make sure you get all the other easy points, you can get a high B or A

Prof. Turner is so awesome! She has a very straight-forward teaching style and she is always willing to help when you have questions. Her final exam is much more difficult than her midterm so keep that in mind. Study a lot for the quizzes; they can be tricky! Always get a head-start on the cases so that you can ask questions and see the writing TA.

Good information for anyone who will be working with children, and Dr. Johnson is a very reasonable professor. She goes over everything at a very slow pace, and makes it so everyone can understand. The group project is very tedious for the first assignment, but the rest go a little quicker. Very easy class, hard to do bad if you show up and study.

There is a lot of extra credit opportunity. Lectures can get a little boring and you do have to read. There are in class activities that you get credit for. For the tests, memorize the slides! Focus on slides the most  then the reading guides, then the rest of the readings.
She is the sweetest, most sincere woman. You can tell that she loves teaching!It is people like her that make me more passionate about speech language pathology.
she is the sweetest woman ever.  she loves talking about her kids and she makes cute little jokes during lecture. extra credit on every exam!

WOW. I never thought there would be a class this easy in college. I attended class a maximum of 5 times, including the 3 exams. I never bought the textbook, simply look at the lecture notes online and the tests were the easiest i've ever taken. easiest a of my life. and the is the sweetest woman in the world! such a love
Extremely nice woman. Exams are easy as long as you look over the slides and do the reading. Assignments are very easy.

Very genuine, sincere professor. Brings a lot of enthusiasm to her classes. Tests are easy as long as you study the slides and read the chapters she picks out. She also did a good job of breaking up lecture slides with interesting video clips to prevent any monotony.

An amazing teacher, made me absolutely love my major. She teachers so well, the exams are easy with extra credit on each. For the James Scholar Project, she let those participating in it to work in groups. ;-) BIG help...overall, an A+ for the class and for Dr. Johnson!

She is awesome, like a mother to everyone.  Her lectures make you feel like it's your mom talking to you. She is super nice. Her lectures are clear and she uses a lot of cartoons (and explains the punchlines!)

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a really engaging lecturer, but I can't say that lectures are really mandatory. There's a weekly reading response to the readings assigned but you only need to complete at least five by the end of the semester. The midterm is 4 FRQs but it's really not bad at all. There is a final paper that is 7-9 pages, but that also wasn't too bad.

Dr Siglos has engaging lectures that you can't help but pay attention to. There are two textbooks but reading them isn't super necessary, it's just the final paper you need to cite them on. For the final, he was super helpful in office hours by telling me what I needed to fo and offering pointers. Midterm was written FRQ that wasn't too bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures overexplain the basics but leave you confused, and getting clear answers to questions is difficult. Be highly aware of grading: what is said in person doesn't always align with the final grades given on assignments. It is extremely tough. Save your sanity

Curtis is great. Class itself is not too difficult if you read the textbook & watch videos. She is super available for office hours if you ever need help. She'll have office hours from 6-8 for example but if someone joins at 7:55 she'll stay on until 9:00 or later. She makes class engaging. Test 1 is not bad, test 2 is kinda hard, final is medium.

Susan is the most enthusiastic teacher I've had and cares a lot for her students. I will say sometimes her lectures were not the most helpful and she would get off track. Also, anytime I would go to office hours for a short question I would end up being there for 40 minutes. Exams were pretty hard, but workload was not bad.
I loved her as a person, and she wants you to succeed. She just goes very off topic and she didn't really explain things well. I've never been so confused in a class.
She is far and away the best accounting professor.

Lots of assignments, so you are not graded on only a few things. Be sure to keep on top of deadlines and do work ahead of time, if possible. Some of the readings and guided reflections are especially practical when it comes to public accounting, so be sure to do them to get the most out of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment: It's homework intensive but as long as you keep track of all the assignments you'll be fine. Useful class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor. Speaks from experience. Expects you to do the reading which provides practical knowledge for public and corporate accountants.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Curtis is very passionate about the subject of accounting and genuinely cares about each of her students. She is very interactive during class and will help students who are falling behind. With that being said, the class can be very challenging at times, and it is easy to get behind. Make sure you comprehend each of the MANY case studies.
She is the best professor I meet in the university.

Professor Curtis is one of the most unique and caring professors I have ever encountered. Yes, ACCY 302 covers managerial accounting, but, if you listen closely, Curtis discusses far more than just accounting. She always makes you laugh and brings a smile your face, even during the Pandemic! She is always accessible and more than happy to meet.

Susan made accounting fun again! I never got any accy grades higher than B+, but she made it a fun class and I got an A-. She gives good tips, and genuinely cares about students. Highly recommend going to office hour and she will dedicate an entire hr helping you.

Having Susan for both accy201 and 302. She is a good lecturer and good at explaining definitions and math problems (tho she sometimes was off the track) But the only issue is that she forced you to do a random presentation during the class and you have to participate in order to get points from that.

Horrible. Make one mistake on the exams, you get the whole section wrong. The total online quizzes had a class average of 66%. She gives you only 15 minutes to answer 5 tricky questions, and you can't skip or go back. It's "you know it, or you don't." Your best bet is to attend the TA discussions and form your own studying group!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Curtis is disorganized. Forgets to show up to the first lecture of the semester because she is "preparing for class". Tricky pop quizzes and won't provide answers to homework questions. Quizzes should be given after we learn the material not before. Take somewhere else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Curtis gets a bad rep because she really doesn't make learning accounting fun. This class will destroy your gpa if you don't teach yourself the material and practice. I review a lot, used at the textbook a few times, but make sure you practice the PRACTICE EXAMS AND CLASS ACTIVITIES. The class isn't bad-- Susan's relentless off-tangent talking is

Knows her stuff but isn't always the best at showing it. Often goes off on tangents for up to twenty minutes, but is able to explain topics thoroughly when focused. Pre-quizzes were the hardest part of the class, so make sure you study beforehand. Class activities help a lot with studying so do them. Gives extra credit towards end of semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Susan is definitely not the best professor if you didn't take accounting in high school. The textbooks are expensive and useless, the lecture notebook is probably the best thing to get even though it is optional. Be prepared to work, go to office hours, and study every day if you didn't take accounting in high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She only teaches 20% of the time, but she does it really well. I did all the recommended practice problems, went to class, took notes, and did several practice exams before midterms and got an A+ in class. To do well in tests you have to understand accounting. This is where the practice problems and lectures helped me the most.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: feel really bad for this course

Prof Curtis is such a nice and lively person but I just cannot learn from her. The class has minimal structure, there are literally no resources to use on your own except the notes you take in class. Textbook doesn't help at all because it doesn't demonstrate any of the math problems, which is like all she tests on. Tests don't match lecture at all
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Susan is a hard person to hate. Her energy and theatrics borderline on obnoxious, but you kind of just admire that part of her. She's really passionate about accounting, and will do everything possible to get you to understand the material (including singing, dancing, and rapping).

Susan Curtis tells a lot of stories during lecture, which isn't  necessarily a bad thing, but it distracts from actually getting students to understand material. Online Mini-Tests are given, and you never know if you're getting questions wrong because you're completely wrong or because of calculator rounding errors. It doesn't show the right answer

Very much a weed-out class. The professor allocates time poorly, often going off on tangents more appropriate for office hours than during a lecture where direct class material should be covered. Discussion sessions are the real chance to learn, and I am noticing the holes in my foundation while taking 202. Concepts are simple, delivery is weak.

If you want help, go find TAs. The professor only go through stuff on PPT, which are already posted on Compass. Things are easy but really need practice. The class is really "optional" as long as you attend her "extra credit" sections to get the points. Her "extra credit" means mandatory attendance.
Dr. Curtis is an amiable personality, who engages with the students. I only wish that the way she graded was no so heavy on the midterms and that her lectures were more in sink with exam content.

Curtis's lectures are funny and entertaining but she spends SO much time talking about unnecessary things. Everything she covers is online. The exams are easy and the final is optional. I made the mistake of buying the textsbooks, the only one your will use is are the lecture note books, never even opened the other two.

Probably the easiest accy class in the department. I only went to class when she announced there are extra credit opportunity and studied all the materials myself at home. It was an easy A if you go through the past exam and make sure you know how to prepare all the financial statements.  And do go to lecture during the Halloween!

She is funny. Amazing lecturer only because her lecture is kind of a relax for me. Only thing I learnt from her is just debits on the left and credits on he right. Be really excite about her costumes during Halloween as well. The course changed a lot after I took it. She added pop quizzes so not sure about the class material right now.

Curtis does a good job teaching a challenging class. Fail one exam, you fail the class. The generic rubric is 50% for Exam 1 and 50% for Exam 2. Curtis posts slides online that contain what is taught in lecture. I would recommend discussion as the TA's are very helpful. She does provide a 40%, 40%, 20% (optional points) grading option too.

Only two midterms throughout the semester (Spring 2016) worth 200 points each. No other way to gain points. Fail one exam and you fail the entire course. Nice person, but horrible professor and has an even worse system of grading. Take at community college if you don't want to risk plumeting your GPA.

This class definitely is not easy. Considered the "weed out" class for students wanting to study Accounting. If you put in the work and go to her office hours though it is very possible to get an A. Work hard from the beginning if you want to do well.
the exams were nothing like the material taught in class or the homework.

Expect teaching yourself everything, going to office hours every week, pulling all nighters, getting failing test grades and then on top of all of that... going to class just to hear her yell at all her students about not working hard enough. Worst "professor" I've ever had.

Worst professor I have ever had. Despite how much you may study, don't expect to do well on the exams. Completely different from the homework and lecture. SO much busy work (online homework, mini tests) that were no beneficial. Lecture was incredibly unclear, text book (Curtis wrote it) is full of mistakes, which made it hard to study. Get a tutor.

Tests are designed for students to do poorly. It is entry-level accy content that Susan Curtis somehow turns into a challenging class. Lectures are never on topic and dont cover the material. Be ready to teach yourself everything, then study nonstop and still do poorly on the test. Unless you have taken accy classes prior, take at a junior college

She is just like a joke. She makes the test extremely hard. I have prepared all the material she gave us for the midterm2, but it terns out she test us on totally different topics and wants us to figure out 7 completely unfamiliar questions in 90 minutes.  I have no idea how she got the outstanding teaching reward last year.

Accounting is an awful thing, but Susan kinda sorta makes it less painful. The tests and homework are hard, but if you work at it you'll do ok. I hated her during the semester, but she's cool outside of class.
She's one of the worst teachers I've ever had.
Worst teacher I have ever had the disfortune of meeting.

Worked very hard in this class and ended up just barely passing the first midterm. Lectures are long and she doesn't teach for half of them, which makes me wonder why I even show up to class. Take everyone's advice and DO NOT TAKE Accy 201 here with Susan Curtis.
Her lecture is not helpful at all and exam is tough.

She's a rare species. Her lectures are mostly long, boring, and most of the time they are pointless. Her new teaching strategy with weekly quizzes did help students learn the material. Students were taught to go through the motions. Discussion sections will be where you learn in this class, so go to those.

SAVE YOUR MONEY AND DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS WITH CURTIS! She barely teaches and if you fail one of her paper exams, you automatically FAIL the entire course no matter how well you do on online quizzes and the final. She won't answer questions that are meant to guide you and will forbid TAs to do the same. I worked very hard and didn't do well.
Worst teacher (would not even regard her as a professor) I have ever seen in my life. There is no point to elaborate beyond that

She did not give answers to homework, quizzes or tests, but expect you to figure it out on your own. She got rid of the group projects, but in turn made the tests a lot harder as well as all free response. She helps you out in the end with 20 points extra credit out of 400 and then adds a curve. GO INTO TA OFFICE HOURS!

This is the worst class I have ever take with the worst professor in this university. Expect to self teach everything to yourself and receive a grade you are not satisfied with. I have no clue how our accounting program is ranked second place in U.S.  Susan Curtis is literally the biggest walking joke alive, and not really a funny one.

Scares you in the beginning, but then the content seems easy. If you attend class and do all the homework (including the extra problems she gives) you will do more than fine. I did not realize this until the second half of the semester after I almost failed. If you chase her down she will help immensely. She is nice but very tough.
worst professor ever ever

professor curtis is pretty nice over all. She might make you think the class is hard but you will end up with a good grade. She is not tricky at all compare to the accy 202 professor. accy 202 exams are not accy exams but more like IQ tests

She doesn't explain anything clearly. Her "lectures" are basically 1hr of her goofing off and less than 20 minuts of "learning" if you can call it that. She wears her student's failures as a badge of pride and won't stop telling you how you will fail. She really doesn't know how to teach at all. Please Do NOT take her if you have a choice.

Lectures are not clear but the examples are helpful, get the notes; if interested in ACCY, do the projects; tests are easy but still requires good understanding; tutors are helpful; she is willing to answer all of your questions but u may still get confused; little EC; not so terrible as others said; 2nd textbook is necessary, 1st is useless

Worst class I've taken at U of I in my three years here. Classes are NO help and she has a foul personality. Prepare to get kicked out of class a few times, get lectured on how poor of students you are, but never really learn much. I love accounting, but this class really turned me off.
easy exams at least

Having taken her class and was one of her TAs, I have to say: you'll be grateful for her later on. Her class is a college class, and a lot of people aren't used to it. You have to be 100% prepared for her class, that's not optional, you'll get more help when you know the right questions to ask, and that's only if you come prepared
If I could give zeroes, I would.  Absolutely the worst teacher ever.  Really does not care about her students or their learning accounting at all.
I think she was a very interesting professor who loves to teach.  Throughly enjoyed her lectures :)
She knows what she is talking about, but is very confusing when trying to teach. The exams we're just tricky and unfair.
Heard how bad she was, but didn't believe it until I took her class....

For those of you who said that she is interesting, you need to see a doctor.  I must say that she is one of the worst professors in this university.  I learned more about accounting in my high school accounting than this class.
The lecture is not efficient but the exam are very tricky. I mean exam is not hard but annoying! She wastes a lot of time in the lecture.
Absolutely worst professor ever. I had not taken two parts exam since I took this class. You have to buy all three books which will cost you like nearly 200 bucks.

Solid professor right here. She could be a little more professional and a little more technical and she could make the class a little harder, but all in all, she actually teaches you accounting. The same can't be said for Shapland. Curtis did a good job helping me understand how accounting worked in a very quick, succinct, and helpful manner.

Overall, this class was terrible. Not only does she expect you to put in 15-20 hours a week for this class, but she gets mad when you ask questions she doesn't see as valuable. Her projects are sprung on you at the last minutes. The TAs are awesome, though, and are willing to help. To do well, you need to do well on all of the quizzes and projects.

Well, tests can be difficult, she is very energetic at times to say the least. TA's are awesome and are willing to help which helped me get through the class. Projects are group but are also a pain. Ultimately, she expects you to know a lot before even starting the class. Class not really curved, so extra credit is probably a good idea

The material is not hard at all, but she does make the learning process slightly frustrating. Don't lose points on online quizzes and tests, and you should get an A without a problem. Oh yeah, do your extra credit.

Absolutely the worst professor I've ever had the displeasure to listen to. Sings, dances, and screams for most of the class period. Is not clear with her examples, and decides to assign homework from her "textbook" (which is never used) when she feels like it. Tests are unclear and hard, and she cut an entire hour from us during the final exam.
She keeps your attention and is really willing to help at office hours.  She is actually one of the better teachers at this school.

The material isn't that tough as long as you go to lecture. There aren't any iclickers but I went to class just to fill out the notes book. Projects are okay as long as you have a decent group, ask TAs for help. Tests are very tricky and hard in terms of wording. Large curve-you basically earn it through the amount of extra credit you do.
She is one of the liveliest and funniest professors I have had at UIUC. She has a magnetic personality and her teaching is par excellence. Highly recommend this class.

It is known as a pretty tough class.  The tests are more tricky than they are hard.  She tries to trick you with words and has none of the above options.  The projects take a good amount of time and effort.  If you put in the effort then you can get an A

people complain and say this is a difficult class, but its not. im not even an accy major and i found it simple. she offers plenty of ec, just read the book like she asks you to before class and youll ace the class.  tests are straight forward. if you put in the time, i promise you youll get an a. this isnt high school, its college.

Susan just is not in line with quality teaching. She would frequently show up late to class, and when she arrived, her lecture slides would not be prepared. If you are taking her class, be prepared for a lot of one sided politics as well. She is a person who values her position more than her students. Terrible teacher.
She is very dedicated to teaching, however, her expectations are very unclear most of the time. Furthermore, here tests remain full of errors and tricks.

Had her before the restructuring of the class. Despite how NUTS she is, you have to take into account the material she is teaching. After taking ACCY 202, you will see that Curtis did a great job with her notes and keeping the class awake (even in this very dry subject) Susan Curtis won't let you get away without work, but she'll make it fun.

Energetic and fun professor! However, the new and restructured version of ACCY201 made her class horrible. Each day she blasts through lecture notes, leaving no time to write or learn them. There were typos all over our group projects (that take 20 hrs), answer keys, exams, and quizzes. Nice lady, terrible class with too much unorganized material.

what a lot of students don't realize is that she knows what she's doing. what makes her different from other professors is that she really does care for her students. she wants to give everyone a good grade, unlike other professors that want to give out bad grades. plus, she always welcomes students to ask her questions. take advantage of that.

Honestly, as annoying as she was sometimes, I really liked her. She was corny, and genuine, and seemed to actually enjoy talking to us which is rare in a professor. Class isn't mandatory but I recommend going. She stressed that we needed the text book (as all teachers do) but I only used it twice so I wish I hadn't bought that. Notes book is enough
Wonderful class. Always interesting to go to. One of my favorite professors.

I can understand why people dislike her so much, but she honestly does know what she's doing. She's been teaching this course for over 11 years. She also helps really well if you go in and see her. The only thing that's hard are her exams and projects, but those are workable. Plus, she really does care for her students.
She is a bit crazy at times but I thought the class was pretty easy.  She has A TON of extra credit so it was not too difficult to get an A, you just have to deal with her craziness at times.
She's super fun and the course is super easy, well, except for the first mini-exam. You don't really have to listen during lecture tho. Do practice quizzes and read the notebook you'll be fine
She took the entire hour and a half lecture to explain what should take half an hour at most. Class wasn't very difficult, though, as long as you do all the homework and pay attention in class.

She tends to go off on tangents unrelated to class. Not much accounting is learned in the first half of the semester.  Its an easy A though, the way its graded.  Yes, 80% of the people fail the first test, including me,  but so many points and extra credit is offered it makes it a semi easy A

This is one of the most ridiculous classes I've ever taken. Prof. Curtis will try to make sure you get a low grade on her tests/quizzes. She EVEN has to REREAD her OWN questions to make sure she understood them. Not much accounting is learned. After taking this class for a requirement, I'm soooo glad I'm not an accounting major at least here..

Terrible teacher, unorganized, likes to play word games instead of focusing on accountancy on tests and quizzes, ineffective teaching method. I've been known for giving out good comments to professors easily, but this is definitely one of the worst teacher i've ever had.

The tests are ridiculous. It's not so much if you have learned the material, but rather if you can answer the questions the way she would. This makes studying difficult, but the class is made so that you can get C's on the tests and still end up with an A. It's still a very frustrating class.

She is a crazy teacher that makes sense about 50 percent of the time.  As long as you understand most of the notes book you will be fine.  The test questions are very hard and the answer maybe different each semester ergo there are always at least 2 right answers for each question.  She does make sure you learn something and grades nicely.

I have nothing positive to say, so I'll keep it brief.  She dresses up in costumes, openly swears, brings her children to class, and dances when she should be teaching.  How is our accounting program ranked #2 nationally???

Curtis might appear OTT at times but she is passionate about accounting. Despite seemingly endless assignments, HALF the points do come outside of tests! With 100+ points in EC, and highly repetitive questions on tests, the class could NOT be EASIER; just keep up with the readings and attend lecs for open book quizzes.I am a PS major but got an A+

Class is 1.5hrs and she talks about so much random stuff then hurries at the end of lecture to put in all the needed material. Expect to do bad in her exams; your not graded on whether you know the material, your grade is based on whether you know how to take an exam or not.

curtis is a horrible teacher...literally every class she is crazy and goes on and on about pointless stuff..rarely teachers useful material..if she actually would teach accounting we would get out of class 40 minutes earlier...i dont understand how UofI accounting is ranked so high with her as a teacher, oh ya be prepared for mistakes on tests/quiz
Susan is not that orthodox with her teachings. She someone that would talk about whatever she feel like in class but expect you to learn on your own. Good luck on the tests/exams ...

A very lazy professor. Copied half of last year's final from the book word for word.  Tries to make the class funny and fails. Instead she could actually teach and make class shorter. It's hard to actually pay attention when she does teach, because those moments are few and far between.  Don't point out flaws in her "system" because she will yell.

Damn...she loves this word.... Strong bias and disorganized on what she want students know...don't like her. I really don't think a good professor is the one who judge people differently.  she is kind of crazy everyday....and most of time, it is annoying. WORST PROFESSOR IN UIUC...

At times, I think she is completely crazy, useless, but then at other times I think she really cares and means well. She teaches you more about life lessons than about accounting itself. Don't expect to be enlightened about accounting after this class. The extra credit will get you through this class and she curves it a ton.

Ignore the previous negative comments. Curtis was an extremely nice and devoted professor. She gave tons of extra time to help all those who truly wanted to learn. I wish they were more teachers enthusiastic like her. I did not suggest a New Professor on my ICES form unanimously like AKPsi. I know they did this because I was a pledge in the spring.

First half of the semester was completely useless, you only begin accounting once half the semester has gone by, and then you you finish off with more nonsense.  Saying that the exams are subjective is the understatement of the year.  Sitting through an hour and a half lecture is painful, but you go for the extra credit.  Final was bizarre.

The first half of the class is completely useless, it is only when half the semester has gone by that you begin accounting, and then you finish off with more nonsense at the end.  Saying her exams are subjective is the understatement of the year.  Sitting an hour and a half in class is painful, but you go for the extra credit.  Final was bizarre.

At first she comes across as goofy and fun, doing splits in class and swearing like she's 10 again. But then it gets old and you realize she's the idiot you thought she was. I don't understand why she's still teaching when her tests are incoherent and full of mistakes. Too bad you have to stick with her if you enroll in business.

If you do all the required readings this class is easy.  Also, go to office hours and talk to Professor Curtis.  She is one of the nicest and funniest professors I've ever had.  Do the work, and the rest will fall into place.

Terrible class, it's unfortunate there is only one teacher for it, because she is an idiot. 90 minute long lectures that could easily be cut down to 30. Extremely disorganized, material covered in class barely pertains to the material on the exams. She is a horrible excuse for a teacher and her tests are full of mistakes due to her incompetence.
Presents the material in a convoluted manner. Deliberately puts multiple answers that could be correct on the tests, but only accepts her version. Overall a very poor teacher.
She's an absolutely horrible professor.  It should be fairly straight forward material but she wastes time singing and dancing instead of teaching.
awful, can't write a test. can't teach a lecture.  material is very easy but she purposefully makes it difficult.  lots of extra credit

The worst teacher I have had in my 4 years at U of I.  I took this class as a senior and was suprised by how awful she was.  She doesn't teach anything.  I was looking forward to learning basics of accounting but unfortunately I didnt.  Discussion lasted 10 mins at the most.  Lots of extra credit  If you are looking for a good laugh take this class

As many others have said, Her lectures are really disorganized and hard to follow. Most students only show up on the off chance that she decides to give extra credit that day. The textbook is barely used until the very end of the semester when you have to literally memorize a few passages. Be sure to memorize exam questions, they will show up again
Wasn't a good experience but I did end up learning something from the course. The way she tests us on material is definitely not fair but I ended up with an A-.

still don't know what the hell I learned this semester. worst teach-yourself style I've ever seen. Half of the final exam was on information either sparsely covered or simply not covered at all. I have a lot of previous accounting experience but was still only to scrape a B+ from this crazy woman. too bad shes the only professor for 201.

Even though she seems like a very nice lady, I don't like her teaching methods. Her lectures are filled with a lot of rhetoric and aren't very well structured. She wastes a lot of class time by making us talk amongst our neighbors to answer a question. The tests are horribly written, and not always related to lecture material. This class was a req.

While Susan Curtis genuinely enjoys teaching and can be quite entertaining, she lacks the ability to adequately structure a class. The classes consist of sitting there and completing frustrating worksheets that correspond to subjects she has explained only minimally. In addition, the test questions are ambiguous, and the point system is baffling.

i really liked prof curtis.  i struggled sometimes because she gave us too much time in class to work on these worksheets that we didn't know how to do, when she could have been teaching it to us.  however, whenever i asked her a question she was very helpful.  i also liked her laid back style.  her kids were nuts, though.

I don't think that Professor Curtis taught me anything this semester. The lectures have consisted of her giving us worksheets covering material that we have not learned yet. We never actually talk about the material that is on our weekly quiz. If you have had accounting in high school you will do fine, otherwise this is not a fun class.

she is good to students. just bear with her kid in the class. and she sometimes had tricky questions, but it is easy if u know the way she tricked u. unfortunately i am not able to figure it out. anyway. i just hope higher accy classes wont let me down like that.
Can't write a test.

I understand the material, read all the online and textbook readings, but still cannot manage to score much higher than average on her exams (which is usually a 70%). She phrases the questions in a way to screw you over and does not give you a chance to prove your knowledge. I feel this defeats the purpose of an exam.
does not teach in lecture. expects students to know everything and definitions that are given are poorly worded. dont know why she even has a lecture.
Terrible at making tests

After going through Prof. Curtis and Prof. Finnegan, I would have believed it if somebody said UIUC's Accounting Program was ranked third or second to the last. The Accy Department must be full of senseless people to let poor teaching like this go on for semesters.

Yes her exams are tricky and yes her lectures can be about pretty useless stuff. But overall, shes a good teacher. She grades fairly, she does what she needs to do. The book is not useless because its what she tests us on. Theres nothing really to complain. Joining this course esp without prior knowledge on Accy means ALOT of outside reading to do.

Susan Curtis is a great teacher, despite the fact that singing and dancing occur in lecture.  She is very nice and willing to help if you go to her.  The class seems disorganized at first, but by the end of the semester, everything seems to come together... You need to be open to her teaching style and you will learn a lot.

Absolutely atrocious. Lectures are just two hour rants about things that are never tested. Tests full of trick questions which undermine any actual learning. Bad communication with students, never gave out final exam grades. NOTE: Composes a supplementary text book and sells it, but it is NEVER used for any test or homework questions. Fraud??

She has no business being a teacher. Never says anything worth anything. If you try to learn the stuff, you will be screwed because all she talks about is how she tries to trick you (which is absolutely true). Memorize the problem sets and learn the ways she tries to trick you. Go to class for extra credit and don't miss discussions.

Curtis is awesome. She teaches a lot of important things for upper level classes in both accounting and finance. She also does a good job of giving good grades to kids who understand the subject. A lot of the comments on this page are unfounded and probably written by bitter insecure  children with entitlement issues. Probably from the N burbs

Tips for future students: (1) Don't buy the book w/ the readings. Never used once. (2) Come to lec for the E/C, Come to disc for the answers for online hw. (3) You WILL get an A on tests if you memorize the practice sets. (4) Yes, the remainder of the lectures in the semester will probably focus on life lessons re: "professionalism". Bring a pillow

By far my least favorite professor at U of I. The entire class is a theatrical spectacle. She actually majored in the arts in college, which explains the abundant singing and dancing acts she puts on in class. Go to class for extra credit. The only useful material is learned after the first midterm. She is disorganized and does not return emails.

reviews.comment: This class introduces basic SQL concepts and Entity Relationship Diagrams. There were 4 CBTF quizzes. There is also a weekly lab that you get to work on with a group (or individual). There is one final group project (can be done individually). Professor does iClicker points, which was nice since we didn't get practice materials for some quizzes.

The first half of the class had more homework (but it was mostly completion pts) and there were a few readings and quizzes throughout the semester. There was one individual project, two papers, and one final group project (could be done individually too). As long as you do the assignments on time, this class is super easy.

This course felt as if the curriculum was pieced together at the last minutes and like the professor had no expertise in the subject matter. Professor would often say comments that would be considered offensive outside of the course. Classroom environment was very poor and did not feel open to discuss topics related to the course.

He was a great guy, I like his personality, but he is a little dull. The class was very boring and I expected to do more discussing but he just talked at us for 1.5 hours. It was an easy class and you can get away with "mindfulness naps" for a good chunk of the semester. Great guy, super kind, but dull class. Easy A.
Sitting through class not being able to interact but only listen to his words is like the electric chair

The class is very unorganized. Expectations are unclear and criteria change. Instructor claims to be accepting of minorities and "mindful" of bias but has a conceited sense of self that makes him hostile and pretentious. He expressed heavy, partisan political views as if they were right or wrong. His lectures often contain inaccurate information.
He seems to be really caring and heartfelt. But its not real, hes definitely trying to pass on this persona hes made for himself and its not believable. Also, hes a bit pretentious and annoying.

He cares for his students' well-being and came up with creative ways to get us to get excited about participating in class. He is very inclusive of people from all different backgrounds and made class a safe place. The only thing I would say I didn't like is that there were changes in the syllabus, but we always had enough time to do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dynamic and exciting teacher. Engaging and a great sense of humor. Good at explaining things. Could be a picky grader. Some of the grading rubric for the assignments was posted at the last minute which was really inconvenient. Opinionated. Still, I enjoyed the class.
Just keep in mind that every week he assigns a group project

Completely mess in logic, the entire lecture is a breaking piece of glass

Lacks enthusiasm which makes it difficult to stay engaged in class. His discussion sets are also unnecessarily long. First professor's layout was more entertaining and useful.

Very unclear in lectures and didn't follow chronological order with content. Exam questions are actual trick questions and he rarely explains the content so you have to guess what he means. The slides ARE SO LONG!!!!!!! He crams a lot of content into a short period and you are expected to know everything he says in lecture for the exams.

Rivier is a good lecturer and his explanations of things are truly very interesting. However, I personally struggled to stay engaged since he talks so so so slowly. If that style is hard for you I suggest rewatching the recorded lectures x2 speed for a recap. His tests are manageable if you learn the lecture material inside and out. Fair class.

I had Dr. Rivier for MCB 252 and MCB 317. He's one of my favorite profs. His lectures can get boring at times, but he makes subtle jokes that kept me engaged. He's great at breaking down complicated topics into terms that makes it easy to understand. Exams are tough, but if you attend lecture and review the discussion materials they're doable.

I really enjoyed his lectures. He is clear and precise in explanation and covers very interesting content. However he doesn't take enough time or effort to write his exams. Duplicate questions and questions with multiple correct answer choices. I was two points from an A and he wouldn't correct an exam mistake. :/

Good Lecturer. He's great at telling the story of scientific discoveries. This makes the class very interesting. Though there are some dry moments. Doesn't require textbook. Exams are fair. Ppl say he talks slow, but I think it's fine. I recommend pre-writing notes before class using the posted slides.

Typical professor for this university, had a pretty good experience with him. Lectures are easy to understand and tests are straightforward if you attend the flipped lectures. reviews.comment: The lectures are dry despite the interesting material and the exams are unfairly tricky.

It really made the class come out with a negative view on it. I would avoid it because many people dropped grades because of his final. He isn't a bad teacher, I just hate how the final was.

reviews.comment: He makes things very clear and easy to understand. And I liked his jokes. Hes very smart and hes interesting and funny too. And i really appreciated the lecture videos being posted. He talks slowly so it was great to be able to watch his videos at twice the speed instead of going to class.

I attended all of his lectures but I liked how there was an option to not have to attend since all lectures are recorded. He taught the 2nd half of 252 and honestly was too slow for me but material & exam-wise definitely doable. Very nice to get to know during office hours as well.

317 was unbelievable easy until the final. Our class had the highest percentage of As in the class than previous years so he made the final really hard to bring it down. I didn't think he'd be like one of those professors but that was a low blow that ruined everyone. I got a 97% on the first two exams but then a 67% on the final

If you have the chance to take one of David's classes, I highly recommend doing so. I had him for both 252 and 317, and he is by far one of my favorite professors at UIUC. The material covered in 317 did have some dry parts, but his humor will help get you through it. You can tell he really cares about the success of his students and likes teaching

If you can find past exams, the first and second exams are just like them. I basically just studied the past exams and discussion worksheets and got near perfect scores for the first two exams. Not sure about the final yet, but I'm hoping it'll be just as easy. Currently have an A
easee peezee lemon squeezee____If you don't get A in this course___ Oh man___ Oh man...

Reviewing the day's lecture online each evening helped me retain the info better for exams. Also don't bother buying the book, you don't need it

Very fair class. Exam questions were very straightforward if you knew the material. I really liked having the lecture videos too. Could get a little bit dry but would add funny tidbits. Also liked how we focused on how we know what we know (ie experiments) instead of just making us memorize what we know.

He records all of the lectures and posts them online afterwards, which was nice. Exam questions were straightforward, but he'd give credit if he worded one poorly.

He briefly subbed for us in 252 and I thought he was great so I took him for 317... God did things change. His slides are sloppy and tests are tough. Discussion was a disaster and did not explain at all what we should know. Lon-capa questions were open note yet still impossible. would not take again. NEVER again.

He's a very below average professor. He is not at all that specific when he speaks about his material but he asks some of THE most specific questions on his exams. Basically, his exams are not really like what he expects us to know. Supposed to be easier than 250, but his lack of clarity makes it slightly more difficult. Would not take him again.

I really enjoyed the class with Dr. Rivier teaching it. The class content was straightforward, and I learned alot. I do not feel that his exams reflected what he wanted us to learn. Half of the exams are easy and straightforward, while the other half full of very long questions with several possible answers. Ambiguous as to which one he wanted

The history of genetics - how we discovered what we know about it - is not an easy thing to explain, yet he did it well, straight to the point and covered the big picture. I like how he gave us the big picture look at it all, and left us with a good understanding of most the techniques used in genetics.

Dr. Rivier's lectures are straight forward, but very dry. His powerpoints are not well organized. His exams are easy but poorly written. I do not recommend purchasing a book for this class. It's not used in lecture and the class is easy enough.

He droned on about topics you learn in high school and then gave tests that tested how well you memorized his slides. Although his questions were extremely easy, especially compared to Bellini or 250, they were poorly worded.
it is hard for history level 100 class. There are three papers, and quizzes is not easy. The grade is weird.

reviews.comment: Her asynchronous lectures during COVID were some of the best ones I have had. As a STEM major, I learned a lot in the class. The focus was more on teaching us how to analyze historical documents and how to think about events from different perspectives instead of memorization of specific dates and events.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great talker and story teller. Lectures can drag on a bit sometimes but all information given in lecture can be used to write your exam with. This class left me out of my element as a stem major and i still felt like i could thrive in her class. TAs grade all exams and papers so don't worry about hard grading. It's not hard (hist100)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Papers do not make sense. There's no topic, no question towards them, nothing. Everything in this class is confusing. I'm a senior and this is an 100 level course, can't even imagine how the freshman feel.
Im a good student, this professor makes me a c student. Really hard grade. Dont recommend taking her classes
Such a harsh professor who likes intimidating students on grading well written papers!
She is such a horrible professor, and grade essays very hard.

Look, she's a tough grader, but these aren't blowoff classes. She's sweet, witty, funny, leads great discussions, and really teaches you how to read primary sources and interpret history. And she cares about how her students do and makes herself available for outside help. Everyone in my class loved her. If you're SERIOUS about history, take her.
Fails good students for no good reasons.
Not fair in grading, gave me a D+ for no good reasons.
Exams were easily to fail

She's a really good teacher and makes the class enjoyable but she's one of the toughest graders I've ever had. I wrote a paper for this class that I had friends and family read and give feedback before I turned it in. They all told me they thought it was perfect and deserved an A. I got a C-
I am a good student with all my history classes, but prof. Rabin makes me a C student.
She is a horrible professor at U of I, cocky and thinks she always right about every thing.
The grades entirely depend on your ta.
Harsh and stern professor.
She is a very solid professor, but also arrogant in class.
Solid prof, but very arrogant.
The class was not organized.

She is a professor I will stay in touch with this is my second class with her and I love her classes.  She is an amazing professor and helps with anything you need help with. I am a poor writer an she knows that and understands my problems and lets me correct anything.  As long as I talk to her about my struggles before.  LOVE HER!

Wow, while this is a 200 level class, Prof. Rabin seriously makes it very challenge with very unique teaching styles. She made a very painful experience on topics. She is very sharp. The most difficult thing was there were no clews on what she talks. The lack of clarity made it kinda tough.

I'm an engineering major, so I thought taking this history class would be boring. But she made it SO interesting! I really enjoyed going to class. You can tell she is VERY passionate and loves what she does, and it shows through her lectures. She expects a lot from students, but genuinely cares. This is a class you should definitely take.

Professor Rabin is very helpful and an interesting scholar. Her classes are full of discussion and while reading the textbook is not necessary, reading the readings in her course packet IS. Exams in 256 are all written essays but you can be creative and explain your point of view. Great course, great professor.

Professor Rabin is very vibrant and approachable and I liked learning from her. We didn't crack open the textbook once, but there were TONS of outside readings. In class she favored letting us discuss instead of lecturing. This was good for the essays because they were geared towards these readings. However tests were a nightmare w/out lecture

Took Hist256 as a first semester freshman expecting to be overwhelmed by this class, but in fact it was fairly easy. Prof is very nice, straightforward, understanding, and actually is concerned about students progress. Reading the primary source documents is important, reading the textbook not as much. Not a tough class if you put some time into it

Everything was essay format so you had to have a good hold on the concepts to get though.  Class was biased towards her beliefs, if you go to lecture and write what she wants to hear in your essays you'll do fine.

The Professor is very nice and does her best to make the class interesting. She is very approachable and truly loves her subject. The problem is some of her TA's have a chip on their shoulder and as they are the ones grading the material it can make things a challenge. Great Professor, be careful about which TA you have.

She knows a ton about history and is willing to help any student. However her lectures are boring and there is way too much reading and writing assigned for such a basic history course. I recommend this class, but it isn't a blowoff.

Professor Rabin enjoys her work and is ready to help students in any way possible. She is very reasonable and down to earth. Her lectures and discussions can get boring if you aren't interested in history, but overall you do learn quite a bit. She is easy to understand. For the honors agreement, I had to write a 10 page paper. It was kinda a drag.
She is very knowlegable of content, not a great teacher
prof. Rabin is amazing! She expects a lot but she really cares about her students and is passionate about what she is teaching. She is very willing to help whenever you need it.

Great Prof! Dr. Rabin is fun, witty, and super smart; however, she expects a lot from her students. I have had her as a Prof. twice and I love her. Interesting and extremely helpful. If you love history, you'll love Dr. Rabin!
The class was way too hard for a 100 intro class. I'm a history major and I could not stand the class. My TA sucked, and the lectures are super boring.

Very good lecturer. Interesting at 9 a.m. She was animated, clear and I really learned a lot. You have to go to class to do well on IDs and section attendance is a must to do well on essays, but this class was a pretty easy A if you do the work
Very good.

Make sure you go to lecture or else you will have a hard time with IDs. Exams are pretty straight forward and can be very easy as long as you go to lecture and take notes. She is a very animated lecturer and very nice.
She was very helpful and an interesting lecturer. You have to go to class to do well, but tests and papers were easy, and if you put in the effort, it's a guaranteed A.
Not a good lecturer
If not in appearance, youthful in word and deed.  Understands the amount of reading history students must tolerate, and is a human being about the situation

I enjoyed her lectures for the most part.  She does say a lot in each lecture, so be sure to take good notes.  She is approachable and friendly.  Her TAs, however, especially the one I was unfortunate enough to have, were awful.  I don't know if she has a say in who her TAs are, but these two this time were terrible!
She condenses alot of material into the lectures, get a voice recorder if you can.  She's very helpful before exams.  But the TA's are AWFUL!!!
as a history major, i was offended by this class. however, she was not nearly bad as the TAs she chose.
Lots of memorizing, but most kids don't like the course... I didn't mind it, email her- she will be helpful.  GET A GOOD TA.
Prof. Morris is great for RHET105! He is very understanding about deadlines.
Genuinely get this guy for rhet 105. He actually has a purpose for every assignment he gives and makes this class actually enjoyable for what it is. Wouldn't take it with any other prof.

Dave is a great professor. He gives really good feedback on your essays and as long as you do the work and participate in class you will get an A. The texts he choose were very interesting and I learned a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Professor Morris for ENGL200. He assigns interesting readings, which are enhanced by his lectures, and he provides very useful feedback as well. I was always excited to come to class. He also is not a tough grader, so if you put in the effort, you will absolutely pass with an A.

one of my fav profs ive ever had. the type of person that you could see yourself sm0k1ng a cig w while talking about poems and papers and such...
he's the type of person who could have been a spy in his lifetime, and you'd never know. 
10/10 great prof, knows his stuff, best feedback, writing improved exponentially. am gna miss him he was the best

Dave is the kind of great teacher you'd only expect to see in movies—humorous, easy to get along with, very understanding about project deadlines and absences, and always insightful to talk to. He actually made me enjoy a class I was forced to take.
One of the best teachers I'd ever had. He's a very generous grader, and his feedback is very helpful. If you have the opportunity to take him, do it; you won't regret it. 10/10
RHET105 was as boring as you would expect, but Dave made sure we didn't have to do more than we needed to. He also let us out early almost every class. If you try in this class, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dave takes the time to make sure his students are engaged, gives extremely clear instructions on what hes asking for on assignments, essays can easily be done, very flexible with extensions and honestly a great class to boost gpa!
Honestly he's just amazing like, he's super chill but just make sure your participating and doing your work
Amazing teacher, even better person. Gives interesting lectures and you should definately consider taking this class.

Professor Morris's Intro to Film class was by far one of the best classes I've ever taken. He was understanding of the pandemic and extended deadlines on papers if you asked. If you like film it is an easy class and full of interesting discussions and lectures.

He is an amazing professor. RHET 105 being a gen ed, he is fully aware of that and does not make you do more than you need to. He is very lenient with deadlines and gives amazing feedback on all your papers to make sure you get a good grade. I would 100% take him again if I needed.
The best

If you have the chance to take one of his classes do it! His lectures are interesting and discussions are more of a casual conversation. He is very understanding when it comes to papers and if you just email him ahead of time you can get an extension on anything without an elaborate excuse. If debating between instructors CHOOSE HIM!!!

My favorite Instructor, I have had so far. His lectures are engaging and he clearly explains the topics you need to know. I had four papers for this class but he gives excellent feedback and we were able to revise our first major paper. He is really nice, funny and genuinely cares about his students. I would highly recommend taking his class.

My favorite professor in my first year. He is a tough grader, but if you keep working and try to rewrite if you need to, you can still get an A. It is a tough process, but I found it worthwhile eventually. He is very knowledgable and alway be patient with students. He inspires me a lot.

Great, fun professor. He does not grade that easily, but he makes sure you get the grade you deserve from the class. 3 long papers for the whole semester and they basically determine your grade. I learned a lot from him. He also allows revising and he is very lenient on deadlines. Just make sure to stop by at his office hours with your draft.
Great professor. He is patient and understanding. The grading was not easy for me in the beginning, but he allows revising and regrades. I learned a lot.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Really thorough with everything, enjoys what he teaches, makes an effort to get to know his students. The best part, he is very lenient about deadlines and rewrites. Basically a cool professor who you can learn a lot from.
Chillest Rhet Instructor Ever. Very Lenient on deadlines, and doesn't grade very harshly.

By far the best teacher i've had. He is very understanding and if you can't turn a paper in on time, as long as you approach him ahead of time he'll give you an extension. Get this professor by any means necessary.

Awesome guy. great class. very knowledgeable and insightful man. i can say i walked out of that class with something new learned or causing me to question something and it is because of his teaching. honestly, great class and teacher

Awesome teacher, very understanding. Allows re-writes for higher grades. Explains everything thoroughly. Makes discussions interesting. Only a few major papers, the rest are small. Go to class - get an A.

Dave is one of the best instructors I've had. He is INCREDIBLY understanding. With all assignments, he completely understands if you need a little more time and will not penalized you. He also allows rewrites and takes only the higher grade. He's kinda funny and knows what he's talking about, too. Definitely a good way to get an advanced comp!

By far the best teacher I've ever had.  Dave is funny, approachable, and just a great teacher.  He made the class really interesting and he isn't smug at all like some other professors.  Bottom line: RHET 105 is required, so try to get Dave as your instructor and you will be very happy you did

This man is a rock god - oh yeah, and an instructor as well.  He shreds on the guitar and on my papers.  If you mention The Simpsons or any seminal prog rock band around Dave, then be prepared to receive the "schooling" of your life.  Some say he's today's Tom Sawyer but I say he's my prof.

Avoid this class if you don't need it. The material was interesting, but the class required a huge amount of studying and memorization. At first, the quiz expectations were somewhat unclear, though they became easier to understand over time. The course itself was not too difficult, but it was very time-consuming and involved a heavy workload.
