reviews.comment: Her teaching just feels like a massive show-off moment for her to pour in all the knowledge she knows. Sure she knows a lot about the subject, but at the same time there is no much material she covers that it is absolutely impossible for one to fully study them before an exam. There's almost 20 lectures plus additional readings per test! Seriously?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are incredibly difficult with lots of memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: As much flack as Ruggles gets for having memorization heavy tests, that's kind of the point of art history. If you are willing to put in the work, this class is extremely interesting and eye-opening. She brings in guest speakers, organizes field trips, and genuinely wants to support her students. Go in with an open mind and can-do attitude.

Don't take this class!!! So much reading. The class is purely memorization-based. you are expected to remember 30+ sites for each test including their name, date location, dynasty, and three significant facts from content spanning 3 or 4 weeks (and that's on top of remembering readings, slides, and vocab). Unrealistic expectations of students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures consist of pre-recorded PowerPoints, E-reader, and a book. Heavy readings every week in order to understand and identify buildings. 3 tests (15% each), 5 homework questions (25% total), and the final (30%). Do not take the class if you don't enjoy memorizing facts and or a new language.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not recommended

Prof Ruggles has a great understanding of Islam, & the historical & cultural contexts behind every site we study. She makes it easy to understand big ideas. This class requires a lot of note-taking. Quizzes were difficult but they get easier once you get the hang of it. The activities we did & the guest speakers we had were pretty interesting.

This is a memorization class. Lectures were fun and learned a lot about history, architecture, gardens, religion and some of another language. This was an amazing class with a great prof. She knows her stuff and more. Knowledgeable and cares for your success and learning. E-Text VERY helpful. TAKE NOTES ON I-CLICKER QUESTIONS! GO TO REVIEW!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved her. I knew nothing about gardens or architecture at all before stepping into the class, and I loved it.

Prof. Ruggles is awesome. She's not strict or hard as much as she's demanding and has high expectations. She loves her subject, and explains everything perfectly. She's got lots of enthusiasm. The papers and tests are graded pretty tough since she wants everyone to think deeply about architecture. Overall great class, highly recommended.
Excellent Professor!  She really knows what she teaches and has been to each site at least twice!  So interesting - definitely a must take course with her

She's very helpful to everyone, a dear adviser friend to international students. She's hard in accessing students' works but supports all the best she can't to improve them. She's an enthusiastic persona, always cheerful and be there for students. She's the best!

Prof Ruggles is a strict but very talented professor. I think she grades a little tough for the class level but she wants to challenge her students to do their best & really learn from her class. I found her lectures very interesting & it's obvious that she knows a lot & that she's passionate about what she studies. She can be a little humorous too

Typically comes in late to class and his lectures leaves everyone confused because he tends to overcomplicate things. There is barely any guideline/instructions on assignments and this class doesn't teach me much.
No syllabus. No Canvas site. Too much of himself and came in (late 15-30 mins or if does he - he did not communicate the arrangement for the snow day at all) to talk about his life.

A lot of people were confused in his class because the way he explains things can be overly complicated at times. There was an instance where he sent out details to an assignment the day before it was due, which caused a lot of confusion. He's really nice and I can tell he tries to offer help, but I find his explanations hard to follow.

Had him for ARTD 333 and ARTD 218, he was not great for either of them. Especially when trying to teach code he didn't give like any foundational knowledge for it and everyone was always so lost. He is always late to class, a few times like 30 min + late. He is super nice but just does not explain things very well or teach either class efficiently.

If you want to actually learn something, do not take this professor's classes. Half of the semester we were on zoom because he was in another country, and when we did meet in-person, he was late to every single class. We had four assignments on canvas that were all posted and due on the last week of classes, and he had no syllabus. Waste of time.
He's a really nice guy who can be a little hard to understand at times but you can tell he cares about his students doing well.

Won't give you pill, but will treat you.

No other way to say it, Genner is the absolute GOAT. Anyone saying otherwise is simply not good at math. Calc III is easy and being able to learn it from THE Deniz Genlik would be anyone's honor, especially mine.

If you have the chance to learn from Genner, I urge you to take it.
Good lecturer and responds to complaints and criticism well. He also gives past exams which help a lot for the tests

Professor Genlik does an excellent job of connecting complex concepts in multivariable calculus to real-world applications. In addition, he can explain the same topic in multiple different ways, and he provides lots of resources for learning outside of lectures. He also pays attention to the needs, questions, and ideas of students.

Deniz really cared about MATH 241, as his lectures were engaging as long as you were willing to put the effort to engage with him.

He is open to feedback, as he adjusted his lectures after getting feedback that they were too fast/not 100% relevant to 241.

He is a new prof, but I can tell he strives to become better each day. Would recommend!

Long personal stories, 5-10 min late every class, and wasting time drawing “pretty” figures on his iPad and had many technical difficulties. Complained about students gossiping about him and negative ratings on ratemyprof. Brushed over important concepts as the semester progressed, skipped some lessons, imo choose more experienced profs (dunfield).

Professor Genlik is a funny lecturer, but can be hard to understand due to his accent and technical vocabulary. Lectures felt fast-paced, and I wish they were recorded, especially for the 8 am section. Homework is difficult and time-consuming, but exams closely match the practice tests. Discussion sections were not very useful, but mandatory.
He's a great guy and definitely improved at teaching as the semester went on. MATH 241 is naturally pretty difficult, but he communicated the concepts very effectively.
First semester teaching in Fall '25. Improved a ton after the first midterm—notes became super clear and matched well with Dunfield's practice exams. Class attendance dropped from 250+ to

He is a new professor, and his lectures improved tons as the semester went on. He clearly cares about getting better. He spent a lot of time getting feedback and figuring out how he wants to teach in the future. Despite having like 600 students, he takes the time to meet students (sat with 2 of us at the table and asked us for more feedback).
Passionate and caring professor. Lots of practice tests available before midterms to prepare you.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Great professor! Always there during office hours and will explain the content very clearly given specific questions (highly recommend to do practice exams/homeworks first, compile them, then bring them to him). Also a very funny guy and will remember you if you engage with him. 

Literally my motivation to attend and grind calc!!!

Funny guy. teaches reasonably well. one downside of this class is that he draws everything by hand taking a lot of time in the process. he also colors in shapes by hand, taking a minute or two in the process.

Genlik spends so much time proving things in a half-baked way rather than actually teaching us the skills to succeed on exam questions. These tangents won't help you on the homework, the discussion worksheets, or the exams. The class is basically grinding past exams hoping the real exam is similar and that he doesn't throw an undeserved curve ball.

Very nice and funny professor. Sometimes told stories if he thought we were bored from proofs. Lots of study material was given for exams so tests weren't bad. You can tell he cares about his students. Highly recommend.

When I had him he was new so he was still finding his voice. So I will say there were some crazy moments...Like the range on the first exam 1%-70%. I think a lot of the problems people had were from the class itself, not the teacher. He was the only calc teacher that I noticed would come to office hours before the exams. Very nice guy

Not too difficult of a class, do questions in back of workbook and you can easily get an A. Genlik is a really nice guy and will help you, was over all really kind whenever in lecture, make sure to attend lecture as thats the only place to get notes. First exam is a hard but if you keep on working and studying you can easily get an A.

Genlik is a caring instructor and made sure to answer any questions students had for him. The course workbook was helpful and a great tool for studying. Exams should be fine if you do all the homework and discussion worksheets with a goal of understanding the content instead of simply completing. The final grade replacement policy saved me.

Would definitely recommend. Nice person and genuinely care of what's happening, ready to help with any questions. If you do all the hw yourself, come to lectures and use material provided you will do just fine.

Dr. Genlik made the content very clear and took feedback from students very well. Specs: Workbook that has the problems you solve in class (you can get by without it but I don't recommend it at all), two large homework assignments are given a week covering content, exams are easy if you study the last discussion worksheet well and pay attention.

Unclear on some course content, asked a question once about something that made sense and her response was "oh i know i'm wrong but statistics is hard", tough grading on homeworks and labs (taking off points for things not in the rubrics), exams and practice exams sometimes did not line up
Do not take this professor for STAT207, she makes this class harder than most CS classes. Take the other professor and save yourself a lot of trouble.
The grading of homework and exams is a little weird, and I got used to that for a month. It is not that bad, actually.

It's nothing like STAT107 where you know in the labs if you're things right, there is no checkpoints in the labs for this course so you could get an answer that works, but if it doesn't align with exactly what the TA's want, you lose points and you can't gain points back. Questions on exams are worded so odd

Very unorganized class

I think these reviews make Julie out to be the devil. Julie is an incredibly kind person, who gives lots of extra credit and assignment drops. She is also a very capable lecturer. The flaws of 207 are that the homework and test questions are vague, and graded harshly. However, it is very easy to get an A in this course if you put in some effort.

While Julie was a kind professor and gave lots of extra credit and buffer points for things like homework and labs, the overall content was very disorganized and confusing in lectures. The tests were very confusing and often very subjective when it came to the answers. If you complete your work and get all extra credit points, you should be ok.

Terrible experience taking the class. The questions on the exams or so confusing to understand, and I feel like she doesn't exactly acknowledge how confusing and terribly written they are. I should never have the guess what a question is asking. If there is any other professor, take it with them. If not, good luck soldier.

Genuinely so much to say. She never has clear grading criteria, and when asked about it in lecture just says that she doesn't know. How do you not know, this is literally your class. She vibe grades based on how she's feeling that day.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Points in exam are deducted for nothing. Awful wording, making a lot of confusion both in homework and exams, but she refuses to answer any questions during the exam.
Great teaching, wonderful lectures, and very easy to understand
She is a wonderful professor, has a love for the game. Diptani is also a top-tier prospect hes one of the best TAs I have ever had.
She is an awesome professor and loves teaching statistics. Yes her homework may be demanding, but she and her tas are always very helpful. The class itself is easy money if you study the materal

Everyone is hating on her, but low-key, she is not bad. The class itself is boring and lame, but she is a fine professor; she is understanding and kind. So, I don't understand the hate watching fr. There are so many resources for this class; I don't get the hate.
The worst prof
Very disappointed that the University has not fired her, she seems nice and all but truly abhorrent at her job, genuinely would not study under her if she paid me to do it.

She is the professor I have most vehemently hated in my educational career. Every online resource claims questions should be differently answered than her solutions. She admits to writing questions badly. Asked her about a question on the practice exam and her response was I don't know the answer, it's badly written hopefully I don't do it again.

She is the worst professor of all time. Doesn't teach, leaves half the material for you to learn, and she isn't flexible with time changes. I would never recommend taking her class, the practice test answer keys aren't always the best, and other sources say it's completely wrong. Test formatting is horrible, STAT 107 is so much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Oh my god does she yap. Her lectures are not helpful, she doesn't explain anything really and if she does she just breezes over it. I don't know how these lectures are an hour and 20min because I walk out every day knowing less than before.

Awfully structured class. The most vague, convoluted questions then she gets upset when the responses vary. Frustrating to be around tbh. Having the same hw split up into gradescope and jupyter notebook (when they could be easily combined) is extremely frustrating.

I know you take stat207 because you have taken stat107 and you really like stat107. Because you like stat107 and you think you gonna like data science and success. NO This prof gonna flip you thoughts, the lecture is useless and not understandable. You would not know what the question is asking on hw/quiz/exam/lab. Me no like ds anymore

Julie is an extremely nice person, very caring/friendly. Her lectures are extremely boring, making her not the best lecturer, but as a complete professor she is pretty good. Lots of extra credit, lots of review material, willing to give extensions if necessary, puts effort into her class, is accessible outside of class, and cares for her students.

If you come to this class with some statistic background, e.g. AP stat, you will be fine and be amazed by how ds is used for analysis in statistics. Prof. Deeke is great professor in lecture, caring for her students. Grading is reasonable and even you mess up something in homework it's not a big deal under drops and extra credits.
This class was well organized and lecture note heavy, but if you complete homework and attend lectures it should be a solid A

This is not a weed out class by any means, but after taking this class, you will know whether you want to continue data science. Lecture info is useless when doing hw and labs, & tests are basically an essay competition. However, there is a lot of leeway with your grade and she is sweet & personable. As a person, I enjoy her. As a prof, SO BORING
Disorganized, no relevance between homework/labs and exam

Lecture materials and labs are very surface-level with no reasoning for the steps taken. Questions on exams are vague and misleading, but she refuses to answer questions during the exam. She has also admitted to not knowing the answers to her own problems. Outwardly kind and helpful, but not good at her job.
terrible professor

She's not the worst professor, but she is not good. There are a lot of hit or misses with people liking her. She is very very nit-picky with HW and lab grading, the TAs in lab are so useless (they just sit there), but she does EC with i-clicker. I wish I didn't drop last semester cause I could have taken with Ellison. Deeke made me like DS less.
BAD BAD BAD BAD BAD INSTRUCTOR! NEVER GONNA TAKE HER AGAIN!

Lectures are vague and seem filled with boring concepts not closely tied to the material. She provides past exams, but explanations are unclear. Some questions need additional knowledge of politics. I've taken 5 Stat 4xx courses, but only 207 feels like a liberal arts course, with many concepts to memorize.
Grading was very very hard. The lecture has little correlation with exams.

Does not create proper notes when teaching. For example will create wordy explanations or interpretations of problems instead of teaching students how to create their own, and does not answer questions if asked on discussion boards. Shame that she is the only STAT207 professor.

As mentioned by a litany of other comments here, Professor Deeke is an outwardly kind person, but her lectures are scatterbrained, our in-class "notes" don't correlate with almost anything seen on the test, and she grades homework with a hypercritical eye.
She is nice but awful at teaching. Her grading criteria are also unclear and subjective. Me and my friend could have the same answer but graded differently.

This professor will be like: Interpret the following situation, but what she won't tell you is exactly in what fashion to do it, filing a complaint soon with the statistics department, disregarding my education on another level!

Professor Deeke is a very nice woman, but she is not a great instructor. Her grading criteria is very unclear and very subjective. Campuswire and office hours aren't super helpful either, because she isn't great at explaining answers or what she's looking for. I got the best help from my lab section TA and CA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: this professor is so incompetent, she will demand so much to only have your grade depend on her interpretation, so sad 😞

Lectures are rushed, and does not correlate well with exam. Some exam point deductions are not even legit reasons. 4pts off for not mentioning one term on a question. Also, how am I supposed to know you are supposed to include it? Also, she gives us a blank notes sheet but does not want to post the filled out version? Weird

Prob one of the worst professors on this campus ngl. She skips through like every other section in each module with notes and doesn't resurface it unless you speak up about it. I took this class KNOWING how bad the prof was. I was told since my freshman year that stat 207 would be mid, and yeah that totally bit me in the butt now. Labs are okay.

Deeke is a really nice professor, but the course is structured pretty poorly. The labs and lectures are disjointed and the best way to study is to use past exams. It's not a hard course, but there was a lot of confusion in instructions. Grading is generous, though, so it's a very doable class- just not enjoyable. Do not take if not passionate.

(STAT 420) Unlike some other reviews, I actually really enjoy Prof. Deeke's lectures. I find them really easy to follow, my only critique is coding could be a little more in depth. My biggest criticism is that she is a VERY picky grader. I would get C's on tests I was sure I aced. Overall I just wish she was more clear on her grading expectations.

Most of the class is coding-heavy but the midterms & final are comprehensive. Tests are nothing like the review materials provided. Very strict grader and is nit picky when it comes to the homework. Made the final project along with a two-part homework due a week before the final exam. Some of the TAs/CAs are no help at all. Only take if required.

Terrible exams, explanations, TAs/CAs (in my experience, lectures, and homework. Give us a project and two homework assignments due on the same day, and less than a week before the final. Not good at answering questions and there is absolutely no late work tolerated for some reason.
Terrible lecture and wording is so hard to understand, the content is not design for us to understand at all.

This professor is terrible. She will describe the simplest things(we know how to subset columns in Python, why are you explaining that?) while completely ignoring explaining statistical concepts (always saying "I don't have the best answer to that question") and on top of that, she always admits that her questions on exams are worded terribly.

Deeke is an awful professor. If you did not take AP Stats in high school good luck. Most of her work is done using python (homework and labs) but half of her tests are on paper. She also does not have a test rubric. My friends would write down the same answers as me for the test and one of us would be right and the other would be wrong. Slow grader

She's not a very good lecturer (goes too fast) and isn't very helpful when students have questions. Expects students to be able to perform well on vague on-paper exams when almost all of the graded work is python jupyter notebooks. Overall, the workload is manageable but she still piled on a final project and two-part final exam in the end.

Lectures were long and often uninformative. All graded work was on Python but she suddenly introduced written exams which were vague and extremely difficult. Questions on homeworks, labs, and exams were worded poorly.

The "Life Happens" policy is very fair and makes it very easy to get a good grade in the class if you do all the work. The class starts off very easy and then eventually becomes pretty difficult.

Lectures can be long and a little bit boring, but if you pay attention you'll be fine.

She did not give a clear grading criteria at the beginning of the semester, than suddenly put everyone's grades in halfway through the semester and everyone had below a B. Not understanding, thinks everyone is using AI. Would never take her class again.
I don't know how she made it past her interviews. This lady teaching a communications class is antithetical to her existence. Period. Stay Clear. You've been warned. Absolutely Awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although she seemed easy initially, she is a tough grader, truly takes attendance seriously, and gives THE MOST VAGUE directions. This is an business technical writing class taken in the fall and her main focus WAS NOT to prepare us for internships or jobs.

Debora is very fair and reasonable. She won't make you do a lot of busywork like some 250 TAs do. That being said, when she assigns homework, she expects you to do your best. The class isn't hard, but don't expect to get an A without working for it.

She is super chill, but then when it comes to the grading, OMGGGGGGG she is so harsh. Some trivial spelling mistakes can give me an A-. Don't expect to learn a lot from her. However, if you want a easy class and a okay grade, her class is a fit.

TA for ENGL 255. She was terrible at keeping discussion sections interesting. She would ask a question and then basically just shrug off the silence. You know a TA doesn't care about their students if they say "this is your discussion, not mine" when no one answers her questions in class.

My first iMBA course. Fantastic professor who clearly loves teaching and often begins with a virtual campus tour. Lectures were engaging, with interviews in the MOOCs and interactive live sessions. Standout lessons on product differentiation and bidding wars. Highly experienced and enjoyable lessons. I didn't want to miss a single live class.

He is not up to par of an MBA program. There are 5 star ratings within this forum, but they seem "sus" because all of them have been written on May 8th (not trustworth). The lecture doesn't provide important info. The assignments are based on principles he made up and not used world-wide business. You're forced to use his made up concept.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture heavy, but they make sense if you go deep into understanding.
His class is a pretty easy A. It's easier than most undergrad classes.
Interesting class and interesting teaching method
He is professional and has a good teaching style especially for class being online
He's really not that bad, you just have to get to understand him and his frameworks. He is definitely a subject matter expert.
I enjoyed his class. People just don't like to do work or think but compared to some underqualified professors I have had, his lectures are refreshing.
Unfortunately, you can't avoid this guy. His study guide makes no sense. The exam is way off from what you have practiced in homework. Awful. Additionally, his lectures are pointless.
Most boring self centered professor ever. Class drags by and he always goes over time. Teaches primarily off of opinions and frameworks he made up.
He is insufferable, rambles on and on about topics of a subject that would be very interesting, if he wasn't the one teaching it. Not sure why UIUC has him teaching, despite such a bad reputation.
super hard class and no way to get good grades from that class. I'm not too fond of his teaching way and I would never recommended it.
bad teacher and bad teaching but I don't think there is another teacher teaching this class. They sign this class name to another teach so students can sign up. He is too bad.

He made Strategic Management a very hard course when it could've been an interesting one. His grading style was so random and unfair to the point where he had to give us a grade curve every time. There were no accommodations for people who had internet or technology issues even though it is an online masters program.
Just finished the course. Never seen such a bad educator. Disgrace of a prof for UIUC
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Live lectures are useless, self-serving, and disjointed. Lectures always go over time, which is difficult for working professionals. More details are passed out in office hours rather than in classes. VERY subjective grader. More time is spent trying to write what the TA will give credit for than actually learning. Very disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I wish I could attach a picture so you could see how I scored a 100 % on every assignment except the final exam. The mean on the final exam was 70 % and the instructor sent an email acknowledging the exam was designed for students to score low.  Do not take this professor if you value your GPA.  He didn’t cover materials on the final exam.

Deepak Somaya teaches his own theories that he made up in his mind. Ex. VARS Framework. Nobody in the world knows what that is. He teaches students to forget about the SWOT analysis and take his unknown VARS framework to analyze. This guy is teaching unknown theories. Beware! Never had a teacher like this guy before. LMFAO
Live lectures are point-less. Graders grade papers as if it were an English class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Deepak Somaya is a complete Fraud.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hey, take my advice, don't take any of his classes. Super passionate, also super rude. He is not the genius he thinks he is, but he is knowledgeable. Very self centered and goes the extra mile to give students as much work as possible. Insufferable amount of attitude, Passion Of Joan Of Arc is not good by the way.

You shouldn't take this class. Derek has good intentions, but he doesn't understand that nobody cares about animation as much as he does. The final week includes both an absurdly hard final exam and ultra-time consuming final project which is ridiculous for an elective about animation. Also he will use up every single minute of the 3 hour lecture.
Boring lectures that sometimes had their moments because of the professor. Grading criteria was often unclear and fairly harsh.

Incredibly unclear with his directions for assignments and explanations of theories. His lectures are always a week behind so whatever material you covered in your previous assignment won't be discussed until next week. The material itself is either dull or useless. No one is ever going to utilize queer or feminist theories.

Dr. Long is a very enthusiastic lecturer. He is very knowledgeable about the world of digital media production. He does not hold back on his criticism of the work you produce which is a good thing and a bad thing. His rubrics are kind of general which is not 100% helpful when you are creating work. He has yelled at students before.

One of my faves. You will watch a lot of interesting films from all over the world and learn the history cinema. He gives great lectures and the assignments feel rewarding and deepen your understanding of the material. The textbook is optional but was still an interesting read when I was able to crack it open. It was a joy to go to class!

The entire history of film is very expansive, and professor Long does a really good job summarizing everything and teaching what is most important. His lectures are always fun and interesting. He assigns a lot of reading and writing assignments, but he gives great feedback for improvement.

Generally nice teacher, teaches what you need to know for the class, but not anything that would be helpful past college. Weirdly really strict on some things and unreasonable sometimes. Kind of passive aggressive over emails. There are nicer/better BADM teachers at Gies so pick one of them instead

This professor is funny even when he doesn't mean to be funny. His best trait is teaching material and then giving you homework that actually corresponds to what he actually taught. It can get confusing sometimes because sometimes you don't know what the terms mean; but at least you know how to reliably get to the result.
Good class.  In my opinion he does explains topics clearly and is a fair grader.  Some students felt the class was to hard, but hey if you don't know what a mean, mode and median not blame him.
Can there be a worse teacher?
OMG - just get out while you can. Incomprehensible and totally maniacal attitude.
If you can avoid him, great, if not, you are fried.

Dr Shukla is very passionate about what hes talking about. I had him for CHEM 452. It was a very project and hw heavy class, but not too much work. He is a good professor who tries to make complex topics simpler to understand. He is realistic and doesn't go too in depth for an introductary course. I wish I went to office hours!
I like his attitude towards class and teaching. Always encouraging us to do better and think about the material instead of worrying about how to get high score in exams

Taking chbe440 in the current semester. I will take Prof Shukla as an instructor for any course that requires critical thinking. He can explain complicated concepts using examples from everyday life. He is able to relate to students in the class and he remembers the name of every student in his class.
This class was extremely challenging due to to level of math difficulty. He tried very hard to explain complicated concepts. Best professor in CHBE department.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shukla often tied his research into the course material to demonstrate applications. Slides were helpful in completing homework and studying for exams. Discussions were enjoyable and allowed us to form our own opinions about viability of processing methods. It felt unique compared to other electives.

Excellent lecture and notes. The exams are written to test the concepts. Lecture and exam review session are super helpful. He does not repeat any problems from past exams. You have to understand the material to get good grades.
Lectures are super helpful, he always gives his hand written notes for reference. Tests are difficult but about similar to other classes in the curriculum. Best controls prof by far

Decoste was a genuinely fun professor with his demonstrations. All the videos and lectures he posted were generally helpful. He also responds to emails relatively quickly and is very approachable and friendly. Exams were pretty harsh and can be difficult conceptually, but they aren't impossible and are heavily curved.

Good at lecturing and going over problems and examples but the exams were VERY challenging. Use ALL your resources and attend every lecture and discussion. Having a strong background in chemistry is also highly recommended. Also does experiments every class and super engaging with students.
Insanely difficult but not impossible. Always read ahead before lecture, grind practice problems, and prioritize his course over all others
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He gave hard exams, but he had good lectures. There are experiments in all his lectures.

Really difficult class, but it's intentional. Watch the videos, read the book, go to class, get help when you need it. Worst part of the class might have been the TAs because they're too smart so they can't explain well. Decoste is engaging and fun during lecture and honestly, a kind person. Just be ready to dedicate all of your time to this class.
Get ready to watch videos or read lots of textbooks.
SAVE YOURSELF WHILE YOU CAN. The lectures are really easy material while the exams expect me to become Marie Curie. It's like you have to channel your inner chemist and you might just pass the exam.

I dare say this professor is the best I have ever seen. The class is very interesting and there is not much homework. But his exams are very difficult! His curves are usually a lot, sometimes 75/120 can curve to 90+/100. Decoste is very responsible and you can ask him any questions, but it still requires a lot of effort.
bro please do not take this class. i'm actually traumatized by what he made us do. i'm convinced this class might be the introduction to rocket science.
He makes lectures interesting and his materials outside of class are fantastic. Extraordinarily difficult, but it teaches you to how to work and think
Decoste is a really good professor and is very engaging in class. However, the class itself is extremely difficult and requires a lot of time spent doing homework and reading the textbook.

Second time having Prof. Decoste, still the best lectures I have at Illinois. Think more about those questions in lectures, homework, and exams, and you will learn far more Chemistry but problem-solving techniques that benefit for yourself in future science and engineering classes.

The guru of Chemistry, there are a lot of amazing contents prepared for you in this course. Even though it is hard, keep up with them and you will learn a lot from him. Exams are hard, but there are curves! Overall, he is a fantastic and phenomenal professor of chemistry at UIUC.
Great professor!
DONT TAKE THIS CLASS EVER. DROP BEFORE ITS TOO LATE

Absolutely a good professor, but the class is so difficult. It was a struggle to keep up on the content. All the materials are in lecture videos which is nice but you absolutely must watch them and attend lecture.
He is a good professor but there is a shit tonne of work and he expects you to do it all. It is tough and I would not take this class again. It really puts you through the wringer.

Professor Decoste was the greatest professor I have ever had the pleasure of being taught by. Not only is he amazing at explaining all the questions you might have, he is also just an amazing person all around. He makes going to lecture interesting and enjoyable. He made what would have been a difficult, stressful class fun.
Dr. DeCoste is a very nice person. He genuinely cares about his students and loves teaching very much. However, it's not easy to get a good grade in his class. Nevertheless, I like this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Decoste is easily the best professor I have ever had. That being said, his classes are hard. You will have days where you feel like you don't understand a single thing going on in class but if you push through you will make it out to the other side smarter than ever.

As a freshman, you might come into his class thinking you understand chemistry well, and he will prove you wrong soon enough. His lectures are great to listen with cool demos. His tests are challenging, but they make you learn the material and the way to think. He's a super nice and inspirational person himself. 10/10

If you put in the work, the class can be extremely rewarding. Understand things rather than memorize or free response will be a trial. He's easy to talk to outside of class, and his office hours are extremely helpful. His class is a fantastic way to prepare for future chemistry courses, and he is a truly inspirational figure.

His class is a "wake up" class for ChemE, Spec Chem, and Biochem students. This class gets you ready for the future hard workload. If you can make through this class, you are more ready than your peers for college. A is very achievable if you do exactly what he tells you : watch lecture videos, study smart and hard.
He's a very good professor but he makes things very hard.  Exams are near impossible but he curves them a lot, and a lot of his content is very conceptual

Imagine a professor going over his hw (proof heavy) during few lectures, leave the last two or three lines for you to fill in. Everything is derived by hand on blackboard even for 2-lecture long proves.

Professor Katselis gives very good lectures that make the concepts clear. It is also very helpful when he does example problems and he explains everything very well. 313 can be tough but he does try to make us understand and encourages us to ask questions and bring example problems.

Dimitrios knows the material like the back of his hand. You see him standing there, closing his eyes 🤔, and 10 seconds later he starts a 40 minute long proof that is super well explained. Very accessible and holds extra office hours. Focuses a lot on proof intuitions otherwise hard to develop. Exams are proof-based and fair. 5/5 recommend.

Katselis is a really good and extremely understanding professor. He is always available to answer questions and provide clear explanations. If you feel like you need more help, do not be afraid to ask for it, as he will certainly assist you. I strongly recommend taking this course when he is the one teaching.

Promises to deliver the class in person but never did. The most boring lecture possible and terrible course organization. no class schedule posted online, no recorded lecture videos. Puts in minimal effort and is just downright irresponsible. but the class is not hard overall (no exams, just a dozen homework problems, and a group project).
Katselis was one my favorite professors too. Very knowledgeable and patient. He is a sharp professor with great passion for the course. I would definitely take any course he would give.

Katselis was one of my favorite professors. If you attend lectures, he will work with you to make sure you get all the material. The material is pretty dry, but he does the best he can to make it interesting.
Great professor, he takes the time to make sure his section understands, and if you ask a question, he will come to the next class with a solid example to help you understand.

Truly enjoyed the course! Well prepared, always willing to hold extra office hours. Prof. Katselis has a deep knowledge of the course material and he can easily simplify difficult concepts, his teaching style helped a lot!
Lectures are not effective at all! I took all exams without following the lectures and I got an A-

Katselis tends to just copy straight from the ECE313 course notes when he lectures. Occasionally, he'll bring his own examples into the mix to try to help, but this class was still difficult for me. He is willing to do review days before exams if time permits. Probability and stats just aren't my thing and his teaching methods helped very little.

One of the worst teaching experiences I've had at UIUC. Instruction was unstructured and relied almost entirely on slides and videos, with little real teaching. The professor was frequently dismissive and unapproachable, showing little concern for student questions or learning. If you don't know the material beforehand, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!

This professor is very poor at instructing and enabling student learning.  He has a few lectures surrounding 5% of what a module consists of and expects us to self-teach everything by googling or memorizing his lecture slides.  Moreover, he is unnecessarily strict and harsh with his replies to questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This is the worst professor I have ever taken on this campus, and this is coming from a senior in his last semester. His lectures are very hard to follow and only loosely outline a fraction of what we are expected to learn for the homework/quizzes, which take up the entire grade. He is also very rude and not understanding at all. DO NOT TAKE
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You will NOT learn a thing. All this old boy do is throw homework and quizzes on your face and tell you to google everything. His lectures and slides will not cover anything other than the basics found on the cheat sheets by R studio or such community.

Don't take this class. He knows his stuff, but he's not fit to teach. There are Github help threads for questions about the homework material and he is usually quite rude and unhelpful, usually deciding to reply something along the lines of "we already talked about this" or "write different code". His TA cares about the class more than himself.
Professor's lectures aren't particularly helpful to the homework. Professor is not very understanding and if you don't have to take this class with him, don't do it. Like seriously, don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Too Vague Rubrics. No explanation. Never answer students' question clearly. Not friendly. The worst teacher I've ever had in my university life. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Only assignments were bi-weekly homeworks, quizzes, and a final project. Was generally ok, but sometimes his lecture videos were hard to follow since the code he was writing was barely visible on his screen. The final project's guidelines were super-vague, no rubric, basically just do whatever.
Not too bad, but would avoid if possible. There are much better and more reasonable stat professors available.
I met my wife in this class several years ago. 10/10 would recommend. Thanks for the group work!
soc 161 was very easy, instead of tests you simply film 4-6 minute videos based on a couple things. There is reading checks every week. Prof was cool and encouraged discussion which i enjoyed
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: take soc 161, easiest gen ed and professor is cool
Wish I took the online version of this class. Performance on tests tank your grade no matter what since only three tests make up the grade. There are also no study guides or textbooks.

reviews.comment: Soc 100 this semester was absolutely terrible. Professor used different methods of running things which ended up failing incredibly. An introductory class for sociology should be an easy A but ended up somehow being a struggle for e

Nice guy. I think he's pretty respectable and seems like he cares a lot about his students. However, the class was a little disorganized (the test questions were kind of niche and there wasn't really a great way to prepare other than looking at the slides). I think it's easy if you just memorize slides and use common sense.

Though he's a good professor, there is little no substance to really help you study in this class. Some of his definitions are overly complicated (especially for an introductory gen ed?), and he doesn't provide any practice questions/tests, a textbook, or essentially any study materials besides reviewing the lecture slides
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The slides are extremely bare and offer no real context, making it hard to learn from them alone. Exam questions are convoluted and often unclear. There are no buffer grades, drops, or extra credit opportunities to help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is surprisingly tough for a gen ed. The weekly readings are long, the discussions don't really match the lectures, and the exams are harder than they need to be, with some confusingly worded questions. You can only miss 14 points all semester to get an A. There are no dropped grades or curves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a great guy and really the only good thing about this class for me personally. The discussion sections never match up with what we learned in lecture that week, so they felt really pointless. As long as you read the readings to do the lecture prompts and show up to class you'll be fine tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the review sessions didn't really match the exams, which made it hard to know what to focus on. lecture and discussion prompts are only worth 3 points each, so they don't help your grade much. the exams are really challenging, and even a TA mentioned they might be too difficult—hopefully the course can be adjusted in the future.

I think this was this professors first time teaching SOC100 and he completely changed the layout of the whole class. Your final grade is primarily based on 3 exams and in class lecture prompts and discussion prompts, you also get no drops from either of these categories. The exams had very specific information and didn't go with lecture slides much

Took Soc 161 intro to pov as gen ed. Lectures were required, really nice professor so it was a chore to attend. Sometimes the grading was questionable, however, the class was quite easy so there were no worries. Nothing but positive things about Prof. Dill and would definitely recommend him.
Brian Dill has been by far one of my most amazing professors. He is very passionate about everything he teaches, and he is a genuine guy.
Do the work in a timely fashion, & you'll have the answers to the exams, and you will pass.

He is a fantastic professor and person. He knows what he is talking about and respects all opinions. His courses are very writing heavy, but you will come out knowing an abundance of knowledge on the subject.

Attendance does matter! He likes papers, not tests. Gives 4 papers, 1 powerpoint presentation. He really knows his stuff and is very passionate about his work. I may not have gotten an A, but I respect his process. If you are doing poorly in his class, it'll be hard to blame him! The class is very straight forward. Readings are barely discussed.

Professor Dill is open to everyone's opinions and loves to engage all of his students. He's very respectful & gives solid feedback. He has a background in poverty from fieldwork in Tanzania, & you can tell he's emotionally invested in the issues we discuss in class. He's definitely someone you should take if you want to get involved in Development

My favorite professor! The work load is manageable and deadlines are always clear. Lecture is really engaging. He is very laid back and understanding, but you still learn a lot over the semester. You can tell he cares about what he's teaching. This class is so interesting I would recommend it to anyone, regardless of their major.

Best class ever. Interesting and easy to follow. Take it for the smaller class size and the fact that there's only 5 quizzes and 2 tests. Weekly readings that are relevant and easy to understand. Plus he plays cool music before every class!
Interesting. Very very organized. If you attend class and do the work, you should get an A.

The lectures are usually interesting, with some topics more intriguing than others. The readings are usually short and don't need to be stressed over. This class will give you a better appreciation for Africa.

Class is really boring but Dill is a great guy and has a lot of interest in the subject.  Hard to pay attention and go to class but if you do you should get a good grade. Only two non cumulative exams and reading quiz about once every two weeks
Interesting lectures, as well as homework. Fun professor, easily approachable for help
He gives great lectures. They are interesting and easy to understand. All powerpoint slides, assignments, and homework are on Compass. TAs do all the grading, but there is no final exam.
Professor Dill is super hot and a great professor.  His tests are straightforward easy if you attend lecture and study for them.  He made me appreciate Africa a lot more!
Great Professor. Keeps material interesting and easy to learn. Sometimes lectures fast. Makes class fun and is always willing to help or accommodate students.

intimidating at first, but this guy knows his stuff. clear descriptions of everything, got to the point. probably the most informative prof i've ever had. grading wasnt bad at all, but i dont think he had much of a hand in it, the TA was the grader i believe. overall great guy, easygoing, cool class

The class was interesting- you get to learn a lot of good stuff. His lectures aren't mandatory and his powerpoints are available even if you don't go. Easy class except for the fact that the tests are in essay format.
Very VERY organized. Everything is powerpoints. Extremely easy homework that don't take much thinking. If you attend class, its easy to get an A.
really great teacher and uses humor very well.  he;s easy going and his class had a great learning environment.

I like Dilger as a person a lot, but this class was not fun. The lecture exams were all online and covered very specific topics from the notes. The final was in person, only 96 questions, and worth 500 points. I went from an A to a B from the final alone. The final was incredibly specific and difficult. No curving or extra credit. He was funny tho.

His low rating is probably due to the material being a bit more difficult and there just being a lot of material. He cares a lot about his students and really puts in a lot of effort to show that. He is very helpful and willing to guide students. If you take proper time outside of class to study, this class really isn't that challenging.
Worst class I have ever taken at UIUC!!!

His exams are tough! Study for them and do not re-use old exams to study/memorize. He realizes that there are old tests out there and he will change them completely. Try and pay attention in class because what he talks about will be on the tests, obviously.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Knows there are past exams out there.  Do not use to study

Awesome teacher! Made material actually interesting. Difficult essay-based exams, but you will do good if you study ahead of time and take your own notes during class. I recommend writing your own notes on the slides as she lectures, that helped me soooo much when I went back to study! Easy grading for miscellaneous assignments and extra credit!

Dilger is awesome. I loved her class. It was definitely a harder course but if you show up to class and take her feedback seriously, you can 100% end up w an A. Optional final, which is great. She's very interactive and is great at explaining concepts. My favorite 400 level class I've ever taken.

Dr. Dilger was a great professor. She was very caring & understood that sometimes extensions for assignments are needed. I gave her a 4/5 though because of the group projects. A majority of the class discussed how disliked the group projects are but she will always keep them. Other than that, her grading was super fair and she was funny/relatable.
my queen, she is so kind and cares about her students
She is sooo biased. all she cares about is bacon and her meats literally. she also talks to us like were 2nd graders and it gets pretty annoying. otherwise class is really easy
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dilger makes lectures enjoyable and I didn't dread going to this class. As long as you go to class and listen to the lectures, you don't really have to study. There are two group papers that are graded very fairly. I spent little to no time outside of class studying or working on the projects.

I took this class SP21 online. Dr. Dilger is such a good professor. She cares about her students and gives ample opportunity to get a good grade. The weekly lesson checks have unlimited attempts and questions from the quiz. You only have to attend 10 discussions and the other 3 give you bonus points. If you take it online you get furry friend time.

This was a really easy class to pass. Could've gotten an A if I did more on my end. Straightforward lectures, quizzes every week, but lesson checks give you questions straight from the quiz and you can take these as many times as you want. Minimal work load. Very, very caring professor. Understands that students have lives outside her class.

If you show up to class and put in effort on the 2 group projects, this class is easy and enjoyable. The exams are really straightforward if you do the online practice quizzes. Really fun and interesting lectures!
Overall a solid course that you can pass very easily if the group project goes well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Dilger has tests that are 100% essay so you HAVE to take her classes seriously. Lectures are usually interesting and have clear leaning objectives she bases her tests on. Go to class, study, get good grades!

Ratings are maybe a bit harsh, but he can come off as unsympathetic and is a harsh grader, which makes it hard to feel encouraged at times. However, he is always very responsive with emails/office hours and gives helpful feedback on assignments. You'll definitely learn a lot in his international law class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Where do I even start with this professor…Just an all-around uncomfortable learning exp. GPA KILLER. This guy takes pleasure in failing you. It's giving him a sense of power over you. The classroom environment is infernal b/c ppl are hostages of participation grade. For the love of God and all things grateful, DO NOT, I REPEAT, DO NOT take him.

if you put the work in, you are guaranteed at least a B and will learn a ton about the material. but he's really bad about answering specific questions, fairly arrogant, and doesn't have the most consistent grading criteria (says one thing but will grade your work differently or take points off for no apparent reason). will round if you participate

I always got staggered by this man's unmatched level of awfulness. Uncaring and contradicts himself every step of the way. In a grand gesture to “lighten your workload,” he split the final exam into two parts to double the work! He is also a nasty person to talk with, as he thinks he is always right. This course didn't upset me. It AMUSED me.

I literally walked out in the middle of his class and dropped it—he can only push a person so far. I'm graduating this summer and he is the absolute worst. I have never experienced someone like this in my life. What is it going to take for the political science dept. to get the message. We are suffocating

Please stand clear. I really felt helpless in this class. He does not care if you are struggling, he does not care if you have other classes to focus on, he does not care about you as a student. All he cares about is that you submit the work he assigns you and hopefully its good. I would be very lucky if I receive a D. WHY DID I DO THIS TO MYSELF!?

This is a class designed to make you have a debilitating, agonizing life. class averages were in the failing range for everything. he expects you to analyze complex cases without helping you to do so. Assigned way too much hw just for all of it to be 10% of the grade. Lectures are so boring people have begun to play happy aquarium for 80 minutes
I had to start going to therapy because of this class. It took a toll on my mental health and often made me feel incredibly stressed and depressed. Would not recommend him to my worst enemy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Of course, the average of exams is C+. But, the professor is really good at being pompous and self-righteous.

Very bad, very unhelpful, never again. If you get Diehl never go to his lecture. Just self-study the material via textbook and YouTube. You are better off that way so you don't get confused during his lecture. Good luck, you'll probably need it!

He is funny sometimes but overall the lectures are horribly slow and boring and you never know what the key takeaways are. Tons of dense readings, but you aren't tested on the material. He doesn't care about whether ur grade genuinely reflects the actual work you put in. This class made me reconsider how much I actually want to go to law schools.

Wow, what a fantastic way to kick off the semester—getting bombarded with emails a month before the class even starts! Who doesn't love course updates over winter break and Christmas and New Year's and weekends? Seriously, does the professor think this is the only class we're taking? I can't imagine the demands during the semester. Nope, dropped.

Avoid this course with Prof. Diehl unless you're ready to sacrifice your sanity. Weekly essays, three brutal exams, and a final paper that feels like a dissertation—it's a relentless grind. The grading is so harsh that even your best efforts might not feel like enough. Save yourself the trouble and choose wisely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
Professor Diehl is genuinely funny in class and has helped me plenty outside of class.

With this being said, the class is downright difficult, so please be aware: you are going to do an all-nighter or two.

As other comments have mentioned, getting an A is nearly impossible unless you are going above and beyond, or you can just settle for a B.

Professor Diehl is clearly intelligent on the material that is being presented, however, the class is very tough to get an A. Doing all the assigned readings, attending lectures, and going to office hours at most will guarantee you a B. The lectures too at times can be boring and monotonous but he tries to bring some humor into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The hardest class I've ever taken with the hardest instructor I've ever had. That being said, he is the kindest man, very responsive and flexible, and is quite literally always there to help you do better. He genuinely wants to see students succeed and that made all the difference in his class.
The best thing I got from his course was the ability to analyze complex political situations with the techniques he taught in class

Very intelligent, clear explanations, and likes to push students. Lectures are ok - the material is interesting but he talks too slow. Hardest grader I've had in college, but that does not mean doing well is impossible. Requires A LOT of effort for an A. Likes to test students on hypotheticals and case studies.

Professor Diehl is a very intelligent man who realy knows his stuff. He explains things very clearly.  You learn an incredible lot from his law class and his classes are very interesting. His grading is a bit difficult but it is worth it if you want to learn something valuable about law.

Without a doubt a difficult professor, but incredibly smart and incredibly helpful.  You will do more to improve your writing in one of his classes than you will just about any other.  Go to office hours! He's very easy to get ahold of and very helpful when you do.
no matter how hard you try, your efforts will not be rewarded. Plus, don't think this is an exception for you. I did that too

By the time you get to the final in the class, you are so damn discouraged because all the effort you put throughout the class apparently didn't pay off, because the grading is insanely hard. I would write paragraphs for the online discussions and get 2/5 on them, and that's just 1 example. Take it pass/fail, good prep for law school.
He is so full of himself. Condescending, arrogant, self righteous - - -. Stay away from him unless you want to learn how not to act like you are the gift to humanity (in C-U of all places!)

RUNNN! do not take this class with this professor. Professor Diehl is a pompous and disrespectful teacher who does not give you time to do assignments, tests are insanely hard and grading scale is sooo messed up!
While his grading and requirements were difficult he taught extremely well. I learned a lot and he was always ready to explain things to me one-on-one.

Tendency to be pompous and disrespectful, and the grading is deliberately opaque.  Although I found the material interesting and did fairly well in the class, I grew to strongly dislike Diehl and that made me really dread going to class in the morning.

Class was decent. Guest lecturers every week. Broad range of topics.  Each class period was LONG. Essays were kind of difficult. Final exam was really good.  Overall, this class was good. And he remembers your name several years after you have him, which is nice.

By far one of the best teachers I've ever had.  Definitely take his International Law class.  Even though it was one of the hardest classes I've ever taken, I enjoyed every single lecture.  He's very clear with his expectations and entertaining in class.  Brilliant man as well.
Difficult class- glad I took it pass/fail.  He's very knowledgable about the subject matter.
Great Class to take if you like learning about a broad range of international issues. Tons of guest lectures from all diferent departments.
I've had Stefan as an advisor and a teacher. He is amazing. I actually had him for HIST 398, but for whatever reason, I can't review him for that class on here.
Stefan was incredible, I have never been more engaged and excited for a class I didn't even have to come to for attendance! Definitely take HIST 209, I very much recommend.
Truly a GOAT professor and advisor! He has great lectures, and you will always gain valuable knowledge from his class. Definitely take one of his classes if you have the opportunity to.
Stefan is the goat! He was my highlight of UIUC! This was honestly my favorite class as well!

Consistently runs over by 1-3 minutes. Engaging lectures with some participation, though he often doesn't have time to field questions during class. Responsive to student needs (moved due dates back, two options for final style). Teaches thematically. 5 essays (including a film criticism) and two exams.

Cool guy. The difficulty of this class is simply related to your mathematical intuition.  He tends to give a bunch of derivation questions on exams, but all I can say is that if you can see its pattern on sight, you can to solve it, and if you don't see it, you probably won't figure it out within an hour.
Good luck have fun
best
If u r in this class, good luck...
Don't bother to come to his office hours. He won't answer any useful questions and would just ask you to read book yourself.
No comments
No Comments
He is an excellent teacher with witty comments and sadistic tests though. But he has a talent to explain very complicated things in humorous ways.

please cut the smart aleck answers... dont even bother inquiring about exam logistics, since he refuses to answer even the simplest question of what chapters are covered on the exam...you're pretty much on your own from there

Professor had own opinion of what work should look like and refuses to allow students to feel like they are smart enough to speak upon a topic. Would hand out Fs like nothing and feedback was both unclear and did not follow her own rubric.
gives students bad grades with no reason.
Never taking a study abroad. This outdated ACADEMIC HOURLY, not professor will give you C on your transcript and make joke and non-respectful comments on your homework.

Very frustrating experience. Expectations felt vague, and when I asked for a clear rubric-based explanation, the response stayed inconsistent and did not directly answer the question. Communication felt dismissive rather than helpful.

I've never been compelled to add a rating on this site until having Dorothy as a professor. The criteria she uses when grading essays is a joke. She asks for your personal experiences then faults you when your own experiences aren't "interesting" enough for her. The mean for each assignment hovers around 60%, it makes no sense.

If you don't write the way she likes and wants with her very unclear grading criteria, you'll be getting 40-60% on each assignment. She provides her own feedback on your own study abroad experience. But the greatest joke is that you can't even resubmit an assignment with a failing grade for a higher grade after implementing her feedback.

This was the least useful class I've taken at UIUC. We've already studied abroad, now being forced to take this class for a grade, and now we are just writing fluff and bs for a few hours each week so that we can show that we've learned and thought about race, class, and other ideological stuff? What is the point of it?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Dolcos' lectures and have found the two midterms (so far) well-aligned with the review and lecture material. I would take a course from him again!
Super easy class with lots of opportunities to boost scores/grades. The topics were somewhat interesting but I can't say I've learned and retained much.

The class was easy. The lectures were pre-recorded from last year, so outside of office hours you didn't really get to see the professor. The exams were super easy, and he gives you a chance to boost your grade by around 10%. The class is only graded on three things (2 exams and 1 paper), so make sure to take each one seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I'm not enjoying his class at all. He's prefaced a few lectures by saying "I don't enjoy this topic," which won't help students enjoy it either. It may be doable to get an A, but the class is so uninteresting through his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Confusing class.  The teacher never wrote what questions were right/wrong on the first exam taken.  The last two exams haven't been graded the entire semester so there is no telling what grade you might have as that is what the class is graded on.  He never uploaded grades on compass either.  I have no idea if I'm even passing this class as of now.

Really nice and helpful professor. The class he teaches is so useful to anyone trying to learn about how the brain works, and it is interesting how he produces scientific data to back up what he says. Somehow he manages to make it really funny too. I would recommend the class to any student, grad or undergrad.

Interesting class, funny teacher, and not too hard if you pay attention in lecture. You learn a lot of interesting things that you can use in everyday life that will impress others, but it's not too difficult to learn. I would recommend it to any grad or undergrad student. I took it as an undergrad and really benefited from it. Check it out!

The class is very interesting, helpful, and I would recommend it to any student,especially a psychology major. Professor Dolcos somehow finds a way to make the class interesting and he is really funny. The class is easy if you pay attention to what is said in lecture, but you will still be able to impress others with how much you learn. Great class

I thought this class was easy and informative. Only journal articles to read, 3 tests, and a 12pg paper.  For this being a joint grad/undergrad class, it was surprisingly easy if you followed the slides and have an interest in neuroscience.  Dr. Dolcos is important to his field so don't be surprised that he authored many of the readings assigned.

She is a great professor and really loves to offer lots of ways for help. There is not really extra credit, but as long as you go to discussion, yes they're attendance based, and stay up with your work, your grade will not suffer a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her teaching style is clear and easy to follow. She makes math understandable. But if you're someone who doesn't do well on tests, make sure you do well on the weekly homework.
Although the lectures can be long, she explains concepts very clearly in a way that helps most students in my class. Very thoughtful and caring in my experience too

Explains concepts clearly for those who struggle with math. Posts recorded lectures in full on Canvas which is great (I skipped all the lectures to watch these instead, super convenient). If you do the weekly homework and keep up with the lectures, you'll do well.
she's a great professor.

Dobbs cares so much about her students and you can tell she loves her job. Attendance is only required for discussions, but her lectures are very helpful and engaging. There are study guides for each test and they were VERY similar to the test, so definitely do them. I would take her class again, I have never felt more confident in my math skills.

Dobbs was very engaging in lectures and was clear about what we needed to know. Attendence is not required The study guides were a godsend and were basically like the test. Felt so confident in my knowledge for every test
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dobbs is an exceptional person. For a Calculus class, Ms. Dobbs made the material very easy to understand and comprehend. All of her exams are JUST like the practice exams, so I would encourage you all to practice the study exams before taking the actual exams. She is nice and caring. If you have to take MATH 234, please take her!

She has good lectures and cares about her students. I've had her for 2 math classes at UIUC and she's been helpful great. She cares about her students and understands that calculus can be imposing for some. Her tests aren't too difficult, and she gives out good review material similar to the exams. If you have the option, register for her section.

She is the best math professor I have had so far. She always takes time to answer questions during the lecture and even stays after the lecture. She responds to emails fast and is extremely nice. If you have the chance to take a math class with Mrs. Dobbs, do it.

Professor Dobbs is a very sweet and well-respected person. She shows genuine interest in getting to know her students and is dedicated to making sure they all understand the material she is teaching, especially when material gets tough. There is never such thing as a "dumb question."
She was a great lecturer and the class was okay. There was a lot of homework, but it prepared you for the exams. The TAs were great too.
The class is pretty easy if you've taken an algebra class before and she explains the concepts very well.

Theresa is an amazing professor and has been a better person. After class, she posts the notes and an online lecture. She is very accessible during office hours. The homework can be a lot sometimes, the first week was 10 questions the second was 50... Would take her again, she offers extra credit on exams, study guides are the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's so sweet and very helpful with all that she assigns. Would love to have her again at some point, super recommended.

Professor Dobbs is probably one of the best professors on campus. Her teaching is easy to understand, and she genuinely cares about everyone in her lectures. The exam schedule was a little annoying, but other than that it was an amazing course.

I actually took Math 112 with her. She is an amazing professor. Very good lectures with great examples. Tests do not have anything that she didn't go over. Her pace is a little slow but for some it may be helpful. She also records all lectures and posts them so you don't have to worry if you miss a day. Would take her classes any chance I get.

For Math 112, Professor Dobbs is an outstanding teacher who truly cares about her students. She's always helpful, encouraging, and supportive. She's available outside of class for any help or advice. I highly recommend taking her class if you have the chance—she creates a positive learning environment that makes a big difference!
Hard homework but super easy tests.

Amazing professor all around. She taught high school for six years, and her passion for teaching is shown even at the college level. If she is an option for a math class, TAKE HER CLASS. She offers extra credit, is fantastic at responding and helping students, and doesn't give into the normalization of weeding out students in STEM classes.

If Professor Dobbs is ever an option for one of your classes, GET HER. She responses to emails within 15 mins, gives a substantial amount of extra credit, and extends homework deadlines if she notices her students struggling.
Professor Dobbs is an absolute angel-- she got me liking math again. If you have the option, definitely take Calculus with her. I have her again this semester, and I'm really glad.

Lectures are very straight forward and engaging. She is a very nice person and offers plenty of resources for help and exam prep. Tests are fair, HW and discussion sheets are way harder than exams. She offers easy EC, but it is not as much as what others are saying. Maybe 2 percent of your overall grade max total. still highly recommend.

She is an amazing teacher. Lectures are not mandatory and a recorded and posted online. She is very funny even to college level kids and knows how to accomodate her students. Her exams are very easy if you've watched the lectures. The homework and discussion questions are usually much harder than those on exams with many extra credit opportunites.

Loved her! This was the first time I did well in a math class (and I actually understood all the content). Her homework/discussion worksheets were a lot harder than the exams, which worked out well because after practicing with them I finished the exam in half the time because I was prepared. She also has tons of opportunities for extra credit!

Professor Dobbs is a phenomenal instructor. She explains everything extremely well and gives very good examples in class. She provides a lecture outline that you can fill out with her as she goes through the concepts. All homework is done online through WebAssign and the exams are very fair with ample opportunities for extra credit. LOVELY person.
Tests weren't too hard, posted lecture videos, attendance wasn't required at lectures, nice and caring professor

Teaches really well, and attendance at lectures isn't mandatory. She'll upload her lecture notes online, so you can go through them if you don't understand something, and you could also rewatch the video lectures. Exams aren't too hard, so long as you pay attention in class and attend discussions.
Good lecturer, makes fair exams, and uploads lectures online

She's very good at teaching during lectures and makes sure you understand what you're learning.  However, there's sometimes a disconnect between lectures and homework/discussions.  Take her if you can because she's actually a caring and funny teacher/professor.  Currently have A- but who knows by the end of semester.

She is a great professor and keeps the material interesting. The class is not hard as long as you complete the assigned homework and attend discussion. She is also very understanding and a nice person. Highly recommend taking her class.

ANSC 450: Was this class difficult? Yes, lectures had between 60-90 slides of material every time and each slid was packed with information. Is Dr. Steelman a good professor? Also yes! He would often stop halfway through lectures and would cut class short if the lecture was dragging. Tests were very fair, packed with info, made class entertaining.

Dr. Steelman seems like a funny and caring guy and loves to teach this topic but he put information on exams we weren't expected to know, he did not show up to class twice when attendance was mandatory, expected us to enter a zoom without letting the class know and never answers his emails. He's tough to work with, but the class is enjoyable.

He is a very knowledgeable man and has lots of passion for his work HOWEVER he is not a good teacher. He oftentimes is not direct with his answers, lectures are hard to keep up with, never straight up about what is on exams. Overall, not a great teacher Lacks organization, makes exams overly difficult, does not seem to understand we are students!

ANSC 251 is pointless & has nothing to do with animals. He is unprofessional & doesn't want to do his job. He doesn't respond to emails & didn't show up to class twice when attendance was mandatory. He never puts grades in and the "extra credit" you earn won't be entered. He makes you memorize random useless facts that aren't even on the exam.

I really enjoyed this ANSC 251 course and found the material very interesting. I enjoyed going to the class because you can really tell that proff.
