Steelman is passionate about his teachings and he was able to make the lectures fun. You just have to study the material a couple days ahead of the exam and your good to go!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely unprofessional. 2 times this semester, he didn't show up to class for our designated review session (before an exam), which left a lot of students underprepared and had lower grades as a result. He has not communicated why he has missed before or afterwards. Does not answer emails often either. Very inaccessible outside of class.
Great professor, hard class but doable if you put in the work.

Dr Smith delivers clear, well-structured lectures, with emerging and controversial developments. Intense lectures but you'll learn a ton. However, Dr Smith takes grading rubrics and deadlines very seriously, you will lose marks even you miss a minor detail (significant figure, font size). You really need to pay great attention to all the details.

Dr. Smith is amazing! The course content was versatile and interesting. Would 100% suggest this course. I learned a great deal from the instructor. He gave constructive feedback, which made the hard work worth it.

Dr. Smith was an amazing tutor. He provided constructive feedback and was easily approachable. The course content was well organized and contained lots of opportunities to explore current topics. Would 100% recommend this course. I am glad I took this course myself.
Good professor, good class. Lots of current topics covered. You'll learn a lot.

Smith is an awesomely passionate professor, but BIOE 199 presented a lot of work in the form of 4 time-consuming group projects introduced simultaneously at the 6-week mark. Class felt oddly planned; annoying but not entirely terrible. Smith is helpful, encouraging, and provides good feedback; he absolutely wants to see students succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Not the most exciting lecturer to say the least. Good guy when you talk one-on-one. Homeworks for this class were useful and actually a pretty big chunk of the grade.

Although it was his first time teaching the class I took, he did a good job considering the amount of material in the course. He's really interested in student feedback, and is actively trying to make the class better. Really approachable!

He's truly one of the chillest professors in UIUC. He's laidback and kind, and he takes care to make all the students feel comfortable and heard in the classroom. His lectures were slow and boring at times, but overall, he always touched on all the important points for each reading. Read and show that you care, and you'll do good in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. Very laid back and gently spoken and could explain the world in very few words. Readings were very dense but he describes everything so well that it's very easy to stay engaged. I was running late once but still wanted to show up to catch his lecture. His theory class genuinely changed my outlook on life.

Dr. Gaedtke is an excellent professor and thoughtful lecturer. His class was engaging, informative, and highlighted many of the existing challenges within the healthcare system. He is a superb educator and interacts with students to understand the meaning of selected in-class texts. No better professor in the English department than Dr. Gaedtke!

Prof. Gaedtke was one of my favorite professors this semester. Everything I had to read for the class was engaging and carefully chosen. This class requires a lot of reading so I would be cautious of that if you have a very busy schedule, but I found it to be 100% worth it.

By far one of my favorite professors I've taken in all my years of schooling. The work he chooses is met with so much intention because he ties tremendously well into his lectures. He loves when people talk too and his passion makes you want to speak your thoughts because he LISTENS, great grader too. Really opened my mind a lot 10/10
Best professor ever
sometimes he gets too arrogant but mostly he is nice
This man is the reason I quit teaching.
Who let this man come out of retirement

The professor does not like to have his ideas challenged. He can come up with every reason as to why he is right and you're wrong. He makes over generalizing statements about students abilities to read and they're often in a negative tone. This shouldn't be a mandatory class especially for educators in STEM, as this class does not cater to us.

The most useless class as a student in education. They put multiple content areas into one course, that the professor does not have any experience with and cannot instruct. The expectations in this class is inconsistent. After putting in hours of effort, assignments are not graded timely, and have no feedback. "change your life"--okay.

The things you learn in this class will be useless. Doesn't grade the assignments so you won't ever know how you're doing and even if you have an assignment graded you won't receive any feedback. Thinks that we as future teachers should be technological geniuses that have all the time in the world to create online presentations for your students.

While the course was beneficial to experience in the field, the professor was unable to make compromises and was not open to suggestions. He was difficult to work with, and did not listen well to others opinions. He often made inappropriate and unkind remarks to the students. His information was out of date.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Yes, this Professor seems to care about education. However, he is unorganized and difficult to work with. He teaches outdated research and technology. He does not listen to any opinions different from his own. And he emailed me this morning (xmas eve) asking me to repost an assignment I had posted in October and to do so by the end of the day.

A lot of the other students in the class were lazy and disrespectful.  Show you care and give him the benefit of the doubt and you will pass with flying colors.  He's rough around the edges, and he's a little out of the times, but he definitely cares a lot.

Unclear  requirements . Makes some fairly offensive remarks on sensitive issues in class, which is surprising as it is an education class. Says that he will provide help and feedback but then doesn't end up doing it. Creates deadlines and then doesn't stick with them, but the class still turns in everything on the original due date. Meh.

He seems approachable but very disrespectful with other ideas. It is pretty annoying. It is 1-credit course and super easy to pass. A lot of group work and discussion. You learn as much as 1-credit course should be.
Awesome Teacher
Was not interested in the students as people. Did not provide useful techniques to utilize in the field. More concerned with past experiences and life instead of the present. Boring.
Keeps you pretty interested, he is passionate about what he is teaching. Good class.

I have never left a review on this site before, but i just have to for Andrew. He was by far the best professor I have ever had. He makes a point to get to know his students personally, is willing to work with you when you struggle, and does these things while doing a great job at keeping the class moving at a comfortable pace.

Andrew is awesome. He's kind-hearted, cares a ton about students' success, and is truly amazing at what he does. He's open to answering any questions students may have and is very quick to respond. Not to mention - he has many great pearls of wisdom about succeeding in the international business industry and becoming professionals and leaders.
A great professor very fair and engaging class. Do your work show up and youll get an A

Andrew is an amazing guy! 100% take him for BTW 250. As long as you show up and do the work you should get an A. Moderate/low amount of homework. He makes class fun and cancelled class a couple times for us and usually let you out early. Takes time to get to know each individual student, please take him for BTW 250, promise you won't regret it.

Such a sweet and caring professor. Although he gives homework often, instructions are clear and he's very lenient about it. Interact with him and he will make class fun for you. If you miss class, he posts class scripts online. As long as you follow the rubrics, do the assignments, and show up you will get an A.

As an international student, Andrew is the type of professor that will help you to understand and teach you how to correctly write. He is very patient, and it doesnt matter if you do mistake writing, he will always give you a second chance to succeed. His classes are well prepared and interaction with peers is essential.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved Andrew Moss! He is so nice and his lectures are absolutely so much fun. There are a few projects and the criteria might seem vague but he is open to reading over and giving feed back! I would recommend meeting with him and making changes.

A real gem. Funny, passionate, and considerate. Very flexible with deadlines and grading and does everything to make you successful. Always cheerful and makes the class exciting. Learned a lot of helpful things from the class. If you're taking BTW 250, I highly recommend taking it with Andrew. You won't regret.

This review is for BTW 263 -- International Business Communication, but it wasn't a choice. Andrew is sometimes late with grading, but gives lots of feedback. I talked to him on the phone and on Blackboard when I had a question. He always answered questions and helped me with any work that was confusing. Great class!

A good class for the advanced comp requirement. Not hard, but a LOT of busy work that sort of builds on top of each other to make longer end-of-unit assignments. Textbook free online and not used until later in class. He gives a lot of great feedback, grading is inconsistent though. Super caring. You finish your work, probably will get an A.
Can be too open ended with grading, go see him to get advice and he will help you. Complicated assignments for a required class, tries to make BTW relevant, not just a mandatory course.

Very subjective grading style and a very laid back attitude with dates and record keeping. He is nice and kind of grades on effort so he will give you a B-/C+ for effort. Giving A's depends on his mood. Don't waste time thinking why you got a B+ on a project, there is no logic behind it. You could not try and get an A on the next project.

He's a reasonable professor, but if you want an A, you'll have to put in the work and remind him of all 6 assignments for grades. Other than that, he's ready to offer good advice and useful lessons, especially during office hours.

He is very disorganized, and he does not stick to the syllabus that is given at the beginning of the semester. Often times it is unclear when an assignment is due. Grading also takes a very long time. We did not receive any assignments until about week 10 into the semester. He gives helpful advice but it is VERY difficult to contact him even email

He has no rubric for his grading, so you'll just be given a grade depending on how he's feeling at that moment. He grades his hw assignments with checks and check pluses. He gave one of my projects  a "B/B+" (what the hell does that mean). It's the end of the semester and he still doesn't have any grades in.

Andrew is a great guy. To say he is super laid back is an understatement. I'm pretty sure people turned in assignments late all semester. BTW263 was an international writing course, it is different than BTW250. Andrew goes out of his way to be nice to his students, basically any comment anyone made in class was the right answer, which is good & bad

Andrew is a very laid back teacher.  His instructions for assignments are very open ended.  He does take a while to grade assignments.  However, he extends deadlines all the time, so you have plenty of time to write your papers.  He gives extra credit once or twice.  Great professor! He's always available to give you feedback on your assignments.

While of course you will be writing a lot of papers which isn't much fun, Andrew will go out of his way to help you write them and improve your writing, and he tries to make class interesting. He also allows all of the papers to be written in groups, so try to make a buddy or two. I would definitely recommend him for Rhet.

Tended to get really sidetracked with grading and discussions to stay within a reasonable time period. We had decently interesting class discussions, lots of weekly written "notebook" assignments, 4 formal essays. I liked that he did give a chance to make a revision on the graded initial submission to get credit that was greater than the 1st try.

He is an easy grader. But his lectures are so convoluted, disorganized and confusing. He may be interesting to listen to in other classes but not in intro to American literature. He is also so slow at grading. He is uncomfortable to talk to one on one. Would not recommend engl 116 with him if you want to truly learn/improve your writing.
Andrew is a good guy and keeps the class interesting. Take rhet with him.

Andrew was a great teacher, he was very good about discussing papers before they were due and after they were graded. However, he did take a long time to grade papers and tests, we ended up skipping some papers because he was so backed up. He encourages you to think for yourself and make the most of your education. That is why we are here anyways!

Andrew was a great teacher. He made rhetoric very fun. Also his workload wasnt as heavy as what ive heard of other professors. He also makes class fun and interesting, very involved. Definitely recommend him for Rhet
Professor Moss was awesome.  He was super helpful and really funny.  His grading is pretty easy.  I highly recommend trying to get him for Rhetoric

Don't take BTW 250 with Andrew if you want to learn how to write resumes/cover letters. He teaches actual business writing. You'll spend the entire semesters on memos and letters. Definitely go to his office hours and have him look over your drafts. He will let you know what to fix. He is quite helpful. I felt his course was very beneficial.

WONDERFUL TA! made an extreme effort to explain everything, had fun and relevant ways of helping you relate to material, excellent at helping his students review. would definitely take any other class he was teaching/TAing!
so much fun in class, very accessible TA. wants everyone to learn the material and get good grades, but doesn't want that to  be a boring and painful time.
He's a good english teacher and is pretty lax on grades.  You should go to class, but his assignment format is pretty easy.

Loved taking his ANTH 279 class and it really challenged my perspective. He and the TA are very accessible during office hours and provide thoughtful feedback while genuinely supporting students' success. Despite the substantial reading load (~100p per week), the course content is engaging and the syllabus is well organized. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable and well-spoken, but it is very theory-heavy and can go over one's head. Looks for a lot of participation, but can be a bit condescending if it's not the answer expected. One group presentation and some essays. A lot of reading (100+ pg/week). Grading is about as tough as the material. Gives days off to work on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a great professor and is very insightful. ANTH279 specifically has a LOT of required reading that builds on the other. Overall, if you don't like reading or have the time to do ~80-100 pages weekly on dense material, take a different class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Everyone says "ANTH 103 is a breeze"... but what they FORGET to mention is that online version is easy and the in-person class is not. If you think you're just going to get past this course without having to attend lecture, do the reading, or study... good luck! Avoid taking this class with Orta at all costs unless you're okay with taking a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: interesting class, but way too much reading. you can skip them and go to lecture, which seemed to workout fine. theres very few graded assignments ( basically only two midterms and like 4 discussion posts) but if you make a quizlet out of the list of words he gives for each midterm, you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: so much reading and complicated content for a gen ed class, probably find another one to fulfill, the work isn't worth it and the terms are super hard to understand, difficult exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do not recommend this class. The professor is alright himself but the class itself is very demanding just for a gen ed class. It's very heavy on reading that is impossible when you have other classes. Not many assignments to help your grade. Exams are pretty difficult. For a gen ed class it is too much work, online class for this seems easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For context, I'm an anthropology minor, but I really enjoyed this class! I really appreciated how he posts exam review terms, they're very helpful. This is a very reading heavy course, but you can get away with skimming the readings if you go to lectures. Really king guy. Discussions are mandatory.
Bad...... really different from what I learned in Utah
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fine teacher I guess
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fine I guess
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As an international student whose English is not very strong, I would say he has shown great tolerance and kindness.
As a native of Illinois, I can only say that the course content often conflicts with my common sense......
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would strongly suggest you take this class online. The lectures were so boring and I could hardly stay awake during them. There are a lot of assigned readings that you have to reference in the midterm and final. The only semi-good thing was the discussions but if you missed more than 2 your grade will drop a letter grade every time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid if possible - really boring & dry lectures, 100+ pages of textbook reading every week (which is impossible to do), and no extra credit. Giving him a 2/5 because he knows how to hire good TAs - my TA was awesome and heard good things about the other ones too. Tests aren't too difficult if you spend at least a week prior studying for them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He says attendance is mandatory but I've never seen him take it. Be careful either way. The lectures are great but understanding the class is very reliant on reading, sometimes an unrealistic amount for how much other coursework I had at times. TAs are great. Don't be late and don't let the door close too hard because he'll glare at you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: se vira

I was not a fan of ANTH 279 as a class. I was not particularly fond of the material which made discussing it and writing papers on it challenging. However, Prof. Orta is great at facilitating discussions, makes everyone feel heard, and is a very fair grader.

If you have to take an ANTH class, take it with Prof. Orta
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Orta is the best! He is open to discussion during lectures, very engaging and fun to listen to if you're passionate about the subject. The class is very reading heavy, but the main books are interesting. I skimmed a lot of the other readings and still did good. Pretty much have to go to lectures as he doesn't post them online.
He is very nice. I learn a lot from this course.

He's a fine professor I guess, but the class structure was focused only on reading and weekly quizzes and discussion posts. He never actually "taught" because there were never any lectures. I only learned from the readings.

A pretty average professor if I'm being honest. He was super well-organized for it being an online class and he responded to his emails quickly. But the class is a LOT of work. It usually consisted of an activity or two, two chapters of reading, a discussion post, and a quiz. The material is easy to understand, but make sure to keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy, but I had to drop the class because I couldn't deal with reading 100+ (usually very dry) pages a week. And then having to discuss them in detail for 3 hours straight. My ADHD just could not keep up lol.

Genuinely nice and caring guy, but awful teacher in my opinion. The class isn't necessarily hard at all but it has four group papers which are never fun in a gen ed. He also revolves lectures and exams around his own personal experience rather than more general anthropology.

Very poor lecturer, was very boring, and didn't learn too much. I found the easiest way to succeed was to just memorize his exam study sheets like a mad man. The test were just regurgitating info back. As far as electives go, this was terrible, group projects were dumb, and graded in an almost nonsensical way.

This class was the worst one Ive taken at this school so far. Youre only graded from two tests, 4 projects, and your final. The group projects were very boring and it was also hard to stay awake during lecture. He reads from topics from a sheet and makes the content seem more complicated than it is. He also does not explain the content well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Definitely did not like this class. Every time I went to it I almost fell asleep. He drones on and on and you don't know what to write down for the exams. The papers were graded overly hard and the books and readings were intense.

Try to avoid him! He didn't do much for any students. Lectures were hard to follow, exams fairly difficult, too much arbitrary grading. Received a grade that ended in -9.96, and he refused to round. Thinks he's a big shot, really didn't enjoy his attitude toward students. Overall, makes life difficult for a gen ed course.
Professor Orta is fairly good at his job. Lectures are not listed as mandatory but for a good grade they are. I was more disappointed with his TA selection for discussion sections than anything else

Though lectures aren't mandatory you must go or else you will fail tests. Take notes verbatim from his slides and pay attention in discussion. The topic isn't too hard but he is very specific on tests!

Orta's lectures are a must: try not to miss any, as the exams are heavily based on them and if you don't want to be cramming last minute to figure out all the material, just GO TO THE CLASS! His lectures are a little hard to follow because he kind of reads from his sheets but I have learned a lot from his class. 3 five page writing assts & 2 exams.

This professor is terrible! The test are very hard. There are a few multiple choice (worth a lot of points), fill in the blank, and 2 essays which you have to do in 40 minutes because he hands out the test late. He is boring, old school, and confusing. He doesn't give out busy work, or any assignments for that matter. 3 test and a term paper.

I'm not sure what the other reviewers are talking about. His exams are super straightforward. He gives a "word list" prior to each exam, and if you know all the definitions, you'll get a 100%. Readings are all discussed in class, so you don't have to do them. Exams only require 5/6 questions to be answered per page, too, making them extra easy.

Professor Orta is a very old-school professor who relies on slides and lectures during his classes. There is a lot of reading but a lot of it is interesting so it is not hard to get through. He provides studyguides before every exam and there are only 3 exams.

Do not take this class with this professor. He is absolutely terrible. You have 3 test and a term paper and that is it. He does not offer any extra credit and the test are very hard even if you study. He is a terrible teacher, he gives out no study guides and does not try to help his students pass the class.
Lots of readings, but if you go to class you can do well without them. Class is interesting, tests mainly focus on general themes. DO NOT take pictures of his slides.

Teaching style reminds me of a high school teacher. He knows a lot about his subject, but expects students to write down what's on his power point slides while listening to what he is saying. One of the most ineffective ways of presenting material. Just don't take this class with him. Choose another Anth103 prof. 103 is supposed to be really easy.

This guy doesn't want us to succeed in his class at all. Too many readings, doesn't go through all of them, useless slide outlines posted online (which are actually just the slides without the content and only the titles) and we can't even take pictures of his slides even though he talks much more than what's on the slides. Avoid him for this class

Terrible class. He is a bad lecturer and when you ask a question he never gives a direct answer, so you usually end up more confused than you were before. His tests are very hard and there's no good prep for it. Requires too many readings-3 books at once. I would avoid a class with him.
I never really go to class, and got As on the tests. Studying in needed and his tests are kind of weirdly structured.. Interesting class though.

I took prof. orta's anth 430 last spring. You will learn/read so many important authors in this class. Hes great for advice/consulting on papers. One word of advice though: the readings are really intense.. but if you can work through it, the class isnt over-bearingly hard. its heavily relient on discussion though.

I took Prof Orta's class last year and he is great. Sure, he may be "dull." but he is very smart and a great lecturer. Honestly, he is probably one of my favorite professors at this institution and deserves more recognition

I'm an Anth major and this class was by far the WORST Anth class I've ever taken in my 3 years here. Professor Orta is boring and his lectures are dull. Could not stand this class. Still got a B+ but it was a struggle since I just didn't care and he made it harder than it needed to be. Tests are hard, so study.
Classes can be boring at times. Some reading are important but some others can be skipped.He is very interested in his subjects and makes some funny comments sometimes.
Amazing professor.  He is super intelligent and it shows.  Class is extremely interesting if you are already into Latin America.
Lectures are pretty boring, but the class is not the hard. You have to go to discussions, but the readings are somewhat opitional because the tests are mostly just key terms.
a. orta rocks my heart
made some wierd comments on race, wierd guy
Studying was needed, I often slept during class, but he taught fairly well.
keeps class relatively interesting and engaging
No Comments
He is the worst professor I ever have. Curve the whole class down
Tough but he gets the work done, you gotta be ready to put in effort for the class if you want to pass. Gives a heavy curve at the end.

He curves down and doesn't communicate this.

He's a funny and entertaining, but he is very unclear and uncommunicative about grading. The TAs were good and did their best, but despite getting far above average on all the exams and homework, I was curved down. When I tried to speak with him about it to understand why, he refused to clarify.

I think Inorganic Chemistry is just a hard class in general. Professor Gewirth really tries and asked us for our feedback several times throughout the semester. Although attendance is not required, highly recommend. He gives bonus points (4 for correct answers & 2 for effort). Exams and homework were hard, but he tried to provide helpful resources.

He really does try to make an effort to get everyone as excited as he is for Inorganic Chemistry. He was EXTREMELY lenient on grading and I felt like I did poorly in the class. He gave out a LOT of extra points. He would ask us questions in class; if you got them right, you got 4 extra credits and 2 if you didn't. Great professor. 10/10 recommend.
He is one of the least respectful individual Ive met in the Chemistry department, more than half of the class received a C and we all worked our ass hard. Avoid this professor at all cost

Generally, an engaging professor with extensive knowledge of urban issues. The weekly reflections can get repetitive, but Professor Allerd provides plenty of resources on Canvas to catch up on missing work.

I took UP136 as someone interested in the minor. Prof Allred has great lectures, and attendance is graded. I enjoy his slides, and he's generally a friendly & approachable guy. The weekly quizzes are short and not difficult if you did the readings. The big projects in the class are pretty simple and as long as you read the rubric, you're good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: not a bad professor, i really don't mind him as a person. you don't really have to do the readings as long as you can understand the material. the exams are open-note, open-book, and non-cumulative. the one thing is that there are a lot of assignments all due at the end of the semester, so this is really a class where you want to plan ahead
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Assigns so many reading reflections each week but doesn't even read them. He cares about this class so little that half of the classes are online when they could easily be lectures (this is not an online class). The workload assigned is easy to fake your way through, but the effort you're expected to put in does not match up with his effort at all
Not accessible and often condescends in class. Does not give constructive feedback and is vague with instructions and grading justification
We had a semester long research project paper and Professor Allred was there whenever we needed help. He would assist with whatever questions and concerns we had.

The class was pretty easy and we were only in class for about 20 minutes each week. I'm trying to learn ASL and this class did not teach me much. I think Susan is super nice, but her teaching style was ineffective.
I don't know why people are saying she was easy to take this is the most difficult Professor here. I have a feeling she's deleting the negative ratings and writing good ratings about herself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Too much homework and is very serious about being technical with signing even if you are a beginner. Will drop your grade so fast if you aren't perfect with signing. Don't take her until the last Asl level 3. She will fail you and not care about your gpa

This Professor is a very difficult grader. If you get a couple wrong answers for the hw or quizzes your grade will go down. She is very strict on everything especially the hw. Another thing there are way too many homework assignments. Take Ivan for the first two ASL classes if you can especially if this is a language requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: My previous ASL Professor did a better job teaching and was more flexible to different levels of knowledge of their students. Professor Weiss was not very conscious of different learning abilities of her students, and I found it frustrating at times. She was however always accessible outside class.
Such a good professor! The book was not needed, but I had prior knowledge of ASL. Her videos are very helpful. Assignments are easy. She does take attendance for the zoom

Susan is one of my favorite professors. Shes kind and cares about her students learning and passing. She also gives extra credit and makes sure everyone knows there is extra credit. She reopened a quiz that I missed when I broke my elbow and made the final more accessible. You wont regret taking her classes.

Because of the pandemic, this class has moved online which makes it extremely hard to learn such a visual language. There were no zoom classes but rather 15 minutes worth of videos to watch The textbook is barely needed, you can look up what you're struggling with. I would take a class again with her if the class were in person.

I had Susan for SHS 221 and I have her again for 321. She is great! We get out of class early most of the time and the class is pretty easy. The book isn't necessary but you can get it if you want extra practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Susan is a very solid professor. She goes over all of the signs in class, but you have to practice at home a lot in order to get an A. She offers extra credit (usually deaf events in the community), and she is very understanding. She doesn't respond to emails quickly, though. Quizzes are straightforward and pretty easy. But PRACTICE!!!

Susan is the most amazing instructor in the world! She makes you feel passionate about learning ASL. She is understanding and a very fair grader. She makes me laugh in class and is nice. She usually ends class a little early and is lenient on grading. I could have gotten an A in her class if I would have practiced.
So so so so so good

Great professor! One of my favorites ever. I'm not the best at sign language but she never made me feel discouraged or stupid and she helped me genuinely learn. You definitely need to go to every class because if you miss one you will miss a lot of info. The Multiple choice tests are pretty easy, but signing one on one is a bit harder. Lots of EC!

I had Susan for both 121 and 221. She's one of the best professors I've ever had the pleasure of having. She truly cares about all her students and wants you to succeed. She is ALWAYS willing to help out if you need it. I wouldn't say it's an easy A, because you definitely have to work. I recommend going to the EC events - really helps you out.

Susan is amazing. I wish I had her again. She is so adorable and fun, loves what she does, and is super passionate about her students. She makes time to get to know your name and face and is always positive and patient. If you skip class or come late, she will not like you.

Susan is one of the nicest people I have ever met. She will work with you if you don't understand something and provides plenty of extra credit opportunities. I had her for ASL 1 & 2 and she is easy to understand without prior ASL knowledge
Susan is awesome! You should definitely take any ASL class with her over any other teacher.
She's great! We get out an hour early. She's straight and to the point. She grades fairly and the multiple choice quizzes are easy.

Susan is by far my favorite ASL prof thus far. She has a very relaxed teaching style and is very willing to work with students when it comes to class conflict/assignment issues. Gives extra time for some things. Very fun in class experience!
Susan is amazing!  She is so much fun and she teaches at a pace that feels comfortable for everyone.  Definitely recommend this class and her!
Susan is awesome guys, you really want this class! She is very understanding and lenient on turning in things.We always got out early and she a very fair grader.
Susan is a great teacher. The classifiers can be somewhat difficult, but not unmanageable. She's a really funny teacher and I learned a lot from her. I would recommend taking this class!
Such a great teacher! She made this class fun & would let us out early most of the time! :)
She was very understand with anything and very helpful.  I really enjoyed this class.
JUST PERFECT AS WORLD ORDER ASL TIMES. FIRE UP ASL! WHAT CAN U ASK FOR MORE! SEE SUSAN WEISS!
I love Susan! She loves teaching and makes ASL fun!
Does not explain concepts clearly. Lectures feel unhelpful — instead of following the textbook, he relies on his own Excel sheets to teach. The so-called 'group discussions' are largely pointless.
I really liked Dr. Dubin's class, he's really knowledgeable about game studies and stats stuff plus he's a super cool dude in general.

If you get him remember that he thinks board games are the greatest thing in the world. They aren't, the games you have to play are really tedious and boring and the stupid table top simulator is really awful. Take this class if you have to but take something else if you can.

Easy to talk with and willing to clarify; however, I do advice having a specific question. He loves boardgames and will use them to illustrate his points so you may be tempted to "zone-out" but don't! You get what you put into it. If you're willing to share about your project, your peers may have some really good resources to help you out.

He's a great lecturer, although sometimes he gets deep in the knowledge spiral and gets caught up in the minutiae of the topic. Is passionate about computer science and librarianship, and is a great resource in and out of the classroom. Would definitely take another class by him. PS, he plays a mean board game.
Completely unresponsive/does not give feedback, but an easy A.  Pretty much go to lectures, read the instructions on the assignments, follow them exactly, and you're golden.

The tests are very fair if you prepare for them and the class overall is very fairly graded. Dunfield is also great at drawing and a good lecturer. He does explains things a little hard though so if you aren't strong at math expect to put in a lot of work in this class.
Great lecturer, but explains things too fast that I couldn't understand

Lectures and notes are pretty good. HW has nothing to do with what is on the exam, practically don't spend too much time on them. Use practice exams to prepare, the earlier the better. Overall, I would say his exams are challenging. He is professional and gives amazing stats about the class.

The homework on Webassign is quite difficult (if you do it yourself...). Dunfield himself is incredibly smart, but I didn't like how much he focused on the proofs instead of applications. I learned best going to office hours. Make sure you do well from the first midterm onwards. I did pretty mediocre on two midterms and ruined my chances at an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This was my second time taking this course and he definitely showed me that having a good professor makes a huge difference. His lectures were super engaging, and he provided multiple examples for each new concept that we learned. Overall a super cool professor and really cared about his students and their wellbeing.

Certainly a tough class, but Dunfield is extremely accessible. He's the most passionate lecturer I've had (although I am just a freshman), and he was helpful outside of class and understanding of extraneous circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great lectures including sketches of proofs and drawings to help visualize concepts (he is very good at drawing). Prof and TAs are available often and lots of resources to help are online, including lots of practice tests that are similar to actual tests. The homework can be very time consuming. ~$90 online textbook is required.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: professor dunfield is by far the best calc 3 prof. his lectures were easy to understand and he is really good at drawing. all the course resources are also easy to access. his exams are quite straightforward if you understand the content.

Prof. Dunfield is very theory-focused and rarely works exam-style examples, which can be tough for average students. I recommend Professor Leonard plus PLT/Merit. Many skipped lectures but still did well using posted past midterms/finals. Homework was much harder than exams.

If you need to take Math 241, take Dunfield. All of the professors cover the same topics and have the same exams. Dunfield's lectures are by far the best of the lot. His drawings are amazing, and he does examples, but he mostly spends his time covering the reasons why something is true, which helped me understand it well. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS!

Lectures are clear and well-organized, with a strong emphasis on theory. He is very helpful and approachable during office hours and willing to explain concepts in different ways. Exams reflect the material covered, and his practice materials align well with expectations. Overall, a supportive professor who cares about student understanding.
Watching videos of the topic instead of going to lecture saved me loads of time as lecture at times was on things not on the tests. He is very approachable and has many resources

Often times skips over foundational material leading him to be "too smart" for the average student. Lecture is often wasted on useless information that has never been on tests and homework is far more difficult than the actual midterms and final. The midterms and final make up about 80% of your grade so bombing one jeopardizes your whole grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 90% of lecture is drawings, 10% is computational/applicable demonstrations. I never learned in lecture. 85% of your grade is exams. I just watched Professor Leonard the whole semester, put his videos on 2x speed and you'll learn 10x as much in the same amount of time as lecture.

For the LOVE OF GOD I hope he puts out lecture videos, this hell house of a course will make your fundamentals terrible if you are not constantly in lecture, and that gets hard sometimes. If you get behind, prepare for the spiral of not knowing the content because there is so little to go off of digitally, the notes are quite sparse.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This rating is for the class structure. No lecture videos + the way we follow the textbook is NOTHING like any online video or resource. Makes it really hard to study if you miss a lecture or get confused during one, and the notes are just "too smart" for people without context on the concepts. Lectures are good, IF you understand them during.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He a good professor, very proof heavy and definitely teaches smarter than the average student, but the homework is really helpful and there's several opportunities to learn content in different ways

Far too smart for the average student. Often skips over foundational concepts, doesn't show steps for examples, and overcomplicates simple ideas. Honors HW is difficult, especially without help. The exams aren't too bad. If you are very confident in your calculus abilities and want to learn as much as possible, take his class. Otherwise, avoid him.

Very good professor, you can tell he's an expert in his field and is passionate about what he teaches. Honors homework is tough but fair, and it does help in fleshing out your understanding on the subject. My one issue is that he's "too smart for the average person", often skipping the fundamental and basic ideas and leaving you very confused.
best math professor ever

Dunfield wants his students to succeed. He's extremely generous with his time and extremely approachable and friendly when answering questions. Very good artist too (important for math) and provides lots of visuals. Great for those who love math and are good at rigorous math language.

Extremely beautiful drawing. Excellent lextures. Best Notes ever. It is an honor to take his lectures. Although the participation is not mandatory, it is still hard to find a seat if came in late. He explained everything patiently, and always willing to prepare students ready for the exam.
GOAT. Just take his class and you will know.
he is good at drawing

He basically has no time to teach you the proof, and shifts fast in topic. If you do not have good foundation, and pre-learned knowledge, you need to spend more time learning by yourself. Nonetheless, he is an interesting professor, and he is welcoming during his Office Hour.

241 students are so lucky to have dunfield as an option this semester. Take him! He is the best professor here. Genius but still can explain things in a way that makes sense. He is passionate about math and just all around a great guy. Class is super organized - never been given so much resources/feedback from a professor.
AMAZING!!!!! He is going to be away at a workshop next week and I am so sad. He is the best professor of my life!
Best professor of my life.
AMAZING PROFESSOR!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Nathan is an awesome professor! He cares about students and wants everyone to succeed in this course. His lecture is very clear, and he will upload handwritten notes for every lecture. The course is tough, but attending his office hour is super helpful! I will definitely take his course again!

Prof Dunfield was an amazing professor who taught the class really well. He really liked the concepts and had amazing drawing skills that are not to be messed with. The lectures were kind of awkward because he'd ask questions and wait for someone to answer and no one ever wanted to answer, so don't be afraid to talk. Office hours were very helpful
Super nice and patient professor willing to explain everything until you understand. Hold several office hours per week, and willing to extend office hour when students' problems are not solved.
Amazing lecturer. His lectures motivated me to get up at 8am.
Great lectuer, though he goes a little fast sometimes. He really knows his stuff too, and is great to ask for help. Easily the best professor Ive had here so far
Professor Dunfield is the best math teacher I've ever had in my life. His office hours are very useful and he takes the time to ensure that you understand the topic if you seek the help.

Amazing professor. So many resources (online lecture notes that he hand-wrote, worksheets and exam solutions, course diary, practice exams, pdf of your graded exam, office hours, etc etc) that can help you achieve the grade you want. Also, I really enjoyed his subtle humor.

Worksheets are harder than tests, but they are very good tool for me to get a big picture of new concepts. Practice exams are much like the real ones. The course is not easy, but u'll feel much easier if your professor is Nathan. The grading is fair. The overall grade will be curved. So dont worry. PS: Hes in suits every day! Like his beard : D

Calc 3 isn't the easiest class but Dunfield is exceptional at teaching its many concepts. The lectures are very informative and easy to understand, and exams themselves are very fair, and you get adequate preparation with many practice exams. Additionally, they are graded very fairly and quickly, and you get to see exactly where you went wrong.

Sometimes I think he is so talented and nice that he should teach sth much beyond Calc 3. If you can please take his class. He explains everything in lectures and hes very approachable outside class. He is patient and ready to every question. Hes also excellent at drawing 3D pictures to help you understand the geometry in calculus.

Dunfield's lectures weren't boring, but sometimes they had no big picture and were confusing. He also sometimes went off topic and taught us things we didn't need for the test, which was annoying. Discussion worksheets were way harder than the tests. Tests were almost exactly like practice tests, so focus on studying from those. Fair grading.
Nathan Dunfield is amazing.

Prof. Dunfield is by far one of the most talented professors I have had so far. He makes a effort to connect with students, especially in a large class like MATH 241. For example, I went to  his office hours once and he remembered my name. Additionally, his lectures are phenomenally clear and handles in class questions exceptionally well.

Dunfield is one of the smartest people I have ever met in my entire life. He is an amazing lecture and while he lectures quickly, they are clear (he is amazing at drawing the 3D shapes). His tests are very difficult, but the practice exams are great prep. I am not great at math but I managed to get through.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Dunfield has very clear lectures and is always ready to answer any questions in a succinct manner. All of his drawings are incredible and make learning the concepts much more straightforward. Office hours can be quite helpful and he makes the effort to know you by name if you stop by and ask questions. Take this professor!!!!!

He's so sweet! I took calc 3 as dual credit, didn't do so well, took it here with Nathan and he's a million times better than my prior instructor. Really helpful discussion worksheets and sends you a PDF of your exams so you can see your mistakes and how you are doing in calc 3.
An awesome professor who is always enthuastic in the lecture. The lectures are instructed clearly and organized well . He's extremely helpful and accessible to students. The notes are really helpful.

Dunfield is probably one of the smartest math minds I've ever seen in my life. Because of that, at times it can be hard to keep up with his lectures and his way of explaining things can be more complex than it needs to be. However, he's a great artist so his visuals are super helpful.
Very good prof, clear and insightful. one of the best ive had during my time at Uni
Perfect sketching just make 3-D much easier
Very good professor. Gives clear lectures and really cares about students. Though the course is tough, you will probably end up with good grades.

Awesome lecturer, very knowledgeable about the material (used to teach at CIT). But he sometimes goes too fast in lecture. Pretty helpful during office hours, HWs and exams are decent, not too hard not too easy. You will be able to do well if you put time in it.

Awesome professor. The class is a lot of work, but he provides you the resources to get the grade you want.  Regularly attending lecture and discussion, doing homework, and going to office hours/the Calc III tutor room will allow you to get the grade you want.

The class's discussion and homework tend to be difficult, but they aren't worth too much of your grade. They're where the problem solving learning takes place, and you should take them seriously, but not worry too much about grades so much as the learning and practice you get from them. Dunfield is a wiz when it comes to his drawings on the blackboards, and he explains the basic concepts very well. I never had any problems with him. He taught at Harvard and Caltech for awhile, so no surprises.
Fantastic teacher. Super fair class. I honestly can't say anything negative about the guy. Awesome beard too. I would 100% recommend.
Best Math professor I've ever had.
He's obviously an incredibly intelligent individual. Possibly too intelligent to be teaching calc III. None the less, a nice guy.

Great professor! He is amazingly well prepared and has intimate knowledge of the material. He's hard, but reasonable. He offers tons of office hours and curves on tests. If you come to lecture prepared, do the homework, and ask questions, he is a very helpful resource. I wish all professors were like him.

He was absolutely fantastic. I came in from Calc BC and my teacher was great. Nathan was almost as good. Very clear purpose and excellent explanations EVERY SINGLE DAY. people seemed to have trouble with his tests, but the curves were huge. I thought they were perfectly fair and not too hard. Take his class for sure

Nathan is a good professor. He's patient and funny in a nerdy way. His tests were fair and pretty straightforward. He draws excellent pictures and teaches at a fairly slow rate. The only thing that's sometimes lacking is the ability to energize us/break the fourth wall during lecture, but it's 8 or 9 AM so it's not all his fault.
Nathan is the best math teacher I've ever had. He makes calc 3 easy by always making sure his students understand each topic. Definitely try to get him!
He's the best! Definitely my favorite math professor I've had. He's great at explaining things, but his drawings WILL make you feel incompetent because he's awesome at them.

Probably the best calc professor on campus. His exams are extremely difficult, but that could have just been this year because hes previous exams were much easier (he showed us his previous exams before each midterm and the previous ones were much easier). However, although his exams are extremely difficult he gives a pretty generous curve.
Great teacher that draws awesome pictures and is very helpful in answer questions and giving explanations.
Great teacher east midterm
He makes the most amazing graphics.
This teacher is a straight up boss. He is the best drawer ever and can help you very easily. He is a great teacher to have for math 241.

Teaches quite clearly and patiently. And draws nice pictures. He really prepares his lectures and discussions. His exams are not difficult; just cover the basic definitions in class. Go to the class, do the hw, and you will be fine.
he's pretty awesome
great teach, interesting lecture,very professional

He really cares about our learning. He is always willing to answer questions, he checks in with students about the pace of the course, he always gives feedback so students know how they are doing relatively, he has extensive office hours, he offers outside material for extra help. He is the best professor I have had.

He's a very hard professor. Attendance is not mandatory, but you definitely need to go to class to understand. He's tough, but he's willing to help his students during office hours. If you put in the hard work, you'll learn a lot from him.

Dunfield is very patient and helpful at office hours, but his lecturing and overall teaching ability is sub-par. It seems like he tries very hard to teach well but unfortunately failed the entire semester that I had him for.
Very enjoyable class. He let you use a cheat sheet on the midterms. It was pretty easy overall just some weekly writing you have to do that's not that annoying.

nice professor, very time consuming for a gen ed but gives out a lot of extra credit. Tests are okay, you really need to know the material to get a decent grade. Lecture heavy and study guides only help a little so its hard to know what will be on the test. slides, homeworks and study guide do not align wahtsoever. very difficult to study for exams
Engaging speaker who really puts a lot of love into his class. Fairly accessible if you need to ask questions after class or by email.

Nice professor who delivers engaging lectures. I enjoyed the course because of his lectures and plan to take more of his courses even though I'm not an astro major. This particular class is an easy A as long as you complete all of the homework. He allows you to bring a piece of paper with notes to exams.

Dunne was a good professor to have for my first semester here. Cares about the material he's teaching. Class is mainly homework based with 4 exams (lowest weighted half) so it's more time consuming than other gen eds. Pretty easy to do well if you review the lecture slides and do the homework.
Very good class although you do need to know your material for the test. You are given a calc and a sheet of paper of notes for the test.
Dunne is pretty chill. You can clearly tell he's passionate about astronomy. I've never really been into astronomy, but he definitely made the course interesting.

Professor Dunne was incredible. Truly cares about the material he is teaching and it helps that it is interesting. Was super helpful with personal situations going on throughout semester and was always very caring. One of the only classes I have taken that was mainly homework based, easy assignments, help bring up grade if did bad on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very passionate and has many extra credit opportunities on tests and outside of. About 2 hrs of reading a week, but is interesting stuff that can be pounded out on a Sunday. Does Zoom during class so u can attend at home.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As long as you pay attention in class, it's pretty easy to do well. Lots of reading to do every week but it's all from the assigned textbook so you should probably be reading it anyway. His presentations are on point, they make the concepts crystal clear. He's my academic advisor as well and just awesome overall. Also absolutely hilarious.

Prof. Dunne is fantastic, I can not recommend his class enough. Lectures were interesting and engaging thanks to the way he presents. He's extremely enthusiastic, and shares that with students. I was genuinely excited to come to lecture each day. The class is easy with an average workload, it's not stressful at all. Take this class if possible!

Prof. Dunne is very enthusastic about the subject and he brings that into lectures. We had required participation through ClassQuestion during lectures and there are Perusall readings (my least favorite thing ever) and homework assignments due weekly. Honestly a lot of work for a gened but you can get an A as long as you put in the bare minimum.
ASTR122, bad grading. Don't expect a good TA. Don't expect the professor to be kind to you especially if its over grading disputes. PERSUAL GRADES MATTER AND HE GRADES THEM HARSH!!

Genuinely nice professor and tries to be funny and interactive. He answers questions and does after class reviews before exams (4 exams worth 35 percent of grade). Its a very assignment based class which is rarer in college. Takes more time than other geneds but worth it. Content is so cool. All about space disasters and how they will/do affect u
Guy is interesting and knows what hes talking about. Class gets bogged down by requiring perusall though
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love Prof Dunne, he is so sweet and genuinely loves teaching. I assume this class would be better in person, but online there are about 60 p of reading a week with required annotations. Lectures also take about 2 hours total. However, learned a lot and loved the class. As long as you take notes on the reading and lectures you'll do well.
Lecture content is good and interesting. Unfortunately, required Packback discussion forum which was a complete waste of time and money.

Clearly very passionate about astronomy and it rubs off. If you go through the readings and PowerPoint slides in the online lectures, you'll be fine. Clear study guides that really make tests much easier, and he doesn't use the camera for Proctorio which is so nice, we even get open notes. Sometimes long readings but the book isn't a challenge
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great and interesting lectures, and as long as you read over the PowerPoint slides, you are sorted. His lectures and slides are very helpful for the homework and tests, and he gives you lots of extra credits in this class. Exams aren't difficult and he allows you an 8.5 by 11 piece of paper for cheat sheets on exams. Easy A+
Tough grader

Dunne is very funny and chill. Quizzes are all online and you get to use one sheet of paper (front and back) on exams. He only assigns a few homework problems that can be tricky but can be figured out. There are observation sessions that you have to go to but those are easy points. Discussion sections is just working in groups on an assignment.

I took Stars and Galaxies with Dunne and it was absolutely amazing. An easy A as long as you show up and do your work. I never once looked at the textbook. Dunne is great and if you have him for a discussion section youre guaranteed to get an A.

Great lecturer, make funny jokes during the lectures. Although somtimes do not show up timely on his office hour, but still patiently explains everything. Homework usually takes more than 4 hours a week if you want extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is such a great professor, he is very passionate about astronomy and he always makes lectures interesting and makes the content easier to understand! He has great jokes! He is a great professor overall.

He's such a dad, lots of dad jokes. He is VERY excited about the stuff he's teaching and does a good job of teaching it, he's very energetic and knowledgeable. it's pretty clear that he loves his job. He does give a few out of class activities and one off-campus that you have to attend.

Very easy class and Prof. Dunne is a good lecturer who is passionate about what he teaches. If you are interested in astronomy, then you will simply love him, but for me, I found the lectures quite boring since it is not my forte. The classwork for ASTRO 150 is very easy and consists of simple writing for article summaries and packback.
he good :)
Professor Dunne is so nice & tries really hard to make lectures fun! 10/10 stand up guy

This class was interesting. However, if you're not a math/ science person like me, you should probably find another Nat Sci & Quant. II class. Unless you plan weeks ahead, professor is ALWAYS busy. My TA is Cail Daley and he's the type of guy who know a lot but not how to explain. THE EXAMS ARE REALLY HARD even w/ a cheat sheet. Good luck :(
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's such an awesome teacher even if you're interested or not about astronomy you should definitely take his class it's not hard and very easy to get an A+. There needs to be more teachers like Professor Dunne that are very passionate about what they are teaching about!
he is amazing!! if you attend the lectures and pay attention, you are sorted.

Lots of homework but they were spread out over the entire semester and were fairly easy so long as you show up and read the articles assigned.  There is no $100+ textbook to buy and the course material is fascinating.  Powerpoint presentations and NO TA section which is EXCELLENT.  Significant extra credit opportunity and lowest homework is dropped
Tests were so hard for a 100 level class-even with a cheat sheet. The homework was so long and boring. Do not take!! :(

Took ASTR 150 as a non-astro major, really enjoyed it! First project was a little math-heavy for my taste but Prof. Dunne is extremely approachable and up for adapting to students' needs, so definitely chat with him if you have any questions or concerns! Lectures are awesome; he's a lot of fun to listen to. Two thumbs up.

He's very knowledgeable on the topics discussed and explains them well - doesn't just read off his power points. If you ask him a question, he almost always knows the answer off the top of his head. BONUS: HE LEAVES HIS SLIDES UP LONG ENOUGH FOR YOU TO TAKE NOTES AND NOT RUSH!!  Tests aren't easy but aren't impossible, and he allows a "cheat sheet"
Very hilarious professor. Easy A class and reading doesn't matter too much.
Online homework is easy. labs and exams are very hard, you are aloud a cheat sheet on the exam but no matter how much info you put on it the exams are still to difficult for a 100 level intro course

This was supposed to be an easy A gen ed but it was not easy. There was so much homework and the tests were really, really hard even with the cheat sheet you can use. Bryan is super nice but I just wish the exams were a little easier and that the lectures were shorter!

Pretty easy class. It doesn't require alot of understanding, but you need to be able to memorize, then A's are very possible for exams, just allow 1hr study per lecture (exams cover 7-8 lectures). Homework quizzes allow 3 attempts, so those are guaranteed 100%s. Not a hard class... getting an A but I don't feel I learned THAT much, to be honest
He talks down on you when you have a question or need clarification.  He can be very rude to students. His class is easy and what you need to know is straight forward.

Very enthusiastic person, but teaching style is very confusing. The materials that are on the test is often not on the study guide, you basically have to remember every bit of the stuff he says in lecture.
His class was interesting, homework load was fair. discussions were easy. but when exams came, they were pretty hard. wish there were practice exams instead of TA reviewing the materials.
Weekly online homework answers can be found online. Lectures and activities were pretty interesting. You can tell he cares about the topic. Tests aren't the hardest and aren't the easiest.
This class was pretty tough due to the exams. You did get a cheat sheet, but sometimes it was not helpful at all. You really need to know the concept. The lectures were quite long also.

I mean he's a nice guy and the weekly assignments/work load are not bad at all, but the exams are literally impossible. Cheat sheet doesn't help, and some of the questions I've never seen before in the lectures. He's not too bad but the exams are honestly HORRIBLE.

Very easy midterms and exam if you had done your homework and went to lectures (I studied less than 3 hours, 3 hours, 5 hours)  Lectures are enjoyable, and the professor gives off a great vibe. Easy classes, easy to follow.

Overall, it's an easy class. All the homework can be found online, and the labs are not too bad. He gives several extra credit opportunities, but his exams are extremely difficult. He lets you use a cheat sheet, but it doesn't help much. Even if you don't do that well on the exams, as long as you do everything else you should be fine.
Even though he lets students use cheatsheet on the exam, you'll find it mostly useless because exams are extremely hard. (But I think he curves grades as well)
Incredibly funny and engaging lectures, not a dull moment.
Dunne is freaking awesome! Take his classes!

He is a overall great teacher. He is super enthusiastic and loves teaching astronomy. There is a lot of work in his classes, but he is fair with due dates. The tests are pretty hard, so you have to go to class and read the book.

2 exams and cumulative final. 3 easy science projects. 2 reports - 3rd one for extra credit. Mandatory iclicker - every answer right is extra credit. Often curves exams about 5%. Really enthusiastic about teaching. Interesting lectures most of the time. Do the extra credit and you'll get an A

Professor Dunne has been, by far, my favorite professor on campus. He is extremely smart, always prepared, uses technology in lectures very effectively, is always helpful and willing to help, in such a good mood it's almost alarming, and has the funniest sense of humor! Book was cheap used & not required. Lectures were optional, but had i>clickers.
Great professor. Very enthusiastic about astronomy and is entertaining in lecture. Lets you use a double-sided note sheet during the midterms and final. A great class to take for the science gen-ed.

Bryan Dunne is an incredibly good professor. As I am thinking about it, I actually have never had a professor who was so enthusiastic and effective. Professor Dunne really cares about making the students enjoy and learn as much as possible in his class. I would recommend this class to anyone and everyone.

He is the absolute best! So enthusiastic about his job which makes learning from him that much better. Not a hard class at all either. DON'T take Celeste for your discussion section. She isn't helpful at all.
Very organized. Easy A. Do the extra credit!

Easily one of my favorite professors on campus. He's very enthusiastic about what he teaches, and he's always in an outstanding mood and is eager to answer any questions you may have. Go to lectures! Not only are iclickers part of your grade, but the lectures are just plain fun to go to. Take this class!

Easy and enjoyable :)...I miss this class.  It's one of the few classes where I learned a lot from.  Just go over the homework/quiz answers for the test and you're good to go.  Don't bother watching the lectures on youtube...they are far too long.

Prof. Dunne is easily one of my favorite professors at this university. I look forward to going to his class three days a week (he's my discussion teacher, too.) He makes class so much fun and he makes these cheesy and relevant jokes. He keeps you interested and awake in class. He's actually the best.

I'm only taking the class because I wanted to add a course mid semester and it was a second half online course. Easy is an understatement. As long as you go over the material it is not hard to grasp. The professor for his online video lecture though speaks way too slow, monotone, and pauses too long making them near impossible to go through.

Sadly, I got a B+ when it was an easy A course because I didn't do half of the online quizzes.  I only attended half the classes and it was still extremely easy.  The quizzes are just like the tests, so use them to your advantage!  He's an interesting lecturer.
AKA Peter Griffin, BEST TEACHER! FUNNY GUY, MAKES CLASS ENJOYABLE AND SOMETHING WORTH GOING TO. Could not have asked for a better teacher.
Amazing teacher. You dont really NEED to go to class, but I always do because I love it. The dorky humor, the mind blowing facts, the enthusiasm, this guy is awesome.

Simply the best professor at the U of I.  His lectures are not only effective, but actually very fun.  The class itself was very interesting, but Dr. D made it enjoyable.  I am actually considering sitting in on this class again this semester.  If you can, take ASTRO 150 with Bryan Dunne.
Very nice guy! love his class!

This teacher is just amazing; he is truly passionate about Astronomy. Also, his class is extremely easy which gives it another plus. For his tests you can bring in a sheet of notes to use and final is just another test. I finished with A+, and had a great time listening to him in lectures.
He is hilarious and very helpful! He explains everything very well and in a way that is interesting. I'd definitely take another class of his!
This is a great class. He's a very fun teacher and makes the class awesome. Easy to get a good grade!
Fantastic class

Dr. Dunne is an extremely good professor. He is very passionate about the subject matter and class is enjoyable. He gives generous extra credit oppotunities and their are daily iclicker points to help boost your grade. As long as you put in a little effort this class is a very easy A. Highly recommended!

Overall was a very easy class if you go to class and pay attention. There are iclicker points. There is one midterm and a final for tests. Homework load isnt bad and is easy for the most part. Take this class for a gen ed!

BEST CLASS I TOOK THIS YEAR! Weekly assessments but you get two tries, you get a double-sided cheat sheet for the midterm and final, and you have opportunity to replace midterm exam grade on the final. Dunne truly is "delightfully geeky" and I loved going to class everyday. What a gen-ed should always feel like! Take this class for phys science!

One of the fairest classes I've had. Dunne gives you plenty of opportunities to ace the class. There's weekly online homework, but you get two opportunities to do it. Exams can be a little tough but doable if you study. Show up to lectures to get easy Iclicker points. A few online labs but they're pretty interesting. Great class, great professor!
Very easy b/c you get a page of notes for your tests. He posts notes online and there is so many opportunities to get an A. Just do the work

Very eccentric and passionate, this prof is delightfully geeky.  Everything is online, you only get a grade for your best 2 out of 3 observing sessions, best 25 scores in lecture, and likewise for other assignments.  The only reason to go to class is the points u get from the iClicker quizes.  Study for the exams & you'll do fine.  EXCELLENT GEN ED

Great professor. Very, very enthusiastic about the subject matter and you can hear it in his voice. Class isn't hard- exam q's are from past quizzes and i-clicker q's not to mention that Dunne is EXTREMELY helpful. He's also pretty funny in a nerdy way--makes the class that much more interesting. If you're gonna take Astro 100, take it with Dunne!
I dont know what everyone is talking about...the professor is kind of okay but his class sucks! I hate astronomy and his class puts me to sleep. Its not easy. Dont take it.

Professor Dunne is one of my favorite professors at the university. He is kind and will do his utmost to help students. He is funny and keeps the class entertaining. He is extremely enthusiastic about Astronomy. I have found this class to be really interesting. It's also pretty easy to get an A in the class!
Dunne is awesome.  This is one of those classes everybody dreams of.  You have to take this class.

Class is interesting. Tests are fair (straight from notes/online hw/old exams). Dunne tries really hard to keep it funny and interesting. Sometimes it's overboard, but overall he's a great professor and it's sincerely interested that everybody understands.
What a lovely, squirrely fellow.
Awesome class, great professor, highly recommended!
This class is super easy as long as you go to most of the classes.  He puts all the notes online, so even if you don't go, its no big deal!  I recommend it if you need a gen ed!

Fun, interesting class.  Learn a lot of not too difficult material.  Good lecture slides with good attempts at humor.  Don't need a prior understanding of advanced physics or anything.  Exams are relatively easy.  Online quizzes weekly.  Discussion is a blast.
Absolutely incredible professor.  Highly recommended!!!
Possibly the best class I have ever taken.  I learned a great deal, was hardly ever bored, and content was explained excellently.  Dunne is a fantastic professor.

Good guy, but out of touch with how much his students understand based off his lectures. His exams did not match up in difficulty to his lecture or HW, but the curve was generous. He is open to answering questions and will make you feel like he cares about your understanding of the course content. The guy just loves signal processing lol.

Not an enjoyable class to say the least. Pretty awful. But from what I hear, Dullerud is at least better than Bahl. Do yourself a favor and take this class in the fall or whenever when Salapaka is teaching it. You will thank me later.
Clear lecturer; quizzes were not hard as long as you came to class; exams were a little tougher, but they're just extended homework problems. I would definitely recommend him.

Dr Geir really explains tough mathematical concepts well. He starts from the basics and build incrementally. He tries to give intuition to each of the mathematical concepts which helps in easier grasping and improves understanding. He goes strictly according to textbook, but I would advise not to miss the lectures as you will get to learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very clear lectures, no textbook, straightforward exams similar to practice exams. Teaches class out of order compared to other teachers so labs do not sync up but its not that big of a deal
Super nice guy and organized lecture notes . All you need really

The lectures are good and the overall organization of the class is phenomenal (there's one course website that directs you to your homework, pre-maide textbook style notes, and lecture notes). However, the style of problems in lectures are not related to the homework, which are not related to tests. Thus its difficult to prepare for your exams.

Dullerud gives some of the most boring lectures I've ever attended. I had never fallen asleep in class before him. Felt like we jumped around on topics, sometimes we'd discuss the same simple topic for a week. Exams were totally off the wall, no way to prepare (sorry). Try to go above and beyond learning the concepts, and you could get an A.

His lectures were kind of boring, and, while he does post them online, his notes are very disorganized. The online homework system is terrible; it does help you learn at all, and rewards gaming the system for points.  I also didn't think the website was much help, and would have preferred a real textbook.

Dullerud's lectures are very clear but also slow and boring. The homework problems are the type that are difficult until you know how to solve it and are then quite simple. The website for this class is phenomenal and greatly improves the quality of the class.
He made the course as easy as it should be. Go to lecture, do homework, and you will be fine. Exams could be a little tricky sometimes, but rechecking several times guarantees you a good grade.

He's a good professor, very thorough (if a bit slow in getting to the next subject) and the homework is helpful. No textbook, but his notes were enough. Watch out for "range" problems; he likes those.

Always prepared, sometimes overdid unimportant material/subjects and didn't get to more important ones.  Always willing to help/clarify/communicate and was respectful.  Recommended.  Tests were meh (kind of fair, kind of tricky, had a few bad questions), but I think it was compensated for by a curve at the end.  2 Hour midterms kind of suck.
not so helpful during the lectures...spends too much time talking about things that are not so important.
worst teacher of ever, extremely arrogant

He is helpful and patient towards students and tends to explain concepts and goals well.  It is important to understand the concepts because he isn't going to tell you how to do every type of problem (which I don't think he should be doing anyway). He has his little phrases that make him a bit quirky.

Very clear lectures. Extremely patient and helpful when you need it. Uses a tablet in class for notes and posts them all online. The homework is tough, hard to do it on your own. The tests were very hard as well. Nice guy too.

During lecture he provides only very simple examples to get the idea across. However  most of the time his homeworks would take so much time.
