reviews.comment: Dyer is the champ, if you normally get good grades you'll be fine. Just don't expect to learn anything from the lectures.

His class was... not great. I mean, I was able to succeed, but still hated every single part of it. I stopped watching his videos since it did not help. Just do as many past exams as possible to succeed in the class. (especially if you do not read, conception is mostly drawn from couple of previous exams)
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very jolly guy. He doesn't teach during lecture, lecture basically exists to test i clicker questions, not to explain anything. If you learn how to use the calculator you can answer any test question by clicking a few buttons. Its a doable A for anyone, just look at his old exams, 80 percent or more of the questions will be from old exams.
Fin 221 was a mostly self taught class for me. Classes weren't very helpful and are self driven. The midterms are also challenging. Would take another professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: the extra credit was easy. the course was set up in a very forgiving way. he did not explain very much of the material and you had to read a lot. he made simpsons jokes more than he taught

I may have an unpopular opinion about Dyer, but I thought he did a great job explaining things in class. As long as you come to class actually ready to learn and pay attention every single time, the material is not difficult. However he has a ton of material to get through in this class, so he can't spoon feed every problem to you. Great guy.

Super nice guy and lectures are relatively entertaining. Though entertaining, he does not cover hardly anything that is tested on. The weekly homework is fairly challenging and a much better representation of what will be on the tests. To learn, I had to read the textbook.

Really jolly guy, but can't teach. Lectures only go over very basic concepts and the exams are far more challenging than the material he teaches. Homework & online quizzes take a long time too. Hope you get a good TA because they're the only one that'll teach you. People that do really well in the class usually read the textbook.

Lectures are very hard to understand because there is very little explanation about what you are actually learning.  He  tries to explain the material with jokes that make it more confusing.  Also, he writes solutions in the worst handwriting I have ever seen.  If you have him I would recommend doing the practice tests.

Maybe his lessons were changed for this semester, but he didn't use any old videos and actually, well, taught. There are still iclicker questions in lecture (which is twice a week) and two group projects, but overall I think he has improved a lot comparing to the other reviews. He's also humorous and makes the lectures interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For Fin 221 you just have to teach yourself everything because this guy just shows old videos that he says you have to watch but they're just a waste of time. If you want to get an A just do all of the previous exams and you should be fine. Go to lecture not to learn but to get easy i clicker points which can be extra credit. The final optional.

Dyer doesn't teach in lecture. He makes you watch videos he made 8 years ago. The videos much like lecture are rarely on topic and can be over 20 minutes long. He talks more about the Simpsons than stocks and bonds. The iclicker questions are difficult if you have not watched his videos. The material isn't hard but you will have to teach yourself.

Dyer is an okay professor for FIN221. Since he has so many students and there is one lecture a week, you have to learn most of the material by yourself. For me, this was easy, since I enjoy finance. This class was tough for people not majoring in finance. TONS of extra credit if you go to class, 3 group project, 4 tests, optional final, drop 1 exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Get ready to spend time learning on your own. He's a nice person, but when it comes to teaching his lectures were not quite relevant (yet you still have to go for iclickers). Exams are multiple choice, drops one. Use past exams and your book to study. Overall, really did not like the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Make sure you do all the extra credits. I regret that I miss the competition at the beginning and I was only few points away from A. One lecture per week and you will need to watch the online video on your own. I basically go to discussion session an office hour to learn all the material. Past exams are helpful.

This is the WORST class I've ever taken. He might be a good person but he is just not qualify for a good professor for not teaching at all. Only one lecture a week and use old past videos online to teach yourself. I can't believe I paid so much tuition for this class. He won't even make up for an important lecture he couldn't show up.
best 3 out of 4 exams are taken and there is a ton of extra credit just for showing up.

This class is just a pain in the neck. The homework is fairly easy but the tests are way harder. You'll need to study a good deal if you want to do well. I thought I was going to fail the class up until the last two exams. Try to keep up with the reading and make sure you really understand the material.

His tests are very similar to past exams. Took the class and learned how to solve his specific problems to pass exams, not really anything about FIN. Homework is mandatory and iClickers are extra credit (helps with borderline grades).

SAVE YOURSELF! Dyer may be nice but he doesn't teach well. Lectures are once a week which first of all isn't enough for this class. TA section was useless because he offered no helpoften times didn't even understand what we were asking and you still had to go to get the attendance points. Exams were too difficult given what was taught in lecture.
If you apply yourself and study the material and concepts, you will do fine in this basic finance course

Dyer seems like a nice man, but he is not an effective professor. You will need to teach yourself as his town meetings are mostly review. I did terribly on exam 1, but after figuring out how to approach the class, I picked my grade up to an A and didn't have to take the final.

The class itself is really easy and straightforward. I never went to class even though I lost some iclicker points, since the lectures are pointless. I agree that the professor is bad, but hey, the material is really easy. Just read the textbook, do the practice exams and A guaranteed.

While I hate how this class is set up, Dyer knows his material. If you follow the weekly outline, you'll be fine. I never read the entire book, just used it for Aplia assignments. Exams were not too complicated, I suggest doing well on the first ones to make up for ones down the road.
Easy A. Read the book, do the practice tests and suggested problems, you are good to go.

This class is not as hard as everyone says. You will have to study for tests but there are 3 practice tests in the course packet. If you know how to do all the problems from the practice tests then you will be fine on tests.
You shouldn't have any problem getting an A in this class if you read the textbook, do the Aplia assignment, and perform moderately well on tests.

GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS! He's the man at office hours. VERY good at explaining, always happy and willing to help. The course structure is pretty good, you don't have to go to lecture. He really wants to see students succeed. The examples he uses are hilarious and riddled with Seinfeld, South Park, and The Simpsons. Doh Doh Donuts is all I gotta say.

The class is pretty hard, as most of it is self-taught. I did not go to lecture ever, but went to the discussions. The class does suck but Dyer is willing to help if you put in the time. Go to his office hours, watch his videos online, do the practice quizzes and the old exams and you will be good. Just takes a lot of time

Self taught class. Material learned is basic stuff compared to the twisted, convoluted form on the exam. Projects are long and tedious. Homework is unnecessarily long (and many times, the book doesn't explain how to do the problem at all).  Exams are immensely difficult compared to what is learned. More frustrating than anything.
You teach yourself in his class. Plain and simple. Don't expect a teacher.

This is a university professor who teaches a pretty useless class once a week (that is optional to go to so no one ever shows up) and expects us to complete hours upon hours of homework and learning on our own.  When he could make class mandatory or even extra-credit based possibly three times a week and actually TEACH us the material.  ridiculous
He was pretty good. Knows his stuff. I didnt even have to take the final for an A

He is absolutely awful. You "learn" from his online videos and do way too much online homework. The group projects are very time-consuming, and you will never be prepared for the tests. You have to teach yourself everything from the book and hope you get a good TA.

Ok professor but I ended up teaching myself. The videos were not helpful to me. Lecture was pretty much a repeat of the videos I suggest choose one or the other. Keep up w/ Aplia! It may take longer than expected. Also read the book (get a hard copy), it really does help. If u have questions don't wait til exam time

The reason we pay these professors is so they can teach us face to face. Nowhere did I sign up for online videos that requires a tall glass of water to get through, but that's how the class is structured. Every point counts so get 100% on Aplia and Pre-flights, and do well on the projects because you're going to mess up at least 2 tests. FACT

This class is tough, but an A is very manageable if you work at it.  You have to teach yourself everything, because the hybrid style of this class is horrendous.  My best advice: Take every practice test and know how to do every single question, in and out.  His real exams are really similar, so understanding the practice exams is critical.

I disliked this course a lot.Dyer is a lazy professor. You will learn everything taught from aplia and dyer reiterates the basics. The exams are sometimes off tangent from the material he is teaching because he took questions from a quiz bank (not written by him).
This is the worst teacher. I ask him one thing and he answers the other. Makes things more complicated than it is.. And his voice is utterly annoyinggggg...>"<

His lectures and all the videos are highly useless. Pay attention to three the following three things and you will do well: do the suggested problems from the book, the practice tests, and the post quizzes. Don't go to class, his voice is highly irritating.
Favorite Professor at U of I! Great teacher who enjoys teaching, sad I will not have him anymore!

Town Meetings are useless. Just watch the videos posted online to do the Preflights and the Post Quizzes. As long as you take notes on them, those should be fairly easy. Do all of the practice/past exams before a test. If you go to his office hr or review he is actual really helpful.

His lazy ways outside the classroom have led to lazy ways in the classroom. He basically puts it on the students to teach themselves everything. His video notes are very easy compared to the tests he gives. Your best bet is to review through the video notes carefully, go through the post-quizzes, and then take the previous exams. He is worthless.

He's a really nice guy and helps if you ask directly but his blended learning is HORRIBLE! The videos are pointless, you learn little to nothing at the "town meetings" and depending on your TA you are screwed.  He's your only option however. Read the chapters, ignore the videos, and take the practice quizzes he gives you to do well in the class.

He's allright. He doesn't lecture but posts videos online. Quiz questions are from question bank easily found from googling. Exams are same as quiz questions so if you take many practice quizes you'll be fine.
Dyer is fun, makes lectures much more enjoyable then other foreign business professors who barely speak english.  Tests are challenging, but can be twerked,  Positive Review or Dyer!!!!

The videos and the lecture are pointless. Discussion is the place to learn everything. The best bet is to skim through the chapters, understand the graphs and bold words, do the practice problems, a couple practice quizzes and the practice test for sure. A few questions are just copied from the previous exam.
Fairly easy class.  You don't need to ever watch the videos.  The professor is a very nice guy, explains thing well.

The class is pretty hard and the stupid "blended learning" format doesn't really help.  If you keep up with the videos and do the assigned problems, you should do alright.  Lecture is kind of pointless.  Dyer does explain concepts pretty well though.

Easy Class. A few of the practice exam questions are on the actual exam. Go to T.A. classes for sure. If you have questions, go to Dyer directly. He is the best at explaining basic corporate finance. He will also share good stories with you.

seems like a cool/nice guy, but thats about it.  he doesn't teach you anything.  class shouldn't be too hard to get an A if you have good study habits, but if not, you could be in trouble.  the video part of the class was just stupid and was a waste of time.  im a finance major, and this class had me question that, especially b/c i didnt learn much

I took the final bc of a mix up with my exam schedule. Big mistake! The online book and videos are a nuisance. I'd rather go to a class than deal w that. Overall it took too long to learn the material. Find a tutor. They will show you in 10 min what will take you a couple hrs to figure out from the reading and videos.

I don't like the new online video lecture system for this class, but overall Dyer is a good teacher.  He's helpful during office hours and explains the material clearly. Out of three midterms and a final, you can drop one. However, the final was much harder than the midterms, so plan on dropping it.

Each exam has 33 problems. U must not miss more than 6 problsms per exam to be in the Safe A Zone (assuming U do well on HW & Extra Credit)! GO TO THE TA sessions. If you think they don't help, then study before you GO TO THE TA sessions :) Personally, I wish Prof. Dyer had taught FIN concepts more indepth.
Tests are very straight forward and cover material on old tests which he provides. Only one lecture now and the other is through online clips which take way way too long.
Thought he was great.  PowerPoints could use a little work.

Hilarious guy - makes the class interesting with cool examples. To study, do the practice exams as many times as possible and read the chapters as many times as possible! You think you know everything but you learn more each time - pulled off an easy A.
Tests are not too bad if you study the tests from previous semesters.  Should be an enjoyable class if you enjoy business.

This is a hard class...The exams are tricky and require a lot of comprehension of the material that he goes over class.  He's a very quirky teacher..last semester he got mad at the NPV or MRR (I forgot) formula on excel and it was quite.....weird...but he is a nice teacher.  I clicker is needed in this class and can help out your grade a lot.

This class is mandatory for all business students. The tests are very hard. If you study the book, do the practice and real aplia assignments, you should be okay. Do the practice tests.  It's a hard class but I learned a lot and got an A.

Go to class for clickers. The calculation questions on the exams are really easy, but the conceptual questions are out of nowhere. Read the book if you want to have a shot at those. Hard to pay attention in lecture. Aplia is a waste of time, but you have to do it. Don't go top discussion, do the problems in the book instead. He laughs for no reason

exams are very hard. ESPECIALLY in the fall semester. Discussion section easy and so are iclickers & aplia HW. Focus on exam study because his exams need good comprehension of material. Also, do the practice exams.

Really really nice guy so it's hard for me to rate him badly bc he's so willing to help. He's answered every email I've sent him asking content questions and even gave everyone a point back on this online assignment bc 1 question was vague. Some tests are tricky, be prepared to work hard (projects, 4 exams, weekly hws) but u can get an A like I did

He knows what he's talking about  but uses the worst analogies. always puts the simpsons or something into his examples which make them sound stupid i.e. duff bond. I got an 88 on a midterm that everyone else averaged a 70 on, but I actually like the class so it probably just depends on how interested you are in finance. kind of annoying. i-clicker

The WORST professor I've had in 3 years, so far. Took FIN221 in spring 07, got a C, had to work butt off for it. Exams are insanely hard, definitely harder than previous semesters. IClicker is stupid, pointless. Homework takes 6 hours every week to do; most out of any bus class I've ever taken, useless for exam.
He loves the Simpsons and constantly talks about it.
Structure of the class was a little unorganized and the tests didn't reflect the material from class very well.
Really fun class, you don't have to go every day because towards the end he starts doing lots of I-clickers so you can catch up if you miss a couple.

A pretty good teacher. He really makes things interesting. His laugh gets annoying from time to time. You HAVE to go to class because he gives you "clicker" questions that count for a part of your grade. There are 4 tests, but makes the 4 tests that we have not over as much material. final is optional if you did alright on the 4 previous tests.

Pretty good teacher. He makes class interesting. He has a pretty weird laugh. His tests can be tricky, but as long as you study you will do fine. The final is optional if you do good on all 4 tests during the year.

He's absolutely enthusiastic of teaching his class. He knows his stuff and were able to use vivid example to apply his concepts. Exams take about 80% of your grade. Just go over his previous exam questions and read textbook twice then you should do well. Highly recommend.

Very personable, funny, easy-to-talk-to professor. Tests are decent as long as you read the book, go to lecture, and do all the practice problems he gives. HW's are online and easy, project is easy. Overall, a great class!

the tests are ok actually if you spend enough time to study.I spent three days to study each time.The calculation is easy if you can do the problems from the bk,the difficult part is the conceptual questions.Make sure if dun only read the bk,but also his powerpoints then you should be fine.Many concepts are similar to the previous exam so do it.

He may know his stuff but can't explain it at all.  Class is boring and exams are hard!  The previous exams are easy and the ones for this semester would be totally different....no comparison!  TA's (and discussion) aren't much help either.  If it wasn't a mandatory class I wouldn't even think of taking it!!

Tests were easy - he gives out all old exams to study from, and they're all MC.  Optional final.  Have to go to lecture for I-clicker questions (which never work), but never discussion.  Genuine, good guy.
never went to discussion. Attended lecture for the i-Clicker points. Easy class if you read the book and do the homework. Easy tests. Optional Final exam. Somewhat entertaining lecture.

Mike Dyer is a gift to mankind that too many people take for granted.  He is an excellent teacher and makes the material interesting.  The class is hard if you are lazy and never study, and easy if you put in some time.  The tests are straight forward and easy if you know what you're doing.

This guy's jokes cant be any more stupid and pathetic.  He spends about half the class laughing to himself about some dumb joke about South Park.  The class is easy though.  By the way, turn your mic down.  AHHHHHHHHHHHH!
One thing to say... "Ahhhhhhhhmmmmm"
Interesting class, his tests were satanic at times though...
Need about an 87% for an A. You need a week to study for his tests. Conceptual questions are the hardest part of his tests since there is no way to predict them. The second project takes FOREVER.
alot of work

Great class.  It can be tricky and you'll probably be frustrated at times but you'll learn and hopefully like it.  Dyer is a great professor.  He makes class fun and the best part is watching him laugh at himself.

I find this class to be amazingly hard, especially if you don't read.  The curve is VERY generous because people do horrible on the test.  If you've taken Fin in the past, it probably won't be anything new, but if you have not, it blows major.
Difficult tests.

Funny when he's not trying to be. Gets excited and voice goes real high. Lecture only worth it to watch how hilarious he is. Exams are comprehensive but easy, each online homework is 20 minutes tops, the book is all you need. You'll still learn a great deal, but in the end you'll be amazed how little effort you needed to pull off the A.
Dyer changed the class this semester, now 4 midterms and an optional final.  The class has a decent curve.  Homework is now done online.  Not a bad class, not as hard as it sounds like it used to be.

For one, Dyer is a really nice guy. If you need help, he is there. The only bad thing are the exams. When going to lecture, I felt that I understood everything going on. When exam time comes, I am shocked by the types of questions asked. Where does he come up with this stuff? Studying non stop will not help you there. Only take this class if needed

This may be the hardest class I've taken so far at U of I. Be prepared for the tests to be nothing like the lectures. Lectures are easy. The tests are not. Make sure you get a good TA because it will make your life much easier. Dyer is a good guy and really tries to make class interesting, but you'll be sick of the Simpsons by the end of class.

Wow! What a hard class, but interesting content.  Prof. Dyer tries to be funny, but really it can get old. ALWAYS goes the full 50 minutes so don't plan to get out early. Fair in giving days off though (post-exam etc).  Get a good TA and things will be okay.  Exams NOT related to stuff in lecture - just do the challenge problems in the book!

Dyer was a good teacher...he has a really weird sense of humor but he knew his stuff, his slides were straight-foward, and his exams were difficult but not impossible, plus he only takes the best 3/4 tests.  And he's also really good about answering questions, esp. considering he teaches a class of like 1000 people.
OK, for the entire semester i went to the lecture less than 5 times(and still get an A), his humor is the worst you've ever heard and his head can't stop shaking.

Prof. Dyer is hilarious!  His jokes are great - they really keep class interesting.  The Simpsons have a special place in my heart now.  The assignments are difficult though so you should go to your TA for help.  Definitely get a head start on the assignments.  Prof Dyer is approachable and funny.

Lectures are pointless because his notes do not give examples that help for the tests. Exams are near impossible and I guessed a LOT...hopefully this guy stops teaching soon....oh and his humor SUCKS.

What was I doing at his lectures? Well, reading newspapers, occasionally taking the notes he was scribbling in his slides, catching up on other homework, sleeping, thinking if I gonna ever pass this class and wondering what the heck he's talking about. Guess, that says a lot about the class.
The exams are hard! It's a little shocking once you're done with the exam. I don't think you really know what to expect. His sense of humor is very interesting (not in a good way).
No Comments
It was an easy class and Dyer is a really likable guy.

I didn't pay attention at all in lecture and LITERALLY guessed on tests, and still got a C. Pretty easy class, make sure to go to TA sections to get full credit (it comes in handy later to get that C). Nice guy, jokes pretty lame. Good time to catch up on Daily Illini.
you can get a B wothout even going to his class, just dont miss TA's meetings. and also, be ready for the dumest jokes you've ever heard from Michael Dyer.
He seems like a nice guy, but the tests suck.  He goes over problems, but not conceptual questions(which are ahlf the test).  Definetely one of the worst classes at U of I.
the guy's like a big teddy bear and funny, in a weird way.  didn't find the lectures too helpful...the discussion sections and reading the book help.

I was expecting this class to be a breeze, but the tests proved to be harder than necessary for the topic at hand. Overall though, if you step up and keep on top of your work, there's plenty of opportunity to get an "A"
Dyer laughs at his own jokes, but is overall a good guy.  The tests were hard, but TA section helps...if you get a good TA.
crazy, somewhat different professor.  watch out for the exams they take work.
good professor

Ok, if you aren't into simpsons, its gonna be somewhat painful...every lecture incorporates mr. burns and homer simpsons into it at least 3-4 times. Other than that, I think that reading the book is very helpful and a smart thing to do before the exam
The lectures are easy - the test is NOT.  The TA's are evil and I began loving this class and hate it now.  Avoid if possible!!!
be over prepared for tests as he goes very in depth and its hard to know what to expect....and hes not fun!
Very Hard to reach in an incredibly over sized class.
He's a nice guy, good at explaining topics.
i will never encounter a more painful way to learn. it simply isn't possible.
No Comments
What a Troll
what a bundle of joy
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Rogowski is one of the nicest people and professors I've ever had. He really cares about his students and is there to help. If you put in an honest effort into his class he will recognize your hard work and try his best to help you succeed.
Great Professor!

405 is a hard course. Audit itself needs a lot of recitation, and it is very test heavy. Two exams will determine your final grades. However, Ed is definitely the best audit professor. He respects each student and will care about not only academics, but anything about us. He can give many real life examples for understanding complicated concepts.
Ed is by far one of the greatest professors I have had a U of I. So passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. Loved the class and him!
Ed Heske is a super fun teacher. I had him for IB 462. He has lots of cool stories to tell and honestly cares about his students. His class is challenging but rewarding.
He is great.  He knows all of his students and really cares about them.  Go Ed!

It started as a regular course, but he turned it into an online one immediately following the first lecture. It would've been nice if he were competent with moodle. However, my biggest problem is that he's very misleading. He'll tell you that a source is optional reading and won't be on the test, but then he'll have a part of the exam cover it.

Robinson is extremely lazy.  He turned a regular class into an online class and often used "guest lectures".  He did not have office hours, just provided a phone number.  He put little effort into this course.  The discussion was a waste of time and the TAs were unfamiliar with the material.  The lecturesassignments were disorganized. Horrible.

Robinson is extremely lazy.  In geog 110, he turned an in-class course into an online course.  The professor did not hold office hours, just provided students with a phone number to call. The lectures he assigned were rarely his own work.  His lectures were  disorganized. The TA's were not helpful and discussion was a waste of time.  Terrible.

Would not recommend taking International Conflicts through him. His quizzes are about as picky as can be and online lectures are boring to the extreme due to his whispery voice and constant repeating of himself. It isn't that difficult to pass but the amount of effort would be much better served through other courses.

I'm not a fan of this class. He's very lazy. First class he decided to make this an online course, we only meet with our discussion sections and TA. Prerecords his lectures so they can just be put on Moodle, more than half the time he has "guess lecturers" - a youtube video of someone else lecturing. I wouldn't take him again.
Trick questions absolutely ruined this class for me. It's a technical class and having annoying quirks like tricks and pop quizzes isn't helpful. Still it's a cool topic.
Online explorations are given with horrible, horrible instruction.
Puts anyone trick questions on quizzes and exams that make the class more difficult than it needs to be. Lectures are pretty interesting and he seems to care a good amount the subject.

Have had him for 379, 479, and 473. Great professor, relaxed grading policies, easy exams, fun class. I've learned a lot about GIS and Cartography from him. Very nice and personable guy. Even met us at Murphy's for drinks after our 479 and 473 finals.

Dr. Robinson is very passionate about the application and theory of GIS. The class was a little tricky but, if you go to his office hours you'll be fine. We never used a text book and I advise going to every single class. Pop quizzes and attendance checks are given at random.

Robinson is probably one of the best professors I have had so far at UIUC. He has a strong passion for GIS and does his utmost best to pass his knowledge to students. I would recommend any class with him, especially this Advanced GIS class. He truly shows students how important and useful GIS skills can be in today's world.

He likes to give out interactive examples, such as video speeches and open debates. Although his class doesn't seem to flow through a rigorous structure, it is logical and also fun!(He is very hot....)

This class was a lot of work, but it was well worth it. This class allowed me to obtain a multitude of different skills. With these skills I am now able to create successful maps. Robinson is also a great professor who is extremely knowledgable on the subject. He enjoys teaching his students and is always willing to help them with the material.

I took the online version of the class with Professor Robinson. Even though this class lacked some of the "atmospheres" found in a regular classroom, it was very well organized and had a lot of content. Professor Robinson was extremely helpful, clear, and understanding. He seemed like a great person and an intelligent professor.
Very helpful but not very clear. Very tough class.
Best professor at Stetson.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Has good intentions but it seemed very scattered and unorganized at times. Overall great guy who enjoys teaching but it didn't make me really interested in the course material.
Nice and friendly. Not too difficult - would recommend for a teacher.

This class is usually one of my favorite hours of my week. Seriously, Andy makes learning fun and always provides really helpful feedback.  I would definitely take a class with him again, even though it's a lot of work.
Dude changed my life, respect.

Unbelievably vague, we've been using a computer program called R and I feel as though we have received NO guidance as to how to use the program. While trying to complete the take home exam I realized how little we have actually been taught and most of the information he has asked us for is foreign to me.

Professor Eisinger is REALLY smart. He started off the semester a little nervous in front of the class, but has improved a lot and I can only see him getting better. He is very approachable and is awesome in office hours. I would definitely take a class from him again
Best grad student instructor I've had.  Cares a lot and takes time to make sure we understand the material.

Not sure if Ed Dole still teaches at U of I. I am a 2007 graduate. BIO101 was my very first class of my freshman year and I struggled big time. I hated science. Ed reached out to me and helped me through his course, made me love and appreciate biology. Today, I am a science teacher thanks to Ed. Thank you!!!
He cares about his students

Though there were assignments regularly and time is needed for understanding the knowledge, Ed is really nice, patient and kind. I enjoyed having his class though I spent much time doing its homeworks.

IB 100 second 8 weeks online with Ed Dole is miserable.  Ed Dole is the most mysterious man in the world. He thinks that everyone loves Biology as much as he does but they don't! This class is not for anyone who doesn't have a girlfriend that is a Bio major.
Horrible class, worst professor. Tons of HW and assignments, hard exams for online section. Avoid this gene class, it will hurt your gpa. Love Life, leave ed dole!

This class is horrible, the professor is insanely bad, the worst professor ever in my study. Avoid this class, it will spend you tons of time for a gene class. And the assignments and exams are hard for online sections, don't hurt you GPA! the worst class

He is the worst professor I have ever seen in this school. Believe me, don't take his online class to fulfill your gene requirement. He gives tons of hw and very hard assignments and exams. This is only a 100 level class, he thinks you are already pro in biology. This is awful for an intro class. I swear I ll not take any IB class after his class.

This class was horrible. i had SO much busy work. during lecture they randomly take attendance and all he does is show you links which is COMPLETELY pointless; you don't learn anything. Dole treats you like a 5th graders and this class is like you are back in middle school science again. AVOID!!

Way too much work for a gen ed class. LOTS of assignments that do not help on the exam. I wouldnt be bothered by this, except for the fact that the website he uses is extremely difficult to navigate. Additionally, he also posts assignments at random times that will sometimes be due in only a few days. There's an easier gen ed out there, kids

This class is ridiculous. WAY too much work for an INTRO TO BIO class. He doesn't seem to understand that. His design of the class is terrible. Website is useless, homework assignments are useless, lab material is useless and the book is useless. DO NOT take this if you're not a bio major, you will regret it, guaranteed.

He seems like a nice guy. Tests are not bad, he gives good review online. The main problem with the course that almost EVERYONE experiences is the ridiculous amount of homework assigned. It's at least 2-3 assignments per week, usually taking up to an hour to complete. His online moodle site is confusing. He really needs to limit the homework.
Awesome guy, the class was a great and pretty easy overview of biology, encouraged me to look into bio further and I wound up with a minor in ESES.

I took ib 100 for a gen ed and i soon realized i could have found a better option. the only good thing about the class is that there is a ton of extra credit (7%) but besides that the class is unorganized and his lectures are impossible to follow. i only got an A because my friend is a bio major and helped me. try to pick something else...

If you are looking at this class to meet a gen ed, pass on it. His lectures are boring and impossible to follow. The website he uses for the class is very complicated. He makes the class difficult for an 100 level course.
Great guy he is so nice and helpful.  He really cares about his students.
He breaks down Biology thoroughly when you don't undestand a topic. He's also very friendly

Super easy class. Sometimes unclear at times but if you can read the text book and study exactly what he tells you (he pretty much gives you the test!) you will do fine. No curve, but lots of e.c. opportunities.

This class is fairly easy but there's a LOT of busy work.  A lot of your grades depend on the TA.  Mine was pretty ridiculous in that I needed to state the obvious when explaining something on an assignment or I'd get marked off for it.  Random in-class assignments (often just signing your name) for points. Way too much work for a gen ed class.

Class was easy if you do the work. Ton and tons of busy work with assignments and such. I myself earned 6 percent of extra credit and earned my A. Study hard for exams and it will pay off. Overall really nice guy though.

Ed Dole is so nice. His lectures are mind numbingly dull, but attendance is pretty much a necessity. Random lecture activities to take attendance. Take-home Assignments every other week. Exams aren't too shabby. Overall, not a bad class, but those take-home assignments might drive you a tiny bit crazy. Oh and don't even bother buying the text book.

Ed Dole has been my favorite professor at u of i. He is a really nice guy who helps his students anyway possible. The class was very easy as long as you do the work- the homework was difficult but we usually covered majority of it in discussion so it wasn't too bad. Overall, he's an awesome professor.

IB101 is a very easy class. I had an A+ going into the final. Most of the information you will ever need is on his website and power points, but he does give easy in-class assignments to take attendance. Overall Dole is very helpful and seems like he truly cares about his students (which is rare here).

Ed is such a nice guy! I had him as my professor and my TA in the education section. He really explains things until you get it. He is the most helpful teacher I've had here and I highly recommend him. Not much homework to do and he offers a lot of easy extra credit. The tests are also extremely easy!

He is a really good teacher! He can be kind of boring during lecture and the homework is hard but the tests only cover main concepts-not specifics and he is so willing to help you in any way possible. You can also get a TON OF EXTRA CREDIT! I really recommend the class to get rid of a gen ed!

Ed Dole is a great professor.  He is very helpful outside of the classroom.  If you do not understand the homework, he will gladly help you.  Discussion sessions are sometimes tedious but are very helpful.  DO THE EXTRA CREDIT.  There is 6 percentage points possible, and the work is not too difficult.  He is very nice and helpful.

boring class. we think someone taught him how to make links recently and he took the idea and ran with it.  study objectives and do the extra credit.  homeworks are kinda hard sometimes and are worth nothing.

Lectures are very boring and there's a lot of busy work. The class itself isn't too difficult. Lecture notes are found online. If you study the lecture objectives, then you should do fine on the tests.
Boring lectures but useful notes.  Website is hard to find what he used in lecture on your own.  Lots of busy work.  Good discussion sections that clarify concepts.

Professor Dole was a great professor. He made very clear outlines of what we had to know for exams and posted them on the course website. The lectures are a bit boring, but Dole is very helpful outside of lectures. The biology textbook is never needed, and exams are all multiple choice. He doesn't give much HW either, so I recommend doing the EXCR.

Oh, Dole. Like your outdated, senile uncle trying to teach you biology. ALL OF THE NOTES FOR EACH LECTURE ARE ONLINE. Tons of busy work. If you work moderately hard, you should be able to get an A. LOTS of extra credit opportunities. In all, a decent class for the 4 credits (with lab).

He is really nice, and he will help you whenever you want to meet with him.  The class isn't too hard either, but if you have questions, you can go to the class website and post them, and he usually answers in a few hours.

Great for a science gen ed because it is not too challenging at all. For each lecture, there are lecture objectives. You really only need to study and know those for the exams. Dole is very accessible and helpful if you need him, and the discussion sessions are also very informative when you don't quite understand the lecture material.

The review sessions are definitely helpful, and I've received a lot of help through the Web Crossing board they have set up. Very boring class though, no matter who's lecturing ... I usually doze off in there, and I rarely sleep in any other class.
Make sure you go to the review sessions.  tests are pretty easy.
everything fort this class can be found on the internet.
No Comments

dole has a mustache, and maybe thats why he talks so muffled and monotone? but the class' website is really helpful for studying and understand the material. discussions are vital; often homework answers are given. not as easy as i expected. but a good choice for a sci gen ed.

Voice makes it very hard to pay attention. Make sure you have a good TA and be sure to go to lab or discussion classes. Concepts are more easilly explained there. Lecture notes are online and exam questions are taken from lecture objectives. If you study the lecture notes, you'll be fine.
good teacher but the class is harder then you think
His voice is sooo monotone, I can barely understand him.  He is boring by nature; he tries to make us understand, but its uneffective.  One of those teachers that you can live or live without.
similar to high school Bio.  easiest class i have taken at U of I.  good lectures, concise and to the point.
a little confusing to understand sometimes but very helpful.  Likes to do little skits at lecture, usually doesn't help explain the concept.

What a sweet lady. She is very informed about the subject matter. She has everything written on the website, very organized and is good at responding to questions. Not intimidating at all. Also, only a couple of tests, which are easy if you study and go to lecture. No final, but a final project. There's a lab section as well, which is easy. Take it

Dr. Herrstrom is such a sweet lady and definitely knows what she's talking about when it comes to geology. The tests are super easy as long as you study. They're even easier if you pay attention to her lectures, which can be kind of boring at times. Overall this is a super easy gen ed.

Really easy class. Prof Herrstrom is very clear, just do the study guides and practice tests using the powerpoints and your notes. the tests combined are worth %30 total so they hardly matter anyway. You have to go to lecture and Lab. Do the Homework, Geotours and prepare for the tests and you should get an A.
Such a great instructor. Super helpful. Overall really easy class, and knocked out two gen eds. Lots of extra credit given. Almost never used the book.

Very helpful and passionate teacher. Responsive over email or in class. Tests are somewhat difficult, you have to study a good amount. You get points for attending lecture and there is always extra credit options.  Pretty easy to get an A.
Such a nice and helpful teacher. Attendance is mandatory for lecture points. Kinda alot of work for a Gen Ed, but still somewhat easy.

She is an awesome teacher! Very passionate about what she teaches and is extremely helpful. Lectures are not mandatory, but she does have "lecture tutorials" at random times which account for 4% of your grade. 3 exams, pretty tough, but a nice curve. This class is easy, & you just have to complete all the work. Go to discussion.
good teacher. just not something i was interested in. pretty easy class. attendance isnt that mandatory as long as you study a bit for the tests with the online notes/study guides.
Very inconsistent with grades, incompetent TA's, no communication about coursework, labs and exams are poorly written, and the course field trip is useless.
Really easy way to knock out 2 GenEds!!!  Professor Herrstrom is a very good teacher and she's really nice

If you need an easy QR2 this is the class to take. every lecture is online, no need to go. the discussion is a computer lab where you do extremely easy assignments on excel. no final exam, just a poster project. 3 exams are hard, but curve is usually big. also, 5 extra credit assignments worth 100 points each=amazing.

After class with Sandy, your life will never be the same.  She is the SWEETEST and nicest lady, and she built our class into a community and family.  She is truly the most positive aspect of my career in the College of Education.  She completely prepared me for success in student teaching and the professional world.  SANDY ROCKS!
sweet

Her CI classes are super easy- as long as you come to class you'll get at least a B. Few exams, and she tells you the answers ahead of time. Super awesome though b/c she's so nice and would never say a bad thing about anybody. ever.
Wonderful, wonderful professor!! Such a sweet lady :)
SANDY ROCKS!

The first exam was tough, especially if you haven't taken a law class. 13 quizzes (lowest dropped), 3 exams ( all open note) + final. Requires a textbook, but I found a PDF online for free. Readings will take 2-3 hours per week. Quizzes and exams generally get easier over time. The teacher is accessible. Advice: on exams, write as much as you can

Endres is an awesome professor who really loves what he does. His ACE 306 class can be intimidating at first, but if you go to class and pay attention the material shouldn't be much of an issue. He posts all his lecture outlines on canvas, but it's more effective to be in class. There are 2 midterms and a final, all open note and a group project.

Very nice. Goes over each case studies in class  and doesn't force people to answer if you didn't read. Might seem intimidating at first, but he won't scold or berate anyone for asking obvious questions.
3/5 workload if you read each case before class. 
1/5 workload if you show up, take notes, and listen about wacky crimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Endres has the best lectures and you don't need a textbook. Attendance is not mandatory but it is literally the only way you will pass the class. Never had a problem with a grade and everything was returned quickly with feedback. Didn't think this class would be interesting at all but ended up really enjoying it because of prof endres
A true hidden gem of a professor within the ACE department at UIUC. Genuinely cares about your success and encourages sharing of personal stories/experiences to further classroom discussions.

Very interesting material. My advice is to go to all classes, keep up on the readings, and see him in office hours if you have any questions. If you do these things, studying for the midterms should be a breeze, honestly.  Just review class notes and readings. Oh, and take more notes than what he puts on the slides.
Interesting material. But you have to show up to class if you want to pass.

Had him for Food Law. Great course overall. He is extremely knowledgeable and has practiced intellectual property law in the area of food patents prior to teaching. Two quizzes with two parts each, take-home and in class. Both were very lengthy. Midterm was pretty tough for the entire class. Just do the reading and go to class and you'll be fine

I enjoyed Professor Endres' class. He's a good teacher, he keeps lecture interesting most of the time. Reading is usually not required if you go to class. I would definitely go because the book is incredibly boring. Questions on the tests and quizzes are from lectures. The tests aren't too difficult and are curved.
Excellent professor who is more than willing to help. Lots of reading, but it is worth it.

She is a great teacher and very fun to be in class with but the material is pretty hard. You do have to buy a textbook and there is a lot of homework attached to it but you don't have to attend lectures to understand everything.

Definitely take ACE 300 with her. One of the best professors I've ever had-- very engaging lectures and so many EC opportunities! As someone said it's pretty hard to get a bad grade in this class. was always willing to help me and several others after class and genuinely so caring and funny. tests were tough but just study study study!

Dr. Endres is a great professor. I was nervous coming into microeconomics after struggling a lot with calculus, but Dr. Endres helped me and some other students during office hours. She is a great teacher and a very fair grader. Definitely take her for ACE 300

Very Good professor. Knowledgable on Applied Microeconomics and the material covered in class. Homework is fair. Very tough grader on tests. One wrong final answer can result in a 10% reduction of test grade even with proper formula usage.
Super sweet and gave so much extra credit that it was hard to not get a good grade. She is very accessible and will give you clear explanations on your grades and why you got what you got.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Super accessible outside of class, and cares a lot about students succeeding. She is very generous with extra credit and practice exams are just like the real exams.
Professor Endres is super sweet and she cares about her students and the class a lot.

Prof. Endres is legitimately one of the kindest people I have ever met. She really cares about her students, and it is clear that she is passionate about the class. The class required a TON of reading, and a lot of quiz and test questions were pulled directly from sentences/paragraphs in the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Really like Professor English! He's really humorous and interactive!!
Three points of extra credits save my life.
You can understand that why this professor only have 1.8 points at RMP. He has too many requirements for us and unbelievable picky.

The lectures are a complete waste of time because you would be better off reading the notes yourself because he doesn't even read through them with any order. The few times he did his own examples they always had mistakes in it. The other problem is lack of examples. You will be lucky to have seen 1 similar problem to your exam question. 2? No way
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I feel like Prof English gets a bad rap and I don't really see why. He gives weekly HW, but they don't take much time and are easy if you know the material or reference it regularly. There's 3 midterms and a final, but so far exams have been fine. His lectures give an intuitive understanding of material and make the class easy as long as you attend

He just likes to show off and grades you extra harsh if you don't come to his boring lectures. All material is based on some previous professor's notes and his lectures are still a mess. He is the kind of person who likes to brag about a PhD degree in math but is not genuinely qualified for real research.

Not helpful at all, does not care about students' learning (cares more about showing off own knowledge), very harsh grader that looks for trivial excuses to dock points, his own understanding of the material is dubious at best given how mediocre his lectures are, very arrogant and rude

His lectures are mediocre. I've learned the exact same concept but with much better professor before. But his expectations are just way too high. Homework questions often require proof methods that we never learned before. The same thing happens for exams! The second midterm was so freaking hard and has questions we've never seen before. Worst ever

Horrible professor. Cannot teach effectively to save his life. Went to his office for a scheduled meeting before midterms, told me he "didn't want to waste his time" if I didn't grasp some of the concepts already. No textbook, and no other professor taught it, so it's not like you could seek help elsewhere.
yep, it is hard. But, I am glad that I am learning. To the axshxle who wants to take it easy, get real.

You literally cannot miss a second of this class if you want to understand. Will mark you absent if you are late. Also, mutters extremely fast and assigns insane amounts of homework. Needed for business but one of the worst classes on this campus. Awful teacher
Great material, Prof talks in a low voice so can't hear in the lab. Entire class is in computer lab. MUST take for excel skills. Gives lot of partial credit. Go to Office hours.

Teacher seems like a nice enough guy but simply can not get class material across to you. There is no structure to the class and he rambles on, often under his breath, making it hard to take notes. Very intelligent man but is not capable of teaching effectively at undergraduate level. Avoid class like the plague
Homework problems take a ridiculous amount of time.  Totally avoid this teacher if at all possible!

This professor is extremely nice. You should attend class, because he gives you in-class problems. Some problems are extremely hard but he is very helpful during office hours (much more than sending an email) I learned a lot about stats in this class & understood Econ 203 better after taking this class. He tries to make the problems realistic.

She grades too harshly and expects you to have an answer every question. The way her grading syllabus is set up is ridiculous. Three things hold the weight of your entire grade so if you do not do that good on them you're more than likely not to pass the class. And some of the things she says can come off rude, but she doesn't really realize it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tbh, class was draining because she's always looking for one answer and she starts out each class so chill but is easily pissed off and has certain expectations that you just have to 'figure out' I liked the content and when she's in a good mood the class was enjoyable but more often than not she's in a bad mood and couldn't leave it at the door...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is stubborn and inflexible. If students don't respond to her questions, she just skips to the next slide. She is a graduate student but wants to be addressed "professor" otherwise, she may not respond. She has high expectations on students, prone to giving compliments but uses phrases "Can anyone elaborate" My friends share a similar sentiment.

She gives a significant amount of extra credit, but the overall course policies and grading are harsh and strict compared to most other classes. She sometimes gives out her personal items and likes to listen to students' opinions regarding the course content. However, she lacks a broad understanding and a tolerant personality.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: AE202 has 2 lectures per week and one worksheet assigned each, due one week later as well as random surveys and writing assignments. There are also multiple projects that overlap with each other throughout the semester. Lectures are read off the slides and not helpful. Difficult not to get an A+ but it is the most pointless waste of time.

Very strict/perfectionist with assignment submissions and invents a million different excuses to refuse to even grade them.  Luckily her class is very easy and was the one place I could relax this past semester.

Yes they do assign a lot of homework but it's usually all very trivial and they are very caring if you have a reason for missing an assignment. Lectures on the other hand were mid but because of the course content being introductory and too diverse, not because they were bad at teaching. Overall good professor, time consuming yet easy classes

Elle uses they/them pronouns which messed with me for a bit but they'd restate their pronouns at the beginning of lecture and not bring it up again. Their lectures are very intricate for the average freshmen but helpful for future planning. Fantastic labs, very helpful professor who's always willing to help.

They are incredibly dry and monotone, reads directly from slides. Slides are very poorly made, extremely small text and high info density with little indication of whats important and whats not. Also very rude and condescending to students. When asked questions that are tangentially related, they don't know.
Lectures are monotonous and we have been doing derivations for 4 weeks now. Homeworks are very time consuming and are not related to the course content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I found her to be very down to earth and pretty funny at times. You can do the homework based off the slides. Sometimes it's hard, but always useful. You can tell that she's very knowledgeable on the material and is happy to explain anything if there's questions. she explains things step-by-step and makes the topics relatively easy to understand.

Assignments must be done in the requested format. But since the grades per assignment is graded very late, we won't know whether our formatting from the earlier assignments are correct or wrong. Assignments can be deducted up to 50% off just for formatting penalties.

She knows the class material backwards and establishes clear and easy-to-follow grading criteria. She's tough in design reviews, but gives constructive feedback and pushes you to come up with the best possible design. The class has no tests, but two group projects that make up 45% of course grade. There's a good amount of extra credit too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She fully and completely understands the material but is NOT the best at the "teach you like you're five" approach that the top professors have. Not bad, but not great, and the class as whole has a system that's very difficult to get used to.

Great Professor! She does care about the students, which can't be said for all professors. The lectures  and tests are pretty straight forward. Can be tough at times during design reviews but she's just challenging you to make a better design. If you like to design and build than you'll like this class. I would recommend her as an advisor as well.
Not helpful and does not give credit unless you do it the way she wants.

I was told she was good and taught well but I think something has changed. Her lectures are not too helpful when asking her questions. She has in-class assignments but you can figure out when because she posts them on her lectures so you just have to look ahead of time. Homework started easy but got harder and is not really covered on the tests.

One of the better professors Ive had. For most of the course she explained the material pretty well, but at the end she seemed to burn out. Exams were easy and focused on the basics of the material. The course was mainly centered around the two design projects and she discussed them a lot in class which was helpful.

She did a decent job teaching the class.  Lectures were pretty good.  Tests were extremely easy,  which was fine but also means no curve.  I think ME 370 was one of those classes that nobody really hates, but nobody really likes it either.  Just do the homeworks and don't fall too far behind.

I've never took any Chem class in my life, but her class made me love and understand it deeply. Her lectures are really easy to follow and she gives demonstrations too! Also, she really cares about students and is pretty chill, I'd def recommend go to office hours at least once. And, for exams, she provides bunch of resources (past exams, hw, etc)

Haven't taken chem since HS, but the class wasn't bad at all. First exam, I got an 85%, but my friends scored that or higher all semester. I fumbled my own grade lwk. She's really chill and lowkey funny, curved exams, and clicker pts helped. Matthew was THE most helpful TA. Do TB readings, they helped a lot, especially when you are confused.
Best chem 101 professor. You'll get lots of homework, but it helps you get practice.
The best Chem teacher you could get for 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. McCarren so much! I learned so much in her class and truly had a strong understanding on all of the topics. The exams are very similar to the practice exams and review sessions are offered. She has a great personality and is super understanding.
Elise, girllllllll, you need a raise!! Urbana needs to make u head of the department or summmm. keep slaying girl, u r THE best. xoxo choose her
She's a really great lecturer, and she's really nice. She made the material super easy to understand, and when she would do demos they were always cool.
She was amazing!! She waits for us to actually write down the material during lectures

GREAT prof! She made things very digestible. The class is set up so that we write the notes with her as she writes on her iPad, really good set up and good pacing. It is a lot of information and can be a shock if you haven't learned chem in a while but she is always open to help and her office hours are helpful.

Dr. McCarren was an amazing professor! Lectures were pretty helpful, and her teaching style truly helped me learn the content. Notes are taken in every lecture, but overall were beneficial in learning. Her practice exams are pretty similar to actual exams, so if you are able to do the practice then it should transfer pretty well to the exams.
Sweet professor, for sure would take again if needed. Good at explaining.
Overall if you are on top of your game, you will pass.

Dr McCarren is a great lecturer and very easy to understand. Everything flows well together. If you need help, please go to office hours. She is much more personable and kind than you'd expect there and it is a great environment to do homework and ask for help. She has demonstrations every lecture that are very cool so that is a plus.

Dr McCarren is the best. She is super caring and always wants to make sure you succeed. Her course is structured understandably and moves at a reasonable pace. Go to her office hours!! She is so much more personable and funny than you would expect and I went to almost all of them to do homework and hang out.

Professor McCarren was an outstanding teacher. She taught course materials very well, and I think her teaching style was great. Prof. McCarren gives practice exams before every exam, which was extremely helpful. Her office hours are beneficial, and she's great at responding to emails and answering questions. Prof. McCarren is the best.
go to office hours and read the textbook! she is super sweet and has amazing lectures, as well as fun demos. my favorite professor ever

Lots of demonstrations! lots of opportunities to better understand the material (explanation videos, office hours after lecture + before exams). As someone who's bad @ chem, taking this before 102 was the best decision I ever made! She's very kind and never lets you feel stupid for asking questions or struggling :)
This is by far the best professor at UIUC.

Professor McCarren is an incredible professor. Her notes are very clear and she's easy to follow. Her expectations are clear and she's easy to communicate with and responds quickly to emails. I highly recommend taking Chem 101 with her.

Prof. McCarren is amazing. While her class is most definitely not an "easy A", it is 100% achievable to receive the grade that you want in this class as long as you work hard, study, and pay attention. Her lectures relate DIRECTLY to the exam material and are CLEAR and CONCISE. Don't cheat on the textbook HW, and do all the past exams!

McCarren was genuinely one of the best teachers I have had in a while. She also encourages you to do well. Going to her lectures is important because she is able to explain everything you read about in the textbook. I recommend reading the pre-lecture chapters and taking notes before you attend the lecture. Her office hours are great too!!

Elise makes it clear what should be known by her students. If you are struggling, it's on you to get help, which is very easy, as she makes herself very available. She posts practice exams around a week before each exam which are almost exactly what the test is like.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor you could have for Chem 101! I took this class the my Fall semester 2022 and it was great. Elise explains everything thoroughly, is very accessible for office hours, and responds to emails quickly. She genuinely cares for students' success and provides students with resources and materials that helped us achieve that.

I took this class because I didn't feel ready for Chem 102 and it was very helpful.The fake labs are a lot of work but the tests are almost identical to the practice ones. Lectures are also easy to follow. Prof McCarren is super nice and I would recommend this class to anyone who wants a review before taking Chem 102.
Would 100% take again, felt very prepared for every test, clear explainer, wish she was also teaching higher level chem

Skips over course materials and chapters in the book. Lecture explanations are very brief. Exams are nothing from the problems she shows during lectures. Lots of homework. TAs aren't much help for labs because they don't even know how to answer questions.

The best professor you can choose!Amazing lectures, the demonstrations were always the best part of lecture and she makes learning chemistry more fun. A lot of work but if you do the studying and pay attention to everything in lectures you will be fine
PS: study early for the final!

Professor McCarren is a great lecturer who really knows how to keep a class engaged. She does demonstrations in class frequently that are quite fun. She is also extremely kind and messages students after exams to congratulate them on improvements from previous exams. This class has a fair amount of homework, but nothing unreasonable.
Cares about students and gives lots of resources!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's definitely the best professor for chem 101, she give great demonstrations during class and you can tell she wants to make sure everyone succeeds in the class. She also does office hours after lectures where you can get help on homework which is nice. She also likes making connections with students. The best professor I've had so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McCarren was amazing! Her lectures were enjoyable with lots of demonstrations (and cute dog photos). She notices improvements in her student's grades. She does lots of practice problems & makes concepts understandable. She is the reason I started to love Chemistry again. I highly recommend taking CHEM 101 with her. The TAs are great too!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was and is amazing, she always brought a smile to my face, and she had great demonstrations. She was really good at explaining the material too. I was terrible at chemistry in high school, and she actually made the material make sense. Love her!
She was awesome, she explain things thoroughly and simply. 10/10 one of the best professors.

Great professor, made content super easy to learn. Extremely accessible outside of class and willing to answer questions. Fun demonstrations that make chemistry interesting. Shows dog pictures before test which is a plus. Lots of homework but easy to finish if you pay attention during lectures/discussion. Tests are hard but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is great, as long as you show up to the lectures and discussions, and do your work you will do fine in this class. It is difficult but all chemistry is.

Professor Elise is an amazing instructor. I have always hated Chemistry with a burning passion and went to having it as my favorite course this semester. She explains topics clearly. I recommend this class to people with a good work ethic. She responds to emails and grades tests promptly. She also notices when her students improve. Best class ever!
If you have to take Chem101- take it with Elise!!! She's the best. Very understanding and reasonable! It's not the easiest class, and there's a lot of homework, but she makes it bearable.

Amazing lectures, explains concepts thoroughly with practice problems. I got 58% on my first exam (before the curve, didn't study enough before). Next exam, I went to office hours before and studied much harder and got a 77% (before the curve). She emailed me noticing how much I improved from each exam. If you are worried about CHEM 101, don't be.

McCarren has made chem 101 very enjoyable. Her lectures are interesting and easy to understand. She gives lots of material to study with for the exams which is nice. I always feel prepared for tests. The labs are sometimes hard but they are done in groups and Elise is always available to answer questions. She is awesome!

She is amazing! She totally changes my mind about chem. She balanced tedious conceptual knowledge with the funny experiment very well. Her sense of humor makes me love to watch her lecture. Her test is all about the textbook homework and lecture knowledge. She will even hold an online review session on the test day.

Elise is the bomb! She made chemistry a piece of cake. Lots of homework, but it's all easy points and you come out on the other side really understanding it. extremely helpful in office hours twice a week and very easy tests if you do the homework and pay attention, lectures are also very easy to follow, entertaining, and graced by her cute dog

reviews.comment: LOVED Elise for Chem 101 this fall. Even with all the lectures online, she made them very informative. Go to her review sessions before exams, do practice tests, review any practice problems from hw or lecture, and you should be good for the exams.

Awesome chem professor! I wasn't looking forward to this class as I'm not a chem person, but she made the concepts easy to understand and grasp. You can tell she cares about her students and wants everyone to succeed. I loved the lectures because she always did experiments which made the lectures more interesting, too.
Great professor, make sure to watch her basic skills videos they will be super helpful for chem 101
Great lectures, Easy to follow

She's definitely one of the best Chem professors. Her lectures are thorough, and easy to understand. Exams are slightly difficult, but good feedback is provided and through the other assignments it's easy to get a high grade in the class if you don't do so well on the exams. A real gem! Cute dog, great personality, entertaining lectures, you can tell she enjoys her job and is passionate about helping students grow. Some of the TAs aren't the best at explaining concepts, but Prof. McCarren always replies to emails and does an amazing job explaining things!

As long as you are able to understand the material and are able to apply it to more broad things, you should be fine. Review the past exams and you should be fine when it comes to taking them.

I took chem 101 with McCarren and it was such a great introductory class. I definitely felt prepared for all the exams and homework. If I ever had a question she would clarify or the TAs would help. Never felt like the exams were set up for the students to fail and all the homework we got was appropriate for the class.

Elise was a great Professor. Her Lectures are informational. She does a lot of demonstrations need to go for the I-Clicker points. You have to do the readings. All in all no real complaints about the class.

tests are literal memorization only unless you are an OCAML expert. The lectures cover actual course content abstractly at best. Worst part is that this course content has few viable alternatives to learn from.

Just the worst honestly. Makes your try to memorize everything and gives little to no help.
The lectures may feel challenging at the start, but it becomes easier once you engage with the material. Elsa is always helpful and patient in answering any questions

Truly the most awful class I have taken at university. Read the reviews below to understand why.

Her teaching sucks, assignment specs are disorganized, and she genuinely does not have good intentions with respect to giving her students a good learning experience.

Absolutely miserable professor teaching insufferable topics in the worst way possible. Avoid at all costs.

It is a nightmare to take her course.
She is not good at teaching. Also she was hostile to students.

Elsa is really knowledgable about compilers and also helpful on Campuswire when people ask questions. The exams are similar to the MPs and she also takes the time to create multiple versions of practice exams.
