reviews.comment:
Elsa knows the content inside out. Her CS421 is well designed, but very content heavy. Offers a lot of extra credit opportunities in quizzes/exams.

Lectures are a bit confusing sometimes, but she's very helpful on clarifying anything on Campuswire.

Overall an underrated Prof that actually cares and wants her students to succeed even if difficult.
Very disorganized lectures and confusing materials. Three midterms and a final with 35% percent of grade. Making CS421 the hardest CS course, which should never be that hard for other professors.

I think Prof. Guner is a really kind professor, she is willing to give underperformed students a second chance, she shows empathy to her students and pushes them forward. I believe I can definitely do better if I reach out to her for help earlier.
She is very hostile and rude. Her lectures are also very incoherent and impossible to follow. I ended up learning the material quicker from other sources online.
The professor is very hostile towards and rude to students. The assignments and EXAMS were full of bugs but there was very little accountability. Take this course with Beckman instead.

Elsa seems like a great person, but the class could use improvement. There is little Professor and TA support on the forums compared to any CS class I've taken. The methods Elsa employs seems a bit dated. HW and Exam questions are always buggy on PL. Weighting of scores makes little sense.
It was the most ridiculous class I have ever taken. No bugfix throughout the entire semester, irresponsible, and purely "on-your-own" class. The Final is 40% of your grade so good luck.

Sets overly-high standards. Did not explain the program used in the course at all, more or less "figure it out as you go." Prepare to spend all your nights and weekends working on ridiculously complex assignments.
She is impatient, always be distracted from the content she is delivering, and jumps to a totally irrelevant subject, very confusing and time-wasting
She is not able to convey the material clearly, basically delivers nothing in her lecture.
Run!!! Professor Beckman is so much better! I use his lecture from past semesters to survive the exam.
The exam has nothing to do with lectures, she is a poor lecturer, not sure why she becomes a professor.

She is supposed to post a quiz every week. She didn't week 5, and only did in the middle of Week 6. Because of a lack of communication, she expects you to read your email every day. She sends emails on the weekend expecting you to check it, and I ended up missing 2 weeks worth of quizzes week 6 because of the lack of communication, so I'm dropping
She literally teaches nothing... but everything shows up in the final, and we have zero practice
Very irresponsive on Piazza. Pretty much always releases HW late, and most of them have repeating issues. Instructions almost always unclear on HWs and exams.
Her 421 is all about memorizing your MPs. And the final exam is sooooooooo heavy.
She is trying to make the class funny though the subject is not interesting. And she gives out practice midterms and finals before exam, and the exams are just shorter version of practice exams
Not bad. Would be great if code generation was covered, instead of spending the first month introducing OCaml.

Elsa's great. Sometimes unclear, but she means well and she's funny, and the course material is really interesting. Sometimes she'll get caught on little things (like other reviews say), but it works out. Ignore the bad reviews from 2013. Some students decided to take solutions into an exam and got caught, so left 1 star reviews. :(

Very hard working and very dedicated to her subject. Don't expect sympathy for laziness. Attend office hours with her and the staff to answer questions. She is a professor at a top CS university and expects nothing less from students. That being said I didn't find anything in the course to be unfair.

Avoid her! She think she is the law in this class. I haven't seen any other class has such unreasonable policy. If you write down something similar to her example or posted hw solution on a exam question, you'll be caught cheating. And if you don't get high score on exam questions, she'll take away your points on similar hw problems.

If you get an exam question from the MP completely right, she will accuse you of memorizing the solutions, which to her is cheating. She specifically makes her cheating policy vague to catch students. The lecture slides haven't been updated in more than a decade. Avoid this professor.

Pros - Interactive during lecture, Knowledgeable in field. Cons - Explanations often given in complicated terminology (Sometimes feel the need for a translator during lecture), doesn't make material interesting, medium-heavy workload, has a notecard policy for exams but doesn't tell the class about restrictions to catch people cheating. AVOID HER!!
I question her personality. She set up a "plan" to lower students' exam grade simply because she think the average is higher than her expectation.

She might be the worst professor in this CS department. She don't teach well and her policy is just unreasonable. She'll take away your homework points if you don't do well on similar problems in the exam.

Decided to make class more difficult semesters this semester by adding 2 MPs and 9 HW assignments. She's a boring professor much like other CS professors, but it doesn't help the material is so dry and theoretical.

Pays great attention to detail and as another reviewer said, she is overly pedantic and gets hung up on little things. That being said, she is an enjoyable teacher who lectures with extreme clarity. The content is hard though, very much so. But listening to her lectures online for the exam made me realize I needed to post a review.

She made her learning kind of systematic, so you can get a good grade by following steps without comprehending. She's very helpful, have almost an excessive office hour, and seems like she is addicted to answering questions on newsgroup. it's sometimes unclear of what the homeworks expects, but is no problem if you read past/sample exams.
Overly pedantic, and not the best at explaining things.  She's not terrible or unknowledgeable, but her lectures aren't stellar.  Just do all the MPs and HWs, and it shouldn't be too bad.
Strict, but generous. Course is well organized with moderately heave load. Getting good grade is not hard, if you do every homework.
No Comments
Serious, strict professor, heavy load, but well organized course (MP's every week). Hard to get good grade.

Class is pretty interesting, I enjoyed the topics but the structure of the class could use a lot of work. The HW assignments can be pretty long and the code needed to complete them can be unclear some weeks especially in the later half of the class. Teacher is nice, assignments graded leniently though, exams are alright, group project can be long
This lady cannot teach

Her notes are so unclear, we only go over a minimal amount of code in class and then the entire HW assignment will be a coding notebook with multiple questions that cannot be answered from the code notes alone. Code notes are also a complete mess and ridiculously long. HW's started out fine and then became impossible due to insufficient notes

Unclear notes, typos in HWs, typos in exams, HW assignments that are may to long and take may more time then they need to be. Class isn't hard, grading is pretty easy, but its frustrating how long the HWs take and how we can lose points for errors in exams/HWs. Class seriously needs to be cleaned up

This HW rn is crazy, the class is fairly easy but the notes and HWs are a complete mess. The homeworks are way to long and tedious and the provided code is very insufficient to complete the homework especially with no chance to ask about it in office hours because of the exam. Ridiculous

First few homeworks were long and tedious however grading is fair. Grade distribution is great as it isnt test heavy; tests are fair with cheatsheet. Projects are with a group like 207 which helps alot in finals season. Overall interesting material and great professor, if you've taken 207 id take her for 430.

Good professor and a great structured course. Her notes are really hard to follow so make sure you watch lectures carefully and write your own notes, otherwise you will be very confused with homework. Highly recommended that you attend class (even if it is over zoom). Very homework and material heavy but it teaches you a lot.
Online class that is very easy to zone out of (as all online classes are). Really not too difficult if you are carrying over 107 knowledge

She is an amazing lecturer and very thorough . She also answers any questions. Weekly labs and homework are relevant to course material and are graded more than fairly. Lectures can seem to get a bit long and boring at times since it is an online course, but you can always go back and rewatch. Overall, amazing professor.

Statistics lectures are only going to be so interesting. Tori does a good job of clearly explaining concepts, and her notes are very thorough. Everything you need to know for the labs will be in the notes. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit as well. The only thing I dislike are her exams, which involve almost as much writing as AP Lit

Good person, horribly structured class. Grade is dependent on labs, lab attendance, 2 projects, and final exam/project. Lecture is so boring and her slides are just scribbles of color. reviews.comment: He is fine at teaching but is very rude and demeaning if you have anything that occurs outside of class (mental health, family emergency, etc.) that may impact your work. He accepts requests for extensions and then calls the student suspicious in front of the class.

ACTUALLY HAD FOR ANSC199 (wasn't an option) I can't recommend Dr. Emmert enough!! He gives great lectures and I always felt like class was worth going to. He's very understanding of life situations and will do his best to help set you up for success. His exams weren't too difficult, and he was always super clear and upfront about his expectations.

Dr. Emmert was not present for the actual labs, but was in charge of grading. The quizzes he sends out weekly are not difficult especially since he also gives you lectures that give you the exact answers.

I took ANSC 199 so disregard to selected course. Dr. Emmert is a great guy who you can tell is very passionate about Animal Sciences and for this being the first time this class was run I would say he did a pretty good job of organizing material and making sure it prepared you for his exams.

Love this professor! Really charismatic, really approachable, and despite me going into this class not caring whatsoever about animal science, I came out of the class having learned a surprising amount about the topic and being way more passionate about the subject! The course is super fair, I became a better writer, and the course was awesome!

If you enjoy self-guided learning, this class might be perfect for you! Professor Emmert seems to believe students grow best with minimal support. The goat fr. He is very likable and understanding. Material is pretty interesting and he is passionate about the subjects. There is a lot of writing in the course but other then the tedious nature the course is a very easy A.

This class was tough. The professor's lectures were disorganized and hard to follow. Asking questions often led to dismissive answers, discouraging engagement. Professor Emmert was amazing. He is very caring and lectures very well. Class was a super easy intro class and had maybe an hour of work a week with one group project that is presented in discussion.

ANSC 205 will drain you. The amount of work that has to be done for only three credits is insane. If you take this class, you will be writing papers from the first week of class to the last. Professor Emmert is a great guy but requires a lot out of the students. I would suggest if you have to take an advanced comp, take a different class.

Super kind and so amazing! Class was super easy and was a good way to get easy credit!

This class makes no sense at all.

This class honestly just makes no sense it, he is all over the place when he lectures, what he lectures on does not relate to the papers, or the readings. He is very well learned, and he will try to help you in any way he can if you just ask. Great professor and person.
He is extremely well learned, and he will help you in any way he can if you just ask. Great professor and person.

Prof. Rota and I = simpatico. He is the nicest, most helpful prof. I've had in college. You write 3 papers and have a very short and easy final exam. He e-mails you the required readings which are concise and interesting. If you need to knock out a 200-level Humanities, Rota is your guy. He has a habit of wearing LaCoste polos every class. CLASSIC!

Professor Emerson is an amazing teacher. He truly makes the subject material interesting (I came into the class thinking it was going to be super boring). The assignments are definitely manageable within the allotted timeline and they are frankly quite easy.

Prof. Sebastião is great. I had him for HK 201. He's a really sweet guy who is willing to help you with anything. He helped me find professors to contact for undergraduate research positions and helped me land my first research position. My biggest piece of advice is to raise your hand in class and answer his questions.
CHLH 314: Intro to Aging. I took this class during Fall 2013 semester. Class wasn't difficult but you gotta work on the assignments. Field trip help me a lot to understand what was going on in class.
Great teacher and great class. He's super nice and will help you with whatever you need. Easy A. Definitely take him if you get a chance.

One of my favorite professors I've ever had! Course work isn't super hard and exams are all online. Attendance is mandatory but you get two excused absences and extra credit opportunities. I would recommend taking any of Emily's hdfs classes!

Emily Hurth is the best professor I have ever had at UIUC. She cares about her students, and it shows! We had 2 exams! A midterm and a final! Both were open-book/open-note online! Does not take attendance, but has 10 unannounced in-class assignments that are worth 10 points and few extra credit assignments that are also unannounced and in class!

Emily has been my favorite professor at UIUC. I have taken all 3 of her classes, and I wish she had more. HDFS 408 was such a fun course, and it was generally easy. Attendance is not mandatory; however, she has a few in-class activities that she will spring on you throughout the semester without always saying when, so be sure to come to class!

She is a knowledgeable professor and I really enjoyed listening to her lectures. The class itself it not too hard as long as you make sure to stay on top of everything. Your grade is mainly based on a few larger assignments (3 short essays, a presentation, and a cultural portfolio) so just lock in for those and the rest of the class is chill.

Learning Arabic online wasn't easy but Prof Saadah made it a lot less difficult than it could've been. She focuses a lot on having students be able to speak coherently and is a stickler for pronunciation. Beware of the cultural portfolio, just about all of us forgot about it until the last weeks of class when there were only 3 events
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She needs to improve on how to teach a language because her way of teaching is not helpful. I would recommend you take the course but expect to teach yourself. If you have any other questions, she will help you but she is very disorganised. She does not clearly state the grading scale and gives a ridiculous amount of homework. Quality over quantity

Eman Saadah was the worst professor I've had at UIUC. She was very harsh with the non-Arab students in her class, often criticizing them in a way that is not conducive to learning or effective teaching.

Too much busy work. Class structure and criteria is messy, note taking structure very unclear, and assignments were too general. Class isn't horrible but it's unorganized which makes me anxious. I dropped it.

can seem intimidating at first, but is super flexible with students and does everything she can to do well. A lot of homework in this class, but she is chill about due dates. participation is important!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Best professor on campus by far!! She makes everything crystal clear and is there for the students!! If all the teachers taught like her then we would all be in good hands

good professor who knows the Arab world very well. She is open-minded and funny at times. The class is not that bad; there are pre class readings, discussions, a couple papers, and one presentation by every student. The work was a bit more than I expected, but I learned a lot from this class.
Awesome teacher. She is very helpful when it comes to cultural confusion, and the readings she puts up are fair and quite interesting.
Although she seems very strict and slightly intimidating, she is extremely helpful. If you show genuine interest in the class and ask her for help, she will do everything she can for you.
Eman is very knowledgeable, explains the material well, and is very invested in helping her students succeed.
Helpful. Shows genuine interest in students succeeding. Not as hard as other reviews would lead you to believe.

Emily assigns the most difficult articles. What sucks is the other students in this class. They are awful and ruin any actual learning. She is not the only professor for this class but it's obvious how much she wants us to learn. I wish this class was smaller.

This was an online summer class which means it was a ton of work in a short amount of time. Emily gave my essay loads of feedback. I'm not into theater, but I learned how to write better. We read a ton for a summer class. She made videos to help which was a nice touch. She clearly cares about her topic and the essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: After taking Emily's first and second Theatre history courses, I can say she makes an effort to improve her teaching practices. This class was very laid back, only having to read a play every week and discuss it in class. At the end of the week, a reflection was due. It was very easy to follow, and I was interested in a lot of the plays.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While very energetic and a good communicator, I often found that her teaching style of DOTD 103 was not for me. There's constant lectures and weekly assignments that feel like there's no point to them. I do think that the class is an easy A but honestly sometimes I would question my sanity in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Goodell often gets sidetracked on things that don't matter and I often find myself wondering why I am in her class. It is very easy to disengage from her class and from my back row vantage point, no one is paying attention. Emily Goodell frustrates me more than I can put into words. I am confused weekly.

For a theatre class she takes her job way too seriously. She is blunt and rude in her feedback responses for your projects/homework again for a THEATRE class. This is not broadway yet she seems to think that way. I wish I could give her a zero rating, because no one should be this concerned about a dumb gen ed class.

Horrible TA. Makes the class way more stressful than needed. Over 1,000 people in the class and tries to say people are cheating with similar responses to a short play explanation. Takes her job way too seriously and the class is painful because of it. Gives no explanations to anything. Avoid at all costs. Not sure if she does any work in the class

He has always spoken with great humility. Moreover, his classes are quite engaging, both in terms of content and delivery, and he consistently goes out of his way to provide substantial assistance to his students. He makes an effort to help students earn as many points as possible. He is my absolute favorite professor in the school's CS department.

The lectures were held over Zoom. The prof did a good job with lectures and sharing relevant content about the game industry. Most of the grade is from the projects and learning how to use game engine(s) to create games. The HW and exams were on PL and reflected course material well. Invest time into the projects, and you'll be fine. Prof is nice!
Fantastic lecturer with awesome material and real world examples. Bends over backwards to make sure everyone is taken care of
He's very active in communicating with students.

He introduces the math will use in this course but never talk more details, which make lectures unclear. It's ok since this course is a CS course instead of a Math course. But, as a cs course, especially most students do not too much graphics experience, he didn't teach too much programming either. Not a hard course, but you'd better not take.

Lectures were useless. Midterms ended up being reading quizzes. MP's were implementations of things Unity does already. Theory is fine but why have lectures that don't pertain to graded content. I wanted to learn how to make vr games and he completely failed at teaching that. Be prepared to teach yourself the final project worth 44% of your grade.

You can tell he is genuinely interested in what he is teaching, and takes as much time as needed to make sure the class understands the material. Very well organized lectures, the 3 midterms are fair, and the 4 MPs are interesting but can take some time. Not having a final exam is a plus!

Professor Shaffer is hands down the most amazing, intelligent, sweet, helpful and nice professor I have ever met in my entire career. He's that professor who will go out of his way to help you. He's extremely understanding of any situation and genuinely cares about his students. His course was wonderfully organized & he explains concepts very well!

Professor Shaffer is really underrated, not sure why.  He's actually a fantastic educator - listens to and addresses students' concerns, makes himself available for office hours and questions, and he's clearly really delighted when we engage in the course material. Definitely would recommend for any course he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Eric Shaffer is the best! He really cares about his students.

Decent lecturer. I'm not sure how much of the CS 357 curriculum is his work, since it seems like Andreas is more in charge, but regardless it is VERY well laid out with lots of online resources. He's not as engaging as Andreas in class, but not bad by any means.

Some extra credits in class so go to class regularly. Four MPs with first two easy but last two take some efforts.  No curve, but exams are pretty easy and straight forward if you read all the lecture ppt. Really helpful professors. It's rare to see professor answer almost all the questions on piazza (hardly ever happen in other cs course)

Professor Shaffer is the best! It should be made clear that classes like CS 103 are organized by professors but taught by TAs, so keep in mind that the low ratings for Professor Shaffer's involvement are deceptive. If you go to his office hours, you'll find that he is more than ready to help.  Our textbook for this class was free and online.
Pair up with someone. You will not get by without it. He's awesome.

This class is awful. The TA's are unhelpful and he teaches the class as if we were programming geniuses even though this class is programming for people who in theory have never seen a computer before. Avoid this class at all costs.

If I didn't have a programming background, this may have been difficult. Shaffer isn't a very active professor, but I got by. The only annoying thing was the book. It was $100 and we used it once for readings that were covered in class.

Worst.Class.Ever. The prof. barely shows; when he does he sits in the back and barely helps. The TAs are in charge, but serve no purpose either. Attendance is mandatory even though all the lessons are online! TAs only walk around to "help" you, but their arrogance & condescension make it impossible for them to articulate or clarify anything.

This professor was one of the worst I have ever had. Towards the end of the semester, I continued to think "I don't know how many more of this professor's lectures my grade can sustain." It seemed like each lecture was just a survival attempt for my grade. The other professor did a good job, but this professor rambled and flew through his ppts.

I strongly disliked this professor. He abused his right to use power points, lectured too quickly to take notes, does not put his slides up before lectures, and generally completely lacked interest in his students. In general, he came off as lazy and uninterested, and if we had had a more concise textbook, I never would have gone to lecture.

He and the other professor for the class were both incredible lecturers.  I was enthralled a lot of the time.  I did well in the class though, so maybe my opinion isn't representative, but I thought he was great.

This guy is the worst professor I ever had. Makes everyone in his classes buy his overpriced textbooks to line his own pockets. The instruction when I attended this class in 2017 was given by a TA that did more than half of the instruction and question answering in Mandarin, which I don't speak. Kudeki also arbitrarily compelled me to leave ECE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor, very knowledgable about the subject. Remarkable that such a senior level faculty member at UIUC ECE puts in so much effort into student learning.

Kudeki is GOAT in lecturing. His textbook is crystal clear in explaining things and he knows the material like the back of his hand. His lectures are engaging and very intuitive, clearly explaining the whole logic flow of EM modelling. Homeworks are guided problems that build on each other and very enjoyable. Recommend 5/5.

His lectures may seem a little disorganized, but he always manages to present the information efficiently and effectively. If you go to lecture and give the class the attention it deserves (i.e go to office hours, ask good questions, and participate in class), he will make it known on your final grade.
In class lectures super interactive, chill in grading, a very pleasant experience to work with this professor. UNDER THE PREMISE OF consistent lecture attendance.

Great at explaining concepts! Professor Kudeki is very chill, and is very accessible outside of class. Exams were very fair, building on the homework material. Overall he's a great professor, you should have no worries as his student.

He uses his own lecture notes so there is no need to purchase anything. The material for both 329 and 350 were hard and his teaching method can be intimating and confusing. His exams are just like the homework so remember to review them. Just write down the end-result for his formula derivations and you'll be fine. Its easy to get a B and higher.

He's an excellent instructor and  know ALL the material presented in class. He does occasionally go off on tangents, and the course material is difficult, but the class is well structured, and reviewing the homework solutions & past exams will easily allow you to do well in his classes.

Professor Kudeki has a bad habit of jumping ahead onto tangents during lectures and losing students. Sorting out what is important and not was difficult. Paired along with a course with a suddenly steep learning curve, this can be overwhelming. But he knows his stuff, SO ASK QUESTIONS! Fortunately, class notes and T.A. office hours were redeeming.

Great Lecturer, and he will help you through any topic and is extremely accessible. Also a lot of people my think his classes are hard and they are, but it is the material itself that is difficult and Kudeki does a great job of explaining it.

Did not have him personally for 329 but the notes from previous semesters that were provided by him are what got me through the class.  On a personal level though, I have seen nothing good about him.  As an adviser he refuses to make eye contact and despises of you if you are struggling at all...NOT what an adviser is there to do!
Awesome. Teaches with so much energy, you can tell he WANTS you to get excited about the material - and it works.

An amazing teacher. Runs around the chalk board, mostly he is just amazing. He knows what he is doing, I understand what he's doing, but sometimes it seems like he is trying to lose everyone that is stupid, which is great.

He's a fantastic teacher, but the material can be difficult.  Mostly I love his accent and his voice.  If I could get an audio-book read by him, I'd buy it and listen to it every day, regardless of what book it was.
No Comments
Kudeki is a great lecturer.  He is enthusiastic (after drinking his huge coffee) and keeps you following along in class.  Everything he teaches sticks.

Pretty nice professor with a nice pace in class. The exam can be a little confusing with vague questions, so make sure to create better cheat sheets. Pay attention to homework as it is worth more grades.

TA's did a good job grading (left a lot of feedback) overall, and are generous in regards to late assignments and whatnot. Professor is active on Piazza, and is obviously enthusiastic about what she is teaching. No surprises on the exams, if you do the homework and study the lecture notes you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor was one of the best at UIUC. She is passionate about the class and it shows in the quality of the class and lectures. The professor is one of the nicest people. Homework is the right balance of challenging and useful. Graduate students present a group project. I would highly recommend the professor and photovoltaics class.

Dr. Ertekin is a great professor. She is both knowledgable and passionate about the subject manner. Coming to her lectures isn't a burden at all. The class homework is very straightforward and the whole learning experience is designed to teach something rather than to stress unnecessary details. Easily my favorite professor on this campus.

I hated physics before his class and loved physics coming out of it. Lecture is mandatory but the demos and his enthusiasm made attendance desireable. Tests are difficult but enough resources to do well are provided. Would recommend!

Most work is done outside of class with pre-lectures, checkpoints, and homework throughout the week. The discussion and lecture only happen once a week and there are quizzes every 2 weeks so you'll have to do a lot on your own but it's not so bad if you really try. He's super friendly and gives good lectures. Lots of extra credit is offered.
Quizzes every two weeks, and lectures are only once a week, so you have to teach yourself A LOT. He encourages everyone to get better at physics by providing extra credit. I'd recommend for phys211.

Dr. Kuo is the goat, his lectures are very clear and he's so nice, patient, and caring if you talk to him outside of class. I asked him some very supid questions in office hours and he kindly walked me through each part of the answer. I really hope I can get him next semester for PHYS211.
Very nice professor and lectures are very helpful. Definitely recommend if you took only regular physics in high school to prepare for physics 211.
Professor Eric is one of the best professors I have had. He is very patient and encourages an environment where it is okay to be wrong/learn from mistakes.

Eric is an amazing guy and is patient when people are confused. He offers a lot of extra credit and bonus points when you improve on something which I appreciate since learning happens over the entire semester. His lectures are recorded too which is very convenient. You do have to teach yourself a little but lecture is only 1x a week so makes sense

Overall Physics 100 was light on course work and content which made keeping up with concepts very easy. He answered questions very well and always had a smile on his face but often got very passive aggressive near the end of lectures if anyone left early.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kuo's lectures include helpful demonstrations and lots of check for understanding questions. There are opportunities for extra credit by correctly answering 'clicker' questions and by attending office hours. There is an online quest in the CBTF every other week, plus a midterm and a final. I recommend him for Phys 100.

Professor Kuo is easily Top 10 professors I've ever had. His lectures are collaborative and comprehensible, his office hours are very useful and all the TAs, LAs, and himself assist greatly in helping you understand the material.

Very nice professor, I agree he does kind of teach as if we're in high school but the material is very similar to high school physics. The class was pretty easy, just take notes of the pre-lectures and sort of pay attention to lectures and you should be fine.

I took physics a while ago but never remembered it being as confusing as he makes it. Maybe it's because he doesn't actually teach and just assigns videos that seem like they're from 2002. He's sassy in lectures and treats us like we're in middle school. While the grading is fair, I'm just disappointed. Honestly killed my excitement for physics.
He's very nice. I'm a visual learner. Although he didn't do that many in-person examples.. he worked through examples on whiteboard

Eric was a good professor for entry-level physics in my opinion and it was nice working in groups during lectures overall I feel if you put in the effort to keep up with homework you should do just fine in this class.

I would give Dr. Kuo a 5/5, only thing that holds it back is that you are somewhat treated like you are in high school. In every other manner, he is an amazing professor, and his office hours will definitely clear any confusing subjects up. The course grading is extremely forgiving. If you put in the work, you will do well! Very kind professor!

PHYS211 was one of the better structured introductory science courses here at UIUC. Watching prelectures, doing checkpoints, going to lectures, and attending discussion is more than enough to learn and acquire the problem solving skills needed for exams. Professor Kuo is a passionate lecturer that is easy to approach.
He explains concepts well and makes the lectures fun
good lectures, explains very well and takes time to understand and answer all problems students have

I had a rough first semester of college with family matters, and he was the only professor that I felt truly cared about me and my well-being. He is so fun, kind, and understanding. I formed my schedule around his classes this semester. He teaches well and just wants you to learn. He also doesn't want you to compare yourself to others. I love him

I took PHYS 100 because I was below average in my high school honors physics class, and I feel polished after getting through the course. Professor Kuo really helped through the lectures in cleaning up my skills. I totally recommend taking this course for others that were meh in high school physics.

He was basically useless when it came to lecture or office hours. You basically teach yourself from the prelecture/homework. I think I failed every single exam and still got an A, however, because he cares more about participation (aka doing homework, bonus points for doing better on exams). Optional exam at end of semester saved my grade.

Amazing teacher who is really good at explaining to any student. He genuinely cares about his students and remembered almost everyones name in a lecture hall of hundreds. Makes learning about physics very fun. His homework is generally long, but lots of opportunities to get 100% credit on and boost your grade.
Okay instructor
Dr. Wood was a kind instructor, though lectures were sometimes boring. Exams were really easy, and lots of extra credit was offered to offset exams being 80% of the course grade.

Dr.Wood was a good professor. The lecture and content are not too heavy, McGraw was used as our homework points, and iClicker was for our participation, there are only three exams. The work is pretty easy, the only thing I'll say is to be aware that she might teach till the very last minute if you were trying to have another class afterward.

I loved Dr. Wood! She is genuinely so nice, and her lectures were always interesting. The exam questions were easy, and there were extra credit opportunities provided. She is so funny and sweet; I would 100% recommend taking a course with her!

Projected to get an A in the class, Dr. Wood is super understanding and is willing to work with you. She makes her lectures interesting and actually teaches beyond what is on the slides. Questions on the test were never a surprise and were based off lectures, attendance wasn't technically mandatory but she does random checks. Take this class!!
I was in a class with this instructor where she did not respect the pronouns of another student, and I find that concerning. Everyone in class should be respected.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ester is super kind and is willing to help you learn Spanish with a smile. It is clear that she is knowledgeable on the language, but also has a passion for the pedagogy that goes behind teaching people how to speak a language. Grading, assignments, and participation where all super fair. Just put the effort in, and you will receive high marks.

Professor Perez Landa teaches a difficult class if Spanish isn't your strongest subject. However, she understands that not everyone is fluent in the language and just expects a lot of effort. You meet in person to discuss and most of the homework is online.

Ester is quite nice and will work with you as long as you put in the effort. She can be fun too so though I don't enjoy foreign languages, with her it was alright. You get what you put in for learning languages.

Said he experimented this semester by giving us 2 midterms and a final instead of 1 midterm and a final as was done in previous classes. Lots of students ran out of time during the second midterm which led worse grades than anticipated. Prof Larson said he would consider giving us a curve at the end of the semester, then ended up not doing it.

The second test was impossible to finish in the allotted time, and he recognized that. Said he would consider curving if we deserved it, but never curved. Lectures moved really quickly, and attendance is mandatory. Should be an easy A, but he has ridiculous tests. Take the other professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was legitimately the worst and most bullshit class I've ever taken. Do timed tests where you have 15 tabs open and are scrambling to decode a trick question even though you know everything sound fun? Teacher is super boring and unorganized. I clickers don't work 75% of the time and never put in any extra credit points.

Would get lost during lectures, so mainly learned content myself. Their are weekly readings, but they're aren't that long. Tests mirror assignments that are given as homework and information in readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Pretty much an excel + stats class. He is a really genuine and kind caring professor, you can tell he cares for the students. Make sure to participate in class and lab for easy extra credit. Help is readily available if needed.

He's a pretty good professor but toward the end of the semester, class started getting a little bit confusing since he lectured at a faster pace. Completely understandable though. Exams, homework, and mini-projects are online via Prairie Learn and lecture is usually just Excel stuff. No physical textbook, uses a free online "Nextbook" instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He's a good professor that teaches well. Class itself isn't very difficult, however it is 3 times a week and attendance effects your grade. As long as you show up and do the work, you'll do well.

Professor Peterson is so enthusiastic about the material he is teaching that it makes it enjoyable to come to class. Lectures are 50 mins and he makes them fun because the materials can get boring sometimes. Genuinely one of the nicest professors I have ever had. Definitely tries to make a difficult subject as easy as possible.

Teaches age-old stuff. Title of course does not match content. he basically teaches statistics that's it. You can learn the same from any site. Wish there were data mining and stuff in this course too. Course is a waste of time and money. He is a good guy tho and willing to help.

Professor Larson is an amazing professor within Gies. Truly shows his passion when teaching and clearly carries out the concepts in lectures and videos provided to us. He also offers tutorial sessions which help us get one-on-one help with certain class concepts. Does give a lot of work but it definitely helps prepare us for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So good! Good pace with material and responds to emails quickly. Stays after class to answer quick questions and is available for office hours. Put in the work for class and it'll pay off. Don't skip class!! It's really useful and the midterm/final exam are reflective of class materials. Homework every week-ish but if you went to class, you're good
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Larson exudes passion and is one of the greatest Professors I have had during my time at Illinois. He works tirelessly prior to and during each semester to ensure the course is well developed and material is presented as effectively as possible. He even wrote his own course textbook to provide a more engaging experience for students!

I consider myself an above-average student, but professor Larson is a very good professor regardless. Teaches with super straightforward examples in every lecture. Super easy to follow along with. Pay attention, do the work, and you will have NO trouble getting an A. On the other hand, if you dont do anything and dont pay attention, youll get a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst prof I have had to date. Goes on talking and talking. No one got anything. Can't explain. Makes you wok like crazy and then does not give a good grade. Lecture heavy. Very difficult questions. Hope I don't have to take another class with him.
Lots of busy work imo. He also uses a honey pot to catch kids using chegg. Be careful with the answers u submit on the quizzes and you'll be fine.

Prof. Larson is a wonderful professor. There is a lot of material to cover in BADM210, but he has a very systematic way of getting through all of it. The Nextbook used in class is also very helpful (and free). If you read, participate, and keep your integrity, you can do quite well in this class.

Eric was hands down the best professor Ive ever had. He genuinely cares about everyone in his large lecture like so few professors do. He knows the material he is teaching is hard and does everything he can to make it easier. If you apply yourself you will be successful and he will be sure of it. 10/10 would recommend Eric to anyone and everyone!

Larson is probably the nicest guy you'll ever meet. He genuinely cares for all students and makes sure everyone is following along in class. There are attendance checks and quizzes in every class. The quizzes are easy, so all you need to do is show up. He gives helpful study guides for both the midterm and final. I would definitely take him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This professor is absolutely awesome. He really cares about his students and making sure everyone in the class understands the material. The course material itself is definitely cumbersome, however, Larson makes sure you are prepared for the exams, gives out study guides, and encourages a lot of participation during lectures.

Mr. Larson is one of the most caring and patient professors I have ever had. The class itself is not too bad and he makes sure to help everyone. He really cares about his students and I actually get frustrated to see when people talk so much during the lecture.

Professor Eric is one of the most involved/caring professors I've ever had. He always tries his best to make sure the class is all on the same page and never gets frustrated doing so. He always supports participation so never be afraid to do so. The class is pretty tough if you've never taken a stats class before. Attendance is graded as well.

He is the nicest and the most caring professor you'll ever have. Always open to any questions and provides excellent feedback. The course is pretty dry and has a lot of statistics, so be ready to spend some time. Study from his slides. Only two tests a semester and a couple of projects. Go to class for participation points.

Professor Eric is outstanding and cares about each and every one of his students. He's always open to questions or conversations after class. Since this was the first time this course was being offered, it was difficult to understand how the tests would be and such but the professor tried his best and was always open to student feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Class is brand new and I was in the first group to take this class. It was basically a statistics class, that was very math heave. There are no tests except a midterm and a final. Homework is only like every 3 weeks, and is kind of time consuming. You have to go to class for attendance points and questions that you're graded on.

He is the nicest teacher and is passionate about the subject. Soft spoken, and wants to see you learn and be better. He tries to make it interesting, but the content is pretty dry. It was difficult to learn the content because it was a little sloppy since it is a "pilot" course. Not a lot of homework and only 2 exams, just go to class.

Professor Larson is literally the sweetest and most kind teacher you will ever have. Always has a smile on his face and is open to feedback, which is great since this is the first year the class was taught. Class was kind of all over the place but as long as you go in knowing that it'll jump around, you'll be fine. Participate, he appreciates it.

Does not provide answers to practice exams. Very tough exam grader, does not give partial credit for multiple choice select all that apply. The material wasn't too difficult but exams gave me some trouble. Average for first midterm was around 50% and no curve was given.

I'm a math major and this is the worst math class I've ever taken. She seems like a nice person but is a bad professor. She is extremely hard to follow and unhelpful during office hours. The assigned textbook is hard to understand. She doesn't provide solutions to practice exams which makes it difficult to study. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Had her for calc III. Not bad for her first time teaching, but the class if very fast paced and you will need to study a lot just her lecture notes. Very organized lecturer though and easy to see the key topics that will appear on the exam. Lots of homework for this class and exam questions are usually like the mock exams. Be ready to work
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: not bad

Course layout v unclear. No excused absences w/o official doc. (even for illness) which is unreasonable, especially since she canceled class when sick but doesn't offer students the same flexibility. HW & practice exam answers are often incorrect. Slides in class ≠ slides provided. Some asgmnts never announced in class but expected to be completed.
You will have to put in 10-12 hours every week just for a passing grade.
Class is tough and she is not a great lecturer but one of the easier teachers for this class which you need because it is so much work. Also get a good Lab TA

If you can avoid taking CEE 300 with Espinosa-Marzal, please do. Horrible lectures due to one of the heaviest accents I've ever heard. Extremely difficult content. Tests are extremely hard, but lets you retake them, which bumped grades as much as 50%. Homework due everyday, but attendance isn't taken. Easy to just leave after you turn it in.
Dr. Esther Ngumbi is one of the best professors I have taken here so far. She is extremely caring for students! Class is pretty easy, just make sure to complete the assignments and it's an easy A.

Dr. Ngumbi is very animated and enthusiastic, but this really is not the class to match her energy. A lot of students are in 110 for a gen ed requirement... the material is almost insultingly simple and common-sense. Still, that probably isn't her fault and she's very kind and caring. -2 points for assigning a group project though. wtf...

Might be the easiest class on campus. no exams, weekly homeworks have easy readings and multiple attempts. projects are very easy. lectures are usually optional and never tested on. teacher is very nice and caring. The best thing is that there is an unbelievable amount of extra credit opportunities available, nearly 10%  if i remember correctly.
Honestly, such an easy class that fulfills a gen ed, boring lectures but you really don't have to pay attention everything is common sense.

This class was so mind-numbingly boring; where the material was always irrelevant either because it was aimed at published scientists, not most college students, or it covered low-level subjects like the story pyramid. This was a huge waste of time and money. Would NEVER recommend. You can raise your GPA with easy classes that are actually fun.

Easiest class ever. You get weekly homework that you have multiple attempts at (max 30 min). You don't have to pay attention in lectures or take notes. No tests, exams, or quizzes, just easy unit projects. Dr. Ngumbi is cool, she doesn't care if you pay attention. My only problem was my TA who had problems with everything and was a tough grader.
Class was easy. Teacher was cool

She was very knowledgeable and cared about mental health. There were weekly assignments that were pretty boring and tedious but didn't take much effort. No exams, just projects that were not very difficult. There was also a large amount of extra credit at the end of the semester, so if you get a decent TA you should be fine.

His lectures were pretty ok but nobody felt prepared for the tests. The homework was manageable and he made sure that we didn't feel overworked but the exams are such a big percent of the grade and the lectures didn't prepare us well for it. He also changes the order of content which is good for our understanding, but makes the class lose focus.

- Content presenting during lectures were unclear
- Said content was extremely different from the homework and other section
- Used the only review lecture to learn new content
- Exams do not reflect the content or difficulty of the rest of the material
- Removed an hour from the final exam without explanation

Very nice to talk to and definitely cares that you learn and understand the material. Unfortunately, ability to teach the material is not great, you need to ask questions to get the full explanation of content during lectures. Lectures are past semester slides rewritten. Routinely late to lectures and tests. Inconsistent with course administration.

Nice guy but not a great professor. Lectures were useful but he usually just read off of slides for the course. Was always very late posting lecture notes and homework solutions, even after students reminded him to post them. Exams were difficult and students definitely felt underprepared for them.

Dr. Escobar does a great job explaining. She does it at a slow pace, so no one gets behind. If you read the moodle presentations and attend lectures, the material will be easy to understand. I would advise being sure that you have the right level of Spanish to be in that class. Otherwise, some students find it challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She doesn't do a good job of explaining anything. Her PowerPoint slides don't seem very organized to me. The topic is difficult but she doesn't make it any easier. She gives an iclicker quiz at least once a week, and she quizzes us on info we learned weeks before. This is by far the hardest Spanish class I've ever taken. Wouldn't recommend it.

This is an extremely difficult class and requires a LOT of work. She could do a better job of explaining the concepts. She always seems to want to rush on to the next concept when nobody understands what she just taught. I wouldn't recommend this class unless you're serious about spanish.

The class is mostly grammar review, so it's not really her fault that it's so incredibly dull. Her PowerPoints are literally the most boring things ever and she does nothing to make the class interesting. She's nice, but so boring.
She's adorable! Mi professora favorita!
good  prof
Rasoul is awesome. One of the best professors I have had at UIUC. Intelligent and kind.

Lectures are crucial. It is very difficult to try and understand material if you do not show up. Prof is good at explaining things, but the course is fast-paced. Ask for help and go to office hours if needed and you will be ok. Homework takes a long time though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is really a gem of ISE. Clear lectures and fair grading. Inspirational and approachable.

My favorite professor in the entire department. Class material is difficult but the course is structured so students can do well if they keep up with the work. Extremely smart and organized. I wish he taught all the courses in the systems engineering curriculum.

This man is one of the rarest professors that possesses a sense of humor at U of I. You joke with him, hes not afraid to clap back. One of the best lecturers in ISE and most memorable one too. He gave everyone who dressed up for Halloween extra credit. Nuff said.
Clear and concise explanations with examples. Emphasizes both theory and applications

EunYi is a kind and friendly professor. Attending lectures is important. Attending office hour is important to get feedback for the final project. The first midterm is relatively theoretical. The final exam requires you to pay more attention to details explained in the lecture. Group project is fun and the professor is very helpful.

Professor Chung was very passionate in not only getting students to truly understand the topics but also actively being curious about them. She provided a great experience through projects that are intended to simulate a real research/professional setting. I enjoyed taking this class and left feeling better prepared and excited for the future .
Enjoyed the class. The professor was passionate about the subject and helpful in lectures and in answering questions. I particularly liked the coding and project aspects of the course.
Excellent knowledgeable Professor!
Terrible lecturer skims over complex concepts, probably a brilliant economist but a lousy teacher

I was really excited to learn a lot in this class as I am interested in this topic. However, he is an incredibly boring lecturer and everyone is on their computers doing something else. If you put in minimal effort you will get an A and he does enjoy talking to students outside of class if you want to learn more.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Esfahani is one of the nicest professors in the department. If you actually pay attention in class, his lectures are great and he seamlessly integrates current world events with his course material. He's always happy to answer questions and take out time to chat with his students. Highly recommend taking a class with him :)

Although attendance is not necessary there are "quick quizzes" or pop quizzes which are easy you just don't know when they're happening. He is a boring lecturer and most of the class is on their computers but he doesn't mind. If you go to his office hours he does like to talk to students and will like you more! If you put in effort you'll get an A!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I cannot describe how great lecturer he is. Funny, humble, and caring about students. He is very patient and has great teaching philosophy. I won't hesitate to take any course with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Caring

reviews.comment: Humble, intelligent, funny. Esfahani seamlessly integrates economic theory, current events, and research together. Some days I only came to class to listen to him lecture. He goes out of his way to make sure students learn and succeed, even if the workload was heavy at times.
Very humble and patient with students
He's humble, one of the best teachers I've ever had. Clear, and interesting slide. Really helpful and wise!!!

Professor Esfahani is one of the best professors in UIUC that I've ever known. He makes sure you get something to learn in the class and he doesn't want you to only care about the grade. He is really helpful if you ask anything both in the class or in his office, very wise and great professor! I recommend you to take his class.
He is the best professor I have ever bee taught so far. In every aspect, he is perfectly great.
Simply awesome. Extremely knowledgeable and best at explaining the content. Has very fair and effective exams/grading system.

Esfahani is knowledgeable, but this does not compensate for his lack of organization and clarity with respect to projects and exams. He discourages hard work by grading sporadically—not according to any recognizable guidelines. Many often complain of professors who disregard students’ workloads in their other courses, Esfahani is one of them.

Absolutely outstanding professor. Extremely clear and very approachable. Class is well formatted, tests were easy, problem sets and quizzes are also helpful. Also an outstanding person from my experience with him. Highly recommend him and his class.

Everything is easy except the tests. The tests are hard because the questions are random and are about the stuff he briefly covered in lecture. There's a quick easy quiz for each lecture which makes attendance mandatory. HW doesnt relate to course and tests are just based on lecture.

This is definitely a fun class. He really makes this class engaging by adding current events or interesting articles he's found in The Economist.There are however, daily quizzes, so be sure to pay attention.
Esfahani is simply amazing. He is approachable and his teaching style quite cool. Plus exams are not difficult at all. An easy A. And a great class.
amazing teacher...easy A given u put in the work
He's very caring and understanding towards his students. And on top of that, he has a great sense of humor. If you just go to class, you'll enjoy this course a lot and most likely even get an A+!

He is the most adorable Middle eastern man and you can understand him perfectly so dont worry! Hes a very easy grader, just do the aplia problems and youll do great.  The final is not accumulative and is short.  Great teacher I definitely reccomend him over the others.
he's awesome!!
Hadi is AWESOME! very open. very caring of his students. He wants the best for your education. If you are a business major, take the econ class with him NOW. :)
Very likable guy. Explained the stuff very well. From what I've heard, definitely one of the better Econ 103 teachers.
This guy is amazing, take this class and get an easy A. The lectures are pretty much mandatory but really its not even that bad.
Great professor, played a kanye west song in class one time. funny and nice, take his class if you can.

He's a super lovable guy.  Tests are really easy as long as you go to class.  I studied two hours the night before for every test, purely off of class notes, and got an A in the class. Definitely take Esfahani.
It's a damn easy and enjoyable class..SHOULD TAKE THIS CLASS! My friends and I can easily get an A+

His lectures were not at all necessary to do well in the class.  The only reason to attend was the quick quizzes he gave as an attendance grade basically.  If I didn't blow off lecture constantly I would have gotten an A instead of a B+.  Besides that, he's a very likeable guy and I LOVE HADI!!!
He was pretty hard to understand and lectures did NOT relate to test!!
Hilarious.
Only thing I didn't like was that there were pop quizzes almost every day in lecture - but they are open note and you can talk to classmates --> easy!  It just makes lecture pretty much mandatory...

quite an easy class. he does have a mini quiz everyday so you have to go to class. the midterm was the easiest thing ever!!! overall pretty good but he does speak about his home country a little too much.
Hadi is so awesome. The class is actually really interesting to go to and he explains everything very well. Mid-term and final are easy. Go to class, you'll understand!

Hadi is so awesome that our class chanted his name numerous times during lectures. He's always laughing and in a good mood. The midterm and final are easy and are very similar to the practice ones online. There are a variety of short online assignments, except for problem sets. Go to class for very easy points. I wish all professors were like him.
Awesome.

This is the greatest professor ever.  If you are considering taking a class with him, stop considering and go do it.  Always laughing, Hadi keeps class interesting without sacrificing content.  He is the master of powerpoint and very clear.  Tests are easy and match the samples provided almost exactly.  Interesting background - great professor.
He's so cute! and a great professor!

Simply stated, Hadi rocks. We all love him. Hes funny, has a very interesting background, and a power point wiz! Daily 1point quizes to keep us from ditching class.. but once you have Hadi youll keep coming back! Great class.. if only he taught Micro..
I love Hadi! Take this class. Now.
He is the best professor I ever had. Take a class with him if you have a chance. It is absolutely worth it.
AMazing...I love Econ now...Esfahani is an amazing teacher that truly cares and is always available to his students. DO whatever it takes to get into his class. Totally worth it..
Hadi Rules!  I didn't want anything to do with Econ and now i love it.  He is the master of powerpoint.  He also made a cool presentation of his life.
He is really funny, helpful, and has a great teaching philosphy, which more people should adopt. He makes learning enjoyable!!
No Comments

This is a role model for other professors to emulate. This professor cares about his students. His expertise is unquestionable, and he knows how to teach a very difficult subject (macroeconomics). We need more like him!
Had him for PHYS401, a class I wouldn't recommend due to the workload. Still, his lectures were VERY helpful and he always answered questions in full.

Will do his best to help you learn and understand the experiments; if it's a condensed matter experiment, he'll help you with the procedure and even do part of the experiment himself (setup, et cetera). It's hard to mess up PHYS403 with his grading specifications. Gives out coffee/tea and cookies on a regular basis.
Very good professor. Grades very leniently. He is on of the darlings of the PHYS department

Lerman posts his lecture notes for the course on his site, and although there are occasional errors, these are great for exam studying. Notably, his exams often ask students to reprove results from lecture. His lectures can be dry, but he covers all syllabus material and a good amount more, if the class is interested (we did measure theory).
Lectures were very good and he was open to questions during lectures. Posts lecture notes online. Tests were easy but heavy penalties for mistakes.

Great lecture and I like that he gives all his notes. However, I do not give a 5/5 since his homework are too easy which are not so inspirational to my understanding in real analysis (i.e. not so honor), and that tests are too memory-dependent. Generally a really nice professor! Definitely take 416H and 427 with him next sem if you haven't already!
Easier than the honors algebra courses in the past. I hope he could cover more materials in greater depth.
Very patient professor.

I really enjoy his office hours and learn a lot from them coz he can give me lots of insights of any questions I ask and elaborate them w/ knowledge across fields in maths. His lecture notes are easy to read and well-organised. He's caring, very willing to help his students to succeed, has a good sense of humour, and is enjoyable to talk/listen to.
The lecture is extremely amazing and he can answer all the questions! The professor doesn't curve your grade. It means that the exams are very easy so that he needn't curve.

Although I did extremely bad in this class, I have to say Professor Lerman is great. Super helpful on office hour. This class is hard for someone never got in touch in pure maths before. I did not get a satisfying grade even though I worked really hard, but this is still inspiring and funny. and most of students in this class do got 90s

He goes through material very quickly leaving everyone confused. Homework is very difficult and the only reason I passed the class is because I memorized the textbook rather than learning from lectures.
Goes over material with little clarification. Poor responses to student questions. Goes through lectures very quickly and didn't try explaining material in other ways.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I've ever had. Explanations are amazingly clear and he really takes the time to make sure you see how the ideas connect. He didn't like some of the proofs as they were given in the book, so he did them differently. Was able to answer virtually any question asked in class.
good professor, very nice, post class notes on line for student to review.  lecture is very clear. study hard and you will be fine.

lerman is a very good professor. this guy knows a lot and he can definitely answer all of the questions you might have, the hard part is the lecture content is so abstract and very hard to grasp. so make sure you keep up the pace within lecture. also, he never curves. so prepare to study hard before exams.

Dr. Lerman is awesome! His exams are hit and miss, but beyond that, he is an amazing professor. He single-handedly restored my faith in the math department at UIUC; I was regularly enjoying and understanding math for the first time since calculus. If the choice is between him and anyone else, take Lerman's class.

Lerman's 416 class was fun. He has a great sense of humor and he knows his content well. He is willing to help students, and you can tell he wants to help you succeed. Even though he speaks clearly, he couldn't explain content well enough for me to understand it. His homework is decent but the exams are hard. Overall, I recommend him.

Tthe best math professor I had in college. His office hour is useful and quite helpful for the exam. The class is interesting and although there are a bunch of proofs , they are not hard to follow if you listen attentively. Exam are somewhat hard but I would say not beyond the materials covered in class. Overall, he is very nice!
He is very hard to follow sometimes. He never curves, and to be honest, his exams are HARD! not recommend at all!

Professor Lerman is a good professor, but the MOST difficult part of this class is that there's no curve. One test was 3 A's, 1 B, 7 C's, 8 D's, 3 F's and there was still no curve (even though there's a mix of grads and undergrads). Otherwise, Lerman has a pretty interesting sense of humor. Encourages questions and doesn't make you feel stupid.

It's very easy to feel overwhelmed, especially in the beginning when he does a ton of proofs. But this class is very do-able with a little work. His tests are extremely fair and straightforward and he gives practice problems almost identical to test questions. He's very smart, and pretty funny. I would take a class with him again.
He knows his stuff.  You learn a lot.  Disagree with his grading methods, but whatever.

His exams are easy.  However, he is arrogant and will give you a lot of discouraging statements. He is not available to help and sticks very strictly to office hours. Just leaves the second his office hours are over. Will even hint that you are stupid.

He is a very good professor, doesn't grade on a curve but his tests are very straightforward, knows alot about the subject and was quite qualified to teach an honors section of 241, highly recommended

HWs are very straight foward. exams are cake. a lot of topics, so you can get lost. but if u apply yourself, it's your chance to learn vector calculus, because he not just know, but also knows how to teach.

Easiest tests ever. I was done with my final in 20 minutes, and I got a 99% on it. Add to that, he does a good job of explaining stuff. Weird sense of humour and possibly obsessed with differential forms.

Poor lecture performance, and homework is a little bit challenging.  She is actually a nice person and generous grader of exam. But it is hard to focus on her lecture. It is very important to go to TA sections if you do not want to lose too much scores due to homework. Most importantly, focusing on worksheet and slide.

Gives out too much work for a 3 credit hour class. Two different online homework assignments due every Tuesday, projects due every Thursday, and both are still due even if there is a test. She messes up a bunch of the problems done in class, which makes it difficult to follow along.

She isn't a very good teacher in general.  She often doesn't do problems correctly in class and simply doesn't explain things very well.  There was often low attendance in class due to these issues.  There often isn't enough time given on exams as well and partial credit is given strictly.

Her expectations are unclear.  Gives the rubric for projectspapers the day they are due or the day before. Takes forever to grade things and provides no feedback. Assigns an absurd amount of reading. Rude when you ask questions. Summer term ended 6 days ago and we still don't have final grades. Truly the worst professor I have had.

This is the third online class I have taken at UIUC and I regret this one.  She assigns MUCH more work than the other two professors I have had for online courses.  She also assigns random arbitrary deadlines, which takes away one of the main points for taking an online class: flexibility!  We have class on Mondays, but work is due all. the. time.

By far my worst experience in a class at the University of Illinois.  This class consists of many controversial topics, however, your opinion is not welcome.  In general I felt disrespected.  Dr. Bauer openly challenged our class and claimed we were not suited to be educators.  However, she was not capable of doing more than read from a slide...

Dr. Bauer is extremely knowledgeable but she has trouble translating her ideas onto us students and in result I am leaving the class feeling disrespected and like I learned nothing the entire semester. There is no flow to the class and the TA's do not do anything to add to the material.

Excellent teacher, so it really sucks that he got fired.  Explained principles very well and made the class fun for everyone.  Even though I didn't get an A in the class, I still learned a lot and wish he could teach me again.  Best teacher I've had at college.
He's is being fired following this semester which is frankly a disgrace.  He is one of my favorite professors I've ever had.  The University is losing a truly gifted teacher

I had him for Psych 100 and he was very clear with everything he taught. This was by far my favorite course so far in college, probably because Eugene was so amazing as a teacher. Very good-looking too! Take a class with him! You'll do well if you put in effort and you'll have a good time too.

He's super helpful in lecture notes, and his quizzes and grading policy is pretty easy. He is great eye candy, and has an awesome sense of humor, so this class was pretty fun, and he was really cool about letting class out early sometimes and giving out treats...even though he was quite a treat himself...:) haha awesome teacher!
He made us take a lot of notes but I think it's because he really wants us to do well.  And he's great eye candy- that sure spiced up the class!

He tries his hardest to make lectures interesting, and when I was getting ready for finals, he let me sit in his office and look at old exams for practice.  My only complaint is that sometimes the quiz questions were a little opaque, but I suppose that's just psychology for you.
best professor I've had at college. he's funny as ****ing hell
He has a good grading policy...and I think he tries his best to make lectures interesting, but I'm not much into that stuff so I didn't like the class too much.

Avoid, he doesn't care about you.

Clearly in the job for a check
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Chris Evans should not be a professor. He rallies up freshman TA's that barely squeezed an A in his class to do all the work and grading for him. Don't bother emailing him, he only answers when he pleases

It's sad to see people in this position at such a good university. I strongly advise not to take his class.

Terrible teacher and even worse human. He hands out all the work to his 14 freshman TA's. Do not take his online course, you will learn nothing. It's all pre-recorded lectures because he doesn't take any time to get to know any of his students. If you try to email him, expect not to her back for days. Don't waste your time; find a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Chris is awesome. The online section of the class is hard. In-person is easier. All grades are given by TAs. Not much lenience for late work.

Really good professor. He's definitely passionate about what he's teaching and tries to instill that into his students, which is amazing. There aren't many assignments in the course which is somewhat daunting when talking about grades, but there were plentiful extra credit opportunities throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Evans is an awesome teacher. He is always very engaging in class and wants his students to learn. He offers a lot of opportunities to get more involved with journalism outside of the class and his class involved real-life reporting. I enjoyed this class so much that I am going to take a class with him again. TAKE JOUR200 WITH PROF. EVANS!!!

Guy is very sloppy and his stomach hangs out, makes sitting in the front row very uncomfortable.
Talks incredibly slow and his class is run terribly with horrible TA hours.
His lectures have nothing to do with the MP all he talks about are random shapes.
Disastrous professr.

CS 225 is a really enjoyable class to take. The professor walks through every step of how the algorithm is developed. Him actually cutting a paper AVL tree and rotating them are by far the best class I experienced in CS. 10% of extra credit, solid exams if you take practice ones, and great after-class Q&A. Highly recommend.
Took him for CS 126 and then CS 225. Had mixed feelings for CS 126 but absolutely loved him for CS 225. Great professor in my opinion.

His lecture puts people to sleep literally. The contents are unrelated to course or we can get little from them. The MPs he writes (not the ones from prior terms) are either unreasonably hard or too vague to understand.

Great guy, hilarious sense of humor, super smart!  Had us all over for pizza, which was nice.  He always jokes that he's not smart enough to be teaching an honors class like this, though clearly he is a genius!
One of the smartest men I've ever met - and he had the class to his house for homemade pizza, too.  Learning from the brightest is always a great experience, so take his class if possible.
Graham Evans is the ****ing best.
He was the best teacher I have ever had.  If you ever get the chance, you should definitely take his class.  He is so excited about the subject and really helpful and nice.
This man is the most supportive teacher/person that I have ever encountered.  He believed in me when I didn't even believe in myself.  I owe all of my successes to him.  Thanks.
Well-intentioned, very hard

Mega Good Professor, really understand what he is teaching and basically answers lots of question after class since he has really deep understanding in this area. U will get a good experience from his class.

Prof. Ewoldt is the best! His class is hard, but he makes it worth your struggles. He is one of the only professors in MechSE who wants you to truly grow as an engineer, relating Fluids content to real-life applications. He loves iClicker, so don't spoof your location, but you should really consider just going to lecture.

Probably the most qualified professor I've had. Taking his ME 310 course right now and it's clear that this guy knows what he's doing. Always willing to discuss material and explains things really well. His course itself is a lot of work but it's not just meaningless busy work, it actually does teach useful skills and concepts applicable to a job.

This guy is fantastic. Want to take him again and recommend him to others. He cares that my classmates and I learn a lot and get good grades. My classmates respect him and so do I. I hope to take his class next year!

Professor Ewoldt is a hard working, intelligent, genius. He, unlike all my other professors, really cares that everyone learns and gets the information they need, but not in the strict, unhelpful way he's respectful and open for any questions, he also has a fun way of teaching while also having us learn. I hope to take your course again next year.
This guy is amazing. He knows so much and is nice to me and my classmates

This guy is fantastic. He is one of the few professors at this university that sounds legitimately excited in every lecture.
