Professor Ewoldt always wants to interact with his students and is always willing to answer questions when necessary. He has a great attitude. I would take a class with him every semester if I could.

He is probably the smartest professor in the ME department and one of my favorite professors at U of I. Unlike many other instructors in ME/TAM, he actually knows what he is talking about. His lectures are organized and logical and he does not simply copy the material from teaching notes onto the board.

Professor Ewoldt is an excellent and engaging lecturer. The downside of lectures is that he split his time with the earnest but much more boring and harder to understand Professor Hu. Quizzes are computer based and extremely unforgiving with no partial credit, however there are retries for each quiz, and the final exam was difficult but very fair.

Really good at explaining tough topics, and wants his students to really understand the material. Always willing to answer questions. There are computer based quizzes, which are pretty tough. Definitely require a lot of study time.

Very enthusiastic about the subject material, coupled with good command of the lecture. Keeps class engaged through plenty of iclicker questions. Strict about technology usage and had a designated area of the lecture hall for its use. If you're seen using anything in the "non-designated" area, he isn't afraid to call the student out.

This professor clearly is passionate about his job and is a good lecturer, however,  he could care less about his students and he is the most arrogant professor I have ever had. They changed the course to include quizzes and I did not pass a single one of them. The structure of this course is garbage and I would never take any other class of his.

Rude. Arrogant. I'll be honest, Ewoldt knows his stuff. He is very passionate about the material. Teaches very effectively. Obviously a smart guy. But, by far the most "full of themselves" professor I have ever encountered. He purposely tries to put his students down and make them feel inferior. Not approachable.
Great professor. His exams are difficult, but he teaches the material very well. Probably my favorite professor at UofI.

Great instructor. Cares about students understanding and not just a letter grade. Go to office hours, will help you through homework and not just give you the answers. Best professor i've had at Illinois So far
Excellent professor, so lucky to have taken 2 classes with him. Challenging exams but study hard and you're fine.

Very engaging and works to keep a class interested in the material. He is young, so easier to relate to, but he also tries very hard to show that what you are learning applies to real-life applications. Both times he makes you work for your grade, but it is a rewarding experience.
Good lecturer, but doesn't care about students.

Lectures are made to be very interesting, with tons of real life examples. Material is taught well. Does a good job of instilling intuition. I felt the workload got a bit heavy, and the TAs were harsh on reports, but the exams were easy if you paid attention. Ewoldt is a very good professor, and there is a lot you can learn from this class.

He was an amazing professor who loves his job. He is interesting and very well spoken. It's not a blow off class, but his interest in the subject makes you want to put in the effort and making the course seem easier.  He is very clear with his notes and is very organized. Be sure to always bring your i-clicker because he is huge on participation.

Ewoldt is very gifted in his teaching abilities.  Lecture is very engaging and he lives for answering questions.  If you are willing to hold up your end of the work, you will come out of the class with deep understanding.  Although, I felt that the weekly written reports were a bit much.

Loved this class-- by no means easy, but he makes you motivated to learn the material. His exams are a mix of tricky material and straight forward questions. He's a great prof with a lot of enthusiasm for the material and for teaching!
Best professor I've had so far.

Best professor I've had at U of I. He introduces and explains new ideas incredibly smoothly, he loves answering questions, and he really cares about his students. His tests are very fair: he covers exactly what we do in class, but in interesting, though not convoluted, new situations.
AMAZING professor. Very interested in what he's teaching and he makes it engaging. Tests were not easy but not impossible, very fair grading and you learn a TON.
Best Professor I've ever had.
Most unorganized professor. Takes months to grade assignments and does not reply to emails at all. Very nice and is passionate about physics, but awful at teaching it. Self taught class for sure.
Obviously very passionate about the class. Will jump to help any student. I haven't interacted with him much in class but overall I liked him.
He's the best

He is SO ANNOYING! He purposely drags out class when there is NO point in doing so. Makes jokes that are NOT funny. Insists on discussing simple topics for 15 minutes when 1 minute would be sufficient. Calls on people randomly because his class leadership doesn't stimulate discussion. Very poor choice of a teacher. Avoid him at all costs!
Jessica makes science fun! The material is easy to get into but a bit diffuclt to understand so pay attention in class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Extremely passionate about astronomy, and her passion is infectious at times. Really makes an effort to connect with the students (occasionally uses memes in her lectures lol), which makes classes a little more lively. Lots of extra credits so if you show up for class and pay attention you really didn't need to study much for weekly quizes/ finals
Is unreasonable and is unhelpful with students' confusion and misunderstandings.

I took astronomy online with Dr. Evans. The class was around 400 people but she did her best to make herself available to us through email and an online Q and A forum. Meeting her at in person exams she is very nice. Overall a caring professor who wants everyone to learn the material.
-Lectures are not clear enough -She digresses a lot -She speaks very quickly (even when you ask her to repeat)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: There are a lot of grades so there is room for error. She gives extra credit for every time you come to class with an iclicker, which boosted my grade a lot. Straightforward class and the lectures were interesting even though i'm not a science person. She is always there for office hours and gives exam questions in class.
Lectures aren't necessary, but I would recommend going because she's an amazing professor. Tests can be difficult, but they're usually curved.
Tough tests, but tons and tons of extra credit, plus curves on all the tests. You could tell she was extremely passionate about space, and she really loved what she was doing.

The great thing about this professor is that even if you don't do well on the tests, you can still get an A in the class. The tests themselves were kind of hard but there are many extra credit opportunities as well as a few labs that are easy As. No textbook is required and neither is going to lecture, really easy A and she's really helpful.
She will give u  review sessions before the exam, If you show up in the review session and read through all her assignment. u will get a good grade easily.

Cares about her students and wants to teach you material so that you'll make it your own rather than have you memorize formulas and words just for exams. Don't take this class if you just want to do busy work.
Easy 400 level class. She is a lenient grader and the exam "problems" are exactly from the lecture. Highly recommend!
Take her class. Wonderful wonderful professor. Exams are straightward and directly relate to materials. She does not want to trick you in exams.
Great professor. Exams are directly from the notes. Just attend class and you will know everything. Easy 400 level econ course.
Great professor who really cares about helping students.  Exams are very fair and there are no surprises; the topics covered are interesting.

The most backwards professor I had. He strategically did not give Professor Review forms to us at the end of the course. He demands perfect attendance and timeliness to all classes, but he showed up late by 10 min to EVERY class (I had an 8AM course w/him). Also, no feedback on grades and no timeliness on those. Rubrics extremely vague. Bad tests.

This guy was the worst professor I have EVER taken. His grading methods were bizarre and difficult and he would never or very rarely provide a rubric for anything we did, so we had little guidance for what he did require. The was rarely available, admitted to not checking his email, and was late in grading everything I turned in.

This professor was the worst I have ever had. The man appeared late to class every day but expected mandatory attendance, he had NO online portal for the class, rarely answered e-mails, rarely appeared at office hours, spoke in monotone, and would randomly speak French mid sentence. He also gave us a 15-20 pg research paper for a 200 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Tested material he hadn't taught or assigned. Lectures useless. Assigned all students to give presentations two days before semester end; tried to make us attend class on Reading Day to listen to them all. He had major health problems during this semester, so I understand that he wasn't at his best, but I think it's time for him to stop teaching.

Most disorganized class ever. No advance notice on when homework is assigned, and always due the next class. Sometimes it gets graded, sometimes not. Prof usually 5-15min late. Got so far behind in the syllabus, he scheduled extra evening classes where he assigned homework due the next class session! Too bad if you worked... Easy grader though.

Prof Bokamba is the shizz, though it's hard to follow him when he starts to go on his ramblings. He is a sweet old man though and his deadlines for homework are incredibly flexible. He forget to take attendance often, but attending each class isn't necessary, nor is doing the readings entirely--he gives an outline for the midterm and final :D
No Comments

Professor Bokamba is the coolest!  He doesn't care too much about homework or test grades as longs as you show that you know what to do in class.  He is very good at getting everyone involved and really helps those who don't understand.  Nicest professor ever!!!

I loved Dr. Claverie! Dreams and Nightmares was more like a Sci-Fi class, but if you like seminar-style class, this is a perfect fit for you. I participated a lot in class and found it more enjoyable. I am not typically one to like writing, but this class made it fun! Only three essays for the semester.

Dr. Ezra Claverie, though a tough grader, really just wants to see you succeed and improve at the things you aren't good at. It made learning how to write good academic essays much more tolerable. He provided excellent readings that gave tools to write said essays, and also the scifi readings (as it was CW: Dreams and Nightmares) were very cool.

Claverie is a very good professor who made class very emjoyable. I surprisingly learned a lot in this advanced comp class and definitely think he prepared me to be a better writer! He is a bit challenging but if you are determined you will definitely succeed in this class.

Mr. Claverie is a passionate English professor, knowledgeable about many aspects of the subject. He does not expect everyone to be Shakespeare but he does require that you do COLLEGE LEVEL work. He made the subject interesting with his assigned readings. I didn't expect to enjoy my degree's junior English requirement but I did thanks to him.
very nice, helpful and was a great class...
Overall nice guy. Attendance isn't mandatory but a good idea because he gives pop quizes. Fair grader, willing to help if you have questions. Good class to use as a GPA booster!

Ezra was a great teacher to have. He's nice grader. Not an easy grader but if you're a good writer, he'll grade you the way you should be graded which is well. He's a cool guy and I'd recommend him as he is also helpful unlike some RHET teachers.

This class is very easy. As long as you go to class and take notes, because it shows up word for word on the tests. He gives you outlines of the exams so you know what to expect. Lectures are kinda boring because he just talks, but it's an easy A. Ezra is a pretty chill guy and nice and always willing to help if you don't understand something.
grades papers very fairly; not difficult to get A's on the papers.  Class readings are pointless, as well as the pop quizzes. Very fun and easygoing guy. I would take a class with him again.

All he does is read off the lecture slides. You dont know your grade because he doesnt put it on compass. He grades very easy (lazy) on the homework assignments, quizzes are ok. All you have to have is have good memorization skills and thats it. Oh and read the textbook as well. He takes questions from the book than from his slides on the test.
Not a good professor, not easy to get good grade. Trust me, do not choose this professor not only because he has a terrible accent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Kalipeni was an OK teacher. He is from Malawi, which has its pros and cons. He knows a lot about developing countries and is clearly pretty intelligent. But the downside is that he has a thick accent and reads straight off the powerpoints during lectures, making them feel long and sometimes boring. It was tougher than i thought it'd be.

Very funny and likeable guy. Interesting life stories. Does not follow syllabus. Quizzes are open book, but he uses old test banks so material does not always correspond with his lectures. His response to any of your problems is "don't worry, it will be okay" (dismissive).  All lecture slides are posted. Makes me laugh every class. Jolly guy.

Professor Kalipeni taught a class at my university this past fall and then left to go back to UIUC.  He is unintentionally funny and though he is tougher to understand (being from Malawi), its always fun to be in his class. I definitely recommend taking a class of his.  If he were still at my school, I'd be taking one with him this semester.

He is very hard to understand and his lectures are very dry. He is fun however and that makes up for how terrible his daily quizzes and tests are. Way too much work for an intro/ gen. ed. class and too many projects requiring you to use labs and resources generally not needed in such a low level class.

I enjoyed the content of this class and the professor is very funny, but I feel I zoned out a lot in his lectures and learnt the most by independent study for quizzes and assignments, if attendance wasn't mandatory I wouldn't have needed to attend. This class has a lot of busy work that can be a little overwhelming

Professor Kalipeni is a friendly person with a great sense of humor. His stories will definitely make you laugh. The class isn't too hard if you go over his discussion quizzes and slides, but Kalipeni can be very disorganized. He hardly ever follows the syllabus. Class is mandatory and can be boring, but his sense of humor is surely one of a kind.
He tries to be funny, but comes off as incomprehensible, and often makes references to his own personal unfounded beliefs. Avoid him at all costs.

Interesting class, really understands it because he is from Africa. Questions from discussion quizzes are on the midterm and finals. Show up to class and you'll do fine!  He's pretty goofy, sometimes hard to understand (accent) and overall good guy, but doesn't stick to the syllabus at all
I am taking Geog 384 this semester. He seems like a very fair professor. The subject matter is very intersting. His accent is a little bit hard to understand though. I took his class in Spring 2009.

Horrible class, very hard for a gen ed. Tests are ridiculous, gives you "example questions" but they are nothing like the actual test...every other answer involves an "all of the above" or "none of the above." Burton is not a good TA. Weird and awkwardly unapproachable...sections got awkward very quickly.

Funny prof, but I usually don't pay attention.  Lecture slides are online.  More assignments than I would have thought.  Seems like something is due every week in discussion.  for discussion do not take burton!!!  alejandro is good.  overall, easy class.
This professor does not care about teaching or is just a really terrible teacher.  Very disorganized class.

The class was very easy, he was entertaining.  basketball players were in my class for the only time in college here.  I missed half a test and still got a B+ in it.  memorizing developing countries were kinda boring but, still an easy grade.
Impossible to cover study materials for final. Memorization required for about 140 countries.

Eh, okay class. If you need a Gen-Ed though its prolly your best bet.  He makes lectures funny at times, but they're not too mandatory.  Study for tests and/or pay attention in class lots.  Lecture notes online are key.

This class sucks. The tests are ridiculous..but that is more the TAs' fault than Kalipeni's. He's really hard to understand. I took this thinking it would be my blow off class and it is one of my hardest...Take something else if you can.

HORRIBLE CLASS!! I thought this would be easy but the test was impossible! He asks you the most irrelevant things from notes and then the most obscure stuff from the books you have to read. You NEED to go to class because he'll randomly take attendance and that counts for 6% of your grade. Be very weary of geog 101 if kalepeni is teaching
Very passionate about his work
attend class, he will screw you over on attendance

Not extremely interesting, kind of a hard accent, but occasionally makes some funny jokes.  Exams and assignments were always easy, a very easy class. Definitely recommend taking GEOG 101 to satisfy the Non-Western Requirement.
should not be lecturing! we can read our own damn notes!

First I have to admit Professor Taghaboni-Dutta is very knowledgeable. My low rating is because she interrupts and talks over students who ask questions only to not fully answer the question. She also says homework should take 5 - 10 mins, yet several others said they took at least 3hrs on each assignment. Unrealistic expectations from her.
One of the best teachers at UIUC. Her stats class finally made me understand how statistics works, after having taken it on before in high school and college.

I'm so confused by the negative ratings here... Her classes were so great in my opinion and I've enjoyed learning from her.  She challenges you for sure but isn't that better than a boring class where its all minimum effort? Its graduate levels... 
She's been so great and is one of the best professors I've had in the program.

I have taken every graduate level class by Professor Taghaboni - she's an excellent teacher and provides real examples within her lectures to allow you to think through problems in an interesting way.  She encourages critical thinking skills and wants to teach you how to think about things not just do things. 
She doesn't put up with B.S.!
Never in my life have I had a professor where I do not understand anything she says. Truly, a marvel. She can speak for hours and no cohesive idea will be communicated.
Hate her class. Do Not Take Anything with Her
She is the worst teacher no more comments. Do not take her elective class. She is a tough grader
Do not take this class as a first class in Gies even if recommended and considering take only this class in a semester. The amount of coursework is absolutely insane and they grade very hard.
Never take her if you have chance.
Don't take her class at all. Bad teacher and bad class. Do not take the class, please.

She is okay as a teacher but her grading is too harsh for a class like this because it is elective and people take it to pump their grades she screw my who group and they got mostly B-. You need to spend hours on this class and her quizzes are too hard only the last one okay.

Don't believe in any good review for her because she might write it for herself. Please don't take the 589 class. It is not worth it because you won't learn anything from her and she grades roughly. it is an elective class. Take something more important.

This is the second course taken with this professor. Yes, the grading is overall easy, but the lectures are way too time consuming compared to many other courses. Too many unnecessary videos. Consicion and more application to real world experiences would be key to improving the overall learning experience.

Professor Taghaboni-Dutta's way of explaining project management tools and techniques is very easy to understand. She makes the class interesting. Group assignments are a bit tricky and you may not get a lot of hints during open office hours however that's totally up to individuals' expectations.
Overall a great knowledgeable professor.

Jake is a great professor. He genuinely cares about his students in DTX 495 and wants us to learn and grow. He remembered everyones names within the first few weeks of class and made it a priority to care for students and their wellbeing. This course is not difficult. If you put in the effort to learn and understand the material you will get an A.
I had so much fun in this class! I'd recommend it to anyone and everyone. Jake's the best!

Professor Jake Fava goes above and beyond in the classroom to teach about student-centered app design. His co-teacher and him create a learning environment that promotes learning from failure without fear. I would highly recommend him for any class he teaches.
Very approachable and understanding. Clearly passionate about and an expert on the material. Classes often go a few minutes over time, however.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Pretty much everything depends on your TA. Overall, it is a very easy class if you work hard and want a good grade. Class meterials were a bit outdated and boring, but my TA made the class so much better!

Very passionate about the subject and encourages students to improve/build their skills. FR207 is grammar and writing based, so grading was very nitpicky. Graded on participation each class. Can spend too much time talking/lecturing, sometimes not enough time on the grammar quiz material. Overall very nice person. FR207 will have a textbook soon.

I'm really not sure if I wouldn't take her class again. It's easy to get an A and it was very easy to keep up with, but the professor is one of the most disorganized human beings I have ever met. She really makes UIUC look bad. She LOVES to talk and is very passionate about her class, but she does a terrible job of teaching and motivating students.

She says her class is easier than it is. A bit confusing at times, but a very nice lady. Soft-spoken, can be hard to hear. Use of lab in FLB to record voice, had a course pack and a very small text book.

attendance is no longer mandatory but you should definitely still go because i didn't and my grades struggled a little despite the class being super easy. everything is really well organized and there's only been a couple instances where ive had a hard time with the concepts presented.
Taught like he loved what he was teaching. Good energy, engaging.

All of the assignments hold your hand through them and all the exams and homeworks and pretty much are the same problems with different numbers. The class organization is one of the best I have ever seen.

Easy class, just do the work. Lots of EC available. The midterms and final exam use the same questions from the midterm practice exams. Do the practice exam enough times and you will see all the possible questions on the exams. Very easy class. don't slack off and use AI or misuse the clicker for attendance, you will get caught.

Amazing professors. Usually like 2-3 assignments in a week + labs but when you do them they really only help your grade. I love this class and it's a really good intro to python and stats. I came in with like 0 compsci knowlege but I definitely learned a lot. Overall amazing professors. Warning though Taylor Swift is like the 3rd professor atp
Omg he is amazing! Him and Karle honestly were so welcoming. I would take this class again if I could. Please take this class if you have to and attend the lectures. They are so much fun!

He was the best professor I have ever met in my life. He gives amazing lectures that is interactive and engaging. His way of explaining concepts made me understand stuffs really fast, so it saves a lot of time during self- study/doing hw. There are lots of creative assignments/labs/projects too! Please take this course if you can :D
He's a pretty nice guy. He reminds me of Special Agent Reid from Criminal Minds. A smart guy who gets his ideas across in a simple way and answers questions well.
Great class and professor seems to enjoy teaching. Lectures are very easy to follow along, and very easy material as long as you stay on track.
The class is very easy and the content taught in lecture is similar to what appears on the homework / tests, so it is very manageable to get a good grade. Offers a lot of extra credit.
You can tell he enjoys what he is doing

Dedicated to course quality. He and Karle give amazing, passionate, clear lectures. They also put out multiple surveys for students to give feedback on the course, and they are always willing to change things up if needed. All course material is provided in a notebook you fill out during lecture (

What is there not to say? Energetic, fun, kind. Him and Karle are hands down the best professors I've ever had and made the intro to my Data Science journey a really welcoming and exciting one. Loved it so much I had to become a course assistant! Really do look forward to this class!

The lectures were engaging, and I enjoyed doing the work for the class because the homework platform made it fun and rewarding. The microprojects were also pretty interesting and made me excited to learn more about data science.
Probably the best teacher you can ask for, for an introductory course. Great Lecturer (even though i never went), if you miss lecture you can just watch the YT videos.

Wade has great chemistry with co teacher Karle. Amazing computer scientist and data scientist who can clearly explain concepts. The course has a great structure with tons of extra credit. Homework is mastery based, labs and projects are well designed, and tons of office hours. The duo have brought data science to Illinois, and put it on the map.
Extraodinary course STAT107. Perfect intro to python and data analysis, and if you don't get an A in this course, you are either feeble-minded or don't work hard at all.
Wade is a cool guy if a bit awkward, but his lectures are great and he does a great job.

GOAT OF ALL GOATS. WADE YOU INSPIRE ME EVERYDAY TO PUSH PAST THE SMELLIES OF GRAINGER TO PURSUE COMPUTER SCIENCE. Very good at explaining and is willing to explain more in-depth if you are confused. Genuinely such a good class I wish I could have the joy of taking STAT 107 again. Very smart professor who's passionate about his craft

He's very passionate with his lectures, and you can tell he knows what he's talking about very well. He really cares about what he teaches. The homework platform for this class is very helpful, and I recommend attending all the lectures for a better understanding. Exams are exactly like the homework and practice exams.

He is an amazing professor. I really was entwined with all of his lectures because of how entertaining he is. He can be iffy, but overall a pretty awesome teacher. He knows his stuff. But beyond the classroom, I don't think he can be that understanding. But as a lecturer, he is one of the best.
Not very understanding with students who are just a few minutes late due to technical difficulties.
good prof, entertaining, a lot of extra credit, easy to follow along lectures

Wade is a great professor and I recommend that everyone take STAT 107. It is one of the best courses on campus. The work teaches you a lot, and is not too challenging. It is easy to get a good grade due to a lot of extra credit and extensions. The work can be done online because lectures are optional.
Super amazing professor, always really passionate about his lectures and works really well with Prof. Karle! Lectures aren't mandatory, they have videos of all their lectures on their website.

Maybe the best class I've ever taken, in terms of design. Everything was well explained and labs gauged lecture material well. It is not hard to earn an A if you do the work, and the homework is designed so that you don't lose any points. Just an amazing class. I have 0 complaints.

I self-studied throughout the entire semester after attending only a few initial awful classes. Completing the notebook for extra credit, but rejected due to a missing notation on one page.Excessive amount of unnecessary homework.

He was a good teacher for this class and made Python easy to understand. But he went quickly many times when we didn't understand syntax and why it was done that way, which can be an issue for some new students. He explains concepts well, but lectures can get boring if you aren't a beginner. The HW and labs are pretty easy if paid attention to.
easy class, easy to follow lectures

Wade is an amazing lecturer. An easy A class that's 4 credits! The homework is online, there's a weekly lab that you work on during your lab section, two projects, two midterms, and a final. The tests are all taken in the CBTF, and there's a lot of extra credit opportunities! There's office hours everyday and a class Discord for HW/lab help!

This class is truly so valuable and the professors excel at teaching and helping. The class uses github and prairie learn to complete assignments and submit labs. There is also a discord that was very useful for getting homework and midterm help. Many office hours available as well!

STAT 107 is definitely one of the best courses I've taken. The course structure is designed in a good way that covers the Pandas library and some basic statistics. They designed a course website with all the resources available, and you can succeed in this class without going to even one single lecture. The professors themselves are very caring.

Wade is clearly very knowledgeable and amusing, high-quality lecturer. Ample extra credit is offered and he hosts professor office hours once a week in addition to TA office hours. You'll complete a practice exam with that pulls from the same question pool as the CBTF actual exam. Do it enough times and you'll get 95%+.

Professor Wade was awesome. He was super dedicated to making the class the best it could be. The homework assignment and exams were all done on prairie learn, so it was easy to study. He always brought a lot of enthusiasm to the lectures. He was also very active on discord to answer any questions.

Honestly love him and Karle. They are such an amazing duo and explain things very well. This was my first ever intro to cs and he did a very good job explaining things. The lectures were amazing and super entertaining. Overall cares about his students and is super funny.
Best professor, take his class pls. He genuinely cares about his student and teaches good stuff.
Great person, funny, encouraging, and is passionate about what he teaches. Wade really wants you to learn and he makes this clear in the lectures and the engaging labs.
Live laugh love Wade. Super sweet guy that knows a ton about what he teachers.

He is a very considerate and friendly professor, and made difficult material understandable and engaging. Most of the lectures included real-world applications. The MPs can be challenging, especially the C programming, but with office hours it is manageable.
The professor is very nice and wants his students to succeed. He is very approachable, and I felt comfortable asking him for help. His lectures are great. Best professor in the CS department!

One of the great professor in CS department. Even though CS240 is a new class, he made it interesting and easy to understand. The first half part of the class is harder, with C MPs that are more difficult. But the second half uses python flask and is definitely easier to understand and also with more fun. Office hours are limited so use discord.

Great lecturer that genuinely cares about students. Grading is fair and exams are very easy overall. Regular administrative and technical issues noticeably detracted from course quality, but given this was the first offering of the course, it's is somewhat to be expected. All said, Wade made CS 240 a great experience in spite of some growing pains.

Literally just assigns book material each week. You end up reading almost the entire book and learning from that instead of the professor. The way the class was this semester, you didn't even need a professor. Just read the book and go program stuff.

Whatever you hope to learn in this class, you probably won't. Class covers some kernel programming, but most lecture content isn't valuable. Uses textbook, but doesn't really test its content. 4 MPs, minimal overlap with lecture, but documentation walks you through. Ok elective, but class like databases, parallel, distrib sys are more important.

Prof Wade is one of the best professors I've had at UIUC! While lectures weren't mandatory, they were extra credit. I still would've gone even without a grade incentive, since he makes learning fun. Great at explaining coding in simple terms- even to beginners. He ties data science to other disciplines like business, statistics, economics, etc.
Best lecturer ever.
Wade is the best lecturer I've had during my time at UIUC.
My favorite person in the department.

Wade is an incredible professor and human being. CS 225 is by far the best course I've taken at Illinois. Not only did I learn a lot of about data structures, but also about their applications and uses in the industry. Highly recommend taking the course.

Wade is a not only a great teacher but a great person. He came up with many ways to improve the course like opening up lecture-question portals, updating TA notes for us, and grading our work when the TA were on strike. I love love love his lectures, never skips them. He encourages us to be creative using the code and share our work.
Wade is very passionate about all things CS. He does a stellar job explaining concepts and relating them to real world examples. You will be in good hands.
Wade is passionate about teaching. He carefully prepared every lecture. He is happy to help his students in many ways. He is a professor who is very popular among his students.
He is super passionate and excited about computer science. He shows great care for his students and really wants everyone to do well. I would highly recommend him.
Wade is such a caring and encouraging professor. Loved this class. He's an amazing lecturer and he's also quite accessible and helping. Would highly recommend.

Wade is an amazing lecturer. His class atmosphere is very lax, yet he has very good control over the lecture hall. He really shows passion in the things he teaches, and he cares a lot about students. For example, he's had open office hours where you can talk to him about anything like career choices. That's a first I've heard of here from a cs prof

There was two professors when I took the class in Fall 2015. He is responsible for the coding part. The material is pretty easy, but the projects are quite different from what we learned. Just make sure you have CS friends that can help you with coding. If not, go to office hours and TA will make sure you understand the concepts.
Was for sure a good lecturer. I wish I had him the entire semester before it was too late. The course was very tough at the time I took it. In fact, it was the lowest grade I've ever got.

His passion for CS made the class 10 times more enjoyable. Although this class sometimes seemed a bit challenging, it was an easy A nevertheless. I truly learned a lot from him! His half of the semester was my favorite.

This class has put me in tough position but I learned so much. Be ready to work for long hours on CS mini projects every week. The prof is great, he is there to help you all the time and there are also TA's. Although I did not get the best grade, this is a class for those who are really into computers and their language/functions.

I think he's a good professor. I had no knowledge of computer science before entering this class and I'm getting an A. If you're having a hard time with the MPs all you have to do is look on piazza or go to office hours and the TAs will help you.

Very passionate lectures and good grades. The activities and machine problems are really easy. Ok, sometimes you may stuck on the MPs, but you can find quick help on piazza. Exam is also as easy as you can imagine(although, I did not get a full point). Will take his class again.
He's a great professor who cars about his students. I don't know why everyone else is being so harsh. Attend office hours, stay on top of your game and you'll do fine.
No. Take something else if you can. He doesn't care about you. Take him if you want to destroy your academic career, he's great for that.

Wade is a really thorough teacher.  Because he's new to this class, he's always surveying students to see how he can better his methods; he definitely cares about his students! Also, the course is graded out of 1000 points, but there are 1050 points available, so you can get up to 5% extra credit.

This course is challenging for non-CS majors. The work load is way beyond the average for 100 level courses. Expect to use office hours at least 1-2 times a week in order to get an A. His lecture style is different and hard to grasp, but put in a lot of effort and you will be okay.
Great teacher but he gives a ridiculous amount of work for what is supposed to be a 100 level course. But if you attend lectures and discussions, you should be able to score at least a B.

The MPs are really hard and take a ton of time to do. Lecture is pointless to go to. I think his only goal in this class is to catch cheaters and make an example of them. It's not our fault that the material covered in the notes isn't enough to do the homework though! Overall it's not too hard of a class if you put the time in to doing the homework
Wade is patient and helpful when you ask any questions on lecture material
Great teacher
Definitely take cs 241 with him!! He is great!
He's awesome! If you can take CS 241 with him, go for it!!!
Professor Fagen is amazing. If you ever get the chance to take CS 241 with him it will be a really good experience. I highly recommend taking the class with him rather than anyone else.

I've never posted here yet but he is so great that I really want to post about him. His class is very understandable and he makes sure students understand what is going on. He knows the material very well. MPs and not easy but very helpful. Overall this is a fantastic teacher, great class, and it brightens up my first semester in UIUC.
Good
Best Professor!:)

Professor Miraftab clearly knows her stuff and is very passionate about her work. She is rightfully respected in her field. However, as a professor she leaves a lot to be desired. She is very disorganized in lecture and in assignments, often forgetting what readings we did. She grades very easily up until the final and communicates poorly about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very controlling with group projects. You need to participate in lectures and if you don't you will be lectured like a child. She was not clear at all about the syllabus and all assignment. She and her TA are not clear or helpful at all. I would not recommend this class at all.

Lectures are interesting, but her grading is unpredictable, she grades all assignments easy except the finals. Final assignments make no sense and she may say you and your group are not following guidelines and did a terrible job. She also forces you to open your webcam for attendanceicipation and becomes rude if you disagree with anything
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I respect Prof. Miraftab for her passion But don't think she did a great job at communicating that passion with her students. She often got preachy and argued until everyone agreed with her viewpoint. I felt like a 4th grader when she called us out (by name) for being late/skipping readings, wanted reports on every step of our group project, etc

She was utilized as a TA in my Frameworks for Inequality and Cultural Understanding. Faranak was usually pretty disorganized. She sprung a final on us last second when we were told previously we would not have one. Although it wasn't difficult, it was still irritating. Only positive quality is her passion for equity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable at the subject. Has the ability to explain sensitive subjects very objectively and without bias. She has a history of being active as an activist in her younger years. This adds to her passion and charm. Very approachable and caring. She might just be the best professor I have ever had in all my school years!
Probably the best lectures I have attended in my life. Lectures touch you at an emotional level.

Incredibly worldly and a true gift to the University/Urban Planning Dept., Prof. Miraftab teaches courses on transnational planning, globalization, and cities of the Global South. She often draws upon her own life experiences, brings candor to class, & begins with "Good Morning, how is everyone doing?" A Published writer and my favorite professor.

Professor Miraftab is very knowledgable and passionate in her teachings. This class if full of eye opening material. There is a small quiz every other week on average and one paper. You do have to work for your grade as there is only 100 points total in the class. I would recommend this course to anyone who has interest in global cities.

Professor Miraftab is very knowledgeable in this subject. She is very passionate and enjoys what she teaches. She makes herself available as long as you show interest in the subject and/or your grade. The readings she assigns relate to the topics covered in class and are necessary for the quizzes.

She taught this class well, if the little description blurb in the registrar interests you then you will enjoy this class. Most of the quizzes you don't even need to do the reading to do well on, it's just common sense.

I loved the way her lectures were always so interesting. She is a very experienced woman, and you can see her passion for the topics discussed in class. Your perspective of the world will really change and you'll understand a lot more about the way things work. Even the assignments were engaging. Just be ready to talk about the readings in class!

Professor Miraftab is a wonderful teacher. She teaches passionately about the materials in this class. The assignments and readings aren't that hard, but it is important that you ATTEND class. She usually reviews the assigned materials for the  session in class, so you don't really have to do all of the readings. Overall, UP185 is a chill class.
Great content. Best class at uiuc in terms of eye opening material , but organization of class is messy.

This class had some great material to look into. I enjoyed all the material covered and everything overall was pretty understandable. Participation  is expected, and the class is easy going. I loved it and gained so much from it. The professor is super helpful and her open hours are helpful incase anything she says is unclear.
Her interest and passion in the topic are inspiring. She's such a nice professor and she's very easy to approach.
She is very cool and interesting.  Always knows her stuff.  I recommend this professor if you want something different and memorable.  I learned alot.
Her class is easy, but sometimes difficult to find the relationship with the guideline she provided. But she is definitely into this issue and very passionate.

She can articulate the material. Otherwise, she is terrible. She has a no screens policy but apparently that doesn't apply to people who use iPads. She will also waste class time ranting about phones and waiting for people to ask/answer questions even though no one wants to. She  has picked out people who obviously had nothing to say.

Although I found the topics discussed in class interesting, I could not handle how confusing Professor Faranak was and ultimately dropped the class. The confusion she causes when asked a question makes asking questions almost useless, she really just reiterates what she just said. Attendance is mandatory and she expects participation.

The class is fairly easy, but the professor is ridiculous. She's really bad at explaining her expectations and is really needy when it comes to classroom discussion/interaction, so get on her good side by talking a lot and going to office hours. Projects are pretty easy and the finals are essay format.

Totally unorganized. Not a hard class though. Interesting, but hard to figure out what's going on in the class. She seems to have no idea of what's she's assigned and when it's due, and keeps changing deadlines. Interesting class though.

Lectures were well organized (prewritten, but not scrolled past too fast 9/10 times). Also explained things in an intuitive manner without simplifying it too much. Made sure to connect concepts to applications to avoid the class feeling like "fake math". Make sure to review lectures if you don't understand concepts tho
He's a great professor and very considerate of students. I love his teaching style.

257 is awfully designed due to the course design. As a lecturer Felix was great, and I would have given him a 5 if it was for a different course. He is a very smart guy and always helping out on the course forum. Only complaint is he scrolled through notes fast, but lectures and notes were recorded.  Would 100% recommend him for another course.

** FOR MATH257 **
This class just tries to do too much with all the coding plus teaching basic linear algebra. You are completely on your own for all of the Python, and only left with lectures for concepts. Tests are helllla hard too. Prof. Leditzky was a good lecturer, but I would personally take the online section.

Incredible. 
Very direct and clear explanations and lectures. Very approachable outside of course as well.

*NOTE RATING IS FOR MATH257: Prof. Leditzky has a thick accent and is difficult to understand at times, what was more problematic was his hard-to-read handwriting during lecture and poor explanation of topics. This class overall is a pain, tests are nothing like the homework with a heavy conceptual focus, and the coding is very irritating.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely bombed MATH 347, so going into this class was quite scary for me. Professor Leditzky really took time to explain problems and answer questions in a way that students could understand, and it was because of that I could truly understand the concepts rather than simply memorizing them for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Leditzky is amazing. His instruction is clear and concise. As the first 400-level math class I've taken, the course materials are not too difficult, and I can understand most of the concepts without a solid background in previous courses. I learned a lot in this course, and he excites me for future studies in the subject. Definitely recommend.
Ravi is excellent at explaining mathematics and providing meaningful insight into questions that students have. He is a chill professor and was very willing to help those who needed it.

You can tell that Ravi is super passionate about math. He's super knowledgeable, a good lecturer, and charming. The class was really hard but I think that's just more the nature of the class. He was also really generous with curves.
Absolutely amazing class, genuinely enjoys teaching and has a vested interest in student learning

My honest rating of this professor would be 2.5 out of 5, but RMP does not have that option, so I'll just roll with 3. Took an honors version of this class, so I'm not sure whether I dug a grave for myself or it was just that bad. In terms of teaching, I'd say he's mediocre, leaning a bit on the good side. In terms of grading, run away.

Prof. Fernando is truly a great educator and person. He is very competent, super kind and approachable. His explanations are always rigorous and he is always ready to give more examples or discuss topic more in depth. Nevertheless, the workload is huge especially if you never had proper introduction to proof writing.

He's a great professor. I think there's a lot I can learn from him which is why I still try to attend his lectures when I can. Rarely makes mistakes in class and usually catches them. Always clear and accurate explanations for things. 
Always very respectful and approachable for any number of math topics or class related questions. He's great.

The professor is extremely knowledgeable and can answer tricky questions quickly. His lectures are well organized and highly engaging, and you learn something valuable in every class. I feel prepared for higher level math courses. He is approachable and very helpful during office hours. He is truly one of the best math professors I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The goat professor

Prof. Fernando has a deep understanding about the elements he teaches, always prepared and explain step by step with excellent logics. He can come up with examples all the time. Workload is reasonable. Will takes his lecture in the future.
The midterms are super difficult! Lots of homeworks, even in midterm weeks!

Mr. Fernando had amazing lectures with examples that progressively showed the concepts and intricacies of the content more and more, leading to a deep understanding of what was being taught rather than a surface-level memorization of the formulas. I found his grading to be fair, and the help & feedback given in office hours was fantastic.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Fernando is a great lecturer - he answers questions well and never makes you feel stupid for asking them. Moreover, he helps you build a great intuition for the basic principles underlying proofs in mathematics, which have been very helpful in all the classes I have taken after 347.
Great professor, would take again.
when he speaks, you feel like all the knowledge of the universe is entering your mind

lectures were pretty entertaining (sometimes funny) and interesting (as an archaeology student). about to take my final today but i'm feeling confident on it because his tests have been fairly easy so far. multiple choice, couple of essay questions. will tell you when something mentioned in class will be on an exam. overall great!
Very interesting lectures. He will tell you what the "testable moments" are, which is very helpful. Very knowledgeable and interested in the subject material.

I took ANTH106 with Professor Fennel this semester; it was a wonderful experience. He is super knowledgeable about anthropology and frequently mentions the projects he was involved with. Although lecture-heavy, he never failed to pique my interest in his class. The midterms are easy and the homework involves some reading. I would 100% recommend.
A very interesting professor, but his final exam was a bit difficult even though I studied quite a bit.

Mr. Fennell seems like a very nice guy. I would sometimes have trouble paying attention (class was a bit early for me,) but when I did it was usually interesting. He posts lecture slides online. Tests come from those.

I thought this class would be boring, but he finds a way to make archaeology interesting. The book is useful, but skimming it is fine if you will read it at all. He's a good speaker and loves talking about the New Philadelphia site. I highly recommend this professor.
No Comments

Very nice guy, passionate abt fluids. He tries to connect class to real world things, which is nice. He also drops a lot of hints in class about what to study for exams, so make sure you attend his review lectures.
Very good prof.

It's important to note that TAM 435 has very different expectations than TAM 335. If you're a graduate student, this class can be an overwhelming amount of work on top of your research. That being said, Prof Feng is amazing. His lectures are some of the best I've ever had, clear and organized, and he really cares about your learning. Super nice guy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing lecture and students are always well prepared for midterms and final.
Great professor who ensures that students understand the material. Course was well organised, and students were well-prepared for the examinations.

Super organized with the material, dynamic lecturer who knows how to make things interesting, clear grading criteria, offers useful extra credit, fair tests/ midterms, HWs are very helpful, and includes real life applications. Very receptive to feedback and always seeks to improve the quality of the course. He's a real gem.

Best prof in the MechSE deptartment. Super organized with the material, dynamic lecturer who knows how to make things interesting, clear grading criteria, offers useful extra credit, fair tests/ midterms, HWs are very helpful, and includes real life applications. Very receptive to feedback and always seeks to improve the quality of the course.
Very hand wavy during lectures and is very condescending during office hours
This man knows what he is talking about. I highly suggest taking him for 361 or any other classes he teaches. I went in multiple times for help and he did a real good job of explaining.

He is a great teacher! The material is straight-forward and assignments/labs are easy. In class quizzes are not that hard if you know what you are doing. One of the nicest professors I have met. Like I am SO taken aback what that person wrote on 10/23. Projects are hard, but do-able. If you have to take 370 he is a good choice.

Extremely disorganized course. Rubrics posted for reports on the day that it's due. Gives very little time for in-class quizzes. Sometimes rude to students in person and through email. Lectures are not very interesting even though the content has so much potential. Take another professor if you can!

Low clarity rating due to his tendency to make easy material seem much more confusing and difficult by always giving detailed theoretical explanations and listing every individual variable instead of just showing you a simple algorithm in practice. Homework can be very lengthy. Exams very easy, though, and he'll tell you exactly what to expect.
FR 156 is a very interesting and easy class, it has 25% of attendence but it is based on the whole class. Just one homework, 2 quiz and 1 final essay it is a good class, highly recommend.

AMAZING. Super passionate. No exams but there are papers. Shows movies in class sometimes. There's a homework sheet due each class but she doesn't check it, it's for preparation. Super understand about attendance. Very sweet. The material is also fairly interesting.

Overall a class I enjoyed going to. Often showed us videos / shared personal experiences in Paris; it was apparent she really knew the subject matter. I appreciated that she understood pandemic struggles and did not grade attendance like prior semesters. There were quite a few books to buy, and our final was an essay so you needed to read.

I like her lectures and everything but let's be honest, she is extremely arrogant and will show you that she is impatient when you try to ask her questions. If you don't mind about the professors, go take this class. Otherwise avoid her at all cost because she is not a cool person to talk to.

Class was synchronous, met twice a week through zoom. Easy gen-ed course, FR156 covers the history of Paris. Required to buy books and read, this helped better understand topic of lecture. She was very king and funny. Overall there was 2 quizzes( on lectures and reading) and a final essay about the books.

Federmeier is very knowledgeable and kind and wants her students to succeed. There are 4 tests but the lowest is dropped, meaning you don't have to take the final if you score well enough on the exams. There are only quiz and test grades though, so tests are weighted 75%.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and kind, wants students to succeed and provides a lot of opportunities to do so, being very available outside of class. Study guides are basically just what the test is, though the tests are 75% of the course grade which is a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She makes the class very easy for you. Attendance is optional, but her lectures are  good so I still went most of the time. There are 4 exams but you drop your lowest score which helps a lot + the study guide has most of the exam questions. Weekly quizzes but you have unlimited attempts to get 100%. She tries to help make sure you get an A.

The course is based off of quizzes that are totaled to 25% of your grade, the other 75% is based off 3 exams. The exams are tedious and you must study so much for each of them, even if you do it won't help. No other way to get your grade up even if you do well on all quizzes, it's not enough. If you are really good at exams, this course is for you!

Great professor for cog psych. Definitely a lecture heavy class but she makes them fun and engaging. Going to lecture definitely helps for being prepared for exams. Workload is super light but be prepared to study for exams. Overall, a really great class taught by a really great professor!

Great professor, hard(ish) class. Her lectures are very engaging, and she is very passionate about the subject. You'll have to study hard for the exams, but the study guides she gives are good. Would highly recommend, I've learned the most in this class than any of my others this semester.

I can honestly say I learned so many cool things in this psych class. Dr. Federmeier is smart, kind, and lectures are interesting. Information is presently clearly. I highly recommend attending lectures as her explanations of the slides are crucial to understanding the material.

She's really passionate about the subject which makes the lectures a lot more interesting! The subject itself is a bit difficult though, and though lectures aren't mandatory + she uploads slides, the slides don't really make sense without the lecture, so prepare to review a lot for the exams. The workload was really light, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely smart professor, and the material is interesting. Not hard at all to do well if you attend lectures and listen. 10/10

I loved Dr. Federmeier! She is so sweet and kind. The exams are not too difficult if you study well. While some of the lectures were a bit boring, I overall found her class to be interesting and I learned a lot. The class is graded by three exams (with an optional final) and some online quizzes, which you can take as many times as needed.

She's nice, but the lectures are very boring. This class is more effective than ambien at helping me sleep, but the tests keep me up at night. The content of the class is semi-interesting, and she does a great job of helping students understand, but the test questions are extremely difficult and do no reflect student's understanding of the material
Friendly and super smart professor who is passionate about the material. She made every lecture engaging, no small feat for a course about ERPs.

She's nice but I found the class very unenjoyable. Lectures were boring, and tests were harder than they should have been. She does curve the class at the end but only by a couple %. We had the other cognitive teacher sub for her occasionally and she was much more interesting and informative-- i would have much preferred her as a professor.

Class was pretty interesting, but can feel long. Make sure to fill out the question packet because most test questions come from it. However, go in for office hours if you're not sure of some answers because sometimes what she is looking for isn't very clear. Don't need to read the book at all, and if you study ppt slides, you'll be fine!

Professor Federmeier is a superb teacher and seems like a genuinely nice person. She really, really knows her stuff, and is good at sharing that knowledge in an accessible way. Lectures are enjoyable and interesting, and pretty much essential for doing well in the course.

Hands down one of the most down-to-earth and genuinely nice professors at this school, which can sometimes be hard to come by. She's crystal clear during lectures and very helpful otherwise. I wound up in her lab afterwards. I recommend waiting to take her class, as the 224 instructors alternate each semester.
She's very professional and teaches students useful information. She is also very helpful. She gives practice problems for the test which make it easier.

Kfed, as I like to call her in my head, is great. Sometimes she's a little technical and it can be hard to follow, but she usually does little mini-experiments in class that are engaging. She's very nice.  Weekly quiz = ezmode, just have the book open as you do them. I barely paid attention in class, just did the practice questions and got an ez A.

She was helpful, friendly, energetic, and professional.  Several professors in the psyc department could learn from her!!  The tests were based on review questions she gave you, and she was very helpful in office hours.  I would recommend reading the book, it helped me a lot!  Attending class is a must, otherwise you miss a lot from slides.

One of the best professors. She keeps the class interesting, and puts all her slides online. It's perfectly possible to get an A without going to class, although I don't recommend it. You really don't need the book though. If you're not interested in psychology, I suggest you stay away from this class. Otherwise, it's pretty fun and interesting!
Exam was tough but having the questions in advance helped.  She also curves.  Lectures are pretty clear and she is enthusiastic about teaching.
Interesting demos and funny videos make class okay.

I heard it was hard, but it wasn't that bad.  She won't post her lectures before class, which makes notetaking hard, but she posts all the slides after lecture and her exams mostly come from the slides.
Class was interesting.  Good lecturer and a nice prof.
Material was hard, but she gives you all the exam questions ahead of time.  She was really nice and spent a lot of time helping me in office hour.
She really wants her students to learn and to think.  Not everybody is looking for this in an intro class, but it really prepared me for later classes and the MCAT.  Recommended!
She was always prepared and clear. The class was mostly interesting. The tests are easy if you actually read the book and lecture slides. I would take it again.

Professor Federmeier is a great instructor in that she creates an atmosphere conducive to learning. She uses interactive demonstrations and videos to help teach the concepts. The grading structure highly advantageous to a student as well. 4 tests, lowest score dropped 30 percent each with easy homework for 10 percent. Tests are not too hard either.

This class does require a lot of effort, but it's definitely worth it - you really walk away with a lot.  There are 4 tests (you drop the lowest) & 3 EASY hw assignments (but she drops the lowest - so you really only have to do 2)  For each test there is a study guide that is EXTREMELY helpful for the exam. Overall: Recommended! :)

This class was not that hard, although some psych majors will find it challenging. As long as you attend lecture and study her lecture slides, pulling off an A shouldn't be that difficult. She doesn't do plus/minus grading, and out of the four exams, she drops the lowest--so you don't have to take the final if you did well on the other three exams.

Possibly the WORST teacher by far. The material was fairly easy, I found myself having to TEACH it to other students because this teacher makes everything SO much harder than it needs to be. The exams were WAY too hard. They weren't impossible, but the material was not as difficult as she made it. She was nice though..

Professor Federmeier is a great teacher. She knows what she is talking about and it really shows in her lectures and exams. Exam questions, while at times quite challenging,are very fair. Going to lecture helps you understand the material. The people below must have not had an interest in Cognitive Psychology..  I definitely recommend this class!
She's a great teacher and she makes the class very interesting. She even shows two youtube videos each class! The tests are challenging but reasonable.

Terrible teacher.  Doesn't care if you get the notes in class.  She speaks a million words a minute.  If you ask a question she'll give you some lame theory answer that doesn't help you understand what she tries to teach.  Cognitive Pysch is something I was interested in, but she totally ruined it.
Great class. great professor

Don't understand all the negative comments (maybe from the same disgruntled student?) Class is hard cause the topic is. You can't just memorize stuff, you have to THINK. And she does a great job at making you do so.  Recommended.

So far through my college experience, this has been the worst class ever.  She makes the class harder than it has to be.  A simple concept can be turned into something where you say to yourself...wth?  And I guess there was a textbook for this class?  Yep useless again from what I heard from my classmates.  Overall, I would rather watch paint dry.
Terrible class. Each lecture ends with her telling you everything she just said is hypothetical...DO NOT TAKE, so boring

One of the worst classes I've ever taken. Professor makes material much harder than it needs to be. The book is worthless, and doesn't explain anything she talks about. She said on the first day she doesn't teach from the book, but the book should be able to be used as a reference. Don't take this class it will screw your gpa up.
Seriously don't take Psych 224 or her. You have been warned. TOO hard.
An ok professor. Recommand if you are interested in psychology. Can be a difficult class for non-psy-interested students.

I hated this class. I thought it would be semi-interesting and it turned out to be a disaster. I feel that she is a smug professor who makes the material a lot harder than it needs to be. She goes through slides very fast. She, herself, is prepared for the class, but doesn't attempt to teach in favor of the student's understanding.
better class than i thought.  she's cute but dresses like an old lady.
No Comments
Don't take cognitive psych because not only is it extremely hard... but really boring as well. If you're in it... please save yourself the semester of headaches and GET OUT.
the best speaker i have had as a professor.  very prepared for each lecture and interesting to listen to.
well designed course, great lecture
Gives a lot of practice exams. Study them and do the extra credit and you will do great

Class is very easy if you go to lecture and take notes. When it comes to exams,  he gives practice exams that are extremely similar to the actual exams. Do as many as possible and you will succeed in the class.
Fisher is the Accy GOAT! will miss his " Go Illini" at the end of every lecture
He is a wonderful professor. Honestly liked this course and everything. He is caring and supportive. Not much to say, simply good. Go Accy!!
ACCY GOD!!!!!!!!
very straightforward class, do all the work and it's not hard

Good attitude and energy in lecture. Well-structured course with plenty of materials to help students succeed. Lecture slides AND videos available. Plenty of support from TAs in office hours and discussion sections. Good homework and practice questions that foster deeper understanding before the exam.

Omg mitch fisher my king. so sweet. explains everything very well. plenty of resources to succeed. lots of extra credit. easy if u pay attention and follow along  in lecture and do the readings. so nice and a great prof, take with him if u can!

He will give you an excellent groundwork for accounting at this university.  Teaches it in a clear, cohesive manner.  Pay attention in lectures, engage with the examples and you will learn a lot with him.  Tests are not too hard as long as you study.  He loves his job and is passionate about accounting so it makes it funner to learn.

Tests are very heavily weighted and challenging, study well. Don't underestimate them as many failed the first exam. Fisher explains concepts well and has iclicker for review in lecture. TAs are very helpful. Class is challenging but doable, prepare well for the exams. Best part is that there is a lot of extra credit you can earn.

Did a very good job at introducing students to accounting. The coursework came very naturally to me, which is not the case for everyone. The class moves very fast covering almost every aspect of basic accounting, so be prepared to catch up if you find it difficult to understand. All lectures and discussion sections have graded attendence.
I have learned more in this class than any other course I have taken at UIUC. Because of this class, I am planning on switching my major to accountancy. Thank you for a great semester Prof. Fisher.

He is easily approachable and happy to help students. However, this class was difficult and quite boring. Lectures were very long, and because there is so much content to learn, you really need put a lot of extra work to learn everything if you want a good grade in the class. Overall, he's a good professor but prepare to put in a lot of work.

Professor Fisher is an excellent professor for this intro to accounting class. I struggled in the beginning, but once I started paying better attention in lecture, I saw a turnaround in my performance. Make sure to take notes, as it will help a lot on the homework (there is a lot of it). He is a nice guy and cares about what he is teaching!

the class was ok and homework+discussions prepared us for exam well. But the lectures were so boring, Fisher just goes over steps but I feel like he could have explained better. I literally fall asleep every single time. also the required textbook was very expensive

Professor Fisher is a phenomenal professor to learn from if you are taking your first accounting class ever. He explains concepts in a very clear manner where concepts are very easy to grasp if you pay attention in lecture. The overall course structure is very defined and it is definitely possible to do well if you put in the time and effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I felt that while the course itself was not bad (the homework was good preparation for exams) I could not stand going to lecture. I only ended up attending lecture about 3 times the entire semester because the way Mr. Fisher lectures comes across as if he's talking to elementary school children. To be fair, it seems like some people appreciate it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. The class is definitely fast paced and can be difficult at times, but Fisher does a really good job teaching and providing the necessary resources to do well. If you put in the work, the class is definitely manageable and you should be able to do well. You can tell he cares about his students and wants them to do well.

Was a pretty good teacher. You need a good base of basic accounting knowledge to do well in this class. Debits&credits, journal entries, etc. He was a good teacher and you don't really need to read the book if you pay attention in class. I thought he was a strong teacher, but not super compassionate and didn't seem to curve the tests.

BEST TEACHER AT UIUC!! Prof. Fisher is extremely caring and wants his students to do well. As long as you prioritize this class, you will get an A. The exams can be challenging but study a lot, make sure you get 100% on all the homework, and do all of the extra credit. GO TO THE LECTURES AND DISCUSSIONS TRUST ME YOU WILL GET AN A.

Professor Fisher is very friendly and approachable if you need help with the material. Lectures aren't mandatory to attend but the material builds off what you learn each lecture so it's easy to fall behind if you do skip. There's a homework in the textbook and a set of problems due every week but there's so much extra credit you can earn.

One of the best professors I had at UIUC. Very funny and knows what he is teaching. Even though Accounting is hard, it was possible to learn easily since Professor Fisher did such a great job on the lessons. However, if you skip class, I bet you will fail, and he gives out a ton of homework so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a really nice guy but he treats everyone in the class like a child. I felt like I was in grade school again. He would ask a simple Iclicker question that takes 30 seconds to solve. He would give us 10 minutes and get mad when we finished the problem early. He treated us like we were ten which was frustrating. Overall, he was a nice guy

Mitch is a pretty good professor for ACCY201, but the course itself is very lecture heavy. If you don't come in with prior financial or managerial accounting knowledge, be prepared to practice the different kinds of problems a lot! There is some extra credit available so take advantage of it. Lectures are mandatory because of iClicker questions.
This is one of the least understanding professors I've ever had. He did not adapt well to the covid-19 pandemic like many other profs did, and was extremely unhelpful during these hard times.

Professor Fisher is one of the best professor Ive ever had. He truly cared about his students and spent a lot of time making sure that we understand the content. He replied to his emails in a timely matter. I had him during the covid19 semester and his transition to online class was very smooth without any interruptions on our learning at all.

Mitch is great, he was very considerate during the pandemic. You just need to do all the work to get an A. It is really easy to get all your points from homework, lectures, etc. Study really hard for exams using past activities and exams and you will be fine!

Arrogant unexperienced professor. Very obvious that it is his second year here. Don't know how people can say his lecture slides were helpful bc he doesn't know how to explain basic concepts and instead goes into way too much irrelevant details that just make you more confused than before. Tests are bs, take any other accy professor if u can

This guy is honestly amazing. It's not too hard of a class if you actually pay attention and don't get behind on work/bs it. Pretty basic accounting tbh so it's a moderately easy A. Fisher is great tho. Im taking his class during the pandemic and the amount of care and consideration he's giving is great. He really loves his job, students and field.

He's a nice guy, but man it's a boring class. Imagine Toby from The Office teaching a class. Not to mention, accounting is extremely challenging for someone who has no experience with it, and this class is ridiculously fast paced.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fisher is great- he has REALLY good lecture slides and is good at breaking things down to make sense to people who don't understand ACCY- he really cares about his students. The only negative thing I'd have to say is there is sometimes too much content covered & the exams are so difficult (coming from a student who studies a lot)

Mitch is a great guy and has pretty interesting lectures. He's funny and tries his best to keep lectures engaging, even though accounting itself is boring. Attendance is optional but going to class prepares you really well for the midterms, which are a large percent of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Fisher is very caring! He posted a lot of stuff on compass and is very patient with teaching. However, the class is a bit boring. Too many materials are introduced at the same time so it could be challenging. Other than this, an overall great class.

I literally love this man, he cares so much about his students and puts so much time and effort into making sure we understand the course material whether in lecture or at office hours. I took his class last semester when it was his first year here and he was already on top of everything, hats off to my boy Mitch, would definitely recommend him.

-Lectures were very boring and hard to pay attention to. -Do ALL the extra credit (It's time consuming but can give you 3.5% of your total grade back if you do it all) -Exams have HUGE weight of grade -Do the discussion H/W & go to discussion (pts. add up) -Understand HOW to do each kind of problem -Studying: Lecture slides & discussion activities

He really takes the time to work through and explain problems in class. If you show up to lecture and do all the homework you shouldn't have issues. Overall friendly guy. Take advantage of all the extra credit

Seemed to enjoy teaching and cared that the students learned the material. But, tried to teach too much material, which hurt the overall effectiveness of the course. Also, the final exam was worth around 40% of the final grade.

This was Mitch's first year as a UIUC professor, and I think he killed it. It is obvious he cares so much about his students. I think there are kinks in the format of the class to be worked out, but nonetheless, great professor. Mitch, if youre reading this, keep it up. Also, dont make the test worth 40% please.

Mitch is an awesome professor! He is new, so it took him a while to figure his stuff out but he is a very effective teacher that listens to feedback. He made ACCY 201 super informative and easy. Yes, the final is a lot of points and he is kind of a goofy guy, but he has given us really great opportunities to earn easy points.

Professor Fisher is a very good teacher. He cares about students very much by providing every week videos and prepared well for every class. Every homework is useful for the course and you can truly learn things from him.
