He is very organized and provides a lot of examples and problems, so students could constantly practice. He truly cares. He puts so much work into his course, posting all the solutions and walk-through videos online. The grading is very fair. Overall, a great professor. Take him for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great guy
Does not seem very prepared when planning ahead. A lot of the grade is towards tests. Also, seems to try to hard to be funny, which has the opposite effect.

I've found Mitch to be a quality professor. His lectures are very thorough, allowing his students to understand all of the topics. He currently teaches an introductory class, so some may find it a bit slow, but it the pace is reflective of the level. Only negative is how test heavy the class is, which the midterm worth 30% and final worth 40%.
Lots of not very good T.V./movie references. Also, for the first several weeks the class moves very slowly, continually repeating the exact same stuff.
BEAST MODE
It's a good class, just please please please make sure to dedicate a lot of time; it's definitely a big heavy lecture and workload class

I really enjoyed him as a person, he was super goofy. You get a point for every lecture you attend so it was worth it to go. Gave an extra credit assignment every week and the discussion homework was completion. The final was worth 40% and the midterm was 30% of the final grade so be sure to actually study or your grade will massively drop
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super kind professor and explains content easily (NO attendance required at all). Posts all of his lectures online. Explains very well, and his homework and exams are both easy. Study with the online homework and practice exam. NO coding knowledge is required AT ALL for labs (super easy). Overall a great class and an insanely great professor.
Amazing professor. 10/10

go to class, do the homework, and take the practice exams and you'll be good. The exams are so easy if you just pay attention & review before. The labs are kind of annoying but you get so much time to do them and don't have class on lab days

Kelly Findley is an example of my best advice when guessing if a prof will be good: Look to see if their degrees/research are in the TEACHING of a subject, not just the subject itself. Kelly very clearly cares about *teaching* statistics well, and it is extremely easy to learn from him as a result. He is also very kind and patient with students.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Findley is definitely the best professor I had last semester. His lectures are optional and he always posts recorded lectures in a timely manner the day of the lecture. His lectures are engaging, he provides detailed note sheets that make taking notes for his class very simple. He provides tons of extra credit! Exams just like homework!
Pretty easy class if you go to lecture, exams have plenty of review materials to study. Professor is easygoing and coursework is reasonable.
Very strict in terms of doing projects a specific way he wants them done.

Professor Findley is a great guy. He gives great lectures and you can tell he really cares about his students and the subject. The class is pretty easy, and there's tons of opportunities for extra credit. Labs are a bit of a pain but its not that bad, you have resources and lab days. If you do the homework and practice exams you should be fine.

Dr. Findley was an amazing professor. He truly cares about the topic he teaches and about his students. Definitely made going to class better. Attendance isn't mandatory but you should go to get the notes because watching the lectures can be a pain. I would definitely take another course with him if I had to take another stats course.

Dr Findley was a great professor! I took him for Stat 212 which was not required by my major, but I took it as a replacement for CS 361, which was allowed by my major. Honestly, great choice, because this class taught me how to read scientific papers, which was more useful for my career path.

Professor Findley is a great professor. You don't need to go into this class with coding/stats knowledge to do well. He does a great job at lecturing; he's very concise and keeps things interesting. There's a workbook, but it's optional to purchase since there's a digital copy. There's also plenty of extra credit throughout the semester.

Kelly is really nice and honestly does explain his content very well. However, the labs are the biggest waste of time imaginable. You are forced to code in honestly a pretty difficult coding language ( at least for beginners) and I truly have yet to see how the "labs" apply to the course or its content.

Kelly is a great professor! I had never taken a Stats class in my life and he made it so easy. Lectures are optional, but if you show up you will do well in the class. Exams are in the CBTF, overall they were never bad as long as you prepare. Tons of extra credit opportunities. He is very kind and I would absolutely take another class with him!

I enjoyed having Kelly as a professor! He is friendly and approachable and was very good at explaining concepts in lectures. I recommend attending lectures even if they are optional because they are helpful. Also, go to the exam review sessions he hosts before each exam! He answers questions and they are hosted through Zoom.

GREAT professor. Super chill super friendly. Stats is not easy, but he made it very easy to understand. His lectures are not mandatory but I would suggest to go to his lectures anyways. His textbook are notes that you can fill in during lecture. There's online ones available for free or you can buy them at the bookstore.

I came into this class with some AP Stats experience which made the material easy to follow, but I believe that anyone can succeed, regardless of prior knowledge in this course! Kelly is an amazing teacher, lectures usually consist of fill in the blank notes where he often elaborates on points in the notes. He made sure to address questions.
He explains things clearly, but for me he did not teach in my preferred learning style. He really likes class participation, but if you are on the shyer side, his class can feel very taxing.

Prof. Findley is a great professor! He explains concepts very clearly and is willing to answer questions during lecture. I do think that he is sometimes too lenient in terms of student participation and he gives more than what the class typically gives back. Assignments and labs aren't difficult, and a great course for introductory stats.
Professor Kelly is a very nice teacher and wonderful lecturer.

Currently enrolled in 212, he is a great professor! I have never taken a stats class in my life, came in completely blind with no prior stats knowledge, and easily got an A on my first 2 exams. He is really clear on what you need to understand in order to succeed, provides a lot of extra credit, and posts recorded exams online. Such a friendly guy!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Kelly was really caring about my success and was helpful during office hours. Would love to have him again!
Very kind teacher, easy to understand, not too fast or slow. Goes over notes and records them. Great Professor.
reading the other reviews was interesting cuz maybe he was nice in the past but this past semester he didnt seem super passionate about teaching or helping students succeed

His teaching style and ability is fine but nothing super special. I learned the material mostly on my own time. He posts lectures online so you don't have to go to class. I tried to go to class a couple times, but I'm glad I didn't because he is hard to talk to.

This professor was soo awful. The class is easy because the content is easy. If you ever have a personal conversation with him you'll know how weird he is. I asked him for help once and he made me feel bad for asking! I would never ever take a class with this man again

I loved Dr. Kelly's classes. I had zero background in stats and coding and he made it so easy to learn. Labs can be tough with the coding but if you find a good partner and go to lab days you can get help with anything very quickly. Lectures are all posted online. This is a professor who only cares about you learning the material not your grade.
Very nice professor! It's a good experience to have class with Kelly!

LOVE KELLY. Very chill and his textbook for the class is really a notebook that he made for each activity and everything you need to learn is in it. However, there are labs almost every week. Other than that, I loved the class.

As someone who hates anything math-related, Kelly made statistics enjoyable. He is very friendly and enthusiastic when it comes to answering questions. I had never coded a day in my life before this class, but with his tutorials I was able to get A's on all of my labs. I recommend STAT212 to any of my fellow science majors looking for math credit!

I absolutely loved Dr Findley for this course! I think students definitely sleep on STAT 212 to complete the requirement for the stats major (212, 200, or 107). 212 was pretty straightforward and when it wasn't, Kelly was amazing at what he does! Loved it! :)

He was amazing at teaching the content! The exams weren't that different from the practice homework, and there were many opportunities for extra credit. The labs were the most challenging part of the class for me since I have difficulty coding, but even then, the instructions were clear enough that they weren't an issue.

Kelly is an amazing professor! He clearly has a passion for statistics AND teaching and knows how to explain stats to complete beginners. Very generous and kind with extensions, understanding of student concerns, and his exams are completely representative of what he taught in lecture. Labs are not hard if you read and follow his guide!

Kelly is one of the best teachers I have ever had. Very caring and will always reply back to emails immediately. Tests are very representative of what he teaches in lectures. Labs can be time consuming but are informative. He gives you the opportunity to succeed and is a very caring teacher!
Good professor. The CBTF quizzes are very very easy except quiz 3, so many extra points. Labs are a little time-consuming.  Don't need to go to lectures.
Super willing to explain things and give extra points. Reasonable and still a good teacher. Exams are p average but he gives a lot of resources

If you have a tablet you can download the "textbook" which you can take notes in. I had this class at 8am so lectures were not that interesting. Reading all the ratings, Findley is a decent professor in my opinion. I had trouble understanding a few concepts and he wasn't meeting me halfway. But overall, pretty easy class, take notes and review them

The notes for this class are really clear and easy to follow and were given printed with a few fill in the blanks. Tests were really easy if you went over the notes, which did not take long. I never went to lecture and submitted every lab late and still got an A. Overall really good professor who knows how to teach and make things simple.

(STAT 200) Kelly Findley is an excellent professor who tries to get audience participation and adds pop culture references occasionally into his lectures. The labs are time-consuming and can be difficult (R-coding), but otherwise, this class is really a bit of a breeze.
Great professor who cares about his students success. He goes the extra mile to ensure his lectures are clear and concise. Occasionally cracks a solid joke too.
Kelly is one of the best there is at UIUC! This man made me feel so cared for and that my success was his success. A true gem; take his class for an amazing semester and you will not be disappointed!
I really enjoyed this class. Highly recommend taking it, especially with Findley. You learn a lot in the course that you can apply to real life, even if you may later change your mind about STEM.

Great lecturer. Clear grading criteria. Quick response time. He clearly takes teaching very seriously and is genuinely an interesting person. The midterms and final are most of your grade, but the final can replace a midterm if you do better on it. Overall would highly recommend taking his STAT400 course.

Kellys lectures can feel a little bit like eternity HOWEVER, he makes the material very accessible. Tests can feel a little tricky but if you pay attention in class (ie go to lecture which you get EC for anyway) and write good cheat sheets, youre good to go. Kelly is very accessible outside of class. The coding labs are actually super fun!

He is by far the best professor at UIUC. He holds many office hours and is always available via email or campuswire. Cheat sheets on all exams, so just write the formulas and definitions. The TAs will walk you through the coding labs. Also, you can get up to 25 extra credit points. I got an A+ in the class but I didnt put in much effort
You can bring a cheat sheet into exams. Also he helps a ton with the coding labs. Wish I could be taught by him for every course.
Terrible teacher. Not understanding of students. Terrible class and even worse teacher. Dont do it.

Prof Findley is great! Took AP Stats previously but there's still a lot to learn (esp with R coding). Grading is very fair with lots of extra credit opportunities, and recorded lectures were very clear w/detailed course notes. Be sure to use campuswire/office hours if needed, Prof Findley and the TAs are very helpful. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kelly is awesome! He's super chill, kind, and understanding! I took his online course and the prerecorded lectures were posted on YT, which you could follow along with in the course notes packet. The feedback given on homework questions, labs, unit reports, and exams is extensive and helps a ton when figuring out where you went wrong. He's great!
Best professor I've had in the Statistics department! Really good lectures and lots of resources and extra credit available. Such a nice guy and also teaches you a lot throughout the entire semester.

Kelly is super chill and very lenient about assignments. He is understanding of our situations and adapts. The work isn't too bad either. Just watch the lecture videos and do your homework. It doesn't take up too much of my week. Exams were open notes so it was not difficult. He also offers extra credit throughout the course.

Findley is super approachable and is very helpful during office hours. He explains concepts very simply and thoroughly. He doesn't add any unnecessary workload. Lecture and homework problems are very reflective of what he expects on exams; he doesn't test on unit assignments or reports. If you listen to the lectures and do the work, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took kelly this semester for biostatistics online. He was amazing! Very understanding, doesnt add on unnecessary stress! He has office hours everyday! Hes super kind! The class does feature 2 group assignments for every unit (theres 5). But if you go to office hours he will help you! Honestly the best prof I have this semester!

Dr. Findley is a fine statistics professor, but he basically just reads off a pocket. His exams are also much harder than the examples shown in class. Additionally, his exams this semester have been harder than the previous semesters by making them more wordy. Wished the standard were normal across the board, especially during the pandemic.

He is the sweetest and is really good at explaining the concepts from class. The content overall is relatively easy as long as you do the notes in the notebook, the homework on Lon-capa and the practice exams when it comes to taking exams.

Absolutely loved Professor Findley. He puts so much work into his class and is very down to earth. He really helps his students out and despite the class being at 8am, lectures are not mandatory and all the information is put online/in a class notebook you buy at the beginning of the term for like 15$.

Dr. Findley is a great professor! He is extremely positive and his lectures were very enjoyable. He provides many materials to prepare for the quizzes and is always willing to help. He gave excellent feedback on assignments, and the group projects are interesting and fun. It was a great class and I highly recommend it!

Findley is the best math professor I've had on campus. His lectures are clear, his quizzes don't have any surprises, and he is super accessible outside of class. He genuinely cares for his students, and will make sure that all quiz averages are high. If you need help with material, ASK HIM. He will be more than happy to help, and you will do great

Dr Findley is the best teacher I've had at UIUC! He's super accessible outside of class and his tests are always similar to problems in the notes or on the homework. He's also super fun and knows most of his student's names by the end of the semester. I'm seriously considering minoring in stats given how much fun I had in this class!

Dr. Findley is an incredible teacher. His lectures are interesting and engaging, the homework is not terribly changing, and all of what we learn is well represented on the exam. Dr. Findley is such a caring and nice guy, you can tell he feels really passionate about the subject and his students, and that is something that really motivated me.

Awesome teacher, He is super cool and he makes it super easy to do well on exams. He is a new teacher but he really knows his stuff. He is always willing to set up times outside of office hours to work with you. Very approachable teacher would recommend.
Dr. Findley is awesome! Don't even mind getting up for his 8AM because he is such a good teacher and great guy.

By far the best professor I've had at this school. There's not enough to fully describe what an amazing class with Professor Fields from the past semester. Honestly, finishing the class left me with concepts that will continue my future. Just an overall outstanding professor who loves her students just as much as she loves herself. She's the best.

Do not expect grades in a timely manner. She is a very kind professor and she cares about her students, but sometimes not having an exam grade from a month ago is scary when you are about to take the next. She will lecture for a bit and sometimes group activities are part of class. Syllabus has errors on it from the last teacher to have this class.

Ms. V is an incredible teacher, she not only gives great lectures, but also she is super kind to all students. She is very responsible and she actually cares about us. She is always super well-prepared for every single lecture, and she always encourages us to and share our thoughts and ideas in class. I love her!!! Take her class!!!

Honestly top 3 professor Ive had here. Super caring about the students and brings great energy to the class. I have the class at 10am and usually show up pretty tired but by the end I have a good amount of energy and am ready to start the day. The class isnt too bad, just have to stay on top of it, but visual politics is/was a great experience.
Best professor in UIUC, not only in the department of Astronomy. Gives detailed explanation to almost everything in class, and cares for students. He is nice to every student.
great guy overall, made astronomy very fun!

Professor Fields was a spectacular professor. I came in to take ASTR404 with him with none of the recommended physics background but I was able to catch on easily with how he teaches. I felt that the homework was pretty hard most of the time, office hours were my best friend in this class. Gives extra credit on pretty much everything.

By far one of the best professors I've had. His lectures are interesting and engaging, homework sometimes has its challenges but he's almost always available if there are questions and there are opportunities for extra credit on every assignment. Exams were very fair with the ability to make an equation sheet.

Professor Fields was not only my favorite professor at UIUC but has been the best teacher I've had in my entire life. He is incredibly knowledgeable, and explained concepts perfectly so that everyone could understand what he was trying to say. Also, his homework and exams were always very well-written: not too difficult but really made you think.

This seminar was required because I'm an astronomy major, and honestly, I am so glad I got to meet Brian (and Bryan, too!), and I am even more glad he's actually my advisor! He is such a wonderful human being who really cares about his students! He's got so much passion and excitement about astronomy, it's fascinating! He's such a sunshine-y guy.
Professor Fields is by far my favorite professor because he actually cares about his students. He's very good at teaching and extremely helpful if you ask questions. He's the best!

I have very little background and took this class as an elective. I have to say Professor Fields is one of the best professors I have ever encountered. He made the class fair and fun. I learned a lot and his teaching methods are just outstanding! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!
His is the best professor. He provides very clear illustration about the content,and the homework is fun and thought provoking. This is the best course I have taken in UIUC.

First, this was an exceptionally easy course.  I went to about half of the classes (and occasionally stopped in to turn stuff in) and got an easy A.  In fact, it should have been an easy A+ if I had done anything the second half of the semester.  He's good to listen to, it's like tuning in to the science channel every few days.

He is very knowledgeable and a truly great guy! He obviously loves what he's teaching and his lectures are always very interesting! Also has a great sense of humor. If you really study, exams shouldn't be a problem. I highly recommend him a a professor!

This professor was the best I've had yet. His TA's and his office hours were at times when I had class so I asked him to meet with me whenever I had questions on the homework. We ended up meeting about once a week and he was very enthusiastic and explained things very well each time. He is a great person, and extremely NICE. He loves what he does.
"If you're alright with infinity, what's a little bit more?"
Fantastic teacher and compelling lecturer.
Extremely witty and great sense of humor.  Very nice and willing to help if you ask questions.  If you take his class, I would suggest getting to know him simply becaues he is such a great man.
The only professor I've ever seen receive applause at the end of the course. Very nice, surprisingly witty, and VERY smart!
"Close enough for government work"

Textbook: None!
Lectures: Long but interesting, learned something new every day. Heavy on complex tech concepts.
Extra Credit: Lots of opportunities (bumping me from an A to an A+). 
Jacob is understanding and though some tech concepts were difficult to grasp, they were explained in a way that ensured at least a basic understanding!

No exams and all quizzes open book. Some assignments are tedious and annoying but they're manageable. Good amount of extra credit. Some of the material is really interesting if you can grasp it but sometimes it does get tech heavy. Lectures move fast and are content heavy, sometimes hard to keep up with. Fisher is a nice guy and is approachable.

Workload is manageable to an extent. There are four individual assignments throughout the semester that are time consuming. There is also a semester long group project, he doesn't give class time to work on projects or meet our group members. Lectures are long and there is too much content that I didn't fully understand. Not my favorite class.

I've heard that these group projects can be hit or miss, so I'm glad I got a good one because you'll be working with the same people all sem! There were lectures and readings each week on Perusall, but get in early to get comments/questions everyone will engage with. Quizzes straightforward if you watch the lectures (I took notes). Good class!

This course is taught completely by a TA, not Prof. Henshaw, but I had a great TA who was very understanding and knew what he was talking about. Overall, the homework assignments take a LONG time and the biggest weight on your grade are the 3 quizzes. Overall, it was manageable but very fast paced.
The TA did not know how to teach.

Took this online with a TA online. We were basically left on our own for homework, which  was a lot. Some material was review but some was new, so learning through a textbook was horrible. Definitely a good course to learn/touch-up grammar, but take in person and maybe you'll be better off. Scraped every last point possible and still only got a B
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class wasn't hard as long as you did the work. 2 discussions a week taught by the TA which was fine because they are all really knowledgeable. The semester is split into 2 by having 2 main essays you work on. Plenty of time to do them with a lot of opportunities for feedback. If you take some time to work in this class you'll get an A

It is kind of hard to rate her because we never saw her all semester, only the TA.  2 main big essays that you do, but other than that it is a pretty low maintenance class.  HW is online and can be ridiculously subjective sometimes (for example asking what a painting symbolizes or something) but it is doable.  No exams/quizzes so that is nice.

1 lecture and 2 discussions a week. Her lectures are mandatory since there's iclicker points. 2 exams and a final (with a retake on 1 exam if you did poorly). 2 essays with an opportunity to edit mistakes for some points back. Lots of useless online homework and workbook activities. She can be helpful, but test out of this class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She was a great professor, but her exams were kind of hard. Even while speaking in spanish, she was easy to understand.

Generally, she was a good professor. Lectures were interesting. But she is very strict with grading. Make sure you READ THE SYLLABUS FULLY. She had important information on there about grading of assignments that you could miss if you don't read it.

She's pretty good doing lectures. She makes them interesting and entertaining. However there is a TON of iclicker points every week so make sure you go to lecture. Also, there is a lot of homework online. But overall, the course was very easy to manage.
Nice and enthusiastic, but also difficult and goes far too fast in lectures. There is also an unreasonable amount of online homework.

Provides a horrible rubric for the class. Huge negative is her importance on rough drafts. 30% of the grade is based on 8 drafts worth 2 points a piece. TA rarely gives 22 on drafts so you basically lose 15% of your grade right away. Her response when asked about extra credit was "afraid not." Never comes to class, required to buy HER book online.
She's very clear and makes the content easy to understand. The exams are a bit difficult.
She was a decent teacher but without my prior knowledge and amazing TA I don't think I would've done as well. She gives random extra credit assignments and points which is a big plus.

I had a bad TA which really killed the class considering there were two discussions a week, but the one lecture we would have was excellent. She infuses humor and intellect brilliantly. A terrific professor.

I was told that I took the class AFTER they revamped it, so it may have been a lot harder since they were testing it out on the new group of kids. She was okay, tried to make things clear, but the exams were SO difficult, and no partial credit. Did my best, but did not enjoy it too much.
She's a sweetheart and very clear with her explanations. Definitely a great teacher.

Never interacted, just the TAs haha. But from what I've seen, she's not to sore on the eyes! The classes/lecture was run by the TAs and all the hw was online I loved the TAs, but the class was ridiculous. The homework wasn't very related to the class and the tests and written exams were incredibly difficult. Pity I have one semester left.
Florencia is one of the nicest teachers you will ever have.  She makes the class interesting and engaging.  Even if you are not very good at spanish she will help you learn.  Very fair grader.

I had her for Spanish 103 and I love her! She is very funny and made discussion entertaining. I believe she grade pretty hard, but she is a awesome teacher. I'd register for her class asap. She is better than most Spanish's teachers I heard from my friends.
She was a great teacher and an even better friend.  I will remember her for a lifetime. Plus, she very pretty, hmhm.
Great teacher. Very understandable, helpful, and fun. Made discussion much more bearable.
Best Spanish teacher of my life... class was interesting and fun. I learned a lot, and things I was confused about from high school were all cleared up! Sign up for her class... asap!

The content of SPAN 141 isn't particularly interesting (it's GRAMMAR), but our section made the best of it and we had a blast. Florencia is extremely knowledgeable and helpful. I wish I could take more Spanish with her!

The part that makes this course so terrible is that each exam has had a question that nobody knows how to do. Literally never taught to us before, Florian expects us to know how to do math or apply concepts that were NOT even taught to us. And you'd think that he would waive a question if literally the whole class got it wrong, but nope!

Probably the worst lecturer I've experienced. Didn't generate any excitement, gave me no reason to come to class other than the grade. Just walks through problems with little to no explanation, doesn't seem to consider that some student's confidence levels may differ. Nice guy, terrible lecturer. TAs were lacking. Only learned content on my own.

This is a new professor granted, but his teaching styles are very ineffective and going to class felt like a chore because I was rather better teaching myself. He is a nice man, but not a good professor. I had to drop this course because I felt unsupported and the TA's were confused to. Now I have to re take the class during the summer and PAY.

He doesn't explain work well, and the class is unorganized. He is always behind on lectures. I learned everything from my TA. He loves to gatekeep the answer keys for practice exams. Homework and exams took forever to get graded. The class is significantly more difficult if you don't have any prior knowledge of the topics discussed in lectures.

For a class that covers rudimentary calculus, this class is so incredibly difficult to navigate. Lectures are always running behind, doesn't teach, just reads off notes from text. Assigns worksheets for discussion topics not yet covered in lecture, forcing TAs to do the teaching, and they're terrible too. You're better off taking engineering calc.

Terrible professor and terrible TA. AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS. He is always a lecture behind, but has no communication with his TAs, so we are asked to do worksheets in discussion over stuff we have not learned yet. Homework is graded for accuracy, and is graded very hard and confusing to understand what you got wrong. TAs are also no help.

The lectures are bad. He also makes it so you have to calculate your current grade for yourself but barely explains how. Because of this, I didn't realize how bad my grade was and I had to withdraw halfway through. The material isn't that difficult he just makes it hard to succeed.

The professor is very hard to understand. His lectures do not represent what is on the exams. He is unclear when explaining things and just expects you to know where he gets certain answers from. It is a very unorganized class; TAs don't even know what is happening most of the time and are not very helpful either.

Absolutely awful as a professor. It's his 1st year teaching and it SHOWS. I ended up dropping his class because of how terribly organized it was. He was always behind on the class notes and then would expect us to know how to do certain problems on the homework WHEN HE HASN'T TAUGHT THEM TO US YET. Extremely petty grader. Hw is graded for accuracy.

Professor would consistently do the work incorrectly and give the wrong answers in lecture. Lecture and discussion problems did not match the exam. Syllabus did not match actual class expectations. Never made ANYTHING clear. Also, very hard to get in communication with via email. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WITH THE PROFESSOR IF YOU DO NOT HAVE TO!!
Amazing teacher! Everyone should get an A.
Really great class

Flavia was a great professor who really cares about her students and the material she was teaching! The course was very manageable and she adapted well to moving online. I would absolutely take another course with her.

I'm sure she's a fine professor outside of COVID, but she was not a good professor online. She was super disorganized and took months to grade just one paper. If you absolutely need this class, then risk it and get ready to be confused, if not I'd say skip this class and her. Also*warning* our final was a final paper and a final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is a professor that cares about her student. I didn't do so well in the first exam but she took the time to help me even when I couldn't make it to office hours
She really cares if you learn and she is more than willing to help outside of class. Definitely recommend having her.
She wants to help you in any way possible, so take her up on that, and you will be fine.

Good teacher. Sometimes it was hard to understand but if you go to office hours or ask her to go over again, she will. I can do without the group project. TA wasn't all that great, seemed scare to teach us.

I don't know why I did not have the experience that the others hand before me. For your sake, avoid as she has become one of the worst professors in the school. She has no consideration for any of her students and quite frankly, has no interest in their well-being. AVOID AVOID AVOID cannot stress any further. Take another class or wait a semester.

I had never taken a stats class before and prof. Andrade helped me to get an A. She is one of the most helpful and easy-to-understand professors I have ever had. She is always available to help and you will have enough resources to get you through the class.
This class is difficult but mandatory best to take it will a easier semester
great instuctor: caring, great examples. relevant homework.  good class.
She's a really good teacher, and her examples are very helpful. Just make sure you do all of the homework, and pay attention in class and you'll be fine.

Very nice. She's very helpful especially if you go to her office hours she'll re explain anything you don't understand. Exams are okay if you study and use the practice exams she gives you. Homeworks easy too, there's about one assaignment a week.

she can be pretty funny. she moves quickly through the material however. if you feel like you are confused go in for help right away before you get too far behind (which is easy to do). the two projects aren't too difficult but seemed somewhat pointless to me. There are three exams (including the final) practice exams and reviews are provided

This class is somewhat easy.BUT it is easy to fall behind. She is such an extremely nice person and is always willing to help with any question you have. There are three exams in total, all of which are so-so.This class is all about keeping up with the material, so if you do that, then you should do well on the exams. The least u should get is a B.

Awful class. Flachsbart zooms through the lectures, covering everything on a surface level. Labs are instructive but boring, team project is fun but educationally useless, and both are time-consuming and unrelated to lecture. Very important for mechanical engineering, but don't be fooled: this is a 3-credit class with a workload of about 5 credits.

Attending the lectures then trying to do the assignments is kind of like being taught how to walk then be expected to do a 200m obstacle run. He speeds through lectures, seems to be nice enough of a person but that does NOT translate into his teaching abilities. Avoid if at all possible.

unclear grading criteria with group project, have been told he cares more for higher-level classes, is a nice person, lectures are only needed for online math questions, expect  to spend 5-10 hours outside class for group project,

Offers help yet if something arises that only he can solve he'll be very lazy and potentially blame you for it. Structure is lazy and exams are just recycled homework. Final project is largely a waste of time and doesn't teach much in terms of MFG. Overall not a bad course but avoid it if you have the option.

Speeds through lectures and doesn't post notes anywhere, so if you miss class, you're screwed. Labs are tedious and lab TA's were awful. Very little communication between any of the course staff. The group project took insane amounts of time and is a huge pain. Grading was usually pretty harsh.

Lectures go way too fast. Having a project meant to be inefficient and useless defeats the purpose of using design principles. Coordination for getting project materials was nonexistent. Expect to spend 10 or more hours on group work before each deadline, depending on group mates. Going above and beyond guidelines for presentations is expected.

Lectures were long and not the most enticing
Labs require minimum 5-7 hours of work per week
Communication between professor and LA's are awful
Rube Goldberg machine takes way too much time outside of class

If you think this class is challenging, drop out of engineering school. Bruce is one of the few at UIUC that teach instead of regurgitating information. The TAs are awful, but that doesn't mean Bruce is a bad professor. The group project is easy, albeit time-consuming. You just have to be ready to try.
Your project better be damn perfect because you will need every point you can get in this class.

The TA I had for this class was by far the worst TA I have ever had in my entire college career. I've heard similar things from numerous sections. They are useless in terms of helping you, and they are out to get you in terms of grading and taking points off of assignments and projects. Bruce himself is cool. It's a shame the TA's ruin his class.

If it wasn't for the group project I maybe would have hated this class slightly less. Don't even waste your time going to the lectures as there is literally no point. He goes ridiculously fast and doesn't even try to teach the material. You'll learn it on Quizlet. The ta's are TERRIBLEfor this class. They dedicate their life to making yours worse.

They constantly change the rules for the project and their grading criteria. They should have that finalized BEFORE the semester; talk about unprepared. They grade the labs SOO slow, and they don't take this into consideration. If you made an error in the first report you won't know until after you submit the 5th report - it'll effect you on all 5.

Professor Flachsbart is fine during lectures. That is all that is good about the class. The HW is due on Friday even though the lectures end Thursday. There are a lot of bad TA that are rude and not helpful. You will not get an A on the final project as they make it their mission to give you a B. Good luck with this class as you will hate it.
This class is a waste of time. I don't think I've learned a single important thing. Feels like a filler busy work class.

If you can take Me270 with someone else do so... but I think Bruce is the only one who teaches it unfortunately. Honestly Bruce isn't that bad himself, but the class is structured terribly. And if you get stuck with a bad TA you will have an awfull experience... my TA sucks
The amount of work that they expect you to put into this class is absolutely ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AVOID him if possible.Lecture is speedreading slides and he doesn't care if students can follow.Homework is released on Tuesday,due Friday of the same week,with most questions have only one try,no extra or late credit. Lab has quiz,tasks,report each week and a project. Midterm has 30 questions in 50 minutes,although they are all from homework.

Pretty easy class, tests were straight from hw problems, just spend a few hours memorizing and you'll be fine. Group project pointless but not too terrible, put in decent effort and you'll coast to a decent grade. However, you will learn absolutely nothing, lectures are pointless and you'll never actually understand any concepts. Terrible professor
He has his pace and his way of explaning things. Usually way too fast.

All of the negative ratings are probably from freshmen who shouldn't be in this class anyway. I thought this class was taught very well. I thoroughly enjoyed Bruce as a professor and personality. Very fun guy who will answer any question you have, but asks for respect in lecture. Was willing to meet 1:1 on zoom almost anytime I had a question.

Bruce does not care about his students. He frequently would not answer questions and go out of his way to make the students life harder just because he can. Class it self was not hard but dealing with the professor was the hardest part of the class by far.

Horrible professor. Rushes through the lectures way too fast. You basically have to teach yourself. The class is just memorizing everything. The course is not well organized. Late credit is almost never given. This might be one of the worst courses I've taken so far at this school.

Lecture attendance isn't "mandatory", but you'll miss all of the important information if you skip. His lectures consist of reading of slides at a breakneck speed, and if you miss the information, too bad. There is a distinct lack of communication both between him and his TAs, and his students. He comes off as an insufferable egomaniac.

The management of the course was quite poor. I could tell there was a big lack in communication between the professor and TA's. The expectations for assignments/projects seemed to be changing constantly. Aside from that, the tests were nearly identical to the homework, so you've got that going for you. Overall, a bit rough.

Honestly impressively bad. Terrible lectures that are just him reading off slides, posts the slides but removes the most important parts to try and force you to attend his lectures. Insufferable personality wise, so incredibly full of himself, unclear instructions all around, and overall terrible. DO NOT TAKE HIM FOR THIS CLASS.

He was incredibly rude and unprofessional. He is vague in his instructions, and he gets angry when you do not follow his vague instructions. He also gives little respect to the students during presentations, constantly interrupting and talking down to them.

Bruce has a very vibrant, big personality. Don't let his critical remarks cut too deep, but listen to his complements and most importantly his advice as they come from a very genuine place. Although he may mismanage certain aspects of his classes (notably, the arbitrary quizzes that are just randomized homework questions), he runs a fun class.

Abysmal experience. I honestly regret not spending an extra semester in college just to avoid this guy. Does not respect the time of his students, and is completely unwilling to spend any of his time improving course content. Lectures were pretty pointless, and a waste of time similar to everything else in this class. Avoid avoid avoid
If you like speedrunning, you would love this professor. He goes through everything at a breakneck speed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid taking courses with him if possible. He did not answer a lot of my questions in office hours. Does not seem to care much about the students.

Very intense - don't take his remarks personally. I wasn't a fan of his personality. He will make you redo things if he sees that you finish the group project early. Tests are CBTF but straight from the homework. Group project is very time consuming but if you make a solid effort, your grade will reflect it. Not the best professor, but no choice.

Bruce is a beaming oasis of light in a soul-siphoning monstrosity of a class. His last name is pronounced "flox-bart", not "flash-bart", and he will flox you hard if you slack off on the group project. If you know how to bargain and agree on a direction of progress with him that you can feasibly pull off, he will be very pleased with the end result
Fun class and very informative. The project was super fun and rewarding but required a LOT of work.

Bruce is a very intense person and has the strongest personality I have ever seen.    The group project is what makes the course difficult.  If you want a good grade on the project you must take all of his suggestions, go to office hours frequently to make sure he still likes your direction, and START WORKING RIGHT AWAY.

Great class (weekly labs, 2 lectures per week, weekly homework, semester group project). You will learn a lot from Bruce, but be ready to work for it. If you show you are trying and come to him for help he will help you; he wont spoon feed you. Prof gives you the building blocks to do the work. Read the notes before class.
Cool material, horrible group project. But only he teaches it so no point in complaining

Weekly homework, Biweekly labs, and semester long project with three presentations makes this class quite a handful for only 3 credit hours given. Bruce is a relatively nice guy. His class is very unorganized and the exams had multiple spelling errors on them, which made the 50min tests a nightmare to finish on time. He grades very subjectively.

Least favorite course in 7 semesters. I found Flachsbart rude and very unprofessional. Doesn't want to clarify vagueness and blames students for lack of understanding. Every aspect of the course fails to teach, so you have to teach yourself, not that you'll be rewarded for doing so. Tests are riddled with errors that make them nearly untakeable.
Very disorganized in general. Tests are disorganized.

For the semester project, he likes neat gadgets that don't work over useful things that do work (if he doesn't think your project is cool, you will probably fail the project). During presentations, he is incredibly rude, condescending and unprofessional. Interrupted and didn't let us finish our presentation and then marked us down for not finishing

Content is very easy, but the exams are graded to pick out mistakes, rather than lack of knowledge. Do the homeworks and know them going into the exams, and try not to make a single careless mistake (and watch out for trick questions). Very supportive outside of lecture, go to office hours if homework's give you trouble.
Engineering Enthusiast.
Great teacher, super patient and considerate. Tests are not that difficult. But a lot of homework every week.

awesome professor. lecture attendance is a must but he pretty much tells you exactly what is going to be on the exams. very helpful in office hours, and always has time for students. only con is that labs are a pain in the ass. even so i recommend him.
avoid if possible
Very exciting class.  Very engaging lecture

Lectures were dry. He asked us literally zero questions. For harder concepts, I wish he would spend some time working through examples by hand to build intuition rather than diving straight into details. Exams were hard (and took place from 7PM to 10PM,). Assignments aren't grades till the end, so you have zero feedback on how you're doing

Assignments are not graded nor are solutions posted prior to finals week. He literally decides when not to show up to lecture and notifies the class 30 minutes prior to meeting for his decision. He fails to release hws or update the calendar in a reasonable time. He cut content from the course due to his own laziness and has bad handwriting.
no one attends lecture because his handwriting is hard to read. Homework grades (as other have said) have not been posted yet and the semester is almost over.  I regret ever taking a course with him.
His handwriting is hard to read. We haven't had any assignments graded yet. Exam solutions have not been posted.

Professor Forbes explains concepts clearly and concisely, allowing him to cover significant material in each lecture. Homework grades are unavailable until the final week, but he answers questions frequently on piazza.

Extremely unorganized class. Homeworks weren't graded until the last week of the semester (we only got 2 of them back before the final) and the solutions took forever to get posted, so you won't be able to see the correct solutions until weeks after the fact. He's decent enough at explaining things, but his handwriting is unreadable
Was activated with the National Guard during the class. Professor Font was extremely understanding and helpful, and provided alternate means of completing the course.
Course covers everything about Premiere Pro from the basics to things as hard as editing moving objects across a green screen. Timely feedback is provided by the instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Heavy reliance on group projects with no useful tips taught in class. There's always a tight schedule before deadlines, so that no one can complete their work decently. Include both projects and exams, and all his classes are scheduled in the early morning. And unfortunately, us MACS students still have to take his classes.

Victor is a chill guy + very lenient in my experience, you might struggle a bit in his production courses if you have no familiarity with adobe (not hard to learn), but there's a lot of leeway with projects. If you want a passing grade, you just have to turn in something. End of semester is always fun when everyone's short films are screened.

Awful! Lectures include content that doesn't apply to assignments and he pretty much just promotes his other classes and shows random movie clips. Heavy on group assignments and doesn't give enough time for groups to meet  before deadline. If you don't already know Adobe programs then good luck cause he definitely won't teach you.
Taking an online class from him becomes very difficult when the Exam is 2 days late in being posted, and he doesn't respond to emails.

Grade entirely based off of 9 homeworks. David Forsyth is by far one of the most inspirational professors I've had the pleasure of learning under. I have never felt such raw desire to succeed and dive into the world of machine learning than I found under his tutelage. 10/10, a south african KING.

Lectures are in-depth and follow along with his book, which makes it easy to review what you were just lectured on. Not necessarily a harsh grader for individual assignments, but the final grading scale seemed to be a bit harsh (got a B+ with 95% in the class). Doing the remission of sins E.C./homework at the end may be necessary to get an A.
Good professor.
Prof. Forsyth is a great lecturer and his book is amazing (and free).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I guarantee you will not regret taking his class if you put a little bit of time into it. David cares more about teaching, research, and learning, than grades and bureaucracy.
Good lecturer. Really nice professor. Very knowledgeable.
Maybe it was just the topic being bland or him just going too fast but I had a hard time following his lectures. Im sure if he taught a more interesting course he would be a great lecturer.
Awesome at lecturing - very clear, precise, and funny. Very disorganized, though. No syllabus or grading policy - doesn't respond to emails.
One of the best Professors Ive ever had. Don't miss out on this class with him

Was not easily accessible outside of class hours. Had very limited office hour times and refused to help/ answer a clarification question on group project despite it being over a week until it was due (even if sent over email). Also, grade is very test heavy. Would not take a class with this professor ever again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good teacher... beware though the midterm and final count for 65% of your grade so study for the exams A LOT. Not much outside work at all. Lecture is not required but I found it helpful.

Attendance isn't mandatory but you should definitely come to class. Prof Fonseca's lectures are crucial to understanding the material and she will always go through examples, which is super important since there aren't many assignments so if you mess up something on exams it'll be bad for your grade. Still, 10/10 would take a class with her again
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: HK200 is a pretty simple online course. Easy way to get 3 credit hours. However, the lecture videos were just of Dr. Woodson (nee Foster) reading off the slides.

I took CHLH 101. It's an easy course, but it's test heavy and Dr. Woodson doesn't do a good job in lecture. She basically reads from a PowerPoint in a video lesson and asks questions on the test that we didn't exactly learn in class. I would've gotten a higher grade, but she's a tough grader. I wouldn't take a class with her again.
Very unorganized, was not very civil when answering questions. Poorly managed class, I'd look for a different teacher, it's normally an easy class.

I got a fine grade in the class, so I can't speak on harsh grading. However, be prepared for a very uncomfortable atmosphere in class. He's extremely high-energy which often comes off as anger. If you're easily made anxious, don't bother. Provides a lot of feedback for papers, but reading the feedback might make you nauseous. Not for everyone.

Not much to add other than what other posts here have said. Unreasonably high standard of expectation from a 100-level course, extremely disorganized coursework, unnecessarily tough grading (nobody I knew got over a 65 in any essay), workload does not correspond to 3-hour 100-level gened. Take /anything/ else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: worst class experience of my life, had to take the credit/no credit option for this class since he graded so hard. don't take any class with this guy
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: forgot to fill out the evaluation forms so here I am. please don't take any courses with this guy unless ur looking to get graded harder than u have ever been graded before. literally a 100 level class and he makes it seem like he's teaching a senior class at the PhD level. crazy lol

What is wrong with this guy? He grades crazy hard and seems to dislike helping students. He was the TA for this course, and now I know why so many people dropped out at the beginning of the semester. I was like isn't this class supposed to be easy? Boy was I wrong. Please don't ever take a class with this guy near it, you'll regret it just like me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: My friend directed me here to express my views about this guy, as we have hated him ever since we started his class. Treated this class like a 400 level course, grades unnecessarily hard, and is an extremely incompetent and frustrating teacher to deal with. My friends and I took this class because we are Asian, and he makes us wish we weren't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is the worst teacher I have ever met in my life. He is stubborn and unhelpful in anything that you ask him, seems to have a superiority complex, and is generally a pain to work with. He grades as if his life depends on it and I can't even begin to imagine what he is like face-to-face. Wish I read his reviews before taking his class, never again.

Really aggressive dude. Literally made me SCARED to go to class because he would choose random people to call on and then scream at if they didn't read the material. I don't know why he's so angry all the time. Also grades incredibly difficult, it's basically impossible to pass his classes.

I genuinely despise coming to his discussion section. HIST 120 has a lot of reading for an intro class, but this isn't the issue. Forrest has no chill, seems to have a god complex, and likes to hear himself talk instead of creating an environment conducive to learning. Many others in his discussion sections have agreed with me on this. AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I regret not dropping my class with him when I could. Warning to other students: If you see he's teaching a class you've signed up for drop it and take literally ANY other class instead.

He was a TA for EALC 250 - INTRODUCTION to Japanese Culture. Certainly didn't treat the class like it was an introductory course. Prerequisite knowledge about intricate history and culture of Japan was required and constantly talked about. Felt like I knew nothing, very confusing class with him. Didn't grade fairly either. I'd avoid this class.

Took a few years ago. Fritzsche is not for the faint of heart, but he's a very rewarding professor. Yeah, you've really got to work for your grade and his respect, and he's got a bit of an ego. But if you are willing to work with him, you will find yourself in one of the most intellectually stimulating and academically rewarding classes out there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He knows how to teach about the holocaust but one thing I didn't really like about his class was how your entire grades depends on the papers. He does offer rewrites but he expects high quality essays and mini essay for the books you don't write about. Overall too much work if you're taking this to be a gen ed course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked Professor Fritzsche when I took his class. Many people seem to have had difficulty taking his class, but his feedback was very helpful for me in writing my final essay on Joseph Conrad. He expects class participation, but if your serious about your education, that shouldn't be a setback.

Fritzsche is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about his subject matter. His grading is strict (2 papers, 60% w/rewrites) and he expects a certain writing style. DO NOT fall back on the readings. His lectures are interesting and will draw you in so if you genuinely want to learn something, take his class. For a gen ed though, look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Fritzsche really knows his stuff, and his lectures (while hard to follow at times) kept me interested. The papers are easy enough, but his grading is quite harsh and takes getting used to... but he offers rewrites and corrections, so it is fair. Come to class, take notes, and read the books and you will probably do quite well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Fritzsche is clearly knowledgeable and cares deeply about the topics he lectures on, but this doesn't make him a great lecturer or teacher. 2 essays are worth 60% of your grade, and he grades them very harshly for a 200-level course. Prof. Fritzsche is open about not being good with tech but will not compromise on simple tech issues.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had. Class was only lectures, had a hard time paying attention with a lack of notes. Super tough grader, expects extremely high of you, but doesn't tell you specifically what he is looking for other than "write like a lawyer." Hates technology and won't adapt, expects you to adapt to him. Again long lectures, also boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Fritzsche has the largest quantity of readings I have every experienced as a political science and history double major, and not only do the readings not match the lecture content, but the amount of work he assigns is ridiculous. I can tell he is incredibly educated and likes to talk about history, but the workload is not worth it.

Fritzsche is a difficult professor. Very educated, but does not instruct well. He has high expectations for papers/analysis but doesnt teach how. He expects the students to know, & if they dont, he is not the most patient or understanding. Denied request for a paper deadline extension, and really tears you apart if he thinks your writing is bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Did not know I was signing up for a literature class. Get ready to read nearly a book a week and cry over the lack of cohesiveness of his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: In the context of COVID, he was extremely accommodating and had the class vote on whether or not we wanted synchronous lectures. Other than that, the uploaded lectures/slides aren't cohesive and are difficult to follow, plus we only got graded on our papers, participation, and the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: GOOD LUCK! Fritzsche teaches 498 on the Holocaust in which he is very knowledgable but wayyyyyy to knowledgeable for his own good. He is extremely hard to please and is very unhelpful if you take a little longer to comprehend. Unless you have a doctorate in history or were born during the Holocaust I would STAY AWAY!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fritzsche should consider being a professor of literature instead of history because he makes you read a novel and write an essay on it about every week. I got lucky to have a great TA, Marco, in 142, since Fritzsche cannot reinforce actual history on his own. I wish he wasn't the only professor for the period I'm interested in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The worst thing you can do is catch him in a mistake or ask about a point where he contradicts the readings. His knowledge of German history is impressive but he thinks he knows as much about other fields, but can't name important figures in those others. He holds grudges, also likes to make students buy his books for reading.

Prof Fritzsche was the hardest lecturer I've ever had. He is nearly impossible to follow because his lectures are scripted and unnecessarily poetic during class. He talks very fast with a voice that is different than his conversational tone. He seems like a nice guy who is passionate about the material, but he makes it impossible to learn.

I thought Ralphie was bad and then I had Fritzsche. His lectures are extremely hard to follow and sound rehearsed--plus he sounds like he is preaching. He will never stay on a slide long enough for anyone to even read what is on it and he doesn't put slides online or tell you anything about what the midterm/final will be one. TA's are no help.

I took this as my "easy" class and the workload was. However, sometimes the subject matter was very heavy (emotionally), but Fritzsche knows how to teach the intense subject matter. It's a very impersonal class and I doubt Fritzsche knew even 1 student;s name, but I recommend it anyways. A lot of mandatory reading.

Professor Fritzsche has a passion for teaching about the Holocaust. He often shares personal stories and gives insight on touchy subjects. The subject matter is not to be taken lightly. Some classes he has cried showing pictures. I can honestly say that I loved his lectures. He has a very dry sense of humor that is very funny if you can sense it.

He is very passionate about The Holocaust and gives his personal opinion every chance he gets. His lectures seem incredibly useless. The only thing that matters is reading the novels assigned and writing genuine papers. Seriously read. I didn't and I struggled big time. Discussions are kinda awkward but attendance is taken in discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He is a very good lecturer, makes the class interesting. However, besides that it really is your TA that does everything else. He can be slightly arrogant. The only thing that matters grade wise was discussion and the papers you had to write for the class. The midterm and final were also essays. Not hard to get and A or B in this class.

Fritzsche knows his stuff.  Super smart.  A bit intimidating at first, but he'll work with you as long you're showing effort.  He's a got very dry wit - I think students don't realize he's joking sometimes. High standards for grading, heavy on writing/essays. He sets the bar high but it's totally worth it.

This professor's lecture are extremely messy and hard to follow. He is overly dramatic and his lectures are overly rehearsed. He spends little to no time communicating with the TAs and has little to do with the exams. The class is essentially based on your TA, I'd avoid this guy if possible.
Fine within discipline, but clueless about literature of non-German fields.  Doesn't like to be questioned and plays favorites.

He is definitely passionate about what he teaches. I trust his information.  It's clear that he knows what he is talking about and has thought about the content of the course. I had him for HIST 142 earlier in a larger class and he was more disconnected. Interesting class, good TAs, good readings, good professor.

Great professor. Took him for The Holocaust- he really knows what he's talking about. However, he didn't make himself available to the students but luckily I had a  great TA. Take this class & take it with him if you're wanting to learn a lot about the Holocaust.

Big lecture means it's all about the TA, since he'll probably never meet you. Depending on the TA, you can skip the endless (and lame) novels assigned. I skipped lectures, read the textbook: he's predictable, and you can guess his view on events. Much more interesting in direct conversation if you catch him after class, though.

Some people just should NOT teach. This guy comes across as so smart and proud and doesn't try to explain things to his students. Instead of him teaching, he goes up there and gives a very general speech about the topic and then disappears. The papers were hard and graded hard even though it's a 100 level non-major gen ed. Stay away from this guy!

I really disliked this guy at first, but several days after our final, I'm really missing the class.  If you attend lectures you barely need the textbook, and the lectures are way more interesting.  He's a great history professor.  Take him if you get the chance - you'll really learn something and care about the material.

My ratings are accurate but take him, he can be confusing, particularly in questions and he can go off on sort of obscure things or get too engrossed (for an undergrad class) in scholarly debates.  However, I am glad I took him.  Made be a better writer by leaps and bounds.  Was tough on that.  Made me think.  Arrogant as heck, but glad I had him.
An arrogant a$$.  He made the class unbearable with his OWN ideals and beliefs about the time period.  Hated going to this class.  Only good part: the final was optinal.
Interesting lectures, but difficult grader. Thinks he knows EVERYTHING. Made our final optional tho,so that was nice. I wouldn't take his class again
Very interesting to listen to, but not a good teacher. He couldn't care less about the students and is very egotistical. If you don't agree with his line of thinking, you don't do well in the class.
He was accessible, strong background knowledge and gave interesting lectures. He was available by appointment.  He pushed me to become a better writer.
A true arogant ****.  Stay away!

I actually enjoyed his lectures, he is a bit egotistical and very liberal but he conveys a lot of information through his lectures. But yes, he seems too busy to teach and often came to the 9am class late and disheveled.
Terrible!!  Very egotistical and extremely liberal.  Pushes his viewpoints on students.
Egotistical--not helpful to students who make attempts for assistance outside of class. Acts too busy to "teach"...wanted to tout research.
Professor Frame is very funny, but the class material is a little difficult. Pay attention during lectures and it'll be completely fine.

Professor Frame is really passionate about meteorology, and it shows through his lectures. Be prepared to hear a ton of dad jokes (they're usually pretty good). Every lecture includes beautiful weather pictures that he's taken over the years, and they really help with visualization of the subject. All the lectures are also posted on Canvas.

He's a super nice guy and you can tell he's passionate about meteorology. However, I noticed that as the year went on his lectures got too fast to keep up with. Also, the tests are harder than they need to be and worth a lot on your grade. If you're looking for a super easy gen ed science I wouldn't take this, it took quite a bit of work.

Be ready for a lecture full of puns. Frame knows all the material very well and has a lot of visuals to help students understand some of the more difficult data. His tests are all multiple choice and the final is not cumulative. It is very hard to not get a B or up!

Professor Frame gives excellent coverage on the basics of meteorology.  His dad jokes are S-tier, and he has an innocent type of humor.  You will not feel stressed in his class.  Listen to his lectures, and you won't need the book to do the homework.  His class is an easy and extremely entertaining 4.0 GPA boost.
Took this for a gen ed and I enjoyed it. The class is very structured which is nice, but the lectures can be a little boring.
Jeff Frame is funny, but kind of loud. He's knowledgeable, but very intense. It's kind of a hit or miss with him. I do appreciate his puns though.

Jeff clearly loves to teach and wants his students to do well. The class is highly organized and he makes sure we know what is expected to be learned. I can't say what it's like in ATMS100 with a large class size, but I can't imagine him not being an organized and passionate professor in any setting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i took this class for an easy gen-ed and it was NOT easy. He’s a really good professor and the lectures aren’t that bad it’s just a lot of lectures. the labs are really hard and we aren’t really taught how to complete them. technically attendance isn’t  mandatory but i recommend going or else you’ll get confused.

Great Professor! This class is extremely well taught and coherent. He makes sure that each new section fits into the big picture of synoptic meteorology. I learned a ton and appreciated that he learns everyone's name and has great/awful puns for every lecture. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Frame is super interested in the topic and makes it a bit more fun. There were a TON of lectures though and it got kind of boring. The textbook is supposedly required, but I really don't think you need it. You definitely have to work for your grade and the material can be a bit confusing to grasp. Overall, good class to take with this prof.
Prof. Frame is a good professor. The lectures were pretty boring, but he typically found a way to spice them up. Grading criteria was really easy.

he took over the legend Snodgrass and I dont think was prepared. The homework's seems harder then what we learned in class and was kind of technical. he was passionate about the topics and taught it well.

Jeff was a really nice guy and teacher. If you aren't a science person, he really explains well and gives a lot of real-life examples to help you understand. There are also a lot of super easy assignments to boost your grades which helps a lot. Overall good guy.

This class itself wasn't bad, but the labs were harder than they needed to be. There are multiple resources to use for help (like online lecture notes and TAs), but you aren't taught how to complete the labs. The math part of this course requires you to recall equations and concepts from any math and science courses you may have taken in the past.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The man does not teach very well. He basically reads off the slides. The study guides he gives help, but there are no real resources to find all of the answers because the slides do not have what you need. At the same time, the lectures do not prepare you at all for the labs. You will get so many points off without knowing why. PLEASE DONT TAKE!
Highly recommend this class if you aren't a science person. You can find the answers to all the reading assignments on Quizlet. He really did care about helping students to do well in the course.

Easy easy way to get science credit. He essentially just gives like 65 free points of hw, labs and participation. The HW are all on Quizlet. He doesn't grade iclickers for correctness. The labs were easy and the TAs helped a lot. The exams weren't that easy so I'd recommend studying but I got an 80 and 83 on 2 and still got an A. Don't buy the book

Dr. Frame is an awesome professor and is really nice. Meteorology 100 is a pretty easy class and each of the 3 test are only 45% of your grade. The final isn't cumulative, it's just "exam 3," whereas lab and reading assignments found on quizlet are worth 20%+ of your grade which is amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jeff is the man! His puns be fire and he speaks well so you won't fall asleep (of course there are days you are tired) and you'll be interested. Jeff is the bee's knees and one day you might at least think what it'll be like to an Atmos major. "What is the answer" is basically his trademark.

Solid, easy gen-ed. If you are even a little curious about the weather, take this class! I learned a lot and had to study very little to get an A. If you like puns and dad jokes, you'll like Professor Frame.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Exceptionally sarcastic and unnecessarily loud. Extremely hard to pay attention to. Gives abundance of office hours, but be prepared when you go to not be personally offended by any remarks he has. Extremely picky on grading. Attendance in class not mandatory but 5% of grade is participation which has no explanation to how it is determined.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Frame is a good professor. He is sarcastic and seems to think everyone in the class is an idiot, but it helps because he explains material very well. Exams are easy as long as you study. Go to labs, I found them to be the most beneficial part of the course to prepare for exams. Lots of easy points/extra credit to make sure you get the A.

Lectures are useless except for iClicker points. Answers to the homeworks are all on quizlet so you dont have to read at all. Tests are difficult but questions come directly from powerpoints but it's a lot of material to study. It's an easy A as long as you study a ton for the tests but he also gives you 8 points extra credit for them anyway.

Prof Frame is great! His class is very, very easy and each lecture has clear explanations and so many puns. He can be snarky/sarcastic. TA review sessions can be VERY helpful if you go to the right one. Reading assignments/iClickers/Labs are easy points. Exams are not cumulative. Easy and interesting class! I highly recommend.

I love Professor Frame. He is so funny and a great lecturer. He keeps it interesting. You need to show up for I-Clicker point and go to lab but if you actually go to everything and pay attention, its an easy A. I suck at math/science and got an A so you can do it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He may appear funny and quirky in lectures but when you see him in office, he is a different guy. When you ask him questions at his office, he's kind of obnoxious and gets offended when you say that you don't understand certain parts of the class material. Also, giving a 1/5 for helpfulness because for the 2 emails that I sent him he did not reply

Professor Frame is an amazing and pun-filled professor. His class is perfect for non-STEM majors. (And for people that couldn't get in ATMS 120) He's a true weather nerd, and loves teaching. The reading assignments get a little repetitive, but they're easy. You get points just for participating on the iclicker questions.
He is a ok teacher. Could be more interesting.  Tests were fair.  Requires attendance and labs are not boring.

He would be a much better teacher if he didn't act so snarky and arrogant. As it stands right now, his attitude makes him pretty hard to listen to. I understand a certain amount of sarcasm is alright from anyone, but Frame is pretty over the top. If it's between his Atmos 100 and Snodgrass's Atmos 120, take Snodgrass.

I enjoyed going to Frame's class everyday. He was very interesting and knowledgeable about the subjects he was teaching. His test can be a little challenging but not impossible and they aren't a big part of your grade. He gives out easy extra credit  and the final is not cumulative and its the same weight on your score as a regular exam.

Tests are not too bad, but Frame is the man. He knows everything about the weather and knows how to make his students interested. Puns are thrown in for good measure. Would highly recommend to anyone needing to fulfill for a gen-ed or just wanting to take an interesting class. Put a slight bit of work in and you will get an A.
Really nice guy and makes the material interesting. Definitely knows what he is talking about and as long as you do the work you're golden!

Grossly misled that the final was cumu; was entirely on tornadoes & supercells. HWs are easy, just be sure to ask questions early. Study PPTs well in advance of exams. Random quizzes announced 1 class prior, start studying ASAP bc they're specific. The boundary layer quiz is notoriously hard. Could have done better in the class if I'd studied more.

All the answers to reading assignments are online somewhere. Find them. Labs are all right if you have smart partners ;) Tests are not that easy just saying. You DO have to study. Book is useless. I-clickers every class so yes go to lecture. Overall easy-ish class. Whatever I got an A. :P
