The assignments and quiz alternate each week, slightly strict but definitely fair grader. The project was like a slightly longer HW. Overall easy to do well if you follow his notes
Even if the reasoning for deducting points is valid, the extent of the deduction feels excessive and, at times, unnecessarily harsh. Course objectives are good.
Fun and different class that prepares you for the real word in a unique way. It's very focused on career preparation. Darren is great both as a professor and a resource.
This course does not teach you much. Unnecessary strict grading.

Great lecturer, always gives clear explanations and examples! His notes are very thorough and he's always willing to answer students' questions. HW/quizzes aren't too hard and there's always office hours to get help when needed. I enjoyed this class and I also thought he was great at teaching SAS for beginners.

He's a kind professor and always gives helpful/useful advice for entering this work field. There aren't that many assignments and they aren't very difficult. The biggest thing is the final project you work on throughout the semester, but he answers any questions and gives you helpful tips on how to improve your final presentation/report!
he is a great man and an even better professor
Great teacher, cares about the students

This class is new, so it could use some work. Overall, there are two total projects and quite a few seminars to listen to. It's relatively simple for a 400 level STAT class. Also, practices some consulting skills.
Darren is a good teacher that will help students if they approach him. If you pay attention what he goes over in the lecture, the homeworks and exams are pretty simple. Good teacher.

Very clear with concepts. This is a hard subject and sometimes classes can get confusing. But if if you visit him in office hours, he explains stuff very well. Plus a lot of the material is available in online videos, make sure you watch them before class.

At UMN: his lectures feel very repetitive. Most of the exam material comes from things he briefly mentioned in lectures. He was very condescending in the way he spoke to students. No extra credits or any real assignments outside of attendance and exams. The exams are 90% of your grade and are very challenging. He was just rude tbh.

Glenn is a great professor and I enjoyed the content of his class a lot. I wasn't expecting the exams to be so difficult. They are closed-note, in-person and worth 90% of the grade. 3 exams worth 30% each. If you take notes in class, do the study guides, and know the material you should be able to do well. Final grades are also on a slight curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Roisman is really entertaining and an expert in the field of relationship science. His lectures are interesting and give you all the info you need to know for the exams. If you do the study guides, you'll do great on the exams. No papers or projects. Great at answering questions about lecture material and potential test questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's wonderful. Very clear in the lectures and describing material presented. Make sure to write down what he says because test material often contained information he briefly said. The class is designed so you get a B- or a B but if you ask for help he's more than willing.

Genuinely nice guy. He knows a lot about the material when people ask questions. Very approachable. Exams were more difficult than expected, but all exam material is in his lectures-no need to read the book. One of my favorite professors because he's actually kind and seems like he wants to be in class
This class was boring. but if you went to class, you got extra credit. the tests were challenging.
don't like hime.
Great speaker, though dull lectures. Attend class for activities. Study even the most seemingly trivial parts of the notes (names of experimenters, not just concepts), try not to daydream in lecture.
Great Prof; knows his material; extremely friendly and great speaker; give plenty of extra-credit, but you have to come to class to take advantage of it
Great Class, Well Taught
Get into his relationship lab as a 290 or 494.  It is extremely interesting, and you get advanced credit.  Definitely worth your time/energy.

After she makes you spend hundreds on required course materials (which can be just as easily replaced by OERs and Canvas), get ready for her to show up late to class regularly and ramble on about random topics. If you're a PS major, try to avoid taking a class with her.

Incredibly nice professor. Always down to Earth with students and is constantly there for them when needed. On top of that, the course was incredibly fun! Structured as an 8 week course that concludes with a week trip in Argentina. Would 100% recommend to anybody looking to explore and learn more about our world!
Very down to earth person and great personality. Unfortunately she is a little on the laissez faire side as a professor.

Professor Sin is among the most unprofessional and unorganized professors I have ever met. She would come to class 10 minutes late, always need help with the technology, and canceling class 10 minutes before it started, was just very unprofessional. Half the time she looked lost and felt like she didn't want to be there. Don't take this class!

While Prof Sin was a good lecturer, the class overall was extremely unorganized, we were left in the dark about things like Icliker points, and she was constantly changing due dates. Easy A, but it was just boring and disorganized

Professor Sin is super lenient on giving extensions and there are homework assignments pretty much every week (discussion posts, short answers, news quizzes, textbook hw), but they are all completion points! There are also three short papers and a final that are graded by the TAs, so it is easy to get As on them if you put in the effort.

This class is super easy A+ as long as you turn in your assignments on time and attend the lectures for iClicker points. Besides that, Professor Sin and the TA are all very kind and give out a lot of extra credit over the 
 semester. But overall, definitely would recommend this class if you want something light and to boost your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall a very nice professor. Very well accommodating to students and their needs. Is also very engaging with the class and often calls on people for answers. Lectures can be a bit long and boring though
Easier than APUSH. Prof. Sin is very nice but the class is very dry and mostly common sense/common knowledge.

Perhaps it was just my semester with her, but Dr. Sin, although being a wonderful lecturer, presented a very unorganized class with a lot of bouncing around and unnatural cadence. The lectures were straightforward and easy to understand. Students should be aware that she calls upon them to answer questions by handing them a microphone.

Professor Sin is an amazing professor! She's very understanding. When I took PS 101, all of the homework and activities are only graded for completion as far as I know. I got 100s in all of the activities - including the two big essays and the final. The class has three essays total. You'd pass as long as you do all the homework. Easy A+
Hands down best professor Ive had at uiuc. If you have the chance to take her for a class I would highly recommend.

Professor Sin really went above and beyond during this challenging time to show that she truly cares for her students. She was not like other professors that claimed they were there for us but did nothing. Professor Sin listened to us diligently and made accommodations. I would love to take a class of of hers again!
Shes great
Great professor! Really want to take a class with her again
A very understanding professor who always has her students best interest in mind. Highly recommend taking any classes she teaches. Course load is very manageable!
One of the most caring and understanding professors on campus, especially during period time of crisis! More professors need to be more like her.

This semester, Professor Sin canceled the final exam to support students' mental health. She is so compassionate, and I am grateful for her. I found her lectures interesting and thought she was an effective communicator!
Awesome
love her
Amazing professor! Really knows what she is talking about, and she is very understanding!

Took PS 101 Spring 2021 with Professor Sin and she was so understanding and accommodating during the pandemic. Writing this review because she just waived our final exam and gave us all credit!! If I could give her a 10/5 I would! If you're on the fence about one of her classes definitely take it!!

Honestly, could not have asked for a better professor during COVID. She was very enthusiastic about political science, very generous to her students. Overall, I would definitely recommend this professor.
The kindest professor ever! She suspended final simply because she felt bad for us

Professor Sin was very accomodating with students given how Covid has made things more difficult. The number of assignments was not overwhelming. Sin kept the classroom light and fun but I still learned a great deal about the U.S..
The lectures were underwhelming, but that was also a side effect of the late, online classes. The lectures weren't really needed, just the discussions and required reading.
Very understanding professor, gives extensions when needed.

She was so understanding and amazing during the pandemic. She has interesting lectures and a super interesting life story. She also canceled the final and gave us the points because she knew how difficult the pandemic and pandemic learning was for us. She is an absolute gem and should be president tbh

She is so understanding and gave us a week off during the semester when spring break was taken away from us. She also listened to us and made breakout rooms less frequent. She also cancelled our final. She is the goat

Absolutely amazing to learn from! She was very lenient with deadlines and made class fun. She was sincere and wanted to hear our feedback on how we felt about the 2021 Spring semester with Covid-19 and all.

Dr. Sin is literally the best professor. She is so understanding and kind, and also extremely knowledgeable at the same time. She is the best. Very fair in assignments and grading, and is open to suggestions from students about the class, what she teaches and the assignments she plans.
Super kind and understanding professor. Great teacher and really enjoyed this class with her
Absolutely an amazing teacher. She knew how hard we had worked and praised and rewarded us. Interesting lectures and easy work load.
so easy.
10/10, during covid semester helped us out and was super understanding
Queen
She just waved the final exam because she felt sorry for all of us suffering from this tough tough year. Respect to a professor who understands our struggle.
Really cares about students, the class is content heavy but if you do the work then your grade come natural! One of the best professors!
I found her lectures very useful and were very easy to follow. She taught the course very well, you just have to learn how to summarize notes and not write every little thing down.

She's a really nice person but I have a really hard time following her lectures. They're all pretty jumbled and hard to take notes off of. Honestly you don't even need to go to the lectures to get an A, just the discussions. I listened to podcasts during the lecture and just copied notes from online. If you do the inquizitives you'll be fine.

This class is structured like a simulation so you need to be present in class and you have to do some work outside of class to prepare your profile. There isn't a ton of assignments, but Dr. Sin is very helpful and the TA grader was laughably lenient. As long as you put in effort, you can get a good grade. Participation is very important

Lectures were kind of helpful. If you did the readings and the inquisitives you would be well prepared for the exam. No cumulative final which is nice. Only 2 papers. Discussion attendance is required and is also kind of helpful.
An extremely poor, monotone lecturer with meandering slides that completely lacked visuals. Essays took forever to be returned and grading criteria were often vague. Readings were almost never used.
Doesnt seem to really to understand the content she is teaching. Any questions asked on the topic she can not answer unless its written on her slides
Very nice and engaging professor, well structured class

Lectures were rather unhelpful and difficult to follow. Some lectures just seemed incomplete at best. Exams (4) were a mix of some minutae from lecture, textbook content, and random facts. Essays (2) were straightforward. Overall, the content of the class was interesting, but I don't think it was presented very well.

I liked this class. She isn't the best lecturer; her PP slides are kind of all over the place and hard to take notes from, but it's ok because she never really lecturers over things that aren't already in the book.  You will be fine skipping some lectures but definitely go to discussion sections!! If you read and go to those you will be golden.

Dr. Sin is a decent professor. She is very enthusiastic about lecture but her slides are disorganized and bad for taking notes. She tests on things in lectures so it is good to go, but they can be boring. Class isn't hard but almost all of the points come from tests and attendance in discussion. Don't skip discussion if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took her class on Political Organizations. The class was disorganized and the syllabus never matched up w/ what was covered in class-but she made up for it by giving us take-home exams. There's one group project where you have to write a 35 page paper on a federal agency. That paper sucked, but she'll give you an A if you put decent effort in it.

Lectures can be a bit boring because the prof spends so long on one topic. But it is not a hard class. Read the textbook. There are also outlines of the entire chapter in addition to the lecture slides on compass. You could easily not do the entire reading and pass.
She was so kind, and her tests were NOT cumulative!!
She's great.  Loved the class.  The simulation was one of the best learning experiences I have had.

She's super smart and knows everything she's talking about like it's the back of her hand. However, the class was sort of disorganized and she goes on lots of tangents in lecture. Tests covered what was in the book more than what was in lecture.

This class was a congressional simulation where everyone was a member of the house of reps - so that was super fun! The TA was an idiot, but Professor Sin always seemed nice. The class was kind of slow moving, but overall it was pretty fun. You write a paper early on based entirely on the textbooks but don't use them otherwise.
Second class with Dr. Sin! You do need to do the readings in order to participate in a smaller class.
Fantastic!

She's an absolute sweetheart, you can tell she really cares about her students and wants them to do well. You could probably pass without doing the readings, but if you do read the homework and come to lectures, her tests are no problem. Three exams, a paper, and a final.

Glumac's lectures are awful and disorganized, he just solves examples with little explanation and posts his notes late, although they're too disorganized to be any use anyway. The HW is hard but ungraded, I failed all the quizzes and the final was doable. I learned everything from YouTube and the textbook and only passed because of the huge curve.

Don't believe what those talented kids said. The quiz score of this course last semester was less than 50% in the class. At the same time, the lecture was very chaotic and clueless. There was no powerpoint in class, so I could only read his messy essays. The teacher has serious procrastination. It took more than half a month to receive the results.

Glumac's ME200 is hard. You are graded on 7 quizzes (2 dropped) and the final exam. This was intimidating and ultimately made it difficult for most people to succeed in the class.

However, if you are diligent with the homework, actually learn the material, and practice doing problems under time constraints, the exams will be fair. You can do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Glumac gives great lectures and uses good examples during lectures. Homework given was helpful for the biweekly quiz, which accounts for 60% of grade. However, he is not organized, sometimes breaks his promises. In short, take his class if you want to actually learn in the lectures, but his class won't be an easy A.

The grading structure of the course was extremely poor. Many people raised concerns about the grading process, which were often dismissed with assurances that the course would be curved. 100% of the course was exam-based. Late quiz and exam return times were the norm leaving little room for improvement. Don't take any of his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 7 quizzes, 2 drops, 60% of grade. Averages usually dipped below 50%, not because of the difficulty, but because of the 20 minute time limit. Based on any material from the last two weeks, so your grade is already gone by the time you catch on to which information he favors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly doubt many kids passed this class (ME200). He makes the quizzes and exams 100% of your grade, and makes them really hard and time-constrained for no reason. Basically the only way to do well is just grind out the ungraded HWs over and over until you can do every problem instantly
Hard to understand, trips over his own words, and doesn't seem to empathize with students. Don't take this course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: dont take his course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There were lots of people who were upset with him in class, but I thought he was great. He really knows the material, makes lots of connections, and he could be pretty entertaining at times (though not in a usual way). Quizzes were pretty easy if you actually do the HW and additional book examples. Only problem is the HW was unfairly graded.

Gives 7 quizzes during the semester, which are totally doable in the time allowed. Great lecturer, probably one of the best ones I've had yet. Knows what he's talking about, and communicates it well. One problem I did have was that he took off points for hw, when he told us in the beginning that it was effort based. Easy final

Would absolutely not recommend. Lectures aren't clear and presentation is very boring. If you enjoy learning from textbook, this is your guy because that's pretty much the only way you'll learn. Start your homework early as it takes a long time.
He makes your quizes worth 60% of your grade. Then makes your quizes very difficult with only 20 minutes to solve in class.
Gives 20 minute quizzes every other week in place of midterms. Quizzes were one problem on anything covered in that time. Difficult to complete in time allotted. Final exam was easy.

Horrible professor. He grades homework, I average a 2225 even though he says it is completion based. His quizzes are hard, and no one ever has enough time to finish them. He is completely unorganized and doesn't use any technology (no online notes, doesn't use the projectors, and doesn't wear a mic). He is VERY boring and annoying to listen to.

Overall, not too tough of a class and easy to get a good grade. Glumac gives seven quizzes, two of which are dropped. Not hard to do well on quizzes; they are similar to the homework problems. Read through corresponding section and view practice problems in the text. Homework is essentially graded for completion. Quizzes: 50%, HW: 20%, Final: 30%

super distracted and disorganized. didn't seem like he was prepared for class at all and it made it really tough to learn from him. that being said, the quizzes were super simple and the final was easy too, but the only things that I learned in this class were things I read in the book
Awesome professor...teaches very systematically...exams are a bit difficult and you need to know everything...cracks a lot of jokes

GREAT PROFESSOR! My favorite ME professor thus far. He keeps you interested, He's lectures are great and he as a cool sense of humor. Class is easy if you pay attention and attend lectures and do the homework. Overall, take any class he teaches, he is a cool professor

Glumac is an interesting lecturer who is very interested in thermo. Quizzes are generally straightforward, although you are sometimes crunched for time. One week is dedicated to "questioning" global warming (AGW). The final is unnecessarily difficult, with many problems bearing only slight resemblance to previous examples, hw, quizzes. No midterms.

Quizzes are relatively easy and open book, but you are extremely short on time. Quizzes are also a huge portion of the grade, and the final exam is very difficult. Homework is crucial. Glumac is a decent lecturer if a tad boring.

Glumac seems like a nice guy but is a lot more focused on his research than teaching. The class was disorganized and his quiz questions were completely random and focused on minute details. Studying for this class meant just memorizing everything on his lecture slides. The final was difficult but had a lot of old questions on it.
Awesome prof. Was overly fair on quizzes in class. They were open book, usually the same as example problems with numbers changed. Final was pretty difficult.
Used student feedback very effectively. Final was on content that seemed less important during the course. Very helpful to go to for questions.
Final not representative of course material and very limited in scope of the material.  Do not take any class from him!
Very responsive to students' suggestions.  Good lecturer, but final worth too much.
No he is not good. You will not learn much FEM and you will struggle a lot. Not a nice person either. If you want to get some good FEM knowledge at U of I stick to Dr. Duarte. Stay away from Paulino.
Not good at all. Everything you read below is 100% true

Passes out tons of his own publications expecting you to read them. Class is straight from powerpoint slides 95% of the time. Gave a misleading practice exam that was not related to actual exam content. Stressed final would cover a majority of topics after 2nd exam - it did not, and was extremely difficult. Can't say I learned much from this class.
His classes are slides that have little to do with learning FEM, and instead show off his research. Not a nice person either.

this professor always talks about his own research, passing out his own papers.  He gives some ridiculously long hw's. the projects are the only useful things i got out of this class.  the tests are outrageously hard and you are lucky if you can finish within the allotted time. it is true that some of his own students do not like working for him

This guy is very mean. In the class he talks a lot about his research, and cover little about finite elements. It is quite surprising that AE420 (and ME471), which is a 400-level class, covers more material on the finite element s than this class. Some of his students told us that this professor is very mean even towards his own students.

this guy is inefficient, always talks about his own research, what the hell to do with the class, he is just full of himself. rumors from graduate students said he is very mean to his own students, but he always pretend to to be nice to other students, no wonder he can be "successful". so befriend the textbook and the TA who is really helpful
Very difficult class with poor teaching and outrageous homeowrks and exams!!!!
Very unhelpful teaching style and personally he is very mean guy! He even distribute the exam in the order of scores from top to bottom, how foolish and childish method in Grad school!!!

This class is an absolute joke.  It's amazing how much that man can talk without actually saying anything!  Unfortunately, there's no way around the difficult homework, projects, and tests.  Befriend your textbook because you will not learn a thing from Paulino's lectures!

She's the sweetest professor, like your aunt or something. iClicker questions make class mandatory but she truly wants you to come to class to learn. Very helpful, makes sure you understand all material. Textbook not required, lectures/discussions are pretty thorough. Even brings food for exams! Made 8am  bearable, probably my fav professor so far.
Awesome teacher! Love her! Class is not boring at all!
excellent professor...really cares about her students. taught the honors section of psych 100 and really tried to make it interesting

Prof. Gladding is a brilliant professor, but not a very good teacher. You can tell he knows his Physics very well, but he makes it rather difficult to learn if you are not good at physics/have little understanding of basic physics. My tip: practice over and over and over again, and work with others who know better what they are doing & will explain
Easy class if you have taken high school physics. Very basic.
Didn't teach anything at all, just went over pre lectures in lecture... wouldn't recommend this course to anyone!

I didn't know much about physics before taking this class and I still don't after taking it. I found everything to be extremely difficult to understand since everything he does is all conceptual. There is no text book so it is extremely hard to study on your own. The tests are extremely difficult however some people found them easy but most did not
Great Professor.

This class is way to hard for itself. It's a required class for so many majors and it takes way too much time. He's better at talking about Jazz. My disc. was awful too. The ta never really helped. The material doesn't seem hard, and they trick you so much on the exams. Everything mistake possible is there.
He just repeated the prelectures in lecture.
This class is not that hard but still effort is needed if you want a good grade. For the final exam, it covers material from the LAB so beware!

this class is very different than classical mechanics. I had a hard time grasping the 1st exam material and end up getting a C on that exam. but I end up getting an A so don't be disappointed to get a bad grade. i found reading the book (prelectures in words) very helpful, and lectures were very entertaining!
He was an ok professor, but he tends to blow over any demo.  Also this class is set up weirdly, which adds to the already difficult topic.  I pulled off a B+ but not easily.
Good lecturer, hilarious and understandable.  Go to his lectures and you'll do fine.  Kind of a hard class, but definitively not impossible to get an A.
Good professor but exams are not that easy. subject itself is not easy. lectures are fun with the iclickers but homework, prelectures, preflights, etc. makes this class very difficult.

Class itself for phys 199ho is very difficult, but he does a good job of explaining the material more or less. Mostly he is good at answering questions rather than lecturing. Very nice guy and understanding, but material is very difficult.

Dr. Golecki gives the impression that she is a kind woman, but unbeknownst to the class during the course, she is cold at heart. Her grading makes no sense. As the semester went on, she gave us false hope that we were on the right track but slammed us at the end of the semester. Dr. Amos however is way more approachable so reach out to her for Q's

The professor does not clearly express what she expects from the senior design projects. Throughout the course, she makes you feel like you are on the right track, until the very last assignment that she grades heavily. Even if you address all of the comments of your assignment throughout the semester, she will still be dissatisfied.

Dr. Golecki gave almost no useful/honest feedback to senior design groups all semester, assigning near-perfect scores and telling everyone "great job." As a result, we were all completely blindsided by poor grades on the final presentation, poster session, and final compiled report, all of which counted very heavily toward the final grade.

Definitely an intensive course. Get ready to work. I was activated with the National Guard during the class and Professor Goebel was extremely understanding and helpful, ensuring that I completed the course despite the setback.

Professor Geobel is so caring, accessible, and understanding. If you have any problems at all, you can talk to her and get it figured out. The course itself isn't too hard, but you do end up doing a lot of outside work since it is an "intensive" course. As long as you commit a couple of hours a week, you will do fine.
Great professor, could not recommend more

Raquel is amazing! She has a very hands-on approach to teaching, and really does care about her students. She is very lenient about late work and a very fair grader. If you genuinely do your best and put in the effort, you will have no issue doing well in her class.
very nice and understanding prof

Not sure what else to say other than the fact that she is by FAR my favorite professor, and her class is the only class I look forward to. Incredibly caring, considerate, and empathetic, she is exactly what a professor should be. Engages with students in a polite and respectful manner. Highly recommend taking any class with her.
She has a lot of energy for teaching, and genuinely cares if you are learning. There is a bit of online homework that can be a lot some weeks, but it helps make sure you are at where you need to be.

She is such a sweet teacher with great energy; she made class really fun. The only negatives is that she is a little unorganized and it is sometime unclear what she expects for assignments. However, she is an extremely easy grader, she mostly looks for effort. I would skip class every once in a while and it didn't affect me much.

She is honestly one of the best professors ever. She sticks to the material in the book and her lessons are straight forward and easy to follow. She cares a lot and wants to see you succeed. As for homework there are two short essays (100 words each) throughout the semester, and online homework with the Pearson website that reinforce the lessons.
Not the best professor, but very passionate about what he does. He wants all students to succeed.
Awesome professor, cares a lot about his students and wants them to suceed.

Great professor with great lectures that bring in outside experience and examples. Very useful content as well for future internships. TA's were not the most helpful but professor was always willing to chat outside of OH and help out.
Awesome lectures! Great balance of theory and practice. Highly recommend this course to everyone.

Mani loves teaching and is really passionate about the industry. He runs a company and tries to inspire students to get involved in starting up their own and keeping up with the rapidly developing construction industry. He lays out goals before every class and will personally sit down with whoever does below average on a test to help them along.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof. Mani is not the greatest lecturer, but the man straight up wants you to succeed in this course and in cm in general. Very well organized course, and if you review online quiz and clicker questions, you will be fine come exam time. Also, go to his office hours he is a great person to connect with if you want to continue in Construction Mgmt.
Very well organized course. Good presentation and very interesting research topics included. However, speed of lecturing is too fast and hard to grasp. A lot of the material is relied on self-study.

HIST 135- I really enjoyed Professor Goffman, she wanted to get to know everyone in the class and treasured everyone's opinions. Sometimes her lectures are fast-paced and hard to keep track of, but overall very willing to answer questions. The content itself is very interesting. She's not a difficult grader and just wants to see you learn.
ruined my life

I had Prof. Goffman for History of the Middle East after WW1, she is a great professor. She is very understanding and accessible, gives good feedback, and manages to give incredibly engaging lectures in ways that many other History professors would consider boring. The workload is never too much with just a few big projects and readings.

This class was very informative and relatively easy. Just do what is expected of you and you will end with an A+. Very fair grader and truly interested in discussion and the topics discussed. Easy to reach by email as well. Would definitely take a class by her again.

This was one of the best classes I've taken in the history department. The readings were engaging and interesting. Just a book presentation, a midterm, and a final but the book presentation was really fun. Professor Goffman really made the class what it was. She was kind and engaging, knew all our names, and was overall a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: I know that a lot of people dislike his exams, which is valid but I would highlight that lectures are amazing and professor is very accessible outside of class. If you have any issues with your grades/assignment he is VERY understanding. Even though the exams are taught he gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and encourages real understanding.
He is good at what he teaches.

Assigned so much unnecessary work for a one-credit-hour class in the Fall. Acts conceited, has nothing of substance to present in a mandatory weekly lecture, and loves to pretend like his class should be everyone's top priority. MSE 494+495 would be much more meaningful if taught by someone more competent and tolerable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Goodman is a good professor, but this class is very hard. Lecture slides are not that helpful, so read the book and attend lecture. Also attending lecture gives extra credit. For exams just do all the homework questions and read the book thoroughly.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams were very difficult and often had specific items from lectures that he mentioned maybe 1 time. And they're still worth most of your grade. Also it was hard to focus in lecture with them being 1.5hrs long and him going on tangents all of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All the lectures, assignments, and reports are completely useless. We weren't able to get started on our projects until the second semester. The "Poppy's Playhouse" project from the first semester was also completely useless. Stop wasting your students' time.
Not too hard of a Class but he just went on random tangents and it was hard to know what would be on exams
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Nothing good about his class. Appreciates suck ups so if you're one of those, you'll do great. Genuine waste of time to take classes he teaches.

I wasn't doing as well as I wanted to in this class and somehow ended up with a B+ thanks to Goodman. Super good guy and an even better professor. This course is hard and I wouldn't say that Goodman makes it any easier but rest assured he will be fair and understanding the whole time.

Really enjoyed the class and his lectures. In my opinion it's pretty easy to succeed in the class if you put in the work, it's graded fairly, lectures are posted in advance, and the exams relate to the homework. He makes a lot of connections to real world applications during class, probably my favorite class of the semester

Very knowledgeable about this subject matter.  Very articulate in class and is able to provide a lot of examples of how we (as the class is overwhelmingly composed of aerospace majors) will use its content in our future jobs.  His exams, though, are notoriously hard, and basically all of our grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Goodman's lectures are difficult to listen to. He's also very passive aggressive if you ask him questions.

Matt's lectures, all in vain,
Slides devoid of substance, plain,
Deadlines were the only guide,
Relevance nowhere in sight.

Feedback lacking, help was nil,
Assignments left us cold and still,
Senior design, half-baked at best,
With an attitude that failed the test.
Zero planning for classes. Worksheets are a waste of time. Senior design is an absolute joke. This class was the least enjoyable part of MSE.

Matt's lectures were useless. Other than deadlines, relevant slide content was non-existent. Provided assignment feedback was inconsistent and/or unhelpful entirely. Overall, his rendition of the senior design course is pretty half-baked and his attitude towards students is unpleasant at best.
DO NOT SKIP CLASS, the slides are utterly useless for reviewing lecture materials, and you have no alternatives. You must take good notes. Homework is okay, tests are graded fairly.

Professor Goodman is terrible at lecturing, and none of his slides are helpful. It is super hard to follow along in class because there lacks consistent structure. He clearly is knowledgable about the topics but he is just a terrible professor. He also is super stingy at grading, and is extremely slow to put grades in as well.
MSE 280 kinda sucks, but Goodman is a great professor and does his best to make it easier and interesting. He is clearly very passionate about the material, and wants to see everyone succeed.
Professor Goodman was really relatable and understanding of our situation this semester and did a really good job of teaching the content!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Goodman is great! His lectures are fun and engaging, and he teaches very well. I would definitely recommend him as a professor.

As a person, he is really friendly and I like how casual class was, but he teaches poorly; class is disorganized/unclear with lots of useless info, and he only briefly touches on topics, making it hard to tell what's important or not. Also, last semester his office hours were very limited and at a bad time. A lot of the class is improv & it shows.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Goodman is an awesome person and he's hilarious. Unfortunately, the class is run poorly. The slides would be empty or populated with a lot of information that we do not go over in class, which makes the lecture slides essentially useless to study from. If you do not take notes in class, you will not pass. Some of the questions aren't covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He tried to be nice and made inappropriate jokes throughout the class, but lost focus on the materials. His teaching style is way too casual and the class was absolutely none sense. Recommend reading the textbook before class so when he goes through the materials (he assumes that you know them already) you can get a better sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good professor, interesting lectures. The class is not too hard, but the test material can often come from specific lecture examples. If he mentions something that is clearly related to a specific major, it will be on an exam. If you miss lecture, you'll probably miss these and the exam questions based on them. We had a lot of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's the type of teacher who knows his topic very well, but fails at delivering it to students in an easily understood manner. His lectures seemed to have a disconnect between teaching the general topic, then asking super specific/obscure questions (especially conceptual ones). Feels like an easy course load until the small amt of tough quizzes/hw
Professor Goodman is really helpful, nice, and straightforward. The class was truly enjoyable and helpful.

Professor Goodman is a pretty good teacher honestly. He is patient, answers questions clearly, and is willing to help those who are struggling. However, his assessments tend to focus a lot of very minute and obscure details, making a lot of the class more memorization based than anything. Be aware of this.

Dr. Goodman is very straightforward about expectations and will answer any questions. The class is chill and he really just wants to help students grow. As long as you do the work, a high grade is guaranteed. Late penalties are tough because the work is so easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the class. Honestly, it is so much material to fit into such a short period of time and he does it well. He is definitely new and still learning the ropes, but if you do the homework and pay attention in lecture, the exams are really straight forward. His office hours are really helpful so definitely go to those.

Professor goodmann is a decent guy, as a person, but lame as a teacher. His lectures are speedy and essentially useless. You will learn more from reviewing his lecture slides which he posts after the lecture. He busted our class for cheating as a whole (we were that class). Avoid group chats. He has past exams that are essential for doing well.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He didn't even give us the ices forms we are required to have. He's a first year teacher and it shows. Good guy, but he needs to get his act together.

I had him for Henry James, and he grew on me over time. The readings are hard- I suggest listening to audiobooks to help. Professor Hutner's lectures also make them a lot easier to understand. Don't skip! The pop writing assignments help motivate you and are graded easy. Overall, he's very knowledgeable, and you'll gain a lot in a class with him.

I took this class in 2023. I hated it at the time. Get ready to have your ego hurt! Even the most perfect of writers will get feedback...I can promise you that. 

Looking back though, he's a great professor. Sarcastic, sure. But he taught me a lot and legitimately made me a better writer. His feedback may hurt your feelings BUT it will help!

Knows how to compile an invigorating reading list. Sometimes brought us banana bread. Unfortunately, he REALLY picks favorites and picks on those he doesn't like. Don't expect to make a point in class without being cut off by him. To do well, keep your head down, carefully write essays, and don't say anything stupid.

I am NEVER one to have problems with a teacher. I have even gotten a D's in class and still liked the teachers. DO NOT take a class with this man. Its his way or the highway. Three kids dropped the class after the the first week. I promise you I NEVER have angry feelings towards teachers.... But this guy... Takes the first and only cake.

I don't know how Gordon Hutner gets 17 blank stares for the entirety of every class, but he does. No one is interested cause all he wants to do is hear himself talk. He comes with no lesson plans and just blabs about whatever comes to mind. He doesn't make sense, his grading does not make sense, I'm not a better writer, I've learned nothing

I have mixed feelings about Hutner. When he returns your papers, you can tell that he certainly takes the time to give advice on how to make them better. But that's really expected from all English professors. I also agree with others that he talks a little too much. Other English professors I had did more by saying less.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nightmare. The book list was pretty interesting, but god forbid if you don't like one of them. He loves to hear himself talk but doesn't make coherent points. His prompts are convoluted. He tends to railroad any discussion into what he wants you to say. Pass.

He's very intimidating. Definitely opinionated. The class is supposed to be discussion-based, but he cuts you off often. The guy is obviously smart, but he makes sure you know it. Don't tell him you dislike the books, because he'll go on a tangent about how you're wrong. Not a terrible class, but if you can avoid it, do. Great book list, though.

Interesting take on modern novels- great thing about it- we are the first to critique. Opinionated,multi-dimensional man who always makes time to help his students out. Reading load is heavy, but only asks of 2 E-responses per book. 2 essays and a few short analysis here and there. Go to class. Do your work. You'll do just fine.

Professor Hutner loves to hear himself talk. He says things that sound intellectual but rarely have much meaningful substance.  He does not like to be challenged and tends to respond to student comments/questions by using them to launch into his own ideas.  I found the reading load heavy, and the discussions discouraged me from staying involved

You read 8 books, and have to do e-responses on each. he gives a few pop quizzes so at least have an idea of what is going on. there are no tests, and not a final, you have to read a book on your own and write 3 seperate papers (about 6 pages each) comparing your book to the books in class. pretty easy class for 200 level LA

Hutner is a dick. He gives one set of directions then changes his mind and makes you redo the damn assignment. Does not listen to anyoen who has a different opinion than his own- either agree or shut up. Teachers at a grad school level, always confuses his students. Try to avoid his class if you can
Loved Archaeology of Death! Interesting material, easy to follow, and easy grading!
Would never recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grace is a fair grader and made sure students were given enough time to prepare and complete assignments. She is effective at giving only relevant information in lectures that will come up on tests, and makes it clear if any lecture content will not be relevant to future assignments. Labs on Friday almost always ended early.

Great, charismatic lecturer. Good intro to biological anthropology, but don't expect to go too in-depth which is fine. Will sprinkle in very interesting random facts that are very fun. Overall did a great job teaching the class, and made it something I looked forward to

Grace is a good lecturer. While many of her lectures are technical, she clarifies that her tests will not have that. The TA goes over every question on the midterm beforehand - so as long as you go to those, you will be fine. Written assignments and labs are graded basically on completion. Good feedback of final paper related activities
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: By far the worst professor you can take this class with. She is the only one that has a mandatory cumulative final during finals week, and also wasted half a class having someone from the textbook company talk about how to use the website the textbook was on. Take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If I had the option, I would not have taken this class with her. Legit gave me anxiety.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Winter is one of the best professors I have had in my time at Gies. This class can be work heavy at some points but the exams are easy as long as you pay attention (and cheat sheets are provided). 
You can tell that she cares about her students and genuinely wants us to learn. Would recommend to anyone.
Winters is quick to judge, but she is very knowledgable and passionate. Go to her office hours and she is willing to help. Structured class and clear expectations. It's not difficult to do well.

She is very smart and knowledgeable but her teaching style is horrible. Attendance is mandatory and worth 15% but the lectures don't actually help anything. Also a ton of busy work just so you might be able to participate in said lectures

You basically have to teach yourself through the 150+ point textbook assignments that she assigns you every week. She claims that assignments will be dropped for final grades, but that's a lie. She also lied about the final and said there was extra credit, but instead made the points count as if they were part of the final. Take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I like the way she teaches. She will interact with students. Although class is a little nervous, it depends on the individual. I  attended every class, so I didn't miss the class score. She's friendly to students, even though doesn't know their names.
Just bad overall, not friendly to students, grades twice as hard as other BADM 300 professors, and lectures are almost entirely useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are a waste of time and attendance is taken randomly. Gives no review for exams. You are basically teaching yourself all of the content and there is a lot of material that is covered. I have heard much better things about the other BADM 300 professors so don't take Winter's class unless you have no choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She often talks about things that really aren't relevant to the class. She tries to talk about cases that are happening in the world right now but these cases have nothing to do with what we're learning and wastes time. You always have to be ready to participate because most of the time she'll just put the mic in your face.

I would avoid taking BADM 340 with Prof. Winter. There are better options out there. I will say that this course was very practical and helpful and she does do everything she can to help you succeed. However, she is a tough grader and your best won't be good enough for her. Keep that in mind.

Professor Winter is passionate about the material covered in 340. She invites speakers often. Class material is interesting and different from most courses. Winter can be challenging, and at times the course is a bit discontinuous and unorganized, but, if you work hard and come prepared to participate, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: He was pretty chill , but zesty. I enjoyed his class as he was humorous.

Grindrod is not helpful. I have emailed him multiple times to see him in office hours and he does not even show up. He rushes through his slides and overall not supportive. Like previously said, I have no respect for him.

Very clear, concise, organized. Laughed a lot at himself and seemed pretty light hearted which was nice. Quizzes were online and you were only given 15 min, if you missed 1 question, you automatically got a B on that quiz. Other than that, if you put in the work you reaped the benefits. Good teacher all around.

He is unhelpful, rude, and his grading scale does not make sense at all. Very unresponsive to emails. Expects you to be experts even though he is terrible at teaching. All he does is read off the slides. I do not respect this professor in the slightest. He uses a weighted grading scale and it is near impossible to get an A in the class. >:(

was fairly easy, made lectures pretty interesting but lots of unnecessary material sometimes. exams were pretty easy. make sure you really practice your transcription skills because he expects them to be fairly decent by the end of the course

Challenging but very interesting class. Lectures and readings heavily emphasize research. Two non-cumulative exams, six quizzes and three article critiques. Grindrod is an engaging, humorous and well-informed lecturer; however, considerable studying is required to do well in this course.

Provided USEFUL powerpoints that help both in/out of class. Daily readings help understand difficult topics but are by no means required to be read. Teaches complex topics but explains well enough. Weekly quizes are not too bad. 2 tests are like quizes but VERY long and can be hard. NO CURVE! 2 article reviews. Overall very good. Says "ok?" alot!

Dr. Grift is a wonderful and enthusiastic professor. His lectures are well organized, and his recorded lectures allow students to revisit difficult material. He is flexible, caring, funny and always in his office, available to answer questions. Dr. Grift is respected by both students and faculty, and truly wants his students to learn and succeed.

Prof. Grift shows a clear love for the material he teaches, but be warned if you aren't interested in the material you will struggle. Its not a fun topic, but he tries his hardest to make it accessible for everyone. He puts a lot of weight on the final, but he doesn't want students to fail. Fun lecturer and great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall, I enjoyed this class.  His interest in the material carries through to the lectures.  However, sometimes the class is a little unorganized.

He mumbles so much and talks really fast. Also he likes to give pop quizzes, but it's hard to ace those when you have no idea what he is talking about. When you need help, his explanations aren't clear and I'd find myself still needing help after. He assumes we already learned what we cover in class. Won't take this class if it wasn't required.
Does a fine job.
he has little interest in haveing the students actually learn his material for the class. he also assumes you have taken classes 2 years ahead of schedule
Unorganized
he is super awesome, like, totally!!!!1111
No Comments

He is definitely "the tiger".  When visiting his office hours he will not have time to help you.  His class is very boring and he makes the quizzes and exams difficult.  He gives pop quizzes quite often.
She said she doesn't like lecturing, but you can't tell. Engaging presentations most of the time. A lot of the work is done in discussion though, so your TA matters more. 2 essays, 2 exams.

ENGL 421: Simply one of the best! Literally zero complaints. Great lectures and interesting readings. Just about all papers and projects are designed to allow students to tailor the material to their own interests. The amount of effort put into the course and quality feedback shows how much she truly cares about students' success!

Professor Gray is amazing! She is super engaging and always tries to relate content to our lives to make it easier to understand. She's super funny and always tries to make class enjoyable. The textbook, participation, and attendance are all required. There are also pop quizzes but it shouldn't be hard if you do the readings.

Professor Gray was one of my favorite teachers! She is really light-hearted and caring and she made a lot of modifications during the pandemic. You have to participate and pay attention, but she's a really good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I absolutely ADORE Professor Gray. I already loved Shakespeare, but her class made me fall head over heels for the plays. She's clear in her teaching, focused, funny, relatable, and overall excellent. I wish I could take this class again; it's been the bright spot in what's been an otherwise crappy semester. Take her classes!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: hard grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This is NOT a blowoff class. Prepare to be inundated with assignments, readings, and in-class discussions. But she's a fantastic teacher. She's open to multiple points of view, you'll gain a true and lasting understanding of the topics, and as for grades, she rewards effort. If you have a passion for the course of study, you'll easily get an A.

She is a great teacher. I love her. She is a hard grader though, harder than most of my other teachers. You definitely have to attend lecture, study and read to get an A but it is worth it. I felt like I learned a lot from her.
Keeps class interesting and engages student discussion well. The class had a really nice balance of written, exam and presentation grades.
recommended
Very good professor. Makes me interested in the subject and wanting to learn deeper about the topic he discussed in class.

I took the lecture in Fall 2023. It is a quite chill class. Professor Howard definitely knows what he is teaching; the best part is his notes on the blackboard. It is so clean and well-structured. You should write them down. His course is the best class I have had at U of I. Office Hour is great and helpful. He is kind and knowledgeable.

Not ECON514 but ECON422. Economic models are introduced in slides and algebraically on the chalk board. Homework are concise and follow the same pattern; definitely cool to see how different concepts change the way the math is done.

He's great to talk to outside of class--he's very careful in selecting his words and is very down to earth.

He was okay. He has a class discussion after reading an article every class which is helpful and keeps the class interesting. The material is a bit dry and as a result he is too, but not overly challenging. End of semester project is not difficult and is easy to get an A on.
Shes really nice and all but if you dont take notes in class you're cooked unless you lock in a month before your test
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Grossman is extremely passionate about her expectations for students in the class and wants everyone to succeed. She always advertises her office hours and hosts review sessions before exams. I'll warn you that her lectures are long, and it's hard to maintain focus throughout the session. There are only two exams and two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very smart and the content can be interesting. Lectures are long and it is hard to stay awake but the tests are not that difficult if you study a few days ahead of time with quizlet. Very accessible and the assignments have clear instructions that make them easy to write.

Grossman was a nice professor. Most lectures got pretty dry after the first 30 minutes, but that's to be expected when there's a lot of information to be put out there. I could tell she's really passionate about architecture history. She will be tough on you if you miss a major assignment/turn it in late, and attendance is graded.

This teach is very knowledgeable in the subjects she teaches. Although her tests are tough, if you pay attention in lecture and take notes, it is easy to pass. She very much emphasizes the information you will need to know for the tests. She is a challenging professor but a nice and intelligent person.

Heather Grossmann is not a good teacher. Although she is very intelligent and the materials in this class is pretty interesting, It is inevitable that you stay awake during class. She has a hard time articulating her ideas, and gives you a 400-level worth of class materials. Readings are useless, just review the recordings of her lecture.

Grossman is by far the worst professor  I have ever had. She assigns long readings that are irrelevant to what we learn in class. The exams are not only excessive memorization, but extremely hard for an introductory course and she only gives you about 4 days to prepare.

When I took IS490, I was concerned that I would be unprepared for the course, but Mohit made sure that all questions and concerns were never left unanswered. I finished off the semester with a lot more familiarity with concepts that were intimidating at the start of the semester. Overall, a great professor who genuinely cared for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was one of those project based classes that prepares you for the real world. He is a great professor, his lectures are always clear and engaging. His feedback was always great in that it gave the exact direction you needed to push your work in the right direction. Great experience, I feel like this class flipped a switch in me.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is one of the best class that I have taken in UIUC. The professor is very dedicated and hardworking. He provides very detailed feedback and guideline for your work. He is very experienced in helping students to build their startups. Although the workload might be intensive, this course does help me to build many amazing projects.

Awesome class! Everyone is super supportive and the class is very well structured. Definitely my favorite course I've taken this semester, and the professor cares a lot about the success of his students.
Awesome professor! Project based class and very supportive environment.
He was the best teacher I've ever had!
Incredible class! Taught us so much about making startups
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Incredible class!

This is the single best class I have taken at UIUC.  It taught me everything I need to know to create a startup from scratch.  The professor is amazing, caring, and teaches exactly what you need to know.  Excellent teaching and extremely educational.

Great professor. The course is well structured and every assignment serves a clear purpose. He is understanding and flexible with students. You walk away with a real project and practical knowledge of how the technology works. Would recommend.

When designing the course, Mohit always thinks from the students' perspectives and what would benefit their learning. He's always supportive and motivating to every student and genuinely happy for the progress you make.
Taking this class I could see that Mohit genuinely cares about his students and wants to help them succeed
Amazing professor! Really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Always prepared for class and designed the INFO 390 MG course well.
Very direct with instructions, very caring towards his students, and genuinely cares about their learning and educational experience.

Mohit was my discussion TA for this class. He was super kind, had a gentle tone of voice, and was very clearly invested in cultivating student understanding. He did not shy away from criticism; rather, he explicitly asked us students how he can improve the course. He provides students with earnest and constructive critique.

Mohit was a great TA to have. He genuinely loves what he does and wants to see each of his student succeed. He keep class discussions enthusiastic and engaging. Outside of the classroom he gives thorough feedback to students on all of their assignments and is glad to help them address any gaps in their understanding of the course subjects.
Good TA and makes effort to include everybody in the class discussion. You can tell he really cared about his students' success.

Awesome professor, super kind, helps students out, and always gets back to his emails very fast! He's excellent and communication and made the class really fun! Please take him if you can! He truly understands what students go through and wants to help out!
Good professor, everything I learned from discussion, I'll be able to apply outside of class
Mohit is a very nice guy
Nice teacher, easy grader, easy to talk to.
Straightforward and there to help his students
Very kind and cares a lot about the content.
Absolutel W he's so nice and cares about his students

Instructor is learned about his topics, prefers full class participation and can conduct lively and interesting lectures. Concepts taught by him were extensively used in the coursework and proved to be quite important.
He gives clear and brief feedbacks which helps in the future assignments. Lectures are fun and filled with activities like healthy discussions and debates.
The teaching style is nice
His in class presentations were good and he used to conduct activities which makes learning interesting.

Has genuinely no idea what she's talking about. Takes points off assignments not because things are missing/wrong but because she doesn't understand anything anyone is trying to say about advertising campaigns
i had a funeral to go to and they didnt let me make up the exam.

Professor was fine, but class was a bit disappointing. Completely lecture and information based with no hands on experience and very little useful assignments. Basically just a PR info overload but no actual experience doing PR related things in class. Pretty easy though

Participation and attendance are weird in this class. Each time you speak up in class, you earn 5 pts out of the 70. But if you speak 5 times during one class, it is still only 5 pts. Sometimes she does slido attendance, but you can't get 100% just doing those, making speaking in class important. First exam is tough, but the others aren't bad.
Reads off slides like she's seeing them for the first time. Awkward long pauses before every sentence. Doesn't seem to actually understand what she's teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Inspirational lectures and great guy. Learned a lot of real world skills in the class
Has extremely unfair attendance policy, and no attempt to make it fair. Show up everyday except that one random day he takes attendance? you lose.

Best professor I've had in college. I actually changed my secondary field of study to Environmental Engineering after taking this class with Guest. Inspirational, makes the material easy to understand, and very reasonable with the gradings. Do not miss the chance to take a class with him!

One of my favorite professors I've had, just because he is very personable and his lectures are extremely clear. Environmental engineering isn't the most interesting topic, so lectures can be boring at times, but I have no doubt I would not have done as well as I did with a different teacher. Attendance is taken daily and all work is done in groups

Really passionate teacher which makes the hour and a half lecture not as painful. Willing to meet all the time, including coming in early and setting up extra study sessions. Constant group work though which can be a pain.

Great lecturer and super nice. Interesting material + lots of practice problems during lecture to keep you engaged. He comes around to help students once he's given the class stuff to work on, so you never feel lost in the crowd. There's a final group project that isn't too hard. I learned a lot and really enjoyed this class overall.

Prof Guest is a very nice guy and he gives great lectures. I wasn't particularly interested in enviro, but I really enjoyed learning from him. You'll be working in the same group for weekly homeworks and a final project & presentation, and he has good policies in place to make sure your members pull their weight. Overall very enjoyable class!

Late to lecture, no apology, looks like just rolled out of bed. Goes off topic a lot & rambles, hard to listen to. Doesn't post the lecture slides, which forces you to come even though she doesn't take attendance. Doesn't let you ask questions during exams. One of the worst teachers I had, don't take her class. No idea how she's still teaching.

Ngl chat, just read that book. Going to lecture is pointless lol. And ofc if you have questions use your TA for help and gt office hours. Just know you're wasting your sleep and time trade-off for your opportunity cost coming to class.
Realized half way through the semester I wasted the first half going to lecture. Read the book and go to discussion. Anything she is going to teach u the book does better

She was very difficult in lectures. Honestly through the first 3-4 units the lectures were almost no use attending. Lots of rambling it's tough to follow. Definitely skim the book if you don't attend the lectures, it's much more helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She does not teach this class; it's all Zoom lectures from 2020 that are poorly edited. She doesn't even show up to class, and when she does, it's only on exam days, where she refuses to talk to students. She is very intelligent, but it seems like she does not want to teach this class. She rambles heavily and gets lost... even on Zoom recordings.
Shes okay i mean as long as you take decent notes the class is okay

3 Exams, final exam, strenuous research project are just some of the large assignments worth points. Unclear teaching, tough grader, and seems confused over her own teaching in class/office hours. Highly recommend not taking any classes taught by her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand what she is saying. She gets lost in her own words. Lectures aren't mandatory, but you prob want to go so you are not confused. Does not really prepare us for exams and taught us stuff then said it wasn't even gonna be on the exam... Go to discussions bc those points will help your grade.

Class is optional but pretty pointless. You don't learn much, and most of the lectures seem like common sense. Still a very nice professor, and the tests are very easy. Easy grading scale, too, and the worst test grade is dropped.
She is not very good at teaching
Unbelievably bad

She is always late to lecture, and cannot work zoom as a seasoned professional. During lecture she goes on long tangents then gets lost through her words, making it extremely hard to follow. Did not prepare me for tests at all.

Lisa Gunderson is honestly underrated. Her course may be tough, but she makes it easy. She can drop your lowest exam scores, which really saved my grade since I was taking a lot of tough courses besides her class. As long as you pay attention, do your homework, take notes, and study enough, you should be in a good position to pass the class.
She's 10 minutes late to every class and shows up with her hair not brushed. Can't work zoom even though she's been teaching this class for years. it's an easy A though

Dr. Gunderson is unorganized and has confusing lectures. Unprofessional when walking into class, usually a couple minutes late. It's insanely difficult to focus into what she's teaching because of her tangents. She even gets lost in what she says.
She rambled and when on tangents. Did not prepare me well for exams, had to learn on my own. She seems very nice, but not effective at teaching at all.

This class had a “flipped classroom” environment, where you taught yourself the material through pre-recorded lectures before coming to class. Class consisted of doing practice problems that you had to turn in at the end. Quite simple and an easy A as long you do the work.

Professor Gundersen rambles forever in a very unclear manner during her lectures. I still think attending lecture is helpful, but you can get the same out of it as watching YouTube or reading even just the summary pages of each chapter in the textbook. All exams are worth 60% of the grade and homework is graded on effort, not accuracy.

I learned more by reading the textbook and watching random YouTube videos than I did in the lecture. She rambles about nothing and then blames us for a low class average.  Exams are non-cumulative, and one midterm is dropped. Not a difficult class, but it's definitely frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Gundersen's lectures gives a ton of opportunities for extra credit, and she is really nice, however I found her lectures to be extremely boring. I found reading the textbook more helpful than the notes she hands out. Exams are all multiple choice and fairly easy. She also always has a practice exam available that is formatted exactly like the exam.
I took the in-person class, but it might have been online. She doesn't teach in class; she posts videos that explain the information using the most straightforward examples. Disappointed.

I took the class FALL 22. Her note packets for lectures were very helpful. Additionally, I really enjoyed my discussion section. We'd go over practice exams and practice problems in discussion! I bought a textbook that was the wrong edition, but then found the pdf online of the right edition for free! So try looking for a free pdf first!
Loved her!!! She's friendly, communicates well, explains during lectures in GREAT detail, and won't hesitate to help you understand! If you have her as an option PICK HER and attend the lectures!

Tests were a big part of the grade. If they have office hours I'd recommend it. I took micro in high school and was still a little confused at times because the topic is tricky. She did a good job explaining things simply though. The practice tests you get from going to the non-mandatory discussion sections were sooo helpful. I had great TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was a little nervous heading into ACE 100 after looking at these reviews. However, I was pleasantly surprised! The lectures weren't the most exciting, but Professor Gundersen was nice and laid out everything we needed to do clearly. The lectures were posted online if you didn't make it to the Zoom which was very convenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took it in Summer 2020, so i don't know about regular semesters, and it only has 4 quizzes in total. Homework are based on textbook, and the textbook is really helpful , so definitely take a look when listening to the lectures and doing homework. She gives extra credit simply coming to at least one office hour. Such a friendly professor.

Super patient, will answer any question that you have. I didn't read the instructions correctly on her extra credit and she still gave me credit! So nice about everything and she grades super fairly and is easily accessible for questions related to exams or homework. I honestly can't say enough good things about her!

Took her statistics class and she was very nice and caring. Lectures aren't really mandatory but she gives a lot of extra credit that can be added towards your exams. Class was fairly easy, as the online homework problems are all accessible if you have Chegg.

Horrible lectures, horrible exams, horrible teaching-style. Don't go to her lectures unless you want a free napping period, they're useless anyways. Textbook teaches better than she can. I haven't been to lecture since the first midterm, and, trust me, you'll be better off not going.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy
