Professor Kim is an amazing professor to take a Gen Ed Geography course with. His lectures have amazing material, and GD does not take himself or the course too seriously, and is very generous with grading and deadlines. He really gets to know every student and has been one of my favorite professors at UIUC. 100% recommend.

She is a very sweet woman and the class wasn't Hell on Earth or anything, but there were issues. Her resistance towards and lack of understanding surrounding technology is very hard to work with. Additionally, it was barely a creative writing course; I love journaling but I don't love spending hours on it for a completion grade.

She is a sweet lady who is very helpful and is always open to helping in or outside of class. She is hard of hearing, but she doesn't make it her personality to speak up. She's very easy on grading, and there are only two or three main assignments, which she allows first drafts and gives loads of feedback. Class

It literally feels like you're back in fifth grade. You have to draw a picture of yourself for attendance every single day. Made us go past PAR and FAR for a "field trip." There were three field trips for this class, none of which were actually used for any writing. Makes you read sex scenes out loud. Barely any writing in a Creative Writing class.
She can't hear for the life of her and she treats this class like its a English majors course. There's a lot of busy work, none of which is very hard. But, the work takes a while to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She's really nice, no doubt about it. I just wish that her class was a little bit more energizing. When she would try to have a conversation with the class, we would be dead silent... I felt bad for her. But, on the bright side, I actually learned a few grammatical lessons from her. She's not that bad :/
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: her grading makes zero sense and the lectures are often meaningless. this is the class you dread going to
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Not such a hard class. The workload isn't as much as other rhet professor. From what I heard, we had the least amount of papers. 2 essays and 1 annotated bibliography. The lecture is very boring because all she does is talk about pointless things. But if you don't want to do a lot of work and don't mind a boring professor then I would recommend her
Tough grader with respect to other professors. Not very clear about what the assignments are. Would not recommend for a professor.

I believe she is also really kind and nice person and tries to be as helpful as she possibly can. The problem is that she talks too much about her personal life and as a student, I didn't wanted to know too much about her father, or stuff like that. But she is good! I heard that she was tough grader, but she isn't. She is generous.
she's nice, but gives A LOT of busy work.

she's a nice enough person, she's just really disorganized. bring your laptop, otherwise you'll be bored out of your mind. her assignments are just annoying and a waste of time, but not difficult. i usually type an essay in 1/2 an hr and do fine (b or higher) not hard, just annoying

Wished attendance wasn't mandatory cuz I felt I didn't need to be there half the time. I swear 2 of her assignments were practically identical which only wasted a lot of my time. Annoying that she only gives A's for "truly exceptional writing"--whatever that means. If I did the work and there weren't any errors, I should get an A, period.

Easily the worst professor I have had.  This class would be fine, even useful with anyone but her.  She'll keep you the entire time, even if she hasn't prepared enough material to warrant an extra half hour.  She self-promotes and soap boxes to the point of requiring us to watch a documentary on wal-mart and reading articles published about her.

What an awful class.  Its easy but so boring it's mindnumbing.  She takes attendence, gives you 6 missed classes before your grade is lowered and every tardy counts as 1/2 an absence.  She's... weird, and scary to look at.

There were no slide decks or PowerPoints used in this class, and the teaching style was extremely confusing. I found her approach frustrating—she was enthusiastic, but ineffective and make it difficult for students to actually learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: There is not a single comprehensive slide for this course. The professor wrote the answer by hand but did not type, and no one understood her handwriting. The review materials are always given by the day before the midterm, leaving people no time to study it. The participation grade was calculated in a very confusing way.

Material taught in class did not match the wording on the test so no one knew what the test Qs were asking for. No core objectives or a slide deck for the topics taught each week, the concepts are taught entirely through case application so we had no idea what we were supposed to be learning. Other 304 profs have slide decks or summary sheets.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! Gives good lectures and provides a lot of examples. Quizzes are based of the lectures and homeworks, so it is important to pay attention. Open note for tests and quizzes. Midterm and final is chill. Homeworks are also very useful.

Good and reasonable professor in general. Lectures were optional but informative, all assessments were open note, gives reasonable curves for tests + extra credit opportunities on HW. HW and quiz solutions would be posted and he gave good resources to succeed on the midterm and final. Would recommend to take him over the other ME200 sections.

Best professor I've had. Quizzes, midterm, and final are all open note and not extremely difficult questions. He does a great job explaining during lecture and even though it's not mandatory I'd recommend attending. Also very understanding and helpful. Makes a scary and difficult class easy.
Best professor ever

So hes goated, i got an A- in the class and emailed him to bump it up and he did it with no questions asked to an A. Besides that hes a really solid guy, maybe not the most interesting but his lecture are super solid and he explains clearly with tons of examples. Open not quizzes and homework with extra credit. Really good guy for a tough class.
He's genuinely a good professor.  Would go to lectures, they help.  Quizzes are easy and useful to study, midterm and final are chill.

Really good course policies for ME200. The biweekly quizzes are genuinely a breeze. His class is open note for all tests including the final. You dont have to attend lecture but I'd recommend it because I think it personally helps you understand the content better. The homework is somewhat tedious but there's room for extra credit there.

He is great for thermo. Lectures are filled with exam/quiz level examples that you need to know for the course. The HWs can be difficult and time consuming but I found that doing all of the problems including the extra credit ones always prepared me for the quizzes and exams. The final only covers the cycles and psychrometrics so focus on that.
This instructor is best for this, what he is teaching.

This man is a robot, but a good one. His class runs at 8am, but you should go. Open-note quizzes and exams so take notes on paper. Very informative class on the basics of thermodynamics with 6 20-minute quizzes and 1 midterm. One drop for the quizzes. Final exam is heavily weighted and mainly covers later content such as cycles and psychrometrics.

The professor is very lenient and generous. Homework is graded on effort, homework has the same weight as the final (with extra credit attached), and all tests and quizzes are open-note on paper. It truly helps in offsetting the high stress of course material. If taking class for credit, pick him over other professors that you aren't sure about.

CAPSIM can be a little annoying, but there's a lot of makeup points. Easy course overall with little work. Show up to class and be a good team member and you're golden. easy A. No midterms or reading quizzes compared to other sections of b201.
A nice person overall, but she spends a lot of class time on long lectures that don't always feel super useful or connected to the actual assignments.
A lot of easy group work, Capsim was fun. You can make up points for capsim. you should easily get an A in this class without much effort.
With so many pointless lectures and awkward events, there was very little time left for actual learning and CAPSIM. It's hard to say I learned anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a sweet and engaging professor! I took this for no credit, just looked interesting, Prof. McLeer is so well-versed and enthusiastic about her class and truly wants the best for her students. Generous grader, lots of readings, great in-class discussions, and great feedback!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely understanding with extensions and provides helpful feedback for all essay assignments. Very passionate about the material she was teaching. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super kind and understanding. Grading is very relaxed, but it's pretty difficult to get away on exams without reading the assigned material. She rarely assigned huge loads of text. It was about an hour per week in my experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor McLeer was honestly such a fun teacher to have for british literature you could really tell in each of her lectures that she was passionate and enjoyed what she was talking about. There's a lot to read which is to be expected in a literature course but you can get through while being behind. My only gripe is her grading is a little strict

McLeer is a very laid back professor. She is lenient with assignment and is very understanding that you have other things going on outside of her class. She offers revisions on some assignment which is a big help to your overall grade. This class has so many assignments throughout the semester. They are not difficult, but time consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a great professor indeed. But she is a strict grader on papers and the first paper's average is C+ to B+. Please consider taking a BTW250 with other professors.

Dr. McLeer is a wonderful professor. Taking her RHET105 section was one of the best decisions I made. She made the class engaging by allowing the students to pick the topics for their papers. She always gives plenty of time to complete the assignments and is a fairly easy. Take her section if you can!

Very friendly, helpful, and kind. Slightly unorganized, but she puts effort into the class and enjoys discussing all types of writing. while the class has a lot of reading and writing, she will help and give all the advice she can. Very relaxed and flexible with students. Would love to take another class of hers if I had time.
Easy class + good professor = A.

Professor Selznick is a super caring and understanding professor. There are 4 major projects, and she gives you two late paper waivers. Class discussion was really thought-provoking, and I really learned a lot!

Although I might've not gotten a good grade (due to my own lacking), she is a great professor. This professor requires effort, hard work, and communication, as with any class. She will work with you if you work with her - take that as you will. She is one of the most caring, understanding, humorous professors that I have ever had. She's the best!

Class is really easy and the professor is super friendly and nice. The only complaint I have is that I realized this is a very boring course LOL. I'd rather take a different advanced composition course
She is great, highly recommend for advanced comp credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is clearly very passionate about the content. I'd recommend it. There are occasional pop quizzes (I think 7-8 throughout the whole semester?). Exams weren't hard. Just read the summaries and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: An amazing teacher, super passionate about her work. Random quizzes during lectures but not hard if you read the material. But overall, amazing professor would take her class again!

Prof. Hilger is very passionate in her teaching and you should attend all of her lectures. There's 5-10 pop quizzes and taking notes of what she's saying in lecture will help greatly in the exams. There was ample time given for the papers and they were graded fairly. Also, read all of the course packet if you want to score well on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very cool class, professor Hilger is a great lecturer and lots of the exam content is from her lectures. Daily readings and many of the readings were very interesting just be careful of pop quizzes during lecture. The texts we read were very interesting and progressed smoothly over different time periods, great class. Essay grading was very fair
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hilger is a good lecturer, and the class is heavily dependent on you showing up. Lecture notes aren't posted and discussions are required. However, the material is interesting and grading is quite lenient. There are about 5 pop quizzes, 2 essays, and 4 shorter "responses" covering the readings. The workload is super light. Def recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The lectures were straightforward. Attendance is important due to the random pop quizzes that are given but they are quite simple if you read at least the sparknotes or actually listened to the lecture. The tests weren't hard as long as you at least went to the review discussion and memorized the given definitions.

Genuinely such a lovely lady. Shows up to lecture with hand-written notes and truly cares and is interested in what she is teaching on. You have to read and you have to do the homework, but if you can handle that then I cannot recommend her more! (P. S. Select Fam as your TA if available, he is incredible and actually cares)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She put effort into her lectures and made class more exciting by adding videos and fun pop culture references into her script. Fair amount of reading for an advanced composition class and grading was really straight forward so pay attention to the rubric. All in all I really enjoyed her class and her teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Lots of reading and material, but she explains it well and makes it interesting. There are surprise pop quizzes during some lectures, so get ready for that, but the questions are so forgiving if you've read. Extra credit on the tests. And responses and essays are pretty straightforward. If you can, choose Fam as your TA, he was so good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Since my class with her was remote, I didn't have to take any quizzes/ tests for the semester, making the course may more manageable. Granted that the lectures are good, I didn't bother watching any of them and did well overall. Lots of essay assignments.

Honestly, the class is not that hard. Although, the hardest part is reading. However, what you need to know about readings to succeed is talked in the class. But overall, if you put some effort, you should get an A. And as a person, she is super nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: She has very thorough lectures, if you pay attention.
Hilger is a pretty great professor, really likes her multimedia. There are 7 quizzes in section that are really easy. The class can get real boring, but Hilger knows what she's talking about.
She's very nice, but the readings for the class can be a little hard
Everything is based on the essays so if you can BS an essay really well then this is the class for you.  Otherwise you just have to show up and say something once in a while

The discussion section took attendance, but the lecture did not. As long as you feel like you can complete the assignments well, the lecture was not really necessary to attend. The course is mostly graded on a group project which is not very time-consuming and you get a lot of time to work on it. Jacquie is great!

Lectured didn't really have much to do with assignments or discussion sections. Our entire grade was basically reliant on discussions and the group project. Lectures were interesting and well delivered, prof was funny. Lectures weren't really necessary though to pass.

I had a 10am M/W lecture for this class which I went to about 40% of the time. The lectures were always well delivered and engaging. Jacque has a good sense of humor and is a good orator. She also attended discussions to give feedback on group projects which I appreciated.
She's very fun, I found her lectures and the discussions to be very useful to the advertising major. Half of your grade is on a group project
Very fun and laidback class structure in discussions and in lecture. Group projects are a big chunk of your grade, so choose partners wisely

Jacquie was great and cares about her students. She has expectations of your work but they are for your own benefit and are reasonable. 9 am lectures are boring and kind of a drag but material/assignments/discussion is not bad at all. Most of the class is focused on group work so try to get a good group!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her lectures were great, although for 9am halfway through the sem I stopped going. Seems like lecture attendance being taken in ADV250 is new and is now taken through a Google form QR code. Very group project heavy, get a good/dependable group to split the work + 2 presentations. No exams/quizzes. Do the work and you'll get an easy A!

Jacquie has a passion for PR and I like the way she taught the course. She posts the slides online. There are plenty of opportunities to get extra credit (the easiest + best way is to participate in lecture). The tests were easy but the grading was subjective. Got a C on one test with no feedback (had to ask for it) but got A's on the others.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE this lady!! Her lectures are not mandatory but she makes class so interesting, so its definitely worth going. Her personal stories are so interesting! Graded by 4 Exams on canvas, and they're not too difficult.

Hitchon always kept class very engaging and interesting. 3 Individual brand assignments and a semester long group project. She was very caring about deadlines and moved them back when she felt like we were moving too fast. Weekly quizzes were difficult, but open book and no time limit, so not too bad. Would definitely take a class with her again!

He is a one of the more decent professors I've had, gives good lectures and likes to make funny jokes throughout, has a good sense of humor, is realistic about the class, as long as you show up to lecture and pay attention you'll be fine. He has a lecture voice that will keep you awake.

He is honestly one of the worst professors I have ever had. Not only does he barely teach what is needed for the Exams, He is just a jerk of a professor. He is extremely uncaring for the students (no grade curving, strict on conflict exams, will curve down to match a 83% average) and just overall boring in his lectures

MATH490 this sem is Computational Math. He is a good professor. The class is pretty collaborative and he is knowledgeable. The midterms are sort of hard, but he understands so he does curve upwards. There is weekly coding hw which is manageable. He is VERY easy to talk to and is always willing to help. I'm confused by others' reviews. Good class.

His class is only for smart kids. If you think you are smart, then take it since all the questions in exams are not straightforward at all. I heard there is another professor in different sections and his exams are much easier than this one. I think his exam is more like you have to know the knowledge very well and interpret it.

This guy obviously should not be teaching. Sure might be a great researcher or smart or whatnot. But to have him teach is to literately hit yourself over and over again in the nether regions with a sack of bricks.

For 285 he was very helpful and pretty funny, I enjoyed going to lectures. Tests were difficult, but in my opinion very fair. Homework takes a while, so start early. Overall I thought he was a good teacher in lecture and pretty funny!

Always gives the hardest homework, you should start a week ahead of time. I didn't find his lectures helpful at all, although some did. My only hope at finishing the homework was going to the office hours. Tests are difficult, based a lot on the homework.

Lectures are very dry. Homework problems assigned are the most difficult ones of the section, usually the last problems (the proofs), instead of explicitly solving functions.  Tests are extremely tough, and he gives little to no practice exam questions. Average on the first test was a 54%. Take a different professor if you choose to take Math 285.

Completely unfair exams with completely unfair grading.  He gives out 1 practice exam for each test, but they are exams written by different professors, that have just about nothing in common to the exams he writes.  Test questions have multiple sub-questions, and you can't get any of the sub-questions right if you get the original question wrong.
Projects and HW could have been organized much better. Wasn't as a bad a professor as everyone makes him out to be. Take 357 with Gambil when it is a joke though if possible.

Took this class a few semester back. I find him to be pretty funny. If you go to his office hours he is very helpful and you can see that he tries really hard to keep students happy. However I don't think it is possible students happy by the nature of the course. Difficult required course which doesn't seem to relevant to people who take it.
If you study the lecture notes, you will do well in the final.

He's a good friend but not a good professor. He's too proud, therefore too caught up on attendance, right of viewing (rather incomprehensible) lecture notes, and refusing to read the newsgroup. Yet, even tho he's not good at teaching right now, I believe with more years, when he let go of the stubbornness of unnecessary stuff, he'll be much better.

Everything previously said is true. His first exam wasn't bad, but for the final, he gave us NO guidance other than to study all homework and lectures, and most of the final was over topics covered near the very end of the course. With that being said, I'm confident I could have done a lot better had i put forth more effort. Just be prepared to wor

He is a horrible professor. This is my first and probably last rating on this site, i just had to let the world know how bad he is. He has a sick fascination with apple and hates everything else. Horrible teacher, him and the TAs never answered questions on the newsgroup when that was supposed to be our first resource. DO NOT TAKE.

This was absolutely the worst professor I've had here. The lectures that he does actually release are purposely illegible to "screw over those who don't attend class". He never released solutions to the last few homeworks, and gave us no information about the final, making it nearly impossible to study for. This man should not be a professor.

Pretty much what people before said. He thinks that uploading lecture notes is our privilege not our right and tries to withhold them to force attendance. He will randomly take attendance to prove that attendance has gone down from the day he uploaded the lecture notes. Out of 75 mins of lecture he brags about himself and his philosophy for 30 mins

He thinks that uploading lecture notes is our privilege not our right. He will randomly take attendance to prove that attendance has gone down from the day he uploaded the lecture notes. Out of 75 mins of lecture he brags about himself and his philosophy for 30 mins. Though he has lots of knowledge he doesn't know how to teach.

Horrible. Lecutures were pointless to attend. Made the material so boring. Spends more time bragging about nasa cal-tech etc... Makes tests super difficult in order to make you study more. Hand writes notes no powerpoint. So tediously boring. Avoid if you can.

I'm upset that Hirani is still teaching this course, b/c he calls on people in class and insults them if they have forgotten linear algebra. I was taking 3 math courses at the time, and decided to drop the class,not because it was hard,but because the professor is really rude. Hopefully the CS dept. will reevaluate him teaching such a huge lecture.
I'm pretty sure he isn't at UIUC anymore but his online lectures are great for this class.
Too many mistakes in the lecture. seems he didn't get prepared before recording

Prof. Hieronymi's recorded lectures go into and explain the material really well, but make sure you take notes on the computational AND conceptual aspects of the material. The exams WILL test you on both. The homework questions (if still on PrairieLearn) are very helpful in preparing for exams.
The content can get confusing, especially towards the end, but as long as you watch lectures and do homework, you should be fine. The exams are never a surprise, it is modeled after the homework.

This class is definitely tough, but the professor is pretty great. I don't think anyone else should be teaching the class. He explains the material really well. Discussions are useless, but his lectures are definitely super helpful. Also super friendly if you ask him questions during office hours

He is a WONDERFUL professor. You don't even have to attend lecture; however, do attend because it is absolutely worth it, it's just a way better experience than watching it online. But, do understand that this course is EXTREMELY difficult. Grade is VERY exam heavy, I nearly failed my first test because I was surprised by how difficult it was.
Great professor, be sure to attend classes and work through all the problems
Linear algebra is standard and exams weren't hard, but they are all about theorems. I skipped class since lectures are posted online and there are lecture videos as well.

He's a great professor and a great lecturer. Really accessible and fair and reasonable. I would absolutely take a class again with him. He is definitely one of the better professors at this university
His lecture is really boring and he makes mistakes during lecture often. Not a very good professor generally speaking.

The epitome of what college professor should be like; Able to teach, extremely fair, understanding, and knowledgeable. Some or maybe most of the college professors will be biased; like having poor course organizations and inconsistencies in grading.
Very well prepared for lectures.

Professor Hieronymi's lectures are clear and straightforward. He posts all lecture notes online and also posts practice problems. He is very approachable and always willing to help. I recommend going to his office hours if you have any questions. Overall, one of my absolute favorite professors.

To be honest I only went to lecture twice, but some people might have benefited from going. He went through a pre-printed lecture note packet, and uploaded it later to compass.   Discussion quizzes were EASY (show up without any knowledge, TA teaches you the material, get a 1010. Exams were EASY. Final was  hard, I went from a 93% to a B+ :(

Good teacher, plus, he provided tons of content from other places. So if you weren't understanding something, you just had to try another source that he provided. The easiness of the first two exams made me ill prepared for the third one though. My fault really, but a heads up would have been nice.
Fantastic professor. Kept lectures as practical and simple as possible. Always posted a practice exam almost identical to the actual exam. Best of all, he made the textbook optional.
For how abstract the course material was, he did a great job presenting the content in a clear way. He was lenient on hw deadlines, and exams were very fair. Also posted lecture notes online.

His lectures were absolutely clear compared to the other 225 professors. On top of that, his fill in notes were a godsend.  Finally, he makes sure that you all succeed.  I've never had a math class where the average from the first midterm be an 86%.  Easy A for a class.
Very helpful and very clear. He is always willing to talk to students and make sure that they succeed. He also tells you exactly what is on the exam. Easy A for sure.

Professoressa Hill truly cares about the success of her students and is always willing to help them. She comes to class everyday with a smile and great enthusiasm. She always encourages participation and is supportive of students' different levels of speaking in Italian. I always looked forward to her class! Take a class with her!

Laura is very kind and helpful. She was extremely accommodating through a very tough semester for me. Although I am not a huge fan of the class she is a great professor. She offers a lot of feedback and help if you need it. She also takes a personal interest in all of her students. Tests and quizzes can be difficult.

Laura Hill is the sweetest professor ever. She genuinely cares about her students and works hard to meet their needs. I told her I wanted to go to med school once early in the semester and she remembered that detail about me at the end. I decided to take 104 with her, despite not needing it for credit. I would highly recommend her classes!

Prof. Hill is very sweet, funny, and manages the class with a comforting sort of ease. Always happy to answer any questions, and always has a smile on her face when teaching. She's interested in her students, grades fairly, and gives great feedback. Class = grammar, quizzes, two presentations, midterm, and final. She prepares you well for them!

for 104! Laura Hill is the best!! she is the sweetest lady and really wants you to do well in her class! She makes sure everyone participates and feels comfortable during class. if you are in any italian class with her you will do well as long as you try! i would 100% recommend her classes!

IF YOU DON'T THINK YOU'RE GOOD AT ITALIAN, YOU'RE IN THE RIGHT PLACE - Professor Hill is one of the best teachers on campus and a loveable person. I didn't know much Italian going into 103, but I got a 95+. She is a great teacher, caring, and a fairly easy grader. There are blogs and tests, but this class (ZOOM ONLINE) is easier than 102.

Laura is an ANGEL! She is seriously so sweet. She's very intelligent and knows how to help students when they are struggling. Best Italian professor I've had. The class is fun because you get to know other students. She does encourage participation from everyone but it's never an issue if you get something incorrect. Highly recommend her!

This is the second semester I've had her, and she is so great! She is so put together and always there to help. The whole class is in Italian, but she doesn't put you on the spot and helps you if you get stuck or don't know a word. She really knows what she's doing and structures the course well. She makes you participate, but it's beneficial!

Laura was fantastic! I was excited about this class from first meeting her for my placement exam over the summer, and the class was even better than I expected. She's from Bologna, and she really knows what she's talking about. She's very kind and understanding. There's online hw a few times a week and a blog post every week.

I took her class out of interest in Italian when I was an undergrad and therefore I got the chance the know Laura for over 3 years. She is the best professor I could ever  asked for learning a foreign language, she is patient and helpful.

I love Laura! She is the nicest teacher on campus. I was very worried for Ital 102, but she made it a lot less stressful! She is always there for you when you need help and really wants you to do well in the class. Definitely take her Italian class!

Laura is amazing! I usually don't like to participate in Italian, but she is so nice that participating comes easy. She is extremely fair in grading, usually not marking off for grammar mistakes in non-grammar sections. Presentations were a fun component to the class and she would sometimes bring candy in! It felt like high school. Nicest teacher!
She was INCREDIBLY helpful and a great teacher. Take her class!
She is such a darling person. Very helpful, understanding, and patient. I miss this class very much!

She is SO sweet and incredebily helpful.  She has always a smile on her face (like mentioned it before) and is very approachable if you ever have any question.  She does not make the student feel dumb if they don't know the answer which makes the whole class to participate and not be scared to get a pronuciation wrong.I would HIGHLY recommend her.
She's so kind! She clearly cares that her students understand what she is teaching and wants them to succeed.
Nicest Italian teacher I have ever had!!! soooo nice!!!!
GREAT PROFESSOR! VERY NICE! ALWAYS HAS A SMILE ON HER FACE :)

You will "present" your homework solutions during the lecture period. Personally, I am not a fan of this format but it is what it is. There is a new homework assigned every class, about 9-12 problems usually. Most of the grade is attendance, homework solutions are collected just for attendance, not correctness. No drops for attendance though.
Take any class this man gives hes amazing. I am about to graduate hes the best professor i have had here truly inspirational.

The class was inverted, with students presenting homework in lectures. Participation and attendance made up 55% of the grade, creating an engaging environment. The professor was the best I've had across 10 chemistry courses, making complex topics clear. Homework was instrumental for learning, but it reduced study stress and enhanced understanding.

I'm a senior by standing and have taken a lot of chemistry, physics, and math classes prior to taking CHEM 442 but I can say with confidence that Professor So Hirata is by far the best teacher in the entirety of college. He is patient, kind, inspiring knowledgeable, and funny in short an absolute legend.

Great class structure- prelectures provide a good outline of material that is filled in during lectures. Dr. Hirata is very open and encouraging toward student questions creating a great learning environment during class. He constantly connects class concepts with interesting research questions to inspire his students.
The class sometimes feels disjoint but it well taught all the way through. Grading is based on exams only. It shows that Prof H loves teaching this class.

His lectures are clear, concise and substantial. Those are definitely worth attending because he knows how to teach and works out problems that are helpful for completing the homework during class. He is approachable and receptive to feedback as well and tries to make the quizzes as fair as possible.
Very clear lectures, and receptive to student feedback. Left me with a good understanding of the course material.

He isnt very good at answering your questions, this class in general is very difficult He gets no respect in class either. The exams are difficult but there is a nice curve. He isnt great, and this class sucks, just avoid it if possible.
Awkward....about all I can say. Is clear in the material he covers but doesn't cover enough.   Bad teaching methods (slides and chalk board) and unprepared to teach this level of course.
He is so unprepared, it isn't even funny. And commands no respect.

You will like this class if you like physics and math in general. A very smart and nice guy. He's willing to offer extra office hours before exams but few people would actually take advantage of that (I guess).
Great instructor. Clear presenter of material, but very boring material. I would highly recommend this guy and not recommend the course he teaches.

She is amazing! Have had her for multiple Japanese courses now. She is very understanding and helpful, and makes the class enjoyable. The only part I did not enjoy as much was the schedule of the class, as it was every day for the whole semester. But she's a great teacher and I would really recommend if you're taking a Japanese course!

Hayashi-san is a great professor and is genuinely dedicated to helping students succeed. The most important thing by far is to make sure you study EVERY DAY. I mean it. While Japanese is a very hard language to learn, Hayashi-san makes it much easier and friendly.

reviews.comment:
Hayashi sensei is a kind and fun teacher. She always is willing to help, but the class isn't too difficult. There are small quizzes about every week on kanji, vocab, and grammar which can be a lot. I'm not sure I improved my Japanese as much as I would have liked to, but I do not regret taking the class.
I recommend Hayashi sensei!

Lectures are very bad, but attending is prudent because each counts for part of the course grade. The class covers so much material that truly understanding any of it is structurally discouraged. It includes all(ish) topics from a ordinary stats class plus many machine learning topics tacked on. Not very good, but extremely easy due to EC.

Such a nice person, a bunch of extra credit, but cannot teach. Lectures are slow and not helpful. Notes are long and redundant. Just self-learn. 4 exams, each administered differently. At least 3 different websites to juggle for the class. Grading is more complicated than taxes. She's nice, but a disorganized teacher.

Take STAT 400 or MATH 461 instead. Most CS+X majors will be able to make this substitution; CS majors not. There is no use for this class that is not better served by some other class. It's an easy class and you will get an A, but it's mismanaged to a degree that no part of the ease is worth the pain. It's odd because Liu is so nice.

Nicest professor i've met with the worst lectures. Genuinely don't know how to feel. You can tell she genuinely cares about students but i cannot for the life of me understand what she is saying. There is A LOT of extra credit opportunities though and the grading for frq is very lenient.
Sensational

Lectures are bad. You can use the textbook to learn or yt vids. Lots of extra credit though, and not a lot of heavy work. They also offer curve, even with your final grade. If you can self learn you'll be fine, if not than STAT 400 might be better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment:
Lectures were sub-par. Recitation from TAs is far more valuable in this course, as the lectures are overly complicated and hard to follow.

TAs were instructed to write vague answers for practice tests so problems could be used on future tests.  Very difficult to learn problem solving without attending office hours since almost 0 feedback is given.

Professor Liu is not a great teacher. The course itself should not be difficult, but the lectures are structured very poorly making even simple concepts very difficult to understand. If you have the choice to take STAT 400 or CS 361, 100% take STAT 400. You'll learn so much more.

This professor is undoubtedly very kind and sweet, but her lectures were hard to follow. There is an incredible amount of extra credit. What I found weird was that there were so many websites used for this one class (PrairieLearn, Gradescope, etc.) and the different exam modes (CBTF, in-person, etc.). She wanted us to try everything, I suppose.

This course shouldn't be difficult, but the professor doesn't help. While I think she's very nice, her lectures are very hard to follow. That being said, I think the course is still quite doable especially with the metric ton of extra credit that's given. Honestly, the 45 minutes of TA discussion taught me more than the 2.5 hours of lectures.

Easily the worst class I've taken here. I think it's clear that Professor Liu is a kind professor and is knowledgable about the material, but she does not know how to effectively teach the course. Lectures are useless and only serve to overcomplicate the course concepts. Exams are also overly difficult. Avoid taking this course if possible.
WORST course ever. No reply to a lot of ed posts including questions of pl autograder.

She is the sweetest professor ever and she makes the tests very easy to prepare for. I barely had to study at all outside of going to lecture. She is seriously very sweet and nice and knows what's she's talking about. Don't listen to these other reviews, if you have an issue with Hongye Liu you're gonna have to get through me first.
A lot of homework, quizzes, and exams. But, most importantly, the notation use and notes are really hard to understand.

- lectures: below average, don't really learn stuff, better off with YouTube videos and textbook
- homework: tough grading
- extra credit: yes
- exams: A LOT HARDER THAN THE PRACTICE OR PAST EXAMS, they can be CBTF or IN PERSON

overall, don't take this if you don't have to, save yourself from headaches.

Horrible lectures, I stopped going to class after the first few weeks and relied only on the textbook to teach me.  Tests are difficult and keep changing in format, from paper to CBTF to in-class PrarieLearn.  Office hours are mainly over zoom and not great.  Content is made hard by the bad teaching.

reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice and the course content, while challenging at first, gets easier if you pay attention to the lectures. There is a lot of extra credit.

The class felt badly put together and very chaotic most of the time, the lectures tend to not make sense and got confusing and the textbook is pretty dry. However, if you talk to the professor in office hours she can help explain things that you were confused on. Expect a lot of self-studying on your own and using online resources like statquest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Can't use proper grammar in her questions, slides and lectures are completely useless, not sure why she's allowed to teach a core required class.

Probably worst core cs class. The lectures are useless as it is just slide readings. Everything is poorly organized. The homework are useless busy work that is graded long after its relevance. 

Only good thing is the curve on all the exams, which is just an indicator of poor teaching.
AWFULL!!! Almost nothing prepares you for the exams. Complete nightmare!

reviews.comment: Professor Liu is very thoughtful and caring about her students.

This class was a nightmare. Not only is the content inherently hard, the professor makes no effort to help students learn it. Everyone fails the exams but there's an often 20%+ curve and extra credit. Homework is pointlessly difficult and does not prepare you for exam content. Lectures are unorganized and esoteric. I learned more from the textbook.

She responds to emails about once a week, usually on Wednesdays from 10am to 11am. Office hours are always packed. Lectures are useless. Take STAT 400 instead if you really want to learn statistics for CS.

reviews.comment: Exams were super hard especially when they switched to an online format. Homework graders are bad and you have to literally submit a regrade and discuss the question with the graders. Also, fake extra credit. The TAs were good though
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One star for being a very nice person. Keep in mind this is a stat class for most of the parts, so be prepared. Very challenging and lost for students who have not taken any statistics courses before.

Just awful.The grading is so bad, so many issues with how class is structured, unclear extra credit, exam material hard to prepare for, home works is on your own no examples, lectures are read from slides, can go on forever. What's so annoying is that department hasn't done anything about it, wish they actually cared about how students felt.

Make sure to partake in all EC opportunities, especially the weekly HW. Get a good group for discussion, to minimize points lost. Survey EC was unclear, and missing a single requirement resulted in zero EC, read them carefully.

I lost the majority of points in Midterm 2 & Final. gl
The only difference between a nightmare and this class is that a nightmare goes away when you wake up.

There are no examples for the homework and concepts taught in the class and much of the content is taught in on your time. And also the professor lacks in ability to take grip from the students. Exam and Homework is something you never saw in your life and it will give you biggest failure of your life.
She is very nice and offers lots of extra credit opportunities, however she structures this class in a way that makes it way harder than it needs to be.

reviews.comment: She is very nice and always makes time for student in office hours, but her lectures and the readings she assigns are so incredibly boring and uninformative. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Caring person, lots of extra credit
I mean, "hilarious", literally. Full of meaningless staff such as group discussion.

As previous responses have detailed, she is sympathetic and caring but lacks empathy. This lack of empathy is her biggest weakness as an educator and precludes her from expressing concepts clearly or responding to student inquiries unambiguously. I say this matter-of-factly, not contentiously, and with sincere hope that this course improves.

This course is indispensable to data science/quant finance careers but is unfortunately poorly taught. Please read Forsyth's "Probability and Stats for CS" and Ross's "A First Course in Probability" and test your understanding with the chapter exercises instead of going to lectures/disc. You will learn more and be better prepared for the industry.
she's very engaging
She's a sweet person but a very poor math teacher. I would look for a different class or professor.

reviews.comment: Avoid her at all costs. Lectures are impossible to understand as she cannot speak English well. She moved tests online so that partial credit is not given, making them way more difficult. I can think of no reason to do this other than she doesn't want to do grading. Tests often don't reflect what was covered lectures. Poorly structured. 0/10.
Could not teach to save her life. She's a sweet person, but an awful teacher.

The atrocious management of this class compelled me to even make an account. The lectures are drawn out and overly general, and the homework and exams require students to spend extra time relearning poorly explained lecture concepts. It feels like the course overcompensates for its complete lack of direction by giving large amounts of extra credit.

In my opinion, the course would greatly improve if there were pre-lecture videos to explain the theory and a lecture with real-time solving of problems similar to the homework so students can also see an application of the theory already taught. I learned the theory in this course by doing homework problems, when it should be the other way around.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: CS 361 is difficult, but Prof. Liu has helped me really understand the concepts. Her lectures are can be confusing sometimes, but if you go to office hours, she is more than willing to re-explain things. She’s also one of the most understanding and kind professors I’ve had, and she really emphasizes the importance of having a growth mindset :)

The lectures are really hard to follow and confusing. It is a pain for those who have no background in statistics/probabilities to follow the lectures. I know the prof is knowledgeable and has tried hard to explain the concepts, but she cannot effectively present in lectures. This makes easy concepts (most 361 concepts) hard to understand.
class taught very poorly

The lectures were not helpful at all. You can't do things like answer questions for credit that would give you feedback and check whether you got things understood altogether, and the homeworks can often be quite unclear in the instructions. Not a great experience, don't want to do it ever again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty good professor, very caring and is very understanding of how students struggle. Class was fairly graded and expectations were clear. Good prof but lectures can sometimes go over time.

She's a very caring professor, but math is not her forte. Her lectures cover the basics with lots of examples, but go overtime. Homeworks are doable (but time demanding), and the exams are not too difficult (difficulty level is the same as or lower than homework's). The project instructions were confusing, but piazza/discussions were helpful.

She's really nice and clearly cares about her students. Her lectures were solid and everything that is needed to do well in the course is in the lecture slides. Homeworks were challenging but not too hard and exams were fair. Overall, I learned a great deal about stats and probability from her and had a pleasant experience taking this course.
She is a real nice and responsible professor!!

Took her 361 class spring 2020. She is by far the best CS prof Ive had; shes super caring about her students (regularly extends her office hours to make sure everyone has their questions answered), while lecture can be a bit slow at times, she goes through everything super clearly and theres never any surprises on exams or homework. Great prof!

This course created lots of meaningless jobs, e.g. mandatory discussions. It is really a waste of time to force all students to go to such discussion with everything understood. Besides, the course is disorganized and the delivery is unclear. I didn't learn much from the course and I think it should be improved.

Overall a poor teacher. Lectures are confusing and hard to understand, even with prior statistics background. Homeworks are not well designed and clarifications and alterations are scattered throughout Piazza. The exams aren't too bad, but the project was kind of a mess. She seems to care about the students, but isn't good at teaching.

Bad lecturer as she mumbles about topics and presents elementary stuff as facts (no proof). I'm a CS+Math major and feel that Math is not her forte, she gave wrong solution(s) to project. Her grading is a joke; she curved the final by adding 10% points to everyone so that the median becomes an A, tries to makeup for teaching by hilarious grading.

The lectures were okay. I took 361 in her second semester teaching, and there was improvement along the way, I honestly didn't have the best experience at the start, but she genuinely wants to run a course where students can learn and engage and get help, which is probably the best trait a professor can have. I hope the poor reviews start to fade
You can definitely tell it's her first time teaching -- confusing lectures, not very good course arrangement.

She really cares a lot about the material and especially the students and is generally a very good teacher. I have never seen a professor as active as her on Piazza and its just really nice to have the professor directly answering student questions.

It's her first time teaching at UIUC, I think she did a great job putting all the important contents in to lectures. Everything on the tests you are able to find on the lecture slides. Homework and projects are sometimes hard/ time demanding. But prof was super available (like you can email her questions and go to her office directly).

her lectures are super confusing. she doesnt help with the coding but just expects you to teach yourself everything. this class has been an exercise in watching youtube and teaching myself. she will yell at you for going to the bathroom in a 200 person lecture. she literally asked people to ask permission to use the bathroom. do not take her class
boring lectures, nobody goes to class

I had him as an advisor. He wasn't great help. I almost didn't graduate on time because of him. I had to go to a different random counselor to put me on course. He's a bit unmotivated to help a student out.

Learned so much but grading criteria is super subjective and unclear. Lots of essays and writing. feedback on these did not make sense. Honestly offended that my letter grades on essay exams averaged to C+. I ended up getting an A- on my official grade so I guess his grading system (based on accumulation of points) was clutch.

I've never had this professor, but he was rude to me on an email, and I did not appreciate it.

Tough class, but worth it if you engage with the content. Lectures can drag, but the professor is knowledgeable. Consider using Unstuckstudy alongside the free textbook to prepare - it helped me stay on top of things.

I had him as an advisor, and not a professor, but I imagine his advisement carries over to his teaching. I had a terrible experience working with him. He would force me into classes I did not want to take, he was very rude would mock me for my questions, and would straight up tell me false information about classes. Talk to someone else.
if you have tripophobia do NOT take this class!

If you expect a hard, but straightforward class this is not it. Joseph leaves all of the grading to his ta and is too lazy to make sure his ta even grades it. If you're going through these reviews and thinking that you'll be able to handle his class, good luck Charlie. I had that confidence too. There's supposed to be 8 modules and we had 5. The nicest professor that I have ever had. However, his tangents and overuse of unnecessary words made the class drag on. reviews.comment: Odd mix, but overall a good one. Because there is no disc. sect for PS 318, many of the questions on reading happen in lecture, and can get awkwardly silent when no one can answer them. Tests essay based, but he gives you the selections ahead of time to prepare. Genuinely caring, promotes a good understanding of topics, but weird lecture structure

He's an animated professor, but comes off as condescending imo. He seems to really care and encourages students to visit him during office hours. Tons of readings (100+ pages per week), lectures are disorganized (no powerpoints; he goes on tangents), grading is fair (2 midterms + final w/ cheat sheets, paper, attendance). Material is really dry

reviews.comment: Requires lots of reading: different articles/books every week. Wrote about 4 short essays and one term paper. No quizzes and only one test (final). He is a nice guy who is open to suggestions and helping you if you ask. Overall he is not a tough grader and this class is not hard to pass if you do put in some work.

reviews.comment: Very practical- if you need an extension because you were lazy, he will grant that. If you need extra help, he is willing to help. Don't play yourself- put in enough work!

reviews.comment: I'd like to keep it short.. As much as i like his personality and kindness, he is the worst instructor i've ever had in my entire life.

reviews.comment: Such a boring teacher. Asks questions that have no answer and if they do, you have to be a mind reader. Soooo much homework for a 1-credit class. Wouldnt recommend this class to my worst enemy. He is an eccentric teacher but will talk on and on about vague and abstract ideas which dont help you at all for the papers he assigns.

PS 220 wasn't an entertaining or fun class. He droned on and on and just laughed at his own jokes. However, he's also an adviser who tries to get everyone to not go into law. I don't listen to him when he tells me to give up on law school, but I wish he would help students rather than making them feel dumb and incapable of succeeding.
Lectures were incredibly boring and you have to work to get a good grade in this class. He uses powerpoints for every lecture and it was difficult to stay interested.

Hinchliffe said that he has not taught this class in awhile so I'm assuming it can only get better. The class lectures can be long, the readings are pretty interesting. Overall, you should do fine as long as you're somewhat interested in Public Policy.

I took his 101 class my freshman year and had him as an advisor. He told me to change my career path my first semester of freshman year. I did not listen to him and I changed advisors. I now have an internship at a law firm where the partners have agreed to hire me in three years once I pass the BAR. Point is DO NOT LET THIS MAN KILL YOUR DREAMS.

The class content itself is very interesting which is why I chose to take the class. If you're looking for a blow-off class, this is not for you. Long 120 minute lectures plus reading assignments that can be up to 120 pages + is not my idea of a blow-off. It isn't impossible to pass though as long as you go to class and do the readings.

So I'm a freshman who took his PS 101 class. READ EVERYTHING HE GIVES AND SHOW UP TO LECTURE. That is what I learned this past semester. This class is serious, but incredibly interesting. I say read because his slides give  brief overview over what you had to read. Political Science is no joke and I think that's what he's trying to show.
Worst instructor ever! He is rude, selfish and arrogant!
I don't know why everyone here hates Hinchliffe so much. I think he's a super nice and helpful guy. I enjoyed 321, and I think he's a great advisor.

Not at all surprised by the other comments- this guys likes to smile while actually being rude to students.  Not a pleasant experience working with him, not just for his attitude but also his ability to effectively do his job as counselor to the students who pay his wage.

How did this man become the director of undergrad polisci studies? Inconsiderate, patronizing, so pretentious, and a lazy advisor. The other two advisors are way more interested and personable. They should stage a coup.

Ok for all the PS101 posters and rookie PS majors: PS is a major that has LOTS of reading as a Junior I have 600 pages a week typically. (I don't read all of it) So the level of reading in PS101 is typical. PS-322 was an amazing class, not hard, although I know of some people who struggled CAUSE THEY DONT READ ESSAY PROMPTS lol. Hinchlife is awsome
Just do the work and study and you'll get an A. Everyone is exaggerating. However, you do have to put a little more effort than you would expect to get an A.

Professor Hinchliffe is a great professor with high exoextations! Although this class is difficult, I've gained allot from the experience. This class is here to get rid of all the Poli Sci major students who don't really have a passion for Political Science. Just do the readings+practice time management. I'm continuing my with my major!

I was very interested in politics before this arrogant man ruined it. Want to ruin your gpa? Take his class. I am now changing my major thanks to this pathetic man. Oh, and as an advisor he is useless.

Absolutely horrible class, demanding 3 hours A DAY for this class, assigning articles with 8 point font and with 20 pages, and expecting it to be done by the next day for another article in preparation for his lectures and the test. I came hoping to do well in PoliSci as I love it, but this professor and class turned me away from it.

I understood this professor was challenging. I was eager for the opportunity to prove myself and learn a lot. Looking back, I regret it. The class was a headache and uninteresting. Yes, there are challenging courses that can be quite gratifying, this is not one of them. Unrealistic reading assignments, annoyingly over-animated powerpoints.
He really isnt as bad as everyone says. If you do the readings (there are a lot) you will have no problems on tests. For papers just make you sure you follow instructions. You should be fine.

Absolutely horrid. My first polysci class, 101 in fact, and the course work equals about a 300-level class. Lucky to be even getting a C, seriously. Essays along with 80-100 pages of reading back to back. Multiple choice tests with nothing covered during class. STAY AWAY from this class, unless it's mandatory...
If you want to keep your GPA high, avoid this professor's classes. you will be screwed for sure

This class turned me away from Political Science. It is by far the most demanding class and it will kill your GPA. He is a nice guy, but not too helpful. If you don't have at least 2hrs a night to spend on this class THEN GET OUT WHILE YOU CAN! Good luck everyone, pray for that 70%.

NO, DON'T,RUNAWAY! I am praying on my hands and knees for a 70.00 in this class, all of the other students pretty much feel this same way. I have never in my life never understood a word the teacher was saying, and I went in for help many times. THIS WILL KILL YOUR GPA. Please listen, I wish I had. He never said anything constructive and definite.
Hinchliffe is a cool guy as a friend, just like to chill... but as a professor, he sucks. You pretty much have to do all the studying by yourslef, so BUY and READ the book.

Professor Hinchliffe expects a lot out of his students. His lectures can be confusing, and he uses material on the exam that was not covered in class. However, he challenges his students, and if you do not mind having to work hard, then his class should benefit you in some way.

As an advisor, simply not helpful at all. Outwardly discourages students from pursuing competitive careers and is incapable of accommodating students needs if it requires he step outside his contrived thought process. If you plan on going into law or a Ph.D. program another advisor will be a thousand times more accommodating, helpful and insightful
essay questions very wordy; uses questions at 200 level. Does not necessarily use information discussed in class on tests.

A difficult teacher and not one recommended for froshoman to take, unless you want an difficult 101 class change sections. That being said, he is very knowledgeable of the material and can usually be pursuaded into giving aid. He makes the class a lot harder than other sections, but in the end the extra practice prepares you for harder classes.

Unit 1 is tough but it gets easier, I promise! He is VERY passionate about politics and it shows in his lectures, very energetic and wants his students to love politics. Going to lecture is very important and so is doing the reading. Tough but manageable and interesting.
Does Not teach well; does not use material on tests talked about in lecture

Very kind man who is extremely intelligent and helpful if you see  him outside of class. Unfortunately, lectures are incredibly dry and the tests are Very difficult- half M.C. half essay... essays usually are fine( broad topics) but the multiple choice is very tricky you need to read the book with a comb to get all of those correct.
Dr Hinchcliffe has a great passion for Political Science. He expects too much on written essays though. If you put in a ton of work into the class you shall do ok.

He's really not as bad as everyone says he is, but I still wouldn't recommend the class. The readings are heavy, boring, difficult, and unfortunately essential. If you study hard, are dedicated, and know your stuff you'll probably end up with a B+ or an A-. There are other PS 101 classes that are easier and more enjoyable though...

At the beginning of the semester I wanted to drop this class.  But as long as you do the textbook reading, study for the possible essay questions, and go to lecture, you can get a decent grade.  I got an A-, which is proof that he does give As.

I'm not sure why he gets such a bad rap. He's accessible and he challenges his students but wants them to succeed. It's true that his lectures are sometimes boring and there is a ridiculous amount of reading with which we did nothing, but overall a good introduction to American politics. For the most part, it's a pretty easy class.
i would advise taking another political science class. i learned a lot, but it takes up too much time.
I was an idiot for taking this stupid class. I could have chosen so many better PS classes to take that would have been easier and more worthwhile. My suggestions: do the online readings.
he is a nice professor and offers a lot of extra credit. it is a lot of work and it is important to keep up but worthwhile. Focus on the online readings he gives, they are key to the midterm

It is true that he teaches this class as if it were a 200 level, but just do what is asked and you'll do well.  He gives you three tries on quizzes and gives about ten extra credit chances, so getting an A is not hard.  He's friendly and approachable and gives you every opportunity to succeed.
Hincliffe has a twin..and his name is Satan.

I took this class as a Gen-Ed. Bad mistake.  As an engineering student i have enough on my plate than to have to read 2 hours each night for this class not to mention that his classes don't prepare you at all.  If you like learning based on reading, you might this class. Other than that, good luck.

Wow this class is horrible. I am not exaggerating but like seriously you might want to try another professor because this guy makes this class almost impossible. It is supposed to be a P.S. class but it seems like a 200 course. I just freaking took U.S. Gov (H) last year and i did very well in it. This guy makes me depressed.
P.S. the syllabus is 18 pages long!!! AND HE COPY-RIGHTED IT!!!

This guy is my adviser and after 3 tries, including a shouting match with the professor, he still doesn't know my name! I have zero idea what the hell he is talking about. He seems to be very biased. Only he would be pretentious enough to record himself explaining how to read a 18th century document and proceed to play it in front of the class.
The most compelling questions this man is capable of raising is how he was hired and why hasn't he been fired.

He likes to give you way more work than necessary, like having to prepare for 16 essays for the final exam.  This class takes a lot of work, but can be interesting when you are reading by yourself...not in class though.  Go to the TA's..they're the best source of help and the only way to understand what is going on.

Ill make this short. Horrible. The man is incapable of listening to anybody but himself.  Completely narrow minded and useless for help.  What's really disturbing is the fact that a professor with only 3 positive reviews of nearly 60 could not only avoid termination, but rise to become the director of undergrad polysci studies.
I actually liked him a lot.  He was really friendly and helpful if you wanted the help.  If you work semi-hard this class is a breeze.
On the first day of class he shook everyone's hand except mine. It made me feel uneasy about him and the class
Don't take this class! If this is not a required course, don't take it.  You have to give this class 100% of your time if you want an A or B. Not worth it.  Take another gen-ed or Prof.

Possibly the worst teacher ever. Useless in lectures. Useless in office hours. He's not a professor, just a staff member (undergrad adviser), and now I know why. The worst professor is better than him. Plus, he is not a great adviser either (but that is a different topic)! Take someone else. Anybody else is better.

You guys are all right. This class is unneccesarily difficult. How could any 100 level course be so hard? His class was a real pain in my neck. And when writing papers he has so many expectations and demands. Its his way or the highway. I STRONGY suggest taking someone else's PS 101 course.
Took this freshman year. The man is hard to understand, tests are bogus. If you plan on slacking off this really is not the course for you.
This class was much harder than the major specific PS 101 class that my friend took.  Joe expects a lot out of the students and doesn't feel that anyone should get an A.

I hardly need to add to what other people have said... but its all true. This class is nuts. He lectures you like a high school student... and then tests you like a grad student. Advice: Make sure that you understand the ridiculous amount of online reading before the exams...or, even better, take someone else's PS 101 class.

The professor is helpful--he expects more out of the students than just a memorization of the topics. The class is not difficult if effort is put into it~ just take it as it is. I had it my freshmen year and it basically served as a wake up call that college is not going to be a repeat of highschool. Go to office hours, TA's are useless.

Joseph Hinchliffe smacks with such blatant arrogance that he believes that, should someone (god forbid) get an A in his class, that it is too easy.  Maybe that is why answers on tests deviate by the most minute measure, and his lectures jump from topic to unrelated topic.  The workload is akin to law school, and even doing it won't assure you an A.

He's a nice person, but there is a lot of work for his class.  The examples he's shown us of A papers and D papers look almost the same to me.  I've always gotten straight A's and I can't figure out what he wants.  If you ask for help, he'll talk to you, but you still never really know what he wants.  He says his class is the most important 1 here.

Makes this class harder than it needs to be. Not very helpful when I went in to office hours. Definitely should not have gotten the grade I did for how hard I studied. I put a lot of time and effort into this class and still couldn't pull an A.  Sometimes he was just totally unfair.
Worst.  Professor.  Ever.
Never take that class.
Joe Hinchliffe sucks. I'm a straight A students and had to work my ass off to get a B. Stay away from this man. He is Satan.
The class is rediculous.  Understandable that there is a lot of information to cover in a short amount of time, but it is crazy the way that Joe teaches.  Very unreachable and the T.A.'s are NO help.

This class is hard because the essays/ papers are graded by different TAs.  They all grade differently, so there is no way of knowing what they want.  My friend had her bro. who is in law school here help with her papers- and she still got C's!!  He is not of much help even if you go in to ask for it, and it is hard for a 100 level
worst class ever.  DO NOT TAKE PS101 WITH PROF. HINCHLIFFE. YOU WILL REGRET IT!
He would've got 0's all across the board had they been offered.

What in the heck is the deal with the class.  We take online quizzes that count for 10% of our grade but we have to read one hundred pages of material to take it and he asks the most detailed questions.  This is introductory and he doesn't test over stuff he lectures on in class.  Stay away it at all possible.
Dont take any of his classes, total Pric!

The difficulty of the class is extremly high. I always thought 100 level courses were of reasonable difficuly. He proved me wrong. Do not under any circumstances enroll in this class unless you are opposed to a 4.0 GPA, because I guarantee you will not get it. He seemes to be a reasonable teacher, sort of, but this should be a 2-300 level course.

This class is hard for no reason, simply put. I have friends who take PS 101 with other professors and pass with an A doing nothing extra ordinary. I will not sleep tonight (Tuesday) because I have to start studying for a mid-term I have for this class on Friday! It sucks. Try Hoffman.

Joseph Hinchliffe sucks at life. He thinks he's hilarious, but his stories are awful. His workload is outrageous and I bust my butt doing his assignments, and have to sacrifice time on other classes and still do horrific. I hate this man.

Although he claims that he is always available and he is, the class is ridiculously impossible to get an A or B in.  It seems everyone is being screwed on his essays and midterms.  Don't take Political Science 101 because I used to like this subject, but now hate it.  Sorry Hinchliffe...
A.K.A. "The magician" because he takes a simplistic course and warps it into a sinister class that makes me want to give up on life.
i thinkn heneed to take chill

I spent hours studying and studying for the first midterm.. i thought i had aced it and i ended up doing terrible!! He is the WORST teacher i have ever had and i want to kill myself everytime i walk into his classroom..he is a tool and adds liberal propaganda into his lectures everyday
No Comments
He is a hard ass.  He thinks that he knows everything and his grading is unfair.  If you turn in a well written paper, expect to get a D or less.  I hate him.  Don't take the class.
more or less worthless
I agree with everyone else, he is really bad.  He is a huge tool, and even though all ps 100 levels are boring, this one just sucks.  Dont take it if he is the professor.

This guy is a complete tool. I see him often and every time have to restrain the urge to punch him in the face. Though I will say his loose interpretation of conventional morality makes him a good poli-sci prof. Boring class + heavy workload + humorless butterbean in a suit = instant cerebral death.

His classes are extremely boring and uneventful. He is more than willing to help you if you go in, but that doesn't make expectations any more clear.  Do NOT take this class unless you want to spend hours on papers only to end up with a grade that you could get coasting through any other class.

He wasn't that bad of a professor- note to all of you out there rating a 100-level poli sci class professor low because class is boring- all 100-level poli sci classes ARE boring!!  It has little to do with the prof.  I had him for a 300-level and he wasnt too bad....
Do not take his class unless you want to die...
he was so bad and really didnt care about anyone but him and his lunches at the Y. I hated him and his class and made me never want to be a politician.
HOrrible!!!
If you are going to take PS 101 make sure NOT to get joe...the class was horrible...and boring...and trust me he has no compassion!
terrible class
BAD NEWS!!!  Lectures were incredibly boring and he's not that fair with grading.  DON'T TAKE HIS CLASSES!
No Comments

JOE IS ABSENT MINDED.  HE WILL JUST GO OFF ON RANDOM THOUGHTS EVEN THOUGH HE BELIEVES HIS LECTURES ARE "RIBBITING" (YES HE REFERED TO THEM AS THAT).  HE TAKES HIS CLASS TOO SERIOUSLY AND ALTHOUGH I AM A POLI SCI MAJOR AND ENJOY POLITICS HE MAKES HIS CLASS MORE THAN IT SHOULD BE.
Very controversial

He is one of the most boring speakers I've ever seen. I once showed him what I was planning on writing my term paper on. He told me not to write about that topic and to write about something else. To make a long story short, I got a D on the paper & was told that the topic was too vague by the TAs!
I like him. Hes my advisor too, and I think he's really helpful and so is my T.A.  He's good about extending due dates.  He's a nice guy, really into poli sci...

No matter what you do, do not, under any circumstances, let this man know or think you are a Republican. He's very pleased with himself, moreso than anybody in the class is with him. He chooses the most oppressively dull textbooks I have ever seen.

Horrible. Has the condescending attitude of my worst teachers from Jr. High, is completely boring (I'd only come up from my crossword when he yelled), and seems to design his tests with the intent of 'tricking' students. Avoid.
If you like Poli Sci, you'll do fine in his class....if you don't - find another class.

Terrible advisor. When I told him my plans to go to law school, he tried to talk me out of it, probably because he hated being a lawyer and assumes the worst of everyone.  Very nice guy though, just don't listen to him.
As a prof. he is intense in class and gives vauge essay topics.  As an advisor he has been no help at all, even rude at times.
If I had one day to live, I would go to this class because it would seem like I had lived a whole life by the time his boring, vague lecture was over.  good intentions, horrible teacher.

He is also an advisor now.  He is a very nice guy, but he is somewhat of a dim bulb.  Make sure you know what all of the college requirements are and do not count on him to catch any errors; take all his "advice" with a grain of salt.
I concur with the previous statements towards Joe Hinchliffe.  Joe Blows
Horrible professor.  expects 400 level coursework in a 100 level course.  term papers are rediculous and ask too much.  the information is not hard, but he has the t.a's grade like nazis

This is the worst class i has ever been in. high school and college combined. though the ta was horrible as well, joe was not much better. his assignments were very vague and his reading assignments were far too excessive to expect of a college student.
Wow, he gives out way too much to read for homework. excited about what he does tho.
Not a good lecturer, and my worst class in college. The class is taught at a 9th grade level, yet one of the essays expected expert knowledge of the workings of Congrssional business and reports.
Made us to buy books to do his assignments. At least 3 books are written by him. How is this allowed? Grading criteria is unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Houston is very knowledgeable about investigative journalism. If this field interests you then this would be the professor to take. He isn't very great with grading and returning assignments though. A lot of the in-class assignments felt like busy work. Instead of buying the book, get the older version for free for the memos/reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His 315 class was the most expensive class I've ever taken. Makes you buy books you'll have to write essays on (that are impossible to find for free online), and 3 of them are his own books!!!! Dude couldn't even hook us up w a discount. Nice guy, but the book thing really made me mad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Horsfall has an unmatched passion for his Viking Mythology class. The course itself is easy, just stay on top of the readings (the first one is long and after that they are short), and have your notes open for midterm and final because it is open note.
