The material was also quite weak most of the actual practical concepts were not covered.

Very knowledgable, nice and patient professor, willing to answer all of your questions regarding lecture and homework.
Midterm 2 is hard since you are expected understand the theoretical proof in the lecture, but she did offer extra credit for this exam so that you will not get a very low grade as long as you follow the lecture.
Lectures were clear, concise, and recordings were available online. Extra credit was available on homework and formula sheets were allowed on exams.

The course materials were manageable until after midterm2. Following the derivations became challenging, as the instructor solves them like exam questions, writing each step out without explaining the reasons and does not check on if students follow. However, she is considerate, often extending homework deadlines.
the exam is really hard, with an average around 80 and 68 there are no curves on the final grade. the exam takes 200 out of 450 points(which nowhere on the syllabus says the grading proportion)
Hard to decipher, unfortunately, what she is talking about due to her accent. Lack of clear sentences, and sometimes takes a bit long on simple questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prepare to self study lectures are worthless.

Her lectures feel disjointed and are difficult to understand. She doesn't explain the topics very well, and I often left lecture feeling more confused. Lecture attendance is graded but it's only 1% of your grade, so I found reading the online textbook a more effective use of my time.
Doesn't teach well in class, and doesn't explain fundamental concepts at all. Not cooperative during office hours. Don't think, this person is interested much in teaching.

Hyungsoo Choi is a great professor; It made my experience with a really hard class, ECE 110, a breeze. Her explanations are informative and made me enjoy ECE110.

Choi's accent is present and makes her a bit harder to understand than other lecturers, but it's quite minor which is a relief. Her intuitive explanations overweight the slight accent.

She is somewhat hard to understand if you do not sit in the very front row. She also does not explain topics very well she mostly just does them and continues onwards. If you are having a hard time watch the other teachers lectures or actually go to them, plus go to office hours and the HKN reviews.
Dr. Choi is very nice and caring but her lectures just don't make sense. I have to teach everything to myself or go to office hours.

Honestly not the best lecturer and sometimes can move fast, but if you bear through it and do your best to understand the material, you will be just fine as the class itself is pretty easy. Homework isn't hard, midterms have retakes, final is mostly review questions.

Professor Choi was not that bad. Her lectures could be boring and sometimes it felt like she was overcomplicating the topics, but the class was not that bad. Furthermore, she answered questions well enough. Outside of the tedious lab section, ECE 110 is an easy course. It would be nice if she could explain things a little simpler, though.
She barely answered questions that students asked during lecture. She also always ran out of time. She also did not talk much about the midterms or criteria to retake them

Bring a pillow to class not for when you get sleepy but so that when she bores you into unconsciousness your head has something to slam into. Bring another pillow as well for when your first one falls asleep. If I hear someone say jero one more time Imma lose it. Horrible lecturer, overcomplicates everything.

To be honest, I couldn't understand her lectures at all so after about a month I stopped attending her online classes altogether. However, the class itself is pretty easy so I got by fine just doing the homework and reading the online textbook stuff.

Not gonna lie, I never showed up (why I didn't get an actual A) because the class is honestly pretty easy. When I did show up, I actually did enjoy her a lot. She has a bit of an accent, but it's nothing serious. I really enjoyed her energetic demeanor in a room full of dead students.(This is from someone who didn't use the lecture to learn)
She is hard to understand and makes easy concepts hard, try to go to Schmitz or Zhou if possible, both aren't bad. The class can be easy, just with her it wasn't.
Clumsy lecture style stops being endearing after the first week. Expect lectures to fall behind homework assignments, so you'll have to do most of the learning yourself.
She is confused with the concepts herself and that is not a good sign for any professor

Hard to understand. She makes simple concepts so complicated. Schmitz is a much better lecture for ECE 110, so get him if you can. Luckily a lot of the course note are posted online. Read them and teach yourself.
Very hard to understand. Simple concepts were extremely hard to understand. I ended up going to other lectures which were much more clear. Seems nice but cannot teach for her life.
Definitely avoid her section if possible, she might be a nice person but cannot teach or understand students questions.
She is very hard to understand. Her lectures are confusing when the material is quite easy. Expect to learn everything yourself.
She interrupted me 5 times before I could finish my question, and I never got my actual question answered. She's not a horrible teacher but I prefer Prof Schmitz's explanations of the material.
The hardest class I've ever taken. Her lecture was the only one that fit into my schedule, but it was the biggest mistake I've ever made. She's absolutely awful, avoid at all costs!
Do not take her class if you actually wanna learn about the subject you will not understand a word and it is a task to remain awake in her class.

She can't understand or answer questions well at all. She reads directly off the slides, and if you ask a questions she will just repeat what she just read. She seems like a nice woman, she just isn't a great teacher.

Although her lack of facility with English sometimes gets in the way, she really wants to help her students and appreciates if you visit her office hours. This is often better than asking a question during lecture, as she often does not understand questions from students right away.
Really struggles with answering students' questions.  Material itself is not that difficult, but I felt like I was completely teaching it to myself, even though I went to class every week.

Definitely NOT an engineering prof, nor does she make any claim to be. I could teach this class after taking it better than she could. Though her class was good comic relief. I got a good kick out of her volte-G drops and her jeroes. She also likes to call on students to explain difficult concepts that she's teaching (?). An UG TA could do better.

I didnt expect much teaching out of an ece teacher but she really lowered the bar. Yes, her english is broken but thats classic u of i engineering and nothing to complain about. She reads off her slides word for word and cant effectively answer questions in class.

She was awful. Really difficult to understand, and she accused me of not going to lecture when I went to her office hours (when I had been to all of her lectures). I recommend signing up for her section and going to Zhang's lectures, so you benefit from his teaching and her class's curve. The distributions can be nearly a litter grade different.
OMG!!! you don't wanna take her class.

She is a miserable excuse for someone that is supposed to teach. Her "jeroes"(zeros) are a constant annoyance.  She consistently doesn't understand questions asked about lecture slides and one day a student spent 10 min. trying to getting his point across to her but he decided to leave because she still couldn't understand. Avoid her at all costs.

The material is clear if you follow along and understand the concepts. Don't expect her to clarify if you have questions. Her accent, pronunciations, and odd wording give you something to smile about, and she's not hard to understand after you get used to her.

Not very effective teacher. She used slides on the overhead for everything and it wasnt clear what we had to know or not. Some lectures we learned material we didnt even have to know. Also shes not a very clear speaker so it can be hard to understand what shes saying. And she says jeero instead of zero. Get the other professor for this course
Horrible.  Shzerdo. (zero).  I actually woke up to go to 8 am to go to a different professor's lecture everyday.  People like this that make me want to leave this school.
No Comments

The one good thing I will say about this prof is that you learn new words like "fultage-ah" and "jero".  Very hard to understand also claims that you shouldn't take notes or pay attention to her and that you should just relax and watch.  The few that stay in lecture are never awake.

I defy anyone in her lecture section to stay awake for the full 50 minutes. Very difficult to understand, which makes the already difficult material even more complex. Don't attend the lectures - just do the online homework and refer to the book and you'll do fine. Exams can be very difficult, but this class gives final grades on a steep curve.

He was a fine teacher, and he provided plenty of materials for you to practice with. I find that if you were willing to put in the effort to do the homeworks instead of using ai and you do the practice tests to study you could fairly easily do well in the class. A little intimidating in lecture but if you  have questions you can ask after class.
tricky tom :[

Tom is retired now unfortunately :(.  Amazing lecturer- I wish I had him to explain material for me in every one of my classes here. Tricky Tom was tricky only if you didn't show up to lectures since all of the exceptions were very clearly given.
Thank god he's retiring.

Very upfront with students that if you don't practice/do the daily hw, you won't get a good grade. The daily hw is very reasonable, and its not for credit. Gives lots of extra practice. Responds to emails very quickly. Ask lots of questions. He will assume you understand it unless you tell him otherwise.
very hard class and not a good professor

He lives up to the name "tricky tom". The exams and quizzes were quite challenging and the exams are worth 600/800 points in the class. The class is very fast and the lectures weren't particularly helpful. The practice exams are essentially the exact same as the exams. Work hard, study the material and do the practice tests.
Yeah... i didn't like this style of class at all. there were not enough assignments (weird, right?) and it was honestly hard to get my grade up.

is definitely one of the hardest classes at this university. If you have to take it Hummel is your BEST bet. memorize how to do the test problems with the use of the old exams. practice about an hour or two per day. Lecture is highly pointless, use ai to walk you through problems. Watch online lectures from time to time. You're gonna get a B at bes
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I thought the class was fair, I definitely underestimated the class. Other than that, i would say his in person lectures are pretty faced and if you didn't read the chapters before lecturing you could get lost. However, he posts lectures online so you can go back. Overall, pretty chill guy and a very passible class.

Overall great professor that has engaging lectures. He calls himself "tricky Tom" -- which is true, he can be tricky and give hard exam questions. However he provides lots of past exam resources & lecture videos which is nice. The only thing that sucks is the final is ~40% of your grade. Good luck, understand concepts, and you will be fine.

Very interesting lectures, he explained things clearly but sometimes he went over concepts too fast. Preview the slides would be helpful to understand the lecture. However, be prepared for the exams, there is a reason for the name tricky Tom. The curves are very generous, do the practice exams and go to discussions then you'll be fine.

CHEM 102 is a difficult class. The exams are curved, but mainly toward lower scores, so if you get above an 85, there is barely a curve on top of that. I enjoyed his lectures, and he's really nice and caring. However, the exams are hard and 600/800 points in the class come from exams. Getting an A is difficult, but it is very much possible.

He calls himself Tricky Tom. His tests are 6/8ths of your overall grade and they are pretty difficult, luckily he provides past exams. It isn't too hard to "just pass" the class, but if you want an A, you are going to have to work for it. His lectures are quick and he isn't the best lecturer. This is very much a weed out class, but all Chem 102 is.

Lectures are not mandatory and videos from 2020 posted on canvas. Quizzes are take home, but are hard. Exams are difficult, but there are many practice exams. Exams are curved if you do really bad, but if you do alright, curve doesn't help much. I enjoyed Hummel's chem class, but the exams are difficult and count for 600/800 points of grade.

Hummel has decent lectures. He has a lot of resources for you to do good in the class like practice tests and lecture videos. However if you actually do good is a different story. His tests are much harder on average than other profs. And the curve only brings the average score up to a C. It wont really help you if you are a decent student with a B

Hummel's Chem 102 class is hard. I'm fairly certain exam grades are overall lower, especially because he does not allow for retakes unlike some of the other professors. His exams are notoriously hard.
But,
I understand the concepts very well because of his lectures. It's hard to keep up, but I learned a lot and feel prepared for future chem classes

Quizzes are hard but take home. No attendance but all material on exam will be in lecture so you should go. He makes the exams hard but you get 3 practice exams to study with before each exam so if you know how to do those you will succeed. Overall a tough class but is definitely the best CHEM 102 Professor at UIUC

Honestly The best choice of chem 102 professors at UIUC, quizzes are challenging but done at home so that's a plus. Additionally he gives 3 full length practice exams to use as study material for each exam. If you know how to do the practice exams, you will succeed on the exams, and all are multiple choice.

This class is not easy by any means, but Hummel was amazing at teaching it. His office hours are great, and he genuinely wants students to succeed. For midterms, he gives previous practice exams. As long as you can do the practice midterms and the textbook problems, you can do well in the class.
hes a meanie and his class is so hard

Class is just hard in general, but lectures are pretty helpful. his tests get curved heavily and are multiple choice so those are pretty nice. Has past tests to use for practice so just use those and you should be good in the class.
His exams are completely crazy, what he gives in lecture and what is asked during the tests seem to be two different worlds, just too hard.
This class has been alright. I'd suggest fully reading the text book. Also test will be curved and the class will be curved as well.

Hummel's lectures are adequate but he teaches the class in way that emphasizes what he calls "the best students", meaning that everyone else fails and definitely expects you to have fundamental knowledge of chemistry.

Great professor, gives lots of resources to succeed- you get out what you put in. Skip the packet that has his presentation slides, pre-watch the lectures instead on Canvas (a lot of work, but worth it). Also, utalize your TA, they're great.

Take advantage of office hours, he's super attentive there. And, exams are extremely important. Study hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is only a total of 800 points in the class. 700/800 of the points come from quizzes/tests/final exam and the rest is homework assignments. You need to study a lot in order to succeed in his class; however, if you do the course is manageable. The exam averages are really low, so the curves are generous.

Hummel is a very knowledgeable professor and if you go in with an open mind you can learn a lot from his lectures. His exams are however incredibly difficult, and without a chem background you do have to work really hard to get good marks, but in turn this class can make you a much better studier and learner.

I enjoyed his lectures as they were entertaining at times, but quite frankly he is not a competent lecturer. He vaguely explains concepts, leaving students to have to teach themselves. If you are going to take Hummel, I highly recommend taking it with merit. My TA quite literally is the reason for my good grade.

Hummel is a nice and funny dude, but the way he structures his class is completely unethical. Seems like he is trying to trick you rather than educate you. His tests are unnecessarily hard. If he didn't curve them, he would be fired instantly.
He's called "tricky Tom" for a reason :(

103 is a lab class, so work is done under a TA. Hummel put in grades in a timely fashion and is responsive by email. Overall, I found the class easy, but lab policies are strict. Precision and efficiency are key. Pre-lecture videos are mostly useless, skim for answers to prelabs. Postlabs can be difficult, so get answers checked at TA office hours.

While Hummel is very kind and funny in lectures, he is telling the truth when he says he writes the tests for the best students in the class. Rather than wanting everyone to succeed, it seems as though he only cares about asking difficult (multi-step MC) questions. He calls himself "Tricky Tom" and tells those who haven't taken AP Chem "good luck".

Began class scared since I hadn't taken chem since sophomore year of high school, but it was ok. You get what you put in. I recommend taking the time to make sure you understand homework material. Every test was fair and reflected provided practice tests, though the third one particularly tricky. work load is comparable to the average AP class.

He was good at explaining concepts during class, and this was enhanced by the variety of models he'd use and fun demos he'd do. He was also pretty funny and a good presence. I'd say watch out for trick questions on exams, and for the final that's worth 37.5% of your grade. I wish that some of the OWLv2 quiz questions were more fair, though.

Definitely would choose Hummel again over the other CHEM 102 professors. His exams can be difficult if you don't study but he provides a lot of helpful resources like practice exams and recorded lectures. The final is worth 37.5% so it's possible to maintain a good grade throughout the semester but mess it all up with the final.
He has recorded lectures posted online to review. The final is worth 37.5% of your grade, but he does curve all of the exams. The quiz questions were definitely unfair.

Lectures were easy to follow and also are all recorded online. Grade cutoffs at the end of the semester are often lowered, so it shouldn't be too hard to get the grade you want. Lots of practice exams on Canvas which made it easy to study, as well as practice problems in the textbook. Lots of resources from him so you really can't fail.

As far as I am aware, the best professor to take CHEM 102 under is Hummel. He oftentimes has the hardest exams and grades, but he is the best lecturer. Much of the grade is based on exams, but he does curve them.
Tests are difficult

Lives up to his nickname of Tricky Tom because he likes to put trick questions on the Exams and Quizzes. However he is really good and enjoyable lecturer that likes to challenge his students. His lectures can be kind of fast at times and will skill stuff when he feels like it but If you do the many textbook homework problems you will be fine.
Chill dude and he knows his stuff. Takenrhis class witout hesitation.

Hummel is such a funny guy but I never learned anything from his in-person lectures. He just goes super fast and I have to end up teaching myself with his video lectures and youtube. His exams were also insanely hard and full of trick questions.

Hummel's lectures can be fast-paced, but his recorded videos are really helpful. Exams are tough, but doing textbook problems and past exams, plus using tools like unstuckstudy ai, can make the class manageable. Overall, a challenging but worthwhile course.

He is a very kind and funny lecturer who wants everyone to succeed. While the in person lectures can be confusing, the video lectures are very helpful. The exams are rather difficult, but doing all of the textbook problems and past exams while going to the CLC at times should help. I would also advise taking CHEM 101 in the fall before this course.

Lectures were fast but were good introductions to the material. You definitely have to put in the work after the lecture to actually understand what's happening in the class. Assigned textbook readings were pointless for me personally because practicing the HW problems and past exams was more helpful for exams (75% of your grade)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hummel makes it very clear from the beginning of the class that you're not actually meant to succeed. In his own words, his exams are "written for the best student in the class". Exams are insanely hard, with difficult lectures...HOWEVER, I don't know what this man just did, but he finessed everyone's final grade and moved it up...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His in person lectures are very fast and overwhelming. I recommend his recorded lectures. They are amazing and if you understand each problem he does on those lectures, you will be set for the homework, quizzes, and tests. Tests are tough but doable, although I am a fast test taker and almost always used all the time given. tough class, good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hummel is a good educator, he has been here for a while so he knows the ropes. His class is difficult for people that chemistry doesn't come easy to. I have to study a LOT in order just to get a 60, but thats just maybe me. MAKE SURE YOU DO ALL YOUR HOMEWORK, it goes a long way. His curves are generous but only if people score low.

Hummel is a pretty good professor. Offers plenty of resources outside of class and has all of his lectures posted in Lon Capa. His tests can be a bit tricky sometimes and he only offers an hour and a half for them (which sucks because you end up guessing on some questions). Most of the topics are pretty straight-forward and lecture is actually fun.

Hummel's a funny guy and knows what he's talking about, it's just the way he presents the material that left me SO confused. He curves his exams like crazy, but I think a professor shouldn't have to do that. They need to actually teach in a way their students can understand. Watching his lecture videos is much more effective instead of going...

lectures are horrible and unhelpful. he goes too fast to take notes and goes over examples more than lectures on content. watching the online lectures is more helpful than going. he loves trick questions and exams are insanely hard, but generously curved. exams and quizzes make up most of your grade. curves save the class

This class forced me to change my major. I took this class twice and still was not able to earn above an D+ in the course. Hummel is not clear in his lectures and exams are extremely hard.The second time i took this class i failed by a couple points and was told  could do nothing. He set me back graduating an entire year.
HARD class without AP Chem experience

Honestly a super chill and funny dude, very nice guy. He lets you out of lectures early a lot. Very hard tests, but he gives previous exams. Also, it felt like a lot of his lectures were just too fast and made no sense. Sometimes I would understand his lectures, but half the time I would be totally lost afterwards. Lots of homework as well.

Hummel is an amazing lecturer if you put in the work to further understand & practice the topics. This class was extremely hard for me at first until I developed a growth mindset & better studying habits. I had a B before the last exam & final and I managed to get it up to an A. Just be ready to put in more work than any high school class(even APs)
Exams are almost all of your grade but if you do ALL of the homework to prepare you will be fine. He gives you a lot of resources and past exams to study which help a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer and real helpful in office hou

Professor Hummel is a great teacher, but his test are extremely difficult. Make sure to do all the homework and practice A LOT or you will not succeed in his class. To prep for his test redo all homework and redo the 2 quizzes before the test along with his previous exams until you know how to do every question.

Tricky exam questions and lots of homework, but explains everything thoroughly and gives lots of examples in lecture. Grade is basically just 3 tests and the final, so reviewing past exams and important concepts is important. Fair grader, curves exams. Overall nice guy and good professor, just gives hard exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor does a great job explaining content during lectures. While some aspects of the class are tricky or challenging, Mr. Hummel clarifies what content will be on exams and how to review. Do well in the class by attending lectures, discussions, and submitting your quizzes on time. Exams received a curve.

Attendance was not mandatory and all his lectures are posted on LonCapa, so missing a lecture was no biggie. Lots and lots of studying required it order to do well on exams. He gives you lots of resources to study/prepare for exams (past exams, text homework problems, quizzes, etc), but some trick questions do pop up. Exams are curved generously.

He seemed really nice and funny but he was horrible at explaining concepts. Chemistry was never hard for me until this class. He just told us information but didn't really explain it. He also rushed through every single lecture and would almost always end early anyway, so it was difficult to keep up with lecture in class.

Absolutely loved Hummel. His lectures were easy to understand, engaging, and he was funny. He genuinely cares about his students and makes sure to answer everyone's questions. Only downside is that his exams are relatively hard as he writes them for the raw average to be around a 65%, but he grades all the exams on a pretty generous curve.

Professor Hummel is simply not good. You can tell he just goes through the motions during lecture. He doesn't teach the subject matter well, he only regurgitates information and does a rather disappointing job of explaining it. I even took 2 years of Chem in high school, and this class was still difficult.

DID MY GIRL CAR*** DIRTY!!!! he's a harsh grader and doesn't explain the concepts very well, I show up to every single lecture take notes go to office hours but that doesn't help. Don't waste your time take Kelley's instead!

Professor Hummel is really nice and honestly pretty funny. He makes learning chemistry enjoyable and answers your emails/questions well. He does give a lot of work to do but it honestly helps you do better in the class. I liked watching his lectures online, he gives good descriptions and takes you through problems well.
TOOOOOOO MUCH QUIZS and HOMEWORK, and none of them can be dropped.

Professor Hummel is a fun professor, and in my opinion the best professor to take CHEM 102 with. CHEM 102 is a heavy course, which is why the class is homework and quiz heavy, but if you work honestly, then getting an A is doable.
Hard class overall but he teaches very well and explains everything clearly

Very test-heavy course with the final worth almost 40% of your grade. Class is doable if you keep up with the course, but it is easy to fall behind. Attendance is not mandatory but you will fail without it. Great lecturer but hard tests.

From what I have heard from other students chem 102 is generally a hard class. Hummel graded hard, and the practice tests did not help. He would rush through lectures, and allow little time for practice problems. His tests had extremely low averages however his curves were generous. He is a funny guy, but I am glad I don't need to see him again.

Lecture is ok and discussions vary wildly based on your TA. With the exception of extended time, I've heard many stories and experienced him not following educational plans and being rude to students with disabilities.

Lecture is not required but I'd recommend attending--especially if you don't want to learn from a textbook. I learned the most from the discussion section (depends on TA because he has no disc. curriculum). The tests were difficult, so finish Lon Capa and text hws ALWAYS. Go to the CLC when you need help--it was so helpfuful. Quizzes are open note.

PLEASE get all the points you can through lon capa, quizzes, text homework. You have to stay on top of this class from day 1. Very intense but doable to get an A. Attend all the discussions and lectures, even though no attendance. Final and midterms consist of 600/800 points so you have to study a lot. Curves all the exams though so kinda helpful.

For chem 102 i believe hummel is the best option. he is very nice and understanding that the class is hard. he is called tricky tom for a reason though (his exams are very hard but if you do the homework and study its possible to pass). I recommend to go to the chemistry learning center as frequent as possible.
How does genius Tom know this? Asks Tricky Tom
This class is very difficult, but with enough effort, you can succeed in it. The tests are super hard, but they are usually curved a lot. Just make sure to study and keep up with lectures
Tons of homework, manageable but requires a lot of effort. Lectures are fun and informative, but you will need to do a ton of learning individually (preferably before the lecture).

I took this class in SP '21. Looking back, Hummel gave you everything you needed to succeed in the class with hard work (lectures + practice tests + textbook for practice). To the freshman: this is a really great opportunity to hone your study skills. Effort is important, but this class taught me that a bunch of effort doesn't beat studying smart.

Hummel's lectures were well structured and he attempts to explain everything in easy terms. There is a copious amount of homework and the final is weighed heavily (which can be an advantage). The TA's were helpful and went over lecture content step by step. Course can definitely be difficult for those with little knowledge of chem so take 101.

1. very clear, funny and effective lecture, might be the best lecture I ever take at UIUC
2. exam are tricky, but prepares well can always help you get through
3. appropriate workload

Pros: 
1. Lecture is pretty darn straightforward and very effective
2. Offer curves for exams and overall letter grade (I got A+ with 95%)
3. Exams are predictable
Cons:
1. Lecture heavy (~1h for each lec, 2 per week)
2. A lot of homework (~25 questions per lecture)
3. You will allocate ~8h per week if you want to get an A (materials are hard)

Pre-recorded online lectures are great, he's good at explaining the material and giving helpful examples. Homework is good practice for the exams and helps improve understanding of the material. However, the exams are pretty difficult and require a lot of studying/practice. Also, almost your entire grade is based off of the 3 midterms and final.

This class is HARD.  Hummel is the best option for this class, take his online course. The lectures are all recorded and you can rewatch them. This class is very hard so make sure to rewatch his lectures.   Good luck!
Difficult class but he makes an attempt to teach you what you need to know and doesn't make it harder than it needs to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Will waste 20 minutes out of a lecture describing things that will not be on any homework question, quiz or test. Purposefully makes quiz and exam questions harder and even admits to it. Only way to do remotely good is to attend office hours, the Chemistry Learner Center (CLC) and other outside help seemingly every single day, on top of other class
Very long and boring lectures. Tests and quizzes are hard. He states that he purposely makes the questions hard.

Tom was a great lecturer, and all lectures were pre-recorded. Problem was that his lectures would sometimes be an hour long, twice a week, and it was hard to find time to watch them. His online homework has 99 attempts and the text homework has an answer key. My discussion wasn't mandatory attendance so I never went. EXAMS ARE SO HARD!!
In my limited experience the best lecturer out of all the CHEM 102 professors. Even if you don't have him take my advice and watch his lecture videos regularly
Tom's lectures give students clear explanation. And the exams are not really hard. All problems in exams are highly relevant to his lectures.

Lectures are pretty straight-forward and don't bother with the textbook. I found that what helped the most is his Office Hours, the practice exams, going over his Lon-Capa HW questions, and going to the Chemistry Learning Center. Please take advantage of these resources. If you put in the work and use the resources given, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hummel is a tough professor, especially if you come from high school Chemistry. The first few weeks are more of a review, but don't let that fool you into thinking that the whole first unit and beyond is a cake walk. Go to this office hours if you have questions, but also DO THE PRACTICE TESTS and understand the concepts you are unsure about.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Hummel's lectures were easy to follow and straight to the point. He is also always available for help at office hours. Make sure to always do the practice exams, they help a lot on the exams, which can be tricky sometimes. He also only grades the evens for assigned homework, but do the odds too, practice is the best way to succeed.

Chem102 is difficult at UIUC regardless, but that doesn't excuse Hummel's poor performance. His lectures are long, uninteresting and often unhelpful. I relied on my TA and outside sources heavily for this course. He's a nice guy and responds fairly quickly. His 3hr exams though, are a nightmare and a half.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Earned his name as Tricky Tom. Gave himself the nickname. If you took 101 you have a head start for the first half. Quizzes are similar to Lon Cape HW. Exams are difficult but curved, and since the quiz avg was lower he curved that too. If you want an A you'll need to put in the work-- office hours, CLC, practice exams, etc. Merit helps a lot.

I loved Hummel as a professor and the first half of the class was pretty doable. Beware of the final though, it was much harder than past exams and lowered my grade significantly from where it was prior.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Wish you luck. If you did not get an A in AP chem, you will struggle. Quizzes are difficult. However, he is such a plug for curving the quizzes, exams, and final. Go to his office hours, he should answer your emails within 2 days. Funny guy, chuckled a bit during his lectures. DO THE READING IF YOU WANT TO PASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Chem 102 is difficult, and frankly wont be easy with any professor. However, Hummel is pretty good. He seemed nice. His exams are difficult, pls take the practice exams he provides, they are awesome indicators. Also, he is tricky. but pro tip: in chem there are A LOT of exceptions, things that seem insignificant. Learn those, he puts them on exams
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hummel is a really good lecturer. The problem is that the quizzes and tests are very difficult problems, so you have to think outside of the box. I did all of the homework with an A+, but got to the quizzes and tests and averaged a C. Very difficult tests.

It is well known that CHEM102 is one of the ultimate weed out classes at UIUC, so no matter who you have the course is going to be hard. Professor Hummel was a great lecturer, you just need to really push yourself to stay on top of the material and study hard for all of his quizzes and hour exams, because he is known as Tricky Tom, and he knows it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As an online class, Professor Hummel's lecture videos were very informative and had great examples. He provides practice exams before the real exam and the questions are very similar. Exams and quizzes can be scaled if the average is lower than expected for him. The 3 exams + the final are about 70% of your grade.

I mean look no chemistry class is going to be easy so if youre looking for a good teacher, you'll be looking forever. I did not expect the tests and exams to be as difficult as they were so I was in for quite a shock. Honestly, having in person classes would make a huge difference. Seems like a great guy who teaches a difficult class.

Hummel is tricky. BUT his teaching style is absolutely phenomenal. His online lectures are straightforward and sometimes he cracks jokes. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! I did not start going until after the second exam and I got an A on the last two quizzes and 3rd exam. You gotta work in this class. But it all pays off. You will be sooo proud of yourself!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Exams are really tough so make sure do to all of the homework problems plus some of the optional ones to make sure you understand everything. Discussion attendance is not mandatory but I suggest that you show up anyway to ask questions about stuff you don't know. For me personally, reading the textbook info before lecture made everything easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Know how to specifically answer questions on the practice exams bc the exam questions are similar. CAREFULLY READ the questions (since he's tricky) & know what's in the notebook since everything is considered fair game. The test are curved & they're a major portion of your grade, so try to study as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tricky Tom tries to be nice to us and that really means a lot. However, he isn't the best at explaining topics and generally assumes that everyone understands his specific method of solving problems. Holds review sessions and does care enough to change his tests for the semester of students taking it at the time. He rounds, curves, etc. Good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nickname is Tricky Tom, and he knows it. Learn and understand the small things, especially the things learned at the start of the unit, you tend to forget those come test time. Don't skip, you'll fail. Take notes, along with what he gives in the handout book. Record lecture or write in detail how he solves problems and his logic for test questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dont take him unless you have too. Nice guy but makes his exams unnecessarily hard - makes them for the BEST students in the class. I consider myself a pretty hardworking student and I dedicated hours to this class. Ended up with a B- and honestly proud of that.

Although Hummel is a nice guy, he is not a very good lecturer. He doesn't explain concepts well, and when he's doing practice problems he doesn't explain it well either. If anything, I learn more in discussion than lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dont be stupid and miss lecture. He gives out test questions in lecture. His tests arent bad at all if u do the work in his class. He honestly has a bad rep cuz people dont want to study. Hes a nice professor. And YES he is TRICKY TOM but if u do the practice tests U CAN CONQUER THIS BEAST.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. Course notes/booklet is very concise and teaches you chemistry well. Exams require studying and practice, but are very fair and representative of HW and lecture material. However, the curves also really suck on them, as anything about 85% and above has virtually no curve, while you need a total score in the 90s to recieve an A.

Hummel is an amazing lecturer. The class is pretty fast-paced but he is always willing to meet with students outside of office hours. Tests can be hard to do super well on because of tricky wording, but he gives you everything you need to do well. The class is unnecessarily difficult but if you put in the work it's very possible to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice and interesting Prof though making tricking multiple choice exams. Even if you know everything you may still get an unpleasant grade in exams. He scales exams with some normal-distribution-like ways so if you score a 20 you get bumped to somewhere near 50 or 60, but if you score like a 88 or 91 there's very little curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Hummel legit made me like chemistry. I struggled in my high school chemistry classes and hated the subject because of my awful teachers. He was different, taught with enthusiasm and managed to fit so much material in 50 minute lectures without making it feel rushed. Still requires a lot of work, and remember to do every HW assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: TRICKY TOM BACK AT IT AGAIN WITH THE TRICKIEST TESTS POSSIBLE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He moves through the material quickly, but will explain most things clearly. He gives a lot of practice exams, and if you do those and the practice problems in the book, you can do well on the exams.

Hummel lives up to his name Tricky Tom, but he's not as bad as most people say. Everything in the class is easy except for the tests. The tests are written specifically to make you believe you have the right answer, but in reality you don't. Go to lecture every day because he covers a lot of material the TA's don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Hummel. He was a fair teacher in terms of laying out what was expected in his class. Lectures are very interesting. This class was a challenge, but I was in AP Chem so be prepared to work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: "Tricky Tom" is known for his tough exams but they are not impossible. If you don't get something that went on in lecture get help at the CLC, his office hours, or your TA's office hours. All his exams are scaled which helps a lot. Homework is worth a lot in the end so as long as you do that you shouldn't do that bad. GO TO LECTURE, handouts book>
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Hummel is actually a pretty good teacher especially one on one. Go to office hours even if you only have one question. Honestly, I don't think the material is all that difficult, but the exam questions can be unreasonably hard. You need to go to every single lecture and discussion if you want to do well in this class. Study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Classes are interesting with experiments and jokes. Clear about what will be tested. Tests are easy as long as you are clear about the concepts (knowing why instead of only understanding the formulas and calculations). Answers questions super clearly if you go to him after class. Rated poorly only because people who don't study much suffers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Thought Tom was rude and just an overall poor professor. Tom was definitely the worst professor I had during all my years at Illinois. Wouldn't recommend Tom to anyone, he's just a nightmare to say the least. I regret every moment I spent in that class. If I could go back I definitely would have taken the class with any other professor except Tom.
Decent professor. exists very well. has not phased out of class. always there to hand out money (so make sure to answer questions).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He provided lots of help to students including answering e-mails at any time, providing past exams... But his tests are little bit hard. Need to study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: From what I heard about other chem 102 professors, Hummel is definitely a solid choice. He goes over example problems consistently in lecture and has cool demos. Although there is a fair amount of work for the class, he's good at teaching it!

Honestly, it wasn't bad. Hourly exams are same difficulty levels as past hourly exams. so get them done ahead of time. Also, do all homework questions (including recommended ones). Do homework after lecture. don't slack off.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very test heavy class, which is very unfair  considering his tests are both tricky as well as low on time.  If chemistry is a weak spot for you, try to take 101 first.  When you get to this class, make sure you take a couple hours out of your week to just revise, this class will kick your ass if you don't put in work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Hummel was really great.  As long as you do the practice exams and the bookwork, you'll be okay.
Do NOT take his Chem102 class if you do not have a strong chem background. By far the most difficult Chem102 professor.

If you put in the effort and show up to lectures and discussions, you'll do fine. Buy the purple book because the practice exams are very useful for studying. The handouts book is also very useful for taking daily notes. For the final exam, go back to correct your old hour exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tricky Tom knows his stuff, but his class is "his way or the highway." Exams aren't impossible, but not super straight forward (combination of multiple topics in one question. He really makes you work for it and I respect him for that. Try to correct him in class and if you are right you can make a small profit. Overall good experience.

Very good professor. Explains things in a very clear and simple manner. He has a good attitude and can be pretty funny in class. This class is very test heavy, the three midterms and final count for 75% of the class and yes the tests are hard. However, there is a decent curve on all tests.  Would recommend.
Great professor, fun guy, tests are hard. He really makes you put in the effort. He truly is "Tricky Tom".

Tests are a little tricky but not a problem after going through the practice versions. Prof. Hummel is especially helpful when you have specific question. He will make it short and clear and explain to you patiently if you're still confused. And you can make money by correcting his mistakes during the lecture. Nice professor, enjoyed his class.
Easy class,

I really enjoyed having Tricky Tom. His class wasn't exactly easy but he is an excellent teacher. Grade is very test-oriented and you won't get a good one unless you prepare for his exams, which are...... tricky. There is always a time crunch for these exams but this does not take anything away from his actual teaching ability. Take him if able to.

His tests are very challenging. You must prepare yourself by reading the material and doing a ton of practice problems from the book. I also did past quizzes which can be found at the chemistry learning center on campus.
Tough class. Need to pay close attention in lectures. Definitely go to discussion and ask questions.

Professor Hummel is a funny guy and an efficient, effective lecturer. His exams are a bit longer than the other professors' exams and perhaps involve more exceptions than normal (hence the name "Tricky Tom"). Nevertheless, if you are going to lecture, doing the homework problems, and studying for exams, you'll do well (he adjusts grade cutoffs).

Hummel is very difficult. Because of the large lecture, help needs to be sought out personally. But Hummel gives it if you ask. His TAs were not helpful. His exams are difficult: more questions than any other CHEM 102 professor's tests and less time to complete them. It almost always is a race to finish before running out of time. AVOID IF POSSIBLE
Pretty fair. You get out what you put in.

Great lecturer. However, there's a reason his nickname is Tricky Tom, and that is because the tests are really hard. However, if you go to his office hours, he is there for you and will help you succeed.
Very passionate teacher. Always gives specific answers to questions. Treats students with respect.

If you need help understanding a topic, go to Office Hours. He is very good and willing to explain the little details to you then, which may not have been possible during the lecture. He like to blow stuff up and do chemistry experiments so that was always really fun to watch. DO ALL THE TEXT BOOK HOMEWORK AND PRACTICE EXAMS QUESTIONS!

So-so section. Since CHEM102 is just a elementary course. Just consider the clarity and performance of him. It's not bad. Textbook is required because there are writing assignments based on textbook on his section.
He does a really good job of answering questions that anybody has during the lectures
His lecture is really amazing.

I loved having Tricky Tom! He's an amazing lecturer and really knows his stuff, but the tests are kinda tough. I took this class over the summer so the class load was also crazy fast. He definitely wants you to learn, and will answer any questions you have, and will even give out money to those who catch mistakes or answer questions in lecture.

I probably skipped his lecture once a week and still ended up with an A. Hummel is a pretty good lecturer but Tim my TA was also really good at explaining so I learn from both of them. Hummel gives me a glimpse of what the topic is about and Tim explains the topic during discussion.  Overall, Hummel is a great professor! His explanations are clear.

Tom Hummel is a great, great lecturer who has a clear understanding of chemistry. Unfortunately, his tests are very hard. He is very approachable if you have questions, and he's pretty funny, which makes lectures interesting. The class was curved quite a bit, so the impossible tests aren't too bad, but they are hard. Not much homework, so study.

Tom was a great lecturer. He obviously knew his material, and he was always there for his students. Yeah, his exams can be tough. However, the format of these exams are almost identical to the practice exams and the homework problems. If you really practice those two materials, you should be set for the exams.
He takes pride in having low exam averages and actively tries to trick students with his exam questions.

Hummel is a tale of two extremes in ways. He's a good lecturer.  He speaks clearly, and is generally liked by the student. He also has a self-imposed nickname of "Tricky Tom" due to his love and affinity for throwing a few curveballs in his exams. If you study the practice tests, he's definitely a manageable professor.

Tom was a very nice professor who was willing to help, but his class was very difficult. His tests are hard, and require a deep understanding of the lectures. Pay attention in class and ask lots of questions!

I loved having Tom. Lecture are simple and fast. His exams can be hard but most of the questions already showed up in past exams and in lectures. He is very humble and respectful of his students; great guy and a great professor.
He's very knowledgeable and wants you to learn, but the tests are unnecessarily difficult. He is very passionate, so lectures are educational and interesting.
Very difficult tests, but he teaches well.

Unless you REALLY like chemistry, I suggest taking Chem 102 with someone else. A good teacher, but expects you to have a strong passion for chemistry even though most people are taking the class to fulfill some requirement in their major. Good teacher, but tests are some of the hardest I've ever taken.

A good lecturer, but makes the exams like he is a mad man. Do not take this class if u want A good grade. It's like makes the test just to make u get a bad grade in the class. In general bad teaching philosophy.

I think Professor is funny and he is a great teacher. If you are interested in chemistry and you want to test whether you have a great foundation in chemistry before, I think you should take his class. I know that the quiz and the tests are obviously hard, but if you could make it through, it will be great chance to have a solid chemistry foundatio
Really good professor. Exams are a little bit hard but if you work hard and do practice exams you can get good grades.

He is an awesome lecturer. Even though the class moves at a fast pace (no matter whose class you're in) his lectures are comprehensive and interesting. Also, attending lecture is important unless you're a genius.  And do your homework.
The class is difficult but by going to class you will be sorted
Tough exams
Very helpful and wants to help students learn material. However, tests are a beotch. Make sure to use practice exams and do ALL of the homework assigned, no matter if it's graded or not.
Don't take this class unless you absolutely need to. Screwed over my GPA.

The tests were terrible. I'm not a chem major and I guess I'm not very good at chem, but I studied a decent amount. I always felt like it was a guessing game and I just hoped I guessed more right answers than everyone else.

How to get an A in chem 102 w Hummel: do most homework problems BEFORE lecture and go over them again before quizzes, go to every lecture as he gives hints on exam content, do every old hour exam available (including older ones in the chem learning center), go to office hours consistently. all gen chem classes are hard regardless of the prof

tried deliberately to trick you on tests. tests are written to be hard, not to check that you understand most of the material. if you don't know every trick and exception, you will not do well on the tests. lectures were fast and very confusing; he just does calculations on the board and expects you to follow them. studied a lot, idk if i'll pass
I'd say he was your average professor. Difficult, but not overly so. I think he was very effective at teaching in lectures. His exams and quizzes were a bit harder than they needed to be.

Very difficult class to come away with an A compared to every other chem class. Tests are not a true test of knowledge but rather a test to overcome his unknown tricks to throw off students. "Past exams" are not indicative of current ones. I got an A raw score on practice exams but low B's on current exams. He WANTS to trick you. Take another prof.

I don't know how he has a good rating. He make Chem much harder than it has to be in order to curve it however he wants. When the average on the exams is barely over 50% you're doing something wrong. Everyone that I have this with is miserable because of him, and when compared to other Chem 102 classes, the exams seem impossible. Don't take him.
Get the practice exam book. The actual exams are very similar.

His nickname may be Tricky Tom, but I definitely think he was the best CHEM 102 professor to have. The tests are very difficult, but are subsequently curved. If you have not taken AP Chem, you need to put in effort to do well. It's not impossible, but don't go thinking you can coast through the class. Great Professor. Funny guy too!
AWESOME. He's hard, but it's so worth it. Best teacher I've had

He's a good professor, but his tests can be difficult (even for a student that did well in AP Chem). There are a lot of subtle things he does to make the exams tricky (earning him the nick name, "Tricky Tom").  However, paying attention in class, doing the homework, and studying by looking over lecture notes and taking past exams is very helpful.

The tests are very rushed but practicing with the past exams is the best thing you can do.  Tom is a little fast in lecture but he is a really nice guy who wants you to do well.  Make an effort to see him during his office hours.

Hummel is a really great professor. People always complain about how difficult his class is, but if you put in the effort, you will do well. Do ALL of the homework problems, not just the evens. Go to his office hours! He genuinely wants to help students and doesn't "dumb down" the material. Class is hard, but I learned so much in just one semester.

He's very smart and knows his field very well. They call him Tricky Tom for a reason though, and you have to be proficient at the material as exams are pretty difficult. Usually, if you can figure out what each question is testing, you should be good. My advice -PRACTICE! Do ALL practice problems and past exams! Many questions are similar.

This was easily the hardest class I had all semester, but it was my mistake that I didn't treat it as such! If you are looking for an easy time with Tricky Tom then you are mistaken! Take your homework seriously and STUDYSTUDYSTUDY, then you have a good chance with his tests. And know your stuff well. He really is tricky!

Very good professor. It is very clear that he knows his stuff and is always helpful to students. Encourages students to ask questions in lecture and overall wants to see his students learn and do very well. I definitely recommend u to take him as your professor

Tricky Tom, as he refers to himself, was very difficult. I have never had to work harder in a class. I even had to hire a tutor. That being said, compared to other teachers he was the best of choice. He works with you throughout the semester and scales everything. Because of that, I brought by C- to a B by the end of the semester.

It's a class worth your time. As long as you keep with with his lectures and the discussion classes on a regular basis, it's a straight forward A for this class. He's very helpful when it comes to his office hours. Quizes, Hour Exams and Finals are curved reasonably.

Tricky Tom was probably the best professor I had all semester. He goes through material quickly at times, so I personally found it helpful to read the book before attending lecture. The entire class is curved, which makes his harder tests much more reasonable.

He is so enthusiastic about chemistry, and I respect him for trying so hard to motivate his students. However, the tests were so extremely hard. If you can't do the hardest homework problems in the book, then you are bound to struggle in this class. Luckily he curves the tests and quizzes. I wished I would have learned more.
Easy

Probably the best teacher I have had while at this university. Everyone says he is super hard, but it pays off in the end because you are able to grab a firm understanding of Chemistry, which really helps if you have to continue taking Chemistry for a major or minor. :) Choose him and you will be fine. The tests are curved, so that's always nice.

He's passionate about chemistry but too fast in lectures. He'll answer questions without being condescending. He'll even give students money for catching mistakes in class. Exams are impossible and test your rate of completion, not what you actually know.  Exams will be 35 questions with 19 difficult calculations in 70 minutes. You must study!

Professor Hummel is what everyone calls him. He even nickname's himself "Tricky Tom." However, he is one of the best professors I have ever had. His exams are made for the top chem students. However, if you do all the work, it is possible to succeed in his class. Plus, he preforms in lecture demonstrations!

Tom Hummel is many things but easy is not one of them. He is a very competent lecturer, and if you use the Chem learning center, and his office hours, it is possible to succeed is his course. You really have to work for an A, because his exams are very difficult. You will learn alot because you must master the material to perform on the tests.

His lecture is clear. However he tends to go a bit faster. Discussion section is the most helpful if you take his section. Exams are hard and mainly dominated with thinking questions. A if you are expert of all the theories and fast in thinking to solve multiple tricky MCQs. However his class has a curve around 68%. Firm foundation -> choose him.

If you have him, GET OUT. He's an average lecturer, but his tests are VERY HARD. He calls himself tricky tom, and there is a reason why he does. It is nice if you do all the questions assigned for homework because he did write the questions for the book, but it's not worth it.

Hummell was a great lecturer if you read prior to attending class. Keeping up with readings, paying attention in lecture, and doing homework and practice exams should get you a good grade. The exams are only tricky if you don't do the suggested problems and practice exams.

Prof. Hummel definitely deserves the title "Tricky Tom." His exams were very challenging because of hard problems and a short amount of time. However, he was extremely helpful, nice, and good at listening during office hours. If you work hard, you can get a good grade in his class
His tests were very hard, and pushed the time limit frequently. You will learn a lot, however, if you don't want to work for your grade, don't take this professor!
Way too hard, you'll learn a hell of a lot compared to the other teachers but the gpa drop is brutal. His tests are pointlessly hard.

If you're looking for the easiest professor, don't go for Hummel. However Hummel will get you interested in Chem. His Exam questions are tough, its all about understanding the material and applying it to questions you might not have even seen. If you don't like Chem even just a little, I wouldn't recommend  taking Chem with him.
Yes his tests are hard, but you learn so much in his class. Go to his office hours; he's extremely helpful! He's also a character in the classroom.
His tests are hard, but in reality, I learned so much in his class. Office Hours are also very helpful because it is one on one help. Best Chem Teacher I ever Had!
Hard as heck, if you get him, get out now. the exams are impossible.

He's a pretty good teacher. I hate chemistry, but he at least made it less annoying than it could have been. He's blunt about stuff and he'll help you out if you ask. Tests are hard, but if you have a good TA, you can figure out at least how to pass them.

Great professor, but somewhat difficult. Makes lectures entertaining and gives out dollar bills, which is an incentive to paying attention. His lecture notes are helpful and the past hour exams are indicative of exam type questions he puts on his tests.
Difficult professor, but tries to make class fun. He is actually pretty funny. Doing the homework and studying regularly will get you a decent grade. Never slack off! It gets hard at the end.
He goes deep into new materials very quickly. Exams are very detailed. I suggest you to have a decent background of chemistry before taking his class.
awful professor, he is funny but i ended up getting a C in the class because he makes everything so confusing. save yourself the stress and take it with a different professor

He is a difficult professor, however he makes class at least fun.  Cracks a lot of jokes which lightens the mood and keeps you interested in the class.  Do the homework assignments and study and you will do well. I would recommend buying his lecture notes, they are very helpful.

wayyyy too difficult of a class for being a 100 level course. I attended every lecture and discussion, and i'm still struggling. Tom is really nice and funny, but his tests are RIDICULOUS. he gives a lot of homework too, which is helpful but excessive. i would not recommend him as a professor.
helpful and clear. difficulty level was quite standard. fun class even if you don't like chemistry very much

Professor Hummel is a great professor and I enjoyed him a lot. His exams aren't necessarily hard, but very detailed (most would say tricky). Well, that's why he nicknamed himself tricky Tom. Fair curves on exams and quizzes. Lon-capa based homework not too bad. Overall, a good and fair professor.

Was an enjoyable lecture, not required. I had taken AP Chemistry, so that made the class much easier. It's pretty much all in the notes packet that he puts on sale, then goes over during the lecture. TA's are helpful and there is a quiz every week. Tests aren't bad, but he likes to pay attention to small details.

Tom has an enjoyable lecture, granted im a chem major, but i think he is funny. He presents material well and has nice notes available for purchase (be sure to purchase). They call him tricky tom for a reason, he pushes your knowledge on the exams and loves exceptions and small details. Read, study book work and be prepared for exam style.
I loved Tom! This Chem class is actually very fun for me. Tests can be tricky, but not HARD per se. Recommanded :)
Stopped going to lecture two weeks in.  A-
Make sure your TA doesn't suck and you'll do fine.

He is a good professor and generally lets you know what he is looking for on tests. He writes challenging tests, and you never know how you do on the quizzes until after he scales them, but it works out being fare to all discussion sections.
He explains things well and he is humorous! Good professor. I like him :>

Probably one of the easier CHEM 102 professors. Explains things well, and puts a small curve on exams. Puts some sort of modified bell curve on quizzes, though not too sure how that is yet. Knows what he's talking about, and review sessions are helpful.
I hate him. I got an A in Orgo, and a B in HIS class? NOT POSSIBLE. And yes, I worked really hard in his class, so my laziness isn't the issue here. It's HIM.
Some people complain about how tricky he is but if you just keep up with your work, it's not hard at all.  He's a great teacher.

Tricky Tom is named so for a reason... his tests are unbearable, stressful, and downright impossible. Attending lectures is almost pointless because I have so much difficulty paying attention to him. Some of his TAs are low quality too.
Avoid at all costs.  "Tricky Tom" takes pride in writing the most difficult, tricky exam possible.  His tests are harder than other teachers and he assigns more work.  Do not take Hummel.
COnFusing chem material! makes his exams for the top two students! everybody else fails...
Good in lecture, clear, enthusiastic, and helpful outside of class too.

Professor enjoys writing difficult trick questions. Can be very mocking to the point it's hard to tell if it's really just his sense of humor, laughs at students having trouble on exams. Teaches only basics, have to really braincramp to figure test questions, problem is time is too limited. Could have been challenging, but very doable, w/o him.

Tricky Tom has earned this name for a reason. He really tries to confuse you on the exams, but be sure to go to lecture and discussion and you will have a good grade. Try hard and you'll do just fine.

Had him last semester. Good lecturer, if you go to lecture he will explain the material well and answer questions. He's a character and I found him funny. His tests can be pretty hard. The quizzes aren't easy either. Its chem 102, you wont get an A for doing nothing.

My TA gave easier quizes than the rest of the TA's.  Because of this, Hummel decided it would be a good idea to screw us over and lower our grades by 4-5 percent.  Would have had a C but came out with a D+.  Big difference.  Tried to reason with him, wouldnt budge.

A difficult class: come prepared to work and study hard!  Tests are very difficult and can also be hard to study for.  "Tricky Tom" can be very helpful 1-on-1, but only if you have specific questions.
I really liked Professor Hummel for Chemistry 1. He is quite the character. I had a good time in his class. His multiple choice tests are sometimes difficult.

Gives good explanations and always seems happy to answer questions or do more example problems.  Despite his clarity in lecture, his tests do tend to be difficult, though not impossibly so.  Attend lecture and section, and be prepared to do a lot of work, and you can come out of the class with a good grade and a good understanding of the material.
he is tricky and worst prof i ever had, don't take him  if u don't have to .also pick a good ta, ta make the quiz not him.some ta are good, some are really bad. and they trying to low ur grade up

Prof. Hummel is extremely helpful. If you don't understand something during lecture then be sure to go to his office hours. His exams are tricky, but he tries to test his best students. Take his class, you will learn chemistry :)

He's most definitely not a bad professor. He's a nice guy, he explains concepts well in lecture, and he'll answer any questions you have, but his exams are very hard. The kinds of questions he asks on exams are tricky and much more in depth than homework problems or quiz questions, so you really have to put an effort into the class to succeed.
Good professor who told you what he wanted you to learn and then expected you to learn it. Some of the exams were difficult, but they were always curved.

I really enjoyed Hummel's class. His lectures were interesting, and he mixed in demonstrations to keep people involved. The class was not too difficult, but it can be if you do not do the homework problems or do not study for the tests. I would recommend the past exam booklet. I was not looking forward to chem, but I ended up liking the class!

Great professor. Very understanding and his lectures are interesting. He is very laid back with attendance, and is very approachable. Very good guy to go and see if you have a problem or if you are not doing well. The best chem 102 teacher, if not more, just had him in 102. would go out of my way to get him again for sure.
He is a great professor.  He explains all of the concepts clearly and makes good use of the materials he gives out.  His tests are challenging but fair.
He is a really nice professor, and his favorite word is "goofy". I heard stories that he gives money to people who correct him :)
Hes a great teacher but the class is kind of hard! Study and do homework you'll be fine!
Hes a great teacher but the class is kind of hard! Study and do homework you'll be fine!
Good teacher, knows his stuff and communicates concepts well

Professor Hummel is not a great professor only to those who enjoy chemistry. He talks way too fast, does easy example problems in class, and expects you to master problems that he says are designed for the "smartest student." His exams are hard. I recommend that you actually have a good background chemistry before entering this class.
Funny, knows what hes talking about, keeps the students attention
Super fun to listen to when in lecture. Likes to do a lot of different presentations to show what we are learning (especially things that involve explosions).

He definitely lives up to his name as Tricky Tom Hummel, yet is an amazing professor. He truly does have the students best interest at heart. Do not hesitate to go ask him for any questions, he is so helpful. Get to know him, and really put forth a strong effort in his class it will pay off. I had to work very hard to get a B, so don't expect a goo

I came into the class only taking it because it was required for me.  I hated chemistry as it was, and altough "Tricky Tom" could be humorous, I found him really hard to follow because he talked so fast and I had never had any idea what was going on. However I had an awesome TA and that helped alot. But this class sucked for me, and I really tried.
I'm never bored in his lectures!

Great lecturer. Very animated and funny, keeps material interesting. May talk fast at times, but his explanations are great if you keep up. His exams are quite hard, but perfectly possible if you keep up with the material.
He is so funny. He is a good teacher, but you need to study on your own. You need to do practice problems if you want your A. He is extremely nice and approachable.
Hummel is a tough but really good professor and he makes class funny.

I'm laughing about every five minutes in class, and he does a lot of experiments (mostly blowing things up) that are very interesting.  I think he explains things extremely well.  If you're a slacker, you'll have a hard time with the tests.  But if you honestly try, I think an A or B won't be impossible to get.

Reading through most of these comments I would have thought the class wouldn't be too difficult and relatively easy to understand.  After taking the class I thought Hummel talked really fast and the exams were hard. I don't know if most of these people just love chemistry but I do NOT agree with the majority of the very positive student feedback
Everything was clearly explained...straightforward

Tricky Tom is the best! He looks like my uncle! Hes a great professor and has a lot of passion for what he does. The exams are not bad at all- just make sure you take your time and read the questions and you will only get a few wrong! He is hilarious and explains things clearly. Make sure you get a good TA though because Hummel doesnt write them!!
Hummel is the worst teacher I have ever had.  Hard Tests.  Don't take!

Nice guy, some material could use more explaining, but overall good lecture.  Online homework sucks and the tests are very difficult, but curved a lot.  Good TAs help a lot in this class since they write the quizzes and go over lecture stuff.

This was an easy class. The past hour exams are monstrously helpful. His exams have a few tricks in them, but take your time on them and think and they're easy to figure out. Tom made me really like chemistry.

"Tricky" Tom Hummel is an excellent teacher. To succeed, buy the past hours exams and the notes. He makes the material easy to understand and occasionally will let you out early. His exams are actually easy if you read the questions and THINK what it is that is being asked, as well as discerning tricks.
Lots of demos and explosions in class. I thought the class was not too hard but many of my friends struggled a bit. The tests can be tricky but if you know what you're doing they're pretty easy

Excellent lecturer; clear explanations of complicated topics, liberal use of demonstrations. Tests are not too difficult if you study and do the assigned homework. Very personable, easily accessible and extremely helpful, and aware of student's issues.

Be very careful with this class because he is a awesome teacher but his tests are tricky so go to the Chem Learning Center and get a past exam so you can know all his tricks. Also, make sure your T.A. is good because they make the quizes not him. If your T.A. is a person that says he will try to fail you, that means get a new T.A
He is a pretty cool teacher but his tests are really hard.

The exams are not too bad he will try and trick and put the mistake answers on the exam, but he warns of this many times in class.  He does a lot of demos, for example on the last day of class he devoted half the class to redox reactions which were all cool.  Don't fall behind in reading, going to class helps, get old hour exam book helps a lot.
He seems to want his students to fail...

This class is difficult but not impossible. You have to work for your grade. Most people do bad on the exams and then they get curved some. Important to review practice exams because they are similar to the real exams. Good luck.
Hey y'all...try to go to parkland to take this class...unless you are urgently need for this class.

Do yourself a favor: get a different professor. Hummel makes his exams hard on purpose, and he often tests on exceptions. I very frequently felt as though he was trying to trick us with the exams to see if we read one line on one page, instead of trying to see if we knew general chemistry. Take a lect/disc session with a TA 4days/week if you can.
Tests are overly difficult to make you do poorly!

Not that easy, but an excellent teacher. I had to work very hard for this class. BUY THE RECOMMENDED NOTES! They help alot. Also, take alot of side notes in the notes packet. Hummel is pretty hardcore. If you haven't been introduced to the material before hand this class is difficult but doable (obviously). In order to get an A you really need to work and do ALL the home work. Overall he's a good guy though, and a great teacher. He cares about chemistry.

Lectures are a little on the boring side unless he's blowing things up or causing himself bodily harm while blowing things up. Nice guy, knows his stuff. Admits to being dumb in college but still makes his tests hard. You have to work to get an A, but its not impossible

Difficult class and difficult professor. Do not take  Chem unless it's requiered or you love it, because you will commit suicide if you take it as a Gen Ed. he was an awful professor
One thing I have to admit, Tom is FAIR.  I came into the class intimidated by chem 102 being dubbed as a weed out class. But if you work hard it actually turns out a lot better than you may expect.

fun professor in lecture, does crazy stuff and cut his hand bad doing some weird experiment one day. tests are RIDICULOUSLY HARD! if u can get into 102A.
