Fun class, interesting material, and an intellegent but down to earth prof.  If the subject interests you... TAKE THE CLASS
Iryce Baron is one of the most engaging and supportive professors I have ever known. She is so passionate and witty in the classroom, and a great mentor outside it. I would recommend her to anybody!
Very interesting feminist class. She's very nice and willing to help, but she is a somewhat difficult grader. She tends to repeat some of the information, but overall the class is very worthwhile.

Never read the book just followed the class materials was able to understand the concepts just fine. It's a plus she really easy on the eyes as well. Great class, do ask she says and you'll be sure to manage and A. Too bad she won't be teaching the class next semester, her beauty still awes me.
Amazing teacher! Very engaged and always prepared to help all your questions. Grading is strict but very fair.
Katie is always very helpful, flexible, and really engages the class.
really cool chick. she's smart and is good at teaching
LOVED HER CLASS. SHE IS AWESOME!!!!!!
Very nice, fair, fun, and cuter than expected. I love her smile and positive attitude...she is extremely smart.

I really like her. The class seems unorganized and doesn't flow very well but she has to teach the course manual. If you get lucky and end up in her section you will have fun, learn a lot, and probably get a fair grade.
Amazing teacher, really helpful and kind. Fair and unbiased grading. Must-take for CMN 111 and CMN 112
Professor that cares about your understanding and success in the course. Good introduction into topics regarding operations and suppy chain.

The course was easy and I would take it again. However, I came across a reply from the professor to one of my fellow classmates that bothered me enough to write this review. His response was dismissive, disrespectful, and incorrect. I will note, this is the only interaction I had with the professor, so I could have caught him on a bad day.

Great professor.  Gives fun group projects and you will learn a lot through his interactive lectures.  Encourages creativity and loves when his class participates in discussions.  A very caring professor.  You will learn a lot in this class and it won't be too difficult.  Grades very fairly and everyone can succeed in his class.

Prof. Kirci is well-versed in field with many related personal experiences. He is kind and engaging, and if you put solid effort into the class you will easily succeed. Assignments and exams strongly mirror lecture content, and he walks you through examples of all problem types. Overall a great class taught by a knowledgeable and likable professor.

Very nice professor. Mostly bi-weekly / sometimes weekly assignment. He is happy to help answer any questions outside of class. Also a easy grader and really just wants to see student succeed in class.

The course was not very difficult and exams are open note, but you do need to study for exams since they're timed. The group project was not too labor intensive and I think he grades it pretty leniently. Prof. Kirci makes an effort to get to know everyone and keep the lectures engaging, which I appreciated.
He's a good professor that doesn't assign much homework. Class has two exams that are both open note. As long as you do the homework and have a basic understanding it's an easy class.
An unforgettable professor.  Everybody knows that Professor Carmen is one of the best (if not THE best) professors in the history of the Political Science Department at the U of I.  A legend.

Ira Carmen was indeed a legend. Probably the best lecturer at the U of I. He'll be great missed as a professor. One of the few professors you didn't WANT to miss class for! Thanks, Prof. Carmen, you served the university well!

The class will really help you establish a good understanding of judicial precedents, thinking, etc... but you REALLY have to keep up with the readings because Carmen will spend most of his class time making jokes and going on conservative rants. Additionally, his (2) tests and grading are a bit harsh, so your GPA will probably suffer.

Simply put, Professor Carmen is the best teacher I've ever had, in college or otherwise.  He honestly cares if you're learning, and he does his best to make the material interesting.  For a fun diversion from regular class material, ask him what he thinks of Keystone Light and/or the Chicago Cubs.

i don't understand how everyone says he is so hard. By no means is he easy but I missed almost half the lectures and still got a B. The guy has a great mind though and I wish I would have went more. Great class
Hard, but interesting.
This guy is a legend, as others have said.  I wish there were more like him.

Carmen is basically a legend here at Illinois. You will learn more in this class than you will in your other 117 credit hours. Pretty difficult, attending lecture is a must and you have to study, but Carmen is not only brilliant but hilarious so making it to lecture isn't an issue.

Like others have said, if you want a blowoff class this isn't it. But if you want a class that you learn a lot and are excited to go to every day, take this class! Carmen is probably the best professor I've had at the University. Hilarious and smart. I just wish I could play pingpong so I could take the Carmen Challenge.
BEST PROFESSOR I EVER HAD
GREAT PROFESSOR. GENIUS
Unparalleled.  Taking his class is the best decision you will ever make.
Best professor ever . .  and I was in his classes over 40 years ago.
Awesome.
Learned a lot, was challenged, but had a fun time throughout.  What more can you ask for?

Carmen's class is extremely difficult since he only gives you two exams; both of which are hypothetical scenarios where one needs to write a judicial opinion citing cases.  However, Carmen is hilarious and says outrageous things ("they have a gene for suicide bombing") that make the class anything but dull.  Your GPA will go down,but its worth it.
No Comments

i never thought the constitution could be more intersting or hilarious. there are only 2 tests for the entire course which does make it difficult however, you'll ALWAYS want to go to class just to hear carmen speak. awesome class. awesome professor.

Ira is an amazing lecturer - the class is difficult - but it's worth it to hear the man talk.  Extremely funny and informative, you will learn more than you've ever learned before from this man.  Signed up for 2 of his classes next semester
Ira makes the class great even if the material is difficult.  For sure taking the second course in the spring.
A fantastic professor who sounds like a cross between Lewis Black and Sylvester the Cat. If you're one minute late to class, you'll face his wrath and mockery.
Amazing instructor, full of passion, which makes going to class fun even if you don't agree with his opinions.  Not an easy class, but I learned so much from it, and him.
A tough class, but one of the best teachers ever. He is one of those people you remember for the rest of your life,and he doesn't mind throwing in a life lesson or twelve every now and then.
Great teacher.  Tells you what you need to know, quirky personality keeps class interesting.
Not easy, but an awesome teacher
One of the best teachers I have ever had

I highly recommend Dr. Ladegaard. He gives the best lectures I've had at UIUC and starts great conversations. He's clear as to what he expects from students and always gives examples that are relevant to the course. The workload is very manageable, just make sure you're in class and do short annotations before class.

So far, getting to the end of the semester, I can see how much I understand criminology than I did before. The only problem I had was the quizzes. The quizzes are what's going to get you, the exams are multiple-choice, but you only get credit for the correct answer. The examinations aren't his fault. It's you HAVE TO READ THE QUESTION RIGHT.

Prof. Ladegaard is one of the best professor I've had. He's passionate about his lectures and not a tough grader. As long as you put in the work, its an easy A. I skimmed the readings and reviewed the material each week and was prepared for the tests. I tried to take one of his classes the next semester because I enjoyed his teaching style so much!

very interesting lectures and course material! professor ladegaard really cares about the course material and it shows through his lectures. the workload is manageable but the annotations can be a bit much for someone who hasn't really annotated readings before. i would definitely take one of his courses again! :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: favorite teacher. gives helpful and useful feedback and pushes you to be better. super thoughtful about cirriculum and puts in effort to teach the class. lectures are super informative and she takes the time to answer questions or go over missed points. it is very obvious she truly cares about students and teaching. i always learn and grow from her

The coursework is presented clearly and she always leaves room if things need to be adjusted. Student feedback is also taken into consideration and it makes the classroom thrive. Project feedback is in depth and explains exactly why certain things work and others don't. Goes above and beyond for her students!

This class was fun and Bo-Linn fostered a really supportive environment among the students. This class was the LEAST nervous I've been in when it comes to critiques. Not an easy class but definitely rewarding, and Bo-Linn is just someone you wanna make proud, ya know?
251 toolbox is boring but bo-linn is a gem. very knowledgable, approachable, and encouraging. couldn't ask for a better prof.

Awesome Professor, she's really knowledgeable and will provide useful feedback. Always opened to help and comment on something. Opened to giving tutorials if you want them. Very clear for what's due for a project. Limits you to certain elements but she's very reasonable as to why. Overall cool and fun person. Feels like a nice friend is teaching.

Bo-Linn is super caring, approachable, and I always looked forward to her class. She gives great feedback, and is very helpful. She helped create a really comfortable atmosphere for critiquing, and I enjoyed her class a lot!
Dr. Ishikawa is a great professor; she is very nice and knowledgeable, and makes the material as interactive as possible. The tests are difficult, but the easier format of labs and quizzes helps.

This class has a lot of memorization and a lot of work. I am taking it online, so I'm not sure how it is normally, but we have video lectures with a quiz after each set of lectures. The quizzes allow multiple attempts so you can take them as many times until you get them all right. The labs are just worksheets with a quiz after and 2 exams.

Her tests are extremely challenging, but the quizzes and labs are very easy. She does her best to make lecture enjoyable and is always happy to help students after class. She enjoys questions and encourages participation., and is very knowledgeable on the subject to answer every question. Would recommend taking this class with a friend.

Labs are not worth 100 like someone else mentioned... theyre only worth 10. She also makes exams way more difficult than they should be. She told us that if we memorized the study guide, textbook, and lectures we still would not get a 100. She told us the exams are designed for people to get Cs. Exams are worth 65% total of the final grade.

keiko seems like a nice lady but the material is super monotonous and dense, and lectures are two hours long and really boring. the labs are easy and help boost your grade, as tests can be hard because there is so much memorization involved.

She is a great teacher. She is also very funny and always has balloons with her. The class is challenging and mostly memorization. But the labs are worth 100 points each and help a lot. The book is not used often but a lot of the answers to the labs and papers in class are straight from the book.

Great insight of the business world and many real life examples in which you can learn the reasons of success or failures of entrepreneurs. The most important is that real life examples shown at class and guest lecturers complement the course content very good.

Noah is an amazing entrepenuer, but can work on his lecturing skills. It's okay though, since SOCW321 isn't lecture heavy. It's an amazing course, and Noah and the course have much room for potential.

Very cool person. Knows a lot and willing to share and engage with his students. Can meet with him at anytime to discuss things ranging from class to career plans afterwards. Because the class is relatively straightforward, you get back what you invest into the class.

He's a cool guy with awesome stories. However, he doesn't really care about you or your start up unless you're making great strides. We had problems that we pointed out and it seemed like he really didn't care. He didn't always come to class and would put other students in charge, which is fine, but we took the class for his advice. Cool course.
Noah was just an inspiring professor. He has experienced alot and he hopes to share his knowledge to all his students. I found myself inspired to do more and to accomplish great things.
The most dedicated professor on campus, hands down.  Great guy.  Young, energetic, fun, passionate.  Brilliant.

In this class, it is not about the busy work you have to complete but rather the quality of the content you produce. Noah doesn't just assign work, he kind of inspires you to be great - when he lectures, you actually find yourself engaged by what he is saying. He resourceful, connected, and willing to help you succeed in anything. Chill guy.
Good teacher and class. It was very interesting material to learn.

Noah has created a class where you are virtually in charge of your success. It's about finding something you care about and working for it. Noah gives great support and helps you reach the goals you have for your organization with his extensive business Background. This class is not a class for a semester but a class for life with a great teacher.
Noah can be intimidating because he is so attractive and smart, but the course is very interesting and you will learn a lot. It relates to real life.

Noah's resume is impressive and his suit game is one point, but I never felt as if I really 'connected' with him as a professor. He conveys his passion for Social Enterprise not through his expressions or evident enthusiasm, but through his actions. When he speaks to the class, he grins often as if he were hiding some secret he was soon to reveal.
One of my favorite courses at Uiuc thus far. Isserman is all about real world application and cutting out the BS. Love the class.

Isserman and this class are both really great. It is obvious that the professor really cares and is passionate about what he's teaching. Noah's also really easy to talk to if you have questions or want to know more about the subject.
Phenomenal. Noah knows his stuff and the teaching team is amazing. If you're looking for a class that is something different and can lead to some awesome things, this is it.
A guy whose passion and knowledge of the subject comes out easily, and isn't afraid to teach in a more modern, engaging way instead of reading off a PowerPoint.

Professor Isserman is intelligent, compelling, and has tons of experience in the field! This course was one of my favorites at UIUC! There is a final project in which you create a social venture and my group continued working on it, turning it into a thriving program in the community! If you want to change the world, take this course with Isserman!
He was very helpful with individual questions and for exploring social entrepreneurship.
Fun, helpful, and OOOO he is hottt.

Prof isserman runs a really fun and interactive class that challenged me to challenge myself to make large social impact as a student entrepreneur. Their isn't much course work, but what is assigned is super useful. Way more introspective and practical than most classes.

Derek is a great professor. He allows a great amount of time in class for discussion, which really allows you to understand what you are talking about in the class. He is very nice and techy, so you will use your laptop a lot. Highly recommended, probably my favorite professor this semester.
No Comments
He is awesome! So helpful and will give you an A if you work hard. I loved him!

For 498, she has control over the curriculum and it's very easy. Her exams were most of the grade, but thankfully they were super easy. Attendance was not graded, there were very few homeworks, and she was a very easy grader. That said, not a lot was learned from this class and she is not the best lecturer. Most content was right from the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: First, Iwona is a horrible lecturer, she repeats herself a lot and is unable to explain fundamental concepts. Her lectures are basically useless. Just read the book and chapters before the test and you will do fine. Final was easiest, but other two exams had a 70% average. Also go to office hours to dispute grading if necessary. Not a bad person.

She's a terrible lecturer. Her explanations are incomprehensible, and she jumps back and forth between multiple examples, confusing everyone. Sometimes < 50% of students will get a Zoom poll correct and she merely continues with the lecture without fully explaining it. To learn anything you have to look it up yourself or try TA office hours.

An absolutely terrible lecturer. Doesnt explain anything, even when the majority of the class gets a poll wrong. Its been over a year of zoom classes and most classes she spends the first 15 minutes fixing her zoom. Im begging you to not have this professor.

Bad management of the course progress. Leave a lot of important topics in last two weeks of the class. Read book helps more than go to the lecture. two midterms were easy, the final was extremely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Well, the lecture part of this class was a complete joke, as the quizzes and tests were almost identical to the homework and practice tests. I could appreciate the easiness of the exams/quizzes if I felt like I actually learned something from attending the lectures. Be prepared for a snoozefest and a lot of self-learning and memorization.
Rambles on and  on and whips through lecture slides. very boring.

In class quizzes & hw due alternate days so attendance is req but punctuality is not. Not an exciting prof, but does a good job. Take good notes! With a little help from the book the hw is not too difficult 0.5-4 hrs/wk, avg 1.5 hrs/wk. Quiz very easy, test (2)/final moderate; DO THE HW+BOOK PROBLEMS and understand them and the tests become simple.
She is a nice person, but a terrible teacher. Better count on books for learning the material. Exams and quizzes are quite easy so nothing to worry about.

Professor Duursma is a fantastic professor. Many have told me 417 is the hardest course here at UIUC, but he explained the materials in a very approachable and interesting way, and the materials are easily digestible as long as you follow along with the lecture. He cares about students a lot and the grading is fair. Strongly recommended.
pretty cool guy!
Lectures did not help
Beside from his thick accent, I could not learn anything from this teacher during lectures. Very hard to follow, ending up trying to teach myself through the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's really into theories and proofs. He is a great professor, though. He takes the time to make sure that you understand the material!
Great proffesor. He really takes the time to answer questions during lecture!

He was probably the best of the calc 2 professors this semester, which really isn't saying much. The class is tough but doable if you study hard. His accent kind of makes it hard to understand him at times and he is also very soft spoken so sit in the front.
The tests are very hard and worth almost all the points. He also has a bit of an accent and talks quietly, so sit in the  front

Overall, I would say that this class was a Marathon, which I largely had to run on my own. If you go into office hours, he does displays a willingness to assist students. However, his lectures are often confusing, and mainly delve into general theory, rather than examples that may be presented on the exams. In short, decent guy, impossible teacher.

I would not recommend taking a math class with him. His tests are very difficult, he goes through difficult material quickly, and doesn't seem to care about his students. If you are able to, take it with a different professor. You aren't missing out on anything.
He's not the clearest for lectures, he could explain the subject matter a bit more.
never update my homework grade after I showed him 3 times and sent him 2 emails, and it accounts a lot for the final grade

Harder than other professors teaching the same course, but definitely worth it if you take math seriously. Very demanding on what you need to know for the tests, but puts in a concerted effort to make sure you understand even the most difficult concepts. Very clear lectures if you can get past the accent and Dutch phraseology.

This instructor is an idiot! He even did not give us a detailed syllabus for his class. He promised us to upload assignments at a certain date but failed to do that many times. What he taught was too ambiguous. Honestly I highly don't recommend students to take his classes.

I couldn't understand the book, but I understood him pretty well. Places HUGE emphasis on exams, and not so much on HW and quizzes. But the exams are usually some variations of problems he's gone over in class at least once, so I recommend attending them.
Extremely smart guy but teaches everything from a pretty general perspective...extremely helpful and goes straight to the point which is an added advantage..highly recommend taking this guy's class
Does not curve.

The guy teaches everything in the most general form possible, all with symbols and few examples that you're later tested on. He is hard to understand but it's evened out by the very low difficulty level of the course.
Try not to select his class if you can. You can learn more completely if you read the book then go to his class.
He was very difficult and taught out of the book, but this math class is a bit difficult anyways, so it's hard to judge him. Could have been more helpful, but he did try.

My favorite IS prof at UIUC. He has engaging discussions and exams that set you up for an A. He is an understanding person with a fun class environment and great expectations for students. Take this class with Prof. Ivanov for Information Systems. The best class I've take within IS and one of the best at UIUC.

Professor Ivanov was a great teacher! I took him last semester in Fall 2020 and his teaching style is one of the best. He makes a difficult topic very easy to learn and has a great sense of humor. He grades very fairly and the test are practical and useful. Just go to the lectures, take notes and you won't have a problem getting a good grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a horribel teacher but helpful. Teaches the course as if it is a literature class. Talking and talking same old stuff but does not present anything new. Total waste of time and I did not learn anything new. He is also not good at explaining. But not difficult to get A.
No comment. Just awful. Do not take this class.
Outstanding professor, would certainly take him again.

Roman is good at leading discussions and making the course material fit the interest of students. He is knowledgeable in Ukrainian literature and art. Exam is long and very related to lecture. In class presentation is important and he gave lots of advice in the feedback. I enjoyed this course a lot and strongly recommend it for general education.
Roman deeply conveys subject matter to students. Loved taking UKR, a great class that I looked forward to every time. 10/10 would recommend.

Personally my biggest problem with this class is that the tests are all multiple choice I think thats a dumb way to run a class but the prof is fine and he was one of the better professors but this class is hard

Professor Contreras is a step above the rest. He untiringly answers questions on Piazza all day and stays after class until every student has their questions answered. His lectures are as clear as possible and he doesn't make the experience boring. The only downside was that tests were challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He gives great lectures and explains the material clearly. He is personable, approachable, caring, and has a good sense of humor. He is always active on Piazza effectively answering questions at all times.

Content-wise, I did not enjoy this class at all and failed to see any relevance to my major. However, this professor is an outstanding guy and great lecturer. He was very active on the class forum and was always answering questions late into the night.

Greatest teacher I have ever had in college so far. Very nice person and love to answer your question.  Explanation is clear and helps you how to think about the problems. Office hours always help. I guess the only problem is sometimes he would be really late to office hour. I had waited for 40 minutes one time:P
He's  willing to answer any question that you ask. He is a  very nice guy and I can't see any reason why you should not take the course with him.

The best professor I've had the pleasure of taking, math or otherwise. Great progression of logic during lectures (even for very abstract concepts), super enthusiastic and receptive to questions of all kinds.  Tests are very reasonable and straightforward, homework ranges in difficulty but is always interesting and relevant.

Ivan is a really fantastic instructor. He can explain those tough materials very well. He often asks students about how to think this question instead of just give you the answer, which help us think a lot during lectures. To be honest, this kind of thinking method really helps you in the exam and in the future learning.

Ivan is a very good instructor, you don't want to miss his lecture. He is pleased and patient to answer your questions after course. To get an A+, firstly, go to every lecture and take notes, exams are based on the notes; secondly, read & think scheduled materials on course page deeply; do hw by yrsf, understand every problems in practice exam.

I truly believe the ONLY reason Dr. Ivy is not a tenured professor is because she chose to dedicate herself to her family and teaches for the love of the material and her students. She knows her stuff and she lights up when she talks about it. She was ALWAYS available to help me, even now that I am not longer in her class.

Amazing teacher!! The most insightful teacher I have had at U of I so far.. contrary to what the person below me thinks.. She can be a hard grader but is definitely fair and only tries to benefit her students. She is very available for any extra help a student may need.Definitely take a class with Anna Ivy if you get the chance

I'm kind of shocked at how great the ratings for Anna are. I had her for 255 and I absolutely dreaded coming to class. She had nothing new and insightful to say. We read great texts, but unfortunately our discussions in class did not do the texts justice. Almost fell asleep every class

Awesome teacher. If you're the type of person who likes to discuss or listening in on discussions, this class is definitely for you. The homework load and grading procedures are fair. You can't completely blow off the class, but if you put in the necessary work you'll be fine.

The class is pretty easy. You'll be doing a fair amount of reading/writing, but if you participate every once in a while and put forth some semblance of effort, you'll get an A. Midterm/final were very easy.

If you can, take a class with Ivy.  She brings in awesome and original analyses of the texts we read.  It's not too hard to get an A in the class if you show up, do a good job on the assignments, and participate once in a while in class. Word of advice would be to be original in papers and follow her advice in terms of how to do the midterm/final.

Prof. Ivy is AMAZING.  She's passionate and knowledgeable about her chosen novels and makes class fun to attend.  She grades fairly and if you put in the work, you should have good grades.  She's very friendly and has an amusing sense of humor.  Take a class with her if you can!

She is one of the best English professors I have had yet. She is a great teacher and genuinely cares about her students. She is not an extremely hard grader but expects good work out of her students. If you have the chance, take a class with her!

Anna is a very nice professor who is quite funny. From England, married to Prof. Barrett of 209. The class is easy you just randomnly particpate and do the work = A. Go in to see her before papers, she will get to know you and therefore like you more. Very sweet would recommend for those who like to DISCUSS the novels alot!

A good portion of your grade is participation based, which is not hard if you read the assignments. The tough parts come in writing the essays, because you're expected to be able to come up with something meaningful and original. The first exam is a time-cruncher, while the second isn't as bad. Overall, it shouldn't be too tough to get an A or B.
Super nice, funny, wonderful discussions in class.  One of the best teachers I've had at U of I.

Anna is a fairly easy grader. On the midterm, she gave credit for a wide variety of answers -- I feel like she's one of the few teachers who wants to see you do well. She gives reasonable paper assignments, relatively short (5 pages), with a couple different topics. She's funny and entertaining during class.

She likes to read into the novels WAY too much. More than half of the "in-depth" analysis seems like she is reaching for it. Tests are pretty easy but I felt like she graded the papers really unfairly. If you don't like talking in discussion, DONT take this class, because participation is expected.

Weekly 1pg papers that aren't graded that tough. Weekly quizzes that are taken DIRECTLY from the lectures. You HAVE to take good notes. Lectures are kind of vague. I didn't feel I was learning anything about comm, just history. Final group project. Final exam was short and easy. Overall the class was tedious and incredibly boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: He will call on you at random to participate. Be ready.

You read through the book pretty quickly. He doesn't assign a lot of homework besides the speeches, but makes you work in groups in class. He keeps up with the grading, and is very helpful. He explains everything very well and is accessible outside of class for help with assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He forces you to speak in only one way. Dumbs down every speech to where you have to restate a small fact several times over and over. Poor grader, takes points off of a speech for small details that don't affect the clarity/message/professionalism of the speech. he said he didn't get my work during spring break, gives a zero, then returns work...

I knew her exams were going to be BS when her own TA said he told Glennon to stop making the test super tricky. Some of the questions comes from the things she said verbally in class which is really hard to get because she talks so fast . But the good thing is she retired so there will be another teacher with MACS 100 .

Glennon really isn't that bad and is extremely nice if you get to know her. Her tests questions are mainly from the lecture notes but the readings are also required if you want to do well. Overall, this was one of the easier classes that I have had during my 4 years at U of I.

Glennon is a babe. Her tests are mainly from lecture notes. If you pay attention and take good notes you will be more than fine in this class. You also get to watch awesome movies and shows like The Truman Show, Little Miss Sunshine, Beavis & Butthead, and a little bit of South Park. Most of the negative remarks are from slackers.

I really don't see why she is getting all of this negative criticism...I mean she does initially come off as a bi*** but her tests are straight from the lecture (JUST PAY ATTENTION IN CLASS) and the movies we watched were pretty funny (The Truman Show, Little Miss Sunshine, etc.) I studied the day before my first exam and ended up wit

I am currently in the class and getting ready for Exam 1 today. I already don't like her or the class. She picks all these old time movies that are not interesting. I don't know what to study for this exam and she is super boring. Thinking about dropping this class and taking a second 8 week course. Any suggestions ?

Glennon does not know how to teach a gen ed. Tests were trickier than needed. Attendance is required. The title of this course makes it seem like a breeze, but effort is a must if you want to get an A. I got an A but I had to push myself to study for a course I did not think I would devote much time to. Look for a better option in a gen ed

Do not take this class. Glennon mostly talked about how much she hated Jersey Shore and discussed extremely radical viewpoints of the media that were very disagreeable. If you want to take a class that you will hate, try MACS 100. Definitely not what I was expecting. The film projects are pointless and her exams are impossible to study for.

MACS100 was okay. You have to attend lecture for clicker questions. Her tests are way too difficult for a 100 level class. She gives you a study guide but half of the material isn't on the test. Don't take this course if you're looking for an easy gen ed. This class isn't worth the GPA drop.

Ivy was pretty cool.  I learned a bunch and she was very enthusiastic.  She's oddly cute in a older woman kinda way.  Even though the class was pretty difficult, I think of her quite fondly.  One of those professors you remember as tough but sincere.  Ivy is great.

This woman takes her PhD WAY too seriously. Yes, she IS intelligent. However, intelligence coupled with hypocrisy is hard to admire. While on the one hand she emphasizes the absurdity of institutional power, on the other, she insists on being addressed as "Dr." Thus reinforcing that which she criticizes. She is full of incongruent attitudes.
Learned a lot about ethics.  Course is hard at first but she is interested in topic and makes ideas clear.

This professor is highly unorganized, yet is a very hard grader. She does not know how to work with basic technology and takes several weeks to grade things! She assigned 3 tests, 2 papers, and 1 groups presentation for this course, and the majority of those assignments were given at the end of the semester. Her lectures are unclear.

Do Not take a class with this woman.  Attendance is mandatory, she talks about non-sense, she is an incredibly hard grader, tons of readings in books and journals.  Tons of work with this woman...plus she is incredibly boring!
Hated her. Besides being ridiculously unorganized, she and my TA messed up the grades for several students in the class. She states her opinions as facts.

Great Class.  Really easy.  If you want to be entertained, go to the lecture.  I'm pretty sure Ivy makes up most of what she talks about.  I studied maybe an hour for the entire class, spent most of my time in lectures doing sudoku, and got a 94. I basically only went to hear the ridiculous things Ivy would say.

I truly liked this class. She's pretty enthusiastic and makes it interesting. The tests weren't bad at all and I loved the content of the class (also loved the book!). Take it if you're an ad major!!! This is for ADV 493 not the COMM class.

The lecture was a joke. I didn't go to more than half. Go to discussion and put in a decent effort on the project, and you will get an A like me. Also do the online multiple choice practice exams. Ivy is knowledgeable, but a terrible lecturer. Unbearable. Get Matt as a TA. He's hot.

She could be pretty boring, but overall her class was not bad. I was always amused when she would talk about things to imply that she was keeping up with technology. She tried but sometimes she seemed clueless. But overall a good class. Interesting content. If you do the readings and assignments you will do great! I got an A!

Best teacher ever!  Even though her lectures were posted online, she tells you questions that will be on the test and shows examples to clarify.  Don't listent to people who say she is awful or boring!  She took time to know everyone's name in our lecture of about 200 students!  Great teacher and easy class as long as you read the book!  :)
She's boring but the class is fine. The quizzes were really easy. You don't have to attend lecture, just show up for discussion with the TA and you'll be fine. Not bad at all!
REALLY DUMB. The lecture is horribly boring. DO NOT GO. She talks about how much she loves blogging, and hates Fox News and ipods. My TA was great too.... But Ivy... shes a piece of work.

horrible teacher! very pretentious. makes you feel horrible every single day. fabricates statistics, grades papers perviously graded by the ta's down. great tas but glennon is so evil that it's not worth it.
She has questions on her power points that she never answers

Her lectures don't have much of a point to them. However, the material covered in the class is quite interesting, especially if you are a prospective Communications major. My TA was fairly knowledgable, and the quizzes administered are pretty easy. If you are a motivated student at all, an A should be attainable.
This class has the potential to be so good. However,   Prof. Glennon has no course structure whatsoever. She had to have changed the schedule eight times.
disorganized class, TAs and teacher. one of the worst classes ive taken.

Don't take this class. The TA's are horrible, and assignments are never explained clearly. I was looking forward to it before I started, but now I hate it. We had a 10 pg research paper due, and neither Glennor nor the TA's stated their expectations. AFTER it was turned in, Glennon spent 15 min saying how we should have wrote it. Very disorganized.

Professor Rowe's style of teaching was some of the most difficult I've had, not just at this university, but in my time as a student. His points were often difficult to grasp, and moved through the material quite rapidly. There were no clear indicators of what points were most important to understand. The grading on the few essays was harsh.
Very funny and leads interesting discussions

6 books to read total and every single lecture was just the class discussing the reading. he likes to go off track sometimes but overall very passionate about his teaching and he was a very fair grader. There was 3 essays worth 30% of the grade plus attendance and 3 extra credit (bumped paper 1/3 letter grade). would definitely take him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a professor that's passionate about his subject and goes above and beyond in answering his students questions. His class consists of some exams with heavy focus on papers. Attendance is not mandatory but tests usually consist of lecture material. He also gives out a good amount of extra credit to make up for faults throughout the semester.
Professor Rowe knows philosophy and brings a positive attitude to class. Would like to see a bit more class organization, but otherwise good.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he's pretty chill and funny. also the lectures are really important if you want to do well in your assignments.

The readings were sometimes difficult for someone not majoring in history, but definitely manageable. This class (HIST200) is a lot of work for a 200-level class, so do not expect it to be easy. He is an awesome lecturer and did a great job at breaking down content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This guy is the freaking GOAT. If you can take him, do it. Had him for HIST350 and 200 and I actually looked forward to his classes. Also wrote me a rec letter. Definitely a great model for what an educator should be. Classes weren't easy, but he was really good at walking students through difficult subjects, so I didn't mind.

I really loved the lectures, he makes you feel very interested about the topic. There's only a few grades in the grade book and I found it easy to get Bs in the class but hard to get As on assignments. Overall, really fun and kind prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor! I have had him for four different courses, and he has been an outstanding instructor in every class.
Marco is a great professor. He is super flexible and wants to help his students. He will look over your paper if you go to office hours and gives really helpful feedback.
Really kind professor, very acceptable level of work, and flexible about deadlines. Great lectures as well!

A really engaging lecturer that really makes it a point to get to know each person in his classes as much as possible. He is very clear with all assignments he assigns and how he wants them to be done, while also allowing for creativity to rise up in the essays that are assigned. Overall, he is a great professor that brings out the best in all.

Marco is GREAT. He is super laid back and will absolutely meet you where you're at if you're struggling. His lectures are usually pretty engaging, though on occasion his papers are a little inconvenient.

This class was so much fun and the professor did a great job keeping the lectures engaging and informative. He was accessible outside of class time and always very enthusiastic and knowledgeable on the topic. This was a study abroad course and I really enjoyed the structure of the course while we were abroad as well.

This professor is one of the two best professors at the university of Illinois, I have taken 4 classes with them because of their incredible ability to teach and provide reflection. I have been astounded by the care and effort they continually put into their classes and students. I cannot recommend this amazing teaching professional enough!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Cares about his students. Very in-depth professor who knows his material. Highly recommend.

I love taking this Professors class. He is very caring and respectful. He is very chill and laid back also extremely understanding. All you need to do is attend the class and complete the papers. Communication is key so email or talk to him about not being able to turn in the papers on time or attending class.

Dr. Jaimes is the best of the best here at the university. His classes are enjoyable and will always leave you with something new. He genuinely cares about the material he teaches and his students, being very flexible with students' needs, like paper extensions. Take one of his classes, you will not regret it.

Dr. Jaimes is by far one of the greats at UIUC, as with every course you take with him you are in for a remarkable learning experience. He is empathetic, genuine, and quite passionate about the material he teaches, and while participation is a good part of your grade, it is of no concern as you will find it hard not to want to partake in his class.

Too many weekly essays that started to feel like busy work rather than actual learning. Because there was always one due, I often completed them just to finish. The study guide did not fully reflect the exam, which made studying difficult given how much content there was. Even my engineering classes prepared students more clearly for exams.
Gives alot of busy work not related to test or lecture material. Wouldve ben a great class if the assignmnets actually related to anything on the exams.

I took PS304 with James (only let me put 303). Don't listen to the negative feedback, I almost dropped PS304 bc these reviews stressed me out, but it turned out to be one of my favorite PS classes. James is understanding, a fair grader, and very knowledgeable. His lectures were very interesting, he's kind to his students, and wasn't hard to get A.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend this class. There's way too much work, he tries to cover too much content, and the exams are a nightmare that are barely related to the lectures. Also didn't help that he got rude and condescending anytime I asked a question or for help on an assignment. Do yourself a favor, take a different class with a better instructor.

This review is for PS 101. Fairly easy class with relatively easy exams and papers, but requires a LOT of reading. Minutiae from readings WILL pop up on exams, so read and take notes! Papers are interesting and fun to complete. Lectures more-or-less summarize the reading (but still do the readings!). Responsive to feedback and forgiving.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: OK I am not going to stand for the Steur hate. He gave us all a free 5% on our exam because he knew we were all very anxious and he is already a tough grader so this was WILD. Steur is a friend to his students. Everyone give this guy a chance his homework is purposeful and lectures are good and full of content. ACTUALLY READ THE TEXTBOOK NEXT TIME!

I do all the homework, put my best effort in, go to class, take really good notes, am organized with my work, participate, basically everything you should do for a class and still am beating my head a against a wall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I didn't think that Professor Steur's class was as bad as many people have been rating it. As expected for every class, as long as you do the assigned readings, show up to class, and complete the assignments with reasonable effort, the class wasn't overly difficult. Boring at times, but he seemed like he cared about feedback and improving his class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you do the readings and engage in lecture you should be totally fine. I could do with less papers but they aren't bad. Steur is good and grades the writing assignments pretty fairly. The exams can be hard but if you have a decent understanding of the readings and practice your AP testing skills from high school you will be more than fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Steur is really caring and supportive of his students. There's a lot of assignments that were not worth a lot, so there's less pressure on everything. The material was very boring to me but he's great at showing videos, making jokes, and fostering discussion to make class more interesting. Not a super challenging class if you do the work.

super accommodating with deadlines and values supporting his students. a LOT of small assignments that stack up and is busy work. class is kind of theory/memorization heavy but if you study textbook you will get an a
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is a content heavy class with numerous papers and difficult exams. Nonetheless, he always asks for feedback and prioritizes student needs. He has given us many different study materials and is always lenient with extensions. Anybody willing to work hard who has a genuine interest in the class should take the other reviews with a grain of salt.

I took PS303 this semester and although it is a bit heavy in terms of amount of assignments, Professor Steur is very caring about his students and very accommodating. Lectures were always well organized and interesting. Exams are a bit difficult but if you go to class and read the textbook and study a bit, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he needs to change this class completely. I am regretting this as my first 300 level PS class because he leaves a bad impression on the department. He assigns way to much without consideration that people have more than just his class and he seems to not like his students and it is so apparent that his students don't like him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Do not take this class. James has made us take so many surveys on how this class can be improved, and he basically is taking our feedback as a joke. Given, he is funny, his tests are no joke. He expects us to know EVERYTHING from the textbook and lectures, and then proceeds to make the essay questions on the most niche concepts that aren't helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Some of the assignments and lectures were beneficial to learning, however, much of it did not match test content and made exams difficult. There is also a final exam and project due within days of one another, with the project being a large amount of work that shouldn't have been assigned to be due so shortly after other papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is interesting and the assignments throughout the course will be useful if pursuing a career in politics, but the final project paired with the final exam is an EXORBITANT amount of work. While the rest of the class may be useful the final project makes this class a burden and a waste of time. Steur doesn't care about his students at all

the study guides do not help at all. all of the exams were extremely difficult and felt like we covered nothing on them.  every single review session was during a time when most people have class making it even more unaccessible.  the assignments were long and tedious and I felt like I did not gain anything from them.

Worst lecturer in the world. Never puts exam-related content in his lectures and there is a huge paper due every few weeks. The content of the papers are never talked about in lecture and you basically have to teach yourself these concepts. Nice guy but condescending when you try and ask a question.

Super kind and cares a ton about his students and their success. Course content can feel a little bit repetitive from other PS courses but manages to stay interesting. The exams are a little difficult but read the textbook and don't miss class and you'll be fine

Good guy, lots of clear grading criteria. Class involves a group presentation, personal presentation and a midterm/final combo MC/Essay test. Textbook can be found online but is required. Read it and the lectures get repetitive but attendance is required. I enjoyed the class because it was a deep dive into the material and stayed interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was the first time Professor Steur taught this course so it was a bit of a trial run, but I think it went really well and will only get better next semester.

He is a difficult but reasonable professor. His lectures are pretty boring, but it makes up for the fact that attendance is optional and he posts almost everything on canvas. The class covers extensive amounts of content, so quite a bit of memorization is required for exam prep.
Definitely a tough class, but a super kind and understanding guy who clearly cares about seeing his students succeed.

Prof Thorner has very very clear criterias in his class and communicates them very clearly as well. His lectures are very helpful and informative and I find most people who don't do well in his class comes as a result of them skipping lecture. He cares very deeply about his students and their wellbeing, especially given this whole hacking situation

Very tough grading and unreasonable exercises given before exams. The actual test doesn't seem to be anywhere similar to the exercises, and most questions on the practice exams make no sense at all. But he eventually cancelled the final exam because of the hacker issue so I‘m gonna give him credit for that.
He was not a good lecturer, but he eventually cancelled the final exam because of the hacker issue so I'm gonna give him credit for that.

Be wary of this teacher, only enroll in this class if absolutely necessary. He never updates grades, makes midterms impossibly hard, and does homework assignments time consuming. The whole class is struggling with ~C grades, but there's no mention of a curve. The silver lining is the content overlap with CS173, which doesn't even apply to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This course is not well structured. You would never guess this was an introductory course. You could spend hours studying for midterms and still somehow do poorly because you could run out of time. I would say that it's useful that homeworks are harder than midterms, but it's the lack of time that really gets anyone. TAs aren't helpful either.
bane of my existence

Questions on the tests are tricky and pointless. They do not reflect the students' understanding of the materials at all. And keep repeating "90% will ensure an A-" does not help while the average is almost a C and everyone is panicing.

The professor cannot write an exam that is actually fair for his students to complete in a 50-minute time period. It's like he wants us to fail. The tests are just so difficult + the homeworks and practice problems he assigns don't even help. He expects us to be able to know how to pull out a trick for exam problems. So unfair.

The lectures consist of him just reading off of slides with several definitions that you MUST memorize as well as proof examples that don't help you in any way for exams. As a reminder, this is an introduction class, yet he teaches like you already know everything. Practice exams are either nonexistent or unhelpful as there are no solutions.
He is starting to get on my nerves. This class is just so difficult. I feel like im constantly worried about the next exam for this class.
Questions in exam are too hard, and the time is not enough to even finish them
Grading in general is too strict. No curve for extremely hard exams.

Reads off 100-page slides with 4-6 proofs without explanation. Rude when asked questions and thinks we have his knowledge INTRO COURSE BTW. We can only use things proven in class but assignments need concepts he barely mentioned+didnt prove. HW takes hours. TAs dont know what he's doing. A 40% was a B on the first test and HE DOESN'T CURVE THEM!
Just have no idea what he was talking about in the lectures

When he teaches he assumes his students are all at his level of understanding the topics. Tests look hardly like the review sheets or homework he assigns. I'm looking forward to this class being over.

Dr. Thorner does not teach very well. He acts like we should already understand the topic even though this is an intro class to proofs. He is very rude when you ask a question. He doesn't explain things well either and even though his tests are curved, they are extremely hard. Overall he is just hard to learn from.

He is extremely unaware of the population in this class. It is called INTRODUCTION to proof writing for a reason. He acts as if everyone in this class is aiming to win a Nobel prize in proof-writing. He expects us to have hundreds of complex theorems and definitions memorized. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if you do not have to.

Exams make no sense, many hard questions but the exam is only 50 minutes. No practice exams. All exams are cumulative. No solutions are given for exercise problems before exam. Lots of homework and you get many points off for tiny errors. Everything is graded harshly. He seems knowledgeable but doesn't know how to teach.

Thorner severely underestimates the difficulty of the exams, lectures, homeworks, and discussion wrksts. Has no empathy for his students and is a rather harsh grader when it comes to HW and exams. Get ready to go to office hours where TAs don't know what's going on in this class. Also, we can't view our current grade until the end of the course.

he instructor seems to lack the ability to clearly explain abstract mathematical concepts. There appears to be an assumption that students are already thoroughly familiar with every chapter, which is not realistic. He described midterm as “cumulative,” and he seems very proud . The lectures often come across as lacking confidence.
he made this class way more difficult than before

Nice prof, BUT he was not letting us to use math symbols of 'for all,' 'there exists,' and 'implies' for some nonsense reason like written in english causes less mistakes. we were literally using math symbols for concepts like divisibility. I dont see how written in english would save someone from making silly mistakes other than just wasting time.
Thorner is getting on my nerves. I am starting out with a 3, but we will see how the class continues. It is just so difficult

He posts lecture videos and barely teaches in class. Tests are very difficult (average ~60) and not similar to practice exams at all, but he curves.  Homework is difficult. I spend 20 hours on homework weekly on average. Everything submitted needs to be in LaTeX, including final.  He talks a lot, so don't ask him questions after class, just email.

This class was well structured and easy to understand. He was responsive on Pizza or email if you ever needed to get a hold of him. 10% of his class was drafting your homework and exams in LaTeX, so get ready to spend a bit of extra time learning to do that. The exams were all take home and open note with a 24 hour time period.

Professor Mondak's class was a very negative experience for me. His teaching style often came across as harsh, and I felt that he sometimes singled out students in ways that were uncomfortable or discouraging. Because of this, the course significantly impacted my interest in continuing in Political Science.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Monday is by far the best professor I've ever had. He likes to crack jokes throughout the lectures, which keeps things interesting. This class was only difficult if you didn't show up. If you pay attention and do the readings it's the easiest class ever.

Incredibly knowledgable and the content was very interesting. Often had competitions for extra credit in lecture and was willing to meet outside of call all the time. Do the reading for the MC tests and go to the review sessions before the exam. Occasional in class assignment for points that can't be made up. Take this class.
funniest professor i ever had. i would've invited him to my election party if that wouldn't have been inherently weird

Loved his lecture. He was very funny and there was an abundance of extra credit. Ended the course with a 104%. 

With that said, the readings were extremely dense and he tends to pick out random details to put on the exam. Take notes on everything.

All in all, very fun and worthwhile class but you definitely need to put in some work.

Mondak is by far one of my favorite profs on campus. He makes an effort to make lectures interesting and his dry political humor makes class so much more enjoyable! This isn't a class you can slack on- he doesnt post lecture slides and exams are fairly difficult. Show up and do the readings and you'll do fine though

Professor Mondak genuinely cares about what he is teaching, and if you actually go to lecture you will learn so much. He trys to make lectures as fun as possible and will share (kind of insane) personal anecdotes.

the glorious Jeff Mondak's election class is literally the reason I did not change my major freshman year. you definitely have to read to do well on the exams, but overall the class is well structured, easy to follow, and the papers themselves are very straightforward and easy to pass.

Mondak is a fantastic human being. His exams are fairly hard because you never know what he will put on them, especially from the book. Make sure to take notes of EVERYTHING, even random facts about his life. He calls on people, especially in the first few weeks. Make sure to send your essay drafts to the TA because it will help you a lot.

Fairly easy class, very good and insightful prof with interesting lectures. Only homework is roughly 20 pages of reading a week. 3 exams aren't bad with avg. grades of ~82%. You get choice of prompt on the two essays. Not a class you can blow off but do the work and its pretty easy. Would recommend.

This class was so dull that I never wanted to be there. He tries hard to be funny and goes on tangents while using class time. The test is like taking the SAT; while taking the test, you will doubt your sanity. I don't know why all these reviews are good, but I think he was a boring professor, and the class was boring too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think he is cool.

He defies description. He boxed Mike Tyson in front of the class and shrugged off every blow. He then proceeded to simply stare at Tyson and knocked him out by his sheer presence. There were no disciplinary issues after that.

Everyone was impressed when he walked across the entire United States in 1 day. He came to class the next day and told everyone that they would fail unless they did the same. He then did it again while wearing a praying mantis costume. Truly inspirational.

Extremely interesting content. Awful Professor. Does not post slides so you have to attend class. Does not give feed back on the 2 papers and 3 exams you take (which are your entire grade). Dullest lectures I've ever had but you need to attend cause what he says in lecture (even in passing) can and will be tested on the exams. Do not trust his RMP%
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mondak is super funny and a great lecturer! However, the exams were super tough, especially because it was heavy on the daily readings we had to do, which also happened to be difficult to understand. This class requires heavy studying and preparation. Go to every class, do the readings, and you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a interesting guy, if you are willing to put in the work(lots of it) you should take one of his classes, I just wouldnt take one of his again because of the very tough grading TL:DR: like the guy, tough grader

Professor Mondak is a phenomena that cannot be accurately described through 300 characters. His mere existence made Chuck Norris weep in envy. One time, a tornado hit our area and we were all told to take shelter. But Mondak, having had his lecture interrupted, proceeded to literally blow the tornado away so he could finish. Best professor ever!

Mondak is an accomplished opera singer turned political scientist, which he demonstrates every Friday. In gorgeous operatic tones, he recaps the major lessons from the week. He doesn't just sing the lessons--he performs them with uncommon passion. Although others seemed more impressed with athleticism, we should not overlook his angelic voice.

just came back from mondak's lecture on pushing the bounds of human achievement. it concluded with mondak participating in a steeple chase to demonstrate (successfully) that he can out run and out jump any horse. based on that i would believe anything he says about politics.

a first class intellectual with a dazzling vertical leap. the most impressive thing is that he would combine the two. he would ask us tough question about something like politics. every time we got one right, he would jump over a really tall thing. by one estimate, his vertical leap is something like 70 inches. michael jordan's is 48.
Really wasnt a fan. Disorganized class and a disappoitnting conclusion.

one of the strongest dancers on the political science faculty. although he is not classically trained as a dancer, his raw talent is eye-popping. it also makes for effective teaching. in my intro class, the prof tried to explain the condorcet jury theory 1000 times. mondak taught it 1 time thru interpretive dance. i will remember it now forever

mondak's summer class is a feast for the mind AND a feast for the eye. at first, i was puzzled that the class was scheduled to meet at the beach. but on the first day mondak gave an epic lecture on the problems of american politics in rhinestone covered speedo. not even james madison could rival this display of political prowess.

it is difficult to know if he is a man or a god. especially difficult on fridays because he wears a He-Man costume. take the politics of dance. you will learn a ton from his interpretative dance stylings (especially the dance about money in politics). this guy can really shake it. he earns every dollar. encore! encore!

this was the most demanding course I have ever took. But it made a man out of me. And the feats of strength which are legendary around here lived up to the hipe. i grew up in the yukon and i have seen men wrestle bears and win before. but i have never seen a man dominate a bear like mondak did. bonus points for wearing bedazzled wrestling tunic

mondak's ability to interpret the complexities of politics through performative dance is second to none. i have have seen many poli sci profs here try to convey lessons thru dance and fail hard. not him. also, his dancing demonstrates the dignity and grace that one would expect from a scholar and a gentleman, despite what some may think.

Just completed Mondak's "politics of good and evil" special topics course. it combined biblical wisdom with raunchy Magic Mike style dancing. i noticed on the syllabus that mondak calls himself an endowed chair of political science. after this class i know why.

Mondak looks like he has been cut from stone and stuffed into spandex. He looks like an old school American Gladiator. Just as impressively, when he lectures, his voice sounds just like the Cookie Monster. That takes some getting used to. But he is a gifted lecturer. And he knows so much stuff about politics. Like stuff I had never heard of.

The semester is only half over but this has been one of the most profound experiences of my life. Professor Mondak is a breath taking combination of Konan the Barbarian and Winston Churchill. He has the rippling muscles of Konan and wisdom of Churchill. Good thing it's not the other way around. Especially cuz he wears those buckskin leggings.

I took this class during summer session thinking it would be a breeze.  But on the first day of class, Mondak--aka the Hulk--smashed a two-by-four with his bare hands and screamed "You do not want to mess with the warrior!" Needless to say, there were no discipline problems in the class. he did lighten the mood with jokes and gave great lectures

Mondak defies categorization.  He has both brains and brawn.  He is both a warrior and a diplomat.  He is both beauty and the beast.  His lectures on politics will expand your mind.  His feats of strength will blow your mind.  Imagine a hairless gorilla with opposable thumbs and vast knowledge of politics.  That is Dr. Mondak.

Although many of my classmates were most impressed by some combination of Mondak's bulging muscles, skin-tight buckskin leggings, and mastery of political knowledge, I will remember him most for his soulfulness.  On the last day of class he sang a wistful version of Bob Seager's "Like a Rock."  I cried without shame.

Dr. Mondak goes above and beyond for this students.  When we all showed for class and door to the room was locked, he smashed through the wall like Kool-Aid man.  Then he dusted himself off and led the class in an epic discussion where the United States is headed as a country. He shows us brawn and brains each day and he is a great American.

mondak is an amazing lecturer and strong like a bull.  but i thought the day he carried the refrigerator across campus was a rare miss.  sure it was impressive to see him pick it up over his head and run down the quad with it and then up all those stairs.  but it took like 20 minutes and he has nothing to prove.  nobody doubts his god like power.

the group project was terrible.  i was in a group of 3 and i felt like i was the middle link in a human centipede.  but mondak was awesome.  he juggled bowling balls while lecturing about voting behavior.  he carried a refrigerator across campus and up 4 flights of stairs then taught us about political parties.  he made learning fun.

Mondak's classes are intense but ultimately good for you.  Before spring break, he overheard some of us saying we were not in shape for wearing swimming suits on spring break.  He then made the whole class run in place all class period long the whole week before break.  The class has helped me learn about politics.  I have also lost 12 pounds.

My favorite part of any day of class with Dr. Mondak is that when he make a really good point, he flexes his massive biceps and pounds his chest with pride like a gorilla.    On average, he makes about 5 to 10 really good points EVERY class.  It is impossible to zone out because the flexing and chest pounding keeps everyone really focused.

Dr. Mondak may be strong, speedy, and agile, but it is his lung capacity that impresses me most.  Yesterday, he challenged the whole class to see if anyone could hold their breath longer than him.  The kid next to me lasted the longest.  Then he starting shaking and turning red.  Mondak won easily, inhaled, and then gave a brilliant lecture .

Although Mondak is very, very strong, his speed and agility should not be overlooked.  His feat of strength last week when he rode the unicycle while doing bicep curls with 20 lbs weights is the most impressive thing i have ever seen poli sci professor do.  more impressive still are his lectures and his ability to get class discussion going.

When Dr. Mondak came strutting into the class on the first day wearing that toga, I had my doubts how things would go.  But he not only looks like bodybuilder, he also talks like poet.  He explains things that seem crazy about politics in ways that seem easy to understand.  He demands a lot but he also inspires.  His toga earns him a chili pepper.

Mondak is clearly inspired by the ancient scholars. He began the first week of class by wearing a toga every day.  It works for him.  His lectures are intense and his muscles are too.  The daily feats of strength are a must see.  So are his biceps and his calf muscles.

i was one of the guys he beat in tug of war.  me and other guys on the football team gave it our best.  this guy is just strong.  that got him mad respect from me and everybody. so we payed attention in lectures and red like crazy to get ready for tests.  tough grader.  tough dude.

Mondak provided displays of raw intellect and displays of raw physical power in every class.  His lectures were always insightful and at the end of each class, he performed feats of strength. One time, he challenged 3 large men to a 3 on 1 tug of war and won easily.  He may be the world's strongest political scientist, in every way possible.

There is only one way to describe Professor Mondak.  He is like Hercules and Robin Williams' character from Dead Poet's Society rolled into one.  He has the body of a Greek God and mischievous humor of the guy Robin Williams played in Dead Poet's Society.  All of this helped keep me engaged as we talked about how citizens think and stuff.

Brings a rare combination of qualities for a professor.  Very smart.  Also a tremendous physical specimen.  I sat in the front row, not by choice, but because I was pulled their by the gravity of his intellect.  Also, he has biceps of steel.  You can arm wrestle him for extra credit, but I wouldn't recommend it.  He is strong of mind and of arm.
Highly recommended. Go to class and do the readings. Mondak is an awesome professor. I wish he taught more classes.

The Mondak-Attack is a fantastic professor and a well-deserved recipient of a chair position in PS. He is extremely enthusiastic and knowledgable about the course material. To top it all off, he has one of the best & driest senses of humor. However, the class requires a fair amount of work. Be prepared and absorb the assigned readings. Weekly Quiz.

Be prepared to read and be accountable for all the assigned readings. Quizzes every week, but they are easy if you have read and attended lectures. He is very knowledgeable and helpful though, and is really funny a lot of the time.
He's so funny! Great professor, and the class isn't especially difficult as long as you attend lectures and do the readings. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him.

This class was pretty challenging.  There were quizzes given every other class over the articles read for the week.  The questions were not really straightforward and you definitely needed to understand the article fully. The papers were graded fairly and the class on a whole was graded on a curve.  Interesting prof, very entertaining.
insensitive, elitist
Quizzes were pretty bogus.  They should have been essay instead of MC.  Many answers to quiz questions were not straight forward.  When its MC they should be.

Format of the class are daily quizzes on reading assignments and two papers... Overall, I really appreciated how straight forward this class was. Come to class (the quizzes are used as an attendance check which make up almost half of your grade), do the work, put some effort into your papers and you will be rewarded for it.
He is an amazing prof who actually cares about his students. He is cute in a dorky way and has some CRAZY interesting stories. He is very smart and has a great sense of humor.
GO TO CLASS! Most of his questions are from the book, but he has random questions from lectures on there too. The tests are short, so every question counts!

This class is spectacular. The readings are fun and really interesting, and his lectures really bring it all together. Plus, he is really funny and has done so much interesting work in the field. He is a wonderful teacher and resource.

UMN DNCE 1210. Great Dancer. Not sure if teaching is her strong suit. Yells a lot and very sarcastic about everything, bringing outside stresses into the classroom. My grade on canvas was an A all semester but then she submits a B as my final. I didn't miss a day of class and completed all the assignments on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First dance class I've taken, was perfect for beginners. Really made sure all students in the class felt included :)

I really enjoyed dancing and creating things in this class, but the teacher was catty at times and did not fully explain assignments. I think less sass and more directions would make a huge difference.

Great prof, clear about what are on the tests, and amazing office hours. In my opinion, office hours is the best way to get ahead and reinforce concepts. Best way to prepare for an exam is definitely doing the practice tests. Overall, great prof and great guy.
The greatest professor I've ever had. Attendance is not mandatory, but I highly recommend attending for extra credit. If you are confused, just go to his office hour and he will explain it clearly.

I took ECON 203 when Will was the head TA in the Fall '24 semester, and he did a great job simplifying a lot of the more confusing topics of the class. He's very straightforward with what's on the exam and is good at answering questions. As long as you do well on the homeworks and do all the extra credit assignments, you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: great course
He is a good person, but his exam so hard
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Overall amazing instructor. Teaching style was very engaging and straight to the point. Very candid about what content will/won't be included on exams, and clearly outlines the grading criteria. Attendance is not required, but go for the extra credit. You just need to lock in for lectures to succeed. Made a formerly miserable course enjoyable.
Clean and easy to follow, highly recommended!

Jessie is the best! Absolutley loved ATMS 201, and being a ATMS Minor she is my advisor for that department and she is amazing at that as well! She helped me in class and out of class. I know it says I got a C- but lowkey that's ALL on me. She did everything she could lol I just didnt do my work.
Professor Choate was a very fun and enthusiastic professor. Her lectures were very interesting, and she kept your attention. Also, many extra credit opportunities were given for this course.

She's a really great professor. When you see her name as the instructor when choosing classes, don't overthink it, take it. She's very caring and loves what she does. If you pay attention and do the assigned work, I'm sure you'll get an A.

I love Jesse. She cares about everyone and wants you to succeed. Homework is short and simple. BIGGEST TIP: During class, she will say "write this down" or "star this." Do it. I wrote them all down, made a big quizlet with all of them, and studied only those for exams. They are usually exactly that and I did well on all the tests without dying.

Incredibly easy and well designed course. There is a fair bit of work since it is an 8 week course, but assignments have videos to guide you. Exams while on ProctorU are open note and open lecture videos, so there is no reason to get an A in this course. Also tons of extra credit.

Honestly, I think Professor Choate's lectures were very fun and engaging! I have no background in meteorology and this class was not related to my major so it was nice to learn something new. Professor Choate makes all the deadlines and expectations for her class very clear, just do your work and take advantage of extra credit opportunities!

Super nice professor! Exams are tough but manageable with studying. Lots of extra credit opportunities if you come to lecture. Very knowledgeable about the subject and made me want to take more atmospheric sciences
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love Jessie. I absolutely recommend this course, especially for ATMS majors. Everything is due Monday and so you structure your week yourself. SO much extra credit it's difficult not to get at least an A. It is a good amount of work (usually 8 hours a week) but it's simple.
