Help videos on every math/excel sheet that basically give you the answers.

This is my first online class I've taken, so I don't have much to compare it to, but I loved this class. Other reviews are heavily exaggerating the course load (imo), but this is an 8-week course, so expect to have to work more and faster. Has help videos for every math problem on the problem sets. Lots of extra credit got me from a B to an A-

DO NOT TAKE! There are like 3 lectures per week and each lecture there's like 3 separate videos that are like 30 minutes each (4.5 hours) and then there's readings, on top of that there's a midterm and a final but during the midterm week she still assigned the normal course load and I was struggling mentally and sent an email and she ignored it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the course isn't necessarily difficult, the amount of expected work is extremely unreasonable. Even with playing the pre-recorded lecture videos at 2x speed, a week's worth of assignments can easily take 8-10 hours of work. It's not hard to get a good grade, but the devotion it takes is laughable given the context of this course.

ATMS 120 is great for non-stem students looking for a science+math gen ed (Science & Quant 2). It's super easy and Professor Choate offers an insane amount of extra credit and provides step by step instructions for every math question. Only issue is that she tells you to buy an expensive textbook but we never used it, so don't bother buying.

Great, engaging lectures. SO much extra credit, would technically have a B but because of EC earned an A. There is a textbook but is completely optional, I didn't buy it and was completely fine. She posted weekly lab help videos that went step by step through all math. Highly recommend!!

Offers tons of extra credit, covering a subject that is both interesting and useful. 

She is exceptionally knowledgeable and passionate about the topic, delivering what are truly the best lectures ever.

Small class teaching, attendance not required, but attending can earn a lot of extra credit and guidance. 

Relatively challenging material, but the grading is fair. 

Extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, gives the best lecture ever.

She is sooo super sweet. So much extra credit, I never did too hot on the labs but am able to still get a good grade because there is many many opportunities for extra credit. This is a great option for your science and quantitate reasoning gen eds.
She has amazing energy and gives out a lot of extra credit

Truly the best professor I have had at Illinois. Super caring for her students and was always there to help me out during office hours. Gives so much extra credit (All the answers are in the textbook but it is not needed as you can find them on quizlet). Do yourself a favor and take this class, its amazing.

Professor Choate is absolutely phenomenal. Even in an extremely large lecture she never failed to ensure that everyone was able to keep up and understand the content. The class itself can be challenging at times but is relatively easy. You're mainly graded on weekly labs with 3 unit tests (non-cumulative). Choate is one of the best profs I've taken
SOOOO much extra credit. Do yourself a favor and take this class. The labs are kind of annoying but they're fairly easy. Exams are all multiple choice and study guides are very thorough.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Jessie is amazing. If your looking for an easy A Quant. 2 course, look at ATMS 120. Its lecture heavy (no discussion sections), but the workload is light and the lectures are engaging. LOTS of extra credit (over 100%), tests are incredibly easy, and she walks you through every lab question. Little to no math, only on the labs. Plus you learn a lot.

This class is an easy quant 2 credit. Jessie gives lab help videos for all of the labs that take you through it step by step, even the Excel parts. Labs take about 2 hours to do. Lectures are 1 1/2 hours but she always finishes early, the longest lecture has been just over an hour. She points out iClicker questions that are test questions as well.

Best prof ever! She walks you through all of the math, best way to get QR credit! Exam reviews explain everything. She recognizes this is a gen ed for almost everyone, and focuses on making sure we get the credit and learn that is useful outside the class. It is obvious how much she cares. Extra credit can bring up your grade by a full letter!

One of the best professors at this school. I took it over the summer in 4 weeks. There are 4 labs and thats it. Took about the whole day to finish all lectures for a given unit, take notes, and complete a lab. Missed the first one because of a family emergency and she let me turn it in a few days late. Also rounded up my 89. The math is fine.

She is passionate about her class and makes lectures entertaining! The only drawbacks are the lab reports which the math is challenging at times. However her help videos have helped me understand the math portion, she is active on forums too!. Tons of extra credit opportunities, if you aren't taking advantage of them then your grade will tank.

Professor Choate is one of the best professors I've encountered so far. She's really funny. Literally gives away the answers to exam questions if you participate and engage. Since the course is asynchronous, it will require a lot of work on your own time.

Was alot of work for a gen ed 100 level course. You have to do a lab every week which is very time consuming. All her TA's grade her work, so it depends how tough they grade. Overall, I wished I chose another course.

Professor Choate is fine, but the class was unreasonably hard. You have to know how to use Excel very well, which I did not know. Lots of extra credit, but doesn't make up for the other work. Do not take this class unless you are literally so good at excel and math.

Prof. Choate assigns an unreasonable amount of work. I took her course the second half of the semester, and she was still making us watch lectures during finals week. For a 100-level gen ed course, devoting 10+ hours a week to lectures, labs, and studying was way too much to ask. Lectures seemed like they could have been shorter, same with labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Choate is amazing. The course is a lot of work but you get used to it. Great gen ed option. There is no math on the exams, only concept-based. The weekly labs have math but she has so many office hours. She also creates online Q&A forums. Tons of extra credit, up to 5% bump on overall grade.

This 8-week class is graded based on 2 (open-note, open book) exams and 7 labs, which is great if your notes are complete. Labs are math-heavy and you should be prepared to have your math skills challenged. However, you can supplement with easy extra credit, including freebie points if you pay attention to emails and watch the weekly review videos!

Lectures are pretty long but that's mostly because you have to watch them online. Tons of extra credits so no reason to get a super bad grade. Prof. Choate is very helpful and very active on discussion boards to answer questions.

Great prof, always there to help you out when you need it but for a 100 level gen ed, this class is unnecessarily difficult. Exams extremely hard and proctored. Labs difficult but again, she walks you through tough parts and has a lot of help available. Even though material was somewhat interesting, wayy too much time spent on a Gen Ed.

I took this class for honors credit and found it very interesting. There is some math and involved but the professor and TAs will walk you through it with examples. I learned a lot about Excel in this class. The lectures were very enjoyable and iClickers are used for participation grade.

I took this course as a gen ed course in person thinking it was gonna be easy. The exams were always super hard and I failed them all. The labs were okay but there was a lot of math on them and they were graded pretty hard.

Professor Choate was great despite the bad ratings I read on here before. There was an insane amount of extra credit and she gave videos + q&as to clear any concerns. Honestly a pretty easy class. Some labs were harder than others but nothing insane. Just dont leave labs till last moment and youll be good.

Having taking the class online, all materials were clearly organized, and she was very open to questions and always elaborated when needed. Labs can be done fairly easily as long as you pay attention during lectures; she gives all the information in a clear format and communicates her expectations clearly.

The class was fully online, but everything was organized well enough so I could find whatever material I needed. She understands a lot of students take this class for the Quant. II requirement and tries her best to make sure nobody is left behind. Overall, she's overall very affable and approachable, even if the class itself wasn't the easiest. :)

This professor is an expert in her profession and is super interested in what she studies, however, this class was extremely difficult. It includes a lot of mathematical prowess and I had to spend hours googling how to do the math because her explanations didn't help much. The lectures are super boring too. She tries to help and EC helps though.

Jessie is very passionate about teaching, and is clear about grading. The labs take awhile (longer than the 2 hours she says), but they're relevant to the course and helped me understand the material. If you have any issues, she is quick to reply and posts weekly help videos for the labs. The videos can drag on, but its a great class I'd recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Posts videos of the lectures and doesn't do anything. you have to teach yourself everything. all the homework (labs) are all pointless busy work that have nothing to do with the class. like why do I have to find how many hail reports there were in 2019, who cares. such a waste of time. if you put in 650 hours into this class, you'll get an A

Lots of homework/ labs and very long lectures, but overall the material was very easy. If you don't do too well on the tests there's a lot of easy extra credit quizzes you can take that will heavily boost your grade. Professor Choate is also very easy to work with in respect to late work/ technical issues.

Fall 2020, COVID semester, 8 week course completely asynchronous. Two big tests (online proctario but open note + open internet). Most of rest of grade is labs, work with other people and you'll be fine. Spent abt six hours weekly on the lab, would've been easier if I watched the lectures maybe. DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. Office hours if you need help!!

For this semester, the class was 8-week long so lots of material per week but Jessie is a GEM and her lectures are very interesting! It clearly shows that she's passionate about the course content and she cares about her students. There is a lab and discussion due every week that take some time. Don't buy the textbook. TONS OF EXTRA CREDITS!!!

She is not as bad as some people say she is. She does care about teaching, even though I personally do not find the materials very interesting. This semester exams only make up 45% of the total grades and during COVID-19 she decided to let us do open-note exams and that really helped. I got away with an A by mostly reading the lecture slides.

I really liked this professor, she was super nice and helpful. There's a lab due every week. Definitely attend lectures, there's always multiple i-clicker points. Exams aren't too hard if you take notes during lectures (slides are also posted on compass) and do the study guides. This is also coming from a non atms major.

Boring and bubbly lectures that are not worth your time. Could easily just pass this class with google. Couldnt explain anything - but does fill in the blank science. Take this class if you dont care about learning.

I heard this class was an easy A so I expected to spend most of my time in lecture zoning out, but Jessie is a gem! She has a lot of passion for the subject material which makes lectures very entertaining. Tons of easy extra credit available and Jessie is very approachable & knowledgable. Just don't buy the textbook for ATMS120 and you'll love it.

Lots of extra credit opportunities, most of which require just a Google search (making the textbook pointless). She's a newer professor, but gives excellent lectures, clearly cares about her students & the subject, and honestly was amazing. This class was definitely a highlight, and she's one of the best professors/lecturers I've had.

She's very helpful and communicative, good at what she does. Course design isn't great as often you are only taught the surface level of a concept in lectures, then the TAs don't do much to help you go deeper. Then your tests often test you on the hardest version of the concept. Lots of self study, but she is very helpful if you need it too.
Very nice person. Gave solid lectures. Explained topics pretty well. She did put a midterm right after winter break which kinda sucked but besides that I have no complaints.

Good lecturer, but our last midterm that was worth 25% of our grade was placed two days after returning from fall break. There was a badly timed snowstorm that caused chaos at airports and displaced many students. We were told that if we couldn't make it because of the weather, we would receive a 0. This was very disappointing and just a bad call.

She's normally very nice, but my one complaint is that we had a test right after fall break and there was a historically bad snowstorm. So many flights were cancelled and impossible to rebook until after the exam. When I emailed her about this, she said that weather isn't a valid reason to miss the exam, and if I couldn't make it I would get a 0.
Gives clear lectures. Nice person

Jenny is an overall attentive professor. She cares about individual students and their concerns, taking time after class to answer questions and replying to emails promptly. During lectures, she is detailed with her explanations and encourages questions. Your grade from this class weighs less on Jenny and more on who your TA is.

really nice professor, her class covers most of the materials, and very easy to understand. also, the test are very related to the material on the class, and even easy than the homework, even though it cannot use calculator. Moreover, she is also willing to answer students questions after class. I will definitely take that class again

This professor was nice, but extremely hard to work with. Her TA's are the most stingiest graders of all time, they have some sort of addiction with seeing you make mistakes. She doesn't go through many examples in the lectures so you will prepare with teaching yourself a good portion of the material. (TA just stood in the corner and never taught).
She is overall a great professor but moves very fast during lectures and explains things well but doesn't go over things. Be ready for a lot of homework and the tests are challenging!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She makes the work outside of class a lot harder than what is done in class and when asked about blames the TAS FOR US NOT KNOWING when it is her job to TEACH US

Overall a tough class, Srikant is a pretty solid professor and makes sure that students understand what's going on in lecture. Hoffemister replaced for Srikant towards the end of the semester, and gave us better explanations than Srikant. Regardless, whichever professor you get is a great professor and most TAs are solid. Exams are pretty hard.

Professor Srikant is a great professor with organized lecture notes and clear explanations. The difficulty however with this class is namely the course structure and tests, which are often very conceptual heavy rather than computational, so you need to make sure you understand concepts at a fundamental level. Do the math 415 practice tests.

Srikant does a good job of navigating the more abstract concepts in linear algebra, and she was always really good with answering questions. Her lecture notes were very organized and well put together, very easy to study from later on. Highly recommend
Honestly best professor you could possibly get for this course.

Srikant did a pretty good job of explaining concepts during her lectures. She also provided helpful examples whenever someone had a tough time understanding. The exams aren't crazy difficult, and it covers topics covered in class. I've taken calculus in the past and I hated it, but Srikant surprisingly helped me enjoy it :)
Highly recommend!

Professor Srikant is amazing. While the class may be difficult, she always asks if students are understanding material and explains things very clearly. She is very easy to reach outside of class and super understanding. She does not take attendance during lectures, but they are very important to attend because the class is rather fast-paced.

About 15-20% of the lectures are Theories and conceptual topics, the rest is computation. The homework is almost all computation. Yet the exams are about 80% conceptual with tons of trick questions to try to throw you off. They also throw a python question on the exam, so if you don't know how to do it you automatically lose 15% off of your exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jenny was an amazing professor and her lectures were very easy to follow. She made sure everyone was well prepared for exams and the grading policies for homework and exams were extremely fair.

I would say the material from 220 is not too hard for me from the beginning, but she did a great job explaining every step to make students understand how to solve questions. Example questions and some discussion questions are very similar to the exam questions, and the only hard part of this course is just the practice questions from discussion.

Ms. Srikant was by far one of the best math professors I have ever had. She taught so well and made lectures interesting and easy to understand. I never expected to love calculus, but I did after taking her class. I highly recommend taking sections with her if possible. :))

When I took calculus in high school, I spent hours sobbing over how difficult a concept was for me to grasp, and then never got it. When I took calculus with Ms. Srikant, I understood those same concepts the first time she explained them. Her extra review sessions for exams were super helpful, and extra credit for doing HW early was a lifesaver

Ms. Srikant was an amazing professor! Originally, I REALLY struggled in the class but I ended up improving a lot in the class. She does really good at preparing you to the best of her ability for their exams, and if you have a bad TA like I did, extra individual work along with her office hours is best. Highly recommend her if you have MATH220!

Makes every lecture 100% worth attending by being super helpful. If you are struggling with understanding something during a lecture, you can easily ask a question and she will explain it. She also hosts review sessions the week of every midterm and before finals week.

reviews.comment: The way she teaches is very thorough and her office hours were amazing
Highly recommend, she was the best math teacher I've had here and her class was interesting!!

Very sweet and helpful professor who knows her stuff and has a very well laid out class. Each lecture clearly covers 1 or 2 topics, and she explains it very well. Notes are provided at the beginning of each class, so just follow along with those and everything makes sense. Exams are questions straight from lecture/homework.

Such a sweet and caring professor! She treats everyone so highly and respects as if youre her colleague not a student which is also so amazing!!! Such a kind person and genuinely cares about her work and her students
Easiest class of my life. take online.
Literally the easiest class. Just need to do a few things on Sundays. Take this online!!!!!

By far the easiest BUS class you will ever take at Gies. She is the sweetest professor and very caring, and the class isn't that boring. Take this class when you have a heavy course load and need an easy A, or if you just want to socialize

Very good class structure, took as a winter class, expect maybe ~3 hours of work a week which is super great for a winter class. Pretty cool lecture videos, lots of great TED talks, HW is pretty easy and simulations are pretty interesting and fun. Professor is very nice, very great class

Professor Ji has given us such a great introduction to the world of consulting through BUS 301 and really focuses on the success of each group's client presentations and overall project roadmap. She is very approachable for receiving feedback and is also very helpful throughout the midpoint and final client calls. Overall, I learned a lot.

B301 totally depends on your client for how much work you have, but Ji is the sweetest and most caring instructor I have had at UIUC. She is one of the few teachers here who I actually believe cares about the well-being of students. The in-class activities can seem like a waste of time but the class is an easy A even if your client sucks so no hate
very good

The professor is very great. She explains things well. This course is about group work, and there are extra credits if your group did not perform well. There is book reading and quizzes before class; it's courses requirement for all profs.

reviews.comment: Jeff is a very passionate and knowledgeable professor regarding negotiations. While he is extremely knowledgeable, there are times when much of what he seeks from planning documents, takeaways, etc., can be vague and hard to understand. Definitely not an easy A, but a worthwhile course that most students should take and will learn a lot from.

reviews.comment: Loewenstein knows his stuff, cares deeply about the subject, and is a skilled, engaging lecturer. He breaks down readings into real-world applications and runs a phenomenal classroom. He's eloquent, quick-thinking, and matches your effort. Even if participation makes you nervous, take this course—you'll grow. One of the best professors I've had.

Teacher certainly has the passion, but unfortunately that doesn't quite translate when it comes to the quality and consistency of tests and exams. The exams and quizzes are written in a way to trick you. I was very excited for this class on creativity, but the course soured not only my impression of the teacher, but of the MBA program as a whole.

reviews.comment: He's got the passion but yaps a lot and goes off topic. Such few grades, lack of preparation for exam and strange, possibly capricious grading. I would also make sure to bring other work. Take it with literally anyone else.

Loewenstein is very passionate about his subject, but the delivery can suffer. Extremely few assignments are graded, and your grade can tank if you mess up even once. Unclear all the way through. Do not take him.

Unfair expectations, always responded to questions with questions, unclear about what to get done and expectations and was very rude to some students if they needed extra help. He expected everyone to understand his instruction the very first time and have no questions or clarifications.

live session quizzes  nearly 20% of grade, you will nearly fail the class on something as absurd as which example clarified the concept to you which did not align with the professor intention for the example.

Superb teacher. Have taken two graduate level classes with him, and have learned loads.

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor! Very insightful, gives great feedback, and actually helps and cares about the students. Course material was made very interesting and very memorable. I actually learned a lot and retained the information.
First time I have ever used this site. One of my favorite teachers at U of I. Fun topic, and he inspires you to do your best. Very engaging.

By far, one of the most rewarding classes I have taken at this school. In class negotiations are fun and there aren't a lot of take home assignments. Loewenstein is a generous grader and is interested in your ideas rather than writing ability (which helps a lot for international students). Definitely a class I looked forward to each week.

The expectations of students are very high and each are critically evaluated on participation in class. There are many writing assignments which are graded hard. Definitely not a class to take just for fun.
Good teacher
Extremely intelligent and well spoken. Definitely makes an impact.
His grading is very very subjective and be careful if you ask him to explain things further as he may get very annoyed. He only has one office hour because apparently he is very busy.

This was probably one of the best classes and professors I encountered during my first MBA year at U of I.  The professor challenges you and your peers to think about original solutions for hard to solve problems.  Overall great class and great professor.
Great prof, learned a bunch!
He's always well prepared for class.

His teaching style is not great at all. Also the course lacks some structure and application. There is so much content but not enough time to really learn anything being taught. He stares at the screen the entire time and his English is not great

bad lecturer, clearly unprepared, incomprehensible notes and never looks up in the class. Only stares in the screen and gives the whole lecture like that.

Josephine was amazing! She was very kind and really understanding. She wants all her students to do well and is always there to help if you are struggling. You have homework every day, but it's super simple and doesn't take that long. The quizzes aren't that hard as long as you study and practice every day.
while also quite challenging I definitely learned a lot.

She is genuinely the sweetest professor I have ever had. All you have to do is pay attention and come to class and she will help you as much as she can. She is also a very caring grader. There is homework everyday but it take 5 minutes max.

Professor Karkafi is so kind and her class is always very chill and a good vibe. She gives extra credit on tests and is in general super helpful. If you want to be successful in her class you must attend every class! Also make sure not to get behind on your homework as she assigns a lot.

Josephine is such a sweet lady! She truly cares about her students and does everything she can to help them. It's obvious that she wants her students to do well; a very easy (but fair) grader. She gives review guides for every test and quiz. Lots of extra credit too! There is a lot of HW, but it helps reinforce the material and it's not difficult.
She was really kind even though I was struggling in class. Helped me through a lot of stuff when adapting to another textbook!

The class loved the teacher, she was really nice, let me take a test at a different time, and wanted everyone to succeed. For me it was an easy class because it starts from absolute zero (I had known how to read and speak a teeny bit), but if you're just starting out I think the level is perfect. She's awesome. Do the homework, its not that hard.

Honestly the best professor I've ever had. As long as you're learning, she will give you a good grade because she concerns herself with you understanding the content instead of focusing completely on whether you missed a deadline or not. She is always available to help outside of class and will take the time to focus on every student.

She's such a sweet professor and she really cares about every single student.  She's super helpful in her lectures, and answers questions very clearly.  I always feel comfortable asking her questions outside of class, and she's always very willing to help.  She wants everyone to succeed in her classes.  She's amazing!
She will be the most helpful asset if you are taking Arab 201 .. Great transition to my next course. Thank you!
Worst guy in the dept. There must be an efficient way to teach the topics. Some assignments feel like torture and repetitive.
John Popovics was always exciting to listen to and clear notes to follow.

If you need to take CEE 300, you should take it with Prof. Popovics. However, you need to be going to TA office hours IMMEDIATELY after the first lab to get your lab reports checked over. These labs are a whole different level of grading and you need to be hitting the ground running. His lectures are extremely engaging and extremely useful.
The WORST guy in the whole CEE department. Never try his course if it's not mandatory.

Professor sucked and was very particular about everything, beyond the labs which took off any points they could, the professor just had that "I'm better than you" vibe and was extremely boring. Tests were memorization based and slides lacked information that was necessary. He did not post answer keys for study material. Comparable to Lucas Wagner.

I loved the professor, the lectures were engaging and the material was presented well, and he offered help outside of class. I hated the grading because it's entirely up to the discretion of the TA and expectations aren't always clear or consistent.

The course material wasn't that bad. The only problem that I gave a 2/5 is the ridiculous unclear instructions grading system. Lectures are fun, but LABs are terrible. TA's gave me a 82 on draft, and a few improvement ideas. While I followed their feedbacks and made changes to my revised draft, my grade dropped to 75. It's unhelpful and unfair.

I've busted my butt in CEE 300 not once, but twice, dragging myself back every semester, hoping for a TA who's got a bit of mercy in their grading. But guess what? Nada. Zero. Popovics is a teaching legend and the course content isn't the worst, but that doesn't save my grade from getting tanked in his TA's writing section, absolutely infuriating!
crazy amount of work, very strict grading on open ended questions..

CEE300 is one of the most time consuming classes you will have to take, despite that Popovics is the absolute best professor to teach this class. Make sure you go to office hours for labs and HW as they will guide you to the grade you want in the class. Additionally before exams go to popovics office hours and ensure you know all the material.

While CEE 300 was easily one of the most difficult classes I have ever taken, I would take it semester after semester with professor Popovics. He is very understanding and clearly cares about the students.

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had.  He made everything interesting and explained very well.  The labs are the only bad part about this class.

Great teacher.  He knows exactly what he's talking about and knows how to explain it well.  He is also very strict when it comes to grading.  This class is 4 credits but requires a level of work on par with a 6 credit course.

He is one of the best lecturer's I have ever had, and he is really good if you meet with him one on one. Always very good at responding to emails etc. You will learn a lot but the grading is ridiculous and your grade will likely not reflect what you know.

Great lecturer. Slides posted online. 1 HW problem due every lecture, but it really helps you keep up with the material. Asks questions before and during lecture to make sure the concepts are getting through. He comes off douchy at times but sometimes it's funny. The hardest part of this class is putting in the time.
Hard, time consuming class but overall a great professor to learn from. Labs and Homeworks have a much larger weight than tough exams. No cumulative final.
Really paranoid professor and A LOT of work for class. HW due every class and Lab Reports are a nightmare!

Extremely strict and tells graders to be strict. Takes off points for everything he can. Homework due every lecture (3 times a week). Boring. Just a jerk in general. If the other professors suck, I still wouldn't take this guy's class.
Nice cool professor ever. only this that is annoying is his paranoid attitude toward report plagiarism.
Fantastic instructor but difficult and time-consuming course
professor who thinks he knows it all and is really rude and mean to students and behaves like a jerk

Fantastic professor, knows what he is talking, demands respect, funny, helpful, though unless the TA's are grading too tough don't expect points back on stuff, usually you don't deserve it anyways, lab reports area hard as are the  exams just get ahold of paste exams and they will help a lot for studying purposes

lab grading is pretty tough, tricky exams but a great professor makes up for it, he seems annoying at first but grows on you and you will soon enjoy his class + lab is actually interesting its only the reports that are tough
Tremendous teacher. Hard exams, though.

Very knowledgeable professor, knows exactly what he's talking about. Tests are pretty hard, homeworks are anal just like any other TAM related class. Class is very well structured and you learn a lot of material. Funny and down to earth with students.
Good lectures but hard tests

Professor Slauch cares a lot about what he teaches, and he has the knowledge to back it up. However, I would warn students to take MCB 250 during a lighter semester. The time you are able to spend studying this course will directly correlate to how well you do on exams. If you have a rigorous schedule, it will be difficult to do well in MCB 250.

reviews.comment: Tough class, but Slauch is clearly very knowledgeable. Exams are complicated. iClicker is used for attendance. There are videos before class, but he reinforces the material in session so it is valuable to attend.

He's great. Pre-lecture videos are a great help and he makes sense of a lot of difficult concepts and processes. His section of the class is the toughest, but he still does a good job of making sense of the material, which is a nice contrast from MCB 150 where I had to rewind a ridiculous amount of times to gain understanding.

test questions were often a lot more in depth than what he goes over in lecture. grading of the class is harsh, there is not a single test retake or drop. you get 3 discussion drops and 1 quiz drop. only one attempt on all the online quizzes. homework has unlimited attempts but it doesn't tell you your score which is useless
Big fan of this guy. Good lecturer -- made me realize that biology is interesting after I bored my way through MCB150. Tests aren't easy but very doable if you put in the time and effort.

Controversial professor that has some people liking and not liking him. Regardless, fair with his teaching and grading. And everything really is from his VCast videos. His lecture feels more like Q&A that ends early. Personally I loved Dr. Slauch as he is awesome professor that is really passionate so Go to his office hour with prepared question.

Very challenging exams, but everything on the exams came from somewhere on the slides. There isn't really any tricks, just a lot of information. His vcasts are the main lectures while the in-person mostly feels supplementary. He mostly does read off of slides, but this is one of the few times that is for your benefit, as it keeps the info concise.

Dr. Slauch was a difficult professor.His exams weren't always the most reflective of lectures and discussion material, as they were usually much harder. After you make it through the second exam (the hardest one) you should be fine. Although this class was challenging, I found the material interesting.

Very good lectures, very fast paced but the lecture videos make up for that. He teaches you everything you need to know for the exams, so as long as you pay attention and take good notes, you shouldn't be surprised by what you see at all on the exams.

If he ever says "We're not gonna worry about that" during a lecture, it will 1000% be on the exam. He breezes over minuscule details that he will make over complicated questions about on the exams. He's not an amazing lecturer so focus and read what he glazed over in lecture slides for the more specific information that will be on the exam.
wish he held office hours. he's clearly knowledgeable about the subject. the way the class is set up it doesn't promote learning in person and the exams are extremely difficult
Biology is tough
Solid professor, knows his stuff.
Professor Slauch is an amazing professor who teaches MCB 250 in a clear and straightforward manner. The course is test-heavy but if you ask questions during lectures you will do well.
Dr. Slauch is an amazing professor and is able to explain details extremely well. However, MCB 250 is a very difficult class, so it is really up to the students to study for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Slauch is one of the most well-respected professors who teach MCB courses. His lectures are concise and there are long Q and A sessions afterward. The tests make up 75% of the grade but they are manageable if you make sure to pay attention to every tiny detail and write everything down.

The class itself is difficult, but Professor Slauch does his best to explain material clearly. The lectures are super helpful, and he goes in depth on each slide instead of just reading off the slides. Make sure you record his lectures - they're super useful. Overall, Slauch does an excellent job making this difficult class easier.
Fun and very knowledgeable. Tough grader though.

Dr Slauch is an excellent professor! He really makes the material accessible and easy to understand, and he's a hilarious and entertaining lecturer. The course requires a lot of studying and effort, but Dr Slauch is always readily available and happy to help students.
Great lecturer. He makes the material interesting but he isn't always clear on what is going to be on the exams which can be pretty tough.

Professor Slauch is amazing!! Truly one of the best MCB professors at U of I. His criteria is clear and easy to follow. Attend lectures, put in the effort, and you will get an A. Don't cram and follow along with every lecture. He's not an easy A professor, but he made the class so interesting. I wish he taught more MCB classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Slauch was very nice and cared about his students.  I always went to office hours and he would go over anything that I would ask about and beyond.  He is very knowledgable about the field of genetics. He is also a medical school professor and would be a great reference in the future for some students.

His lectures are engaging and concise; he lets you know what you need to know for exams and what is just supplementary detail on the subject. He puts complicated concepts into colloquial terms, so it's beneficial to pay close attention during his lectures. He only tests on material covered in lecture/discussion; there should be no surprises.

Dr. Slauch is hands down the best MCB professor at U of I! You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and is so knowledgable when it comes to the microbiology field . He makes lectures engaging with his enthusiastic descriptions! His exams are definitely challenging, but its stimulating and you actually learn the material!

Dr.  Slauch is a great professor. You can clearly tell  he is passionate about what he lectures. Students sometimes get mad because he makes the exams difficult. All he is trying to do is make you work hard for an A in the class. If you put time into it and go to office hours, do a little work on this class every day, you can get a decent grade (A)

Slauch is cool. He's a good teacher. He's also very good at writing exams. They'll be very in depth and tricky, but if you study enough you can do well on them. It's a challenging class but it's manageable.

Dr. Slauch is great. Very energetic speaker with a sharp sense of humor. He's the perfect cool scientist :). This class requires a lot of studying and critical thinking, but that's to be expected in college, folks. If you put in a lot of work, you're going to get a grade you want and you will enjoy this class :).

He is an okay professor. He is not a good speaker/lecturer, and the material itself is difficult. Also, this is a weed out class, so there are things that are unnecessarily difficult, like the homework. His tests aren't bad, but I prefer Dr. Farrand's tests because Dr. Slauch uses awkward wording. Also, Dr. Slauch asks really picky questions.

His tests are easier than Farrand's but still require a lot of work.  Be sure to do well on the first test because a lot of it is review of 150.  Go to office hours every week for homework and find a group of friends to work on homework/quizzes with.  Slauch is a great professor but the material is very difficult.

He has a very awkward smile. He is easy to understand and keeps your attention well. Not boring. His exams are easier than Farrand's but they still require detailed studying. Record the lectures. Do it. Book is not very important. He has many office hours and he is overall a very nice guy. Waves to me from his car when he sees me.

Slauch wasn't a bad teacher, but the course was really poorly run by the course coordinator, and therefore miserable. He's very clear during lecture. Pay attention in lecture and don't skip class because the book is worthless.
Very hard class; he's difficult to follow.

not gonna lie..slauch is hot..haha but seriously he's hot..in addition to that useful info..slauch was a great teacher/hot..his teaching style was very clear..he kept us engaged during class and he is always available for extra help..his exams were challenging but with enough hard work..an A is very much possible to achieve/he's hot

Slauch was a really good prof. He made the lectures very engaging and if you get the chance to talk to him after class, you will see that he's the nicest guy. He's always smiling when he explains things to you. You can tell he really loves MCB. Fine, his tests weren't the easiest but if you paid attention in class and studied, you should be fine.
Professor Slauch was clear and held your attention.  He was also fair and very approachable.  Not the easiest class, but you can do well.  He was much better than Farrand

Really good lecturer. You can really succeed in this class if you take good notes (or buy a recorder if you tend to miss things) and learn every detail of the powerpoints. Slauch does not try to trick you on tests- they are directly from what he talked about in lecture.
Homework was very difficult. Little details much more important than big concepts....for some reason.

Good lecturer, and he makes you understand the concepts. Too bad the tests and homework do not reflect these concepts, but instead see if you can remember miniscule details instead of key points. The tests are impossibly hard. If you thought you could take MCB 250 AND still have a life, you are sadly mistaken. Pre-meds, prepare to be weeded out.
Terribly hard class, The homework is not at all reflective of the exams. No practice exams to help guide you. Terrible.

This is probably one of four difficult MCB/Pre-med classes you'll take. Slauch is a good teacher, but his exams are a difficult. I recommend you get a recorder and tape the lectures & listen to them before tests. Falling asleep in class is easy and very detrimental to your grade...buy a recorder, go to discussion, study hard and you'll be fine.
He writes some of the toughest exams I've ever taken at U of I

He definately knows what he's talking about, very intelligent man. Easy-going guy, not too strict. I think he explains with good clarity, but the class definately takes a lot of work on the student's part. He's not as friendly to students as some other professors I have had, but overall a good and competent professor.

This is a tough class, especially if you aren't planning on going to med school, then it's just plain ridiculous.  Slauch is definately better than Farrand, he definately knows his material but space out for a minute in class and you are in trouble.
Tests aren't that bad if you pay attention in class.

I think he's very helpful although sometimes his lectures can get boring and complex.  He's definitely a better professor than Dr. Farrand.  When you attend his office hours, he'll help you until you understand the material.
He is actually interesting and he is easy to understand and take notes with unlike dr.farrand...his jokes aren't that bad

he knows his material and laughs at his own bio-related jokes.  he comes off kinda harsh, but is actually a pretty funny guy.  he's clear about what's on the exams. he's not as bad as everyone here thinks
Its quite obvious that he doesn't want to be lecturing, and is only here for research.
Professor Frink from the Simpsons, anyone?
This guy is impossible.  He is boring, his slides have no information on them, and the test are hard.
he's funny

Such a brilliant professor, she is one of the rare professors who is both very brilliant and has a very deep understanding of the materials she is teaching while having a great teaching capability and communicate the subjects in a manner that is very easy to understand.

Her lectures were very nice, and she was overall very enthusiastic and helpful during and outside the lecture. She was very accessible outside the lecture as well. It was one of the classes I looked forward to going to.

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had. Made me fall in love with the world of Mathematics again; suddenly, going to lectures was fun again. I couldn't help but smile during her lectures. Her office hours are really helpful and attentive. Overall, great class, great person, much love and care.
really really nice professor. Respond to emails super fast.

One of the most kind and genuine people I've ever met! She really cares about her students; her office hours were extremely helpful, and she always seemed very excited and willing to answer questions about any math. She has a contagious passion for math-- I couldn't help but smile during lecture, and I learned so much from her. Highly recommended!

Very attentive and cares a lot about her students. Responds to emails very quickly with detail and great advice to help students improve. Office hours are great and personal, and asking questions is key to the class. The textbook helps and its content is used in class. Homework is essential for exam prep and lectures are very well taught.

There is a lot of extra credit in this class, and the material itself is not that diffcult. The only annoying part is that a bulk of your grade is the midterms, so I'd go to class until after the 3rd midterm. At that point you'll have enough extra credit for an easy A.
Amazing and sweet-hearted. Genuine, wish I had visited more in Office Hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Loved her class. Was not difficult at all, and all the review you really needed to do for her exams was going through the slide shows, and even then most of it was common sense. Lectures were not mandatory but she gives out extra credit for attending them. She also would increase your grade on the write-ups as long as you could justify why!

Great teacher, very fair and does what she teaches. Really early class but attendance isn't mandatory (you get extra credit though) and the lectures are recorded. You get a notes sheet for the exams and she lets you use Chatgpt for papers as long as you acknowledge it. Very fair teacher and I enjoyed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor White is so charismatic and sweet. The class was enjoyable despite the heavy amount of content, she explains the connections between topics very well. This was one of my favorite courses I've taken at UIUC, mostly because of Professor White's teaching methods and care for the class. Highly recommend!
really care about student. Kind and warm teacher.

Amazing class and professor! I learned a lot in this class and I can use this information in my future careers. The professor is really knowledgable and caring and talks about current events which are also interesting. The exams and homework assignments weren't too hard if you go to the lectures or look over the slides that are posted. Great class!

This class is very hard and you have to put in a lot of work to succeed. But Shapland gave lots of tips on how to do well in the class, and if you follow her tips you will do well. Biggest thing is going to all the lectures. Its easy to fall behind and very hard to catch up. But she is very nice and explains everything very clearly

didn't feel respected and she wasn't good at delivering clear instructions or content. The class was made harder than it actually should be. wasn't helpful during office hours, tests are too tricky, doesn't help students succeed, will NOT take any one of her classes again

ACCY 202 is a class meant for hard work and practice. This professor goes above and beyond to make the concepts clear, and she is so accessible outside class.

Not as bad as some make her/the class out to be. The grading criteria is confusing so I suggest reading the syllabus heavy at the beginning of the semester. ACCY 202 is not that bad. The grading is incredibly fair as exams are fairly curved and plenty of extra credit is given, even just for going to lecture.
