Professor Shapland is really a super professor. She can meet the criteria of a "university professor". Remember to treat lectures, discussions, and homework seriously because those powerpoints are really helpful. Go to her office hour, and you can find her great passion for the subject. Finally, this course is not easy, but do not lose confidence.

Professor Shapland is very accessible to students who need assistance, and I strongly recommend attending her office hours for extra help. She is very helpful and can provide insights to where the exam questions could go. The course is challenging but fair as the questions are similar to the lecture materials.

Professor Shapland is easily the best professor I have had. She is extremely good at teaching accounting. If you show up and do the work, you will succeed in her class. I especially love how all of our homework is on the same platform, and it is all very uniform. Also, I could always find an explanation video of the topic on the course website.

Professor Shapland is amazing! Her teaching style was easy to understand, and because of her, I actually declared a double major in accountancy.  I have learned so much through ACCY 202, and she was always easily accessible if I needed help.  If you put in the work, you will have no problem taking this class.
The homework and exam difficulty is just totally different. She doesn't teach that well and expects too much from our exams. Also, the exam takes over 50% of our final grade, so good luck lmao.

Professor Shapland is a super nice and wants her class to succeed. However, she just makes the class unnecessarily hard. The amount of time and work you have to invest into this class is beyond ridiculous. In addition, her exams are extremely difficult as answer choices can range from 4 all the way up to 8 choices. You cant even guess on exams.

Professor Shapland is great! I took her ACCY 202 class during the summer session, and felt that it was paced appropriately. She was always willing to answer questions and take extra time out to help students.

Overall, I think she's a very straightforward person - she teaches the concepts very well, her homework and group projects are very fundamental to understanding the subject, and she's helpful if you just show up to her office hours. She wrote my letter of recommendation for JD app and added great details I forgot. Very helpful and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed ACCY 202 and getting to know Professor Shapland. She was a great professor who took the time to get to know me and helped me a lot throughout the course. She was willing to write me a letter of recommendation for a scholarship I was applying for and gave me a lot of great advice about pursuing a career in accounting.

Professor Shapland is extremely helpful and knowledgeable but she does require that students put forth an effort to succeed in the class. However, she is very flexible when it comes to meeting with her for extra help or clarification and as long as students are willing to learn and work hard, she will take the time to ensure you understand.

She is not a good person at all. She is very condescending and honestly can be very rude/not understanding at all. However, her class is very straightforward. You need to watch the lectures since her test questions have random little facts she says in them. You need to do the lecture notes and green sheets and you'll most likely get a good grade.

This is not an easy class but Professor Shapland understands that and gives students many opportunities for practice and help, you just have to actually put in the work. She is incredibly caring about her students and if you want to do well, she will help you as long as you are willing to help yourself. Hard work doesn't go unnoticed in this class.

While ACCY 202 has a reputation for being a difficult class, it really is about the effort you put into it. If you read the book and pay attention in lectures you will have no issue doing well in this class. Julie understand this is a difficult course, so she gives you plenty of opportunities to practice the content and come to her for assistance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is always patient and explains everything very thoroughly in lectures. The grading criteria that she sets are fair and clear. I learned a lot of accounting skills from her. Caring and approachable professor! Great class! Highly recommended!

Prof. Shapland truly wants you to work for the grade that you desire. She does make the curriculum pretty challenging, but it allows you to get a strong understanding of the material. If you work hard, study for the tests, and want to learn, then you will get so much out of the class. I truly learned so much during it, and she is a great professor.

ACCY 202 was one of my more difficult classes in undergrad. At first I was unengaged and struggling, however, professor Shapland was my saving grace. She reached out to me for extra help and guided me to a B. I wish I leveraged her as a resource sooner. That being said, use all of the help you can get and you will be successful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was challenging, but it creates a solid foundation for other ACCY classes in the future. If you attend lectures and take good notes, you will do fine in the class. Julia gives you a pretty good note packet where you just have to fill in blanks and follow along in class. This makes note taking and studying for exams easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I took ACCY 202 with Professor Shapland and, though the course was online, I learned so much in her class and truly feel it is one of the reasons I performed so well in my 300-level accounting courses. It was a challenging course but Professor Shapland is a great professor that gave all the tools to succeed, you just need to make sure you use them!

Awful class and online only doesn't help!!!! Had to take this class but it was way too difficult for a non-accy major. Lectures are very long and hard to follow and exams are extremely difficult and include material not discussed in class or in readings. Also very stressful with very confusing class site and lots of homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Can't listen to her talk I fall asleep. Extremely stressful and challenging for no reason as all. Most of the students in this class are taking this class not because they are interested in Accy but because they have to, given the fact most students aren't interested in Accy the class is taught in a way that you are getting a PHD in Accy.

Very unorganized compass page with various links that lead to the same place. Lectures are very long and hard to follow. The material on the test was much harder than the homework that we were given. The first exam was basically impossible and many people received under a 40%. You basically have to teach yourself the material.

She really knows her stuff. I enjoyed her for this reason. She can be tough but she will help if needed. A lot of people think she is intimidating but she just really knows her stuff. If you show up to lecture, pay attention and do the work you should have no problem

Very long and heavy lectures. Tests are quite difficult. We were tested on things she didn't teach. Her take-home exams that were worth 10% back on tests sound like a good idea but were in fact terrible and did not help your grade.

Julie Shapland isn't that bad of a professor. Her tests are difficult like many people say, but if you study hard for them and review all the material, you should be ok. There were 5 exams in total this semester, and you need to make sure you watch all the lectures and do the connect homework. If you slack in this class, you definitely won't pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Compass page is super unorganized and hard to navigate. Things that should be together are separated into so many different folders and links. Videos are long, need to watch on double speed to get through them.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her test questions are meant to trick you and are very confusing. She talks a lot and you have to watch her videos at 2x speed to be able to get through it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Shapland sets you up for success with detailed lectures and guiding notes. If you put in appropriate effort towards class assignments and study for exams you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took Shapland's class when COVID-19 hit so the class was half in person and half online. Her lectures in person were great, she is awesome at explaining concepts and keeps you engaged in class by doing i-clickers. When we switched online, she did recorded lectures that were also very helpful. Tests are not bad if you actually study.

Everyone fails the midterms so she curves the class. Julie tries to make sure the class is as tough and stressful as possible. She thinks quarantine has made class easy so she made our quizzes harder and taken away our promised curve. She then gave us 6 homework assignments due right after our midterm. People are dying give us a break like cmon.

WORST CLASS WORST PROFESSOR. She doesn't teach you a single thing in lecture, no lecture slides, and just gives you clickers & quizzes and teaches you based on those. She doesn't follow any type of structure and moves way too fast for a required intro ACCY class. Only perk of the class is extra credit. Overall, so difficult and would not take again

Julia designed the course for students to really read the textbook and understand accounting. She provides enough instructions and exam prep stuff to help students, so if you pay attention during classes and study for the exam, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Shapland expects everyone to be accountants when the xlaaa is required for any Business major. She speaks way too fast and expects us to know the material as soon as she says it. She uses words we do not understand and flips around way too much. We are students not professional accountants, please relax. New test structure is awful too.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: More difficult than ACCY201, really. My final grade was going to be a C, but the extra credits and curves made my grade a B+. Extreme time pressure on the graded activities (quizzes), tricky exam questions, and more. I like her as a person, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Though the Accounting courses are boring in general, you can learn a lot with Julia. Many extra credit opportunities. She really wants everyone has a good performance in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Somehow failed every exam but still managed to pull off an A. Just attend all lectures for the points and do all the extra credit and an A is not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Julie is a great professor. As long as you do all the work and everything she tells you to do you will be fine. It takes work in this class, but you really learn how to study and she gives plenty of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This class was incredibly difficult and stress provoking, but the curve saved my grade. I failed every exam and still got a B+ because I attended every lecture and got extra credit. The lectures are really long and boring and the workbook is hard to follow and is far too detailed. Julie is a very caring professor but takes her job far too seriously

Prof. Shapland is the best professor I've had at this university.  She lays out what's expected of students and does everything possible to ensure that people get a good grade in her class.  The material itself is difficult but if you study it you'll do fine.  People complain about getting a bad grade in the classbut they don't put in the work!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class material is tough and the lectures are so dry and boring. The class notes are far too wordy with unnecessary detail. Exams are impossible but the course is curved a lot. There are clicker attendance points in lecture and discussions are mandatory.

She has unrealistically high expectations for her students, so going to office hours isn't a fun experience. Really thorough workbook (lots of unnecessary detail). The exams & especially the final are challenging. She gives a lot of extra credit which comes from doing the homework early & attendance, so that saves everyone's grade.

ACCY 201 and 202 are two different stories. Shapland makes herself accessible to all students. The exams are challenging. You need to know the material to the fullest extent to succeed. I've heard kids who have gotten 100% on exams and 30% on exams. Go to lecture, discussion, office hours, and do not procrastinate homework and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Communicates concepts well and was happy with the teaching and lecture packets. Tests are hard, do not underestimate them. She is a great teacher but can often pile on work. Stay on top of things and follow the detailed syllabus. I reached out to her multiple times and she solved my problems, no hassle.

Professor Shapland is a great professor and knows the BEST way to teach her students accy. She explains EVERY details clearly to help you REALLY learn the materials and pass the exam. Exam may be hard, but as long as you attend her lecture and take down the notes, you would have no problem getting a good grade! She is definitely inspiring!

Awesome lecturer. She knows the stuff is boring, but her notes packet is amazing. If you go through the notes packet and actually learn the material you will do great. Exam are fair but by no means easy. Have to work at it but she is a great professor.

She is the reason I am an Accy major. I learned so much and really enjoyed the class. She realizes her material is not the most riveting and engaging material so she makes jokes about it. She is a clear lecturer and if you study the notes, skim the book, go to class, and do the green sheets, you will do well.
Awesome professor! She is so cool :)

I've never had a teacher with a more organized lesson plan. Her textbook with PowerPoint slides and practice exams is very thorough and basically everything you need to pass her tests. Her exams are exactly what is taught in her class, no trick questions. I got Bs on the exams and the final, but she curves the class fairly well.

Nice person, bad teacher. Her exams and final were unreasonably hard. Homeworks and projects were pretty easy, but she did not prepare us for what she tested us on. Pulled off a good grade in the class, but I don't feel like I learned the material.
Very organized, get's to the point, no fluff. Very fair grader of projects and HW, unlike Curtis in 201. Very smart, knows her stuff.
Worst professor I've ever had. Boring teaching style and useless words I the package.. She has never used the reading book, and the course package has a bunch of useless words in it.
Overall easy A. I received 102% until the final exam. Final was brutal. So do well during the semester and get as much easy point as possible.
Outside of the brutal final exam, it is a very easy class.  Do the assigned homework and you're golden.

Worst professor (if you can call her that) I've had at U of I. She's ineffective. I received an A+ in her class by teaching myself accounting. I received one of the highest grades in the entire course because I didn't listen to her. Students who pay attention get worse grades. Conclusion: her teaching counters understanding of the subject matter.

She is the worst professor that I have had. Her notes are very unorganized and confusing. Be prepared to teach yourself in order to slightly learn the material. She is rude and unhelpful and it is very difficult to learn anything during class. I worked so hard in this class and got nowhere close to the grade I deserved.

While she has good intentions, she often comes off as unorganized. Had I not received such high grades on my first two exams, I would have been in trouble. Do well early and you won't have a problem. Also, after the change to ACCY 201, ACCY 202 is much easier and a decent amount of it is review.

Professor Shapland does a great job at teaching the material. The material is tough but she does a nice job laying out her coursebook with practice problems and worksheets that if you actually do prepare for class and do the sheets she recommends after as well you will do great in the class. She was always more than happy to help in office hours.

Great teacher. The material is tough, but if you put the time and effort into the class you will do great. She always makes herself avalaible to help you and provides plenty of examples in class. If you put in the effort to learn the material, you will get an A

The Professor is extremely helpful and does her best to keep you interested in the class. She is understanding and knows if you are a good student (yes, even in a big lecture she knows exactly who you are! :D). Overall, she is a great teacher who has excellent teaching as well as real world experience in accounting and business. Great class!!

She is a great professor (and really nice) who provides students with everything they need to do well. The class is fairly graded, but requires effort. The lecture notes are detailed and understanding them is essential. Utilize the book for more in depth explanations and clarification. If you still have difficulties ask the tutors, TA or Shapland.

She is a very good teacher. She teaches in a very organized manner, and she explains things clearly without any ambiguity. She is very easy to access both through emails and her office hours, and she answers questions nicely. Definitely encourage to visit her office hours if you've got questions.

Straight forward course.  The material isn't too tough if you pay attention in class and do the (small amount of) reading recommended.  Shapland is a cool teacher who actually makes learning accy fun and interesting.  She is VERY willing to help & easily accessible through emails and office hours.  Pretty easy A if you do what you are suppose to.

Professor Shapland is a great teacher. She explains things really well and is easy to reach by email or office hours or after class if you have any questions. She's not one to try and trick students, and the tests only reflect material taught. I would definitely take another class with Prof. Shapland if I could.

She explains things in class very clearly, and she balances her lecturing and practice/exercises in class very well as well. Her office hour is very helpful, but there are always a lot of people in her office before exam period, so recommend go early if you've got questions. She definitely makes me love accounting.

The class is more technical than 201. Shapland teaches with clarity & passion and overall very helpful. Go to her office hours if the material is unclear or to just introduce yourself. She wrote me a recommendation for a scholarship I won. The exams may seem difficult but review old exams to get a glimpse of what to expect. iClickers are required.

Professor Shapland has a deep passion for accounting. Because of this,she wants her students to not only perform well,but to also understand the practice of accounting.  As a result, Accy 202 may be challenging at times, but this  class is by no means impossible. Professor Shapland will go out of her way to help    you and the grading is lenient.

She's an ok professor though I did like her a bit better than Curtis. I read the book for about the 1st 1/4 of the class and referenced to it when I needed. I didn't like the book n i think i could have done w/o it but def get the lecture notes. Do the old exams n go to class. Even if u don't do well on exams other pts should make up for it.
Great Professor. She teaches with clarity and passion. Tests are just like old exams. Notes package is very helpful

The course design is extremely bad. The book is not sequential, so for one reading you may end up having to flip through it 5 times. This makes you not want to read. ACCY 202 starts out fine, then, one class you can miss a few things, and bam, you start getting lost and it's a downward spiral.

she definitely isn't a student-friendly professor. she doesn't enjoy answering questions and does her best to shoo away students. she's rude and not an encouraging professor. i put a ton of time into this class and i'm still not getting the results i want. she always passes off her students to the tutors instead of answering the question herself.

This class really isn't that bad.  Shapland is so much better than Curtis.  Don't read the book.  Study a couple days before the test and take the past exams.  It's not that hard of a class if you put a little time into it.

Very considerate of students schedules, takes the time to answer questions throughout lecture, homework is easy(you get 99 attempts), test are tricky but usually even out with the group project score. Overall she is a great professor.

this class is ridiculously hard and demanding. she thinks we have all the time in the world for this class. i hate it, but it's required. she's a nice professor and you can tell she knows the material, but i don't think she teaches the material very well. plus, her exams are crazy hard.

She is clear on the lecture but she is not helpful at all.If you ask her a question, she will tell you to go back and read the book. Her administration sucks. She forces people to change groups without giving any reason.
Test questions this semester were much trickier than past semesters. It almost didn't matter how much you studied. I questioned whether she knew the difference between income and profit.
Great professor, she takes the time to thoroughly explain tough concepts. Past years papers are provided, which helps a lot.

Shapland was a great lecturer and definitely a breath of fresh air after having Curtis.  This class will teach you a lot, but an A requires a great deal of work. Also, you don't need to do hardly any of the readings.

Studying for the exams is necessary for this course - Do not slack off on any of them. Study the notes. The textbook is not really necessary and do not buy the new edition just because she said so. Her course is very detail oriented...you'll know when you see her compass page. I learned quite a bit from her.

Lectures are extremely boring to sit through. Lots of iClicker questions so attendance is somewhat required. Test questions are HORRIBLE. Too many questions where multiple answers seem to be correct. The group projects are very time consuming and hard. But hardest part of the class are the exams. Prof. teaches straight from notesbook
Great professor. Very clear about what is expected and what to do. Dont really need to read the book. Just read the notesbook and do the green sheets. Best professor so far.

One of the best in the school. Very clear about what she is going to give her students. And also requires her students to be clear about the materials. If you do the green sheets in the course packet and fully understand them, the exams seem quite straightforward.

She was a good teacher, but test questions were horrible! Too many subjective questions that could have many justified answers. Final was harder than it needed to be as well. Plenty of extra credit though, so it makes things a bit better
She's the best prof I've ever had in college!
great prof! you can learn a lot from her. but please attend the lecture everytime
Awesome Professor - always willing to help, answer emails/message boards and explained material very well. Tests are pretty difficult but she always offers tutoring and office hours before tests.

Awesome teacher. She really know her stuff. Although the class is pretty difficult, it is by all means manageable. As long as you understand how to do all the questions that's in the notes packet, you should be fine. You will walk out of the class feeling like you learned a lot.

Much better class than 201. The material you cover is actual accounting, unlike 201 which is mostly business ethics. Her tests are difficult, as she is really testing if you know the material rather than if your able to memorize old questions. It is more difficult than 201 but at least you feel like you're in a top ranked business school.

Very fair. If you were doing what you were supposed to, you will get a good grade. I got high Bs on all of the exams and got a solid A in the class. Most people got either an A or B. Also always willing to help

HATE HER!!! someone earlier said she doesnt try to trick you...LIES!!!! julie shapland is a liar, even though her notes are def waaaayyy better than curtis, her tests are RIDICULOUS! you HAVE to read the test questions really carefully coz she totally tries to trick you. omg I HATE HER. also shes so boring and i hate lecture. atleast curtis danced

She's a good professor who teaches material well. At the same time though, she makes her tests more difficult than they need to be. I felt like I knew the material well enough but then the exam questions were made out to trick you or just make it more tougher on you. But lots of extra credit and easy pts to accumulate throughout the semester.

Shapland is a really nice professor who is always willing to help. The projects are hard, but if you go to her office hours, she typically helps out a lot.  Overall, her lectures can be a tad boring, but she is a great professor who knows a lot about the subject.
EXCELLENT notes... waaay better than curtis. Tests can kind of be tricky, lots of projs, but lots of extra credit. Really good teacher overall!

This class is pretty boring but a major improvement on the horrific ACCY 201 with Curtis. Material isn't hard, lots of extra credit and a big curve. Unfortunately she does put a couple questions from the book on the tests and you still need to read the questions carefully, but she doesn't deliberately try to trick you.
There are a lot of extra points. I got low Cs on all the tests and still got a solid B in the class. ITs not bad.
She strongly resembles Meg Ryan at the peak of her early 90s romantic comedy prowess. Only downside is it's a major distracting factor during crunch-time on the mini-tests. Oh well.

Always willing to help and a very nice person. Lecture can be kind of boring, but everything is pretty straightforward. She also curved a lot so if you put in the effort, you should be able to get an A
No Comments

Passionate about the subject and sharing it with his students. Straightforward, organized lectures, and provides examples in lecture and problems in the homework with diverse applications to demonstrate the scope of the field. Exams may be slightly challenging at times, but homework prepares you well.
Great lecturer and very detailed / clear lecture notes

Makes the subject very interesting. His lectures sometimes include videos, which make it that much more immersive. His notes are always published before the lecture, so you can prime yourself if needed. Highly recommend this professor if you are trying to learn the subject!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor and great guy. The tests aren't easy and the class isn't easy for sure, but he is a really good professor and is really good at teaching and explaining concepts.

A professor that goes above and beyond for the student. His lectures are very clear and he even provides supplemental material for content that is especially difficult. He places emphasis on homework over exams, which i appreciated.
Very helpful and caring. His lectures are very straightforward and not confusing. I took it over the summer so it was a very small class.

Very passionate in the subject.
Amazing Lectures
Best professor by far, lectures were super nice, exams were really great, I would take them again.

Caring and takes student feedback seriously. Homework assignments were easy. Textbook is unfortunately mandatory since all the assignments are through Cengage. Projects were fun. My only issue was the exams. It felt pointless to study for them since they relied heavily on minutiae from the textbook, and open-internet didn't really help.
This class was so comically easy. I love Yellowdig discussions.

Professor Kim is truly one of the most caring professors at this university. It is abundantly evident that she cares about her students and their success. She gives fantastic feedback and it is clear that she has a passion for helping students learn. She also has a very warm and positive attitude and vibe that she brings to class.
The Professor is really chill.

The class is part of the business minor and asynchronous. The textbook is mandatory since all the weekly assignments are done on there. The class is super easy and informative and as long as you do the work on time and follow the rubric for the two major assignments, you should get an A in this class. The two midterms were on Canvas and were easy.

Professor Myoung is a very kind and knowledgable person. She truly cares about her students and wants to see everyone succeed. She even bought us pizza! Her class is quite interesting and she's very lenient with grading. It is groupwork heavy though, as you stay in the same group the entire semester. Highly recommend you take this class with her!
Outstanding professor, one of the best at Gies. She is very understanding and kind, and has interesting lectures. I would take her again if I could.

Practice exams are nothing like the actual exams and you genuinely cannot predict what will be on it. You have to read 2 30- page scientific articles at the end of every unit and he expects you to read and comprehend all of it. Any math questions are coated in layers of unit conversion. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Although the Exam2 was easy everyone got good grade,but cannot disguise the fact that he doesn't like teaching. He made the class hard. The extra reading materials are not helpful and are unrelated to the content they are just additional boring things you have to memorize to prepare for his exam.
A middle-tier lecturer among the MCB faculty.

Professor Kim is the best professor I've ever had. I took the class Fall 2024 and his class prepared me very well for the MCAT. His office hours were super informative too. He'd ask us to send in questions beforehand so that he could prepare slides to explain concepts in detail. He's also super willing to meet with students outside of class.
most unorganized proff ive ever had. good luck

You read 3 10-page research articles and other articles serve as lecture. He only goes over the figures and expects you to read and digest the rest. That becomes your test. Don't feel prepared for the MCAT because there is no clear curriculum of Biochem. He is very nice though! No curves despite 66% average and no one got 100% on the first exam.
Very good lecturers that is engaging. But material seems a bit iffy and you can't predict at all what will be on exam

Professor Kim is truly one of the best lecturers I have met-he makes the course so engaging for us! Even though the content feels a bit tedious sometimes he makes sure we understand every bit of it....he has always been really helpful whenever I emailed him outside class-he even helped me get connected with a research opportunity in biochem!

For this professor it's a shot in the dark of what is on the exams. He only cares that you know the random weird factoids that he expects you to figure from reading the textbook, covers 5 chapters per exam of dense content + lecture mat. The office hours were strange since you have to know the question you want to ask before the lecture was taught.
Exams are tougher than the content he lectures about. He expects you to memorize specific details from articles , which is not reflective of the material.

He often asks the class what the answer to what he was saying. He makes us read the textbook which is old and arbitrary. His tests did not really test on the overall concepts but more specific details. He occasionally cracked a funny joke, and overall he seems like a good dude. Spect.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He made my Philosophy class into something incredible. I always enjoyed philosophy but he made it into something else. I left his class every day with more questions about how the world works. He is also very accomodating and understanding. He adds fun jokes into the class and answers questions beautifully.
Very good explanation of the text and very generous and helpful office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this class as a random GenEd, and honestly, the only reason I didn't drop it was because of the professor. He's really chill, and although there is a lot of reading and annotating, if you attend the lectures and go through slides before essays/tests, you will be fine.

Professor Sanders is the best! His lectures are so on point, make difficult philosophy easier to understand, and he encourages meaningful dialogue without dragging on. He lets different opinions be heard, but is also super smart and uses logic for truth. He is also very down-to-earth and hilarious! Just be ready to read and put in effort to learn.

This was one of my favorite philosophy classes I've taken. Professor Sanders is a really good lecturer and explains things very clearly. If you take good notes, go to office hours, and ask for feedback on the essays, you'll probably do very well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Sanders is an absolutely brilliant, once in a lifetime kind of professor who's tremendously well spoken, educated, and thorough with his ideas, not to mention kind. He breaks down convoluted philosophical jargon into plain English, and inspires you to think about how it applies to your own life. I really regret not going to his OH more.

Really liked the experience of having him as a professor. There is some reading, but it is not an excessive amount of it. Lectures are very fun, and I really feel like I learned a lot. Studying for these exams does take a lot of time though if you want to excel at them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Kirk Sanders is an amazing teacher and is very passionate about what he does. While there is a lot of reading, if you pay attention in the lectures, it can help give you a recap on the important topics of discussion. This is not a blow off class but it's certainly one I have enjoyed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Too much reading, has potential to be interesting, but made boring by excessive amount of reading. He expects you to read whole plays and gives lots of textbook reading. Seems to be passionate about his work, but the reading and no test reviews make the class a bit more difficult than need be. Good lessons, and helpful grader, but too much reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class to fulfill a gen ed thinking it would be an easy 100-level class, but the amount of reading takes hours on end and there are no test reviews at all. Out of all my other higher-level courses, this class took the most time and effort which was very unexpected.

This class covers some interesting topics that are made dull by the reading assigned. He typically gives 2-3 hours of reading from not very interesting sources (whole plays; Iliad, etc.). The amt of reading makes it hard to learn, and there's so many things he wants us to remember for tests, but offers no review. Nice guy, much reading, hard tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Sanders and his TA, Emma Frank, totally phoned it in for his Fall 2020 Intro to Greek Culture Although he assigned a lot of reading and papers, its pretty clear neither he nor his TA took the time to read any them. The grading was arbitrary and capricious based on some matrix only they knew. I thought I was taking 115, big mistake!

I took this class as a gened, and it might have been one of my biggest regrets. I was expecting a class that would be fun and enjoyable, not my most stressful class of freshman year. There was WAY too much reading assigned, and it was so hard to manage getting it done with other classes. I feel like I didn't learn anything bcs of the workload. :/

Took his intro to Greek culture and have never had to read so much in my life. Took this as a gen ed and because I was interested in the topic. Never want to go through this class again. He provides no reviews for tests. He seems cool, but too much work overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The best professor ever!
We love you professor sanders!
SUCH A GEM THANK YOU FOR PUTTING SO MUCH CARE AND EFFORT INTO ONLINE LECTURES THIS TERM US STUDENTS APPRECIATE SOULS LIKE YOU!
An amazing person and teacher.

As everyone else said: this man is brilliant. He uses every class to display his love for philosophy, and he is fantastic at explaining abstract concepts from the readings. However, do not take the prior warnings about his grading lightly - supplement this course with an easier GenEd to balance out your GPA. I'd still highly recommend this class.

Sanders has a remarkable talent for pedagogy. During lectures he manages to translate abstruse philosophical writing into plain English without oversimplification. He also has a sense of humor. All this being said, he's one of the most brutal graders I've encountered at UIUC. Only take one of his classes if you're truly motivated.
VERY knowledgeable and helpful. However, his 80-minute classes get really boring. EXTREMELY HARSH GRADER.
Great teacher. Witty and knowledgable.
Sanders is one of the best philosophy teachers at Illinois, he loves what he teaches and makes the material very understandable
Kirk is a great guy. But he grades WAY TOO HARD.

As everyone else noted, Sanders is BRILLIANT. However his intelligence seems to be my downfall, he grades papers with unreasonably high standards-and though he will go out of his way to help you revise papers and talk during office hours, he will still end up returning papers with just as many comments and corrections as the original draft.

Learning ancient Greek is definitely not easy, but he does a great job teaching it.  He is really helpful and is super clear. Not to mention that he actually wants his students to succeed in his class. He is also pretty funny, which makes class more enjoyable.  Overall, great professor.
i wish he would stop grading our papers as if we're harvard students...=(...we're just mediocre U of I students...seriously...harsh grader
taking his hellenistic philosophy this semester. AWESOME teacher.

Like other comments, ancient philosophy has never been my interest before I went to this class. Professor Sanders *always* has a clear explanation on almost every single topic that we discussed in class. He also has a good sense of humor which is very uncommon among philosophy professors here at the U of I!

Like another person posted, Ancient Philosophy is never the most intersting thing, but he is a wonderful professor for it. He is very clear on what he expects and explains the reading well, which helps greatly with Aristotle. I would reccomend him for any Philosophy class as he puts in jokes and will take questions throughout his lectures. Good guy

Ancient philosophy is a bore no matter whom you take it with, but Professor Sanders does a fantastic job with what he has. He's a really bright and witty guy who makes Plato and Aristotle clear. The midterm and final aren't hard if you've been keeping up with notes and lectures (go to office hours, it's really helpful).

This Professor does not care about his students. I reached out to him 3 times across the semester and never got a reply. DO NOT TAKE HIM! He does not do any grading himself, he just leaves all the work up to the GitHub autograder.

The grading system and structure of the course is flawed. There are too few assignments and no drops/regrades so if you make any mistake that affects the R file, you lose all credit (no partial credit) even though your work was good. The lecture vids are from years back, notes are messy, and you learn more from reading the R for Data Science book.
Poorly designed course

Hw dur Fri but you have until Sun to turn in code that returns and error or is irreproducible. If your code returns an error or is irreproducible (he is VERY unclear about explaining how to check for irreproducibility) you will get an automatic 0 bc of his autograder. Then good luck fixing the grade bc his email ettiquete is abysmal.

Worst grading criteria ever, and then being penalized with an all-or-nothing grading system is the nail in the coffin. It is horrible how much stress you must endure to ensure your assignments work, or you don't get a redo, and you lose out on those points. There are no in-person lectures, just labs, which are hard, btw, cause they are timed.

I'm convinced that the professor writes all positive reviews here lol. I think his all-or-nothing grading system might stem from his laziness: unwilling to try to understand students' code and their logic to give partial credits and provide constructive feedback! If there is 1 tiny error in the code, you're cooked.

Ridiculous grading system! First, if you have 1 error then you will receive 0 for the whole thing. Secondly, he sucks at wording problems. Most students are always confused about what to do. Also, he doesn't want to teach that much. In the final weeks, he only spent 25-35 minutes teaching but expected students to understand the content entirely.

I think Professor Kinson has a good structure for this class once you get used to it. It was super easy to get a good grade. Final project was easy, so were exams. The notes were useful and he always took time after class to address individual questions. He did show some favoritism but it was towards students who did their work and did it well.
No other courses at the UofI made me feel so insecure because any mistake made in any assignment/exam give u a straight zero

Kind of funny, but does not teach real lectures. No partial credit, stupid grading system. Slow grader (said he didn't care enough to grade our assignments, which is why it was graded late). Questions were worded very poorly.

Assignment grading system is awful. Labs are 3 or 4 points which means if you get 1 problem wrong that means you get 0.66 or 0.75 percent right away. Errors are easily occurred using R, but he gives 0 for any assignment with any kind of error. No points for completeness at all. 

I think he should rather use prairielearn than GitHub submission.

The course offers a supportive learning environment that includes collaborative experimentation, a student-friendly exam format that allows for two tries, and a responsive professor. This approach makes learning complex programming concepts much easier and more efficient.
Antiquated teaching
Lol if your test or project has 1 error it's GG

Genuinely don't get the low ratings here - Prof Kinson was great. Weekly assignments graded for completion, and the labs/exams are based on his weekly notes. He gives you two chances to take each lab and exam. Super friendly and helpful after hours. Practice submitting an assignment before it's due; points off if directions aren't closely followed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely a tough grader. Unclear project guidelines.  Low scores on final projects are given. Points are deducted for minor errors in hw and labs.
A new project was added this semester, and he didn't give the grades according to the time he said in the course, and it was delayed for several days, which was very confusing.

Questions are vague and unclear, but grading is all-or-nothing so there's no way to actually demonstrate understanding of the material even if you get it wrong. Everyone gets a different lab assignment, which all vary wildly in terms of difficulty. Overall, your grade is in no way reflective of how well you understand class materials and concepts.
Totally don't know how to teach and the only learning materials is lecture note. Also, he change the online open note exam to in class close note exam before exam one week.

not a lot of homework, but class isn't structured that well. there aren't any lectures (only notes) and the in class labs are comically confusing. he's an easy grader, though, and updates your grades in the class frequently. he's a funny guy too!

Work is assigned to everyone equally at random, so it is highly recommended you go to class everyday. Workload isnt terrible, and its mostly take home and open note. He SUCKS at wording questions/giving directions, so assignments are way harder/more time consuming and than they need to be
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Biweekly homework assignments due, one midterm, and a final exam. The lectures don't help out all too much, but the corresponding notes that he provides with the lectures are helpful. Homework was due Monday night, you should start it the week before, and go to office hours because he was helpful with that. A nice guy, albeit a bit boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Okay lecturer, his notes were good to get through most of the hw, TA's were the really helpful ones though. He's kind of rude and condescending when answering people's questions in discussion forums. Sounds like he's talking down to you or just wants to make you feel dumb for asking a simple clarification question. Wouldn't take his section again

Kinson is a great person but in terms of class and programming knowledge he has a long way to go. Stat 440 gave the option of working in R or Python and Kinson doesn't know Python well. Because of that, the Python version of class notes were often missing and getting help was difficult. Overall it was an easy class but be careful.

Great guy, but has not a single idea how to teach the course. Lecture videos are confusing/difficult to understand, and usually don't have a lot to do with homeworks and midterms. You'd basically need to learn 90% of the material by yourself. His replies to student questions on the course websites are about as unclear as his lecture videos are.
Get ready to learn everything on your own. He is very unorganized and he doesn't explain things well. The info taught in the lectures doesn't line up with the homework.
Yikes. This class is mostly self-learning with almost zero useful guidance or teaching from the instructor. Try to take it with another professor if you can.

This guy has no clue what he's doing. This is a class for students ne w to using R, yet Kinson doesn't teach us anything! We literally have to teach ourselves everything using online resources, as if we have no professor. Maybe it's due to COVID, but Kinson is pretty much useless and I would advise taking this class until he gets it together.

I would say only take him if you're very comfortable with a statistical programming language. I was very familiar with R prior to taking his class so the homework and midterm was not too bad for me. The lectures are not that helpful for the most part, but he usually gives hints to the homework if you just ask.
-poor teaching ability and generally unprepared -mismatch between content taught in lecture and hw + tests -unclear instructions and expectations on hw
He doesn't really teach the material in the homework and exams. Be prepared to do A LOT of self-learning.
Take with another professor

Awkward experience. The lectures are not only useless but also waste of time, you are really on your own to learn everything. Attendance is required and there's quiz every week. The worst lecture experience I've ever had.

He's a nice guy and down to Earth. But he doesn't know how to teach. Maybe it's because he's new to lecturing, but his lectures are some of the most disorganized and unhelpful I've ever had. I stopped showing up pretty quickly to study on my own instead. He doesn't show up prepared. Spends the first 10 minutes of class booting up his laptop.

He seems like a nice guy, but man he's just not good at explaining R coding. The class structure is so confusing and I learn nothing from going to lecture. I've had to learn pretty much everything from online resources.
The lectures are awkward. Never give clear instructions to assignments. Keep working on the same data without making any progress.

GO TO CLASS! Attendance is not required, and if you choose not to go don't blame the professor for falling behind. With that being said, I didn't go and just crammed the posted lecture and did fine :)

Pretty much all of the material is from the lectures with only a few explanations provided in the readings. Professor Barrow knows a lot about what he's teaching he sometimes has a problem simplifying it but he always answers questions. Literally all questions. Just sometimes you need to ask the same question 5 different ways.

professor barrow is extremely passionate about what he teaches and a great person. however, i ended up wishing i had chosen a different gen ed because his lectures were very hard for someone who has never taken an astronomy class before to understand. it's hard to take notes because the lectures are so jam packed of info.

Professor Barrow was very interested in the topic and had and clearly very knowledgeable. However, he lectures exceptionally quickly and has very long slide presentations making it very difficult to take good notes during class.

Professor Barrow is a genuinely good guy and he wants all of his students to succeed in his class. He offers an extra credit opportunity and the final will only help your grade. The class was lecture heavy, with each lecture being jam-packed full of information, but the discussion sections help break down what was learned in class.

She's not the best at explaining concepts as she doesn't in go in depth enough. A lot of people will struggle in her class because she expects you to understand the concepts already, so I recommend learning some content before taking the class. Her exams are exactly like the homework so if you do well on that you'll be fine for exams.

Fine professor but worse person. If you make an accident on something small about an exam or homework she has no mercy and will refuse to give you credit for what happened. Lots of homework. During lecture make sure to take good notes and show up everyday as the i-clicker points are very important. Hard, but manageable with hard work.
exams are very hard to study for and usually average around 40%
I recommend taking Chem102 with a different professor
Disorganized slides and pre lecture notes that are bad at teaching the content, unhelpful lectures. Passive aggressive at times.

lowk condescending and the in-lecture questions are nothing like the exam questions. Best piece of advice is to do the prep exams and try to view the lecture slides before lecture because it'll give you more time to understand the concepts. She's OK in office hours.

Very test-heavy, multiple prep exams and bonus exams were released; however, problems shown on homework and prep exams were nothing like what you have seen. They are designed to trick you and are nearly impossible to do well on with no curve. The first exam average was 42% material is nothing like other classes and is far more difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The material isn't even hard, it's her absurd questions that she throws in on the exams that she never talked abt! And its only 15 questions, no curve!!! I would study so much in this class and genuinely understand the concept, but on the exams it's just a guess, honestly, like you'd be better off calculating probability.
She spends so much time on simple concepts and completely glosses over things that need clarification. Very condescending to questions in my experience.

Marville's class has graded iClicker questions during the lectures that are often harder than what was previously presented and considered "trick questions" on previous exams. Her class only has 3 multiple choice midterms, while other 102 classes have 5 exams with multiple attempts per question. She explains concepts in the hardest way possible.

She does not care about helping students learn, she purposely explain concepts in the most difficult way possible. She doesn't seem to care about teaching, but rather proving her own intelligence. Little of the material is remotely similar to the exam. On the bright side, I met some lovely TA's at the CLC. Switch out of her section asap.

Definitely get 100s on all of the homework/assignments. You will need it as a "safety cushion" for exams. As of fall 2025, exams are out of 15 points (excluding the final) then weighted, so not much room for error. Exams are also tricky. One word or exception can change the entire problem. Get the 24 bonus points, they're worth 3 exam questions.

Exams were on ALEX, which was bad for me. I had no experience with Chem before this, so it was rough. My friend, who took AP Chem, enjoyed it, but I didn't understand the lecture. She moves the fastest compared to the other professors and does an unnecessary unit at the end. If CHEM is just a required for engineering, then do not take her.

I took AP Chem, got a 5, and had A's both semesters in HS but nothing could've prepared me for this. The lectures and discussions give you false confidence and when you take the midterms you realize 75% of the exam (which are 15 total questions) are problems you've never seen before. Steer clear of this course. Should've listened to the warnings.

Dr. Marville is not as evil as some of the older reviews say, but the class is tough no matter what. The best piece of advice I have is to do ALL the worksheet pages that correspond to the lesson and to review the lecture slides before lecture. Also, set reminders for homework that way you don't miss any. Godspeed, everyone.

I admit that it is 80% of me for the score. But there are few things to say about CHEM 102.
She skims main stuffs real fast.
The way she elaborates on the materials is hard to follow.
Pop-up iClickers are hard.
She is inspirational for her few last words before the final. So you might not learn chemistry but you might learn other lessons to mature.

Do not take this class. The average midterm scores are around 50-60, and she doesn't curve. Though, there is a retake after each test but it averages with your previous score, which makes it not as helpful. This class is not worth your time and you will be better off taking other sections, just look at the GPA distributions for each respective one.

The midterms are very difficult and so was the final and she does not curve ANYHTING. Her lectures are not great and she provides close to no study material. If you take this course be prepared to self teach

Gang she's reformed from her academic probation days, I will say though her exams are still very difficult. Make sure to get perfect scores on hw and extra credit and you'll survive. She does not give enough study material for exams, and her questions can be tricky, the final is not as bad as the midterms imo.
I wouldnt take her if I were premed

After scoring 40% on the first midterm, I had to self-study the entire course. Lectures focused on inessential info while skipping key topics, and discussions were useless. However, her mock tests, prep exams and worksheet booklets were lifesavers that carried me throughout. She will test your test taking skills more than learned topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's not as bad as she's made out to be. Her tests seemed fair, especially if you do the homework and take advantage of the extra credit mock exams, and she gives retakes for all 3 midterms. She's also pretty good at communicating important concepts in lecture. Biggest downside is that she often spends lectures repeating very similar questions.
This class made me reconsider my entire major. Take any other chem 102 section and save yourself (and your gpa).

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. I really do not understand how she is still a professor. She is not welcoming AT ALL. If you have doubts, just ask Youtube or chatgpt. She is extremely unhelpful. Whatever she teaches does not come in the test. She purposely makes the exams so hard and confusing. A really bad nature. Please take any other professor available

If you can, switch teachers ASAP. I didn't find the material hard, however this course certainly was. She is a fast paced lecturer, lots of homework that felt all over the place because they were on different websites. Her discussion can be helpful, she goes over old exam problems, but she doesn't explain the concepts to how she solved them.

Dr. Kelly Marville is doing too much but never enough. She doesn't curve any tests and allows retakes. However, these retakes are an average of the original and the retake score. She also does in-class clicker questions that are GRADED, which will mess you up BIG TIME! She skims the material and expects you to get them right.
Awful professor. Incredibly disrespectful, refuses to admit any fault.

While the lectures themselves were coherent and well done, none of it showed up on the exams. She specifically said she tries to make the questions confusing to "make sure we know the material", but will put material we haven't learned yet on major exams. She also is rude when students ask questions, and condescending.

Please, please, PLEASE do not take Marville if you want to maintain a good GPA. She's an eloquent and fantastic lecturer, but everything you're taught in class might as well be forgotten because literally nothing on the homework, iClicker questions, iClicker assignments, pretests, discussion packets, OR practice tests is on the exam. 15 ?s Btw.

she is incredibly rude. she laughs at the students when they ask questions, making you feel extremely dumb for being confused. the test averages are always like a 50%, and there are retakes but no curving. if you can avoid her, do it, because even the ta's talk bad about her.

Dont take her, actual exams are nothing like hw or prep exams, averages are 7/15 on exams and does absolutely nothing for curve even tho everyone fails. Theres other professors teaching chem so take them not Marville

I would never in a MILLION years take this professor. DROP the class immediately. She doesn't care about the students. You can't understand her at all. The exams are the worst part of this professor. You can study all you want, but the questions are never like the ones on the mock hour exam or the practice exam she gives.
Taught nothing in class, rely only on learning via online resources. If you want to learn anything you have to teach yourself.

FIND ANOTHER PROFESSOR IF POSSIBLE!

Marville is the toughest teacher I've had at UIUC, and the class is a total weed-out. Her lectures move fast, and there's a lot of homework. The average on the exams were always around a 50% and she doesn't curve the grades. If you go to get help at the CLC, the TAs will literally badmouth her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Was on academic probation for a reason.

When I first signed up for Marville in FA24 I thought I was low key cooked. Her reviews RMP were awful and… they were right. She's an extremely fast lecturer, who lacks the basic ability to teach humbly. However, she's not unfair. She's very nice with midterms, which are practically identical to the practice exams.

do not take her. save yourself. i took her twice. dropped the first time, took her online class next se, and regretted it. she doesn't teach, just talks insanely fast and doesn't show you what's on the tests. study guides and practices are nothing like tests. if you take her, good luck and prayers, may God be with you because this teacher is satan.

Dr. Marville's class is difficult, but she gives you all the resources you need to succeed, and it's the student's job to take advantage of them. Going to discussion section was SUPER helpful even though points aren't awarded for going. There are also a lot of assignments other than exams that can help boost your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very rude professor
Good luck.

Doctor Marville is great at explaining difficult concepts. She has a well-structured class and gave us a lot of practices to prepare for exams. Definitely an amzing professor for introductory chemistry.

The lectures are alright, but sometimes they're pretty confusing to understand. Lots of opportunity to practice on the content, and she offers a lot of ways you can get good grades in the class (retakes, dropping quizzes and homework), so for me I felt like I was given a lot of leniency. Tests are do-able, especially if you take advantage of retake
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was afraid of taking her class because of the other ratings, but honestly the professor wasn't that terrible. I would absolutely recommend taking notes before lecture and staying on top of assignments, but she is overall nice when you come to office hours.

I think her class is pretty good, lectures are clear most of the time and resources are easy to attain. She does go through lectures fast sometimes, but slides are also posted online. Tests are pretty easy if you come prepared, final wasn't bad either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Marville is clearly knowledgable about chemistry, but unfortunately she's not as skilled at explaining topics and concepts to students, especially for a general chemistry course. Also, beware of her grading policies-she told our class she would be curving the final, and she didn't curve at all.

Lots of studying. Lectures are very fast so notes need to be taken before lecture. Tests only have a few questions on many topics which make studying very important. Use your TA and Office hours early on so you don't fall behind. Lots of practice questions and study material given. Very nice teacher but difficult content.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Marville gets a little too much hate. It's true she produces the lowest GPA average for her class out of all CHEM102 profs, but I think she is really inspirational and provides a LOT of resources for help. Don't forget to look through the printable practice exams in ALEKS resources. Put in the work and you will do well. Good luck!

Dr. Marville is definitely enthusiastic to teach chemistry and wants her students to do well, but the way that she presents the material is hard to follow. She goes through slides quickly and just reads from them, rarely elaborating. Tests are extremely hard and often have questions that were barely covered in class.

Would rate a 0 if I could. I would rather have a middle school chemistry teacher try and lecture me on this course. Her pacing is way too fast, she never explains any concepts, and is a really harsh grader as averages on all her tests are failing grades. Not to mention she is very condescending and gets upset when a student asks her a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Not a terrible professor as people think, her slides are very organized and there are prerecorded lectures online. The scary part is that her grading scale is extremely unforgiving. The average for every midterm exam is a failing grade and exams are NOT curved. I recommend attending EVERY discussion to consolidate knowledge after each lecture.

Here's advise: the iclicker assignments are almost always questions we did in discussion. To get a 12/15 or more in mock exams do the practice exam that's not for points a day before, they are almost identical.For hour exams go over the overview of questions and try to match the hints with problems you did in discussion, prep exams, and wrksts.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I should've read the reviews before taking this class. All she does during lecture are practice problems and she never takes the time to explain any concept in detail. Despite studying really hard and attending every lecture I would still do bad on the hour exams. 
And the class average itself is not great.

Aleks grading system is HORRIBLE in the way that you'd jump from a 100 --> 66% on a 3-question prep exam because of a tiny rounding error etc. The class was fine bc I learned it all from AP Chem. Her exams are fair/predictable, she emails the topic of every single question in order and you can find another version of that topic on her prep exams.
Take this class with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
Ap Class didn't help. She didn't either...
You know what helps though?
Choosing another professor!!!
Save yourself and your sanity, or if you wanna hate your life, your family, your job, and your roommate, choose this class. This class has been so frustrating, I had to break off a 6-year-old relationship with my girlfriend... I miss her :(

If you never took AP Chem try to avoid her section, but if you have to settle for her, the online section is better. Her class relies on you coming into class already having some understanding about the content so keep that in mind. I-Clickers are annoying but manageable, exams are only 15 questions so that can screw you over if you don't prepare.

I made the mistake of choosing this class and didn't check her rate my professor beforehand. I don't find her teaching style very helpful, I would teach myself most of the time, the notes and worksheet took 2 hours on average, the in class iclickers were terrible because they are very stressful especially for a topic we just learned.

Just finished the final exam. Just know these ratings you're seeing are generous compared to what she actually is. She is not understanding, helpful, nor does she effectively teach her class. Her way of teaching is rambling off words that r on the slide and does not explain. She was put on social probation for a reason. DO NOT TAKE THIS SECTION.
Good luck going to med school with Marville killing your GPA!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Kelly Marville is a brilliant professor with much experience, but her grading procedure makes her class so hard. She refuses to curve (even with failing averages) while giving the most work and hardest exams of the 102 professors. She offers retakes which is the only reason people pass. You'll have a letter grade higher with any other teacher.

I took online Chem102 with Dr. Marville this semester and while she's not that bad of a teacher, her grading procedures are terrible. There are 3 'hour exams' that consist of 15 multiple choice questions in 50 mins and are extremely difficult. There were over 100 kids in my section and only 7 got a perfect score on one of them.
Probably the toughest Gen Chem I teacher out there, but her lectures are well made and the grading criteria is well-lined out. If you put in the work, you'll be fine.

I was nervous about Marville going into the course because I read this page, but honestly I don't feel like she is as bad of a professor as people say she is. Tests are pretty easy, though punishing if you make some mistakes, and her lectures are pretty good, even if she goes fast sometimes.
rip if you have Marville

not terrible for a weeder class. doing the practice problems on the discussion worksheets helps a lot because they're pretty similar to the exam questions. i usually have to review the slides myself after lecture because she tends to rush through them. ridiculous amount of weekly homework.

YALL. DO NOT MAKE THIS MISTAKE. pick another teacher. She was on social probation because she failed too many students a couple years back and she hasn't changed. Her tests are not curved even though the averages are around 55%. The wording of the questions on the exams do not make sense. DONT TAKE THIS TEACHER!!
guys......

Dr Marville rush through her slides, she expects the students to have read/written down what was on the slide in 5 seconds and moves on. We can't ask questions during lecture because it takes up too much time during class. Her explanations for difficult concepts don't make sense, and I end up teaching myself the lecture using YouTube videos.

Professor Marville's class is challenging, but the lectures and homework are very helpful in learning the material. Utilize all the online resources, including unstuckstudy, to prepare for the exams. Attend every class and stay engaged, as the iClicker questions can impact your grade.
