She is alot better in the spring for chem 104 because she knows that people who take general chemistry ii are not whiney engineers who are "forced" to take chemistry and she is alot better.
I loved this class because it was the bomb

Dr. Marville is a excellent professor and is always willing to help her students. I would strongly suggest attending office hours and asking for help when you need it, she will respect that and will be more willing to give you a good letter of recommendation in the future. She is a great professor and mentor to entering freshman.

Marville is always ready to help you, as long as you show that you have put in the work and attempted to understand the material. She really wants her students to succeed. Do the book problems and practice tests. This makes the class so much easier.

Lectures are good for explaining material, I didn't even buy the book. I suggest looking through the PowerPoints before class so they make more sense and so you can ask questions/go to office hours as soon as possible. Speaking of office hours, they're really important if you ever want to be liked by her. Quizzes however are unnecessarily hard.
Very cut throat hard professor, clear concise lectures. Expects the best from her students

Amazing lectures. Concise. fridays were fast-paced,useful clicker days.. I received an A- in this class after the very very very brutal final (Study hard for it guys!) Chem discussions are pointless to go to unless you have a good TA because she posts the worksheet keys online. Do not read the textbook, go off the powerpoint, hw worksheet problems.

She is an incredibly smart woman and gives great lectures. However, she can be very intense when lecturing and she expects you to completely understand the material at the level she does for exams. Loved her as a professor but this class is very difficult. Be prepared to put a lot of time in.

Dr. Marville is a very intelligent woman. However, here intelligence makes it difficult for her to understand that even in a general chemistry class that some topics may be difficult for students to master or even understand. she embarrasses people for not understanding material in lecture, she makes her class extra difficult. I would not recommend

She speeds through lectures and expects you to be prepared beforehand with the knowledge she will be covering in class. Her tests are pretty difficult. But if you really put in the effort, you should manage to do ok.

She is very intelligent, but she expects her students to understand the material as well as she does by the exam, which is a very hard standard. My biggest criticism is that she gives you fairly simple problems to solve in lecture and discussion, then makes them much more complex on the exam without you having practice at that difficulty level.

Dr. Marville is an extremely intelligent woman but she speeds through lectures (50 minute classes and she was done in 25-30 minutes almost every time) and expects you to understand what she's saying immediately. DO NOT TAKE CHEMISTRY WITH HER if you want a good grade. Never struggled with a science class more than this, and I'm a senior now w a 3.7

Marville is a very organized and efficient lecturer. Lectures are easy to follow. She doesn't like stupid questions, which scares a lot of people away. A lot of people on here have said that her tests are unfair, but they are very doable if you understand the material and are a decent problem solver.
She is tough, but a good teacher. Avoid if possible, her tests are actually the worst thing ever.
Lectures are fast-paced. Tests are difficult. She expects you to have some understanding of the material before she teaches it.

If you want to have a good GPA by the time you graduate I strongly suggest avoiding Marville. She constantly mentioned the engineers in class and purposefully made the material harder for their sake. Tests were significantly harder than every other chem class's. Lectures were unclear and very confusing. Biggest regret taking her class.
Amazing teacher, tough tests.

Please! Please! Please! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH MARVILLE! She was condescending, rude, and degraded her students; even to the students who worked hard. If you do not want to be verbally abused then do not take her class!
She's tough but you feel like you understand the concepts after lectures.

If you can, avoid taking this class with Marville. Condescending doesn't even begin to describe her during office hours. Looking back, the material was not hard at all, but her explanations were often confusing; she made basic algebra seem like rocket science. Would not recommend her class at all.
This class is taught as if you have already taken AP chemistry. Don't ask questions, you will receive a condescending response.

Marville is an extremely serious and strict professor. She doesn't sugar coat anything and her explanations are often unclear and end up confusing you more. Tests are really really hard, but she gives you the opportunity to do better on the re-take. Online homework can take long, especially because you only get 10 tries.

She is very rude in office hours and acts like it is a hassle to help you. She makes this entry level course ridiculously difficult. Where other professors assign problems from the book she simply says "do them all". DO NOT HAVE HER
hard

She's a very difficult teacher. I never went to office hours for her because everyone else told me she was super rude to them. Her tests are insanely hard and she speeds through lectures. Try not to take her if you can.

She means business. Don't take this class lightly and definitely don't mess around. She can be intimidating at first, but if you genuinely care and want to do well... then this class should be no problem. And never have your phone ring in class, she WILL kick you out!

I took 17 hours my first semester at UIUC, all technical courses as I plan to go into engineering.  This professor told us we had to memorize the periodic table, and we did not need to.  Her tests put Hummel's to shame.  This teacher makes Chem 102 the hardest entry level course in this school.  Get Tina for your teacher if you value your grades.

Very good lecturer, and clear about what will be on the tests. Tests are hard but fair. She is extremely intelligent and explains things very well if you go in and ask. She can be intimidating but she's actually very nice and happy to help. I you're willing to work hard and put in the effort, she will prepare you best for higher level chemistry
She was not very good at lecturing. Her level of explanation wasn't up to par and I had a really hard time learning the material in her class. Would not recommend.

She teached the lectures very well.. Because they were so simple. The tests on the other hand were unnecessarily difficult. I dont know why she made the tests so difficult when the overall concepts were portrayed as rather simple

Marville definitely knows what she is talking about, and I can see how a lot of students think she is tough. Even though the exams are pretty difficult,there is nothing in them that she doesn't go over. Just visit a TA instead of her office hours-- she can be intimidating. Overall, a fair teacher if you're willing to put in real effort in her class

she definitely knows what she is talking about.. but i think she makes her exams a lot harder than they need to be. the material is already pretty difficult as it is, and she makes them even harder. also, the only way you can get points back on the exam is by "retaking" the exam online, but you only get 2 tries per question and its still hard.
Just get a different professor. Please

People are right, Marville's exams are difficult but not rediculously so. Everything on the exams is covered at one point or another in lecture so as long as you go, study hard, and put in the time to do the make-up exams you should be able to get at least an A-.I enjoyed this class

Marville knew what she was talking about. However, she had the expectation that you would automatically understand what she was saying and had prior knowledge of everything. Her lectures were very simple however her tests and online quizes were impossible. She was also very very mean during office hours. Save yourself and get a different professor
Very smart lady, but she does not know how to give lectures. She gives gives worksheets that are only half as hard the exam questions. She is very difficult, even with having a 3 on the Chem AP exam.

Her lectures are just her reading her ppts way too fast to understand. Exams are unnecessarily difficult and I truly regret taking her course. Extremely arrogant and only tests you on little caveats & exceptions. Horrible, professor overall who doesn't care if the students learn or not. She's just mean for the sake of being mean. Take Huang.

She is a great teacher. She knows the information she is teaching and she knows how to teach it. Many people say that she is very hard and I would agree. If you study you will do fine. She is a great person. I had an hour conversation with her just about random topics. Great person, great teacher, difficult teacher. I recommend her by far.
Very Sweet lady! Class was very difficult

Marville is a fantastic teacher who knows her stuff and also knows how to logically teach it. She has funny stories and brings the energy in her lectures. Her class is a really humbling experience for all the engineers that think they know everything, so study if you want to do well! I would highly recommend her if you want a quality chem class.

Exams are very hard! Retake exams are harder than the exams themselves. Discussion didn't really help that much. Be sure to do the worksheets because most likely they are exam questions. If you want a better grade for chemistry, go with a different professor.

really hard on exams and quizzes. Although there is a retake after every mid-term, the questions are even harder than those in the exams. The average scaled score for the second mid-term is only 67, if you want an easy A on this course, better choose another professor.

Dr. Marville clearly loves chemistry, but she is not good at teaching it.  Her's is my least favorite class because the material she covers is not at all like what she puts on her tests.  The tests are much harder.  Not to mention she is very condescending to students during office hours and when asking general questions. I would avoid her classes
She's a decent lecturer. It's a bit annoying that she starts a few minutes before the class period starts. Other than that she makes things pretty clear in class.

Dr. Marville is a very smart woman, but I think she lets this get to her head. She is not a nice person. She acts superior to her students, and it is very annoying. Try to avoid having her as a professor if you can!!

Dr. Marville is a very engaging lecturer and obviously knows her stuff. However, in office hours she is still amped up so be prepared for the same sort of dynamic personality if you go in. Her tests are very difficult.  If you want an A you most know every piece of the material and understand it.  The final was easier than expected.
CHEM 102 is pretty hard, but I think Marville does a good job of preparing people for the exams and lecturing effectively. She curves the final grade by half a letter or so.

Dr. Marville knows the chemistry very well, and usually does a great job at conveying her knowledge to students. She is, however, VERY condescending to students in office hours. The class is moderately difficult, and if you need help I recommend going to a TA- she will just make you feel worse about yourself.

Dr. Marville is a great professor in that she is very clear as to what you need to know. She'll tell you what mistakes to avoid. She does show a little bit of bipolarity in her personality, so try not to be intimidated--especially during office hours. She chews everyone out! Keep going though! I promise it'll pay off and get you a better grade.

Completely swagged owttt! She's awesome! Her powerpoints tell you everything you need to know. Make sure you do the weekly worksheets and study hard, because exams are difficult and you only get 10 minutes for each quiz. She's clear about what her expectations are and what she wants you to know.

She was very organized which was nice. She puts all her powerpoints online for easy acess. Do not underestimate her tests. People say chemistry is hard at UIUC for a reason. She makes the class hard but is a responsible teacher. After talking to my friends She is defaintly the best choice out of the three 102 teachers

I got used to the accent, but I never got used to the frantic Iclicker quizzes in lecture. Tests were extremely difficult, and she makes the tests to set you up to run out of time if you don't have the material down solid. Weekly online quizzes are timed also but homework gets you a lot of points. Overall stressful but she's extremely knowledgeable

Marville clearly knows her field. However, taking her for 102 was intimidating. She is intense in lecture to keep everyone's attention and forgets to turn in down in a one-on-one office hours situation. I would highly recommend her IF you don't think you will need to go to office hours. Otherwise, Hummel is the way to go for 102.

Marville is a magnificient teacher. The way she constructs her quizzes and iClicker questions prepare her students for exams. Attending every lecture will benefit anyone who takes her class. Any problem we do, she goes over and explains. She always gives tips for how to take exams. Considering I had Jamieson last semester, she's a great switch.

The class itself was stressful to say the least. Iclicker questions were extremely challenging and given without prior warning. She would teach the information, then immediately quiz on it. Accent took time to get used to, and speeds through the material. Gives a fantastic curve at the end of the course so half the class wouldn't fail.

Very knowledgeable in her field. Provides many real world examples to clarify content. Extremely difficult exams, but manageable if you prepare correctly. In the end, the class is curved. However, don't let yourself take that for granted.

Her quizzes are pretty tough, but the homework and quizzes are  easier. Just don't miss much on those and you should be fine. She is kind of tough and moves fast, but she really does want you to do well. Not to mention she has an awesome accent, so at least that will make you pay attention in class.

She has an awesome accent that takes a while to get used to. She moves very fast in class, however has the powerpoints available online. Her quizzes and homeworks were fairly easy.Marville and my TA thought I would do well on the exams, but I failed all of them. They are very tricky and hard. My advice is do well on ALL the homework and quizzes.

Good lecturer who provides you with all the study materials you need.  HOWEVER, her exams are very difficult.  practice exams may be easier than actual exams, but the quizzes are very close to the difficulty of the exams.
she is really nice and funny.  the ppts which you can also downland on the lon- capa are really clear and useful.  I missed my final exam but she still gave me another chance. she is awesome.
While her class and exams were difficult, if you study and know how all of the theory works it is very doable.
She uses practice exams that are easy and the actual exams are impossible

Unless you are a whiz at chem before entering the class, I would go with another professor. Speeds through material that could take weeks to learn in just 50 min. Her tests are pretty near impossible & look nothing like the material she gives you to prepare with.  Chem102 is a challenging enough class; taking it with Marville makes it much harder.

CHEM 102 is a challenging class with any professor at U of I. Dr. Marville's exams can be difficult, but she does give you plenty of materials to prepare you for them. The key to this class is to practice. Do the weekly packet in discussion (q's similar to test/quiz q's). I like that her quizzes were online, because they were essentially open book.
exam's and the final was hard, but she curved our overall class in the end!

I honestly wish I would have looked into other professors before choosing her class. It was so difficult. The exams looked nothing like what she taught in lecture, the homework, or even quizzes. Rarely curves. Yelled at our class because people did so badly because it was so HARD. She is the worst professor for chem 102.
Calls students ungrateful, rarely curves, gets angry at scores below average, knows her subject well but that's her downfall.  She is not a teacher, she is better off doing instead of showing.

She doesnt teach right and yells at us for getting a bad average midterm score. Curved our exam 3 from a 50% to a 60% and called us ungrateful. Horrible at teaching and going over material. She didnt care if we failed her class either, saying "see you next semester!" Do yourself a favor and take someone else for chem 102..

She has a fantastic Jamaican accent and knows everything about chemistry. Unfortunately, she zips through material really fast and I often left lecture feeling lost. Luckily I had a great TA and didn't have any problems with the class overall. I never used office hours but I heard hers were great, she'd sit with students for hours until they got it

She seems very knowledgeable about chemistry but she is definitely not geared towards being helpful to others in the classroom. She has a confusing way of doing stoich, moves too fast to take notes and comprehend them in lecture, and she makes easy concepts seem difficult. I would not recommend this professor to ANYONE. She also isn't approachable.
She's a nice woman, very knowledgeable, but she belongs somewhere other than the classroom.

This class is a breeze if you took Chem 101 and took it seriously. IF you didn't take 101 then prepared to study like crazy for the first exam. Marville explains everything you need to succeed in the exam but almost to the point that she makes it seems getting an A on the exam is better than actually understanding the concepts.
Extremely hard class, but she is fair overall.

I think Marville was probably one of the best Chem 102 professors available all you have to do is put in the effort. My advice to you is go to class, she basically tells you what topics and types of questions will be on the exam. Do the mock exams, the worksheets, the homework. You can get an A if you just put in the effort.
She has a tough class but gives you all the materials you need to be successful.  Just do the practice exams PLUS the extra worksheets and you will be fine.

Marville is a decent teacher, but manages to make fairly easy material seem confusing.  She has a confusing way of doing stoich, but her tests are straight forward.  Go to class, take notes (don't just print off the powerpoint), study the notes the night before the test, and you'll be fine.
Only reads off powerpoints, explains everything in a confusing manner, doesn't clarify anything

She's a good chemist, but a bad teacher and unfit to instruct anyone about anything. She has ZERO desire to help struggling students and gets angry if you don't understand her nebulous, disorganized way of explaining concepts during her office hour. But the whole point of office hour is to learn what you don't know. So it defeats the purpose.

best teacher i ever had!! if you go to her office hour,you will know she's very patient at explaining,she'll make sure you truly understand the materials. She had spent over half an hour with me for just one question and make sure i understand, very approachable, you'll know if you talk to her...i just love the way she teaches!!!
She's got an awesome accent. But she doesn't explain things in a way that makes sense. Also, her tests are pretty hard if you're not used to working for your As

There are better chemistry professors out there. Her tests are relatively easy...the problem is she really doesn't teach in class. All she does is repeat the power points, but attendance is mandatory so you have to go to class anyways. So, yeah....if you are already good in chem or you are good at learning things on your own, then go for it.

I loved her! She takes the time to get to know her students, and she spent extra time with me in office hours before the exams, even when she was only supposed to spend 20 minutes with each student. She actually cares about how her students are doing, and her exams are easy if you know you're stuff. Plus, her accent's cute. WAY BETTER THAN TOM H!!

This class is definitely challenging. Dr. Marville is a great chemist, her skills as a professor are lacking sometimes. Study every bit of material for exams and do practice worksheets. This class is not an easy A, but it is doable.

I would say her class isn't easy. I also would say that if you TRY a little harder, you will be fine. If you struggle, just go ask professor, because she is more than willing to help you. She is very nice and encouraging. I like that she always takes time to help the students first... no matter how long it might take.

She is the best professor that I have been met. Her office hour is infinite.Once, I stayed in her office for 3 hours asking questions, and she always smiling to help students answering questions. Exams are easy first time, and then gets harder. But she curve a lot. but she has accent, everytime I have to go back to read ppt again after lectures.

Very hard to understand her. Her lectures are also pointless because she talks super fast and just reads off the powerpoint. But the lectures are mandatory because she gives iclicker points. Her exams are extremely difficult and confusing. I recommend you go talk to her once a week about the material. Her powerpoints arent helpful too.

I would recommend her to anyone.  She legitimately cares about her students, which is sometimes a hard thing to find on this campus.  Exams are pretty difficult but her office is always open and wants to help. The accent is a little much at first but you get used to it.

She is extremely open and helpful. She talks really fast in lecture but if you ask her to slow down she does. Her tests are difficult, but she curves and having a good TA will help tremendously. Probably not as good as Hummel, but definately 2nd best
He is one of the best professors I have ever met. He always give positive feedback which is really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor. He cared about his students and wants to help succeed. The course may be difficult but he knows what he is doing and is passionate about actuarial science. I wish more courses here were taught by him.
Best professor in Actuarial Science Department. Pretty nice on grading.

Lecture is not mandatory but it's easier to understand slideshow notes if you attend lectures. Tests and quizzes are all very fair and pretty straightforward. Only tricky parts is memorizing the formulas because there's a lot.

He explained complex concepts very simply, lectures were great.  He tells you exactly the type of problems that will be on the exams.  Very little homework.  Show up to the lectures for extra credit.  I did not use the textbook, only the examples for studying.  50% final is stressful.  Great class, great teaching.  Hoping to have him again soon.

Lazy professor. Did not tell us what was going to be on the final until 4 days before. Never had homework or outside reinforcement. Reads off of textbook. By week 4 no one came to class. Cannot say I have learned anything in his class.

His teaching is far to difficult to follow. There is no homework and no clear expectation of what is tested on. I do not feel like I learned a great deal as slides are vague. There are not many resources on canvas to study. Midterm average was a 60.

This review is for ASRM 210, he posts lecture slides with many mistakes that are not addressed unless you catch it yourself in an already hard class. Hard to understand, and gives almost no direct resources that actually relate to the things that will be on the exam.
Most boring lecture. Reads off of slides and textbook. No homework you have to guess what's on exams. Exams have typos.

I think she is great at explaining topics and she clearly cares about her students, and she's funny. She is very very good at responding to homework questions outside of class on Campuswire. Test heavy class, but there are a lot of opportunities to get extra credit on homework for doing homework early.

She seems to be nice enough. I thought this class would be a breeze having already taking Calc 1. She explained simple concepts very poorly. Tests at CBTF were very different from lectures and even practice tests. I would switch sections. I have no doubt she is very intelligent, but doesn't seem to be good at teaching concepts.

She is an excellent lecturer but does not upload material (she lectures on a blackboard). Her class is very test heavy and the exams are very challenging. The final 2 (out of 4) CBTF midterms are quite different from the practice tests and homeworks. The final exam is also very tough. She is very kind and connects with students well.

Professor Kim was a great professor and was mostly clear with explanations during lecture. There are many opportunities to practice and revise content before exams and quizzes. I personally understood her teaching style but sometimes she would go through examples really fast and I would have to take pictures to review later.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is very nice, but often times it felt like her lectures did not prepare for what was on the tests. The examples given in class were usually much simpler than those covered in grades discussion sections and ESPECIALLY those seen in quizzes. Be prepared to put in lots of time studying for tests to do well or if you have not taken calc.
Good experience. Lectures were clear and easy to follow. Exams were definitely harder than I would expect from the lectures, in the sense that you can't just memorize formulas, you have to think.

She is a great person who cares about her students, however the tests you will take at the CBTF do not align with the material taught in lectures or the homework at all. Make sure you memorize how to do the practice tests instead, and you should do fine on the actual tests for the most part.
The first two exams are not bad because they are very similar to the practice exams the last two are more difficult. She is a pretty good lecturer and seems like she cares. Her exams are at the CBTF.

She's okay, friendly, but really hard to follow in lecture. You really gotta put in effort outside of the class to do well on the exams. It's worth most of your grade and hard to come back from a back grade. Really try in discussion as well. If you feel good about your calc knowledge it's okay but expect not to retain much from lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very test-heavy professor, exams in CBTF every two weeks, and many questions on exams with only 50 minutes to answer. If you can't consistently score high on exams, you won't get good grades. If you are a bad exam taker, don't take this class; you will get a bad grade. She doesn't curve. HW, worksheet, and exam are way harder than what she teaches.

It's clear that she cares about students and wants them to succeed. Her teaching is pretty standard, as if you were following the textbook. She's willing to give tons of support. Quizzes were tough and exams fair, but there's a good amount of resources to help you prep. Calc 1 is a learning curve for 1st years regardless of prof, but she's good.

She made so many mistakes in lecture and wasn't that great at teaching, in my opinion. The exams were way harder than any of the material we were given in class, and I never felt prepared. I had to essentially teach myself everything.

She was very difficult to understand and many time she made no sense when teaching. Throughout lectures she would make many basic math mistakes. If you are required to take the class please choose another professor, and if you have to take it with Dr. Kim prepare for her to connect to students through jokes and fun however not actually teaching.

Honestly just prepare to be doing a lot of learning outside of class. I wish I would've had more time to take advantage of office hours because lectures are simply not enough. I would recommend familiarizing yourself with the topics BEFORE even going into lecture because she jumps into complex concepts without giving any background on what it is.

Dr. Kim is very nice, funny, and caring. Her lectures are absolutely amazing, she explains concepts extremely well. Attendance is not manatory for MATH221 but it's absolutely worth it to wake up for an 8am when she's the one teaching.
She does not understand the material that well and constantly makes mistakes. Rushes through problems and expects students to finish them and understand the notes
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Plenty mistakes within lecture, often goes off-track, never answers questions directly, struggle to finish problems, messy handwriting, difficult exams that don't line up with the difficulty of lecture and homework notes. Often has her notes pre-written, BE FAST!
Would avoid this professor at all costs. Cares more about socializing than teaching!

Kim is a great person, and she engages well with her students. She often goes on tangents and makes lots of mistakes in class. She connects well with her students socially. During lectures it's hard to read her handwriting and I would often have to look at another professor's notes to understand the topics. She moves fast in lectures as well.
Professor Kim is very caring of her students. She tries to make the lectures as fun as possible and is an easy grader. If you are going to take Calculus, I definitely recommend taking her lecture.

didn't teach in class. Nice lady but cared more about connecting socially, than academically. she left many problems unfinished on our first day learning the topic cause "you should be able to finish it yourselves.Clear she thought everyone had a background in calc or was able to teach themselves. If you cant teach yourself you just might fail.

This is a case of a really nice Professor but is not a great lecturer. Lectures felt unplanned and often over complicated a topic despite her good intentions. My discussion TA sat in on one of her lectures and said "I understand why she has the lowest class average for the tests." Once again she is very nice but struggles to teach content clearly.

Down to earth professor who tries her best to make material as palatable as possible. Tends to rush through lecture material, often leaving problems incomplete. Is helpful on a one-to-one basis through various resources. Homework and other assignments usually much harder than lectures and exams, nonetheless grading is more favorable than harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Her teaching style is inconsistent and will confuse you if you have never taken calculus.  Better off watching full lecture vids on youtube

Lectures were a bit rushed, but there was a lot of material to cover, so A LOT of studying (3-5 hours/day) is required in order to get a good grade. Online homework and discussion worksheets are way more difficult than what's on the exam. Professor Whittlesey does care about our mental health and likes to give as much exam credit as possible.

Prof. Kim is kind and always willing to help. Calculus is a difficult class, and there's a lot of time you need to put in outside of class. Even with three lectures a week, it's unrealistic to expect to learn everything. I did well in this course by keeping up with practice problems, and I would go over every topic carefully before an exam.
good professor, teaches well, but the overall course content is difficult regardless of who your prof is. this course if very exam heavy. also be sure to be ready to drop $100 on the online text!

She's a nice lady but her lectures dont provide any helpful information at all. She rambles on about topics that make no difference, an example if when she talked about texas for 20 minutes for a 50 minute class. The help she gives after class also just leaves you with more questions. I recommend taking another professor, if you have her good luck.

She was nice but definitely one of the worst professors you can get for calc.  Lectures rarely made sense, had to learn a majority of the material outside of class, and exams were significantly more difficult than other sections.  Don't recommend.

I enjoyed her enthusiasm for the topic, however, a lot of the time the lectures only tangentially cover the homework assignments. I also felt the exams were a bit unfair, and I often felt like I couldn't really prepare for them, no matter how much I studied. The worksheet assignments were also disproportionately hard. Calc III is tough, good luck.
the material for this class is a breeze if you've taken high school calculus, can be easily tested out with proficiency exam, didn't study too much and received an A, took this class fall of 2021

Whittlesey has a charismatic personality, but her lectures are largely unhelpful. Midterms and the final make up 75% of the grade, so a perfect hw grade doesn't mean much. Midterms are usually 7-8 questions, so if you do badly on one question, you're already screwed. She also claimed that she would curve the final grade, but she did not.

I personally stopped attending lecture after the first exam, her lectures are simply not good, and the worksheets you do are way too hard, since they were graded by completion and not correctness. However, her exams have this weird way of making you feel smart for doung them properly. Use Paul's Online Calc Notes, and self study for the A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sometimes you need to do some reading outside of the class for better understanding on the materials. But the professor is really nice and patience. If you got questions you can always go ask.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Whatever you do, don't take this professor. Her test averages were at least 20-30 percent worse than other professors with the only trade off being that she will "curve the class at the end". The exams are extremely tough with averages in the mid 60s.

The main problem with Whittlesey is that the exams are more difficult AND graded much harder.

Her lectures were just her word vomiting her notes onto the chalkboard and then most likely making a mistake and having to erase everything and start over. It was her first time teaching 24 but I have heard from other students that she is like this in all of her classes. Find some other teacher. It's not worth it.
awful professor, not every hard exam, not any useful practice.

This is easily the worst professor I have ever had. You can put so much work into this class, complete the reviews and homework, and then the tests will be absolutely nothing like any of it. The average for the class is extremely low and she does not care about her students at all. Avoid Calc 3 with her at all costs because it is impossible.
Exam every two weeks at CBTF, only 5-6 questions. If you get two wrongs you will fail the exam. THe lecture is basically she's reading the slides. Don't take 221! take math220!

The lecture videos are just of her reading of slides, of maybe two examples and then moves on. The tests in the CBTF are all or nothing. Even if you know the material there is still a chance that you could fail the examlets. Be prepared to look up other lecture videos, and practice a whole bunch outside of class.
Probably the best calc teacher at UIUC. Lectures were super clear and she was very fair with grading

Lectures were clear and explain concepts pretty well. Tests were often difficult and sometimes much harder than quizzes and practice exams. There were several opportunities to get points though, and grading policies were fair.

Final is pretty easy. She gives extra credits if you finish WebAssign earlier. I don't think she is a good teacher but you can get an A as long as you spend some extra time. PLEASE DON'T TAKE Math 231 with Lena.

Not only was the class content disorganized, you'll also receive a lot of painfully difficult coursework. You also have at least 1 quiz or test weekly! But the coursework doesn't relate back to the quiz or test at all. If you get a bad TA like I did then there really is no hope to pass. My tip is to switch class immediately.

I do feel at times she goes through tough concepts quite fast, so self-revision is important. Exams are usually HARDER and not similar to what's given as practice. Quizzes and Exams can be dropped, and there is some extra cr

The exams are way more difficult than the homework/practice exams/worksheets. The lectures go over easy problems instead of the more difficult ones we see on the worksheets. Office hours are only once a week with the professor and she is very slow with answering emails. There is extra credit if you do homework early which in nice.

She seems like a really nice person who admittedly makes good lectures, but some questions on her quizzes and tests cover material that we have not even learned yet. There is no way to solve them unless you have already taken higher level math, and when you email her about asking for how to solve it with what we learned it is complete radio silence

Linear Programming is somewhat difficult, but Prof. Whittlesey makes the course interesting. It's her first time teaching this course, so the homework is quite tricky and conceptional, but she will surely do much better in the future semesters.

reviews.comment: Professor's lecture is cool. She is a cute person.

reviews.comment: It's definitely a tough class and there is a lot of work that needs to be put into it. That being said, go in for office/tutoring hours if you are confused with anything as it is much more helpful than just the lectures.
I thought that the class was extremely challenging and I did not find her very helpful at answering my questions, but this may be because I was so lost for most of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Calc II is SUPER hard but she is a great professor. She will explain things as well as she can, but it really is up to you to do your homework and go to tutoring to figure the rest out.

This class felt like a very long marathon to live through. The homework was very stressful and difficult. To get a good grade, you have to put in every single bit of effort you know how to give. There were many TAs available for help. Kim was good at explaining lectures, but it was very fast paced
she is really funny and clear during classes. Super patient too.  unexpectedly she made the class actually interesting. overall, comon its math you have to study for it.
Funny, very concise in lecture, very good at explaining things, cares about her students' success

Kind professor who will go out of her way to help you so long as you ask for it. With that being said, her lectures can sometimes be unorganized and not very clear. Attending office hours is highly recommended.
I like this professor so much. She is hilarious and makes learning math such a interesting thing!
Good teacher.

Very good lecturer and sarcastically funny. Quite helpful if you attended office hours, and doing midterm/final exam reviews are a must. Class was difficult and she was challenging, however I would still recommend this professor.
Excellent professor, very clear examples, and generous curve.  She may be a little more difficult on the exams, but it is very reasonable for Calc for peoplewho have taken calculus.

Took her calc 1 class, she is a lecturer and lecturers like one. Her class is harder than the other professors calc classes. She is clear and makes sense, she will take the time to explain at office hours. I bought the book, very expensive, used it for homework once. Only reason to buy is bc it is required for calc 1 through 3.

Book is pricey and only used twice. Buy it on IBX and get WebAssign from the source. Whittlesey is clear, concise, passionate, and sarcastically funny. If you don't care, you won't do well. Don't sleep, chat, or disrespect her.  Do the midterm reviews.  They tell you almost exactly what will be on the exams. You'd be a fool not to. Best TAs ever.
I thought she was great!  she really explained well, and made calculus somewhat enjoyable!

She is a great professor! The class isn't easy and the homework and tests are hard, but if you put in the effort, you can do well. She is extremely helpful, especially in office hours, and funny. Definitely recommend her for Math 221!
She is the best professor giving me lecture at this semester.

Had way to much homework per week; it was all so unnecessary. Never had any idea what was going to be on the exam, plus the TAs made you feel stupid for not understanding something. Waste of time considering I still havent learned anything.

Horrible class. Web homework will consume your time enormously. Her lecture is disorganized and unclear. Exams and quizzes are ridiculously difficult. I saw 90% of people couldn?t finish the exam when the time was over. I expect A for this class but I don?t want to meet this professor again.

Took her class last semester.  Was sick for the first exam and spoke with her about missing the exam.  She said to get a doctors note and two exams would be averaged instead of three.  Received a zero on the exam and a D+ for the course.

Her tests are really hard. Make sure that you go to your TA office hours, otherwise you will be so lost. I hated going to lecture, but I had to since some things she explains a specific way (and thats necessary to get the points on her exams/quizzes). Try to avoid!

The class is challenging, but not impossible. She is an excellent lecturer. She may go fast but if you review the notes afterwards it's not really a problem. Exams are extremely difficult, so make sure you study. There is ALWAYS a huge curve so it's not bad.

Smart professor, but not the best at explaining problems. She leaves out steps and often leaves me confused. You will probably benefit more from your T.A than her. Her study guides are generally harder than her test, which aren't too bad.

I am a freshman coming from a low income high school and so far my grade for this class is A-.  Go to every lecture and discussion, study her study guides + homework problems and you guarantee yourself at least a B.
tests are not real situations; far too difficult

I'm not sure why people think she is so bad. If you pay attention, stay awake, study for the tests, and go to her office hours, you can do ok. She is a pretty funny person. Sometimes her lectures can be unclear, but she tries to work with the class.
Her tests and quizzes are ridiculously hard, and I have yet to stay awake for a whole lecture.  Try to get a new section if you get this class.

Not good at lecturing, but they are a must if you want to pass. Very helpful when I needed help for filing for withdrawal from the course. However, I did hear there was a huge curve on the class, so maybe it was unneccessary, but oh well.
Poor teacher. Does not explain the basic elements of calculus well, so her students suffer. I always thought I did well at math, but she showed me otherwise.
Dr. Whittlessey does not explain mathematical principles enough for a freshmen calc class for architects. Many people in the course I took in Fall 2005 failed it.

Horrible class. She makes it tedious and impossibly hard. The TA that I had could NOT speak English and made it seem like a chore when I came to her for help. The tests only cover the incredibly difficult concepts and the study guides are ambiguous. GET ANOTHER PROFESSOR!

She likes to start some lectures with pointless videos but its alright. I had to literally read the book to get an A. My TA was pointless. Best to read over the material before the lecture. She likes to go pretty fast. I don't think her outfit ever changed. Black top. Brown Bottom.
She went too fast, so if you have never taken calculus before and have her try and find a new teacher.

I have not seen calculus before i took this class. I bombed my first midterm, but then the second midterm was easy, the third midterm was okay. The final was so hard, but really curved. All you need in order to do well in this class is study your butt off.  This is not an easy class, but if you try then you should do well. I ended up getting a B.

class isn't very interesting. you will need to go to all lectures since notes are only in lecture. make sure to always be paying attention and that you understand the material since the exam is ten times harder than what she teaches. the final is crazy, she curved like crazy since no one understood anything on it. take the class if you like math.

Very  nice teacher..She really cares about her students and their understanding...Can also be very funny...Lecture is mandatory because of the notes she gives...Exams are very hard, especially the final

Very poor teacher.  She weights the tests to the hardest  material, so if you get everything until the last day of each chapter you'll fail. Oh, and she wears the same thing everyday, seriously gross.

A hard class, go to lecture at every opportunity. If you haven't had any calculus experience it may be difficult for you. I know it was for me. She's funny and encourages participation. Don't sleep in class, pay attention and do the homework. Study and memorize what she tells you to. You'll do fine.

Teaches and explains things well, i recommend you go to the lectures if you havent seen Calc in high school or you will be lost. She does not communicate at all with the TA's so you dont really know what the tests are going to be like. She makes up the tests probably two days before the test and the study guides she gives dont really help much.
teaches as if everyone's already learned calculus.  not a bad teacher, but goes really fast. difficult class.

This class isn't that difficult for people who have seen calc before and had a pretty good understading understanding of it. The difficulty of her exams aren't consistent. She is a good teacher but I recommend this class for people who have an interest in math otherwise it can get a bit boring and difficult.

She is a good teacher who clearly knows what she's talking about but she does run through material quickly.  For Calc 1 she taught to the level of those who had seen Calc before in high school.  She varied the difficulty of exams, one was hard, one was easy, and one was just okay.

very nice lady.  i had calculus beforehand but i still found her a very good teacher.  Better calc teacher than the one i had in high school.  she actually cares how her students do and explains things pretty well.
kind teacher. good at explaining things and explains more for those who don't understand
HORRIBLE CLASS AND RIDICULOUS EXAMS!
drop now!!! she goes way to fast   . she makes her test harder than they actually are just because she asks you some pretty random crap. bad teacher

Nice lady. Her style is for those who somewhat understand the material beforehand. prepare to invest in tutoring or get help from someone who knows what they're talking about because in class you won't find that for the amount of help you'll need.

this teacher goes way too fast in class.  u end up just writing the whole time and not understanding anything.  i would recommend not taking her class if uve never taken it in high school.  she also wears the same clothes every day, a black t shirt and khaki slacks. eww
Go take her class if you think you're good at math. She's pretty fast.A cool person.

Horrible! Don't even bother trying to look at her test checklists. You'll end up studying for topics that won't ever be on the midterms! She's so random and half the time I don't even think she knows what she's teaching. If you can, find a different math professor!
one word: drop this class

although i refer to her as "witlessly", she's a good teacher who enjoys saying "slice it up" "chop" "x not" and other weird things...you must see her be a mime in a box, and i'm tellin ya, who wouldnt tap that fine heiney
a good teacher..however i didnt see her after the first week because i did not attend class..but she wrote easy tests
a very good math professor, makes calculus easy to understand even if you aren't a "math person"

Khoury's great at explaining content so just pay attention in class and you'll be fine

My favorite Political Science professor I have had so far. Her lectures are so easy to follow along and the way she structures her class is so helpful for succeeding. The content is genuinely interesting and she explains the concepts in a way that is engaging and easy to understand and apply. She is so sweet and personable as well.

One of the best professors I've had! Amazing at explaining things in a relatable away and clearly cares a lot about what she's teaching. Class is very low maintenance, but you want to make sure you do the readings! Reflection papers aren't too difficult and help you understand the material better. Take her social movements class!

Professor Khoury really cares about what she talks about in her class. She shows care for her students and she really makes the lectures very interesting. I really love how she does case reflections and no exams. The case reflections are pretty easy to do and the class was overall really nice!

Professor Khoury was super nice and the class is pretty chill - no tests and a short paper biweekly. We also had the opportunity to talk with a few movement leaders throughout the semester. If you do the necessary reading and turn in case reflections you should get an A.

Loved Professor Khoury. Extremely knowledgeable in her field. Got many guest speakers and other experts in the field to come talk to our class. A lot of exercises to understand how and why certain scenarios happen. Would definitely take a class from her again.

(SMC) Dr. K is highly knowledgeable in her field. However, that does not stop her from conveying messages in an entertaining and easy-to-follow method for students to understand the complex social theory around social movements. She made this class easily one of the most valuable and entertaining classes I have had at UIUC. She's a great professor!

if you hate overly structured classes then this is for you, no quizzes, only a few short (2-3 page) papers one every 2 weeks over whatever you want. Social Movements and contention taught by her is fantastic. A great new teacher who is always ready to help.

CONS: If you get a bad group for a project your grade could be lowered, quality of the course is completely dependent on your TA for discussion. Online Lecture videos were long and boring. The discussion sections are also pretty boring. took this class asynchronously. was a very easy class-barely studied and if i did, it was the night before the exam. at the same time though, some concepts taught in this course were generally interesting to learn about. knipp explains things so well in his textbook (the required e-text for the course).

reviews.comment: Pay attention to study guides and watch the screenings and you'll do fine. One of my favorite professors I've ever had, take his MACS 282 or 496 if you can. The fact that this class has so many students means he can't be as accessible to everyone as he wants, but he runs himself ragged trying. But you may need to remind him to reply to your email.

Good prof that is passionate about what he does and cares about students. Does not post lecture slides so attendance is essentially mandatory to receive information that will be on exams. reviews.comment: This class was really difficult as there was a lot to memorize. The averages on exams were not good, but he did offer a bit of extra credit. Knox also provided homework as a resource, which was slightly more helpful than Miller's. Far too much information for one semester. He was very nice and funny, though. Iclicker is used.

Good luck. All his exams are a whole bunch of nothing with answer options from A-E and most of them are "none of the above" "all of the above" A and B only." I have learned nothing. He reads off of his slides which are useless. You have to teach yourself for everything. Class averages are never higher than 60%. For how old he is, he needs to retire

Personally, Knox was way better than Miller. Knox gave extra credit on his exams and homework/quizzes to try and get your grade back up. The exams overall are difficult but you're more likely to do better on his. I liked the material of this course but it was a LOT for a 200 level. Knox honestly is horrible. He asked for feedback when he provided no study resources and when students expressed concerns he blamed it on the students rather than his teaching methods. You basically have to teach yourself, and even then it's super difficult. The tests are more "understanding the concept" type questions.

Professor Knox refuses to make the effort to help his students. What he has been doing for the "last 15 years" will be the way he does it until the end of time. Fair grading. the end-of-semester workshop is a little annoying, but still a great class to take. Textbook material takes up 40% of the exams. Invest in one.
Great class, learned a lot. Material applicable to everyday life. Grading fair and the lectures were interesting.

I love this class. Professor is really clear and interesting. However you will despise the textbook but she is forced to use it. Easy grade as long as you do your end of the work. Study what is only on the study guide & you get to make your own grading scale to play towards your strengths (i.e. if your good at writing papers) .. take this class

Professor Knobloch is great. She is really enthusiastic and makes an effort to connect with students. The material in this class is really interesting and useful. The tests are really easy if you do the study guide (which requires the textbook) and the writing assignments are not time consuming.
Loved this course! It was challenging but I learned a lot. GREAT PROFESSOR.
Not sure what previous poster was talking about! This was a hard course but I learned a lot.

Class is super easy. 3 "papers" throughout the semester, 1 page each..just rewriting what she has already told us in class. Exams are easy, all multiple choice. While her lectures can be confusing, she's willing to explain anything students are confused about- even after lectures. She also frequently reviews previous lessons. Her grading scale is very fair, she gives an easy extra credit assignment that brings up your final grade by 3%.
Very interesting and well taught class. Readings could be abstract but there was good class review on the different materials.

reviews.comment: Class was ok, some of the readings felt repetitive. The grading was a bit harsh with no real explanation behind it and she was not in attendance for some classes due to other commitments. I definitely would not recommend taking her classes during the summer.
She is a rockstar instructor. Is very knowledgable and articulate. A fair grader and an interesting background. She is organized and clear.
A very particular grader, but very willing to discuss assignments ahead of time.  Very knowledgeable and eager to help those who show interest in the work.

Prof is very nice and receptive to feedback. Grading should be lenient according to what he said in lecture 1, but it's not listed in syllabus. Class is very boring material unfortunately. Need to read textbook on your own time as the slides are not very good and lectures are not comprehensive. prof is very kind, though.
Lots of course components (homework, quizzes, tests, etc) but very lenient grading. Lectures are clear and material is not too complicated.

The course is heavy on math, be sure to know linear algebra and multi calculus well before taking it. The slides are the worst and not on point, along with super little explanation on key points, will need a lot of out of class research and YouTube. The course is pretty difficult in content itself.
No

Andreas is a really nice professor. I would say he is the best professor I ever had at UIUC. He always prepared for his lecture, explained everything in great detail. I think he developed the homework system. I would recommend taking CS357 with him. It really helps me with my Python.
Professor is always prepared for class and really friendly to the students. He really cares about teaching and can explain topics in different ways if you don't understand it.
the material is dry but he is super enthusiastic about the course and tries to be as clear as possible.  He gives quiz online to make sure we actually understand the material, good teacher.

One of the best CS professors at UIUC. Although this class's material is rather dry, he gives enthusiastic lectures and puts a lot of work into the class. He's very helpful and goes out of his way to provide feedback and react quickly to logistic issues. He also maintains the course site and welcomes feedback from students! Andreas is awesome.

very cool guy, receives feedback and adjusts the course accordingly. I wish every professor was as thoughtful and helpful as he is. Although the class somewhat lacked an organized way of presenting the material, i'm sure he will improve that in no time. I have great respect for him

He's a good guy and cares about his students; I'm not sure he's the best teacher for this class, though. Lecture format is weird with only notebook scribbles and Python demos to study from. Homework questions were hit or miss when  it came to their  relevance to the coursework. Tests were usually brutal and depended somewhat on lucky guessing.

I had her for ECON 456, and I genuinely do not understand how her rating is so low.  She proved to be an absolutely amazing professor though.  She is a strong lecturer, a fair grader, she is quite knowledgable, and she works very hard to help her students.  The workload is a bit high - but normal a 400 level course, and the expectations are clear.

Contrary to popular opinion, I enjoyed her as a professor. The class is somewhat unorganized and the grading criteria is all over the place. The exams are all written and very difficult to complete in 80 minutes. Make friends in this class to work on homework because otherwise it's impossible (there are no guidelines). No extra credit and no curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The most ridiculous class I've ever taken. The professor is the worst professor I've met in the college. She taught nothing in lectures and only wasted time on talking about homework guidelines. What's the worst is that she would never answer any of your question after class. Also the homework is terrible. Never take this class please.

She's the worst prof that I met in my life. She use more than half of the class to talk about her requirements for homework. Few knowledge about economics. No past exam example for the exam and she says she never gave curve. Her homework will cost lots of time and her grading is confusing. The worst thing is that her attitude is totally bad.

She is one of the most confusing and horrible prof I have seen in my life. 5 hws take up around 20% of your final grade. Grading without any guidline and spending the whole lecture on explaining the graph for the hw. She even refuses to answer your question right after the class simply because it is not her office hour. Don't take her class.
This is probably one of the easier upper level econs. 5 homeworks, 2 midterms, and a final paper and presentation. It is not necessary to attend class.

This is the most time wasting professor I have ever seen. She spends at least 30 minutes of each of her lessons on explaining poorly written homework guidelines or slides. The rest of the time she spends explaining descriptive statistics graphs.  Grading emphasizes  form over substance. If you want to learn Economics, do not take her class.

Professor Kleemans is great! She is one of the best professors I've had at UIUC and certainly one of the best within the Econ department. Definitely take her if you are looking for a class that isn't too hard, but will teach you a lot.

Professor Klonoff graded pretty hard and the majority of the grade was based on the discussion assignment she assigns every Friday. She was accessible outside the classroom which was good but the iClicker questions were confusing. Lectures were just her reading a powerpoint so you need to put extra time and work to be able to succeed in this class.

All she did was read off her slides, and you had to teach yourself. One time she went 7 minutes over class time and I ended up being late to my next class. She also likes to call on students out of nowhere to answer her iClicker questions that never made sense. Grading system in this class was just based on exams and quizzes and one group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class structure was a hybrid of in-person and online. You basically teach yourself as the professor uploads PowerPoints on Compass; it was very confusing. The only in-person interaction you'll have is in your discussion section and with your group project. Stay on top of your group and semester project, follow the syllabus, and you'll be okay.

She is the worst professor I have had on this campus. The rubric doesn't even tell you the class structure, you learn from PowerPoint, the assignments have no rubrics and you get stupid points taken off. Also, people don't show up to class and you have to do group projects that don't connect to the course work. I have never been more confused.

Not much to say because Prof KC was nonexistent for this class. You basically just teach yourself the material off of powerpoint slides. Prof KC pops up before the exam to just reiterate the material you just taught yourself. You meet with a TA once a week for them to give you the answers to the homework. Horrible class structure.

There is literally 3 days until the course is over and I still do not know 75% of my grade. The last email did not even state the correct meeting date for the last of the only 3 lectures we actually had. Last assignment people got credit back for 3/5 questions, but I got those right so my grade didnt boost like everyones. Not very fair at all.

The teacher reused material from CHLH 201 for her slides. No live lecture or recorded slides, just PowerPoint. Made it incredibly difficult to absorb the material. The whole class is based on seven things you learn from the first two things. Very redundant.

I have never in my life taken any class that was as bad as this one. No organization, no class structure, discussion sessions nothing happens, assignments lack basic instructions, literally every aspect is bad. We saw the professor only twice this semester and she keeps repeating that we should be "brave". How about you be brave and fix the course?

The lack of communication between Dr. Klonoff-Cohen and the teaching assistants in this course is astounding. Neither the professor nor the teaching assistant shows up to class prepared. Difficult to figure out what to do for assignments due to vague directions, a lack of examples, and no rubric, so you have no idea what they're looking for at all.

Absolutely awful course! Lack of communication between her and the TA just resulted in some of the discussion sessions doing weeks more worth of work! Nothing is organized and there is literally no teaching being done! Worst class in my 4 years at UIUC.

I would have to say that this is so far the most disorganized and confusing course I have taken in community health. There are grammatical and spelling mistakes in her lectures slides and the way the lectures are set up makes absolutely no sense. I am somewhat confused as to how this is even a course considering how badly its put together.

She doesn't teach in a way that's clear, and is often contradictory in her lessons. Majority of the class gets iClicker questions wrong. She is combative when you ask a question and is absolutely not open to suggestions. Easy course, horrible teacher.
Very unclear on instructions. Changes the syllabus whenever she feels like it.

I had an A in this class up until the final. Theres only 6 assignments and 2 projects, but they dont have clear grading criteria. The class is also structured weird, and I feel like I learned nothing. Definitely work on the first semester project in advance because thats where I screwed up. Not a bad class if you dont procrastinate.
Dr. Kline is a great professor who has a passion for horses and teaches very well
He was a great professor overall. I went into this class with a good impression and left with a better one. Highly suggest.
Really great professor, tests are straightforward and gives you past exam to study from. Lab final is super, he let's you look at the stations before the exam at the stock pavilion.

In this class you get to train a weanling horse in ground manners! The COOLEST class I have taken hands down. Tests are nearly the exact same as the practice.  Easy A, super fun, and a professor who is really into what he teaches.

So easy and fun. Tests are very simple and he basically gives you the answers while you are taking them. Exams are almost a photocopy of practice exams with minor changes. When training the foal, only expects you to try, helps when you have problems, and shows you the correct/better way one on one when you ask.
What a great guy. Really earnest and clear in what he teaches with reasonable expectations for you to absorb knowledge. Clear and concise, I like going to his class.
Nice guy, but make sure you are upfront with him. He is understanding and will give you help if you ask for it.
Put in the work,  he will notice,  your grade will reflect. Procrastinate  and you will hate  this class.
Super hard class but worth it! He is the best man for the job!
A tough cookie but extremely knowledgeable, helpful and an excellent teacher overall.
Really know's his trees but requires work. class isn't a big deal but labs are. stay on top of studying ealry
No Comments
Awesome teacher. Seems to really know the material presented in class.

She was not a very good professor. She was late to discussion every time and never handed back our papers in a timely fashion. She was a lenient grader but if you're looking for someone you can learn from, she's not the person.

Good class. The readings were really interesting and many class periods were devoted to discussion. No textbook, but lots of individual articles. The research project was fun. Michelle was very reasonable about assignments and really easy to get along with. I think she really cares about teaching and it showed.
Michelle brought in interesting readings and topics, and made the class more than just following a textbook.  She was very reasonable about workload and helping students.
Michelle is really cool. She is very fair and the class is pretty interesting. She's also not a very hard grader.
Is always accessible for help with the course and you can tell she cares about her students. Material is a bit boring, but enjoyed the class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly, it was one of the most boring classes I took. We spend 3 hours each week in class learning nothing, yet attendance is mandatory. If you just watch the pre-lecture videos, you'll get an A on tests. The group project was very easy, just pay attention to the rubric. Overall, the content is similar, if not easier, than an AP Stats course.
Lost all my interest in the topic of the class after taking this class. Self study is what kept me going. Lectures are just a waste of time
Nice and caring person. Lectures are not very interesting and a lot of workload.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Honestly a good professor. She cares a lot about her students, and the class is pretty good. One of the few professors I've never heard a complaint about in college which should tell you a lot
She really cares about her students, is always easy to access, and answers questions thoroughly. She sets up review sessions and rewards good attendance, though it is not mandatory.
You can tell she really cares about her students and always tries to be accessible outside of class
Amazing professor who really cares about students and dedicates a lot of time to the class!
Improves over time and worth it

This class was boring. If you want an easy A where almost no effort is required, this is a good course for you. I tried to follow the material at first, but his lectures had little engagement. He is also hard to hear. All the slides are posted on canvas, and all homework is open note.

Dr. K was really enjoyable to have as a professor. His expectations were very clear and easy to follow, and was always super easy to talk to and ask questions through email or in person. The projects, homework, and exams were pretty much exactly what he told us they were going to be from lecture and graded very generously. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although the class is quite rigorous and requires much time to do well on the tests, I enjoyed the class a lot. On lab days, the TA and Dr. K come around and answer any questions you have that can help you on the exam. Hard class, but totally worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His exams literally make no sense. He can never elaborate on the slides, if you ask questions, he can't seem to answer any. I need this course for my major but it was such a waste to take it.

He marked multiple people absent while they were in class sitting in front of him, and this was daily. Also, he's weird to talk to, he'd avoid eye contact and mumble. Never really knew how to answer questions about the stuff we'd talk about. Hard to contact via email as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. K is an ineffective professor. I was disappointed to take his course because he's incapable of teaching. He mumbles, reads off of slides that make no sense, goes on tangents for way too long, and cannot answer basic questions about the material he's going over. Overall his exams are a nightmare because you barely understand the classwork.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sandy is the best professor at this school. She is super funny and makes class very engaging.
I want to add more tags. She is inspirational and respected. Amazing person overall.
Best teacher!

Sandie is a wonderful woman and a great professor. She teaches extremely relevant information for social workers (GET LICENSED!) and does so in an engaging way. She is extremely accessible for her students and wants to help. The material can be difficult if you're not familiar with law but be communicative with Sandie and ask questions.

Sandie knows the content well and makes it very clear. She' s got an edgy sense of humor and takes risks. I will probably learn more from her class than any other. The exams are very detailed and not a walk in the park. You must study.

Sandra Kopels is the best teacher in the school of social work.  She holds an MSW and a law degree and her class is extremely entertaining and fun while at the same time educational.  She will make you laugh...ALOT!
shes the bomb dot com

Sandy is a great teacher. She is crystal clear and you learn stuff that is actually really helpful. One of the things that I didn't love about her was that she wasn't very good at being respectful of more conservative views, however most of the social work program is like that so it wasnt really surprising but it does make it hard to speak up in cl
She is, without a doubt, the strongest faculty member in the School of Social Work.  Her class was amazing.  Very, very highly recommended--do not pass up the chance to take her class.
LOVE Sandie.  Dynamic, easy to understand, informative... ignore her diagnosis, she's great!
Fabulous professor!  Really really smart and funny.  The best prof I have ever had at any level.  She make learning fun!

The best professor I have had, ever.  Cares about her students and your success is her success.  Very helpful and well known to be extremely interesting and funny.  You will learn and be glad you did!
This professor is amazing! Lectures are really well put together and exams are not too bad. Took this for advanced comp so lots of writing but on interesting topics. Would recommend

Mr. Kourtikakis is really nice and easygoing. He tries to make lectures enjoyable and humorous. For grading, he always has a rubric and follows it well. The expectations are pretty clear. He also gives great extra credit at the end of the semester which boosted my grade from an A- or A to A+. I also got an 100% on my 2nd exam and a 96% on my final.

Dr. K is great. He truly is passionate and teaches well for students who are still getting a handle on college. The class has easy weekly readings online. There is a textbook, but I got by just fine without it. 4 essays, all 700 words. 3 exams, the first one is tough, but everyone struggles. Don't get stressed, class gets easier as it goes on.
Awesome professor to have as a freshman majoring in political science! he made everything so smooth for me and so did the TA Alondra.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kourtikakis is one of the best at UIUC. He cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. The class was extremely well structured and it was super easy to understand what is expected of you. If you just follow the syllabus, this class is a piece of cake.

Passionate about teaching and not just doing research. The first unit is a little tricky, but it gets easier as the semester progresses. Total of three exams and three short papers, most of which are easy as long as you dedicate a little time to study the material. There is a textbook but cheaper digital versions are readily available (wink wink).

This is advanced comp. class but very easy, so don't let that discourage you from taking it. Not a tough grader on the papers and test are super easy. I have taken other classes with him and all are very manageable. Also provides lecture videos if you don't want to go to class. There is extra credit if you need it adds 1-2% to final grade in class.
First unit is hard but the next ones get easier. lots of easy points in discussion questions and lecture quizzes. 3 tests and 3 essays - important to do well on these if you want an A

Easy class. All lectures are recorded. None of the assigned readings are needed because he goes over them in his lectures. In fact, exam questions testing on reading content are based on his summaries in the lectures, not the readings themselves. Essays are also very straightforward. Will be taking him again for an easy A+.

I love professor K. He is incredibly smart and explains the material very clearly. Lectures are all recorded online for PS348 and attendance isn't mandatory. I do think the exams are slightly hard but if you pay attention and watch the lectures you'll be fine. Professor Kourtikakis is by far the best and most caring professor ive had!

Really nice lecturer, clearly cares about giving good lectures and helping students learn. All lectures are recorded online and posted after. Straightforward exams and grading. Good professor, good class.

Really great professor. Attendance not at all mandatory, said the textbook was needed but I got through the course fine without it. Really engaging in lecture, exams were pretty straight forward, difficulty would've been lower if the final wasn't cumulative and worth roughly 30% of grade. All lectures are recorded, would definitely take him again.
Very insightful professor that brings positive energy with each lecture. Class is structured nicely and you end up learning a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: GOAT
The best professor in the PS department. His lectures are so nice and he genuinely makes the topics interesting for you. The exams are fairly easy as well!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Kourtikakis is one of the best professors I have had here. Lectures are engaging and his knowledge and feedback is great. Weekly quizzes that are easy and essays that are also not bad. Midterm and Final can be somewhat tricky but not terrible if you study. Overall amazing class and would recommend to anyone looking to learn about W. Europe.
This professor is my favorite on campus. He cares about his students and tries his best so they may all succeed. His lectures are not boring and are actually fun to be in. Love taking his classes.

He is such an engaging and kind professor. I genuinely enjoyed all of his lectures and learned a lot for it being a 100-level class. The material is not too hard as long as you pay attention to his lectures (either in-person or the posted recorded ones) and the tests are very fair as well. I highly suggest this class.

Dr. Kourtikakis, undoubtedly, is one of the best undergraduate professors for Political Science here at the University of Illinois. His lectures are incredibly thought-out and put together, and have enough pacing where you can go through a lot of material, but still unpack information that was just given. Outside of class, Dr. K is always helpful.

Amazing professor. Lectures are very straightforward and everything that is on the exam is discussed in class or in the weekly assigned readings. You can tell he loves the topic he teaches and always takes time in class to throughly answer any questions we have. Take notes in lectures and on readings and you'll do fine.
awesome professor
Professor Kourtikakis is one of my favorite professors at the University of Illinois. He obviously enjoys what he is teaching about and it shows.

This class can be a challenge, but Professor Kourtikakis is awesome, and so were this year's TAs; they were consistently engaging and accessible. Just go to the lectures, keep up with the readings, and make lots of time for the compositions.

Professor ks lectures were always super interesting because he attaches great examples to political science concepts. He really wants to see his students succeed and had great teaching assistants to help with any concerns. The only thing about this class was that there was a lot of papers to write but then again it is a advanced composition class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Amazing lectures--So many papers
