reviews.comment: Dr. Kourtikakis was caring, fun, and knowledgeable, and the course was not difficult. If you are looking to fill a requirement, it's definitely a good pick. However, I didn't feel like we really looked deep into the material -- most of what was learned was pretty base-level -- so, if you're really interested in the field you might want to rethink.

Prof. Kourtikakis is one of my favorite ever professors. He is an incredible lecturer, and he is also very kind. He is quite knowledgable about his field and cares that students are able to understand the material in his classes. I would recommend him to anyone for any class he teaches.
He is so nice and makes some funny jokes. The work load is easy and the material is interesting

Hes honestly such a great teacher to have. I dont recommend buying the textbook since he already summarizes it in his lectures effectively. Just make sure to take notes, and youre pretty much guaranteed an A.

Okay so Mr. K is awesome. He will assign readings but he literally goes through everything in his lectures so you can either do the readings and just zone out in class but still go to class because he does clicker stuff, or not do the readings. I did the first option and got an A. Theres very little work in the class and he's charming and adorable.

I took PS 385 solely because he was teaching it. You can really tell he cares about his students. He's pretty funny and grades generously. I thought the material was pretty interesting. 4 papers, short MC quiz every other week, final exam, and policy paper-- not too bad. You could probably go w/o the textbook. Highly recommend taking a class w/ him

I took this a governing globalisation with him and got an A+ in both classes. His tests are super easy, the papers are grade generously, and he gives plenty of Extra credit. His classes are pretty interesting and he's a good lecturer and a really nice guy. Overall good teacher who runs low maintainence easy A classes.

Nice guy and a great lecturer. Topics can sometimes be dry but he'll break up the boring parts with antidotes/stories. Class requires 3 short papers, 2 exams, and a map quiz, none of which are especially challenging.

Dr. K has made my freshman year & renewed my interest & passion for polisci. He is an incredible teacher, has interesting lectures, funny, & although the papers are challenging, he is incredibly accessible, helpful, & wants you to succeed. Lecture attendance is key for doing well on exams. I hope I can take more of his classes in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures are interesting and grading is simple (term paper, an alternating quiz/essay every week, and final exam). None of assignments, except maybe the term paper, are particularly challenging, as he's a very lenient grader. He's generally nice, but I found him pretty condescending whenever students asked questions.
Professor K is fine but the class itself is super boring. Lectures are slow and painful. You can tell he cares about his students though and the class should be an easy A with a decent effort.

Dr. K is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. His lectures are straight forward and easy to follow. You do not need the textbook. All of the information for the exams is put on a straight forward study guide. All of the information comes directly from his power points. There are a couple opportunities of extra credit.

Dr. K is the sweetest and most caring professor at the University. I took this class for fun and decided to pick up poly sci as a double major because he talked me into it. The class is extremely easy if you put in a decent amount of work, but actually go out of your way to meet/talk to him because he's honestly the best.

Lectures could be a bit boring sometimes but as long as you copy down the powerpoints then you should be good. Dr.K is good at making boring material interesting, and he was very helpful outside of class. If you show up to class, then this class should be an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Genuinely a really nice guy and teacher. What I thought was going to be a boring class was interesting and he is so upbeat you can't help but like him. His grading is very straight forward and as long as you show up and memorize the slides you'll get an  A. I would definitely take another course with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The professor is really good at explaining the textbook reading-- you really don't have to get the textbook as long as you go to class and take notes. The powerpoints aren't posted, though, so be sure to go to class. Essays are a breeze but the exams are a little tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probably one of the nicest professor I've ever had, and with what can sometimes be somewhat dry material, he does an incredible job of relating it to current events. The guy spent an entire class period answering any questions we had after the election. Tests are multiple choice and 5 short answer (always one definition). Take the class.

Pretty solid Professor. His tests and essays come straight off the powerpoints, so don't bother with the textbook. Gives lots of extra credit and iclicker points. Lectures are generally fairly interesting. 3 two page papers and 3 multiple choice and short answer exams (1 is the final) plus a short weekly reading. Really nice guy, too.

Took Professor Kourtikakis this past semester & enjoyed the class. You will have: 5 reflection papers throughout the class as well as weekly reading quizzes, 1 final paper & 2 Exams. The Exams are dense, so make up your points with the papers & the extra credit which he offers. Doesn't put the notes online so going to class is a must.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor, class is definitely passable as long as you put in the effort. You don't need to read the textbook, but just show up to class and pay attention and take notes. Professor is really helpful and knows what he's doing. Tests are easy if you study and pay attention in class. Papers are long, but not too hard.
Tells you everything you need to know in lecture. Very straight forward with grading.

He's pretty great. The lectures aren't usually boring, and he knows when they are so he tries to make jokes. Two papers - one 5 page paper that is excruciatingly painful to write, and then a 3600-word research paper. Reasonably easy class, and great for the ACP requirement. You have to attend though- valuable iclicker points!

What an amazing professor! As long as you go to class and keep in contact (office hours, emails, etc) you'll do well. While the material can occasionally be difficult, he is very clear about what he wants from you and very fair.  As long as you show him that you're engaged and trying hard he will do everything he can to help you out!
Favorite poli sci teacher! If you go to class you will get an A! Don't need the textbook because exams are straight off his slides. Also counts as ACP, only two easy essays.
Class was incredibly easy, mainly because the exams were a joke. Attend class and pay enough attention to copy down the notes and it's easy.

He's the best teacher in the political science department hands down. Really kind and helpful when you go to his office hours, his lectures are so clear that if you go to class and review your notes, you're set for the exams. The paper topic was also really interesting! And he's funny too. I can't say enough good things. He's the best of the best.

I cannot stress how great of a prof. Kourtikakis is. Go to class and take notes and you are guaranteed an A. His lectures are so clear it's difficult to get confused or do poorly. Tests are straight from the lecture and the essay questions are always based on your opinion. Best professor I had throughout college.

Midterm, final, 8-10 page paper, map quiz, and a works cited 10% of grade. GO TO CLASS FOR A GUARANTEED A.I can't stress that enough. He gives you a study guide for the exams and all the information comes off his powerpoints. Great teacher, good for PS majors. Will look at your stuff too.

The class was extremely easy, though you do learn a great amount of information; which means he was great at explaining ideas and concepts. Everything on his exams are based on his presentations, so if you go to every lecture and take good notes; there is no need to by the textbook.

This is the second time I've had Kourtikakis and he doesn't disappoint (taking him again next fall, too) Lectures are straightforward and interesting. Start your research paper early and you'll be guaranteed at least a B. Really good class for PS majors needing their adv comp class. Overall, I learned a lot and definitely recommend.

I rate my interest as low just because of my personal preference for PoliSci. But indeed this professor was extremely wonderful so I was motivated and worked hard and got an A+. Do all the extra credits! He's hot, too.

Great professor! His lectures are powerpoint based and everything on the tests is based off the powerpoints. Easy class if you take good notes. He always makes sure to answer any questions you may have in class. I'm taking him again this spring. Definitely recommend him.

Although his lectures are boring, his explanations of class material is clear. You don't have to read the book if you take good notes. However, I still suggest skimming/reading the important parts especially the articles (Provides an extra layer of review). Everything was made up of exams which were just fine if you study.

Awesome professor. His lectures are always structured and presented clearly. Has a cool accent, which I dig. His tests aren't too difficult and are actually rather easy if you take good notes. Homework is virtually nonexistent, but tests pretty much determine your grade. I highly recommend this professor.
He is very helpful and knowledgable. I can actually say that I learned something in this class; although, it was somewhat boring.

I had him for another class, politics of Western Europe.  The guy is a class act.  He is super nice, clear, organized, and really kind and helpful in office hours.  I disagree with the other rater.  His classes aren't difficult.  If you go to class and take good notes, you will succeed.  He has high expectations, but helps you reach them.

Excellent prof, passionate, knowledgeable with vast experience in subject matter, extremely helpful outside of class, fascinating lecturer. Wise, intelligent but also highly, highly respectful of students. Tough grader, has high expectations, study hard for exams, DO THE EXTRA CREDIT, otherwise the best professor and best PS class I've ever had.
He is a great professor, and teaches NPRE 247 very well. Try not to ask stupid questions.

Out of all the classes I have taken, this professor was the worst. Overall ok dude, but not a good teacher. Hand writing is horrible and hard to read. Unwilling to answer questions if he doens't like your question. Overall extremely hostile enviroment that is not conducive to learning.

Extremely fair grader. You will definitely have to read the book and go to lecture to get an A in this class. Try and do the homework early so you can come to class with questions, because he will answer questions in class. Overall a very interesting and engaging class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor. He gives clear requirements for every assignment, going so far as to tell you everything you could possibly lose points for on the computer projects so you can make sure you get a good grade. Tests are long for the time given, but if you go to class,do your homework, and make your cheat sheet you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Unclear criteria for important assignments. Condescending towards students. Will not answer your question if he decides you should already know the answer. Pay attention in lecture all you want, when you get to the homework you will not know how to do it unless you fully read the preceding chapter.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Is this really an introductory class? I really doubt it. Computer project are graded harshly. Exams are so hard that your cheat sheet becomes useless.

Agree that he cares his Pokemon rather than his students. It is exactly 24 hours before the final, and he has 3 hw solutions that are still not posted. No sharing materials for study and review, since "the textbook is your study guide" he said in class. Cannot understand his explanation in most of the conceptions.
Never meet such bad professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Kozlowski is one of the greatest profs I have ever had. Prepare to work hard, especially with the computer projects. He teaches in a very structured way. Follow the book, show up, and PAY ATTENTION and the homework and exams will be no problem. Just prepare to work!

His class is hard and his computer projects are graduate student level. Exams are basically homework questions. Not a bad professor but I cannot learn much in his class. Grading in computer project is harsh. Average professor, don't expect too much from him and be ready to work hard.

Professor Kozlowski is absolutely incredible.  I was worried that he would be hard to understand, but he has honestly been my favorite professor thus far at UIUC. NPRE 247 is rather difficult, CS 101 will NOT, and I repeat, NOT help you when it comes to the computer projects.  Other than that, he grades fairly and is just an awesome guy in general.
Very nice professor. The exam might be hard but if you are familiar with particular proofs, you will get good score.
This class was very difficult but the professor was fantastic, office hours were extremely useful.

He is a good professor and knows and likes the subject very much, which will be evident from his enthusiasm about the subject in class. I do however think that his lectures are rather dry. I personally believe that I learned more outside of class from his slides and online resources than from lecture. He is quick when it comes to emails and is kind

Excellent - very accessible (use the help sessions and email), listens to students when something isn't clear. He wants you to succeed - if you're motivated, you'll do well. The tests are half like the hw and half conceptual questions. Most problems involving proofs are variants of proofs done in lecture. Some memorization of theorems is necessary.

Sasha is a gem. He is a real mathematician  he's curious and really interested in the material he teaches. He doesn't want to give anyone a bad grade and is very generous while also effective. I adore him and definitely recommend taking a class with him if you get the chance!

Professor Kostochka is really awesome. He is always accessible during office hours and homework sessions. You can ask about the homework and notes if things get unclear. Exams are not too difficult as long as you study hard. Highly recommend this professor.
Amazing professor! Learns the names of all his students, accessible for office hours and questions, very kind and funny. The class is difficult but it's interesting and the lectures are very good.

He teaches clearly. He is nice and helpful. In the current semester, he held weekly help sessions which are very useful. He tries to remember the students' names, which makes me feel good. Graph theory is a hard course, but he is quite successful in explaining it well.

He seems to know what he's doing. However, his classes tend to get boring, people tend to skip lectures more and more frequently. He doesn't provide any additional study materials besides the homework, and a practice exam for only the first exam. His grading is not lenient at all. The quizzes are no easier than the exams. No curves thus far.
He is very good. He explains very clearly. His dialog with students is also very nice.
Professor Kostochka is very experienced in graph theory. He's pretty nice and caring to students. Sometimes his lecture is not that organized and logical though.

Really love him! Best Professor in Math Department. Homeworks are not easy, but you can always choose 4 of 5 questions to answer. Exams are easy and you can drop the lowest one. Also, Professor is sooooooo nice and enthusiastic. If you can take his class, then take it!
Because of his heavy Russian accent, lectures are not always clear. Difficult homework problems.

He is the best professor I have had at this university.  He encourages students who do not understand the material to go to weekly study sessions and office hours.  He also encourages students to ask questions.

He is very nice to his students and helpful in office hours. He also holds review sessions every week the day before the weekly homework is due, which is also helpful. The class itself is fairly difficult if you aren't great at proving things, but his grading scale is extremely generous. He also gave us 5 exams and took the top 3. Good professor.

Graph theory with Kostochka was a demanding class.  He expects that you memorize all of the propositions, theorems, definitions, etc, so don't fall behind.  I felt that I learned the most from homework sessions he ran, rather than lectures. In class I wasn't sure which details were most important. Generous grading scale. Great Russian accent!

Alexandr (I had him for UG LP), is a nice guy, but tries way 2 hard and needs to follow a clearer approach in lectures. Students in this class already understand LP, because it is mostly grads in CompuSci; beware if ur taking it as UG Math. My advice would be to get to know him and do ur best. He's easy on the grading, so you will be ok if you try.

EDIT: im in med school now. Dr. K definitely overhyped how useful orgo would be in med school. But I can't say it didn't help. It did kinda help for MCAT. Last few units were really relevant. I will say this class did strengthen me academically and it's also very interesting. I don't regret taking it. Dr K does have bit of a strange vibe to him.
I still think about Koerner from time to time years later because he traumatized me
He really was terrible during covid times and didn't have any sympathy for students.
W Goat, will be missed

This man is very overhyped. He was extremely toxic and very demoralizing during his office hours. I feel like I would've learned more if Axelson taught this class as the material wasn't necessarily hard, but this class lacked structure and the exams were a jumbled up mess compared to Chem 232.

Tbh I don't get the hype. Coming from an orgo1 lover, the material is VERY dense and his flipped class model does a poor job at actually teaching it and breaking it all down. I found his videos to be disorganized. 95% of succeeding is how good your cheat sheet is. Also, I found Dr. K to be discouraging and toxic. I stopped going to in person class.

Dr. K is by far one of the best professors I have ever had at UIUC. For anyone going through Chem/ Stem routes, you should definitely take his course. He makes the lectures enjoyable with stories and only tests what he teaches. I highly recommend Dr. K!

Good showman, but horrible course instructor. A monkey can get 120/200 in his exams (and so many of them are just naming stuff). You are even asked who is a rap singer and who's a chemist in an exam! An average of a 20-minute online lecture is required each day. Yeah, take it if you want a high score but not learn anything about real chemistry.

Dr. Koerner is the best professor I have had so far. He and his TAs were very lenient in their grading. His lectures were also interesting, considering he would tell you how to kill your roommate with an aphrodisiac. The class still is hard, and you need to put in a good amount of work, but most people end up with an A.

I learned a lot from this class. There was a TON of material, but he made up for it with cheat sheets and lenient grading (the averages on most tests were in the 80s). Just make sure to stay on top of the material. Sometimes he did get carried away with telling stories but I loved how he constantly related organic chemistry to real life.

Professor Koerner is like an immigrant parent. Very caring, and although I don't agree with all his tough love anecdotes, I appreciate what he gets right. It's a very difficult class, but Dr. Koerner implements policies to make it easier on students. Do as many practice tests as possible, and the in-person section is easier to keep up with.

Dr. K is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about teaching this class. He has lots of interesting applications and stories related to the content which makes the class very engaging. Tests are difficult, but TAs graded generously. It's possible to get an A if you can put in a lot of time. Dude is the GOAT.

Dr. K is one of the best teachers I've had and also one of the funniest. His lectures are amazing and extremely in-depth, but will also relate complex organic chemistry topics to tacos, breakups, Spiderman, and everything in between to help you learn things. Dr. K is one of the nicest, most passionate, and most knowledgeable teachers I've ever had!

One of the best profs I've ever had. The material is very challenging but he gives extra credit and grades very easily. If you're willing to learn, you should be fine. If not, there's no way to coast through. Also a super cool guy  with some great stories. Ignore the haters, Dr K is an absolute mad lad.
He needs to learn to listen more to his students needs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. K is a great guy with lots of interesting stories. He tries to prepare you for things like the MCAT and uses real life examples. There are 4 exams + a final (one is dropped and replaced with the highest). There's 40+ points of extra credit which is super helpful. You get a single page cheat sheet for each exam. I had it online so less stressful

I learned a lot in this class and enjoyed it a lot. His lectures can get lengthy at times due to his stories. Lots of content because he focuses on preparing students for MCAT/DAT. The overall grade is all exams w/ few extra credit points. The exams were fair and you could use a cheat sheet.

There is a difference from preparing you for med school and just being cruel. Take this course elsewhere.

Reminds me of highschool teachers being extra cruel so they can "prepare you for college". And going to college and realizing they really did not need to do that and could have just been fair instead of needlessly hard.

I took this class a few years ago and would have said awful things about Professor Koerner and the class immediately after taking the final. However looking back, although extremely difficult, the class is helpful in terms of preparing you for medical school and making future chemistry courses more manageable. Requires much work but is rewarding.

Dr. K is truly an amazing professor. It's clear that he cares about his students and he loves what he's teaching. It's a Chem 300 level class, so yes its hard. Despite that, I've never loved lectures more than his.

Dr. K is truly one of the best professors I've ever had. You can tell he genuinely likes what he is teaching, which makes his lectures enjoyable. It's one of the few lectures I don't dread. You won't pass this class unless you study really hard, watch his lectures closely, and make good notes. Thankfully, he gives a lot of extra credit.

Dr. K is the best professor I have ever had. Orgo II is tough- no question about it, but Dr. K does an amazing job of supporting every student throughout the course. I took the course in the spring and had to drop due to my own shortcomings and took it over again this summer. I have never met a more empathetic, knowledgable, and kind instructor.

One of the most disheartening classes I've taken! His video lectures were unnecessarily long and agonizing to get through. He made the content more confusing than it had to be. Get a good orgo book or find other resources to learn the content cuz his notes are jumbled! He is not available outside of class and is not a good teacher. Be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. K seems like a really smart individual. However, I feel like he has it in his head that he's doing everything in his power to make student's lives easier. Although, this is just not the case. I personally felt that I would have succeeded more in this course if the format was not as it was. Beware of the four-question exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wanted to take since freshman year. Online setup was info. without interaction. Heard great things abt past preceptors; not comparable this semester & not very engaged nor passionate students. Class Facebook group was toxic Q&A board. Class was more fight for points than understanding. Let down. Wish I could take it over. Growth mindset required :)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Exam heavy, and lots of random luck on which 4 MC questions you are tested on. Compass crashed with exam 4 a week before finals and he moved Exam 4 into finals week, that sucked. Many people overreacting about his unprofessional comments. Honestly he just roasted a few keyboard warrior students. It was actually funny.

This class has an unnecessary structure - having 20-30 lectures per 5 question exams for the amount of credit hours this class was was not worth it. If you have a job (or life outside of school) a good grade is really hard to obtain without completely overworking yourself (aka me). He also was rather unpleasant when it came to upset students.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: "TONE" Koerner screamed, as he melted down in front of 300 students... he's a great professor if you wanna get a degree from clown college.

He thinks 4 multiple choices can determine your understanding of the course, is unsympathetic and downright rude&unprofessional to students who are just voicing their opinions after suffering from his terribly formatted exams. I have no words for this professor and how the chemistry department allows hardworking students to be screwed up like this.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this class was a nightmare. the last exam was too hard and tricky,no amount of studying could've prepared me for the questions. It was super unfair imo. he also started to get aggressive towards students in his comments in the class facebook group when they were just trying to understand the posted answers/voice their opinions. Shame on you Dr K
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This guy is awful. Not to mention the exams are ridiculous in that they only consist of five questions, but hes disorganized and had to reschedule the fourth exam. Hes disrespectful and acts like a child when people oppose him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. K might be a good person, but he is a horrible professor. You have randomly generated exams where 4 multiple questions decide what letter you grade you get. Miss one and you're not getting an A on that exam. Who thought that was a good idea? Hate to say it but no respect to Dr. Koerner.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams were 5 questions which is not only anxiety filling but getting one question wrong places you at a B. To add, the questions are randomly generated so no student get the same 5 questions. But some questions are easier/harder than others. I had friends that would get high B's without studying all by chance. If you have luck, you can get A.

I have never seen a more manipulative and unempathetic professor in my entire academic career. He pushed our last exam into the finals schedule, meaning we have to take our last exam and final on the same day. He broke the syllabus contract and bragged about how no other professor would be able to break the rules in the way he did. Will b reported.

As if this semester couldn't get worse, our 4th exam malfunctioned on Compass. Not Dr. K's fault, but instead of voiding it he moved the exam to our final exam day and we need to take this exam and the cumulative final within 3 hours on the same day - on less than a week's notice. So much for "not needing to study for the final" if you do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. K is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. His Orgo II lectures are so clear and detailed; he gives you every single tool you need to succeed in his course. You have to watch the lectures closely and make sure you understand the content, once you do, it makes the exams a breeze!

Literally one of the most frustrating classes I've ever taken. Dr. K seems like a really nice person outside of class and his lectures are interesting, but his exams are impossible. I don't understand how hours of content can be tested on an exam that only has 4 questions. I wish I had taken this class another semester :(

Not sure how he was in previous semesters, but he really just used Spring 2021 class as a bunch of guinea pigs. Ever hear about standard deviation Dr.K? 4 randomly generated questions...? I don't know how you justified that to yourself.

I picked the tag hilarious because his class structure makes me laugh. :) I worked hard in this class only to have exam questions that are generated by luck to screw me. 5 questions is not enough to determine if a student knows the material or not. Honestly I thought he was a nice teacher and would listen to the concerns of the class, but nah. <3
AWFUL CLASS STRUCTURE
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I find it really sad to see a professor change their entire class structure on a whim during a pandemic, and then completely disregard all feedback from all students who criticize it. As a professor, if everyone is telling you there is a problem with new the changes you have made, at what point do you stop lying to yourself that everything is okay?
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Koerner is an AMAZING professor and amazing lecturer, his lectures are so interesting and you can tell he really is passionate about what he teaches. He gives so many resources to pass the class, BUT with the exams being the only grade, its incredibly difficult to improve your grade if youre not on top of things from the start.

After transitioning to the Spring 2021 online semester, Dr.K has completely changed the structure of the course and has treated his students as guinea pigs. 4 question exams randomly generated are clearly unfair indicators of a students knowledge of the subject. He states "he can't make it any easier"although "60% of students got at 2/4 or lower...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I did all the practice exams, watched the sample exam videos, created posters, and watched 2-3 lecture videos everyday. �� Not good enough. Dr. K is great but structured the class poorly the 4 questions of multiple choice depends on luck. I studied like crazy but I got insane multiple choice questions. Dr. K how could u do this? �� I did everything
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Koerner is a good lecturer, yet the class structure is just awful. Lecture videos are long yet are seemingly easy to follow, but the exams are almost impossible. It doesnt help that each of the 4 MC are 40% of the final grade and you cant go back to check your previous answer. With this class being online, I wish there was a little sympathy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. K. seems to expect that each of his students devotes all 168 hours that are in a week to his class. He consistently posts 5-6 hours of lectures a week for a 3 credit hour class. The exams are difficult and only 4 MC questions and 1 free resp. While a few students do have 100% in the class, the majority of our class currently has a C or lower.

Dr. K acts like your friend (more like a salesperson), but the online class is flawed in structure & he continues to push that this is the "easiest class ever". There are only 500 points in the class, & each exam question is worth 10 points. You can ONLY miss 3 exam questions THE ENTIRE semester to get an A. He doesn't show much compassion, either.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Koerner is great lecturer - he makes the lectures engaging and enjoyable. However, he has structured his class and exams in such a poor way. The fact that you are unable to go back to previous questions (a core test taking strategy) and the exams are five questions, there is essentially no room for error.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. K is extremely intelligent and very thoroughly explains material. However, he creates outrageously hard exams that are tough to finish in the time frame. He will not stand for excuses or any struggles. He will blame your failure on lack of studying even if that is not the case.

A significant part of the grade is centered around exams that have only 4 multiple choice and 1 free response. The lectures are great and his teaching is good, but the skills learned are not reflected in exams well. He does not address the clear issue with have one MC determine 10% of the exam score. The class structure is not great so beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. K thinks he gives u everything to succeed in his class. A privileged view to have. Everyone is dealing w/ something different. & he's not available. Dr. K has no exceptions on any policies, ie. rec letters for only A's. Science teachers at UIUC, consider a student's growth or effort, not their grade. "More than machinery we need humanity."
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor at the university. Hard grader but the only person I actually enjoyed going to their classes
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Greatest professor at UIUC. Gives you all the resources necessary to succeed in the course. His lectures are amazing too! He's really good at mixing stories with the material to keep students engaged as well as making the topics practical to real life. It's still a tough class so you have to spend lots of time studying, but 20/10 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. K is the best professor I've ever had. He truly cares about his students and his lectures are so entertaining you might actually come out of the class loving organic chemistry. His tests are very difficult so prepare to spend countless hours studying, but I'd do it all over again if it meant taking another class with Dr. K. 11/10 experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Never felt like I deserved my grade more than this class. I knew literally nothing about orgo before taking it with Dr. K. Regardless of what grade you end up with, you'll walk away from this class having learned a lot. 13/10 would take again.

It's quite rare to find a teacher who can make such a difficult and boring topic both easy to understand and fun to learn. Lectures were engaging and filled with humor and life lessons. However, I seriously disliked Dr. K's insistence that students memorize even the most obscure reagents/molecules that are guaranteed to NEVER show up on the MCAT.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: My favorite but also most time consuming / challenging class of all time. However, I averaged 100% on my top 3 (of 4) exams -- (lowest gets dropped) -- so put in the time and the effort pays off. Tip: he likes to rotate molecules / flip / make diastereomers for the B level questions. Pay close attention.

Most useful and life-changing class. His passion for chemistry is contagious. His teaching style is very effective and I've learned how to teach pretty much all from him. If you want to do well on the MCAT, please, be smart, suck it up (because the class is hard) and take this class. Orgo 1 with Dr. Kell will not prepare you.

Classes are filled with life lessons, real-life applications of chemical ideas, and actual moments for personal growth.  I HIGHLY recommend attending office hours - he answered all my questions, gave exam-like questions for practice, and gave great advice for my personal statement on the AMCAS (!!).  The ideal teacher, 12/10; made me love orgo

Even though the exams are challenging and that the course has a flat grading scale, we were able to drop our worst score. Also, the average for quizzes is 97-100% , and there are plenty of opportunities for easy extra credit. Lastly, this was the most challenging class I have taken, yet Dr. Koerner makes it very relevant, enjoyable and engaging.

Best professor I've every had teaching the hardest class I've ever taken. Be prepared to grind and you'll do well. So many resources available, but you have to put in the hours if you want to do well.

Dr. K is a great professor. He is able to relate his own experiences to organic chemistry. Attendance is not mandatory but you MUST go to class or you WILL fail! The class is hard, but there are tons of ways to get help. Exams are difficult, but fair with no surprises. It's hard to get less than a B if you study/review the way that he recommends.

Dr. Koerner is an excellent professor with plenty of real-world experience to draw from, and this shows in his class. He's easy to like and will help you any way he can. That being said you will have to work your a** off to do well in his course, but you will be much smarter for it. While attendance isn't mandatory, you shouldn't skip this class.

Dr. K is very cool and likes telling stories. He will shove A LOT of information at you but it is all pretty clear. It is remembering it all for the test that is the tough part. There are 14 office hours available throughout the week so someone is there to help. Hard class but recommend taking.

Prof. K is the best ever. He is very understanding and well kindly explain anything that is confusing. My TA was great as well, so this class is highly recommended. The test are straightforward based on the study guides. You will for sure do well in this class if you try.
had to write another glowing review for the goat Dr K. He is so incredibly kind, flexible with assignments, and easy to talk to. I've taken PS100 and 328 with him and couldn't recommend him enough

Clear presentations and good at explaining the material and answering student questions during class. Small assignments buffer your grade— weekly online quizzes and three short writing assignments and three exams. If you pay attention in class and/or read the news, you will do fine.

Awesome professor & class. The writing assignments are super interesting too. He basically gives you the exam questions on the study guide so there's never any curve balls. Cannot wait to take a class with him again

Professor K was a really insightful professor. He was a great resource with research and papers outside of class and is very willing to take time out of his day to help his students. Class topics were also very interesting and having a professor who has the passion for what they are teaching makes for a great class setting.

Prof K is great. He is very understanding about the lives of students and helped me out when I was in a rough patch. His lectures are great and he always posts them online too. I'm taking him again next semester because his class was manageable and I learned a lot!! He definitely has a passion for what he teaches and it shows :)

Incredibly interesting class, and Professor K is extremely smart and well-spoken. Writing assignments were short and easy, but the final project is most of your grade anyway. He allows you to explore a topic in-depth, and there are some interesting and thought-provoking prompts. Fun paper to write and most in the class did well on it

Professor K truly wants to see his students succeed and understand the material. He really explains the concepts of political science deeper because he is super knowledgeable. He gives clear grading criteria and has been/ was super flexible on deadlines because of covid. Highly recommend taking him for political behavior, excellent class.

Prof K is easily one of the kindest, most knowledgeable professors at UIUC. He is very passionate about his research which makes class discussions all the more interesting! He is unassuming and humble about what he knows- so students never feel silly for the questions they ask; as well as so accommodating and considerate! Highly recommend PS314!

The best PS professor I've had at UIUC. He's super accommodating and understanding of student needs - always gives extensions when you ask for them. There weren't too many assignments for this course, so participating in class discussions is important.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor K was the best professor I've had at U of I so far. He's intelligent, witty, and he knows how to make topics fun and interesting. I would recommend that you take as many courses with him as possible if you are a PS major. Even if they don't seem interesting to you by the title, trust me you'll enjoy his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is a great class to take for the social studies gen ed. He gives out reading quizzes online, but they are not too hard. 3 non-cumulative tests (with study guides), + 3 short writing assignments are the only grades. Only meet Monday and Wednesday with Friday discussion sections (which are not too bad). Take for am easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is a good, knowledgeable, responsive, and passionate professor! Easy class if you show up for iclicker points and skim the book to do the weekly online quizzes.  He gives you study guides before the exams that have the test questions on them basically so super possible to get A's if you do them.  I thought it was an interesting class.

I really like Prof K. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches. But, I didn't like the way this course was set up. He very rarely lectured and spent most of class asking people their opinions on research; I can't say that I learned very much fro this. He's great when he lectures, but not so great when he just leads discussions.B
Very knowledgeable professor with a passion for what he teaches. Enjoyed the class tremendously despite initially not being interested in the course subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor K was the best teacher I had this year. He explained things really well and made political science interesting. A decent amount of reading is required (but you could really skim). Good class, good guy. He's good at being unbiased, even during election season.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is passionate about what he is teaching. This class is quite interesting. He explains things well. Every week we need to read a chapter to finish reading quizzes and a short article prepared for discussion. Tests are easy, as along as you do the study guide(questions are all dragged from study guide).
Excellent professor. He says what he expects of you, and follow that and you'll do well.

Really really enjoyed his class. It's clear he cares about students even if most students are just scrolling on Facebook during lecture. He uses iClicker points a lot for participation so be at class! His slides are very helpful and engaging and I learned a lot. Tests aren't hard if you study. He even gives an extremely helpful study guide.

I  tried to take this class before with different professors and it did not turn out well. I really enjoyed this professor and the class. Go to class and go to discussion and you will be fine. Prof seems kind of nervous but he is very nice. Exams are not bad at all.

Dr. K is a new professor. For a new professor, he was amazing in his first semester. Specifically, he improved a lot after the midterm evaluations. He is very clear and it is clear that he's passionate about what he's teaching. He asks if anyone has questions every few slides, and is always willing to help out a student.

She is a very harsh grader and chooses topics to talk about in class that she knows nothing about. It is impossible to get an A in this class and I would never take this class again because she has a superiority complex and should not be a teacher. She does weekly quizzes but never actually teaches the content throughout the week, the class fails.

Might be the worst class I have ever taken during my time at college. Most ridiculous grading contract I have seen. Almost impossible to get an A given that you start at a B. Only thing this class does is bring down your GPA.
Do not take this class. One bad assignment and your gpa is cooked. Also heavily group project based
I would rather take an 8am class than have this teacher. DONT TAKE HER FOR ANY CLASS

Take caution when registering. You start the class with a B and you have to go way above and beyond to get anything higher than that. One mishap or late assignment revision on her "grading contract" penalizes your grade by a whole letter. Grading is too subjective and way too critical, would not recommend.

This professor's teaching style made the course unnecessarily stressful. Instead of helping students improve, the feedback often felt harsh and discouraging. I did not feel supported in developing my writing skills throughout this class.

Where do I even begin with this class? It claims to use a "mostly labor based" grading contract to reduce anxiety but in practice grades feel subjective as can be her standards shift pushing students to argue for grades. Lectures are filled with low value activities that rarely help the actual portfolio and mostly restate what she wants to see 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her rigged grading system gives her way too much power over your GPA. Because she's such a strict grader, missing a single rubric point on one assignment can tank your final grade by an entire letter. It got to the point where I was in genuine fear of submitting assignments, knowing she could instantly kill my grade for the semester.

Easily the worst teacher I had throughout my whole life. Her grading criteria does not make sense and will mark you down a whole letter grade if you forget to do something that isn't in the directions. Would rather write a 10000 word essay every day for a semester than take a class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the worst teacher I have ever had. If you mess up an assignment in the slightest way, you move down a whole letter grade. Your grade by default is a B and you can only increase your grade by doing extra things outside of class that are not reflective of your work. She is very knit picky and harsh when it comes to her grading.

Course has a unique structure that adds several unnecessary components. Instructions for assignments are unclear and graded very harshly. The course is designed so that you start with a B and if you mess up on an assignment, rather than it receiving a poor grade, it is just marked incomplete so if you mess up more than once your grade drops to a C.
Dont take her class please!
Terrible professor. Do not take her class. She has a bunch of extra criteria in her grading that are not very specified in assignment rubrics. Very difficult to please.

She has a different grading system that has so many unnecessary extra work to get an A unlike the other Rhet professors. You have to do extra peer reviews and group presentations to get an A whereas in other Rhet classes, you just turn in your papers. Other Rhet classes also gave more freedom in the topics you can choose for your research paper.

easy gen ed, she requires a textbook for some weeks' readings but honestly you can get by without it. interesting lectures. low-stakes quizzes and the typical response papers. posts slides online. discussion sections were actually pretty interesting too. overall good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I thought the lectures were organized very well and I found them interesting. The class was easy and I didn't find it necessary to do any of the readings.

This course was very similar to another course that Dr. Kramer teaches, ANTH 104. I realized halfway that the course reviewed a ton of the same material in ANTH 104. However, the class was still enjoyable and my TA made discussion constructive and comfortable.

Could've been interesting, but lectures were incredibly dry and boring. Walls of black text on white background and far too many examples for easy concepts. Lectures weren't really linked to textbook or paper topics. Easy A class if you're good at papers. No homework, no mandatory attendance. Skipped more often than not and still got an A.

Loved this class, 10/10. The papers were so fun to write since you could choose pretty much anything as long as it was connected to the prompt. You don't have to do the readings to do well as long as you pay attention to the lectures. Was a very nice class to take to fulfill Gen Ed reqs, and Dr. Kramer responds to emails pretty fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The material of this class was so fascinating, and Professor Kramer taught it in a clear and understandable way. Grade was based on papers. The discussion section did feel a bit pointless, but it could definitely be better with a different TA.

I really enjoyed Professor Kramer's class! The lectures she provided for our class were interesting and she delivered the lessons in an understandable and relatable way. Definitely recommend for an easy AND interesting class.

I took Professor Kramer for ANTH271 after having her in ANTH101 the previous semester. Professor Kramer is a very engaged and interesting lecturer given that a student generally cares to pay their professors the respect they deserve for their time and dedication. She clearly cared very much for students' understanding of the material.

Kramer's lectures weren't very interesting. One could possibly get away without attending them. All the material she covers in class is available in the lecture notes she uploads before class starts. Make sure you do the textbook readings for the quizzes but there is no need to go over the textbook for the final.
Was not a very good teacher. She tended to force her political opinions on the students and was not very helpful. Would not recommend to anyone

I have taken so many advanced level courses and while I took this as a Gen Ed, I found it to be even harder than the three advanced courses I was taking. She is so pretentious and is very discouraging whenever you have questions. On top of that tests are worth 35% each and contain little of the information learned in class. Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She wasnt a very interesting lecturer and the topic COULDVE been interesting, but the way she had explained things just was dry.

A great teacher, who covered a lot of material without seeming rushed. The class was really interesting, and due to its small size, it was easy to participate in and feel like a part of the discussion. The papers were actually fun to write, which is something that almost never happens for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment:
He is very sweet and deeply knowledgeable in his subject. 
He loves what he teaches and keeps us up-to-date about the latest news and happenings in the world. 
He provides engaging case studies and ensures his teachings are both clear and concise.
I find his personal anecdotes really inspiring!

Prof. Kraatz is a great professor. His lectures were very interesting and I loved the cases he choose to review. He does make you buy a few HBR articles, but that is a small price to pay for the knowledge. He tends to be uptight, but that is really only a facade. I learned a lot in this class, and I would definitely recommend Prof. Kraatz.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Normal class.  He did pick up some nice cases and articles for us to read.
Great materials used in class. The class is sometime boring but his well constructed cases and theories are perfect to understand leadership.
He is a great professor. I love him!
No Comments

Has an issue with lectures where her 'Umm" and "Uhh" are said more than actual lecture materials. Perhaps it's a lack of confidence or knowledge of materials. In her exams, she seems very nitpicky on the tiniest of details that you left out, even if you covered everything else or described them near perfectly. Very inefficient teaching style.

Big nonbeliever in the "perfect student". You automatically start at 95% and are ripped apart for small mistakes that she doesn't outline in assignment objectives. Readings are interesting, but are incredibly long with terrible academic language. Also loves to talk at you for the entire lecture and is usually the only one "right" in discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Romberg's lecturesshe told them in a story-telling way that was really interesting to me. Readings were all posted online, three open-note in-class exams. There is a lot of material that the class covers, so I think it would be much harder if you miss lectures.

Lectures are.. fine but feel twice as long as they actually are. Seems annoyed by students asking questions and is passive-aggressive. Struggles with technology often which is odd for a young professor. Denies accommodations based on if she thinks you need them or if it is convenient. I don't recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ignores student feedback to improve lecture quality. Claims that accommodations are built into the class and therefore ignores the requests of disabled students. Passive aggressive in emails with students. Finds ways to blame students for not understanding the content despite them asking for help and giving specific feedback.

Don't bother with the textbook but make sure to buy the additional readings packet. Keep up on those readings because they're incredibly relevant and come up during tests. Tests are challenging but you can bring notes. Her lectures are amazing and she likes students that speak up. Always willing to talk outside class and give specific feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. She can explain everything clearly and even though if you didn't do the reading, you can still understand most of the material. Test is accumulative but it does make me memorize the material better. This is what art history about, right?
Best slides in the department. Tests follow what's been practiced on homeworks.  Would take again.

Has an overinflated since of ego over her own lectures. Attendence is "mandatory" (10% of grade; well worth the dock if you're not deadset on getting an A), but lectures are extremely bloated with trivial, snail's pace calculations. Easy B, annoying A if you're not good at entertaining yourself through a dull lecture.

Great classes, lots of content but all very well explained. Examples dissected. Weekly homework force studying every week, which is actually good because the material is extensive and can't be learned in a blink of eyes. 1-4 questions worth points every class. Exams are too long for the time lot, so you have to be incredibly sharp to finish it.

Had to miss an out of town job interview because of her exam attendance policy (no excused absences.  That includes medical emergencies).  I pay $100k to attend UIUC to make myself marketable to employers, and this lady forgets why she's in business.

Very math intensive class, and she hits you with slide after slide of numbers. Be ready to do a lot of review and put in a lot of time for homework. She does split up tests into  "quizzes" every two or three weeks with one final, which is definitely a better system. She also puts everything online if you miss a class or don't understand something.
Teacher makes her TA do all the work barely comes to class even though its only once a week.

Lectures are completely a waste of time. She doesn't seem to prepare anything for the lectures. I doubt if she made the slides herself. Homework is completely on yourself to learn everything needed and nothing is covered in lectures, with minimal instructions. You can't learn anything in her class. If you want to learn webdev, don't take this class

Nice person but terrible professor. Lectures sucked so I had to learn all the concepts using W3 schools and YouTube. Prof NEVER responded to emails or Piazza posts, and TAs rarely responded on Piazza. If you want to learn web dev, do it through free online resources, internships, or building your own projects. This class is mostly a waste of time.

The professor repeatedly saying "eh" like 3 times in every 5 word sentences and can put you into sleep very quickly. TAs are just as lazy as her, and have the same teaching style that put people to sleep. Grading is ridiculous and the midterm is a big lie. It impresses me that they managed to make simple web programming into a big nightmare

I don't usually rate any professors but I just had to for this class. Lectures were boring and un-engaging: one month in and they had to switch to fully online cause no one would come to class . Course staff is unresponsive, taking weeks to respond. Project proposal feedback is taking over half the time given to develop our prototypes. It's a mess

She is still saying "um" every couple of minutes in class. People should be vocal about this in piazza and ask her to practice lectures before hand. To make matters worse, she is starting to say "uh." instead of just "um" repeatedly during her lectures. It's like a professor who has a hiccup that follows the pattern knowledge hiccup knowledge
I don't know why one of her tags is amazing lectures if she seems so unorganized during lectures, saying "um" seemingly every 5 seconds.

Ridiculous class, I got a C, but tbh, she uses the word UM every five minutes in class, I am surprised U of I would even hire her. Forget about that, there were several consecutive lectures where her TAs did the lecture and still used UM repeatedly. The other reviews are bogus, the fact that she uses UM nonstop is real.

Has a lot of reading. The class is well organized, but I am not sure what Ranjitha adds to the class. Each class is a discussion of a specified paper. You also had to do a data driven design project at the end which was fun. Didn't learn anything about machine learning, data mining etc..
Some MPs were long, but the class overall was amazing. I definitely learned a lot! Ranjitha is really knowledgeable and enjoyable to listen!

Awesome class, and I can learn a lot  technique for finding full-stack (MEAN) web development engineer. The professor is beautiful and hot, and TAs are handsome. If this course can reduce the project works, and increase the number of the projects, it will be great. Good to know, this course do not have finals, Bad to know this course has one midter
Awesome professor, strongly recommend choose her class!

The tests were unnecessarily hard and filled with difficult concepts not taught in class and trick questions. The MP's were long and the grading criteria for them was rarely if ever clearly defined. She let her TA's run the course for the most part other than the lectures.

This is a tough course but Prof. Hoganson and the TA I had were both excellent. I think the grading is relatively lenient but you do have to know your stuff for the exams. If you're into American history, I'd recommend taking this class with Prof. Hoganson.

Took this class during the hardest semester of my life. Prof. Hoganson and the TA for the course, Ruth Mandala, were very understanding, patient, and willing to accommodate. Content-heavy, but Prof. Hoganson consistently addressed questions and provided support. It's overwhelmingly clear that she loves her work and wants each student to succeed.

While a nice person and a decent professor, she is incredibly inept at technology and struggles to post things online, edit work, etc. She grades papers like she's critiquing a PhD dissertation instead of an undergrad research paper. Boring to listen to and hard to work with, avoid her if you can.

Professor Hoganson is very passionate about her subject. If you attend lecture and participate in discussion while completing all of the assigned readings you will do fine in this class. She does not entirely understand how to use Canvas or any technology for that matter so there will be some complications due to that during the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class was not as hard as I thought it would be. Discussions are mandatory, but lectures are not. You have to do a lot of readings, but certain discussion leaders can make it enjoyable. Instead of 3 Midterms, there are 3 Short Papers (2-4 pages). If you are a good writer, take this class. It is very doable, just a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Class was definitely difficult and challenged me, but the subjects were really interesting and I enjoyed the lectures and everything I've learned in the class. It is definitely not an easy A, but I did not have to go out of my way to pass the class.
I like history, but her annoying voice and comment made me hate history. Would not take another one of her classes.

This woman is from the stone age and taught as if it was 1934. I saw her trying to take a call on a calculator. In all seriousness, her inability to operate the most basic forms of technology limited the class. It's a disservice on U of I's part to put a professor at the helm who thinks Canvas is a fabric. Boring lecturer too, just pitiful overall.

Dropped this course halfway because it is AWFUL. The lectures are hard to follow. Didn't know my grade in the class in Week 8 because she didn't know how to use the Canvas grade section. Then learn how to? Or use another way to let me know what my grade is. TA never answered his email. Do not take this class. Waste of time.

She is the worst professor I have ever had. Gives you these weird kinds of popquizzes that make you to go to lecture and actually grades them. gives them at the very last minute always late to next class. also extremely rude and makes all her students feel bad about themselves.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Definitely get the books and do the readings. Pay attention in lecture, it'll make your life so much better. But most importantly, do the readings before class, otherwise you'll be lost. Tests are mostly essay format.

Professor Hoganson is enthusiastic about what she does. Often dull content though, and she moves too fast through the powerpoints where often times you don't have time to take proper notes. Had to read 3 novels on top of the textbook & source readings. Take home midterm was helpful as opposed to in-class. Reasonable class but be prepared to read.
Interesting course if you're interested in Modern US history.

Her lectures are pretty interesting, uses a lot of videos and examples to break up straight lecture.  If you like American History you'll like this class, there's 2 papers a midterm and a final, papers aren't on the easiest topics but manageable and exams were not too bad at all.  Grade also includes in class quizzes and section participation

Although many students don't like the content taught in her class, I really enjoyed her class and I really felt that she went out of her way to make the class fair for students. She made it extremely clear what would be on the exams and even gave us some slack during the TA strike.
Boring lectures, excessive reading, and an overly difficult final exam (if you don't remember all of the readings, you're screwed).

Teaches a very skewed view of history. This class is American history until 1877, and we didnt touch the revolutionary war, war of 1812 or the civil war at all. She taught about minorities and womens history. A little of that is ok, but this is not a minorities class. A LOT OF READING!! tests were made impossible, and were 3 hrs of essay writing
She was a very nice professor who seemed to enjoy what she was teaching. I enjoyed her lectures greatly. The midterm was not too difficult as long as you kept up with the readings and the lectures.
Awesome!

Overall, she was very nice and knew what she was talking about. She worked around a TA strike to make sure we didn't miss any of the information necessary for the exam. There was only 1 midterm and a final. Listens to classes;even as far as allowing us to submit questions to use on the final.Did have a lot of readings but nothing to hard.

Yeah, she definitely did not teach history the way I was expecting a college level course to be taught.  Also, she did spend waaaaaay too much time on minorities and women's sufferage rather than other pertinent political issues and interesting figures in history.  We talked about the actual battles of the civil war for no more than 5 min

If you have a bad TA then you are in for a  LONG semester. Prof. talks very quietly in lecture and tends to ramble a little. Very passionate about her subject material but lectures are straight from the readings. All grades are from essays and writing so your grade is basically up to your TA.
We had to read four books. I used to like history...before I took this class. The lectures what she bases the class on but they are EXTREMELY boring.
she seems really biased against the guys in our class. she encourages people to participate but when we do, she completely downplays our thoughts. i feel like a moron in her class.

Prof Hoganson is a real good teach. The class was interesting and if you go to all the lectures, you will get a good grade in the class. The tests arnt to hard at all and she keeps you interested during lectures. Overall, great teacher, pretty good class.

I would avoid this class if you aren't a history major/accustom to history courses. She teaches rapidly during lecture, and all of the TAs grade difficultly. The average in my section was a C+. I come from Business and I had no idea what the TAs wanted in the papers until it was too late. Interesting material, though. 2 Papers = 35% of the grade

Amazing professor, the best or second best I've had in all 4 years. Don't have to read the book in either HIST 170 or 274, just pay attention in lecture and regurgitate info on test to get a good grade. Both HIST 274 and 170 (adv. comp) are good classes to take. Extremely knowledgable, she knows what she's talking about, and she's very nice.

Midterm and final are memorizing terms. Not a difficult class if you follow instructions. Class is actually interesting for a non-history major. She teaches with a slight liberal/anti-American bias. But who in the history department isn't a socialist? Get Mike Lehman as you TA.

Prof, Hoganson is a very interesting and helpful professor.  She really makes history alive and relevant.  Personally, I think it's good that there are people out there who know America isn't perfect and while she never seemed biased against America, it's not a bad thing to present America's faults.

Professor Hoganson is an extremely bias professor.  She constantly focuses on projecting the United States of America in a bad light, and very rarely mentions good moves that America has made throughout history.
No Comments

Lots of quizzes based on readings you do before class. Took at 8am and he's so monotone so can be pretty boring. Very easy grader and laid back. He's a little awkward but you can tell he's very interested in what he teaches. I liked him but I don't know if I'd take him again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mr. Todd was an awesome teacher for us! He was very supportive, patient, and understanding. Though Mr. Todd can seem passive and monotonous, you really just need to listen and pay attention to his words, because he really knows his stuff! He is very passionate about philosophy. He's a really awesome guy once you get to know him. Yay Mr. Todd!!

He allowed us rewrites for our big papers worth 20%, so that was awesome, that made it so it was a very easy A.  Sometimes boring, but he's passionate and knows what he's talking about.  If you pay attention you can learn alot about life and philosophy.
great class, interesting, and got a lot out of it. I would suggest Todd for this class for sure.
todd rocks! Hes an awesome guy and listens to his students!

Todd is just a really cool guy. He is really helpful, and you just have to warm up to him. While he has a somewhat monotone voice, he is really funny, extremely smart, and passionate about his subject.

Very knowledgeable about the material and passionate about the humanities. Somewhat monotone voice, but always open to any discussion.  Still needs to work on some teaching methods but I think it's a class worth taking and he's a more than tolerable teacher. Humorous at times if you can catch it.  Allows handing in of late assignments,understanding

At any given moment, 2/3 of the class will be asleep from his extremely monotone voice.  He obviously does not know how to teach and should not be allowed in a classroom. I have never had a teacher his bad. I loved philosophy before I took it with him.
He speaks in monotone and good luck to anyone who thinks that they can understand the material or stay awake through class because both are impossible to do!
Incredible professor. Straightforward and really emphasized what we did in class. She demystifies mathematics really well. I would take MATH541 with her if I could.
Never ever cared about how students felt, ex. missing zoom meeting for review, etc.

She is generous with deadlines, generous with time during exam.
The exam is simple as long as you remember all concepts and finish HW carefully.
Lecture is a little bit boring.
Great professor.
Great professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The 2 tests and final are each worth 30% of the grade. The review sessions for these are VERY similar to the exams themselves, though. This professor has a thick accent, but is still easy to understand. I would recommend going to most lectures and not reading the textbook. Class lectures can be quite boring at times, so you don't have to go to all.

One of the most understanding professors I have taken a class with. Not only is she extremely knowledgeable, she also explains well and will take her time to explain everything if you do not understand a concept. 347 might be your first proof class, make sure you take it with her.
Amazing professor. She really brings her personal understanding of the subject when explaining concepts. Her lectures show her passion for the study of mathematics.
Go to classes, take notes, go over your notes before exams, you will pass!

One of the best professors I've ever had and I pray that I get to take a class with her again. Go to lectures or you won't pass because there's a lot of notes and the textbook won't help. You need the textbook since it has the homework in it and the homework helps a ton for the tests. Knows what she's talking about and is incredibly helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Excellent teacher, even better person.
She is the most helpful and kind teacher I have ever met. If you are required to take MATH 347, please choose her.

She's a pretty fair professor grading wise, is very passionate about what she teaches, and definitely cares about her students. However, she can sometimes rush through material bit fast. Overall, great professor for an introductory proof class.

Amazing professor for an a beginner's level proof class. This was my first proof based math class and she was awesome! She explains every concept very thoroughly and always asks to make sure it made sense to everyone. Also she has funny math jokes to keep everyone interested!

She is a nice teacher but make sure you don't sneeze around her... She lectures once a week. She jumps into a topic without explaining anything. The tests are very straightforward just make sure you go to her/TA review sessions. Also if you get stuck on HW go to class and she will usually answer your question. Also her accent is not too bad.

No quizzes or attendance. Go to all review sessions (including ones held by TA's) and it will be an easy A. Split up online HW within your group. She says she includes questions about online HW on exams but I haven't seen that yet. Mathematica is not only an easier courseload, but it's also a lot easier to grasp. Wish I did mathematica in all math

This is my favorite math course and Denka is one of the best professors in UIUC. She is very patient and helpful. She is the kind of professors who do care students.Also, using Mathematica makes the knowledge of Differential Equations very clear and vivid. You can not only learn the theory but also learn the programming and how to apply theories.
Very helpful in office hours and answers questions fully and completely when asked
Fair teacher who cares about her students.  Will go out of her way to answer your questions fully. Very good professor.
Best math professor so far at U of I. Her lectures actually make sense and she actually teaches you what you need to know for the tests and homework. She actually kind of cares.
Enjoyed the class, best math prof so far in college
She is the best math professor for Math 285. She is very helpful and caring. The tests are not hard if you study her notes carefully and read every small detail.

She was a great professor and does her best to answer any questions her students ask.  She has some really good stories and advice, I would advise against missing lecture days because you can learn so much in such a small span of time.

This class is the highlight of my Freshman year. In the lab, you look at the basics session and do the homework having little clue what the mathematics is, but after attending the class session by Prof. Kutzarova, you come out having a clear idea how to solve a given problem using both the traditional and mathematica methods. She gives good advice

Denka is a nice teacher, but her teaching is extremely confusing and you'll walk out of most lectures more confused than you were when you walked in. However, her tests are straightforward (just memorization) though VERY comprehensive. Learn every side-detail she puts up there [mathematica course]

This is the first professor whom i felt like actually cared for me to understand the grade i got. The course is challenging but not difficult and she goes over your exam with you so you can know it better and learn from your mistakes. Definitely take a course from her.
Almost no outside of class work. The professor is very helpful, and tells hilarious stories. She also knows alot of incomprehensible information about rocket science.

I had Denka for Diff Eq.  She is an extremely nice woman and is actually quite funny.  She is really helpful in class and gives really good lecture notes.  The tests are pretty easy and are graded really fair.  Anyone who says her English is bad is just trying to complain bc they got a bad grade. I would definitely take another class she taught.

Professor Kutzarova understood the merit of the Mathematica system better than other professors I have had. Her lectures were always very clear and thorough. Found exams to be extremely fair in terms of material presented and grading.

I took the mathematica version of differential equations. Subject is presented very nicely, although there are many differences between this and the standard class. Keep in mind, it is very hard to teach this class since it is half on the computer. She is very helpful if you talk to her personally about issues you are having.

MATH 285 was the first mathematica course and the last MATH course i had to take for engineering.  I was afraid on the first day of class, but Denka really helped me overcome my fears, and enjoy the class a lot.  Denka is very intelligent and passionate; she had 3 office hours per week and was really helpful in relating math to the real world.

Really not as bad a professor as most think. I did end up having to teach myself Calc III, but it wasn't much more than a couple hours each week before a quiz and then a cram session before an exam. The curves are pretty nice and shouldn't be too hard to get at least a B.

Oh...what to say about Denka... First and foremost, she talks to the board. Also, the first exam she gave my class had a lot of WTF action going on, because she made it RIDICULOUSLY hard. I'd seen the same exam she gave the previous semester, and they weren't even remotely similar. Sweet lady, but hard to understand. Get someone else if you can.
I like her but her class is really hard. I failed most of her exams. But she gives a great curve, so I still did well over all!

she sucked, i couldnt understand her at all and all she did was proofs, she hardly ever did any examples in lecture. I went to lecture even tho i was clueless as to what was going on. the only reason i got a B+ is because my TA was amazing...he actually spoke english
