The 2 writing assignments were easy, and all other grading elements were based on completion (attendance, HW, etc). Brutal exams. No additional resources to study for them, and needing to memorize over 200+ concepts is impossible. Textbook is useless but needed for HW.

It depends on your TA, but this class changed a lot since the first time I took it, it is definitely easier and structured better. Show up to class to get participation, do the InQuizitive, and ask questions it is a lot of information, as well as attend the review sessions, and do writing assignments. Overall just be prepared to do outside studying
Very forgiving system (so many drops), lots of reading but manageable, and grading scale makes it likely you'll get an A if you put the work in.

Class was taught by TA but prof held review sessions before every exam. Only provided one practice test per exam and for our honors project made us do a group project. TA was knowledgeable but kind of boring (esp @9:30am) material was the same things I learned in AP psych, w/o it I saw my friend struggling to learn the content. Lots of memorization

PSYC100 was taught by a TA so I never came in contact with Professor Travis. The TA I had was extremely knowledgable and deeply caring. The exams were overall very fair and easy to do well as long as you adequately study. Papers were graded mostly on participation. Overall, very painless course as long as you put a little effort.

Despite the amount of work you put in, this class is ridiculous for it being a 100 class. Was excited to learn about  a lot of the topics but the setup of the class was a lot of busy work, no way to study old quizzes for exams, a lot of reading just to do mediocre on test. Professor was MIA. Grade scaling makes zero sense. Just take another class.

The class is shitty gen ed where you never interact with the professor, the assignments are all busy work, and for some reason the exams are weighted really heavily? Apparently professors don't like doing their job and think that telling us to "read the textbook" is a good way of teaching the material. At least the material itself is easy
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class shouldn't be hard, and to be honest, it isn't. I took AP psych in high school, and it's the same concepts, everything's the same. The grading is what's bad. I don't know who makes the exams, but they should be more considerate. Take a look at the average grades for fall semester 2021, and then this spring semester 2022. Something's off.

Everyone commenting saying she's a terrible professor is just hurt because they didn't put in any work at the beginning of the semester and now they are complaining because the professor wouldn't change the grading policies the day before the final... honestly not a terrible class and the professor does care about her students.

I'm confused by the students freaking out right now. The average for the course is an A- but they're all upset because the professor said she thought the grading procedures were fair. There's a lot of reading, it's a kinda boring course, but is't really easy and the majority of people get A's. What else do you want???

Would not recommend it. Makes a 100-level course feel like you're taking a graduate school class. Very rude, and not understanding. Would rather plenty of students fail than change policies to benefit everyone. Would not want this professor again if my degree or life depended on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would understand the stance that the professor took about this semester's restructure, but when a variety of students reached out for help due to concerns about grade inflation the outcome was surprising. The professor instead was condescending towards her students and went onto admit life is not fair. Instead of being helpful she shamed everyone
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not recommend this course with this professor. The assignments given in this course are too excessive for a 100 class course. Not mention that none of this matters when the final and midterm is worth 48% of your final grade. Students who have done all of their work this semester will still have to worry about their grade with the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: inconsiderate and has no sympathy for her students

The professor is extremely stubborn and not understanding of her students. She was confronted about the unfairness and difficulty with the course and responded with "sometimes life is unfair". Had a miserable time this semester and completely ruined it too. Definitely not an easy 100-level class or GPA booster.

The course structure was awful. It is heavily based upon the readings which are easily over 20+ pages a week. You're not given access to exams or quizzes after you take them so you cannot see what you missed or use them to study. When students reached out about the course she condescendingly replied and didn't offer any curve or extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Actually the least understanding professor I have ever had, awful course organization and structure. My class emailed her talking about how unfair and unhelpful she and the course were and she responded rudely with things that did not at all justify her actions and also ended the email with "sometimes life isn't fair".

never saw the professor unless in office hours. my TA Haley West is amazing, but a lot of decisions are up to Lisa. She was rude in email and very very inconsiderate. Grading procedures are extremely unfair, any teacher who would willingly not use their power to alleviate a little more stress on kids/students gets an F---- in humanity from me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This semester was unfair. Last semester, the class was asynchronous, without midterms, or a final exam, and now there are several midterms and a final. The lectures don't help for exams, for a 100-level course, it is not structured well. The average midterm grades are low, and there are no curves. A lot of work needs to be put in for an A.

She is so understanding and has a passion for teaching. She appreciates the students who actually show up to class. She was willing to discuss any 'unfair' grade or confusing quiz question. Just pay attention in class and take good notes and this class will be a breeze.
Easy class but too much reading assignments. Theres no exams to do. TA did all the teaching and professor did nothing to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took psych100 in it's hybrid format. You do all the reading on your own (get ready to read a lot) and come together to meet once a week for lectures from your TA and a graded group assignment. You will never see Lisa Travis, your TA will do all the work for this class, so get a good one. If Jessica Siller is still around TAKE HER! You learn a ton
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Grading criteria is clear and it's very easy to do well in this class. However, be ready to read the textbook and take lots of notes otherwise you won't do well on the quizzes. Don't skip class because it is worth a fair amount of points. She is super nice and willing to help you with whatever class problems you may come across though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Changes due dates frequently! Make sure to constantly check your email:)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is incredibly easy, but there's a lot of reading. I would take it if only because it's a very easy 4-hour credit course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: SO MUCH READING, other than that, it's basically AP psych. Super easy A if you even skim the textbook. There's lots of quizzes, but they're really easy and a good way to keep your grade up. Lecture activities are stupid easy and you get points for them, so another way to keep your grade high. No midterms, finals, or tests, but 2 easy projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is boring.

This class is way too difficult for its own good. It covers literally EVERY ASPECT of psych. Don't take it if you don't have to. The prof is average. She does her best to make the class interesting, but it's impossible to stay interested.

Not a bad professor at all.  She was nice and always answered any questions. There is a lot of material to cover in the course, but I felt she did a good job. If you go to class, you can get an A for sure.

There is way too much material covered in this class. Professor Travis did her best to deliver the information in the most comprehensible way possible, but it felt like she was nervous every time she started talking. I felt bad for her- not a great lecturer.

Don't take this class unless you have to. You have to know a TON of material and it is not as interesting as you might think it will be. Exams are MC but are still difficult. There are also quizzes and assignments you have to do outside of class (10 quizzes and 4 assignments I think) that are fairly easy.

Her voice is very annoying, but she is always willing to help, and she knows the material very well. Read the chapters before you go to lecture and everything is quite easy. It is possible to get an A in this class, but you have to be willing to put in the time and effort.

Good teacher, always willing to help. Though, in the first few classes, she sounded very nervous, =). lectures are not always interesting but the online materials are extremely helpful. Keep reading and try to re-read the book again before midterm and final. Make sure you did the practice text before midterm and final.

She has the most annoying voice EVER. She gets confused a lot and can confuse her students in the process. She's nice but she often runs out of time and skims over important info. READ the book and take the practice exam. If you can't make it to class it's not that big of a deal because her slides are online. Give your iclicker to other people.

Really nice, a little goofy. In class quizzes and assignments that you will get full credit for, but you have to be in class. Only a couple short out of class assignments, super easy A. Exams contain written and multiple choice, but if you go to class, understand the notes and skim the book, you will do great. Overall easy and interesting class!
No Comments
her passion for the subject shows. but tough grader. expects too much of students. gaaaa!!!
Good teacher overall

The material was difficult, especially because we were expected to learn based off youtube videos.  But, if you went to Llewellyn for help, you could tell that he knew the material very well, and was able to explain it pretty clearly.  Definitely go in for help!

All material given in this class is all online through online webcasts and online discussions. The online webcasts are average and the discussions are all taught by TAs who are inconsistent. First exam material is the easiest, while the second is hard. Curves are very generous though. Keep up and do all of the given practice and go to office hours!

While this course may be difficult to keep up with since all lectures are online, with enough studying(about 10-20 hours/week), it is not difficult to do well in the class. Go to office hours as often as possible, and keep up with POTDs. Good luck!

Just keep up, and it's really pretty easy. Watch video lectures seriously for the 30 minute span. Do the practice problems sometime before the test. and work on quizzes with friends. Curves are super super generous. Very possible to get an A in this class. If you get the hang of it, it's pretty easy to grasp all concepts. All self motivated.

This class is all online. It's a lot of self discipline because you technically do not have to attend lecture... If you keep up and do all the POTD's, quizzes, and mock exams he gives out, I think that it is all shown fairly on the test. Dr. Nick is one of the best professors I've ever had.
I hate organic chemistry, and it's really stupid that the class is online.  The professor doesn't even have a lecture.

This class has a lot of resources for students who are struggling, and there's a grading exception to help students who are struggling early on in the course. Even though it isn't easy, it isn't terribly difficult if you pay attention. By the end of the class, you can solve almost any mechanism you look at using the tools you acquire.

Orgo is hard. And it's a mess at U of I because it's online. You have to do everything you possibly can to understand because the lecture videos are unclear and oversimplify the mechanisms. I found the POTDs were too easy compared to the quizzes and exams. VERY generous curve. Do all your work so you can use final modifier. Otherwise you're screwed
REally helpful professor. Listen to his online discussion, much better than the TA led ones. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!!

Nice professor; generous curve; useful resources. He is always ready to help you whatever via email or office hrs. KEEP IN MIND!!! do you quiz problems with study group, go to SI at least onece a week, it is not that hard to get A.

Probably the hardest class I've taken in my three years at U of I. However, Dr. Nick is a great professor. Discussions are very helpful, as are the (optional) homework problems. Grade consists of weekly quizzes, three midterms and a final. Effort is essential to success.

Yes, there are weeks where you have to put in 15+ hours, welcome to college. Dr. Nick does a great job in debunking the funk of organic chemistry. There are tons of resources available, he archives all of his online discussion sessions, and his curves are always fair. Best chemistry teach I've had so far, highly recommended.
Well, he is nice. Just homework, quiz, and exams are way beyond the lecture's material. Do not expect a good grade unless you spend 15hrs per week on CHEM 232 only.
You have no idea about this class. Extremely harder, if you want to get B+ or better. 2 hr per day, not include discussion , online video, SI.

In the beginning, I didn't really try hard in this class and that was a BIG mistake. But towards the end, I studied really hard and I began to understand everything. He's a GREAT professor. So good at teaching in my opinion. DO NOT slack off and go to discussions! Work really hard from the beginning and you'll do fine.

I thought his tests were really fair. He gave curves for each exam which were very generous. He always held exam reviews. Class is a lot of work and effort is key to success. His final was a great representation of the "mock exam" Great professor

Wow..If you wanna take a class that makes you hate your life I highly insist Orgo with Llewellyn. His tests are redic and barely reflect lecture material. He def assumes everyone is a chem major and loves the stuff. Having the class and all materials online though is pretty nice, but not worth the redic expectations

One of the best and easiest psych classes I have taken! The exams are easy as long as you review the lecture slides, and they give enough extra credit, which boosts your grade a lot. Would recommend to anyone.

Dr. Lleras is an awesome professor with lots of knowledge as well as humor. He made lectures very engaging and easy to remember. As long as you do your assignments and understand the basic concepts of the lectures, you should do great. I had gotten one C on a test, but extra credit and the other assignments helped so take advantage of it.

Dr. Lleras is a really nice and funny guy who always made lectures interesting. The demos that we did with him were also really fun to do, such as the M&M one. It was also really adorable when he talked about how Hermann von Helmholtz is his hero. He also used pictures of his toddler daughter as examples of color perception, which was really cute.

Professor Lleras was kind and funny. He kept lectures engaging with demos and videos that made the content more interesting. If you attend lecture and take notes, the tests are super easy. Save your money on the textbook because I did not use mine.

Really easy-going person, and despite all the content that is covered, the exams are super straight-forward. Only topics covered in lectured on are on the exams, and it is really easy to do well in this class!
Best professor ever, he made every lecture interesting by his anecdotes and experiments.

I would recommend! You can tell he's very passionate about psychology when attending lectures, and the class isn't too difficult. The exams are mostly memorizing topics and how things work, but the grading is very fair and the homework/quizzes aren't hard to get full points on. I missed 2 HW assignments and got a C on one exam and still got an A!
Very entertaining and fun guy, class was pretty easy

Dr. Lleras is amazing! He was by far one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are very interesting, and the class is relatively easy if you pay attention. He is so nice and genuinely wants his students to succeed. He also has pre-recorded lectures on Moodle, which is so helpful for studying. I would 100% recommend his course!!

I literally LOVED this class. The lectures are genuinely so interesting and even if it's a boring topic, the way he lectures still makes it entertaining. There's lots of cool demos and even though the lecture material is sometimes super detailed or difficult, you can easily ace an exam just by using a quizlet or reviewing your notes. 5/5

Caring professor who shows passion for what he teaches. Difficult to understand in lectures with accent, though provides all lectures/material online which makes the class very easy. Tests are easy as long as you pay attention in lectures. Outside coursework is a tad heavy, though not difficult. Overall a very nice teacher, very interesting class.

His lectures are boring to sit through, but he does a few cool demos and makes funny jokes. Each exam are only 45 mcq, 3 of which he drops off, so you only need a 42/25 to get a 100%. I got 100% on every exam by just filling out the study guide from his videos, that I watched the day before. First psych class I ever took. 11/10 easy A+

Since COVID Lleras has the options: in-person or his online modules to get lecture material. Most of the quiz questions were the lecture questions on the online modules so I got 100% on the quizzes everytime. He does have an accent and his slides don't have much information, but his homework was graded on completion so it was an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes & professor/TAs are so nice. They really want you to succeed (ex: provide study guides). Quizzes & homework are online. Great course structure & grades in a timely manner. 3 really easy exams (no final & non-accumulative) (vocab recognition). Lectures are posted so if you can't make lectures, you wont fall behind!

I found the textbook readings & lectures interesting and easy to understand. There is a LOT of lecture time, but it actually doesn't feel as long bc much of it is examples. I recommend having the textbook open while you watch for harder concepts. You will 100% succeed in this course if you pay attention to the lectures and do the homework.

Asynchronous version = pre-recorded lectures, 3 proctored exams, and assignments. Lectures are engaging although Professor Buetti is more clear, material is fantastic. Some modules combine very basic physics and biology, and some human anatomy as well. Overall, a very straightforward and easy class, especially if you have a background in science.

Hes a very nice man who wants you to succeed. However, all tests are proctored online, he can be hard to understand, puts zero words/content on lecture slides, the lectures are incredibly boring and arent compelling whatsoever. Nearly impossible to get an A unless you knew content beforehand. I wouldnt take this class/prof again. Just my $.02

Not gonna lie, this class was really hard for me to understand. I dont know if it was because of the overall topic or the way lectures were presented, but if I hadnt pulled through for the last exam and did the extra credit, I wouldve failed. The professors do try their best to help the students, but this class is too hard for a gen ed for psych
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Writes really hard exams and the lectures are crazy boring. If you're not interested in becoming an eye doctor don't take this course. Too many anatomy terms. Get ready to spend a ton of time studying if you want even a B. He's a caring professor, but doesn't understand how to teach to humans. Cheating is rlly hard as well. WARNING! Brace urself!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's really chill and wants to make class the same way - easy A. His class has 3 Exams(60%) + 9 easy quizzes online ( 10%) + 3 discussion post online (one per test - you just answer a question in a short paragraph 20% - very lenient with grading) Only complaint - Attendance was mandatory with iclicker (don't even need to get answer right 10%).

The class is relatively easy, which is good because he is a tad hard to understand every now and then. I didn't use the textbook much at all - just attending lecture was good enough for me, as long as I paid attention. Only exams, no homework or papers to write. He's a very likeable professor!
Only 3 exams, non cummulative. No lecture participation and I recieved an 89% by just using the lecture slides. TAKE THIS CLASS!
Greatly underapreciated.

Terrible. Half the class dropped the course after his midterm. He got sick late into the semester so got absolutely NO feedback on any of our projects so we still didn't know if we were doing the project according to the way he liked it. Believe me, its either his way or the highway. Also literally spent an entire class talking about shoes.

I had a lot of trouble with this guy. He was sick during the semester and was late to class almost everyday. He canceled class 4 times as well. He liked to get off-topic during the lectures and talked about stupid stuff like what kind of computer he likes, etc. I didn't learn anything at all in this class.
DO NOT take with hodges!
No Comments

Loves to talk about anything and everything except the material on the slides.  Very interesting teacher though.  Test wasn't too bad, just put some effort into the projects/presentations and you'll be fine.

Never stays on topic but his conversations are at least somewhat interesting.  Only got through three powerpoints the entire semester.  No exams or final, just one presentation at the end of the semester.
His lectures were very unorganized and asked very niche questions on exams, class averages were ~45%. Do good in Braz's section and take final and you'll be ok

NEVER AGAIN. His exams made no sense and the format was select all that apply. His lecture slides had way too much info and he just reads off those slides. I put my blood, sweat, and tears in this class and ended with a terrible grade. You have to teach yourself. Prepare for crashouts FR. Heartbreaking.

There's a lot of content in this class and not a lot of time or explanation provided by Loman. I would recommend going to the TA's office hours as much as possible since they often taught me the material.

The exams are extremely hard, and they are almost completely unrelated to what is taught in class. The grading is very harsh. Taking this course will seriously hurt your GPA, even if you put in a lot of effort. All I can say is: if you see this person, run. Try every possible way to take a different one instead.

the worst professor I ever had. puts way too much information on the slides and expects you to know it all even though the exams never reflect the lectures. he clearly does not care about this class nor any of his students. exam averages are around 50%. goodluck because you will need it.

Class is very test heavy and judging from other reviews test averages are the same now as they were a few years ago and that is LOW. There is a difference between "hard teaching" and him, hard teachers push you to know the material and want to see you succeed, I believe he does not care if you succeed or fail.

If you want to do well in this class spend an hour after each lecture compiling your notes, brush over them once a week, and go to office hours (the TAs are Awesome)! Most people in this class don't put in effort to learn the material and are susprised when they score poorly. Dr. Loman is a hard professor, but I feel I gained a lot from this class.

You can try your absolute best and still not achieve anything in his class. He suggestion for the exams is literally "know everything" and will pull out examples that he has never shown a demonstration for other than offhandedly discussing it in lecture. The averages were 61% and 51%. He cannot educate, I wish you all the best.
I try to see the positive in every professor. Couldn't find one for this professor. Good luck ANSC majors

Worst professor at uiuc hands down. Does not care about his students. Exams NEVER reflect the lectures. This class gave me stomach ulcers and made me have to start antianxiety meds. My counselor says they hear a lot about him and someone was supposed to talk to him to make his class easier for upcoming semesters so hopefully that's the case.

Definitely the worst professor I've had the dishonor of “learning” from. His slides are very confusing and complicated. He expects his students to understand very complex concepts even though, as is stated in the syllabus, it is a “basic introduction” to the subjects of cells and metabolism. His material was neither basic nor introductory.

As an animal science major who was forced to take this class, it's horrible. The only reason I did semi good was because of Braz. He can't teach and reads off of slides expecting you to just understand and know what he's talking about. Class averages don't get higher than 40% and then blames it on us for not studying. No curve either. Goodluck.
Guys...If you cannot get into a vet school it is all his fault

Easily the worst prof I have ever had. Unbelievably confusing lectures with way too much information on them which is BARELY covered on the exams. Exam averages are terrible and he blames it on the students. Reading the textbook fully outside of class would be the only saving grace, teaching yourself the material. Never again.

one of the laziest. Lecture material is mostly pictures. Homework do not include answers that are on the slides or lectures. The average exam grades are 40-53%, and he blames it on our lack of studying. He words exam questions in a way that doesn't match any previous assignments.  He answers questions very swift. he is only teaching for lab money.
Class made more sense when I skipped lecture and just taught the content to myself.

took 221 last year and suffered through the first half of the semester; hearing the current horror stories, it seems prof loman has somehow gotten even worse with practice. hw is still single-attempt despite half the content never being covered in lecture, exam averages are once again barely above 50%, and he clearly has no respect for his students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i am definitely not clever enough to take his class...

You'll suffer in this course. As a major/vet school requirement; it's a marathon, not a sprint. Maybe one day Loman will provide study resources, acknowledge struggling students (56% exam avg come on dude), and cultivate an approachable environment. His TA's are mini-me's of himself: condescending, egotistical, and disinterested in student success.

He got annoyed when people couldn't answer a question he asked in lecture and when someone tried to answer it and got it wrong he got more annoyed. He does not explain concepts well and he goes too fast. He is not understanding and it is very hard to do well on his exams. He gives no practice exams.

Actually terrible. He literally made mistakes on the slides all the time and would say, “I'll change it later,” but never did. This has cost me so many points on assignments and on exams. I learned that in this class you just have to teach yourself everything.

Probably the worst professor I have had the misfortune of taking class from. Not only does he degrade students for not understanding difficult content, but he takes pride in low test scores and tries to justify incredibly low test averages. Be ready to sit through the most boring lecture of your whole life and teach yourself all of the content.
You can do well so long as you wear pleated pants.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super hard class, makes it even more difficult with a professor like him.
Goodluck ANSC majors....
Genuinely doesn't care about his students at all. The second half of the course with Dr Braz was by far much better; she's the only reason I ended up with a B and not lower
Worst class I've had in. Crammed three days of lectures into two, didn't take time to explain anything thoroughly
Worst professor ever. DO NOT take any classes with him.
Genuinely the worst class I have taken. Was not receptive to students need with low exam averages.
This class was truly something else, exams had me scratching my head. The class just consists of weekly homework assignment and 4 exams. Stay safe out there.
Worst teacher ever. I think there is soemthing wrong with him. Makes a interesting class miserable

Louvnis does not seem to really care about his students all that much. Run-of-the-mill boring college class. He goes through the lecture super slow and doesn't seem to really go in depth on our subjects. Barely any review for the tests, questions we never learned the material for, and a harsh grader. Take another professor for ADV 284 if you can.

He is an absolutely awful professor who does not care about his students and seems to get joy out of people struggling. Most boring and monotone lectures, and it feels like he's reading from the textbook directly. Test questions are worded for you to answer wrong, and the group projects and assignments have little to no continuity across. Awful.

Attend lectures, as he will provide checkpoints throughout, and these questions will appear on the exams. Studying is straightforward. Group projects were ok, not difficult at all, but they were kind of boring. He is passionate about client data insights. Teaches you how to use MRI Simmons. It's a good class if you want to go into data insights.

I'm not sure why this professor receives so much criticism - the discussion assignments are manageable, the exams aren't overly challenging, and the content is engaging. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you go to every lecture, the exams should be fairly straightforward. The easiest way to study for the exams is to review the lecture slides!

He is a terrible professor. You have lectures, discussion sections, & group projects-- and each of those things hardly relate to each other. Pierre is a horrible, monotone, long-winded lecturer. The 1st exam was awful, but if you study all of the slides very well, you will be okay. TAs luckily grade group work fairly. Good luck on the exams tho...

Horrible class. It's clear he has no idea how to run a class. Slides, project instructions, and sometimes test questions are incoherent. Overall an extremely unpleasant class. TA's do their best to make the class somewhat okay but at the end of the day they aren't the ones running it.

The actual content and work in this course are not too difficult, but Professor Pierre makes it hard to enjoy learning it and doesn't seem to actually care about his students succeeding in his course. He's very strict on due dates, which is understandable, but is sometimes rude to students and seems inconvenienced by questions during the lecture.

I think that Dr. Pierre has the potential to be a good professor but his class needs reorganizing. He is clearly very passionate and gives strong lectures that further emphasize the concepts introduced in the class but this class has far more work than it should with the deliverables and he doesn't budge with this.

Test questions are super specific, and he doesn't allow for a lot of leeway. His lectures are pretty bland, and are almost word for word bullet points of the textbooks. Assignments don't help you prepare for the exams at all. Learning how to use MRI Simmons is the only helpful takeaway, but other than that this class is a bore/waste of time.

I only have 350 characters to describe my disdain for Pierre so I'll cut right to the chase. Chat GPT could explain the course material with more humanity and zeal for life than this guy could ever hope to. His exams are riddled with poorly thought out questions with subjective answers. Hes personable as a cactus, won't answer questions in class.

Professor Pierre has no understanding of how to prepare students for exams. His lectures regurgitate what is said in the $250 textbook and his only advice was to "study what you think is important." TAs were no help because they were not able to see the exam question formats before the exam date. Questions are insanely specific and give no context.

Professor Loughran is by far one of the smartest people I've ever encountered. Her ability to explain dense theory in an understandable way (without having to dmb things down) is unbelievable. Her class is by far the most challenging class I've ever had but has been the most rewarding as well. (Put aside more time than you'd expect to read)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: ENGL 301 is a tougher class but at no fault of Dr. L. She aims for us to grow comfortable with difficult material and to "stick with it". This class does deal with a few uncomfortable topics. You'll need to accept not immediately understanding what you're reading, but I couldn't recommend a better guide for critical theory. Highly inspirational.

Please take this professor when or if you take ENGL301. Loughran's lectures are pristine and clear. I learned so much from this class and it continuously proves itself to be useful in my other classes/life. The readings are challenging, so I recommend setting aside longer periods of time read; regardless the lectures clear up things from readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor genuinely cares about the wellbeing and success of her students. While her grading may be tougher than what you are used to, she is very aware of her students' limits and knows how to push them to success. Her class is on the difficult side, but the workload is very manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor cares a lot about her students and genuinely wants them to succeed. She is a very tough grader of writing, but she does this to push students and better their writing. She is one of my favorite professors and definitely challenges all her students, because she knows what they are capable of.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor creates inappropriate relationships with students by chastising them in class and taking offense to student feedback. The professor also arranges private meetings to further harass students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor in the English Department by FAR! Made extremely difficult reading material feel like a breeze. However, if you do not go to class regularly, you will be lost. Mandatory office hours visit because she cares and wants you to succeed! Take home exams easy if you take note and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: While she is absolutely brilliant, the more I reflect on her class, the more I realize how outrageous her behavior was. She would throw tantrums directed towards students and make inappropriate, hurtful comments. Many of my classmates expressed during conversations outside of class that they felt her teaching left them emotionally exhausted.

Prof Loughran's classes are so interesting and she really wants her students to understand the material and think critically! Her lectures and slides are easy to follow and she's funny which makes the class run smoothly. She is passionate about critical theory and def knows what she's talking about! Tests are easy if you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Loughran is described by many as "goated" or "the goat" and it makes sense. It is sort of hard to explain but she relays a lot information in a way that is thought provoking while also clear. She gets students to think critically and overall just very knowledgeable and I took many classes with her because of how good she is.

Professor Loughran is definitely one of the better professors here at UIUC. She has very thorough lectures and loves critical theory and close readings. Sometimes can come off as condescending, but she truly does know the material she's teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Loughran is one of the best professors Ive had at this university. Shes super passionate about critical theory and clearly wants every student to understand the material. She isn't going to just hand things to you, but the push to gain your own understanding of the material is more helpful than anything. Great professor and course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Loughran is an amazing teacher. Her lectures are in depth and she's really knowledgeable about all of the material and explains it so well. She's funny and for every assignment she gives extensive feedback. Take her 301 class if you get the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR! I took her Intro to Critical Theory class on a whim and was not disappointed! Her lectures were immersive and inclusive and she was very understanding about it being an online lecture. I was really amazed by the range of topics covered in the class that she managed to tie together.

Professor Loughran is very organized with her lectures and really cares about teaching and her students. She was one of the most understanding teachers I had during the pandemic and she made a lot of modifications to help us succeed.

I took Prof. Loughran for ENG 301, and she was one of the best professors I've had as a sophomore English major. Lecture attendance is mandatory, but it's worth it because she clarifies difficult theories and offers interesting perspectives on them. If you walk out of the class empty-handed, you did something wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She assigns a lot of readings (but I didn't read about 75% of them and still did fairly well) so you really don't have to do all of them. She's very funny and creates a welcoming environment. Also-- critical theory is insanely hard stuff and she does a really good job explaining/elaborating. Grading takes a while to get used to, but it's fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: We discussed about 10% of the assigned readings, but ALL of it was on the exam- annoying. Why assign reading in an ENGL class if we're not going to discuss it at all? Survey is supposed to be broad, but she assigned just to assign readings. On exams, she only wants to hear what she wants to hear. biased towards her own beliefs in literature

honestly her teaching style just was not for me. she's very lecture heavy and also calls on students who she thinks are not paying attention. grading wise i would say is pretty fair i guess, although it is kind of unclear as to what actually makes up your grade

Prof. L. did something different this semester (SP17) and dramatically changed the way she teaches 255. At times,  I felt very lost and disinterested in her lectures while other times she gave an especially unique perspective. Attendance is mandatory (1 free absence). 2 projects, 6 short response papers, and weekly quizzes in section for grades,

Loughran is one of  the best professors I had in my time at UIUC.  Loughran's lectures are both interesting and incredibly informative.  I took both 255 and 301 under Loughran's careful tutelage and they were easily my favorite classes.  I always felt known and comfortable in class.  10 out of 10 would take those classes gain just for fun.

Professor Loughran is a professor who can change your life or at least your perspective on it. Survey classes are in their very being made to cover a large array of subjects but Loughran does a phenomenal job making it an eclectic and interesting bunch of texts. Take her course if you're eager to learn and be challenged. Talk to her after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It's a survey class, so I'm not working closely with her. However, her lectures are solid and the reading load is fair for a 200-level course. (I hear she's cut it down, so I guess she's good with taking feedback too.) Overall, this class is nothing special but I'd be interested to have her in a smaller, discussion-based class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had to work hard to get an A in this class - it's not impossible, but you definitely need to put the effort in. It's a LOT of reading and writing every week, and the they tend to be more on the difficult to understand/boring side. That said, Loughran is cool and generally flexible, and gives great and useful feedback on papers and assignments.

She knows what she's talking about and is clearly very passionate about teaching. There is a lot of reading and you need to keep up with it, but it usually isn't too bad. I had tried taking ENGL 255 twice before and dropped because of bad professors and she was a lifesaver after two bad experiences! Midterm was take home but final was challenging.
She's a wonderful lecturer with a great insight in what she teaches. Very clear in what she expects, and is easy to talk to. She made my semester a great one.

Without a doubt one of the best teachers I've ever had. 301 is a requirement for the English major and can be pretty intimidating, but Prof Loughran is a phenomenal lecturer. She's a tough grader and makes you work for it so if you're one to slack off this won't be an easy time for you. But the class is so worth it, she makes it less intimidating.

I really enjoyed her class-definitely have to keep up with the reading to succeed though. Lectures are super important to attend. Tests focus on short responses and an essay, plus background on authors, and some quotes. She is very knowledgeable and laid back. Definitely take this class with her if you can.

If you have a chance to take a class with Professor Loughran DO IT. Her classes are not blow offs in the least, but they make you feel like you are actually in college and challenge you to improve your writing and reading.  I literally jump at the chance to take more classes with her.  Helpful, understanding, and personable...she's the best.

She is an expert in the subject and her lectures were fascinating. She is also really funny and good at referencing pop culture now and then. She allowed blog posting as substitution for essay writing, which was fantastic. The class was, however, not a blowoff in the least bit and required a high amount of reading.

She is by far the best English professor I have ever had. She is genuinely interested in the material and students. Literary theory is so difficult to read and understand, but Professor Loughran makes it interesting and relatable. If you put in the time and effort, you WILL succeed.

One of my favorite teachers of all time. She brought the material to life and made everything interesting and applicable to daily life. She also loves pop culture and incorporates it into lecture frequently. Reviews were helpful and she went over important test material and key words minutes before exams. Take ENGL 255 with Loughran. She's awesome.

Despite having no choice but to teach Survey, she honestly seems extremely invested and interested in it anyway. She has a great sense of humor. Go to lecture! Missing one can hurt you. It's a lot of work and reading, but pay attention, do the study guides, and you're good to go. And go to the exam reviews. They're fun.

Brilliant insights, well-organized and interesting lectures, straightforward exams, and a great taste in music. Would recommend this class to anyone with a deep interest in American History and Lit, not just English majors who have to take it.
Interesting lectures, incredibly insightful, grades fair. The class was a lot of work/reading (but all surveys are) but if you came to lecture and studied her guides you did fine.

Super nice, good taste in music, really helpful, and her lecture material is easily understood. Passionate about what she teaches and brings a good attitude and atmosphere to the class. Studying is necessary for exams, but if you study the study guide you should do well. I got an A and I'm a slacker. :)

Trish Loughran is the BEST professor I have ever had! She brought amazing insight to everything we read, was very easy to talk to during office hours, and continually encouraged each and every one of us. The class was intense but I am such a better writer now for having gone through it. She really goes above and beyond for her students.

Extremely Great! Very clear, and I could tell she really loved what she taught us. Very quirky personality that helped lighten the mood when discussing deeper topics. Very interesting person, and very fair grader. DO THE STUDY GUIDES!!! Everything on each of her exams were either on the study guide or in the review session. She WILL NOT trick you.

Great professor! Very organized and clear. All tests contained exactly what she said they would. She provided study sheets and review sessions. She also tried to learn the names of the 200 kids in the class and will take questions in lecture. She is very knowledgeable and very fair.

i needed to read the textbook for this class. it wasn't that bad though because the readings were actually interesting. although the class is really hard, when i put forth the effort and did the readings, i started getting a lot out of it.

Great prof!!  I love this class, she offers great insight into the readings.  There are 3 exams, with a take-home essay with each.  Keep up with readings and its easy.  She puts powerpoints, her lecture notes, and studyguides online.  Very open to students needs, cut down reading after students said they were struggling to keep up.
So smart; can be intimidating, but nice when you do your work. You will learn but don't take the class if you plan to slack.

Prof. Loughran's class was one of my favorite English classes. She gives you all the info you need, her exams are straight from her lectures, and if you do the work you will be fine. She seems intimidating at first, but is actually quite nice and helpful if you give her a chance. Recommend this class if she is the professor.
explains american literature quite clearly and effectively.  Her lectures make many other professors look unprepared and unprofessional

not sure what some of these other comments are about... difficult lectures, lots of notes, but exams are written to be completed easily if you actually studied/attended class/paid minimal attention. her study sessions are a great help. she will take any comments/suggestions you make into consideration, especially about the exams.

she gets a bad rap, but i'm not sure why. if you don't like her lectures, don't go, the notes she reads from are online, as well as the powerpoint slides she uses. her exams are a bit strenuous, time-wise, but the material is not complicated. her take on the material she presents is usually very original and impressive.

Trish is not the devil that some people make her out to be. Her tests are not all that difficult if you actually take the time to study for them. What nobody here has mentioned yet is that if you failed the midterm, you had the chance to drop the grade completely in place of the grade you got on the final exam. Her lectures are very bland though.

I think she may have read some of the comments previously posted on the website and completely changed when I had her.  We lucked out sort of and had a small class so it was easier to pay attention and learn.  You HAD to go to class and read.  She held test reviews and brought donuts & pizza.  3 or 4 small tests and gives study guides!  Pretty easy
No Comments

Good: she offered a large selection of paper topics. Bad: the grading was strict, the tests were long and difficult, the lectures were extremely boring, and she was very rude. She told the class that she intentionally made the midterm difficult in order to punish those who did not come to lecture and those who slept through it.. ?! not very fair.
There are exactly 5 reasons why this story works. Exactly 3 reasons why that other one doesn't. Exactly 2 interpretations of it all. Memorize it. Also, be bland. Be very bland.
Trish is crazy, her tests were literally impossible to finish, as evident in the amount of F's she enjoyed handing out.

Lectures are boring...She doesn't use a mic a lot of the time, and I never want to see another timeline again after taking this class.  Exams are HARD and take more time than you're given.  If you have to take this class, get a really good TA and read all texts and study HARD.  Seriously.

Joyless and very condescending towards the class. Her tests were easy but she gave us very little time to do them. When OVER HALF the class received D's or F's on the midterm exam, her response was that we should "get serious". Also employs a nigh-exclusively autobiographical interpretation for nearly every text we read. Not fun or good at all.
borrrrrrring lecture, tests were very hard. TONS of reading

This professor should not be teaching. He rambles for over an hour about the first four slides of every lecture and then skips explaining later slides. Prompts class to explain these ramblings back to him repeatedly. Quiz after every class. Labs and TAs were great, the class was worth it for them, but don't expect to learn much from the lecture.

Horrible, doesn't follow along the class timeline, talks about AI like it's the biggest thing ever and barely touches on course content. TA doesn't attend office hours and needs to be spammed before doing anything. Professor barely seems to know the content and doesn't bother explaining anything technical about it, rather talk about it ambiguously.

While Prof. Sha is clearly a pioneer in the field, he is not a good teacher. Lectures are super boring and poorly taught. For some reason the final is 30% of the grade which is weird given it is the only exam.  So even if you do super well in everything your grade is determined by the final. Labs were cool but had no correlation with the lectures.
Easily the worst professor I've ever had. Does anything but teach and literally just rambles all lecture.

The slides are barely covered in the lectures, and you will instead listen to his "philosophy" that are NOT EVEN CLOSE to the topic. Can confirm he got mad at a student during the mid-term presentation. I hope the class will improve over time, otherwise your time can be better spent than staying in this class.

He assigns midterm presentations that have very little guidance and ambiguous rubrics. He expects these presentations to be better than his own lectures, which are lacking, as the only memorable parts of his lectures are the tangents he goes on. He gives no help on what to add to presentations, but gets mad if we skip the smallest topics.
Just ridiculous teaching and ambiguous requirements / syllabus
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's basically the one who discovered and developed all the material taught in the class. He can ramble in lectures. Homeworks and labs help teach the material.

The entire material of the class could have been taught in 3-4 weeks. Unfortunately, he would spend a lot of time talking about lots of unrelated things and stories. HWs and assignments in the lab were not exactly related to lectures. I would not recommend the class and the prof.

Prof. Sha is the guy who pioneered the field real-time systems. No doubt He knows everything and has vision. The course is packed with topics with the assumption that you MUST research about them after class.  Don't miss classes. Read the books.  If you want to be a real engineer, take it and survive it! OS knowledge is an absolute prerequisite.

I was really interested in taking a course on embedded systems. I signed up for this class but what can I say! He is the worst professor I have ever had (in term of teaching not personality to be fair). He doesn't teach, he just show up, try to be funny, and leave. Concepts are not defined or explained in organized way. This course really sucks.

Terrible lecturer, you're better of reading the slides. He's a nice guy but it takes more than that to be a half decent professor. I can't believe the CS department keeps this guy on. The class itself is pretty bad too but that's a different matter.
Quite literally the worst professor I've ever had.
His cs class is like philosophy
Good lectures, but she lacks control over the course and grading, and also gives off fake vibes when you talk to her.
OMG I could not deal with the way she talks dude, literally so like valleyyyyy

Professor Luetkemeyer is one of the best professors I've had. Her lectures were amazing and I've always walked out of a lecture understanding everything she explained. She explains hard concepts in a way that everyone can understand. She is also very accessible outside of class.

Gave everyone a 100% on the final exam when canvas was down. Very smart and passionate about his field, sometimes goes beyond the scope of the course but is very nice and willing to help. Occasionally told interesting stories about former students and their experiences in industry.

You can tell that Professor Lumetta genuinely cares for our learning, not only in 120 but also in future ECE courses. He's very kind and communicative. The class itself is difficult by the nature of it, but Lumetta is great at discussing abstract topics in a way that makes sense.
Goat. Good decisions in times of crisis.
Good professor! Give a lot of useful advice in learning including labs, hw, lectures,etc., Clear logic and mindset and an amazing course

He is actually the GOAT no exaggeration this man is a legend. The class is not free and you definitely have to put in work but the homework he gives is very intuitive and comprehensive and there's plenty of resources like his course note also the cyberattack situation was insane and then he just gave everyone a 100. We all love him. GOAT professor.

Prof Lumetta is very smart but like book smart. None of the practice exams have solutions provided so we as a student have no idea if our answer is correct or not. Also, this is just a rumor but if you get a grade that's below like a 50, you test score gets curved down. Happened to my buddy Eric twice. I would say this though: to be continued...

Prof. Lumetta wrote the CompE curriculum at UofI, and teaches 391 with a practiced ease. Though he sometimes covers content way beyond 391, if you read up before lecture, you will learn a /lot/. In one-on-one interactions, he's super patient and kind. He loves what he does and is good at it.
He delivered fantastic lectures in ECE 220 but I think he didn't do a good job in ECE 391.

Yes, Prof. Lumetta is a nice guy, in OH and accessible. But, his lectures are confusing. The final project is literally a nightmare at this point. This is a parallel programming class. But he wanted us to build a CNN from scratch within two weeks. By the end of the due date, there are teams didn't even how the CNN backpropagation works yet.

Used Prof. Wen-mei Hwu's slides and apparently he doesn't know what the slides were about at least once every lecture. Covered it with silence and awkward laughs. Poor explanation of the concepts here and there.
Great professor. Has a powerful voice, and explains very well. Also makes lecture very conversational.
Great professor! He explains hard materials very well!

Very knowledgeable and nice guy. However, his lectures are EXTREMELY difficult to understand. Requires atleast one more viewing online. Good thing that his lectures are recorded. That said, he is very patient and willing to help during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: When the course I must study was about ECE198 the same time like this last year, he taught ECE220. But now when we are studying ece220, he is teaching ECE198. I don't understand what is he doing?

Although I struggled a lot in his classes, I think he is still a great lecturer with inspirational talks about the lessons, the real experience in industrial work and he makes his students broaden their horizon and push up their limit! Would like to give him a big hug and want to take his classes again!

Prof. Lumetta went above and beyond the course curriculum by intriguing his students with cool stories about major companies. He's a total nerd - one test, he started writing the time left in IEEE, but it's awesome. Relates to his students so well. Class is difficult as hell, but he makes it entertaining and clearly loves what he does.
He will take your points off even if you write a good comment.

The course is ECE498SL. I could not put SL in the course number due to character limit. The class is extremely fun. The first half talked about in-depth C++, including how the object oriented features are implemented at C or ASM level. The second half focused on light parallel programming using POSIX thread. The MP were quite hard but helped a lot.

ECE391 is the most interesting required course in ECE. The MP were extremely helpful and fun, but the lecture could get people lost at some point since he frequently went off from the track and started talking about stuff beyond the course materials. As a result,  students with strong background love the course while the others hate it.
He's a super knowledgeable professor. Really thanks him for designing this new 190 sequence :) Homework and exam problems are pretty challenging, but all very reasonable.

He is smart and he is probably the best  prof in ECE 391. Don't complain because it is not his fault to make the class so hard. It is designed to challenge you. 391 is the hardest ECE course here at U of I but is also the most useful course ever here at U of I. You will get what I mean when you got interviewed by big companies on OS questions.

Professor Lumetta is very knowledgeable, but teaches fast & overestimates his students a bit. If some people in the front are nodding there head, does not mean everyone gets the concepts. 391 is ridiculously hard, and thankfully he gave us a curve to save a few the shame of a C at the end, nevertheless the last MP matters, get a good group!!
Unsolvable Machine Problems for the time frame. Poor explanation of course materials

Good teacher. Good sense of humor. He's definitely a nerd; the beard signifies his commitment to the FSF. Not easy though; you should already have an interest in the subject to get everything out of the course (like in all ECE classes).  Difficulty is about right. Those who complain probably just got bad grades out of apathy or under-preparedness.
Professor Lumetta 0wns.
This Prof knows nothing about teaching. He, like most profs at University of Illinois, get paid for research only. U of I at Urbana Champaign is not a good school if you wana learn.
This guy is smart but do not know how to teach. Having a Ph.D does not mean we will know how to teach others. I am totally on my own.
Steve Lumetta is my world
good instructor. This class is super easy and interesting for people already familiar with programming and linux, if not, this will be your hardest class.
Very charismatic.  One of the few in the ece department.

Offers a tough class, but he's very knowledgeable and runs a very entertaining lecture - probably the best ECE course I've had in 3 semesters. MPs are time-consuming and sometimes complex, but not impossibly difficult - lots of help is available. Lots of engineering design/tradeoff "thought" questions on exams.

Worst class i've ever taken. MP's are too hard. The teacher's philosophy is to present students with what he calls "the impossible" so we can reach our potentials which is total bs because you will not solve those MP's ever. Exams are over arcane material as well. Take CS125 instead...

Very hard class, the MPs take a lot of work, but he prepares you well for them.  Not a very above average teacher, but not bad either.  Mostly just go over examples of programs, he never teaches C, you have to pick it up from the book and the examples if you don't already know it.  The class is a lot of work, as with most ECE classes.
No Comments
Awesome, awesome, awesome class.
No Comments

Professor Luckman is a very kind professor who is dedicated towards making her course as engaging as possible. She is a super caring person who personally checked in with me after hearing about personal issues that I had during the semester. Even though I personally didn't like Capsim, the way she structured her class made up for it. Best 201 prof.

Luckman is awesome! She facilitates an inclusive environment for all learners and really enjoys the subject. She grades fairly and makes all students feel welcome and encourages us to learn and grow. I could not have asked for a better experience. She is easy to access outside of class as well and empathizes with students.
Fantastic teacher and easy class! You can tell she really enjoys her subject.
Excellent teacher. I learned a lot from her class. I thought the homework was challenging due to how long it took me to finish while I was working full-time.

Amazing professor. You can tell she actually cares about her students as people. The class is fun and interesting if you engage and make an effort to know your classmates. Would definitely recommend her for B201. And don't worry about the capsim simulation. It makes no sense at first, but you'll pick it up quickly.
She was a great professor and cared about her students! Made the class super enjoyable and fun, definitely would recommend and would take a class with her again!

Professor Luckman is a really great teacher for BUS 201. The class itself is not very challenging but she really helps make the class interesting and demands your attention during days when there is a lecture. She also includes lots of in-class activities to keep you present during class. I would take a class with her again :)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good teaching style, nice lady with helping with homework and class atomsphere

Luckman has GREAT interaction with students and encourages discussion like no other professor. Makes CAPSIM enjoyable and always has great help there. Other assignments however were a bit odd. Did NOT enjoy Digication essays and online discussion posts, which other B201 I guess don't have to do.

She's a genuinely great professor, one of the better ones at UIUC. She doesn't just present material that we learn and forget just for a grade, she doesn't care about the grade rather she wants the student to grow as a person. She's all about participation and involvement in the material, so try to get interested in the class and ask questions.

One of the best professors I've had! Homework isn't bad at all - simply reading an article/listening to a podcast. It gets tough when you have to work on the simulation. So be ready! You will have to put in work outside of class to understand the simulation, but she makes the class barable and fun! (She's super nice too! Always ready to help!)
Solid, upbeat prof. Seems nice and accommodating. Class was exceptionally easy, though I still learned some useful things.

Easiest teacher for BUS 201. Don't take anyone else or it will be a lot harder for you. Go to her office hours if you are doing bad on Capsim. She will give you a better grade the more effort you put into the class. I would've failed Capsim, but I went to her office hours four times, came in last, and she gave me an A on the project.

Olsen is awesome-clearly knows the content of the course very well, and also is very accessible outside of class. Awesome teacher, but my critiques are that his lectures go to fast, and the problems assigned for the course are not too similar for the exam questions. Otherwise, if he is teaching your class, I can guarantee that you will learn lots!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The material was difficult but he takes questions well and is always willing to re-explain things. The class is linalg heavy and there's little to no review, but that's sort of expected at this level. Would've preferred more exams each weighted less though, the exams covered too much and each question ended up being worth 0.7% of the final grade.

Great professor! He knows the course content very well. Very approachable and patient. Takes time to clarify doubts. Doesn't curve the class or drop a few worst hw grades (and there is a lot of hw), so hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm taking this classs now. This is CS450, which I feel too smilar to CS357. Honestly, I would say Prof Silva in CS357 is a better teacher than Olson. Olson is fine, though. But he is somewhat boring and I don't feel he really masters at these numerical computing things.

Took this class with no prerequisites.  He was always very approachable and helpful.  Provided basic codes for homework/projects that definitely took work to modify, but it was doable.  Tried to cover a little too much theory in lectures so it didn't always make sense, but I did learn a lot!
Great Professor, great course, lots of things to learn, minimal examination pressure
Great professor! Very approachable and knowledgeable.  He is one of the nicest professors I've ever had.  Get him if you can.

Lectures are hit-or-miss. Sometimes they're really clear and organized, other times they're all over the place. Sometimes assumes we know things from pre-requisites that we don't (mainly linear algebra). Not too big of a problem considering the exams are multiple choice. Very nice guy though.
Teaches very well..But tends to go very fast over the slides..
He is a good teacher and you learn a lot.

Badly organized notes and lectures. The structure of math 257 is probably part of the problem, but I would not take another class with Luecke. Doesn't have good lecture material or practice questions, and lectures were not helpful for test prep (as of fall 2024).

He's super nice and is really good at answering questions. He skipped over a lot of slides in the lecture but what he did teach was super helpful. Do all the extra practice and you'll be set for exams.

I attended one lecture; math257 is the worst intro-engineering/math class at the university; do the prarielearn homework and extra practice and teach yourself everything. He seemed nice at the lecture I attended. Take over Jer-Chin Chuang

Great class, very easy workload. Exams are open note, the only group project is a debate, not a lot of homework. Lucero's lectures were engaging to listen to. The only downside no computers are allowed in class, only hand notes.

Definitely an interesting class, but the assignments are practically nothing to worry about. She held debates and they were super fun. Her lectures were interesting (but she did not allow any technology in her class). I wasn't the biggest fan of the class but she's the reason why I started thinking about sustainability differently.

Overall fine experience. She cares a lot about what she's teaching, and helped me out with someone slacking on a group project. The no laptop policy is a little odd, and taking notes on paper is a lot slower for me.

Dr. Lucero is a phenomenal lecturer. She creates an environment that encourages students to pay attention to lectures, engage with content and enjoy and take away lessons from lecture slides. Grading is primarily determined by attendance, two exams, and debate. Dr. Lucero is the closest thing UIUC has to Indiana Jones. participation is encouraged
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this professor! She was super nice and you could tell she cared about the students. I really liked her approach to teaching. Our attendance was taken through writing haikus about the topic of each class. You have to work with a group of about 4 people, and be in 1 debate during the semester. Exams weren't bad if you look at the readings.

She's very passionate about the material she's teaching. She talks about her research experience which is cool! You won't pass if you don't attend class, as this is the biggest points grade. She can be a bit scatter brained, but has good intentions overall and is always available to help when you need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Half the time she isn't there and when she is she calls people out for cellphone use in a 400 person lecture. She doesn't allow laptops which is really annoying and half the time the iclicker didn't work so even if u do show up you probably won't get points. Minimal work though, easy A.

Lucero was probably the worst professor I've had at University of Illinois. The class was an 8am and she wouldn't allow laptops. She called out students in front of our 500 person class to embarrass them. On top of her behavior, her voice is something no one should have to endure for 2 hours a week. Only take this class if you have to.

Hardly ever did I understand what she was talking about during lecture, but exams may include a few things that she discussed in class. So ask the TAs for clarification, who are kind enough to help. Also, the extra credits may help.
Professor Lucero is so much fun and she's very intelligent and passionate about anthropology. She is very engaging and her lectures are pretty interesting. Would recommend taking a course with her!
Lucero's speech is unorganized and she always seems to just look at the computer and read the slides verbatim. Gives off an annoyingly pretentious vibe.

Ms. Lucero is a heavy self-promoter. She has no problem going on a tangent to tell her class how great she is at anthropology. Ms. Lucero is also frequently late to class strolling in 5 to 10 minutes late, relying on her teacher assistants to fill the time waiting for her to get here, if she shows up at all.

Her lectures are long and feel disorganized. TA's give their own presentations on some days which liven things up a bit. The grading process is very straightforward. Two midterms and a final. Nothing else. If you fill out the study guide for each exam and maybe attend a few extra credit events you can easily get an A.
No one ever has any idea what she's talking about. Sit in the front since she never turns on her microphone.

Overall, she is knowledgeable in the field. Her lectures are just reading off the powerpoints verbatim. But the material is easy to learn and memorize, which is why I got an A. However, she has guest lectures often, so she only comes to lecture only 1 day a week. Even though I got an A, I would not another class with her.
Dr. Lucero is very engaging and intelligent. However, if you do not find interest in her topic/teachings it might be boring for you. Overall pretty easy (besides exams!). Great class.

She's very passionate and opinionated which may be troubling for less interested or more conservative students (as previously mentioned). However, Lucero is very knowledgable, available to students, fair, and generous with extra credit.  Exams can be challenging but there is no reason not to get an A if you attend class and participate in projects.

I love Dr. Lucero! She makes this class so interesting, has a pretty good sense of humor, and if you stay on her good side and attend class she is one of the most helpful professors you will meet. She is very opinionated and will let you know her likes and dislikes. It can be difficult but attend class and study for the exams and you will do fine.

I loved her jokes, but a politically conservative student would likely take offense to a lot of things she says. The first exam was of average difficulty. Make sure you participate in the group presentation because it is student- graded. The final exam was optional!
She's kind of ditzy and you can tell teaching is not her #1 priority.  She's very vague in her lectures and I honestly didn't really learn much in her class, but it was an easy A. She's cute though.

She does not care about her students and teaching is not one of her interests. She is unhelpful even if you go to her office hours. She will not explain her grading of tests. Her grading procedures are completely arbitrary. She takes 5 points off (of 100) off essay tests for "vagueness" without giving feedback as to what a correct answer would be.

she does not help you. she does not explain test grades or what she wants of the class and then walks out instead of the room after everyone has done miserable on a test saying that all grades are final and that she will not speak with anyone regarding their grades or their test. i am an A student but may be getting as low as a C in this class.
Love her!

Pretty interesting class but essay tests were somewhat hard. You get the questions a week before the exam itself but questions are very vague. And she's not really helpful in answering questions. She's also very passionate and rash in her opinions. I still enjoyed the class. Got an A thanks to numerous extra credit opportunities. Final is optional.
She's pretty funny, and she's awesome.
Steer clear of this professor. She shows little empathy for students and is an unnecessarily harsh grader, particularly on tests and homework. Worst professor I've had at UIUC so far.
avoid this professor if possible
Tough but fair grader, compassionate towards students and always willing to go more in depth outside of class/in office hours.
Tough grader. Avoid if you can.

Do anything you can to make sure you get a different professor for this course, she is inconsiderent, a tough grader, and a 'hands-off' teacher. A lot of her content is copy and pasted from the years prior and she won't give you any feedback on your homework unless you come to office hours, and even then she'll still be difficult.

Professor lyons is the best professor I have ever had in my life. She cares about your success and will not let you fail should you truly put in the effort. If you work hard, you will learn. She is an amazing mentor. If every professor at this university was like her, the UIUC would be the top school in the nation.

As an alumni from the College of ACES, I understand the desire and passion Professor Lyons puts into her work of teaching. Her curriculum is not easy and she will demand a lot out of you. I recommend that you follow her guidance as she is preparing you for the future. Her purpose is to make this world a better place.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This lady is completely convinced she is your boss. You will hear her frequently reference the boss employee relationship in class when ordering you around. "You wouldn't do X to your employer would you?" I literally PAID for her to teach me, not order me around. Expect incessant emails about minutiae, unreasonable grades, and irritating behavior.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Because of the rating on RMP I was so scared to take her class, however, Prof Lyon is literally one of the best professors in the college of ACES. She values you understanding the materials taught in class over emphasizing letter grades. She is also very caring and tries to make lectures as enjoyable, getting an A in her classes is very possible.

I took both ACE 474 and 476 with prof. Lyons. She is a tough but fair grader. Her class is not easy but you can learn a lot. She is the professor that cares the most about her students compared to other professors I had. She does her best to help students willing to work and learn. If you want to take easy A classes, just avoid her classes.

I would not like to be a horrible person. But I have to say Lyons is the most mean professor I had ever seen. In her depiction, I am acting like the worst student ever in the world which both me and all my classmates know I am not. I am enough for this kind of unfair treatment. Thank you so much for letting me know how mean a professor can be.
One of the most unreasonable professors I've encountered at U of I. She enjoys making tasks difficult for students, avoid taking her classes at all costs

Professor Lyons is an extremely difficult teacher.  ACE 476 is a very hard class with the toughest grading procedures I have ever dealt with.  The lectures are boring and there is too much emphasis on the final project.  I do not advise to take any courses with her.
not nice at all.
Hardest course taken at ACE

Super boring lectures; midterm review was 4 pages for 18 multiple choice, 3 short answer, 1 essay; Did not enjoy the class at all; great if you are searching for a job internship though (very willing to help)

Professor Lyons is one of the most thoughtful professors on this campus.  She goes out of her way to try and set up students with employers.  The class is a whole lot of work, but you learn a great deal.  I would recommend her class to anyone with an interest in finance or even more specifically, financial planning.

Taking this lab class this past semester has inspired me that MCB is the path for me. Dr. Levesque has been such a wonderful teacher, she really cares if you understand the material and is a joy to be around in class. She's a very honest grader though, but you can tell it's because she cares, so just make sure you have your details right.
