She lectures about random things that have nothing to do with the stories we read, and then quizzes us on things that are neither in the stories, nor in her lectures. She's also a horrible procrastinator.

Buy the lecture notes and the book and don't bother going to class. Rini spends the whole time reading straight from her notes. The only thing that you might need to go to class for are for the pictures that are going to be on the tests. Honestly, you'll be fine as long as you read the book. The tests are very straight forward.
Memorize your workbook and do the readings. Just attend class to take pictures of the slides or get a friend to do it. Very attainable A and no +-.

Easy A.  Don't have to go to her lectures, just read the study guide and textbook.  If you decide to go to her lectures, then you don't have to read the textbook, just copy down the lecture notes because you won't be able to understand her.  It's really an easy class.                                                      by Namen, "the ramen", Mehta

Super nice person, but not a great lecturer. Really smart and obviously knows her stuff, but goodness she is so boring. You don't really need to go to class. Interesting material and an easy A, but not great for lectures.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!!! SO So boring....you will fall asleep. Not necessarily hard....but so boring.
The most boring class I've had this semester. Stay AWAY!!!!!!! Not necessarily hard, but you will fall asleep in every class.

Easy class.  REALLY boring lectures, but I never go and I do fine on the tests.  Also impossible to hear in lecture.  Tests are easy as long as you read.  Luckily, the reading is pretty interesting.  Not a bad choice.

The readings are really interesting but the lectures are super boring. Attendance at lectures isn't mandatory at all and usually on 25% of the kids show up. She's really boring and hard to hear in the back. I would however recommend going to discussion, that's where you actually learn. It's an easy A class.

I thought the material was interesting and even though she is not an outrageous lecturer, if you pay attention you can really learn a lot and she can actually be quite entertaining. I took two classes by her, both were easy A's because I enjoyed the material we covered.

A very easy non-western course where skipping lecture is not a problem. If you attend discussion section weekly and review the material in the study guide you're provided, this is an easy A. The paper was a breeze. As long as your wrote memorization skills are pretty strong, you'll have no trouble with this course.

Average lecturer, but she knows her stuff. I did my honors paper with her and she was extremely helpful. The class was interesting but relatively easy. She's always willing to help a student, though, and tries to make the lectures as interesting and clear as possible.
No Comments

I skipped this class all the time--I maybe attended 5 times, including the lecture where we had to turn in our essays.  She emphasizes going to class for all the pictures (which are used on the exam), but if you know the material by studying the book, you'll be able to guess what the picture is portraying.  Easy A!
Awful.  Impossible to understand and horrible instructor.
No Comments

I didnt want to do this class, she uses lots of powerpoint, but it was boring and it was hard not to fall asleep.  She tried to make some jokes in class but was occasionally hard to understand.  Not a hard class so it will be a good non-west gened if you have any interest at all.

The class is not hard at all, it really depends on how you are able to differentiate the names... You need to know many terms, concepts, and names for the exams. The instructor clarifies the readings as well as the major storie, if you go to lecture and discussions then you will be doing great!

Asian Mythology... I'm sorry, I can't stand to hear this woman lecture. Her voice is like nails on a chalkboard. Lectures are boring. Material is kind of interesting... but I wouldn't suggest this class to anyone.
(rating for his 420) 420 is definitely MORE THAN 2 Credit (final project is ~ 35h) but his lecture is chill and easy to follow

Nice guy, but bro is the most boring lecturer I've ever had. He literally puts me to sleep every time. And the whole class doesn't listen to him and just talks over him and he doesn't care. He also does useless examples in class that don't teach a thing. Sometimes he lets us out early tho :). Overall he is nice but such a boring lecturer, dont take

Professor Moon is the GOAT. His lectures are amazing; even though he can sometimes drone on, he explains topics with ease and goes out of his way to answer students' questions fully. Very approachable, nice guy, too. He made the structure/content of the exams very clear and definitely wanted us to succeed. He helped make this a very fun class.

AWESOME PROF best prof for 220 pick him over bhowmik, ivan, whoever. Literally leaks exam stuff, for the final review his github had EVERYTHING on how to preorder, postorder, print tree, tree height, it was like the bible.
Very organized and good at explaining concepts. Highly recommend. This man is the GOAT.
I love ma G Moon.
Very good prof, he is a little boring but if you pay enough attention, he's very good at explaining things - I preferred him to Chen
Professor Moon is good at his job and teaching the given material, but he's boring and doesn't make class engaging. Lectures are useful but not really necessary to pass the class.

Didn't know at first if I should have taken Prof Moon for ECE 220, but so glad I did. A really honest, nice and intelligent guy who is a great lecturer. I think one of his best qualities is that if he is asked a question that he doesn't exactly know the answer to, he will go out of his way to figure it out for his students. Highly recommend!

Super fun lectures, as long as you pay attention in lecture tests are super easy and you don't need to read the textbook. Projects are a bit vague on expectation but just put in effort and you're good. Final project is fun too! He's always making jokes and finding ways to make the lectures interactive.

J.W. is VERY entertaining, and his lectures are worth attending. Most of the grade for the class comes from a few multiple choice tests and a final group project where you design the concept for your own musical. Overall, if you pay attention, study for the tests, and put a little effort in you will do great. Definitely worth taking for two gen eds

Like this course very much. One downside is that JW don't provide the powerpoint, so its hard to catch up with him for international students or people who lack theater knowledge, and i have both problems. But I still think worth it, and got an A+ easily. I went to New York Broadway to see 'harry potter' and Chicago to see 'mamma mia!" in holidays.

J.W. truly cares about his students and their success and perspectives. He clearly loves what he teaches, and that passion and enthusiasm are infectious. He also does such a good job of providing a complete historical context to all the musicals covered in lecture. I

I can safely say this class will end up being one of the greatest courses I will have taken here. Each lecture with Mr. Morrissette often feels more like a comedy sketch than a classroom setting. I didn't know many musicals outside of incredibly popular ones prior but ended up learning so much about the social history of them and Broadway itself.

One of the most amazing professors I've ever had-- hilarious and passionate about what he does. Makes lecture so fun and worth going to (esp bc they are not mandatory) and every lecture with him is always a joy. Tests are pretty easy, one final group project at the end. Highly rec if you are a theater nerd!

Great professor, highly recommend. The exams require reading the book in detail but otherwise no complaints. The lectures are optional but he makes them worth going to, and he's very nice to the students.
His lectures were really engaging and somewhat humorous. Attendance isn't mandatory but highly suggested as nearly everything either said or presented in a power-point would be used on exams.

Although I'm not much of a theater guy, this class was pretty interesting and I enjoyed it. The class itself is not too difficult as it entails discussion/response forums, 2 critical essays, 1 performance treatment essay, and the final project. The other assignments aren't hard, but the project is since you have to create a musical from scratch.

Fantastic professor! JW was engaging and really cared about his students and the material he was teaching. He adjusted the meeting locations at the end f the semester to make sure everyone was able to isolate before going back to their families over break. A hilarious person and an incredible teacher.
Never met the guy but I did nothing and got an A so if that's what you want take this course

I'm taking Theatre 101 which is being taught by JW and honestly it's one of the most fun classes I've had so far. Lectures are mandatory in the sense that you get clicker points for them and he often includes some questions from lectures on his exams . The material is easy and he makes the class super fun and interesting, definitely worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: INTERACTS WITH STUDENTS

This was one of my favorite classes I've taken at UIUC so far. JW is engaging, hilarious, and passionate about his lectures, and the information is all very interesting and delivered in an enjoyable format, with videos and guest lectures to enhance the class. If you pay attention and take notes, the class is very easy to do well in, and it's fun!

One of the most amazing and inspirational professors I've ever had. Easiest gen ed i know. As long as you go to lecture and have at least some passion for the fine arts, you are guaranteed an A for this course.

J.W. Morrissette is God's gift to theatre. THEA170A is just for theatre majors, but if you did theatre in high school and are looking for a gen-ed that you will enjoy, take THEA101 or THEA110 simply to listen to J.W.'s lectures. He's great!

J.W. is an amazing person. Hilarious, inspires, makes you want to listen- even if you're not that into Theatre. Not writing intensive. 4 Exams (he didn't give us a final! Love him!!!) and only 2 theatre treatments (see a play and review it, plays sucked but easy to bs) also I got to choke a TA in class. Super fun class! Def. recommend!

Really great class even for those not super interested in theatre. There are 4-5 papers followed by a fairly easy group project. The papers are easy and graded the same. tons of extra credit. The tests get fairly specific about the shows, creators, dates, # of performances ect. I recommend quizlet. Definitely take this class if you can

Easy online class. Make sure to plan everything out because they don't take late work. Buy your performance tickets ahead of time to avoid not being able to attend a show. Quizzes are online & everything should be on quizlet. No final, just two projects, which are fairly easy so long as you don't procrastinate. Lots of extra credit, just do it all.
He is not afraid to say things but he is also considerate of how people may feel. Doesn't feel like a lecture, feels like a comedy show.
JW is professional and enthusiastic.

Amazing class! He made every lecture so fun and plus it gets you out of 2 GEN ED requirements. He always kept the class entertained and really taught us so much about theater. This is a MUST TAKE class!

Took the class because I like Broadway musicals and don't regret it one bit. HILARIOUS guy, really fun and interesting lectures, especially if you're interested in the subject matter. Even if you aren't, I highly recommend this class because it's a super easy A. Also there's a textbook but I barely read it and got by just fine.
Fantastic Professor!!! Loves teaching and lectures are amazing!!!
JW for president
Took the class online. Super easy. I ended with a 105%

Loved J.W.! I took the class because I heard it was easy, and it is! JW is hilarious and makes lectures way more engaging than I thought it would be. You have to write one paper and there are 5 exams, but everything is relatively easy. I'm glad I decided to take this gen ed.
Most inspirational professor I have ever had.
Awesome professor!
I LOVE this man. He is the BEST professor on this campus. If you need a humanities class to take, TAKE THIS ONE! JW is the BOMB. And he's funny.

I LOVE this class. He's seriously the best. We listened to Pop Lock & Drop It during a Shakespeare lecture, and he cracks jokes all the time. Class is actually interesting. Take this class!! You'll love it and I have a 110% if that tells you how easy it is.

I took this class online, and it was very easy, every chapter has an online quiz, however, you get unlimited time to do it, and you can find all of the answer in the readings or the power point slides he gave you. There are also some online discussion, which was very easy. You are require to attend 3 theatre plays, and write a easy 2~3 page paper
Great professor. Knows his stuff, easy to work with and available to students.
What a great class! Best prof on campus!
he is one the best most enetertaining professors at U of I. even though i had no interest in Theatre, he made really fun. take this class!

He clearly loves theater and is VERY entertaining. I looked forward to lecture for the most part. The textbook was needed for tests but the lecture notes were most important. He gave study guides as well. Overall Easy A.
He's the best! Take this class!
this class was such a good idea to take first semester, freshman year. such an easy class, the profssor played po-lock-and drop in the middle of shakespeare, need I say more?
He is the most entertaining professor at U of I that I've ever had. Lectures were hilarious and exams were a walk in the park.

He is the best teacher I have encountered at U of I so far. Thanks to him I survived my first semester at the U of I, I don't know where I would have been w/o his quirky comments and THEA101. He loves what he does and it shows; J.W. is an awesome/the best teacher ever hands down.
Best teacher on campus. I loved going to class everyday. Always got something new out of the class. Helped me whenever I needed it. Big supporter throughout the whole year.

very easy and prof was patient even when the "jocks" were being loud during lecture. cool guy, funny and interesting, and you learn a little thea too. 3 plays at krannert mandatory. take this class with friends. iclicker required.
This man makes life so much fun.  He is so hilarious.  He makes class a party everyday.  He's especially patient with all the students taking this class for a gen ed.
I had him for intro to theatre. He was an awesome professor and made theatre enjoyable.This is by far my favorite class at u of i

He is super funny and nice! Lecture is very interesting. Get someone to take your iclicker if you can't make it to class. No final or midterm. You have to go to three plays and write one page for each but they are graded very easily! Take it for an easy gen-ed.

I had Professor Stodolska for RST 230. The video lectures average 45 minutes - 1 hour. There's a lot of awesome information that you learn about barriers in recreation and health/psychological conditions in the second half which are excellent to know! The lectures are a bit tedious, but as long as you do the work you will enjoy the class!

The class was Diversity in Recreation, Sports, and Tourism.. 90% of the course content (and tested on) was about various health conditions and items that didn't necessarily apply to recreation. It felt like recreation was an after thought in this course. Prof. Stodolska herself wasn't bad, just sometimes difficult to understand. Exams weren't good.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The  grading scale of the class is needlessly difficult—it weighs the exams similarly to some of my engineering courses—and the late policy is similarly punishing. On top of that, a stupid amount of content is covered per exam. Two topics per week every week and all of them could be on the exam. Way too convoluted for a GenEd.

Class design itself is way too extensive for any 200 level class. There was 58 different topics on the last exam to give you an idea. Not to mention if you do not watch two hours of lectures weekly, you will not do well. Avoid this class if possible. If not, be ready for tough grading and a headache from lectures.

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR!

Professor Stodolska can be very rude during office hours making it very hard to communicate to her and get help. Doesn't help that the TAs don't help out much either. My assigned TA claimed to have forwarded an email of mine to the professor but lied to me and forwarded the email 7 DAYS AFTER HE TOLD ME HE ALREADY DID!
Does not adhere to consistency of learning by usi

RST 230 is completely online. You watch 2 ~1hr videos each week and take 2 quizzes all on your own time. TAs can be harsh graders, make sure to follow the rubric, and take the time to look over study guides to properly prepare for tests. Overall not a bad professor or class, just boring.
excellent, always glad to assist the students

Very interesting lecturer and I found myself really enjoying the content more than I thought I would. There are a few main assignments in this class in addition to exams, but she makes instructions very clear so as long as you read carefully it's very straightforward.

My favorite professor so far. She makes lectures as interesting as possible, even if the material might not be. There are two, four question quizzes a week which are very easy. There are 4 assignments, which are also easy if you follow the rubric. There are 3 exams , and she outlines everything that will be on them, as well as the difficulty.

Nothing much to say other than Monika is great. Very well versed in her field, and knows what she is talking about. Lectures are very informative. Her lectures do tend to get long, but the class is asynchronous so watch on your own time. She has TAs helping her grade and organize the class, but it's truly a very easy A.

Dr. Stodolska cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She makes the lectures engaging and helps inspire us to do our absolute best. There are four assignments, which are very easy if you follow directions. There are three tests, make sure to do the study guide, it helps a lot! I enjoyed the class and found it to be very interesting.

I really enjoyed this class and although she might be a little hard to understand at times, she really helped the students understand the material. There are three tests for this course with four assignments. The assignments are all pretty interesting and there is a lot of information for the tests but the study guides help a lot.

She is so beyond nice and caring. She makes each of her students feel special and appreciated. She does the most she can for a student with special circumstances and truly wants her students to get a great grade in her class. I want to take another course with her!

We got switched to online because of covid, but this class was still pretty easy to get a good grade. She makes lectures interesting with stories and interacting with the class, though some of the lectures are very dense with material. I recommend taking notes for pop quizzes. Also she has super in depth study guides for the exams which help a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of my favorite college professors thus far. The most genuine person and super interesting lectures. Definitely take this class.

Monika is definitely the best professor I have had at UIUC. Although her lectures aren't mandatory, you won't want to miss them since she has the coolest life stories. There are 3 exams that are very similar to the study guide/lecture slides. Pop quizzes every so often, but they are open note. Take this class!!

Monika was great, nice, and approachable... I loved her class! Lots of interesting information and you end up covering a lot of health info towards the end if you find that interesting. I took it for my US Minority gen ed. 4 assignments were fairly easy, pop quizzes are open note (so take notes), 2 midterms and the final was not cumulative.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Monika's lectures were interesting and the topics were common sense. This class had two midterms and a final. All three were SO EASY (I studied maybe an hour for each and got 100% on all 3). There's about 10 pop quizzes that are so easy (directly from notes) and 4 assignments that you get 100% on if you follow all directions. TAKE THIS CLASS!!
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Decent course, great professor. Wide variety of topics covered, most are common sense. 4 assignments, pop quizzes, a midterm, and a final are all that are in the grade book.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests? Not many--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Really nice teacher. You have to memorize a lot of stuffs but exams are pretty easy. There are also some interesting assignments experiencing minority groups. Very good choice for gen ed.
She is really really sweet!! This class is not hard at all and actually very interesting. She tells you exactly what will be on every exam.
talks w/ a polish accent.  can't understand her all the time.
No Comments

Dr. Sivapalan is a professor that provides lecture material that are borderline irrelevant to the course. I was one of the most active participants in this course, and even then, I often felt confused on what he expected from us. On quizzes, you must provide specific words in your prompt for credit. You won't be given any info about your grade.

I tend to not listen to these reviews and take the class with the professor anyway. But these reviews are very accurate. I was never confident going into a quiz or test, even when I studied. I would avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is much more difficult than it should be. Siva's lectures consist of about 60 slides of outdated and useless pictures and graphs. It is never clear about what you'll be tested on. He doesn't give feedback if you get something wrong on a quiz or test. I was most excited for this class at the start of the semester, and hated it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most frustrating professor in 4 years, a term project 25% of our grade wasn't discussed at all until he mentioned we should've started weeks ago. The content wasn't difficult to understand, but if you get something wrong you don't see why. Grading seemed pretty loose, not much structure.

The worst professor I've ever had at UIUC. Gives long, repetitive, boring lectures. It is rarely clear what the required readings and work are. All of his quizzes are pop quizzes and he never explains his grading. The class shouldn't be that hard but becomes so because you never want to attend class because of how boring it is.

GEOG370***Siva is a very knowledgeable professor and has taught me more in this class than I have learned from so many other classes. He uses real world examples and is very good at reviewing material multiple times so the entire class knows the main points and concepts of each topic. He's very experienced and it shows.

The most horrendous professor in all of Urbana-Champaign. This guy does not even know what is going on in the class, and literally copies the notes from the previous semesters. He gets lost multiple times in class, and surprises you on every test. He is a complete disappointment and teaches you nothing. I don't think he actually knows probability.

Absolutely the worst prof. you can ever have. for a class. First of all, he copy paste from the other professors notes. second of all, he doesn't even know when the review session for the exam is! He says something and he will give you the complete opposite on the exam. He ends lecture early when he didn't even finish the lecture.
The professor is very helpful if you reach out to him and pretty good at teaching. The course is hard but Professor Sivapalan makes the course more manageable.

He seems extremely smart but sometimes forgets he is teaching undergrads. Hard class! It was heavy on mathnumber crunching. He is helpful if you ask questions, but it is easy to get lost. Slight accent, talks fast, does not post grades online, no class schedule posted, limited notes posted. Uses chalkboard. Nice guy and considerate though.

Homework very difficult & used lots of differential equation proofs.  Class project took a lot of time but only worth 10% of grade. He did not give graded homework back until he was handing us our take-home final (took 20+ hrs to complete). That being said, I did much better in the class than I expected to and did learn a lot.

Very theoretical in his lectures, very little to do with actual realistic learning. Sometimes interesting. He said once in class (and yes, this is an engineering class) that "practical equals boring, to me." The final exam was worth 75% of our grade, was a hella-hard take-home final, and covered a bunch of stuff that we never went over in class.

This was a special topics seminar on watersheds as complex systems... Siva made it pretty interesting, but was often hard to follow due to speaking very fast and assuming people knew things they didn't.  Was very helpful outside of class, though, and coursework was minimal.  Expected students to be able to argue back and forth whith him.

Definitely take a class with prof Ali if you can! Super easy grader and responds to emails fairly quickly. There was a bit on an issue taking the final this semester with ProctorU and he got all of us refunds! Very kind person who wants you to grow :)

This class was sick. He literally just has what I assume to be a few bullet points and then talks for 1.5 hours. No prepared presentation, no white board, no nothing. He's really well articulated on what he talks about. I never did any of the readings and got nearly 100% on all the tests. Be engaged and raise your hand in class and you'll do well

Professor Ali is one of the most amazing professors that I've ever learned from. His classes are not structured around exams or homework; instead, they're about actually learning something and enjoying your time in his class. Be prepared to show up to all lectures, but he's such a knowledgeable and charismatic instructor that this won't be hard.

The class was very simple and easy. No homework other than the given readings but weren't really necessary. Tests were very easy if you went to the review session. Attendance is mandatory as the class is based on the discussions and questions presented in class.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with Ali, do it. He emphasizes that he wants you to leave the class having learned something and grown as a person, the grade is just a university requirement. Easy A class. This class is a lot of deep talks about the soul and reaching your highest self. Classes are always discussion based.

He does a great job in making what he teaches useful to everyone, you can tell he is engaged and passionate in whatever class he teaches. As long as you show up to class, pay attention and take notes you will be fine.

Dr. Ali is always ready to go into a deep conversation. He based his class question and answer style. Take notes and be focused. Highly recommended to take this class. Read and be prepared to ask questions.

literally sweetest prof ever. she will keep you so engaged in the lectures as she is so passionate about early american lit. show up to class and youll be fine. there is readings every week that can be long but once you learn how to skim it, its not bad. review the quotes on the slides she posts and you'll be fine for exams.

Lecturer is good, but be prepared for hundreds of pages of textbook readings, memorizing a million quotations and their authors, and bizarre grades on papers that have no rubric. Also if you miss more than 3 discussion they start lowering your whole grade by 5% for each absence. If you miss 6 you fail the class. Insanity.

Great lectures from Dr. M that are actually very engaging. Makes a lot of difficult concepts and readings both interesting and easy to understand. There are not a lot of assignments, and I would recommend re-reading the material after lecture to better understand the context she gives, but it is not difficult to succeed with Dr. M. 10/10 no regrets

Prof. Murison is easily the best lecturer I have ever taken a class with. It is so apparent how much she loves early American literature, and despite its occasional mundanity she managed to make every class engaging. Yes, there's a lot of reading, but if you figure out how to skim + focus on the passages she highlights in lecture it is an easy A.

Professor Murison is great. Her passion really pours into the lectures and makes class engaging. She makes sure the exams are easy! She WANTS you to do well and also walk away from 255 with a piece of literature that will stick.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She really only lectures, the TAs take care of discussion. But she makes lectures very interesting to listen to. Only bad thing was that electronics could not be used (notes by hand, unless DRES required otherwise). She does make slides readily available. Overall great and funny lecturer.

Professor Murison is so much fun in lecture and really spreads her passion for the readings we studied. Even online class is made enjoyable, but it's important to participate. Grades depend on participation, reading responses, and quizzes (every two weeks). Kind of a lot of reading but not boring in the least. Awesome TAs. Make some memes.

She's honestly the best teacher ever. She focuses more on her students learning and  being able to better themselves rather than the grades. She offers the chance to do rewrites. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS. Talk with her about the books and the paper prompts, etc. and ask for writing tips. She's SUCH a sweetheart. I want to take another class of hers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She enthusiasm for the short story, accompanied by her expansive knowledge of literary history, made for an interesting and engaging class. While the course load was heavy and Professor Murison's expectations were high, the class was enjoyable and definitely fulfilling.

She's a clear and energetic lecturer, and clearly passionate about her subject. It's easy to get excited about literature when she talks about it. This is NOT a blowoff course, but if you go to lectures and do the readings you should be just fine. She's also incredibly kind and cares about her students - get to know her if you can!
Prof Murison is totally hot, like totally, amazingly hot.

Professor Murison is so passionate about literature and she makes lecture interesting.  Her class is not a blow off class, however.  You really have to try and read the material, because there are a lot of assignments.  She is a great instructor and person though!

She is an awesome lecturer - passionate, humorous, and clear about literature. No, her class is not some easy blowoff, but it is rewarding and fair. Exams were easy if you went to lecture and read the material! I highly recommend her. My favorite lecturer I've had to date.
She is awesome. She is passionate about English and it shows in her lectures. I would recommend her to friends who have to take 255.

This class is a lot of work, but if you put in the effort it pays off.  Essays were very doable, pop quizzes in discussion were annoying but manageable if you do the reading--which there is a lot of.  I tanked on the midterm but pulled off a B in the class by studying the key terms and quotes she went over in lecture.
Professor Murison is a WONDERFUL professor! She is so passionate about literature, and makes herself available to help students if you need it. I loved this class and recommend it!
Had her for an honors seminar. Struck a great balance between Prof. insight and class participation. It was participatory in such a way that class required careful attention and independent thinking.

Murison is one of the best professors I've had.  Her class is difficult, but the material covered and her discussions are so interesting that it motivates you to do well.  She is very helpful with papers...take her classes, they rock.
She is my favorite teacher and I look for classes that she teaches.
You have to read a LOT for this class, but she is very helpful and an overall good teacher.

These reviews are accurate. He rambles during lectures and won't post slides. He doesn't know how to use Canvas and only hands out grades in-person. He asks for student engagement in discussion but talks over them. He asked the class for the definition of antisemitism then told the class I wasn't allowed to answer—the only outspoken Jewish student.

Kevin Mumford is currently my professor in HIST276. The course is lecture heavy. Although the lectures are not attendance mandatory, he does not post the slides from lectures. He often skips slides during class. This is a good class if you want to learn about African American history, but it's a lot of cramming since it's an 8-week course.

His lectures are often unclear and are interrupted with his side-tangents and side-conversations with his select-few favorite students. He does NOT post lecture slides as he wants to "value" the students that show up to his already terrible lectures. He does not provide study material and does not guide students on how to succeed in his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mumford is by far the worst professor I had the displeasure of taking a class with. Would not respond to emails, and didn't grade anything until the very end of the semester. We tried to raise our concerns and he dismissed all of them. Changed syllabus 4 weeks before finals. Don't take a class with him.

Professor Mumford skips slides in the slideshow because he says that they are unimportant. He refuses to share the slides with students. He then tests us over the slides. When grading the midterm and book review, he provides no criteria for grading and no feedback, only a letter grade. The "required" textbook does not contain the class's material.

Vague about whats expected on papers. By the end of the year he had memorized maybe 4 names in a class of 20. Very rude and has a habit of contradicting himself. This class is required for history majors and it was very frustrating that he was the only one who taught the class this semester. Dont waste your time taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I'm a history major and I dreaded this class. Assignments are unclear and there are few graded activities. With a 15 person class, you would think he would learn our names, especially since a good chunk of our grade of participation, but he was still asking us our names the last week of class. I feel like I sat in class and learned nothing.
Probably the most unstructured class I have ever taken. Unclear lectures, doesn't have a rubric for any of his assignments, you need to pander to his ideas in order to do well. DO NOT take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She was great, super easy on grading and always gave extensions if you ever had any conflicts.
Great teacher. Understands mental health very clearly and is very lenient. Great professor for RHET.

Bess Myers is my favorite teacher that I have had at the University of Illinois so far. She is so nice and caring and stresses that she does not want the class to be stressful for you. Also, If you need an extension she will give it to you without questions. If you take RHET 105 I highly recommend you take it with her she is the best!

Such a good professor, she was very understanding with every assignment. Very flexible with due dates. She just wanted you to try in the class and if you put in your best effort, you will receive an A.

Prof Myers' section of Rhet 105 is amazingly easy. She is very accommodating, you can get extensions on anything and the grading is very lenient. Her lectures are not that interesting, and you can do just as well by not going to class and reading the posted slides. Easy A, stress-free, and she truly cares about the wellbeing of her students.

I took this class whilst working for the Army (National Guard). The stress involved made school very difficult Dr. Bess made it 10x easier. She has a no stress classroom and was very flexible with all of the assignments given. As long as you communicate any issues, she is willing to accommodate. Best professor I've ever had. 10/10 would take again.

A Murphy class is genuinely a stand-up comedy special. His lectures are engaging, funny, and easy to understand. My only regret as a graduating senior was not taking more of his classes. He is fast to respond and will always review your essay outlines before you turn them in with great feedback. I truly cannot say enough great things about him!

Murphy is my favorite professor! He is interesting and genuinely loves what he teaches. He wants you to succeed and is super available outside of class. It's easy to prepare for his exams, and since they are short essay questions, he will review your answers and your paper outlines and tell you exactly what you need to say/do to get it right.

Prof Murphy is extremely knowledgeable about topics of persuasion. Participation isn't mandatory, but his lectures are based off of expanding on his slides, so if you don't attend you won't know the information for the exams. Graded by 2 essays, 6 quizzes, and 3 exams. Very passionate!

Attendance isn't mandatory but you will screw yourself over by not going to class (I would know). The exams are 30 questions multiple choice and you need to study for them. Other than that there are quizzes and essays, but I got As on those pretty easily.

your grade consists of 2 papers (2-3 pages), 3 exams, and 6 quizzes. the quizzes are so easy a baby could do it. the papers are so short and if you send him an outline ahead of time - you will get a good grade. the exams are difficult but he drops the lowest one. just go to the lecture and take notes and it will be fine.

I came into this class scared of Professor Murphy's reviews but I really enjoy his class. His class structure is very clear, and he is very kind. Attendance isn't mandatory but I truly recommend going, it helps a lot. There are six simple online quizzes, three tests (four, lowest grade dropped), and two writing assignments per semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Murphy is extremely passionate and informed about the presidents, historical facts, and how presidential rhetoric has changed, which made this class interesting. The lectures could be pretty boring and difficult to know what information is important. You will learn a lot about the presidencies and the important speeches presidents make.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He really is a nice guy. Cares for his students / is passionate about what he teaches. But the lectures are hard to follow, and you really have to be familiar with terms to pass the class. 3/4 very difficult tests count for your grade, the rest is 6 quizzes and 2 papers. I got an A average on everything except the tests and barely passed.

Use the lectures for all criteria for any paper or assignment. You'll be fine if you do that. Dr. Murphy uses his lectures for information for his class not google or any other online resource. DO NOT USE GOOGLE. Oh yeah, and don't use google.

I love this professor.. amazing human being and very easy to understand algorithms. Professor Murphy is 1000% better then Peter Kimmel. 
Leave Peter and go for Murphy I bet you will get A+

Professor Murphy was a really nice guy, but not the best lecturer/professor. You have weekly quizzes (easy and you only have to do 6/18) and 2 essays due (tough grading). 3 exams. That's it. So make sure you're doing the quizzes and you send your essay outlines to them beforehand because it's not clear what makes a successful paper.

Professor Murphy is a cool guy but not the best professor. He expects students to write papers using only his lecture videos. He also does not provide notes of any kind or guidelines for papers; youll just have to keep rewinding his lectures. Gave me Bs on my papers without even providing us a syllabus or a specific rubric to follow. Weird class
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 3 exams, 5 10-point "homework assignments" (easy), and 2 essays. That's it. You'll need to take very solid notes and understand each of the concepts he talks about in lecture to do well on the exams. Can be very tough. Not to mention, this is a HISTORY CLASS. It is technically about persuasion, but don't be mistaken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Murphy doesn't know how to gauge his students' knowledge of the course. Beyond the exams, you have maybe five assignments the whole semester, so your grade is weighted pretty heavily by each of them. He refuses to make any sort of lecture notes, so if you miss a day of class you have no way of knowing what you missed. Overall bad prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: THIS WAS THE WORST COMMUNICATIONS (HISTORY) CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKEN IN ANY YEAR OF SCHOOLING EVER!! His lectures do not help you at all , he prints all of his lectures out and puts them on a somewhat hard to read overhead projector and the stuff he does put up is only a term, he verbally explains the definitions so good luck getting carpal tunnel!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had a 4.0 until his class. I'm a really hardworking student, but he is absolutely ridiculous. His tests focus on really difficult concepts and the lectures are incredibly boring. I worked my butt off in this stupid class and it destroyed me. I would never recommend this class or professor to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: These lectures are just him going through presidential speeches and different rhetorical elements used in the speeches. Very boring lecture, but attendance is taken for a grade. Tests are only 30 questions so it's very easy to do poorly especially because they are very challenging. Your grade is based on attendance, 3 exams, and 2 papers.

CMN 321 by Murphy is the worst communication class Ive taken. This class is very pointless (you dont actually learn about persuasion skills) and by the end of the class you dont learn anything valuable from it.

3 tests (25 questions each), two papers. Thats it.  Rather boring lectures.  I would not classify this as a communication class.  As others have stated, there is more emphasis on the history.  Very misleading class title.  Ten points off for each class missed/late 10 min.  I would personally not recommend to a friend.

Don't take unless you're interested in taking a history course. Not sure I learned one thing in this class. Grades so tough on papers and tests suck. Worth 100 points but only 25 questions? Setting you up to fail. Don't take this course.

Only 2 papers and 3 tests. Very tough grader on the papers and the tests are 100 points and only 25 questions meaning if you get a few wrong your grade drops drastically. Lectures are long and very boring.  He mispronounces words and his voice is incredibly annoying. Definitely would not recommend this class.

Wish I could take this class again. Murphy is awesome and there's no homework besides two papers (two pages each). Don't need to do the readings and if you take good notes during lecture, tests (there are three) are a breeze. Honestly just a great class and very interesting - take it

This class is made for history majors, yet is labeled a strategies of persuasion course. This class should be called The History of Presidential Speeches. Overall, the course is very misleading and there are barely any point opportunities. You need to go to class yet do not receive credit for going.. He essentially does not care about students. GL

I would recommend that you don't take this course. The tests are difficult and only 25 questions, meaning if you miss only a few your chance of getting an A is out the window. There are 3 tests and each test covers roughly 5 weeks worth of notes of which he somehow narrows down to 25 questions. No study guide, and he grades the essays extremelyhard
He can be funny. HOWEVER, he is a tough grader on papers and attendance is ABSOLUTELY MANDATORY. Good. Luck.. Chuck.

Easily my favorite class I've taken and easily the best lecturer I've had at UIUC. The lectures are engaging, fun, and he makes things very clear. 3 tests and 2 papers are the only grades in the class, but if you go to class, you won't have an issue with them. I would take this class again if I could.
Great class and professor. Don't have to do the readings; tests are verbatim from lecture. Really funny and nice guy. Would take this class again

It was supposed to be a class about persuasion theories, but it could have doubled as a US president  history class. If you don't like history, absolutely do not take. He uses presidential speeches to explain every single concept. And he goes on and on about the history part instead of the communication concepts. Tough to figure out what to study.
Best professor I have come across. Knows how to explain the information in a manner that each student can understand. Great guy, amazing teacher!

Dr. Murphy is a phenomenal professor. The course seems easy because he explains everything with complete clarity and passion. It's clear that he loves what he studies and he wants to share that with students. He's entertaining and engaging and has such a wealth of knowledge on public rhetoric. There is no better professor in communication at UIUC.
Murphy is an old school guy, teaches with an overhead instead of a powerpoint.  His exams come from everything he says in class, nearly word for word.  Very easy class.

I liked the class. The TA Katie Irwin is also awesome. Make attendance a priority and take detailed notes. Your hand might hurt from writing so much by the end of it but in the end you learn a lot from a really smart guy who is internationally known for his rhetoric research yet he still is pretty humble and nice to us :) also he tells good jokes
Energetic, easy to follow. He tests on his lectures in class, so just take good notes. Tests are not hard and he is interesting to listen to, does great Bill Clinton impressions. Smart guy

his classes are very entertaining. He is a very fun teacher to be with. If you are a fast note taker, it is a very easy class because he gives out tests and essays based on what he says in class. I am an international student so i had to record his lectures and listen to them to take notes but i enjoyed this class very well

Murphy has lectures that are well organized and easy to follow. He himself is just an entertaining guy (although yes, his jokes are bad). If you go class, and attendance is mandatory, so I would, it is a very easy class not only to get a good grade in but to learn something as well. Very much enjoyed, would like to take another class with him.
Attention grabbing

He is a good teacher, and incredibly knowledgeable! You have to go to class since he takes attendance. His exams are fair but you need to study. He grades papers hard so definitely go in and see him before you write it
Myong is very passionate about research and it shows in the class. If you understand the papers inside and out, you'll be fine on the tests.
Myong's class was very interesting and a great intro to BIOE classes.

If you have experience reading scientific papers, you're fine. Otherwise, this class is very difficult and she's very unclear in her explanations and it's hard to remain attentive during class. I will never take another class with her. Smart lady though. Nice too.
Unhelpful, Uninterested professor. Can't explain topics at all. Difficult exams. No office hours. The classes topics and articles were very interesting but the professor lacked all teaching ability.

Well-taught class with lots of great features: weekly journal discussions, almost no homework, and a fun group project. Prof Myong really encourages students to put serious work into the projects, and students get a lot out of it. Super approachable, friendly person.
Took the CHP course.  She was somewhat disorganized and lost (or just never returned) some of my papers.  Though very accessible for questions, she was always rather vague.

I thought that she was an excellent professor. I had her for a CHP course, which was smaller so I think that we had more time with her than most other classes would have, but I thought that she was great about making herself available to us and explaining things if we needed help. We read a lot of stuff and I just really loved the class.l

Her portfolio grading system was AWESOME! Some of the in class readings were completely boring, but she was really helpful in explaining everything. Our one-on-one meetings really helped in rewriting the essays. The portfolio grading was really easy because you got to rewrite your 3 best essays for your final grade -AWESOME-

I agree with the paper thing. Her topics were ambiguous so even the best attempt wasn't good enough. Her lectures didn't contain much information because she just wanted us to read stuff in class. She focuses a lot on vocabulary and how we should know it but uses weird vague examples on the exams, which only take like 15 minutes.
She assigned several essays then made us rewrite them because HER directions were unclear. Her lectures were fluff, but exams and quizzes were quite difficult - especially for a survey course.
Awesome TA, she really knew her stuff. The class was pretty easy and included a semester long group project that was fairly simple.
Awesome lecturer, really down to earth, easy class and very lenient.

The class is the best way to get the literature and arts requirement out of the way without taking some snooze of class. There is a decent amount of reading, but the topics are modern and relevant. Every week you post online about the reading. The midterm is in class but the final was take home. There's a group video project at the end.

His tests are HARD and the final is HARD. I got an A in the class because he doesn't give +/- and he curves his class by a little (880/1000 is an A). I expected this class to be an easy A but if I were to take it again I would NEVER because it stressed me to much not going if I was going to get an A or not. take Dunne NOT him.
Dr. Myers is extremely helpful and very funny. You get a lot out of his class vs the other guy's class. If you just study hard for his tests, you can definitely get an A
Great teacher, and he's funny and sarcastic. Iclicker points are super easy to get. i would take him vs Dunne.

the other professor who teaches this course guest lectured for my class twice... myers is definitely more interesting and unless you are 5 yrs old or want to learn astr magic school bus style i would recommend myers over dunne any day. the textbook is unnecessary and everything is easy.class is interesting and you will learn something. great gen-ed
Myers is awesome!! He is very clear and helpful and cares about his students. I LOVE his accent. He is definitely super super HOT.

DO NOT take him... He screwed us over with the final exam and he managed to veil his evilness by his candy and hot brit accent. Then hath the moment of the final arrived. If you get a chance take Kaler instead..
Great guy, class may not be the biggest blow-off but it is relatively easy if you come to class. If you like astronomy, you should definitely take this class.
Final exam was kind of horrible, but he is hilarious, and probably the sexiest goddamn professor at U of I.
No Comments
ASTR 100 is not a blowoff like I thought, but if you get the lectures on-line and read from time to time, you will be fine.

I LOVEEEE Sergio! Seriously, he is the best of the best. He made learning Spanish so much fun, and I learned so much, especially how to actually conversate with a native speaker. He boosted my speaking confidence so much, I couldn't recommend him enough. If you get him, consider yourself lucky.

Being a spanish minor and being a transfer student, I was very very nervous going into my first actual spanish class here at UIUC. That all changed when I got to experience a class with Sergio. He is quite literally the funniest and most helpful TA around. He can separate work from play, and provides genuine feedback that will get you far. Thank u!
Sergio is my new favorite professor. It was the most fun I had learning Spanish ever!

There is a good amount of homework so be ready to tackle that, but otherwise Sergio made class so much fun and truly cares about his students. He is the only teacher I would want to teach me Spanish cause he makes it simple and really helps his students out. Couldn't have better things to say. Attendance is a little mandatory so go when you can.

Sergio is easy to talk to, so if you have questions or issues with info being learned just straight up ask him. He is very personable and treats us like both students and friends (perfect balance). I am not good at Spanish, have not taken it in 5 years, but I feel comfortable and supported in his class. Cannot recommend Sergio more!

Amazing!! I refuse to take any other professor after having Sergio! He makes class so fun and interesting! I am actually excited to learn when I get to his class!! I highly recommend him as a teacher!

This course had a lot of homework and was pretty hard. Sergio made sure to alleviate this the most he can. He made the activity more fun. He helps with homework whenever you ask. He is very clear about what he wants with writing assignments and will help a lot. If I was taking any Spanish class I would do whatever it takes to get him as a teacher.

Sergio is so funny and makes the class so entertaining. if you have the option to take his class 100% should do so. the class itself has material that could be difficult and can have a lot of homework, but Sergio is super helpful with the material and helps with any problems you ask about.

Spanish 130 was a requirement for me and I dreaded taking the class. However, with Sergio as my professor, the class ended up being fun and allowed me to learn a lot at low-stress levels. If you take this class, having Sergio as a professor will make life so much easier and you will breeze through the class while somehow learning the material.
Sergio was an amazing instructor and always available to help. He truly cares about student success and it makes the hard coursework / load much more bearable.

Haven't taken Spanish in a bit so this class was slightly challenging. There's a heavy courseload on the online side of this class but the website if forgiving and Sergio was willing to help clear up confusion within online homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I was so nervous about taking spanish but Sergio has made the class so much better. He is an amazing TA and I am so lucky to have him. He slayed !

A great TA, tries to expose you to Spanish as much as possible and encourages positive learning. Very funny and not afraid to joke around. Answers quickly outside of class and is willing to help instead of throwing you to the lions.

Super amazing and learned a lot. Forgiving. Would want him as a TA again.
Very helpful with all questions and very accessible outside of class. Always encouraging and engaging in class. Class was always so much fun. would very much recommend!
Such an amazing person in general! Has amazing energy in every class and is always encouraging for every student! Is very understanding and always has a positive mood!
Loved taking this class with him! Made it very easy and accommodating to students' needs.
Please never take any classes with this guy. Thick accent, doesn't turn on camera, always reads off slides (which are not even in presentation mode). No flexibility and understanding at all.
Just reads off slides and doesn't teach. Extremely thick accent.

This class is just awful. Don't know why this i-school at UofI even hired this teacher. He doesn't even turn the cameras on when lectures over Zoom. Neither does he explain things. Basically, he reads the slides out. He doesn't take any questions. He doesn't reply to emails properly and he doesn't hold any office hours at all.

I could talk about why this guy shouldn't be teaching forever. To start, his lectures are EXTREMELY boring and highly unengaging. He simply reads the presentation slides like we can't read them for ourselves. It often feels like he has NO IDEA what he's talking about judging from a few instances when students asked questions. FOR IS 407 BTW

I took this class for my major elective, and it was my greatest mistake. I should've dropped it when I had the chance. The professor didn't have clear grading rubrics and his assignment instructions were also unclear. The canvas page was also unfinished and the links to modules were set up inefficiently.

lectures were screen shared ppts not in presentation mode so it was impossible to see the details in graphs and images.  
professor refused to provide information on why points were deducted from assignments unless you were willing to call and speak to him on the phone outside of class.  
he had an abrupt way of responding to questions in class.
This professor does not have assignment grading standards and lack of passion. Bad attitude during emails and feel not respectful.
She is the sweetest professor I've ever had, she made brownies for us each class, but is very painful to watch use a computer.

She's a sweet woman, but she needs to retire. She cannot work technology, would not open assignments when she said she would, and takes off tenths of points for things that are not explicit in the assignments' directions. She's knowledgeable, and I'm sure she was an outstanding elementary educator, but she should not be teaching college students

Dr. Mac is very chill and sweet. She cares a lot about your wellbeing and success in the class, and is very accessible to meet if you need anything. She has amazing ideas for classroom tools & inspiration to help young students succeed in elementary school. Assignment descriptions are clear, and she always gives good feedback. OH PICKLES!

I have mixed feeling about Nancy. On the positive side, she's very knowledgeable about how to teach students to read and write. She gives good examples and stories. However, she is a tough grader and sometimes her comments are bogus and she removes points for the smallest things. Overall, I enjoyed her class but just put effort into your homework.

Dr. Mac is a sweet lady who has a lot of technological issues. She doesn't really know how to use Canvas and the grades there aren't accurate. She barely answers her email and often goes off-topic. She was extremely caring and talked with us when we came in upset and crying because of another professor. She taught us a lot about teaching in general

Hmm.. where do I even start. A combined 15 minutes out of the whole three hour class was actually helpful/ informative in any way. She rambles.. on and on.. about nothing.. the whole class. The class assignments and directions are just a mess, everyone is confused, and honestly this course feels like such a waste of time. Its honestly a joke.

She's not a tough grader. She gives helpful, thorough feedback on the case studies. She's sweet and sometimes struggles with technology, but very knowledgeable. It's clear she knows what she's teaching. Answers all questions if you stay after class to talk to her. The 2 textbooks didn't feel super helpful with the reading responses.

This class is a 1000% a mess. No order, no guidance, you're just expected to guess what she wants in assignments or takeaways from class. Dr. Mac is very unorganized and unclear but doesn't accept that. Class is super long and you leave with no clear concept of what just happened
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She goes off topic A LOT. Needs a personal assistant because she is a mess. She's super sweet just a terrible professor. You barely learn anything and her exams are on stuff she claims to have taught. No study guide is given. Instruction on papers are very unclear. Tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Todd is a very detailed lecturer and does not read off slides! He is engaging, funny, and caring, overall a really great teacher. The course material was not hard to understand, just make sure to attend Lab and do not skip. Dr, Todd is the best teacher in all of U of I and very handsome!

Dr. Todd is intelligent and approachable. Lecture slides are a bit text-heavy and he's VERY much into methodology, so don't take this class for the theoretical aspect. Also a 15-20pg final paper. Still, it's all doable and even fun if you ask for help; he's accessible and supportive. An example of how kind-hearted professors make everything easier!

Awesome professor! He tries his best to engage students in the material when it can become quite boring. Attendance is not mandatory but there are pop quizzes. If you attend enough classes you'll start to notice a pattern in when he gives them out and can work around attendance. Exams are very easy. Very interesting and easy class.
No Comments

Easy class. Teacher is totally hot! Loved going just to see him. :)...class is ok. Gets a bit boring at times. Group project is ok, final paper is 10 pages, which is pointless. Paper was the only thing I did not like. Overall not a horrible class.

Horrible class. Wish I had dropped it when I had the chance. Gives avg of 100 pgs of weekly reading and tests on it. Final project consisted of 14 pg group paper, 10 pg individual paper, a class presentation, all on top of a CUMULATIVE FINAL. Worked harder for this 3 hour class than the 7 hours of 300/400 classes I was taking. Just awful. Avoid.

She might be great in person But this class is TERRIBLE to take online. She does not respond to questions or emails. The assignments are unclear and the timeline are murky. No assistance given from professor aside from forcing you to buy a textbook you wont use.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class in person with Nancy and it was amazing! I highly recommend taking the course with her and not online because she really sets you up for success and is a great support for her students. There were 3-4 exams and papers but going to class, taking good notes, and ask any questions about your confusion and you will do great!

Nancy is a great lecturer on campus. She is extremely qualified and offers great insight into what we are covering in class. I recommend going to class as much as you can because the materials are 100% on the test. Additionally, the test objectives are very clearly stated everywhere and she posts the powerpoints on a continuous regular basis.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Homework is time-consuming. Class is proofs building off each other, and it is very easy to get lost. It was his first time teaching; he was approachable in office hours, but attending every lecture and making notes is super important. Lecture notes were available and not bad. Grading criteria were a little harsh. No A- or B+, so it hurts your GPA.
Graded one exam for a whole month

So uh I learned nothing from this class, failed every exam, never got 100% on the homework, and got a B. My score was above average.
Never responded to emails, did not grade exams for months, and it felt like pulling teeth getting help at office hours.

You should get the textbook for this class. Although it says on the syllabus that the textbook is optional there are a few questions in his homeworks/quizzes that refer to ideas in the textbook that are not in his lecture slides. Very lecture heavy and hard to pay attention sometimes

Professor Scott is very lecture heavy and will use the entire time during class to lecture. Make sure to pay attention because his slides are not easy to go through and understand on your own. There is an online textbook that is required and homework assignments/test questions can be based on the textbook rather than what is said during lectures

He talks a lot and it's very slow and monotone and hard to pay attention. His slides are just screenshots from a textbook and he takes months to grade assignments. We spend most of class talking about random anecdotes, but then we are examined on difficult calculations, so it's hard to score well on the test.

I never had a professor who takes so long to return your email. Takes several weeks to grade the very few assignments we have in this class even though he has a "grader". Exams are definitely challenging. Goes on tangents about the most irrelevant topics in class that doesn't have much emphasis on what he's trying to teach. Overall 2/10 prof

Not fair that great profs who teach hard classes like supply chain get blasted. Prof Scott was great! Really knows his stuff and really cares for students. Don't believe the person below about the pandemic. They don't sound like they didn't work hard and are salty about their grade. Prof. Scott is awesome!

I don't know what the bottom 2 reviewers are talking about. They probably didn't do well in the class or work hard. Just because there was a pandemic doesn't mean you shouldn't work hard. I personally loved Professor Scott! Yes, his class is tough but he is a great prof!

Most difficult and frustrating class. He doesn't respond to students' emails about assignments. His assignments and cases are way harder than what he teaches in class and expects us to figure it out. His grading is also very stingy. If your answer format is not specific enough even though it's right, it's still marked wrong. Very disappointed.

This man is the worst professor I have every had. In the middle of a pandemic, he assigns more work. We used to meet every Tuesday and Thursday for 90 minutes. Now, he assigns 2 hours worth of videos and powerpoints for us to do BEFORE our zoom class at our scheduled time. He expects us to be fine with this extra work and claims its nothing new.

didn't love his teaching style or the powerpoints and there aren't many other resources, and it is hard to find material for this class online. I would recommend attending as often as you can but the lectures are pretty dry and contain a good amount of extraneous information

All of his classes are basically supply chain management majors that are very passionate about the subject. I think to do well you really need to have a background of SCM before you join the class to see if it's really for you. I didn't like the class and left the major. Overall, he's nice, but he could come up with some better teaching techniques

Brief homework assignments every other week, several in-class assignments, and easy exams (1 midterm and a final) that will only be over what he covers during lecture. His presentation is a little dry, but he is a very nice guy and will help you if you need it.
Lectures are dry with mostly powerpoint reading. Mostly because he is new to the school. Nice guy though, just hope he can put more time into his teaching methods and grading speed.

Grade is mainly on weekly group projects (written papers) and the two exams so you have to do well on all of them for a good grade. Not easy, required a lot of work but not overly difficult since he is straightforward and fair. You'll have to work for a good grade

He takes forever to grade things, but probably b/c he didn't have any TAs. Tests are VERY straightforward, AKA if you study his lecture slides and the study guides, you'll probably ace the exams. Assigns group papers (5-9 pages, around 4 people per group) on readings, but thorough reading isn't necessary as long as you get the gist of each article.
Professor Nelson is a great professor and teaches the class well! He is very caring and is knowledgeable about Information Systems. I would take any class he teaches

Professor Nelson is one of the most compassionate professors in Gies. He is very knowledgeable in the field of IT Governance and is very down to earth and approachable whenever you need assistance throughout the semester. I would definitely take another class with professor if the opportunity arose.

He's a nice guy but an absolutely terrible professor. People tend to like him because his material is very easy, but most of the time learning in his class is non-existent. He gave us a "practice" for the midterm, and it was literally 1 powerpoint slide that has 5 bullet points in it. I'd take another class with him since he's an easy A+

He is very nice and understanding with a strong interest and knowledge in field of IT governance.
Always was respectful of our time and rewarded those who did come to class.
Provides a choice of assignments (i.e., only have to do a certain # of each assignment type).
Overall a great class taught by a great professor in which I learned a great deal!

He is the nicest guy at the UIUC. Take him and only him for this class if you want an A. Be responsible and do all the required work (which is very reasonable and not a lot) and you will do fine. Although it's a 3-hour class, he always let us out early.
The nicest professor ever!!!!!!
nice professor ever!

Fantastic professor, one of the most genuinely nice and helpful I have had thus far. Its a 3 hr class but he almost always lets you out early. There is also some very cool projects for the class (3d printing, IT certifications).
Really knows his stuff, and always cracks jokes in class. Tests aren't hard if you study the quiz questions. Great professor, and even though it was a 3 hr class, he never used up the whole period.
Matt is a great professor who knows a lot about his field. The class is very straightforward and as long as you follow his clear instructions, you'll get an A.
Great class. Loved my whole time there. Matt is a great person and has reasonable expectations from everyone.

I wouldn't say she's a tough professor but she just doesn't do her job well and I had a very poor experience in her class. No grades were in the grade book until the end of the semester, feedback was either nothing or just slandering your creative style and not necessarily the technical aspects. Not great for genuine critique.

doesn't do anything except nothingburger "conversations" with students. doesn't teach anything, doesn't try to work on actual designing, no organization, doesn't post grades EVER, doesn't give clear instructions, has no interest in doing anything besides working on her own personal stuff during class time

She is inconsistent, gives approval for project ideas only to tell you to change the entire idea the next class, this happens often. It's a waste of time. She also wastes our time by being late to every meeting, usually by almost 10 minutes. She gets away with teaching literally zero skills by saying that what actually matters is networking.
Disorganized class, no communication, the class focus is not about learning, and even if it does teach you something, it has no value. There is no gain from taking her courses in general.
Super easy to engage with in class not boring at all catered to student needs and gives good feedback
Half of the reviews are lies she's a free A class of you just do your stuff

She never communicated with her students. How do I take class with you while you never reply any email?? She gives no care about her students. The design of curriculum is not clear and hard to follow. I don't know how good her art is but she sucks as a professor.

I don't know why she never reply the Email. Even if I asked when can we talk about my grade and other course related questions inperson, she said she will reply my email later after class, but there is still nothing in my inbox. Also the course setting is awful, as a designer, she even don't tell us how to design, but tell us to training AI.

Extremely disorganized class timeline. Does not respond to emails. The assignments kept changing, requirements and expectations were not fully communicated, or she would contradict herself. Has frequently cancelled class only hour before, or wasted an hour of class time to take care of things that should be dealt with outside of class.

It's incredibly frustrating to be in a class where nothing is explained clearly, leaving students feeling lost and overwhelmed. To make matters worse, with only three days left until the semester ends, no grades have been posted. The combination of poor communication, disorganization, and a lack of transparency feels disrespectful students.
has no syllabus. I feel like all her classes use the same PowerPoint and barely organized class structure. She's nice tho

I disliked this teacher very much. He did not explain the material well at all and sped through the powerpoints. unreasonably tough in expectations and demeanor. He seems unhappy in his role as a teacher.

The class wasnt organized at all. He posted the review for the final exam on Friday, when many people were taking it on Monday. He groups the in person and online class together when they should not be. They are two separate classes and should not be according to one another. I would not recommend his online class to anyone.
He broadline ignores his online students and grades almost purely off tests. If you're a bad test taker, I would recommend looking elsewhere

reviews.comment: TA for Astronomy classes. He is okay just a little boring and forces group projects and discussion
