reviews.comment: Extremely disorganized. Currently doing a take home midterm (only midterm) due the last week of classes, when there's also an in person final. He assumes a lot of knowledge outside of class. He teaches mostly for himself and maybe for the top of the class. Taught some classes where questions were not allowed. And there weren't office hours. AVOID!

La Nave is a difficult professor because he's not good at teaching.

He has an accent, and he doesn't explain the material well, so you're better off relying on the organic chemist. His TAs also suck at teaching and the discussions are pretty useless. The one highlight of this course is that the tests are practically the same every year.
As someone who took around half of calc 2 in high school, I was amazed by how awful his lecture was. Ended up not showing up to lectures after two days. The tests are OK to easy though.

Gabriele La Nave isn't a great teacher, and you'll have to be disciplined, read the lecture notes before class, and come in with some understanding of what he's covering in class to get something out of the lectures. But the tests are easy if you review the practice tests. He's also really nice and knows ball.

Estrucan lecture was peak 🔥

He genuinely yelled at students in lecture. One time a guy was wearing sunglasses in class and he stopped class to tell him he was disrespectful and asked him if he wanted everyone to lecture in the dark just for him. He is a bad lecturer on top of his accent, and he put my grades in wrong and to this day he has not answered my emails to fix it.

He's a nice and chill guy overall but is terrible for any kind of teaching or explanation requires. I spend whole semester trying to figure out what's the connection between discussion worksheets and lectures. All tests were super easy tho.

La Nave is a really nice person, although sometimes that can be lost in his confusing explanations. The worksheets during discussion sections have no relation to the class at all, but La Nave could get his point across through his notes sometimes. Tests are basically the study guide, though, so it is a very easy class to do well in.

He seems like a fun guy and really enjoys teaching the material, however lectures always got confusing and off track. Discussions didn't add any additional learning benefit either. There were also random attendance checks so make sure to go to lecture. The midterms are very similar to practice exams, which was nice.

Terrible lecturer, the worksheets didn't really connect with the material, and the homework was annoying to deal with. His tests were really similar to the past ones, but I'm terrible at memorizing questions and not very good at teaching myself math so I never did very well on tests past the first midterm. Made me dislike math again.

La Nave is a below average lecturer but he is nice and answers questions well. I would highly recommend self-studying and past papers are a must (are always extremely similar to the actual exam). Discussions can be hard but TAs are lenient graders and willing to answer questions.

His lectures are really difficult to understand, as he confused me more than helping me. I just went through his notes before exams, and I was fine. DO THE PAST PAPERS, because 90-100% of the paper is from that.
Lectures are very unclear and confusing, tests are extremely easy. You need to learn how to self study.

Generally a nice person but dude can't teach. The extra credit for attendance is NOT worth it and you could understand the material much better through self studying. Luckily bro is too lazy to come up new exam questions each year so that every midterm and final is almost identical to past papers. You get an easy A at the cost of not learning much.

Left this course with less knowledge of calculus than I entered with. Discussions are incredibly disconnected from the content and strayed as far as Real Analysis...this is Calc 2. Doing well is not difficult as others have iterated, but actually learning and benefitting from the instruction is quite the task.

Lectures are useless he cannot teach. Spent the whole semester self-studying. Discussion sections are useless too, the worksheets are on unrelated topics. Takes forever to update grades on Canvas. The only good thing is that the midterms are very similar to the practice he sends.
He does not know how to lecture. I leave class understanding less about the topic than I knew going in. He should not be the only professor teaching 231E. Run away from this man please I beg you.

Professor La Nave clearly enjoys math, however as the semester went on his lectures became increasingly incoherent. Exams in this class are the SAME AS THE STUDY GUIDES. Getting a good grade in 231E is easy but actually understanding the content is difficult. Discussion worksheets and Paper homework are only graded at the end of the semester.
My grade dropped from an A to a B because apparently going to discussion is mandatory. We didnt do anything useful In discussion, only weird worksheets that had no correlation to our classwork
Class is easy if you study past midterms, other people just are not looking at them.

Lectures do absolutely nothing for anyone. Lecture notes are usually wrong and don't line up with the topics on the homework or worksheets. Multiple online homeworks are due every week along with written homework. His tests are pretty similar every year luckily. Do not take this course if you do not have to.
HES SO BAD AT TEACHING THIS GUY IS HORRENDOUS. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS UNLESS YOU ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO, AND PREPARE FOR THE WORSE.

If you take his class, my biggest advice is to study the past midterms. some questions are exactly the same as the practice, and a lot are similar. Don't expect a copy, but know it pretty well. Generally, he is really nice but the lectures are hard to follow and his organization skills could be better. Also, you have to buy a homework software btw.

Lectures can be hard to follow, especially if you haven't taken AP Calc BC since then it would be all new material for you. Exams are easy and almost the same as his practice exams. I would avoid taking engineering calculus and just take the regular MATH 231 since it's literally the same course but less convoluted. Get lots of chances on online hw.

He really is a good professor and a good person. He was very accommodating with his test conflict policies and his practice exams didn't veer far from the real tests. His lectures are slightly unorganized but nothing that you cannot follow by asking questions and paying a little extra attention. Love you G!
Honestly a really nice person. His practice midterms are basically the same as his actual ones but the lectures are definitely hard to understand sometimes.
Very caring for the students but bad organizational skills.

His lectures are horrible and don't teach you anything. He also makes you pay for a bad homework software and gives lots of additional written homework despite teaching nothing. Take the proficiency test if you can, don't waste your time.

The homework is tough and constant. The lectures are hard to understand and might as well be taught in the minecraft enchanting table language. If you ever, ever, have a chance to take a different professor, take it. My first year at this college is fantastic, except for anything to do with Math231. 0/10 would recommend pole vaulting over this.
Won't take again
Would not recommend

The beginning of Prof. La Nave's lectures are somewhat understandable, but as every minute passes, they become incomprehensible and confusing. Expect to walk out 5 minutes late with your head filled with more questions than answers. If you want to do well in the class, do all the practice exam problems and be your own teacher.
A little hard to understand and he does not teach the subject very well

This guy cannot lecture and his discussion worksheets are horrendous, they have nothing to do with the course material and are very difficult for no reason because they don't reflect what we learn in class or what we do on exams. Besides this, he does give extensions on homework and his exams are very easy, almost identical to practice exams.

I somehow know less calculus than I did before taking this class. He's a nice guy (I think) and his midterms were just like the practice ones, but his lectures were absolutely incomprehensible. Also could never answer questions correctly, even about the syllabus. He writes 'r' just like pi. Drove me crazy. If you value your sanity, AVOID.

Prof La Nave is the most disorganized professor I've had. He'll randomly postpone/prepone homeworks, exams take forever to be graded, and homework grading is running 13 weeks behind. It's a 16 week course, how are they so far behind?

It's also clear the discussion worksheets aren't made by him and have nothing to do with the course content

The professor is a nice person, and he extends deadlines. However, I do not benefit from his lectures at all. He makes the material more confusing. discussion worksheets were weird; it's like physics, not math. The written assignments are super confusing and not helpful at all. The only good thing is his exams are exactly like the practice ones.

Nice guy and is super understanding. He extends deadlines for many assignments and seems to genuinely care about his student's education. That being said however, man can't teach. AT ALL. And there are lots of assignments that take forever to be graded. Although the exams usually aren't as hard as the homework. so pretty much a 50/50 kind of guy.

reviews.comment: Professor La Nave may not be the most amazing lecturer, but he is a good person who seams to really care about his students. He always extends deadlines and the midterms are very close to the practice midterms. He has struck a good balance between making the class rigorous while making sure it isn't harder than it needs to be.

incredibly erratic teaching. he got so mad when people stopped coming to his lectures he made attendance mandatory halfway thru out of pettiness. does not post any good information on the class page horribly unorganized. just memrize the previous practice midterm answers and the tests will be fine. go on youtube to learn dont waste time on this guy

Terrible professor, he couldn't teach if his life depended on it. When people started watching online lectures instead, he got mad and required attendance instead of trying to fix his horrible teaching. Avoid him at all costs
Bro cannot lecture

His action of taking random attendance is rmeaningless. I think he should make his class fascinating rather than obliging people to attend the boring lecture.

Terrible lecturer, speaks terribly, makes so many mistakes writing notes, rambles a lot. Never responded to any of the emails I sent him. Probably the worst professor I've ever had. Lectures were unbearable to listen to, grades took forever to be updated, exams were MUCH harder than practice exams, overall 1/10 experience- and math is one of my favorite subjects.
this professor sucks so bad.......

reviews.comment: Literally refuses to take any sort of feedback. The class wouldn't have been half bad if he JUST LISTENED TO THE FEEDBACK. If you email him with feedback, he won't reply. Even if it's a question (with feedback attached), nothing. The exams are significantly harder than the practice ones, and MUCH more of a time crunch as well. Nice guy, but avoid!!

Lectures are painful and sad, text to speech has more life to it. The course site is terrible, resources are hard to find and nothing gets updated: e.g. the "mideterms sic practice questions" page has one bullet point "mideterm 1 practice questions" which doesn't link to anything. Lecture notes hard to read(and never posted, although promised), hard to follow his lecture. Casually go from one textbook to another, hard to get a reference. In one word, HARD! Don't even try.

He basically flies off the syllabus one month into the semester. Never posted anything on time. The lectures are incoherent and his explanation manage to make me know less about the subject. He changed class meeting time multiple times over the semester, creating much inconvenience. AVOID. I am surprised that the department let him teach at all.

Never in my entire life have I seen a professor make more mistakes in lectures while explain concepts I am already having difficulty understanding. His enthusiasm in recorded lectures makes me want to give up and I genuinely feel like I haven't learned anything in the course. If you have a chance to pick literally any other professor, do so.
AVOID at all cost. Incoherent lecture, never takes in advices from students and I admire all those who persevere through his class

So basically this class was a joke because of him. Due to his serious disability to teach, I ended up losing knowledge about Linear Algebra rather than learning it. If a student ever sees his name on their schedule as his or her lecturer, I truly wish them the best of luck and hope they make it out alive.

preface: im a 4.0 student and a senior. this was the worst class ive ever taken. la nave had no desire to teach. as im writing this, i still havent seen my second midterm--taken in late march. pointless lectures. pointless book. i could've learned a lot, but la nave was hands-down the worst professor that i've ever had. avoid him at all costs.

A nice guy, but can't teach -Doesn't know how to write on the board -Literally just reads direct quotes from the textbook & doesn't expand on it at all -Refuses to give the solutions to practice worksheets -Your grade depends in the class average, but he refuses to say what the avg is -TAKES FOREVER TO GRADE

The *worst* professor I've ever had. Terrible, unclear lectures make material that should be easy, extremely difficult. This class is horribly disorganized, with him mixing up/not grading exams, taking >30 days for us to see our scores, and forgetting to assign homework until right before finals. I don't even know my grade. Avoid at all costs.

WORST professor ever! Do NOT take any class with him if you can avoid it. He does not know how to explain ANY concept in a clear way, his handwriting on the board is illegible, and it took him over a month to return each midterm score (we only got the last one back a WEEK before the final). The grade is also 90% the two midterms & the final. RUN!

The class was horrible. The two tests made up 50 percent of the grade total, so making a small error would completely destroy your grade. While he emphasized the process rather than the result, he wasn't lenient with partial credit for the process. Took a month to get tests back, also wouldn't give answers to exams after the fact. Avoid him.

The class had no clear direction. We changed textbooks a couple weeks in. The homework was rare and did not reinforce the lecture material. He invited me to do research with his group before saying he was going to be gone over the summer, then couldn't be bothered to send me a few sentences of recommendation for an internship I was pursuing.

After the grade of the final test and your letter grade was posted, my friend informed me. I sent him 2 emails but never replied.

He taught only a little but made lots of mistakes. He did not want to copy the examples from the textbook but he proved his own examples often in mistakes. Lectures are required and very boring. Lots of homework also! Tests are tough!
try ur best to avoid him.

he always complain about that we don't pay attention in class. He never tried to make the class attractive and useful. Nobody wants to watch him restating what is already in text book. And he  failed to write the exactly same example because he did not want to just copy from the textbook. Meanwhile, he did not prepare enough. So you know ....

He doesn't know what he's lecturing, constantly makes confusing errors during demonstration in class. Disorganized, unprepared, and a person who designs the course only to minimize your course grade instead of helping you learn the knowledge.
Class is tough, very fast, a lot of material is being covered in a short time

Semester started out okay, but then things just got terrible. He is not a clear, concise, or useful professor. Currently, we are about to retake our second midterm (because everyone failed it the first time), but he has a) cancelled class, b) not given office hours, AND c) not given us our exams back. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS.
Not the worst professor, but I would most definitely choose a better one given the chance. Too disorganized.

Worst math professor I have EVER had. Disorganized, writes all over the board, does not erase anything neatly, assigns homework that he does not even teach, and so many other HORRIBLE things about him. Currently, we don't even know when our second exam is. This class is ridiculous. Stay as FAR away from this man as you can. He is horrible

A good teacher! He is humorous and interesting although sometimes in class he would go far away from what he really wanted to teach. Nice Grading too. Make sure you know the important places in differential equation. Then choose him!

Very smart man, and he does a very good job making sure you understand what is important in solving differential equations. He's funny sometimes. I would recommend him for 441 because he wants to be around students who are interested in the theoretical part of differential equations. Lower level class students of his can speak for themselves.
Attending his classes is not much help. He talks in a very confusing way. I learned most stuff from the book. His exams are very similar to his mock exams though.

The only thing that got me with the class was the harsh grading. For an intro class, I think it's harsh to expect perfect journalistic writing, especially when it comes to interviews. Many people take this class to see if they want to switch majors, so it was a bit wild to see the grading system. Everything else was fine.

Class is well structured. A fair bit of work but it is an advanced comp elective. Hardest part was getting interviews for assignments. Grading is a bit harsh, however there is an appeal process and I was able to get 12 points back. Overall recommend for the advanced comp credit.

This course was practical and relevant to my career goals. Unlike CS 105, which felt disconnected from journalism, this class offered useful skills. Professor Margaret was knowledgeable and supportive, and our small group learned a lot together. The FOIA-based final project was a highlight, and I'm leaving more confident in my data analysis skills.

The professor encouraged open communication, and the course content was manageable. We gained valuable experience in designing and creating using tools such as Adobe Illustrator, Excel, and Flourish. Each week, the professor emphasized learning through hands-on exercises, encouraging us to apply the concepts to our own examples.

The course content was well-structured and challenging. I gained valuable skills. Without this course and Prof Ng's guidance, I might have been too intimidated to explore coding or data journalism. She made the material accessible and approachable while consistently challenging us. I believe every journalism major would benefit from this course.

Prof Margaret Ng is very thorough, and her lectures are clear and easy to follow. She explains different skills in a way that makes them simple to grasp. I was initially a bit nervous about learning how to create websites in this class, but Prof Ng and our TA were always supportive and encouraging, reminding us not to get frustrated or give up.

I would describe this course as a class that was 'no pain, no gain'. The class was not the easier but I went to office hours for consultation a lot. Prof. Ng provided constructive comments from time to time. Overall, amazing classes. I learned so much and really enjoyed all of the projects.

Professor Ng provided many constructive comments. I incorporated these into our final submission. She hosted a really amazing class this semester. I learned so much and really enjoyed all of the projects. Looking forward to seeing this lovely professor for data journalism in the fall.

One of the greatest classes I took in my undergrad years! Prof. Ng is VERY kind and she is willing to stay after class and hold personalized office hours to discuss class work and career plans with me. Gained lots of professional and personal perspective through my conversations with her.

I really enjoyed this class last Spring. Grades was based on participation, lab, assignments, presentation and project. Syllabus is very clear. The best thing in this course was that I got the chance to work on real life dataset and exposed to different multimedia skills such as web, graphic design using adobe illustrator, excel, HTML or more.

She's a very kind professor. I can manipulate datasets with ease and comfort after the course. I have a better understanding of the basic design principles & concepts. I also acquire skills to visualize data using Adobe Illustrator which's very practical! She's also very communicative through email if you have any questions/concerns. Love her.

I enjoyed Prof. Ng classes. She is very knowledgeable. I learnt a few software (EXCEL, SQL, etc.) to handle data: data management, cleaning, analyses and so forth. I enjoyed attending to her office hours when she shared her experiences and resolved my confusions in class assignments. She is a genuinely nice teacher who really cares her students.

While the class itself was fun and I learned a lot, Prof Ng is a toss-up. She's very knowledgeable, but can be a tough grader sometimes. I do feel like she tends to forget she has a Ph.D. in this topic, not the students. She also tends to move very quickly so you can get left behind. Just make sure to read and go to office hours when needed.

Gives feedback but not always kindly. Almost no resources for learning the actual exam material besides the occasional useful slide or the internet. BAD SLIDES

This class is a confusing mess. The lecture slides are HORRENDOUS. Like PLEASE USE LATEX OR SOMETHING INSTEAD OF TYPING FORMULAS! Content is easy to learn but it is conveyed so uniquely poorly that you will finish the class confused on what you actually learned. She HAS to revamp her slides, assignments, and course documents. AND THE FORMULA SHEETS

Rude to students and has absolutely terrible lectures, but the class itself is easy because of the weird grading structure. If you are genuinely interested in learning what is presented in this course, most of your learning will have to be done individually through online resources or the textbook. Avoid this professor at all costs.
Disrespectful and unprepared Professor
sucks, very rude and aggressive.

Terrible class. The lectures are incredibly confusing and she does not clearly explain any procedures for solving problems. And then you get assigned homework about topics you have not covered at all and know nothing about! The homework is not reflective of lecture and the exams are not reflective of homework or lecture. Also just kinda mean.

Overall decent, her test are very easy but be excessively careful because if you don't score 100 on at least one of them, you are definitely going to be among the 70 percent of students getting A- instead of that less than 10 percent getting an A.

Not super difficult if you study a few hours per week. Decent class over all but her lectures didn't hold my attention. My biggest gripe is that her tests are math heavy multiple choice tests, where the questions build off of each other. So if you can't answer one question you are kinda screwed. But she does drop two of the four tests.

She was not the best teacher, pretty confusing but her class was very easy. Make sure you study the homework, do the practice exams, and try to get your hands on the older practice exams for more help. You drop one exam and a chance to skip the final. take her class in the spring!
Horrible lecturer. Has very little idea how to teach. HW has missing information that you cant find/know exactly which numbers she uses.
if you can avoid this professor please do it'll be worth it trust me
bad professor, do not take this course

In this class is where I first started using Python, and Professor Ha made it very easy to understand through her video lectures, which were very clear and concise. Our lectures were also interactive, which helped us improve our programming skills more by actually doing the problems, and the practice exams were very accurate to the real exam.

reviews.comment: professor was super nice and i really enjoyed stat107. never taken python before but ha makes it super easy to understand!

Good professor. The lecture videos explain concepts very well. The homework can be challenging at times but, if you go to office hours she will walk you through the problem. You definitely learn a lot in this class.

She used past year's content, (didn't even bother to make new videos) and multiple mistakes (didn't even bother to correct, example: in the regex lectures, she couldn't do one of her own example and just let it go saying it won't be that hard for hw or exams). Feel bad to have this kind of instructors in the department.
The readings are complicated and honestly boring, Dr. Nguyen as a teacher, is boring, and their lectures feel like a chore to complete.
Very well spoken, passionate and just over all incredibly cool

I gained so much knowledge about fashion history + practices from this class! The lectures were easy to follow and I could do them at my own pace since they were async. reviews.comment: Super accommodating in times of stress. Really cares about the material, passionate during office hours, engaging. It was a good time.
Mimi is an amazing teacher I've taken three of her classes so far.

Mimi is fantastic! She assigns a lot of dense reading (150 pages a week) but it's not necessarily dull and I got by several weeks not reading. Yes, she stutters but it's good because it gives you time to finish writing her sentence. She is extremely articulate and well-educated. Her job is to convey some abstract ideas, so the class could be tough.

She is brilliant and engaging, and her perspective and insights are much needed here.  I found her to be very generous and helpful.  She changed my way of thinking, and helped me think in a more nuanced way.

Mimi Nguyen is one of the BEST teachers I have EVER had. ive learned so much from her classes and i continue to think deeply about the themes. the fellow commenters here are out of hand, a blatant example of sexism and racism. dont take a class that requires attention, reading, and critical thought if you don't want that!

I'm surprised there are so many negative reviews for Mimi Nguyen. I thought her class was fascinating, and her passion for the subject was highly evident. This class isn't an easy A by any means, but the instructor is highly accessible and willing to clear up any misconceptions you may have.

Her lectures were really long and tedious, and it was difficult to follow along and take notes. She sometimes took weeks to post powerpoint slides, which makes it impossible to prepare for pop quizzes. Most of the readings were difficult, especially for a gen ed.  A lot of them had nothing to do with Asian American Pop Culture. Not what I expected.

Maybe she is smart and well informed... but you can't understand much through her unique mixture of obscurantism and valley girl speak. And as another rater noted accurately, she tries to cow you into submission by saying that you as a student won't understand the readings. Ugh.... why would you ever assign this woman to teach ?

This class showcases everything that is wrong with social study classes today. Hopefully you like watching Yeah Yeah Yeahs videos on YouTube as a means of gaining cultural awareness, because this class is chock-full of moments like that. If I could describe this class in a few words, I would say: "Hipster culture; Amateurish philosophy".
Over complicates everything...sometimes the point she is trying to prove isnt even that deep.

While she seems fun, bubbly & young,her teaching is poor. Assigns hard readings (50+ pg per class) and said she didn't expect us to understand them. I don't doubt that she's well educated, but her comments so confusing and long that you lose what the point was in the 1st place. Utterly distracted by her lack of speaking skills."uh uh uhhh".

You get the vague sensation that Nguyen is talking down to everyone in the class. Ironically enough, she nevertheless lacks elementary teaching skills. Her counterculture/alternative tastes seep into almost everything she talks about... Regardless, an A is achievable if you have a brain in your head.
Readings are way too difficult and very irrelevant.  Lectures are boring.  Uses way too many big terms.  Over-complicates everything.  Expects too much.  I'd best avoid her class.

So hard. Horrible speaker. Knows a lot about material, unable to relate to introductory level students. Did I mention horrible speaker? Grades are based on pop quizzes. Readings are ridiculously difficult unless you are already familiar with the material. She is not approachable. I am so glad this class is over and I would never take Nguyen's class

I didn't go to class toward the end because I would just fall asleep.  Lectures were utterly boring.  She needs to work on her speaking skills -desperately.-  She really does say "um" "ya know" or "such as" over 300 times in lecture.  I got bored one day in class (suprise) and made a tally sheet.

If you're interested in: 1) attend a long lecture that's sure to put you to sleep, 2)frusrate yourself with how much you hate this class and how mimi teaches, 3)go nuts on every pop quiz and essay you have to write, 4)have no clue what you're doing on the tests, and finally 5) ruin your gpa then this is the class for you.  find another class!!!

Don't take this class!! save your gpa!  She can't teach!!  the essays you read are too hard to understand and she doesnt simplify them at all in class.  she talks over your head with huge words and says um,ah, and right literally 600 times a class.  lecture is boring and she gives pop quizzes.  worst class i have ever taken! hardest 120 class ever
Absolutely fantastic.  Fascinating, challenging, cheerful, organized.  I'm in love with this professor.

Lan Chaplin is a great Professor! She takes her time explaining what is expected of you and gives you all the resources and help you need. She is very passionate about what she teaches and it shows through her lectures. The midterm is not easy but you can easily get an A if you study all her lecture slides. Final project assigned 1st day. Take it!
She was great but definitely had her favorites!  It was kind of annoying.
No Comments

This woman is one of the most humble teachers Ive ever met at UIUC. Its rare that a person can piss her off. Keep up with the readings and other assignments, then youll pass. And dont miss class either because itll hurt you in the long run.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Ngo really knows her material and is available to teach intersectional materials. She is funny and engaging. The hardest part is that she has a hobby of staring you down so be ready to feel intimidated
She is funny, but the class is hard. When you write an email to her you get no reply from her. You can't find any studying materials on compass.

This was the hardest class I have ever taken. If you're considering this as an elective, don't do it. The course is pretty unorganized with some lectures, some purely class discussion, and readings that are SO HARD to understand even after talking them out in class. With that said, Ngo is one of the coolest, nicest teachers you can have at U of I.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is the hardest I have ever taken. The readings are very difficult to understand, but Ngo is willing to explain it to you over and over again. You will be called on in class, and "I didn't do the reading" is not an option. However, Ngo's sense of humor and style and generosity with food makes coming to class prepared worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Absolutely wonderful. Warning -- she does cold call students, but it honestly keeps you accountable because the material is extraordinarily dense. But she's hilarious, super intelligent, and a very genuine person who represents her most authentic self in and out of the classroom.
Love Professor Ngo!  Amazing class, super relevant material, and she's funny.  I learned a ton.
Wow, really smart and funny.  If you want to know about queer theory, queer of color critique, trans studies  or radicalization, this is the class to take.  She really cares about students.
Fiona is awesome! Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. She can be kinda confusing, but she makes class extremely enjoyable. She bought us pizza a couple times.
Awesome lecturer, very funny.  Material is difficult but worthwhile and revolutionary!  Highly recommend this class &prof!

Very interesting class. Fiona was also very funny. At times she was a bit confusing, but going to discussion sections cleared everything up for me. Tests were very easy if you paid attention. She often gave study guides with everything you need to know. The only downside is reading material that had to be read before lecture.

She's a good teacher, very funny. Grade comes from 7 "worksheets" due throughout the semester that consist of answering questions extensively,a presentation, and participation. It's a small class so be prepared to be asked to speak in class because it is mostly discussion about readings and films watched in class.
Pretty boring class, though she's entertaining enough.  Assignments really sucked, but the material is more or less interesting, albeit irrelevant.

No exams, though a few pop quizzes. Lecture is hilarious but not necessarily mandatory. 3 large assignments with several parts. They are time consuming but not extremely difficult. One group project studying a space on campus. Section attendance mandatory. Not overly hard material but time consuming assignments.
Excellent class, excellent professor. The lectures she does are so great, and she's hilarious!
This class is boring, and it required everyone to participate. The reading materials are incredibly hard. Not recommend taking her class.
There was no exams or finals.  Everything was based on quizzes and presentations.  She is a fabulous teacher! I'd take another class with her in a heartbeat.

Attendance isn't mandatory, but she does give out quizzes. Great, knowledgable, hilarious and accessible professor, uses a variety of content that's all fairly relevant (video, handouts online and on compass). You don't have to do all the reading so it's okay if you fall behind. Didn't really learn anything new but good class.

She's awesome!  Incredible sense of humor, gives plenty of time for assignments.  The readings are pretty dense and you definitely have to keep up with them.  I've talked to her after class a lot and she's really good at explaining things further.  Definitely recommend her, and she has awesome suits!

Awesome, but don't make my mistake: do NOT take her for more than one class in a semester. she assigns papers in all her classes at the same time and you will be beyond swamped.  even if they're not the same dept- i've got GWS 250 and AAS 120.  also assigned the same or similar reading in the two classes.
The Dr. Ngos what is going on!
Interesting class, difficult discussion - go prepared to class

Ngo is a good professor, showed me a new way of thinking. Really challenged my point of view and introduced me to critical theory. Take a class with Ngo if you are really interested in the subject matter. Only take it if you are a philosophical kind of person.

The readings are impossible to get through and the course packet is way too expensive. She is not very openmined and the work is extensive and hard, but if you are interested in the topics, she knows what she is talking about
No Comments

this class was not at all what i expected. definately not easy and some of the class readings were very dry/did not really make sense. she was not really open-minded and you really didnt have enough time for tests. if you have an interest then take the class, but basically just hope for an easy ta.

Absolutely hilarious, makes lecture fun. The topics are very interesting, even though some of the readings can be very dry. Has two point quizzes every few Wednesdays, so attend then for sure. Get Rose as a TA!

I loved this class it was so much fun the only hard part was that there were very few assignments and so it put a lot of pressure on those three papers. Carl is really funny and made the lectures super interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Carl was awesome and his class was so so much fun. I would definitely take it again if I could, the only disclaimer I would give is that it is a LOT of reading and the three essay exams take a really long time if you want a good grade. Overall loved this class and lectures were always really fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are long, boring, & feel pointless, but it's important to attend due to the movies, which are on exams. The main grades are "pop quizzes" (usually announced beforehand) and 3 noncumulative exams which all are essay writing similar to AP history. All communication is done by email, which can be annoying. As a person though he's pretty nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Wonderful professor. Very understanding and takes the time to learn you by name. Lots of reading but his class is an intimate discussion that he leads. Great accent and really nice guy. As long as you let him know you're missing class, he's very accommodating and respectful about personal issues. Tests are easy if you go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: He is really into the class.  As said, his accent is adorable.  My only complaints about the class was the high number of films you have to watch outside of class and the exams were a little unclear.  Otherwise, the books are good and he is fun.
Professor Niekerk is adorable! His class is fairly easy and he isn't boring when he lectures. He cracks jokes and remembers everyone's names. He's a good professor and the class is an easy A.
Prof. Niekerk is adorable and brilliant! Love his classes.

Took his sex and literature class my freshman year. He is really funny and is really understanding about missing classes as long as you contact him before and don't make it a habit. Don't have to read the books to do well, just take notes in class and write down the main points he says and know how to elaborate on those. Interesting class, great gu

Great teacher, really knows his stuff, and his essays and tests aren't too difficult if you've been to class and know the major themes of each of the novels and can come up with references from the text.

This class is not an EASY A but it is a doable A... go to class everyday and take notes. you really do not have to even read the books you just have to remember what he says about the books and repeat it in your essays and the midterm/final. He is really funny and a nice guy so go to his office hours if you are struggling. I got an A in the end
Prof. Niekerk is the greatest. I learned every day, and I wanted to read and prepare for him and for this wonderful class. So clear, loves what he does, and very cute.

I took this class as a freshman, and I really enjoyed it. Professor Niekerk has such a passion for the subject, and he's really knowledgeable too. He's pretty lenient on absences, but he'll definitely take points off if you miss more than he allows. Also, his accent is so cute.

This class was also a GWS 270 class. Awesome professor. Not difficult in this class, keeps the class interesting with unique reading selections. Very funny and helpful. Totally understanding if you have to miss class for something in your family even without an excuse form. Midterm and Final= easy if you read your novels
No Comments
Great guy and a good teacher. Keeps the discussion going in class. Ill miss him dearly

Ger 199: He's a good man and a good teacher. The homework is almost daily with reading. The reading itself isn't so bad--some of it might get hard but that is the literature side of it....the discussions good too. The mid-term was easy, and the papers aren't so bad either. Grading is fair as well. His accent is charming.

Amazing. Put 20pt extra credit on midterm 3 which boosted my grade above 100%. There was no homework so it's up to you to participate and make sure you understand. Significantly lessens the busy-work burden on strong self learners but punishes slackers who need to be forced to do practice to succeed.

When I took ECE374B, there was no homework and grades were based on quizzes and exams. The content was challenging, but the professor explained concepts clearly and worked through examples in lecture. Quizzes and exams were tough, but fair. Great professor, difficult course.

Class structure was not good. Lectures are not mandatory. Lab is not mandatory. We have 2 quizzes a week in lab. 3 midterms and no final. Quizzes are relatively simple, but it's hard to figure out what exactly you should study for. Exams are relatively difficult, but are curved. Our curves were 6 pts, 16 pts, and 1 pt respectively.

the content in this class is very challenging, which is expected, but kani does a great job teaching it. lectures and labs were helpful, and the practice material made things clearer. the course felt organized and fair, and it wasn't as overwhelming as it first seemed

Literally one of the best professors I've ever had. Extremely clear in his lecturing style. Also very patient with answering questions. He used to curve exams to have average 70, which means even if you don't do well, if everyone else scored low you don't have to worry. He's also just a very kind person in general

he spends 20-30 minutes going over the prelecture question, so the last 30 minutes of lecture are super rushed. he frequently mentions content before we actually cover it, which makes it hard to understand current content. skips thru lost of slides. 75% exams and 25% quizzes with the retake replacing even if its lower made this class awful. 👎👎👎

With every year, his tests get longer. Two years ago, his exams were 4-5 questions long. This semester, each test is 7-8 questions long. That is, with the same duration. I don't understand how he expects us to finish the test and do well. Not to mention, exams and quizzes make up our whole grade.

Your whole grade is based on midterms and quizzes. I think it's insane how the grade you get in the class is based off three 75 minute exams and a bunch of 5 min quizzes. Though, he does provide you with a cheatsheet created by him for the midterms. Also, the actual midterms aren't REMOTELY close to the previous/practice exams he provides us with.

One of the best professors in the ECE department. Clearly cares about his students and explains all his policies thoughtfully. Good lectures and very well-run course website. Content is tough but he makes it manageable.
Used lots of examples in his lectures which I liked.
Please finish asynchronous videos.
If you attend lectures and discussions, getting a A is pretty easy. HWs are tough but I just used drops on tougher problems and it was fine.
Great lecturer and all the content is available online. Lots of practice exams and recordings so its not essential to go to lecture, but it is pretty easy to fall behind if you don't.

Good lecturer. Terrible course backend. TAs freely cancel office hours without finding someone to substitute. Kani needs to get control over his staff. The homework questions are okay, but the solution keys are terrible. TAs will blindly cite the key, even though much of the time the key barely answers the question (it would barely get half credit)
Made a very hard class manageable for the students. Criteria was clear, curve was generous. The best lecturer for ECE 374, makes confusing concepts easier with his great example problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I enjoyed his midterm drop policy.
I wish he teaches CS473 or CS475.

He is the GOAT. Course policies are very lenient and fair but be warned, he will probably not make exceptions. Lot of students get turned off because of his rigidity but I'd rather have 4 exams with one drop than 3 exams with conflicts.
Great lectures, reasonable amount of work. Learned a lot and went back through his notes for my leetcode prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't think he is a great lecturer since he just mostly reads off of the lecture slides and often assumes that we are already familiar with certain topics that he never covered, some of which I don't think we were expected to know. He is relatively lenient on grading though, but I think properly teaching us the topics is more important.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's one of the nicest professor out there.
Care about students, very clear explanation for algorithms, getting an A- and above would be easier than section A.

He definitely cares about the students and the stuff he is teaching, in fast, he tries all he can to make the course more meaningful (I think he is still trying, there is a long tough way to go). Even though the course content is absolutely hard, I personally still learned a lot from spending time and attending lectures. Kani is a great professor.

Kani just really cares about his students and the content. You can tell how much he wants to change the course for the better, too. In general, the exams are hard, but the homework and discussions do prepare you for them. I struggled sometimes, but I really learned and enjoyed the content.

Overall, I would take him again 100%.

Although this is a hard class he has been(t an amazing professor throughout. He is truly someone who cares about his students and makes a very difficult class fair. I was struggling a lot towards the middle of the class and reached out and he really took the extra time to help me succeed.
A nice guy. Could be a better lecturer especially closer to the end of the semester, but far from bad. Truly does care about students, which is more than I can say about most professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (finally) I personally didn't come close to an 100+, yet I can certainly say I learned a lot from Kani's section. I can also say I probably understand algorithms better than many A section students (including the emotional student behind that most likely bullshit review). And content-wise, this IS a pretty-very challenging class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: (pt 3) Despite Kani's generous curve (which seemed to have piss off some A students-but like, if you care so much about your class grade, you should've taken his section instead of complaining profusely in the A section LUL), it is very difficult to get above 100: no one just "gets it easily."

(continued) And to get above a 100, you *definitely* need to understand the material very well & learn a lot (I personally know some of the special 16 students who got above 100). So I can rule them out as not the salty keyboard warrior behind that review. Additionally, no one "got over 100% easily,"

The review below complaining Kani's section being "so easy I got above 100" is 100% bullshit-I'm sure it's coming from a comically salty A section student, who isn't even in the B section. How do I know? It's very difficult to get above 100 raw score-only 16 students out of hundreds of B section students were able to.
He is a patient, caring student, and generous professor.
Difficult class as expected. Extremely flexible and lenient grading policies.

I don't know why he has such a low score here. Overall good prof, caring students, and taught me a lot, turning a hard algorithm class into a fun class (although it is still hard and you should put all your effort into the class). He gives a good grade to everyone. He put tremendous effort into the course, and I would say his hardworking paid off.
Has no caring for the student. Doesn't care about students's mental health at all. Also, I don't think he can score more than 60 in the 374 exams. Doesn't know the materials. Bad professor

This class has a reputation for reusing old homeworks and tests and I think most people took it with that in mind. After the first midterm I realized old materials wouldn't help me and just made sure I knew the coreconcepts presented lectures which helped a lot. Tests were definitely hard but the final grade was very generous I think....

I am not really sure why students are filled with hate. I think the course was absolutely fine, same goes for the professor. Most students wanted to work on HW and exams that are borrowed from previous years, which Prof. did not do. if you want to apply yourself and work hard, take this course and prof.
He made our final with problems and concepts we had never seen before to challenge us to see who deserves to pass. All because students complained that they couldnt read his handwriting lol
This professor's lecture is not clear. Taking photos is not allowed in class, even if there is reflection.

This teacher does not allow cell phone photos in class. Students are not allowed to take pictures of the board to record the board. Even if you sit in the back and can't see, you are not allowed to take pictures. It's really mean.

I really enjoyed this class but is was definitely difficult. He is a nice person and I think he is a great lecturer and is very passionate about the subject. Although, the homework is due at 1pm on Wednesdays and is very exam heavy.

This class was definitely difficult but manageable. He gave many examples during class, many which were close to the questions on the actual exam. Homework is due in the middle of the day, and are done during exam weeks as well.

Grading was way too harsh. Literally no partial credit. I normally get A+ in math courses with ease, so the A- was quite disappointing. Spent 10+ hrs/week, solutions in the homework were super long and arduous, and this doesn't match up with the 441 experience of students from other sections at all. I'd recommend you take a different section.
Passionate lecturer. Exams cover basic concepts but grading is a little harsh. Homework takes a while. Overall a fun guy.
80% test scores on average one question in exam = 10% in total grade. Not easy exams and massive homeworks. Unless spend 15+ hours per week or no A.

Professor Tzirakis is definitely one of the most passionate and caring professors I have had. That being said, the course is made to feel a lot more difficult than it needs to be. I felt that concepts that could have been explained in a simple manner were overly complicated. The homework are difficult and the course is a lot of work.
VERY GOOD!
nice

If this is your first experience with differential equations, avoid professor Tzirakis. Infact, avoid this professor either way. Egotistical and hard to believe he gives any second thought to his student's success and the quality of his teachings. You will find yourself completely reliant on the textbook and other material found on the internet.

Honestly one of the worst professor that has taught a class I have taken. Maybe it was because it was the first semester we went online but idk. Very rude and combative in his response to questions. To be fair, I stopped going to lecture a couple of weeks in, but even when I went I thought they were fairly useless. Got by studying the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Some of the least well prepared or helpful lectures I've had, attacks students who ask questions, and combative when questioned. I never actually asked him a question after seeing his response to others, and quickly found it best to just read the book instead.
He is a clear lecturer. But sometimes, he does not motivate topics too well or goes overtime in lecturing. Some early homework assignments were too long.

Material is extremely difficult to follow. Don't take this class with him if it is your first diffeq class. He expects you already have experience. Extremely harsh grader on exams. I failed both exams even though I only got half a question wrong on each of them. Gets angry and defensive during lecture if you ask any questions (especially "dumb" one

Goes through lectures extremely quickly while leaving students confused and lost. You NEED to go to office hours and study the book a lot. Teacher expects you to understand the basics rather than teaching the basics. Was told this class was a blow-off class, but it is definitely not. Requires lots of work inside and outside of class. Don't reccome
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Engineering student for Math553 PDE here please, 1st, are you familiar with lebesgue convergence theorem, n-dimension sphere surface area and many other concepts in functional analysis?  if not, forget about this course. 2nd, you care about why the solution to a PDE exists and why it's unique rather than how to solve it?  if not, forget about it.

Dr. Tzirakis is an amazing professor who loves the material he teaches. It is very difficult to make ordinary differential equations interesting, but his lectures and applications make the course (while more abstract than MATH 285) much more useful. Take the course with him.
He is a great Professor, knows the material very well, approachable, nice person!! A lot of HWs!! good grading , very hard

Friendly personality. Not arrogant like some higher level professors. Likes to lecture without looking too closely at notes so he'll make a few mistakes, but takes student corrections well. Has an accent but easy to understand after a few classes. Explained concepts well. Tests were very straightforward and similar to homework and study guide.
Good professor. His questions come straight from homework. His grading was fair, and he tried to help the student out frequently.

Pretty easy class. Exams are only a few problems so make sure you know how to do everything on the study guide as well as covered in the homework. Not the best partial credit either. He doesn't try to mess you up. He's just making sure you know the material that he taught. Many 100's were achieved on exams in my class.
He's a nice guy. His exams are on study guides and homework. Make sure you study all problems on your study guide and homework, then you can get 100/100

The hardest part of this class is getting up for 10 AM lectures (not even that early) which have required attendance. The professor covers interesting topics and is very entertaining in lectures. Three essays (~1000 words) throughout the semester. Textbook is easy to get and usually covers the same content as lectures.
You have to go to class. Graded on participation and 3 papers. Very simple class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were pretty interesting. There were 4 main writing assignments spread through the semester but you only had to do 3. We also didn't have class on the weeks that the assignments were due so that was really nice. Those were majority of the grade, not many other assignments. Textbook was barely used, but was helpful.
Have to go to class to get a good grade. Very understanding and easy grader.

I took this class over winter break and thoroughly enjoyed it. My only critique is that the grading took till the final week, and he was a little hard to reach at the beginning of the semester.There are no midterms, but be prepared to write. He provides video lectures that serve as a recap; those are so helpful! Def manageable over winter or summer

Took this class over winter break with Prof Noonan. Was his first time teaching over a break so things were not especially straightforward, but he seemed engaged and willing to help anyone with anything. He wanted everyone to get As and the work was minimal and could be completed at your own pace. Great class for a Winter/Summer session!

Fall 2025 was the first semester Noonan taught this course. It was entirely online, so there were some minor hiccups. The entire course is open-note, but I recommend purchasing the textbook for your success, especially considering there are written assignments in this course (in other words, not all questions are multiple-choice).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: DR NEWTON IS THE GOAT!!! as a student with ADHD i struggle with deadlines a lot and she is SO kind and flexible. didn't expect to learn much bc i took this as a gen ed but learned a lot. also she wraps the course up before finals week which is so nice
I LOVE DR NEWTON. She is one of the best instructors I have ever had.
Never expected Advanced Comp to be this facile. Big shoutout to Professor Newton (Norcross) who made this a pleasant experience.

Dr. Norcross is awesome! Taking BTW 250 with her this semester and she always has such a positive attitude and is willing to help out with whatever. not sure how other instructors set up the class but she always requires drafts and does peer reviews which helped me stay on track a ton!

Class is writing intensive, and there is a group project at end. She is very nice and will help you with your questions, and is not a harsh grader, but also does not just hand out As. She is very flexible and reasonable. A great professor to take for your advanced composition requirement.

Ineffective in creating a clear vision for the direction of course expectations. With a performance based course, final grade does not reflect quality or impact on academic achievement. Displaying poor creative liberty in delivering content, course is lecture heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Craft is a super caring person and a great advisor, however some of her lectures are painfully boring. Overall just do your reading and its an extremely easy A.

I have only had her for one class and I love her. I took FSHN 140 which is a super easy class. Basically just a participation grade with a few group projects. She is easy to work with, kind and genuine. She is also a good adviser.

Jill is by far the best teacher I have had in my four years here.  She is very helpful and willing to work with you if you have a conflict or problem.  You can go to her and talk about anything and is very helpful as an advisor when it comes to registration.
I agree with the above statement.  Also, walks around with her son in the kitchen with no hair net on and then lectures us on sanitation issues! So ironic.
She is arrogant and annoying. Thinks she's God's gift to the world and does absolutelynothing to help while in the lab. Projects and quizzes are ridiculous... way to much for a 4 credit hour class.
No Comments
Just a boring teacher

Nora is a great lecturer who explains every topic with relation to the real world application. Class is pretty easy. Only complain is that the grader for the homeworks is really harsh. Final was a bit harder than I expected, but overall great class.

There are online and in person sections of this class. If you take it online but are on campus, you still have to go in for tests and presentations, which means you're required to skip other classes for this class. The grading is brutally tough, with justifications that are laughable ("You should have known this from 320" etc.). Graded iClickers
Very accommodating and kind.

Perhaps the most compassionate Philosophy professor on campus, which is saying a lot, because there are quite a few incredibly compassionate ones. He's just an incredibly pleasant guy who does a great job of connecting with his students. His lecture style isn't perfect for me, but the smile he delivers it with makes up for it. Take him if you can.

Noel is a good professor and is passionate about philosophy but often goes on tangents and stretches conversations longer than they should be. Overall interesting material but it's hard to understand since he jumps around a lot with topics during lectures. He sometimes posts slides, get ready to write because the lecture notes are lengthy.

He was a great teacher who cares about his students and their opinions. There are 3 papers and a couple small assignments, but nothing overwhelming. Attendance is not mandatory, but I would recommend going!

It's very clear how passionate Prof. Noel is towards the subject of philosophy. That being said, I did have many times in class where I felt I was not getting what I needed from his lectures due to allowing a lot of students to speak. While in-class opinions are valuable, it often impeded with my learning and understanding of the topics we discuss.

I loved Dr. Saenz! His course was pretty easy; I took the ACP option, and there were three relatively small papers. His lectures were very interesting, and I learned a lot in his class. It made me very interested in philosophy when I wasn't before. He is super nice and is always willing to answer questions. I would definitely recommend his courses!
Very nice professor

An amazing professor or lecturer. He made a somewhat boring class entertaining and engaging. The TA will make or break your experience so ask around and get a good one. But the actual course and workload were ideal and I'd highly recommend for anyone.
He's the best! The workload of this class is super low and Noel made everything crystal clear. A shame for anyone who received a grade that's lower than an A.
Very clear in explanations, you can tell he enjoys teaching and is openly available to help.

Saenz is obviously very passionate about the material but his lecturing isn't the best. Sometimes his explanations will become jumbled because he mixes up words, goes on tangents, and trails off without finishing his sentence. It's best to read the book and do LOTS of practice problems (especially if you take a long time to solve proofs, like me).

This class was the class that I could blow off until the exams and then cram in a bunch of knowledge to get an A. A lot of long lectures, I learned more from the youtube Phil 102 professor than him. He talks really fast but if you actually read the chapter and try on your homework you'll do fine, after all- the exam questions are in the txt
His test questions are straight out of the textbook. He is available outside of class if you need help and cares a lot about his students doing well.

Dr. Saenz is an excellent orator and you can see he's very passionate about philosophy and wants his students to be, too. PHIL 100 is a writing intensive and if you go to office hours the (800w) papers should be easy enough. The quizzes in discussion can be tricky, so do well on them because those and the papers are your only graded assignments.

He is a good teacher and clearly knows his topic well. However I wasn't a fan of the structure of the course. Our entire grade was one long paper broken up into 4 sections that we turned in throughout the semester. But the paper is all on one topic, so there's no reason to studyreally learn the other topics of the course. Wasn't challenging at all

Most of the lectures and discussions don't even show up on the exams but they're great to listen to nonetheless. A great speaker and if you're just a little bit into philosophy he makes it very interesting.
Very cool guy. Very encouraging and loves when students get involved during lecture. Very passionate about what he teaches. Makes learning the material fun.
Favorite professor. Great lecturer and very generous with his time and consideration. Would definitely recommend everyone to take a class with him.
No homework! No paper! yay! Nearly all test questions are from slides posted online. He is really passionate about teaching.
THE BEST!! He's so nice, helpful, understanding, and cool.  Take him.

His passion for philosophy shows when he lectures. He teaches the class in a very engaging and intriguing manner. If you have the chance to take a class he is teaching, don't miss out on the opportunity!
Noel is very engaged in the subject and he takes time to clear up any questions in lecture. Overall a very good professor.
This course overlaps with some of the other required courses but that is not the professor's fault
This is a very theoretical class but he made it much more interesting than I had expected
very helpful class for learning how to develop materials  Most of our other classes are too theoretical.
Very theoretical class; never any practical teaching on how to actually teach and implement TBLT. Not open to differing opinions. Very teacher centered, lecture based class style.
Expects everyone to agree with his own opinion of TBLT, although told we should formulate our own opinions on the subject.

Will not be very helpful if he feels that you disagree with his views on Task-Based Language Teaching.  Tells you to form your own opinion then expects you to agree with his!  Expects everyone to adopt his teaching methodology.
The class wasn't organized well and gave a very limited view of what TBLT is or could be.

Such an awesome professor. She clearly cares about the content she teaches, and makes it enjoyable for her students. It's difficult material, but her review sessions help a lot with exams. I would take this class again if I could!

This class was honestly hard because it was so biology heavy. The material was really complex, but the professor clearly loves what she teaches and it comes across in how she lectures. She is so passionate about the material and it makes the difficulty bearable because her passion is just that contagious. I would absolutely recommend. 10/10

Professor Liang is one of my favorite professors I have had here, I never write reviews but had to leave her one. PSYC210 can be hard but she makes it really clear. Also, if you are ever confused on material she is super welcoming with questions after class and will never make you feel bad for not understanding something. Awesome prof.

You can feel Professor Liang's passion for neuroscience in her lecture. Her lecture contents are relevant to real life, making the class interesting and memorable. The lecture organization is also clear and easy to follow. She appreciates students who are hard-working and willing to ask questions. She really wants students to success! :)

I found the content in this class to be very informative and interesting. The slides were very helpful and easy to understand. The exams were multiple choice and free response; the free response questions were difficult but going over the content and understanding the processes would be helpful. Overall I feel like I learned a lot from this class.
Great professor! She clearly teaches material, and includes some fun anecdotes so it makes more sense. Also provides lots of resources, and a clear study guide throughout the course.
Very caring professor. I enjoyed her lectures.

she was my favorite professor for this class. her lectures were really engaging and interesting, she's very sweet, and she goes above and beyond for her students. i also liked that she recorded every lecture and even took the time to write out closed captioning for all of them. going over the recordings helped me a lot.

She's super clear, direct, and simple with her teaching. Lectures are easy to follow, posted online before class, quizzes are open note, and exams were fair. She's super kind and appreciates those who go to office hours (I never did tho). She is fun too- enjoys handing out veggies from her garden to students who ask questions in class!

Dr. Liang was an excellent and wonderful Professor. You can tell that she cares if her students succeed, and she does her best to ensure that everyone understands the material. I recommend attending her lectures as she provides real life examples on top of her material to help you connect it to the real world, which in turn makes studying easier.
Prof Liang is incredibly caring about her lectures, and her relationship with students. She encourages us to go to office hours, she spends time answering questions, clearing up issues.

Professor Liang's lectures are engaging and interesting, they were easy to follow and she answers any questions people have very clearly. Her demonstrations of some concepts made them a lot easier to understand, and the stories that she tells in lectures help make connections between content and real-life applications.

She is very caring and easy to reach, she encourages all students to go to office hours. She explains material thoroughly and is more than willing to go back and explain more. Overall a great teacher.

She's a great teacher. Makes sures student understand before moving on, tries her best to make sure you get what she is saying and gives real life examples of what she is talking about so that it is easier to understand

Professor Liang was without a doubt the best professor for this class, she explained everything so well and made sure all of her students understood the material before moving on. I would 100% take another one of her classes and I recommend everyone in this department to do the same.
The delivering of the lecture is boring. Her speaking stresses on random words, making it tiring to listen attentively. Otherwise, the material is solid, and she obviously knows what she teaches.

This was a tough class but I learned a lot. Need to put in the work to get a good grade. She recommended 3 hours of studying per week for a good grade. 5 participation questions based on random lectures (5%), 3 exams but lowest dropped (25%), 5 online quizzes (5% each), and a final (20%)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: So glad I took 417. As others have said, Professor Liang genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. She uses feedback to improve her lectures, shares funny anecdotes that relate to the current topic, and makes sure to emphasize which material will be tested. Tip - attend the lectures and the study sessions before exams. It helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She is willing to help students anytime. The exam is not so difficult that you would do just fine if you prepare well.
A solid professor, interesting lectures/pretty funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Liang is a really nice person. She cares for students and is passionate of teaching. She has an accent, but she is not hard to understand since she speaks slowly. There are three exams and a group project, but they are not hard if you go to lectures.  Very good and worth-taking class.

reviews.comment: She gives test questions away during class... so show up. She was sweet and made sure we were all on board.

Prof Liang is one of my favorite professors in Psychology Department. Her lecture is really really interesting. She tries to apply everything she taught into life so that we can memorize it better. Indeed, she has a heavy accent but as long as you get used to it, it's alright.

reviews.comment: For everyone in 210 thats giving professfor Liang a bad rep, I highly recommend taking an ADVANCED psychology class with her. Im in her neuroscience of eating and drinking class ,psych 413, and shes a phenomenal professor. Shes very excited passionate about her research as well as her students. English isn't her first language so give her a break.

reviews.comment: You could always sense that she invests a lot of effort to help you understand the course contents. Interesting class

Professor Liang is funny and honest. She's not harsh on students and their questions. But she's kind of hard to understand; she has a heavy accent. I recorded all her lectures and replayed them while studying. Got an A on the exam. RECORD the professor! It will really, really, help.

She's a sweet woman, and likes her students. But she's not a good lecturer. Her lecturesPowerPoints give contradictory information, and what she says will be on the exam and what is on the exam are two different things. Exam questions are worded in strange ways to try to trick you. Nothing against her personally, but that's the way it is.

Professor Nuesiri teaches a very confusing course that left most of the students confused as to what they were supposed to take away from the lectures. He is very intelligent; however, he expects all of his students to think the way he thinks, which led to further confusion and frustration on our parts.

I didn't have any expectations with this class. I thought it would be a simple overview of social and environmental problems, but instead we read a lot of articles and papers that were challenging. We had to distinguish the problems ourselves as we read and listened in lecture. Nuesiri is tough in a way that he wants us to constantly think beyond.
Absolute worst teacher I've had at U of I. Rude, horrible attitude, impossible to understand. Doesn't explain his expectations and leaves his class confused without any direction.
Mr. Ochs was an amazing teacher. I am glad I chose AgEd as a major and had the opportunity to take his class. Highly recommend!
Mr. Ochs is one of the greatest teachers I've ever had. He cares about his students and is overall very genuine. If more teachers were like him, the world would be a better place.

Very quality professor. Very nice guy that tries to make class as interesting as possible, and he assigns very easy and simple work. Attendance is mandatory, however, and you can only miss one class. Definitely taking another one of his classes!
Unable to express clear directionsopinions, confusing on expectations, blabbers forever about things.  Regretting taking any course in Ag Ed with the current staff.
Lectures and topics are good and engaging. Dr. Oh docks points in various grading categories for unknown reason. She is a tough commenter and responder so be sure to communicate about expectations.
She was very nice, but could have been more clear on her expectations for the final paper.

Prof Oh is awesome! I took ENGL 200 recently, and she's amazing. She's very passionate about her work, and is willing to help you!. Feedback on close readings is very VERY important, as it will help prepare you for the final essay. As long as you participate in class (even if it's once/week) and stay on top of reading/deadlines, you'll be good!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She did not provide a rubric/instructions for the final essay, and docked students points for unknown reasons.

Dr. Oh is definitely passionate about her work and this class was so interesting !!  She explains her lectures in heavy detail with lots of examples - I also loved the novels she picked out for our genre units... helped me relate to my culture in a PWI school with a teacher who isn't even the same ethnicity as I am. She was able to get engagement!

reviews.comment: Very kind, knowledgable about postcolonial and environmental studies and compiles fantastic (though copious) reading lists. However, her classes are so disorganized and her lectures are all over the place (she also talks at a breakneck speed). We barely got through the copious assigned readings.

ENGL285. Prof Oh is nice & the material is interesting but the format of the class was a mess. Usually she'd lecture for a bit & then we'd do think-pair-share, but there are other small assignments (communal note taking, mandatory paper workshops) that are easy to forget about. Tough grader with papers; it's hard to deduce what she's looking for.

Rest in peace Mrs. Oberdeck.

i personally was able to get through the class, but that's because i already tend to enjoy learning about american history, so your mileage may vary. some of the more recent criticism here is true--it was difficult for me to hear her in lectures even as someone who sat close to the front. overall just an average big lecture class.

reviews.comment: She is not a good teacher in general. She's monotone during the whole lecture and trails off at the end of every sentence so you can hardly hear her. You have to teach yourself the material through the readings because the lectures are useless. And even though they're useless, you still have to attend them to get credit.

Just no. She doesn't know how to teach. She does not know how to use her microphone; her voice is almost impossible to hear during the lessons and we have to do an in-class assignment to earn credit. The Compass is unorganized and it is hard to find assignments. Due dates are written on the syllabus, not the Compass.

reviews.comment: I took it in Fall 2019. The lecture itself is kind of tedious, and she seldom graded our work. However, she gives Extra credit to students through paper and movies. It is helpful for practicing writing analysis paper. Her TAs are very responsible by grading most of our work and giving very helpful feedbacks.

reviews.comment: I dont know why everyones bashing her. Shes a fantastic professor, very educated and caring. My class was asynchronous Illinois history was excellent. I am grateful I took her as a professor. The course is exciting. She responds to emails right away. If you put in the work, he will pass.

Her lecture style is not conducive for taking notes. Its highly anecdotal in its nature so difficult to take notes of important facts. The lecture deviated into gender studies/queer studies, often to opinions rather than anything backed by fields of study, to discuss events. Many key events were glossed over and some were outright incorrect.

reviews.comment: Extremely smart. Doctorate from Yale and it shows in her comprehensive, yet tedious lectures. Similar to APUSH, except for increased levels of DBQ's and readings
