Funny guy, pretty decent lecturer. But he doesn't upload any slides, so if you miss multiple lectures its over 💔.  A LOT of content covered in both the textbook and the lectures. The exams.... don't even get me started. I just crashed out taking the last exam. Studying won't help. Grade relies heavily on exams so just pray.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Class was just ok. 
Avg for the exams is always 65-75. Reading the book is definitely important and so is going to class for the notes. Go to all discussions and do all 4 assignments, free points. Studying felt useless but do it anyways, start at least 2-3 days before, master the book vocab. exam qs were confusing 
DO EC ASSIGNMENT 4! (grade boost)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Vargas is the best lecturer I've had so far and 8/10 times I enjoy going to his class. That said these have been the worsts tests I've taken at school. No study guides and don't miss any lectures. There's honestly nothing you can really do to prepare for the tests. Good luck

Vargas is top 3 coolest professors I've had. On the other hand, he doesn't upload any of the lecture slides (which aren't in the textbook) so don't miss class. The tests were also very hard for me bc there's a ton of content. TA's r useless and they sound annoyed that I would even ask a question. Currently taking 281 and I can't wait to finish
There is no idea about the exam, no information about the general content of the exam and no revision material is given.
No study guides, too many exams.

NOT A GOOD professor, never gives review material, won't even cover his own material in lecture, but still will test it on the exam. He intentionally made each exam difficult and did not allow taking photos of slides in his lectures, and I don't understand what material he expected students to use to revise for the exams.
In Vargas' Adv 281, there are not many assignments, so everything is test dependent. The material is very boring and not engaging at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Patrick Vargas is a good person and very knowledgeable about his field, but, this is a very difficult class. it. Attendance is mandatory and if you miss a lecture you'll be screwed. Vargas intentionally makes this class a lot harder then it should be by not providing a lot of study materials.

CONS: some things could've been explained better; no study guides; prof. easily distracted // PROS: lively lectures; clear class structure & grading criteria; prof. was helpful & always willing to answer questions; overall nice and funny guy. // I think this is a class where some people get it and some just don't. Would 100% take this class again.
Patrick is a cool fellow, he knows the stuff he's teaching is kinda boring but he makes lectures worth going to. Can't say the same for my TA.

not the biggest fan of this class, but Patrick is super sweet. he sends an intro email every week with the weather and checking in on us. the lectures are sleep-inducing and don't match the book content. TAs aren't the best and the projects suck, but it's required if you're in ADV so have fun.

Patrick is a sweet professor and you can tell he cares. He sends an email every week asking how the class is and talks about the weather. However, this class is a little boring and there is a lot of reading. They upload free pdfs of the book though so you don't have to buy anything. As long as you do the readings and watch the lectures you'll pass
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was a lot of work with very little payoff, IMO. If you're in ADV it's not like you have a choice, so buckle up and enjoy Vargas's dark humor and entertaining lectures. This course is pretty much a mix of BADM 320 and STAT 100 so I'm not sure why COM requires it.

Professor Vargas is very knowledgable on the topic, however, his instruction and communication abilities are sorely lacking. You can learn a lot from his class, as you can see what an expert in their field looks like and also how bad communication skills can hamper overall performance.

I like him as a teacher but the exams cover way too much content. I'm in this class right now studying for exam 2 and I literally thought about jumping off a roof. but good luck guys since its a required class :)

He's an engaging speaker and the content of the class is super interesting but at the same time I wouldn't look both ways when crossing the street on the way to exams hoping a car would just take me out. Even if you study for the exams early it's still like cramming as much info into your brain until it physically cant retain any more info.

Prof Vargas is a really funny and engaging professor. For example he told us about his dominatrix friend in college. He cares about what he is teaching and doesn't just follow a textbook to teach this class. I highly recommend him for ADV 281 and I hope to stay in contact with him now that I am done with the class.

I loved Patrick, he was really knowledgeable about the research side of advertising. The only thing I would say is make sure you go to class because lectures aren't posted and he explains confusing things in class, so write down things he says as well. He's hilarious though, it's always worth it to go. Discussion is kind of a pain though. TAs bad
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This guy is fricking hilarious. He knows his stuff and you NEED to be in class because he never posts any of his slides online. But, you are allowed to take pictures of his slides lol. He's a very open person and a good teacher. Also very informative during office hours. But I didn't have the greatest TA, so I was very reliant on him heh.
He's great, but the class is hard. Be prepared to take notes everyday in class and read the book if you want an A on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Good luck. He's a cool guy, but that being said his exams are hard (no study guide). There are 4 assignments throughout the semester, the first 3 aren't too bad, the last one is a bit harder (ask for help). Read the book, he'll put some info into the exam. There's some extra credit & he doesn't curve. Go to class or you won't get the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He is a reallyyyy cool guy and tries to make lecture semi interesting. That being said the tests are ridiculously hard and he refuses to curve them. He asks a lot of questions like: Is it just A, A&B, all of the above etc. which makes it very hard to get a question that you would normally know the answer to right.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Patrick has been one of my favorite professors over the two years that I've been on this campus. He knows how to effectively incorporate humor and his strange anecdotes to keep your attention in lecture. Attendance wasn't mandatory, but I never wanted to miss class because I genuinely enjoyed it. His tests are pretty tricky, but they didn't kill me

(ADV 281) Three tests, and four assignments, nothing more. Assignments are SUPER easy, but the tests.. give yourself some time to study. They're definitely not hard, just a lot of content but give yourself a couple days to study and you'll be fine. I got a 91 on the first test, but the second was a little harder so I did a little worse.

Vargas is an awesome guy. He's had a lot of experience in the field and plans his lectures pretty well. He is definitely quirky/vulgar, but if you take good notes and keep up with reading the chapters you'll find the class to be both easy and interesting. Best tip: If a subject shows up in both the text and lecture then it WILL BE on the exam

Vargas is definitely a character. His class is interesting but you really have to read the book to fully understand the material. He spends a lot of time talking about random off-topic things in class. He gives a lot of good examples if you can pay attention. He won't teach 481 anymore after this semester so not sure if he'll still teach?

Professor Vargas is a great teacher. Although class was not mandatory, I went to everyone, including the Friday class because he actually makes learning interesting. He is also hilarious. Although the class was tough, I got a B. Would definitely recommend taking any class with him.

Vargas is a hilarious guy, and weirdly attractive, but as a professor (my semester) he was sub-par. I've heard this class was easier in the past, but fall 2012 was hell, he did a HORRIBLE job explaining material, provided almost no guidance on what we need to know for tests and from the book, and gave awful/ ambiguous instructions for assignments

Material isn't hard, but too much for one class. Should be two separate classes. Lack of any outline/study guide for the text only compounds this problem. Course is disorganized and Vargas often skips class or shows up and decides not to teach. When he does teach, he derails often with bad jokes/anectdotes capitalizing on shock value and vulgarity.

Not a bad class to learn some thing from. The materials are from popular press and easy to understand. A little lack of structure in teaching and digress considerably.Helpful when personally contacted.

I had Vargas for both 481 and 490 in the same semester.  He's a super interesting guy but only really teaches well in small discussion settings instead of in big lectures.  481 was really hard to sit through for the whole semester but 490 was one of my favorite classes.  He makes pretty difficult tests, but it's not hard to at least get a B.

I took two classes with Vargas simultaneously (481 & 490) and find him really entertaining and helpful.  His classes are difficult and require a lot of reading/note taking outside of class, but his classes are entertaining.  Yes, he goes off topic a lot, but that's what makes his classes fun.  He's really helpful if you talk to him in person.

Vargas is a controversial teacher. Students either like him or loathe him. Class is interesting, but yes, the stuff that appears on the test may be quickly went over. There are chances to get points in 481 and emerge with an easy B. Don't freak out when people gripe about the class - you can handle it.

Extremely difficult class. While he seems interested in what he's teaching you, it's often irrelevant to all tests and textbook material. The exams are extremely specific and very tricky rather than fair.

Class is entertaining but you don't actually learn the material. Tests are ridiculous; you're responsible for lecture and textbook (even what he doesn't cover). He refuses to put any slides on compass, and provides no study guide/outline for the tests.

Vargas is a great teacher of social pyschology, an essential ingrediant of advertising. He relies on the students to contribute to class, but when they falter he has a ton of interesting and knowledgable subejcts to discuss. Take his class if you are majoring in ADV.
i feel like im a math major now .. argggg

I took the Psychology of Advertising class. It was Vargas's first time teaching the course, so it was fairly disorganized; however, he is just an amazing professor so it didn't matter! So hilarious and fun to talk to. Not bad to look at, either.

Vargus is amazing. Fun & interesting class. Lectures are interesting and he is hilarious. Tests are hard and the final project is a ****. Whatever, you have no choice of taking the class. It's required.

He was an amazing teacher and really introduced me to advertising. It was great when the first day of class was to try 3 shots of vodka and they were all the same and see what perception could do. I was completely in awe and I thought he made learning research an amazing thing!
So funny.
Amazingly smart and interesting guy.  As well as great to look at!
worst. class. ever. didnt help that he was more focused on making sexual references to everything than actually helping us understand the material.

Vargas is engaging and well-prepared.  he keeps it interesting and i've never liked the material he taught, but i was always interested and i genuinely enjoyed lecture.  deep respect for him, and he's very helpful and friendly!

Vargas was really chill. I had him for the intro seminar Fall 2006 called the Psychology of Advertising. Read the books and connect the papers with the reading. The class was long but he's a really smart and cool guy. He likes when you speak up and tell him different things about you. Really intelligent dude. Weird but smart.

this man is a great teacher, is funny, helpful, clear, and last but not least, he's a hottie.  my only complaint of the class is that i  sometimes wasn't able to concentrate because i was staring at his charming smile.  if only he wasn't married...
No Comments
His class is so refreshing... tells the best stories. But the class is still hard!
No Comments
i love this man
No Comments
He is GORGEOUS!!!!!!!!!!!!!
just finished the last class with professor Hillmer, he is everything the other ratings talked about. please consider taking this class if you have any interest in philosophy at all.
Professor Hillmer is the best professor I've had at UIUC. He's inspirational and helps you find life purpose.

Graduated in 2000, so I took his class approximately 25 years ago... one of those professors that I like to look up every-now-and-then just to see what he's up to.  It's been half my lifetime since I had any interaction with him... but what I wouldn't give just to sit and talk philosophy with him sometime.  Such an amazing professor and man.

I am writing this review 10 years after taking this course. I just googled him because his kindness left a lasting impression on me. You will be lucky to have met this man. Nurture a good, respectful relationship with him and you will learn about philosophy and life. Journey continues

Prof. Hillmer might be my favorite professor at UIUC. He's amazing, caring, and kind-hearted. Very understanding of everyone's situations and one of the best lecturers. Even if it's a boring lecture his projected voice makes it interesting! If you are deciding between this and CS 210 definitely take this course
Very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Hillmer is a great professor but teaching a difficult class. Definitely harder than other advanced comp classes and only should be taken if ready to write very long papers.

Hillmer has great ratings, because he's an interesting man and will give you an A. If you are an individual who is grounded in logic and reality, there is a slim chance that you will actually get anything out of this class. His 80 min classes are 60 min of fussing about, 20 minutes of confusing, stream-of-conscious lecture. Great man, Bad teacher.
Professor Hillmer is somewhere between "goofy" and "eccentric". Show up to class, write the dozens of papers, and you'll probably get an A.

I will never forget this class.  In all honesty, I think it was the best class I took at UIUC.  Every person I recommended to take this class came back thanking me time and time again.  Some topics were rough at times (ppl have diff interests), but at the end, I was glad I stuck it through.  Take it, and you'll never regret it, guaranteed
The journey with professor Hillmer was amazing. He's an incredibly nice guy and cares about every each one of the students.

Prof. Hillmer was incredibly helpful in teaching the class, and I came away with a much better understanding of ethics and philosophy. I only had one issue with the class: I didn't care for his use of the causality proof for the existence of a god, as this argument is flawed. Unfortunately, theology took front stage in some discussions on ethics.
Professor Hillmer's journey is a must take! Best class I'll ever take at UIUC!
Best teacher I've had. He is very helpful and he listens and talks well of every student that is in his class.
Amazing course and professor. So fair and understanding to students. Got an A fairly easily
Excellent professor, very understanding.  Highly recommended.

Professor Hillmer is easily the best professor I have ever had. He teaches the ECE ethics course and does a remarkably good job at it. He is very enthusiastic and care greatly for his students. His course is advanced composition but it was still not too much work. I am very glad I took his class and that I got the chance to meet him.
Great lecture and high curve

He is an amazing professor. He explained all concepts really clear and proved everything to you step by step. His homework is proof-heavy which is nice for training abstract math problem solving ability. His exams are computation-heavy (no calculator), so be careful with calculations! He is generous with time during exam and generous with grading.

Super knowledgeable and passionate with well structured lectures. Always open to questions during or after lecture. Responsive and understanding regarding students' difficulties during online learning. Exams were somewhat computation heavy for an abstract class, but not a bad thing.
Best math professor I've had at UIUC
Guy is very passionate and a really nice guy. I wish I went to class more and signed up for a later section though. Reallly smart guy but sometimes a bit confusing when explaining concepts.

If his lectures were recorded, i would listen to them to go to sleep. Extremely boring. the labs and main group project are very useful, and will teach you CAD. i dont think lecture content really mattered, but at least you can watch the pretty sunrise from the CIF windows.

Prof. Philpott is a nice guy, but not a good lecturer. I'm sure some of the things he said were important, but I would struggle to recall a single thing I learned in lecture. Overall the class is pretty easy but picks up in workload near the deadline for the final project. Just pray you have a good group or you'll be stuck doing the whole project.

He is the only professor offered for ME170 and only offers annoying 8am slots, topped by a monotonous voice that will put you to sleep. You don't really get much out of the lectures but the class itself is so incredibly easy that you don't even have to pay attention during the lectures, as long as you follow the instructions during the labs.

The only cons to this class are the 8am lecture lol, but other than that i loved this class and got to use my imagination for the final project. He does have lecture class assignments so you are required to go but they are interesting. Great class overall

Wanna have a fun semester? Take a shot every time he says "APriori". Seriously though, Prof Philpott is great. He clearly knows his stuff but his 8 am lectures makes the class rough. Just do the lecture and cad lab assignments properly, don't procrastinate on your final project, and you'll get an A even if you get a terrible team like me.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Although the 8AM lectures are very rough to get up for and may be slightly boring, Philpott is extremely educated with CAD and overall is a lenient and nice professor. As long as you put in some effort and get decent group-mates, you are almost guaranteed an A in the class.

Philpott is very passionate but his lectures are very heavy. He moves quickly and expects students to understand/apply stuff he barely goes over. He gives lots of free points and isn't a tough grader because he understands it's everyone's first design class. Just pray that you get a good group for the project or this class is 5x more stressful!
Great Professor who is passionate about his field. Is an expert. However, you may skimp on the books he suggests.

Professor Philpott is a nice guy. The lectures are rough at 8am, and he gives in class assignments to make sure people show up. This was the only bad part about the course. The class is largely graded by lab assignments and a final group design project. It's an easy A if you show him that you do the work and think about your project.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class itself is really easy, it's just 3D modeling, even with no prior experience it should still be an easy 8. Philpott knows 8 ams are rough, so he is a real bro about it and gives away answers for in-class assignments which will boost your grade. Overall, he really knows his stuff and despite the early class time I was never bored in lecture

The 8 am lecture was rough, and his voice kinda makes you wanna go to sleep during it. That being said, if you show up to lecture and do the assigned homework, you shouldn't have too hard of a time in the class. Also, there is a group project at the end of the semester, so be prepared to devote time to that.

Philpott is a really chill guy. 8am is a bit rough, but he gives you the answers to the lecture class assignments. Pretty easy class since you just follow a textbook to do the lab assignments. Design project at the end is a lot of work, but it's not bad.
It sucks that this lecture is at 8 am, however he gives answers to all the homeworks if you show up. Irregular grading scale (lower percents = higher grades) which is very nice

Ok so Philpott is a pretty cool person. I've learned CREO before taking this course so it isn't hard. Basically all what you are going to learn in this course is in the lab and from the textbook. Here's some advice: Go to every lab and sign in, do exactly what the textbook tells you to do, submit every inclassassignment in time and you'll get an A.
Brilliant man. Awesome person. Granted, lectures are a little dry for 8 a.m., but it's not his fault. Take a class with him if you get the chance.

Lectures are optional in my opinion. The material covered in lectures is about manufacturing and is never tested on. The true material is learned during labs (how to use CAD software), which is for a grade.

Easy. Don't have to go to class. If you do go, you get the answers to the homework. Go to lab and get your work done and is an easy A. Just have to hear him clear his throat a lot, but there are worse things.

Pretty good class overall.  You learn a lot more than you think.  You don't learn much from lectures, but sometimes he'll do the homework during them, so that's nice.  Real chill guy-brings a lot of prior knowledge to the class, which can be interesting at times.  You learn much more in the Labs than from Lecture.

Obsessively clears his throat. Pushes his software almost every class. Didn't really learn much in lecture, but there are in-class quizzes. Labs always took me more than two hours. It's really an easy class, though. You should get an A. It's just extremely annoying.

The guy loves his accomplishments. He loves to tell you about his software he made...which sadly i can tell you the name of it and who uses it and why because...hes told us so many times. ITS SO BORING. but, the class is quite easy and the labs make sense the way they are layed out so...good job.Easy grading scale though
Easy A. Show up for quizzes, if you sleep in have a friend do it. Professor is nice and helpful, his accent is awesome, the chairs and too comfortable and you will doze off.

Extremely boring teacher, but you still have to show up to 8 am class because there are in-class quizzes. I would either bring homework to do during class, or I would just go to sleep. I learned the most from doing the labs, and from my TA.

Philpott is a cool and nice guy but his class is extremely boringgg!!! I hate going to lecture but overall the class was easy because the labs make up a huge % of points. Labs are easy if you follow instructions. Quizzes r hard and unpredicatable so you have to show to every lecture. I don't think there was ever a single lecture that i stayed awake

Good guy and I realize he can't help it, but his lectures are SO BORING. Labs are straightforward. Easiest class I've taken so far. In class quizzes are a pain in the butt, but they aren't difficult. Show up for the quiz and take a 50 minute nap.

Class is 8am and there are graded quizzes given in class.  Hard to stay awake because the lectures are boring, but he tries to make things exciting.  Hes a very cool guy and is extremely nice.  He is my academic adviser as well and hes awesome.  Knows everything about pro/e.  Good lecturer, and his british accent helps u stay awake

The class is really boring and it sucks that it's at 8am.  If you have ever used any CAD or 3D modeling programs before then the lectures are basically pointless but he gives out quite a few in class quizzes so it's a good idea to go.  Philpott explains things well but it's easy to figure everything out in the lab section.

Brilliant guy, knows his stuff, admits that he wishes the lecture wasn't at 8am.   Ask him about his research, it's amazing!  Seems to have trouble remembering faces so if you say hi to him out of  class you might get a blank stare.

DFM can be a pretty dry course, but Philpott makes it interesting for the most part. Loves to show videos in lecture. The homework can be a bit tedious, but the exams are fair and he'll let you use an index card for notes. He knows the material very well and actually does this stuff in industry, so you'll learn a lot.

This class bored me to tears. But I was in no way interested in learning about proEngineer. At first you might think his accent makes him interesting but you'll soon find the sound to be monotonous and dull. He seems to understand though that there is not much to learn during the lecture but  go if you want the 15% of your grade from lecture quizes

This class was pretty interesting as a whole. The 8am lectures with Philpott were a little boring to say the least, but he realized it was boring too, so he cancelled a lot. You should probably just stay in bed. The final presentation was pretty fun, and watching him react to what some people presented was hilarious, especially if they were stupid.

Way cool guy. He's from England, which makes the common phrases he uses exponentially funnier. He's the kind of dude you could see having a beer with. It's a pity his class is at 8:00am -- I would have preferred to be awake for his lectures, since they were on-point and told you what you needed to know.

Philpott is a very good teacher for the ME 170 course. He really knows his material and is very helpful. He tries to put a lot of necessary material in the lectures which are difficult at 8 am. Throws pop quizes once in a while. Important to go to lectures. They will pay off in the long run.

First of all; Very hot british accent. 8am class, but the sound of the accent keeps me awake. Hes a great teacher. If you go to him for extra help, he is very keen on helping. And he definetly sound like he knows his stuff!
Great guy, very approachable. Hard to stay awake at 8am lecture, but most of the learning is done in the lab anyway. Always hear only good things about him.

Well he is a really nice guy, has a great british accent, and will talk to you if you want to talk to him about ANYTHING.  Only thing is that in ME 170 almost all learning is done in the lab so his part in the process is minimal and hard to stay awake during if you have it early in the morning.
Nice guy, he puts his everything into the class. Experienced Fellow.
Good lecturer, but tough to stay awake at 8am.  This class is mostly learned in the lab, but Philpott tries to explain the difficult parts at class.
cool guy. easy going

The class is fun, but the lectures are very dry. Just try and stay awake. He'll throw pop quizzes at you for attendance purposes in lecture, so go. Really cool guy who will always help you out if you need it.
His lectures are boring as hell but, having worked with him in the Ford Lab, I can personally say he's a really cool guy.
Cool, but lectures are boring
balding :(
He is unclear with his instructions, and gives terrible feedback on essays and papers. One of my least favorite teachers ever in my academic career.

He's a smart guy, that loves to show it. The assignments were vague and his reasoning for grading was impossible to follow. If you visit office hours and get as much info as to what he wants, then you'll do well. However, he pretty much wants your analyzes to follow what his ideas are. Not a lot of room to interpret things your own way.

It is extremely important to meet your deadlines. Although I met mine and received an A in the course, many of my friends lost letter grades for forgetting to respond to online convos. That noted, the material's extremely interesting and abstract. Ernstmeyer breaks it down pretty well while maintaining interest.
Awesome class, awesome dude.

This class in no way represents a 100 level. It is way too involved and is not worth the work just for a gen-ed requirement. Phillip is condescending and refuses to explain topics in a way that undergraduates can understand. It also is not rewarding when the teacher constantly tells students that they are wrong.

This class was challenging, but Prof. Ernstmeyer was always available to help clarify any confusion and would gladly take questions in class.  We were expected to discuss poems in detail, make well-informed interpretations, and recognize poetic devices and styles.  This class was one of my favorites, and Prof. Ernstmeyer really knows his stuff.
Very knowledgeable and well spoken on the subject matter.

Phillip was an excellent instructor. He obviously spent a great deal of time and energy preparing for the course and each class. He was always willing and able to meet outside of class to discuss the texts and other ideas. He is very intelligent, kind, helpful, dedicated and a good listener-always turning student comments into class discussions.

One of my favorite professors. I could tell he is extremely interested and knowledgeable in what we were covering in class. He always encouraged participation and discussion, but had his own points to make to ensure we understood why we read what we did for the day. Personable and very helpful. I highly recommend him.

fantastic teacher, especially in the poetry survey field. extremely knowledgable about the content of the class and an overall very pleasant fella. I highly recommend taking a poetry class with this man if you actually want to get something out of the class.
Incredibly intelligent and interesting to listen to. You will enjoy whatever subject he is teaching. Wu-Tang for life.

I couldn't have asked for more from Phillip's Poetry Since 1940 course. His dedication to the class is, honestly, astounding. He does a fantastic job of leading a class discussion that draws on student feedback but is still focused. Super available and willing to help. His love for the poetry we covered is infectious. Brilliant course.

Awesome professor. Class involves a lot of reading & writing but that is obvious. Be prepared to re-write essays multiple times. Nonetheless, great, cool professor who talks a lot but really helpful if you ask for help! Go to his office hours, he really helps & won't mind helping you! Class might not be that interesting, but this teacher rocks!

Great professor! I hope to take one of his classes in the future. He is incredibly smart and intersting, and quite amusing at times. Poetry will take on quite a new meaning for you if you take this class. It will be difficult at times but that's how college is. I doubt you will regret taking his class.

I always looked forward to this class! Phillip is a very genuine and intelligent teacher. He was always willing to meet with students and eager to hear various interpretations of the poems we read. The course included a refreshing variety of poets instead of the dead white male norm. The expectations were very clear, making it easy to do well.

Great class! If you attend class, participate and turn in all assignments on time you will be very successful! There are no actual letter grades. Grading is based on if you meet the deadlines and participation. Although there are no grades, he still gives tons of feedback on assignments so you can easily see how you're doing!

Negatives: 30% of your grade is ambiguous because it's partcipation and overall improvement in course. Prompts and explanations of them can be confusing at times. Positives: VERY HELPFUL especially at conferences. 70% turning in papers on time. No grades. Just lot of postive criticism that help you improve as a writer.
his commentary was really harsh but you get to grade yourself

Philip, is probably one of the most intelligent people I have ever met.  His grading is a little vague and ambiguous, therefore I have no idea how I am doing.  Everyone in advanced comp does not care about the material they just want their grade and be done with the requirement.  His assignments are harsh and somewhat unrealistic.
Excellent teacher. If your lazy, deuce out of that class quickly.The course is easy in that your not graded on content, but rather promptness and effort. Funny dude.

Cool professor that may use swear words but hard class. You will have to  put a lot of hours into writing long essays. Attendance not mandatory but turning homework 1 day late= 1/3 of a letter grade reduction. Hard but not impossible class, just thons of hours writing and revising papers. Talks too much for too little material. Helpful though, ok.

Possibly the hottest teacher I've ever had. Not only that but he was damn good at his job. I absolutely adore this man. He gets very into the class and the readings and is incredibly intelligent. I had a lot of interesting conversations with him and he taught me a lot. If you just ask him for help he will definitely help and you will do well.

Very good teacher, obviously will not be an "easy" A, but if you do the things he tells you to do you will be just fine. A good teacher and extremely knowledgeable. If you take his class, be prepared to write a several papers.

Phillip was an excellent TA. He knew the material and explained it well while using his humor to keep the class active. We also got to watch Boohbah one day, haha. I definitely recommend taking his class. Plus, he's hella' attractive.

Cool guy. He takes attendance every class. But the majority of class is spent watching clips from movies. The course consists of two papers, a midterm, a final, and weekly quizzes over the movie of the week. It's nothing unmanageable, I didn't do much and somehow ended up with an A-.
One of the harsher grading teachers. His prompts are overly complicated too, but you will become a better by the end. Not a hard class, just not the "easy A" most RHET 105 classes are

The lectures are incredibly boring and not really applicable to much of the work in the class. You will learn CAD from this class, but it is mostly self taught through the labs. The class is not hard to do well in, I had no CAD experience and my group's project sucked, but if you meet the requirements you will get a good grade.

His ME170 lectures are more than boring and meaningless. He immersed himself in his own world. Also, when he has some problems for the class, he never listen to his students and refuse any advice. Maybe he earns enough for his life and not care about students anymore.
Dude literally can't stop talking about his program aPriori. Other than that, he is pretty hard to listen to for an entire lecture, but the class itself is easy if you go and do your labs.
Really boring class especially at 8am, which is the only time it was offered. Class in general is very easy. Learn Creo and Apriori and you will be completely fine for the labs and the project.

ME 170 is extremely easy.  There are in class assignments that are guaranteed 100% if you are in class, no tests, and the rest of the class is a lab.  In the lab you follow the book step by step.  The last four or so weeks of the semester are a group design project.  Lectures are somewhat dry but you have to tough it out for the assignment credit.
Amazing professor. Knows the material inside out and makes classes very enjoyable.
Very active outside the class communications. Prompt in answering any doubts.

The lectures are very good, but their relevance to the actual assignments and quizzes is lacking. You are pretty much on your own for assignments, because it seems like they dont have answers themselves.

Good lectures with some humor scattered about. This was an online course so I was surprised by his quick responses in the student forums. His explanations are clear and helpful. His course includes a particularly challenging routing assignment that provides good opportunities to learn.
super cool teacher, recommend his CS538 and CS241
clear lecture! nice person
Very clear on his lecture, coolest professor I've met.
interesting guy
Chillest Prof you can ever have. Amazing Guy.
Great teacher

This was my easiest class this semester. All you have to do is participate and try. The class is different because you have to get out your comfort zone (if you've never taken a dance class), but there isn't anything difficult or technical about it. Don't slack off, though. It's an easy A, but you have to put in the work on tests and projects.

I loved having this class in the morning. A great way to start off the day and very relaxing. It could get pretty weird though because of all the partner work, but it was very unique and different. You will love Professor Johnston and his TA. Would recommend.
He does not give homework and his class is easy. However, if you miss one of his class or answer the questions incorrectly in his midterm , you could probably not get an A.

I was expecting to dance. We rolled around on the floor and massaged each other literally the entire time. It was awkward and boring. But the quizzes are insanely easy (i memorized the study guide while walking to class and got 100% on all of them) and same with exams. Easy easy easy A.

I was looking forward to dancing in this class, at least simple steps, but we ended up pretty much rolling across the floor the whole time or massaging our classmates. It was definitely an easy A though. Study guides are given for the weekly reading quiz and the midterms. You also have to attend 6 performances, which can be slightly annoying.

Great teacher!! Really enjoys what he is doing. You have a quiz every lab, but they are super easy! Tops like 5 questions per quiz and he sends you the study guide so you can pass! Honestly one of my favorite classes, it relaxes me so much, and I also enjoyed the shows very much! I recommend everyone to take it:)

I was really nervous for this class when I found out what it entailed, but I ended up having a blast! He's a great guy and has so many fascinating stories to share! Also the lab was a rejuvenating start to my morning!I recommend it.

He's such a great teacher! You'll absolutely love taking this class with him. There is quite a bit of writing for this class, but it isn't hard. Also, the cost of watching performances is $10-$20 and you have to watch 5-6 of them. He gives a lot of extra credit, so don't worry. Take this class if you can!
Dr Pillai is a ray of sunshine in the storm that is UIUC chemistry department. Her lectures are awesome, exams are tough but fair if you grind enough.

She is a very nice professor, however the class is so test heavy. Often the tests are harder than promised. I wish we had more practice tests like orgo i. But i think content wise she knows what shes talking about and answers questions well. You should know core orgo concepts really well before taking this class.
very good profeseeer -- thank you Smitha Pillai for everything
Genuinely one of the best science professors Ive had. She's so kind and caring. Dr. Pillai is da goat

I took the class Spring 2025 out of pure interest and don't regret it. Dr. Pillai is super kind and invested in your success. Nothing about the class is in an attempt to trick you. If you simply show up to class, ask questions, study, and actually get to know the professor, you're realize you can be really successful. Do it!

Favorite professor I've had in college. She explains difficult concepts very clearly, and the midterms closely reflect the course material. She is very accessible during office hours and genuinely cares about her students, making organic chemistry feel less intimidating and even enjoyable.
Such a caring professor. Goes above and beyond for her students. Very clear when explaining concepts. 10/10 recommend.

She's a wonderful professor. The concepts obviously are hard as this is an upper-level course, but she makes it very clear she is willing to help whenever needed. Lectures available through video, review sessions are very helpful. She does re-grades on exams. Go to the reviews, do the practice worksheets and watch the lectures and you'll do fine.
She is a very amazing professor.
Very clear about what she was teaching and material being tested. Lectures were organized with no unnecessary asides or wasted time. Very good understanding and accessible for regrades.

Assignments were straightforward but the exams were super hard and the questions were so open-ended that it was difficult to do well on them. Plenty of extra credit opportunities but the credit was negligible compared to the weight of exam scores. Lectures were interesting though. There's a textbook but you don't really need it if you go to class.

The lectures are very heavy, and the teacher does ramble, but I skipped a lot of the classes, didn't pay attention in lectures, didn't read the textbook pages, and still passed the class with an A. All the resources are posted on Canvas, and it's not very difficult to understand the material without attending class.

super nice prof but unfortunately lectures are just heavy rambling. 20 minutes is spent on recap and then she begins teaching but it is not super coherent or all that interesting. youll have to balance the trouble of locking in for open ended exams and trying to stay awake during class to listen to her lectures
I did not like this class because I didn't learn anything that wasn't in the textbook. It felt useless to go to lecture. Her grading isn't really clear and it's hard to get 100% on any assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice professor but a very strict grader. Her exams are very open-ended ended making them harder to study for. Attendance is not mandatory, but if you don't listen to the long PowerPoint presentations, it'll be harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was nice but not a good teacher. Her lessons didn't feel organized and lectures felt not coherent. Also her class was heavily based on participation which makes no sense when the lecture is that big.
Meh teacher

She's a nice person and course content is easy, but her grading system is awful. No feedback is given when points are taken off on writing assignments. There's a rubric, but it's literally three bullet pts. Test questions are lecture based and vague. She's big on participation. Textbooks rarely used so save your money

Just was not an interesting course and she's new and it's kind of clear. Her slides aren't great and her lectures don't feel coherent. It feels like she goes in without a plan and it doesn't feel like the information is presented in an effective manner. She also puts a heavy emphasis on participation which makes no sense for a 100ish person lecture
Really great professor, one of the most caring teachers I have had

Structure: 4 (50 pt tests, 10 pt essays, 10 participation pts) + 15 extra credit pts. Her lecture skills need some work (talks around a point), PPTs also need work (either too much or little info). Tests are easy and based on lectures. Participation required even though there's over 100 people in the class-annoying. Every point counts. 7/10 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Enjoyed his lectures and kept up with the content well. Fair amount of work for a 100-level class, but very doable. Keep up on the assigned readings for each lecture/discussion, as there will be pop writing assignments on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: enjoyed it the lecture was interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: his teaching was hard to follow, and he was strict on no technology and paying close attention. The work itself wasn't insane, but you have to stay caught up with the readings because his way of keeping attendance is with random writing assignments. Due to the fact that there are barely any assignments, if you do bad once you're cooked
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (Context: I write untainted from the end-of-semester events.) I think this is the most rigorous section of 416 there is. A friend sent me the 416H final exam, ours is so much deeper. Rigor comes in multiple ways. The content is hard, advances quickly, builds upon itself. But also there is a lot of homework. Probably too much. Albin is a great prof.
He is such an incredibly nice person and truly cares so much about every student. Definitely one of my best math Professors ever.
generous grading
Too much homework.
Very kind, helpful. Taken with online breakout rooms with the lecture being YouTube videos, and you could drop the final if you get a B on all the midterms.
One of the best math teachers

The course was easy. You could easily get an A in the course and not take the final if you get B's on all the midterms. The lectures were recorded and online, as well as hand-written. In class, we would often do group work and he would hop from breakout rooms. Very easy to catch up. Personally, Professor Albin was a very respectful and kind person.

Genuinely the worst math teacher/professor I've had. It was an online class so there a good chunk of work had to be put in outside of the allotted time. His videos were very unengaging and theory based, so they made no sense. If you're someone who is not a theory heavy person, I would avoid him at all costs. Also, be wary of the CBTF for exams.

Speaking from a perspective of someone taking his class online: I guess he is a nice person, but his youtube videos are bad. Like he skips so many steps without any kind of explanation. It is helpful to look at his videos as a review when you have understood the contents before, but definitely not when you are trying to learn new stuff.

The online class turned out to be just watching youtube videos. The time slot of lectures became his office hour. I don't pay tens of thousands of dollars just to watch Youtube vidoes. I genuinely don't think the videos are helpful neither. I just ended up having to ditch all of my ECON class to go to the in-person lectures of the other professor.

overall nice and smart professor. but you really need get ready to do A LOT OF WORKS if you are gonna choose his section. His logic jumps really fast and sometimes you need to pause the video and think by yourself cause he will just briefly explain things seems obvious for him but those may not be straightforward for us
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Albin is wonderful! He can always answer your questions patiently and give great lectures. Zoom meetings are mandatory. A lot of homework but practice a lot from them. There will be practice exams for online midterms and online finals.
A lot of hw. I wrote like 20 pages per week, so do not procrastinate. Zoom meetings are mandatory. Really nice professor tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy. Pretty organized and approachable. Exams are medium difficulty. He does not curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best math professor I've had so far! Cares about his students and will answer your questions clearly. Very knowledgeable and comfortable with the subject which made him an excellent teacher. Some TAs I know say he's amazing, so he's clearly respected within the math department. A lot of hw, but we had 2 weeks to do it so it wasn't that bad.
A smart Prof. Cared about student. Easy to communicate.

Professor Albin is very accommodating during the COVID-19 quarantine. He is also very knowledgeable, and can explain things very clearly if you ask the right questions. I personally have a hard time understanding everything in lectures, but other people except me seem to be doing really well in exams so maybe it is my problem. A lot of homework.

The lectures were really enjoyable. He explained abstract ideas in a very systematic way. This was partially credit to the good choice of textbook -- there were a lot of great examples for each concept, and they did really help a lot in later courses.

Professor Albin to my eyes is a true suave gentleman. His lectures were phenomenal and clear. He is a brilliant man and will know the answer to any question in class. The midterms were fair and he will always post a practice exam. The only downside is the amount of homework, as I had to pull an all nighter every week before homework was due.
Great lectures, very inspiring, but very heavy and very hard homework. He made me realized that math is non-trivial, but I am a trivial man.

Try to avoid him! He leaves you tons of difficult homework to do but only grades a small portion of them(randomly). it's like u complete 7/10 of problems correctly, but the grader only counts the other 3 wrong-answer-problems.  And there is a huge difference between his lecture and homework/test. Office hour is very crowded and useless. No curves.

In terms of teaching, his teaching is pretty standard. Math 417 is a difficult course and per math stackexchange the best way to learn the material is do as many exercises as possible;  the amount of homework makes sense, but it is cumbersome. Midterm 2, 38% got an F  33% got an A. The course is time consuming

Since 417 is a tough course, he has done his best to help students to learn it well. He assigns lots of homework but grader only grades part of them. However, the homework only counts for 25%, and he gives easy exams with bonus question, which makes it possible to get more than 100 in exams. After Exam 1, 50% of students are in A range.

Wonder why he got so many positive comments. Worst math professor so far. Leave you tons of nonsense borin homework to do, which means you need to spend about 10 hours in 2 days to hand them in. Only grade a small portion of the hw so that you cannot have your work respected and receive valuable feedback. Drop the class and don't waste your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: By far the best math prof I've had so far! Lectures are challenging and rewarding.  Albin always has the answer to any question and is very well respected by students.

Probably my favorite math professor so far.  Overall very good.  He very deliberately went through the material, but also was super willing to go back and answer questions from the class.  I really appreciated the historical anecdotes he threw into lectures about where the math came from.  Best math class here so far.

Amazing teacher, crazy brilliant.  Sometimes it's hard to follow his work, but he will definitely go back and explain *if you ask him to*  Always excited to go to his lecture and try to learn; he is an excellent teacher for an incredibly hard class.
He is one of the best teachers in the math dept., and is very organised. Do not miss class and then definitely easy A. Do not miss class you will have to put in now work outside class.
By far one of the best teachers in the math dept., knows the material very well and can answer questions really well.
Clear in lecture and always be prepared for any question.
She does not plan her lessons. She seemed to be lost when she was "teaching."
very caring & helpful professor.
i enjoyed her SLA class. she is so knowledgable.

Had her a few years back. At first thought she was fun and engaging. Over the semester she seemed less and less cating about the class and was passive aggressive towards a few student and even openly shamed a few. Also basically just threw us on a website instead of instructing not to mention didnt upload a rubrick and was pissed when called on it.

I would never take this course again. Pierce often appeared unprepared to teach and frequently seemed lost in class. Additionally, I found her grading to be very unfair, and her behavior to be inconsistent, swinging from very friendly to passive-aggressive without warning.
She was such a cool professor. She taught me a few classes in Ling department; they were all fun.
Professor Pierce was very disorganized and her classes were improvised. She did not seem to care about her students.

She is a very friendly professor. She listens and tries her best to understand her learners. She is also funny and excited. I never got bored in her classes. Her class site is a bit disorganized though. I felt seen and super comfortable in her classes, which is essential. I wish she stayed longer. I hope she enjoys her retirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Hodson does not grade anything, and the course is essentially self-guided. Providing no feedback on any assignments, Hodson is uninvolved and unhelpful.

Regarding content, the resume and cover letter practice taught in the course is useful, and I liked the practice of exploring career choices, but I felt there was quite a bit of busy work.

Don't take 108 if you want to build your "professional skills" unless you want to learn how to work with an unavailable and uncaring boss/manager. Modules are rarely posted on time and are often incomplete or empty. Most examples are 5+ years old and don't reflect the current market. Grades aren't entered 2+ months after class end/due date.

Easy course. There aren't any tests, but the final project is time-consuming. She doesn't really keep up with grading assignments though. The class consisted of posting on a discussion board and some career type of assignments. Mostly working on your resume, cover pages, KSAE, etc.

This is the second time I've had Professor Hodson and she has not changed. She never posts the lesson material when she's supposed to and is no help. Her classes are extremely easy, but she makes them so frustrating for no reason.
An easy class overall but did not receive grades back until the last minute, not very accessible outside of class, and a lot of work to but into an online one credit hour class.
Too much work required weekly and little to no direction for assignments

NRES 108 does not require a large amount of work. The best part, It is all about yourself and discovering what you want to do for a career. There is a discussion and homework assignment each week and a final paper.

Worst professor. Never responded to emails. Assignments were not graded until the last week of the semester. No feedback throughout the whole semester to prepare for the final project and exam. Also does not seem qualified to teach research methods to masters students.

This was a great class as we had the opportunity to teach kids at a local elementary school for 8 weeks. However, I felt as if there could have been more direction. We had to create lesson plans and give a final presentation & mock interview for the final without much instruction. It really was a lot of work for a 2 credit hour class.
This man taught be how to skibize the fluid mechanics into perfection. 10/10. Would take again.
This dude is the SIGMA! He grades fair and loves talking about Brainrot and Hawk Tuah! Spit on that Thang! Overall, Professor Plancon is pretty skibidi and I'd give him 3 big booms.

Professor Plancon did a decent job at teaching our class. You could tell he was very wise but likes to reminisce on his college days and how much he loved "brainrot". Overall this is a tough class but he made it much more enjoyable. He grades too harshly though. Chill out on that Plank.
grading criteria were pretty vague. A lot of lecturing. I did not learn much in the class, but at least it wasn't too hard.

Not sure if I signed up for a Rhet course or a Documenting Inequality course  because we seemed to talk about civil issues more frequently than rhetoric/writing & research. Expectations were unclear and syllabus was inconsistent. Grading is extremely subjective. She lacks conciseness, clarity, and comes off as overly-abrasive and self-proclaiming.
She does not teach CS-210, but I have had her tutoring appointments for my essays. We had good conversations on the essay's structure. She also helped me with grammar mistakes.

She makes a simple paper into an unnecessary amount of work. Not only do you have to write this huge paper, you have to do the weekly emails, weekly reports, connections, and argument mapping. On top of that she still wants to have lecture on long, boring readings that have nothing to do with what anyone is writing. Unnecessary amount of work!!!

If you attend class and genuinely contribute to conversations, Samantha's discussion section will easily become your favorite. She clearly cares about the quality of discussion and works hard to make sure class is worth your time. When she's not teaching, Samantha often meets with students. She's a fabulous reference and a knowledgeable teacher.
AWFUL! She doesn't explain what you need to do.

Very easy coursework, by the syllabus it should be hard.  Got on A, barely read anything, but there was a lot of stuff due.  If you followed diligently you could coast without doing a thing for the last half of the semester.

crapped out an essay at 3 am the day it was due, it wasn't long enough and i forgot half the requirements, I got an A and the third highest grade in the class.  I really have no idea what you'd have to do to get a bad grade out of her but I think her mind is going a bit.  she pauses in the middle of words and loses her train of thought.

I think watching paint dry was far more exciting than her class: her lectures are impressively boring. I took "Gender History until 1877" which is truly only about white women in New England, Mayflower-1877. Tests are pretty easy: IDs and essays, however her assignment grading style is very arbitrary.

She is a wonderful Professor and easy to talk to. You just need to reach out to her and show that you care. The material is interesting too. Basically Pleck's classes are what you make of them. If you're going to have a bad attitude, than you will have a bad experience.

It is really a shame that she is called Professor.  She is an old women who no longer belongs in Academia.  Her class is not interesting and neither is her lessons.  She very rarely understands what she is teaching or the questions being asked in her class.  Overall a pretty awful teacher and a if you can avoid her then I highly recommend it.
The topic of this class was women presidential candidates, and I loved writing 20 pages . . . but as a professor, I learned nothing from her.

She is an old lady that doesnt really seem to know what shes doing.  I can never really judge how I did on tests and essays because her grades seem to be sporadic and random.  She is very technologically challenged also.  Pretty nice lady though overall.
This class was pretty easy with a light workload for a 400 level history class. The material was interesting, but she was kind of a hard grader with papers

Scatterbrain is the word. This woman's head runs on her own wavelength and doesn't slow down for anyone. She's very friendly, a bit whacky, really knows her stuff, but makes you work for your grade. She's one of the few professors out there who deliberately challenges her students. Her mindless thought trails during class can be quite entertaining.
Kind of a scatter brain...doesnt really know how to stick with one train of thought...
No Comments
No Comments
Tough grader. Very picky. She's fantastic at explaining. You can really tell she's doing what she loves.

She is a great instructor and if you follow along in lectures it isn't too difficult to stay on track. Math 285 itself is a well structured course and it does a good job helping students learn fairly difficult content. However, the auto-graded exams can be frustrating, as you may get no credit for showing your work if you made one small mistake.
Prof. Yu was an absolute gem. Her lectures were so clear, and it was very apparent that she cared about her students. Attend lecture and you will do well!

The professor was very enthusiastic about teaching and helped us learn through examples, which is the best way to learn this subject. I felt confident about the midterms and the final. She is also accessible through flexible office hours, during which she thoroughly covers each topic. Overall, she is the best math professor I've had at UIUC!

Dr. Polly Yu is amazing!!! Her lectures are so detailed and have a lot of practice problems, and she is very good at explaining the content. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it is worth it to go. She also gives hints about what type of questions are going to be on the midterms and final during class. She is definitely my fave prof. so far at uiuc!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was ok. Don't feel like writing more.
Title IX needs to look into him.

The worst Game Theory class ever. Hard to understand what he is trying to convey. He spend two hours talking about Nash Equilibrium and I still could not understand it. However, I just spend 5 minutes read the book and everything is much more clear. He talks in a plain tone, so many of us fall asleep easily in the lecture.
Good lectures, homework is hard but few.

Great professor! However, lectures can wander off topic quite often. Doesnt give too much work, and nice curve. Homeworks can be difficult be are very interesting as he challenges you to come up with sometimes odd solutions to tricky problems.
Should retire
It is totally incomprehensible to read slides, with strange mathematical symbols and confusing letters.

This was the worst professor I've ever had. His complete lack of care for this course and his students were obvious. Good luck ever getting a real explanation to a question from him. Don't even waste your time trying to have a real discussion. Avoid his class at all costs!

The mathematical notation is disaster. You will waste 3-5 hours to understand what exactly he try to express. He always make easy concept 3 times more complicated. The slide make me feel that he try to show off his very bad math.
was absent most of the time and left the class to be taught by teaching assistant professors who refused to answer any questions, gave poor or wrong guidance and wer bia

Easiest materials taught in the most bewildering fashion because of the mathematical notations he uses in his lecture slides are unfathomable. He needs to practice his mathematical notations: superscripts, subscripts, capital letters, lower case letters, greek letters, orders/limits of summation, and everything in between.
Extremely smart, pushes his students to learn everyting!
He's so smart and hot!
THE BEST OF ALL CLASS I HAVE TAKEN MY WHOLE LIFE
This professor is a great example of why the business school is ranked among the worst of the top 50 in terms of quality of classroom instruction.  Enough said.  If you get him, well good luck.
exhilarating

Dr Polites is incredibly caring and truly loves what he does. He has so many pearls of wisdom and truly wants everyone to do well. Its easy to doze off or not pay attention in class but what he has to say is truly important and should be listened to. The class is pass/fail based on just attendance but he is very understanding in emergencies.

Dr. P is super hilarious and an awesome educator! He is very professional, extremely intelligent, and an awesome physician. He deserves an award for his teaching efforts. Glad he teaches the undergrads on the importance of medicine. All of his students love him and he has such a good heart!

Doesn't do her job of being a TA. No knowledge of material. I would drop the class if I ever had her as a TA again. Other students in the class would do a better job of being the TA since at least they pay attention during class.

Literally knows nothing about the education system even though she teaches a curriculum and instruction course. The guidelines are unclear and she is super sassy and takes no accountability for her mistakes. She just blames us when she was the one who was unclear. Would make a good social science teacher but terrible for an education course.

Posey is the worst TA I have ever had the displeasure of 'learning' from. She is unqualified to be teaching a class within COE, and she has no knowledge of the ELED program or teaching. She assigns 8 hours of work a week that she never reads, and she refuses to put due dates on Canvas. She never has any idea what's happening and is honestly mean.

Posey acted defiant towards all students and refused to make any assignments clear and accessible. She contradicted herself nearly every class. She is rude and made students cry. She called us inconsiderate and deflected any opportunities to self-correct or take responsibility for her mistakes.

He is a kind man, but I don't know if his personality is meant to teach a class that is inherently boring in itself. He is incredibly smart and respectable, but I think a difficult class without an outgoing professor does not do very well. A class like this needs someone enthusiastic and relatable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The concepts taught in class can be pretty difficult. Be sure to pay attention and take good notes, because he just writes notes on the board and doesn't use powerpoint. He's a very fair grader and you can do well in the class if you regularly attend class and take good notes.

The class is relatively straight forward, but the concepts are relatively hard to get down. The grading is fair the professor is very helpful when it comes to the overall information. The topic is hard in and of its self. If you are a good note taker you should do fine in the class. He does not slides! So you have to pay attention in class!

Worst professor in Accy I've had. Doesn't reference textbooks nor notes, just assumes we all know what he is talking about. Hard as hell. No lenience in grading. Take Stern, Wang, or Zhou if they're available.
Hard, useless, mean. Impossible to do well.

Worst class I took in the MAS program.  Professor is completely useless, because there is a disconnect between what he teaches (ineffectively, too!) and what's on the examinations.  Appears to be helpful, but is a pretty useless fellow.  Class needs more grade inflation and less pretentiousness
Overall good class. Professor really challenges you to think.
Good person, tough course. However, he was a really fair grader and had reasonable expectations from us. Would take another course with him again.
One of the most boring classes on this campus; sucks that the professor is super dry & lame himself. Exams are very difficult and material is vague.
Passionate and knowledgeable. Exams are fine. Much better class than 250!

Dr. Prasanth is a great professor. It's important to note what he speaks verbally, as everything is fair game for exams. He takes concepts on slides and constantly makes connections and how they relate to problems like cancer which keeps me engaged. He is really funny too which makes the atmosphere welcoming. Very knowledgable, and would take again
Probably the best lecturer in the MCB Biocore series.

An all-around great lecturer. Will teach you the things you need to know although sometimes it's hard to say what you do and don't need on the exams. This class overall shouldn't give you too much difficulty as long as you keep up with lectures. Number one piece of advice: don't buy the textbook. It's free online somewhere and you don't need it.

Prasanth is my favorite MCB lecturer so far. He is great at explaining things, cracks a ton of jokes, and genuinely cares for his students. His tests are extremely fair The only qualm I had is that it can be hard to understand what he is saying because he talks very quickly and has a thick accent, but I just rewatched his lectures slowed down after

Sometimes it was difficult to know what was important and what wasn't on the slides. He does talk pretty fast so it helps to go back an rewatch lectures. I didn't use the textbook but I did go back and rewatch each lecture to review for exams.

The lectures are so disorganized and there is not a clear outline for the lectures. He goes through things really fast which leaves no time to take notes. You will have to rewatch the lectures to really understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are great. He is really good at introducing new topics and thoroughly explaining complex processes and why they're relevant. Those lecture slides with the animations are A1 fam. He does go through things fast; he's being concise covers a lot of material. You will have to rewatch the lecture and/or read the book to get all the details.

He is so knowledgeable and his lectures are so organized. He posts them online which I appreciate. The readings are not mandatory but they really help. Exams are difficult but manageable if you put in the time. I will miss his teaching, not many other professors at this university know what they are doing like he does.

Talks really fast in lectures and explanations are sometimes vague so it's hard to keep up with notes or retain solid conceptual understanding. Tests make up most of the grade (around 75%). Friendly and accessible outside of class, and answers questions during lectures. Could be better, but overall a satisfactory experience in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm taking this class during the pandemic and so far on the course for an A-. I gotta say, the man knows his facts. He's on of the most knowledgeable professors I've ever seen. However, this doesn't work in a students favor. He lectures so fast it's almost too fast to take any notes. Be prepared to study a lot in this class too. Reading required.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor managed to turn interesting Biology topics into a slog. He is not a great lecturer but he seems like a nice guy.
Very boring at times but he explains the material well. Talks a little too quickly, but he posts the lectures online which is nice.

The first half of 252 was honestly my favorite. I loved the pace of the lectures & I honestly learned so much. Once you get used to his accent, you notice subtleties -- his sassiness, for example. Absolutely amusing! I wish Prasanth taught more courses -- enjoy him while his time in course lasts!!!

Pollock was great! Discussion based classes that were truly engaging and broke the material down. I encourage you to participate- but you'll still enjoy class if you don't. Pollocks easy to talk to and gives great feedback. He also gives lots of time to complete papers, offers 1on1 advising, and cancels a full week of classes when a paper is due.

Tony gives fantastic, hilarious lectures. He is incredibly passionate about the material and is super supportive of students. I don't think he has a negative bone in his body. Readings are also super interesting. There is a lot of homework (usually one short response per class) but these are tiny-- he also allows revisions on summative assignments.

Dr. Pollock (Tony) is just about the kindest teacher with whom I have ever worked. In discussions, he is enthusiastic and provides technical jargon to apply to concepts. He also reviews essays 1-on-1 with students and gives helpful feedback. I made this RMP account just so I could give him a perfect score. Take his classes! You won't regret it!

I do not have a bad word to say about Tony. I took this class as a sophomore b/c I just transferred, so it was a little rudimentary and definitely geared towards freshmen transitioning away from high school. However, I got so much out of the class and was able to enjoy it thoroughly. He will give you back as much as you put in, which was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tony was genuinely the best teacher I have ever had in my life. You could tell how passionate he was about the subject matter and how much he wanted us all to succeed. He was always willing to clarify things and give as much help as possible. Overall, his class was an excellent introduction into the English major.

He is very easy to get in touch with and has great policies surrounding absences due to illness. Very receptive to students and takes time to show he cares about students participating in class. 

Homework was not time consuming at all for this course, a great addition to a busy schedule. 

Overall, he is very kind, encouraging, and enthusiastic!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tony is an incredible teacher. His ability to make sure the entire class is engaged in the conversation is incredible. You can tell he takes the time to read his students' responses to the readings because he finds a way to tie in your ideas about the reading. I only say attendance is mandatory because you will not want to miss his class.
Tony is AMAZING! He is so helpful, kind, and caring. I highly recommend going to him outside of class for feedback. He is so accessible and really helpful. Also, he's super passionate!

If you can take a class with Tony, DO IT! He is the best professor I've had here. In ENG 200, he gives you short reading assignments every class and then asks you to write a brief response about the reading, you get credit as long as you do it. He's a pretty easy grader for the couple essays you do as well. He's also super understanding and helpful
Tony is awesome! He cares about his students and really validates all of your ideas. Very intelligent but also very down to earth.
He is really good at getting to know his students. He is good at communicating and helps you improve your writing. Best professor I've had so far.

Great teacher! His lectures were super engaging, even if they were about a topic I wasn't super interested in. He somehow found a way to get almost everyone to participate during lectures; you could tell he genuinely wanted to know your opinion. Most of the assignments were graded on completion and he graded the ones that weren't very easily.

Tony is the best. That's it, that's the tweet. He is exceptionally passionate and knowledgeable about the course material, and it shows in the energy he brings to every class. He treats all students and ideas with enormous respect, and all of his teaching practices encourage genuine intellectual growth. Do yourself a favor and take a course of his.

Absolutely awesome professor! Everyone who gets the opportunity should take a class of his as he is both good at teaching and accommodating! Discussions are helpful for doing well on the essays as they provide a good starting point and guidance.
Great teacher! He's super understanding and doesn't make the class stressful. I always looked forward to coming to his class :)

Tony is absolutely awesome, like really really awesome. If I could take every single english class with tony I would. He gives great feedback on essays, is super easy to reach, and cares a lot about his students. He wants everyone to succeed and it shows.

Tony was a great professor. Took this course as a free elective for a break from my usual STEM courses. This was by far my favorite class this semester. Assignments are very doable and do not require a heavy time commitment. Tony is super passionate about the works we read, so discussion during class is extremely engaging and fun.

Tony was by far my favorite professor this semester. I absolutely loved his class; we read several novels, poems, and wrote about 6 papers. For every class we'd have to email him a journal response on the reading; also, the more in depth your journals, the better your papers would be. He's a great prof and a great guy, and I hope I get him again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: really awesome guy, cares about his students, interesting lectures, encourages class participation, gives a TON of super helpful feedback, one of best professors I have had at this university

Tony Pollock is one of the favorite professors at UIUC. He was very engaging in class, and was super helpful to anyone if they didn't understand the text. Always has a lot of energy. Very understanding if you miss class due to an illness or someone else. 12/10

Absolutely amazing guy. Cares deeply about his students and wants everyone to succeed. 2 short and 1 long-ish paper with an opportunity to revise one for a higher grade. Workload is fine. Highly suggest talking with him in office hours to solidify ideas for essays and chat about class. Highly recommend -- one of the best in English at Illinois.
i love tony. this is the 3rd class i've taken with him. by far the best professor in the english department

Tony is an amazing teacher. He learns every students name and really gets to know them. he is a very fair grader and gives chances to rewrite. He gives awesome lectures and is so funny. He makes the classroom feel very comfortable and he picks great books to read.

Tony is very by far my favorite professor I've ever had. His class is mostly discussion-based but he is so open and non-judgmental about student in-class responses that discussions can be really light-hearted and interesting. He is SUCH a nice guy and I wish he could teach all of my classes.
i love tony. hands down one of the best professors at uiuc. i took engl200 with him and am going to take engl245 with him in the spring. if you get the chance, take his class.
Just an overall great dude. I am a lazy student and i still did well. furthermore, i wanted to do well in his class. He cared a lot so it made me care more.

Tony was very accommodating. If you want to meet with him, he'll work on your schedule. Every paper you turn in to him gets not just initial feedback but he also sends out a personalized paragraph of specific things about your paper that he liked or thinks you could improve on. Very energetic, and he obviously cares a lot about teaching.

Professor Pollock was a great teacher for my first English class at UIUC. He gave great feedback on all of my papers and was really knowledgable on the books he taught. I would highly recommend taking him for ENGL 200.
