Pollock is definitely a great teacher. He tries his best to engage all his students and genuinely cares about each and every one of us. He is a great person and gives good feedback on papers.

Tony is Incredibly smart, yet very down to earth. He's super helpful in office hours, whether it be to talk about a reading, or to get feedback on a rough draft. He grades on a system where you submit a draft, then revise and resubmit with the grade counting twice as much the second time. Above all, stand up guy who made going to a lit class fun.

I feel like this is more of a discussion class than a lecture for sure. I couldn't imagine having any other professor for this class. He's hilarious. Every time he curses catches me off guard. I would recommend Pollock to anyone.

I've already written Tony a review and here I am again. I graduated but still remain fascinated by this man. In 16 years of attending school, he is the best teacher I ever had. I don't care if you don't even need one of his classes to graduate - take it anyway. Spoil yourself by being one of his students. The best of the very best.
Great class! Tony really knows what he's talking about and keeps the discussion flowing and interesting! He made every short story we read in class engaging!

Be in Tony's class is the one of the few most enjoyable things you can do as an adult. He is such a pro to deliver the messages and techniques in the literature, at the meantime engaging your thoughts with optimal respect.

Tony is an amazing teacher. You could tell how passionate he was about the material, and his class was always insightful. Would definitely take another class taught by him. Easily one of the best classes I've taken at U of I so far.

Tony is absolutely a riot. All of his classes were really engaging, hilarious, and he really brought the material down to everyone's level - which is nice considering it's 18th century fiction. If you take a class with him, chances are you won't want to miss a single class because he makes classes so much fun for everyone in the room. He's awesome.

Tony is the best professor and teacher I've had. You will -never- feel afraid to speak in one of his classes. He engages all of his students, and whether in class or email or office hours, you always get the sense that he wants to be doing this and wants to help. Equally hilarious and insightful. This is how an English class should feel.

Tony is easily the best English professor I've ever had and I'm going into my senior year of college. Class was 1.5 hours long but it flew by. He is ALWAYS there for his students, gives INCREDIBLE feedback, and is one of the most patient people I've ever met. Take a class with him if you ever get the chance; swear on my life you won't regret it.

Great teacher. Keeps class interesting and always like to lighten class up if its a boring topic. He can always make the class laugh and helps understand dense materials.  Always helpful at his office hours, genuinely loves the material and will do anything for a student to help them succeed.  If you have opportunity to take a class with him DO IT
I love this guy.  Hilarious and informational.  How have I not discovered him four years ago?

Tony is one of the best professors I've ever had. He immediately engages you with the material and emphasizes an open classroom discussion. He gives awesome feedback on papers and is great to talk to during office hours. ENG 300 was a fantastic class and I 'd recommend taking anything he teaches.

Pollock is one of the greatest English professors here at UIUC. He's refreshing, fun, super excited (it may sound nerdy, but this man really loves teaching what he teaches), and super chill about everything. His classes are engaging and challenge your intuition, but I guarantee you will leave the classroom as a more refined and educated person.
He is really funny and interesting which kept my attention. He is very intelligent and when he teaches, it is always clear. Teachers like him are why I am an English major.
I LOVE this teacher.  By far my favorite I've had so far. Go to his office hours before an exam because he's super helpful. Also, if you can get to know him because he wrote me a great rec letter.
Extremely energetic, tons of fun, and the exams were EASY!

He kept the material entertaining, the discussion lively, and the textbook costs low. He took the time to listen to us despite the fact that we weren't always on the mark, and he learned our names in record time. Great teacher--what more can I say?

Tony was one of the best professors that I have had at the U of I. He made everything really interesting and I actually wanted to read the assigned books. He was also really helpful with papers, and anything else you may have had questions about.
Prof. Pollock is an amazing professor and definately made class interesting. He's a great guy and funny and I'm recommend taking a class with him.

I had never heard of Mary Wollstonecraft or Eliza Haywood before I took this class, nor could I ever imagine that I'd care about them. Not only did I love going to class, but Prof. Pollock always put things in context, which is something a lot of English classes sorely need. He was also really helpful with all the assignments and papers.
big t ran a pretty fun class. i think he makes it clear what he expects of his students, and that sometimes verges pretty close to "just regurgitate what we've discussed in class"

He's probably one of the only professors that you will encounter that truly cares about each individual student within a lecture of 200+ students. Texts that may otherwise be boring are incredibly fascinating in his lectures. Hilarious, helpful, and awesome!! Loved him!!
Best English class! He is easy to understand and very interesting. Also he is funny and not boring.

AMMMMMAZING! I am in love with Tony Pollock. He is completely brilliant and hysterically funny. Best class I've ever taken (103). Minimal work, totally engaging and interesting. I want to take another class with him.
Hands donw the best English teacher I have had the pleasure of being a student of at U of I.  He is brilliantly smart without the cocky arrogrance of many professors of his stature

Tony Pollock is a philosophy major, teaching Intro to Fiction. He doesn't treat it like usual English professors; he makes it easy to understand, and interesting. He's funny, smart, and knowledgable. He doesn't make you learn things you don't need to know, and if you just go to lecture, you can get a fairly good grade.

Tony Pollock is awesome-- super helpful, very interested-- he makes you feel like you have 100% of his attention and he always has great suggestions and insights.  One of the nicest people in the English dept.

Love the projects we have in this class and the coursework + canvas are all very helpful in learning and improving as a designer. He has very clear guidelines on his assignments and posts everything ahead on canvas, making it very easy to navigate. However, there are times where his critiques are a little harsh but they are always very helpful.

Bro he is actually so mean...like his classes give you professional results and good projects, but oh my god, his feedback is so mean, like do not expect any compliments from him. He is actually so scary and kind of stuck up in the way he gives feedback because he expects you to follow what he says instead of conversing to find a middle ground.
He gives great feedback. Very encouraging and easy to approach for questions. I would definitely recommend taking his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He scrunched 16 weeks of work into 8 weeks instead of cutting down the workload, so you get a lot of projects done but they're all at half effort. Even without 4 other classes to deal with it would still be a ridiculous amount to do, especially with YouTube videos as the only lessons. If you have to take this class, learn Figma over the summer.

Josh's class was enjoyable, with constructive feedback and beneficial guest lectures. His flexibility to adjust the course to our interests and what we didn't know was really helpful. He also included additional industry-specific skills that I haven't been taught in other design classes. Overall, the class was a good amount of work but manageable.

Probably the most boring class and professor I have ever came across. Do not take this class. HW is all busy work that doesn't relate to the lectures. No clear grading criteria, he just decides what he wants your grade to be at the end. The lectures were 120 mins and he always went over. Save yourself and take a different class.

Prof is nice and gets you to push your thinking but this class is so boring. It's already at 80 mins but he always went over time. So much homework that doesn't relate much to the lectures. Class is called leadership but it's not really about that. Probably wouldn't take again.

Gupta class diff than exp. Class on leadership more like a class in psychology. I attended regularly & by end of class no one was there bc attendance not required. Assignments r personalized to us. Wish class was reformatted. Did make me reflect on my goals. Lectures should be 50 mins max. Too long 1:20 min. Lecture not related to hw as much. 5/10.

Very supportive and encouraging of all topics written about. Creates a warm, welcoming environment. Strict grading criteria but never unattainable, and easy to go by. Many opportunities for revision. Would definitely take course again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I LOVE JULIE
The BEST CW professor on campus. Her CW100 put me on the path to declaring a CW minor. Super funny & discussions are never boring.

The one thing about this class and Julie is that participation is key. She is the funniest person I have ever met, while also being caring and giving amazing feedback on your writing. I wish I could have her for every creative writing class I ever take here!

Professor Price is certainly a creative writer and a good one at that. She is very poetic, witty and overall incredibly caring. She gives great feedback and in a very respectful way. I would say that my writing technique has improved after taking this course, 5 stars.
Julie is one of the best professors I have had so far. She is funny and knows how to give you good feedback. After two weeks in CW 100, I declared a CW minor.

Professor Price has a lot of humor and is so understanding of personal circumstances. She allows for revisions up until the end of the semester and gives great and clear feedback on assignments. She passes out paper assignments around 3 weeks before the assignment is due. Gives great examples of topics through other short readings.

Not even done with the semester yet and I already love her. She creates such a good, open, and comfortable environment for the class. Her expectations are fair and you'll do well in her class if you meet them. She's also really funny and approachable.

The best writing professor I've ever had or heard of. Take her nonfiction and trauma writing workshops if you want your life/work to change forever in the best possible way. I couldn't love this woman more.
Take her class. You won't regret it. Get ready to be challenged but leave changed.

If you can manage to find a spot in one of her classes, take it! You won't regret it. She pushes you to write and improve. The energy in her class is amazing and I always looked forward to seeing her. Her feedback is great and she is always willing to hear you out outside of class.

I love her more than life itself. She is so funny and cool and laidback. I really really respect her and look forward to seeing her. I'm definitely not a kissass so this is a big deal coming from me. She is definitely my favorite professor so far. I am gonna try to take as many classes with her as possible because I think she has a lot to teach me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Julie is and will always be my favorite professor. Her readings, lectures and discussions are wild and interesting, and her feedback is helpful and kind. She really helped improve my writing as a whole, and motivate me to keep going. She's just an amazing person-- I strongly recommend every class she's ever taught!

One of the best professors I've ever had and an even better person. Gives fantastic feedback and really inspires you to want to continue writing. Her class was incredibly therapeutic with how laid-back it was and was something I really looked forward to going to. I'll always be mad that I won't be able to take more of her classes.

ulie Price is the most amazing person on this campus. She is not just a professor. She is a mentor, and an amazing human being. She will not only walk you through every step of writing pieces in narrative fiction, poetry, and creative non-fiction, she also gives you the option to earn back ALL points lost in revision. TAKE CW 100!!

Julie Price is the most wonderful and influential professor I've ever had. She really cares about all of her students and, I believe, would do absolutely anything to see them succeed. She gives wonderful feedback and makes sure you leave her class with better skills than you came in with. She's also hysterical and makes class a lot of fun.

Julie is the only professor at UofI who I really connect with. She is hilarious, dark, a spunky hardass, and more compassionate than any prof I've met. She creates a community vibe in class where people get serious about their writing while still having a lot of fun. She makes you work, but why else should you be at University? Highly recommended.

She's worth taking a class with. You will write many poems, but it's up to you to revise as she doesn't (or didn't in this class) require a portfolio or grade revisions. Strongest rapport I've probably ever felt in a class because she is able to tie everyone together well. Good experience.
Julie is just amazing! She is so chill and insightful! she was a hippie and still is at heart! she is the whole reason i continued my cw major 3

I took both 106 and 206 Julie and she's a real star. Wise and understanding of what students need to hear in workshop. A blast to work with. Please note: Show up to class on time. Turn on assignments on time.
She is the most entertaining and passionate professor I have ever met. She makes writing fun.

Julie is an absolute gem. Her class is fast-paced, witty, fun, and genuinely useful for writers of all calibers. If you are one of those people who can't seem to make it to class on time, however, be warned that she has absolutely abhors tardiness, and will deduct points for it without mercy.

I also took her CW 106 class. And for both classes, she made me a better poet and gave me a lot of poetic motivations to go on with my own voice and style. I will greatly miss going to her class as they were the highlights of my two semesters with Julie.
Probably the best professor I ever had.  She taught and inspired me a lot.  Just love her!!

Possibly the most passionate, funny, and interesting professor I have had at U of I so far. Her poetic knowledge was amazing and her ability to even make your worst poems look best always works to your advantage. Though sometimes I wondered about the sincerity of her compliments. But she is a good professor overall and I'm glad I took her class.

I hate writing essays but I love her class. She is very nice and helpful. I hate writing but I got mostly A's on my papers. I believe as long as you put effort into writing, she will def give you a good grade. also, only four papers for the semester. all with interesting topics. take rhet 105 with her!!
Does anyone know where she went to?
Julie wont be returning as a teacher here  : (   She was fabulous!
She is the definition of a hippie poetry teacher.  She is hilarious and a fair teacher.  I would recommend taking any class she offers.

She was a great ass teacher. She was funny and she made the work easy. We were only given four papers for the semester and  we were allowed to return them all in for full credit after corrections. It's sad that Spring '07 is her last semester here but if you can find one of her classes available, register for it.

Terrible class. I had to give her a "good" rating because she was very easy. But go ahead and ask me how much I learned: NOTHING. Her writing instruction is utterly useless! If you want an easy A - take her! If you want to LEARN something... search elsewhere.
Easiest class i've ever had. Revisions for papers for new grades, funny teacher. Easy class.. just go to it and you will get an A.

One of the best, if not THE best teacher I have ever had. Julie is extremely willing to help as much as the student wants. She is Very approachable. Grading is fair. Very tactful with criticism, and gives A LOT of praise where it is deserved.
She totally rocks!
A great, fun, helpful instructor who makes me love going to class.  My writing has taken on a whole new attitude.  Julie is the best teacher I have EVER had!!!
She is so awesome! She really makes you work feel meaningful.
A highly superior instructor, as well as a human being. She not only made me a better writer, she changed my life. I love this woman.

"This is probably the easiest course to get an A in, you'd have to try really hard not to get one" - Professor Kalita. Very interesting class about water taught very well. In-class participation, weekly hw, one project, no exams, and final is online. For an 8-week course that covers two gen-eds its great, and everyone needs water so good to know.
Very nice professor, terrible class. So much homework, pointless lectures, and a 12-page term paper about water, need I say no more. What is it with 100-level gen-eds? I would avoid this class.

Dr. Kalita is a very understanding and kind professor. There were very few homework assignments. The main things are the midterm paper (10-15 pages) and the final group project. But, as long as you put in effort and do not start at the last minute, you will be fine. The lectures seemed to drag, however, he was passionate about the topic.

Dr. Kalita is clearly very well-respected and is funny, but the class itself is poorly organized and I still have no idea what it was really about. Found it kind of boring and just overall not worth taking.

Dr. Kalita is the chillest nicest professor you'll probably ever have. There are like 6 homework assignments, a midterm paper, and a group project in this whole class (ABE 199). The rest of it is watching Kalita talk about water. Admittedly the 90 minute lectures drag. He's awesome but the lectures are a little boring sometimes. Easy A though.

Told us the first day we would all receive an A in the class. Field trips, a 15 page paper, a group presentation, no tests, very little homework, and an end of year party. Attendance not strictly enforced, but definitely encouraged. Very funny, caring, kind and intelligent professor.
Great class!  The learning objectives were clear and Dr. Kalita does a good job at generating student interest in the material.

I had Dr. Kalita for an honors class "water in the global environment". Lectures are 3 hours, but very interesting and he kept the class engaged.  We took a few cool field trips (best one: NGRREC near St. Louis). Very passionate about his field and has a good sense of humor.  It was interesting to hear first-hand stories from him about this field
Amazing professor. Really cares about the students and tests were really easy since it's open book open note. Only problem is he never gives back exams on a timely matter.
This is one of the greatest professor in the ABE department.He really cares about each and every student.
Awesome teacher.  Wants to make sure students know the material.  Does a great job of relating material to real world experience.

This was the most boring class I have ever taken in college, and while at first Dr. Kalita's high energy and positive attitude made the class better... He eventually just became annoying. It's really hard to understand what he's saying, but usually he writes stuff down. Tests were basically all from the notes, but you should still study.
Makes sure students understand the material, is very straight forward about tests and homework.
He is very easy to get along with and interested in making sure the students understand the content discussed during class.

The class is alright and its not super difficult although I think he creates the activities himself so it's definitely confusing sometimes. All the exams are online. he marked that the textbook was required and then when i got to class he said we don't need it fr. so that pmo

The most chill professor I've had this semester. Every assignment we have is online, including the midterm, and the few homework assignments we have are extremely simple to follow (and he also goes over how to do them in class). Couple extra credit opportunities, but you really don't need them. Lectures are also pretty interesting too if you attend

Such a laidback professor! His knowledge of the subject is extensive & the course does not require a textbook, which is nice for financial reasons. The class was pretty easy & not stressful in the slightest. Thanks, Prof. Christi!

Surangi taught one of the most interesting classes I've ever taken, all about how species evolved due to their biology and geography of the Earth. This class introduced much of the primary literature needed to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: DONT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!! Is very disorganized. The professor makes it hard for no reason. All the tests are only essay questions where she asks questions about things we havent learned. The leacures are not helpful at all but are required to go to. The labs are not helpful at all but are required to go to. He grades very harshly for assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a very sweet, likable person and a great lecturer BUT IB407 is a new class, and it is terrible right now. There is simply way too much content. Exams will kick your put inless you are good at memorizing lists of plant families. If you need the plant ID credit TAKE SOMETHING ELSE like dendrology.

Gives an overwhelming amount of content and does a poor job of preparing us. She also squeaks in class and it's super hard to hear her, even though the class size is quite small. The slides she prepares are hard to follow. For exams, she gives us lousy resources with not enough time to utilize. Overall made for us to suffer and fail
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class if you have the chance! I'm not a biology major so I felt a little out of place, but it didn't stop me from learning or getting a good grade. Amazing professor, super knowledgeable, and loves to get into issues with students to pick our brains. Great class, great professor.
IB 105 is a tough class. Lots of homework and things to do. The class is read tons of article and watch many videos then do the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: IB 105 online. This class sucks. Do not take it. You have lots of work to do. Currently suffering by taking this class. Way easier classes to take for the same credit.
I  spent  most  of  time  on  this  course , though  it's  just  an  elective. Too  much  homework  and  tasks!!!! In  addition, I  didn't  learn  anything  interesting  and  useful  in  this  class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I have taken her online class IB 105 which is second-half semester course. This course is definitely not an easy A course. It requires so much work. If you are switching from tough elective course to IB105 by this professor, you would have more work load then before.

Surangi is a fantastic professor! She genuinely cares about all of her students, and is very intentional about offering help and ensuring that everyone understands the material. Take good notes, the material is not hard. Should be an easy A, she gives a lot of extra credit. If you are present in lecture and discussion, tests are not hard.

Go to lecture, take notes, pay attention to things she repeats (she repeats a lot - but for a reason). The tests can be tricky because you get a lot of allnonecombination of the above answers. TA's lecture notes are posted before tests - compare them to yours to study and you'll be fine. Between iClickers and online questions, there's SO MUCH EC.

She is so terrible. she is the least clear lecturer you'll ever have and if you pay attention to her saying "RIGHT? RIGHT? RIGHT?" she says it at the end of every sentence I'm not even kidding. you can't even pay attention while she's lecturing because her speech is that poor
She constantly wasted time with pointless slides that had nothing but pictures on it and waited in silence for people to answer he inane questions. Just all around awful.

Her class was absolutely awful, in four years I have never been motivated to actually review a professor until I had her. This class was highschool material but she constantly insists on asking questions like what is a hypothesis to 100 people and waiting for a response with the answer on the slide. Tests are fairly hard designed to trick you.
Professor Punyasena is very nice and helpful. She gives good explanations and has informative and interactive powerpoints. I really enjoyed having her as a teacher!

Dr. Pu was amazing! Her class was very intriguing and it was easy for her to keep students interested.  There is a pretty big group projects but everything is done at a pretty slow pace and feedback is given for everything!  Her TA's are also very sweet and easy to work with.

I really liked Dr. Pu. She's really funny, her lectures are pretty engaging, and the class directions and objectives are great too. I do love her test policy too. There aren't really many or any general EC opportunities I can think of, but in all honesty, do the readings and participate, and you will not need it.

Attendance was done with iClicker, but she often forgot to open it during class, leaving many students with absences when they were at the lecture. Lectures aren't related to discussion sections (although that may have been my TA). The group skit was awful, especially since we had a final exam anyway.

She is extremely funny and is good at explaining the course material. She is also very understanding when it comes to absences or extensions. I don't really like the course's content but she still manages to make the class fun.
Yujie is super approachable and really cares about her students. The class activities are awesome and make learning fun.

I took Ms. Yujie for Hist 220, she is a caring teacher and very accessible if you ever have any concerns about classwork. I found her grading fair and reasonable, and the readings were never too long. I recommend her to anyone looking for a 200-level history to take!
She is very enthusiastic and passionate in her teaching. She is also very kind and reasonable.
She is helpful and good at teachingI really enjoyed her lessons!

Jeanne was an amazing professor. I had her during my first semester and it really made me realize that I had picked the right school for me. She really cares about her students and wants everyone to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Jeanne is a wonderful teacher with great, applicable assignments. Just beware that there are in depth assignments every week. That being said, this has bee the most helpful class I've taken in my time at the iSchool.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Class is actually interesting, engaging, and something to look forward to. The readings seem excessive sometimes, but the material is relatively interesting. She is caring and very approachable.

Jeanne is a very effective professor with practical assignments and excellent feedback.  She grades very promptly so that you can adapt your skills for the next assignment.  I did a presentation and got the grade in the same day with feedback.  Like another reviewer, I appreciated the fact that group work was eliminated. Too impractical for online.

Awesome class. She's a straight shooter with a sense of humor. Especially appreciated that she knows how difficultawful group projects can be, so they are eliminated from her syllabus. There are a lot of assignments, but they're actually kind of fun. Engaging class. Highly recommend!

Really wonderful teacher with an awesome sense of humor and a great approach to reference and customer service.  Assignments and lessons are extremely practical, even if you already have experience working in a library.  Highly recommended!

Incredible teacher. She was very organized, enthusiastic, knowledgable and helpful. Great communicator and fair grader. I like that her class was really practical; it wasn't into abstract theories. She also had a great sense of humor and was really open minded. Provided great feedback on assignments.

Awesome teacher, awesome human being. Jeanne really knows how to teach and keep her students involved.  Assignments can be tough, but she's always there to help, so don't leave it for the last minute!

Jeanne is a great teacher.  She is thoroughly knowledgable about reference and has much experience in the field as well.  She teaches (and gives assignments) in a very practical manner;  a student can actually apply what he/she learns in future jobs.  Hghly recommend.

Puacz is enthusiastic and very intelligent.  She knows her topic and makes class interesting.  The assignments were reasonable (you had an assignment most weeks, but only had to answer 4/7 questions.) Fair grader.
She is a fantastic teacher. Really knows the subject matter and has a well organized class with clear objectives, achievable goals and clear values. Do take reference with her.

She's very knowledgeable and explains topics clearly, but she is extremely rude and condescending to students. No one wanted to ask her questions because we were all intimidated by her. She is also very strict about making sure no one is doing anything besides taking notes in class and not on their cell phones/online.

Kimberly is an AMAZING professor! This class was very interesting and very relevant to your love life and family. She is very good about explaining things clearly to help you understand the material. Must attend class to get some notes that are not in the readings. 3 tests, one small essay, and one large essay at the end of the semester.

There's quite a bit of reading for this class, but most of it is far from boring. Her lectures are interesting. Also, before the exam she gives you a recap of everything you need to know, so you know what to study.
Horrible Teacher. She is leaving this year thank goodness. Had to email her to correct many wrong answers on the review. TA's are much more helpful!!
She makes Elementary Math harder than it has to be.

Really useful course, just wish this course was taught by someone else. Her accents can be tough to understand; however, she had the most ridiculous grading scheme I've seen since elementary school. Really good professor. Every concept is explained very well and the tests and homework really make sure you understand the concepts well. Class isn't easy but def interesting. Highly recommend taking it with this professor

I really like David. He's a great professor!

adorable... really knows his stuff.  he is SO WILLING to help you if you need it -- and go to him after your exams.  he'll talk to you about how to study better and he'll go over material with you, too.  makes a huge effort to know everyone personally (that's incredible for 120 students!).  take this class.

Take another course if possible. This course will waste you 3 hours of precious time each week. It's not a easy course, but you will not learn anything useful either. Super subjective in research methods and discussions.

The class was only graded by the final, 3 midterms, & a term paper. Not forgiving & the midterms involved essays. Regret taking class

reviews.comment: I never felt I gained anything from attending lecture. Every lecturer just read off the slides. It was an easy class but was pretty heavy with busy work for a gen ed.

Makes sure to cover the important points in lecture but likes to go on long tangents and can get kind of boring at times. He has weekly reading quizzes which aren't that difficult even if you skip lecture, just have to skim the slides for main ideas. There are a couple papers and two exams(both online), not too bad if you want to knock out a req.

reviews.comment: Teach this man how to use a microphone

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Layton. His class was very reading heavy but it was alright because I really did learn a lot. He is obviously very passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches. He does a good job at asking good, critical thinking type questions both in lecture and on exams. Take this class if you're looking for a fun challenge.

Layton was alright. I wouldn't say he is a good prof/lecturer but he wasn't as bad as others I have had. A fair warning though, this man -preaches-. He doesn't lecture like a normal person; when you are in his course you will feel like you're at the local baptist church listening to a sermon. If you can get past that it's okay. 4/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Layton is pretty hard to follow during lectures. He is very boring. There are weekly quizzes in TA sections and if you get a good TA, they're not too bad. Reading assignments are very, very heavy but you won't die if you don't read. The exams are online so it's not too bad. I wouldn't recommend taking this if you're not interested in religions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Layton really cares about what he is teaching.  however, you won't get an easy A.  There's a lot of material, and the tests are worth 30% of the grade.  The final is noncumulative, but the course is heavily weighted on exams.  He does give study guides which is helpful though.  A great professor, and you'll learn some great things about the Bible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Layton is very passionate about what he teaches and makes very clear what he wants for exams. The material makes it a lot harder than the standard 100 class. You must keep up on all readings/lectures, but he's always willing to help you outside of class. Don't take him if you want an easy A; take him if you want a rigorous and stimulating class.

I agree with the other reviewer, this class is an easy B but it's an incredibly difficult A. The weekly pop quizzes are graded harshly, meaning you have to constantly be up to date on all of the readings. Despite finding the subject interesting, it was hard to stay focused through the lecture. 13 of the students in the room were usually asleep.

This was a very interesting course, and Layton has a very strong command of material. Readings are long, and the topic matters are complex to say the least. But he is super helpful, and is there to see the success and learning of the class. Attendance isn't mandatory, but the class would be pointless without it. An easy B, but an A is tough.
Layton is clearly passionate about this topic. Lectures are easy to follow and quizzes (usually every friday) are extremely easy. Decent grader and Exams were easy

I really don't know why he others have been calling him difficult or unclear. In my opinion, Layton is very clear, excited about what he teaches, and loves to pose thought-provoking questions. As someone who is not religious, his non-religious analysis of the Bible is very helpful and he's super approachable. Take a class with him if you can!

Weekly quizzes, 2 papers, midterm and final. Extremely difficult to pay attention to in lecture. Very cryptic teaching style. Tests are intense-- take forever to prepare for, but are straightforward if you put forth the time. If you're a solid Christian it will drive you crazy. His theology is very odd.
Great class - learned a lot, and Professor Layton's teaching style made the lecture seem smaller. While this advice may seem obvious, speak up in class and use the study guides!

I really enjoyed this class. I actually anticipated it to be harder than it actually was. Be prepared for a lot of reading, which is understandable for this type of class. Dr. Layton is very knowledgable and easy to approach for questions. I recommend taking this class!

This class was pretty difficult. The grading was tough and the material was not that easy to understand, especially if you don't have a prior knowledge or background about the Bible. The professor however is nice and knows a lot about what he teaches and is willing to help you out. Not an easy gen-ed...
Best professor I've ever had. If you want to actually learn something, take a course by Layton. Don't take his courses if you're looking for blow off classes. They are pretty demanding.
awesome!

He was an awesome professor! He knew what he was talking about, was funny, and was really interested in the subject which made it easier to learn. There is hardly any assignments, 3 papers,2 midterms and everything is done on powerpoint, which he posts online, but i would recommend going to lecture because he explains it in more depth.

Professor Layton is one of the best professors I have had. He is really knowledgeable. The class seemed like more work than I expected for a 101 course but I do not regret taking it. It was really interesting. Although attendance is not mandatory we did have quizzes. I would recommend this course if you are willing to work. Notes are posted online.

I wonder what the preceding comments mean about "learning" about Christanity. If they're looking for that in the Bible as Literature, then they're missing the point. It's not a religion class but a literature class. Layton's fine and he's does allow room for interpretation unlike what the preceding reviewers hint at. He's actually a pretty good pro

Both classes were terrible. World religions and The New Testament classes. LUCKILY I took Bible as Lit and got another prof, and the class ended up being GREAT. Layton basses all his theology on assumption and builds it on quicksand. It's absolutely ridiculous. Take these classes if you want to learn debunked theory. Terrible prof.

A lot harder than I had expected. do not be fooled by the 101. You are expected to know a lot more for this class than any other 101 classes I have ever taken. Also it is not learning about Christianity, it is about how to read the Bible. I dont recomend this class

Solid professor and class, but nothing exceptional. He knows his stuff, presents it clearly, and does a good job of presenting it in an objective, scholarly manner without any religious/ideological commentary one way or the other. Be warned that this class (Bible as literature) is deceptively hard, despite the impression of a blowoff course.

Wow, talk about picking favorites. It was obvious he was out to get people that didnt respond to his questions in class. Thanks a lot for giving me the 60% on the major paper instead of the the 59% that would have failed. My same quality of work got progressively lower grades throughout the semester. Take the class if you like kissing butt.

Said during the first session of a Religious Studies class, "This is not about religion. If you disagree with me, I don't care." Also told us not to ask theological questions. He's still teaching a theory that was refuted 200 years ago. Don't go if you actually want to *learn* about Christianity.

I sat there through all of his lectures about christianity and i didn't understand what he was talking about.  He could have been talking about anything he was so vague.  He really really really was unclear on what he was talking about.
Cool guy and good profesor.  Made the class easy.

He gave a great historical approach to religious history, and really formed relationships with his students.  He was extremely helpful, wanted to do anything he could to help students get ahead.  I wish I had another class with him this year.
ANSC 250 was an easy class and very interesting. ANSC 199 was also very easy and she is very nice.

reviews.comment: Super sweet professor! Her online class was laid out really well with lectures she recorded herself.  Easy grader and gives good feedback to improve, but takes awhile to grade anything

reviews.comment: Very easy class if needing a western gen ed! Professor is super nice, and I could get all my work done in a day some weeks. You do have to buy an online textbook, but it has all the answers to the quizzes and can be helpful for the few and short essays. No final exam just a project that was very easy to do and kind of fun if you love dogs!
Sarah is a super sweet teacher and  enthusiastic about her classes. Very lenient with late work, and quizzes are always doable provided you did all the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very easy but well run class. The assignments which Sarah gave were very engaging and informative in regards to animal sciences. Her grading policies and weekly workload was very fair and I overall really enjoyed the structure of the course. Highly recommend this course if you want to take a fun or interesting elective.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This was an extremely easy class. The lectures are all recorded and if you take notes like I did it might take you a while but otherwise I got all my work done on the Sunday it was due. Ms. Richardson is very sweet and if you email her about any problems or extensions she was very understanding.

Professor Richardson is an amazing spokesperson. She tries her best to make ANSC 250 as interesting as it can be. Professor Richardson made ANSC 250 very fun and engaging. I recommend anyone to take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This was an optional discussion along with ANSC 250, which I really enjoyed. It went over the material discussed in 250 and helped to clarify anything that may have been foggy. The only points for this course were attendance and the final essay (80 points), so you have to put in the time and write the essay well. She is awesome, though!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She wrote the textbook herself and seems very interested and passionate about what she teaches. She is also very kind and loves to chat outside of class if you have comments or questions. In my class, there were four reflective essays for the term, but one was dropped, and as long as you put in effort, you should score well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was a great professor, extremely passionate, and really the best you could ask for. The course was very easy, I took the online course and had zero issues. The material is very basic but you learn a lot if you aren't familiar with many companion animal topics. She gave biweekly assignments which gave her plenty of time to complete the material.

Take this class! Easy, and you learn a lot. Homework is hard! Quizzes are easy, and there's one final project. I was recommended this class, and I would recommend it again. Also, do not rent the movie - it is not needed for an A+.

Sarah is wonderful! She is extremely passionate in her lectures and makes them very engaging. If you are an ANSC major I recommend taking this course because if you actually put in the effort (which is what you're SUPPOSED to do) you learn a lot. Because of her, I got more involved in advocating for animal welfare. She is also a good recommender.
Sarah Richardson is an excellent professor! She is very passionate about the topic she teaches. Overall, the class was very easy, and I learned a lot about companion animals!

Very easy class I took it as a gen ed, and there is no final or midterm but there are quizzes and her grading is not hard at all. There is one group project but it was easy to do and didn't take too much time to complete. Lots of extra credit too.

Sarah is a really nice and understanding professor. She has guided me on course material and even other credits outside of class. I enjoyed her lectures as they were easy to understand and interesting. The e-text is required but she writes it herself so it isn't a standard boring one. She responds fast and is compassionate about what she does.

the course is very straightforward and you will get a good grade if you complete all the assignments. I took it online and the lectures were pretty pointless, most of the information was covered in ANSC 100 and ANSC 101. Easy A, but I didn't learn much.

Sarah is overall a pretty nice proff. This class is pretty easy just a handful of tedious work at times. One thing that sucks is that you have to buy packback access to be able to post your discussions.  you did get extra credit for joining the class live tho
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class is an easy A as long as you do the assignments with a mild amount of effort. Lots of extra credit. However, the class is incredibly boring if you already know basic things about companion animals.

Very long lectures (in an 8 week class, 3-4 hours of lecture would be normal), but they were interesting at least. Very clearly passionate about her work, and the class was a breeze. Despite it being an 8-week course, I was easily able to keep up with the work, and got an A+ by doing one extra credit assignment. Easy tests, easy assignments, easy A
the class itself is easy but she is not very understanding of mental health

Quiz/discussion/short response paper due every week. Professor was alright. Sometimes her opinion come off as facts as she's teaching, and although she states that she's not gonna push her opinion onto you, it's very clear what she thinks you should believe. Nonetheless, her class was easy. No meeting times.

Daniel Roche really takes the time to make sure his students are doing well and that they understand the material. His lectures are interesting, and he leaves comments on your work so you can improve. It is a lot of work, but I found it to be helpful and relevant for the future. If you start the work early and ask questions, you will be successful.

Try to take BTW 250 with any other teacher! His assignments were long and time consuming. He graded things harshly as well. I also did not feel as though the assignments we did would be helpful to me in the future/

Dan Roche is an amazing professor. He is very knowledgeable and inspiring. He also very funny at times. Heavy workload in his class, time consuming assignments. Instructions can be unclear at times, so you have to ask questions.

He requires far more work than other professors of this class, was expecting an easy A and he graded things harshly. His lectures were extremely boring. He gave very little in class time to work on things, all assignments were completely homework. He consistently cold called during class. Was my least favorite class of the semester.

Clear grading, helpful and kind. You will learn a lot from this class. However, as it is a Advanced Composition class, there is going to be lots of writing. If you put in effort I don't see how you wouldn't get an A

Many writing assignments, but that is expected from the course description. He is very knowledgeable and shares a lot of his past experiences in production & game development! He gives detailed feedback and is fairly lenient with grading. Definitely take a writing course with him if you can!

Very kind professor with lots of knowledge on the game industry! He was very lenient with grading and gave amazing feedback for your assignments. While attendance wasn't required since lectures were recorded and posted, I'd encourage attending the lectures to get to interact with him--he's a fun guy to talk with, and he tries to make lectures fun!

Took BTW 263 and was very impressed with his knowledge on the game industry and various related disciplines. He was always very compassionate towards his students and is very fun and friendly.

Highly recommend taking a course with him, one of the best professors I've had so far.

Roche is one of the best professors I have ever worked with. His course is really useful and he really taught me lots of practical skills and tips about the game industry. His advice inspires me a lot. Really appreciate taking his course.

I took BTW263 with him this semester. He is such a nice professor and the course overall is interesting! Although the papers take time, they are fun and the professor gives detailed feedback. Highly recommend this course!
One of the most nicest and inspirational professor I've ever met :) Took BTW263 with him and the class was so much fun. Woud definitely recommend this class to anyone interested in game design!

This was a pretty generic and lightweight writing class. You only have 4 big assignments, each about 4-6 or so pages of writing each, and Dan tries his hardest to make them practical to industry. I would've appreciated faster grading, it took up to a month, but he was always pretty lenient and gave good feedback anyways. Approachable and nice guy.

Assigns 200+ pages of reading weekly with short-notice reading responses due the next day. Limited expansion on theoretical readings in class, strict grading with unclear criteria (especially on essays), required summaries for absences, and occasional use of class time for videos not clearly related to course material.

Profe is nice but he assigns SO MUCH readings. His class is Tuesday and Thursday and on Tuesdays, he'll assign 4-6 readings each 40-50 pages long to be read and completed by Thursday. This is not law school or grad school. People have other things to do besides read hundreds of pages for a singular class in one day.

-21 degrees and he still expected us to show up at 9 am. his "policy" went from "no longer answer individual student emails expressing confusion about any.. You are responsible for knowing and understanding..." to "one's absence given lecture.. required to submit a 150 word minimum prose summary or 200 word minimum outline". not worth it. fade.

reviews.comment: Profe is an awesome person; he's super easy/enjoyable to talk to and caring. This class is poorly structured, though. I don't feel like I've learned as much as I expected.

This was profe's first time teaching the class, and I enjoyed it. There were a lot of long readings for lectures, but we always had class discussions about them/did participation exercises. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

The professor expects students to only think through the lens of the three main texts in the course. You are not allowed to give your own thoughts and opinions in your work. As much as the three text are insightful, this was a very narrow approach to a diverse topic.

Also throughout the course his slides had errors every time.

Any questions I would ask him he would get wrong, replied to all of 1 email from me over the whole semester. He promised a curve and didn't give one. Lectures have no relevance to the homework or quizzes. Teaches the proofs of equations instead of the actual content we need to understand to succeed in exams. did not teach

Professor Sowers seems like a good person. I can't say the same for his teaching abilities.  He passed slides like there was no tomorrow, so you couldn't even digest the 20 triple integral proof you were still trying to decipher. Technically, he's a good person but terribly bad at teaching. I had to teach myself and his lectures did not help at all. TERRIBLE TEACHER.

Doesn't know how to teach well at all, every lecture is basically a powerpoint read sometimes full of mistakes. Pretty much everyone in the class was forced to self-lecture themselves. He doesn't care for his students very much as well, releasing final review worksheets literally only up to 2 days before the final. Avoid him if you can.

After the first few lectures, I switched to a different professor, who was 5x better. When asked any questions, he typically gave a non-answer. Incorrect slides and poor instruction. Do not take him unless you want to learn that his favorite number is 5.

You're better off self-teaching than listening to Dr. Sowers.  Genuinely the worst math teacher I've ever had.  His lectures are really confusing and he doesn't problem solve.  I got away with teaching myself all the material, but I think relative to the homework, tests are easy though, but consistent across all calc sections, so get someone else.

He is unresponsive to students, often ignoring emails or brushing off questions. His lectures include humor but are proof-heavy and not exam-relevant. There are frequent errors on slideshow. Where do I begin? This professor is extremely unorganized, never prepared for lecture, and oblivious to the empty classrooms he lectures to. Firstly, I wanted to say that I learn best from a teacher in lecture. Unfortunately, Richard Sowers did not give me this chance. I was forced to self study and my grade reflects it. I have never gotten a C in a math class and was devastated. I hope the university fires this man and contacts other universities to prevent him from teaching again.

Very bad, very unhelpful, never again. If you get Sowers never go to his lecture. Just self-study the material via textbook and YouTube. You are better off that way so you don't get confused during his lecture. Good luck, you'll probably need it!

Richard Sowers is easily by far the worst teacher I've ever had the displeasure of having. His slides are absolutely abysmal with mistakes all over and it's common to spend the entire lecture watching him attempt to decipher his own jumbled mess. He values proofs over his own students. If you have questions you'll likely get shamed. Genuinely awful

This is probably the worst educator I've ever had the displeasure of having. Avoid his class at all costs. He doesn't care for his students at all, and is an absolutely tragic lecturer. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.

I don't dislike him as a person, but his lectures are just plain useless. They almost never contain any useful information on how to actually apply things and only focus on such high level derivations and confusing examples that I never know what I actually need to do until I ask a TA or look through practice solutions

Richard Sowers must be removed from the University. He can barely teach, he has soooo many mistakes on his slides, and is very disorganized when it comes to giving us any information on grades or exams. He is the worst professor I have ever had, DO NOT EVER TAKE.

reviews.comment: Going to lectures was a waste of time. Slides made simple concepts seem like rocket science with complex notation. Not a single practice problem was done during lectures. All he did was read off the slides that had countless errors. He often struggled to answer questions and it seemed like he didn't knew what he was talking about.

Honestly, he is a good person. However, teaching is not his thing. Lectures were absolutely horrendous. I came out with negative knowledge. I genuinely feel like if he picked up his slides and taught the topics that would appear on the test and homework, he would be amazing. But please, if you do not plan on self studying, do something else.

His lectures used overly complex notation and commonly contained mistakes. His lectures were also overly focused on proofs and too little time was spent actually explaining information pertinent for homework and/or tests. Sometimes a lecture on certain topics left me even more confused. Self-study is your friend.
The lectures were not great..
Hes really hot

Slides were frequently incorrect, explanations were absurdly complex for the level of the class (using real analysis terms for calc 3 topics like continuity). To put into perspective how bad his lectures were, at the beginning of the semester there were ~300 people in lecture, by the end it was near 30..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was one of the worst professors ive ever had. The lecture slides had so many mistakes and he rarely did a problem in class, mostly he just put the answer up on the screen and moved past it so fast we could not recollect what he was talking about. he also forgot to post topics for the exam. you have to self study with no idea of whats on tests.

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher who has slides with excessively redundant proofs full of mistakes and confusing substituted values which nobody understands at all. He can not explain concepts in an approachable and coherent manner. NEVER TAKE HIS COURSE EVER

This was the worse professor I've ever had, it was like he had never opened a calc textbook in his life. His lecture slides were riddled with mistakes. He was rude to students who had genuine questions, and he takes pride in wanting students to fail. Do not under any circumstances take his class.

His slides are extremely useless with unnecessary complex notations and many mistakes, making it impossible to understand anything. He doesn't properly answer any questions. He only teaches what he feels like and doesn't cover topics on the midterm. Going to his class made me feel stupid and I felt like I would fail (I self studied the course).

Professor Sowers is easily the worst teacher I've ever had. He is not a good lecturer, and does not prepare students for exam content at all. He does not post material that we are supposed to get and that other professors post (such as practice exams, exam solutions after the exam is out). He does not answer student's questions well.

He does not teach the class well, lecture slides are filled with errors and overly rigorous proofs. Avoid him if possible and if not don't feel bad about skipping lecture and reading the textbook/watching videos instead.

Terrible professor. Looked like he was proud of his teaching which was in fact a complete mess. The lectures were disorganized and he made tons of mistakes literally every single class. The workload was reasonable though. If you really wanted to learn DL, avoid him at all cost
The man cannot teach. Stopped going to lecture and started to understand the material much better. Avoid.
His lectures have less than 10% of attendance. You can see how horrible his lectures are.
“What's your favorite number?”

I absolutely hated my experience with Richard Sowers. He didn't know how to teach, notes always had mistakes, and when he corrected the notes they were still very confusing. I learned more by skipping lecture.

Not a great professor by any means. He spends all of his time going over proofs and using notation that I have never seen before. His slides are also full of mistakes and always need to be pointed out by the students. Just for reference, on the first day of lecture, there were more than 200 students in attendance. Now only about 30 show up.

This guy just cannot teach. He seems like a decent person, but that does not make up for the abysmal lectures that use notation completely irrelevant to the class, and does not translate at all to the homework or discussion questions which are nonsensical themselves just like the lectures. Just read the textbook and you'll do okay

The homework is absolutely horrid and is nothing like the exams. The discussions are also horrid with the questions being very confusing. The TAs are nice and better teachers than the professor himself.

I have never before seen a professor who cares so little for his students. His lectures, as mentioned before, are a complete mess. Riddled with errors and taught in a manner that makes most young students unable to understand even the easiest of concepts without talking having to search it up themselves. Please do not ever go to Richard Sowers ever

His lectures are difficult to understand and don't cover all of the information in the textbook which ends up in the midterm exams. Compared to the textbook, the methods the professor uses to reach the required material is unnecessary and inordinately complicated, making content difficult to retain.

The lectures make 0 sense and do not help. You will have to learn everything on your own and spend time on going to tutoring with the TA's that actually help you learn. The TA's will be your best friend so make sure you do that. Although the professor can be funny, he is useless for the information and does not help you understand.

reviews.comment:
I think Sowers is a wonderful professor, but that may be because I use math to cope with my problems.

Dr. Sowers improvises his notes, things get nuanced. I'd highly recommend IE 534 if you want to learn mathematics notation or just how to communicate your ideas with mathematics. Writing machine learning reports is kinda fun if you can speak math
This professor does not prepare for his class. In his class materials for deep learning. "backprop" becomes derivatives, "RNN" takes a plan-observer system, which is wield in deep learning.

He made almost no preparation for this class and he paid no effort in slides and lecture recording. If you want to actually understand the materials, you have to self-study on google or ask TA. All he does is providing the topics.
Really rude and incredibly condescending. Huge superiority complex, and does not care about anyone's feelings or about treating people with basic human kindness. Very disorganized and spacey as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: HIs classes are interesting. Go to class and you will pass the exams. Exams are easy. Not accessible outside class.

His classes are really lively and interesting. He gives extra credit for projects. Exams are easy if all his lectures are attended. He connects bookish knowledge to the real world recent applications. I will love to take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Try to take Math 415 instead. This used to be a good course then they revamped it. Professor sowers is an ok professor during lectures but gets off topic a lot. Pop quizzes weekly and necessary to go. Biggest issue was he would lecture on 10 subjects, test you on 2/3 but wouldn't give you support to succeed (no practice problems or book problems)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I have ever had in my life (which is saying a lot).  He is extremely unprepared for lectures.  He has countless mistakes on every lecture slide that makes it nearly impossible to follow  According to him, if you "stare at the notes long enough" they will make sense.  He is very disorganized when it comes to assignments and deadlines.
Sowers is one of those guys that is so smart it affects his ability to teach. I went to class bc the course was difficult but i never got anything out of lecture.
He is the worst professor i have ever met in this country.

I dropped this class on the last day. Math has some extended deadlines, it was shortly before the final. Retaking it created a couple issues, but I was stressed by the arbitrary nature of the class. About 3 (not long) homework problems all semester, no syllabus, no book, only partially distributed notes with errors, gave identical exam 2 and 3. Wat

Sowers' class was the worst class I've had at UIUC. He had no plan for the class and made it up as he went along. We didn't cover the material that one expects to learn in real analysis. The whole experience was a waste of my time and money and its a disgrace that the math dept. has so little oversight over their courses.

He is the worst teacher I have ever met. Before him, I thought all the American professors are friendly, helpful and experienced in the teaching field, but he is absolutely not. He doesn't teach real analysis and he doesn't follow what he said.

The consensus of the class is that he isn't teaching us the material he should be teaching us and that's not good for anyone. All the exams are a lot harder than he first tells us they wll be because he doesn't adquately prepare us for them. I hope for your sakes he doesn't teach this honors course again, you won't learn real analysis.

Read the textbook, do the homework, sit in the front of the class room. Simple recipe to guarantee an A. Sowers is a menacing dude, extremely menacing, and quite funny too. I'll miss the witty speeches given before surprise quizzes and him calling out students who leave once they realize there isn't a quiz... only to quiz them at the end of class!

Dr. Sowers cares that his students understand the material, and though his exams can be challenging, he doesn't use trick questions and he gives lots of partial credit.  He's got a great sense of humor, too, which really helps you stay awake in class - the material can be quite dry at times.

Keeps lectures interesting by involving students and has a good sense of humor. If you pay attention in lecture you will hardly need to look at the text book. Exams are very straight forward, not too hard to get an A.

Does not quite prepare the lectures, but he is very familiar with this field. Really likes to ask students questions in class, which makes me a bit stressful. The exams are not difficult, if you have tried several old exams from his archival.

His teaching order was different from the textbook, which made it hard to use the book efficiently. The way he carries his class could be made more comprehensible, but overall, he is a good teacher, dedicated and demanding.
Awful prof. Speaks fast and confuses everyone. Also uses notation different from the book , which made class confusing. However, he had a nice curve at the end. So I managed to get an A-.
One of the best in the department.
Took the course over Coursera. There are four modules, six HWs, and four CBTF exams. You get to drop the lowest HW. The professor is very responsive in Campuswire and email.

Prof. Tahboub really gets how to teach online. The class is heavy but a few weeks of lectures and assignments are posted ahead of time. She always replies quickly Campuswire questions and DMs. Honestly, one of the smoothest online classes I've taken.

The professor is supportive, caring, and responsive. The Coursera-based course is lecture-heavy. 6 assignments have a 1-day grace period, and the lowest grade is dropped. There are 4 low-weight CBTF quizzes (each around 5%). Always check Campuswire for updates. One practice exam is given for each quiz, but real exam expectations may be unclear.

Absolutely awful. Assignments are graded slowly, mistakes for the course material and assignments aren't announced to the class so you have to read every single Campuswire post to be caught up on the newest version of the material. Relying on students to catch crucial updates buried in forum threads feels lazy and unfair.

The class is structured very well and her teaching is clear and organized. I like how she breaks down complex topics. You can tell she really cares about her students, she's always willing to help, whether it's through detailed lectures, office hours, or responding to questions really quickly.

The lectures were mostly her reading from slides with minimal explanation for some topics and over-explaining for others. Homework and exam expectations were often unclear and both were graded very specifically, with no room for minimal mistakes or even a slight lack of detail. Very disappointing class and a deeply unpleasant experience.

Oh wow, what should I say about this??? It's rare to see a professor who is so underprepared for the class. I'm quite speechless actually. She would blur through important and new concept but spend 10 minutes explaining what does "True Positive" mean. It's a shame she's teaching data mining, which is a subject I was really excited to learn about.

Very nice guy. While he does mostly lecture off of the slides he does also get the class engaged throughout lecture. Tests are clear once you realize he pulls the essay prompts in the same patterns for each tests. Very fair grader as well. He was courteous enough to round my 92.5 to a 93 as well. Overall, I'd recommend.
Pretty laid back, and as long as you do the work in the class and go to lecture you're fine. Pretty clear lectures and fairly interesting.

reviews.comment: If you don't really care about Christian religions, or if you are non-religious, I wouldn't take this class. Rudolph is passionate about the content, but he goes through lectures so fast, and what he says lowk is more important than what is on the slides. Also, there's like no assignments in this class, so if you do badly on the exams, I'm sorry.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Prof. Rudolph was so chill. Had him for PS 202: Religion & Politics and it was pretty easy. You don't have to attend lecture since all the notes are posted on Canvas.

You have 3 quizzes and a paper for the semester. He gives you a study guide for each of the quiz. It's all memorization. Lock in to study before, you'll most likely get an A

while he's really nice, the lectures were boring and posted online. only attended the ones prior to the first exam and then never went again. exams are essay format but questions are decently similar pattern wise on all three exams. I dont think they actually grade the final paper and was given a good grade for a kinda mid paper. idk if I recommend

The first two weeks of class are incredibly dull but then it picks up. He mostly reads off the slides, which are posted online. Anything important mentioned in the readings is in the slides or explained in class i.e. you don't need the readings. Three exams and a paper.

Rudolph is a good professor, his lectures are a bit dry though since he just reads off the slides so a little difficult to keep your attention. No need to go to class, lecture slides were posted. 3 exams, 75% and a research paper, 20% make up your grade. Tests were straightforward with the lectures but didn't give them back so hard to get feedback.
Always willing to meet with students and answer questions.

I liked Rudolph. He's a super nice professor. I recommend attending class, but he usually just reads off lecture slides. Your entire grade for the class is 3 written exams and an 8-10 page research essay. The tests aren't super tricky, so if you study for the exams you'll probably do well.
I really enjoy him as a professor he is great. The exams

Absolutely no need to go to class, I got a 98 and barely went. He just reads off slides which makes class very long, but the slides are online so you can do it all yourself. The exams are very straightforward and everything that you need is in the slides. He does not give much feedback on grades either. Easy A though if you're prepared for tests

The content covered in PS 202 was interesting, and I appreciated how much content we were able to cover, but the class itself was pretty boring and lecture-heavy without much room for discussion. Tests were straightforward, just go to the lectures and skim the readings if you really want to understand the stuff (but you don't have to read in-depth)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rudolph posted lectures early, which made it easy to work at your own pace. I appreciated the flexibility of this asynchronous class.

Online. Three-exams and one major paper. Zero feedback on any grade. Asynchronous, lectures are legit 30-50 slide PowerPoints with pretty much reading what's on screen. All exams are open-note, I did not even bother reading or watching the lectures after the second week. Just opened the power-point and books. (Exam is a whole-day thing. 9am-9pm).

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS especially online. There are only 4 assignments without clear instructions that are subjectively graded. you receive NO written feedback, and there is not a single rubric for the entire course. The professor has done the bare minimum for this course, and does not respect student efforts

At the start of the semester, put 4 months' worth of powerpoint slides on Compass. We are expected to just look at his PPTs and that's it. No lectures, no class meetings, no discussion board, no office hours, no communications whatsoever, no way to even get in touch with literally anyone in the class. So lazy and apathetic. TERRIBLE experience.

This class was online and asynchronous due to COVID, and this guy didn't even make an effort. The *entire course* was downloaded PowerPoints with audio clips you had to manually click on. Every other professor at UIUC has figured out how to record lectures or use Zoom, but this guy apparently can't be bothered. Lazy! This was an easy drop.

Professor Rudolph will not surprise you mid semester with new homework assignments or extra credit for that matter.  He has 3 exams and a term paper for grading.  He is extremely generous on topics you can use for your term paper.  Some people believe he is monotonous, but I found that he was extremely clear in his expectations and his material.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He never tried to stump us on the tests. It's a lot to learn, but I studied for about 2-3hrs for the tests, and I did well. The final is NOT cumulative, which is great!!

I was skeptical coming into this class about the correlation between real world politics and religions of the world. I bought the books, and started reading them, pleasantly finding interest, which supplemented the class portion making his presentations interesting. I enjoyed the class, seeing more than regurgitation and tests.

Lectures were very very boring but the tests were easy. All you have to do is fill out the study guide and study it and you'll get an A. Never payed attention is class/went to class and I got A+s/As on all of the tests. Don't bother getting the books either, I never read them. Overall, Rudolph is boring but has an easy class. He was also very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tests are memorization and long essay questions. Lectures can be boring but are usually interesting enough. Class covers a Ton of information, which I liked. Class is very well organized and Rudolph has it down to a science. You don't need the books. One 10-12pg paper due at the end of the semester.
An easy enough class with not a lot of requirements.

EASY CLASS IF YOU HAVE GREAT MEMORIZATION SKILLS. YOU NEVER NEED TO ATTEND CLASS, JUST USE THE STUDY GUIDE HE GIVES BEFORE THE TEST. ITS THE SAME INFO ON THE EXAM. DO NOT READ THE BOOKS. HE TELLS YOU WHAT HE WANT YOU TO KNOW ABOUT THEM IN LECTURE, WHICH IS TRIVIAL INFORMATION. RUDOLPHS A REALLY COOL GUY, BUT CLASS CAN GET A LITTLE DRY

Like others said, tests are just about memorization.  It's a lot fo information that is covered in the tests.  There are 2, and then a paper (10-12 pages) and a final.  Not the most difficult class, but not the easiest.
Interesting class. Cares about his students.

don't bother buying the books, exams are based on lecture powepoints which are on compass. If you do the study guides and memorize what's on them, you'll get an A on the exams and never have to attend lecture. Monotonous at times, but not bad. Interesting material.
Very nice guy and is willing to help students who need it.

Nice guy but very dry and monotonous.  Recaps readings verbatim in lecture, tests are mindless regurgitation, doesn't hand them back.  Completely devoid of comprehension or application, grade is based purely on how much you're willing to memorize.
Tests are pure regurgitation and he doesn't hand them back.  Nice guy but unenthusiastic and very dry, making 1hr.20min. classes seem like an eternity
Very Interesting Class... He basically summarizes readings in lectures, I never read anything and got an A in the class. Very nice professor, helpful
No Comments
Super boring.  Reads right off of Power Point--which is available online--but still takes random attendance in class.
He's a great lecturer, and makes the material so intuitive!

Excellent professor.

reviews.comment: Poised, patient, and impressive. Having experienced other ML courses, I can confidently say his lectures stand out with their clarity. Though our interactions are brief, I'm grateful for his approachable and supportive demeanor.

Professor Zhu is a really nice guy. He respects students' ideas about the self-proposed final project and offers useful suggestions. Gives very difficult homeworks without showing how they are done; condescends to his students. Allows late homeworks, but with a penalty. Very little time given during exams, which are tough.

Unhelpful. Ridiculous exam.

Poor.

Can't communicate.

Be prepared to learn the theory of stats learning and work hard on HWs and projects.
Harder than you would expect especially he asks you to write your own function and do a lot of things that are unnecessary.

reviews.comment: I personally do not recommend him for STAT 542, it is overwhelmingly challenging because of 80% of the hws you will have to write your own algorithm to do certain analysis. reviews.comment: STAT 432 is based on ISLR, but Professor Zhu introduces more topics in this course from Stack Exchange, etc. and covers few topics in more detail. Assignments (except 1) were easy especially for people who have already done a course in machine learning using R or have read ISLR.

reviews.comment: Professor Zhu is a very good professor. His lecture makes me wake up at 7 and he is super humorous. But his homework and exam is hard. Instead of build-in functions, we have to write our own function in R. The exam contains mostly"choice" questions that need you to judge each answer and choose several answers. Really push us to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Zhu is the best instructor I've ever had during my time at U of I. He truly cares about his students and well prepares for the lecturers. More important, what you learnt from his class will be extremely helpful for your future career. Of course, his class is tough, but you won't regret making efforts for it.

He is a good professor with passion. He is willing to help students and he likes to make jokes in lecture. But he kind of makes definitions confusing. His lectures are clear at first, but as the contents gets harder, he gets worse at explaining. I have to read textbooks to understand the concepts. But he is always willing to help.
You will never feel boring in his class.
great professor, explain things super clear and gives very useful insights
