Honestly the most straightforward class I've taken: lectures cover what's on the homework, discussion problem sets summarize the homework, and the exams cover the discussion problem sets. Plus, he had a great grading policy that rewarded continued effort in the class, replacing midterm grades with the corresponding part on the final if you improved
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The young professor holds a high sense of responsibility and his lecture is very passionate and useful. The professor is very patient to answer questions and provide help during the office hour. Really nice teacher. And the course digs deep into the details and statistical theories of diverse statistical learning algorithms, which is useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ruoqing is EXTREMELY humble, smart, and nice. He tries to get everyone involved in his lecture and is willing to answer questions in details. Wish to take other courses taught by him, but no chance since I have graduated :)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: They don't not know how to teach. They are not caring! Avoid taking this class with this professor.
definitely not born to be a teacher. not attentive at all, ignored emails often and very flat "teaching".

Professor Rurik's course was disappointing. His traditional lectures lacked interaction and made students uninterested. He focused on statistics and required filling out Excel sheets, while the previous professor emphasized pedagogical concepts. I had to drop the course due to Rurik's rude behavior and lack of teaching skills.

Dr. Wade may come off as a bit cold initially, but throughout the semester, I came to admire him greatly for his intelligence, interesting personal anecdotes, and for the research he does outside of teaching. The course itself was incredibly enjoyable, and I find it unfortunate that I won't have the opportunity to have him as a professor again.

Dr. Wade was an amazing professor and allowed students to discuss topics outside of this course, but relevant to social work and the state of the profession.  Absolutely would take again, wish the school of social work offered more classes from him.

I have never had a professor like this before. Yes, he might bring good discussion, but the arrogant "must be exactly how I think" attitude this individual gives off should definitely be looked at by the Dean of Social Work. He grades too hard, people are different and think differently. Other ways of thinking are not welcomed and it's so rigid.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great professor and great class. Essays take time and effort but he is lenient and an easy grader.
Very flexible with deadlines and understanding. I followed the rubrics and got good grades.

Steve is one of the best teachers if not THE best I've had at UI. He's thoughtful, fair, flexible with deadlines, and always available to meet when I'm not sure about something. Plus he makes class interesting with his funny sense of humor and mix of small group and independent activities.
His grading is very subjective. I don't think it's based on the syllabus. He is also not good at giving feedback and offering suggestions to students.
His classes are a bit boring, and many of his practices will ruin my interest in writing. If your writing style is not to his liking, he will unreasonably give you a low score. Not recommended.
Absolutely love this guy.

Stephen Runkle is really a great teacher. His dedication to students made my RHET 105 experience engaging, especially with its political theme. Besides, he is always responsive and willing to offer extra assistance, ensuring students feel supported.

I took it last semester and it was amazing - he was caring, inspirational, and humorous. Fair grading + Good feedbacks. Although it was a 8 AM class, he made it very energetic through his passionate teaching style. He's also very supportive - wrote college recommendation for my transfer application, and clearly he's the BEST professor in RHET 105.

I took this class almost 2 years ago and I am still thinking about it. Mr. Runkle is genuinely one of the most passionate, kind, and interesting lecturers I have ever had as an English teacher. I took this class as a freshman in engineering, and it struck me like no other. The gen ed was not only manageable, but I took away a lot from the class!!

Stephen Runkle can lecture on and on you don't have to pay attention at all, but you might enjoy the class more if you do. He gives relatively little coursework and is incredibly generous with due dates. There is no teacher better to have for RHET 105 because he makes taking a required gen ed not that bad.

Runkle is a very caring prof! His class was structured around the digital age and included 4 big essays. There were other smaller assignments as well. Very understanding about deadlines + offers feedback and help on most assignments. Class can get boring because ppl don't participate but he cares about content and helping so much. Highly recommend!

Runkle is a very chill, respectful professor. Everything is completion with the exception of four essays throughout the entire semester. Participation is for a grade, but I still got an A without participating in his class once. Runkle's class is the Kung Fu Panda definition of a Level 0 class.

Dr. Runkle is the Rhet 105 professor you want to have. Several assignments are for completion, and only 4 essays are graded. He's very flexible with deadlines, and he is always happy to offer feedback to help improve your essays. Very caring and understanding professor.

Although its based on rhetoric, he makes very engaging for students. It is a college writing course, so he does not easily dish out As on essays, but everything is mostly completion. Super understanding for deadlines and allows revision all on essays. Professor that truly cares about his craft and aims to inspire others to do the same.
While this professor is kind and understanding, if you're not writing in his style, then good luck getting a decent grade!

In his class rn. There is way too much work to do, and he doesn't give out 90+ grades easily like other lecturers. I heard that for the other rhet 105 lecturer, they have like 3 essays in total and the starting grade is like an 90, but we have weekly assignments, four 1000-words essay and a research paper and it's difficult to get full credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I hate writing essays and I'm not very good at them, but Mr. Runkle was a great professor. The class was boring at times, but the class was nice to have.
I enjoyed this course. We learned a lot and got the incredible opportunity to self reflect. Would recommend this professor.

Ostensibly, Steve's class is focused on examining social media, but actually he's designed something more interesting and important: a class that challenges students to examine themselves and the people they're on the way to becoming as they go about their lives on screens. I loved Steve's class and how it forced me to reflect on my habits.
Professor Steve was very great and kind.

Steve is very specific about how he wants you to write, which is good and bad. He tries different ways of teaching, like giving a project (make a video essay) to do during classtime and post it or just having class discussion or analyzing a student's paper in class. He gives a lot of feedback on essays. but he expects too much.

Steve was one of the best English teachers I have ever had. He is so clearly knowledgable and brings so many inspirational insights to class. He is very good about deadlines and if you need to you can turn in essays late without any penalty. The course content is also very relevant and interesting which makes writing essays a lot easier.

This professor is unusual  in a good way. Class was focused on social media influence but we talked about a lot of things, everything from furbies to the bodylines of 1960s Lamborghinis and the glamorous daughters of country music stars. Not too much reading and papers were manageble. One of my best classes.
Awesome professor, offers feedback on drafts! The lecture is not too discussion-heavy and he is understanding of deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I'm going to miss this class and the way Steve made me interested in examining how social media is influencing the way I live and think. I think it helped my writing skills; DEFINITELY the class opened my eyes to my own habits and the strange effects social media is having on us. I don't like writing, but I loved the way Steve taught the class.

Steve is a great, helpful, funny professor. Assigns the same nickname to everyone: "Nephew".

Class focused on various effects of SoCal media as well as the way Russia's attack on Ukraine is being presented on TikTok. Come to find his Aunt Jeremy Jr became world famous in China thanks to Meitu's face-perfecting app! 

Ain't nobody got time fa dat!

Runkle is a really caring and interesting professor which completely changed the way I viewed rhet 105. I have never been an English student so I was worried coming into this class but the way that Runkle taught his class made it easy for me to be motivated to work on something I personally don't care for. His grading is very clear and is fair.
Chill cat. Cool class.

Professor Runkle is a nice guy, but hes serious about COVID mask mandates. Often he tells students to pull their mask up over their nose. Its a Rhet class, but he focuses on social media and how its influencing us. He likes controversial topics and prompting students to think about why so many people are so stupid and lost.
Very understanding and a genuine person.

Really cool guy, that Mr. Runkle. During SP2021 he was very lenient with deadlines, as obviously more important issues were going on in the world. He often cancels lectures or prerecords them. He's very curious and gives good feedback. He encourages group conversation both on zoom and discussion boards. 10/10 do recommend.

Runkle was a good professor to have during COVID. He was very lenient with deadlines and seem to care about the challenges we're facing. Also his zoom lectures were interesting. Nice guy. Very helpful and reasonable. Not a crazy amount of work.

Mr. Runkle was extremely patient and helpful. He understood that we are dealing with a lot of craziness now more than ever and gave me extra time to finish my work. Class met once a week synchronously and he was always willing to meet on zoom if I needed to talk. Great professor!

I took RHET 105 with Runkle during the Fall 2020 semester. He was SUPER lenient with deadlines. The assignments were often open ended and related to current events and social media. Runkle is extremely kind, really loved his class.

Runkle is the BEST. Super lenient with deadlines due to COVID. Gives a "Do these things in the semester and you will get an A" so that you feel more apt to write creatively. He assigns 3 major essays and gives incredible feedback. Office hours are kinda late at night but its okay. He has synch lectures but sometimes replaces them with videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Steve is awesome! Really nice guy and loves his students. I took RHET 105 and he named his course "Life in the Age of the Mobile Device" so readings and discussions were basically talking about things like social media, technology, and smartphones. Deadlines for papers are very reasonable and readings are not super long.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Rarely do I like English classes but this one was actually interesting, partly because Steve chose good topics and gave us lots of options within those topic to write about.

Steve is a good guy and fun in class but his standards for a freshman class are maybe too high. I had to work TOO hard to get an A. He looks like Keanu Reeves if Keanu Reeves had no hair and a face that looked like Steves. I like the class a lot, but the Grading should be more realistic.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You cant stop a train with bacon? With this provocative question, the journey began. None of us would ever be the same. Gifted brand new whistles, we were instructed to blow them when the learning reached a boil. And blow them we did. In one case, all the way to Idaho. Thats when the bacon moved over. It was time for something meatier.

Runkle exudes interest in writing and thinking and tries to make students feel the same way. The course theme was cool (new social medias effects) but class discussion got repetitive. Runkle was funny, strange in a good way, and fair about workload and grades. Write precise descriptions and really develop your ideas and youll get an A.

I asked how to get A in the class and he couldnt tell me All he said is read and think about it and start your essay early. I asked how to get A on the paper and he didnt say. Thats a simple question. A teachers job is to tell you how to get A in the class. He just talks in class and it was confusing!!!

Steve is a dynamo. One minute hes talking about How to write a research paper and then he stands around and sing his falsetto describes particular of a sandwich he made last night. He just looking at us and smiles. like hes a genius or a silly actor full of magical cheese or beans. I learned how to be a better thinker about writing a paper o

We talk taboo stuff in class, including politics. We talk about technology a lot and how its changing our lives and culture. Some reading, not crazy, and four essays. Obviously thinks Donald Trump is a Bloated animal uterus.? We analyzed the evidence and medias role in the mess. Chill dude. Grades Main essays hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mr. Runkle was a blast in class, yet not afraid to take me to school! In HS, I was used to adding words to a paper to get the word count up. He's more about getting rid of words and focused on critical thinking. The assignment was something like "identify a moment that changed your life." Well, I'd checked all of my luggage for a flight from A

Wouldn't have chosen any other professor for RHET 105. Gives helpful feedback and is a fair grader. I really like that he due dates for papers were fair. Also, he hosts office hours every week which is helpful.

I would not recommend this professor if you want an A or an A+. He is a strict grader and is too unrealistic with the goals he asks from freshman students. His prompts are so complex to the point of confusion. He talks a lot (which I don't mind) but most of the time it is unrelated to the actual writing and learning process.
Top 2 or 3 classes I ever took.
Steve was very helpful to help me understand how to make my essays better when I went to office hours. He's a very helpful professor and a nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I was recommended this professor by my roommate who had him last year and said he was really nice and the class focused on technology. It wasn't what I expected but he is very helpful and I think my writing is better. He makes a lot of comments on your papers, which i liked.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Sometimes overexplains things and gets a little lost in tangents, but it's part of his personality, which is really cool and easy-going. I liked how much he seemed to believe in what he was teaching. Made me think about big ideas. Felt a little lost sometimes but talked to him after class and it made sense. One of my best classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Steve is a great guy, but more of a philosophy teacher. He takes a holistic approach to all papers, meaning there is no "taking sides" in any paper, whether is be analytical, research based, or story. Be prepared to question a lot of things and write a bunch (10) of small 1 page papers in addition to 4 big assignments. There's a group project too.

Steve is a lecturer who's passionate about what he's teaching. He also always has office hours every week, so you can look for help. However, there is no clear grading criteria, which makes it very difficult to really know what he looks for in the essays. There are also no extra credit whatsoever, so that makes your final paper worth a lot.

Steve is a great professor, not only for his interesting lectures (always prepared with questions, explanations and reflections), but also for his helpfulness. He makes himself available to discuss the assignments (only three papers and small projects) I would highly recommend to take RHET 105 with him

Awesome teacher. Only 3 papers and a group project. Participation matters a lot towards the beginning, but he's not uptight about it. He's always understanding and makes himself available a lot. Makes you work for your grade, but he's a fair grader. Steve's the MAN!

Professor Runkle is one of the best teachers I have known. Sometimes it's a little hard to know what he wants your essay to be like, but just talk to him and he will explain. It seems like maybe that's the point. The whole class seems like it's about figuring things out. Most of his assignments make you try to figure out what something means .

Steve is a great lecturer who genuinely cares about his students. He makes you really wrap your head around the essay topics, but it is less work compared to the assignment other rhetoric teachers make their students. He is always there for his students and a great guy in general.

Easily one of the best professors I have ever had. Mr. Runkle is so caring about his students, and deeply wants them to succeed. He gives terrific feedback on in class essays. Take his feedback seriously, and you will do well. I could not recommend him any higher.

I say now to all the world that this man, this teacher who names himself as "Stephen" Runkle on the course syllabus but who goes by "Steve", and whose name may or may not really be either, I say now before the assembled world that this man does indeed believe that he is cool. But that's okay, because he is, indeed, quite right.

Steve is a righteous dude. And if you've ever ridden through Pittsburgh on Amtrak at night & seen the bridges spanning the city's trio of rivers like necklaces of light, then you know what it's like to be pleased by a thing. Steve's class pleased me. It's not your average potato salad-type affair of busy work punctuating spells of boredom.
Runkle is the man.

One of the best things about Steve's class is we had it indoors. It can be very cold or hot or sometimes even windy and indoors was a tremendous choice. Plus his volume as appropriate most of the time. Sometimes something like a radiator is banging in a class, which can be really annoying. If the class is at lunch time, be sure to eat before it!

Do you think maybe cheeseburger is the answer? I think fun but it wasnt fun all the time. Class begins and everyone is sitting. A camper with all the latest apps and attachments was wheeled out like a prize from Price is Right. Now whom do you think is your daddy? This was not an appropriate way to celebrate anything. Even the fish was bad. Very.

Mr. Runkle brought a lot of energy and interest into a class that I expected to suck. He's one of the best teachers I've ever had. He actually seemed to care about what he's doing. The last review says that Mr. Runkle didn't explain his comments or criticisms on papers. That's totally ridiculous. His comments were EXTREMELY helpful. So was he.

Runkle was by far my worst professor I've had. He never showed A papers in class and therefore we did not know what an A looked like. I got C's or B's on my papers and he would not help me understand why. Also, his handwritting SUCKS. Can't read his comments on papers. Find a different professor for Rhet. I know there are better ones out there.

The classroom teacher dressed in swanky time-traveler regalia & looked like the end of the world almost all the time. He flaunts the imaginary tuna & peels the secrets off your skin. Be advised that this may spell catastrophe.
He is a nice guy but is not very open minded about the papers as a rhet professor is supposed to be but is very helpful and also very understanding.Overall a fun guy but he grades hard

This class was ALL about Ham Chowder. How to make it, what it tastes like, its textures, its history, how the ham is best prepared, the history of swine farming in Italy. If you love--really L-O-V-E--Ham Chowder and want to completely exhaust the topic, then absolutely take Steve's class. Me? I'd rather read and write about other things.
Very engaging professor. Papers were fair. The first one he grades hard on because he really wants to get the point across. The other 2 were extremely easy.
Stunkle just flipped the script on y'all and now he's going freestyle. Get on down wit yo bad self, Steve. Oh yeaaaaaahhhh!
Great teacher. Funny guy. Had a good time. Cheers.
Easy... Just work hard in your essays and keep giving your 2c in class no matter hoe fun/full the topic. Follow these steps and land yourself an A
Awesome professor. Very helpful and tries his best to make it interesting and fun. Moderate coursework and anyone who follows  his guidelines is assured of a good grade.
awesome teacher. really made an effort to make the class interesting. take his class if you can, very highly recommended.

Steve has a beautiful mule--perhaps the most beautiful in all the land--and he brings it to class most days. That was fine, but toward the end of class he'd usually ride the mule around the room while we just watched. Or he sat there buzzing the mule with his stupid little remote control helicopter.
First day of class this guy walks in and twirls a heap of his own loose meat right on the desk. Held a swirl just like a DQ cone. Amazing. After that, things went down hill.

One Word: Mister Jerry Christmas is at your service, making all stops between really interesting and not!!! On a lighter note, Jerry would like to thank Mr. Rinkle for a fine semester of one-liners and haberdashery. Cheers from the Indian subcontinent! (No animals were damaged in the making of this commercial).

Steve gives a lot of good feedback on papers and I'm proably a better writer after his class. I didn't like some of the subjects and sometimes the class was boring, whatever. He's a really nice guy though.

This guy began every class screaming at the top of his lungs every imaginable dirty thing he could possibly invent about my family. Neeless to say, by mid-semester this got a little old. Fortunately, after all the ranting was over, Steve wheeled out tubs of ice cream and toppings an everyone enjoyed building their own beautiful ice cream sundaes!!!

This class was fairly boring.  A lot of sitting around with Steve trying to pry discussion out of blankly staring students. But overall it wasn't that hard; for all three essays I turned them in exactly as he handed my rough drafts back and I received at least 5% higher than he said I would if I turned it in as is.

I liked Steve. I just had him for Advanced Rhetoric and it was a really good class. He makes the discussions lively and interesting and makes a lot of comments on papers. A lot of these people say he's a tough grader, but I don't think so. I agree that he is particular, but I think that's a good thing. A couple negative commets here...just haters.
Mr. Runkle runs a cool class. Very interactive. It's one of the few classes I've actually (sometimez) enjoyed attending. I like all his high-flying slam dunks (so to speak).
Awesome guy but he grades pretty hard.
Steve is cool, smart, funny, fair, and helpful. I think his grading is a bit too tough and his handwriting on papers is terrible. Otherwise, he's a great teacher.

This fellow seems to think hes Pittsburg WITH the cream cheese. But, whatever. He wears a white or a blue shirt everyday. Hates cell phones. I think he's a right proper citizen. Students need to talk more in his class. he needs to make them do it. I liked Steve's class. I'm the Russian judge, I give him an 8.5.

I liked Steve's class. He's friendly and clever. Some of the assignments were cool, but I think he should have more small assignments so students can boost their grade if they don't get good grades on essays. Overall he seemed like a fair, smart, interesting teacher. I would recommend his class.
Guy is a boss. Keeps it real 24/7 and even puts some good ole stank on the hang low.
EASY! BEST RHETORIC TEACHER!

I took Steve's class a couple years ago and he was great. It could be difficult to get an A because he's really particular, but he offered great feedback and gradeed fairly. He created a very comfortable class thanks to his humor and relaxed demeanor. I recommend his class. He made me like Rhet while most of my friends though their teachers dull.

Steve is easygoing and personable. The subjects of the essay assignments didn't always interest me, but he gives many helpful comments on drafts and is very encouraging. Class was entertaining and interesting some days, not so much other days. Overall he's an excellent and intriguing teacher.

I worked very hard in this class to get a paper that he considered acceptable.  I went to speak with him about a grade and he insulted my work (which I had rewritten after my rough draft) throughout the entire meeting.  Very difficult grader.  I have always been a very good English/rhetoric student and he made me feel useless and stupid.
Professor gives very less work! Highly recommended!

Very approachable guy.  His class is very boring to attend and grades papers pretty hard.  Make sure to consult him about papers before submission because he expects very specific details.  But whatever, he's cool.
As you can see from the previous post, the english of his students is really poor. Therefore, I would recommend you a different RHET 105 teacher if that's what you're looking for.
He is a very helpful Rhetoric teacher.  When you ask for help, he will gladly help you.  But you HAVE to ask for help.
Really nice guy

Steve was an awesome teacher. I can honestly say that he is one of my favorite teachers that I have ever had. I loved listening to what he had to say because he said it with such clarity, precision, yet so carefully choosing his words.
Incompetent lecturer. Superficial contents. Focus of exam questions are completely useless. Overall a huge waste of time.

His slides are clear, the lecture material is clear. What sucks is the way he's organized CS210. The class readings required paid memberships, assignment grading depends *heavily* on graders, etc. However, there is no way to reach out to him about the issues and improve the class. Cool guy otherwise.
He made the class really interesting. He was very mediocre. don't expect excellence but not expect it to be bad
Great professor, and a pretty chill low-stress class. Just make sure to go to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: There were several bumps in the road for new assignments, but overall, his lectures are some of the clearest out there with many detailed examples.

He is a SWEET AMAZING & beyond AWESOME guy. He's one of those profs WHO CARE ABOUT TEACHING. He will repeat concepts, connect them to something relevant today, & help you whenever you need it. MPs are not hard nor easy (which is great so you get to learn). He reviews topics b4 a semi pop quiz (warn in advance. 2 or 3 unless ppl skip lect). TAKE HIM

He is new to teaching this course. As a person, Ryan is a great guy. It seems like he wanted to do too much to overhaul the course and as a result, made the class significantly harder. He tries to make up for it in different ways. He is getting a feel for how to teach the class, so I believe he is worth giving a chance.
Ryan did make the class a bit harder, but it was manageable and worthwhile since we learned so much more.
The MP was annoying...made the class harder than anticipated
Seems to enjoy giving his students a hard time. Absolutely not recommended.
The course use to be quite fun before, but he has made it harder, starting from the first MP itself he made it impossible.

Lectures helped compile the readings for each week, attendance wasn't taken at the lectures, and lecture notes are online. Very interesting content, fun professor, and the exams were online and open-note.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy. Funny, engaging, and obviously cares about teaching. Lecture material is recycled, however; 95% of lectures consist of prof. Shosted reading off of slides. Lots of little assignments and readings that are easy to lose track of as well.

Dr. Shosted is a really nice guy, he clearly has a passion for linguistics. But he didn't appear to put much effort into his course, they were more run by the TAs, which led to things often being unclear. The course was a lot more work than anticipated. Lectures aren't mandatory, and often don't align with the exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I made the mistake of taking this class as a gen ed. Much more work than I anticipated, but the material was definitely very interesting. Attendance not required, but lectures were very good and worth attending. Funny guy and engaging lecturer.
Exceptional professor. The class is a fantastic introduction to linguistics and is very approachable.

Do NOT take this class unless you absolutely have to! The workload is ridiculous with a project that takes up a lot of time outside of class and some students were unable to complete parts of it due to their computers not being compatible with excel. Final exam was 3 hours with over 50 questions, and a lot of students were unable to finish it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof.Shosted was very funny and nice, which showed in his lectures. But, for a 100-level class, there was way too much reading (between 60 and 80 pages a week from a very vocabulary and scientific term-heavy textbook). Luckily, all the exams were online and open-note, but the amount of information was overwhelming at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Hilarious

reviews.comment:
I got a C+ because of my own problems, but Dr. Shosted was a great professor. Make sure you go to lectures to fully understand all of the concepts, plus they're usually fun :)
The textbook is used for reading assignments.
He and the TAs were very helpful when I had problems and he's happy to hear about your language discoveries or experiences.
A class professor and group of TAs. You will be lucky to have him for LING 100 and DO NOT SKIP LECTURES!!! They're very engaging and helpful.

This class is very difficult material but Shosted does a great job in reviewing core concepts over and over and checking in to make sure we understand it. Don't skip lectures or you won't make it, the book and online portions aren't enough. Semester project is also intense but if you commit and ask for help he'll help you succeed.
I really enjoyed Ling 100, and Prof. Shosted really made it so much better. He's an engaging and educated lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Shosted is very passionate and an engaging lecturer. Even though the course materials can be difficult, especially the course project, he makes himself readily available and the guidelines very easy to follow. He is also very understanding and lenient. I would highly recommend Prof Shosted as a Ling professor.

I came to University of Illinois in order to study with him, and I'm unbelievably disappointed. He doesn't care at all about his students, and is extremely passive aggressive. In private conversation, he all but told me that I shouldn't consider a career in Linguistics during week 1 of class. Really tries to make you feel small.

Professor Shosted doesn't seem like he cares very much about his student's success. He assigned a ridiculous amount of work for someone who doesn't truly teach it. He is a hard grader with very little sympathy or understanding for extenuating circumstances. I wouldn't take another course with him if I could help it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Love him! He makes lectures interesting and engaging, and is overall super cool and approachable. I'm definitely taking another one of his classes.

Despite how boring many classes were made as a result of online delivery, Prof. Shosted gave really amazing lectures and tried his hardest to keep the course interesting and informative. The subject matter isn't entirely intuitive for those who don't have prior experience in linguistics but the class is still very easy. Would easily recommend him.
prof shosted was cool but VERY hard class. maybe ling isn't for me but I found this very difficult so I would not recommend to non linguistic majors. lots of reading and hard concepts.

Shosted is a genuinely uncaring professor. Phonetics with him was an absolute nightmare, and even students who came into the class absolutely loving him hated him by the end. He talked big about not "wanting us to stress out" but then doled out the most ridiculous workload I've ever had in a course with no coverage of content on hw or exams.

The project for this class will consume your life. You need to no life this class to get a good grade. Not only do we have a MASSIVE (40+ hour) project, but we also have 2 midterms, homework, and a 25% final that takes THREE HOURS. Shosted seems like a cool guy, but this class has too much work and he has no compassion for how much work we put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All online quizzes come before lecture, so you don't receive a formal lecture on the information. Doesn't cover all the info in lecture, tests you on things you never talked about or saw on homework/quizzes. Semester long project - takes over 50 hours. Final worth 25% of the grade, and cumulative. Doesn't know when things are due.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: you learn a lot in this class.... because he assigns hours of readings and homework that you do on your own while he covers the bare minimum in class. linguistics students beware
Never take his classes unless they are absolutely required
You don't have to go to lectures, but it's worth it because he's hilarious. Easy A and a fun class.

Dropped the class halfway through the semester, but not because of the professor. He's great and cares about all his students - even took the time to learn my name after one office hours visit. Exuberant amount of memorization, semester long project and intermittent online assessments. Wouldn't recommend as a GenEd, mainly due to dedication needed.
Very entertaining lecturer. You will learn a lot, and the grading is fairly generous. Definitely take his class! Also, the TAs are fantastic.

Excellent professor. He cares deeply about the subject material, and his lectures reflect that. His lectures are funny, and explain the material very well. It is not difficult to get an A, but you should definitely read the textbook.

I loved this prof! The lectures weren't mandatory but I still went to every single one just because he made it so interesting. I learned a lot in this class and it wasn't too hard. He really cares about the subject and the students-- I highly recommend this prof and ling100 as a whole, especially if you're trying to get a feel for linguistics.

I loved this introduction to Linguistics! Apparently they redid the whole class this semester, and it was great. The tests are online and open book/notes/etc. There's a project the whole semester, but it's split into milestones and it's very manageable. There are homework assignments and reading quizzes, but EVERYTHING is done online which I liked!

Shosted's approach to teaching is absolutely horrendous. As he all but brags, he deliberately makes this class as hard and frustrating and soul-crushing as possible because (direct quote) "welcome to my world". He gives every indication of being unhappy with his career and taking it out by punishing his students. Avoid his classes at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He was really funny and made the content more interesting. He is a good lecturer and I enjoyed the class.
He was funny and engaging!!

I don't know why the last review that shows up here is so bad. I am in his LING100 class and I couldn't ask for a better professor. He's hilarious and willing to work with students to make the material more manageable. Easiest A I ever got. Look forward to taking him again next semester :)

Shosted does not teach the class well, the TA's mainly teach the class. The class is easy overall just do the homework and go to discussion. Read the textbook there's  a reading quiz every week they're easy but read the book to not fail. Attendance is 10 percent of your grade so go to lecture even if it sucks!

I'm genuinely surprised he doesn't have better ratings than he does. Everyone currently in my class fully enjoys his class and he has the entire class in laughter all the time. If I had to describe him in two words, they would be "lovable jerk". He's simultaneously incredibly sincere and very sarcastic which makes for interesting discussions
The first day of class, he asked us to tell jokes and then explained what part of linguistics made them funny. Lecture slides are informative and full of puns.

Prof Shosted is probably the best professor I've had on U of I campus ever. He really breaks down everything so it's understandable and is more than willing to help out during office hours or email. He makes sure you're understanding everything by asking mandatory questions in class. They're not bad since he always gives a heads up the class before

This is an amazing professor and a wonderful person. He is clear and enthusiastic, always willing to help. Expects you to read the material and complete assignments on time. I would definitely recommend his classes.

Most boring class. It's about languages such as Klignon and Elvish. I would not take again. Doesn't really help and expects you to remember linguistic terms even if you're not a linguistic major. Terrible and so boring. I hated it

Absolutely Excellent. I thoroughly enjoyed his class. He is concise, consistent and absolutely clear on everything he expects. Would highly recommend this professor. I have learned a great deal from him.

Seems like a nice guy if you got to know him, but his attendance policy made me skip class. Asks questions on previous readings and if you don't get them right, you lose points for participation - in front of the whole class. If he changed his methods, I think I would have really liked the class.

This is the worst teacher I have ever known or taken classes with. He combines lack of knowledge, rudeness, and insincerity in teaching his classes. He's careless about students and cares only about his research. I never recommend this professor to anyone.
Probably my favorite professor at U of I, he has a great teaching style and is a fair grader. You'll need your textbook for his classes.
I didn't like him and I hated the class. He wasn't clear on assignments or what is going to be on the exam. I have learned nothing from him.

I enjoyed his class. It was interesting and pretty stimulating. I didn't like when he called out your name for questions, that made me dread class sometimes; it's also his method for attendance, so GO to class... Read the book to understand the material. Reasonable and friendly professor. Coursework is average but helpful for tests.
I think Ken is a very insightful professional, his lectures have a lot of deep layers.  He is not a harsh grader at all, and reads everything you have to say, I think he is an incredible teacher.

Ken Salo is unfortunately an incredibly poor Professor, who I highly recommend avoiding. After taking UP 160, I left wondering what, if anything I had learned, but I could not think of anything. It felt like Prof. Salo had long stopped caring about it. The class was nothing more than unimportant discussions, with no new information.
Professor Salo comes into class with lots of swag. He brings up interesting topics and his classes are some of the most enjoyable I have had. Would for sure recomend.
Very boring and lack of clarity, he doesn't know how to teach at all, plus he constantly changes assignment due date and requirement, not a hard class but not recommended
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Can be demeaning and demanding. He is passionate but not very well organized and can sometimes leave you hanging. Overall not bad but go with someone else if you can

Ken is an amazing guy, but his teaching is all over the place. Luckily I had a great TA this semester, or I would have been way more confused. The content of this course was very interesting but I ended up disliking the class because of how unorganized it was and how much writing there was.

A competent person, but not a good teacher. His lectures meandered without any focus. The class schedule was ditched early on, and it seemed like he was improvising the semester as he went. He would make up extra credit assignments on the spot with very short notice. Never answered emails. Not a hard class, but not worthwhile.

Professor Salo is a well-intentioned and smart man, but he is also extremely liberal. This class requires you to write a lot, so make sure to pick a viewpoint that leans left if you want a good grade.

Hes just honestly not a good teacher. Not a hard class to get an A or B in, but he will stress you out with his complete lack of organization, and total lack of clarity. He also will just surprise you and come up with randon assignments and little clarity at all times.

He's an excellent teacher who is very understand with issues in your personal life that may conflict with class. He's always there to make your life easier and is super passionate about what he's teaching in "Teaching Ferguson." The assignments are not complicated and you will do well on them if you put effort into it, but it's not hard to do.
You don't have to read every chapter of the book but just your chapter you're going to present on and show up to class and listen you'll pass flying colors.

I only really read chapters when we had presentations on them or when we had writing assignments coming up. Expect lots of those. In order to make the course load less immediately intensive he has multiple 500 or 250 word assignments and one final 2,500 word assignment. Lectures are mandatory only because you hear his thoughts on various topics.

Defining what was required for a good grade was extremely difficult, he is constantly modifying the syllabus: adding assignments, removing some, changing others. Talking to him and emailing him for clarification will not help as I've done both and each time his response has been different. Extensive writing, relatively harsh grader, presentations.

Prof. Salo really knows his stuff, he makes you think critically and broaden your views. Class can get kind of awkward and quiet if people don't participate, as he relies heavily on discussion. Prepare for A LOT of writing. For my class it was 5 papers plus 1 longer final paper, but most of the essays build on each other and are repetitive.

Professor Salo's class may lack some structure at times, but it is far from horrible. Salo is an extremely intelligent teacher that truly wants his students to look at the world's events critically. The class consists solely of writing assignments which aren't too hard if you put some effort into them. Also, Salo is always willing to help.

Salo's long winded musings have little basis in reality. he gives vague and confusing instructions for assignments and will change the goals half way to deadline. be ready for saturday morning walking-tours and 3,000 word essays. take this class if you are willing to walk all over the city and write endlessly.

This professor is a very essay-heavy teacher. Too many group projects and pointless filler assignments as well as so so so many readings it is honestly ridiculous. She also takes attendance but class is so boring you never want to show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took MCB 450 for minor requirement; absolutely ridiculous amount of information to memorize.  She basically reads the textbook to you and then asks you detailed fill-in-the-blank questions during exams. Class average was extremely low, so they applied a "generous" curve of 1%.

The most unengaging and robotic instructor I've had. Sarkar appeared unconcerned with student success in the class, racing through 60-slide (!) powerpoint presentations at breakneck speed. Grade based on just three exams, one of which is a cumulative final worth 50% of the total grade. Class average was 66%, a C by the scale. You teach yourself.
this class was extremely hard. it has WAY too much information, especially for a summer class. the tests are very difficult and the class is out of 400 points-just 3 tests and a final
Makes stats very easy to understand.

He is actually a great person to have in your class. He cares about the students and actually teaches instead of reading from the notes. What I like about him is that you get a chance to drop your final if you do well in participation, homework, and your midterm. But the catch is that you need to participate and do HW. overall I recommend him!

Great lectures. I had taken statistics in a nearby community college and always struggled with quantitative methods. However, in ACE 264 i found the lectures and the material really approachable. The homeworks helped me stay on track too.

I got a B- in this course but I recognize it's my fault. I did not spend enough time on the material. I would recommend Prof. Dall'erba again and again. He helped me a lot with his and his TA's office hours. The lectures are very clear but you have to be focused while in class. He has a great sense of humor too.
Very good course. You have to come prepared and ask questions but you learn so much from this course.
AWFUL STAY AWAY

This class was pretty difficult. There are three exams and one homework assignment most weeks. He drops the lowest of these four categories. The exams tend to have some trick questions. The best part of this class was that lectures were online and in person and that exams were open book and online. He was funny which made lectures a little better.
Asks a lot of trick questions on exams and lectures are hard to follow. But the class is not that difficult and Professor Dall'Erba is pretty funny.

This class is miserable. There are 2 midterms, one final, and 10 homework assignments, each of those categories are worth 25% of the grade. For the final grade he takes the best 3 of those scores. The homework is tough and don't expect to learn much in class, he just reads complicated statistics formulas off a PDF. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are 3 tests including the final. He gets rid of one with the worst grade but the final was hard and long. So you dont get a chance to drop one of the first 2 exams and replace that with the final. Homework was time consuming, but if you use the notes and ask questions about whats required you will get an A. His English isnt very good.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shes a grad student. She brings a lot of energy to the class! PSYC238 is a LECTURE & is demanding: 6 quizzes (drop 1), weekly readings & questions, 2 papers. Shes very helpful especially in office hours!, advocates for students (were inperson in COVID)but UIUC has rules about what she cant offer us. Shes caring, supportive, kinda funny & weird

She is really smart and informative, but not a good teacher. Usually during lectures she will monologue for 50 minutes, and wont engage at all with the students and how they are with the material. Interesting course, but honestly would rather just have had recorded lectures because it feels like she is just talking to herself most of the time.
Snarky replies when students asked questions. Blamed students for not understanding material during 10 second review questions. Great subject to learn about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A professor that was once a good teacher. Now, his insight and advice are dated/not relevant to the world of archival sciences. He talks about “enduring value” of records (when all of his advice has little enduring value). He mentions making students “employable” while not understanding the current job market. Save yourself the headache and avoid.

Scott has been doing this for a long time and clearly knows a lot. However, the instructions are not always clear, and when they are he is incredibly particular about everything. It makes it hard to be okay with making mistakes as he makes it very known when you have made one. He also puts a lot of pressure on the future.

While this professor is knowledgeable about the field, and not a bad person, he is beyond frustrating to have as a professor. He requires extremely specific answers, and honestly quite full of himself. His goal seems to be to catch students out. He has decided opinions about everything. He adds stress and intensity to everything.

Professor Schneider is the goat. You can tell she is very passionate about the course in the way she teaches in lectures. I had her for discussion, too, and she was awesome. She makes the course very engaging and interesting, whether it's about reptiles, amphibians, or pocket pets.

Amazing lecturer!! Classes were super engaging, and going to lecture was genuinely fun. I had her for my discussion section as well, and we got to see so many cute animals and do a lot of hands-on activities (super fun). She's actually passionate about what she is teaching so you should take this class if you love animals too!
Great lecturer and really cares about her students.

Super easy gen ed. I definitely recommend taking this class to fulfill. This was the first year that there were exams in this class, but they are super easy. There are 2 exams and a final. However, if you attend 11/13 of the discussions, you don't have to take the final. I do recommend going to discussion because it will help with the exams.

Lectures are pretty easy, especially if you're someone who loves pets. In discussion, they bring in a lot of pets, and they are adorable. There are also extra credit opportunities at almost every single discussion. Technically discussions aren't mandatory, but if you attend 14/16 or something like that, you get an automatic 100% on the final.

Professor Schneider's ANSC 207 class is very easy. I would highly recommend taking this course if you need to fulfill a science gen ed. The class occasionally brings in cute pets! There aren't any tests, just assignments to complete. You do need to be careful about deadlines, though. Overall, this class was fun to take.

The animals in this class were so cute! They brought in pets once in a while and it was my favorite part of class. I did think the class was kinda boring besides that. Everything was easy enough to do without lecture, but participation was mandatory. Should be a zoom class tbh.
I honestly like the pets, but the professor is bad. The class is kind of silly tbh they teach you things that would take 5 seconds to google.
This class was amazing, It was fun and engaging, and the material is actually useful as many people have pets. The Discussion sessions sometimes bring pets and they are adorable!!

I found this class to be very easy and required little to no effort, but I was not impressed by the instructors. They are not considerate of students time or efforts, and the curriculum is passive aggressive. This class doesn't trust students to be accountable for themselves even dismissed people by table like middle schoolers.

Very easy class, with online lectures and in-person discussion. You do not need to watch lecture content beforehand to do well in discussion as a lot of it is just another lecture. You do one group activity for credit for the day, and sometimes they bring in pets.
I dont know what to say, he does not consider real situations....
people hyping him up for no reason he is lowkey kinda bad
Lectures teach you everything you need to know. Professor was reachable outside of class and is always very willing to answer questions.

He is a great professor and taught ECE 110 really well. I wasn't enrolled in his section but I always watched his lectures online and learnt the whole curriculum through that. He was very helpful and made complicated topics easy.

Schuh is pretty good overall. He typically explains concepts concisely; however, sometimes I wish he would deviate from the lecture slides a little more to keep the class engaged. Most of the time, it feels as though he is reading from a script. Other than that, he's a great professor and is good at explaining the topics in 110.

Took ECE 333: he didn't have the correct exam information for the first exam and no reply to email that stated that. Had the wrong time, place for exam, and the lectures that the exam covered. Resulted in cheat sheet (allowed for the exam) not properly covering the material since exam covered "lectures 1-8" , but heavy material from lectures 9-12.
pretty good at teaching, clear that he likes what he does

This professor was great. This was my first class transferring from community college, so I didn't know what to expect. The main difference was the exams. The exams were harder than the homework, but if you pay attention to the lectures and understand the homework front to back, then you'll be okay. He also can go over exam questions if you missed.

fine professor with a steady voice and firm tone, but he often spends entire classes on just two or three problems. He often shows unnecessarily on mathematical calculations of a problem, even when the key starting steps are the use of ECE concepts/tricks and the pure math part could be streamlined instead of being elaborately worked out in class.
Tests are easy as long as you do all the review and homework questions. He teaches decently well and if you don't understand, his office hours help greatly.
Very good lecturer, makes sure all questions get answered and does a great job answering any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures are not very helpful. He just does examples in class, and there is no textbook to read from for class to understand the background concepts. Even though I can solve most of the problems presented, I understand little to nothing about what is actually happening beyond the circuit.

Even though I feel like I can do most of the problems, I understand nothing. I get the idea of cutting back on derivations and purely conceptual lectures, but in this class, it's been pushed so far to the extreme that I feel like I haven't actually learned anything except for how to plug and chug from the extensive list of formulas we're given.

Schuh was great! I entered UIUC without any background experience at all and was nervous about taking 110. But his lectures were always so clear and never felt rushed. Overall, I would highly recommend Schuh if you are taking 110.
He is not as helpful as people claim to be. His lectures are better than the other 110 lecturers, but he is not very accessible outside of lectures.
ECE 110 is a very well structured class, and Professor Schuh gave the most helpful lectures. Grading is easy compared to most ECE classes

Professor Schuh cares about students' learning very much. His lectures are very good and understandable, and he makes it easy for students to ask questions. The content of the class is not very difficult, but if you want to be able to retake quizzes show up to class for iclicker credit. 10/10 professor and lectures.
His lecture notes are the best! Best 330 teacher. Note that getting 4.0 in 330 is still difficult in terms of percentage (~20-25%).
The songs he play before the lectures are goated.
Not a great lecturer at all, but does answer questions patiently. Students in his class literally have the second lowest average class GPA compared to other sections.
Pretty good in terms of UIUC standards. Very fair.

Professor Schuh was a really enjoyable lecturer to have for ECE 110. He was really great at answering questions and was very thorough with his explanations. He was quite knowledgeable on the course material, but did not always know what was going on outside of lecture (in regards to the class). Homework/tests were pretty straightforward and fair.

Professor Schuh has a great lecture style and answers all questions patiently after every section. Both his offline engagement with students and online recording styles are great. The course is not test-heavy, and all quiz problems come from the review section problems along with retake opportunities.

I love Sergi. Studio is difficult, but if you put in the work, then you will get a good grade. He really cares about effort, and you need to take his suggestions. His feedback is very clear, and he is very nice and funny. One of the best Architecture professors. The only downside is that he is not very tech-savvy, but your TAs will help with that.
Funny and gives good straightforward feedback

This class was required for my course but he was such a harsh grader. Anytime I asked a question he told me to search it up online and never helped me. I once asked him for help about an upcoming test which was our only grade for the semester and he laughed at me. He is sarcastic and funny but not a good professor and doesn't help you.

I LOVE SERRAT! Obviously, studio is a lot of work, but he is super understanding and does his best to adjust assignments to be more manageable. He is scary on first impression, but he is a nice guy and hilarious! He loves precision and neatness in your work and gives thoughtful feedback. As long as you apply his suggestions, you will succeed!

Course is a LOT of work, but that's with any professor in studio. He's a little intimidating at first but ultimately very grounded and compared to other studio professors he is pretty realistic with assignments. I've personally really enjoyed my time in his section.
He seems extremely intimidating but he's really funny. Definitely doesn't know how funny he is though. Humble king.
Fine professor, very good course structure.

He clearly knows a lot about the topic and he does a pretty good job explaining the material most of the time. I personally didn't really vibe with his teaching style, but I'm sure others would like it. To me, he comes off as rude and condescending when asking questions and during office hours, and acts like you should already know the content.
He takes his time to help students out!
Meticulously created amazing lecture notes which covered all topics with specific example problems and solutions.

Regardless of my final grade due to a bombed final, Schmitz is the only thing keeping me alive in the EE section of ECE. I have not had the privilege of having him as a professor, but his recorded lectures are a godsend.

Had him for ECE 110 and 198. Great dude, genuinely cares about his students and wants to see them grow. Lectures can get a bit boring (they aren't bad tho), but outside of class he is great to know and genuinely passionate about ECE and passionate about making sure his students succeed.

His online lecture during covid saved my day!
He taught with clear logic and a good explanation of all the core concepts during a relatively short period of time. He used many good examples to demonstrate his ideas and increase students' understanding.
He recorded many helpful videos about labs.
Hope I have the opportunity to take his ECE220!

A great professor! I had him for 110, and now 210. 210 is an incredibly difficult class, but Schmitz clearly tries to help students understand: he answers questions thoroughly and will take as much time as you need to understand. He constantly asks for feedback because he genuinely wants to improve the course. Highly recommend his lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Good teacher, gives clear lectures and adapted well to online school. Takes feedback very often. The course itself had some issues, but no particularly awful experiences. Holds weekly office hours.
Professor Schmitz is fantastic, lectures are engaging and presented well. Don't miss office hours though, they really help solidify the material.
Great professor, enjoyed his class

I tried to like Schmitz; I really did. Unfortunately, his lecture style makes it incredibly hard to participate. In addition, he was consistently dismissive toward feedback about the class (which he runs). Prepare for unreplied emails and ignored discussion posts if you have anything critical to say.

Professor Schmitz is a kind professor who explains concepts simply. He's a really good teacher; circuits make sense when he explains them. He's very well organized. Be aware though, Schmitz does NOT like if you miss lab, and he can be a bit no-nonsense when you're trying to explain why you need your deadlines extended because your grandpa died...

Prof. Schmitz is a great lecturer and always teaches the material and answers questions clearly in a way anyone can understand. He's also just a wholesome guy who truly cares about his students succeeding and learning to the best of their ability. Even people who don't have him attend his lectures because he makes learning fun!

Professor Schmitz was great for ECE 110. In his lectures he give great intuitive ways to understand problems which helps engineering students grasp concepts better in my opinion. He also handled having the class online to the best of his ability. You can't go wrong with him for ECE 110!

Schmitz is my BOY. He's super chill, and explains things far clearer than any other ECE prof. Very accessible. Lectures can go a little fast sometimes, but he usually catches it and pauses to encourage questions. Super friendly, always willing to help students even with trivial stuff, and just an all around good guy. Best ECE 110 prof for sure.

Don't pass up the opportunity to take his class! Office hours before and after class are extremely convenient especially since he is also an ECE academic advisor and is open to any type of questions. He puts some life into engineering and truly made me feel like I was in the right place.

He's a real cool dude, down to earth and passionate. Explains things well and will take questions during lecture. Holds office hours conveniently before and after lecture, and will definitely go the extra mile to help students out. He teaches the content well and doesn't rush it, gives you a good intro to electrical engineering.

As a non ECE major, this was the hardest class in freshman Fall. I felt that the foundational concepts of the course was rushed quite fast, and it was difficult for me to keep up with the harder stuff, despite attending support and doing self-study. He is a good professor, but be prepared to self-study using the textbook a lot if you are a non-ECE.
Good lectures and make a entry level class interesting and applicable to both future classes and daily life.

He is good for ECE majors, however, any other major will not do well with him. He is not an understanding person. If you do not understand the work he will make you feel unintelligent and the work seem trivial. If you do take his class, you will be relying on the help of TA's to understand the material. His class is very demanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I didn't know absolutely anything about electronics when I entered Prof. Schmitz's first lecture. I basically chose ECE as a guess (my parents are both electrical engineers). It didn't take much time for Prof. Schmitz to reassure me that I had made the right choice, making me fall in love with electronics in no time. Excellent professor and person.
Very good professor. Clear and patient when explaining content. Takes time to create well prepared lectures. Take the class with him if you have the chance

Although I've had many technical course instructors; Professor Schmitz is very effective at relaying the information in a clear and concise fashion. The material presented is not based so much on technical ability to decipher problems so much as it is required to have a thorough foundation of the fundamentals. Professor Schmitz is a great teacher!

Just a disclaimer, in ECE 110 you can go to any lecture, so even if you can't get Schmitz, try to make his time slot available, that's what I did. I found my actual lecturer greatly over-complicated very simple topics. Schmitz does a good job of making things easy. Do practice test, and try in Lab and an A is doable for anyone.

Schmitz himself is a nice guy and is pretty good at making things seem easy. However, this means sometimes it may seem easy to him but the class won't understand (as seen by i-clicker results). Otherwise, the class isn't too hard, just study for exams with practice exams. Lots of resources outside of class to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor for 110. Works through problems in class and answers questions well.

Best 110 professor there is. He is much clearer than the other lecturers and does an amazing job of helping you to actually try and understand and learn concepts rather than memorize. Use the course notes as a resource before every lecture to understand concepts even better.

Easy for any ECE freshman I would say. Sometimes you don't need to go to the lecture. As long as you read all the lecture notes and do practice problems. I also registered the honor lab section and it was awesome. The lab section could be easy or hard depends on your partner.

Has a tendency during lectures to sort of try making some conceptsproblems seem easier by asserting they are not that hard. However, he is a very nice guy and really truly genuinely wants to see every student succeed. The amount of support available in the course is very high.
Good professor.

Prof Schmitz does a fantastic job of explaining the material. His lectures are also inspirational in that he urges and prepares you to do well in future ECE classes with little tidbits of advice he incorporates in lecture. He also stays after to answer everyone's questions.

The professor is very disorganized. He did not provide information on the course grade breakdown until after the first midterm, and he provides very little guidance on what to expect for the exams. The exams are graded by few things and make up a steep part of the grade. Additionally, the lectures are generally unrelated to the graded content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grade of the course is solely based on 2 exams: one midterm and one final. Strictly following the standard grade system and no curve at all. (You will get a B- at 82%)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Disorganized, poor flow. Limited practice, no partial credit hinders learning Unfair grading: no partial credit. Useless 200+ page "cheat sheets." Inefficient setup.
Course ought to be pen+paper & calculator.
Avoid this class altogether and try to get credit from another stats class.

This professor seems to have a consistent approach to teaching, with lectures and exams remaining the same over time, which can make it easier to achieve a high score. He is very nice, although his focus on teaching may not be as strong.
Exams were a bit intensive -- but he sounds like Mark Rober so it's chill.

He was pretty okay. The lectures were typically very good. However, the course lacked recourses (i.e recorded lectures, meaningful slides, lecture notes, etc.). The grading was "vibes based" and lacked rubrics. The course is all assessment based, which is tough. This class dropped my gpa a bit, but overall it was an okay class and professor.

His canvas is poorly structured, slide decks uninformative, lectures unhelpful, weekly quizzes unnecessary, no practice exams annoying and exams unnecessarily hard for a gen ed class. If you read textbook, plug the slides into AI, and spend 1hr/week outside or instead of class and learn from the many excellent TA's it should be an easy A.

so much reading in this class, do not take it if you want an easy gen ed. grading is pretty lenient, but there is just so much out of class work and the lecture slides have almost no words on it so it is hard to go back to them.
Way too much reading for a 100-level class. Grade is determined only by quizzes and exams. Lecture slides are useless for reviewing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes is unacceptable due to bad questions. Exams or quizzes will have too detailed questions. Bad grading system: test heavy, no curve applied.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It is a very interesting course and Sepkoski is very engaging. Quizzes and exams are easy if you understand the material but there are just way too much reading. Make sure to go to EVERY lecture because the slides contain minimal information. Don't get too stressed out on the readings because I aced both exams while missing out a whole textbook xd
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, very passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches. Lecture slides hold ZERO information since he knows his stuff, so although attendance is not graded, you really need to go to all the lectures. Weekly readings are assigned, though not all are totally needed for the quizzes. Midterms are fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grade is made up entirely of exams, quizzes, and in-class essays. The quizzes are six points each, and getting one question wrong can have a big impact on your overall score. Some quiz questions are really strange so review does not work. The slide did not help with the review because it only had a lot of pictures and some non-focused content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was a good professor overall, and had engaging in lectures, but there was way too much reading for a 100 level history class. Weekly quiz grade is entirely dependent on whether you do the reading and attend every lecture. Lectures aren't recorded and the slides have minimal important information because he knows the material, so don't miss any.

I didn't attend a lot of lectures, and it reflected in the grades I got on the weekly quizzes (still passing though). The readings are useful and help with the quizzes and exams, and the take-home essay isn't too hard to write when you use your time wisely. Also, for the lectures I did attend, he was very engaging and provided useful info.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Sepkoski was an amazing professor but this class is very term-heavy and you have to be paying attention in lecture to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great lectures. Easy but really interesting class

Professor Sepkoski is a very fun and engaging lecturer, who *often* talks about interesting topics. A couple of lectures towards the end of the semester seemed rushed, but still a bit interesting nonetheless. Weekly quizzes are very focused on lecture content, so lots of note-taking is suggested.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Sepkoski was a great lecturer, even when the topics discussed weren't all that interesting. This class is probably too much work for a 100-level class, but the grading is very lenient so it balances out. Lots of reading. Lectures slides are posted but I recommend the lectures because Prof. Sepkoski provides the necessary explanations

In lectures he jumps between different topics and doesn't make it clear how they relate to each other so its easy to get lost. Weekly reading quizzes aren't bad if you read but its a lot of reading each week. He clearly knows a lot ab what he is teaching and is passionate about history which makes the lectures less boring. There's 1 take home essay

I actually had him for 268 in SP22 and loved the class!! The lectures and accompanying content/readings were really fascinating and since that was where all of the information came from, he was really animated about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures for the most part were super interesting and I generally enjoyed the course material. He honestly seems like a chill guy, but sometimes the stuff that he puts on his weekly quizzes was barely mentioned in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He usually assigns reading out of the textbooks on top of primary source readings then you get weekly quizzes on those that aren't too hard. In lecture, he talks so much and it kinda gets boring but you deal. The exam wasn't awful; as long as you've been following along in class you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: he uses iclicker which is unfortunate because the lectures don't always relate well to what's on the quizzes. if you skim the book you'll be fine. overall not a great prof but not horrible either

Honestly the best professors I've had in Econ department. He is knowledgeable, patient, and caring. The problem sets and exams are really well-designed. Super supportive and accessible in and outside the class. Perfect explanations of all kinds of stat and econometric concepts. Attend the lecture, be success, and be well-prepared for future.

Amazing professor and eager to see students succeed. Class is lecture and test heavy. There are supplementary problems sets with good feedback. Very fundamental and foundational course. One of the best classes I've taken.

1. Really really nice person, care about his students.
2. His teaching is amazing. His office hour is very helpful as well.
3. Patient enough to all questions.
4. Hard exam but well designed.
5. Problem sets are well designed.
6. Hard work pays off.
7. One of the best professor in the department IMO.
A very nice and excellent professor. He always tries his best to help students. His 471 is definitely the best course I have ever taken in my college career.

a little tough if you don't have a level of understanding of statistics. (take some stats courses before this) But he did well in explaining all the concepts.
I like it he handwrites the all notes in lectures.
Office hour definitely worth going. 
You pay effort to it, you'll get what you deserve, generally in this class.

Incredibly supportive instructor; will go to all the ends to answer questions during and after class. Even though the class has prereqs, he explains all the concepts from the very beginning. The course is hard with long difficult problem sets but considering the effort that he puts into the class, the assignments and challenging exams seem fair.

I took it in his first semester teaching, the class was not easy and you had to put effort but he was very helpful and actively tried to be as fair as possible with grading. Definitely one of the top professors in the Econ department. If you want to learn and are ok with putting in effort 471 with him is a solid choice.

There is one individual research project as well as a group project which will take most of your time out of this class. There are 3 exams that are self explanatory if you understand the content. If you put in the work, you should have no issues passing this class. From my own personal experience, she is a fine professor who wants you to pass.
My least favorite class I've ever taken. The content is very straightforward, but she makes the tests so difficult. Many test questions are so long that it's fatiguing to just read through.

Attendance is mandatory, but she kind of just reads off the slides. 
She makes it clear what is expected on the exams and in the assignments. They are very lenient on grading.
Exams are relatively difficult, but it's the wording rather than the concepts. Review sessions more helpful than the review guides. Just go over the lectures.

I, too, showed up to lecture, took notes, did an average amount of studying (making a quizlet), and still struggled immensely. This class was so unnecessarily hard. I consider myself to be a very dedicated student, and this class really did test me. It just does not need to be such a difficult class, especially for undergrad. Overall disappointed.

Take this class if you get off from torture. Tests are nothing like the study guides or slides. Went to almost every class, did all assignments, watched/read all required material, and still struggled. Exams are full of awfully worded questions, and the screeching voice is enough to drive anyone crazy.
DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS, WORST PROFESSOR OF MY LIFE, PUTS RANDOM FACTS ON THE EXAMS AND MAKES THEM IMPOSSIBLE DESPITE TELLING YOU IN CLASS YOU DON'T HAVE TO MEMORIZE BUT WE HAVE TO
Big yapper, the professor claims to be rated poorly on rate my professor. My review, circumscribed within the written rules cannot specify why, but it would surely be felt by some.

I was so excited to take this course but was really disappointed. The lectures are rushed, questions on exams felt like they were trying to trick you, grades for exams took 2 weeks to get back. Study guides were so comprehensive it was just overwhelming. The average on exam 1 was 77%. Take this class with another professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For your own sanity just do not take her. She only reads off the lecture slides and goes through them extremely fast and never once stopped to ask if we understood the content.
