Attendance is mandatory even though all she does during class is read straight off the slides. There are other 300 level courses that are better, trust me!

I really feel like PSYC 100 shouldn't go this deep... Dr. Shenouda's lectures are pretty good, but her exams are extremely specific and tough. Seriously, get ready to read and memorize every tiny detail from the textbook and lectures. Definitely not an easy A.. I ended with an A‑ and had to work my butt off for it. Consider a different professor.

Unfair exams requiring you to memorize every inch of the chapters since they test you on the most random, niche facts. Harsh grading on ALL assignments. Points always taken off for the most trivial, unnecessary things despite overall high quality of work. Trust the course disparity website and take this class with literally any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this with this professor. No study guides or rubrics. You will have to read approx. 200 textbook pages per exam (which, in my summer session, is once every week) and memorize every word that you read in order to do well. Questions on exams are like niche trivia that appeared in the corner of the book, not questions of comprehension.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The course had shallow content with inconvenient holiday assignments. A 2 pm deadline for the final presentation added stress. Kaltura penalized tech issues, disregarding recording preferences. Mandatory Saturday exams with complex Zoom setups were frustrating. The design lacked consideration for student well-being.

Avoid this professor at all costs. Points were taken off for reasons that sounded like excuses/not stated, TA Labs were useless, communication between TAs & prof was non-existent, and instructions were so UNCLEAR yet no rubrics? Heard & saw that PSY363 was way more concise and fair in coursework and structure with a diff. professor from friends.

Shenouda is the worst professor I've had at uiuc. She's condescending, rude, & her & her TA's are no help. She'd be better teaching grad students instead of undergrad bc that's how she structured & taught the class. The exams had stuff that weren't from reviews and instructions for the group project were also unclear and we had to go to the dean.

ICES eval: At least ensure each section is receiving the same lectures highlighting concepts that will appear on the exam. I will not be recommending this course to other students, and I wish I knew the structure of the course surrounding this application-based, highly construable subject.
I HATED this class. I am getting a B without using textbooks but it was genuinely one of the worst classes I have ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The test questions had random facts from the lectures and textbooks so you never truly knew what topics of questions you would be asked which made studying nearly impossible since it seemed like you needed to memorize the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took the PSYC 363 summer course after not being able to pass PSYC 379 and getting a W. Dr. Shenouda explains the material very concisely and her TAs helped out a lot during office hours. The assignments were easy to complete and there was a lot of extra credit. I did pretty well for an 8-week summer research methods course tbh!

I was scared to take Prof Shenouda based on the reviews of her on this website, but she was a great professor! I took an online 8-week research class with her over the summer and it was wonderful. There are long and tedious assignments, but that's what you get with an 8-week class! Lectures were by Shenouda but most of the contact was with a TA.

PSYC245 could be interesting and have potential if it was taught properly. Unfortunately the set up for this class is not well laid out.There are no powerpoints or videos. Instead they have audio lectures that are hard to understand with no visuals.The grading is relatively fair.The primary grades come from 2 proctored exams and 2 4-6 page papers.

Idk much about her but I took her PSYC201 and its beyond easy and really interesting. Completely taught by the TA , the only grades are 5 easy quizzes and a midterm and final along with iclicker. Take this class!!

While the content was not everyone's cup of tea, it should be noted that the professor did also warn us in the beginning of the semester that she was going to stick with referring to the gender binary. Plus, students were attacking the professor way too much. If you don't like the content, just drop the class. The professor was just doing her job.

When students asked to talk about more current topics and for her to include information about gender besides what is within the binary, she ignored these requests and said that it was not the focus of the class. Why would you teach information that's not current or relevant? We aren't paying thousands of dollars to be taught old information. 0/10.

I really wanted to like this class but it was so disappointing. I didn't learn anything I didn't already know except maybe how men and women behave slightly differently in extremely specific research studies. The majority of my time in this class was spent being upset about everything that was missing or incorrect.

in the first lecture christine says this class is based on the gender binary, but just because she states that doesn't mean its okay. she ignores students, uses severely outdated sources, enforces many gender stereotypes, and often invalidates her students. i have no idea how this class is still available to take, it's awful. 0/10.

This is the absolute worst class I have ever taken. Despite being titled Psychology of Gender, this class goes above and beyond to ignore genders besides cisgender men and women. This course was extremely outdated and the professor failed to cite her sources at times. She is not open to skepticism or constructive criticism. Do not take this course.

This class was probably one of the worst classes I have taken during my time here and this is my last semester. Throughout this class, students have been bringing up concerns of feeling invisible due to how binary-focused and outdated this class is. Be prepared to feel extremely frustrated by the lack of evidence to support the research cited.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class was somewhat interesting! Be prepared for hard test. Shes a great person and provides plenty of informing studies. Be prepared to have rude classmates though.

This is the worst class I have ever taken. It is completely outdated and the professor does not care at all about student feedback or concerns. The entire class is just memorizing gender stereotypes and research about the differences between men and women. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Not sure why there are so many negative reviews. She very clearly states during the first day that her class focuses on actual studies, so be prepared. Her class is extremely informative and can be used to explain social issues even she doesn't clearly state them. If you have the ability to form your own thoughts you'll be fine. Amazing Professor

I took the winter session course. Tests were all on lectures and textbook readings. You NEED to read the textbook. They provide a "read more in the book" topics list at the end of lectures. That plus lectures will get you about 90% on tests. Read full chapters thoroughly to get a higher A. It won't take over your break and isn't a ton of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The assignments in class are actually interesting and really help you learn the material. The tests are very challenging though, so make sure you read the textbook! She is also very receptive to concerns/questions so if you're struggling, reach out and she'll help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Shenouda's lectures are pretty boring but they arent hard and you can click through if you need. Lots of reading lot of work but its all pretty easy to skim. BUT she does gives extensions on every assignment without asking so you have time so you can get as many as you want.

Took her class online. 4 TA's who all graded differently. All assignments were written so even if you knew the material, you could still be screwed. She was unorganized and took points off the two course papers for things clearly marked on the opposite rubric for the other paper. Was really looking forward to the class: ruined, horrible experience.

The class I took was an online course, so I can't speak for any in-person sessions, but overall the class was a mess. Tests covered completely foreign material that wasn't covered in the lectures. No exam study materials were provided. It was extremely unclear which knowledge was important and what wasn't.
Don't take this class with this professor unless you really have to. Just terrible.

I had Dr. S for two semesters, and honestly, all the bad ratings about her feel like they're from someone else. They are older; perhaps she found her reviews and took the feedback to heart. She's a great prof, and if you pay attention and try, you'll do fine. If you sit on your computer and play games during her lectures, you'll not do so well.

The exam questions arent fairly framed and do not accurately reflect lecture material. The assignments, although not difficult, have unclear rubrics and are unfairly. The lectures are also poorly organized. Theres too many documentaries. She is in general a bad teacher, has a poor understanding of her own material, and her voice is annoying.

Pretty bad teacher, is not open to discussions. When students question her after exams, she is defensive. Lecture material is boring. Sometimes she tries to be relatable in the most cringey way.  One of the worst classes I took out of all the classes I've taken at UIUC.

Ill sum this class up by telling about how our TA talked to us after grading our papers.  The whole time she told us how wrong everyone was and how we interpreted the questions wrong and how over half the class did the wrong thing.  they yelled at us even though they where the ones who made things unclear also all her studies are archaic and old
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: She's pretty terrible. She ignores questions from students, the tests are way more difficult than they need to be, and she literally told us "don't think about the questions too much, just be stereotypical." She's teaching us gender stereotypes that are outdated/not applicable anymore and only teaches us stereotypical issues, not how to solve them.

She's an ok teacher. Slightly annoying voice, boring lectures. Tests were much harder than they should have been, but she does curve them quite fairly.. TA's graded papers very harshly (but that of course depends on your TA). The class content itself was very interesting, it was just taught quite dryly.
All her students dislike her all the way through the end of their degree or quit.
Very Bad Explanations
Cannot lecture

The professor herself is very nice, the lectures are meh. The problem is that the curriculum for 212 is so frustrating and so much harder than it needs to be that a lot of the time you're just lost unless you've had prior experience with the material. Stay ahead of each topic and self teach my friends

Overall she was a good professor, the materiel was well presented, however, there was a lot to cover so you have to go to lecture and do the homework's/practice exams if you want to learn it well/do well on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The course is inherently hard. It is difficult to teach well, however her teaching wasn't anything special. Most of the learning is done on your own through prelecture and homework. She sometimes doesn't answer questions, but in an online setting with 100 people in the class, I can imagine it is difficult.

Prof. Sickles is a decent lecturer, but lectures only make sense if you watch the prelectures closely. Weekly homework problems are very time-consuming and midterms require a lot of studying to do well, though these are due to the course itself, not by any fault of the professor. If you put in the work, an A is attainable, but definitely not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: While the physics department at UIUC generally has the same curriculum, Anne Sickles just doesnt teach it well. Her lectures are 95% iClicker questions with poor explanations, and the other 5% is random comments about the zoom chat. Not a good teacher. I had to watch other professors lectures to learn anything or teach myself. Very nice though.

Worst physics 212 professor at UIUC. Avoid her at all costs. I had an A-throughout the semester until the final. My section was forced to take it a week before the other kids, and these later sections were able to cheat. Overall, their average final exam grade much higher, but the phys department still wouldnt curve our section. Sucky situation.

Good at explaining physics concepts but not that great at answering questions. If you follow the pre-lectures closely, she will make perfect sense during lecture. She was not the course director so class-specific complaints were not her fault. She was a good professor and has fun stories from working at high-profile physics laboratories!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I don't know what all these people are talking about her tests being crazy hard, I got an A on each of the three midterms without too much preparation. Her lectures are a little light on actual content, so it's important to do the prelectures.

Maybe it has to do with online classes during the COVID-19 pandemic... maybe it has to do with the physics department. Either way, her class was horribly organized and she seemed to not know the answer to many of the students questions - the labs and discussion sections were also horrible.
Not a good lecturer

The physics department at UIUC does the same thing for each section, regardless of who is the teacher. Same HW, same lecture slides, same tests. However, Anne Sickles is by far the worse professor. She simply reads off the clicker questions, cannot explain ANYTHING, nor tries to. Her Exam 3 and Final exam is a full week before all other sections.

Her exam was terrifying. Yes, she told us to do the practice exams and everything will be fine. However it turns out none of the problem was even similar to that of homework or past papers. And what's ridiculous is when she tells you that you will be fine with the exam. Do not trust her words about exams.
Unorganized lecture and homework. Office hour helps little. She doesn't show any passion in teaching during lectures.
Boring lecture, just read Griffiths by your own. Exams and Homeworks difficulty are unpredictable and inconsistent.
Not a very good lecturer. Also the homework is wildly inconsistent in difficulty.
Unclear think flow throughout the lecture, concepts not explained with enough examples.

I found her explanations of problems unclear and hard to follow. All she did was read off the lecture slides that were made for her by the flipitphysics company. She didn't seem to care that much about teaching. Office hours were not very helpful, I would not recommend her.
Lectures are fairly clear, only complaint is that she'll interrupt lecture to tell the one kid in the back of the lecture hall to get off his/her phone/laptop. Tests are similar to homework problems.

Uses pre-recorded lecture videos that aren't helpful, coding questions on test aren't reflective of HW or practices, group activities are not helpful towards learning, textbook is very minimal and poorly explains concepts, MP's aren't helpful either
The class follows a flipped format, with prelectures and weekly group activities. The prelectures which were quite long. The videos were quite dull and not explained especially well.

One of the only classes at UIUC where reverse classroom works due to many helpful TAs. Lecture videos are comprehensive and very similar to homework / exams. Many people complain about Exam Coding Questions, but really arent that challenging, usually arent similar to homeworks, require you to think outside the box but not overly difficult
her lecture videos are so bad at explaining things. GA's are not related to the content we learn and become about following mindless instructions

This class is a joke, and this professor is a joke. Her lectures don't help with learning anything. The exams are difficult for no reason. I genuinely feel like she wants her students to fail. Avoid this class if possible, and if you can't, GOOD LUCK.

She's the worst CS professor I've ever seen. none of the videos do a very good job at explaining the concept. this course need some linalg background, she never recap the key linalg concepts, keep saying review on your own. coding question in quizzes sometimes are too time consuming, course is overall doable but i'll never take her class again

The coding questions on the biweekly quizzes are awful. They tend to veer away from the course content that we have been practicing, and they tend to differ from the practice quizzes substantially. If you ask for help on Discord (our main method of communication), it is likely that you will get a snarky response from the professor or TAs.

The content of the coding questions on the quizzes are substantially different from the lectures, HWs, and GAs. Unless you have a REALLY good understanding of Python, you will struggle on the coding portion of the quiz. Practice quizzes are good for non-coding, but even then, questions completely different from the pq show up on the actual quiz.
Great professor:)

Mariana is a very supportive professor, and the course itself contains a lot of resources to learn. The course policy for late work is very fair, and I believe the content is a decent mix of informative and easy. While I do think improvements can be made on the material, I think it's in a pretty good state, and Mariana's a good reason why.

I had the online section, and it was very doable. The textbook is the most crucial thing in this class; it helps a lot for homework and especially quizzes. The GAs and MPs were also doable, and Discord helped answer any questions. The Python questions on the test were the hardest parts. Her videos are also helpful, but the relevance for HWs is tiny

The structure sucks, have a STRONG linalg background if not go back and review. start learning python especially the numpy library! the coding questions on quizzes are very difficult. Lecture videos suck and homework does not connect to test and those optional study halls USELESS!!! TAs can not respond in timely manner and theres A TON OF WORK.

Flipped structure means you watch lecture videos before class. The videos are good but don't relate too much to the HW. The tests are fine and you get access to the MC questions beforehand, as well has get the course textbook in the CBTF. She is also super nice and loves education. Overall a great class, but you need to be well versed in LinAlg.

Great professor, very patient and works with her students to help them be successful in the class! The class is very linear algebra and multi-variable calculus heavy so your strengths in those topics basically determine what you get out of the class.

The prof is very hard to follow and her material does not co-relate to the homework. I have used github as reference for these homeworks and have been good so far. Grind hard before quizzes and you'll be 'chillin

three weeks in and this course is already a disaster. the quiz had broken questions which the professor promised would be taken care of later, however now she is only giving the option to retake the entire quiz but won't give points for something that's her fault cause it could be unfair to other students.

The professor puts in no effort for this class. She runs the class using the same material from a previous professor from 9 years ago. That's why the TAs and the professor are clueless and leave it up to us to figure things out.
Least organized professor at the university. No flow between topics. Has outdated lecture videos which don't do a good job explaining.

Some people find this class to be tedious due to the PrairieLearn setup, however I found that it allows for students to get out of the course what they want to. The practice quizzes and quizzes have the same bank with unlimited practice quiz attempts. I think anyone that put in ~10 hours/week could receive an A.

This class should not have been this hard. The quizzes were always a pain when it came to the coding questions. How are people with very minimum coding experience in Python expected to know to just code with the math based leetcode type questions?
Professor Silva is an amazing teacher and person. I got to know her better during her office hours, and ultimately had her write me a letter of recommendation.
Awful note ecosystem. Frequently, the prerecorded videos will have typos, and / or are explained poorly.
Know your linear algebra before taking this class...
I did not find the lectures that helpful. If you do the homework, it should be sufficient to do well on the quizzes. The MPs could be documented better.
This class trolls hard

She did not care about student's opinions and feedback until way too far into the semester. At the end it turned out ok as long as you did the practice quizzes and exam but her as a prof would not recommend.

Besides being extremely petty, she's actually a good/fun professor. This class could've been a lot more boring but she made it fun and something to look forward to every week. It's an easy A if you do the work (which is not a lot).

The course website has a lot of useful resources (helped me a lot with learning Python), and lectures were decent. All the homeworks, group assignments, and quizzes/exams were on Prairelearn. Group assignments were doable, quizzes and homeworks were similar in difficulty, and she allowed us to use resources on the course website during quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor did not adjust well to online teaching. The course itself is fine, and pretty easy. However, there were at times frustrating issues with the online courseware this professor was using. It wasn't always clearly communicated. I am someone who reads the website, and is self motivated and I still struggled to figure out what she wanted.

Prof. Silva was a good professor. Her notes were really helpful for the quizzes and her lectures were decent. The homework prepared you for the quizzes. As long as you attend lecture and keep up with the homework, an A is not too difficult. She is really caring and even reviewed my buggy code personally on Piazza. One of the most underrated profs
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Some of the coding problems on the homework were hard to debug. The homeworks prepared you well for the quizzes. I found all the quizzes and the final managable. The lectures were not that good, and while I managed to figure out how to do the problems on the exams, I did not understand the theory behind many of the concepts.

Okay so I took this class in Spring 2020 (the semester of COVID). The first half of this class was in person as normal and it was fine. The beginning of the class was definitely a little tricky in terms of material though. After things transitioned online, Prof Silva was extremely accommodating and caring and I really admired that.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Mariana is unreasonable and super petty. Probably needs therapy (I mean same)

Professor Silva is many things, but a good teacher is not one of them. The quizzes focus on everything you didn't see in the homework. She has specifically said she searches the slides for things she did not put in homework to test on. Pretty unprofessional, always talking about how she knows students do not like her in a weird way
good prof!!!
Stuck up. Debugging is sometimes really difficult, absolutely garbage problems at times. Office hours is a complete joke
Too much in a hurry. Always talking faster than anyone can understand. Can't survive without rewatching lectures. Pretty fun at times though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes are so hard to pass and she will never give you a break from homework and quizzes. Very time consuming and even when you'll study for the quizzes you won't do well.

She made the class a LOT EASIER than before, since the Prairelearn NOW gives us the answers to the questions we can share with more people ahead of time. I'm a math major and I took it as Math 357, so I took the class for an easy A cuz I had the help of people ahead of me. She forgets to record her own voice but that doesn't affect my performance.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I wouldn't give her a high grade because she turns off the volume of recording intentionally to force students to take her class. Besides that, the rest is fine.

This class is a ton of lin alg later on, so be prepared for that. She's a good lecturer, so if you pay attention you should be fine. All lectures are also posted online which was super useful. Very steady workload, weekly homework and a CBTF quiz every 2 weeks. ALL other practice material is in the textbook, so get it if you think you'll need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Love that course materials are available online. Great lecture notes and explanation of difficult material.
Mariana (Silva) Sohn's last semester teaching TAM 251 :(, she has moved to CS so you'd better register for CS 357 next sem if you want to be taught by her! Best teacher ever!
Prof. Silva is the BEST I've had in Chambana. A pleasure in lecture and office hours, cares about students, answers emails (quickly), and fantastic lecture presence. Highly recommended!

I wouldn't say Silva is a great professor, but she makes it very easy to get a good grade. Quizzes are directly from the homework and the final is simple if you generally understand the concepts. At the end of the day, as long as you understand how to do each homework question this class should be an easy A.
Great teacher. Class isn't too difficult, although at times the online quizzes (taken at a testing center) can catch you off guard.
The lectures are easy to follow and she feels approachable as a person. The volume of homework seemed a little high, but don't let that keep you away from her classes.
Very well explained material.  If you stay on top of the homework and go to lectures, it isn't hard to get a high A.  Make sure you understand early topics since the material builds upon itself.
There is a lot of homework for 20% of the final grade

She's so friendly. You can tell she genuinely cares about the success of her students. Lectures were easy to follow and helped a lot with understanding. Plus, she records them and uploaded them online which is INSANELY helpful, especially around finals season. Highly recommended.

Best Professor I've seen in U of I. Amazing lectures offered, and very clear explanation. Dr. Silva is always open for students.  I took her TAM 211 for my first semester as a freshman in college. I get an A+ and end up with 102%. I am sure if you take her class, work hard and go to office hour often, you will perform as good as I did.
Dr. Silva is a great professor - very clear and structured lectures, fair exams (she gives major hints on exam content).

One of my best professors so far. Her presentation of the material is very clear –  I highly recommend her. Also, some advice: attend all review sessions. The example problems are almost identical to the ones on the exams.
Awesome professor! She makes everything understandable and tells you exactly what's going to be on the midterms. Go to lecture because she moves quickly.
so nice and helpful! offers lots of extra credit and the exams are very straightforward. she even tells you what's going to be on them. one of the best professors I've had.
so nice and helpful! offers lots of extra credit and the exams are very straightforward. she even tells you what's going to be on them. one of the best professor's I've had.

She is very helpful and teaches very well.  Her cheerful manner really helped since the class was at 9 am.  She is definitely one of my favorite professors.  Tests weren't really all that hard and there was plenty of extra credit available.  If you can take a class with her, take it.
She is really good and cares about her students. Helps a lot during the tests and wants her students to excel.

Awesome professor. She was very helpful throughout the entire course, and you can tell that she actually cares about her students' success.  She was really good at preparing us for exams, and would give a clear outline for what to expect on midterms and the final. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her.
Very kind and helpful. She definitely cares about her students.
Easiest TAM class Ive ever had. Plus she TEACHES other than teacher like Keane.

She is the absolute BEST tam professor I've had. She actually cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She posts helpful lecture notes and provides review sessions for her students (seriously, no tam professor has ever done that). She is really friendly and nice and most importantly, TEACHES! Take a class with her!
Lecture is a tad bit redundant but going or not going won't deteremine your grade.  Her tests are tough as they are purely theory based and no numbers are in any problems.
Was unnecessarily disrespectful.
He gives different points for the same answers by students. Marking is not clear. No clear rubric. Worst graduate course experience!

If you have the option to take Sinha for ME 320, DO IT. He is extremely clear about his expectations for the course, and makes learning very relevant to real life and industry specifically. My favorite class in college so far.

First time teaching Fa'12: He is good by adapting to the students after the average was a 48 on the first exam. The problem solving sessions with the TA were useful. He improved as the semester went along. I think he has potencial to be a good prof.

First time teaching Fa'12: Had trouble teaching and conveying his point. 48 average on the first exam. Asked for feedback, and adapted the course. The optional sessions with the TA were helpful. He got better at the end. I would say I would give him a shot again.

ME 300 is a very difficult class. Sinha doesn't do much to prepare you for the exams except go through the formulas to use, so the average for the first midterm was 48/100. I got an 89, but only because I read the book thoroughly - if you only listen to Sinha, you won't learn all that you need to apply what you learn in the final.
Fantastic at engaging students during lecture directly and indirectly. Exam problems are generally just easy-medium versions of the example problems in the textbook

He is an amazing lecturer that genuinely cares about his students. Lectures are entertaining and informative. His grading is harsh, but he balances it with a large overall curve. Very enthusiastic about the material. Best lecturer I have had
He's such a nice guy and cares about his students; super respectful. His lectures are always great and I never missed his class. Class is test-heavy and you actually have to study for it.
Amazing individual who respects time.

Very testy heavy class, but I did exactly average on all the exams and still ended up with an A-. The TAs were very helpful and gave a lot of partial credit. As long as you put effort into completing the homework, showing up to discussion, and finishing the CCD project, you should be fine. Prof Rogers really cares about his students too.

Prof Rogers was a great professor that was passionate about the topic, but also strived to make class fun. He genuinely cares about his students and proved it every lecture. Exams were pretty similar to practice exams/book problems, but the final was difficult and required more critical thinking. Also he's from New Zealand which is pretty chant.

Nice guy, the structure of the class is pretty easy, 12 HWs 20pts each(2 drops), 2 exams 40pts each. The HWs are easy if you follow his R code and are graded very leniently. Exams are a challenge but not too bad and are graded fairly as well. The notes/slides could use improvement as they can be a bit confusing but overall its a fairly easy A
He is nice. The course content is harder than I expected, but just pay some time outside the course to learn deeper about the content.

He speeds through lectures, and it is sometimes unclear to understand the purpose of a specific concept. I advise not to go to lectures and to learn independently from his videos. There were so many things said in lectures; most days, I would understand 30% of the lecture. HWs were iffy some weeks, and the Exams were too. Be he doesn't have a final
Very clear and straightforward lecturer, good at answering questions

Professor Simpson is a very nice professor. He is very easy if you show up to lectures which not a lot of people go to. He is also a very fair grader and made the class very assessable. Anyone who does poorly just doesn't put in the effort.
Lecture is somewhat boring and might be hard to focus if you have a low attention span but if you actually listen to him you learn a lot and he's a nice guy.
Useless lectures, homework is stupid
He even puts up lecture notes online. Just take the class with him man.

Really nice guy, and a good-but-not-great lecturer.  I found the material pretty difficult, but he have a very generous curve so I ended up with an A-.  I definitely learned a lot.  This was my third stats class at UIUC, and he was my probably favorite professor so far.
the best professor, really kind and helpful, don't hesitate, just take his class

Extremely stressful class. Grading seemed inconsistent, with frequent deductions for minor formatting rather than content. Rubrics were very unclear, making it difficult to earn many points.

Uses Moodle, making assignment tracking difficult. Assignments could only be submitted 8am–4pm on the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Constantly complains and overreacts about people being 1-2 minutes late, never actually reads papers and only cares about formatting. For some reason makes papers due at 4 PM. Horrible professor, never succeeded in actually teaching anyone nor in gaining their respect.

Honestly, I had a great class with him. He provided constructive feedback in class and was primarily concerned that people arrived on time. He graded super easily and there was 14% worth of extra credit offered. I had a friend who took the same class with a different professor, and her class was a lot more difficult than this one.

Saw him chastise people in my class for being about 3 minutes late, not following the instructions that he had forgotten to post on Canvas, making a change on an essay he had suggested the previous class, and using the bathroom during work time, when he was not speaking. Class is easy, but he is extremely nitpicky, so follow the rubrics exactly.

Everyone loves Slowbodnik. He loves taking his job seriously, because we do too! The material is INCREDIBLY interesting. All the films are from the 1900s! If you love watching movies and writing about things that don't matter, this class is for you! ;) Don't be late, because he's EXTREMELY sensitive and will get offended if you are. Joke of a man

Slobodnik is difficult, impatient, and opinionated.
Things he has gotten mad at me or others for include:
Handing him a paper that fell on the floor
Going to the bathroom
Being on a phone
Being 2 minutes late on the first day of classes
Not getting an attendance sheet that was passed around.
Holds class late but is mad if you are late
DO NOT TAKE!

Things you will get chastised about by Slobodnik:
- going to the bathroom
- standing up to hand him a paper
- coming to class 2 minutes late quietly
- not having perfect formatting on rough drafts in class
- standing up to throw out trash
- unscrewing water bottle with any noise

He also just loves to go on tangents that take away from class time.

I took MACS104 class looking for a stress-free gen ed. He would call late people in front of the whole class. One movie to watch per week + two/ three others to write essays on. Essays were also long. He let us revise papers if turned in early which was helpful. His edits on the paper were about grammar errors and not about the actual content.

Grades only by format, but not content, of papers. Harsh Grader that makes no sense. Not Clever. Never gets the submission pages of any papers or quizzes set up on time. Rude to students who offer kindly reminders. Consider twice before taking BTW 250 by Slobodnik.

This man should not be teaching, period. Every time I walked into his classroom, I knew I was going to feel uncomfortable in some way shape or form. Whether it's him being homophobic or him talking about women in inappropriate manners, there's always something he says that is extremely problematic. Not to mention, he's extremely grumpy.

He is passionate and knowledgeable but lacks the warmth, kindness, and understanding that makes a good teacher. He is rude for genuinely no reason. He makes an interesting subject lifeless because of his harsh personality and grading. He inundates students with work. Even if you normally are good at English: DON'T DO IT. It is not worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Never takes the chance to explain any material at all. Grades and takes random points off, none of which have rubrics. Rude, short email replies.

Awful. Publicly humiliated students for being 30 seconds late, made us feel stupid, went off on tangents 3x every lecture, and was just overall an unpleasant person to be around. I did NOT learn much; he focused more on formatting and citations rather than the actual content.

Genuinely rude and uncaring. He will call you out if you're late or if you get up to throw something away and keeps you over class time. Feedback on my papers were contradictory to what he says in lecture and on the hand outs he gives. Overall the most incompetent professor I ever had. Planning on dropping the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Text required but I didn't use it. Will be uncomfortably rude if you speak to him before class starts or you're late, will single you out in front of everyone. Repeats himself a LOT. Unclear grading guidelines, but willing to critique drafts. Nothing is online, you get tons of handouts per day. Passionate for the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: He loves films, it shows quite a bit. Gives out a lot of handouts, and most are useless (like reviews or something). I had four major papers, he seems to grade easier if you talk to him about your paper beforehand. The exams are not the best, but not horrible. The films he chose were very interesting ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easily my worst professor so far. He will go on rants about the most irrelevant things and will keep talking even after the bell rings. If you show up late you will get singled out publicly. Everything is done on paper so you can't check your grade or assignments online. He will handout 2-4 useless papers per day. Drop or transfer from his section.

Worst. This will be the first and the last time I rate a professor. His tone is terrible in explaining things. Keep complaining about stuffs in the society, he barely skim through textbook and expect us to always be prepared for everything. Your tuition deserves to be invested in a better place. DROP IT WHILE YOU GOT A CHANCE.

reviews.comment: He's very rude and grades tough. Papers are often graded harshly without constuctiove feedback. Would definitely not recommend taking the class.

reviews.comment: Thinks too much of himself and the class. Very rude when it's not even necessary and the content of the class was interesting but pick to be with someone other than him.
Assigned lots of busy work and graded by deducting points with very little constructive feedback. Generally unpleasant.

Do your best. Must attend class and submit your weekly assignment in deadline. He is kind of old-fashioned type. Not checking email and using online system. His own guideline is very important, so if you follow his guideline correctly, guarantee A grade. Think he gives curved grade.

reviews.comment: He is very strict about attendance and turning in your papers on time.  He has no patience for laziness and will make it known.  He can be rude and harsh at times but he is a good teacher.  He knows what he's talking about and I learned a lot from him.  If you are sensitive, don't take it.  If you want to learn, I would definitely suggest his class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was an unecessary tough grader. Focused more on irrelevant points of a paper rather than actual content(i.e syntax of works cited vs. entire paper). In class he doesn't have the best attitude. Yet his students to be cheerful. Food for the thought: you get what you put into the world. Overall, don't take his class you will not get an A.

Very unclear with directions and when will take points off for minor details. If you revise your papers towards all of his notes, still won't get a good grade on it. His email responses are very rude and how he criticizes his students is untactful. Do yourself a favor and find a different professor.
Knows his stuff and makes class entertaining

This class is easy if you're neurotic, but hard if you don't pay attention to fine detail. That being said, I made a few typing errors and was not penalized. This course was self-paced and it was hard to keep on schedule with no due dates. Some mistakes on compass that do not benefit the student. He usually does not fully answer questions via email

This guy is majorly unprofessional. Not only does he send emails without salutations, but he forgets to post essential notes needed for writing assignments. When you email him about said notes, he rudely responds and acts as if it is your fault. Clearly he thinks this 100-level is SUPER IMPORTANT.

This class is a 100 level course but he acts like it's a 300 level. I'm taking it right now & I'm just extremely disappointed in it. I was excited to take this course & now I'm constantly stressed about doing the insane amounts of homework done instead of actually learning the material. You have to watch at least 6 hours of film a week. Don't take.
He gives obnoxious amounts of homework.  Its a 100-level class and it's requiring much more work than any 300 or 400 classes.  He's a difficult grader and takes a rude tone in comments.

This guy knows his stuff. I got out of the class with an A-, but I couldn't slack off in the class. Use his office hours for papers! He's a tough grader, so if you're not a very good writer, don't be shy asking for help. His class is a fun discussion, but don't think it's an easy class because you're watching movies. It's a pretty interesting class

He's very knowledgable and passionate about what he does. However, he is a tough grader on papers, you can't slack off on them. Utilize his office hours! It's a fun discussion class, but don't think it's a blow off class because of movies. He does a good job of challenging everyone.

The negative reviews threw me off, this guy is great! The lowest grade I got on a paper was a B+, but you need to put effort into the assignments. He's full of energy and loves talking about films, and encourages you to approach him. If you pay attention in class, do the readings, and go to the lab, you'll do fine.

I was terrified to take this class after reading reviews but I'm glad I did. He is passionate, very clear, few papers for homework and rarely refers to book, and xams are straightforward. HOWEVER, he is rude via email, rarely lets discussion out on time, and goes off on tangents. Take this class if you have him for discussion/dont take if online.

Obviously when someone comments "tough, but fair" is totally written by the professor himself....because simply he really just sucks... he has no respect for students,(if he did, i wouldn't say he suck),  not responsible NOT FAIR because he is not helpful, and who writes tough but fair?!  Overall, it is just a frustrating class. Hopes he improve.

He is so bad... Never answer your question clearly. Minor mistake may cause much deduction in this class. He teaches business writing and tells you to write politely, however himself never did that...

In order to get an A in this class, do not let this teacher be short in his emails/ comments. Whether an online course or not, find a way to have him look over your drafts! Ask SPECIFIC questions, never assume. Spend at least 10+ hours on assignments in order to perform well and use terms from the textbook. Note that the final is worth 900+ pts.

Terrible! Has killed all film interest I ever had. Grade suffered because of miscommunication on Compass; he couldn't care less. Incredibly tough on assignments, short through emails requesting assistance, same in his office hours. He assumes his assignments are intuitive and forgets that this is a 100-level course.
He's extremely unhelpful and expects you to spend 10+ hours on the homework he assigns on a weekly basis.

Never read the book, the papers are your grade. He is VERY tough, but also fair. Lets you have your paper reviewed before turning it it. Is nit picky but you learn a lot and he really does care about that class and is very vested in it. Don't take if your not a worker or your a slacker!
Very tough teacher but fair. Nothing is online and grade is based mostly off of the five papers. Tends to ramble on tangents but does care about film.

Worst teacher I have ever had. Very rude through email, and it's an online course. He assigns a ton of homework weekly, expect at least 9-10 hours on dumb unnecessary assignments. Grading is extremely tough and unpredictable. NEVER TAKE A CLASS TAUGHT BY THIS MAN
AWEFUL. DO NOT TAKE.

this guy is the worst human being on the face of this planet. he is an awful teacher and needs to retire. his class for lack of a better term, SUCKS, and he is not helpful at all. I must email him at least once a day because of all the errors he makes to the compass page, and he never makes a point to help you.

Don't know where to begin with this guy or class. Anyways, i'll begin my rant. First off, the class is pointless. It's basically stuff you learned in 5th grade, such as how to write a letter. That, however, is not what your grade is based on. If you make one small citing or bibliographical error you get penalized ridiculous amounts. (continued)

Most comments people left here are actually true. I regret not coming here before signing up in his class. He tries everything possible to make the class hard by distributing low Bs and Cs.  He found a way to make BTW250 which is by far the easiest course on campus very hard by trying to screw you in every way possible..

You never know what you are going to get on your assignments, no matter how much time you spend on them.  Won't go over papers after he has graded them.  Gave me corrections for my papers that had nothing to do with them.  BAD teacher.

I can't stand him!  He is the most unhelpful teacher ever.  Online classes tend to need clarification and he never answered the questions I asked or directed me to some where else.  The class is pretty easy, but I do not like him!!

Very clear on what he wants for assignments, there's a template for basically everything so follow that if you're unclear. Overall a really nice guy who is willing to help you if you ask for it.  The only thing is that tells semi-related stories for a lot of the class period.
online class is WAY more writing then it is worth... grades the essays pretty toughly... can be kind of a jerk... do not recommend

Overall, it was an easy class.  For an adv. comp. credit, it was less writing than I expected.  A lot of the writing was group writing which was kind of annoying.  He was a nice guy but I didn't learn a whole lot about writing.  He also tended to take up a lot of class time telling irrelevant stories.

do not take his online class, it is very hard,   and he has no professionalism.  does not address you by your name, or even offer to help you, instead he redirects  you somewhere else.  worst online class experience ever, and its intro to film.  bad teacher

There are a lot of essays in this class so if you don't like writing DO NOT TAKE THIS! It is manageable though and if you go in to his office hours he is really helpful... overall I would say take it cause it's not bad at all.

most useless class and man ever.. he found a way to make btw 250 hard by trying to screw you in every way possible.. focuses on minor details that shouldn't matter.. doesn't know much about business writing as he told me to include references on my resume and a summary of my skills at the top.. no thanks i'll take the tips given to me at the bcs..
very unfair and biased when grading papers. gives bad grades if does not agree with your opinion. tip: be republican and gay and you will get a good grade!

Professor Skabelund is one of the best professors I have taken at this university. He is very passionate about the material and willing to repeat himself if you have a question. Great lecturer and loves making calc jokes!
Great professor! Had a really good experience with his class. would totally take another math class with him

Some people love him, but I found his lectures incredibly hard to follow. It wasn't just that the material was hard, it was the way he explained it. He always spoke as if he was unsure of what he was saying. You can tell he's a really nice and intelligent person though.
A great lecturer. Explains the theory well and the application. Would take another class with him for sure.

Just how it felt since I studied a ton but exams were all hit or miss since i had no idea what they were gonna be.

reviews.comment: He is incredibly knowledgeable and is usually spot on with answers to students' questions. His explains the lecture problems and examples clearly and throws in jokes here and there to keep things interesting. Also doesn't hurt that his voice is super relaxing hah
The practice tests are not very useful.

By far the best and hardest math class I've taken (Calc 3 Honors), would definitely recommend him. I knew a lot of the stuff going in, but his explanation gave me perspective and rigor. Tests are long for the time, but if you really know the stuff they aren't bad. Amazing mathematically rigorous explainer.

reviews.comment: He is not good at teaching at all.

He has an amazing personality, and is very approachable. The lectures cover the material pretty well, but explanations often lack the simple, big picture so that it is very easy to get lost. Once you get lost, your best bet is to pull up Paul's math notes and hope you aren't missing any content.

Professor is a nice guy, but as a first year teacher of an honors class he is not experienced. Lectures and blackboard writings are sometimes hard to follow. Class is very competitive with a bunch of wizards
Great lecturer, had home for the honors section. He really likes math so he teaches it well and he has a full understanding of the material. He's also funny so the lectures aren't as dry.

best professer

Great caring professor. He gives hints on what's on the exam, provides study guides from past exams. Weekly quizzes, drops 3 lowest.  The apple tasting is awesome! Best  prof I've ever had. Made me fall in love with horticulture.

Dr. Skirvin is one of the best lecturers I have had at the University. He is knowledgeable and funny and really cares about his students. Often he will give hints as to what will be on the exam or quizzes in class.  As long as you attend lecture, you will do fine in this course.

I am a recent U of I graduate who took Skirvin's course last spring. All I can say is that he is an excellent professor and I regret not taking more courses with him earlier in my college career. Professor Skirvin is a dedicated, hard working man who cares deeply about his students' success.

Dr Skirvin is my favorite professor I have ever met. He is a genuinely great guy with a goofy sense of humor. Lectures are mandatory, as all of the quizes/test questions come from them and not the book. Extra Credit is everywhere and the class is fun. DR SKIRVIN IS THE BEST

He is one of the best professors I have had. He is really passionate about teaching and very understanding. He made me enjoy and WANT to come to lectures, which are mandatory anyway. Study what is on the power points and take old practice exams and you will do great on the tests. Overall, if you can, definitely take a class with him!

Great guy. Loves his students, teaching is his life. As an engineering student, I would have to say that I got more out of this horticulture class than any of the classes in my curriculum that semester. Oh, and there's free food and plants. Take this class if you have the chance. He's a great guy to know.

Skirvin is an incredible instructor. I wish more professors cared about their students' success the way Skirvin does! He's an incredibly intelligent and knowledgeable man and HORT 100 is a great elective to take! There's TONS of extra credit but you do need to study for the exams. Take this class!

Skirvin is the best professor on UIUC campus, hands down! Very nice and helpful and loves to teach. Multiple choice exams and weekly easy quizzes is the entire bulk of your grade, but attendance is mandatory as he doesn't send slides out with notes. High recommend taking this class!!
Go to class. A lot of what he talks about will be on the exams. On another note, Skirvin is amazing. I had no interest in plants, but he can make anyone enjoy his class.

He's the BEST. My favorite teacher so far. He cares about his students and he makes sure you know it! He's so funny and animated!! :D And he gives extra credit for doodles and jokes (horticulture graffiti) on tests.
Best professor, best class, take it!!!

Hands down my favorite class and my favorite professor so far.  The material is interesting, Skirvin makes you want to go to class even though most of the time its not required.  Take this class, even if its not in your major!!!

Skirvin is the BEST professor. You'll will WANT to go to class because he makes it enjoyable. Look at the past exams...and you will get an easy A. Daniel, the TA, is also very helpful. I wish he taught more classes!

Professor Skirvin is my absolute favorite professor on campus. He often invites his students to extra-curricular horticulture-related events, all of which I've attended and absolutely enjoyed. His classes are interesting and splattered with hilarious stories of his travels around the world, his childhood, and his family. He is the man.

I Love Skirvin! My favorite prof at U of I for sure. This was one of the few classes I have ever taken that I actually looked forward to going to class. He is hilarious and I took another course he offered b/c I like him so much!

Professor Skirvin is amazing! He tells the best stories EVER! The class is super easy and he gives EC. You will never want to miss this class. He makes learning about plants incredibly interesting and fun.
This guy is one of the coolest professors I've ever had.  He's interesting, keeps relevant to the topic, and is extremely enthusiastic about his subject.
The Skirv dog is awesome! He loves his job. He makes topics easy to understand and gladly answers any questions.  His stories are instant classics. Take this class!

Best professor! He's funny and interested in his lectures. He has great stories. Just review your notes before class for the quizzes, which are almost every Thursday/Friday. MAke sure you go over the practice exam Q's because the majority of the exam were right off them. Go to class to take notes that aren't in the book. He offers E.C. for jokes.

This class is awesome although depending on the lecture his voice can put you to sleep. He's a great teacher he's funny and has great stories from his time as a child and as a student at Purdue. He is able to retire but still teaches for the fun and loves the kids. Very Enthusiastic and easy tests and quizzes (as long as you look over your notes).

Professor Skirvin is the best professor I had all semester. He's so cool. You can usually catch him after class if you need him, but he's not particularly skilled with technology so it might not be worth emailing him. He's very relaxed and if you attend class and take some notes, you should pass his class, no problem. This was my day's highlight.
Skirvin is a magnificent professor. He makes horticulture interesting whether you are into that kind of stuff or not. His classes are fun and easy, and he has a sexy beard as well.

LOVED skirvin...best professor i've ever had...one of the few classes i didn't like to miss because it is interesting and he's so funny. also, he gives TONS of extra credit and as long as you go to lectures, you are guaranteed to get an A. i highly suggest taking the class 2nd semester because you get extra credit for the flower show.
Great teacher. Great guy. Tests reflect what he talks about in class, where he tells you what to expect.
Skirvin the Skirv Dog, is SWEET--- he is flawless and always waves good-bye when I leave class early.
Fantastic Professor!-Makes lecture worth going to~
This class was so interesting and Professor Skirvin is great
coolest guy ever...seriously he's easy and so is the class.  best teacher at the university
awesome!

Fun!
omg soooo nice! i love skirvy!
i <3 Dr. Skirvin! he is very weird and quirky which makes class interesting

Skirvin is the best teacher I've had so far...he's funny and really likes to talk to his students.  He thanks our class repeatedly for taking his class...he really loves teaching and is an all-around AWESOME guy.  Take his class!! :)
Funny Teacher
He is a great teacher - funny, enjoys teaching, cares about students.  Loved the class
BEST TEACHER!!!!
Very good, enthusiastic, funny, makes class interesting.
Skirvin is the most hilarious teacher ever.  His class is actually entertaining and if you read over your notes the day before the exam, you'll get good grades!
very enthusiastic about material, class is fun and interesting, one of the best professors i have ever had.

Hardest part: keep up with the readings. Everything else is super easy & fun! Her lectures are clear & organized. Test material is properly emphasized. Group work is interesting. Quizzes are small but reflect the reading; hence its importance. I hate the subject of History, but I really loved her class & she made the subject so cool for me.
