reviews.comment: Jon is a great lecturer, but I never took notes in the class. For exams, just make flashcards on all of the terms in the workbook and memorize. Most of the homework assignments are online, but I lost a good amount of points during the discussion quizzes because I didn't do the reading. If you do the work, you'll get an A.

Overall, easy class, just google flashcards for it and study it to ace the exams. 3 non-cumulative exams & no final. Really passionate and somewhat eccentric professor. Discussion is mandatory and there's weekly assignments that feel like busy work. The workbook is basically a study guide.
Great and interesting class from an awesome professor. Tests are very easy (matching, true/false, vocab) and homework is very short. Highly recommended.
The grade is pretty much entirely exam based. If you mess up one exam, you're kind of out of luck to raise your grade.

I would take any other class taught by Jon, he was awesome. CLCV 115 was so easy, as long as you do the assignments (3 a week, each take about 20min) and show up to half the classes you will pass no problem. There are no tests for this class and most of the time Jon just talks about random Roman/Greek history but he's fun to listen to.

Everyone will tell you this is a super easy class, and it is. If you keep up on the little assignments and studying. It got a little too close for me by the end of the semester because I missed some homework. As long as you don't forget you're taking this class, cram for the tests, listen to his awesome stories in lecture, then you'll get an A.
Love Solomon! Super funny. Highly recommend greek and roman mythology; if you study for the tests its an easy A because he tells you exactly what will be on the tests!
Solomon is great. He is a good lecturer and has a lot of funny stories. The class is easy, just memorize the study guides and practice tests and you can easily get an A on the tests. Loved the class!

I lost a lot of points because I never showed up to lecture, but I did show up for discussion all the time. Lots of little assignments here and there, and there's no actual final but there are 3 MC midterms and 3 in discussion essays. I did alright in that class, but it's definitely not an easy gen. ed like you would have wanted.

Very interesting class. Solomon is really interesting lecturer and he loves telling stories about his expeditions that relate to the material taught in lectures. Exams require a bit of memorization but you can spend a couple of hours before the exam memorizing and easily pull off an A.
Just a really funny guy. It's like having a comedian as a professor.
amazing teacher!!!

Solomons is a great professor, but I did not enjoy his class at all. There is a lot of busy work, and a lot of reading and memorization. Lots of little assignments you have to do. Workbook and discussion book are expensive and mandatory, and assignments require you to tear out pages, making them worthless at the end of the semester.

Not to confuse with CLCV 115111. 116 is the Roman Achievement! SO SO easy! 4 one page papers, 3 of which you can rewrite. I went in for help on the fourth but the TA just gave me a 4545 instead. Two 80 point multiple choice tests that are solely memorization like literally memorize all dates, authors, books etc. Random web searches etc but easy
Jon Solomon is one of the best professors I've had so far.  He is extremely knowledgeable about his topics and wants to spread his knowledge to you.

Solomon was such an interesting guy! He made the class a blast. The material was all in one convenient book made by him, saving you money instead of having to buy a million books. The papers and assignments were easily done and quickly done. Some reading, but it was interesting. TAs were typically eccentric and fun as well. Great, fun professor.

This class so easy. 4 papers, 3 of which are 1 page and the 4th one is 3-5 pgs double spaced. a good amount of websearches and prequizzes which are easy and I could do in class during lecture. The tests are pure memorization of the exact information so lecture is kind of unnecessary. And for every paper, he basically told us what to write. EASY.
Incredible professor, makes class so much fun. Cracks jokes and has a good time teaching. Highly recommend taking his class!

Solomon was one of the best professors I had this semester. He was really engaging and made the course fun. He's really knowledgeable on the subject. If you need a gen ed class, this is definitely a class worth taking!

Great lecturer and you can tell he is passionate about the subjects which make it an interesting class. Solomon is a real smart guy, that is evident. The exams are as easy as memorizing a list of terms. If you do the work an A is impossible not to get. My only complaint is that he is so busy he can't dedicate a ton of time to students emails.

One of my favorite professors at UIUC!! He is completely entertaining and loves to share his life stories, very passionate about subject! I would recommend this class to anyone who has the slightest interest in the subject! You will learn a lot. Tests are all multiple choice and he gives you a study guide that the questions come straight off of

Great professor, very interested in topic which makes the class very interesting. I really enjoyed the class and the workload was very easy to handle. I would highly recommend over CLCV 111/115 just because of the smaller size and there is no discussion section.

Solomon is super chill and hilarious. His TA is too if you just talk to him.  I found that I didn't need to read any assignments in order to pass the class, but what he aims for is that you become an educated individual, so you can sound intelligent.  I found his lessons useful in other aspects of my life, but again it's not mandatory lectures.

Class not mandatory at all, but he is very entertaining. Basically tells you everything you need to know for the exams, and put forth some effort for the writings. Even though there are a lot of readings, I never really read them and I did fine!

This class is fairly easy however WAY too much work for a gen ed.  There's a ton of reading that he expects you to do and his lectures are completely pointless, all he does is read the textbook to you and shows you some video clips.  There's A TON of writing in this class as well.  Overall bad class

BEST teacher! You buy the workbook for his class and there is a decent amount of reading but nothing strenuous. He is very funny. He's excellent in using things from current movies and such  to tie to points he is trying to make. Although attendance is not mandatory, I enjoyed going to his class. He's very knowledgable and humorous!

All your preconceived notions about this class and professor are probably accurate. Taking it with Solomon is not only fun but also very easy to do well. No "textbook" but a lot of supplemental material and course workbooks.

Solomon was a wonderful professor. His class was not only easy, it was interesting and intriguing. There was not a cumulative final, only a "last test." He's very into what he's teaching and he passes on his passion to his students.

His class was easy and entertaining, being humorous and  making tests that, while you do have to study at least 2 hours for, are more than fair and in-class tests that are extremely easy since he literally tells you the answer after he tells you the question. I recommend him for any class he teaches because he's a really awesome guy.
Solomon is the man. He keeps lectures entertaining and is very helpful. Super easy class. Only two tests all semester and 3 papers. You can rewrite all the papers. TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HIM
The best professor ever
He is awesome! Very funny! He makes his lectures interesting, and as long as you do the assignments you'll be fine!
He is awesome.
Solomon cracked me up! Easy class, interesting lecture (and I'm an engineer), and good communication. Just get a good TA and your set. The exams are a joke.

I thought he was hilarious. Often makes jokes, tells stories, and swears during lecture. He makes the class fun where it could be quite boring. I enjoyed lecture quite a bit, plus the multiple choice exams are SO EASY if you go to class. He knows what he is doing and he knows how to entertain a lecture hall of 300+. I highly recommend him.

GREAT professor. Powerpoints are really interesting and he is very smart and knowledgeable. The class is really easy too because he teaches the information so well. Exams are not hard, just use the study guides that are provided in the required text and you will ace them. Highly recommended professor, take ANY class he teaches.

I thoroughly enjoyed listening to this professor speak about so many things from philosophy, to influences of Greco-Roman culture in modern times. I agree with a previous comment that he is one of the most knowledgeable professors on campus that can keep you listening

Jon is amazing. The most fun, interesting, captivating and knowledgeable professor i've ever had. Lecture notes aren't online so you have to go to class but it's worth it- he makes the class a blast. Not hard material either, very intriguing. take this class! i love jon!

you are required to buy a course book which has study guides for each exam. just study whats on the study guide then you will be set. exams are very easy but essay exams are annoying especially your ta is anal about thesis and 5 paragraphs. some readings are long
Exams were really easy as long as the relevant stories were read(or summaries were read). Pretty funny guy with interesting material. I'd take it again.

The work load of this course is a lot more than I anticipated. If you are looking for a fairly simple gen ed look elsewhere. Yes, the class is interesting and exams are straight forward, but time would be better spent studying for other classes.
Easy class. Exams are super easy. Goes over all the material in lecture so reading isn't necessary but you need the book for the random quizzes in class.

The Best class I've ever taken so far! Solomon makes his class very entertaining through showing movie clips and even throwing in some personal stories and pictures. The class wasn't hard but homework had to be done to get a good grade. For exams, just memorize the required pages and stories and you'll get an A.

The funniest professor I have ever had and definitely knows what he is talking about. Wants everyone to do well and connects movies with mythology which was pretty cool. Also had him for a discussion and he was really cool. Take classes with him!
I enjoyed my study abroad experience with Prof. Soloman. He made Rome a very fun and intersecting place, always eager to answer questions and always provided good info. Brilliant man !

Amazing teacher, amazing class.  Very manageable workload, we read 2 books, he highlighted each chapter in class so you knew the important things, wrote 3 1-page papers, a bunch of workbook stuff, and 2 tests, no final.  He makes intro to greek cultures actually interesting and easy!  If you need a gen ed make sure you take this class with him!

If you don't like mythology, you're not going to be too interested in his class. It is, however, very easy and because I love mythology, very very interesting. This man actually knows everything by heart and loves his subject. He's really funny in class and likes to make fun of himself. He makes lots of pop culture references. Lauren's the best TA!
Jon Solomon, ... I wish all my professors were like Jon Solomon.

Decent professor and easy but boring class.  The lectures are pointless and boring but he gives out simple attendance assignments sometimes.  There are some books to read for the class but you don't need to read them.  There are three, one page essays that are really easy and the tests are all memorized multiple choice.  Overall easy gen ed.

A really awesome professor.  All the homeworks and tests are easy if you put in just a little time.  Some people say he's not cool in office hours, but I've been several times and he's nothing but nice and easy to talk to.  His lectures are interesting and amusing.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! I loved this class. So easy if you pay attention during lecture. He explains everything and goes over all readings, so you don't even have to read them (even though the readings are all extremely interesting). Homework, papers, and tests are ridiculously easy. Most intelligent teacher I've ever had. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Excellent professor! Keeps the class interesting with the use of media and passion. I highly recommend this course for anyone trying to complete their non-western requirement. It is also a double dipper! I was intimidated by the syllabus at first but after taking the class, one should not be. The papers are very fair and he allows a re-write.

EASY and INTERESTING class!  Great teacher!  He is so understanding and lenient.  He is one of the only teachers who realize that gen eds are not top priorities.  Tests are all multiple choice, and he gives you a study guide.  You get to rewrite all three papers if you get a bad grade.  As long as you fill out the homework you will get a 100%!

Jon Solomon is by far one of the best teachers I've ever had.  His interest in the subject matter is both a pleasant surprise and contagious, as he makes great jokes ("My name ith Arithtotle, I'm a philothopher!"), and has quality slide-shows which include video and clear images of the most famous historical art.  Take his class and love it.
Reaallyy..not so good. I signed up for the class because I saw good reviews here, but I don't quite agree with them.

He is the best teacher in this school.  He is really committed to his subject area.  He uses different kinds of technology to teach the class and it is all around interesting.  I took an extra class of his just because he is an awesome teacher!
Best class I've taken at UofI. Lectures are interesting and pretty funny. As long as you study exactly what he tells you you'll be more than prepared for exams.
this class would be so easy if our TA wasn't so hard on our papers.
Exasperatingly easy.
Solomon is easy, interesting, and has one of the most entertaining lectures on campus.

good class, quizzes are easy and the material is interesting enough. the homework isn't too bad, and tests are fine. i don't know if it's because of prior knowledge or the class, but i seemed to know the material pretty well during and after i took the class. recommend!

This professor's grading is extremely easy and fair.  His tests are just worksheets (front and back), one page.  He is very lighthearted in lecture.  However, I agree with what others have said about his awkward office-visit demeanor.  He is extremely cold and mean in person.

SO EASY!the only time you actually have to work for the class is the 3 essays.But its still easy becos he gives you lots of hints and its googleable.The midterms are SO easy if you did study,its so BASIC.
Do not listen to what anyone on this board says. this teacher is incredibly easy, as well as nice. and hsi TA grades like were in junior highschool. TAKE a class with solomon!

The subject matter he covers is often pretty boring, but he makes it interesting. He is always making jokes ("Terence is like South Park"), and if you come to lectures, he gives you the answers to pop quizzes. A lot of reading is required, but you don't have to read everything to get a good grade in the class. A lot of writing is required too.

pretty rude and he doenst even answer his students emails. Also, the exams require a ton of memorization of little facts that have nothing to do with the lectures he gives. The Ta's are way too critical when they grade the essays

This guy has been the coolest techer i've had all year, he is hilarious he spoon feeds answers to 'pop' quizes. Even though there are alot of LONG reading assignments, if you're interested in it, it's not so bad.
Awesome

Although you need to read a lot of materials for this class, they are not that difficult if you are interested in learning Greek Mythology. Also the assignments are not that hard and it's easy to get all of them right. Prof.Solomon is very nice. But one of his TAs is a bit too critical.
Awesome professor. Hilarious, tons of pop culture references in every lecture. Long reading assignments, but I rarely bothered to do them. Wish he taught engineering.
No Comments

This has been my favorite class so far.  It's the one class the entire year that I actually look forward going to.  His lectures are actually very interesting and he is very humorous, and not in a cheesy way like a lot of the professors at the U of I.  I definitely recomment taking this or any other of his courses.

This guy is hilarious. He is the only professor I've seen that can make a whole theater full of students laugh. He makes his tests easy, he gives hints to answers on pop quizzes, and the material is interesting.  I learned a lot of cool trivia in this class. TAKE THIS CLASS. Jon Solomon is awesome.
No Comments

She is a wonderful professor and very knowledgeable. She has many different ways of instructing this course, but we read the entirety of War and Peace. Despite the length of the novel, she made it quite manageable. She sometimes gives pop quizzes, but she often warns the class beforehand. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is honestly great. There most definitely was a LOT of reading, but the material was phenomenal (I am a Russian major, so I am a bit partial). She is a very fair grader, very understanding, and she tries to spark conversation. Lectures can become boring, but she does her best to re-catch attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: If she's offering a course, take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It is discussion-based every day, so make sure to read.  The only difficult part of the class was when the readings would be too long from the Monday-Wednesday span, but I always caught up because the books are worth it.  Other than that, participate a lot and she's a pretty easy grader and very fun!

Prof. Sobol is one my favorite professors ever.  She is a great lecturer, extremely knowledgeable and passionate about Russian literature, and always willing to provide help if needed.  It was a pleasure take her class on War and Peace.

Great professor! Reading (max 25 pages) every week, 5-point quiz on the reading. He also goes over the quizzes afterwards. The amount of lecture may be a turn-off for some, but it always relates to the reading, and he allows for class discussion. He's always very happy to share his knowledge and answer questions. Taking him again in the Spring!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: at the beginning of the class, he always ask what happened for this week. He talks randomly, do not focus on one topic. But not bad.

He is eager to teach. He talks a lot so its defo not the best class to take early. Attendance is taken by paper and there is a written quiz every other week. They were based off the readings and from the lectures but he doesn't go over the readings before the quiz (READING HEAVY). Plus grading is relative so it's very questionable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was not a bad professor but he did went off topic most of the time. Be prepare to read since there was a in-class quiz every week on Tuesday from the readings. We had to do two questions but only one of them gets graded but you don't know which one it is so put effort in both answers. There is an essay at the of the semester but no final.
His lecture is really disorganized. He is very strict person. just RUN AWAY
Lectures usually were disorganized because he went off topic a lot, so sometimes they were hard to follow. As long as you understand the concepts and somewhat pay attention the class isn't bad.

This class can be difficult, but as long as you do the readings and engage with the concepts in and out of class you'll be fine. Matt is a great lecturer and the topics are super interesting. I did struggle with getting A worthy posts/papers in the beginning, but after being proactive and regularly asking for feedback, I ended the class with an A+
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Matt is a really great lecturer. The class did a feel little disorganized and I didn't really understand how they graded things. Matt seemed pretty accessible outside of class (never tried) and will go over grading if you request it (which he told us all). I learned a LOT in this class-- put in some effort, write well, and you'll do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Soener did a good job at unpacking the readings, but he can go at a fast pace. You can excel in this class if you do your readings and attend class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: TONS OF READING AND HE NEVER EXPLAINS THEM. Speaking too fast to follow. Extremely disorganized. Closed-book exam with ambiguous review guide and grading rubric. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gives difficult readings and doesn't explain them in detail. He talks about outside examples and uses them to compare it to the reading . It is annoying and difficult to understand. He is a bit un organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: so Matt has a few bad reviews but tbqh I had a great time in his class, it's one of my favorites that I've ever taken. The subject matter is difficult, but I think Matt did a great job of explaining it. He's young so he is a bit disorganized but not to the point that my grade or comprehension suffered. Just read + take good notes and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Matt is a good guy, hes just disorganized. We have so many readings, he posts vids explaining them but theres no agenda to them, so listen closely and take notes. He doesnt even grade our papers, the TA does, so go to TA office hours at least once during the semester. The papers are not hard to write. Just answer the question given. Weekly forum
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: only good things about th e class were the things without him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The only good thing about this class was the group videos. The discussions were more like miniature essay questions with vague grading points, based on a fail/pass grading system. Worse than some of my community college professors. The assignments were weighted heavily and vague/over explained to the point of confusion. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: His grading criteria was not clear whatsoever. Also, his lectures were unorganized and hard to follow. The readings were so hard and there were SO MANY, and he offered little substantial feedback. Lastly, he spied on your watching of the videos and used them for a grade. Just not fun and didn't learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a bit boring, but mostly because class is 1hr 15min. 2 short reflection papers 500-1000 words, and 2 5-6pg papers, one of which is the final. Super clear on grading w/ rubrics, and lays out his slides very clearly to get exactly what you need for weekly quizzes (5q ea.) and for the papers. Low stress class.

If you have to take philosophy, you absolutely should take Spino. 4 papers, 2 are very short reflections that are really super easy (email them early and he'll give u suggestions). Quizzes every week about readings but they're 5 questions and super easy (and open for whole week). Very understandable, kind and an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He may say that you need the textbook, but honestly you don't. As long as you have an online version of it, you're fine we don't even use it. His papers are doable, but his quizzes can be a bit hard to pass at times. He's accessible outside of class and will help you in any way he can. His lectures are a bit lacking, but take him for an ez A/grade.
He's very fair and knowledgeable. One test, a few writing things and you can choose between a final test or paper. Do the readings and be prepared for class.
Great TA, very willing to schedule additional meetings with students.  Very helpful explanations.

AMAZING! When I say I genuinely looked forward to coming to class, I mean it. Pierpaolo really cares about you actually learning the language and he is deeply passionate about teaching it. He was super helpful and engaging which definitely contributed to my retainment of the language over time. I 100% recommend him as a prof.

Pierpaolo was an amazing prof and a great mentor. Literally had no issues with him whatsoever and made Italian super fun to learn. He is really good at getting to the core of what you are struggling with. You will learn a lot without all the tediousness of other profs. Def one of the best profs in this departments.
He is a lively teacher and really cares about his students! Really great guy, he will make you laugh and learn at the same time.

Pierpaolo was one of the best Italian professors I've ever had during my 2 years of learning the Italian language. You learn so much and remember everything he teaches. He's super funny and always cares about his students to make sure that they do well in his class.

Pierpaolo is by far the coolest professor I had in college, and I learned an immense amount in his class. He is a great guy too, and truly cares about his students and their learning. I would strongly  suggest taking his classes and getting to know him as well as you can!

Pierpaolo is an amazing instructor who will not only make sure that every student is caught up in class, but will also make himself available anytime outside of class should anyone need help. Easily one of my favourite instructors who I would highly recommend.

Pierpaolo was by far my favorite of my Italian instructors. He is cheerful in class, funny, and takes the time to get to know each of his students. He was available outside of class whenever I needed. If you're smart, you'll sign up for a class with Pierpaolo.
He's a super awesome and funny person, that also cares a lot about his students! I highly recommend him as a teacher!
One of the kindest and best professors I've ever had!
Best teacher I have had at Oregon! Loves all of his students and does his best to help everyone succeed.

Pierpaolo was one of the best professors I have ever had. The way he taught not only made me feel comfortable to participate but I actually learned in an environment where I didn't feel intimidated or nervous to answer. He really cares about his students and wants them to learn and you receive that positive energy in every lesson.

Really awesome professor. I had him multiple times during my first year of italian. He really helped set me met up for success here at the University of Oregon pursuing italian. Pierpaolo tries his best to make sure that the material is clear and understood. He has no problem coming down to  the student level, which helps so much!

Pierpaolo was one of the few professors I've had that really did care about his students, how they were doing in his class, and helped them in any way he could. He was fun, easygoing and also presented the material in a helpful and useful manner! Best first Italian professor I could have asked for. 10/10 would recommend.
She is nice but her class is pretty hard and sometimes confusing. One time in her class, she put a wrong chart for explaining the statistical analyses about law thing about which I forgot.

Julia is such a caring instructor; you can tell she's really passionate about what she teaches. She and the TA are tough graders, but they do provide good feedback. Also, please do the extra credit. That's the only reason why I didn't get an A in the course lol.

She's funny, she's witty, and she gives everyone in class the benefit of the doubt. She really tries to bring a spark to her lectures, even when we were covering more boring material. Plus she's pretty hot. So there'e that.

I don't know why an accounting student doesn't like Professor Anderson. Although ACCY301 itself is really hard, he explains things very well and is super clear. Following his step in class, I am sure you can really learn things.

I agree to some extent with the other rater saying the class was hard. I disagree that Spencer was uncaring or unengaged. Maybe one of my favorite "hard" classes I've ever taken. I don't mind the difficulty because I learned a TON and the curve was HUGE (like 20%) and were told it would be. Great for people who take ACCY seriously.

Genuinely one of the worst instructors I have ever taken. He lacks both the desire to help students as well as the ability to make the content bearably interesting. His exam averages are significantly lower than the other 301 instructors. The class is curved but I would rather not be on the brink of failing before an unknown curve is implemented.

He made it clear that the class was all about taking the readings and interpreting. He accepted any kind of interpretation so long as you could explain your reasoning. The perfect professor for people that enjoy debate and discussion. He gave great advice during office hours and has continued to give me advice since I finished his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Spires was the best. Really intriguing lectures and discussions. Always there if you need the help and pretty funny. There's a ton of reading but he always clarifies questions during discussion. TAKE NOTES!!! The tests are open note so if you don't take notes or go to class you'll be in trouble for the tests. Overall loved him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved Professor Spires! Lots of reading but well rounded lectures that summarized every piece that was assigned. Great feedback on papers and overall easy going and chill.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Much more interested in social justice than helping his students perfect their craft (like a lot of English profs). Shameful

He is really helpful in and out of class. He is always willing to help and is flexible on submissions and exams. Lectures are very interesting and he tries to make them interactive and fun. 100% would recommend.

Professor Spires has been an awesome English 200 professor; I feel like I will leave his class ready for 300/400 level work. His revision process for essays appears a bit hefty, but he definitely knows what hes talking about when he comes to writing and well help you get better. Be prepared to be in class though; only three freebie absences!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He's very nice, but clearly a new teacher. Discussion is somewhat slow. Books are okay. Some are a little repetitive but if he teaches this course again Oryx and Crake was awesome! I would recommend him, he definitely helped with my writing. But only view grades in the class, so if you rely on homework points and quizzes you're out of luck.

Loved Dr. Span, way better than Educ. 202. Professor Span was very open to students opinions rather than focusing on giving out grades. Also had cheesy jokes but who doesn't love one at 9 AM from that man.
Professor Span is a fantastic teacher; he's really energetic and enthusiastic for what he has to lecture. Very clear and concise, never a boring time with him.
Span is very good.  Tells good stories and sticks to books.  Straight forward and well organized.  good info regarding the civil rights era. tells jokes constantly.

Professor is really interested in topic, which is nice. And if you don't want to read the book (very difficult to read) his powerpoints are helpful. But he'll only give you them if theres a majority of the class in attendance. Grades are all on the RAs, if you get a good one then you should be fine.
Professor was decent. Lectures were somewhat boring and he didn't always post lecture slides. Overall, great TA's who make the learning more clear and are super helpful with whatever you need.

Honestly, this class has a lot of organization issues. Span, if you ever read this, LISTEN TO YOUR TA(s). Most of them seem to have a better understanding of how the course should be ran. He was a good instructor though. I would recommend.

Professor Span is probably one of the most enjoyable lecturers I've ever had. I thought the class was going to be boring and awful (especially since the professor last year was exactly that), but Span has proven to be dorky and intelligent and wonderful and really makes me interested in the subject, even though there is a lot of reading.
The best teacher you could ever have in Social Foundations. A breath of fresh air, extremely intelligent and on point!
This guy is awesome. I took about 2-3 classes with him and you can totally tell that he cares about the course content.  You can't skate by but you get his all, and you'll definitely learn alot!
Great professor!

Had him in an online class.  He read his lectures.  He was willing to answer questions and was a nice guy.  However, I could have not listened to the lectures and still gotten my A.  Not a good class.
No Comments

Wonderful instructor.  Very interested in students and the material.  He is more concerned with the student getting the material than with grades.  He is very helpful and insightful.  Wonderful class.
Cute professor, great at teaching. Approachable and very clear.

While calc 2 isn't going to be a cakewalk no matter who your professor is, Spencer truly made it as easy to understand as possible. His lectures, while often rushed towards the end, were very helpful in understanding the concepts, and while I wouldn't call his tests easy, they were very fair. Spencer has incredibly cute mannerisms as well.
Extremely interesting and easy course???
Awesome teacher. Very clear in lecture. Made Calculus II very understandable. Exams were fair too. Overall great class. It's unfortunate that he won't be teaching for next semester.

Super nice guy and really fair with his exams and homework. He was funny and fairly easy going. I recommend reading the book on your own time because that is a huge help. He is clear with his work and explanations. He is also great in office hours and he is an understanding guy. I highly recommend his class if you have the option of professors.

Dowdall is the man. He's a good explainer, his tests are not too bad. Homework is kinda difficult, but most of the difficult stuff on it will never be on the test. Let us have a "cheat sheet" on the final" on 11 by 8.5 paper. Funny dude. Highly recommend him.

Dowdall is boss. He is very courteous and is always willing to help whenever needed. His exams are fair as long as you've been keeping up with the material. He made a very difficult class seem like a breeze. I definitely recommend him!
Very easy going, just go to class and pay attention and you'll do great. Exams are fair and homework honestly is the hardest part of the class. He's pretty funny too
Love him!
He's just so cute!! Both his class and himself :)

I highly recommend Dowdall for Non-Euclidean Geometry. He was very organized, explained content clearly, was always willing to help with questions/confusion, spoke clearly, and was knowledgeable in his content. His exams, quizzes and homework were fair, and he allowed for corrections on exams as well as one dropped homework grade.

Professor Dowdall was one of the best math teachers I have had. He made class somewhat interesting and was very clear what his expectations were. His tests were very fair, and he allowed you to get points back through test corrections. I would def recommend taking a class with him
Amazing knowledge but cannot explain well. Thick accent. Speaks at a leval we cannot understand.

He does have pretty thick accent, which makes it hard to understand. 
Make sure you follow his lectures and powerpoint or you might be behind by a margin. 
Actually put a decent effort into this class, do the homework and ask constant questions if you want to be successful. I think it was pretty hard to understand everything at first.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really cant understand the negative reviews. The guy is a genius, you will learn a ton. He doesnt want to give anybody a bad grade, just do the work and make an effort.
Has amazing quals but terrible teacher. Can't understand a word of what he's teaching. Speaks like an alien with a heavy accent you can barely understand. Did not learn much in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Knows his subject well but is very theoritical and lecture heavy. Does not seem to know how anything is applied in industry. I found his lectures to be boring and put me to sleep. Course grading is fair and you can get B easy. Great prof if all you want to learn number crunching and complicated math not of practical value. Not bad though overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Arun is a demanding professor who makes you to think hard in assignments and exams. If you pay attention in class, you can learn many new stuffs about B2B marketing. Not a easy course but topics are interesting.

Arun has an extremely touch and go personality. He's the kind of teacher that says there are no wrong answers, yet every answer is completely wrong and he lets you know it. During our group presentations he was passive aggressive and interrupted almost all of them even telling one student to stop reading off of the slide, he could do that himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fun class with lots of group exercises

This professor is knowledgeable and tries a lot to make the classes interactive. Sometimes it becomes a bit too much like you are forced to interact even if you don't want. Lots of assignments but gives prompt feedback.

Awesome and chill prof. Made the course stress-free by organizing assignments in the beginning of semester. Really well-prepared for class. Interacts a lot in class and outside, and gives personal attention. Only negative is doesn't let anyone use laptops in class, so it is difficult to take notes.

Love his lectures, wish more were like him. Really great at delivering material, and takes students' work and feedback to heart. Did a lot of cold calling in the first half of the semester, which sometimes catches you off guard. But his classes are lively and engaging. Gives constructive feedback on group projects. Really wants students to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: bad

He is an amazing professor! He taught the materials well and was very helpful. But only take his class if you are willing to put in the amount of work he is asking for, which could be quiet challenging.

Probably the least accessible professor I've ever had. He set up Piazza so we can ask questions, yet he never looks at it. Emailing also doesn't work.  Don't expect him to follow his syllabus because its so vague that it makes it easy for him to switch things up last minute. Just really distant from students. Terrible professor. Also thick accent.

AE 454 might not be as fun as the other more "hands-on" control classes, but the understanding of Lagrangian and Hamitonian dynamics systems are very useful if you are a control engineer, and sri did a pretty decent job presenting his material. He is also patient to students and is willing to explain things in class if you ask him.
The course offers little engineering application. Most of it is derivation and proofs. No real world application offered. Poor lecture structure and execution on the part of sri.

Really intimidating, expects you to remember a lot. He really likes his dynamics, so sometimes he gets a little ahead of himself and is hard to follow. Office hours with TAs were really helpful, tests weren't too bad if you understood the homework. He was a bit more easy going when I had him the next semester.

Prof Sri has to be one of the best professors in the department. He can certainly be intimidating, and the tests a tad difficult. But once you come out of his course, you would have learnt a lot about Dynamics. This is definitely one of those classes where the grade should not be a factor while looking back at what you have learnt.

He takes a while to get used to because when you first meet him, he can be kind of intimidating.  Overall, his lectures were clear and was helpful in lecture to any type of question.  You could only get office hours with if you had questions about theory- for homework, he would tell you to see the TA. Grading was very fair.
No Comments
Conway >> Sri
The way he explains the concepts is very clear and logic.
Dr. Kannan may be the best professor I've ever had. He teaches beautifully, emphasizing conceptual learning over numerical application.

The best professor in college of business. He has superb ways to explain finance. Very easy to understand finance material. I don't need to read any textbook (his explanation is packed with all info from textbooks ) to solve difficult problems in the exam.
Superb professor! Focus very much on fundamental logic and reasoning, and he links what's happening in the financial world to his classes.
Good instructor, very well-prepared and disciplined. The only possible drawback is lack of slides with lecture notes.
Awesome teacher, great guy. I could see where he could be hard, but he cares about teaching and about helping his students a lot more than a lot of the other FIN professors.
Very difficult class.  Kannan is alright, but plan on putting in many hours for his class.
Good teacher, tests weren't too bad, as long as you do the practice problems you'll be fine
tests were tough, hard to understand his english

He sucked. The lecture was very boring, he didn't really seem interested. He made the class very impersonal. Homework was strictly graded and he didn't really seem to be bothered with any grading complaints people had.
Venkat is an ever helpful and super nice TA. His review sessions before the exams are extremely useful, do not miss them. Has a foreign accent, but was understandable.
Pretty passionate about his subject.

Idk why the other comments hate on her. I genuinely think this is the second most helpful class after cs225. Maybe the most helpful if you are into AI. The MPs are great and I learned a lot. Class structure is clear. A lot of extra credit and very reasonable grading. Highly recommend. The professor gives really good feedback on the final project.

I don't know what crack the other students are smoking this is the best class in this university. She teaches all the latest stuff, like EVERYTHING. all the blockbuster papers its great.

I do understand she is monotone, and mid at lecturing, but she is extremely knowledgable, slides/content is insanely amazing, everything is there. Take this class
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are boring; she talks over them without writing or going into detail. You never learn code for the MPs, so you have to have a reasonable basis for a lot of ML, and there are no test cases, so essentially, you test and run everything blind. Her quizzes are built to be anti-ChatGPT, which sometimes becomes anti-human.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Before you chose this class, just know that the MP's for Lana's class is time consuming to say the least. I do go to her lectures, and she does mention good details, only thing i would've hoped was for her to actually write down on the slides as well, not just talk over them. Also for Mp's she doesn't provide a rubric, you learn details on ed stem.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: just a poor prof. dead inside. terrible at explaining.
One of the best professors for computer vision!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She just reads slides out loud in class. She doesn't really care if you understand it. She isn't one of those teachers that tries to built up to concepts, or walk you through the intuition behind understanding something. Its more like here is information, I'm just going to keep pushing through slides. Her MPs are great however.
CS 444 is one of the worst classes I have taken at uiuc. Absolutely no structure to the class whatsoever, do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors that I have ever met!

Class covers some extremely interesting concepts. Svetlana does a piss poor job of explaining them in lecture. Her lecture slides consist of condensed material from a textbook and she literally reads the slides aloud in class. There are no explanations nor any followup discussions apart from the ones she prepares beforehand.
She is clear and consistent with her lectures. Materials are interesting.
Excellent preparation and time management. She is a very sincere professor and the best I've ever had.

Quite a poor professor. She has interesting research but has no clue how to properly lecture. Slides are verbatim from the book as are the exams. Does not help at office hours and has a terrible laugh. Keeps track of students attendance mentally… and calls you by name. Awkward.
Terrible professor. Boring lectures, unhelpful in office hours, exams are entirely memorization.
Very boring lectures, slides are a condensed version of relevant book chapters, graded class participation, exam is entirely memorization, unhelpful TAs
Amazing professor. One of the most intelligent people I've heard speak in my time as a student at Illinois. Yale is lucky to have him.
Very interested in the content. A very passionate and intelligent professor. One of the most thoughtful professors I've had at this school.
Prof Svolik is a nice guy, but he did not show much interest in the class. He seemed to be more interested in his research. He compensated his lack of helpfulness with hefty amounts of extra credit.

Svolik is very intelligent. He  presents class material in a naturally sophisticated manner and makes the seemingly dry subject matter the root of all fascination. Easy class that leaves students with valuable information permeated by a phenomenal lecturer.

Professor Svolik is smart and a great lecturer. My favorite part of the class was his lectures, my least favorite part was listening to all of the boring presentations. Tests were very easy to prepare for if you actively listened during class. Problem sets were very straight-forward also. Overall, easiest poli sci class I've ever taken.
Prof Svolik is engaging and incredibly smart. Class is not difficult. Short midterm and final exam. Only 4 additional hw assignments. No essays.

YOU DO NOT NEED THE BOOK FOR THIS COURSE. 1 MIDTERM; 1 FINAL. HE IS EXTREMELY SMART. TESTS ARE A LITTLE DIFFICULT. 4 HOMEWORK ASSIGNMENTS. A REASONABLE AMOUNT OF EXTRA CREDIT. WARNING: THE CLASS CAN GET PRETTTYYYY BORING.

PS 397 was my favorite undergraduate class. Prof. Svolik is so knowledgeable, gives clear explanations, makes material interesting, has helpful teaching style. He inspired me to continue on with graduate school.

PS397 course was so well taught, I challenged my self and took his game theory class which was difficult but, out of all of my courses at U of I, the class that I got the most out of. I will always think of things in a 2x2 matrix of payoffs and losses. Thanks for one great experience, take any all his classes for a great challenge; do the reading.

Excellent professor. He assigns lots of reading, but it's manageable. He is very good at explaining concepts, clarifying difficult topics, encouraging discussion, etc. Don't let his intimidating Slovakian accent fool you, he tolerates a fair amount of shenanigans as long as y'all stay on track. Do the work, participate, and you're gold.

Professor Srull is a wonderful man and a great lecturer. His lectures are entertaining and informative. He always ends the lecture by wishing us the best and seems to really care for his students. Online learning is hard but the exams are very manageable. If you do the work, you will do great!

Professor Srull is a great professor! His lectures are entertaining and educational at the same time. Section X is asynchronous and your grade is determined by 3 exams which aren't cumulative. There is a lot of reading and the lectures are quite lengthy, but as long as you do it you'll do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His lectures are very boring and there's no way of knowing what is or is not important because he doesn't post slides or definitions. There's no textbook, only a novel so you're left wondering what you do and don't need to know. your entire grade is based on 3 exams so if you don't do well on the exams you're screwed
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He never used power point Dont pick this course unless you can record the whole lecture and write down everything he said.

The professor himself is a goofy guy that is interesting to listen to during lectures. However, do not take section X. The class is graded only by tests on midterms and finals. The tests are also only multiple choice and have random questions which makes it hard. Most of the material you have to learn is from the textbook. Also no + or - grades.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is literally reading from an online textbook every class! He gives you "outlines" but they're actually just the section names of what he's reading from, and he reads straight from his printed textbook for each lesson. Because of this, unless you can write down and study each word he is saying - tests are very hard. Even then they're still hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: ONE OF MY FAVORITE PROFESSORS. The way he teaches is very intuitive, he has a structure and follows an outline, but doesn't just read from a slide. He is very passionate about the material and is so goofy. Everything is so interesting, class flies by

My only complaint is with the grading of his exams. Each exam has its own curve, so an A could be a 44/55, 38/55, etc. But the only thing that really matters is the final point total for which he makes a grade scale for at the end. So you never really know what your grade is until the final one is posted into the grade book.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Makes Psychology much more difficult then needs to be. Whole grade is based on four exams and a subject pool. Exams are pretty hard but curved. Lectures do not cover stuff in the book so you have to go to lecture plus read the book. This takes up a lot of time.(About 8-10 modules)You never know whats going to pop u on tests. Take regular section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The biggest thing about PSYC100X is that your grade is based on 4 exams and subject pool participation (basically 20 pts extra credit), and his exams are half based on the book and half based on lecture. His tests are pretty hard so you have to read the book and go to lecture, but there are huge curves (for my class, a 44/55 and 38/55 were As).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had little motivation to go to class as the lectures only include a couple words for 1 hour and 20 minutes and Prof. Srull just talks the whole time. I had no clue what the test questions would be on or what to take notes about! Also there are no - and + grades which sucks if you get say an 89... at least the prof was kind of interesting.
read the textbook, attend the lecture and take notes, you'll get an A. and honestly don't think the lecture is always funny...

Professor Srull is a really interesting person. He knows lots of insights on Psychology. 4 tests plus subject pool added together make up your final grade. There are very BIG curves on the test, but if you want to do well, you probably have to show up to majority of the lectures. A lot of people don't go to class, so that's why the curves are big
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, pretty quirky, and a great lecturer. He makes the material very interesting and easy to understand. Tests are a little difficult (you need to read the book), but nothing too bad. He curves the tests and also the class at the end (very generously). Overall, great teacher, great class. Wish he taught more courses!
Easy A but the readings do take long. Lectures are long and boring.  No homeworkquizzes and only 4 tests and subject pool.  It took me two days to prepare for the tests.

Easy class but poorly organized with little hope of actually learning material. Without a curve, nobody would pass the class. Exam questions are on specific studies he mentions briefly in class, and you cannot look up the study on your own since he doesn't cite them. Do not take this class if you are genuinely interested in the topic.

You have to attend every lecture and take good notes, but you can get away with cramming the chapters the night before and get an A.  Very funny and likeable professor. Made the class go faster with his anecdotes.

He's a pretty goofy guy but he knows psychology in and out. He has interesting stories and gives good examples. He teaches section X, which is different from any of the other sections. There is no homework just 4 exams and a subject pool. His exams are pretty hard, but he uses a generous curve. Just go to class, take notes, read the book, and study
A is manageable if you read the book and attend lectures. Exams are tricky, but the curve is forgiving. Overall pretty fun class.

I don't know how this class got a reputation of being easy, it is anything but easy. The only "easy" part of this class is that there is no homework except reading. Curve isn't that crazy as people made it seem. Take the regular section.

Srull is a pretty good professor. Class is not mandatory and can be boring but it is helpful for the exams.  He explains things very clearly and simply.  Exams are tough but if you read the book and go to class it is not bad.  Very generous curve.

He's a good professor. Going to class and taking notes is a must as some of the stuff he says literally shows up word for word on the exams. Sometimes he will talk about one bullet point for almost 30 minutes but once you get past his style of lecturing, it's a good class. Curve is generous just make sure you read all the sections from the book
Uses overhead projectors with minimum words and goes off on pointless tangents. There are about 10 chapters to read in the textbook for the exam, and his exams are very specific and very hard.

This class had only three exams, and there were no essays, no participation, and no textbook. That being said, it is very important to go to lecture, even if it is not mandatory. The lectures were easy to follow, albeit boring at times, and the exams were not bad either. I am not a psyc major but I could take this class without any problems.

Pure audible lecture. Non-relevant tangents. Doesn't teach the non course related textbook (right-wing biased with cherry-picked studies). Curved exams yes, but with the grounds of arbitrary questions.
Don't even bother going to his class! EVERYTHING is from the book, and the exams are too hard for this level.

TOO EASY. Go to lecture, listen, and read what he assigns. Takes like 3 days at a slow pace to read it all. His exams are tricky but not terrible and don't worry, his curve is pretty much ridiculous (in a good way). Easiest class I had this semester. NO homeowork, no stress. Just 4 exams and 6 subject pool experiments. Easy A

Just a classic lecture with over three hundred people. Typical aloof professor, although he spoke plainly and was not condescending for the most part. Not having a discussion section made the class pretty impersonal and a little more difficult than it would have normally been. Enjoyed multiple choice tests and there was a curve.
Amazing lecturer. Very interested in the topic and knowledgeable. Friendly, helpful, enthusiastic.
After every class I feel as though I had just witnessed a ground-breaking speech. Srull presents information in a crystal clear manner. He is very easy to follow.
Very good lecturer - Never had trouble understanding/following what he was saying. Though not mandatory, lectures are a must. Must read the textbook as well. Very interesting class.

The class is easy enough if you STUDY for the exam, READ the textbook, and ATTEND & take notes at all lectures. Lectures can be dull though, as he tends to be THOROUGH w/materials. but he is very helpful if you have any questions before and during exams. The curve for the class is generous.

He might be sort of odd and quirky in personality but in my opinion he's an interesting lecturer. Content of the course was intriguing. He can be pretty funny when he wants to. You HAVE to go to class and MUST do the reading in order to even have a chance on the exams. exams are decently curved, he's pretty generous.

If you want an A, memorize all the vocab, important names, experiments, and take detailed notes in lecture. Type your lecture notes because he can go deep into detail. Consider buying the study guide, it helped me a lot. Some practice questions in there end up on the exam. You can get an A as long as you are willing to work for it. Decent lecturer.

The hardest part of this class was the sheer amount of information stuffed into 4 exams with 55 questions. The readings and the lectures were totally unrelated but both were on the exam. Curve was EXTREMELY generous however.
Very nice and helpful

one of the worst professors i've ever had. he mumbles a lot, repeats the same sentence 10 times at a rate of 0.2 mph, his lectures aren't clear. you have to read the textbook because its on the exam but he doesn't go over anything that's in the book. exams are harder than you'd expect

His is fun and states everything clearly in the lecture. You should write some notes in lecture and also read some book, but materials are not hard. So as long as you attend the lecture and read book, you will get an A.

By Jove, I could not figure out why his teeth are disgusting. They were so distracting even when I sat in the back. Anyway, READ the book AND go to class. Failed the first test because I did neither, and ended up with a B. I redeemed myself with 3 more tests and a generous curve. Do the subject pool, it's required. That's how idiots get C's.

This class should be easy, 4 NONCONSECUTIVE exams and 6 subject pool participations, however if you never have taken a psych class (like me) DO NOT take this class with him. I feel like this class is easier for ppl who have prior knowledge. His examples go on for 20 minutes and lectures seem to take forever. He does curve the grades, which is aplus
Great teacher. The material is interesting and the tests are not hard as long as you attend/pay attention in lecture AND read the assigned chapters.

Read the textbook, go to class and take a lot of notes. With these, you'll do great one the exam. For the first exam, 43/50 = A. Material is interesting though, so its not too hard to concentrate. If that doesn't work for you, bring a recorder.

I liked Srull. I think he does tend to lose track of himself every so often, but that's part of the fun. Read the book, no really, do it, and take notes in class no matter how he rambles, and you'll be good to go. Three exams make up your grade, but they are curved significantly. Social Cognition was really interesting.

He does ramble in the class, some people get bored, but exams are fine if you study both lecture notes and textbooks. My highest exam score: 47/50. Make sure you read textbooks thoroughly. If you miss class then get notes from classmates, since he doesn't post it online. Be aware that his letter grade don't include +/- so it's either A or B.

avoid this class i hated srull. awful professor should not be here. sucks. if you are a freshman don't take this class until your sophomore year or atleast until your g.p.a. is high enough to handle the toll this class will take on it. i cannot tell you to avoid this class enough. BOOOOO!!!

A few ?s... 1. Why is this awful professor rated so high on this website 2. Why is professor at U of I. The avg of each of the tests is a D and then gets curved, why is that positive? Lecture is awful and hard to follow. I would say read the book but that might not help. Take psych at a community college or something, not with this guy!

If you are a good test taker or have previously taken AP Psych definitely take PSYC 100 Section X with Srull! Just show up to class, take notes, manage your time well so you can finish the module readings and you will get an A. The psych studies are interesting and some of them pay you for participating. This is a very straight forward class.

Although attendence is not mandatory, getting an A in this class is highly dependent on your regular attendance. Srull is an entertaining professor and keeps students' attention fairly well. Make sure you read the book, because he will pull about 25-30% of the exam questions from it.

What a dreadful professor. Rambles on with unrelated anecdotes and focuses on topics really unrelated to social cognition. We spent the last few weeks on evolutionary psychology for gods sakes. I'm not sure what we learned in this class that's related to social cognition at all. Pretty easy class though if you can stand to go to class.

The only grades come from exams which are *mostly* lecture based, so go to lectures. He explains things very thoroughly, which can be helpful, but also boring at times. The exams are not too hard, and are curved. My raw score was 78% which ended up being a solid A.

Awesome teacher.Class is interesting/funny and hes reasonable.changed a test two days before we were supposed to have it because someone raised their hand and asked him to bc of the heavy reading load,so he held a class vote right there. Going to class is pretty crucial, not mandatory.Worst part of the class is the book, which you do need to read.

i thought X would be a breeze, and granted it prolly would have been if id tried harder. class was boring to me because it took him 10 minutes to get through one example, so i got frustrated listening to him. but if you pay attention, read the book, you'll do fine.

only 4 difficult test. Half the material comes from the book, half from lecture, and he doesn't talk about whats in the book at all. Very difficult class, stressful, do not take sectin X. He doesn't have office hours. Sometimes hes interesting and funny, but i would rather it not be funny and get a good grade...

I'm torn. The pros to the class are that there are just 4 tests and that there are no other academic commitments for the class with the exception of the subject pools. The cons are that the subject matter is boring and just skims the surface. He seems nice enough, although I never actually got to know him.

Okay. I'm confused. Everyone is saying this class was hard? What??? This was the easiest class I've taken BY FAR at UIUC. All you have to do is go to lecture (his tests use examples STRAIGHT from it), read the book, and memorize the definitions. Ignore the people saying it was hard- they have to be Communication majors or something... so easy...

I had him for Psych100X freshman year and he was AWFUL. but then I took Psych353, social cognition, with him and he was AMAZING. So much better to upperclassmen then he was to the freshmen. Tests were easy if you went and took notes and paid attention. Couple questions from the book on each test. Highly recommend this class!
his test have almost nothing to do with his lectures or the books and your grade only consists of 4 tests. Do not take this class.
Overall he's a bad professor.  This is supposed to be an intro course, and he doesn't offer office hours, and tests extremely difficult material from the book.  Only good part of is the curve.

whoever writes on here that the class is easy they are lying, it consists of 4 ridiculously hard tests, i read all the chapters and still did bad on them...when he talks in lecture its boring and really hard to pay attention to,and to be honest doesnt help on the tests, i have no idea what more to do to do good on the tests take normal psych not X!

Teacher definitely likes to talk, classes is better than most, but I still fell asleep. All the points are based on 3 tests, but there is a HUGE curve, so as long as you somewhat pay attention and study, you should least get a "B". Lectures are different from the book, but your expected to know both for the test.
VERY fair with the curve. Must go to class and do the readings if you want a good grade. Very funny guy. You have to be willing to put in time for this class, but it's worth it!!

Loved this class!  The topics were interesting and he gave fun examples.  One of the few classes where I enjoyed going and didn't want to miss lecture.  He tests over the book but doesn't teach from it.  The book is kind of confusing, but overall the class is pretty easy.  Don't talk during class or leave early.
going to class and taking notes is vital, along with reading the book... the class is heavily curved, with the cutoff for an A being 199/240 this semester.. which isn't difficult to pull off

Section x is a lot easier than the other psych 100 classes. You don't learn as much, but it is worth it for the gen ed. Some reading, but not as much as the other sections. Also, he loves the sound of his voice! His examples can go on for over 20 min. Overall the class is okay, i would take it again

He really does know how to beat a dead horse, that's for sure. He'll exhaust examples to the last syllable, this guy loves the sound of his own voice. I really didn't think he was that great of a teacher, personally, but the class was okay and it wasn't that difficult if you studied and read the book. definitely don't talk in class or leave early.
What a great guy! He's really funny and knows what he's talking about. Go to class, take notes, and read the book liberally and you'll be fine. Highly recommended!

rambles on about so much stuff, pure auditory lecture. covers too much stuff, and book sections that we are expected to know have nothing to do with what is in class. take it if you like taking a lot a lot a lot of notes and trying to pay attention to a rambling professor, not knowing about what you'll be assessed with.

Loved this class! I took 100x with him freshman year and liked him so much I took this as a non-major when I saw he was teaching it. Tends to beat examples into the ground which can get kind of boring, but overall a pretty easy and interesting class. DO THE READING!!!
Don't take the regular psych 100! This one is less work and you probably will get a laugh in every lecture.

This professor issues exams which are significantly based on his lectures. Textbook material is rarely discussed but is necessary to do well on the exam, however. There were no review sheets handed out for all 3 exams (that's all the work that is required), which makes it harder to study for. No EC/quizzes to raise grade, so don't screw up there.
he was a really great professor!! you have to go to class and take notes and read the book for tests. Great guy!!!

Interesting class and very fun teacher! However, you should attend class to take notes and you have to read if you want to get an A in the class. Amusing stories in class, but it can sometimes get a little boring. And DO NOT talk during lecture!
MUST go to class to take notes...I had to get a D on the first exam to realize that. Other than that, he's rather amusing. Just for the love of god, don't talk during class or come in late.
I had fun in this class. Good professor :)

Great and rewarding class! Although I was able to ace all the exams, it was not without work. Make sure you read all the text and go to all of the studies! it is very important to read the text and go to lecture and take notes. However, if you can read all the text in a couple of days, that is all the studying you should need to do before the exam.
Take this class!!!

Love the class!  The prof is hilarious and the material is interesting...only the last two sections though.  The first third is kind of dry, as is any introductory material.  All you have to do is go to class, take notes, and read the book...you'll be guaranteed an A!

Had him in an intro to psych class maybe 10 years ago.  Full of himself and completely unsympathetic.  As a teacher for the last 7 years, I'd say the only thing I learned from him was how not to treat students.
Read the book. Go to class. He's funny.

all you have to do in order to get an A is take notes from the lecture and read. he makes his test half from lecture, half from the book. this is the first class ive actually read the book and i needed to. its not hard and as long as you were at lecture. good teacher. lectures can be a little dry though

Lectures were boring in the beginning, but got progressively more interesting.  Class is fairly easy.  Lots of reading though.  Make sure you do the practice problems at the end of each module because he takes many of his test questions straight from those.  Threw lots of random questions though which hurt my grade.
Easy if your read the book and take good notes. 4 exams and one subject pool. The curve ended up being 200/240 for an A

Read the book and take as much notes as possible in lecture. He tends to go off on stupid tangents, but also very likely to throw a curveball question on the test. Hes kind of a wierd guy but funny at times.

Lectures are funny, but the exams can be hard if you don't read the book.  Notes pretty much mean nothing, just read the book and do the chapter exams.  I missed an A by like 2 points, so make sure you get as many problems right on the exams.
There are 4 tests each worth 55 points and a subject pool worth 20. read the book, especially the end questions because they are always on the tests.  Easy A if you read . . .
Funny lectures.  If you read and study you'll be fine.  Some test questions are taken straight from the end of the modules in the book.

If you read the book, you will get A after the curve for sure. So, read it! Go to the lectures. He's not boring, he's fun to listen to even though he repeats himself 3 times on everything. Doing experiments are annoy!! But it helps your grade.

Was funny and made class interesting, but got redundant at times and his exam questions are very particular. You have to read to do well, but the book is a pretty easy read. His lectures were inspirational, informative, and had plenty of class participation because Professor Swigger has an amazing ability to make many topics interesting. This is the professor you want for a Political Science class. I took him off the recommendation of a friend and I cannot recommend him more myself.

Dr. Swigger is an amazing lecturer. However, you shouldn't take his Political Psychology course expecting an easy A. Nearly half your grade will hinge on a 3-part project, and the other half on two exams. Both exams are taken in essay form, so make sure to keep in mind that he is a tough grader who only provides feedback if you reach out directly.

Extremely hard intro class. Be prepared to take quizzes before every class. These quizzes as well as a few exams were the only things determining your grade. It seemed he gave little care of his students success and down talks students who have questions during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cool, assignments can sometimes be vague but he'll help you get there if you ask him.
he's not cool. he is boring. tries to be funny but he doesn't realize he is the only one laughing except for the butt-kissers.

Nathaniel (cool name, not!) was a horrible TA. Not only did he have an annoying/whiny voice, but he would go off on tangents and run out of time to cover the material.  Thankfully, I was a senior and only needed a B- to get on the  bronze tablet.  Apply the PIHFF test, nothing libelous here!
Most pessimistic person I have ever met.  Answered emails sarcastically.  Overall this class was terrible.
This guy is smart, interesting and funny. Basically everything that the professor wasn't. Made getting up for an early Friday morning discussion not as completely awful.
Very funny dude. Also kinda cute. :) Definately the best TA I've ever had on this campus.
this guy is tight

Bridget is very passionate about her topics, but has a "reinvent the wheel" approach to her educational theories. She has under 10 years experience in her own public K-12 music classrooms, but is still knowledgeable. Difference in philosophies aside, Bridget has a glowing smile and personality that will make you excited to go to class.
Approachable and helpful! Had fun getting to know her.

Dr. Sweet is incredibly knowledgeable and helpful. I often felt pushed outside of my comfort zone with some of the projects she gives, but I never felt isolated or unprepared to do the work. Also, go to her office hours and talk to her. She will teach you just as much about music as she can help you balance everything. Love her teaching!

Fun teacher who knows his stuff.  Very approachable.  I work full time and Joe was always willing to take extra time to work with me and my schedule.  He also provides lots of feedback on your writing, which was great!
Great professor.  This is the second class I've take with Swenson.  Loved it!

Great professor, he's at Hamline University now. I had him for general philosophy, and while attendance was very optional) he still talked to me, never held my absences against me, and he's just an all around swell guy.  His examples are a bit confusing at times, and he repeats them a lot, but I always found them helpful.  Had him for two classes

He's at Hamline now. Great professor and good class so far.  There's alot of reading  but Swenson does a good job of making sure that you see all  the important points.  I think his lecture are hilarious.  I would recommend taking his classes.

The history of modern phil is not always an interesting subject.  However, Joe did decently.  He was open to other viewpoints.  My only two gripes were the rambling (which was every class), and his inability to think of examples than Larry, Bob, and White Castles.  A well studied Nietzsche scholar.  First half was boring, bu the second was nice.

Talks about White Castle and uses the example of "Larry"...he's a Nietzsche scholar, though, and he's got his**** together in that aspect. Sometimes rambles, but again, very knowledgeable and he can help you out of anything, all you have to do is ask him questions.

GREAT professor. Extremely approachable and very knowledgeable. Do the reading and you'll be fine. He even lent me more books on philosophers I wanted to know more about. Overall, best class I've taken yet.

He tends to ramble. Little room for class discussion. Haven't been able to pay attention. Just study the handouts he gives you. otherwise its easly for an honors class. in my opinion this class is horrifically boring though.

Swenson's a great guy.  Down-to-earth, friendly, and always willing to help.  Also, he's willing to consider other viewpoints.  Class was incredibly easy, too.  If he's still around, you'll want him as a TA.

joe was a cool guy. he explained everything pretty well, and u could always go to his office hours if u needed more help. overall, this class was easy, just remember to skim over the readings before class because he likes to change the dates of the reading quizzs.
he sucked.
Was really nice, was very clear, gave really funny examples! I would take another class with him if he taught one...and he's kinda cute in the Minnesota kind of way!
Very helpful even though she is not the most experienced. Worked very hard to make sure we understood the material and was also very easy to relate with.
Sara was extremely helpful! She seemed to care about her students.  She improved as the semester went on, and I would like to take another class with her!!!
I would definitely recommend taking PSYC 100 with Sara. She's so nice, very helpful and tries to make the class fun and interesting!
I could explain the material better than her, going to lecture was pointless. She banned computers- are we in high school? She looks bored when teaching the information and just wants to graduate.

Ok, so Sara is just a TA, but she was awesome! I wish I could have more classes with her. She was helpful, and she taught the material really well. Also, she was fun. There were 4 essays that were super easy, quizzes that were kind of tough, and just 2 exams that I got Bs on. I highly recommend her.

He's a very good teacher teaching a dull subject. A lot of the class is random stats, but the exams really aren't too bad. I did all the readings a week before the exams and I did fine. He was even nice enough to let us take the final exam online.

Teacher is quite boring. No correlation if you go to class or not as no one really pays attention when they do go to class. Teacher expects you to remember arbitrary numbers even though he says he won't, he's extremely nice and is willing to answer any question, but tests are hard teacher is boring! I recommend not taking his classes.
I think he's trying to be funny but he can come off as mean and mocking. Makes asking question miserable!

He was a great professor, however his test were somewhat difficult, but he ends up curving them 15 to 20 points. I found his lectures interesting. Definitely a high correlation between going to class and getting good grades. Go to class, pay attention and you'll get an A.

I wish I would have dropped this class after the first day. The topics sound interesting, but he mumbles when he talks and is SO boring to listen too. Not to mention the articles he expects you to read for class everyday are VERY long and then for the exam he takes some random statistic and expects you to know it.
First-class educator
No Comments
