Online class with super easy setup, almost guaranteed an A as long as you did the work. Content was usually current and interesting. Recommend for anyone.
Time waster.
This class was crazy easy. Because it was online I didn't hear much from Professor Sydnor, but she seems to care about what she does, so that's nice.

KIN 142 is certainly among the easiest As in the school. It's only online for 8 weeks. It's about five hours of work per week for a guaranteed A. Additionally, you only need a 90% to get an A. The only way you wouldn't get an A is if you miss a couple assignments because there is no late or extra credit. The class was pretty interesting too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: An excellent, well prepared teacher. Loves her work!

Katherine Syer was an excellent teacher. She was beyond professional, always exhibited expert knowledge of the topic, was extremely helpful and thorough, but most of all, an enjoyable presence in class. I would recommend any course she instructs.
Too hard of a class.

Dr. Syer is a wonderful teacher.  Her enthusiasm has no end, much like her knowledge.  I have taken three classes with her and enjoyed them all.  She will push you to be your best, but that is why were in school, right?
No Comments

WAAAAY too hard for a 100-level GenEd. She knows what she's talking about, but unless you enjoy memorizing a fewhundred classical pieces along with every detail, you will be miserable for a semester. Would probably be a great prof. for upper level classes
Passionate about the subject. Willing to help. And very easy on the eyes. Great Accent! (Canadian?)G'day, eh?
No Comments
Lectures are easy to follow and very interesting, but it's very difficult to do well in this class. It seems as though tests are made in order for you not to do well on them.
No Comments

She is absolutely awful, please save yourself the grief and don't take her class.  She's so snotty and very much enjoys the sound of her own voice.  She tries to make her tests impossible and has no concept that students have other classes and homework.  Read her ISU reviews if you don't believe me; they're even harsher than these.

Unlike other students, I enjoyed her. She is sarcastic sometimes, which people might misinterpret, but otherwise I thought she was funny. Encourages you to find solutions or answers yourself first before just giving them to you. Knows her stuff, but def. doesn't take BS from students.
She has no interest in capturing her student's attention or interest in class subject.

The material is straightforward, if you study the study guides you will be fine. Projects are a waste of time--they're something a high school would assign.  She is nice unless you disagree with her or challenge her viewpoint. It's a joke and an easy A.
She's a good teacher if the material was interesting.  The RSO projects are fun, but the readings are plain and dry.  She does a good job with what she has to work with.

I struggled with the readings as a non-history student, but learned a lot from this class. She is super kind and flexible with deadlines. I had a lot of personal problems come up, and she was always super helpful and understanding. I recommend her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Symes is a great lecturer and 141 in general was good time. Very engaging and always had something insightful to say. The exams are all written, but they're pretty easy if you remember what the lectures were about. Go to lecture OR read the book, you don't gotta do both unless you didn't understand. Do read/skim the primary sources for discussion.

I had some difficulty with the papers, but if you're a history major it probably isn't a problem. As for this professor, she is absolutely lovely! Classes were engaging and fun, and the textbook she wrote for the class is informative but not dry. No tests, you summarize what you learn in essays which you have a few days to write.

I love Professor Symes and she is a brilliant person. Her lectures are great and super engaging, but much reading is required. Your grade is only determined by a few things, so make sure to show up/participate in  discussion and get to know your TA and how they grade papers. Other than that, I loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No exams but lots of interesting readings. Meetings are structured discussions with some lecturing. Graded based on essays and discussion participation. (Taken during COVID)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: You don't need to attend lectures for discussion is mandatory and you need to read the sources for those. Buy the online textbook! It will help you with exams because when you study for the terms on the exams you can search by the specific word and see every time that word was referenced or mentioned. Ask your TA what they grade for on the essays.

SHE IS AN AMAZING LECTURER. The only reason I got a C is because my TA was terrible. I look forward to taking a class with just her and no TA, because I really learn a lot from her. She is the sweetest lady ever.

This class asks a lot for a 100-level course. The final requires you to memorize an essay ahead of time, fill out 45 paragraph-long ID terms (only 4 of which actually appear on the exam, the other 40 are a waste of time), and papers are graded tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Symes is a good professor, but the class is asking way too much for a gen ed. There's only one midterm and a final, but these are really hard and don't have much at all to do with the lectures. Going into the exams blind is probably as easy as going into the exams having been to every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class itself is very easy. I never went to lectures and got 97% on the midterm, however, if you trying to fulfill your Advanced Composition require I don't recommend this class unless you truly enjoying reading history because they require you to read very bland material. The papers are graded leniently though, just a drag to write them.

I wish that the history department would give her more classes to teach. Shes by far the best history teacher Ive taken in undergrad. Passionate, entertaining, intelligent. She has a way of making each student feel intelligent and that they want to speak up in class. Lectures are fast-paced and kept me interested the whole class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy A. I stopped attending lecture after the midterm and ended up completely fine. Jun Huang was my TA. He's alright, he let me re-write a paper when I got a B+ on one so pretty much as long as you read the textbook/go to discussion (lecture you don't need to), you'll be fine.

This class is a great Gen Ed grade booster. An easy A. Lectures are not that necessary to succeed in the class. Professor Symes textbook is amazing and written to perfection. It is your best resource in this course. Read the textbook (30 pages a week) and you should be fine. Also Liz Adamo is the TA you want. She is amazing and gives little HW.

She's an amazing professor. She did theatre and gets really into what she teaches, which makes it much more enjoyable. She really knows what she's talking about and is very helpful. There were also quite a few extra credit opportunities. I wasn't a fan of history before this class, but it was such a great experience. Would love to take her again.

Carol is super helpful when it comes to the assignments.  I got a B on one and she let me re-write it to get an A.  She does not grade harshly.  She knows what she's talking about and is super intelligent.  There is reading but it's not overbearing like in other history classes.  If you have the chance take a class with her because she is so cool.

Great Class, really knows her stuff, lectures were intriguing and full of her own insights.  go to lecture and discussion and youll do well.  Tests were essay format but as long as you pay attention in lecture youll do fine as everything important is overemphasized... easy A and a great class

I have hated history my entire life until I took this class with her. I'm not even done with it yet but she deserves the review now. She's absolutely brilliant and makes history fun. If you have the chance to take a class with her (especially 141), DO IT!
One of most interesting professors I have ever had.  Easy class if you pay attention and do the minimum. Recommended if you need some history course as a gen ed or cause history is your thing

Discovered that only like 5% of what she lectures on is on the exam, so I stopped going after midterm. Section attendance is mandatory-- Ryan Bean is a sweet TA. 2 papers, 2 exams. I just read the textbook and went to section and got an A. Gives essay q's and exam ID's out, only somewhat hard part is putting in chrono. order.
Great class
Energetic and very into what she teaches I enjoyed every lecture even though they were early in the mornings.

Most of what you've read here is true. She likes to ham it up during lecture, but she is high energy and extremely smart. I loved having this class early in the morning, it set a good tone for the day. Make sure you attend discussion classes. Tests are tough for 100 level. And yes, she is kinda hot, and it is a bit distracting! I liked her!

She is a passionate lecturer and very approachable. However, her midterm and final is IMPOSSIBLE. She expects you to know words from the material that was not covered in lecture. She chooses 10 words from the whole term and doesn't give a list of terms to study. I studied about 70 words and 1 of those made it on the test.

I LOVED this class!  It was an interesting topic for me and Professor Symes is very interesting and enthusiastic and she's very good at leading class discussions.  She's very approachable and helpful.  There was a lot of reading which was necessary for discussions. Three four papers but no tests.  Take her classes, she's awesome!
She was an animated and passionate teacher, but the material was difficult, and the T.A's are terrible. I do NOT recommend this course!

I already learned much of what was covered in this class in high school and I'm a history major, but her exams are IMPOSSIBLE (highest IN CLASS on midterm was 91%). She does seem passionate about what she teaches, but the lectures are ultimately useless. Material gets covered way too fast and you are expected to know everything in-depth for exams &

For this lecture class your fate mostly depends on your TA. Her lectures are pretty cool. I had no interest in ancient or medieval history prior to this. Quite a bit of reading, quite a few papers. Pretty hot though.

I did not enjoy this class at all. I felt that she did not do a good job with linking the material in the book to lectures, and even less to the midterm and exam. I did not feel she was a great lecturer, either, although every now and then she did something interesting in class. The only good perk I can think of is that I had a good TA...

Hit or miss with Symes; the class itself is not bad, you should plan on attending lecture and taking notes because the combination of lecture/book/extra readings is what makes up the exams. TAs were ok, if you talk to them about papers/exams and get them to clarify exactly what you should write you'll get an A. Very enthusiastic professor.

I would never have taken this had I known what I was getting into.  Tests are extremely hard.  Papers topics may as well be written in a foreign language far as much as I understood them.  When I tried to get in touch with Prof. Symes, she was out of town and told me to ask my TA.  I'm not a history major.  This was way too hard for an intro class.

This was the worst class I have ever taken in my life.  If you like history at all, this class will make you hate it.  On the bright side, Prof. Symes seems to really know what she is talking about and is even entertaining once in a while.  Not much in lecture helps with the test.  You are pretty much on your own.

Prof. Symes is AMAZING. I have had her for both HIST 492 and HIST 141. She is probably the most intelligent and influential women in our history department. Though her lectures may seen a bit forthright and foreboding, that's just her. Also, research your TA before choosing one. I had "DemonFace" and it has sadly changed my loving view of TAs.

Symes clearly has a theatrical background - she has a commanding stage presence in a large lecture hall, and uses it to her advantage.  Her lectures were very well done, with a clear focus each lecture.  She is clearly incredibly well versed in the field.
Very hot, kind of distracting.

I really didn't like her very much as a teacher.  Her lectures were pointless and had nothing to do with the tests.  She also seemed to be very arrogent and not very caring.  Maybe she is a good teacher in small class settings, but I definetly would avoid her in a large lecture format.  Also, all her TA's seemed to be very weird.

Symes is awesome; seriously she rocks. Perhaps one of the smartest people I've ever met and the nicest. The previous reviewers definately are either ignorant or immature, because Symes is consistently ranked one of the best HIST profs every semester. Look at the List of Teachers Ranked Excellent on UIUC website. Last word: Symes is the cut.

Her lectures are boring and don't really teach you anything relevant to the class.  If you are good at history and writing, the class isn't too hard, but if you are not it can be very difficult, especially if you get a bad ta
She sucks. I think I have been to this class 5 times as it is redundant and boring. I hate her theater etiquette and really wish she would stop, its embarrassing.
GREAT lecturer, very demanding in reading however

Great Prof., very well educated and very credible. Her methods were very unorthodox and she kept you on your toes.  She does tend to relate historical events to theater, but who wouldn't given her background?
OK professor. Quoted a lot of Shakespeare. Topics were interesting but her ability to communicate them effectively was mediocre.
weird...

Every day is the "Carol Symes Show". I've never had such a self-indulged, arrogant teacher. She tries to mask idiotic content with enthusiastic babble, and I find it endlessly annoying that she tried to read historical documents to the lecture class IN FOREIGN ACCENTS. I think my mom did the same thing when she was reading books to me when i was 3.
She demands a lot, but rewards hard work.  No tests in history 445.
self righteous and boastful.  Annoying and obnoxious.

I found her to be very interesting and enthusiastic about History, which made the class go by very quickly.  Although she talks very professionally, at other times she'll describe events and people in our own words.  Cursing and such is not a problem with her.
She thinks very highly of herself.  She knows history though and teaches with lots of enthusiasm.
No Comments

She's a militant feminist.  I think the only thing I learned in that class is that women have always been treated badly.  The class itself was informative, and the test where easy as long as you studied.

I enjoyed her lectures.  She is an extremely enthusiastic teacher, and speaks tons of languages.  She made it fun.  Make sure that you go to lecture and read the book.  She is the best professor I have had yet.

History with Carol Symes is definitely a journey...and if you don't mind listening to how Shakespeare relates to the early Egyptians, you'll love her class.  If you don't go to class, you're screwed, unless you can decipher the historical meaning of a slide of a Pope Urban action figure.

I never realized that everyting in history had to deal with the poor treatment of women until now. This was one of the worst history classes that I have taken, I cant say that I learned anything from her reciting the same dates over and over again for all of lecture

Symes knows a lot about theatre and a lot about history. The problem is that she tries to relate the two. I almost walked out of her Agincourt lecture because it was that stupid. She was explaning it courtesy of Henry V.

I enjoyed lectures not for material, but for her new costume everyday.  Gets really into drama.  Enjoyable to watch for her dramatic flair.  Textbook NOT WORTH THE $170.  Didn't even use it.  Study the slides and you'll be fine.
She is one of the most enthusiastic professors I've ever met, and she tried to infuse a lot of originality into the class.   Recommended.
okay I had a 9am with her, and its true, she loves history. but her teaching methods suck. she just reads off her slide show every day. you cannot stay awake.
She totally loves history and makes the classes excellent. Just don't take her 9 AM, because you want to go to these classes!
So hot!

Pat is very knowledgable about Calculus/ math in general and is MORE than willing to meet outside of class to help students understand. He is very personable as well. Tests are quite reasonable, homework is optional (except for 2-3 mandatory assignments), and Pat is pretty funny at times. There's really nothing negative to say. Pa was great.
Best math teacher ever!
Easy quizzes and tests.  But the class material itself is pretty difficult.  So be aware!
Made me lose all interest in a course that I was otherwise excited to take.  She is very disorganized and provides very vague feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: ruined my life
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Chaplin is very knowledgeable in LGBT+ history & one of THE best lecturers. However, throughout HIST 200, I found myself loving her course to absolutely despising. Dr. Chaplin is kind, and may offer support, but she is such a tough grader and assigns so many readings... even the smartest students in class expressed extreme levels of stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you are going to take one of her classes make sure you care about the subject or you will hate it. She is so passionate and engaging, she forces you to get to know your peers and fosters a great learning environment. She will push you and make you read, but she wants to see your best work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is an extremely tough grader who grades essays off of her own opinions. Meaning, if you do not agree with her, your grade will suffer for it. She assigned at least five books to read and at least three extras. She also assigned three movies to watch which you then had to write a reflection essay on. The class is extremely lecture heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Chaplin is really an amazing professor. Her lectures are incredibly engaging and she is very kind to her students. Her personality really does shine through in the best way and I was always so excited to attend her class, even if we had to move to zoom for that semester. I highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Chaplin.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I am a senior history major. Her history class is probably the hardest I had. Exam 1 was 50 minutes for six pages on zoom. Exam 2 was six pages, plus you have 5 more writing assignments I would recommend not taking her. Her workload is unnecessary to much writing, no multiple-choice questions.I wish I didnt take only B this class, no deans list.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: The amount of info covered in this course is extensive and Dr. Chaplin is not very good at pacing her lectures based off it. It felt like her lectures were all over the place and she's not a very flexible professor during these times. I think she made the class harder than it needed to be. If you're taking this for a gen ed requirement, don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Her lectures are interesting for the most part. There are some really boring lectures. In order to excel in this class, you're going to have to read the primary sources assigned each week and read the textbook. There are also >15 graded assignments. Get ready for a lot of writing. 98% of our assignments were writing assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Coming in as a Freshman I took two history classes and this one was by far my favorite. The lectures are great, and the work is not heavy based. Overall, the class is very well organized and its easy to get the hang of what is asked to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Graded by few things--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Chaplin comes across as extremely knowledgeable and understanding. The course assignments are well organized, not too much reading, even the text book is only extra credit. However, I recommend reading the textbook because most of her zoom lectures (having to cover such wide expanses of time) are very overarching and not as detailed.

Not even a history major, just took this class as an elective for fun. One of the most engaging/interesting lecturers I've had in college-- she made me want to come to class. You have to put in work and know your stuff to get good results, but she hand feeds you the information you need to know, so go to lecture.

Dr. Chaplin has single-handedly become my favorite professor I have ever had. She is extremely knowledgeable on modern French history and it is evident in her lively lectures. It is imperative that you come prepared by doing all of the readings and assignments for the class as participation is key for your success. Amazing professor and class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As a lecturer, she is good and she covers the content pretty well. However, the assigned reading is just too much. There are required textbook and primary source readings every week, but after the first month, I just stopped cause there was too much. There is also no place to see your grade since the TA does all the grading.

Honestly, the BEST professor I've encountered. I have had her for two different semesters now, and it's been thoroughly enjoyable. She expects a lot from her students so if you're looking to skimp through her class then maybe she's not the professor for you. Hilarious, engaging, CARING, honest. She will make you a better student.

EXCELLENT lecturer. The woman knows her stuff. Her personality can be a bit "edgy" but honestly, if you pay attention in class/really just aren't rude, you can cultivate a good rapport with her. I don't know if I'd like to have her in a discussion section, but as a speaker she's solid and you DEFINITELY will not regret attending her lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The exams are reasonable. If you attend class, you should be totally fine. Notes have to be taken by hand. Just a note though, if you're rude or annoy her in some way, she is not afraid to give you a taste of your own medicine (not my personal experience but my observation). In general, I would not take a class taught by this professor, again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Lectures were interesting. Waaay too much reading for a gen-ed 100 level class. Have to go to lectures because of pop quizzes, but they're not hard. She's a good professor who was able to keep students' attention.
Very good. Very fun. Knows her stuff

Professor Chaplin is one of my favorite professors at U of I so far. Even though her class was a gen-ed, she treated all of her students fairly and engaged everyone during discussions and lectures. The lectures were usually interesting and fun due to her stories and style of teaching.

The amount of reading is insane, but the class itself is intellectually amazing. You will learn so much, you won't know what to do with it all. Class discussions are stimulating and some of the most engaged and thoughtful I've experienced. Challenging, but rewarding, class.

Typical professor in a large lecture course. She wasn't the greatest and the reading expectation on top of the section readings were completely unnecessary. Class was easy, but lectures were not interesting and made mandatory by pop quizzes.

She is hard and very straight forward but she waits and works with you until you get your facts right. Or she'll be the one to encourage you if she's learning something new herself. Very attentive even in a huge lecture class of 300!

Dr. Chaplin is a wonderful professor. She cares so much about her students and wants them all to do well. She is quite demanding but in return she makes the material come alive in discussion. I would take any class for which Dr. Chaplin is the professor.

I took 140 last spring, and this is WAY better. Her syllabus/course is fair. Her lectures are really good and focus on one aspect of the time period rather than cramming it all in there. Shes very enthusiastic and passionate about her material. I recommend taking 142 w/ chaplin for your west. civ gen ed/requirement(if your hist major)
Knows her stuff. Kinda boring class but it's what you need to know about the subject

Professor Chaplin is a great teacher!I've only been in her class for a couple weeks.But she's great.She works with us, gets to know your name, leads great discussions & gets you involved in the discussion. And she def. seems like one of those teachers who actually cares.  She also explains everything that isn't understood & makes it seem personal.

This was my favorite elective in 4 years at UIUC. It is clear Professor Kasdan is here because he is (1) passionate about the topic and (2) interested in helping students. Having the opportunity to learn about media entrepreneurship from an actual entrepreneur was extremely valuable.

Mr. Terry is the literal best!! He made TE 200 such a joy and my favorite class. If I could take this course again I would in a heartbeat just to be in his class again. He is a fantastic teacher and such a remarkable, remarkable human being. I will forever be grateful to have had him as my teacher.
Project based class. TA's do the grading but he'll change ur grade if u ask nicely enough, great dude. Follow the rubric on assignments.

I had Professor Kasdan for TE 200 and he is the man! He always made class super fun and engaging! You will be working towards an idea for the IDEA Fair as a cumulative project and he is extremely helpful in giving you the guidance you need! I did not really consider myself an entrepreneur before the class, but I have changed my mind thanks to him!

I took TE 200 this semester. Professor Kasdan was always engaging and taught well. It always felt like he was very prepared for class and shared helpful and relevant information. If something came up he was also flexible about due dates when he could be. I recommend taking him.
I think Terry is a great professor. He also has a good amount of knowledge in entrepreneurship and teaches well.

Professor Kasdan allowed us as students to explore innovative, creative, and technical opportunities. I loved how group oriented this course was, and how willing Professor Kasdan was to share his experience, his expertise, and his mentorship.

Terry Kasdan is easily one of the best professors I've had at UIUC. I just finished taking ADV409 and I honestly can't recommend it enough. Professor Kasdan really cares about his students and makes an effort to get to know everyone. He's super encouraging and gives great feedback. A lot of 409 is focused on group work so try to get a good group!
I took TE200 because it's required for the innovation llc. The material is pretty easy but Professor Kasdan made it interesting. Like others say he's very caring and wants to see students succeed.

This course overall is pretty easy and Kasdan is a great if not inspired lecturer. He makes students feel at ease and creates a great environment but can't really inspire students (though this may be due to the dullness of the material). Overall though, he was very kind and genuinely interested in students which helped to make the course enjoyable.
Good professor

Professor Kasdan is one of the best instructors I have encountered at UIUC. He genuinely cares about his students and is very helpful and thorough in class discussions. This class is great due to its unique design and I believe it to be a phenomenal course that teaches entrepreneurship because we act as though we are entrepreneurs in the class.
This was one of my favorite classes at UIUC. This class is how every elective should go. Terry is a great professor and genuinely cares about students.
Professor Kasdan really cares about this class and his students and that shows each week in class.
This was an amazing class. Real life business experience taught by a successful entrepreneur. Also very engaging with students and wants to see us succeed. Id take this class again if I could!
Always open to helping students, very thorough with lectures, and gives enough time in class for the semester-long group project. Overall a great person and teacher!

Professor Tewksbury is now a professor at LMU and I had the privilege of taking him in my last semester here for CMST 3571. TAKE HIM!!! Even though class is lecture heavy, he is SO intelligent and you can tell he truly cares about his class and his students. He is so kind, funny, and gives such interesting lectures. I learned so much.

Really great professor. His passion for the material is clear, and he does a good job of keeping everything relevant and interesting. You definitely need to study for the tests and pay attention to the big concepts (some of which were introduced ONLY in discussionso go to that). Very understanding and accommodating overall to student concerns.

One of the best classes I have ever taken. Wonderful professor. He gives very specific examples and explains the materials very well. He is very nice and patient. Helped me a lot on the final paper. Definitely recommend his class.
Interesting lecturer- will never get out early. Spontaneous attendance. The tests are fairly easy- the final paper is very detailed and long-graded on the harder side. overall nice course
He´s an amazing teacher! Highly recommended class, but my TA was no good

Great teacher. You will really learn a lot from him. He's great to talk to and get to know as well. If you're a communication major interested in Media, this is a great class to take and a great professor to get to know!
very nice guy, knew his stuff. go to class and you'll be fine. you can tell he LIVES for teaching which is awesome.

Loved it. He's a very interesting and engaging lecturer, and he does a good job of keeping your attention. You can tell he's passionate about what he's teaching, and he makes the class interesting. Attendance is a must, but the book isn't necessary and the tests are all over your notes.
he's great
I really enjoyed this class.  He does a great job of explaining the material and overall the class was not that difficult.  Pay attention to the lectures and you will be fine.
Definitely take a class with Professor Tewksbury while you are at U of I. He is very enthusiastic about teaching, helpful and makes the material interesting.

This is definately not a blow off class. It's interesting material and he is very enthused about it but some of it is suprisingly hard to comprehend (and remember for the tests.) This class turned out to be not as interesting as I hoped it to be.

Ted is amazing. He makes the classroom and his office hours a safe space for sharing, and he pushes you to be better because he actually wants you to be better. He can be sardonic and harsh with feedback, but it's the best, most useful feedback you could get. Some assignments seem a little unnecessary or scary, but they prove to be helpful later.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Condescending toward certain students, making comments like "did you make that up off the top of your head?" "Thanks for your prepackaged comment". Feedback made no sense. I totally get that the purpose of workshop is to hear feedback (that's why I took it!) but one time another student made me visibly uncomfortable and he did nothing to step in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Didn't find his feedback helpful at all. He's also very sarcastic which I don't personally have an issue with but this could definitely rub people the wrong way. Class wasn't hard but I wouldn't take him again.
Great feedback. Honestly felt like my writing improved because of him. I'm not the best with deadlines but I felt myself wanting to be productive.

Ted Sanders is probably my favorite CW teachers I've had. He has a great sense of humor and is really great at critiquing work in a critical way because you know he really wants to help you improve your writing. He gives off an amazing atmosphereprobably the best one I've had in a workshop class. I would take another one of his classes again :)

Ted is someone who will treat you like an adult. He won't put on child gloves like some of the MFA students in the department do. He won't tell you what you want to hear, he'll tell you what you need to hear: the truth about your writing. If you want to get better, I recommend him. If you want to go nap in a bed of daisies, take someone else.

Ted is a rare combination of a brilliant writer and a brilliant teacher. He's brutally honest. He won't tell you what you want to hear and he has made kids cry in workshop. That being said, he's surprisingly approachable and super committed to making sure his students get better. If you are serious about writing, this class is invaluable.

i loved how his vibes were so chill. this class was based on 5 papers written periodically through out the semester. he grades honestly and provides constructive feedback. he always said don't write to please him, just to get the point across. one of my favorite teachers.
He was very laid back. Apparently he was a tough grader, but I never got anything lower than an 85 on my papers. I'd highly recommend him.

Cool guy I guess. Likes to swear in class, so he isn't like 90% of teachers/professors. But at the same time, his classes aren't easy. He grades tough. If you wanna do well, you have to write the way he wants it to be written. Listen closely in class and you should do okay. Also, he's lax on attendance but skipping alot will hurt ur grade in theend
He's an okay teacher. He's a little  low-brow for my tastes. I took the class so that I could have help with academic writing - instead we mostly do creative writing.
No Comments
While I wouldn't call him hard, he is a stickler when it comes to grading.  If you're looking for an A you'll be frustrated.  Easy to get a B however.  The class itself is uselss but required.
Yehya was the best TA I ever had because he taught me how to sign extend my registers. Would recommend this experience.
We making it out of Lebanon with this one!

Great TA who's clearly passionate about the course and brings contagious excitement to his students! He's very knowledgeable and his review sessions are incredibly helpful for studying before midterms. Very good speaker; inspirational, engaging, and (sometimes) funny. Truly a gem in the ECE department! Say hi if you see him at McDonald's :)

Amazing TA for ECE 120. He loves the class and goes out of his way to make sure students engage with the material and understand the topics. He runs a review session before each exam which covers everything you could expect to see and goes in depth on the thought process of problem solving. Very engaging lecturer and in 1 on 1 discussions

He is an awesome TA for ECE120. He is knowledgeable on every aspect of the course, and clearly very passionate about the content. He cares about each and every student and is willing to provide help all the time. Just don't pull your phone out during a midterm, or he might ask for your NetID.
certified top 10 professor in all of history!!!
Simply the goat

Dr. Barnes is so sweet and you can tell she really cares about her students. The assignments are really easy and as long as you talk a little in class she is very generous in her grading. The reading was also really light for a 300 level class. She is also super funny and flexible. 100% recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super supportive in giving feedback, interesting teaching style and materials. The lectures were easy to understand, I did not complete all the readings but they were all interesting and not tricky for getting a good grade. If you have any questions, no matter for this class or your personal life, talk to her!
Very sweet, makes material comprehensive
It's really easy to get an A in this class as long as you participate in the discussion and do the readings but there are only two books so it's pretty easy to stay caught up.
She's really sweet and funny. Respectful of how busy students are and takes that into account. She puts a lot of work into her lectures and knows a lot about gender and women's studies.

Professor Barnes is awesome. I was wary of taking this class as I don't love history but she makes it enjoyable. I learned a lot and I actually enjoyed going to class. She made sure to check in with her students and be supportive during the pandemic. Take prof. Barnes, it's really worth it. Weekly quiz, one long paper, points for class. NO EXAMS!!!

Professor Barnes was one of my favorite instructors this semester!! She was not only really personable and understanding, but she was also just a great teacher in general. She explained every subject matter in great length and provided tons of student resources for further understanding.

Prof. Telgarsky's ML class was one of the most engaging classes I've taken as a graduate student. His teaching style was great and he made it easy to understand dense mathematical material at a more intuitive level. He's also very patient and really seems to care about making sure he answers students' questions well.

His class doesn't use any slides or textbooks, he hand-writes while he teaches. He teaches well, answers students' questions, but he often forgets to upload the materials. Need some basic concepts of ML and math before taking it (lots of math!!!). 4 hws and 2 projects, but not a heavy workload.
His teaching approach is lacking, as he tends to avoid actual instruction in the classroom. However, he excels in identifying which studies and research areas are worth focusing on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not even his student yet but felt the need to rate based on online lectures. Matus is conscientious and has a great sense of humor. He is also emotionally intelligent, with a deep understanding of how students perceive the material in realtime. This, paired with his clear logical intelligence and passion for the subject, makes him a great teacher.
The teaching skill is really bad. The professor simply reads the slides and nothing more. Would not recommend. Try some other lecturers.

Don't know anyone who pays attention in this class (RUSS-122). Great and very interesting guy, but a disorganized lecturer. Professor is rather absent-minded and rambles quite a lot; so many tangents. Course is extremely confusing and lectures jump from point to point seemingly without reason.

This guy doesn't know how to use canvas, did not remind any student that midterm is coming in class or via email or canvas, grades homework very slow, can not remember student's name. He even forgot to grade my midterm 2 week after the mid term week

Very knowledgeable and passionate professor. This class had a great selection of books/movies to analyze and I definitely enjoyed it. Work per week varies quite greatly, but over the quarter you'll read 3 books, 1 play, and watch 5 movies, and write roughly 15 pages. If you have any interest in fiction whatsoever I would recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Tempest is one of my favorite professors, his lectures are really interesting and he's an expert in his field. Get to read a lot of great books and watch some really interesting films. Easy assignments and grading policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor is a really nice guy and the lectures can be interesting. However this class is simply not worth it due to the amount you have to write. Over the course of the semester it'll add up to 10-15 pages of writing about Russian topics you have no idea about. Only take this course if you can write long papers with ease and know about Russia.

DO NOT send him an email at the last minute - he checks his email maybe once a week. Also takes a while to grade papers. He is quite intelligent, but tends to ramble! If no one answers his questions - he will call on you. All in all a really nice guy!

Pros:  -accessible  -always answered any questions I had -shows interest in his field  Cons: -lectures are very dry.  -scatterbrained (has a tendency to go off on tangents) -doesn't use notes or any form of outline when he lectures, so it's very hard to follow.  -syllabus is virtually non-existent, so you're clueless a lot of the time.

Great guy. Rather absent-minded (couldn't follow the syllabus, use technology, or remember the time or his students' names). This was the easiest class I ever took, but I still learned a good amount (about a fun topic!)
Interesting, funny, tends to get off topic a lot and so I can't always follow him in class. Fair and an easy grader. Pleasant guy.
Looks like a mad scientist and is British. How can you go wrong?
Totally hot and a true genius!
Best Professor I've ever had or known.  He is first rate, a bona fide expert, and outstanding individual.  I'd recommend his courses to anyone serious about learning Russian or Bulgarian.

not a very hard course, only 2 take home exams and a term paper, plus one easy inclass presentation. i just skimmed the books the day i wrote the midterms and did a very small amount of research for the term paper. id suggest taking a class with him, especially if you know a lot about russian culture and literature

The best Russian professor EVER!  I still miss his class since taking it back in 1996 and I still read the books from his classes.  If anyone is thinking about taking his class, listen to me about him:  I thought he was arrogant and stupid before taking the class but afterwards found him to be the best! I truly regret not taking more of his classes
Awesome guy.  Love the hair.  He believes in studying pop culture, and knows how to make it very fun.  Great professor.  Take his classes.  Very fair grader.

Great, engaging lectures. I can tell she's really passionate about what she is teaching, however lectures can feel a little long at times. As long as you show up to class and take notes, the exams and assignments are pretty manageable.

Although I'm not done with the course, she has been a very enjoyable lecturer– probably one of the few ARTH professors that actually have me engaged to the content. She gives in-class assignments, which are super easy, and is very generous with extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class desperately needs discussion sections. The lectures are incredibly long and hard to follow, then she gets upset when nobody can answer the questions. It seems like she uses big words to make the topics seem more important, but it just makes the concepts more confusing. Had to reteach myself the material before the first exam.

she made me take my final online for half credit because I wasn't in person I remember her other past classes they got to take their final at home and I'm sure I'm going to get a D in this course. Her class sucks I feel bad for all the students who have to take her course since its mandatory

Terri Weissman is one of my favorite professors at university so far. She is so passionate and knowledgeable about Design History. She makes me excited to learn about the intricacies of design history. I love going to her lectures and I would recommend ARTH 211 to any design or history majors.

Her lectures are just her rambling about every little fact she loves about the artists and you are expected to remember these details. Extremely entitled and believes that the world revolves around her class. She has an attitude when you need any kind of accommodations and will make sure to give you a hard time before finally just agreeing. ick!

I don't see why a design student should be required to know everything about art history when they've got a shit ton of other things to worry about already. For someone who loves history, you will definitely get what you want from this class. For people who have been forced to take one of these history classes, it's just an insane amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her lectures are extremely boring, no logic and make no sense.
Tests are not hard, but definitely not easy either, Inspirational lectures, lecture notes are super important.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: After taking a few lecture based courses, I find her class the easiest to understand. Her materials are very structured and interesting at the same time. If you just attend and pay attention, you'll do great. Knowledgable and passionate, she is easily one of the best professors out there.

This was the coolest class ever! You make your own movies, which is so much easier than it looks. Class discussion was really fun and inspiring. I feel like I learned so much that I didn't even know I needed to learn. Also, the class was small, so we all got to know each other really well. If you can take this class, do it!!

Very amiable professor, you learn a lot of stuff in depth from her, all the examples she picked are very helpful as well. She gets mad at some students because they give no respect to the course. She even has made slides to some students according to their personal interest, you will like her!

Lectures are super boring, she is unhelpful and gets mad at students for not knowing the material that she doesn't teach well. She attempts to be eloquent but ends up confusing everyone. She likes to hear herself talk. She posts study guides 3 days before the exam expecting all students to do well on an exam that she scheduled on Reading Day.

No study guide was provided for the final exam unlike other sections, which is just one example of how unclear her expectations are. Grading rubrics are only provided after assignments have been graded primarily based on criteria not included in the actual instructions.

She answers nearly all questions with a blank stare and unhelpful responses.

Hands down the worst class I have ever taken. It amazes me how she makes the class completely impossible to comprehend even though she is the one who created it. She always says this class "requires a little bit of imagination" but then she has a set answer in mind and then will say "your imagination will be constrained".

Terrible, just terrible. First of all, the class is so boring because she does not know how to engage students (monotone). Second, her grading is completely unclear and she will tell us to 'use our judgement' but then expects one right answer. Very unhelpful when we ask questions, and she will not point you in the correct direction.

Arguably one of the worst professors that I've had here. She is the worst at engaging students and is not good at teaching students. She also has no patience for her students. I do not recommend taking her class.

The grading criteria are not clear. She didn't provide you feedback and still give you a low grade. You never know why you were deducted by so many points. She doesn't have much patience when replying to your email and you have to wait for like a month to get her feedback. If you have to take ACCY405, choose someone else!!
Very outdated class. Decent guy but very bad professor.

He was horrible at explaining any content. Lecture slides were mostly images as he'd just yap. When there were equations - there would be no explanation of what the equation was for or what the variables represented. He also doesn't provide all the necessary equations to solve problems.

The class average for the first exam was 44%, Stark decided that it would be funny if he invited a previous student who he had given an job offer to. Had the previous student explain why she loved geotechnical engineering and then preceded to laugh as he told the class that he would never extend an offer like that to us because we were incompetent.
DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH TIM, RUN FOR THE HILLS.

Given this was a sophmore level course, the reading was light and easy and I genuinely enjoyed going through modernist lit and poetry with him. I will also say that he puts up guardrails around the topic matter than ensure students stay in the moment and topic of the poems being analyzed, instead of going awry in their analysis of the pieces.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His grading albeit tough, has a clear explanation and allows students to improve their writing and comprehension provided they go to office hours and go over their papers with him. I would recommend paying the utmost attention to his lectures which practically give you the tools to write your paper and the different topics you can engage with.

He gives a lot of unsolicited advice but frames it in a way where you can't really say no to it. I enjoyed that he was outspoken about his political beliefs and makes sure that he's respectful of pronouns, etc. But his language is a bit outdated and comes across as racist, or ignorant at the very least. His handwriting is impossible to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The teacher is very strict! As a person with social anxiety, I did not like talking in front of the class. No participation accommodations were offered. Essays are heavily graded and you cannot read his handwriting at all. Be prepared to be called out in class if he assumes you are not paying attention (very humiliating). Attendance is strict too.

Literature is my passion, but I stopped attending classes halfway through the semester bc the prof was kinda racist, makes weird comments, singles you out all semester if you stand up for yourself. I was one of two Black people in the class and he called me by the other Black person's name. Loved writing the essays, but prof ruined the experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took ENGL 241. Professor Newcomb is easily one of the worst professors in the English department at UIUC. He's awful. He hardly teaches and refused to accommodate students with disabilities. If you try to get Disability involved, he will take his frustrations out when grading your papers and will make snide comments. I hated his class.
Made snide comments and class was boring/not well structured
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, fascinating class, I learned a great deal about film theory. I wanted to say however that he did not use trigger warnings before films, and there were a few with loud noise, shocking scenes, and uncomfortable topics that made me very uneasy. If you have anxiety or are disturbed by movies with heavy topics, think twice before taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed having this professor. He is clearly passionate about film, literature, and the arts in general. He has a great sense of humor, but he does not tolerate cellphone use/repeated tardiness in his class. He's pretty quirky, but an overall kind and efficient professor. We only had a handful of minor assignments and a few 4 page papers.

Coen brothers film class. He was very enthusiastic about the subject matter and fairly laid back and pleasant in contrast to the other reviews I'm seeing on here. He was more interested in having fruitful discussions than he was in being a punitive instructor or administering pop quizzes and lots of homework/readings. Flexible deadlines.

Yeah Professor Newcomb is definitely uppity and can be pretty mean at times. The prompts for his papers can be really convoluded and he's honestly only looking for a certain thesis an pretty specific supporting arguments. Overall there are multiple crude names that would be perfectly fitting for the dude.

Spends weeks on one topic, repeating lectures and material but spends one quarter of one class session on topics that make him uncomfortable or he does not find interesting. He is uppity, has low expectations of students and is passive aggressive, manifesting his anger/disappointment in assignments and offhand comments.

Horrible class- boring and repetitive.  Room was always freezing cold and the movies weren't interesting at all except JFK.  Teacher wasn't really willing to help.  I wouldn't recommend this class or teacher.

Great film class. Three papers, one final and attendance/participation. Not difficult since every other class was just a movie screening. Seems uppity at times, but just wants to see effort and participation in discussions.
Flaming ball of fire

I was a bit bored.  He did not have a good questioning style that created class participation.  We mostly sat and stared at each other.  I even started asking questions (of the class) one day because I couldn't stand just sitting there.   The texts were interesting, just not the way he presented them.  I did however like his use of Dr. Strangelove.
showed lots of fun clips in class
not bad class.  he teaches it well.  he makes it sound a lot harder than it is.   i didn't buy any of the books, and still got an A
pretty funny
Interesting class, he presents the material well.
No Comments
No Comments

This teacher "doesn't believe in academic inflation", so he just basically grades everything down 10-20% from what you could expect in any other course. The book is basically common sense and the lectures are really dull. If you have the choice to take it from somebody else, do it.
Tim is my favorite! Very interesting -- and incredibly hot!
Very strict teacher but as long as you do what he says, you will get nothing less than an A. He also is very helpful in office hours.
Awesome guy.  Really fun class.  He's kind of a hard grader, but he'll make you better at speaking.

Tim is my all time favorite teacher!!!  He gets his students, plus he's hilarious and makes class fun.  He's very clear about what he's looking for and how he grades.  Some people say he's strict, but if you do what he asks you'll be fine.

Lectures weren't mandatory, and it really didn't matter if you skipped because they're identical to slides. The exams are pretty easy, and most questions are straight from the slides. Professor Johnson is great, but lecture can be boring.
Tom is cool. He gives good lectures and the exams aren't super difficult. I learned a lot in his class.

Great class, the lectures are very informative and interesting and the amount of assignments and availability of extra credit make it easy to get a good grade in the class. The tests are somewhat difficult, but as long as you review the material beforehand they're rather straightforward. The professor is very accessible outside of class.

I thought natural disasters was really challenging because our grade is primarily based off of tests which I found to be rather impossible. And I truly did study for them, it's just I found the material a lot to grasp. Also for the essay everyone got C's and he was kind of unclear on why. Overall I didn't enjoy the class.
Good teacher.  Made class interesting and really cared about his students.  Overall good class.
Easy class, very understanding prof., subject material not difficult
nice professor, steady pace, easy grade

His accent is not hard to understand and his demos are fun. The information in the lectures isn't really new as he mostly just repeats the prelectures. Just go to the lectures for the bonus points (2.5%) and learn through homework and practice exams and you'll be fine. The labs and discussions are also easy as long as you pay attention.

The information in the lectures isn't really new as he mostly just repeats the prelectures. Just go to the lectures for the bonus points (2.5%) and learn through homework and practice exams and you'll be fine. The labs and discussions are also easy as long as you pay attention.

I would say save yourself some time and skip the lecture but it's apart of your grade. Prof. Relies too heavily on the lecture slides and iClicker questions (~80% of lecture is just iClicker questions).
He was just really unenthusaistic and hard to understand,   Scott was the GOAT tho IYKYK
Chill professor. Actually gives demos in class. Fun class.
as someone who had him for both Phys 211 and 214... he aint it fam. but you will survive.
Tsokaros has a very thick accent so his lectures are hard to understand. However, he is a nice person. Only did well since I knew most of the material from high school.

His accent was tough made it tough to understand what he was saying. Additionally, he never really explained the concepts well and relied more on the pre-lectures for you to understand the concepts. Went on parental leave during the middle of the semester and I learned more from the sub than from him.

This guy's accent was thick and difficult to understand, which didn't help that he taught things in the least intuitive way possible. I took mechanics in high school, so I tuned him out after the first couple of days. This class is tough if you haven't taken Physics C, but if you remember concepts from Physics C it is very manageable.

Although he has an accent and sometimes makes small mistakes with confused handwriting, he is a good person overall and has a good sense of humor. For this class most of the things you will learn with your TAs so try your best to pay attention in the discussion section

The professor was hard to understand with his accent, Stelzer was easier to understand and was much better explaining things. This class is easy if you took AP Physics, but you could get an A if you study hard and didn't take ap.

I really enjoyed Physics 211 with Professor Tsokaros. He is a kind man and a good lecturer. Some people say that he talks too quietly, but if you sit towards the middle or front of class, you will not have any trouble hearing him.

PHYS 211 all has the same grading but Tsokaros was a really bad lecturer. He is quiet and hard to understand through his accent. Just go to Stelzer's lectures, he is tenfold better. Nothing against Tsokaros as a person, but his lectures are complete dog shat. For PHYS 211 in general, it's pretty difficult since I didn't take AP Physics or PHYS 100.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: has an accent, but still pretty funny! got a standing ovulation at the end of the semester

had an accent which made it hard to understand him at times, lectures are not necessary but mandatory due to iClicker, labs were useless and usually ended an hour early for each one, discussion TA was really good this year, took this class twice and staying caught up with work is biggest piece of advice, try to complete homework on time
Generally good lectures, demonstrations are pretty great. Never confused on a concept leaving class.

Professor Tsokaros was cool. He takes the time to explain all physics concepts approached well so that everyone has the potential to go outside of lecture, complete the homework, and master the concepts. He also did super well with the in-class demonstrations and got a standing ovation at the last lecture of the semester.

Straightforward lecturer and makes sure to reiterate all the important topics you need to know for the exam. Super nice and very approachable. The class material is important for the MCAT, so it's nice that he makes the it easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Unlike many other MCB classes and really focuses on concepts rather than memorizing. A lot of information is taught, but you leave the class feeling like you have a good foundation in physiology and understand enough fundamental concepts to dive into more specific topics.
Highly recommend!
Covered the basics of physiology in an easy to understand manner.

I loved this class! I learned so much that involved my own body and life as well as others! This was one of my favorite MCB classes and it counts as an andanvced MCB course for anyone looking to get an extra 3 credit hours.
Very resposible
Great professor, makes his lectures easy to understand and explains concepts multiple times and in various different ways.

Professor Tsai has been one of my favorite professors at UIUC. His lectures are always very organized and interesting, and time passes quickly. He is great at explanations. He incorporates stories and descriptions in such a way that you actually remember the lecture material many days after class. He cares a lot about the success of his students.
record attendance by iClicker questions.
Few opportunities to get extra credit.

Priscilla had an extremely strong accent and was difficult to understand. She would constantly ask for discussion, although her lecture style left room for almost no space to talk, claiming what she said was correct regardless of whether or not you found a source that said otherwise. She brought some pot, pans and sticks for us to play on one day.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Took it FA2017 Have to admit that since this is her first semester ever of teaching, the course was a bit unorganized, but the material and the exams are rather easy, as long as you pay attention in class and discussion sections, do some work before exam (one midterm, one final), I have no music background whatsoever still easy A for everyone.

It's a shame that Prof. Tse's lectures were unorganized and unfocused, because the course material is actually quite interesting. Her guest performers were fun to watch, and some of her reading responses made you think critically. She's clearly knowledgable but has a hard time articulating her thoughts, and her exams were very easy.

You can evidently tell that she cannot speak English, demonstrating faint control over the class and the course material. The confusing lecture with esoteric readings might be the only resource you can resort to in order to deal with the next-level exam.

She seems like a nice person, but her teaching was rough. Her lectures were confusing and the readings were difficult to follow. The listening examples were hard for everyone, including those with musical backgrounds. It just seemed like no one knew what was going on or what was expected of them.

Not good. Demonstrated little control over the class, gave incredibly unorganized and un-detailed lectures, and never clearly explained course content or assignments. Did not seem prepared for lectures, or interested in being there. Nice woman, but should not be in charge of such a large class. Was recommended this class, severely disappointed.

Do not take anything she teaches. Her grading expectations are ridiculous, especially since she doesn't even teach anything in class. Half of the class is spent by her yelling at people to put their laptops away, or trying to get people to participate in a large lecture. She is not a good professor and tries to make the course hard on purpose.

This class is way more difficult than it needs to be, especially since so many people take it as a gen ed. She publicly calls people out in lecture for talking, yells at people for using laptops to take notes, and then tries to get people to participate in a large lecture. The lectures are boring, there is not a ton of graded material. Good luck.

Class is meant to be World Music, but you don't really spend time on music material. It should maybe be called World Performance instead, as that is the focus for a large part of the class. Little graded material, just 2 exams, 2 papers, 2 journals, and some extra credit. Weird iClicker questions. She's a nice lady, but poor course structure.

Easily the worst professor I've ever had. She got through about 5 of 20 lecture slides every week and her exams were terrible. For example, there were multiple questions that specifically ask for 2 examples of something. Then when we get them back we find out that she actually wanted 4 examples and didn't give any credit to those who gave 2 example

Anush is one of the best professors at UIUC! She always has clever ways to explain material and is super honest about how she understood things when she was a grad student. She also hates giving tests, so take an upper level grad class where she isn't forced to give them. The only hard part is homework, which you present and is graded by a TA

Prof. Tserunyan is an awesome lecturer. While every so often she may make a mistake in a proof, she always makes sure that everybody knows where the mistake was and what it was so as to clear up any confusion. She always brings a bit of humor to her lectures and is always open to questions.

Anush is likely the best lecturer I've ever had. She explains the motivation behind definitions and theorems, gives illustrations to help you understand new concepts and organizes things in a logical manner. She is very responsive to student questions and her deconfussion sessions are also helpful. Would take another class with her in a heartbeat!
Anush's class was an amazing introduction to logic. I feel like several new horizons have opened up. The problem sessions were a helpful addition to the course.

Anush is a very helpful and thoughtful instructor. She is willing to answer any questions you might have through email or in person. Homework is generally harder than what is tested. There are designated "deconfusion sessions" where you can come in and ask about any problem on the homework. Overall, I strongly reccommend her.
It was a nice class with Anush. She is just as awesome. Good researcher and good lecturer. Explains everything in a way that everyone in the class can follow her.
Amazing, she is one of the best lecturers I've ever seen.
Bad

WORST TEACHER EVER! She tries but is not a good teacher. Her section is much for difficult, much more intensive than all other sections. I feel that I'm not even in linear algebra. She writes very small and does't communicate what she is trying to say. She is too lazy to put up lecture notes or even give the answer key to practice problems. Avoid.
She is terrible, every comment on here is the truth. Doesnt even care about her students, avoid at all costs

Worest teacher!!!! I don't think she even understands that we have more than her classes. I feel like she explects us to be a mathematician on day 1. Don't just try to avoid her. Do avoid her. She is soooooo bad!!!!!!
By far the WORST professor I have ever had since attending U of I. I don't recommend her to anyone. Avoid her class unless you want to be tested on abstract linear algebra.
I saw my midterm grade was 60 and I wanted to suicide. Right before I did that, I found out that the average score was 56. Thanks Anush for saving my life.

Holy crap, this prof is worse than TA. Even i could teach better than her. No answer to homework or practice problem and the reason is she has no time to write, LMAO. Never care about students and no willing to help. Avoid it or welcome to hell.

AVOID THIS SECTION. She is the worst professor I have ever met in UIUC. There is no solution for any hand-in homework. Her lecture is boring and helpless. And the exam is hard and ridiculous. Also there is no solution for practice exam simply because she have no time to write it.

AVOID her class at all cost! Her explanations are extremely lost and it is very easy to get lost in her class. Less than half of the class attend her class and half of that are not even listening to her. Exams are ridiculous and there are no curves for individual exams. This is applied linear algebra, but she makes it seem so abstract.

IF YOU ARE CLEVER ENOUGH TO READ THIS, AVOID HER. Anush is certainly a smart and nice teacher, BUT she doesnt teaches her staff right. Her lectures are useless and boring. Her midterms dont relates on what the textbook materials. I haven't felt so bad about a math class in my life. Studying anything before midterms is useless for her classes. AVOID
It seems that she cares nothing about her students. Lectures go too fast and has no patience for answering questions. Try to avoid her as much as possible.

One of the worest professor. Classes go way too fast. Never pauses her class for questions. Lecture for 50 minutes straight. Unorganized blackboard writing and illegible letters. She thinks the average of the class grade should match the understanding of a person who is confused by the main concepts of this class. Who the hell does this?????
Does not care about teaching class, avoid.
Cares more about her research than teaching. I've learned more from searching Google than in lecture.
The class makes no sense until about the last two weeks. Lectures didn't relate to the work of the class. He is a really nice guy and is helpful if you go to him. Not an overly demanding class.

Textbook example of a professor who has all this great research but no teaching skills. Rarely stayed for class. And although the class name is "urban transportation planning," we focused more on crunching numbers than anything else, rendering the class useless for learning much of anything useful about transportation planning - NOT recommended.

Easiest class I have ever taken, but also the worst and most boring. I missed 3 questions on a quiz and still got 100%. Lectures are long and a waste of time. He can be difficult to understand and is never in the country. This class pushed me to change my major.
This is the easiest class ever, but the most boring one too. You will fall asleep during every lecture and be asked to esplain over and overe the most obvious points. Avoid it if you can.

I don't know what the guy before me was smoking but Kim is a jerk and a crappy teacher. He double scheduled my UP116 class and left his enept Research Assistant to teach it, which she did rather poorly. When he did come back he treated the whole class like high schoolers and was a bonafide ass.

Although the class isn't overly easy, he makes up for it by being extremely helpful and truly cares that everyone understands the material.  Very, very nice guy, too--can't help but like.  Would recommend this statistics class.

Honest opinion: she's unorganized, but it's an easy class to pass. She's not necessarily racist, but racism has affected her to extremes where she talks about racism a lot. I don't think I should pay for a class of where she lectures about racism and any off topic lecture, and not the actual topic at hand.

She is such an amazing human being.  She gave great insight into organizations and really does have a passion for what she lectures.  Class is easy and she is super understanding.  One of the best professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had this course my freshman year at the University. The course was not extremely easy, but as long as you communicated with her and showcased effort you did well. She also offered lots of opportunities to succeed in this course. I didn't do the best on every exam, but I ended with an A.

She does not often reply to emails, so if you missed something youll have to go to her in person. look at the canvas page frequently and remind her if something is locked and there are often multiple places u have to submit assignments because she struggles with organizing canvas.Attendance is not always required. But the workload was easy and fun!

Worst professor I ever had in my life. Tests were impossible and had nothing to do with what we learned in class, but she also showed clear favoritism to her students of color. One time she made all the Jews stand up in class ranked which of us looked the most Jewish. She also asked us if we celebrated thanksgiving implying that we weren't American
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is the typically archetype of nice person but terrible professor. She is a bit lazy regarding grading projects and assignments but the A shouldn't be hard if you are able to get on her good side. You learn a lot of stuff u can take outside of the classroom but a lot of the stuff on the test isn't taught in class. Attendance should be optional.

Pros: Dr. Wright-Dixon is a great person, teaches many things beyond the textbook, and makes you a better communicator, and if you want to, a more understanding person. Read textbook and do EC. Cons: The only downside to her class is that her lectures don't always match the textbook. Sometimes she takes a while to get grades in as well.

Trina is a very passionate teacher who seems to care a lot about the topics presented and students. However, I would not recommend taking one of her classes if you do not have to. Exams are written and based heavily on readings. If you take one of her classes do not expect any flexibility with late work as she can be very unforgiving.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: She kind of rushed the lectures and really got annoyed when people chose to not participate. The class was not graded by many things, and many of the exams and quizzes were mostly based on the readings. Her syllabus needed a lot corrections throughout the semester and she never responds to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice person but maybe not a good instructor. Took forever to reply emails. Exams were fine but had to be prepared to remember lots of things.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a good lecturer, bad customer service, never reply emails Funny class but incontinence

The worst course I've ever taken at a University. I just didn't learn anything from lectures. Calling this an "applied" course is a stretch. Lectures felt ill prepared and there wasn't very many parallels drawn to the real world. The exams felt VERY unfair. The grading was harsh and the questions were made to stump students.

Exams are very heavily based on textbook readings (which aren't specified, but multiple chapters that the exams could pull from). Much of class time is spent listening to stories about her life or waiting for her to put her phone away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Wright-Dixon was nice, but not a great teacher. She would tell personal stories a lot, and the material covered in lecture was a tiny portion of the exams. Exams were almost solely based on very lengthy readings, with the prompts being quite specific, making it difficult to study for, yet were the main portion of overall grade.

very hard grader, lectures for like 2 slides a class period, gets off topic super easily. her tests are fair but she is an incredibly tough grader on the written portion making it hard to get a decent grade.

I have taken 2 classes with Professor Wright-Dixon, both of which I enjoyed. She is very knowledgeable and compassionate. Lectures are very interactive. Come to every class prepared. She says everything for a reason. Pay close attention and do the work you are assigned. If you put in the work you will get a good grade.
In-class work is basically not a thing but read the book and youll be fine since youll be looking at lecture slides during class. Didnt really learn much from the slides so class wasnt great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class wasnt difficult but disappointed in how the class seemingly taught me very little about organizations and communication.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took her class without any information and she became my favorite professor! She uses her own experiences to discuss the materials and is hilariously funny. Students were busy raising their hands to answer. It wasn't to get her attention, but because they all ENJOYED the class! Attendance is mandatory, but you will love to be there.

Professor Wright-Dixon is one of the best professors I have had. She brings great energy to her lectures and deepens the knowledge of her students through interactive instruction. If you do the work you're expected to do and behave respectfully, you will be fine. I strongly recommend taking one of her classes.(:

Lectures are vague, uses the book but doesnt utilize in class much, usually on phone during class time, microaggressions towards students, expects students not to form assumptions yet she does, can be very passive aggressive, class allowed students to learn more than surface stuff about each other but failed to connect course content at times
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor I have ever had in the Communication department. Wasn't afraid to discuss hard topics and really cares for her students. Her office is literally always open and the most helpful professor I ever had- even outside of the classroom. There were 2 projects and exams were easy.

Lecture videos + Homework tutorials mean listening to this prof's voice for 3+ hours a week outside of class. I can't stand listening to his voice anymore. I feel like I haven't learned much because of the pace of the class. Thought that this class was meant for the library students, but I still don't know how to use it in such context.

Trainor is an amazing professor. The workload is a nightmare in the summer, and he didn't have a TA so no assignments were graded in a timely fashion, but he makes himself available like no other prof I've had. He holds optional labs, which you should attend. He's empathetic and truly wants all of his students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy
