reviews.comment: Kevin Trainor is one of the best programming instructors I've ever had. He puts a ton of work into his course materials (recordings, lectures, homework assignments). His class may seem dry at first, but it's only because he is incredibly thorough. Everything he includes in the course ensures that students are prepared for the assignments.

Trainor is incredibly thorough with this directions and assignments. You can tell he's taught the course many times. It was not the most exciting class but I learned a lot and now feel capable of working through simple programming problems. Take his class if you want to learn Python or practice your skills!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor. I struggled at the beginning of the semester but once I figured out what worked for me (watching his YouTube lectures pretty closely at 2x speed--guy talks very slowly!!) I learned so much and felt so accomplished by the end of the semester. He provides a ton of feedback and resources, really seems invested in his students.

I absolutely love Kevin and would recommend him to anyone in School with an interest in coding. His course IS430 is a good starting point for you to learn Python as a rookie, though the course is a bit shallow. IS439 is an excellent course you should not miss! Kevin is very niceand is extremely good at explaining ideas in a very lucid way.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: DO. NOT. TAKE. THIS. CLASS. This was the biggest waste of money. You essentially teach yourself via his YouTube lectures and things you have to find online. Seriously, I learned more from random YouTube people than I did in the class. When you have trouble, he's zero help. He's nice, but a terrible professor.
I had a good time in his classes, they were difficult but interesting. He isn't at UIUC though, he is at Notre Dame as of the present time, (October 2025).

It's a great capstone course for those who care, but at the same time it's terrible for people who do care because of the tendency of many others to not care. I pushed my group and developed the team skills I never got before this class.

He tries to be helpful but is very unclear. He confuses vagueness for open-endedness, giving no useful guidelines other than formatting rules. CHBE 431 is poorly paced causing some learning to be wasted and multiple assignments to be due at the same time (unnecessarily). One of the only engineering design courses to not involve corporate advisers

The class may be the most time you ever spend on class. Luckily the professor is often very clear on what he expects and is always willing to help after or outside of class. Class is not mandatory and notes are online, but contain gaps that are filled in only in class. Professor is big on class interaction, which helps learning significantly.

One of the coolest professors I've had so far. Super encouraging and showed that he really cared about the success of his students. Always played music at the beginning of class, did demonstrations, and was really hilarious and engaging. Highly recommend taking his class.
He made the iClicker and IOLab that you have to buy for the course.

Great lectures, funny, great demos. Not on canvas, there's a course website. Decent amount of work with prelectures, checkpoints, iclicker attendance in lectures, and homework, all twice a week for each topic, but helpful. Some lectures are basic but if you put in the work, won't be hard to get at least a B+

Tim Stelzer is a really good lecturer with easy explanations and demonstrations. I just unfavor the course material because it does not reach the root of things. But he elaborates on it and gives us more grasp. If you want to get more out of physics, you can use Kleppner's book Introduction to Mechanics too.

Professor Stelzer was a great lecturer who frequently reviewed student feedback and built lectures around the pre-lectures, using experiments to demonstrate principles. He offered plenty of iClicker bonus points. TAs were very helpful. Labs felt unnecessary to me. Exams were somewhat challenging but similar to practice tests. Highly recommend him.

He's awesome. He's always energetic, funny, engages the students, and is ready to a put a show for you in lecture. There's always a demo in lecture, and is decent at explaining the concepts. The one thing is that (like all other PHYS 211 lectures), you need to participate in the iClicker questions to get attendance credit.
Professor Stelzer's lectures are really fun, and help to give an intuitive understand of Physics. I was able to learn a lot more here than by just doing theory at high school!

His lectures are exactly how all lectures should be. He's happy to answer all questions, and takes feedback from the prelectures.  Amazing prof, and definitely makes the difficulty of the class bearable.

Stelzer is a great and engaging professor and he's great at helping students with classes. Not a gripe with him but PHYS 211's grading scale has decently higher percentages than standardly used for each letter grade, which is odd.

The best professor I've had at UIUC. Tim is a phenomenal lecturer, and he is able to consistently explain topics in a way that is easy for students to understand. He is also extremely nice, and cares about each and every student. We love Tim Stelzer.
Great professor who had profound insights in the contents of the course, lectures were always clear, concise and greatly helped in completing the homework/labs/discussion quizzes.
Stelzer is a great lecturer, and you can tell he has a lot of fun. His demos are always great, and he explains the material well.
Very responsive to feedback from students, actively addresses questions sent in during the prelecture during actual lecture. The demonstrations during lecture were very helpful and also fun to watch.

Best lecturer I've had yet, I'd legitimately wake up on time to make it just to physics and then go right back to bed. Incredibly engaging and a great teacher. Curriculum is structured great as a whole. Biggest issue is that you need a physical iclicker but honestly I fully get it you should be paying full attention in his classes.

The professor is goated but the audience is just not it. The in-lecture experiments really intrigued me but there wasn't as much hype or applauds as I expected, which is why he gradually lost enthusiasm in the end of the semester. If you're taking his lecture in the future, please cheer this poor guy up, his efforts really need yall's appreciation!

Professor Stelzer is the best professor I've had at UIUC. He prioritizes his students and has a great teaching style. His exams are almost a copy of the practice exams and the bonus points from lectures boost your grade at least 3%. Try for discussion quizzes, but labs are useless. Minimal effort still secures a 100% in Labs. Overall the best class

Great teacher and guy, seems to really care about his students. Midterms are pretty similar to homework problems, and you get bonus points from iClicker questions. Beware, he curves down so an 83% is a C+ and an 80% is a C in his class.
He was super engaging and passionate about the material. I had already taken this class in high school, so I can't really say how it would be learning it for the first time.
This guy sucks. His video explanations for exam review do not match with what he is writing. In addition he skips many steps.
Taught the material well, I learned much more than I had in high school. Is interactive with his students when it comes to demos or asking questions. Very likeable overall. Exams are not too bad.
Prof. Stelzer explains things really well and is overall great, the only thing is that he does not allow laptops in his lecture which is absolutely ridiculous.

Great professor, makes jokes to keep us engaged, and demonstrates concepts through real-life examples. Very engaging class and very helpful. Lectures and pre-lectures are basically the same, so just go through them before exams.
he is the goat. Goated. Take if applicable or possible. Very engaging Lectures!

Came in with little physics background. Professor Stelzer gives good and engaging lectures, and you can tell he is passionate about both physics and his students. Course can take up a lot of time, but the tools are there for anyone to find success in this class as long as they put in the work which is how it should be.
obviously very passionate about teaching, does a very good job of explaining difficult topics, and overall seems like a nice guy.

Very good professor. Hilarious guy, very entertaining lectures, cool demonstrations. Watch the prelectures until the material makes sense. Homework is fairly representative of the midterms, provides lots of review material for all exams.
Prof. Stelzer keeps the lectures engaging with demos. Tests are challenging, but the workload is manageable. Using unstuck AI alongside the textbook helped me prepare effectively for this class.

Stelzer's lectures are clear and easy to follow, and he has some entertaining demos. PHYS211 is time-consuming in general and can be difficult, but Stelzer is a great lecturer. Exam curves/grades were pretty lenient. iClicker participation in lecture helps, and Stelzer gives thorough explanations for the poll answers.

One of the best professors ever. He taught lectures incredibly well, and even though the exams and content were hard, he cared about us as students and as human beings. Always set a good tone in class, I HIGHLY recommend you try to get this professor for a class.

Even though I don't like physics, Stelzer made the lectures entertaining. He's great at making students feel involved and engaged in lecture activities. The class has a good amount of homework, but it gives you good practice to understand the material. In my opinion, the labs were unenjoyable and boring, but they boosted your grade.

Steltzer is a good physics professor with a great sense of humor and makes his lectures interesting with demonstrations. Attendance is mandatory with the iClicker, but I found it insightful. Completing the pre-lectures is also very helpful to your performance in class, so pay attention to them.
Hilarious and super laid-back professor. Lectures are mandatory but enjoyable. Tests are tough but workload is manageable and easy to understand.

Professor Stelzer is an incredibly kind man and a great teacher. He truly shows that he cares about his students and answers questions well. His lectures are very informative and entertaining with great demonstrations. The class can be a little challenging at times but is graded very fairly.

Fairly experienced in his craft, his lectures are engaging and he often does lots of crazy demos.  He knows his stuff and is very approachable, but in the day and age when everyone's phones have accelerometers and can cast votes, he still makes all students purchase his own inventions (iOlab, iClicker, homework website) that do those same tasks.
Tim is awesome. Go to his lectures. He's super cool to talk to. He's like an awesome dad.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you have the chance to take one of his classes, do it. He is an amazing lecturer, a very caring man, and is absolutely hilarious.

this course is set up to be graded super fairly thanks to king tim stelzer. very homework heavy, but drills the information into your head. i thought physics was the worst but tim is the best. i want to hug him he played the beatles before lectures and threw footballs up the loomis lecture hall. only love for tim

Fantastic professor, extremely engaging and very helpful, especially out of class. Very entertaining lectures. He made physics interesting for my class, and help us all learn how to be better physicists.
nice guy and nice lecture, exam difficulty is about average, can always get a nice score if works hard.
He's very funny and engaging and includes students in demos. Really enjoyed his 211 class

Professor Stelzer was the best professor I've ever had here. My whole lecture class gave him a standing ovation after his last lecture. He explains the concepts perfectly, he is hilarious, he is often available to help, and he is passionate about teaching. The course itself wasn't perfectly crafted, but his lectures are awesome.

I hate physics and the way this class is set up. He's a nice guy but I would prefer if we were lectured during the actual lecture times instead of learning through stupid, extremely fast-paced, 2 min prefecture videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Stelzer is an amazing professor. His lectures are fun, informative, interactive, and he provides really useful tips that you can't get from the prelectures. He really knows his stuff. The course is extremely well-organized and everything is always clear and well-defined. Highly recommended.
Steltzer is good and wants you to succeed but Physics 212 wants you to fail with everything in its soul.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Such an awesome professor! Thank you, Professor for such a great introduction to physics at UIUC. He made a semester with unfavorable online circumstances fun with the synchronous lectures. Pay attention in lecture and take notes, he explains concepts really well. The TAs were super helpful as well.
Fabulous guy, lectures are so great that I didn't need the textbook.
Very kind and caring professor. Made class enjoyable.

Amazing lecturer! Seriously my favorite Professor Ive had so far, makes me glad I chose physics as a major and really makes you enjoy doing the work. This is my 3rd or 4th time taking mechanics, and I thought I knew just about everything to know, but Professor Stelzer really adds depth to the material that really enriches your understanding!

It's just my second semester, but Stelzer is definitely my favorite professor so far. He makes the lectures as engaging as possible, which in a world where many professors just drone on monotonously and make me zone out, is fantastic.
I really enjoyed taking 212 with Stelzer, he really seems to enjoy teaching it, and lectures were always fun

The class is a lot of work with no extra credit, it's very test heavy as well, but labs are almost free points if you're careful, and the practice tests are extremely helpful. Stelzer is one of the most kind and caring profs I've ever had, you can tell he really loves teaching and physics. Incredibly motivated to help, all around 10/10 human being.
great lecturer, discussions and HW not too difficult or long, easy lab grading, most of grade determined by multiple choice exams, very helpful practice exams provided
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Amazing lectures--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is fantastic. Best professor I had this semester. He is a rare combination of knowledgeable and caring. The content is challenging at times but he makes learning it enjoyable.

He is awesome, very chill dude and teaches his lectures in the funniest ways. Effective but the class itself is fast-paced, so you have to keep up outside of lecture. He gives you good opportunities to do well but it's really up to the student to stay focused.
Stelzer is an absolutely incredible professor who makes each lecture feel exciting and engaging (even over zoom!) to the point where I looked forward to physics lecture every week.
Loved his lectures! He made me attend all the lectures, without any sign of fatigue or rush. Kept the class entertaining.

Tim Stelzer is an absolute physics unit. He did amazing lectures this year over zoom (covid time) and seems to really enjoy what he does. Prerecorded experiments and overall I had a really good experience in his class.

Dr. Stelzer is an amazing lecturer. I took this class during COVID and even with the lectures being all online he and his team worked really hard to encourage participation and to assure that we had the tools needed to succeed. We would regularly fill out surveys as to how the course was going and changes were made to make the climate better.

He is passionate about physics, and sharing his knowledge to his students. He is always open to answering questions and is genuinely interested in his students' success. He wants you to do well. The course is pretty hard to get an A, but he makes it interesting.
Great professor. He did a great job in making the lectures enjoyable.

Prof. Stelzer's a real G. He's extremely motivating and caring, knows his material, and an all-round nice guy. And funny. Would definitely want him to teach me physics for the better part of 4 years here.

Stelzer is a great professor whose lectures are a joy to attend due to his in-depth knowledge and light-hearted humor. Stelzer answers each and every question he receives with enthusiasm and respect. When classes moved online due to COVID-19, Stelzer made sure to take time out of lecture to give us much needed encouragement and support. Solid dude.

Probably one of the best professors at this university. He cares a lot, his grading is clear, his lectures are entertaining. His classes are not the easiest, but if you put the work in, you should be able to get an A.
Honestly I hated PHYS 211 but he makes the content less daunting and is extremely amusing. 10/10 would recommend.
A very knowledgeable man, with the best teaching ethic I have ever seen. Also, absolute mad lad when it comes to making the best jokes during lecture.
Great guy, excellent professor, amazing lecturer
Great lecturer, listen and do the practice tests and you'll succeed

An amazing prof with amazing lectures. Cared a lot, had amazing demos, the exams were fair, and the class was really well run. The only problem was that the class size was very large and people liked to talk loud enough that you couldn't hear him on occasion, but he usually managed to quiet those people down. Hands down the best prof at UIUC.
Hes the best

A really great guy and professor. He takes what is a difficult subject and makes it so much easier to learn. You can tell he values each student. The entire set up of this class is so helpful. It's a class where you get what you give. What ever grade you earn is truly what you deserve and reflects what you know.

E&M is a difficult subject, but Tim made it so much easier and much more enjoyable. He's hilarious, gives awesome lectures, and clearly cares about his students. I wish I could take another class of his because they're absolutely amazing. There is a lot of work involved and it's not an easy class, but it's doable & it's very much worth.

Stelzer is honestly one of the best professors I've had so far. He's so kind, sarcastic and that is what makes his lectures awesome. He's super passionate about physics and one of the inventors of the iClicker. Such an inspirational person. I recommend him for ANY physics course ever.
I second what the rest of the people say about him. He's amazing.

Prof Stelzer is an absolutely great guy. His lectures are so funny and he is so passionate and witty that he makes you like the material too. sometimes professors make you feel dumb for not understanding the material but he is so supportive and easy to talk to

This professor specializes in physics education research and it shows. The lectures are very well thought out, evenly paced, and seem extremely well rehearsed without feeling scripted. The grading for the course is all right with B's being common. The professor does make an effort to reach out to individuals, but the sections are very very large.
Stelzer made lecture fun and the material very approachable, I mostly learned from taking practice exams, but his lectures helped a lot too.

AWESOME PROFESSOR! This is the first time I've ever enjoyed a lecture. Professor Stelzer is passionate about his subject, and great at simplifying complex concepts. He also uses tons of demonstrations which are actually really interesting. Would definitely recommend!
Awesome professor! He is really passionate about his subject and an AMAZING LECTURER. Would definitely recommend!

Really awesome professorthis is the first lecture in my life I have ever enjoyed. Mr. Stelzer uses a lot of examples, analogies and step by step explanations to make really complex concepts easy to understand.
Great teaching skills and brilliant at answering questions
A great professor!!

Really nice professor, he really wants the best for you. He teaches well, but sometimes it felt like I learned how to take test/do homework, not the concepts themselves. Test were tricky, but if you try on homework, labs, and quiz's you should be fine.
Stelzer is a fun professor and his lectures are always interesting. The grading scale makes it harder to get a B, so watch out.

Prof. Stelzer seems to be involved in a lot of research regarding the best methods to teach undergraduate courses. You can tell that he really cares about how his students are doing because his lectures affect his research as well. He makes himself incredibly personable in a 300 person lecture hall, and I always loved going to his lectures!
Fun lectures, understands the student's point of view, made me glad that I took the class
Even though the class was difficult, he makes everything sound very interesting and really puts a lot of effort into making lectures fun.
Really good teacher, makes class fun.

Stelzer is awesome! I thought the class was well organized and very reasonably graded. Lots of cool material, useful lectures, neat demos! He really cares about the class so it doesn't feel so impersonal in such a huge lecture.

I thought the class was pretty difficult, but honestly so many people have so many differing opinions on it that it can go any way for you. You either think its easy, or you really have to work for a good grade. Stelzer himself is the man - hilarious, good presenter, makes plenty of connections to applications, awesome demos. Lots of fun!
awesome professor
Funny professor, and he teaches great.
Amazing professor, clears all the concepts very well in class and a plus point he is really funny

This class was hard. If you are good at physics, you should be okay. However, the teaching method used wasn't helpful. Professor seemed to care for students but I found this class confusing and annoying. I've taken four physics classes at UIUC, so far they have been pretty dull, boring and confusing. Department should probably change things up.

Amazing lecturer and very good at answering questions even though he does it with a very subtle sarcastic attitude that is humorous if you catch it.  Uses lots of good props and in class examples to show how the physics works.  Tests are tough but you have a pretty clear idea of what you are about to get into from the practice exams.
Don't take physics here- hard and boring. Professor was decent at explaining, pretty good at office hours but that doesn't make up for the way the class was comprised.

I personally didn't like this class, tests were hard but the homework was doable. If you give this class time, you could do well. However, having taken several physics classes here with a similar teaching method, you'll end up struggling. Wouldn't recommend unless you have to take this class.

Class was hard. Didn't like the way the class was taught, but there was some easy grades like labs. However, I found myself lost a lot of the time, tests were unfair at times. The physics classes I've taken here so far have been questionable to say the least. Get a tutor or don't take physics at this school

Don't take this class. In fact, avoid physics at UIUC, they don't know what they are doing. Tests are unnecessarily hard, labs tedious, homework unhelpful and lectures boring. This department needs reworking asap. Take this class at a community college.
Nice guy, but can't teach. Class was a mess, most people taught themselves physics. A lot of complaints about the physics department/program this year. Can't say I'm surprised. Buyer beware.

This dude is the bomb.  The lectures are a lot like what you got from 211, but his delivery is really clear and he's a really charming professor.  The course itself is a natural progression in difficulty from 211, so no big deal there.  At least for 211 and 212 so far, the physics department really has it together.

Decent guy, but can't teach. Lectures were extremely boring and unhelpful if not confusing. The midterms and final were very hard. Prelectures/checkpoints are useless, lectures were confusing, and homework hard. Ended up teaching myself. The UIUC physics department should be very disappointed; the physics program itself has been a let down.
Lectures were boring and he often confused himself. Homework took forever, tests are doable, some hard.
One of my all time favorites
Best prof I've had in the physics department. He's great at explaining things and is really funny.

His lectures are typically clear and somewhat helpful. Most of the learning is done through smartphysics, but he often can clear up confusing topics in lecture. He is genuinely interested in his students despite the fact that it is a large lecture and will respond to your needs if you have questions or any problems.
He is very enthusiastic about teaching, always make sure you understand the materials. He made physics easy for us, I felt sooooo lucky to have him as my phys212 professor.
Great teacher, very clear about everything and spends the first 5 minutes of class trying to clear up confusion with the material.

Super funny guy, i love him. Good teacher too. He actually knows how to teach. In lecture, there might be some things you dont completely understand, but if you go to him afterwards, he will be great at explaining it face to face. Real tough course but hes a super helpful guy. You gotta study hard, hrs of homework, and ask him questions after class
If you attend lectures and actually put in effort the class isn't too hard. He's interactive in his lectures, and makes jokes. He genuinely wants to help and is able to do so effectively.

His lectures were pretty interesting. He tried to ensure that everyone understood the material. He always thanked his students for asking questions, and I liked that. He also made jokes which I personally thought were very funny. Exams were fairly easy. Labs were extremely tedious, but that's not his fault. Attend his lectures if possible!

Great professor.  I would recommend him over all other lecturers for this class.  He is nice and really goes out of his way to make sure students understand.  Exams are very thorough but pretty straight forward.
Funny, entertaining and super helpful. Highly recommend him.

He is probably the best professor I have ever met. Super awesome guy. I had credit for PHYS212 before the class but he was too good so I didn't drop it. Lectures are engaging and well-organized. Exams difficulty are just right. Homework and pre-lectures are pretty helpful, discussion too. Labs were annoying, but all labs are annoying so whatever.

He was an amazing teacher, with dry humor, and fantastic demos. He really made the lectures interesting; they just flew by. So great!! And his grading is fair, and his iclicker bonus points save you a whole lot!

Without a doubt the best professor I have had thus far. Makes very difficult material easy somehow. The work he and his colleagues have done with physics education is incredible and absolutely works. I would certainly gotten a worse grade in E&M with a less talented professor. Highest recommendations for Stelzer.

Tim Stelzer is great! He is funny, does cool demos, loves to teach, and likes talking to people. Phys 212 can be a little rough for some people because there's more "imagination" involved, but like other Physics courses here, if you do the practice exams you should be fine.
Great professor.  Highly recommend him.  Makes lecture fun. Demos are cool and he makes jokes during class.

Great techer, you can tell he actually cares about his students. The only thing is that he makes things seem so easy in class and it can be frustrating when you're doing things on your own that you realize are actually hard.

TRULY OUTSTANDING!! He is so funny and really gets a lot across to you. Not a single complaint. Quizzes is what got me, stay on it. Demos really shine. Highly recommend Stelzer, I also had Mats for a few times and he is also super good. Cannot go wrong.

This guy is really cool and you can tell he wants his students to learn, however he also makes a lot of comments about how easy and simple the stuff is even though I struggle with it a lot which is really frustrating.  Go to his office hours and introduce yourself if you're having trouble and he'll try to help.

He's soooo much fun! Humor and teaching mixed to perfection. This class is hard because of the exams, so theres nothing you can do about that, but if you have to take it, you'll learn the most from him!

Stelzer was a really great teacher, very interesting and a good lecturer. However, I didnt anticipate HOW INCREDIBLY TOUGH the tests would be and I completely FAILED the first one. But with enough work and effort I was able to end up with a B in the class (thank goodness). A lot of work altogether, so keep up on it or you will suffer.

Stelzer is a really funny guy who is also pretty brilliant.  Great at teaching and explaining, exams weren't too bad either.  Lectures are the bomb since he always has some sort of sweet demo and has the class laughing with his physics jokes. I would highly recommend him.
Great professor, knows what he is talking about and does cool demos.

Great professor. Great sense of humor, charismatic, makes class fun. Required you to "get to know" your neighbor. He often went in the nosebleed section and chatted with students before class. Great taste in music. You can tell physics is his passion. He's a great dynamic teacher, always striving to help and doesn't put you to sleep.

Great guy. Likes to joke around. Explained things well. Exams were difficult. I'm probably biased since I don't like physics but if I were to choose a professor to teach me physics it would be him. I see him riding his bike around campus all the time :)
Really good at explaining the material and keeping your attention, really funny and down to earth guy.  Class was easy to sit through and funny.

He is hilarious! I really enjoyed going to lecture because I knew he'd be entertaining every day. He's also a very good professor in that he is passionate about his subject. The class is tough, but get him for lecture if you can.

practice exams definitely help on the hour exams. He is better than the other phys 211 lecturer so get him if you can. he does so many fun demos and has good jokes! however, if you're not a physics person, you def. need to study harder to get an A.

Very clear and passionate about physics.  This is a true american professor who knows what he is talking about and wants to share his knowledge with others.  I have never had a more interesting professor.

T-Dawg is awesome! Very entertaining and great at teaching. Normally it sucks when some of your grade is based on attending class, but his lectures are the bomb so it doesn't matter. I recommend him to anyone. Thanks for a great semester Stelzer!
Amazing, fun, helpful, awesome, easy

Great professor. He is very funny in class, which makes his lecture great to attend. The material is kinda tough at times, but the exams are very fair. There are many years of practice exams online, and if you do all of those, getting at least a B will be VERY EASY.

Stelzer is a great teacher and one of the funniest professors you'll have, but I don't have a physics kind of mind, and the class was just insanely difficult for me. Homework would take hours, and the tests were very difficult. Since there's not textbook, you're really going to have to do the practice exam questions in preparation for the tests.
T-dawg is the man! He's definitely one of the best professors in the physics dept. He can somehow make you excited and learn about physics. He genuinely seems to want you to learn. He's awesome.

The professor is fantastic. He makes every lecture fun and interesting, however the class is HARD, especially if you didn't have a decent physics class in high school. Exams are tough and there's NO CURVE. Labs however are pretty straight forward and are a good grade booster. Homework can be tough but its doable.
Awesome lecturer. He keeps you interested with demonstrations and humor. The class is difficult but he does an excellent job explaining concepts and giving examples.
Great lecturer, explains well, keeps you interested, pretty normal guy. Also, he has a funny subtle humor.
Amusing lecturer. There's no reason to avoid this professor.
Great prof for 101, not so good for 212.

Great lecturer, quick to reply with emails and is very helpful. Makes great jokes. Tests are pretty easy if you go to discussion section and understand/do well on the quizzes. Do the homework yourself or you will fall behind.
Very fun and entertaining.  Class is fair.
Stelzer was a really good professor... his tests were extremely hard for me, but lectures were interesting because of demos.  And he gives out cookies.
Totally disconnected from class outside of lecture, TAs do everything and make impossible quizzes. Weekly difficult online homework, class is not curved.
Best Professor.  Going to class is enjoyable and he is very helpful.  Try hard at discussion, work on homework, attend class- you'll do fine!
I can't say enough good things about this guy.  This was the first class I've actually looked forward to going to here.
Hilarious, best lecturer I have ever had. Tests are somewhat difficult though.
Easy class but lot of work. Go to class, have a good time, work in discussions, do your hw, go to lab, and you'll get an A- easily.

I LOVE PROFESSOR STELZER!!!  He is an amazing teacher and he makes me laugh every time I go to class.  He explains things very clearly.  He is so funny and I would probably marry him if he wasn't 20 years older than me because he's so funny.  HAHA.  Just kidding.  But he is awesome!
Amazing, enthusiastic, helpful, hilarious, easy going, makes physics the most fun class EVER
Without a doubt, the best professor I have EVER had!  His is honestly the only lecture I have ever tried to make it to.
he's awesome! really nice , fun and sweet, and very approachable when you need help. tests are hard though, but that's to be expected. he rocks for giving out cookies in lecture! :)
He was my fav teacher.  Very nice, Very funny, and never made you feel dumb for asking questions.
Lecture was like pulling teeth.  Did well in class and missed next grade cutoff by 2 points...The guy won't review my stuff or give me a chance to get those 2 points, what BS
Absolute best teacher I have had at Illinois.  Even makes people want to go to class.  No other prof can do that for me.  Should teach 102 also.
Great teacher, makes class fun.  It's Phys101, so not that easy for some
Funny, nice guy - makes class fun to go to
nice and funny professor, interesting class (always has demonstrations to show)
great class
No Comments
No Comments
Good job, highly recommend

Did not come to class prepared, did not even read the slides she was to be presenting that day in many cases. Would dock points on assignments for things that were not in the assignment description and she had never given feedback before. Culturally insensitive on multiple occasions. Alienating students when they ask questions.

Didn't come to class prepared, often did not review material beforehand. Often didn't know the material and would look answers up on google during class. Did not grade assignments until the last minute, even though students asked her to grade assignments to know how they were doing in class. Didn't have rubrics for assignments.

She was consistently unprepared for class. This was a DSM-5-TR class and she was not up to date on the current edition. The Canvas page and the syllabus were not aligned and she never fixed it. She had us do "Personality Disorders Charades" and targeted a classmate during this activity. I learned more from just reading the DSM and being in therapy.

Her course was the one I was most excited about but after the first month of class I began to dread the course. She provided no rubrics and was not clear on what SHE was looking for in assignments. She would give generic and unhelpful feedback. Her syllabus and course materials were never up to date. AVOID HER CLASSES!!!!!

Professor never reads materials before class, so she is learning things as she teaches. She said that she was trained in the DSM-V but for our textbook and NASW accreditation requirements, we were taught from the DSM-V-TR, so she was teaching us inaccurate and outdated information.

She does not come prepared and does not give clear instructions or provide rubrics for assignments. The canvas and syllabus were never set up accurately. The material was not taught well. Activities were not helpful and there was one activity that many students found to be insensitive. Overall the experience with this professor was disappointing.

Her Canvas as her syllabus never lined up. She was incredibly unprofessional and cried during class. She would never grade with a rubric but take points off for things that "weren't looked at closely enough." It was very clear she didn't know what she was teaching about and would rely on students to explain topics she didn't understand. Unethical.

She didn't look at the premade slides before class. A PTSD video was explicit and she had not seen it or warned. She would grade work saying that we did not include things that were not taught (and there were no rubrics). She said it was "controversial" to work with trans clients (many of us in class LGBTQ+). She was offensive and unethical.

One of the worst lecture slides I've seen. 150 slides with random blurry tables and figures copied and pasted into. Lectures are hard to follow and homework does get annoying.

It's unfortunate because he is passionate about what he teaches. Just really hopes he cleans up his slides and organize the course.

The homeworks for this class are very difficult, so try to find a partner. The material is super boring, but pay attention because you WILL be asked about small details. Also a PC laptop is required for the class to do the HWs. Macs will not work. The tests are not long, but study every detail because that's what half the questions are.
Hard to understand. Super boring. Didn't learn anything. And if the test is open book, forget about it, super hard.
Above Average

He is not bad. He knows what he is talking about. I do not know why everyone hates him so much. Give him a break. Any professor would seem bad after you have had Dan Work for the first half of the class.

Lectures are pretty boring; just reads off ppt slides, throws in a few anecdotes. The lecture slides could have been more useful in doing the homework. Exams were a bit long, but open book open note. Overall good class.

He was fine; not great but not terrible.  Basically just reads off the powerpoint slides, but he def knows what he's talking about.  I dunno why everyone says he keeps them late; we got let out on time every single day.

Unbelievable... He is the only prof. I've ever had that runs class past the bell every single lecture.  He is totally unapologetic about it too.  In fact, he gets angry when people leave a minute or two after the bell.  His exams are easy and the homework is easy (when it isn't so blurry from being copied so many times that you can't read it.)
Awful.  Lets class out late every single lecture.  Every. single. time.  Then he whines when people try to leave at the bell.

He runs over every single lecture then he complains when people want to leave.  He has made me late for an exam because he started yelling at me when I tried to leave 2 minutes after the bell.  He knows what he's talking about, but he is very very boring and he doesn't work for the student at all.  The homeworks he assigns are unreadable.

This class is utterly a joke, it's honestly a stretch to call this a class. It is randomly graded based off how your TA is feeling, all the course staff is inaccessible and there is no rhyme or rhythm to when assignments will come out or how anything is graded. It might actually be interesting if run by a different employee but not this one!

The class was unbelievably disorganized. Assignments have different due dates depending on where you looked, and took as long as 8 weeks to grade.Professor has no relationship with the class outside of creating lectures (which did not relate to course content clearly).TAs graded harshly and were rude throughout the semester to emails and questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: FAA 201 is an extremely disorganized class. Grading takes a long time. The professor is unreachable, you can only ever get in contact with class TAs. There is also group project which is extremely difficult to organize with the class being completely online. I would try your hardest for find another class to cover the gen ed requirements

FAA 201 is the most disorganized class I have ever taken. The lectures provided are hard to listen to and the assignments are simple, yet difficult to complete with the given information. The grading is unnecessarily harsh, and things are never graded in a timely or fair manner. Would not recommend.

The FAA 201 class was disorganized, with grades and deadlines not aligning with the syllabus. The small size didn't prevent a lack of structure, and the grading process took 6-8+ weeks with minimal feedback. Discovering my mid-term grade at the semester's end added stress. Only recommended for fulfilling general education credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Although he knows the material, he has no clue how to teach it. Longest and most boring lecture ever! The only time I ever learned anything in this class was in the discussion groups with our TA. Don't take this class if you have the option of choosing something else!!!

The single worst teacher at the University of Illinois. Disorganized. Rude. Took pride in embarrassing students, and he did that frequently. Lectures have nothing to do with material in the book. Exams, while online, still reflected nothing in the lectures. NEVER take a class with Lou Turner, and I'm shocked such a prestigious school hired him.
Very heavy on Theory. I learned nothing from the class, will play movies every week.

Overall a fun and interesting class. She is a laid back and knowledgeable professor. Four movie review papers throughout the semester which is each assigned with four people and one final paper which is assigned with a partner. No individual work, but it can be easy.

Professor Turnock is very knowledgeable and passionate about film. She received her Ph.D from University of Chicago and the great Tom Gunning was on her dissertation committee. Engaging PPT lectures were paired with film screenings in the class on 80s American cinema. If you get the chance, take a MACS class with her!
Screenings are too long and lectures are boring.

His accent is hard to understand. His lectures and discussion were completely pointless and always underexplained and skipped steps. He refused to accept my accommodations, told me I wasn't smart enough to be in his class, and week 8 he went back and changed all my grades from the first 2 weeks (I joined the end of week 2) from excused to 0s.

While he's kind funny, his lectures are pointless and it's more worth it to watch a youtube video from home where you can get explanations on how to actually do things. Hardest bit of calculus from his class is deriving what he's saying.

Tumanov is the worst professor I've ever had. Taking Calc 1? RUN!!! His lectures are pre-written notes with a heavy accent, zero explanation, and skipped steps. His tests are impossibly hard with brutal time limits. He's inflexible and seems to enjoy student misery. Save yourself the pain and pick literally anyone else. You've been warned.

This professor gave very difficult exams in a short time span, leaving you not being able to finish the exams most of the time. It was also very difficult to follow his lectures as he didn't follow the textbook and had prewritten notes which often skipped steps.

Consider taking a different professor if you don't want to struggle in this course. Tumanov uses pre-written notes to teach rather than working out problems on the board. His accent along with that makes it difficult to understand what he says.
Very difficult professor. I recommend studying a lot as his lectures don't prepare you for the exams at all .

learning like a dog and got a C
If you currently has no religion, I urge you to pick one and start praying if you are in his class.
Do not take with him

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I've had in my whole life, super hard to understand with his thick Russian accent. No one attends lecture because of how hard to understand it is. Getting an A in this class in nearly impossible. Switch out this class asap. His exams are extremely hard, and very hard to score high on.

Worst professor I have ever studied with; He only reads from lecture notes (which he post on canvas) and NOTHING ELSE. Does not really understand what a student is asking when they actually asked an in-depth question about the lecture. If this is actually the scenario for others, I do not recommend taking his class unless you have no other choice.

reviews.comment: Tumanov was the worst professor I have ever had in my entire life. He had a thick russian accent that was incomprehensible and would only read over his notes that he did a day prior. He often got confused by his own notes because he skipped steps. Do not take this professor. Drop the class and take it at a community college or another semester.

reviews.comment: He doesn't speak a single ounce of English. If you have him please switch! It was very bad all semester!

Tumanov is a nice man but a bad teacher. His lectures aren't worth attending because he doesn't work through or explain problems, he only reads off his notes which are mostly proofs. Exams are also difficult. If you need to take 220, take it with any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He reads off his notes, never wrote a single thing on the blackboard. He has a heavy accent which is very hard to understand. His tests are way harder than his practice problems. Will never take a class with him.
The course provides enough materials and notes to do the self-learning but the lectures are really difficult to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Whatever you do, PLEASE take a different professor for this course. I was lucky enough to have a great TA help me through the semester, but even he couldn't save me from Tumanov's messy and confusing lectures. I can tell Tumanov is passionate about calculus, but his teaching style is abhorrent; he never once worked through a problem by hand.
Just took my final

Very nice man, weak lecturer. Exams are tough. Expect to spend 30+ hours a week studying. Weekly quizzes are manageable. Your best bet is to the lecture notes, do the problems in the workbook, use outside resources. I also recommend looking over for mistakes and asking for regrades, he's very willing to do so.

there hasn't been a single lecture where this professor has written on the chalkboard and i usually end up more confused than actually learning anything. i highly recommend finding another professor that teaches math 220

If you are going to take Math 220 and this is the only professor left, forget about it and take it at a community college. This class is so disorganized. 75% of the time the professor is either babbling about some math nonsense that has nothing to do with the lesson or the note problems don't match the text book problems at all. Don't do it.
Absolutely the most horrible professor probably here at UIUC takes points off for the most random things

Your grade in Tumanov's class is very dependent on how much effort you put on your own time. He is a very passionate individual, but his teaching style during lectures lacks depth. I could not rely on his lectures alone to learn the material. PLEASE go to office hours and tutoring sessions at the Jeffries Center if you take his class.

Honestly the worst professor I've had so far. He has an extremely heavy accent, so you can barely understand him sometimes. On top of that, he has prewritten notes that sometimes have errors. He doesn't teach, he just reads through the notes. Doesn't ask questions to try and engage the class at all. I don't redolent taking with this professor!!!

reviews.comment: Very hard to understand and won't work through problems shown will only talk about them. Make sure to do homework and fully understand it otherwise the class is a lost cause.
Does not know how to teach, only suing prewritten notes. Decent person, but horrible at teaching.
He's not teaching at all.
This guy cannot teach. Better to watch youtube lectures than actually go to his. You can barely understand him cause his thick accent and he uses messy pre-handwritten notes to teach.
Teaches off hand written notes and barely explains what he's doing.

It's very hard to understand what he's talking about because his English isn't very good. He reads from prewritten notes that often contain errors, leaving everyone confused. If you have him, good luck you'll probably end up learning from Khan Academy and YouTube instead.

When he doesn't know what to say in English he just starts mumbling. He uses prewritten notes and goes by fast.

reviews.comment: just don't bruh...

Horrible accent, basically had only discussion to really understand anything, and no overall teaching is actually taking place, just reading off from the notes with no explanations. Tests every week and everything is so off schedule, lectures were one week ahead, discussions a couple days ahead and tests were one week behind. Don't recommend.

Very hard to understand his speech, he has a thick accent and broken english while also going through example problems much too quickly, moving onto new questions without even waiting. He makes calculus seem much, much more difficult than it actually is.

reviews.comment: I literally dropped his 220 lecture while I was inside the lecture hall. He doesn't use a microphone, just tries to speak loudly, which makes it literally impossible to understand him as he also has a thick accent and broken English. I don't think those are inherently bad qualities of a professor, but you literally cannot hear the guy.

Tumanov is one of the kindest and most caring people I have met. Always smiling and encourages participation in his class. Hard class and his class structure was something I wasn't a fan of though. His exams are easy but there isn't really anything to pad your grades. His class is not for the faint of heart.
