reviews.comment: Only once in a week for three hours and he will only teach for first one hour that too just going through the textbook and the remaining time he will either ask students to form into groups to discuss something or he will ask us to work on homeworks. In the later case,, he would just go to his office room and we could hardly learn anything from him

Exams did *not* accurately reflect material taught in class, nor the textbook(s).  No exam feedback at all before the final exam was *graded*.  Did not outline grades/expectations until final grades were released.  Would not recommend.
Very disorganized.  No feedback on any assignments.

Incredibly nice professor. While COVID definitely threw a monkey wrench in how the course was run, she was very accommodating and tried her hardest to make sure the class was still interesting despite being delivered online. While not entirely a cakewalk, the class is still pretty easy and is very fun if you're interested in the Vikings.

Dr. Hoefig was one of the best teachers that I took at U of I. She knew so much about the material and really cared about us understanding and having fun with it. Not a tough grader at all and I learned so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was an amazing class. She is great when it comes to connecting medieval culture to the present day - we talked a lot about ethnicity, race and gender identity.  Sessions were always so interesting and I felt like I not only learned a lot, but also expanded my worldview more with each class.
Participate and take notes. The exams are very specific to in-class lectures so pay attention.

She is really an amazing professor. I learned so much about system development. Her course has helped me a lot with interviews and getting internship. I will say, be sure to actively listen in class and participate (she cold calls) and you will get a lot out of the class. TIP- she always gives extra credit points for participation- speak up!

Always cold calls her students even if they just came back from the bathroom (?) - doesn't even know what she's teaching. She genuinely just chatgpts her entire course and doesn't know how to answer other questions. The way she teaches in class is somehow different from her slides and she includes things not in the syllabus which is so confusing.

She is such a strange grader and does not give clear expectations of projects. Also it is a no technology class you take notes on paper, lecture is not engaging. She also cold calls and gets angry when you get the answer wrong. Exams are also kind of rough for a badm.

She will cold call for students to answer questions during lecture so you would need to pay attention. She also has stopped students mid presentations to make critiques, she means well but she has grilled a couple groups mid presentation while other students are also watching. She does asks questions on the exam about everything covered.

If you ask for feedback on an assignment, she may tell you it looks great but upon receiving a grade she will take off random points. Reintroduced readings on test as a punishment despite previous class feedback being horrible about it. Deletes outlook on Fridays at 5pm and often ignores emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Be prepared to participate in this class because she calls on random people or people who don't look like they're paying attention! But despite her coming off a bit strict, you can tell that she really cares for her students and wants the best for them. Just make sure you are respectful and pay attention in class and you will love her and do great!

Great professor. Not only we went over important system analysis topics but she also went over how they can be valued in a variety of careers and she did this through many guest speaker lecturers who gave us a better insight on how they have been used. She does cold call a lot but she just expects the best engagement out of her students.
Somewhat struct but very clear lecturer and very receptive to feedback and asking questions. Would definitely take again! You learn a lot if you actually want to engage in class and all.

Class puts you to sleep. Talks in  monotone and bores students. Keeps repeating same old stuff again and again. Nothing new. Class is an easy A but nothing learned. If you just looking for grade take it. Not really of any use in job search as you basically learn nothing new. Has a strong accent. She is good lady but just does not know how to teach.

Professor Haran is the best! She is very compassionate, thoughtful, and cares a lot about her students! She is an excellent lecturer as well, makes the 3-hour class very engaging. Class exercises are very useful and helps a lot for exams!

She knows her stuff but cannot express it well. If you try hard and do some reading on your own, not difficult to understand though. Exams are not too easy nor too difficult. Again if you try hard, getting a B not a problem. Not an inspirational prof for sure. Don't be surprised if you find yourself falling asleep.

This was an FYS class that I was in. Dr. V was funny and very chill. Good bonding class, not hard, and it was a good class overall. Obviously students don't really get to pick their fys but he was a great professor overall and easy to talk to— would reccomend.
Horrible professor! In my twenty some years of schooling I have never encountered a professor worse then him. Avoid at all costs!!! You've been warned...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Vieregger is one of the most approachable, practical professors in the College of Business. His experience speaks for itself, and I can assure you that if you take his class, you will absolutely not regret it. This guy is the man.
Professor Vieregger is one of the best professors that I have ever had. Very knowledgable, approachable, and makes an otherwise mediocre class exciting. Highly Recommend.

Excellent professor with great practical business knowledge that he enjoys sharing with his students.  All 449 classes have a lot of projects and assignments, but Dr. V does a good job of making them interesting and fostering class discussions on the case studies.  Exams were fair, assignment grading was fair.  Highly recommended

So much work outside of class, very exhausting class. The sheer amount of homework is absurd, and most of the time there is very little guidance provided. Expect to spend 6+ hours outside of class time on homework a week. Assignments are difficult to understand. Lectures are fine, usually pretty engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I took this professor for 372. He does not even post the syllabus and makes an ECE kid teach the class. Absolutely horrendous.
Made my life harder. Teach an EDM class with almost nothing about EDM.
Disorganized!
Lectures are very disorganised. Too muchbat once. Random projects, worst idea ever. 2 tests ,5 different projects. All the ideas were good but it was all touch and go . No real depth to the material

The materials were significantly disorganized. Each lecture introduced new concepts without alignment to prior or subsequent content. The majority was touch-and-go, lacking detailed explanations by the professor. Pre-read was impossible as future materials were locked, denying student access. Improvement definitely warranted!!
Very terrible and unorganized.

The course content is very unorganized. The professor doesn't seem he really knows what he is teaching on his class. TA is much more helpful than the professor. By the way, the accent is hard to understand.

Prof. Sachdev is a nice person, but a terrible professor. He repeats himself too often, and has trouble explaining the content. The lectures were painful to get though. The course was very unorganized, and the assignments didn't contribute to the learning of the material. Overall, the course was not applicable, and the prof didn't make it better.
pretty fair teacher, a lot of passion

His voice is boring and monotone and he teaches badly. Just reads off the slide. Cannot understand anything he says. Though he throws out software tools, if you go ask him to explain about them he gives some vague answer. Very difficult to understand his accent. Horrible teacher, I am sorry to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Has thick accent. I was barely able to understand what he was saying. Jumps around and does not explain any thing in depth. Throws out big terms but if you ask him he cannot explain anything thoroughly. I felt like I did not learn anything in this class. I will not recommend taking this professor for any course.
Great professor and I will definitely take his class again. He rewards hardworking students with a Nobel Peace Prize. Thank you.
Vishal was an amazing professor. Very easy to talk to and his lectures were always well prepared. He gave me great feedback on my work but it is important to keep up with assignments.
Does not know how to teach. Excessive amount of work. Keeps repeating same thing over and over and does not help students. Take this course with someone else.

Not an easy grader. Group project is annoying too. Overall not a great lecturer and the tests are pretty difficult. He is really good about meeting with students for office hours, however. Take this class with a different professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: easy class and cool prof

Overall, average.  I didn't like the way the class was structured (lots of discussion posts and then critiques of others' posts) and the final project required more skills than the average person without much of a tech background had.  The material was interesting though, so this class would be great with a better professor
Worst professor I've had at UIUC. EXCESSIVE amount of work for literally no reason and he is very boring and monotone. Take a different section at all costs.

I thought that Professor Sachdev's class was surprisingly interesting and relevant to the real world. He is very knowledgable and funny and is very willing to offer help, as long as you ask for it! His tests do include a lot of memorization, but luckily they aren't worth too much of your grade. I also felt that he always graded homework fairly.

Wish I had checked here before I signed up. Jesus! Stay away from him. Trust me. This is the first time I have ever left negative feedback on any professor. THE WORST ever in all aspects including structure of course, grading, and teaching skills. Very narrow minded as well. Stay away. Probably will get an A, but waste of time.

not an enthusiastic teacher, doesnt hand back the tests at all, very monotone, doesnt seem to like his job, does not announce homework assignments, and just seems like a very depressed person in general. it was a depressing time going to class knowing that nothing even remotely exciting will come out of him during the lecture to help liven up the c

The single most time consuming 3 hour course I've ever had. 5 assignments (varying from 2 pages single spaced to pointless group assignments), a project that included a 9-10 page SINGLE SPACED paper, and 2 tests.   15% of the grade is participation and he talks the entire time, leaving no room for students to participate.

Interesting class w/ a real-world focus. However, he will drive you insane. He doesn't announce the assignments, compass HW is posted 12 hours before it's due, and you don't know what to expect on tests. The tests are memorizing the hundreds of IT words you read - nothing more. I expected more from a 300-level class. He is an easy grader, though.

It's a privilege to learn from Dr. Vogler. He is SO knowledgeable and passionate about his work. If you have a passion of your own for the same topic or something different, he will help you explore that within his classes. He cares for his students as people, so be honest with him about your needs, and you will have a great time. Easily the best.

You are lucky if you get to take a class with Dr. Vogler. If you genuinely want to grow as a student, he is the professor for you. Pay attention, go to class, and engage. It is not difficult to get an A if you apply yourself. He wants what is best for you.

Stefan is BY FAR the best teacher in Sociology, so if you can, take all of his courses.

I think the expectations of students were high despite little to no guidance. He is too much of a tough grader, I think at times even the TA found him to be unreasonable. I feel as though the group project shouldn't have been such a large part of the final grade. I genuinely think my cortisol levels went out of whack because of this class.

IMO Professor Vogler was a solid teacher, unlike what the other reviews say, but the class was just made too difficult even for the best of us. If your group messes up one assignment, anything but an A- is already out of reach. He seems like a good enough guy with a great amount of knowledge about his field, but pedagogically this class was not it.

SO unreasonable. Last minute decided to threaten us with a surprise final exam with less than a week's notice even though the syllabus had said our final would be a group project. Only decided not to do this after being flooded with emails. Rubrics were very unclear. Even his TA didn't know what his expectations were.

Vogler's lectures are awful. He goes over vocabulary the entire time and often has bad examples or no examples at all. Grading procedures and expectations are unclear. Sometimes, he doesn't post rubrics until after assignments are due. The rubrics seem pretty general and straightforward, but when grading, he is very specific. Avoid at all costs.
A great professor and a stand-up guy. One of the people who makes the finance department worth it. Either take his classes or do the practicum.
He is the best, I wish I could taken ore of his classes but unfortunately he is retiring this year. All the best to your future life professor vonhammne.
A pretty fair professor who is very knowledgeable about all areas of finance, accounting, and management. He treats all the students nicely and not super critical like some other finance professors.
I wish my head is a camera.

The professor (Charles Voigt) is nice, but the class is VERY boring. Unless you are very good at memorizing, don't take it! The material wasn't hard at all, but the amount of material was TOTALLY unreasonable. I took this class thinking easy-A. No way. Not unless you're into memorizing TONS of things and have no other classes.

If you're not a horticulture major, watch out... NOT an introductory class, as it claims to be. Most non-hort majors ended up having to take this class pass/fail. Homework? Easy. Quizzes? Easy  Tests? Far too specific. Mass-memorization. TONS OF MATERIAL. we're talkin 10 pages of notes a lecture...typed, single-space. take Hort 106 with TOM Voigt.
Most boring lectures and assignments - mean if you ever need help or compassion.  This class is an easy A but he won't let you make any quizzes up
Other the exams being very difficult, the rest of the course remains interesting and a fair workload. The final project was especially interesting, and a great opportunity for extra credit.
Great lecture. Good professor
Professor Kindratenko is one of the best lecturers at in the department. (He's up there with Prof Angrave). Dude is brilliant and helpful and will make sure you understand every minute concept.

Kindratenko's lectures were probably the best lecture available for this course when I took ECE 120 (FA22). He has a bit of an accent, but he is still easily understood. Your success in this class depends less upon learning from lecturers but from homework and the discussion worksheets, and utilizing office hours. Good professor and good course.

Professor Kindratenko is a very good lecturer and is knowledgable about the field. He explains topics very well and will sometimes crack a joke (also has fun accent). The one negative is that he is sometimes hard to reach outside of lecture, but this is okay since 120 has a great course staff behind the scenes.

Some of the things I liked about Professor Kindratenko were that he was able to explain the finer questions that might've risen from the course material quite well, and his teaching style which made the harder topics in the course quite easy to understand with the help of examples. I would wholeheartedly recommend taking his courses in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Quite literally the best teacher I've had since elementary school. Amazing at explaining any questions you might have and very caring as well as helpful.
Kindratenko is my guy.
If you are taking ECE120, he is the only guy to go to.
I love this guy.
Dude's a legend.
Best professor
Professor Kindratenko is the best ECE professor I've ever met. He answer all my questions patiently after class and explain the ideas clearly. Definitely recommended Freshmen to take his ECE120.
Made ECE 408 way harder and more useless (those. tests. especially. are. so. stupid) than it had to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Knows the material extremely well and is very helpful. Programming isn't too bad in the class. Tests are straight brutal lmao. Still learned a lot, though. Def recommend

Professor Kindratenko is very nice and is a great lecturer. He knows what he's talking about, and he's very good at explaining concepts. Very polite, cares about his students. His tests may be brutal, but you learn so much from him. I definitely recommend him!
Begin to miss Kindratenko when taking ECE220 :(

Good professor. Lectures are fast, and there's a decent amount of content, but Kindratenko makes it doable. You'll have to get used to the Russian accent, but it's nothing that makes the professor unintelligible.
I had the other professor and almost failed but watching his video lectures got me that A
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I really enjoy the class he taught.
Really great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Has a great Russian accent.
Great professor, even better accent

Kindratenko is a great, friendly lecturer and he explains the material like you have never seen before. Once you get used to the Russian accent, you start to explain the material in a great way. He can be sometimes fast but it is because there is lots of material to cover in this class. I would recommend him no matter what. Expect to work in 120.

Kindratenko is kind and talks to you like you have never heard the material before. His lectures were chock-full of information that helped me get an A. He could've gone a little slower in the middle portion of the semester but pace was perfect otherwise.

A fantastic lecturer able to cover everything in the perfect amount of detail. He does not waste your time, that would be your fellow classmates who ask uneducated questions i.e. Syndrome. Accent is easy to understand and he has an extremely advanced and in depth knowledge of anything else you will need to know, super computers etc.
That Russian accent though.

I took it over the summer and I think this is the first time they offer this class for summer semester. To be honest, the tests are fair and I think they are easier than the tests from normal semesters because it will cover all topics in 8 weeks. Prof. K is very patient to students and the practice exams are very similar to the actual exam.

This class is difficult. It's definitely not impossible, but you're going to have to work for it. The homeworks are long and require a lot of independent learning. The labs are ok. The exams are tough, but reflect concepts from the HWlectures. Prof Kindratenko is a great lecturer and is really helpful in office hours. You'll learn a lot with him.

Kindratenko is a great teacher. I took his ECE120 class and to be honest, it was unnecessarily difficult, but that's college. He's helpful when you ask for it. Pro tip: always go to  his office hours to review your graded tests with him. He may give back a lot of points!

Good class, it does gradually get harder but as long as you master the concepts and design process, still an easy A. Dr. Kindratenko specializes in GPU computing, he's quite knowledgeable in organization and algorithms. His lectures can be interesting or boring depending on whether you like the subject or not, but great accent!
The class was ok but as a person, he Agent K is very condescending.  When asked a question, make sure it is an "intelligent" one or else he will mock you
Great guy. The class is a tough class and he definitely doesn't baby his students. Overall, take his class. Great guy and an awesome accent.
I took ECE190 last semester and dropped it. Now it makes more sense,

He co taught this class with Loui. I really enjoy his style of teaching. He is straight forward, knows what he's talking, and all around good teacher. Def a good experience with him as a teacher for a class I don't really enjoy
Awesome lecturer! His russian accent can sometimes make it hard to understand, but he's great at explaining concepts, and he's funny too! Best prof for ECE 190.
Perfect!

Let me tell you this, I had her last semester AND this semester for two different classes. She is the BOMB. Super sweet, amazing, helpful and fun! I got an A in the class I had with her last sem. and an A this sem! TAKE CLASSES WITH HER. SHE MAKES CLASS FUN :) #teamvogel

Amazing professor! This has to be my favorite class that I have taken in college. She is straightforward on what she expects from students. Her assigned readings are doable and she reviews them in class! It is impossible to not know whats going on! Show up to class and try to pay attention and you will succeed!

Dr. Vogel was an amazing professor! She has great passion for this class and it comes off in her teaching. She does not try to trick you, what is presented in the class is what is on the exam! So therefore, review the power points. There are 2-4 movies that we watch that are pretty engaging, so take notes on that. You also get a study guide!

She is a great teacher and will provide you with everything needed to get an A.  It is an easy class and the TA is exceptionally easy on the grading, but it can get super boring.  Would definitely recommend her!

This class has been one of my best classes at UIUC. I took this class because I needed it for my gen ed and I really started looking forward to attend this class. The professor is very informative and very entertaining. There are 2 really easy assignments and a final. You must go to class because he knows if you don't. I highly recommend it!
Awesome Professor!  Easy A and interesting class.
Great Teacher! Go to class and somewhat pay attention and you will get an A.  Nice guy and very funny.  Interesting class too.

I had no prior interest in the subject, but this professor Chumachenko made it quite interesting and entertaining. He has good sense of humor and is very supportive. Take his classes and you'll have fun. He also is good in grading.
This class was very easy. It was kind of boring, but it was worth it. The textbook readings did not line up with what we learned in class and were not tested, so buying the textbook is not necessary.

A very strangely funny professor. This course doesn't really require a lot of work to pull of an A, but I actually learned a lot about Ukraine. He is very blunt and honest about his opinions (i.e. how he dislikes Soviet Union/the poor technology advancement at UIUC lol). Take this class so you can relax, learn about another culture, and get an A!

Professor Chumachenko may ramble on a little bit he knows what he's talking about and tries to make it interesting. Overall his class was simple and easy as long as you come and sign the attendance sheet most days.  There is only attendance, a few (2-3) short papers and a final exam that go into grades, and he is not a tough grader.

The guy is an excellent teacher: intelligent, educated, and knows a lot beyond the subject. He is a real erudite! His lectures are fun to listen and watch - it is a real performance with jokes and unexpected turns.He just loves to help when you have a question. His grading is always fair.

Professor is the nicest guy ever! always makes little jokes in class and willing to help whenever needed. Just show up to class, write 1 paper and 1 exam.  Not difficult at all, and somewhat interesting. Just take a few notes, and you'll do fine.

He is such a nice guy, is really excited to each his students, and hopes that each of them does very well in his class. I definately recommend the class...it counts as a gen ed and is very easy. I also heard that his other class, Ukr 218 is a good one.

(Also GWS 286) Professor Vostral is an amazing professor, I really enjoyed the class- U.S. Gender History since 1880s. She related our readings to current debates on women's issues. Not a lot of work- short/reasonable readings for class. 2 group presentations/essay which were fun and really hands on with material. And another 2 pg essay-easy! Take!

Vostral is a nice woman and she is interesting, but she grades WAY too hard. her assignments are unclear and i agree with another comment on this site. since its an intro to gws class people's opinions are uneducated and ignorant and she doesnt do anything to correct them. i bet she'd be better teacher for a higher level class

Horrible. DO NOT take this intro to GWS if you want to learn more than the uneducated opinions of your peers. Literally all we did was talk about our opinions, and since this is an intro. course, these people had no idea what the hell they were talking about, therefore I learned NOTHING. Her assignments are pointless.
Professor Vostral is awesome!

Prof. Vostral is great! She is kind, easy going and her discussions are very fluid. Eye opening class and very enjoyable. She doesn't expect a lot from her students, and she'll only work as hard as you do!
Tougher class, but a great professor that really helps you understand the material.

This class and the material itself is difficult and it is a lot of information at once. I felt that the lectures were overwhelming and it was difficult to learn quickly / as the class was going on, but this is at no fault to the Prof. Vuong Persson. She is kind and wants to help you as much as possible.

Prof. Vuong Persson was such a sweet professor that truly cares about her students. She does her best to make the content understandable and tries to accommodate students. She's super accessible and works hard to help students succeed. The class is tough, don't get me wrong you gotta be ready to work, but Anh as a professor was awesome.

He may seem like an awkward turtle when you first meet him, but he cares a lot about his students. I had a meltdown in his office and he talked me through it and even helped me figure out what I could do. Josh doesnt control what happens in lab so I would suggest to be best friends with your TA, they do the grading after all. The Lab reports kill.

I think Josh is a good example of somebody who's smart but not that great of a teacher. His lectures were mostly just reading from PowerPoint slides, which weren't helpful at all. Besides, your TA matters much more for lab, so go to them and find out what they want, since they're the ones actually doing all the grading. P.S. He's not a bad guy.

Professor Josh really wanted to help and his lectures were helpful in understanding the materials we were dealing in the lab. However, TA matters the most in this class. If you are taking the class, talk to TA first to see what he/she expects in your paper. There is one lab report due every week so try to squeeze out at least 4 hours for the paper.
Nearly lost my 4.0; got lucky with a nicer TA Make sure you are friendly with your TA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: bad homework and project problem selection that leaves you high and dry because they are hardly connected to what he taught the class.

Lectures were poorly designed and sparsely attended.  Doesn't really connect homework content to lecture content.  Class average on both midterms (each 20% of final grade) was in the 40s.  Huge curve at the end.  

Professor is hated by most of his students.  They say he's simply not effective at teaching especially not for how strictly he grades.

If you're in aerospace and can avoid taking any classes with professor Chang (and trust me I've taken 321, 352, and now 353 with him) AVOID taking classes with him. He grades 10x more harshly, shows very little empathy, reads off of slides, and overall shows very little comprehension of the material he is supposed to be teaching.

He is compassionate, very patient with questions and listens to our problems.
But despite this, a lot of people in his class say he is ineffective at actually teaching.  
The exams he gives are notoriously hard and he (with a smile on his face) says he enjoys making them so.
He was nice and chill. Did exactly what a professor should do for AE100 class. In general I had fun and met a lot of new aero people. Not too much work and very doable, no stress at all.
Very average teacher. Not a super hard grader, sometimes assigns a lot of work, teaches you essentially what he is supposed to. Very annoying to listen to and very loud. Otherwise nice.

He taught AE 353 but he would put homeworks, projects, and exams on the same week. He didn't clearly mention the requirements for the project but would harshly grade them, giving people as low as 0 points for a project worth 40%.
Very good lecturer, explains everything well and is nice to students. He is popular, and I would agree.

He is very respectful and always comes into class with a big smile, very patient with students and cares about all of us.  He is very enthusiastic about the material he teaches and I'm glad to have had him as my first taste of what's ahead to come as an Aerospace major.  With this being a 100 class it's not really in-depth into concepts though.
Professor Chang gives good lectures that are easy to follow, and gives clear examples that help understand course content. 251 isn't an easy class, but I'd highly recommend Chang.

He is one of the best professors I have met at UIUC. His lectures are clear and straight to the point. He is also a very nice person and kind to students, and the difficulty of exams and finals are reasonable.
Gave good lectures and homework prepared us adequately for the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I would describe him as the average joe of professors. Not bad but not great either. Lectures are okay, but they often won't fully prepare you for the hwk, which is reasonable, but some hwks are pretty friggin hard. Hwks prepare you decently for tests, but always expect to have 1 brand new pretty hard question on the test.

Dr Chang is a really organized professor who knows how to deliver the course material and course expectations very clearly. His lecture notes are neat and serve as very good reference materials when doing homework. The homework, while tedious, prepares you very well for the tests and exams, giving you a clear sense of direction always.

TAM210 is an easy class to pass, especially if you've never had any experience with this course content before. However, if you're looking to pass with an A, you'll need to put in a lot of studying to actually understand the content. Your final grade is very dependent on the quizzes and the final exam, don't mess up!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chang is a good guy. Really tries to make lectures enjoyable. Would take again, especially over Admal.
Great Professor, my favorite class this semester

Professor Chang is warm and friendly, but neglects to teach the material in depth. His "flipped classroom" style requires a great deal of independent learning, which is difficult for such complicated topics in thermodynamics. I felt ill-prepared for nearly every quiz and exam. Be prepared to do lots of work without help or instruction.

Dr. Chang was honestly pretty good. His lectures were engaging, and he taught the class well. Exams were based on past homework problems, so if you did the homework (which is required) you were pretty much guaranteed an okay score on the exam. Probably one of the better engineering professors here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Change is a great guy. His lectures were very useful and I learned most of what I needed to know in lecture, unlike my other classes. Homework can be difficult, but office hours are helpful. Overall great professor.
He is a great teacher and a great guy. 10/10 recommend.

I had professor Chang for TAM 211 in 2019, and I was not impressed with his lecturing. However, this year I took his TAM 251 section, and he had improved greatly! He had a good balance of theory and in class examples that often translated well to the homework. He also tried his best to make something as terrible as TAM entertaining.

Lectures were honestly useless as the homework was nothing like lectures, but welcome to Engineering I guess. I wish they would do a hard homework problem, but nope they just ignore it like it never happened. It felt very disorganized at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Chang is a good lecturer if you pay attention in class. He does lots of examples but sometimes theyre oversimplified for the difficulty of the homework
Explained the reading concepts very clearly. No homework other than the readings.

I took two courses with her and wish I could have taken more. She is incredibly knowledgable and passionate. She's also friendly, kind, and tries to make her class as fun as possible for students. Her lectures focus on the readings, which she's fabulous at explaining in depth, so reading out of class isn't a must.

This post updates a post I made Dec. 21st. when I was disgruntled at Professor Weinberg. I want to set the record straight. Professor Weinberg gives amazing lectures, which makes the material in the course seem simple, when it is incredibly complex. Professor Weinberg cares for her students and wants the best for everyone. -Shane Werner

Arrogant and Unprofessional at times when discussing certain topics. She appears self righteous and mixes her personal views with her professional teachings. Her lectures are boring and she wants you to stay focused. If you want to wake up every day coming to see someone who is in her 50s and often shows an angry face, take Weinberg.

One of the worst professors at uic, Weinberg always mixes her personal opinion with her professional opinion. Her lectures speaks of human logic but absent good hearts which reflects how often she hates Christianity. Stay away from this professor. Her class doesn't add any value to real life other than rant about how smart she is. 2 + 2 = 4

I wouldn't waste my FAFSA loan on taking her courses, there is nothing good that she can teach and to try to make it look that her class is worth it, she is a harsh grader. Her lectures are many times slow, she often comes with a mean demeanor to the class and hates it when students aren't paying attention because she is boring.

Professor Weinberg seems harsh, but her class is incredibly informative and well put together. If you talk to her she will absolutely help you. The papers are not graded too harshly either. Overall great intro class.

I don't usually leave reviews on here, but I just had to for Dr. Weinberg. Not only is she extremely intelligent and knowledgeable about what she teaches, but she also lectures in a way that makes it easy to understand some difficult course material. Papers are graded hard, but they are graded fairly with great feedback. Take PHIL with Dr Weinberg!

She's a fantastic professor and person. The only gripe I have is that she's not willing to say "yeah you've basically got it"—you've got to say EXACTLY what she's thinking in class for her to accept it. It's a little annoying, but it's a tiny flaw in an otherwise airtight teaching skillset. She's very personable.

Weinberg's class is easy and straightforward, but she can be very rude at points. She would give very little credence to the questions asked by students and would be very dismissive unless she liked you as a student.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unprofessional at times when discussing certain topics (e.g. God) and fails to asses student understanding in lecture; but she gives room during class for questions and thorough feedback, and her TA grades fairly easy. Showing up to class is essential to pass the class. She goes really fast with the slides, so try and write as much as you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Shelley is a great lecturer and every class will be good to watch. You don't need to read the readings really except for paper writing. There are three papers to write and they are graded hard but fair. The papers are all the points.

The class itself is a bit confusing but Dr. Weinberg is super sweet and considerate. She words lectures in a way that we can understand and it's actually intro level. She keeps the class interesting and she's probably one of my favorites. Literally in no way mean, she's also super funny.

I don't love school at all, but I LOVEED this class. She is so clearly passionate about philosophy which made the lectures really interesting and genuinely enjoyable. She goes through the slides quite fast tho, so I recommend taking pictures of them if you don't think you'll be able to get it all down. The info on the slides were IMMENSELY helpful.

I took ACP and it was great! Prof Weinberg selects great TA's that are always willing to help you out on the 3 big papers that basically determine your grade. The reading material is fascinating and Prof Weinberg is an extremely inspiring and captivating lecturer. Her passion for philosophy is evident, and it makes you want to learn it all too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: good class
She does a good job of engaging the class and breaking down the important ideas of the text.

I love Professor Weinberg! She's a great lecturer, which is helpful considering the course is about different metaphysical and epistemological systems from the early-modern period. She'll answer any questions or objections in class and encourages class participation. Highly recommend going to paper review sessions with T.A. if you want to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Shelly is such a good lecturer and you can really tell she's passionate about philosophy. I loved taking her course. She doesn't do any grading but she's always down to help you with your papers. It's best to go to lecture because anything you need for your papers is basically discussed in lecture. Strongly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She isn't the greatest lecturer, but she is sure knowledge. Not much assignments, but grades are VERY HARSH. Materials are quite interesting, but not interesting enough that motivates you to learn. I took it for advanced composition and regret much for such decision.

Shelley is just amazing. She has an excellent command on early modern empiricists (Especially Locke). She is great as a professor and LOVES philosophy and this love permeates through to her lectures as well. One of the best professors I have ever had the privilege to learn from

Professor Weinberg is one of the most amazing people I have met. I have learned a lot from that class, and her. Anyone seriously interested in learning a uniquely smart way of viewing philosophy should take any of her classes :)

Great Professor. The material was not exactly a walk in the park, but she does a wonderful job helping students understand. She is funny also. Enjoyed the course simply because of her, I could have done without Leibniz lol :)

Shelley is a wonderful instructor and I absolutely recommend taking her class. She is very reasonable when it comes to grading and submission dates. So long as you are invested in the course, she will be willing to help you succeed. Tells jokes in class all the time and always happy to be there.
she's brilliant. awesome!!!! TAKE HER!!!!!!!

Tough grader on homework, but the class isn't too bad. The lectures seem to mesh together since everything seems the exact same as the previous lecture. Second half of semester is very challenging. I kind of regret taking this class because I don't like thinking critically, but for others, it maybe be helpful.

This woman is so funny! I feel like every lecture is her venting about her life to all of the students. She hates my class because we don't really do a great job of staying attentive, but it's pretty fun. As for the curriculum, I feel that i made a huge mistake taking this class, it is way too simple.

This class was a lot of fun and really taught you how to look at argumentation. Beginning of the semester was really easy, but review often, because it gets a lot harder near the end. She takes attendance, but her pleasant awkwardness makes class fun and entertaining. I recommend this class.
She's good and cares about her students. Plenty of energy.

She is harsh on papers, but she's really helpful and wants you to understand the materials. I feel it's hard to not like her class, at least students in our class all say they enjoy it a lot. Her first few weeks are easy, but it suddenly gets hard, be prepared, don't complain after you get bad grade on a paper!
She is really nice and helpful, she inspires me to minor Phil!

She takes attendance for every lecture and discussion! There is not much work to do for the class but she wont give you A. The first assignment is misleadingly easy and from the second one on, she starts to give low grades. No finals, no exmas, but she(or maybe the TAs) is harsh on your papers.

I find her a great teacher.  She is living the life you would imagine a philosophy teacher to live.  This class has interested me in going into law, an unforeseen venture.  She selects great TA's too.

My main criticism is that the class moves a little slow sometimes; we had to cut out everything on Kant. She tries to make things as clear as possible and wants students to understand the material. Overall I enjoyed her class a lot. To succeed in the class you MUST do the readings!

I think the lectures were just like okay, I feel like it just boiled down to being way too many I Clicker questions and too few examples/explanations. The class overall wasnt too bad until the final, which was really bad for like everyone. However, toward the end of the year the communication regarding grading was not good.

Good lecturer, helpful. TAM212 is super hard and the grading policy makes it hard to do well, but West explains things clearly and does lots of examples. Paying attention in lecture will make everything else a little easier.

Prof. West is a great lecturer. The class goes over difficult content but he explains it really well. ME 340 is also a well laid our course. I like that it places less emphasis on labs and more on homework and actual learning. Exams are about at the difficulty one would hope for so just pay attention in class and you'll be ok.
West is a good professor, and genuinely nice guy. However, TAM212 is an awful class that is set up horribly. Definitely take West to make a tough course a little better though.
Good lecturer, but the assignments and assessments are not very well designed.

Decent professor, but it's impossible to contact him outside of class (doesn't respond to emails). In my opinion the prof doesn't matter too much in this class. The most important thing is to do the HW's and go to office hours.
Professor West is funny and friendly. TAM classes are tough, and they're graded strictly, but he really does his best to take feedback and try and help students.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor. Funny, pretty clear, always tries to engage the class in the lecture. Final was hard, but as long as you complete the HW you shouldn't do worse than a C in the class.

After taking TAM251 with other Tam professors, I now appreciate West alot more. He was a very good lecturer. Provided helpful examples for the hw and didn't try to fail you like the rest of the TAM department. Being honest, the final is hard, but if you do good on the hw, discussion, and quizzes (are exactly like hw), then you'll be fine.

His lectures aren't useful for the homework or quizzes, but they're very informational and he's passionate about what he teaches. Let me just say that this isn't a class I fall asleep in. The dynamics reference page provides all you need for the homework and quizzes for this course.
Good professor, cares about how his students are doing in class. Material is pretty easy, but he keeps lectures relatively interesting.

Very good at providing a concise overview of difficult topics.  For me, the homework was what provided the needed practice to master the topics.  Lectures were useful, but the repetitive practice is what really allowed me to learn the material.  Quiz retake policy was very generous.  However, the final was significantly more difficult.

West is not a great professor but this class is not very hard. Lectures are basically useless because he wastes time on conceptual iClicker questions rather than questions like those on homework and quizzes; however, the material is not too difficult and easy to learn. The final exam is a bit tricky, but can be solved easily when simplified.
Our semester was basically a guinea pig semester for 212 to try out new things, so although there were some bumps in the road,  he was very helpful and understanding along the way.

Really taught the basics well. Had some issues making exams that were of a proper difficulty. The midterms were too easy so the final was made to be impossible. If he can figure out the course organization I would recommend to take it with him

The tests during the year were really easy and many of us got perfects. However, the final was so ridiculously hard that out of the 150 students in the room, only a handful left before the 3 hours were up. A few problems were featured that were not covered in class.
Great professor, take his classes if you can.

Good explanation, well-structured and patient. Nice guy! Tests were easy, but final exam got a little bit difficult. But as long as you do all the past paper and get familiar with the homework, should be easy to get A.

Many of these reviews are slanderous. His absence policy IS brutal, but getting an A in this class is very doable. Weekly quizzes which are generally easy if you read like the syllabus tells you to. He provided sufficient resources for even the least competent of people to get A's on the midterm and final. Show up, read, and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Avoid if possible.

Class isn't insanely hard content, but you really need to make sure you're getting your basic concepts down. If you do 60% more in the first 4 weeks, you'll get adjusted and the class will be smooth sailing until the Midterm. Midterm and Finals are very very manageable, and account for 60% of your grade alone. Just pay attention in lectures. 👍
