reviews.comment: Lectures with little explanation for difficult topics and excessive explanation for easy topics. Long tangents on completely unrelated content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a senior student and get a D in his class. ChatGPT is far better than him. Don't take his course unless you want to get an easy D. Worst professor I have even seen.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Professor is nice and enthusiastic, but he does not upload slides, and the slides he does have in class are just filled with text, as if you're reading a paper in PowerPoint. 
There's a lot of reading - like at least 100 pages per week.

His lectures are not that useful when it comes to first intaking information. Mark my words: READ THE TEXTBOOK before going to his lectures and ask questions what you don't understand. You should also be focused during lecture because he often deviates from the textbook. I wouldn't say he is a good professor, but not horrible either.

You will lose 10 percent if you miss 2 classes and 20 percent if you miss three. He is arrogant and self-centered. Communication with him is fruitless because he simply doesn't listen. You can learn nothing from his class. Each class only contains contents that you can self-study within 5 minutes. Don't waste your time on him! Don't waste your GPA!

Course covers interesting material, but he is a low quality professor. He's arrogant, a tough grader (vague feedback, such as "I don't like this paragraph"), and generally unfeeling. Goes on tangents about logic and historical figure trivia, which might have relevance if he tried teaching instead of reading off typo-ridden drafts of his 'book'.

Not a good teacher. He copies and pastes paragraphs from the texts books into his powerpoint and just reads them off the slides in our lectures. As for the final, he will not tell you the format of it and gets mad when you ask. Not only that but he also won't put the answer key up for the final exam review. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! The professor is rude and not helpful, the content in the beginning is not helpful and the second quarter of the class is like the math portion. We were given no time to actually study and practice the math portion, the grading is super harsh especially for a 100-level course. I absolutely would NOT recommend!!!!

The fact that they gave this dude tenure is a joke. The dude will go off on the most pedantic pointlessly boring rants about classical propositional logic that doesn't apply to the class. The lectures do not cover half of what the textbook covers. He refused to give us a final exam review answer sheet to study saying "come to office hours" at 8:30.

Chris Weaver is arrogant and treats this 100 class as a 200-300 level class. Tough grader on the midterm paper and attendance is mandatory. Flies through lectures and just reads off the Powerpoint and refuses to explain material when asked for clarification and just tells students to "refer to the textbook".

Professor Weaver is arrogant and rude. His email replies to questions are often unhelpful and demanding if a topi was covered in class. The lectures are just him reciting quotes and essays that he copies into a large document that are notes. When asked questions to clarify a topic, he just simply tells you to reread the section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you just want to learn something about the philosophy without a physics background. Professor Weaver never explained the content well if you are not interested in the physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are essentially essays copied and pasted onto lecture slides. There are also a lot of readings. This class is cross listed with philosophy 419, but it leans too heavily  on the philosophy side. The professor does not speak clearly either. He does have good office hours though if you have questions so use that as a resource
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very unclear grade criteria

The course is quite challenging. Never reply emails. Some people did get reply, while others didn't. I sent emails at both the mid-term and final, but I didn't receive any responses until the end of the course.
It was said that the final exam would replace the score of the previous exam, but he didn't also was no curve applied either.

Lectures consist solely of reading off slides.  Has an accent, not the easiest to understand.  Don't bother showing up to class, just learn off the textbook.  Better off completely self studying for the class and exam P.  Take STAT400/410 instead if he is teaching this class.
He gets stopped in thought during lectures leaving a prolong silence.

Only class that has both taught me so much w minimal stress/commitment. Ancient reviews originally scared me away, but shes the only CS/PSCI prof where I have genuinely enjoyed coming to each class. She seems scary bc she plays devils advocate (pushes back every1s answers), but its all play. Partic (+reading journal) is most of grade w final paper

PS is not known for its great teaching, but even Wendy Tam is a disappointment. She lectures unintelligibly from withered yellow notes from her own grad school courses, often copying them directly to the blackboard without explanation. She is rude and abusive to students, and avoids office hours like the plague. You deserve better than her.

Horrible professor.  Could not convey material at all.  This was a required stats course for graduate political science students and very few of us learned anything.  She made fun of us, graded capriciously, and never held office hours.

Horrible, horrible, horrible.  Neither clear nor helpful.  Makes fun of us if we don't get the idea.  Demanding, but doesn't want to help us.  Got the material the next term in a statistics class that was a lot better.

Just the worst.  Bad and confusing lectures.  Exams fairly easy though. Never there for office hours.  Hard to talk to.  Class was easy because I had the material in other classes, but this teacher is just bad.  Take 270 from someone else if possible.

There is little or no narrative in his teaching. His lectures seem to have no direction and he can't focus on a topic he is explaining. When you teach a topic you need to make a general explanation of the big idea before you delve into details; he can't do this. Please avoid this professor as he doesn't seem to take his job seriously. NOT engaging.

Despite what people say, I took his class during the summer 2024 semester, and personally, while I found his exams difficult, I believed he was both a fair grader and explained concepts clearly. He was not very hard to talk to, as long as you show up and participate in his class, you'll be good. I liked him.

Professor He frequently gets confused in the middle of lecture and spends multiple long, silent minutes trying to understand again. His explanations are not the best either, even when answering student questions. He definitely knows what he's teaching, but could use some work on lecturing. You'd be better off with someone else.

By far one of the most poorly structured courses in the Technology & Management curriculum. There is no clear grading criteria and by far no vision on where the course is going as it is just an abundance of content that has little application. Especially with this class geared towards non-engineering students, there is no opportunity to learn here.

Despite the negative connotation that Prof He brings from WAF, he was actually OK for ECE340 in SUM24. Lecture was just going over the powerpoint, which is a summary of the required textbook. He summarizes the textbook very well. The exams were fair, averages were around 75-80%, with low being around 60%. Very accommodating for exams. Great guy.
I'd rather watch paint dry then listen to him. Good Luck
You cannot understand him and he makes a lot of the process so much harder than it needs to be. The class itself is already difficult and it just makes it worse.
Hard to understand, talks to the chalkboard. Its better to read the book than listen to him, he makes the class more confusing than it already is.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Can not teach, you can barely understand what he says
Difficult to understand. Does not explain anything clearly. Writes equations on the board and does not go through any of the steps. Lecture feels like it is all over the place.

Pretty much a super average professor.  Has an accent but you can understand him.  Delivers the information and not a lot else.  He did a bunch of examples from the book, but they often didn't feel too helpful.

Taking both STAT425 and STAT385. I feel that her STAT425 is better than STAT385. However, she maintains the patient style in her OH. She has many experiences with R and always gives good feedback. However, her exam is a little bit tricky to use Canvas, so taking her 385 does need attention and time to prepare for the exams.

She is a very nice person, and you can feel you learned a lot if you go to her OH frequently and ask questions. She is willing to share her knowledge and experiences with students. Her exams are reasonable with extra credit. However, her study materials are messy, so taking her class requires students to be organized enough to overcome this...

Best statistics professor at UIUC. Had her for both 425 and 426. Lectures are solid, but she's super easy to get in touch with if you ever need help with any topics. People giving her low ratings clearly just didn't try. She gives amazing explanations at her office hours and both homework and tests are pretty easy for a 400.
She's a good professor. Although R is banned from using in midterms, the course is still great overall, and I'm sure the lectures will be productive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall, I think professor Jia is a good professor. Lectures didn't go super in depth, so just showing up and listening will probably only give you a surface level understanding of the material. But if you ask questions or go to office hours, she gives good explanations with examples. As long as you don't slack off too much, you'll do fine.

I had her for 425 and 426. Her teaching definitely improved in 426. I recommend attending the lecture; just looking over her slides is not enough. She's very personable and patient during office hours. Exam questions are just like the practice exam.

Run. 
She has no clear structure and does not follow the slides. She uses no recordings as a strategy to maintain attendance rates.

Had her for 425 and now 426, she is the goat, it's hard to believe people like stepanov over her. They have stockholm syndrome for him. Tests are not bad just make your formula sheet good. Her extra credit is the best! Clutch for my last undergrad semester

Maybe she's better for STAT425, but do not take her for STAT385. It's clearly her first time teaching it. Despite being known as being an easy course, she had to curve the exam because it was so different from the study guide. Class content is all coding but exams are all written and you can't use R, which is the worst class setup in my opinion

Lectures are much harder than the homework and exams. Going to her office hours is very helpful and she answers all your questions if you do. The exams are also very straight forward and she gives a good practice exam before hand.

Lectures are hard to follow. Plenty of extra credit just have to take advantage of it. Most people are bipolar when it comes to liking her, one day they praise her the next day the discord is blows up with critique. Just keep doing the work and use AI if you dont understand anything and youll be alright. Crazy how people think 410 is easier

Her lectures are a bit confusing, and I don't know if that is the content of the course or how she lectures. But take an hour out of your week and go to her office hours and you should have no issue. In person I found that she is a huge help. Also her TAs seemed pretty forgiving with grading, lots of partial credit.
Nice person but this course made me want switch out of the major

Nice person but very meticulous grader and very unorganized. Though the material is relatively easy, lectures were a mess and the material was haphazardly thrown together. (E.g. the random R snippets with no context in her slides). I thought I did well but when I got my midterm back she is very picky. Would avoid at all costs
Very insightful lecture and organized slides;
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was alright
Good professor! Give extra credits, listen to students' questions about the exam questions and give points back. Well prepared lecture. Share lots of tactile sensors during class time.

Miserable person who can hardly call herself a professor, unwilling to listen to students, difficult to work with outside of class, doesn't know how to teach anything to anybody, I can't believe someone can get paid to be a professor and then just barely even read the slides in class, nobody knows what she says in class because of how fast she goes

The lectures are boring, dry, and hard to follow, and cover topics you will not have yet covered or will ever focus on in CHEM 236 - despite her husband teaching that class. She also relied on the TA for EVERYTHING, including course logistics. At least she never skipped class, though her exam averages were almost as low as in CHEM 236...

Labs and their reports were fine enough, but the exams were ridiculous. Averages never exceeded 50%. People will try to tell you lectures are unimportant - this is untrue. Majority of the exam questions were either best answered with preexisting 236 knowledge or little blurbs from lecture

Professor White's lectures can seem dull, but they're essential to pay attention to if you want to do well in the class. The exams are very tough, and you are given a limited time. For the lab reports, the grading falls on your TAs, so it depends on how generous they are. Professor White is very kind, and she'd give out free snacks before lecture.

The knowledge of the course is mainly taught by TA and the professor gives her lecture by simply reading the PowerPoint. Completely a waste of time if you go there.
 The first exam had  the average of 64, which was higher than TA's expectations. So on our next exam our average was 46. It's dreadful. 
Be sure to complete past papers before exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's safe to say that Professor White has mastered the art of making learning organic chemistry an exercise in frustration and futility. If you value your sanity and GPA, avoid like the plague.
Tests are hard, tests will cover things that were not emphasized. Not sure if this is normal, but there were only ten lectures worth of content.

Tests are based on lecture material, but unrealistic in terms of scope. The professor knows the material, but the TAs know more about what is actually going on in lab than she does. Memorize all HNMR, C-13 NMR, and IR chemical shifts/group locations in advance if you want to succeed on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is honestly not as bad as everyone says she is. I found her to be a pretty alright professor. Her lectures are easy to understand if you have a background in the topic already, but they may be a little fast if not. Otherwise, it wasn't bad. Much of the class is run by the TAs, and they are extremely helpful and kind. Tests are hard, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Don't let the other reviews fool you: you will be okay! Labs are much easier and much better planned than 203/205 and the examswhile difficultare manageable. Prof White never once yelled at my class and the TAs were caring and accessible. I learned a lot.

The labs are not too bad as they are graded by TA's. Her lectures are not extremely useful but will give you around a 510 point boost in tests if you know the material. She's notorious for not replying student's emails, but the TA's are extremely helpful and dedicated. I learned a lot from the course, maybe not too much from her specifically.

Professor White can be very intimidating.  She often jumps into the material without giving her students any background on what she is going to be teaching.  The lectures weren't very organized, and she assumes that her students know way more than they actually know.  I would not recommend her, but she is usually the only one teaching this course.

Christina White is the kind of professor to specifically say something won't be on the exam and then make it 25% of the exam. She loves to stand in front of her unreadable mechanisms and get upset when anyone gets something wrong. She does not have office hours and does not make herself available. Belongs in a lab and out of the classroom.

She is extremely intelligent but her teaching methods are not the best. According to her, if you're taking the class you should already have an introduction to organic chemistry. Her exams are extremely long and convoluted. Work hard!!!

She is not a nice person but an ok professor. She's a good lecturer but very mean to students and most did not like her. Be prepared for lab exams - they're difficult and she does not curve. She has yelled at us several times and brags about her research. But very possible to get an A with lots of studying

She is a really horrible person. Extremely mean and degrading. The class itself can be enjoyable (esp compared to old chem classes), but the only thing that save me were the TAs. Be prepared to study for her lab exams and don't expect a curve. Try to avoid her.
I'm in love...

I enjoy Orgo Chem and I had taken Chem 236, the lecture course, in the previous semester, so the material wasn't the issue. Biggest complaint is the professor herself. She has no interest in teaching at all which she explicitly stated to me in a research group interview. If you are looking for a real teacher look elsewhere. Avoid her at all costs.

His section was harder than the last two, but I learned the most and really enjoyed his section. Just study the lecture notes really hard and you'll be ok. He also tells interesting stories during his lecture time.

If you're planning of taking ANSC 222, I would just know that Dr. Wheeler is a great professor and I  enjoyed his anatomy section, but his exams are not very picture heavy. You don't need to label much of anything rather you should focus on origin and insertion and directional questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While he only taught for the first few weeks of class, he was a very thorough and smart professor. This class has very few points associated with it in the long run, so tests matter a lot to your grade. He uses a model up front while lecturing and likes engagement. Buy the textbooks he recommends, study, and pay attention and you will be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, super nice, and explained the material very well. The lectures had a LOT of information in them so he had to explain a lot and can sometimes be a little hard to fully understand at the first go around. If you study you won't have any problems. Going to the lectures was a huge help in really understanding the material.
Bad lectures, gets off topic 24/7.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wheeler is very passionate and engaging! However, the lectures can feel very long, and there is a lot of memorization needed to do well on tests/quizzes. He did place blue text boxes on information from the slides that we would need to know, yet, a lot of the information that was not emphasized explicitly would also appear on exams/quizzes.
If you just study you'll be fine. Put in a decent amount of work and use a bit of common sense and you're good. Don't fall behind on studying tho because it can be a bit to cram.

I took this Fa21. Wheeler does the very first portion of A&P which is strictly anatomy. He does well at telling you which parts to know. However, he did on one occasion disagree with the book. The other professors for the class had objectives which can be hard for anatomy but I wish there was a way he could incorporate their lecture styles.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wheeler was an amazing teacher for the majority of the anatomy section. The material can get pretty dry and there is not a TON of extra explaining for him to do since it is a lot of memorization, but he makes it seem much less daunting once it is time to go home and study. Great teacher and he has really great stories from a fantastic career.

Prof. White is a very knowledgeable professor. He does have a unique lecture style but once you're used to it its fine. Exams and homework are hard. He expects you to be able to apply what you learned in class. Per the earlier comments, he does mention certain people in class that he is comfortable joking with but its not detrimental to the rest.

Only Prof. I have had that goes to class less than I do.  Never on time, years pass before exams are returned, and flips through lecture slides with no explaination.  Clearly only teaching because U of I make him.  An hour spent reading the alone is better that going to class.  Avoid him at all costs.
Plays favorites.  Developes a clique of toadies and apple-polishers, to whom he gives favorable treatment.  Sarcastic and unhelpful to those outside the clique.
Shes always willing to help and gives good feedback. She doesn't give study guides but she will basically tell you whats on the tests if you ask
She's awesome! She understands completely! I would take another one of her classes if i could!
LOVE HER!!
Great professor!!!She is very helpful. But to do well you should study regularly and especially do a lot of the suggested problems because she puts them in quizzes and sometimes in exams as well.

She's terrific if you put in the effort. She's very on top of responding to email and providing you with every possible resource she can. The class is obviously difficult...but if you really want to learn chem and you put in the effort, you will learn it.

Whitteck truly cares about her students and offers numerous resources for her students to succeed. However, in order to do well, you have to take the initiative and devote much time and effort to this course. Overall, wonderful teacher.

Exams are impossible! Quizzes can go either way, do the suggested problems because a lot of the quiz questions came straight from that. Definitely print out the lecture slides, she teaches straight from the power point which is annoying at times.  She does post "video lessons" on compass which can be a really helpful review.

Not a great lecturer; you'll probably want to print out the notes from the web and study on your own. Quizzes and exams were definitely harder than one would expect, but if you study on your own and manage to find a good TA, you should be able to pass.

Lectures are just ok and the exams are hard, but curved a little. Ultimately i would say take another professor if you can. Labs are a pain in the arse, you pretty much get a crappy grade for alot of work.
No emotion

Teaches from power point so notes are impossible in class. I learn better when I take notes, this teacher made it very hard to take notes so I just wrote what I could then read the chapter to make sure I understood the rest of the material.

Great teacher. Sometimes confusing, but willing to take questions in or out of class, and to explain as many times as necessary. We took Hummel's exams, which was fine becasue the material was still pertinent to what we covered in class.

Try to get Hummel instead, she's only going to be here for one more year.  Hummel's exams are easier.  Good use of powerpoints, although can be really boring during lecutre. Never anything interesting during lecture, disappointment after gretchen

Really a solid teacher, and she is willing to work with students until material is understood. The content is difficult (I mean c'mon, it's chemistry), but she made it relatively enjoyable. I still use the excellent lecture notes as my chemistry reference. For more ratings, her name was Erin Elliott before she got married...

Natalie is one of the easiest teacher at U of I. She is not only beautiful, she is also very fashion on what she wears. Besides the look, she is also an excellent teacher, she is extremely nice to international student, she grades speeches extremely easy, i believe if you follow her instructions outline on speech, it is almost an guarantee an A.
She is good teacher very friendly pretty and smart and humor. I enjoyed the class so much and I loved the grades. Must take public speaking.

she really know how to teach!!She teach so well.i really don't want to take this class,but it was a requirement for my major. She made it so fun and she is very nice. Overall, she explain and teach the materials so well.
I love this professor!!!
What a Fantastic teacher!
Well, I only have one thing to say: I love her!!!!!! She's very helpful and nice and caring and pretty of course=D
very helpful, very easy, very fun. nuf' said

Natalie was a fantastic teacher for CMN 101! She teaches the class extremely well and makes it quite entertaining. She also had a quick wit and a great sense of humor. She also uses games to teach the points as opposed to just lecturing. If you have to take CMN 101 I suggest taking it with Natalie for the best experience
Professor Wilson-Brown is knowledgable and cares about film, but classes can drag on. Classes usually consist of both a lecture and film screening.

She was fine. I think her class dynamic sucks because people don't really care about watching the movies and she doesn't enforce any rules so no one really pays attention to her lectures. Also a lot of the things she teaches are followed up by assignments so it's great if you're overwhelmed, but also made me check out a lot during class.
do not take..
Unclear feedback. Disorganized course would not take again.
Boring class and professor would yap a lot, but also a very easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was my second time having Carrie, and it was an overall very similar (and still good) experience compared to when I had her for ADV301. This course was light and easy in terms of work--only 3 essays, 2 group projects, and a few very short in-class assignments. If you follow the directions, do the work, and submit on time, you will get an A.

Lectures were very insightful and I was always engaged in class. She does not respond to emails at all which needs to be changed, but she is very accommodating if you talk to her after class. No exams, but come to class to get points for the in-class participation assignments. 3 papers, but they are 1-2 pages each and are pretty interesting topics.
Carrie is a really intelligent and helpful professor. While class is not mandatory, there are in-class assignments, and a good amount of writing is involved.

Not a good experience with her, for some students she's more open to helping them than others. not responsive outside of class. Attendance wasn't mandatory but she's most likely to play favorites with those who do attend. I think the course she teaches is very fun, but she needs needs to do some reconstruction with it. Very critical of your work.

Carrie has a great passion for the influencer industry and social media as a whole. ADV 301 (becoming an influencer) is easy--you have to make a social media post once a week. However, there are a few other assignments that were a bit tedious to complete (and you only had a short amount of time to do them). Not very responsive to emails either.

I took ADV290 (Social Media for Social Justice) and you can tell she's passionate about the subjects she teaches and enjoys teaching students about it. It's very lecture-heavy, but towards the end it becomes loose. The only downside is that she is not reachable outside of class because she doesn't respond to e-mails. Other than that, she was okay.

Professor is new to UIUC, I had both ADV 310 and ADV 290 in the same semester with Wilson-Brown. Received my lowest grades in my entire college career in these two courses... coincidence? Professor said attendance was not mandatory, but would give pop quizzes in class that you could not make up. Influencer class is popular, but I regret taking it.

I had Carrie for ADV290 (Becoming an Influencer) in the Spring and absolutely loved the class. It felt very informal and chill. She does take a while to grade assignments, but she doesn't give that many and is very understanding of her students' time commitments. I enjoyed the class and would take it again.
Class structure didnt work for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very unorganized and takes a very long to grade even the smallest homework assignment. She questions why kids are getting 100s in her classes, but then never even puts out a full syllabus.
Took ADV 290- Becoming an Influencer and hated it. She is so unorganized and does not really specify course content yet expects you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I thought Becoming an Influencer was going to be a fun class but it was not at all. Professor Wilson takes forever to grade assignments and provides unclear feedback. You have to make several social media posts and she is very judgmental about them so there is little room for creativity. Unnecessarily hard and the class was disorganized, don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lectures are super heavy and he keeps yapping on and on. I personally had to teach myself the material in my own time which was better than listening to the lectures. Also the grading of the Labs are not consistent -- they are supposed to be graded on efforts but are instead graded on accuracy and points are taken off for niche details.

Lectures are a pretty good cure for insomnia, but he's very knowledgable about the topics. Pretty convoluted grading for the labs. Overall not a very difficult course, but the amount of work took me more time than my 400-level courses somehow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were a bit boring and hard to follow

Took this class partially in-person, but went online halfway through bc of COVID. Decent amount of work if you haven't coded before, but otherwise totally manageable. Willits actually cares about his students and their understanding of the content... class is easier w friends!
Unclear grading curve. Lectures were less helpful than the textbook, and there were no practice exams or example problems.

No mock exams, no lecture notes, and boring lectures. You can literally learn nothing on class since it is difficult to follow his teaching, all you can do is to read the textbooks before the midterm and expect the questions to be friendly (actually this won't happen).
Mid-to-good lecturer, awful handwriting, and terrible grading criteria.
Honestly an amazing professor he is very lenient with exams and curves a lot when students don't do so well. He's also funny and entertaining. Overall, just a really good professor.

Terrible lecturer. If you sit down for the hour you get to watch him scribble proofs terribly on the chalk board in the most horrendous hand-writing imaginable. Learn from the textbook you are better off not going to lecture. He is funny but not helpful and his attitude when you ask for help during office hours leaves much to be desired.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The instruction is very unclear during the lectures. Tests are weighted extremely heavily and homework takes forever to get grades back. He is a funny guy, but not a good instructor. Don't expect to get homework back before taking the exam that covers that material.

Funny and great proffesor. Weird but he teaches well. If you ask him a question he makes sure to answer it to the best of his abilities even going off-track from lectures sometimes.

He wants you to learn and ask questions. Great Prof. Glad to have Math 213 with him.
If I could give a 0 I would
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Legitimately the most annoying accy professor at U of I. She cannot teach, and does not care about structuring lecture material to fit exams. I actually had my exam grades improve when I stopped showing up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Curves grades at the end of term, class is difficult so although she does not take attendance, it is important to show up to class, it is very easy to fall behind, but hard to catch up. Written problems on practice exams are similar to what you will see on the actual exam.

Avoid at all costs. Moved through lectures extremely fast and read word-for-word off the screen. Did not go into detail at all. Tests are difficult and leave no room for error. Tests cover a lot of material, and "Everything is fair game" when there are 980+ slides. Just don't take her

Terrible at teaching! Avoid her if at all possible. Goes extremely fast in lectures and expects you to know the little details for the exams. Grades the short answers on exams very tough. Homework/quizzes are McGraw Hill, so they don't have anything to do with the exams/class. Overall, just not good at her job and does not care.
She was good at explaining concepts and open to any questions. Her office hours are very helpful.

Literally take any other professor for this course. She does not teach material that is at all relevant to the in class exams. It is a course where you need to use your textbook and could honestly skip lectures.
She was awesome. I learned a lot and I am planning to take her classes again this coming semester. Project was very useful.

Melissa is an expert in her field. A lot of individual and group activities as well as detailed assignments are required. He is heavy on in-depth and well defined analysis of each assignment that can be frustrating and challenging but certainly teaches you more than you anticipated. I worked hard for my "A" grade.
This class focuses almost entirely on performative education. How to say the right things.

I'd pass on her class unless you want an easy class. Considering what I paid I should have taken something with more meat. Read articles. Say what you think. She's ok with that. Very constructovist. I want to know how the world works so I can get a job. Watch out for projects. If your project looks less than others you are down graded.
LOVED this class. I learned so much, and her lectures were always engaging. I knew exactly what to work on with assignments and expectations were really clearly stated.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Took a few classes.   Needed hours.  Content normal, no new.  She just repeats what the students say.   It's not a "present knowledge and educate the student" type of class.  It's "whatever the student thinks is ok, their ideas shape the class."  One project, I met the requirements.  Others did more.  I got graded down.  Wouldn't discuss it with me

I can see why students might not enjoy Professor Wong's teaching style. You have to want to succeed and be willing to work for it. If you're not willing, don't bother taking her classes.  She's an excellent professor if you're going to make an effort, and if you really care about what the subject matter. I would love to take another class with her.

I enjoyed the class and thought it was very interesting. Although I didn't have her in person, she did her best making the online lectures engaging. There are only quizzes, discussion/reply posts. The feedback from the TA's for the discussion wasn't too helpful most of the time, but you should be fine regardless. Definitely a cool class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Top notch quality professor. I love her so much I took her twice! Highly recommend for anything business law related! She's probably on my top 3 professors at UIUC.

Prof. Wright is amazing! She made business law so fascinating. She is one my few 5-star reviews. Her lectures are great as are the real life examples she presents. She is funny, caring, and will go out of her way to help you succeed. Read the textbook, do the assignments, and go to lecture and you will do well. I would absolutely recommend her.

You don't need the book, but the lecture videos can be dry. Professor is great though, she uploaded lecture notes for each of the videos so I'd recommend using those to study. Weekly discussion prompts were all 1 page long, but the graders were very picky and would provide too vague explanations for point deductions. Easy but a very dull subject.
Great professor. The content is really boring but she does her best and it is obvious she cares about the subject

I liked her a lot. I enjoyed her lectures and they were almost always under an hour. She's very approachable. Make sure you understand applications of the specific laws you're learning. The book isn't necessary but it's clear, helpful, and a great way to review

She's really nice and uses real life examples that helpful. Very dry class but it's what she has to teach. You don't have to go, but get credit for going and EC at the end if you go to all classes. I recommend getting course hero because a lot of reviews and more helpful docs were on there.

Prof. Wright's Intro to Numerical Optimization contains tons of useful materials and should be taken by anyone that is interested in Optimization. You will need to spend tons of time reading and learning all the lecture notes, but she gives grade very fairly. As long as you make enough effort, your grade won't be bad

Professor Wright is awesome and does her best to make sure everyone does well! The material can be dry at times. 3 exams - kinda difficult because there is a ton of material on them, and 6 in-class quizzes. She gives 25 points extra credit if you miss 4 or less lectures! She recommends the book but I didn't buy it and still did well

Margaret is an amazing lecturer and has a great personality. Business law could easily be very dry, but she consistently had funny anecdotes to help you remember concepts . The class did not require a lot of work; my semester there were a ton of extra credit opportunities and the tests were heavily curved. "Way to go Margaret"
not only does she give so much extra credit but it  is also very easy to earn the extra credit. got Bs on all test but ending up getting an A+ in her class because of extra credit

The exams were really hard and lecture is boring, but Prof. Wright was very nice and accommodating when you had questions or issues with MindTap assignments. SO much extra credit was offered which saved my grade.

Her tests have tricky questions, so make sure you really know all the concepts. Tests aren't cumulative and are mostly completely on the lecture slides. If you attend almost all her lectures for iClicker points, she gives a lot of extra credit.
Great teacher, very insightful and friendly as well. material and tests were easy
Great prof!

Every week in this class an essay with 800+ words was due, along with quizzes, and along with lectures in which you were graded directly on participating multiple times (participating once would genuinely fail you for the week). It was insane how much was asked of us in this course, it ruined the entire desire to learn about the subject for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a great professor! It's clear he's passionate to teach and to hear your ideas. I learned a lot in this class because it forces you to look at history in a different way. But don't slack off- sometimes the readings are long but they are really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: (This was a 104 class but the website doesn't have that option for some reason) Pretty good at letting the workshop flow naturally. Only stepped in to address writing errors that he saw consistently throughout multiple stories. He had office hours, but one time he never came. Really really nice and a good pick for amateur and experienced writers.

Very nice man. However, this class is pretty hard. Attendance is mandatory with your microphone on & you have to participate like 5 times on live discussion sections in order to get points for the week. Lots of homework, a lot of readings, participation matters, can't skip ANY online discussions, many papers, NO LATE WORK EVER, very tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved this class. I took his online class and it was attendance and participation heavy but it was worth it. The readings are incredible and he makes you work, but it is all productive. He's incredibly intelligent and I think this class is so worth the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I always come to this this place for recommendations on classes, but do not leave comments.  Professor Wright is very good. Very, very good. Kind individual. He changed how I look at English.  I am a senior leaving here, all you before me, take him. Quite nice individual. Helpful.

If you have to take RHET 105, definitely take it with David Wright. It is not a hard class, but he does help you become a better writer. He keeps an informal classroom and is willing to work with you.

David takes workshopping to the next level.  You need a bit of a thick skin about your writing to take the workshops, but if you can do that, you'll grow SO MUCH as a writer.  He's really clear about his requirements.  One thing that threw me off was he didn't give written comments back, but he'll talk to you a lot about your piece outside class.

Very cool and down to earth guy. Loves to tell jokes and is very engaging. Unlike a lot of professors his jokes are actually funny. But he lays out exactly what is expected and follows it. If you give effort the class is not hard.

An engaging professor who likes to make sure Lit is applicable. I appreciate his encouragement in writing, and he is very approachable and friendly. Not an easy professor but definitely worth taking and getting to know.

The topics we have to write about are absolutely pointless and stupid not to mention boring. My writing did not improve whatsoever. In the end, his graded on a paper is really not about its content, but based on his option.
Cool professor and helpful.

Generally a nice guy and genuinely tries to make the material interesting when it isn't. Lots of reading and discussion in class is only really useful if you've read the assignment. Mostly independent work and not many chances to recover a bad grade. Still a good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Took Irish Myth as an elective and man, was it FUN! Prof. Wright taught me so much about medieval Irish culture and helped me to not only understand but enjoy otherwise tricky texts. His classes are discussion based which encourages people to really get into the genre, and now I just read this stuff for fun. Great prof. and a nice man. Love him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Old English is no joke. Not talking about the Bible type Old English but rather Beowulf old english. This is an entire new language. While the material is tough, you have to work to understand. Professor Wright does his absolute best to ensure that students understand what is going on. If you fail an exam, he will offer a makeup to get up to 80%.

When I first started the class, I hated Chaucer, but professor Wright made it interesting and you can really tell that he is passionate about teaching and what he teaches. He is always willing to help you and really prompt about getting back to your emails.
Conveys things clearly. Cool old man. Course consists of discussion of assigned readings in a seminar setting. Take him

Great professor. Her lectures are the opposite of boring, she is hilarious! She tends to go on tangents and may not cover all the material needed to know in class. Material is pretty interesting, but the book gets repetitive. Easy class. 3 tests and a weekly one question response which is easy. I highly recommend this class! You will love her!!

This class was pretty easy, yet very interesting. Professor Wright lectures a lot, but also likes class discussion. Make your opinions heard and she'll definitely lie you. For the every day responses just skim the readings and make up what you can adding in personal experience and you'll do great.

Mrs. Wright is a helpful professor and her lectures are interesting. She adds personal stories to help with a point. She grades fair on her tests and is reasonable. You need to attend class and hand in responses.
hated it

hypocritical with her teachings. She believes that she is "too nice" and is on an ego trip trying to prove to her students that she is a credible professor. Likes to flaunt her accomplishments. No room for mistakes. Says she understands what students go through and that life happens but when something actually happens, she does not understand.

Professor Neely is bald with a big white beard.  He looks like the true philosopher that he is.  Or a wizard.  Either way, he has a way of explaining philosophical concepts so they actually make sense.  Highly recommended, especially since he is likely close to 100 years old and won't be teaching forever.
I would not take this professor. He is completely strange and I never had any idea what he was talking about. You have to be pretty ODD to like philosophy...and thats all i have to say about that!

Neely is the man, very knowledgeable and an engaging lecturer. Worth it just to see his stereotypical philosopher appearance (long white beard) and to hear the various anecdotes from his youth. The only weakness is that it's effectively a straight-up lecture, very little participation. Take this now as he will not be teaching much longer.
Just do not take his course!!!

He is the WORST professor I have ever met during my 3-year college life. He is a bad lecturer, what he teached in class has almost no connection with the content of exam. Besides, our final exam's content is twice more than our exam 1, but the time limit is the same.

Martin's favorite thing to say is that he's just a "facilitator," and that learning is all up to the students, but the further we get into this class, the more I fail to see why he's even needed in the first place. There has never been a moment when he's actually helped me understand something, but it doesn't seem like he cares. Avoid at all costs.

ACCY304 is hard and boring anyway. Since it is required, all we can do is to pick one professor that is a nice person. Compared to another new professor for ACCY 304 in Spring semester, Wu is better because he is not strict at all. Wu is a really nice person. Although I almost never participate in the class, I got 90+ for attendance. Memory is key.

Professor Wu does not conduct class in the most interesting way but he does make the class very straightforward in terms of what will be on the exams. If you show up you will get full participation points and he grades presentations and other assignments very leniently. Exams are all standardized by the department so every prof has the same exams.

HE IS THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER! He doesn't genuinely want to help students learn or do better. He is very difficult to communicate with and acts selfishly towards his own interest which is research than spending time with students or teaching. Even if he seems to know the content, his attitude towards teaching and students disqualify the standard.
Wu is not really the best lecturer and he is very vague about what exactly is going to be on the exams. However, his exams were very easy and I received an A while putting in minimal work.
He thinks he is smart. Unfortunately not. He is not good at teaching at all worst professor ever

The guy knows what he's talking about. Yes, he has an accent, but it's not difficult to understand him.  You don't book a single journal entry, but you do have to apply concepts of internal control systems. This involves thinking of the bigger picture which is probably why accounting majors struggle. Less memorization, more application of concepts.

I cant speak for entier class. But my experience with Prof. Wu was great. I took it at Fall 201. Martin even gave me the textbook!! He is knowledgable and experienced. The class was hard b/c content is so tangible but Martin teaches you to think rather just to study like a monkey. Although I got B, which is disappointed, I would recommend him!!

You are very lucky to see this message. I knew Wu would not be very good, but he still surprised me. The class was more than boring. I've been there every classes but still learned nothing. I cant agree more with one comments above: even TA fell asleep in his class. Grading criteria is a mystery. Two words for all of you: Just Dont!

He was difficult to understand at times and likes to go off on tangents that are irrelevant to the course.  The class lasts nearly 2 hours but, could easily be 1.  He is not willing to help students and is more involved in his research.  The TA slept every class period or texted. He does not take your viewpoint into consideration. Overall, not good

Wu is a knowledgeable prof, but is very hard to understand. Let's students do most of the teaching for him, yet disagrees with most students' viewpoints. Extensive case assignments (14 individual, 2 group). Does not utilize compass for whatever reason. Overall would recommend taking 304 with someone else.

Unless your views match his, he pretty much discounts what your opinion. It's annoying how little structure there is to the class and how smart he thinks he is. The class was interesting at first, until I realized the professor and material was all smoke and mirrors. Participation is a huge chunk of your grade and you have a case due most everyday.

Wu is an awful, awful professor.  He teaches you literally nothing, yet he acts like the class is so important.  It is a total waste of time and is pure busy work.  The previous poster that said dumb kids feel smart is completely correct.  These topics are common sense, and a lot of dumb kids get really into discussing the simpleton topics with him
No Comments

Eh... so so professor.  He thinks he is a lot smarter than he really is because he has the best answers to questions, but I would hope that the professor would have better answers.  Really forces you to think, which is good, but classes really really lacks any kind of structure.

He is very passionate about teaching. Many of teh negative comments on here are there because the material is very intangible. Class is what you make of it. He teaches you to think rather than to take tests with identical problems as given in class like a monkey. If you have an entreprenuerial mindset you will like class because youll apply it.
He is passionate about his teaching, but he can easily get on your nerves..I would recommend not taking him..also, he would never directly answer your question.

worst class i've ever taken, worst teacher i've ever had, common sense yet i got an awful grade, can't understand what he says and if you could it'd be worthless anyway, class lasts full two hours, stupid kids feel smart because material is so simple and participate extensively, just drawing out the overall suffering, ahstrategicahhsystemsahhproach

MATH 231 is, as expected, a very challenging course. Wyser is a solid lecturer, though his attitude could be better. He's not very patient and tends to rush through his responses to students' doubts. But he's knowledgeable and passionate, which is more than you can ask for to pass this course. Just keep up with WebAssign and always attend section!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good and clear professor. He sometimes gives off an attitude like he doesn't want to be there, but you kind of just get used to it.

It was tough learning all of the disparate material, not to mention taking my first proof-based class, but I would highly recommend Dr. Wyser. He was really accessible, and his notes were clear and concise. I had to do a lot of reading from the text to get it, though. And the homework was pretty challenging at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Wonderful lecturer. As a math minor, he really helped me develop my mathematical maturity. His lectures were clear and informative, and helped me fill in the gaps that the book missed. I would highly recommend taking him as your first upper-level math professor.

Prof. Wyser is not very good at proof-based math. Porf. Wyser don't like to use definition, which make me feel he is not a good mathematician. So, his lecture will not help you to build a math foundation. And I can never understand why a math lecturer emphasis so much on attendance.
He is a cute professor. His exams were not very difficult. He answered emails quickly and tried his best to help students.

His lectures are awesome. Sometimes he looks like he is angry but he is not. He is just tired (maybe not, but he doens't hate you!). He cannot be a mean person because he has three daughters. Also, he is very very smart and the grading is not harsh. He is teaching next fall so I recommend this class. p.s. I think he is nice.

He did good at lecture but not good at being individually asked problems. His lecture is very clear and he did well on notes on the blackboard. However, he would get annoyed quickly when you have some difficult questions.

Overall he is a very intelligent man, and he does do an excellent job giving lectures in class, as they are easy to follow. He writes legibly and stays consistent in notation. The class difficulty and workload is manageable. The big problem, though, is he does send vibes that he doesn't want to teach. In office hours, he gets very annoyed quickly.
Early in the semester, he seemed like he did not want to be there at all, but he seemed more invested in the class as it went on.  He improved a lot and made class worthwhile.
Prepare to google. He doesn't teach much in class.

Xiaohui is a good instructor -- not the best, but not terrible either. I think his teaching methods, while not very entertaining, are still very direct, organised, and clear. He shows examples and then proofs. Many students complain about there being too much theory taught, but keep in mind that STAT400 is a math theory focused statistics course.
His Mid-term was fine. However, his final is gonna be like Thanos holding all the infinity stones. Almost the entire class might be fail if there is no curve.

Mediocre lecturer at best. His tests are extremely hard and he doesn't curve, so he will destroy your GPA. The TA's are only help half of the time since only some of them actually understand what's going on. This class was an awful experience from start to finish.

Awesome teacher, funny insightful extremely helpful

Best teacher I've had at U of I so far. Classes were never boring and she is great at leading interesting and engaging discussions. Not much work, just reading and a giant paper at the end of the semester. Participate and you will get an A.
see for yourself. some people loved it others hated it... no middle of the road.
always excited and supportive, particularly when we had to do our own research.  a few too many articles, but a great class.

I don't understand how anyone could say she was a bad professor. She's just about the nicest human being on earth and is very concerned about students understanding the material. always seems excited about class, and wants to hear what students think.  very heavy reading in class but interesting.

Can be sort of quirky but makes the class interesting. Her tests truley tested your understanding of the material. I will for sure try to take another class with her.

The professor definitely is the best yet, he is so nice and caring for his students! One time I had to get surgery, and missed the finals, instead of giving me a low score. He knew I was familiar with the subject and gave me a B+, and also patted my back saying that mistakes happen.

Honestly, after this, I would love to do this again. His classes are wonderful. The lectures are so inspiring and exciting, it can be a bit bland at times. But this professor deserves his credit 100%. He helps everyone when they're struggling!

His class is horrible. Even if everything is open book it doesn't matter, you spend more time out of class trying to figure it out then you should.

This guy is completely useless in lecture. His accent is hard to understand, and he talks extremely quietly. That being said, the class isn't that hard. The exams are open book and open notes. Utilize TA office hours and you should get an A without a problem.
Best Professor ever met.

Great prof, prepared well for lectures and you could tell he really cared for his students. very good prof

boring lectures.  never gives review sheets.  doesn't respond to emails.  gives way too much reading for his class. final is cummulative- which means about 3 books and a packet full of readings.

very good professor, she explans everything clearly and tries to make student understand every formula behind the idea. class attendances are important, otherwise you will fail the exam.

Amazing professor! One of the best at this college, teaches with so much passion and really kind and respectful. If you attend his lectures, you are almost guranteed a good grade.

Great guy. Always has engaging material and is truly worth trying for in class.
One of the best professors at Gies!! Classes are fun and exams are super easy!

One of the best professors at UIUC. He's funny, relatable, and genuinely cares about his students and about the content he teaches. BADM 320 has been one of my favorite classes I've taken in college and it was thanks to him. Definitely take his class if possible, you will not regret it!

The GOAT himself. Professor Wolters always had great lectures even for being 8am. Get a seat in the front row if you can. Wolters is a unique professor. Overall, he's the most energy i've seen in a lecturer and he knows how to tell a good story to back up material. Overall, he knows his stuff but could improve there.
Very funny professor; motivational and bright. His classes were in early mornings but his lectures always woke me up with the awesome vibe he had.

Dr. Wolters is friendly and a great instructor. He made the course enjoyable and everything was straightforward. The class was very easy and he cares about his students. The quizzes and exams are super easy and the questions are mainly common sense, expect nothing less than an A.

He is a very good professor and very knowledgeable, but.
Easy A but you learn nothing

Great guy and great professor
Prof. Wolters is an amazing professor. I really enjoyed having class around the world each week. The course is extremely easy and there is a lot of practical application to the lectures.
Professor Wolters is fantastic. His lecture videos and practice exams are very helpful and his travel channel is very inspiring. Awesome class!
Great professor that makes a boring Business Gen ed fun. He really cares about his students and he makes the class easy for those who don't necessarly care about marketing.

Great professor and easy class. But to be honest sometimes I will get tired of his way of teaching after 20 short videos a week. You will learn but you will probably get bored in the online environment.
Best ever

Mark is right up there with the best professors at the university. He makes learning the material super easy and he cares about his students a lot. Great professor. Easy class. Take it

Mark was so amazing, I just transferred to uiuc from a different school and I was worried about jumping into a 300 level marketing course, but he is by far my favorite professor and I bet it'll stay that way! Very passionate professor, taking his lecture feel great.

I love this guy, he's so informed and in touch with millennials, it's great. If you have to find another session to attend, you'll get attendance credit

He is a fun guy and his lectures are very informing. Your grade is based off of three midterm exams (no final) and a few very easy participation points. To pass the exams just study previous exams and they will be easy.
All I can say, I will miss his class. He connects everything well to what understand. And he is nice in addition to that.

Wolters is amazing. He makes his class really easy and is super nice and relatable dude. He has random attendance checks but will excuse if you have a good reason for missing. Hes a genuine and funny guy who understands what his class is and doesn't make it something you have to worry about. He markets his social media/youtube stuff in class a lot.

Best Professor at UIUC! BADM 320 is so much more than marketing, he teaches you all the basics of business and terminology that you'll use in real life business deals. A must take! Buy the book since the review exams & attendance check papers are in there (gives you until the 1st exam to buy it though). 3 exams (no final), 1 quiz, & attendance. As long as you go to class & pay attention you'll pass. He makes class fun & the material is interesting. Exams aren't hard if you watch his playlist & look at the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Uses examples from his YouTube channel business to complement lessons. Humorous approach to subject material. Encourages further learning especially in marketing field.

Best teacher! He actually cares about the students and understands how busy we are. Lecture is optional but you are missing out on the funniest professor on campus. Mark Wolters is hands down the BEST professor at UIUC. I really wish he could teach all of my classes. The man explains everything so well and his lectures are very entertaining. Such a great professor! Best professor I have had! Gives attendance checks, but lectures are fun and he sometimes hands out food. He really cares about his students. Great class!

One of the best professors at UIUC! Really cares about the students and teaches in a way that we can relate to. I didn't mind attending lecture because he made things interesting. Would highly recommend Wolters, he is a great professor and great guy.

Probably one of the my favorite professors I have had on campus! Definitely take his class. I have used the basic marketing concepts learned in other classes, and it's an easy A!
Cool guy

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! But seriously, he's extremely entertaining and actually cares that his students take away something from his class.

Great teacher, funny and easy going. Defiantly take this lass with him!
Awesome teacher and even greater guy. Realizes he is at this university to promote the academic and professional growth of his students. I definitely recommend this course.

super entertaining! makes class fun & makes it really easy to study for exams with his helpful videos. loved him so much I'm taking another class of his!

Great teacher!

awesome professor!Funny and grabs your attention

Great, easy

He is my favorite teacher. The class was awesome.

He is the man. You only have to show up to a handled up of class to fulfill the participation portion. There is also a ton of extra credit. Cares a lot and make the lectures enjoyable when you go to them
Mark Wolters is the best professor I've ever had at the U of I. He is really passionate of what he's doing. I highly recommend taking this class.
Wolters is the man. Highly recommend.
best professor ever! If his lecture is 8 in the morning, i will still highly recommend you to choose that section!! that's the professor's charm!!

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!
He made the class interesting and i enjoyed going

Favorite professor at U of I! He genuinely cares about his students, is passionate about teaching, and knows how to keep students engaged. He also gives students the grade they want/deserve if they meet expectations.
Hilarious!

First time I've ever written one of these. Quite simply, you are at a loss if you don't take Wolters.  Not difficult, extremely captivating, and still learned more than most other business classes.
Great professor!

Awesome teacher!
Watch the videos and read the lecture slides and you will do very well! Wolters is super nice and funny and very easy to understand

Mark accommodates this business core class for everyone. His classes are fun and entertaining, and he's honestly there if you want to know more about marketing (or more). He honestly cares about the subject and his students. The exams are pretty straight forward - just review the powerpoints and watch his videos. You should get an A!

One of the best teachers I have had at U of I. Very interesting guy, he makes the class so easy to understand and you'll want to go to class to hear about all of his amazing experiences from around the world!
Super cool guy. Doesn't want to give you a bad great. There are attendance quizzes once a week, but going to class is the only work that you have to do besides studying for tests
great professor who's passionate when it comes to teaching but reasonable when it comes to grading.

Mark Wolters is a great professor. He is passionate about what he teaches and also very knowledgable. He particularly wants his students to really learn his material, so he goes above and beyond to make sure that every learning style is accommodated.

Great class! I hope he teaches BADM 320 for years to come! He doesn't make you do annoying McGraw-Hill online homework. There are only 3 exams, but you will be well prepared for them as he provides videos that will help you for the exam. WATCH THE VIDEOS - a lot of questions come from the videos verbatim.

One of the best professors out there! He can makes it really entertaining to come to class although the material can be a little dry sometimes. He tries his best to make sure that everyone understands by making videos that can be found on youtube.  Hes very fair on tests, straightforward questions, not tricky. Overall good guy. Totally recommend!

Amazing professor! He is so passionate about teaching and the subject, it is hard not to respect the guy! I definitely recommend taking this class with him! He is so helpful and makes great videos to help for studying! He is also funny which makes class more enjoyable!

Mark is the best professor.  His lectures are so much fun and he is very knowledgeable. You can tell that he loves what he does and he is more than happy to help if you have a question.  Make sure you take this class with him! Or any other class that he teaches for that matter.
Pretty cool. He makes sarcastic jokes. Sometimes funny.
Mark is an awesome Professor! I'm really happy that I had classes with me! Really knowledgable guy full of real life examples! Top Notch!

He has the perfect combination of knowledge, energy, dynamics and personality. He has the differentiation factor! Unforgettable classes! I was extremely lucky to have him as a professor at Nova School of Business and Economics, in Lisbon, Portugal.
Even having to explain some "not-really interesting" things, we also did well. Also, really good, individual tips after presentations; never saw something like this...
Really fun... but, which is the most important, really good explanations and good teacher. Going to his classes really makes sense, and you never get bored
This professor is Awesome!! He makes things so clear with perfect examples and this together wihth the energy that he brings to class; AMAZING!

The best professor I ever had. Enthusiastic in sharing his knowledge and experience, and genuinely interested in the students. A wonderful person, funny,inspiring and a great educator. The only thing I could point out as area of improvement would be to give more feedback on students work - how can we improve, why a certain grade,etc.

Favorite professor at UIUC. He's passionate about teaching and very knowledgeable about sales, marketing and business. Classes are entertaining and very informative. He's very approachable and cares about his students. I highly recommend taking any class he teaches. If you do your best you should get an A and you'll learn a lot along the way.

(Random module in Nova University) I just thought that the course/teacher did not had much value. A lot of common sense presented in a clever way, but still nothing that made a big difference (for me at least). To be fair it was always entertaining though.
Mark is not only a competent professional but also a friend for his students. If your taking a 8am class his energy  will definitely wake you up. 5 stars
one of the best professors I had
Interested in the students, very direct and clear, funny and easy to talk to. 5*
Very helpful. Very enthusiastic. Nice guy. Knowledgeable. Class is fun and we learn a lot about the real world. Good combination of theory and practical.
Makes class fun and exciting to come to.  Awesome teacher! Take this class!

I think Professor Xu is sharp and efficient in terms of teaching skills, which is so crucial for Junior year in Architecture. Students learn a lot with this type of teacher; He is open as well. You don't have to agree with him on everything to get a good grade
The worst professor in the world!!! Easy to get bad grade although working hard. He don't know how to teach, but good at making you into bad mood!

Only knowslikes Rhino and Illustrator; has discouraged the use of Photoshop.  Doesn't always understand exactly what question someone is asking.  Loves doing Rhino tutorials... Loves.  Needs to manage his time better for desk crits. You can avoid him forcing you to change your project by tying everything to your concept.

Very knowledgeable professor. If you show interest and put work towards your project then he will too. He knows a lot about Rhino so make sure too pick his brain. The only negative is that he doesn't talk too much about architecture theory, which I was hoping he would. Solid professor though, make the most out of his section by asking him questions

He changes students projects at the last minute and makes horrible decisions. All his design choices are tore apart in review. He docs people for being 1 minute late and again changes your project no matter how much you object. He takes to belittling students who do object. Simply put a horrible professor to be avoided at all costs. Very bad breath
He does not take the time to get to know you or your project if he deems you unworthy of his attention. This is unacceptable, as it is a 4 hour class 3 times per week, with only 16 students.
The teaching style is completely discouraging, tough, harsh, and speaks very rudely.
trash trash and only trash
Too much tasks.

She was a good researcher but not a good teacher. Her classes are very knowledgeable but unfocused, the exams have content beyond the classroom, and the knowledge is difficult for graduate students to understand. There was a lot of homework and very low grades given.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Decent class. Mike was good and is clearly passionate about advertising from the perspective of an evolving digital world. However, the group project has randomly assigned groups and is to be worked on 100% outside of class (keep in mind there are over 100+ students). Attendance is not included in your grade, but you will lose points if you skip.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun and easy 300 level course. Mike is kind and understanding.

Super understanding of personal things coming up that prevent you from turning things in on time, he let me turn in a big assignment a day late just because i asked. He also gave everyone a good grade on the quizzes if you simply mentioned something from lecture. Super funny and nice, definitely recommend.

Mike is an awesome teacher. He is fun, caring, and flexible. The class project was interesting and practical. The class isn't even required to meet formally for several weeks. You should get a good grade as long as you work with your group. Much of the grade is just based on whether or not you completed something. I would recommend this class.
Literally saved my GPA. Final project was graded for completion not quality. I can see how he would be hard in any other class but honestly if you want an easy ADV gen ed this is it.

It's really not that difficult. He lectures every class, but before the test, he posts the lecture slides online himself. Each week, there is a simple SHORT response (usually 1/4 of a page long). Some group papers, simple stuff. Pretty easy to get by with at least a B. You need the book for the tests though, I got by just reading the bolded words

Really really unhelpful professor. Barely any guidance or feedback on tests or papers. Just gave the final and still haven't gotten our grades back for the previous midterm, which was taken 2 months ago. Assignment guidelines aren't specific, practically no feedback. Love PR because of real world experience, but this class will make you hate it.

One of the toughest classes I've taken. The tests are based off a mixture of anecdotes mentioned once in lecture, lecture slides, and vocabulary not mentioned prior to taking the exam. The average of our first exam was a 67%. Avoid at all costs.

If attendance wasn't mandatory you'd be better off just not going to class. She does offer limited extra credit which is nice, but she simply cannot teach, so be ready to do poorly (IE a C or lower) on both midterms if you don't try to teach yourself the material on your own time. Oh, and she doesn't allow computer notes.
I've taken Yujeong's classes the past 3 semesters and she has always been my favorite! She makes sure that everyone has the resources to succeed and is an overall caring professor

[This review goes to PS180]
Took her class last semester - she was very caring, inspirational, and supportive. She made her lecture interesting using a tons of vivid examples. Grading is fair and a lot of extra-credits were offered. She had done a lot of research about China, and she wrote me a recommendation letter for my transfer. BEST professor!

As someone anxious about emailing professors, this experience confirmed my fears. I asked what percent the final was worth, expecting a simple answer. Instead, she replied, “if you had used your calculator, you would know…” Her condescending tone made me feel stupid for asking. If you want a supportive professor, I'd recommend looking elsewhere.

Sometimes it was hard to understand what she was saying, but she did a good job of getting her point across to the class. Course structure was good and made logical sense when going from one topic to another. Essays throughout the semester but are not too overbearing. Easy questions on quizzes that are usually showed to you beforehand.

She was a great professor Purdue of her exams they were very ambiguous in the way she worded things. You could study and study but still do poor. Overall I did well enough. But I would not take this course again. Great professor hated how she grades and

Professor Yujeong Yang is one of the best professors I have ever had! She is nice and light-hearted which makes lectures fun to participate in. There was not too much homework in the class (one weekly assignment due every Sunday). However, do not wait until the last minute to work on the assignment! You will not finish it on time. 100% recommended!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Sincerely cares for her students, one of the best professors I have had. Offers tons of extra credit opportunities and wants you to get the best possible grade in the class. Responds well to feedback and changes things based on student input. Super passionate about the topic and wants you to be, too. Show up to class and you'll do well.

TA grading was strict sometimes and others not. PS100 with her is easy, I missed the lecture a few times and still got full attendance, the same thing with discussion. Papers are very easy. Midterms are direct answers from lecture.

She is one of the best professors I've ever had. Please take her if you can. She truly cares about her students and does everything in her power to help you. I took her PS 100 and I'm taking PS 343 with her this semester. I'm so excited.

Professor Yang is a very sweet and nice professor! Very accesible for office hours and very organized. WhenI took PS 100, she offered two extra credit opportunities. Exams & quizzes are pretty much just the slides she presents in class. If you review and memorize the slides before a quiz or an exam, you're gonna do great. Easy A class.

Pretty easy class. As long as you take the slide show notes you should have no problem getting an A. She goes over a few quiz questions in class before we take the quiz. All assignments are online except two midterms and the final. Weekly quizzes and reading assignments but both easy to get 100 on. She is a really nice professor.
GOAT. He is one of the best teacher I have ever had.

I took this course for my business minor. The professor was super great, always made sure you knew what was going on, and very chill. He was very understanding if you were late to class or submitting an assignment, and the "textbook" is all online for free provided in the Canvas page (so no need to pay!). 10/10 professor.

Great professor! He was super friendly and even learned everyone's names by the end of the class. Was very accommodating to everyone and gave a lot of flexibility for people to leave class early if they knew the material. The class material was taught at an excellent pace and cared a lot about if people understood the material before he moved on.

super nice guy and is understanding. I can tell he just wants you to understand the materials and he created the course to be digestible for any level coder. If you are in CS/ have coding experience this class may not be for you but if you want a supportive environment to learn, this is a great class to take.
