reviews.comment: Organic chemistry is hard. The fundamentals are challenging. But, the professor takes all this into consideration. There are prelecture videos, lecture videos, suggested textbook problems, quizzes and review sessions to help through the course. He replies to your emails and encourages everyone to come to office hours. Good luck buddy

He really wants his students to learn the material. He's a clear lecturer and will take student feedback to help everyone get the most out of class. He gives a lot of resources for you to learn outside of class if something was unclear. As long as you make an effort, the class is very manageable and interesting!

Dr. Zimmerman is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. He really cares about his students, even after we leave his class! The class it really tough and you have to work to get a good grade, but he will help in any way he can. I definitely recommend him to others! I would love to take his class again!
You will never be prepared enough for his exams. In the total grade add up, there is no homework portion. Your letter grade is based on only quizzes and exams.
I like the way he teaches.

Professor Zimmerman really cares about his students. He made prelecture video and lecture videos and he had two sets of office hours every week. He also had review sessions for exams. Lectures were engaging. For a high grade, it is important to know reactions, mechanisms, and stereochem. The grading was generous, with A82, A-80,B+78,B69,B-67

Zimdawg deserves that title because he is top dawg. He provides pre-lecture videos, video lectures, his own hand written notes on top of his already amazing lectures that are perfectly clear. He has plenty of availability for questions and office hours. No homework; all grades are from challenging exams and quizzes with a generous curve.

Professor Zimmerman is by far one of the greatest professors I have ever had. His love for organic chemistry is clear and resonates in his teaching approach. He  provides all of the resources that are necessary to succeed (i.e. pre-class and post-class videos).  While organic chemistry is a difficult course, he clearly explains all topics.

Professor Zimmerman has been one of my favorite professors at U of I. He really cares about his students and teaching and it really shows. The class itself is difficult, but it you love chemistry it won't be that bad.
Really puts in the effort to help students out.

Great professor who's very willing to help. Organic chemistry can be a hard subject, but Zimmerman explains things in a easy to understand and intuitive manner. The course itself had a generous curve and was very organized with video lectureslecture notes posted online. Not the easiest class, but very manageable if you put in effort.

I'm a straight A student and I'm struggling in this class for a C. Goes over so many unimportant things in class and in recordings. Know the mechanisms, NMRs (for later), and you should be fine. Everything else he says, don't bother writing down, you won't need it. The only good thing about this class is that the curve is relatively generous.

Prof. Zimmerman is extremely dedicated and eager to help. Extremely organized and has videos for every lecture. Material is hard but grades are curved so it's easy to get at least a B. One of the best professors I've had.

Hard class. Mediocre professor. I hate how sometimes instead of explaining or giving reasons, hes just like, you should already know that based on what you learned in gen chem. so it sucks if you forgot general chemistry material or if you didn't have the gen chem professor he's referring to. really fast paced class. get ready to work for it.

Zimmerman did a very good job teaching about laboratory techniques. I enjoyed his anecdotes about his experienced in the lab and his overall laid back lecturing style. Exams and quizzes were pretty much all or nothing with almost no partial credit, which was one of the only downfalls of the course.
Fun and good professor.  orgo is hard, but he gave us clear and organized notes. he did talk about the history of some chemistry, which was interesting.  he definitely cares about his students.  =)

He is a nice guy but is not a good teacher. He goes over unimportant things like the history etc. but does not go over explanations. He almost never explains mechanisms and sometimes gets them wrong. It is desirable to reason through mechanisms because there is a lot of material. He does not give the theoretical background to do this though.
So far he's pretty good

She was amazing! She made material that could be seen as dull very interesting and funny. 10/10 would recommend to any other student! The tests were challenging but she makes so much of the material easier to understand, by giving us stories about it, we were able to remember what was needed to pass.

Seriously, she's SO hilarious. She has the best stories and she's a total sweetheart. I literally never wanted to skip her class. Exams were kind of tough but the project was actually pretty interesting.  Plus, she's like, Claire Dane's doppelganger. So cute!
She is so cool!

This guy loves Chinese poetry. He can make a poem or text about the most dull topic the single most interesting thing you'll ever hear. It's been three years and I can still remember some of his more passionate lectures on poems. Go to class, bring your book, and be ready to recite, and he'll love you. Ask him to read stuff in Cantonese too.

Hated this professor with a passion.  He seems nice, but he's a jerk.  He graded all my essays a full letter lower than I usually receive for comparable writing.  When I explained this to him and asked about extra credit, he told me I was insulting him.  I know other students in the class who had similar experiences with him.
Great class & prof!
Professor Cai is wonderful--he really knows his stuff, is generous with students, and he's funny too! But most important he communicates the value of learning Chinese & all its possibilities.
Crappy teacher.  Not lenient at all, especially with mid-terms.  No make-up exams.  Assigns too much work.  Hard to understand.

This guy's a great teacher for Chinese. He knows a bunch of stuff, he's patient and helpful. He does a good job at explaining class material. Homeworks, quizes, and exams are all very easy. Plus he makes the class fun by talking a lot about off topic subjects.

Generally awful lectures.  Unprepared, unorganized.  Sloppy.  Doesn't seem to care about students.  Exams seem to be fairly random and he offers no guidance or help at any point.  Misgraded my first exam twice, despite my clear explanation; eventually got the points.  Could have been a good class but wasn't.  Avoid.
unorganized lecture, exams diff a lot from regular assignments, avoid him if possible
Zoltan Furedi might be a good math advisor, but he does not care about the classes.  His lectures seemed unorganized and not very helpful.

Prof. Gille is a great lecturer and discusses her personal experiences in ways that are really intriguing. So far, SOC 366 has been my favorite course to date. Great course with the most interesting readings I have probably ever been assigned.

Her instructions are very long and detailed, and at the end of it, you still aren't sure what the instructions are. One thing about her though, is that she is very helpful, she is always open to questions and helping along the way. Her classes reminded me of a highschool class.

The professor is not helpful. Questions are not welcomed and reading assignments are overwhelming. Even half of my class dropped. The class itself is not difficult. It is not rocket science.  It is just a lot of work for a 3 credit hour class.

Honestly, she is a good teacher.  Just because her class is not "easy" does not mean she did not teach effectively.  You will have to work for your grade, think outside the box and hit the books.  This is a professor with excellent life experience and promotes a world view from outside of the typical American.

I love Zsuzsa! I am purposefully taking a class with her this semester I liked her so much in 366, and I am also planning on taking an independent study with her.  She is extremely knowledgeable and understanding. If you have any interest in Eastern Europe or Environmental studies I suggest taking a class with her.
He was the best!

Hi Mr. Zumdahl I hope you read this. I never took a class with you but we are using your AP chem book(9th ed) & I have a few constructive criticisms. 1st I don't understand how octahedrals contain 6 bonds, doesn't octa mean 8? And 2nd on p. 481, Figure 10.34 says there are red Zn ions, but they're actually purple. But overall the book is  helpful.

Generally a good guy who is motivated by getting students involved in chemistry.  Unfortunately I did not agree with his teaching methods; he relies on TA's to do the teaching.  Go to lecture to watch demos and discussion to learn.
Great guy.  Really made chemistry fun.
Was the only chemistry professor who didn't get totally annoyed with me (and I've taken a lot of chemistry)  Wonder where he is now; I could use some reccomendations...

Not the best lecturer, but teaches students something important...to be excited and enthusiastic about chemistry.  His class made me realize that I enjoyed learning about chem and was ready to pursue it as a career.
full of himself.  should loan his car to students who have to buy his new books every year.
this man can't teach. he is awful. he is lazy. he also has verablly abused students on many cases. Loves going to krannert though.

Somehow I think he is still a teenager. Mentions sexual innuendos alot, and the many sports cars he has. Fair teacher, but honestly not really required. By studying his book, and going to discussion, you will do good.
No Comments
Love the viagra jokes
No Comments
Very smart, very funny.  Could be more accessible
Tends to go off on tangents; a lot of physical chemisty begun
No Comments
No Comments
She is a great teacher and is very enthusiastic. She is a fair grader and gives many a's. It is not hard to do well in her class.
Loved her class! Heather is an easy grader and always has funny jokes to tell in class! Very enthusiastic and happy go lucky!
Great teacher. Very friendly and easy going. Work can be over tedious but not impossible.

Overall it is a fun class and isn't hard to well in. She is a nice person and tries to help you to succeed. It's just a lot of little assignments which can get annoying but she can't control it. Also one of the books is a rip off, we don't even use it.

I really like her but she grades kind of tough! I thought my speech was good but still got a B. Overall though it's a relaxed class. Everyone here has to take it and she's better than the girl I had last semester.
Super nice and loving.  She grades fairly easily and will help you get an A on any paper you want help on.  Tries to keep the class light and fun.
This was by far my favorite class of the semester. You truly couldn't ask for a better instructor in Heather. She was amazing; the whole class loved being there!
very friendly. amazing teacher!
Heather is super friendly and a great public speaker. I'm taking her class now and it's very clear she knows what she's talking about.

Definitely a time-consuming class (watch out for lab 2.1 and lab 7), but not as bad as people make it seem if you start early. Chill prof, twitch streams were very useful (saves a lot of time when first learning vivado), lectures were somewhat useful for quizzes (which tended to be pretty random). Office hours get really busy near lab due dates.
Not as hard or time consuming as I expected overall. some of the labs need better documentation.
Great professor. The material covered in the course is excellent and is applicable to industry. Loved his twitch streams and lecture style.
He teaches a tough course that requires a lot of work outside the lectures. That being said, he prepares you very well for the more difficult parts of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
Amazing professor overall- lectures are interesting and I like how his class is formatted. Twitch streams are P cool

reviews.comment: I wasn't a fan of the course organization, especially after a full semester of transitioning from Quartus to Vivado. The lab documentation was okay at best and sometimes didn't include all the relevant information. The lectures were useless, though I will say he has a good presentation style (separate from the material!).
bro he doesn't know verilog or fpga or rtl or vivado or anything. sadly a required course i had to take it and it sucked
horrible lectures and vague documentation

reviews.comment: Good professor who has been taking efforts to improve ECE 385. Used to be a 2 credit hour class which he pushed for 3 credit hours. Also moved to the industry standard Vivado rather than Quartus. Course in general is time-consuming and quiz questions are easy to answer if you attend his lectures. Very accessible outside class in his OH.

I really loved ECE 385. I wouldn't consider this class to be hard, just a lot of work but I genuinely loved the course content so it made the long hours easy. We switched over from Quartus to Viviado last semester, and I think the transition was pretty graceful due mostly to the love and care Zuofu put into the documentation/lab materials. 10/10

This class is not "difficult" but rather time consuming. One lab per week with a demo and quiz when its due. Quiz is one technical question, pretty lax. You must start early on the labs to do well, reports are pretty easy given you follow the rubric. Prof. Cheng is a fun lecturer who explains concepts well along with adding a good amount of humor.

Won't comment about the lecturing itself, as he basically just summarizes lab instructions..

However, course itself very straightforward: no exams, very fair 5-min quizzes, lab demos with very fair grading, and lab reports graded very nicely. If you put in work and go to office hours, CAs will help you learn and get A 

+ Final Project very fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The lectures really depend on your learning style. If you like a professor that blurts out a bunch of information at one sitting then go ahead. He assumes that you already know the terms that he is using, which is frustrating because there is no pre-lecture or anything we can read to be familiar with his topics.

reviews.comment:
He genuinely cares about you. I took the class and am now on the course staff. We discuss ways to help students and never try to be mean.

Best professor in ECE UIUC.

Gives very little guidance and the course itself is pretty much a trainwreck. Many times TAs or the professor himself will hsve to clarify that a third of the instructions are outdated or wrong. Frustrating course and he does not seem to want to change it.

reviews.comment: This course was easily the most time-consuming class I've ever taken, expect 20-25 hours of work per week. However, if you put in the time, it's doable. Prof. Cheng clearly knows what he's talking about, and his lectures are useful. His answers can be quite long-winded at times, but he's very caring and helpful. Overall, a solid professor!

Great teacher and a great class. Lectures were online, but he had the highest quality online lectures out of any other class that I had due to his high tech stream setup. HW is just a weekly lab and report; if you start at least a few days early and go to open lab you will get an easy A.
Professor Cheng is an awesome lecturer, and is very accessible outside of class. His labs teach you a lot. He's very cool, I would take any class with him.

Lectures give plenty of examples. The homework usually has one trick problem so going to office hours is recommended. If you understand the lecture notes and homework then you'll be set up fine for the exams. Not terribly hard if you take time to learn the material. Simpler than it seems.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Cheng is great. He is very clear, helpful, and I learned a lot from every lecture. ECE 205 was not too terribly difficult but it was a decent amount of work. Stay on top of everything and you should be fine. Would highly recommend this professor.

Took his ECE385 a year ago, and has been TA for this course for the second semester. Thanks to the work done by him and excellent TA team, the organization of this course has greatly improved. Lectures are info-dense, exams are reasonable. Labs are especially important. Prof. Cheng is very accessible and clear.
Solid Lecturer. Very good at answering questions. Beware of test questions covered in-depth verbally in lecture, but with little screentime in the slides and notes

reviews.comment: You will learn. So much without  experiencing  the usual drawbacks. Take this prof you can't go wrong.
Very helpful professor. Was willing to use his own time after office hours to help clarify things for students.

He was very knowledgeable about the subject matter, as well as being able to simplify it for new students to the electronic circuits.  Able to answer questions well during lecture.  Totally willing to work through examples with students during office hours for clarification.  Sometimes makes mistakes on the board, which most people usually catch.
As long as you sit at the front of the class room at do pay attention to the class, this should not be very hard to get a good grade. Also, pay great attention to the homeworks.

Dr Cheng is not good at organizing his lecture. And his exam is not easy. However, if you go to his office hour very often, and work hard, it would not be hard to get an A. At least, Dr. Cheng offers a generous curve. He is a nice guy and keeps himself open to students. He usually replies his email very fast.

This class broke my high grade streak. I poured hours into studying.  I also watched an ENTIRE CLASS by MIT on equivalent material!  He teaches you basic circuit analysis. But his exams test on circuit design.  And the graders gave 0 partial credit on any problem. They ended up curving the class a full letter grade.  Avoid ECE 205 and this prof!
EXTREMELY rude and condescending. Would respond to questions with sarcastic/rude answers. Try to get a different TA.

She way by far one of the worst professors I have ever had and that is saying a lot. Even if you do everything she tells you chances are your grade will not get any better. She required way more than any other CMN 111 instructor, made us dress up for speeches, which again, no other professor did, and she sorta treated us like middle schoolers.  This class is easy, but I wouldn't recommend this instructor.
